67ed00fa8583.sentence: As a type of static analysis it compares two different equilibrium states, after the process of adjustment (if any).

5365a90e7836.title: Comparative statics
5365a90e7836.sentence: It does not study the motion towards equilibrium, nor the process of the change itself.

838c4acf7b1b.title: Comparative statics
838c4acf7b1b.sentence: Comparative statics is commonly used to study changes in supply and demand when analyzing a single market, and to study changes in monetary or fiscal policy when analyzing the whole economy.

558251ea01f8.title: Comparative statics
558251ea01f8.sentence: Comparative statics was formalized by John R. Hicks (1939) and Paul A. Samuelson (1947) (Kehoe, 1987, p. 517) but was presented graphically from at least the 1870s.

6fef36c83539.title: Comparative statics
6fef36c83539.sentence: Comparative statics results are usually derived by using the implicit function theorem to calculate a linear approximation to the system of equations that defines the equilibrium, under the assumption that the equilibrium is stable.

42e5bd460253.title: Comparative statics
42e5bd460253.sentence: One limitation of comparative statics using the implicit function theorem is that results are valid only in a (potentially very small) neighborhood of the optimum—that is, only for very small changes in the exogenous variables.

b16205a42d43.title: Comparative statics
b16205a42d43.sentence: For models of stable equilibrium rates of change, such as the neoclassical growth model, comparative dynamics is the counterpart of comparative statics (Eatwell, 1987).

b45441189a25.title: Mathematical optimization
b45441189a25.section: Classification of critical points and extrema > Sensitivity and continuity of optima
b45441189a25.sentence: The envelope theorem describes how the value of an optimal solution changes when an underlying parameter changes.

d22d3f7c97e7.title: Mathematical optimization
d22d3f7c97e7.section: Classification of critical points and extrema > Sensitivity and continuity of optima
d22d3f7c97e7.sentence: The maximum theorem of Claude Berge (1963) describes the continuity of an optimal solution as a function of underlying parameters.

888346e51e8c.title: Price signal
888346e51e8c.sentence: A price signal is information conveyed to consumers and producers, via the prices offered or requested for, and the amount requested or offered of a product or service, which provides a signal to increase or decrease quantity supplied or quantity demanded.

f0d054d6cc2e.title: Price signal
f0d054d6cc2e.sentence: When a certain kind of product is in shortage supply and the price rises, people will pay more attention to and produce this kind of product.

5eec2a2a5748.title: Price signal
5eec2a2a5748.sentence: The information carried by prices is an essential function in the fundamental coordination of an economic system, coordinating things such as what has to be produced, how to produce it and what resources to use in its production.

62eccbd47b64.title: Price signal
62eccbd47b64.sentence: According to Friedrich Hayek, in a system in which the knowledge of the relevant facts is dispersed among many people, prices can act to coordinate the separate actions of different people in the same way as subjective values help the individual to coordinate the parts of his plan.

ecc2241f9487.title: History of economic thought
ecc2241f9487.section: Neoclassical (19th and early 20th century) > Continental neoclassical > Friedrich Hayek
ecc2241f9487.sentence: According to him, price signals are the only means of enabling each economic decision maker to communicate tacit knowledge or dispersed knowledge to each other, to solve the economic calculation problem.

ef921cc22b1f.title: Price signal
ef921cc22b1f.sentence: A monopoly may set prices so as to maximize monopoly profit, while a cartel may engage in price fixing.

9e25cea4ab9b.title: Price signal
9e25cea4ab9b.sentence: Conversely, on the consumer side, a monopsony may negotiate or demand prices that do not reflect the cost of production.

5b731ea1312c.title: Price signal
5b731ea1312c.sentence: Financial speculation, particularly buying or selling assets with borrowed money, can move prices away from their economic fundamentals.

b43e3578128a.title: Price signal
b43e3578128a.sentence: Credit bubbles can sometimes distort the price signal mechanism, causing large-scale malinvestment and financial crises.

5c227ce83ee5.title: Feebate
5c227ce83ee5.sentence: Fuel taxes can create important price signals that can make consumers aware of non-internalized costs of fuel consumption such as greenhouse gasses and other pollutants, and raise funds to offset this externality.

571a94d65e6b.title: Demand response
571a94d65e6b.sentence: In economic terms, consumers' usage of electricity is inelastic in short time frames since the consumers do not face the actual price of production; if consumers were to face the short run costs of production they would be more inclined to change their use of electricity in reaction to those price signals.

c48151c004a2.title: Market economy
c48151c004a2.sentence: A market economy is an economic system in which decisions regarding investment, production, and commerce (the distribution of goods and services) are guided by price signals resulting from the forces of supply and demand.

b8a8781025f9.title: Market economy
b8a8781025f9.sentence: Market economies exist along a spectrum, ranging from minimally regulated to highly regulated systems.

bc26ee217a7f.title: Market economy
bc26ee217a7f.sentence: At the least regulated end are free-market and laissez-faire systems, where government involvement is largely limited to providing public goods and services and protecting private property rights.

e90df76cf2e9.title: Market economy
e90df76cf2e9.sentence: At the other end of the spectrum are interventionist market economies, where governments take a more active role in correcting market failures and promoting social welfare.

0df17118f150.title: Market economy
0df17118f150.sentence: For market economies to function efficiently, governments must establish clearly defined and enforceable property rights for assets and capital goods.

7aff478740f8.title: Market economy
7aff478740f8.sentence: However, property rights do not specifically mean private property rights and market economies do not logically presuppose the existence of private ownership of the means of production.

2030bfac48e1.title: Market economy
2030bfac48e1.sentence: Market economies can and often do include various types of cooperatives or autonomous state-owned enterprises that acquire capital goods and raw materials in capital markets.

77c14abd65a7.title: Market economy
77c14abd65a7.sentence: Market economies rely upon a price system to signal market actors to adjust production and investment.

a3fbe292edd1.title: Market economy
a3fbe292edd1.section: The role of supply and demand in a market economy
a3fbe292edd1.sentence: When there is strong demand but limited supply, prices increase, signaling to producers that there may be opportunities to increase profits by producing more of that product.

157b9775e796.title: Market economy
157b9775e796.sentence: Governments can intervene by establishing price ceilings or price floors in specific markets (such as minimum wage laws in the labor market), or use fiscal policy to discourage certain consumer behavior or to address market externalities generated by certain transactions (Pigovian taxes).

b3a73c3a0737.title: Market economy
b3a73c3a0737.sentence: The economist Joseph Stiglitz argues that markets suffer from informational inefficiency and the presumed efficiency of markets stems from the faulty assumptions of neoclassical welfare economics, particularly the assumption of perfect and costless information and related incentive problems.

fb174102002f.title: Market economy
fb174102002f.sentence: However, Stiglitz does not advocate replacing markets, but instead states that there is a significant role for government intervention to boost the efficiency of markets and to address the pervasive market failures that exist in contemporary economies.

5894bab28745.title: Market economy
5894bab28745.sentence: A sustainable market economy seeks to balance economic expansion and environmental preservation.

c945790a9dee.title: Market economy
c945790a9dee.sentence: Tax incentives, carbon trading programs, and environmental requirements are just a few ways government rules and policies encourage enterprises to adopt sustainable practices.

993c8c4785a9.title: Price controls
993c8c4785a9.sentence: Price controls are restrictions set in place and enforced by governments, on the prices that can be charged for goods and services in a market.

3adb2577f242.title: Price controls
3adb2577f242.sentence: There are two primary forms of price control: a price ceiling, the maximum price that can be charged; and a price floor, the minimum price that can be charged.

280f4ef4f1b4.title: Price controls
280f4ef4f1b4.sentence: A well-known example of a price ceiling is rent control, which limits the increases that a landlord is permitted by government to charge for rent.

c58b9cbd06d9.title: Price controls
c58b9cbd06d9.sentence: A widely used price floor is minimum wage (wages are the price of labor).

8eb061f4b742.title: Price controls
8eb061f4b742.sentence: The intent behind implementing such controls can stem from the desire to maintain affordability of goods even during shortages, and to slow inflation, or alternatively to ensure a minimum income for providers of certain goods or to try to achieve a living wage.

49f5033cf869.title: Price controls
49f5033cf869.sentence: Price control policy has existed since ancient times.

2276e776c7b7.title: Price controls
2276e776c7b7.sentence: The Code of Hammurabi Law 234 (c. 1755–1750 BC), for example, stipulated a 2-shekel wage for each 60-gur (300-bushel) vessel constructed in employment contracts with ship builders, among many other laws regulating commodity prices and wage labor rates.

5d567c4c5b94.title: Price controls
5d567c4c5b94.sentence: The Roman Emperor Diocletian tried to set maximum prices for all commodities in the late 3rd century AD but with little success.

d0a7cfc7c81b.title: Price controls
d0a7cfc7c81b.sentence: The primary criticism leveled against the price ceiling type of price controls is that by keeping prices artificially low, demand is increased to the point where supply cannot keep up, leading to shortages in the price-controlled product.

921da492bdc1.title: Price controls
921da492bdc1.sentence: As with Diocletian's Edict on Maximum Prices, shortages lead to black markets where prices for the same good exceed those of an uncontrolled market.

a4315d18ecb2.title: Price controls
a4315d18ecb2.sentence: A classic example of how price controls cause shortages was during the Arab oil embargo between October 19, 1973, and March 17, 1974.

797bfe0aaa12.title: Price controls
797bfe0aaa12.sentence: Long lines of cars and trucks quickly appeared at retail gas stations in the U.S. and some stations closed because of a shortage of fuel at the low price set by the U.S. Cost of Living Council.

d5ed67f58d5e.title: Price controls
d5ed67f58d5e.sentence: The fixed price was below what the market would otherwise bear and, as a result, the inventory disappeared.

3c2f9e3a53f0.title: Price controls
3c2f9e3a53f0.sentence: Although price controls are routinely used by governments, Western economists generally agree that consumer price controls do not accomplish what they intend to in market economies, and many economists instead recommend such controls should be avoided; however, since the credibility revolution started in the 1990s, minimum wages have found strong support among some economists.

a9f03b6ab799.title: Energy subsidy
a9f03b6ab799.sentence: Energy subsidies may be direct cash transfers to suppliers, customers, or related bodies, as well as indirect support mechanisms, such as tax exemptions and rebates, price controls, trade restrictions, and limits on market access.

cb4f9ebe1cc7.title: Price controls
cb4f9ebe1cc7.sentence: In 1971, President Richard Nixon issued Executive Order 11615 (pursuant to the Economic Stabilization Act of 1970), imposing a 90-day freeze on wages and prices.

124f486a036b.title: Supply and demand
124f486a036b.section: Microeconomics > Equilibrium > Changes in market equilibrium
124f486a036b.sentence: Practical uses of supply and demand analysis often center on the different variables that change equilibrium price and quantity, represented as shifts in the respective curves.

5e1a35fb71fc.title: Supply and demand
5e1a35fb71fc.sentence: (A movement along the curve is described as a "change in the quantity demanded" to distinguish it from a "change in demand", that is, a shift of the curve.) The increase in demand has caused an increase in (equilibrium) quantity.

1b1a816d518b.title: Supply and demand
1b1a816d518b.sentence: The increase in demand could come from changing tastes and fashions, incomes, price changes in complementary and substitute goods, market expectations, and number of buyers.

7f03547aeba1.title: Supply and demand
7f03547aeba1.sentence: In the diagram, this raises the equilibrium price from P1 to the higher P2.

1bd3c401373b.title: Supply and demand
1bd3c401373b.sentence: This raises the equilibrium quantity from Q1 to the higher Q2.

0f81f3162c99.title: Supply and demand
0f81f3162c99.sentence: For example, assume that someone invents a better way of growing wheat so that the cost of growing a given quantity of wheat decreases.

d3ba06bd370c.title: Supply and demand
d3ba06bd370c.sentence: Otherwise stated, producers will be willing to supply more wheat at every price and this shifts the supply curve S1 outward, to S2—an increase in supply.

9a83ca2953e8.title: Supply and demand
9a83ca2953e8.sentence: This increase in supply causes the equilibrium price to decrease from P1 to P2.

2a5099ef1102.title: Supply and demand
2a5099ef1102.sentence: The equilibrium quantity increases from Q1 to Q2 as consumers move along the demand curve to the new lower price.

96d501c09721.title: Supply and demand
96d501c09721.sentence: A rise in the cost of raw materials would decrease supply, shifting the supply curve to the left because at each possible price a smaller quantity would be supplied.

e61410a7edbe.title: Price mechanism
e61410a7edbe.sentence: In economics, a price mechanism refers to the way in which price determines the allocation of resources and influences the quantity supplied and the quantity demanded of goods and services.

ccff1553f117.title: Price mechanism
ccff1553f117.sentence: The price mechanism, part of a market system, functions in various ways to match up buyers and sellers: as an incentive, a signal, and a rationing system for resources.

292d8e5ee963.title: Price mechanism
292d8e5ee963.sentence: At competitive equilibrium, the value society places on a good is equivalent to the value of the resources given up to produce it (marginal benefit equals marginal cost).

25fee25c88d8.title: Price mechanism
25fee25c88d8.sentence: This ensures allocative efficiency: the additional value society places on another unit of the good is equal to what society must give up in resources to produce it.

c6f654b1c450.title: Price mechanism
c6f654b1c450.sentence: For example: the oil crisis of the 1970s drove oil prices dramatically upwards, which in turn caused several countries to begin producing oil domestically.

8fac419cc3be.title: Price mechanism
8fac419cc3be.sentence: If fuel becomes more expensive, then the demand for fuel would not decrease fast but eventually, companies will start to produce alternatives such as biodiesel fuel and electrical cars.

5d149adef783.title: Price mechanism
5d149adef783.sentence: An auction is a price mechanism where bidders can make competing offers for a good.

0546363989f6.title: Price mechanism
0546363989f6.sentence: The highest bidder would be awarded the transaction.

a7cacc189e02.title: Price mechanism
a7cacc189e02.sentence: In greenhouse gas emissions trading, companies doing the "bidding" argue that Earth's atmosphere can be seen as affected almost uniformly by emissions anywhere on Earth.

b35a7a93820d.title: Price mechanism
b35a7a93820d.sentence: They argue further that, as a result, there are almost no local effects, and only a measurable and widely agreed climate change effect, of a greenhouse gas emission, justifying a "cap and trade" approach.

7f766daa5429.title: Price mechanism
7f766daa5429.sentence: Somewhat more controversially, the approach was applied even earlier to sulfur dioxide emissions in the United States, and was quite successful in reducing overall smog output there.

ed7731ca48c8.title: History of economic thought
ed7731ca48c8.section: The World Wars, Russian and German Revolutions, and Great Depression (early to mid 20th century)
ed7731ca48c8.sentence: In this essay Mises critiques planned economies as a rejection of the price mechanism, and describes how rational and efficient allocation of resources is only possible through market forces reflecting the subjective values of resources in each given time and place.

1ad3a77558bb.title: Total cost
1ad3a77558bb.sentence: In economics, total cost (TC) is the minimum financial cost of producing some quantity of output.

0ceb1dc641e9.title: Total cost
0ceb1dc641e9.sentence: This is the total economic cost of production and is made up of variable cost, which varies according to the quantity of a good produced and includes inputs such as labor and raw materials, plus fixed cost, which is independent of the quantity of a good produced and includes inputs that cannot be varied in the short term such as buildings and machinery, including possibly sunk costs.

c9d9c0602f24.title: Total cost
c9d9c0602f24.sentence: Total cost in economics includes the total opportunity cost (benefits received from the next-best alternative) of each factor of production as part of its fixed or variable costs.

7cd0010730be.title: Total cost
7cd0010730be.sentence: The additional total cost of one additional unit of production is called marginal cost.

59818c9dfe4d.title: Total cost
59818c9dfe4d.sentence: The long run total cost for a given output will generally be lower than the short run total cost, because the amount of capital can be chosen to be optimal for the amount of output.

b96e998acc83.title: Marginal cost
b96e998acc83.sentence: In economics, marginal cost (MC) is the change in the total cost that arises when the quantity produced is increased, i.e. the cost of producing additional quantity.

11fff4b6d1d9.title: Marginal cost
11fff4b6d1d9.sentence: Marginal cost is different from average cost, which is the total cost divided by the number of units produced.

1257080f0c4e.title: Marginal cost
1257080f0c4e.sentence: At each level of production and time period being considered, marginal cost includes all costs that vary with the level of production, whereas costs that do not vary with production are fixed.

662416715e7a.title: Marginal cost
662416715e7a.sentence: For example, the marginal cost of producing an automobile will include the costs of labor and parts needed for the additional automobile but not the fixed cost of the factory building, which does not change with output.

83b7a01ca275.title: Marginal cost
83b7a01ca275.sentence: Marginal costs can be expressed as ∆C/∆Q. Since fixed costs do not vary with (depend on) changes in quantity, MC is ∆VC/∆Q. Thus if fixed cost were to double, the marginal cost MC would not be affected, and consequently, the profit-maximizing quantity and price would not change.

911a4245243f.title: Marginal cost
911a4245243f.sentence: At some point, the marginal cost rises as increases in the variable inputs such as labor put increasing pressure on the fixed assets such as the size of the building.

4332b9b40ea2.title: Marginal cost
4332b9b40ea2.section: Decisions taken based on marginal costs
4332b9b40ea2.sentence: If the sale price is higher than the marginal cost, then they produce the unit and supply it.

b298032f07b4.title: Marginal cost
b298032f07b4.section: Decisions taken based on marginal costs
b298032f07b4.sentence: So the production will be carried out until the marginal cost is equal to the sale price.

dd838e97e668.title: Marginal cost
dd838e97e668.section: Relationship between marginal cost and average total cost
dd838e97e668.sentence: The marginal cost intersects with the average total cost and the average variable cost at their lowest point.

91f693051b24.title: Marginal cost
91f693051b24.sentence: Where there are economies of scale, prices set at marginal cost will fail to cover total costs, thus requiring a subsidy.

58f2268a2328.title: Marginal cost
58f2268a2328.sentence: Most recently, former Federal Reserve Vice-Chair Alan Blinder and colleagues conducted a survey of 200 executives of corporations with sales exceeding $10 million, in which they were asked, among other questions, about the structure of their marginal cost curves.

0e09861ee60e.title: Marginal cost
0e09861ee60e.sentence: Strikingly, just 11% of respondents answered that their marginal costs increased as production increased, while 48% answered that they were constant, and 41% answered that they were decreasing.

41d60eb73896.title: Profit (economics)
41d60eb73896.sentence: In economics, profit is the difference between revenue that an economic entity has received from its outputs and total costs of its inputs, also known as "surplus value".

d90f74164b49.title: Profit (economics)
d90f74164b49.sentence: It is equal to total revenue minus total cost, including both explicit and implicit costs.

3934144e4b86.title: Profit (economics)
3934144e4b86.sentence: An accountant measures the firm's accounting profit as the firm's total revenue minus only the firm's explicit costs.

6b8df9dcdaa6.title: Profit (economics)
6b8df9dcdaa6.sentence: An economist includes all costs, both explicit and implicit costs, when analyzing a firm.

aaa098d567ce.title: Profit (economics)
aaa098d567ce.sentence: Therefore, economic profit is smaller than accounting profit.

29fb4058d799.title: Profit (economics)
29fb4058d799.sentence: Normal profits in business refer to a situation where a company generates revenue that is equal to the total costs incurred in its operation, thus allowing it to remain operational in a competitive industry.

3c483314f0b8.title: Profit (economics)
3c483314f0b8.sentence: It is the minimum profit level that a company can achieve to justify its continued operation in the market where there is competition.

44a359cec0d4.title: Profit (economics)
44a359cec0d4.sentence: If the company's total revenue is equal to its total costs, then its economic profit is equal to zero and the company is in a state of normal profit.

2a5c405260f3.title: Profit (economics)
2a5c405260f3.sentence: Companies do not make any economic profits in a perfectly competitive market once it has reached a long run equilibrium.

a2bd15f0a3ff.title: Profit (economics)
a2bd15f0a3ff.sentence: If an economic profit was available, there would be an incentive for new firms to enter the industry, aided by a lack of barriers to entry, until it no longer existed.

4fdf23e2199d.title: Profit (economics)
4fdf23e2199d.sentence: Once this has occurred a perfect competition exists and economic profit is no longer available.

9f2348280a88.title: Profit (economics)
9f2348280a88.sentence: Economic profits arise in markets which are non-competitive and have significant barriers to entry, i.e. monopolies and oligopolies.

d12664cfdd7d.title: Profit (economics)
d12664cfdd7d.sentence: The existence of economic profits depends on the prevalence of barriers to entry, which stop other firms from entering into the industry and sapping away profits like they would in a more competitive market.

c0424d8c736a.title: Profit (economics)
c0424d8c736a.sentence: Examples of barriers to entry include patents, land rights, and certain zoning laws.

b91156600153.title: Profit (economics)
b91156600153.sentence: It is a standard economic assumption (although not necessarily a perfect one in the real world) that, other things being equal, a firm will attempt to maximize its profits.

cd5ebf1054b0.title: Profit (economics)
cd5ebf1054b0.sentence: In markets which do not show interdependence, this point can either be found by looking at these two curves directly, or by finding and selecting the best of the points where the gradients of the two curves (marginal revenue and marginal cost respectively) are equal.

a1705f672133.title: Profit (economics)
a1705f672133.sentence: The social profit from a firm's activities is the accounting profit plus or minus any externalities or consumer surpluses that occur in its activity.

b710a6f4803d.title: Profit (economics)
b710a6f4803d.sentence: Pollution is an example for negative externality.

14a578527df8.title: Profit (economics)
14a578527df8.sentence: Competition laws were created to prevent powerful firms from using their economic power to artificially create barriers to entry in an attempt to protect their economic profits.

0c7c8930371a.title: Monopoly
0c7c8930371a.sentence: A monopoly (from Greek μόνος, mónos, 'single, alone' and πωλεῖν, pōleîn, 'to sell') is a market in which one person or company is the only supplier of a particular good or service.

48289308303d.title: Monopoly
48289308303d.sentence: A monopoly is characterized by a lack of economic competition to produce a particular thing, a lack of viable substitute goods, and the possibility of a high monopoly price well above the seller's marginal cost that leads to a high monopoly profit.

0cb914e56d1a.title: Monopoly
0cb914e56d1a.sentence: Although monopolies may be big businesses, size is not a characteristic of a monopoly.

bec91ac76aed.title: Monopoly
bec91ac76aed.sentence: A small business may still have the power to raise prices in a small industry (or market).

2698db4358e9.title: Monopoly
2698db4358e9.sentence: Monopolies derive their market power from barriers to entry – circumstances that prevent or greatly impede a potential competitor's ability to compete in a market.

7599f3ac95c3.title: Monopoly
7599f3ac95c3.sentence: There are three major types of barriers to entry: economic, legal, and deliberate.

b4783440616c.title: Monopoly
b4783440616c.sentence: - Profit maximizer: monopolists will choose the price or output to maximise profits at where MC=MR.

a0fe60ebf8e1.title: Monopoly
a0fe60ebf8e1.sentence: Contrary to common misconception, monopolists do not try to sell items for the highest possible price, nor do they try to maximize profit per unit, but rather they try to maximize total profit.

9dd5f4bb8047.title: Monopoly
9dd5f4bb8047.sentence: According to the standard model, in which a monopolist sets a single price for all consumers, the monopolist will sell a lesser quantity of goods at a higher price than would companies by perfect competition.

b680892d4012.title: Monopoly
b680892d4012.sentence: Because the monopolist ultimately forgoes transactions with consumers who value the product or service less than its price, monopoly pricing creates a deadweight loss referring to potential gains that went neither to the monopolist nor to consumers.

5f23543c2c3c.title: Monopoly
5f23543c2c3c.sentence: The theory of contestable markets argues that in some circumstances (private) monopolies are forced to behave as if there were competition because of the risk of losing their monopoly to new entrants.

bb10ba37914c.title: Monopoly
bb10ba37914c.sentence: This is likely to happen when a market's barriers to entry are low.

bcc2e3f33a78.title: Monopoly
bcc2e3f33a78.sentence: When a company is determined to be monopolistic, steps to mitigate the monopolistic behavior include governments extracting monopoly profits, forcibly fragmenting the monopoly and changing regulations to hinder anti-competitive practices.

cad9b5e58481.title: Monopoly
cad9b5e58481.sentence: The term "monopoly" first appears in Aristotle's Politics.

4a6126b221d1.title: Monopoly
4a6126b221d1.sentence: Aristotle describes Thales of Miletus's cornering of the market in olive presses as a monopoly (μονοπώλιον).

a3dd61bc6f7a.title: Perfect competition
a3dd61bc6f7a.sentence: In economics, specifically general equilibrium theory, a perfect market, also known as an atomistic market, is defined by several idealizing conditions, collectively called perfect competition, or atomistic competition.

0c76edcf2167.title: Perfect competition
0c76edcf2167.sentence: - A large number of sellers and buyers, or low barriers to entry and exit – A large number of consumers with the willingness and ability to buy the product at a certain price, and a large number of producers with the willingness and ability to supply the product at a certain price.

3a868b111fe6.title: Perfect competition
3a868b111fe6.sentence: As a result, individuals are unable to significantly influence prices.

62bdd17615a4.title: Perfect competition
62bdd17615a4.sentence: - Homogeneous products: The products are perfect substitutes for each other (i.e., the qualities and characteristics of a market good or service do not vary between different suppliers).

2158de6d137f.title: Perfect competition
2158de6d137f.sentence: - Perfect information: All consumers and producers know all prices of products and utilities they would get from owning each product.

0d3fc10a5318.title: Perfect competition
0d3fc10a5318.sentence: In theoretical models where conditions of perfect competition hold, it has been demonstrated that a market will reach an equilibrium in which the quantity supplied for every product or service, including labor, equals the quantity demanded at the current price.

154fede40979.title: Perfect competition
154fede40979.sentence: This equilibrium would be a Pareto optimum.

689756c610c8.title: Perfect competition
689756c610c8.sentence: - Such markets are allocatively efficient, as output will always occur where marginal cost is equal to average revenue i.e. price (MC = AR).

b21e69112e7a.title: Perfect competition
b21e69112e7a.sentence: In perfect competition, any profit-maximizing producer faces a market price equal to its marginal cost (P = MC).

e5770cab448a.title: Perfect competition
e5770cab448a.sentence: In the absence of externalities and public goods, perfectly competitive equilibria are Pareto-efficient, i.e. no improvement in the utility of a consumer is possible without a worsening of the utility of some other consumer.

59176f774c99.title: Perfect competition
59176f774c99.sentence: This is called the First Theorem of Welfare Economics.

9c54aa0c9290.title: Perfect competition
9c54aa0c9290.sentence: In a perfectly competitive market, the demand curve facing a firm is perfectly elastic.

530e342926b0.title: Perfect competition
530e342926b0.section: Normal profit > In competitive and contestable markets
530e342926b0.sentence: Economic profit does not occur in perfect competition in long run equilibrium; if it did, there would be an incentive for new firms to enter the industry, aided by a lack of barriers to entry until there was no longer any economic profit.

bbc9562a4487.title: Perfect competition
bbc9562a4487.section: Normal profit > In competitive and contestable markets
bbc9562a4487.sentence: New firms will continue to enter the industry until the price of the product is lowered to the point that it is the same as the average cost of producing the product, and all of the economic profit disappears.

6a86675126fb.title: Perfect competition
6a86675126fb.sentence: As mentioned above, the perfect competition model, if interpreted as applying also to short-period or very-short-period behaviour, is approximated only by markets of homogeneous products produced and purchased by very many sellers and buyers, usually organized markets for agricultural products or raw materials.

fd2232b8a920.title: Agricultural economics
fd2232b8a920.sentence: The farm sector is frequently cited as a prime example of the perfect competition economic paradigm.

9d40c116f60c.title: Perfect competition
9d40c116f60c.sentence: The use of the assumption of perfect competition as the foundation of price theory for product markets is often criticized as representing all agents as passive, thus removing the active attempts to increase one's welfare or profits by price undercutting, product design, advertising, innovation, activities that – the critics argue – characterize most industries and markets.

62ac47d623fd.title: Perfect competition
62ac47d623fd.sentence: They are not criticizing the price taker assumption because it makes economic agents too "passive", but because it then raises the question of who sets the prices.

8642dc93c416.title: Market power
8642dc93c416.sentence: In economics, market power refers to the ability of a firm to influence the price at which it sells a product or service by manipulating either the supply or demand of the product or service to increase economic profit.

778b0b9f944d.title: Market power
778b0b9f944d.sentence: In other words, market power occurs if a firm does not face a perfectly elastic demand curve and can set its price (P) above marginal cost (MC) without losing revenue.

e6063528b946.title: Market power
e6063528b946.sentence: Market participants in perfectly competitive markets are consequently referred to as 'price takers', whereas market participants that exhibit market power are referred to as 'price makers' or 'price setters'.

ae493e786acb.title: Market power
ae493e786acb.sentence: The degree of market power firms assert in different markets depend on the market structure that the firms operate in.

eadb36c73dcc.title: Market power
eadb36c73dcc.sentence: There are four main forms of market structures that are observed: perfect competition, monopolistic competition, oligopoly, and monopoly.

f4b1adbe3665.title: Market power
f4b1adbe3665.sentence: Perfect competition and monopoly represent the two extremes of market structure, respectively.

fc6117019c7b.title: Market power
fc6117019c7b.sentence: Monopolistic competition and oligopoly exist in between these two extremes.

3de51c06ebc1.title: Market power
3de51c06ebc1.sentence: Without barriers to entries, above normal profits experienced by monopolists would not persist as other sellers of homogenous or similar goods would continue to enter the industry until above normal profits are diminished until the industry experiences perfect competition

dd55fbc13992.title: Market power
dd55fbc13992.sentence: These barriers include the control of scarce resources, increasing returns to scale, technological superiority and government created barriers to entry.

6dbd871c7ae6.title: Market power
6dbd871c7ae6.sentence: OPEC is an example of an organization that has market power due to control over scarce resources – oil.

805a2a14a33f.title: Market power
805a2a14a33f.sentence: The higher a firm's markup, the larger the magnitude of power.

5d293d87cf59.title: Market power
5d293d87cf59.sentence: This said, markups are complicated to measure as they are reliant on a firm's marginal costs and as a result, concentration ratios are the more common measures as they require only publicly accessible revenue data.

33725fb2dfba.title: Market power
33725fb2dfba.section: Measurement of market power > Concentration ratios > Herfindahl-Hirschman index
33725fb2dfba.sentence: The HHI is a more widely used indicator in economics and government regulation.

9c87e2cf93ef.title: Market power
9c87e2cf93ef.sentence: The degree to which a firm can raise its price above marginal cost depends on the shape of the demand curve at a firm's profit maximising level of output.

3341d56ad91c.title: Market power
3341d56ad91c.sentence: As PED increases in magnitude, the P/MC ratio approaches 1 and market power approaches zero.

f3ab05a3395f.title: Market power
f3ab05a3395f.sentence: Market power within competition law can be used to determine whether or not a firm has unfairly manipulated the market in their favour, or to the detriment of entrants.

55bda01c4416.title: Market power
55bda01c4416.sentence: The Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890 under section 2 restricts firms from engaging in anticompetitive conduct by utilising an individual firm's power to manipulate the market or partake in anticompetitive acts.

dbb8de191fff.title: Market power
dbb8de191fff.sentence: Jean Tirole was awarded the 2014 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for his analysis of market power and economic regulation.

3e55e1556b29.title: Oligopoly
3e55e1556b29.sentence: An oligopoly (from Ancient Greek ὀλίγος (olígos) 'few' and πωλέω (pōléō) 'to sell') is a market in which pricing control lies in the hands of a few sellers.

619bbba2c937.title: Oligopoly
619bbba2c937.sentence: Firms in an oligopoly are mutually interdependent, as any action by one firm is expected to affect other firms in the market and evoke a reaction or consequential action.

f13b5560e2dc.title: Oligopoly
f13b5560e2dc.sentence: As a result, firms in oligopolistic markets often resort to collusion as means of maximising profits.

89573337b0f9.title: Competition (economics)
89573337b0f9.sentence: Companies in an oligopoly benefit from price-fixing, setting prices collectively, or under the direction of one firm in the bunch, rather than relying on free-market forces to do so.

4e5e0f252322.title: Competition (economics)
4e5e0f252322.sentence: Oligopolies can form cartels in order to restrict entry of new firms into the market and ensure they hold market share.

f83f3e98d591.title: Oligopoly
f83f3e98d591.sentence: Although aggressive, these laws typically only apply when firms engage in formal collusion, such as cartels.

7f1f74075226.title: Oligopoly
7f1f74075226.sentence: Corporations may often thus evade legal consequences through tacit collusion, as collusion can only be proven through direct communication between companies.

bf3c3f00af4a.title: Competition (economics)
bf3c3f00af4a.sentence: A duopoly is a special form of oligopoly where the market is made up of only two firms.

51e6e2c354bf.title: Oligopoly
51e6e2c354bf.sentence: Many industries have been cited as oligopolistic, including civil aviation, electricity providers, the telecommunications sector, rail freight markets, food processing, funeral services, sugar refining, beer making, pulp and paper making, and automobile manufacturing.

bf94cb46bd3c.title: Competitive equilibrium
bf94cb46bd3c.sentence: Competitive equilibrium (also called: Walrasian equilibrium) is a concept of economic equilibrium, introduced by Kenneth Arrow and Gérard Debreu in 1951, appropriate for the analysis of commodity markets with flexible prices and many traders, and serving as the benchmark of efficiency in economic analysis.

e6d2827acd82.title: Competitive equilibrium
e6d2827acd82.sentence: It relies crucially on the assumption of a competitive environment where each trader decides upon a quantity that is so small compared to the total quantity traded in the market that their individual transactions have no influence on the prices.

77b9248a12a8.title: Competitive equilibrium
77b9248a12a8.sentence: - Satisfaction (market-envy-freeness): Every agent weakly prefers his bundle to any other affordable bundle:

1b9f939f2cc7.title: Competitive equilibrium
1b9f939f2cc7.sentence: - Market Clearance: the demand equals the supply, no items are created or destroyed:

20117e2c0be4.title: Competitive equilibrium
20117e2c0be4.sentence: A. Single item: Alice has a car which she values as 10.

91f432d3738f.title: Competitive equilibrium
91f432d3738f.sentence: Bob has no car, and he values Alice's car as 20.

84aff49f642c.title: Competitive equilibrium
84aff49f642c.sentence: In fact, every price between 10 and 20 will be a CE price, with the same allocation.

2f1d4389999a.title: Competitive equilibrium
2f1d4389999a.section: Existence of a competitive equilibrium > Divisible resources
2f1d4389999a.sentence: The Arrow–Debreu model shows that a CE exists in every exchange economy with divisible goods satisfying the following conditions:

f4f248a4407e.title: Competitive equilibrium
f4f248a4407e.section: Existence of a competitive equilibrium > Divisible resources
f4f248a4407e.sentence: - All agents have strictly convex preferences;

1fdc47abc591.title: Competitive equilibrium
1fdc47abc591.section: Existence of a competitive equilibrium > The competitive equilibrium and allocative efficiency
1fdc47abc591.sentence: By the fundamental theorems of welfare economics, any CE allocation is Pareto efficient, and any efficient allocation can be sustainable by a competitive equilibrium.

306d0459c227.title: Competitive equilibrium
306d0459c227.section: Existence of a competitive equilibrium > The competitive equilibrium and allocative efficiency
306d0459c227.sentence: At the competitive equilibrium, the value society places on a good is equivalent to the value of the resources given up to produce it (marginal benefit equals marginal cost).

6db599cf39ff.title: Competitive equilibrium
6db599cf39ff.section: Existence of a competitive equilibrium > The competitive equilibrium and allocative efficiency
6db599cf39ff.sentence: It does not in any way opine on the fairness of the allocation (in the sense of distributive justice or equity).

990c29be4be4.title: Competitive equilibrium
990c29be4be4.section: Existence of a competitive equilibrium > The competitive equilibrium and allocative efficiency
990c29be4be4.sentence: An efficient equilibrium could be one where one player has all the goods and other players have none (in an extreme example), which is efficient in the sense that one may not be able to find a Pareto improvement - which makes all players (including the one with everything in this case) better off (for a strict Pareto improvement), or not worse off.

7aa16c4d3434.title: Imperfect competition
7aa16c4d3434.sentence: In economics, imperfect competition refers to a situation where the characteristics of an economic market do not fulfill all the necessary conditions of a perfectly competitive market.

70ce67974398.title: Imperfect competition
70ce67974398.sentence: If ANY of the above conditions of perfect competition are dissatisfied, the market is imperfectly competitive.

46972abb6fa5.title: Imperfect competition
46972abb6fa5.sentence: Imperfect competition causes market inefficiencies, resulting in market failure.

633c15a43066.title: Imperfect competition
633c15a43066.sentence: - Market firms are NOT price takers and hence have control over the pricing of their goods and services;

c26b7a8f6abd.title: Imperfect competition
c26b7a8f6abd.sentence: - The market contains ONE seller or none;

5916334aa0d7.title: Imperfect competition
5916334aa0d7.sentence: - There are barriers to market entry and exit;

411972b9f940.title: Imperfect competition
411972b9f940.sentence: - There is information asymmetry between buyers and sellers;

aa8a5e27384a.title: Imperfect competition
aa8a5e27384a.sentence: - The market's goods and services are heterogeneous or differentiated.

299ba83ca7f7.title: Imperfect competition
299ba83ca7f7.sentence: The degree of market power refers to firms' ability to affect the price of a good and thus, raise the market price of the good or service above marginal cost (MC).

8c757bd84dd8.title: Imperfect competition
8c757bd84dd8.sentence: The greater extent to which price is raised above marginal cost, the greater the market inefficiency.

a4a0ccd97499.title: Imperfect competition
a4a0ccd97499.sentence: In the most extreme case of a monopoly, producers overcharge for their good or service, and underproduce.

9e8c78a7d1ac.title: Imperfect competition
9e8c78a7d1ac.section: Range of imperfectly competitive market structures
9e8c78a7d1ac.sentence: There are four broad market structures that result in imperfect competition.

090a4ae24ee8.title: Imperfect competition
090a4ae24ee8.section: Range of imperfectly competitive market structures > Monopolistic competition
090a4ae24ee8.sentence: A situation in which many firms with slightly different products compete.

8fd61c50f353.title: Imperfect competition
8fd61c50f353.section: Range of imperfectly competitive market structures > Oligopoly
8fd61c50f353.sentence: In an oligopoly market structure, the market is supplied by a small number of firms (more than 2).

fe8ce9ea473a.title: Imperfect competition
fe8ce9ea473a.section: Range of imperfectly competitive market structures > Oligopoly
fe8ce9ea473a.sentence: Moreover, there are so few firms that the actions of one firm can influence the actions of the other firms.

ba4153b41a5b.title: Imperfect competition
ba4153b41a5b.sentence: The imperfect market faces a down-ward sloping demand curve in contrast to a perfectly elastic demand curve in the perfectly competitive market.

235935515a93.title: Imperfect competition
235935515a93.sentence: Imperfect conditions theorists believe that in the aggregate economy no market has ever, or will ever, exhibit the conditions of perfect competition.

49aa15781c03.title: Marginal revenue
49aa15781c03.sentence: Marginal revenue (or marginal benefit) is a central concept in microeconomics that describes the additional total revenue generated by increasing product sales by 1 unit.

c0a61e7934cd.title: Marginal revenue
c0a61e7934cd.sentence: Marginal revenue is the increase in revenue from the sale of one additional unit of product, i.e., the revenue from the sale of the last unit of product.

d941dae38c3a.title: Marginal revenue
d941dae38c3a.sentence: In a perfectly competitive market, the incremental revenue generated by selling an additional unit of a good is equal to the price the firm is able to charge the buyer of the good.

a8ef1b0c7e49.title: Marginal revenue
a8ef1b0c7e49.sentence: This is because a firm in a competitive market will always get the same price for every unit it sells regardless of the number of units the firm sells since the firm's sales can never impact the industry's price.

0e545f4cb4d9.title: Marginal revenue
0e545f4cb4d9.sentence: Therefore, in a perfectly competitive market, firms set the price level equal to their marginal revenue (MR=P).

1d7841d72167.title: Marginal revenue
1d7841d72167.sentence: Therefore, a monopoly firm lowers its price on all units sold in order to increase output (quantity) by 1 unit.

9ad6e5661172.title: Marginal revenue
9ad6e5661172.sentence: Since a reduction in price leads to a decline in revenue on each good sold by the firm, the marginal revenue generated is always lower than the price level charged (MR<P).

9290a9b732cc.title: Marginal revenue
9290a9b732cc.sentence: Example 1: If a firm sells 20 units of books (quantity) for $50 each (price), this earns total revenue: P*Q = $50*20 = $1000

cb3d9472a2d8.title: Marginal revenue
cb3d9472a2d8.sentence: Then if the firm increases quantity sold to 21 units of books at $49 each, this earns total revenue: P*Q = $49*21 = $1029

b3a1756ec265.title: Marginal revenue
b3a1756ec265.sentence: Therefore, using the marginal revenue formula (MR) = ΔTRΔQ=($1029−$100021−20)=$29

52da6958ce31.title: Marginal revenue
52da6958ce31.sentence: Profit maximization occurs at the point where marginal revenue (MR) equals marginal cost (MC).

d3fa68597b2b.title: Marginal revenue
d3fa68597b2b.section: Marginal revenue curve and marginal cost curve
d3fa68597b2b.sentence: Therefore, a company is making money when MR is greater than marginal cost (MC).

87f304237dd1.title: Marginal revenue
87f304237dd1.section: Marginal revenue curve and marginal cost curve
87f304237dd1.sentence: And when MC = MR, it is called profit maximization.

140695059001.title: Marginal revenue
140695059001.section: Relationship between marginal revenue and elasticity
140695059001.sentence: When a monopolist firm is facing an Inelastic demand curve (e<1), it implies that a percentage change in quantity is less than the percentage change in price.

d91232045ff2.title: Marginal revenue
d91232045ff2.section: Relationship between marginal revenue and elasticity
d91232045ff2.sentence: By increasing quantity sold, the firm is forced to accept a reduction of price for all the current and previous production units, resulting in a negative marginal revenue (MR).

9e5fdfcb774a.title: Marginal revenue
9e5fdfcb774a.sentence: The marginal revenue curve is a horizontal line at the market price, implying perfectly elastic demand and is equal to the demand curve.

81eab9882620.title: Marginal revenue
81eab9882620.sentence: The marginal revenue curve is downward sloping and below the demand curve and the additional gain from increasing the quantity sold is lower than the chosen market price.

7693afdab43a.title: Cost curve
7693afdab43a.sentence: In economics, a cost curve is a graph of the costs of production as a function of total quantity produced.

8ec35fbadc91.title: Cost curve
8ec35fbadc91.sentence: Profit-maximizing firms use cost curves to decide output quantities.

6f24858f5185.title: Cost curve
6f24858f5185.sentence: There are various types of cost curves, all related to each other, including total and average cost curves; marginal ("for each additional unit") cost curves, which are equal to the differential of the total cost curves; and variable cost curves.

73da58c402bd.title: Cost curve
73da58c402bd.sentence: Some are applicable to the short run, others to the long run.

e134f3263180.title: Cost curve
e134f3263180.section: Short-run variable and fixed cost curves (SRVC and SRFC or VC and FC)
e134f3263180.sentence: Since short-run fixed cost (FC/SRFC) does not vary with the level of output, its curve is horizontal as shown here.

c6b96766d162.title: Cost curve
c6b96766d162.sentence: Since fixed cost by definition does not vary with output, short-run average fixed cost (SRAFC) (that is, short-run fixed cost per unit of output) is lower when output is higher, giving rise to the downward-sloped curve shown.

b6d7cda5c544.title: Cost curve
b6d7cda5c544.sentence: Marginal cost is relatively high at small quantities of output; then as production increases, marginal cost declines, reaches a minimum value, then rises.

0eb4de163e38.title: Cost curve
0eb4de163e38.sentence: This shape of the marginal cost curve is directly attributable to increasing, then decreasing marginal returns (and the law of diminishing marginal returns).

62a367172bbf.title: Cost curve
62a367172bbf.sentence: The long-run marginal cost curve is shaped by returns to scale, a long-run concept, rather than the law of diminishing marginal returns, which is a short-run concept.

4c8401345614.title: Cost curve
4c8401345614.sentence: - At a level of Q at which the MC curve is above the average total cost or average variable cost curve, the latter curve is rising.

c8034f12a767.title: Cost curve
c8034f12a767.sentence: - If MC is below average total cost or average variable cost, then the latter curve is falling.

1c6327836b8c.title: Cost curve
1c6327836b8c.sentence: - If MC equals average total cost, then average total cost is at its minimum value.

a3127867b326.title: Cost curve
a3127867b326.section: Empirical shape of average cost curves
a3127867b326.sentence: In a survey by Wilford J. Eiteman and Glenn E. Guthrie in 1952 managers of 334 companies were shown a number of different cost curves, and asked to specify which one best represented the company’s cost curve.

e262a560635b.title: Cost curve
e262a560635b.section: Empirical shape of average cost curves
e262a560635b.sentence: 95% of managers responding to the survey reported cost curves with constant or falling costs.

224096c37be7.title: Monopoly
224096c37be7.sentence: A natural monopoly is an organization that experiences increasing returns to scale over the relevant range of output and relatively high fixed costs.

87d581131657.title: Monopoly
87d581131657.sentence: A natural monopoly occurs where the average cost of production "declines throughout the relevant range of product demand".

b162ab4e12d9.title: Monopoly
b162ab4e12d9.sentence: When this situation occurs, it is always more efficient for one large company to supply the market than multiple smaller companies; in fact, absent government intervention in such markets, will naturally evolve into a monopoly.

43ad68115f88.title: Monopoly
43ad68115f88.sentence: An early market entrant that takes advantage of the cost structure and can expand rapidly can exclude smaller companies from entering and can drive or buy out other companies.

c88ce3d48fef.title: Monopoly
c88ce3d48fef.sentence: In 1848, J.S. Mill was the first individual to describe monopolies with the adjective "natural".

97bc4dd3286c.title: Monopoly
97bc4dd3286c.sentence: At the time, Mill gave the following examples of natural or practical monopolies: gas supply, water supply, roads, canals, and railways.

f17ddb736fa9.title: Monopoly
f17ddb736fa9.sentence: Fragmenting such monopolies is by definition inefficient.

14961434a7f3.title: Monopoly
14961434a7f3.sentence: The most frequently used methods dealing with natural monopolies are government regulations and public ownership.

9a3e854bb247.title: Monopoly
9a3e854bb247.sentence: To reduce prices and increase output, regulators often use average cost pricing.

8e2912652423.title: Monopoly
8e2912652423.sentence: This pricing scheme eliminates any positive economic profits since price equals average cost.

fc263dcec6cb.title: Monopoly
fc263dcec6cb.sentence: Companies have a reduced incentive to lower costs.

9aecc0aa5dda.title: Law of supply
9aecc0aa5dda.sentence: The law of supply is a fundamental principle of economic theory which states that, keeping other factors constant, an increase in price results in an increase in quantity supplied.

d038e94b87fb.title: Law of supply
d038e94b87fb.sentence: This means that producers and manufacturers are willing to offer more of a product for sale on the market at higher prices, as increasing production is a way of increasing profits.

6b43342ce59f.title: Law of supply
6b43342ce59f.sentence: In short, the law of supply is a positive relationship between quantity supplied and price, and is the reason for the upward slope of the supply curve.

23da444009d0.title: Law of supply
23da444009d0.sentence: For example, a job paying £20/hr attracts more interest than a job paying £15/hr, and a high interest rate attracts lenders and deters borrowers.

775abb846ee6.title: Law of supply
775abb846ee6.sentence: For example, if the costs of production, such as wages, decrease, then the manufacturers can produce more goods for the same price, so the quantity supplied will increase.

0e16e3ceb6cb.title: Law of supply
0e16e3ceb6cb.sentence: If the number of suppliers increases, or if the capacity of a factory producing the goods increases, the quantity supplied will increase.

5643a527ccea.title: Law of supply
5643a527ccea.sentence: Other factors can include government policy—government subsidies to encourage certain products decreases the overall cost of production.

23b8822b52a5.title: Law of supply
23b8822b52a5.sentence: However, government taxation can cause the cost of production to rise.

1a477be48e81.title: Law of supply
1a477be48e81.sentence: For some products, such as in agriculture, the quantity supplied is dependent on the weather.

18ef7848bedc.title: Law of supply
18ef7848bedc.sentence: The law of supply and demand states that, for a given product, if the quantity demanded exceeds the quantity supplied, then the price increases, which decreases the demand (law of demand) and increases the supply (law of supply)—and vice versa—until the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded.

dd0d2d2ec548.title: Law of supply
dd0d2d2ec548.sentence: Some heterodox economists, such as Steve Keen and Dirk Ehnts, dispute the law of supply, arguing that the supply curve for mass-produced goods is often downward-sloping: as production increases, unit prices go down, and conversely, if demand is very low, unit prices go up.

935dd50a1dc0.title: Price elasticity of supply
935dd50a1dc0.sentence: The price elasticity of supply (PES or Es) is commonly known as “a measure used in economics to show the responsiveness, or elasticity, of the quantity supplied of a good or service to a change in its price.” Price elasticity of supply, in application, is the percentage change of the quantity supplied resulting from a 1% change in price.

592346f4d828.title: Price elasticity of supply
592346f4d828.sentence: When PES is less than one, the supply of the good can be described as inelastic.

468ac1d0b0d3.title: Price elasticity of supply
468ac1d0b0d3.sentence: When price elasticity of supply is greater than one, the supply can be described as elastic.

6bd358716541.title: Price elasticity of supply
6bd358716541.sentence: An elasticity of zero indicates that quantity supplied does not respond to a price change: the good is "fixed" in supply.

4931a6b3325a.title: Price elasticity of supply
4931a6b3325a.sentence: If the elasticity is exactly one, the good is said to be unit-elastic.

c05471a874e7.title: Price elasticity of supply
c05471a874e7.sentence: Differing from price elasticity of demand, price elasticities of supply are generally positive numbers because an increase in the price of a good motivates producers to produce more, as relative marginal revenue increases.

b5930e157e4d.title: Price elasticity of supply
b5930e157e4d.sentence: For example, availability may cap the amount of gold that can be produced in a country regardless of price.

e0d6ff29f7d9.title: Price elasticity of supply
e0d6ff29f7d9.sentence: Likewise, the price of Van Gogh paintings is unlikely to affect their supply.

6f2d6c38b4f3.title: Price elasticity of supply
6f2d6c38b4f3.sentence: The more time a producer has to respond to price changes the more elastic the supply.

c50e7a20527f.title: Price elasticity of supply
c50e7a20527f.sentence: Supply is normally more elastic in the long run than in the short run for produced goods, since it is generally assumed that in the long run all factors of production can be utilised to increase supply, whereas in the short run only labor can be increased, and even then, changes may be prohibitively costly.

6db68ae8ecb9.title: Price elasticity of supply
6db68ae8ecb9.sentence: The greater the extent of spare production capacity, the quicker suppliers can respond to price changes and hence the more price elastic the good/service would be.

3e9b1570c9fd.title: Price elasticity of supply
3e9b1570c9fd.sentence: However, as capacity becomes fully utilised, increasing production requires additional investment in capital (for example, plant and equipment).

65dcf0b07a82.title: Price elasticity of supply
65dcf0b07a82.sentence: Since the price must rise substantially to cover this additional expense, supply becomes less elastic at high levels of output.

d73cc213d187.title: Price elasticity of supply
d73cc213d187.sentence: Suppose that there is an increase in demand for apartments.

67b715f17bce.title: Price elasticity of supply
67b715f17bce.sentence: Ceteris paribus, the more responsive (elastic) the quantity of apartments supplied is to changes in monthly rents, the lower the increase in rent required to eliminate the shortage and to bring the market back to equilibrium.

6e8dd0df63e8.title: Economic rent
6e8dd0df63e8.sentence: In political economy, including physiocracy, classical economics, Georgism, and other schools of economic thought, land is recognized as an inelastic factor of production.

6280e2827344.title: Cross elasticity of demand
6280e2827344.sentence: In economics, the cross (or cross-price) elasticity of demand (XED) measures the effect of changes in the price of one good on the quantity demanded of another good.

822d2cb17a10.title: Cross elasticity of demand
822d2cb17a10.sentence: ηBA=0 implies two goods are independent (a price change of good A is unrelated to demand change of good B), so changes in the price of product A have no effect on the demand for Product B. Example: bread and cloths.

1defa2f073ee.title: Cross elasticity of demand
1defa2f073ee.sentence: Example: the cross elasticity of demand of butter with respect to margarine is 0.81, so 1% increase in the price of margarine will increase the demand for butter by 0.81%.

51693055fdf3.title: Cross elasticity of demand
51693055fdf3.section: Results for main types of goods

510da2fd464c.title: Factor market
510da2fd464c.sentence: In economics, a factor market is a market where factors of production are bought and sold.

aa6abd29a996.title: Factor market
aa6abd29a996.sentence: Factor markets allocate factors of production, including land, labour and capital, and distribute income to the owners of productive resources, such as wages, rents, etc.

76308d76d2e8.title: Factor market
76308d76d2e8.sentence: Firms obtain the inputs (factors of production) in the factor markets.

12433086b481.title: Factor market

450a84a9b1fa.title: Factor market
450a84a9b1fa.sentence: In most respects these markets work in the same manner as each other.

7bcd1e2db61d.title: Factor market

56db0476b166.title: Factor market

a953e68c9ddb.title: Factor market
a953e68c9ddb.sentence: Due to diminishing marginal production, the marginal production of a factor that is in abundant supply is low, and hence the price is low, while the marginal production of a factor that is in scarce supply is high, and hence the price is high.

3ed45886ab1f.title: Factor market
3ed45886ab1f.sentence: Thus, when the supply of a factor decreases, its equilibrium price rises.

f9beb818253e.title: Factor market
f9beb818253e.sentence: The definition of a monopsony is an economic market structure that comprises a sole purchaser of a particular good or service in the factor market.

e91da5ebae31.title: Factor market
e91da5ebae31.sentence: A monopsony is a situation in which a single buyer dominates the market.

292a7dba21bc.title: Factor market
292a7dba21bc.sentence: An oligopsony is an economic market state in which there is a small pool of dominant buyers.

4ad61558439d.title: Factor market
4ad61558439d.sentence: In this situation, a firm sets the market price it will pay for the factor rather than taking it as market-determined, and the amount of the factor to purchase is chosen at the same time subject to the constraint that the price-and-quantity combination is a point on the market's factor supply curve.

abfb181aa326.title: Factor market

70d33b970571.sentence: There are growing concerns with monopsonists and oligopsonist in areas with specific types of labor.

afa610a5648b.sentence: The cooperation of several inputs in many circumstances yields a final good and thus the demand for these goods is derived from the demand of the final product; this concept is known as derived demand.

737f79b826b1.title: Demand curve
737f79b826b1.sentence: An intermediate good is a good utilized in the process of creating another good, effectively named the final good.

7ac03c8eb965.title: Demand curve
7ac03c8eb965.sentence: The relationship between the intermediate goods and the final good is direct and positive as demand for a final product increases demand for the intermediate goods used to make it.

f381f3fd680f.title: Factor market

0de1de21bc7d.sentence: The price of labor and the quantity of labor demanded are inversely related.

2481dc4697a0.sentence: Veblen goods appear to go against the law of demand because of their exclusivity appeal, in the sense that if a price of a luxurious and expensive product is increased, it may attract the status-conscious group more, since it will be further out of reach for an average consumer.

6c5be243d212.title: Law of demand
6c5be243d212.section: Exceptions to the law of demand > Veblen goods
6c5be243d212.sentence: Examples of Veblen goods are mostly luxurious items such as diamond, gold, precious stones, world-famous paintings, antiques etc.

b00dfaa2a8e6.title: Law of demand
b00dfaa2a8e6.section: Exceptions to the law of demand > Veblen goods
b00dfaa2a8e6.sentence: Thorstein Veblen referred to this sort of consumption as the purchase of goods that do not exhibit additional utility or functionality but offer status and reveal socioeconomic position.

e43fda13381f.title: Price floor

e43fda13381f.sentence: An example of a price floor is minimum wage laws, where the government sets out the minimum hourly rate that can be paid for labour.

c2a488472f20.title: Price floor
c2a488472f20.section: Effect on the market > Minimum wage
c2a488472f20.sentence: In this case, the wage is the price of labour, and employees are the suppliers of labor and the company is the consumer of employees' labour.

b2dffaffe0a5.title: Price floor
b2dffaffe0a5.section: Effect on the market > Minimum wage
b2dffaffe0a5.sentence: When the minimum wage is set above the equilibrium market price for unskilled or low-skilled labour, employers hire fewer workers.

eb8d690f4644.title: Price floor
eb8d690f4644.section: Effect on the market > Minimum wage
eb8d690f4644.sentence: Employers may cut their use of labour by switching to a "self-serve" model in which customers do an action previously done by staff (e.g., self-serve gas stations); or buying machines, computers or robots to do part or all of employees' jobs (e.g., automated teller machines in banks, automated ticket kiosks in parking garages).

ad1756d9bc22.title: Price floor
ad1756d9bc22.section: Effect on the market > Minimum wage
ad1756d9bc22.sentence: At the same time, a minimum wage above the equilibrium wage would allow (or entice) more people to enter the labor market because of the higher salary.

7ca8dbd41a14.title: Price floor

98f875a2e708.title: Market mechanism
98f875a2e708.sentence: In economics, the market mechanism is a mechanism by which the use of money exchanged by buyers and sellers with an open and understood system of value and time trade-offs in a market tends to optimize distribution of goods and services in at least some ways.

c911ba4c62d6.title: Market mechanism
c911ba4c62d6.sentence: The mechanism can exist in free markets or in captive or controlling markets seek to use supply and demand, or some other form of charging for scarcity, to choose among production possibilities.

67b91e287dd7.title: Market mechanism
67b91e287dd7.sentence: They not only tell producers what to produce but also inform the producers to produce what people want.

aa03b23abd9a.title: Market mechanism
aa03b23abd9a.sentence: The more inaccurate the information gets, the lesser will be the economic coordination which will in turn lower satisfaction of wants.

24217b486450.title: Market mechanism
24217b486450.sentence: However, the market mechanism often cannot optimize for public goods, owing to problems such as the tragedy of the commons.

40995a5a22c1.title: Market mechanism
40995a5a22c1.sentence: For example, modern highways have been good for economic development, but it has taken government planning and allocation to bring them into existence.

4f2c1467c914.title: Market mechanism
4f2c1467c914.sentence: In a free market economy, all the resources are allocated by the private sector (individuals, households, and groups of individuals); in a planned economy, all the resources are owned by the public sector (local and central government); and, in a mixed economy, some resources are owned by both sectors, private and public.

d857286516d2.title: Zero-profit condition
d857286516d2.sentence: In economic competition theory, the zero-profit condition is the condition that occurs when an industry or type of business has an extremely low (near-zero) cost of entry to or exit from the industry.

9fc2b43f6955.title: Zero-profit condition
9fc2b43f6955.sentence: More and more firms will enter until the economic profit per firm has been driven down to zero by competition.

84a376a1e9e6.title: Zero-profit condition
84a376a1e9e6.sentence: In this situation, some firms not already in the industry tend to join the industry if they calculate that they will make a positive economic profit (profit in excess of the cost of acquiring investible funds).

d518e01113f1.title: Zero-profit condition
d518e01113f1.sentence: Conversely, if firms are making negative economic profit, enough firms will exit the industry until economic profit per firm has risen to zero.

92dfcb23d328.title: Zero-profit condition
92dfcb23d328.sentence: The situation with zero economic profit is referred to as the industry's long run.

53982f112f60.title: Zero-profit condition
53982f112f60.sentence: This description represents a situation of almost perfect competition.

4e68b13c2cf2.title: Zero-profit condition
4e68b13c2cf2.sentence: Historically, this condition was present in most gold rushes, as diggings required nothing but manpower and few skills or machinery.

f4f38e7c3e92.title: Zero-profit condition
f4f38e7c3e92.sentence: For example, few gold prospectors became wealthy, but many formed successful businesses selling shovels.

207d16e5177b.title: Growth imperative
207d16e5177b.sentence: Therefore, a market economy with profit-oriented companies is compatible with zero growth, as it is in the models of neoclassical theory (→ zero-profit condition).

f80fe11965a3.title: Economic surplus
f80fe11965a3.sentence: In mainstream economics, economic surplus, also known as total welfare or total social welfare or Marshallian surplus (after Alfred Marshall), is either of two related quantities:

3c8954f3dc18.title: Economic surplus
3c8954f3dc18.sentence: The sum of consumer and producer surplus is sometimes known as social surplus or total surplus; a decrease in that total from inefficiencies is called deadweight loss.

6c3953745cd8.title: Economic surplus
6c3953745cd8.sentence: In the mid-19th century, engineer Jules Dupuit first propounded the concept of economic surplus, but it was the economist Alfred Marshall who gave the concept its fame in the field of economics.

17f2fd54b97a.title: Economic surplus
17f2fd54b97a.sentence: On a standard supply and demand diagram, consumer surplus is the area (triangular if the supply and demand curves are linear) above the equilibrium price of the good and below the demand curve.

c2f3984593dd.title: Economic surplus
c2f3984593dd.sentence: Likewise, in the supply-demand diagram, producer surplus is the area below the equilibrium price but above the supply curve.

3eafd9294c84.title: Economic surplus
3eafd9294c84.sentence: Early writers of economic issues used surplus as a means to draw conclusions about the relationship between production and necessities.

ec91c1eb78cc.title: Economic surplus
ec91c1eb78cc.sentence: In the agricultural sector surplus was an important concept because this sector has the responsibility to feed everyone plus itself.

f160c49aaeee.title: Economic surplus
f160c49aaeee.sentence: The non-agricultural sector is therefore limited by the agricultural sector equaling the output of food subtracting the amount consumed by the agricultural sector.

1f8c76213063.title: Deadweight loss
1f8c76213063.sentence: In economics, deadweight loss is the loss of societal economic welfare due to production/consumption of a good at a quantity where marginal benefit (to society) does not equal marginal cost (to society).

253782fd8fbe.title: Deadweight loss
253782fd8fbe.sentence: In other words, there are either goods being produced despite the cost of doing so being larger than the benefit, or additional goods are not being produced despite the fact that the benefits of their production would be larger than the costs.

8df1584707c3.title: Deadweight loss
8df1584707c3.sentence: The deadweight loss is the net benefit that is missed out on.

bea4915f90ac.title: Deadweight loss
bea4915f90ac.sentence: While losses to one entity often lead to gains for another, deadweight loss represents the loss that is not regained by anyone else.

27a69110045b.title: Deadweight loss
27a69110045b.sentence: Non-optimal production can be caused by monopoly pricing in the case of artificial scarcity, a positive or negative externality, a tax or subsidy (the excess burden of taxation), or a binding price ceiling or price floor such as a minimum wage.

42f2ca82edd4.title: Deadweight loss
42f2ca82edd4.sentence: Assume a market for nails where the cost of each nail is $0.10.

9c1419e4ab01.title: Deadweight loss
9c1419e4ab01.sentence: In this example, the monopoly producer charges $0.60 per nail, thus excluding every customer from the market with a marginal benefit less than $0.60.

7f631292c559.title: Deadweight loss
7f631292c559.sentence: The deadweight loss due to monopoly pricing would then be the economic benefit foregone by customers with a marginal benefit of between $0.10 and $0.60 per nail.

411c44b82310.title: Deadweight loss
411c44b82310.sentence: For example, if in the same nail market the government provided a $0.03 subsidy for every nail produced, the subsidy would reduce the market price of each nail to $0.07, even though production actually still costs $0.10 per nail.

d5e65d99c923.title: Deadweight loss
d5e65d99c923.sentence: Consumers with a marginal benefit of between $0.07 and $0.10 per nail would then buy nails, even though their benefit is less than the real production cost of $0.10.

107146339499.title: Deadweight loss
107146339499.sentence: Amie and Will each receive a benefit of $20, making the total surplus from trade $40.

aced12060a2b.title: Deadweight loss
aced12060a2b.sentence: However, if the government were to decide to impose a $50 tax upon the providers of cleaning services, their trade would no longer benefit them.

5a69cbb84c41.title: Deadweight loss
5a69cbb84c41.sentence: Government revenue is also affected by this tax: since Amie and Will have abandoned the deal, the government also loses any tax revenue that would have resulted from wages.

df2cd22486c2.title: Deadweight loss
df2cd22486c2.sentence: This $40 is referred to as the deadweight loss.

23900b14dcf5.title: Deadweight loss
23900b14dcf5.sentence: Price elasticities of supply and demand determine whether the deadweight loss from a tax is large or small.

493b98ee9c0c.title: Deadweight loss
493b98ee9c0c.sentence: As the elasticities of supply and demand increase, so does the deadweight loss resulting from a tax.

8debe8ece879.title: Deadweight loss
8debe8ece879.sentence: Where a tax increases linearly, the deadweight loss increases as the square of the tax increase.

a56c48823fda.title: Deadweight loss
a56c48823fda.sentence: Thus, doubling the tax increases the deadweight loss by a factor of 4.

2c9bb5b6ce42.title: Gains from trade
2c9bb5b6ce42.sentence: In economics, gains from trade are the net benefits to economic agents from being allowed an increase in voluntary trading with each other.

e892c1f733af.title: Gains from trade
e892c1f733af.sentence: In technical terms, they are the increase of consumer surplus plus producer surplus from lower tariffs or otherwise liberalizing trade.

c43313118c1c.title: Gains from trade
c43313118c1c.sentence: - specialization in production from division of labor, economies of scale, scope, and agglomeration and relative availability of factor resources in types of output by farms, businesses, location and economies

1866c8af8ec6.title: Gains from trade
1866c8af8ec6.sentence: - a resulting increase in total output possibilities

762807183659.title: Gains from trade
762807183659.sentence: - trade through markets from sale of one type of output for other, more highly valued goods.

3c69d30a5657.title: Gains from trade
3c69d30a5657.sentence: Market incentives, such as reflected in prices of outputs and inputs, are theorized to attract factors of production, including labor, into activities according to comparative advantage, that is, for which they each have a low opportunity cost.

7386fde4e0bc.title: Gains from trade
7386fde4e0bc.sentence: David Ricardo in 1817 first clearly stated and proved the principle of comparative advantage, termed a "fundamental analytical explanation" for the source of gains from trade.

f55934f4db6e.title: Gains from trade
f55934f4db6e.sentence: The proof does not state that no involvement is the best economic outcome.

8dffbfb5220d.title: Gains from trade
8dffbfb5220d.sentence: Rather, a large economy might be able to set taxes and subsidies to its benefit at the expense of other economies.

51244e92e1b1.title: Gains from trade
51244e92e1b1.sentence: But from publication of Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations in 1776, it was widely argued, that, with competition and absent market distortions, such gains are positive in moving toward free trade and away from autarky or prohibitively high import tariffs.

1049644b8997.title: Economic surplus
1049644b8997.sentence: Consumer surplus is the difference between the maximum price a consumer is willing to pay and the actual price they do pay.

589b0f9bb5fa.title: Economic surplus
589b0f9bb5fa.sentence: - Consumer surplus, or consumers' surplus, is the monetary gain obtained by consumers because they are able to purchase a product for a price that is less than the highest price that they would be willing to pay.

c518a5dbf3db.title: Economic surplus
c518a5dbf3db.sentence: An example of a good with generally high consumer surplus is drinking water.

d28d219487e5.title: Economic surplus
d28d219487e5.sentence: People would pay very high prices for drinking water, as they need it to survive.

1e1e92e29ac3.title: Economic surplus
1e1e92e29ac3.sentence: The utility of the first few liters of drinking water is very high (as it prevents death), so the first few liters would likely have more consumer surplus than subsequent quantities.

b2ea404a826c.title: Economic surplus
b2ea404a826c.sentence: This reflects the fact that consumers would have been willing to buy a single unit of the good at a price higher than the equilibrium price, a second unit at a price below that but still above the equilibrium price, etc., yet they in fact pay just the equilibrium price for each unit they buy.

258a3c4a1409.title: Economic surplus
258a3c4a1409.sentence: Diminishing marginal utility means a person receives less additional utility from an additional unit.

95ab976d2298.title: Economic surplus

97341e51a0c6.sentence: The consumer surplus (individual or aggregated) is the area under the (individual or aggregated) demand curve and above a horizontal line at the actual price (in the aggregated case, the equilibrium price).

2fe4b894e32c.title: Economic surplus

2fe4b894e32c.sentence: If the demand curve is a straight line, the consumer surplus is the area of a triangle:

f6d674471e77.sentence: If the change in consumer surplus is positive, the price change is said to have increased the individuals welfare.

ce5866c7a419.sentence: If the price change in consumer surplus is negative, the price change is said to have decreased the individual's welfare.
