b4cdd9b0cb6c.section: Consumer surplus > Distribution of benefits when price falls
b4cdd9b0cb6c.sentence: When supply of a good expands, the price falls (assuming the demand curve is downward sloping) and consumer surplus increases.

9977bc13f034.title: Economic surplus
9977bc13f034.section: Consumer surplus > Distribution of benefits when price falls
9977bc13f034.sentence: This benefits two groups of people: consumers who were already willing to buy at the initial price benefit from a price reduction, and they may buy more and receive even more consumer surplus; and additional consumers who were unwilling to buy at the initial price will buy at the new price and also receive some consumer surplus.

40ff6e0deb06.title: Price discrimination
40ff6e0deb06.sentence: Price discrimination, known also by several other names, is a microeconomic pricing strategy whereby identical or largely similar goods or services are sold at different prices by the same provider to different buyers, based on which market segment they are perceived to be part of.

3313b278d585.title: Price discrimination
3313b278d585.sentence: Price discrimination essentially relies on the variation in customers' willingness to pay and in the elasticity of their demand.

53efe5236301.title: Price discrimination
53efe5236301.sentence: For price discrimination to succeed, a seller must have market power, such as a dominant market share, product uniqueness, sole pricing power, etc.

bfb0d188a46e.title: Price discrimination
bfb0d188a46e.sentence: Without market power when the price is higher than the market equilibrium, consumers will switch to sellers selling at the market equilibrium.

445e1230203d.title: Price discrimination
445e1230203d.sentence: Moreover, when the seller tries to sell the same good at differentiating prices, the buyer at the lower price can arbitrage by selling to the consumer buying at the higher price with a small discount from the higher price.

3239ec985a66.title: Price discrimination
3239ec985a66.section: Types > First degree: perfect price discrimination
3239ec985a66.sentence: The optimal incarnation of this is called "perfect price discrimination" and maximizes the price that each customer is willing to pay.

c27bafce299d.title: Price discrimination
c27bafce299d.section: Types > First degree: perfect price discrimination
c27bafce299d.sentence: As such, in "first degree" price differentiation the entire consumer surplus is captured for each individual.

8809f6abaddc.title: Price discrimination
8809f6abaddc.sentence: In second-degree price discrimination, the price of the same good varies according to the quantity demanded.

6562e07c1d88.title: Price discrimination
6562e07c1d88.sentence: "Group pricing" (or "third-degree" price differentiation) – dividing the market into segments and charging a different price to each segment (but the same price to each member of that segment).

c3c29695ddeb.title: Price discrimination
c3c29695ddeb.sentence: Typical examples include student and senior discounts.

82498016bb01.title: Price discrimination
82498016bb01.sentence: The purpose of price discrimination is to increase profits by capturing consumer surplus.

0e42525ed6d9.title: Price discrimination
0e42525ed6d9.sentence: Price discrimination transfers some of this surplus from the consumer to the seller.

5173e35683e6.title: Price discrimination
5173e35683e6.sentence: Drug-makers charge more for drugs in wealthier countries.

33fe41ce9f8f.title: Price discrimination
33fe41ce9f8f.sentence: Pharmaceutical companies may charge customers living in wealthier countries a much higher price than for identical drugs in poorer nations, as is the case with the sale of antiretroviral drugs in Africa.

99d08d788078.title: Price discrimination
99d08d788078.sentence: Since the purchasing power of African consumers is much lower, sales would be extremely limited without price discrimination.

e4d858bffc99.title: Price discrimination
e4d858bffc99.sentence: The first/second/third degree taxonomy of price discrimination is attributed to Pigou.

9a924058b8bb.title: Economic surplus
9a924058b8bb.sentence: - Producer surplus, or producers' surplus, is the amount that producers benefit by selling at a market price that is higher than the least that they would be willing to sell for; this is roughly equal to profit (since producers are not normally willing to sell at a loss and are normally indifferent to selling at a break-even price).

7b41a7fdaaf3.title: Economic surplus
7b41a7fdaaf3.sentence: Producer surplus is an economic indicator of the benefit that producers receive when the market price of the good or service they supply is more than what they require to do so.

5e43832b0940.title: Economic surplus
5e43832b0940.section: Producer surplus > Calculation of producer surplus
5e43832b0940.sentence: Producer surplus is usually expressed by the area below the market price line and above the supply curve.

db535f9b63fb.title: Economic surplus
db535f9b63fb.sentence: A rise in market prices, everything else kept constant, will lead to greater producer surplus as each extra unit of quantity is sold at a higher price.

0b3f4b0faa50.title: Economic surplus
0b3f4b0faa50.sentence: Other things being equal, an increase in production costs or a fall in the market price will decrease the producer surplus.

83459f3db2b0.title: Economic surplus
83459f3db2b0.sentence: An increase or decrease in tax rates or subsidy levels, changes in new technology and competition also can impact the level of the surplus as they tend to change production costs or market prices.

bb3e8d17a6c6.title: Economic surplus
bb3e8d17a6c6.sentence: It is used to find out how government policy interventions (taxes, subsidies, price controls, etc. and policies implicated in trade) affect producers.

8dc0835e50ed.title: Economic surplus
8dc0835e50ed.sentence: The rule of one-half estimates the change in consumer surplus for small changes in supply with a constant demand curve.

1d57ae7166a3.title: Economic surplus
1d57ae7166a3.sentence: Hence, the change in consumer surplus is the area of the trapezoid with i) height equal to the change in price and ii) mid-segment length equal to the average of the ex-post and ex-ante equilibrium quantities.

b848e18891a0.title: Economic surplus
b848e18891a0.sentence: - Q0 and Q1 are, respectively, the quantity demanded before and after a change in supply;

dfa982a6bc29.title: Economic surplus
dfa982a6bc29.sentence: - P0 and P1 are, respectively, the prices before and after a change in supply.

b846eca3cd68.title: Deadweight loss
b846eca3cd68.sentence: Harberger's triangle, generally attributed to Arnold Harberger, shows the deadweight loss (as measured on a supply and demand graph) associated with government intervention in a perfect market.

81733370f240.title: Deadweight loss
81733370f240.sentence: Mechanisms for this intervention include price floors, caps, taxes, tariffs, or quotas.

2cbc5039bf72.title: Deadweight loss
2cbc5039bf72.sentence: It also refers to the deadweight loss created by a government's failure to intervene in a market with externalities.

a93b6833e166.title: Deadweight loss
a93b6833e166.sentence: In the case of a government tax, the amount of the tax drives a wedge between what consumers pay and what producers receive, and the area of this wedge shape is equivalent to the deadweight loss caused by the tax.

cd418095f147.title: Deadweight loss
cd418095f147.sentence: The loss of such surplus is never recouped and represents the deadweight loss.

3d98e3835f67.title: Deadweight loss
3d98e3835f67.sentence: Some economists like Martin Feldstein maintain that these triangles can seriously affect long-term economic trends by pivoting the trend downwards and causing a magnification of losses in the long run but others like James Tobin have argued that they do not have a huge impact on the economy.

439d9b2fffb2.title: Market clearing
439d9b2fffb2.sentence: In economics, market clearing is the process by which, in an economic market, the supply of whatever is traded is equated to the demand so that there is no excess supply or demand, ensuring that there is neither a surplus nor a shortage.

37e436677f54.title: Market clearing
37e436677f54.sentence: A market-clearing price is the price of a good or service at which the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded, also called the equilibrium price.

67e4f9596b39.title: Market clearing
67e4f9596b39.sentence: If the sale price exceeds the market-clearing price, supply will exceed demand, and a surplus inventory will build up over the long run.

03cf7e4aede5.title: Market clearing
03cf7e4aede5.sentence: If the sale price is lower than the market-clearing price, then demand will exceed supply, and in the long run, shortages will result, where buyers sometimes find no products for sale at any price.

d0c55d48b699.title: Market clearing
d0c55d48b699.sentence: For example, consider a scenario where a community experiences an earthquake that destroys all houses and apartments.

d451984cd845.title: Market clearing
d451984cd845.sentence: The sudden demand for new housing will create a temporary shortage of houses and apartments in the market.

d02efd9b6232.title: Market clearing
d02efd9b6232.sentence: However, if prices are free to change, construction companies will build new houses in the short run, while new companies will enter the house and apartment construction market in the longer run.

49a626e0c088.title: Market clearing
49a626e0c088.sentence: As a result, the housing supply will increase, eventually reaching a point where it equals the new demand.

d35864463767.title: Market clearing
d35864463767.sentence: An example of excess supply is Christmas decorations that are still in stores several days after Christmas; the stores that still have boxes of decorations view these products as excess supply, so prices are discounted until shoppers buy all the decorations (to keep them until next Christmas).

120244fa818f.title: Market clearing
120244fa818f.sentence: For 150 years (from approximately 1785 to 1935), most economists took the smooth operation of this market-clearing mechanism as inevitable and inviolable, based mainly on belief in Say's law.

beea722dd5cb.title: Market clearing
beea722dd5cb.sentence: But the Great Depression of the 1930s caused many economists, including John Maynard Keynes, to doubt their classical faith.

c06060205f89.title: Market clearing
c06060205f89.sentence: If markets were supposed to clear, how could ruinously high unemployment rates persist for so many painful years?

f0505c717201.title: Market clearing
f0505c717201.sentence: Most economists see the assumption of continuous market clearing as unrealistic.

e3c360e3e5c6.title: Market clearing
e3c360e3e5c6.sentence: However, many see the concept of flexible prices as useful in the long-run analysis since prices are not stuck forever: market-clearing models describe the equilibrium economy gravitates towards.

335d47b7e86d.title: Shortage
335d47b7e86d.sentence: In economics, a shortage or excess demand is a situation in which the demand for a product or service exceeds its supply in a market.

1d522970cfcd.title: Shortage
1d522970cfcd.sentence: It is the opposite of an excess supply (surplus).

160a8a5b6198.title: Shortage
160a8a5b6198.sentence: In a perfect market (one that matches a simple microeconomic model), an excess of demand will prompt sellers to increase prices until demand at that price matches the available supply, establishing market equilibrium.

babf2f20c1dd.title: Shortage
babf2f20c1dd.sentence: In economic terminology, a shortage occurs when for some reason (such as government intervention, or decisions by sellers not to raise prices) the price does not rise to reach equilibrium.

8a3c12ef7d3d.title: Shortage
8a3c12ef7d3d.sentence: In this circumstance, buyers want to purchase more at the market price than the quantity of the good or service that is available, and some non-price mechanism (such as "first come, first served" or a lottery) determines which buyers are served.

a9758246b4f8.title: Shortage
a9758246b4f8.sentence: - Price ceilings, a type of price control which involves a government-imposed limit on the price of a product or service.

ecb7c66e4852.title: Shortage
ecb7c66e4852.sentence: - Government ban on the sale of a product or service, such as prostitution or certain recreational drugs.

671e982f359d.title: Shortage
671e982f359d.sentence: - Decisions by suppliers not to raise prices in order to maintain friendly relationships with potential future customers during a supply disruption.

c23af2b9ae53.title: Shortage
c23af2b9ae53.sentence: - Black (illegal) and grey (unregulated) markets in which products that are unavailable in conventional markets are sold, or in which products with excess demand are sold at higher prices than in the conventional market.

338437298d07.title: Shortage
338437298d07.sentence: - Artificial controls of demand, such as time (such as waiting in line at queues) and rationing.

8570b99cc167.title: Shortage
8570b99cc167.sentence: - Increase in demand for substitute goods.

257cf22ea1d1.title: Shortage
257cf22ea1d1.sentence: Economic shortages caused by higher transaction costs and opportunity costs (e.g., in the form of lost time) also mean that the distribution process is wasteful.

edf5231ab043.title: Shortage
edf5231ab043.sentence: Both of these factors contribute to a decrease in aggregate wealth.

a35b5ee09e39.title: Shortage
a35b5ee09e39.sentence: - In the former Soviet Union during the 1980s, prices were artificially low by fiat (i.e., high prices were outlawed).

fe4c84115686.title: Shortage
fe4c84115686.sentence: Soviet citizens waited in line for various price-controlled goods and services such as cars, apartments, or some types of clothing.

e81181552a05.title: Human overpopulation
e81181552a05.sentence: Additionally, many economists and historians have noted that sustained shortages and famines have historically been caused by war, price controls, political instability, and repressive political regimes (often employing central planning) rather than overpopulation.

a67b9f837499.title: Price ceiling
a67b9f837499.sentence: A price ceiling or price cap is a government- or group-imposed price control, or limit, on how high a price is charged for a product, commodity, or service.

e91230dd2be7.title: Price ceiling
e91230dd2be7.sentence: Governments impose price ceilings to protect consumers from conditions that could make commodities prohibitively expensive.

8c6edb84084d.title: Price ceiling
8c6edb84084d.sentence: Economists generally agree that consumer price controls do not accomplish what they intend to in market economies, and many economists instead recommend such controls should be avoided.

9f9142d12be2.title: Price ceiling
9f9142d12be2.sentence: There is a substantial body of research showing that under some circumstances price ceilings can, paradoxically, lead to higher prices.

3e11e7d63801.title: Price ceiling
3e11e7d63801.sentence: The leading explanation is that price ceilings serve to coordinate collusion among suppliers who would otherwise compete on price.

3907c5a1b9e2.title: Price ceiling
3907c5a1b9e2.sentence: One research paper documenting the phenomenon is Knittel and Stangel, which found that in the 1980s United States, states that fixed an interest rate ceiling of 18 percent had firms charging a rate only slightly below the ceiling.

4a36dd9f35a4.title: Price ceiling
4a36dd9f35a4.sentence: States without an interest rate ceiling had interest rates that were significantly lower.

b8a34bbbeff4.title: Price ceiling
b8a34bbbeff4.sentence: According to professors Niko Määttänen and Ari Hyytinen, price ceilings on Helsinki City Hitas apartments are highly inefficient economically.

2a614e79098e.title: Price ceiling
2a614e79098e.sentence: They cause queuing and discriminate against the handicapped, single parents, elderly, and others who are not able to queue for days.

d9820078124f.title: Price ceiling
d9820078124f.sentence: They cause inefficient allocation, as apartments are not bought by those willing to pay the most for them.

8c2fb523dbcb.title: Price ceiling
8c2fb523dbcb.sentence: On January 10, 2006, a BBC article reported that since 2003, Venezuela President Hugo Chávez had been setting price ceilings on food and that the price ceilings had caused shortages and hoarding.

369d57d6a25e.title: Price ceiling
369d57d6a25e.sentence: Isabella Weber and her colleagues argue for price caps to combat sellers' inflation.

9694d2c7ba9a.title: Price ceiling
9694d2c7ba9a.sentence: Paul Krugman changed his mind and expressed interest in adding price caps to the toolkit to fight inflation.

4b4135852b6d.title: Price ceiling
4b4135852b6d.sentence: Rent controls were instituted in the US in the 1940s by then-president Franklin D. Roosevelt and his newly-formed Office of Price Administration.

dafe5b8c404d.title: Price ceiling
dafe5b8c404d.sentence: The Office instituted price ceilings on a wide range of commodities, including rent controls that allowed returning World War II veterans and their families to afford housing.

285b84bab09a.title: Price ceiling
285b84bab09a.sentence: Following the predictions of economic models, this policy lowered the supply of rentable properties available to veterans.

74372007f63a.title: Price ceiling
74372007f63a.sentence: At the same time, there was an increase in homeownership and the number of homes for sale.

18acc40464e7.title: Price ceiling
18acc40464e7.sentence: This outcome could be explained by landowners converting their rentable property to sellable property, due to the financial unviability of rental markets and no incentive by the landowner to destroy their property or leave it vacant.

775152f2a0a3.title: Profit maximization
775152f2a0a3.sentence: In economics, profit maximization is the short run or long run process by which a firm may determine the price, input and output levels that will lead to the highest possible total profit (or just profit in short).

95dcfebe109a.title: Profit maximization
95dcfebe109a.sentence: In neoclassical economics, which is currently the mainstream approach to microeconomics, the firm is assumed to be a "rational agent" (whether operating in a perfectly competitive market or otherwise) which wants to maximize its total profit, which is the difference between its total revenue and its total cost.

1b411ad0ff98.title: Profit maximization
1b411ad0ff98.sentence: When a firm produces an extra unit of product, the additional revenue gained from selling it is called the marginal revenue (MR), and the additional cost to produce that unit is called the marginal cost (MC).

6dcbf25c059e.title: Profit maximization
6dcbf25c059e.sentence: When the level of output is such that the marginal revenue is equal to the marginal cost (MR=MC), then the firm's total profit is said to be maximized.

ecd437e7ab3d.title: Profit maximization
ecd437e7ab3d.sentence: If the marginal revenue is greater than the marginal cost (MR>MC), then its total profit is not maximized, because the firm can produce additional units to earn additional profit.

d6521705d3b2.title: Profit maximization
d6521705d3b2.sentence: The intersection of MR and MC is shown in the next diagram as point A. If the industry is perfectly competitive (as is assumed in the diagram), the firm faces a demand curve (D) that is identical to its marginal revenue curve (MR), and this is a horizontal line at a price determined by industry supply and demand.

893c45e51562.title: Profit maximization
893c45e51562.section: Changes in total costs and profit maximization
893c45e51562.sentence: In the short run, a change in fixed costs has no effect on the profit maximizing output or price.

16f0f2397a78.title: Profit maximization
16f0f2397a78.section: Changes in total costs and profit maximization
16f0f2397a78.sentence: The firm merely treats short term fixed costs as sunk costs and continues to operate as before.

4965ae9f18da.title: Profit maximization
4965ae9f18da.section: Case in which maximizing revenue is equivalent
4965ae9f18da.sentence: An example would be a scheduled airline flight.

e095e812c546.title: Profit maximization
e095e812c546.section: Case in which maximizing revenue is equivalent
e095e812c546.sentence: The marginal costs of flying one more passenger on the flight are negligible until all the seats are filled.

283dd3bcbcc8.title: Profit maximization
283dd3bcbcc8.section: Case in which maximizing revenue is equivalent
283dd3bcbcc8.sentence: The airline would maximize profit by filling all the seats.

a6f9da0c94c5.title: Profit maximization
a6f9da0c94c5.sentence: The maximization of producer surplus can in some cases reduce consumer surplus.

feb90aea9184.title: Profit maximization
feb90aea9184.sentence: Some forms of producer profit maximization are considered anti-competitive practices and are regulated by competition law.

ed30335ccad8.title: Bounded rationality
ed30335ccad8.sentence: In economic models based on behavioral economics, implementing bounded rationality implies finding replacements for utility maximization and profit maximization as used in conventional general equilibrium models.

a8809bbbb13e.title: Production function
a8809bbbb13e.sentence: In economics, a production function gives the technological relation between quantities of physical inputs and quantities of output of goods.

53d282d0dda8.title: Production function
53d282d0dda8.sentence: To satisfy the mathematical definition of a function, a production function is customarily assumed to specify the maximum output obtainable from a given set of inputs.

c4c9e98579f5.title: Production function
c4c9e98579f5.sentence: The production function, therefore, describes a boundary or frontier representing the limit of output obtainable from each feasible combination of input.

981a6f70057a.title: Production function
981a6f70057a.sentence: In the production function itself, the relationship of output to inputs is non-monetary; that is, a production function relates physical inputs to physical outputs, and prices and costs are not reflected in the function.

d24b78a7286e.title: Production function
d24b78a7286e.section: The theory of production functions > Specifying the production function
d24b78a7286e.sentence: where Q is the quantity of output and X1,X2,X3,…,Xn are the quantities of factor inputs (such as capital, labour, land or raw materials).

3ed10f231193.title: Production function
3ed10f231193.section: The theory of production functions > Specifying the production function
3ed10f231193.sentence: For X1=X2=...=Xn=0 it must be Q=0 since we cannot produce anything without inputs.

153aecfa50d9.title: Production function
153aecfa50d9.sentence: The production function is one of the key concepts of mainstream neoclassical theories, used to define marginal product and to distinguish allocative efficiency, a key focus of economics.

92968d99840d.title: Production function
92968d99840d.section: The theory of production functions > Homogeneous and homothetic production functions
92968d99840d.sentence: If m>1, the function exhibits increasing returns to scale, and it exhibits decreasing returns to scale if m<1.

874a76653146.title: Production function
874a76653146.section: The theory of production functions > Homogeneous and homothetic production functions
874a76653146.sentence: If it is homogeneous of degree 1, it exhibits constant returns to scale.

a081f48f57cf.title: Production function
a081f48f57cf.sentence: In macroeconomics, aggregate production functions are estimated to create a framework in which to distinguish how much of economic growth to attribute to changes in factor allocation (e.g. the accumulation of physical capital) and how much to attribute to advancing technology.

77e749b422f0.title: Cobb–Douglas production function
77e749b422f0.sentence: Paul Douglas explained that his first formulation of the Cobb–Douglas production function was developed in 1927; when seeking a functional form to relate estimates he had calculated for workers and capital, he spoke with mathematician and colleague Charles Cobb, who suggested a function of the form Y=ALαK1−α, previously used by Knut Wicksell, Philip Wicksteed, and Léon Walras, although Douglas only acknowledges Wicksteed and Walras for their contributions.

0b6e1294c44a.title: Cobb–Douglas production function
0b6e1294c44a.sentence: The Cobb–Douglas production function is especially notable for being the first time an aggregate or economy-wide production function had been developed, estimated, and then presented to the profession for analysis; it marked a landmark change in how economists approached macroeconomics from a microeconomics perspective.

cfa7ca7b7a14.title: Production function
cfa7ca7b7a14.sentence: Some non-mainstream economists, however, reject the very concept of an aggregate production function.

141e1239b69d.title: Production function
141e1239b69d.section: The theory of production functions > Criticisms of the production function theory > On the concept of capital
141e1239b69d.sentence: During the 1950s, '60s, and '70s there was a lively debate about the theoretical soundness of production functions (see the Capital controversy).

1575956d6e24.title: Production function
1575956d6e24.section: The theory of production functions > Criticisms of the production function theory > On the concept of capital
1575956d6e24.sentence: The debate began in 1953 when Joan Robinson criticized the way the factor input capital was measured and how the notion of factor proportions had distracted economists.

c5115725f05d.title: Fixed cost
c5115725f05d.sentence: In accounting and economics, fixed costs, also known as indirect costs or overhead costs, are business expenses that are not dependent on the level of goods or services produced by the business.

07f9c6ef41f1.title: Fixed cost
07f9c6ef41f1.sentence: They tend to be recurring, such as interest or rents being paid per month.

eb84cd56ae72.title: Fixed cost
eb84cd56ae72.sentence: These costs also tend to be capital costs.

47a58d0e984f.title: Fixed cost
47a58d0e984f.sentence: As another example, for a bakery the monthly rent and phone line are fixed costs, irrespective of how much bread is produced and sold; on the other hand, the wages are variable costs, as more workers would need to be hired for the production to increase.

d41e35139e9d.title: Fixed cost
d41e35139e9d.sentence: Fixed costs are not permanently fixed; they will change over time, but are fixed, by contractual obligation, in relation to the quantity of production for the relevant period.

188245497dc5.title: Fixed cost
188245497dc5.sentence: By definition, there are no fixed costs in the long run, because the long run is a sufficient period of time for all short-run fixed inputs to become variable.

06692777cb03.title: Fixed cost
06692777cb03.sentence: Fixed costs are considered an entry barrier for new entrepreneurs.

969c6d7307f8.title: Fixed cost
969c6d7307f8.sentence: Some writers also refer to "mixed costs" or semi-variable costs, which are partially fixed and partially variable: thus telephone costs could be treated as "mixed" because the total cost would include the variable cost of actual calls.

bc7931dd3c64.title: Fixed cost
bc7931dd3c64.sentence: In business planning and management accounting, usage of the terms fixed costs, variable costs and others will often differ from usage in economics, and may depend on the context.

3f9babf268ec.title: Fixed cost
3f9babf268ec.sentence: In recent years, fixed costs gradually exceed variable costs for many companies.

ff7a63f50663.title: Long run and short run
ff7a63f50663.sentence: In economics, the long run is a theoretical concept in which all markets are in equilibrium, and all prices and quantities have fully adjusted and are in equilibrium.

53ea36b2f857.title: Long run and short run
53ea36b2f857.sentence: The long run contrasts with the short run, in which there are some constraints and markets are not fully in equilibrium.

c87e883a445d.title: Long run and short run
c87e883a445d.sentence: More specifically, in microeconomics there are no fixed factors of production in the long run, and there is enough time for adjustment so that there are no constraints preventing changing the output level by changing the capital stock or by entering or leaving an industry.

d9b05a5d15fe.title: Long run and short run
d9b05a5d15fe.sentence: This contrasts with the short run, where some factors are variable (dependent on the quantity produced) and others are fixed (paid once), constraining entry or exit from an industry.

d4b41d2f394f.title: Long run and short run
d4b41d2f394f.sentence: In macroeconomics, the long run is the period when the general price level, contractual wage rates, and expectations adjust fully to the state of the economy, in contrast to the short run when these variables may not fully adjust.

b52af2adf065.title: Long run and short run
b52af2adf065.sentence: The differentiation between long-run and short-run economic models did not come into practice until 1890, with Alfred Marshall's publication of his work Principles of Economics.

aba809345296.title: Long run and short run
aba809345296.sentence: However, there is no hard and fast definition as to what is classified as "long" or "short" and mostly relies on the economic perspective being taken.

0cafcd4cb254.title: Long run and short run
0cafcd4cb254.sentence: In the long run, firms change production levels in response to (expected) economic profits or losses, and the land, labour, capital goods and entrepreneurship vary to reach the minimum level of long-run average cost.

ed4e14067da6.title: Long run and short run
ed4e14067da6.sentence: - Enter an industry in response to (expected) profits

c599e2a4e8dc.title: Long run and short run
c599e2a4e8dc.sentence: - Leave an industry in response to losses

885d35451a07.title: Long run and short run
885d35451a07.sentence: All production in real time occurs in the short run.

e6a22467215a.title: Long run and short run
e6a22467215a.sentence: In the short run, increases and decreases in variable factors are the only things that can affect the output produced by firms.

6745984d5798.title: Long run and short run
6745984d5798.sentence: They could change things such as labour and raw materials.

7aa4ba65f03f.title: Long run and short run
7aa4ba65f03f.sentence: - Increase production if marginal cost is less than marginal revenue (added revenue per additional unit of output);

8eb0192bcda4.title: Long run and short run
8eb0192bcda4.sentence: - Decrease production if marginal cost is greater than marginal revenue;

a9ed30040497.title: Long run and short run
a9ed30040497.sentence: A famous critique of neglecting short-run analysis was by Keynes, who wrote that "In the long run, we are all dead", referring to the long-run proposition of the quantity theory of money, for example, a doubling of the money supply doubling the price level.

f0d84ac59f34.title: Returns to scale
f0d84ac59f34.sentence: In economics, the concept of returns to scale arises in the context of a firm's production function.

cc4503dd7a2b.title: Returns to scale
cc4503dd7a2b.sentence: It explains the long-run linkage of increase in output (production) relative to associated increases in the inputs (factors of production).

b4420c53e7e6.title: Returns to scale
b4420c53e7e6.sentence: - If output increases by the same proportional change as all inputs change then there are constant returns to scale (CRS).

bd03815d8103.title: Returns to scale
bd03815d8103.sentence: - If output increases by less than the proportional change in all inputs, there are decreasing returns to scale (DRS).

6b4755ed4584.title: Returns to scale
6b4755ed4584.sentence: - If output increases by more than the proportional change in all inputs, there are increasing returns to scale (IRS).

fa22f4642b85.title: Returns to scale
fa22f4642b85.sentence: The main reason for the decreasing returns to scale is the increased management difficulties associated with the increased scale of production, the lack of coordination in all stages of production, and the resulting decrease in production efficiency.

f5d2e0d3138e.title: Returns to scale
f5d2e0d3138e.sentence: The main reason for the increasing returns to scale is the increase in production efficiency due to the expansion of the firm's production scale.

95ef1131074f.title: Returns to scale
95ef1131074f.sentence: Typically, there could be increasing returns at relatively low output levels, decreasing returns at relatively high output levels, and constant returns at some range of output levels between those extremes.

7cc8788e5ef5.title: Returns to scale
7cc8788e5ef5.sentence: In mainstream microeconomics, the returns to scale faced by a firm are purely technologically imposed and are not influenced by economic decisions or by market conditions (i.e., conclusions about returns to scale are derived from the specific mathematical structure of the production function in isolation).

c2297ef95edc.title: Returns to scale
c2297ef95edc.sentence: Assuming that the factor costs are constant (that is, that the firm is a perfect competitor in all input markets) and the production function is homothetic, a firm experiencing constant returns will have constant long-run average costs, a firm experiencing decreasing returns will have increasing long-run average costs, and a firm experiencing increasing returns will have decreasing long-run average costs.

7746df55f5dc.title: Returns to scale
7746df55f5dc.sentence: and, for a > 1, there are increasing returns if b + c > 1, constant returns if b + c = 1, and decreasing returns if b + c < 1.

080a5549afb0.title: Carbon lock-in
080a5549afb0.sentence: > …industrial economies have been locked into fossil fuel-based energy systems through a process of technological and institutional co-evolution driven by path-dependent increasing returns to scale.

1d8847082d61.title: Monopolistic competition
1d8847082d61.sentence: Monopolistic competition is a type of imperfect competition such that there are many producers competing against each other but selling products that are differentiated from one another (e.g., branding, quality) and hence not perfect substitutes.

568e1e90876b.title: Monopolistic competition
568e1e90876b.sentence: Textbook examples of industries with market structures similar to monopolistic competition include restaurants, cereals, clothing, shoes, and service industries in large cities.

3d5c6938cdb3.title: Monopolistic competition
3d5c6938cdb3.sentence: MC companies sell products that have real or perceived non-price differences.

19b988ce35e9.title: Monopolistic competition
19b988ce35e9.sentence: The goods perform the same basic functions but have differences in qualities such as type, style, quality, reputation, appearance, and location that tend to distinguish them from each other.

bed197b71e0b.title: Marginal product
bed197b71e0b.sentence: In economics and in particular neoclassical economics, the marginal product or marginal physical productivity of an input (factor of production) is the change in output resulting from employing one more unit of a particular input (for instance, the change in output when a firm's labor is increased from five to six units), assuming that the quantities of other inputs are kept constant.

40f0517959e6.title: Cournot competition
40f0517959e6.sentence: Cournot competition is an economic model describing an oligopolistic market where firms simultaneously compete by choosing the quantity of goods to produce and sell in the market.

7d52ac25aaf7.title: Cournot competition

a978e962f835.title: Cournot competition

d273920c2cc8.title: Cournot competition

1b2b8cd530bd.title: Cournot competition

261440fd6ed1.title: Cournot competition

8f28f3426b4c.title: Cournot competition

12f898610a42.title: Cournot competition

d9dc6f3943d2.sentence: An isoquant (derived from quantity and the Greek word isos, ίσος, meaning "equal"), also known as iso-product curve or equal product curve in microeconomics, is a contour line drawn through the set of points at which the same quantity of output is produced while changing the quantities of two or more inputs.

543e14c7c889.title: Utilitarianism
543e14c7c889.section: Application to specific problems > Social choice
543e14c7c889.sentence: In social choice and operations research, the utilitarian rule (also called the max-sum rule) is a rule saying that, among all possible alternatives, society should pick the alternative which maximizes the sum of the utilities of all individuals in society.

cad54b090e17.title: Utilitarianism
cad54b090e17.section: Developments in the 20th century > Wealth maximization
cad54b090e17.sentence: Another 20th-century offshoot of utilitarian-style thinking, often labeled wealth maximization, has its economic roots in the "potential Pareto improvements" advanced by Nicholas Kaldor, John Hicks, and Tibor Scitovsky.

0044be2d191b.title: Utilitarianism
0044be2d191b.section: Developments in the 20th century > Wealth maximization
0044be2d191b.sentence: While traditional Pareto criteria require that no one be made worse off, wealth maximization—closely tied to the Kaldor–Hicks efficiency—permits changes that increase overall economic surplus even if some parties lose, so long as the winners could in principle compensate the losers.

647071acccfb.title: Utilitarianism
647071acccfb.sentence: A common objection to utilitarianism is the inability to quantify, compare, or measure happiness or well-being.

d0ca2cb882d1.title: Utilitarianism
d0ca2cb882d1.sentence: The objection that "utilitarianism does not take seriously the distinction between persons" came to prominence in 1971 with the publication of John Rawls' A Theory of Justice.

9e7e0a076ce3.title: Animal rights
9e7e0a076ce3.sentence: The two main philosophical approaches to animal ethics are utilitarian and rights-based.

51073420322e.title: Animal rights
51073420322e.sentence: The utilitarian philosopher most associated with animal rights is Peter Singer, professor of bioethics at Princeton University.

9d4bb7689209.title: Social welfare function
9d4bb7689209.sentence: In welfare economics and social choice theory, a social welfare function—also called a social ordering, ranking, utility, or choice function—is a function that ranks a set of social states by their desirability.

b01526fd06f4.title: Social welfare function
b01526fd06f4.sentence: Each person's preferences are combined in some way to determine which outcome is considered better by society as a whole.

2253929b2385.title: Social welfare function
2253929b2385.sentence: Social welfare functions are studied by economists as a way to identify socially optimal decisions, giving a procedure to rigorously define which of two outcomes should be considered better for society as a whole (e.g., to compare two different possible income distributions).

d0e0785291ab.title: Social welfare function
d0e0785291ab.sentence: However, a social welfare function is different in that it is a mapping of individual utility functions onto a single output, in a way that accounts for the judgments of everyone in a society.

ac191aaed516.title: Social welfare function
ac191aaed516.sentence: - Ordinal (or ranked voting) functions only use ordinal information; i.e., whether one choice is better than another.

6c66db8c1d25.title: Social welfare function
6c66db8c1d25.sentence: - Cardinal (or rated voting) functions also use cardinal information; i.e., how much better one choice is compared to another.

b04d05d38ce1.title: Social welfare function
b04d05d38ce1.sentence: In a 1938 article, Abram Bergson introduced the term social welfare function, with the intention "to state in precise form the value judgments required for the derivation of the conditions of maximum economic welfare." The function was real-valued and differentiable.

7595222b1073.title: Social welfare function
7595222b1073.sentence: But in (1935, ch VI), Lionel Robbins argued that how or how many utilities, as mental events, change relative to each other is not measurable by any empirical test, thus making them unfalsifiable.

57fdabe60aa3.title: Social welfare function
57fdabe60aa3.sentence: Arrow's impossibility theorem is a key result of social welfare functions, showing an important difference between social and consumer choice: whereas it is possible to construct a rational (non-self-contradictory) decision procedure for consumers based only on ordinal preferences, it is impossible to do the same in the social choice setting, making any such ordinal decision procedure a second-best.

323e6099f062.title: Social choice theory
323e6099f062.sentence: Social choice theory is a branch of welfare economics that seeks to extend the theory of rational choice to collective decision-making.

19f15584d572.title: Social choice theory
19f15584d572.sentence: Social choice studies the behavior of different mathematical procedures (social welfare functions) used to combine individual preferences into a coherent whole.

5551aa26af74.title: Social choice theory
5551aa26af74.sentence: It contrasts with political science in that social choice theory is a normative field that studies how a society can make good decisions, whereas political science is a descriptive field that observes how societies actually do make decisions.

e2fbe7809bf6.title: Social choice theory
e2fbe7809bf6.sentence: Real-world examples of social choice rules include constitutions and parliamentary procedures for voting on laws, as well as electoral systems; as such, the field is occasionally called voting theory.

44711c0a07bb.title: Social choice theory
44711c0a07bb.sentence: The earliest work on social choice theory comes from the writings of the Marquis de Condorcet, who formulated several key results including his jury theorem and his example showing the impossibility of majority rule.

44a22e46b20f.title: Social choice theory
44a22e46b20f.sentence: Kenneth Arrow's book Social Choice and Individual Values is often recognized as inaugurating the modern era of social choice theory.

6acb9151c638.title: Social choice theory
6acb9151c638.sentence: - Utilitarian rule – sometimes called the max-sum rule or Benthamite welfare – aims to maximize the sum of utilities.

4e4241d2c256.title: Social choice theory
4e4241d2c256.sentence: - Egalitarian rule – sometimes called the max-min rule or Rawlsian welfare – aims to maximize the smallest utility.

90e63b0eb1b3.title: Social choice theory
90e63b0eb1b3.sentence: Gibbard's theorem provides limitations on the ability of any voting rule to elicit honest preferences from voters, showing that no voting rule is strategyproof (i.e. does not depend on other voters' preferences) for elections with 3 or more outcomes.

31c5f29f3aca.title: Social choice theory
31c5f29f3aca.section: Key results > Amartya Sen's Collective Choice and Social Welfare
31c5f29f3aca.sentence: 19 years after Arrow's Social Choice and Individual Values was published, in 1970, Sen would publish Collective Choice and Social Welfare, which "expanded Arrow's original social choice framework".

ef7c776fd76a.title: Social choice theory
ef7c776fd76a.section: Key results > Amartya Sen's Collective Choice and Social Welfare
ef7c776fd76a.sentence: Whereas Arrow had penned his theorem with the assumption of ordinality, Sen introduced the assumption of cardinality, or interpersonal comparison, into the social-choice theory model.

d359ed6783f6.title: Social choice theory
d359ed6783f6.section: Key results > Amartya Sen's Collective Choice and Social Welfare
d359ed6783f6.sentence: Sen replaced utilitarian welfare economics' "individual utility" with the concept of "capability," which can be defined as a person's freedom of choice and economic mobility in a society.

74309473ef76.title: Social choice theory
74309473ef76.sentence: Later work has also considered approaches to legal compensation, fair division, variable populations, partial strategy-proofing of social-choice mechanisms, natural resources, capabilities and functionings approaches, and measures of welfare.

4f812ec93dd7.title: Market distortion
4f812ec93dd7.sentence: In neoclassical economics, a market distortion is any event in which a market reaches a market clearing price for an item that is substantially different from the price that a market would achieve while operating under conditions of perfect competition and state enforcement of legal contracts and the ownership of private property.

d81a45f3b2cb.title: Market distortion
d81a45f3b2cb.sentence: In other words, a distortion is "any departure from the ideal of perfect competition that therefore interferes with economic agents maximizing social welfare when they maximize their own".

5540d292c8ad.title: Market distortion
5540d292c8ad.sentence: More generally, a measure of distortion is the deviation between the market price of a good and its marginal social cost, that is, the difference between the marginal rate of substitution in consumption and the marginal rate of transformation in production.

f55a1a98f66a.title: Market distortion
f55a1a98f66a.sentence: Such a deviation may result from government regulation, monopoly tariffs and import quotas, which in theory may give rise to rent seeking.

1fcbf887b08e.title: Market distortion
1fcbf887b08e.sentence: Other sources of distortions are uncorrected externalities, different tax rates on goods or income, inflation, and incomplete information.

1476dc693f29.title: Market distortion
1476dc693f29.sentence: Each of these may lead to a net loss in social surplus.

8a17fb6d8f6d.title: Market distortion
8a17fb6d8f6d.sentence: A proportional wage-income tax, for instance, is distortionary, whereas a lump-sum tax is not.

86e16959d557.title: Market distortion
86e16959d557.sentence: In a competitive equilibrium, a proportional wage income tax discourages work.

365f64529924.title: Market distortion
365f64529924.sentence: They are often the response to market failures, i.e., circumstances that prevent perfect competition and achieving an optimal equilibrium in the market.

2ccc5391ff84.title: Emissions trading
2ccc5391ff84.sentence: These revenues might be used to improve the efficiency of overall climate policy, e.g., by funding energy efficiency programs (ACEEE 2019) or reductions in distortionary taxes (Fisher et al., 1996, p. 417).

efcdabe185ca.title: Distributive justice
efcdabe185ca.sentence: Distributive justice concerns the socially just allocation of resources, goods and opportunities in a society.

0f187a8b0fe7.title: Distributive justice
0f187a8b0fe7.sentence: It is concerned with how to allocate resources fairly among members of a society, taking into account factors such as wealth, income, and social status.

07c1c896fdff.title: Distributive justice
07c1c896fdff.sentence: Often contrasted with just process and formal equal opportunity, distributive justice concentrates on outcomes (substantive equality).

85e19eee80f4.title: Distributive justice
85e19eee80f4.sentence: Most contemporary theories of distributive justice rest on the precondition of material scarcity.

0fcff2f3e59f.title: Distributive justice
0fcff2f3e59f.section: Theories of distributive justice > Justice as fairness
0fcff2f3e59f.sentence: In his book A Theory of Justice, John Rawls outlines his famous theory about justice as fairness.

586e976d21b4.title: Distributive justice
586e976d21b4.sentence: Centred on individual utility and welfare, utilitarianism builds on the notion that any action which increases the overall welfare in society is good, and any action that decreases welfare is bad.

9e0cbecff0c2.title: Distributive justice
9e0cbecff0c2.sentence: Based on a fundamental notion of equal worth and moral status of human beings, egalitarianism is concerned with equal treatment of all citizens in both respect and in concern, and in relation to the state as well as one another.

0e98e1650e5c.title: Distributive justice
0e98e1650e5c.sentence: The slogan "From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs" refers to distributive justice in Marxism according to Karl Marx.

0527e0191c56.title: Distributive justice
0527e0191c56.sentence: Distributive justice in an environmental context is the equitable distribution of a society's technological and environmental risks, impacts, and benefits.

6864d27d5aed.title: Distributive justice
6864d27d5aed.sentence: Environmental burdens fall disproportionately upon the Global South, while benefits are primarily accrued to the Global North.

ab270eaee2d1.title: Climate justice
ab270eaee2d1.sentence: - distributive justice, which places the emphasis on who bears the costs of both climate change and the actions taken to address it.

72229e3cec54.title: Distributive justice
72229e3cec54.sentence: Within the context of Western liberal democracies in the post-WWII decades, Friedrich von Hayek was one of the most famous opposers of the idea of distributive justice.

64ff5570527d.title: Distributive justice
64ff5570527d.sentence: For him, social and distributive justice were meaningless and impossible to attain, on the grounds of being within a system where the outcomes are not determined deliberately by the people but contrarily spontaneity is the norm.

271aa977f610.title: Distributive justice
271aa977f610.sentence: In his book Anarchy, State, and Utopia he stresses how the term distributive justice is not a neutral one.

b341dd32e6f4.title: Distributive justice
b341dd32e6f4.sentence: In fact, there is no central distributor that can be regarded as such.

e06fef5076ae.title: Allocative efficiency
e06fef5076ae.sentence: Allocative efficiency is a state of the economy in which production is aligned with the preferences of consumers and producers; in particular, the set of outputs is chosen so as to maximize the social welfare of society.

32f52953c418.title: Allocative efficiency
32f52953c418.sentence: An allocatively efficient economy produces an "optimal mix" of commodities.

e6c351018a57.title: Allocative efficiency
e6c351018a57.sentence: This is achieved if every produced good or service has a marginal benefit equal to or greater than the marginal cost of production.

f5c0d3af33fc.title: Allocative efficiency
f5c0d3af33fc.sentence: A firm is allocatively efficient when its price is equal to its marginal costs (that is, P = MC) in a perfect market.

f1933b8aa570.title: Allocative efficiency
f1933b8aa570.sentence: Therefore, the market equilibrium, where demand meets supply, is also where the marginal social benefit equals the marginal social costs.

bac667e690ff.title: Allocative efficiency
bac667e690ff.sentence: At this point, the net social benefit is maximized, meaning this is the allocative efficient outcome.

84200dc64c93.title: Allocative efficiency
84200dc64c93.sentence: At this point the social surplus is maximized with no deadweight loss (the latter being the value society puts on that level of output produced minus the value of resources used to achieve that level).

c0a3c834f997.title: Allocative efficiency
c0a3c834f997.section: Examples > A numerical example of allocative efficiency
c0a3c834f997.sentence: From the graph we can see that at the output of 40, the marginal cost of good is $6 while the price that consumer is willing to pay is $15.

0246e10860dc.title: Allocative efficiency
0246e10860dc.section: Examples > A numerical example of allocative efficiency
0246e10860dc.sentence: The optimal level of the output is 70, where the marginal cost equals to marginal utility.

b2564cbc5991.title: Allocative efficiency
b2564cbc5991.section: Examples > A numerical example of allocative efficiency
b2564cbc5991.sentence: At the output of 40, this product or service is under-consumed by the society.

a53d535f506f.title: Allocative efficiency
a53d535f506f.section: Examples > An example of allocation inefficiency
a53d535f506f.sentence: The monopolies can set the price above the marginal cost of the production.

6f715408ad40.title: Allocative efficiency
6f715408ad40.section: Examples > An example of allocation inefficiency
6f715408ad40.sentence: It results in the dead weight welfare loss to the society as a whole.

30f4f36400aa.title: Allocative efficiency
30f4f36400aa.sentence: When a market fails to allocate resources efficiently, there is said to be market failure.

9365abf3fe75.title: Allocative efficiency
9365abf3fe75.sentence: Market failure may occur because of imperfect knowledge, differentiated goods, concentrated market power (e.g., monopoly or oligopoly), or externalities.

af9bc53df510.title: Allocative efficiency
af9bc53df510.sentence: It is possible to have Pareto efficiency without allocative efficiency: in such a situation, it is impossible to reallocate resources in such a way that someone gains and no one loses (hence we have Pareto efficiency), yet it would be possible to reallocate in such a way that gainers gain more than losers lose (hence with such a reallocation, we do not have allocative efficiency).

ab44e8f7e521.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
ab44e8f7e521.sentence: The first states that in economic equilibrium, a set of complete markets, with complete information, and in perfect competition, will be Pareto optimal (in the sense that no further exchange would make one person better off without making another worse off).

33b868f0546d.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
33b868f0546d.sentence: The second theorem states that any Pareto optimum can be supported as a competitive equilibrium for some initial set of endowments.

f5a4be6198d2.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
f5a4be6198d2.sentence: - Firms and consumers take prices as given (no economic actor or group of actors has market power).

6bfe68e54ae8.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
6bfe68e54ae8.sentence: The theorem is sometimes seen as an analytical confirmation of Adam Smith's "invisible hand" principle, namely that competitive markets ensure an efficient allocation of resources.

f709140755f4.title: Invisible hand
f709140755f4.sentence: Milton Friedman, a Nobel Memorial Prize winner in economics, called Smith's Invisible Hand "the possibility of cooperation without coercion." Kaushik Basu has called the First Welfare Theorem the Invisible Hand Theorem.

bcf5596d6476.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
bcf5596d6476.sentence: However, there is no guarantee that the Pareto optimal market outcome is equitative, as there are many possible Pareto efficient allocations of resources differing in their desirability (e.g. one person may own everything and everyone else nothing).

f04d344d3f84.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics

f04d344d3f84.sentence: The second fundamental theorem has more demanding conditions.

1292c9a4ee8e.sentence: - The preference relation ≥i is locally non-satiated and convex for each consumer i

3f272129c1d9.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
3f272129c1d9.section: Assumptions for the fundamental theorems > Second Fundamental Theorem
3f272129c1d9.sentence: - The production set Yj is convex for each firm j.

198202e29cb3.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
198202e29cb3.section: History of the fundamental theorems > Abram Bergson and Paul Samuelson (1947)
198202e29cb3.sentence: Samuelson (crediting Abram Bergson for the substance of his ideas) brought Lange's second welfare theorem to approximately its modern form.

65a5db6e7d20.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
65a5db6e7d20.section: History of the fundamental theorems > Abram Bergson and Paul Samuelson (1947)
65a5db6e7d20.sentence: He follows Lange in deriving a set of equations which are necessary for Pareto optimality, and then considers what additional constraints arise if the economy is required to satisfy a genuine social welfare function, finding a further set of equations from which it follows 'that all of the action necessary to achieve a given ethical desideratum may take the form of lump sum taxes or bounties'.

318e8568fae1.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
318e8568fae1.section: Assumptions for the fundamental theorems > Common failures of the assumptions
318e8568fae1.sentence: - Externalities: In many instances, prominently pollution & climate action, this assumption is violated.

5570d11b1580.section: Assumptions for the fundamental theorems > Common failures of the assumptions
5570d11b1580.sentence: In certain instances, a Pigouvian tax can restore the pareto-efficient allocation.

fdcbd4e5d2bf.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
fdcbd4e5d2bf.section: History of the fundamental theorems > Oscar Lange (1942)
fdcbd4e5d2bf.sentence: Lange's paper 'The Foundations of Welfare Economics' is the source of the now-traditional pairing of two theorems, one governing markets, the other distribution.

5f429733b650.title: Fundamental theorems of welfare economics
5f429733b650.sentence: The fundamental theorems do not generally ensure existence, nor uniqueness of the equilibria.

bbde970e6c8d.title: Distribution (economics)
bbde970e6c8d.sentence: In economics, distribution is the way total output, income, or wealth is distributed among individuals or among the factors of production (such as labour, land, and capital).

d177b4bf5976.title: Distribution (economics)
d177b4bf5976.sentence: Here, interest is often on the fraction of income going to the top (or bottom) x percent of households, the next x percent, and so forth (defined by equally spaced cut points, say quintiles), and on the factors that might affect them (globalization, tax policy, technology, etc.).

c726f10c95e8.title: Distribution (economics)
c726f10c95e8.sentence: Distribution has been central in the study of political economy since the 19th century, as shown in scholarship by Adam Smith, David Ricardo, and John Stuart Mill.

c77f04d47fdb.title: Distribution (economics)
c77f04d47fdb.section: Descriptive, theoretical, scientific, and welfare uses
c77f04d47fdb.sentence: In welfare economics, a level of feasible output possibilities is commonly distinguished from the distribution of income for those output possibilities.

f693eb7a4c70.title: Distribution (economics)
f693eb7a4c70.sentence: In neoclassical economics, the supply and demand of each factor of production interact in factor markets to determine equilibrium output, income, and the income distribution.

e853853f65e3.title: Distribution (economics)
e853853f65e3.sentence: Vilfredo Pareto proposed the distribution of income can be described by a power-law: this is now called the Pareto distribution.

ae65e22e605e.title: Ecological economics
ae65e22e605e.sentence: Resource and neoclassical economics focus primarily on the efficient allocation of resources and less on the two other problems of importance to ecological economics: distribution (equity), and the scale of the economy relative to the ecosystems upon which it relies.

d7bfc8282cee.title: Ecological economics
d7bfc8282cee.sentence: Drawing upon a transdisciplinary literature, ecological economics roots its policy work in monetary theory and its goals of sustainable scale, just distribution, and efficient allocation.

9b6d03c57021.title: Equity (economics)
9b6d03c57021.sentence: Economic equity is the construct, concept or idea of fairness in economics and justice in the distribution of wealth, resources, and taxation within a society.

282906ac0a1b.title: Equity (economics)
282906ac0a1b.sentence: Equity in economics refers to a condition of fairness where the economic processes and their outcomes do not unduly favor or disadvantage any particular group or individual.

a2dd9e50ff8e.title: Equity (economics)
a2dd9e50ff8e.sentence: Equity may be distinguished from economic efficiency in overall evaluation of social welfare.

0d9a50b36e07.title: Equity (economics)
0d9a50b36e07.sentence: Equity looks at the distribution of capital, goods, and access to services throughout an economy and is often measured using tools such as the Gini index.

875f4d7e2322.title: Equity (economics)
875f4d7e2322.sentence: Defining equity presents inherent challenges due to its subjective nature, which depends heavily on societal values and individual perceptions of what is considered fair.

47ba43c5bc15.title: Equity (economics)
47ba43c5bc15.sentence: Public finance in theory and practice highlights this difficulty: "Economists find it difficult to formulate an acceptable definition of distributional equity because it would require interpersonal comparisons of utility." In practice, it may prove impossible to equalise choices without seriously impeding social objectives in other areas, such as the attainment of efficiency or the preservation of liberty.

4ed3dce7c238.title: Equity (economics)
4ed3dce7c238.sentence: According to Peter Corning, there are three distinct categories of substantive fairness (equality, equity, and reciprocity) that must be combined and balanced in order to achieve a truly fair society.

fc127ec5dcc5.title: Equity (economics)
fc127ec5dcc5.sentence: It has been studied in experimental economics as inequity aversion.

415ffd3d42b6.title: Flexible mechanisms
415ffd3d42b6.sentence: The basic economic argument in favour of flexibility was that, in principle at least, issues to do with fairness ("equity" in the language of economics) could be separated from efficiency (i.e., reducing emissions most cheaply).

63f9b01265fa.title: Flexible mechanisms
63f9b01265fa.sentence: From this viewpoint, flexibility through emissions trading could promote efficiency, while arguments of equity could be partially addressed through, for example, the allocations of emissions rights between different countries.

aee8b4b15940.title: Productive efficiency
aee8b4b15940.sentence: In microeconomic theory, productive efficiency (or production efficiency) is a situation in which the economy or an economic system (e.g., bank, hospital, industry, country) operating within the constraints of current industrial technology cannot increase production of one good without sacrificing production of another good.

342ad7155099.title: Productive efficiency
342ad7155099.sentence: In simple terms, the concept is illustrated on a production possibility frontier (PPF), where all points on the curve are points of productive efficiency.

81bb448a73b7.title: Productive efficiency
81bb448a73b7.sentence: Productive inefficiency, with the economy operating below its production possibilities frontier, can occur because the productive inputs physical capital and labor are underutilized—that is, some capital or labor is left sitting idle—or because these inputs are allocated in inappropriate combinations to the different industries that use them.

58c43da723b2.title: Productive efficiency
58c43da723b2.sentence: In long-run equilibrium for perfectly competitive markets, productive efficiency occurs at the base of the average total cost curve — i.e. where marginal cost equals average total cost — for each good.

bcf466e32ad1.title: Productive efficiency
bcf466e32ad1.sentence: An equilibrium may be productively efficient without being allocatively efficient — i.e. it may result in a distribution of goods where social welfare is not maximized (bearing in mind that social welfare is a nebulous objective function subject to political controversy).

09223515c850.title: Productive efficiency
09223515c850.sentence: Productive efficiency is an aspect of economic efficiency that focuses on how to maximize output of a chosen product portfolio, without concern for whether your product portfolio is making goods in the right proportion; in misguided application, it will aid in manufacturing the wrong basket of outputs faster and cheaper than ever before.

3e1df6f72911.title: Productive efficiency
3e1df6f72911.sentence: Due to the nature and culture of monopolistic companies, they may not be productively efficient because of X-inefficiency, whereby companies operating in a monopoly have less of an incentive to maximize output due to lack of competition.

bff1e27cddfa.title: Productive efficiency
bff1e27cddfa.sentence: However, due to economies of scale it can be possible for the profit-maximizing level of output of monopolistic companies to occur with a lower price to the consumer than perfectly competitive companies.

32cd1d90db7b.title: Productive efficiency
32cd1d90db7b.sentence: By improving these processes, an economy or business can extend its production possibility frontier outward, so that efficient production yields more output than previously.

f62d01d022f6.title: Productive efficiency
f62d01d022f6.sentence: The most popular for estimating production efficiency are data envelopment analysis and stochastic frontier analysis.

446d2f906921.title: Kaldor–Hicks efficiency
446d2f906921.sentence: A re-allocation is a Kaldor–Hicks improvement if those that are made better off could hypothetically compensate those that are made worse off and lead to a Pareto-improving outcome.

618ac52f4ccf.title: Kaldor–Hicks efficiency
618ac52f4ccf.sentence: The compensation does not actually have to occur (there is no presumption in favor of status-quo) and thus, a Kaldor–Hicks improvement can in fact leave some people worse off.

ce2e7ae69166.title: Kaldor–Hicks efficiency
ce2e7ae69166.sentence: A Kaldor–Hicks improvement is an economic re-allocation of resources among people that captures some of the intuitive appeal of a Pareto improvement, but has less stringent criteria and is hence applicable to more circumstances.

b1a8a39d03fe.title: Kaldor–Hicks efficiency
b1a8a39d03fe.sentence: However, in practice, it is almost impossible to take any social action, such as a change in economic policy, without making at least one person worse off.

5912be0c62b0.title: Kaldor–Hicks efficiency
5912be0c62b0.sentence: While every Pareto improvement is a Kaldor–Hicks improvement, most Kaldor–Hicks improvements are not Pareto improvements.

ecd1475ae3a0.title: Kaldor–Hicks efficiency
ecd1475ae3a0.sentence: For example, a voluntary exchange that creates pollution would be a Kaldor–Hicks improvement if the buyers and sellers are still willing to carry out the transaction even if they have the intention to fully compensate the victims of the pollution(which is unlikely to occur).

825097dd49be.title: Kaldor–Hicks efficiency
825097dd49be.sentence: The Kaldor criterion holds that an activity moves the economy closer to Pareto optimality if the maximum amount the gainers are prepared to pay to the losers to agree to the change is greater than the minimum amount losers are prepared to accept.

0900a2a57207.title: Kaldor–Hicks efficiency
0900a2a57207.sentence: John Hicks claims that adherence to the criterion moves the economy toward Pareto optimality if the maximum amount the losers would pay the gainers to forgo the change is less than the minimum amount the gainers would accept to so agree.

c426748d0d18.title: Arrow's impossibility theorem

bef84bf5264e.title: Arrow's impossibility theorem

36513f2331f5.title: Theory of the second best
36513f2331f5.sentence: In welfare economics, the theory of the second best concerns the situation when one or more optimality conditions cannot be satisfied.

ae3ec57f0c21.title: Theory of the second best
ae3ec57f0c21.sentence: The economists Richard Lipsey and Kelvin Lancaster showed in 1956 that if one optimality condition in an economic model cannot be satisfied, it is possible that the next-best solution involves changing other variables away from the values that would otherwise be optimal.

c4471528cfb0.title: Theory of the second best
c4471528cfb0.sentence: Politically, the theory implies that if it is infeasible to remove a particular market distortion, introducing one or more additional market distortions in an interdependent market may partially counteract the first, and lead to a more efficient outcome.

358b0dc6d46e.title: Theory of the second best
358b0dc6d46e.sentence: In an economy with some uncorrectable market failure in one sector, actions to correct market failures in another related sector with the intent of increasing economic efficiency may actually decrease overall economic efficiency.

a324029d074d.title: Theory of the second best
a324029d074d.sentence: A common misinterpretation of the theory, sometimes termed the fallacy of exhaustive effort, is the assumption that when one optimality condition cannot be satisfied, satisfying as many of the remaining conditions as possible must yield the second-best outcome.

60c9b7580e99.title: Theory of the second best
60c9b7580e99.sentence: The theory of the second best demonstrates the opposite: because optimality conditions are typically derived from an interdependent system, perturbing one condition alters the marginal trade-offs throughout the entire system, so the second-best optimum generally requires violating all remaining conditions as well.

0a582db4e82c.title: Theory of the second best
0a582db4e82c.sentence: In practice, the error arises when policymakers treat the individual conditions for a first-best outcome as separately desirable goals—for example, liberalising trade while ignoring an environmental externality because "free trade is good," or deregulating markets while assuming away imperfect information because "competition is good." Each such prescription satisfies one condition from the first-best list, but without the others in place, it can reduce welfare relative to doing nothing at all.

11d0316df9af.sentence: According to the compensation principle, if the prospective gainers could compensate (any) prospective losers and leave no one worse off, the alternate state is to be selected.
