d7fc0dc9d3b5.title: GDP deflator
d7fc0dc9d3b5.sentence: In economics, the GDP deflator (implicit price deflator) is a measure of the money price of all new, domestically produced, final goods and services in an economy in a year relative to the real value of them.

ea369d4c01f0.title: GDP deflator
ea369d4c01f0.sentence: The formula implies that dividing the nominal GDP by the real GDP and multiplying it by 100 will give the GDP Deflator, hence "deflating" the nominal GDP into a real measure.

07912e1ced0e.title: GDP deflator
07912e1ced0e.sentence: Like the consumer price index (CPI), the GDP deflator is a measure of price inflation/deflation with respect to a specific base year; the GDP deflator of the base year itself is equal to 100.

f2f8bfd47a58.title: GDP deflator
f2f8bfd47a58.sentence: Unlike the CPI, the GDP deflator is not based on a fixed basket of goods and services; the "basket" for the GDP deflator is allowed to change from year to year with people's consumption and investment patterns.

5750073a1b31.title: GDP deflator
5750073a1b31.sentence: A price deflator of 200 means that the current-year price of this computing power is twice its base-year price - price inflation.

ee940f9650f9.title: GDP deflator
ee940f9650f9.sentence: A price deflator of 50 means that the current-year price is half the base year price - price deflation.

2efa4c791963.title: GDP deflator
2efa4c791963.sentence: In practice, the difference between the deflator and a price index like the Consumer price index (CPI) is often relatively small.

3f9a29c01e54.title: GDP deflator
3f9a29c01e54.sentence: On the other hand, with governments in developed countries increasingly utilizing price indexes for everything from fiscal and monetary planning to payments to social program recipients, even small differences between inflation measures can shift budget revenues and expenses by millions or billions of dollars.

702026320a42.title: Macroeconomics
702026320a42.section: Macroeconomic models > Specific models > AD-AS model
702026320a42.sentence: The AD–AS model is a common textbook model for explaining the macroeconomy.

2d5a7c2b21fc.title: Macroeconomics
2d5a7c2b21fc.section: Macroeconomic models > Specific models > AD-AS model
2d5a7c2b21fc.sentence: The original version of the model shows the price level and level of real output given the equilibrium in aggregate demand and aggregate supply.

0839a2458f0f.title: Macroeconomics
0839a2458f0f.section: Macroeconomic models > Specific models > AD-AS model
0839a2458f0f.sentence: The aggregate demand curve's downward slope means that more output is demanded at lower price levels.

901742ed0cd1.title: Macroeconomics
901742ed0cd1.section: Macroeconomic models > Specific models > AD-AS model
901742ed0cd1.sentence: In many representations of the AD–AS model, the aggregate supply curve is horizontal at low levels of output; it becomes inelastic near the point of potential output, which corresponds with full employment.

b3b6d512b3e0.title: Macroeconomics
b3b6d512b3e0.section: Macroeconomic models > Specific models > AD-AS model
b3b6d512b3e0.sentence: Since the economy cannot produce beyond the potential output, any AD expansion will lead to higher price levels instead of higher output.

412e6d89a6bb.title: Macroeconomics
412e6d89a6bb.section: Macroeconomic models > Specific models > AD-AS model
412e6d89a6bb.sentence: In modern textbooks, the AD–AS model is often presented slightly differently, however, in a diagram showing not the price level, but the inflation rate along the vertical axis, making it easier to relate the diagram to real-world policy discussions.

81932012031d.title: Macroeconomics
81932012031d.section: Macroeconomic models > Specific models > AD-AS model
81932012031d.sentence: The AS curve is upward-sloping, consistent with a standard modern Phillips curve view, in which higher economic activity lowers unemployment, leading to higher wage growth and, in turn, higher inflation.

54a51992316a.title: Macroeconomics
54a51992316a.sentence: In the 1980s and 1990s, endogenous growth theory arose to challenge the neoclassical growth theory of Ramsey and Solow.

f6847ae2c496.title: Macroeconomics
f6847ae2c496.sentence: This group of models explains economic growth through factors such as increasing returns to scale in capital and learning-by-doing that are endogenously determined, rather than the exogenous technological improvement used to explain growth in Solow's model.

c4c0544544c3.title: Macroeconomics
c4c0544544c3.sentence: Another type of endogenous growth model endogenizes technological progress by explicitly modelling research and development activities of profit-maximizing firms.

21c8aa245e58.title: Endogenous growth theory
21c8aa245e58.sentence: In the mid-1980s, a group of growth theorists became increasingly dissatisfied with common accounts of exogenous factors determining long-run growth, such as the Solow–Swan model.

bc429325d7ea.title: Endogenous growth theory
bc429325d7ea.sentence: They favored a model that replaced the exogenous growth variable (unexplained technical progress) with a model in which the key determinants of growth were explicit in the model.

58b453006bce.title: Endogenous growth theory
58b453006bce.sentence: The endogenous growth theory primarily holds that the long run growth rate of an economy depends on policy measures.

42bec89954b9.title: Endogenous growth theory
42bec89954b9.sentence: For example, subsidies for research and development or education increase the growth rate in some endogenous growth models by increasing the incentive for innovation.

6e5462ebcfa5.title: Endogenous growth theory
6e5462ebcfa5.sentence: The theory also focuses on positive externalities and spillover effects of a knowledge-based economy which will lead to economic development.

e93d5d2fb46d.title: Endogenous growth theory
e93d5d2fb46d.sentence: Paul Romer (1986), Robert Lucas (1988), Sergio Rebelo (1991) and Ortigueira and Santos (1997) omitted technological change; instead, growth in these models is due to indefinite investment in human capital which had a spillover effect on the economy and reduces the diminishing return to capital accumulation.

f54c060bc259.title: Macroeconomics
f54c060bc259.section: Basic concepts > Measuring the supply of money
f54c060bc259.sentence: Two common ways of determining the total money supply in an economy are M1 and M2.

515fe5e92634.title: Macroeconomics
515fe5e92634.section: Basic concepts > Measuring the supply of money
515fe5e92634.sentence: M1 is money that is liquid.

bfabf8d2abf5.title: Macroeconomics
bfabf8d2abf5.section: Basic concepts > Measuring the supply of money
bfabf8d2abf5.sentence: This obviously includes cash, coins, checking account deposits, and similar items.

c55d25d8b19a.title: Macroeconomics
c55d25d8b19a.section: Basic concepts > Measuring the supply of money
c55d25d8b19a.sentence: M2, however, includes time deposits, saving accounts, and money market mutual funds, which are not as liquid, in its measurement.

3965baf8ba77.title: Macroeconomics
3965baf8ba77.section: Basic concepts > Measuring the supply of money
3965baf8ba77.sentence: Liquid refers to a financial asset that can be quickly converted into cash without significant loss of value.

f597d4e336d4.title: Macroeconomics
f597d4e336d4.section: Basic concepts > Measuring the supply of money
f597d4e336d4.sentence: It is important to understand the money supply, as it affects interest rates and plays a central role in monetary policy.

b77a80c66247.title: Monetary policy
b77a80c66247.sentence: Monetary policy is the policy adopted by the monetary authority of a nation to affect monetary and other financial conditions to accomplish broader objectives like high employment and price stability (normally interpreted as a low and stable rate of inflation).

2a999169b171.title: Monetary policy
2a999169b171.sentence: Interest-rate targeting is generally the primary tool, being obtained either directly via administratively changing the central bank's own interest rates or indirectly via open market operations.

6ce8c3320bb5.title: Macroeconomics
6ce8c3320bb5.sentence: Via the monetary transmission mechanism, interest rate changes affect investment, consumption, asset prices like listed companies' shares prices and house prices, and through exchange rate reactions export and import.

df4ba63ba10a.title: Macroeconomics
df4ba63ba10a.sentence: In this way, aggregate demand, employment, and ultimately inflation are affected.

736539531988.title: Monetary policy
736539531988.sentence: Monetary policy is often referred to as being either expansionary (lowering rates, stimulating economic activity and consequently employment and inflation) or contractionary (dampening economic activity, hence decreasing employment and inflation).

027ae8e965ab.title: Monetary policy
027ae8e965ab.sentence: Today most central banks in developed countries conduct their monetary policy within an inflation targeting framework, whereas the monetary policies of most developing countries' central banks target some kind of a fixed exchange rate system.

111514c7eccd.title: Monetary policy
111514c7eccd.sentence: Monetary policy affects the economy through financial channels like interest rates, exchange rates and prices of financial assets.

763fb9455d73.title: Monetary policy
763fb9455d73.sentence: This is in contrast to fiscal policy, which relies on changes in taxation and government spending as methods for a government to manage business cycle phenomena such as recessions.

e8b46c708ef9.title: Monetary policy
e8b46c708ef9.sentence: In developed countries, monetary policy is generally formed separately from fiscal policy, modern central banks in developed economies being independent of direct government control and directives.

a60763042768.title: Macroeconomics
a60763042768.sentence: When nominal interest rates are near zero, central banks cannot loosen monetary policy through conventional means.

f1a2526b784d.title: Macroeconomics
f1a2526b784d.sentence: In that situation, they may use unconventional monetary policy such as quantitative easing to help stabilize output.

fe6a6c72e95a.title: Macroeconomics
fe6a6c72e95a.sentence: The division into various time frames of macroeconomic research leads to a parallel division of macroeconomic policies into short-run policies aimed at mitigating the harmful consequences of business cycles (known as stabilization policy) and medium- and long-run policies targeted at improving the structural levels of macroeconomic variables.

99bd6ae11a50.title: Macroeconomics
99bd6ae11a50.sentence: Stabilization policy is usually implemented through two sets of tools: fiscal and monetary policy.

7b2f6e0fe551.title: Macroeconomics
7b2f6e0fe551.sentence: Both forms of policy are used to stabilize the economy, i.e. limiting the effects of the business cycle by conducting expansive policy when the economy is in a recession or contractive policy in the case of overheating.

2dab6c23b3d1.title: Macroeconomics
2dab6c23b3d1.sentence: Structural policies may include labour market policies that aim to change the structural unemployment rate, or policies that affect long-run propensities to save, invest, or engage in education, research, and development.

529e94b4fa04.title: Macroeconomics
529e94b4fa04.section: Macroeconomic policy > Comparison of fiscal and monetary policy
529e94b4fa04.sentence: Economists usually favor monetary over fiscal policy to mitigate moderate fluctuations, however, because it has two major advantages.

b7d88d9a21a2.title: Macroeconomics
b7d88d9a21a2.section: Macroeconomic policy > Comparison of fiscal and monetary policy
b7d88d9a21a2.sentence: Independent central banks are less likely to be subject to political pressure to pursue overly expansionary policies.

f9dcf1e2fa10.title: Macroeconomics
f9dcf1e2fa10.section: Macroeconomic policy > Comparison of fiscal and monetary policy
f9dcf1e2fa10.sentence: Second, monetary policy may suffer shorter inside lags and outside lags than fiscal policy.

5455f418566d.title: Macroeconomics
5455f418566d.section: Macroeconomic policy > Comparison of fiscal and monetary policy
5455f418566d.sentence: There are some exceptions, however: Firstly, in the case of a major shock, monetary stabilization policy may not be sufficient and should be supplemented by active fiscal stabilization.

5f88e9ace0df.title: Macroeconomics
5f88e9ace0df.section: Macroeconomic policy > Comparison of fiscal and monetary policy
5f88e9ace0df.sentence: Secondly, in the case of a very low interest level, the economy may be in a liquidity trap in which monetary policy becomes ineffective, which makes fiscal policy the more potent tool to stabilize the economy.

5ddf56ca0bf0.title: Macroeconomics
5ddf56ca0bf0.section: Macroeconomic policy > Comparison of fiscal and monetary policy
5ddf56ca0bf0.sentence: Thirdly, in regimes where monetary policy is tied to fulfilling other targets, in particular fixed exchange rate regimes, the central bank cannot simultaneously adjust its interest rates to mitigate domestic business cycle fluctuations, making fiscal policy the only usable tool for such countries.

e4056e0a8cb4.title: Macroeconomics
e4056e0a8cb4.sentence: Some fiscal policy is implemented through automatic stabilizers without any active decisions by politicians.

4760c5af5ee1.title: Macroeconomics
4760c5af5ee1.sentence: Automatic stabilizers use conventional fiscal mechanisms, but take effect as soon as the economy takes a downturn: spending on unemployment benefits automatically increases when unemployment rises, and tax revenue decreases, which shelters private income and consumption from part of the fall in market income.

6e1d2a00667a.title: Macroeconomics
6e1d2a00667a.sentence: Automatic stabilizers do not suffer from the policy lags of discretionary fiscal policy.

589acbb74107.title: Monetary policy
589acbb74107.section: History > Central banks and the gold standard
589acbb74107.sentence: With the creation of the Bank of England in 1694, which was granted the authority to print notes backed by gold, the idea of monetary policy as independent of executive action [how?] began to be established.

004382f078cb.title: Monetary policy
004382f078cb.section: History > Central banks and the gold standard
004382f078cb.sentence: By this time the role of the central bank as the "lender of last resort" was established.

da8fbe25531b.title: Monetary policy
da8fbe25531b.section: History > Central banks and the gold standard
da8fbe25531b.sentence: To accomplish this end, central banks as part of the gold standard began setting the interest rates that they charged both their own borrowers and other banks which required money for liquidity.

777986cf123d.title: Monetary policy
777986cf123d.section: History > Central banks and the gold standard
777986cf123d.sentence: During the period 1870–1920, the industrialized nations established central banking systems, with one of the last being the Federal Reserve in 1913.

546f23ed96ae.title: Monetary policy
546f23ed96ae.sentence: There is very strong consensus among economists that an independent central bank can run a more credible monetary policy, making market expectations more responsive to signals from the central bank.

95a82ee69bcd.title: Monetary policy
95a82ee69bcd.section: Monetary policy instruments > Open market operations
95a82ee69bcd.sentence: Through open market operations, a central bank may influence the level of interest rates, the exchange rate and/or the money supply in an economy.

566bfd918c17.title: Monetary policy
566bfd918c17.section: Monetary policy instruments > Open market operations
566bfd918c17.sentence: Each time a central bank buys securities (such as a government bond or treasury bill), it in effect creates money.

5aeb418fee56.title: Monetary policy
5aeb418fee56.section: Monetary policy instruments > Open market operations
5aeb418fee56.sentence: The central bank exchanges money for the security, increasing the monetary base while lowering the supply of the specific security.

3715bb02be3f.title: Monetary policy
3715bb02be3f.section: Monetary policy instruments > Open market operations
3715bb02be3f.sentence: Conversely, selling of securities by the central bank reduces the monetary base.

d808f5b50fea.title: Monetary policy
d808f5b50fea.section: Monetary policy instruments > Open market operations
d808f5b50fea.sentence: Open market operations can influence interest rates by expanding or contracting the monetary base, which consists of currency in circulation and banks' reserves on deposit at the central bank.

dae0bda767da.title: Monetary policy
dae0bda767da.section: Monetary policy instruments > Unconventional monetary policy at the zero bound
dae0bda767da.sentence: Other forms of monetary policy, particularly used when interest rates are at or near 0% and there are concerns about deflation or deflation is occurring, are referred to as unconventional monetary policy.

e04984e20de2.title: Macroeconomics
e04984e20de2.sentence: Quantity easing can be implemented by buying not only government bonds, but also other assets such as corporate bonds, stocks, and other securities.

504984cec333.title: Macroeconomics
504984cec333.sentence: This allows lower interest rates for a broader class of assets beyond government bonds.

b57538971c8c.title: Monetary policy
b57538971c8c.section: Monetary policy instruments > Unconventional monetary policy at the zero bound
b57538971c8c.sentence: These include credit easing, quantitative easing, forward guidance, and signalling.

13f4238e939d.title: Macroeconomics
13f4238e939d.sentence: Conventional monetary policy can be ineffective in situations such as a liquidity trap.

9730f4788007.title: Monetary policy
9730f4788007.sentence: Since 2017-2018, a growing number of central banks have started to consider the effects of climate change on their operational frameworks for monetary policy and supervisory policies.

40828744f01d.title: Monetary policy
40828744f01d.sentence: In the continuation to a famous speech by former Bank of England governor Mark Carney in September 2015, central bank have justified this work by the fact that climate change will likely generate more volatility in certain markets, some inflationary pressure either due to climate shocks and extreme weather events and linked with an overly slow and disordered transition, and generate climate-related financial risks on the financial sector.

f3e6dd8e4f5d.title: Monetary policy
f3e6dd8e4f5d.sentence: This work was spearheaded by the foundation of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) in 2017 by the Bank of England, Banque de France and the Dutch central bank.

f129a33346de.title: Monetary policy
f129a33346de.sentence: The NGFS is composed of more than a hundred central banks and financial supervisors.

cbcdee5747f7.title: Monetary policy
cbcdee5747f7.sentence: Proposals for climate-related adjustments to central bank policies range from green macro-prudential rules, green quantitative easing, green collateral framework rules and green refinancing operations.

a6cf9d94f6d4.title: Monetary policy
a6cf9d94f6d4.sentence: In 2021, the European Central Bank has announced that it will "tilt" its corporate bond purchases (effectively implementing a form of Green QE) and look at ways to incorporate climate factors in its collateral framework.

6b0fbbe97dfa.title: Monetary policy
6b0fbbe97dfa.sentence: The ECB has however refrained so far from implementing a "green interest rate".

f4733f6ac24b.title: National accounts
f4733f6ac24b.sentence: Generational accounting is a method for measuring redistribution of lifetime tax burdens across generations from social insurance, including social security and social health insurance.

5e6b87aa78b6.title: National accounts
5e6b87aa78b6.sentence: It has been proposed as a better guide to the sustainability of a fiscal policy than budget deficits, which reflect only taxes minus spending in the current year.

292a2f20e89f.title: Fiscal policy
292a2f20e89f.sentence: The three stances of fiscal policy are the following:

0c2355b9ac8c.title: Fiscal policy
0c2355b9ac8c.sentence: - Neutral fiscal policy is usually undertaken when an economy is in neither a recession nor an expansion.

7df90cc35295.title: Fiscal policy
7df90cc35295.sentence: The amount of government deficit spending (the excess not financed by tax revenue) is roughly the same as it has been on average over time, so no changes to it are occurring that would have an effect on the level of economic activity.

faa8dc20d6e6.title: Fiscal policy
faa8dc20d6e6.sentence: It involves government spending exceeding tax revenue by more than it has tended to, and is usually undertaken during recessions.

753514e01c73.title: Fiscal policy
753514e01c73.sentence: Examples of expansionary fiscal policy measures include increased government spending on public works (e.g., building schools) and providing the residents of the economy with tax cuts to increase their purchasing power (in order to fix a decrease in the demand).

e7d71d8c7221.title: Fiscal policy
e7d71d8c7221.sentence: - Contractionary fiscal policy, on the other hand, is a measure to increase tax rates and decrease government spending.

c4245820f4e4.title: Fiscal policy
c4245820f4e4.sentence: This has the potential to slow economic growth if inflation, which was caused by a significant increase in aggregate demand and the supply of money, is excessive.

2dafb252813f.title: Fiscal policy
2dafb252813f.sentence: However, these definitions can be misleading because, even with no changes in spending or tax laws at all, cyclic fluctuations of the economy cause cyclic fluctuations of tax revenues and of some types of government spending, altering the deficit situation; these are not considered to be policy changes.

db91bb78b409.title: Fiscal policy
db91bb78b409.sentence: Therefore, for purposes of the above definitions, "government spending" and "tax revenue" are normally replaced by "cyclically adjusted government spending" and "cyclically adjusted tax revenue".

f1bc5c0175db.title: Fiscal policy
f1bc5c0175db.sentence: Since the 1970s, it became clear that monetary policy performance has some benefits over fiscal policy due to the fact that it reduces political influence, as it is set by the central bank (to have an expanding economy before the general election, politicians might cut the interest rates).

5ea233db626e.title: Fiscal policy
5ea233db626e.sentence: Monetary policy is generally quicker to implement as interest rates can be set every month, while the decision to increase government spending might take time to figure out which area the money should be spent on.

c2e436c0a180.title: Fiscal policy
c2e436c0a180.sentence: A liquidity trap occurs when interest rate cuts are insufficient as a demand booster as banks do not want to lend and the consumers are reluctant to increase spending due to negative expectations for the economy.

970c542d816e.title: Fiscal policy
970c542d816e.sentence: When a deep recession takes place, it is not sufficient to rely just on monetary policy to restore the economic equilibrium.

151c6f84744a.title: Fiscal policy
151c6f84744a.sentence: Government spending is responsible for creating the demand in the economy and can provide a kick-start to get the economy out of the recession.

a68f4a21b482.title: Fiscal policy
a68f4a21b482.sentence: These policies have limited effects; however, fiscal policy seems to have a greater effect over the long-run period, while monetary policy tends to have a short-run success.

2f441e8a6fda.title: System of National Accounts
2f441e8a6fda.section: The SNA framework > Satellite accounts and supplementary tables
2f441e8a6fda.sentence: Each of the SNA core accounts can be complemented with annexes providing extra details, sub-accounts with more detailed breakdowns of data, satellite accounts linked to the core accounts, and supplementary tables (or account variants) providing additional information.

7d58067ef317.title: System of National Accounts
7d58067ef317.sentence: Chapter XXI of the 1993 SNA manual gave attention to the design of separate environmental-economic accounts as a way to extend analytical capacity, without altering the core SNA accounts.

90e4f9dfc95a.title: System of National Accounts
90e4f9dfc95a.section: The SNA framework > Satellite accounts and supplementary tables
90e4f9dfc95a.sentence: The non-core accounts are in principle always optional (there are some exceptions to this norm in the European Union).

4f8404adc69b.title: System of National Accounts
4f8404adc69b.section: The SNA framework > Satellite accounts and supplementary tables
4f8404adc69b.sentence: NSO's produce them, if there is a need or demand for such accounts, and if there is a budget to produce the accounts.

f56bf2b3d598.title: System of National Accounts
f56bf2b3d598.sentence: - SNA 2008 formally recognized satellite accounts for environmental-economic topics (including material flow accounts, emission and pollution accounts, and energy accounts) and encouraged the use of the parallel System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) for detailed environmental accounting.

3e2eda45d40e.title: Purchasing power parity
3e2eda45d40e.section: Calculating PPP factors > Simplified > Big Mac Index
3e2eda45d40e.sentence: The Big Mac Index is a simple implementation of PPP where the basket contains a single good: a Big Mac burger from McDonald's restaurants.

15fa5339d115.title: Purchasing power parity
15fa5339d115.section: Calculating PPP factors > Simplified > Big Mac Index
15fa5339d115.sentence: The index was created and popularized by The Economist in 1986 as a way to teach economics and to identify over- and under-valued currencies.

bc1bf46ee380.title: Purchasing power parity
bc1bf46ee380.section: Calculating PPP factors > Simplified > Big Mac Index
bc1bf46ee380.sentence: A Big Mac is perishable and not easily transported.

a778bd92a3dd.title: Purchasing power parity
a778bd92a3dd.section: Calculating PPP factors > Simplified > Big Mac Index
a778bd92a3dd.sentence: That means the law of one price is not likely to keep prices the same in different locations.

db93300dab01.title: Purchasing power parity
db93300dab01.section: Calculating PPP factors > Simplified > Big Mac Index
db93300dab01.sentence: In the white paper, "Burgernomics", the authors computed a correlation of 0.73 between the Big Mac Index's prices and prices calculated using the Penn World Tables.

69deb2a7b083.title: National accounts
69deb2a7b083.sentence: One use of economic-growth data from the national accounts is in growth accounting across longer periods of time for a country or across to estimate different sources of growth, whether from growth of factor inputs or technological change.

d42ffd86f893.title: Productivity
d42ffd86f893.sentence: When multiple inputs are considered, the measure is called multi-factor productivity or MFP and is typically estimated using growth accounting.

69e9235b8c49.title: Total factor productivity
69e9235b8c49.sentence: Therefore, some economists believe that the method and its results are invalid or need to be carefully interpreted and used along with other alternative approaches.

5b0e34f5963d.title: Consumption (economics)
5b0e34f5963d.sentence: Consumption refers to the use of resources to fulfill present needs and desires.

e012424d2afb.title: Consumption (economics)
e012424d2afb.sentence: It is seen in contrast to investing, which is spending for the acquisition of future income.

fe86b135880d.title: Consumption (economics)
fe86b135880d.sentence: According to mainstream economists, only the final purchase of newly produced goods and services by individuals for immediate use constitutes consumption, while other types of expenditure – in particular, fixed investment, intermediate consumption, and government spending – are placed in separate categories (see consumer choice).

8d452c34567d.title: Consumption (economics)
8d452c34567d.sentence: In most countries consumption is the most important part of GDP.

d3f4aaa4198e.title: Consumption (economics)
d3f4aaa4198e.sentence: It usually ranges from 45% from GDP to 85% of GDP.

79676b0aabc8.title: Consumption (economics)
79676b0aabc8.sentence: Where consumption is equal to income minus savings.

3aac7e3348f4.title: Consumption (economics)
3aac7e3348f4.sentence: Income: Economists consider the income level to be the most crucial factor affecting consumption.

8b1227bf394c.title: Consumption (economics)
8b1227bf394c.sentence: In microeconomics, consumer choice is a theory that assumes that people are rational consumers and they decide on what combinations of goods to buy based on their utility function (which goods provide them with more use/happiness) and their budget constraint (which combinations of goods they can afford to buy).

0b65241d0a8c.title: Consumption (economics)
0b65241d0a8c.sentence: Consumers try to maximize utility while staying within the limits of their budget constrain or to minimize cost while getting the target level of utility.

0be43d3c51df.title: Consumption (economics)
0be43d3c51df.sentence: Aggregate consumption is a component of aggregate demand.

fff61311739f.title: Income
fff61311739f.sentence: Income is the consumption and saving opportunity gained by an entity within a specified timeframe, which is generally expressed in monetary terms.

6d76b4208ae8.title: Income
6d76b4208ae8.sentence: Income is difficult to define conceptually and the definition may be different across fields.

073232b4e728.title: Income
073232b4e728.sentence: For example, a person's income in an economic sense may be different from their income as defined by law.

bbab98e2cb51.title: Income
bbab98e2cb51.sentence: For households and individuals in the United States, income is defined by tax law as a sum that includes any wage, salary, profit, interest payment, rent, or other form of earnings received in a calendar year.

5c62cafc654d.title: Income
5c62cafc654d.sentence: For a firm, gross income can be defined as sum of all revenue minus the cost of goods sold.

545884f6b388.title: Income
545884f6b388.sentence: Borrowing or repaying money is not income under any definition, for either the borrower or the lender.

2682902b1a41.title: Game theory
2682902b1a41.sentence: Game theory is the field of applied mathematics that models interactions between multiple agents as "games" of strategy between "players".

5102a5626b22.title: Game theory
5102a5626b22.sentence: It is a scientific method of describing, predicting, evaluating, and selecting choices (or "actions"), often with the view of maximizing utility outcomes (or "payoffs") for one or more players.

aee2c7bcec81.title: Game theory
aee2c7bcec81.sentence: In game theory, a "game" is an abstract, mathematical representation of an interaction between agents ("players"), meant to capture the most basic properties of the game, namely:

564c2b34ac37.title: Game theory
564c2b34ac37.sentence: - the choices or actions available to each player;

898a2fece40a.title: Game theory
898a2fece40a.sentence: A game is cooperative if players are able to form binding commitments externally enforced (e.g. through contract law).

a734477885a9.title: Game theory
a734477885a9.sentence: A game is non-cooperative if players cannot form alliances or if all agreements need to be self-enforcing (e.g. through credible threats).

c9b97295256f.title: Game theory
c9b97295256f.sentence: Players in game theory are generally assumed to be rational agents in a formal, mathematical sense.

f2a1ec890be1.title: Game theory
f2a1ec890be1.sentence: Rational agents act as if they have consistent preferences and unlimited computational capacity to achieve their well-defined objectives, and they behave in a manner in order to obtain the maximum possible payoff.

46e3b84b30c9.title: Game theory
46e3b84b30c9.sentence: In other words, an act profile is a Nash equilibrium if each player is playing a best response to the joint play of the others, such that no player could have improved her payoff by changing her act while all others kept theirs the same.

66761fde8575.title: Game theory
66761fde8575.sentence: Game theory as a field had its genesis in the 1944 book Theory of Games and Economic Behavior, written by mathematicians John von Neumann and Oskar Morgenstern.

f0618369a09f.title: Game theory
f0618369a09f.sentence: In 1994, the Nobel Prize in economics was awarded to the mathematician John Nash, the economist John Harsanyi, and the economist Reinhard Selten for their pioneering work in game theory.

0140913680aa.title: Game theory
0140913680aa.sentence: Game theory is a major method used in mathematical economics and business for modeling competing behaviors of interacting agents.

d43022597fa6.title: Game theory
d43022597fa6.sentence: Game theory has applications in the natural, formal and social sciences, including biology, computer science, economics, law, logic, political science, systems science, and philosophy.

f0731506cc71.title: Game theory
f0731506cc71.sentence: Since the decision to take a vaccine for a particular disease is often made by individuals, who may consider a range of factors and parameters in making this decision (such as the incidence and prevalence of the disease, perceived and real risks associated with contracting the disease, mortality rate, perceived and real risks associated with vaccination, and financial cost of vaccination), game theory has been used to model and predict vaccination uptake in a society.

8551848cc218.title: Homo economicus
8551848cc218.sentence: The term Homo economicus, or economic man, is the portrayal of humans as agents who are consistently rational and narrowly self-interested, and who pursue their subjectively defined ends optimally.

44df5faca4de.title: Homo economicus
44df5faca4de.sentence: It assumes that agents always act in a way that maximize utility as a consumer and profit as a producer, and are capable of arbitrarily complex deductions towards that end.

b74f11fedfcf.title: Homo economicus
b74f11fedfcf.sentence: They will always be capable of thinking through all possible outcomes and choosing that course of action which will result in the best possible result.

53c6a5c74e3e.title: Homo economicus
53c6a5c74e3e.sentence: That is, the individual seeks to attain very specific and predetermined goals to the greatest extent with the least possible cost.

64f93624555c.title: Homo economicus
64f93624555c.sentence: Note that this kind of "rationality" does not say that the individual's actual goals are "rational" in some larger ethical, social, or human sense, only that they try to attain them at minimal cost.

a48c35665df6.title: Homo economicus
a48c35665df6.sentence: The term "economic man" was used for the first time in the late nineteenth century by critics of John Stuart Mill's work on political economy.

20b6df7082f0.title: Homo economicus
20b6df7082f0.sentence: > It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker that we expect our dinner, but from their regard to their own interest.

12aac4210331.title: Homo economicus
12aac4210331.sentence: As a theory on human conduct, it contrasts to the concepts of behavioral economics, which examines cognitive biases and other irrationalities, and to bounded rationality, which assumes that practical elements such as cognitive and time limitations restrict the rationality of agents.

5c8693260872.title: Homo economicus
5c8693260872.sentence: The rationality implied in Homo economicus does not restrict what sort of preferences are admissible.

2c115adf83c2.title: Homo economicus
2c115adf83c2.sentence: For example, an agent's utility function could be linked to the perceived utility of other agents (such as one's husband or children), making Homo economicus compatible with other models such as Homo reciprocans, which emphasizes human cooperation.

f2a06b7034fd.title: Homo economicus
f2a06b7034fd.sentence: In advanced-level theoretical economics, scholars have modified models to more realistically depict real-life decision-making.

34861bc2bb25.title: Homo economicus
34861bc2bb25.sentence: For example, models of individual behavior under bounded rationality and of people suffering from envy can be found in the literature.

618c143abd1f.title: Bounded rationality
618c143abd1f.sentence: Bounded rationality is the idea that rationality is limited when individuals make decisions, and under these limitations, rational individuals will select a decision that is satisfactory rather than optimal.

b9d8c945c6ed.title: Bounded rationality
b9d8c945c6ed.sentence: Limitations include the difficulty of the problem requiring a decision, the cognitive capability of the mind, and the time available to make the decision.

5dfa035e376b.title: Bounded rationality
5dfa035e376b.sentence: Decision-makers, in this view, act as satisficers, seeking a satisfactory solution, with everything that they have at the moment rather than an optimal solution.

12415ecbd05e.title: Bounded rationality
12415ecbd05e.sentence: Therefore, humans do not undertake a full cost-benefit analysis to determine the optimal decision, but rather, choose an option that fulfills their adequacy criteria.

aecf05509279.title: Bounded rationality
aecf05509279.sentence: Bounded rationality was coined by Herbert A. Simon, where it was proposed as an alternative basis for the mathematical and neoclassical economic modelling of decision-making, as used in economics, political science, and related disciplines.

f416cece2577.title: Bounded rationality
f416cece2577.sentence: Simon used the analogy of a pair of scissors, where one blade represents "cognitive limitations" of actual humans and the other the "structures of the environment", illustrating how minds compensate for limited resources by exploiting known structural regularity in the environment.

205f3baa40ea.title: Bounded rationality
205f3baa40ea.sentence: Simon suggests that economic agents use heuristics to make decisions rather than a strict rigid rule of optimization.

c6aaabc6bea5.title: Bounded rationality
c6aaabc6bea5.sentence: They do this because of the complexity of the situation.

0e0b101a19af.title: Bounded rationality
0e0b101a19af.sentence: Gigerenzer proposes and shows that simple heuristics often lead to better decisions than theoretically optimal procedures.

497692d3f391.title: Bounded rationality
497692d3f391.sentence: The connection between nudging and bounded rationality lies in the fact that nudges are designed to help people overcome the cognitive limitations and biases that arise from their bounded rationality.

48955c5c6213.title: Bounded rationality
48955c5c6213.sentence: The collaborative works of Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky expand upon Herbert A. Simon's ideas in the attempt to create a map of bounded rationality.

06b80778163a.title: Bounded rationality
06b80778163a.sentence: Three major topics covered by the works of Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky include heuristics of judgement, risky choice, and framing effect, which were a culmination of research that fit under what was defined by Herbert A. Simon as the psychology of bounded rationality.

cd2971129537.title: Behavioral economics
cd2971129537.sentence: Behavioral economics is the study of the psychological (e.g. cognitive, behavioral, affective, social) factors involved in the decisions of individuals or institutions, and how these decisions deviate from those implied by traditional economic theory.

46259142a4e1.title: Behavioral economics
46259142a4e1.sentence: Behavioral economics is primarily concerned with the bounds of rationality of economic agents.

c311930f2c5e.title: Behavioral economics
c311930f2c5e.sentence: Behavioral economics aims to improve or overhaul traditional economic theory by studying failures in its assumptions that people are rational and selfish.

c0176d9d2e5b.title: Behavioral economics
c0176d9d2e5b.sentence: Specifically, it studies the biases, tendencies and heuristics of people's economic decisions.

d843f47cdf32.title: Behavioral economics
d843f47cdf32.sentence: It aids in determining whether people make good choices and whether they could be helped to make better choices.

9b79fa10576c.title: Behavioral economics
9b79fa10576c.sentence: Behavioral models typically integrate insights from psychology, neuroscience and microeconomic theory.

f8b562f9e842.title: Behavioral economics
f8b562f9e842.sentence: Behavioral economics began as a distinct field of study in the 1970s and 1980s, but can be traced back to 18th-century economists, such as Adam Smith, who deliberated how the economic behavior of individuals could be influenced by their desires.

242b3586c727.title: Behavioral economics
242b3586c727.sentence: In The Theory of Moral Sentiments, Adam Smith wrote on concepts later popularized by modern Behavioral Economic theory, such as loss aversion.

a4f00d66b5cf.title: Behavioral economics
a4f00d66b5cf.sentence: A rejection and elimination of psychology from economics in the early 1900s brought on a period defined by a reliance on empiricism.

d1701ba936ed.title: Behavioral economics
d1701ba936ed.sentence: Economists instead conceptualized humans as purely rational and self-interested decision makers, illustrated in the concept of homo economicus.

eace3327a8fe.title: Behavioral economics
eace3327a8fe.sentence: The quantitative study found that there was a significant spread in behavioral economics after Kahneman and Tversky's work in the 1990s and into the 2000s.

75a1349ab0dc.title: Behavioral economics
75a1349ab0dc.section: Honors and awards > Nobel Prize > 1978 – Herbert Simon
75a1349ab0dc.sentence: In 1978 Herbert Simon was awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences "for his pioneering research into the decision-making process within economic organizations".

ee0e60919c4e.title: Behavioral economics

ee0e60919c4e.sentence: In 2002, psychologist Daniel Kahneman and economist Vernon L. Smith were awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.

a738bd6b0712.title: Behavioral economics
a738bd6b0712.section: Honors and awards > Nobel Prize > 2017 – Richard Thaler
a738bd6b0712.sentence: In 2017, economist Richard Thaler was awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for "his contributions to behavioral economics and his pioneering work in establishing that people are predictably irrational in ways that defy economic theory." Thaler was especially recognized for presenting inconsistencies in standard Economic theory and for his formulation of mental accounting and Libertarian paternalism

3448d99a0be6.title: Prisoner's dilemma
3448d99a0be6.sentence: In game theory, the prisoner's dilemma is a thought experiment involving two rational agents, each of whom can either cooperate for mutual benefit or betray their partner ("defect") for individual gain.

86420ad58db9.title: Prisoner's dilemma
86420ad58db9.sentence: The dilemma arises from the fact that while defecting is rational for each agent, cooperation yields a higher payoff for each.

73001743a41d.title: Prisoner's dilemma
73001743a41d.sentence: The puzzle was designed by Merrill Flood and Melvin Dresher in 1950 during their work at the RAND Corporation.

46f863aeaf83.title: Collective action problem
46f863aeaf83.sentence: The prisoner's dilemma is a simple game that serves as the basis for research on social dilemmas.

6cbc2c4d043f.title: Collective action problem
6cbc2c4d043f.sentence: The prisoner's dilemma model, one of the most famous examples in game theory, is crucial to understanding the collective problem because it illustrates the consequences of individual interests that conflict with the interests of the group.

f0657346aceb.title: Prisoner's dilemma
f0657346aceb.sentence: In environmental studies, the dilemma is evident in crises such as global climate change.

17d4dde4f715.title: Prisoner's dilemma
17d4dde4f715.sentence: It is argued all countries will benefit from a stable climate, but any single country is often hesitant to curb CO2 emissions.

5baa2bc0f5d2.title: Prisoner's dilemma
5baa2bc0f5d2.sentence: An important difference between climate-change politics and the prisoner's dilemma is uncertainty; the extent and pace at which pollution can change climate is not known.

c1813217e76a.title: Prisoner's dilemma
c1813217e76a.sentence: This difference suggests that states will cooperate much less than in a real iterated prisoner's dilemma, so that the probability of avoiding a possible climate catastrophe is much smaller than that suggested by a game-theoretical analysis of the situation using a real iterated prisoner's dilemma.

d54523a9d613.title: Prisoner's dilemma
d54523a9d613.sentence: Although metaphorical, Garrett Hardin's tragedy of the commons may be viewed as an example of a multi-player generalization of the prisoner's dilemma: each villager makes a choice for personal gain or restraint.

e058c80df517.title: Prisoner's dilemma
e058c80df517.sentence: The collective reward for unanimous or frequent defection is very low payoffs and the destruction of the commons.

30a712b82bce.title: Prisoner's dilemma
30a712b82bce.sentence: The prisoner's dilemma has been called the E. coli of social psychology, and it has been used widely to research various topics such as oligopolistic competition and collective action to produce a collective good.

26a39817169f.title: Behavioral economics
26a39817169f.sentence: Experimental economics is the application of experimental methods, including statistical, econometric, and computational, to study economic questions.

d5bed81f478c.title: Behavioral economics
d5bed81f478c.sentence: Data collected in experiments are used to estimate effect size, test the validity of economic theories, and illuminate market mechanisms.

ad72f3733a93.title: Behavioral economics
ad72f3733a93.sentence: Economic experiments usually use cash to motivate subjects, in order to mimic real-world incentives.

fd0ed16726f1.title: Behavioral economics
fd0ed16726f1.section: Honors and awards > Nobel Prize > 2002 – Daniel Kahneman and Vernon L. Smith
fd0ed16726f1.sentence: Kahneman was awarded the prize "for having integrated insights from psychological research into economic science, especially concerning human judgment and decision-making under uncertainty", while Smith was awarded the prize "for having established laboratory experiments as a tool in empirical economic analysis, especially in the study of alternative market mechanisms."

6486b0ead50d.title: Behavioral economics
6486b0ead50d.sentence: Some economists see a fundamental schism between experimental economics and behavioral economics, but prominent behavioral and experimental economists tend to share techniques and approaches in answering common questions.

d626d064a3bf.title: Social norm
d626d064a3bf.sentence: A social norm or norm is a shared standard of acceptable behavior by a group.

69e3c7ccef4b.title: Social norm
69e3c7ccef4b.sentence: Social norms can both be informal understandings that govern the behavior of members of a society, as well as be codified into rules and laws.

59ce57a0fa08.title: Social norm
59ce57a0fa08.sentence: Institutions are composed of multiple norms.

cb76c6bb042f.title: Social norm
cb76c6bb042f.sentence: Norms are shared social beliefs about behavior; thus, they are distinct from "ideas", "attitudes", and "values", which can be held privately, and which do not necessarily concern behavior.

c4e5c40d418e.title: Social norm
c4e5c40d418e.sentence: Norms are contingent on context, social group, and historical circumstances.

d2126fc79281.title: Social norm
d2126fc79281.sentence: Some stable and self-reinforcing norms may emerge spontaneously without conscious human design.

a8c71fe9d127.title: Social norm
a8c71fe9d127.sentence: Peyton Young goes as far as to say that "norms typically evolve without top-down direction...through interactions of individuals rather than by design." Norms may develop informally, emerging gradually as a result of repeated use of discretionary stimuli to control behavior.

bc76f5b107ec.title: Social norm
bc76f5b107ec.sentence: These informal norms, if broken, may not invite formal legal punishments or sanctions, but instead encourage reprimands, warnings, or othering; incest, for example, is generally thought of as wrong in society, but many jurisdictions do not legally prohibit it.

2df560e6815e.title: Social norm
2df560e6815e.sentence: Deviance is defined as "nonconformity to a set of norms that are accepted by a significant number of people in a community or society" More simply put, if group members do not follow a norm, they become tagged as a deviant.

f64d6a38d8d5.title: Social norm
f64d6a38d8d5.sentence: Those who do not conform with social norms are considered "deviants." The life cycle of a norm occurs in three stages: (1) Norm emergence – norm entrepreneurs seek to persuade others of the desirability and appropriateness of certain behaviors; (2) Norm cascade – when a norm obtains broad acceptance; and (3) Norm internalization – when a norm acquires a "taken-for-granted" quality.

8ddf91219350.title: Social norm
8ddf91219350.sentence: A norm gives a person a rule of thumb for how they should behave.

257633e57391.title: Social norm
257633e57391.sentence: However, a rational person acts according to the rule only if it is beneficial for them.

c606969a6a21.title: Social norm
c606969a6a21.sentence: Another general formal framework that can be used to represent the essential elements of the social situation surrounding a norm is the repeated game of game theory.

abec8ef49043.title: Free-rider problem
abec8ef49043.sentence: However, the impact of social norms on privately- and voluntarily-provided public goods is considered to have some level of effect on free-riding in many contexts.

f16364c987f1.title: Free-rider problem
f16364c987f1.sentence: The impact of social norms on actions and motivations related to altruism are often underestimated in economic solutions and the models from which they are derived.

4c8dcb636f1b.title: Collective action problem
4c8dcb636f1b.sentence: A collective action problem or social dilemma is a situation in which all individuals would be better off cooperating but fail to do so because of conflicting interests between individuals that discourage joint action.

c2b8730ab9ea.title: Collective action problem
c2b8730ab9ea.sentence: Problems arise when too many group members choose to pursue individual profit and immediate satisfaction rather than behave in the group's best long-term interests.

7845f4a1d76e.title: Collective action problem
7845f4a1d76e.sentence: Examples of phenomena that can be explained using social dilemmas include resource depletion and low voter turnout.

877176eecf50.title: Collective action problem
877176eecf50.sentence: Environmental problems such as climate change, biodiversity loss, and waste accumulation can be described as collective action problems.

1b6caf7a263b.title: Collective action problem
1b6caf7a263b.sentence: Without governmental regulation, however, individual people or businesses are unlikely to take the actions necessary to reduce carbon emissions or cut back on usage of non-renewable resources, as these people and businesses are incentivized to choose the easier and cheaper option, which often differs from the environmentally-friendly option that would benefit the health of the planet.

f2a58d91333c.title: Collective action problem
f2a58d91333c.sentence: The most prominent modern interpretation of the collective action problem can be found in Mancur Olson's 1965 book The Logic of Collective Action.

06fb7745399b.title: Collective action problem
06fb7745399b.sentence: Olson argued that individual rationality does not necessarily result in group rationality, as members of a group may have conflicting interests that do not represent the best interests of the overall group.

43bd372e493a.title: Collective action problem
43bd372e493a.sentence: Olson further argued that in the case of a pure public good that is both nonrival and nonexcludable, one contributor tends to reduce their contribution to the public good as others contribute more.

bd4544ce8eeb.title: Collective action problem
bd4544ce8eeb.sentence: The collective action problem can be understood through the analysis of game theory and the free-rider problem, which results from the provision of public goods.

a69d5e3ac34d.title: Collective action problem
a69d5e3ac34d.sentence: David Hume provided another early and better-known interpretation of what is now called the collective action problem in his 1738 book A Treatise of Human Nature.

b336c166597e.title: Collective action problem
b336c166597e.sentence: Hume characterizes a collective action problem through his depiction of neighbors agreeing to drain a meadow:

25fe3ad00e8b.title: Collective action problem
25fe3ad00e8b.sentence: The collective action problem has been addressed in political philosophy for centuries, but was more famously interpreted in 1965 in Mancur Olson's The Logic of Collective Action.

656482a1dc2e.title: Heuristic (psychology)
656482a1dc2e.sentence: Heuristics (from Ancient Greek εὑρίσκω (heurískō) 'to find, discover') is the process by which humans use mental shortcuts to arrive at decisions.

b52fef1cb20a.title: Heuristic (psychology)
b52fef1cb20a.sentence: Heuristics are simple strategies that humans, animals, organizations, and even machines use to quickly form judgments, make decisions, and find solutions to complex problems.

c0d511f4fb6d.title: Heuristic (psychology)
c0d511f4fb6d.sentence: While heuristic processes are used to find the answers and solutions that are most likely to work or be correct, they are not always right or the most accurate.

f23d57541efc.title: Heuristic (psychology)
f23d57541efc.sentence: Judgments and decisions based on heuristics are simply good enough to satisfy a pressing need in situations of uncertainty, where information is incomplete.

fca6c10d8be6.title: Heuristic (psychology)
fca6c10d8be6.sentence: In that sense they can differ from answers given by logic and probability.

229c3f92f99f.title: Heuristic (psychology)
229c3f92f99f.sentence: The economist and cognitive psychologist Herbert A. Simon introduced the concept of heuristics in the 1950s, suggesting there were limitations to rational decision making.

57dcca41bb4e.title: Heuristic (psychology)
57dcca41bb4e.sentence: Herbert A. Simon formulated one of the first models of heuristics, known as satisficing.

b1f1a39743aa.title: Heuristic (psychology)
b1f1a39743aa.sentence: In the 1970s, psychologists Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman added to the field with their research on cognitive bias.

d1ebb00be2d9.title: Construal level theory
d1ebb00be2d9.sentence: Construal level theory (CLT) is a theory in social psychology that describes the relation between psychological distance and the extent to which people's thinking (e.g., about objects and events) is abstract or concrete.

e9270a33f9f3.title: Construal level theory
e9270a33f9f3.sentence: The core idea of CLT is that the more distant an object is from the individual, the more abstract it will be thought of, while the closer the object is, the more concretely it will be thought of.

edb8a200d100.title: Construal level theory

12ce48b61dfe.title: Construal level theory

827d0f3440c7.title: Prospect theory
827d0f3440c7.sentence: Prospect theory is a theory of behavioral economics, judgment and decision making that was developed by Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky in 1979.

9f02d56b2f37.title: Prospect theory
9f02d56b2f37.sentence: Thus, contrary to the expected utility theory (which models the decision that perfectly rational agents would make), prospect theory aims to describe the actual behavior of people.

067fb6800462.title: Prospect theory
067fb6800462.sentence: It centers on the idea that people evaluate the utility of gains and losses relative to a certain "neutral" reference point regarding their current individual situation.

a41bbfb46520.title: Prospect theory
a41bbfb46520.sentence: Thus, rather than rationally maximizing a fixed expected utility, value decisions are made relative to the current neutral situation and not following any absolute measure of utility.

7f8fcc2f97bd.title: Prospect theory
7f8fcc2f97bd.sentence: Prospect theory stems from loss aversion, the observation that agents asymmetrically feel losses more acutely than equivalent gains.

f515d9465dc6.title: Prospect theory

388d9df77597.title: Prospect theory

aa61134c8b17.title: Prospect theory

368be85351fc.sentence: In psychology and behavioral economics, the endowment effect, also known as divestiture aversion, is the finding that people are more likely to retain an object they own than acquire that same object when they do not own it.

b04e85873ddc.title: Endowment effect

c4d0dca37710.title: Endowment effect

1bbd680acf4b.title: Endowment effect
1bbd680acf4b.sentence: The term endowment effect however was first explicitly coined in 1980 by the economist Richard Thaler in reference to the under-weighting of opportunity costs as well as the inertia introduced into a consumer's choice processes when goods included in their endowment become more highly valued than goods that are not.

c52b8038ede0.title: Status quo bias
c52b8038ede0.sentence: A status quo bias, or default bias is a cognitive bias that results from a preference for the maintenance of one's existing state of affairs.

2a82825d5485.title: Status quo bias
2a82825d5485.sentence: The current baseline (or status quo) is taken as a reference point, and any change from that baseline is perceived as a loss or gain.

d0ad4c164bcb.title: Status quo bias

e191ffc26e7e.title: Status quo bias
e191ffc26e7e.sentence: An individual weighs the potential losses of switching from the status quo more heavily than the potential gains; this is due to the prospect theory value function being steeper in the loss domain.

f998c6443a7d.title: Strategic dominance
f998c6443a7d.sentence: In game theory, a strategy A dominates another strategy B if A will always produce a better result than B, regardless of how any other player plays.

310a5fe43ca0.title: Strategic dominance
310a5fe43ca0.sentence: - B strictly dominates (>) A: choosing B always gives a better outcome than choosing A, no matter what the other players do.

3d9abd133476.title: Strategic dominance
3d9abd133476.sentence: - B weakly dominates (≥) A: choosing B always gives at least as good an outcome as choosing A, no matter what the other players do, and there is at least one set of opponents' actions for which B gives a better outcome than A. (Notice that if B strictly dominates A, then B weakly dominates A. Therefore, we can say "B dominates A" to mean "B weakly dominates A".)

c9c86a37f7db.title: Strategic dominance
c9c86a37f7db.sentence: - Strategy B is strictly dominant if strategy B strictly dominates every other possible strategy.

6bc182e41db2.title: Chicken (game)

97bdb2731b4f.title: Chicken (game)
97bdb2731b4f.sentence: The principle of the game is that while the ideal outcome is for one player to yield (to avoid the worst outcome if neither yields), individuals try to avoid it out of pride, not wanting to look like "chickens".

363504756fb4.title: Chicken (game)
363504756fb4.sentence: The name "chicken" has its origins in a game in which two drivers drive toward each other on a collision course: one must swerve, or both may die in the crash, but if one driver swerves and the other does not, the one who swerved will be called a "chicken", meaning a coward; this terminology is most prevalent in political science and economics.

c15d1b15510c.title: Chicken (game)

7b447818c268.title: Coordination game

40e8b04f98f1.title: Coordination game

79634753ae03.title: Coordination game
79634753ae03.sentence: A typical case for a coordination game is choosing the sides of the road upon which to drive, a social standard which can save lives if it is widely adhered to.

cd5f0116415b.title: Stag hunt
cd5f0116415b.sentence: In game theory, the stag hunt (also referred to as the assurance game, trust dilemma or common interest game) describes a situation or game where participants would be better off cooperating to achieve a more ambitious goal (hunting a stag together, which succeeds), but can choose a safer option (hunting a hare on one's own) that protects them from a bad outcome (hunting a stag alone, which fails, while the other hunts a hare).

1a25ecb56cd9.title: Stag hunt

15fe0c180b33.title: Stag hunt

3dfdf75c9867.title: Stag hunt
3dfdf75c9867.sentence: One hunter can catch a hare alone with less effort and less time, but it is worth far less than a stag and has much less meat.

e387d09dc5d1.title: Stag hunt
e387d09dc5d1.sentence: Formally, a stag hunt is a game with two pure strategy Nash equilibria, that is, stable attractors where an individual player cannot improve their position with a different strategy if the other players' strategy remains constant—one that is risk dominant (hunting hares individually) and another that is payoff dominant (hunting a stag together).

dbf7dd55561a.title: Stag hunt
dbf7dd55561a.sentence: The stag hunt differs from the prisoner's dilemma in that in the stag hunt there are two pure-strategy Nash equilibria: one where both players cooperate, and one where both players defect.

880fc53b6f31.title: Stag hunt

ce6df2966477.title: Extensive-form game
ce6df2966477.sentence: In game theory, an extensive-form game is a specification of a game allowing for the explicit representation of a number of key aspects, like the sequencing of players' possible moves, their choices at every decision point, the (possibly imperfect) information each player has about the other player's moves when they make a decision, and their payoffs for all possible game outcomes.

ca2874dde21f.title: Extensive-form game
ca2874dde21f.sentence: Extensive-form representations differ from normal-form in that they provide a more complete description of the game in question, whereas normal-form simply boils down the game into a payoff matrix.

adf3a9a1d4c6.title: Game theory

f0adb77c5a84.title: Extensive-form game

0ca303578182.title: Extensive-form game
0ca303578182.sentence: A play is thus a path through the tree from the root to a terminal node.

beb11eb62ce0.title: Extensive-form game

9e522f439725.title: Extensive-form game

9e25c85829c6.title: Extensive-form game

b939d9a5540c.sentence: Like "Chicken", the "War of attrition" game models escalation of conflict, but they differ in the form in which the conflict can escalate.

9e07f2519fdf.title: Chicken (game)
9e07f2519fdf.section: Related strategies and games > War of attrition
9e07f2519fdf.sentence: War of attrition models a situation in which the outcomes differ only in degrees, such as a boxing match in which the contestants have to decide whether the ultimate prize of victory is worth the ongoing cost of deteriorating health and stamina.

4c77d684ccba.title: Chicken (game)

4c77d684ccba.sentence: Chicken models a situation in which the catastrophic outcome differs in kind from the agreeable outcome, e.g., if the conflict is over life and death.

a08039b8d161.title: Chicken (game)

a08039b8d161.sentence: The war of attrition is another very influential model of aggression in biology.

4959f1aecee4.title: Chicken (game)

4959f1aecee4.sentence: The war of attrition seeks to answer the question of how contests may be resolved when there is no possibility of physical combat.

f0360b3ce452.title: Zero-sum game
f0360b3ce452.sentence: In situation where one decision maker's gain (or loss) does not necessarily result in the other decision makers' loss (or gain), they are referred to as non-zero-sum.

ef913e20ba0b.title: Zero-sum game
ef913e20ba0b.sentence: Other non-zero-sum games are games in which the sum of gains and losses by the players is sometimes more or less than what they began with.

9ec1c7525ef7.title: Zero-sum game
9ec1c7525ef7.sentence: In contrast, positive-sum or win–win games describe a situation in which the interacting parties' aggregate gains and losses can be more than zero.

144bca7ed25b.title: Zero-sum game
144bca7ed25b.sentence: Thus, a country with an excess of bananas trading with another country for their excess of apples, where both benefit from the transaction, is in a non-zero-sum situation.

21dca3704ffb.title: Zero-sum game

37f4c878823b.title: Zero-sum game
37f4c878823b.sentence: While some political strategies have been called zero sum, politics and macroeconomics in general do not have to be zero-sum due to cooperation, synergy and economic growth.

8da5b89e51d2.title: Zero-sum game

d296388ad93d.title: Zero-sum game
d296388ad93d.sentence: Zero-sum thinking is captured by the saying "your gain is my loss" (or conversely, "your loss is my gain").

61e4efe8c3c3.title: Zero-sum game

6d58bc67ef03.title: Zero-sum game

57564cd8d7c5.title: Zero-sum game

4cd5bad5e8e0.title: Zero-sum game

49149cd9656d.title: Zero-sum game

97fe3742e0b3.title: Coordination game

2fd5f3798b3a.title: Coordination game

8035a5b88626.sentence: A hybrid form of coordination and anti-coordination is the discoordination game, where one player's incentive is to coordinate while the other player tries to avoid this.

e293f0789c79.title: Coordination game

e7d435597d2b.title: Coordination game
e7d435597d2b.sentence: When academics talk about coordination failure, most cases are that subjects achieve risk dominance rather than payoff dominance.

c71e96a6d6d9.title: Coordination game

9a43cdeb0feb.title: Coordination game
9a43cdeb0feb.sentence: Players are more likely to fail to coordinate on a riskier option when the difference between taking the risk or the safe option is smaller.

e4edb7c6b521.title: Coordination game

7bf191671d3c.title: Coordination game

69e9641094a5.title: Coordination game

da63dd60ce6f.title: Coordination game

9529c2bc3a29.title: Coordination game

6398edfb6d63.title: Coordination game
6398edfb6d63.sentence: Sometimes these refinements conflict, which makes certain coordination games especially complicated and interesting (e.g. the Stag hunt, in which {Stag,Stag} has higher payoffs, but {Hare,Hare} is safer).

0cdf043a63a0.title: Coordination game
0cdf043a63a0.sentence: In social sciences, a voluntary standard (when characterized also as de facto standard) is a typical solution to a coordination problem.

23940d9de0a6.title: Coordination game
23940d9de0a6.sentence: The choice of a voluntary standard tends to be stable in situations in which all parties can realize mutual gains, but only by making mutually consistent decisions.

b93f72622d92.title: Coordination game
b93f72622d92.sentence: In contrast, an obligation standard (enforced by law as "de jure standard") is a solution to the prisoner's problem.

b9c06ae01bd2.title: Repeated game
b9c06ae01bd2.sentence: A finitely repeated game is a game in which the same one-shot stage game is played repeatedly over a number of discrete time periods, or rounds.

866b65ea61db.title: Repeated game
866b65ea61db.sentence: A player's final payoff is the sum of their payoffs from each round.

cebda6abf94a.title: Repeated game
cebda6abf94a.sentence: For those repeated games with a fixed and known number of time periods, if the stage game has a unique Nash equilibrium, then the repeated game has a unique subgame perfect Nash equilibrium strategy profile of playing the stage game equilibrium in each round.

86a39ae3b348.title: Repeated game
86a39ae3b348.sentence: The unique stage game Nash equilibrium must be played in the last round regardless of what happened in earlier rounds.

ab44b5a9b978.title: Repeated game
ab44b5a9b978.sentence: Knowing this, players have no incentive to deviate from the unique stage game Nash equilibrium in the second-to-last round, and so on this logic is applied back to the first round of the game.

9a651393c7c3.title: Repeated game

9a651393c7c3.sentence: To interpret: this result means that the very presence of a known, finite time horizon sabotages cooperation in every single round of the game.

618c9ed5c434.title: Repeated game

618c9ed5c434.sentence: Cooperation in iterated games is only possible when the number of rounds is infinite or unknown.

94af06444594.title: Repeated game
94af06444594.sentence: If the stage game has more than one Nash equilibrium, the repeated game may have multiple subgame perfect Nash equilibria.

ffb8974bda5a.title: Repeated game
ffb8974bda5a.sentence: While a Nash equilibrium must be played in the last round, the presence of multiple equilibria introduces the possibility of reward and punishment strategies that can be used to support deviation from stage game Nash equilibria in earlier rounds.

20d1198cdf68.title: Repeated game
20d1198cdf68.sentence: The punishment may be playing a strategy which leads to reduced payoff to both players for the rest of the game (called a trigger strategy).

9e8554736c4e.title: Repeated game
9e8554736c4e.sentence: However, if it is known that the other player is following a trigger strategy, then the player expects to receive reduced payoffs in the future if they deviate at this stage.

2036ac8d1289.title: Repeated game
2036ac8d1289.sentence: An effective trigger strategy ensures that cooperating has more utility to the player than acting selfishly now and facing the other player's punishment in the future.

33bb868df417.title: Cooperative bargaining

455e05786da1.title: Cooperative bargaining
455e05786da1.sentence: This could be some focal equilibrium that both players could expect to play, or zero if no agreement is reached.

e26c4d887c0a.title: Cooperative bargaining
e26c4d887c0a.sentence: This point directly affects the bargaining solution, however, so it stands to reason that each player should attempt to choose his disagreement point in order to maximize his bargaining position.

102200e331f6.title: Cooperative bargaining
102200e331f6.sentence: Towards this objective, it is often advantageous to increase one's own disagreement payoff while harming the opponent's disagreement payoff (hence the interpretation of the disagreement as a threat).

d942c927a076.title: Cooperative bargaining
d942c927a076.sentence: The egalitarian bargaining solution, introduced by Ehud Kalai, is a third solution which drops the condition of scale invariance while including both the axiom of independence of irrelevant alternatives, and the axiom of resource monotonicity.

c8dd6b5ba9da.title: Cooperative bargaining
c8dd6b5ba9da.sentence: Under these conditions the solution attempts to grant equal gain to both parties.

8971144d954f.title: Cooperative bargaining
8971144d954f.sentence: In other words, it is the point which maximizes the minimum payoff among players.

c9a392ff0f75.title: Cooperative bargaining
c9a392ff0f75.sentence: Kalai notes that this solution is closely related to the egalitarian ideas of John Rawls.

a488e0d210b5.title: Cooperative bargaining
a488e0d210b5.sentence: Independence of irrelevant alternatives can be substituted with a resource monotonicity axiom, as suggested by Ehud Kalai and Meir Smorodinsky.

c77ac550c50a.title: Cooperative bargaining
c77ac550c50a.sentence: This leads to the Kalai–Smorodinsky rule, which selects the point which maintains the ratio of maximal gains.

dee68359c098.title: Cooperative bargaining
dee68359c098.sentence: In other words, if we normalize the disagreement point to (0,0) and player 1 can receive a maximum of g1 with player 2's help (and vice versa for g2), then the Kalai–Smorodinsky bargaining solution would yield the point ϕ on the Pareto frontier such that ϕ1/ϕ2=g1/g2.

909fa6dd0621.title: Cooperative bargaining
909fa6dd0621.sentence: The Nash bargaining game is a simple two-player game used to model bargaining interactions.

b8c6bdf34207.title: Cooperative bargaining
b8c6bdf34207.sentence: In the Nash bargaining game, two players demand a portion of some good (usually some amount of money).

6899ee26dd0a.title: Cooperative bargaining
6899ee26dd0a.sentence: If the total amount requested by the players is less than that available, both players get their request.

a5972c0a6928.title: Cooperative bargaining

a6c89b9b2056.title: Cooperative bargaining
a6c89b9b2056.sentence: There are many Nash equilibria in the Nash demand game.

be009b194f7c.title: Cooperative bargaining
be009b194f7c.sentence: Any x and y such that x + y = z is a Nash equilibrium.

9a3a324e4576.title: Cooperative bargaining
9a3a324e4576.sentence: There is also a Nash equilibrium where both players demand the entire good.

fc5451a4ad0d.title: Cooperative bargaining
fc5451a4ad0d.sentence: Here both players receive nothing, but neither player can increase their return by unilaterally changing their strategy.

ae5b6d393f1a.title: Cooperative bargaining
ae5b6d393f1a.sentence: Nash (1953) presents a non-cooperative demand game with two players who are uncertain about which payoff pairs are feasible.

a09cf922d0f1.title: Cooperative bargaining
a09cf922d0f1.sentence: In the limit as the uncertainty vanishes, equilibrium payoffs converge to those predicted by the Nash bargaining solution.

a0532f1d12f9.title: Cooperative bargaining
a0532f1d12f9.sentence: In Rubinstein's alternating offers bargaining game, players take turns acting as the proposer for splitting some surplus.

1b2fbcb187bb.title: Cooperative bargaining
1b2fbcb187bb.sentence: That is, after each step the surplus is worth d times what it was worth previously.

9aab7cc608ae.title: Cooperative bargaining
9aab7cc608ae.sentence: The division of the surplus in the unique subgame perfect equilibrium depends upon how strongly players prefer current over future payoffs.

c62fa6fdb50c.title: Cooperative bargaining
c62fa6fdb50c.sentence: Rubinstein showed that if the surplus is normalized to 1, the payoff for player 1 in equilibrium is 1/(1+d), while the payoff for player 2 is d/(1+d).

b4283d616c49.title: Cooperative bargaining
b4283d616c49.sentence: In the limit as players become perfectly patient, the equilibrium division converges to the Nash bargaining solution.

1fc048b59c34.title: Extensive-form game
1fc048b59c34.sentence: A game with perfect information is such that at any stage of the game, every player knows exactly what has taken place earlier in the game; i.e. every information set is a singleton set.

c72a66eb0e56.title: Extensive-form game
c72a66eb0e56.sentence: Any game without perfect information has imperfect information.

91c16c86588e.title: Extensive-form game
91c16c86588e.sentence: One player does not always observe the choice of another (for example, moves may be simultaneous or a move may be hidden).

53a69c56b11c.title: Extensive-form game
53a69c56b11c.sentence: If a game has an information set with more than one member that game is said to have imperfect information.

dd170e543deb.title: Extensive-form game
dd170e543deb.sentence: In extensive form, an information set is indicated by a dotted line connecting all nodes in that set or sometimes by a loop drawn around all the nodes in that set.

0f411e1affb3.title: Extensive-form game
0f411e1affb3.sentence: It may be the case that a player does not know exactly what the payoffs of the game are or of what type their opponents are.

48f7b91099fd.title: Extensive-form game
48f7b91099fd.sentence: In extensive form it is represented as a game with complete but imperfect information using the so-called Harsanyi transformation.

4e372980be96.title: Extensive-form game

fe0aef3e60e7.title: Extensive-form game

58c1192443be.title: Extensive-form game
58c1192443be.sentence: Nature's choice is represented in the game tree by a non-filled node.

d1327512f8da.title: Bayesian game
d1327512f8da.sentence: A Bayesian Nash Equilibrium (BNE) is a Nash equilibrium for a Bayesian game, which is derived from the ex-ante normal form game associated with the Bayesian framework.

4653280278ef.title: Bayesian game
4653280278ef.sentence: A strategy profile σ=(σ1,σ2,…,σN) is a Bayesian Nash equilibrium if, for every player i, the strategy σi maximizes player i's expected payoff, given:

10b18c4cb171.title: Bayesian game
10b18c4cb171.sentence: - Their beliefs about the state of nature (based on their type),

8c4682d5b6bb.title: Bayesian game
8c4682d5b6bb.sentence: - The strategies played by other players.

0daad8077e2b.title: Bayesian game
0daad8077e2b.sentence: For a Bayesian game, the concept of Nash equilibrium extends to include the uncertainty about the state of nature: Each player maximizes their expected payoff based on their beliefs about the state of nature, which are formed using Bayes' rule.

03f40bbd4ec2.title: Bayesian game

03f40bbd4ec2.sentence: Bayesian Nash equilibrium can result in implausible equilibria in dynamic games, where players move sequentially rather than simultaneously.

aeea3ebfbe37.sentence: This means there is a Bayesian Nash equilibrium in which all participants reveal their true preferences.

627d1f4466a6.sentence: An information set of player i is a subset of player i's decision nodes that she cannot distinguish between.

3b8ab96493f1.sentence: While a mixed strategy assigns a probability distribution over pure strategies, a behavior strategy (or behavioral strategy) assigns at each information set a probability distribution over the set of possible actions.

14789d8fe3e8.title: Strategy (game theory)
14789d8fe3e8.sentence: Roughly, a mixed strategy randomly chooses a deterministic path through the game tree, while a behavior strategy can be seen as a stochastic path.

cf69d74e3d72.title: Strategy (game theory)

28bc961e69a7.title: Strategy (game theory)

0c34a2bef052.title: Tit for tat
0c34a2bef052.sentence: Generous tit for tat is a variation of the tit-for-tat strategy that introduces a mechanism for forgiveness to prevent long cycles of mutual defection.

d5e22eb78005.title: Tit for tat
d5e22eb78005.sentence: - If the opponent defected in the previous round, usually defect, but with a small probability, choose to cooperate instead.

0636ff4485bc.title: Tit for tat
0636ff4485bc.sentence: In a standard tit-for-tat scenario, if one player defects due to a mistake, miscommunication, or "noise" in the system, the other player will defect in the next round.

509946c08834.title: Tit for tat
509946c08834.sentence: By allowing for occasional forgiveness, this strategy can break the cycle of retaliation and return the game to a state of mutual cooperation.

a16a40d0bd92.title: Tit for tat
a16a40d0bd92.sentence: Game theorist Robert Axelrod, who coined the term, found that while risky, this strategy is highly effective in environments with "noise" (imperfect information or errors in execution), as it prevents accidental conflicts from escalating indefinitely.

169e1e8cbdc5.sentence: Depending on the situation, a slightly better strategy can be "tit for tat with forgiveness": when the opponent defects, on the next move, the player sometimes cooperates anyway, with a small probability (around 1–5%, depending on the lineup of opponents).

735930cc89cb.sentence: Studies in the prosocial behaviour of animals have led many ethologists and evolutionary psychologists to apply tit-for-tat strategies to explain why altruism evolves in many animal communities.

615e41f0a9dd.sentence: Reciprocal altruism works in animal communities where the cost to the benefactor in any transaction of food, mating rights, nesting or territory is less than the gains to the beneficiary.

8d1ef9b12a93.sentence: Mechanisms to identify and punish "cheaters" who fail to reciprocate, in effect a form of tit for tat, are important to regulate reciprocal altruism.

f918cb3d5c15.sentence: For example, tit-for-tat is suggested to be the mechanism of cooperative predator inspection behavior in guppies.

8b258d79e795.title: Tit for tat

65e039fc56de.title: Evolutionary game theory
