65e039fc56de.sentence: Kin selection – (inclusive fitness of related contestants) | Kin – genetically related individuals | Evolutionary game participants are genes of strategy. The best payoff for an individual is not necessarily the best payoff for the gene. In any generation the player gene is not only in one individual, it is in a kin-group. The highest fitness payoff for the kin group is selected by natural selection. Therefore, strategies that include self-sacrifice on the part of individuals are often game winners – the evolutionarily stable strategy. Animals must live in kin-groups during part of the game for the opportunity for this altruistic sacrifice ever to take place. | Games must take into account inclusive fitness. Fitness function is the combined fitness of a group of related contestants – each weighted by the degree of relatedness – relative to the total genetic population. The mathematical analysis of this gene-centric view of the game leads to Hamilton's rule, that the relatedness of the altruistic donor must exceed the cost-benefit ratio of the altruistic act itself: R>c/b R is relatedness, c the cost, b the benefit

2ed94aff82be.title: Evolutionary game theory

2ed94aff82be.sentence: Direct reciprocity | Contestants that trade favours in paired relationships | A game theoretic embodiment of "I'll scratch your back if you scratch mine". A pair of individuals exchange favours in a multi-round game. The individuals are recognisable to one another as partnered. The term "direct" applies because the return favour is specifically given back to the pair partner only. | The characteristics of the multi-round game produce a danger of defection and the potentially lesser payoffs of cooperation in each round, but any such defection can lead to punishment in a following round – establishing the game as a repeated prisoner's dilemma. Therefore, the family of tit-for-tat strategies come to the fore.

494946eacf04.title: Evolutionary game theory
494946eacf04.section: Contests of selfish genes > Routes to altruism
494946eacf04.sentence: Indirect reciprocity | Related or non related contestants trade favours but without partnering. A return favour is "implied" but with no specific identified source who is to give it. | The return favour is not derived from any particular established partner. The potential for indirect reciprocity exists for a specific organism if it lives in a cluster of individuals who can interact over an extended period of time. It has been argued that human behaviours in establishing moral systems as well as the expending of significant energies in human society for tracking individual reputations is a direct effect of societies' reliance on strategies of indirect reciprocation. | The game is highly susceptible to defection, as direct retaliation is impossible. Therefore, indirect reciprocity will not work without keeping a social score, a measure of past co-operative behaviour. The mathematics lead to a modified version of Hamilton's rule where: q>c/b where q (the probability of knowing the social score) must be greater than the cost benefit ratio Organisms that use social score are termed Discriminators, and require a higher level of cognition than strategies of simple direct reciprocity. As evolutionary biologist David Haig put it – "For direct reciprocity you need a face; for indirect reciprocity you need a name".

750ed8afecb6.title: Derivative

807a93cde6f1.sentence: In mathematics, a differential equation is an equation that relates one or more unknown functions and their derivatives.

6065d8d9c3c4.title: Differential equation
6065d8d9c3c4.sentence: In applications, the functions generally represent physical quantities, the derivatives represent their rates of change, and the differential equation defines a relationship between the two.

97ba106d178f.title: Differential equation
97ba106d178f.sentence: Such relations are common in mathematical models and scientific laws; therefore, differential equations play a prominent role in many disciplines including engineering, physics, economics, and biology.

ce16343e99b0.title: Differential equation
ce16343e99b0.sentence: Only the simplest differential equations are solvable by explicit formulas; however, many properties of solutions of a given differential equation may be determined without computing them exactly.

d826e3a08865.title: Differential equation
d826e3a08865.sentence: Often when a closed-form expression for the solutions is not available, solutions may be approximated numerically using computers, and many numerical methods have been developed to determine solutions with a given degree of accuracy.

9341b5dc135f.title: Differential equation

b4f2fefbaaad.title: Differential equation

3faddeb7f2a7.title: Differential equation

ca5b5663db5d.title: Exponential growth
ca5b5663db5d.sentence: Exponential growth occurs when a quantity grows as an exponential function of time.

8a2bae23823f.title: Exponential growth
8a2bae23823f.sentence: The quantity grows at a rate directly proportional to its present size.

5a64e4a90ca3.title: Exponential growth
5a64e4a90ca3.sentence: For example, when it is 3 times as big as it is now, it will be growing 3 times as fast as it is now.

a3e138df48e2.title: Exponential growth
a3e138df48e2.sentence: One bacterium splits itself into two, each of which splits itself resulting in four, then eight, 16, 32, and so on.

4a0b7edbdd08.title: Exponential growth
4a0b7edbdd08.sentence: Terms like "exponential growth" are sometimes incorrectly interpreted as "rapid growth." Indeed, something that grows exponentially can in fact be growing slowly at first.

44ea94f90068.title: Exponential growth
44ea94f90068.sentence: - Economic growth is expressed in percentage terms, implying exponential growth.

3fbaab5cc2de.title: Exponential growth
3fbaab5cc2de.sentence: Example: If a species of bacteria doubles every ten minutes, starting out with only one bacterium, how many bacteria would be present after one hour?

8e8b3cebf99d.title: Exponential growth
8e8b3cebf99d.sentence: After one hour, or six ten-minute intervals, there would be sixty-four bacteria.

035e224c4353.title: Exponential growth
035e224c4353.sentence: If the constant of proportionality is negative, then the quantity decreases over time, and is said to be undergoing exponential decay instead.

34a38dad7676.title: Exponential growth

7a5d027ab881.title: An Essay on the Principle of Population
7a5d027ab881.sentence: The book warned of future difficulties, on an interpretation of the population increasing in geometric progression (so as to double every 25 years) while food production increased in an arithmetic progression, which would leave a difference resulting in the want of food and famine, unless birth rates decreased.

1f26081c00d6.title: Exponential growth

5e2029208116.title: Exponential growth

da8cb7dc8575.title: Constrained optimization
da8cb7dc8575.sentence: In mathematical optimization, constrained optimization (in some contexts called constraint optimization) is the process of optimizing an objective function with respect to some variables in the presence of constraints on those variables.

b39c3877efc0.title: Constrained optimization
b39c3877efc0.sentence: The objective function is either a cost function or energy function, which is to be minimized, or a reward function or utility function, which is to be maximized.

ac80dab64a0c.title: Constrained optimization
ac80dab64a0c.sentence: Constraints can be either hard constraints, which set conditions for the variables that are required to be satisfied, or soft constraints, which have some variable values that are penalized in the objective function if, and based on the extent that, the conditions on the variables are not satisfied.

151701567034.title: Consumer choice
151701567034.sentence: The models that make up consumer theory are used to represent prospectively observable demand patterns for an individual buyer on the hypothesis of constrained optimization.

d9f12447e7e9.title: Constrained optimization

d9f12447e7e9.sentence: If the constrained problem has only equality constraints, the method of Lagrange multipliers can be used to convert it into an unconstrained problem whose number of variables is the original number of variables plus the original number of equality constraints.

8ccc44da570a.title: Constrained optimization
8ccc44da570a.sentence: With inequality constraints, the problem can be characterized in terms of the geometric optimality conditions, Fritz John conditions and Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions, under which simple problems may be solvable.

2b856481df97.title: Constrained optimization

b6db6f5d98fc.sentence: If the objective function or some of the constraints are nonlinear, and some constraints are inequalities, then the problem is a nonlinear programming problem.

68b7e4bbb4ff.title: Convex function

b549fa839b87.sentence: Linear programming (LP), also called linear optimization, is a method to achieve the best outcome (such as maximum profit or lowest cost) in a mathematical model whose requirements and objective are represented by linear relationships.

ac2a5e25fc38.title: Linear programming

c8fc8e5b38b2.sentence: In mathematical dynamics, discrete time and continuous time are two alternative frameworks within which variables that evolve over time are modeled.

7b87711cddf5.sentence: Discrete time views values of variables as occurring at distinct, separate "points in time", or equivalently as being unchanged throughout each non-zero region of time ("time period")—that is, time is viewed as a discrete variable.

fc2bc25b6448.title: Computable general equilibrium

9c6f926959cd.title: Computable general equilibrium
9c6f926959cd.sentence: In contrast to input-output models, which estimate the quantities of inputs like wheat, energy, labour, and capital required to produce bread, a CGE model can assess how a wage increase might affect the amount of labour used in bread production.

1dbc58c66052.title: Computable general equilibrium
1dbc58c66052.sentence: CGE models are descended from the input–output models pioneered by Wassily Leontief, but assign a more important role to prices.

50bb27e44363.title: Computable general equilibrium
50bb27e44363.sentence: They have been used widely to analyse trade policy.

4daa52c0136d.title: Computable general equilibrium

07af344bddb2.sentence: Constraints may involve institutional review boards, informed consent and confidentiality affecting both clinical (medical) trials and behavioral and social science experiments.

21891ee1db41.title: Choice modelling

21891ee1db41.sentence: An experimental design (below) in a Choice Experiment is a strict scheme for controlling and presenting hypothetical scenarios, or choice sets to respondents.

19537f317a62.title: Bayesian inference
19537f317a62.sentence: Bayesian inference (/ˈbeɪziən/ BAY-zee-ən or /ˈbeɪʒən/ BAY-zhən) is a method of statistical inference in which Bayes' theorem is used to calculate a probability of a hypothesis, given prior evidence, and update it as more information becomes available.

e0b53a9d050f.title: Bayesian inference
e0b53a9d050f.sentence: Fundamentally, Bayesian inference uses a prior distribution to estimate posterior probabilities.

c9a856daf2bb.title: Bayesian inference
c9a856daf2bb.sentence: - The prior distribution is the distribution of the parameter(s) before any data is observed, i.e. p(θ∣α).

5c2fadeed2c2.title: Bayesian inference
5c2fadeed2c2.sentence: Bayesian updating is particularly important in the dynamic analysis of a sequence of data.

8f233b0bc6be.title: Bayesian inference
8f233b0bc6be.sentence: Bayes' theorem is applied successively to all evidence presented, with the posterior from one stage becoming the prior for the next.

d214fea23558.title: Bayesian inference
d214fea23558.sentence: Bayesian inference has found application in a wide range of activities, including science, engineering, philosophy, medicine, sport, psychology, and law.

e5ae536dc9be.title: Bayesian inference
e5ae536dc9be.section: In frequentist statistics and decision theory
e5ae536dc9be.sentence: A decision-theoretic justification of the use of Bayesian inference was given by Abraham Wald, who proved that every unique Bayesian procedure is admissible.

0221d44de379.title: Bayesian inference
0221d44de379.section: In frequentist statistics and decision theory
0221d44de379.sentence: Wald characterized admissible procedures as Bayesian procedures (and limits of Bayesian procedures), making the Bayesian formalism a central technique in such areas of frequentist inference as parameter estimation, hypothesis testing, and computing confidence intervals.

41f89ff83a7d.title: Bayesian inference
41f89ff83a7d.section: In frequentist statistics and decision theory > Model selection
41f89ff83a7d.sentence: In Bayesian model comparison, the model with the highest posterior probability given the data is selected.

eeda399e34f7.title: Bayesian inference
eeda399e34f7.sentence: There is also an ever-growing connection between Bayesian methods and simulation-based Monte Carlo techniques since complex models cannot be processed in closed form by a Bayesian analysis, while a graphical model structure may allow for efficient simulation algorithms like the Gibbs sampling and other Metropolis–Hastings algorithm schemes.

4750fb1efdff.title: Bayesian inference
4750fb1efdff.sentence: The term 'Bayesian' refers to Thomas Bayes (1701–1761), who proved that probabilistic limits could be placed on an unknown event.

d87ba2bb3af1.title: Bayesian inference
d87ba2bb3af1.sentence: However, it was Pierre-Simon Laplace (1749–1827) who introduced (as Principle VI) what is now called Bayes' theorem and used it to address problems in celestial mechanics, medical statistics, reliability, and jurisprudence.

f3e72de39df6.title: Bayesian inference
f3e72de39df6.sentence: Early Bayesian inference, which used uniform priors following Laplace's principle of insufficient reason, was called inverse probability (because it infers backwards from observations to parameters, or from effects to causes).

54fe7a380f6c.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
54fe7a380f6c.sentence: In statistics, maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) is a method of estimating the parameters of an assumed probability distribution, given some observed data.

ababe0d8f76d.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
ababe0d8f76d.sentence: This is achieved by maximizing a likelihood function so that, under the assumed statistical model, the observed data is most probable.

9a7769c30df6.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
9a7769c30df6.sentence: The logic of maximum likelihood is both intuitive and flexible, and as such the method has become a dominant means of statistical inference.

c9bbef6fa6df.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
c9bbef6fa6df.sentence: cannot be solved explicitly for an estimator θ^=θ^(𝐲).

e2b2da5cd0a7.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
e2b2da5cd0a7.sentence: Instead, they need to be solved iteratively: starting from an initial guess of θ (say θ^1), one seeks to obtain a convergent sequence {θ^r}.

b25a29c5433b.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
b25a29c5433b.sentence: The consistency means that if the data were generated by f(⋅;θ0) and we have a sufficiently large number of observations n, then it is possible to find the value of θ0 with arbitrary precision.

db5c5a0fb869.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
db5c5a0fb869.sentence: A maximum likelihood estimator coincides with the most probable Bayesian estimator given a uniform prior distribution on the parameters.

e103426c392c.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
e103426c392c.sentence: However, maximum likelihood prediction fails to propagate the uncertainty around the maximum likelihood parameter estimates into the prediction.

8345bbde7967.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
8345bbde7967.sentence: It was Ronald Fisher however, between 1912 and 1922, who single-handedly created the modern version of the method.

c977e2e0dd77.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
c977e2e0dd77.sentence: Early users of maximum likelihood include Carl Friedrich Gauss, Pierre-Simon Laplace, Thorvald N. Thiele, and Francis Ysidro Edgeworth.

7188ef78560d.title: Discrete choice
7188ef78560d.section: Prominent types of discrete choice models > Estimation from choices
7188ef78560d.sentence: Discrete choice models are often estimated using maximum likelihood estimation.

ca4c0714d737.title: Probit model
ca4c0714d737.sentence: The parameters β are typically estimated by maximum likelihood.

d2cea51cdd95.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
d2cea51cdd95.sentence: Maximum-likelihood estimation finally transcended heuristic justification in a proof published by Samuel S. Wilks in 1938, now called Wilks' theorem.

f606a65d2552.title: Panel data
f606a65d2552.sentence: In statistics and econometrics, panel data and longitudinal data are both multi-dimensional data involving measurements over time.

475099d93c73.title: Panel data
475099d93c73.sentence: Panel data is a subset of longitudinal data where observations are for the same subjects each time.

d37aebe2fb57.title: Panel data
d37aebe2fb57.sentence: Time series and cross-sectional data can be thought of as special cases of panel data that are in one dimension only (one panel member or individual for the former, one time point for the latter).

8a1e424f525a.title: Panel data
8a1e424f525a.sentence: A balanced panel (e.g., the first dataset above) is a dataset in which each panel member (i.e., person) is observed every year.

1f2d08858356.title: Panel data
1f2d08858356.sentence: An unbalanced panel (e.g., the second dataset above) is a dataset in which at least one panel member is not observed every period.

396c0ad7d8ec.title: Panel data
396c0ad7d8ec.sentence: μi are individual-specific, time-invariant effects (e.g., in a panel of countries this could include geography, climate, etc.) which are fixed over time, whereas vit is a time-varying random component.

98149b259303.title: Panel data
98149b259303.sentence: If μi is unobserved, and correlated with at least one of the independent variables, then it will cause omitted variable bias in a standard OLS regression.

85f198bfc337.title: Panel data
85f198bfc337.sentence: However, panel data methods, such as the fixed effects estimator or alternatively, the first-difference estimator can be used to control for it.

1ec9a2043cd5.title: Panel data
1ec9a2043cd5.sentence: Random effects is one such method: it is a special case of feasible generalized least squares which controls for the structure of the serial correlation induced by μi.

1b21804ed828.title: Panel data

f76b93efb3f2.title: Kuznets curve
f76b93efb3f2.sentence: Subsequent cross-country research by Windarti, Hlaing, and Kakinaka, using panel data from 130 countries between 1975 and 2010, found a clear non-linear relationship between income and weight-related health status, with obesity rising in low-income settings and falling in high-income settings.

a5cdd7446f45.title: Statistical hypothesis test
a5cdd7446f45.section: Technical description of the null hypothesis
a5cdd7446f45.sentence: The null hypothesis is a default hypothesis that a quantity to be measured is zero (null).

9bab88c82473.title: Statistical hypothesis test
9bab88c82473.section: Technical description of the null hypothesis
9bab88c82473.sentence: Typically, the quantity to be measured is the difference between two situations.

b1abf891db45.title: Statistical hypothesis test
b1abf891db45.sentence: The test compares two hypotheses: a default null hypothesis (denoted H0) and its negation, the alternative hypothesis (H1).

4db9ee78b859.title: Statistical hypothesis test
4db9ee78b859.sentence: Possible null hypotheses are "this drug does not reduce the risk of having a heart attack" or "this drug has no effect on the risk of having a heart attack".

c7f4a3faeb53.title: Statistical hypothesis test
c7f4a3faeb53.sentence: Paul Meehl has argued that the epistemological importance of the choice of null hypothesis has gone largely unacknowledged.

09c8e1eae430.title: Statistical hypothesis test
09c8e1eae430.sentence: When the null hypothesis defaults to "no difference" or "no effect", a more precise experiment is a less severe test of the theory that motivated performing the experiment.

8a2df6c56da4.title: Statistical hypothesis test
8a2df6c56da4.section: Performing a frequentist hypothesis test in practice > Interpretation
8a2df6c56da4.sentence: The p-value is the probability that a test statistic which is at least as extreme as the one obtained would occur under the null hypothesis.

baab4623f6ba.title: Statistical hypothesis test
baab4623f6ba.sentence: If this probability (called the p-value) is less than, or equal to, the significance level of the test (denoted α), then the null hypothesis is rejected.

377e0e73f738.title: Statistical hypothesis test
377e0e73f738.sentence: The test does not conclude that the null hypothesis is false, or that the probability that the null hypothesis is true is less than α.

483426e9ba28.title: Statistical hypothesis test
483426e9ba28.sentence: The procedure works by assessing whether the observed departure, measured by the test statistic, is larger than, or equal to, a value defined, so that the probability of occurrence of a value that is at least as extreme is small under the null hypothesis (usually in less than either 5% or 1% of similar data-sets in which the null hypothesis does hold).

f489894f8be3.title: Statistical hypothesis test
f489894f8be3.sentence: Statistical significance does not imply practical significance, and correlation does not imply causation.

703ab3483dfd.title: Statistical hypothesis test
703ab3483dfd.sentence: - A type I error, in which the null hypothesis is rejected despite the null hypothesis being true, with probability α=P(reject H0|H0).

d25b56b08cea.title: Statistical hypothesis test
d25b56b08cea.sentence: - A type II error, in which the null hypothesis is accepted despite the alternative hypothesis being true, with probability β=P(accept H0|H1).

e267a653cc3a.title: Statistical hypothesis test
e267a653cc3a.sentence: This is the same as the significance level of the test.

4532ef37d580.title: Statistical hypothesis test
4532ef37d580.sentence: The quantity 1−β is called the power of the test.

dfe79178570e.section: Reporting of results > Interpretation of statistical results
dfe79178570e.sentence: Regarding Type I errors, a typical RCT will use 0.05 (i.e., 1 in 20) as the probability that the RCT will falsely find two equally effective treatments significantly different.

855c19c81cf6.title: Statistical hypothesis test
855c19c81cf6.sentence: To minimize type II errors, large samples are recommended.

e42ea5354448.title: Design of experiments
e42ea5354448.sentence: Random assignment is the process of assigning individuals at random to groups or to different groups in an experiment, so that each individual of the population has the same chance of becoming a participant in the study.

186924004b6c.title: Design of experiments
186924004b6c.sentence: The random assignment of individuals to groups (or conditions within a group) distinguishes a rigorous, "true" experiment from an observational study or "quasi-experiment".

db5f3593df48.title: Design of experiments
db5f3593df48.sentence: However, it tends to balance known and unknown confounding variables between groups on average.

6e04a3f6b12b.title: Design of experiments
6e04a3f6b12b.sentence: Comparisons between treatments are much more valuable and are usually preferable, and often compared against a scientific control or traditional treatment that acts as baseline.

a4808a537551.title: Design of experiments
a4808a537551.sentence: For example, in observational designs, participants are not assigned randomly to conditions, and so if there are differences found in outcome variables between conditions, it is likely that there is something other than the differences between the conditions that causes the differences in outcomes, that is – a third variable.

098d0280fcc9.title: Randomized controlled trial
098d0280fcc9.sentence: A randomized controlled trial (RCT) is a type of statistical experiment designed to evaluate the efficacy or safety of an intervention by minimizing bias through the random allocation of participants to one or more comparison groups.

de64ba6aa8c3.title: Randomized controlled trial
de64ba6aa8c3.sentence: In this approach, at least one group receives the intervention or process under study (such as a drug, surgical procedure, medical device or diet), while the other groups receive an alternative treatment, a placebo, or standard care.

46c6a2f4e0fc.title: Randomized controlled trial
46c6a2f4e0fc.sentence: - "It eliminates bias in treatment assignment," specifically selection bias and confounding.

20e5531f1a13.title: Randomized controlled trial
20e5531f1a13.sentence: RCTs are considered to be the most reliable form of scientific evidence in the hierarchy of evidence that influences healthcare policy and practice because RCTs reduce spurious causality and bias.

9e4d3e8a1b0a.title: Randomized controlled trial
9e4d3e8a1b0a.sentence: Results of RCTs may be combined in systematic reviews which are increasingly being used in the conduct of evidence-based practice.

5c871473caa3.title: Randomized controlled trial
5c871473caa3.sentence: If the effect of the treatment is small, the number of treatment units in either group may be insufficient for rejecting the null hypothesis in the respective statistical test.

d72b8c2abe40.title: Randomized controlled trial
d72b8c2abe40.sentence: RCTs can be expensive; one study found 28 Phase III RCTs funded by the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke prior to 2000 with a total cost of US$335 million, for a mean cost of US$12 million per RCT.

9d51bc59c6f8.title: Randomized controlled trial
9d51bc59c6f8.sentence: For instance, RCTs may be improper for studying medical interventions with "obvious" benefits to patients, as such practice would unethically deny the control group of effective treatment.

e971992ccd79.title: Randomized controlled trial
e971992ccd79.sentence: In the posthumously published Ortus Medicinae (1648), Jan Baptist van Helmont made the first proposal of a RCT, to test two treatment regimes of fever.

60b1d6826259.title: Natural experiment
60b1d6826259.sentence: A natural experiment is a study in which individuals are exposed to experimental and control conditions that are determined by nature or by other factors outside the control of the investigators.

03ae97fe94ae.title: Natural experiment
03ae97fe94ae.sentence: The exposure process may resemble random assignment.

4388731741ce.title: Natural experiment
4388731741ce.sentence: Thus, natural experiments are observational studies and are not controlled in the traditional sense of a randomized experiment (an intervention study).

6d6807e3b3d1.title: Natural experiment
6d6807e3b3d1.sentence: Natural experiments are generally more reliable when there is a clearly defined exposure or intervention that affects a well-defined subpopulation (with a comparable subpopulation remaining unexposed), such that differences in outcomes may be attributed to the exposure or intervention.

7735e6fdca3a.title: Natural experiment
7735e6fdca3a.sentence: Natural experiments are employed as study designs when controlled experimentation is extremely difficult to implement or unethical, such as in several research areas addressed by epidemiology (like evaluating the health impact of varying degrees of exposure to ionizing radiation in people living near Hiroshima at the time of the atomic blast) and economics (like estimating the economic return on amount of schooling in US adults).

c15874acbce5.title: Natural experiment
c15874acbce5.sentence: One of the best-known early natural experiments was the 1854 Broad Street cholera outbreak in London, England.

9a065f7f22f2.title: Natural experiment
9a065f7f22f2.sentence: Snow found that the Southwark and Vauxhall Waterworks Company, which supplied water to districts with high attack rates, obtained the water from the Thames downstream from where raw sewage was discharged into the river.

5963c4cbd4f8.title: Natural experiment
5963c4cbd4f8.sentence: By contrast, districts that were supplied water by the Lambeth Waterworks Company, which obtained water upstream from the points of sewage discharge, had low attack rates.

839a85d3acf1.title: Natural experiment
839a85d3acf1.sentence: Using statistical methods developed in econometrics, Angrist capitalized on the approximate random assignment of the Vietnam War draft lottery, and used it as an instrumental variable associated with eligibility (or non-eligibility) for military service.

753c806cd8e1.title: Natural experiment
753c806cd8e1.sentence: Angrist found that the earnings of veterans were, on average, about 15 percent less than the earnings of non-veterans.

55e3bb7cafe6.title: Natural experiment
55e3bb7cafe6.sentence: In the twentieth century, as regulation improved and pollution fell, providing the conditions for a large-scale natural experiment, the trend towards industrial melanism was reversed, and melanic forms quickly became scarce.

a30951b667e4.title: Natural experiment
a30951b667e4.sentence: The study also noted its own weaknesses which potentially suggest that the inability to control variables in natural experiments can impede investigators from drawing firm conclusions.'

8a836c4d009f.title: Impact evaluation
8a836c4d009f.sentence: This involves counterfactual analysis, that is, "a comparison between what actually happened and what would have happened in the absence of the intervention." Impact evaluations seek to answer cause-and-effect questions.

c5f1fb3bb871.title: Impact evaluation
c5f1fb3bb871.sentence: The 'counterfactual' measures what would have happened to beneficiaries in the absence of the intervention, and impact is estimated by comparing counterfactual outcomes to those observed under the intervention.

13f73052311f.title: Impact evaluation
13f73052311f.sentence: The key challenge in impact evaluation is that the counterfactual cannot be directly observed and must be approximated with reference to a comparison group.

a8f09a72b706.title: Impact evaluation
a8f09a72b706.sentence: There are a range of accepted approaches to determining an appropriate comparison group for counterfactual analysis, using either prospective (ex ante) or retrospective (ex post) evaluation design.

c54db302e98d.title: Difference in differences
c54db302e98d.sentence: The control group is often used as a proxy for the counterfactual (see, Synthetic control method for a deeper understanding of this point).

fc85a86a6862.title: Rubin causal model
fc85a86a6862.sentence: The Rubin causal model (RCM), also known as the Neyman–Rubin causal model, is an approach to the statistical analysis of cause and effect based on the framework of potential outcomes, named after Donald Rubin.

07b27cad845c.title: Rubin causal model
07b27cad845c.sentence: The causal effect of a treatment on a single unit at a point in time is the difference between the outcome variable with the treatment and without the treatment.

db848eb952a6.title: Rubin causal model
db848eb952a6.sentence: For example, a person would have a particular income at age 40 if they had attended college, whereas they would have a different income at age 40 if they had not attended college.

b0d7802060f0.title: Rubin causal model
b0d7802060f0.sentence: To measure the causal effect of going to college for this person, we need to compare the outcome for the same individual in both alternative futures.

b7de33176391.title: Rubin causal model
b7de33176391.sentence: The potential outcomes framework was first proposed by Jerzy Neyman in his 1923 Master's thesis, though he discussed it only in the context of completely randomized experiments.

f7221ce42894.title: Rubin causal model
f7221ce42894.sentence: Rubin extended it into a general framework for thinking about causation in both observational and experimental studies.

58c8e47aba41.title: Rubin causal model
58c8e47aba41.sentence: However, randomized experiments allow for the estimation of population-level causal effects.

c86dc443f83d.title: Rubin causal model
c86dc443f83d.sentence: Because of this random assignment, the groups are (on average) equivalent, and the difference in income at age 40 can be attributed to the college assignment since that was the only difference between the groups.

e8fd4b74e610.title: Rubin causal model
e8fd4b74e610.section: An extended example > Average causal effect
e8fd4b74e610.sentence: One may calculate the average causal effect (also known as the average treatment effect or ATE) by taking the mean of all the causal effects.

c75535a62e6b.title: Rubin causal model
c75535a62e6b.section: An extended example > The assignment mechanism
c75535a62e6b.sentence: The assignment mechanism, the method by which units are assigned treatment, affects the calculation of the average causal effect.

236551d277ae.title: Rubin causal model
236551d277ae.section: An extended example > The perfect doctor
236551d277ae.sentence: The perfect doctor knows how each subject will respond to the drug or the control and assigns each subject to the treatment that will most benefit her.

612d7e7826b5.title: Rubin causal model
612d7e7826b5.section: An extended example > The perfect doctor
612d7e7826b5.sentence: The perfect doctor distorts both averages by filtering out poor responses to both the treatment and control.

1154d3216442.title: Rubin causal model
1154d3216442.section: An extended example > No causation without manipulation
1154d3216442.sentence: The causal effect of new drug is well defined because it is the simple difference of two potential outcomes, both of which might happen.

e678cf0945bc.title: Rubin causal model
e678cf0945bc.section: An extended example > No causation without manipulation
e678cf0945bc.sentence: We can't manipulate Joe's height, so it makes no sense to investigate the causal effect of height on weight.

201338abec1c.title: Impact evaluation
201338abec1c.sentence: Impact evaluation assesses the extent to which an intervention (such as a project, program or policy) is causally responsible for observed outcomes, intended and unintended.

0c7ea1bd4aa7.title: Impact evaluation
0c7ea1bd4aa7.sentence: In contrast to outcome monitoring, which examines whether targets have been achieved, impact evaluation is structured to answer the question: how would outcomes such as participants' well-being have changed if the intervention had not been undertaken?

e6d3039ca59d.title: Impact evaluation
e6d3039ca59d.sentence: Impact evaluation helps people answer key questions for evidence-based policy making: what works, what doesn't, where, why and for how much?

98e8920090c8.title: Impact evaluation
98e8920090c8.sentence: Randomized field experiments are the strongest research designs for assessing program impact.

6743f90f53aa.title: Impact evaluation
6743f90f53aa.sentence: Quasi-experimental methods include matching, differencing, instrumental variables and the pipeline approach; they are usually carried out by multivariate regression analysis.

f106a21f6b39.title: Impact evaluation
f106a21f6b39.sentence: The main problem though is that regardless of which design an evaluator chooses, they are prone to a common problem: Regardless of how well thought through or well implemented the design is, each design is subject to yielding biased estimates of the program effects.

93f08eebb4d6.title: Impact evaluation
93f08eebb4d6.sentence: While experimental impact evaluation methodologies have been used to assess nutrition and water and sanitation interventions in developing countries since the 1980s, the first, and best known, application of experimental methods to a large-scale development program is the evaluation of the Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) program Progresa (now called Oportunidades) in Mexico, which examined a range of development outcomes, including schooling, immunization rates and child work.

3cc92cbc38c4.title: Impact evaluation
3cc92cbc38c4.sentence: In contrast with 'black box' impact evaluation approaches, which only report mean differences in outcomes between treatment and comparison groups, theory-based impact evaluation involves mapping out the causal chain from inputs to outcomes and impact and testing the underlying assumptions.

f20e95b435c1.title: Program evaluation
f20e95b435c1.sentence: Program evaluation is a systematic method for collecting, analyzing, and using information to answer questions about projects, policies and programs, particularly about their effectiveness (whether they do what they are intended to do) and efficiency (whether they are good value for money).

ec388f446783.title: Program evaluation
ec388f446783.sentence: In the public, private, and voluntary sector, stakeholders might be required to assess—under law or charter—or want to know whether the programs they are funding, implementing, voting for, receiving or opposing are producing the promised effect.

03897a412e19.title: Program evaluation
03897a412e19.sentence: To some degree, program evaluation falls under traditional cost–benefit analysis, concerning fair returns on the outlay of economic and other assets; however, social outcomes can be more complex to assess than market outcomes, and a different skillset is required.

802f8b4833eb.title: Program evaluation
802f8b4833eb.sentence: Program evaluation may be conducted at several stages during a program's lifetime.

cae961e73b86.title: Program evaluation
cae961e73b86.sentence: A needs assessment examines the population that the program intends to target, to see whether the need as conceptualized in the program actually exists in the population; whether it is, in fact, a problem; and if so, how it might best be dealt with.

8a09c5cd995a.title: Program evaluation
8a09c5cd995a.sentence: Process analysis looks beyond the theory of what the program is supposed to do and instead evaluates how the program is being implemented.

04332026fe78.title: Program evaluation
04332026fe78.section: Conducting an evaluation > Assessing the impact (effectiveness)
04332026fe78.sentence: The impact evaluation determines the causal effects of the program.

0493c4e7e62d.title: Program evaluation
0493c4e7e62d.sentence: Finally, cost-benefit or cost-efficiency analysis assesses the efficiency of a program.

104d983bcd24.title: Program evaluation
104d983bcd24.sentence: Perhaps the most difficult part of evaluation is determining whether the program itself is causing the changes that are observed in the population it was aimed at.

2a9091dcfb6b.title: Program evaluation
2a9091dcfb6b.sentence: Events or processes outside of the program may be the real cause of the observed outcome (or the real prevention of the anticipated outcome).

04ea862e561e.title: Program evaluation
04ea862e561e.section: Methodological constraints and challenges > Budget constraints
04ea862e561e.sentence: Frequently, programs are faced with budget constraints because most original projects do not include a budget to conduct an evaluation (Bamberger et al., 2004).

86f2ba2cd09b.sentence: If the evaluation is initiated late in the program, there may be no baseline data on the conditions of the target group before the intervention began (Bamberger et al., 2004).

bc24d0ade97b.title: Additionality
bc24d0ade97b.sentence: Additionality may be evaluated ex post, as is often done in the practice of program evaluation, or ex ante, as an initial eligibility screen for issuing credits as part of an environmental or other public goods market.

bb6ea4ce3f3d.sentence: Since it is impossible to see both potential outcomes at once, one of the potential outcomes is always missing.

0bb0c5298a23.sentence: Because of the fundamental problem of causal inference, unit-level causal effects cannot be directly observed.

4a024896636c.title: Difference in differences
4a024896636c.sentence: Difference in differences (DiD or DD) is a quasi-experimental statistical technique used in econometrics and quantitative research in the social sciences that attempts to mimic an experimental research design using observational study data by studying the differential effect of a treatment on a "treatment group" versus a "control group" in a natural experiment.

94a4ffbd3cd4.title: Difference in differences
94a4ffbd3cd4.sentence: It calculates the effect of a treatment (i.e., an explanatory variable or an independent variable) on an outcome (i.e., a response variable or dependent variable) by comparing the average change over time in the outcome variable for the treatment group to the average change over time for the control group.

386bc3413f37.title: Difference in differences
386bc3413f37.sentence: Difference in differences requires data measured from a treatment group and a control group at two or more different time periods, specifically at least one time period before "treatment" and at least one time period after "treatment".

8764a1cd9977.title: Difference in differences
8764a1cd9977.sentence: Not all of the difference between the treatment and control groups at time 2 (that is, the difference between P2 and S2) can be explained as being an effect of the treatment, because the treatment group and control group did not start out at the same point at time 1.

dd1621db8e04.title: Difference in differences
dd1621db8e04.sentence: DiD, therefore, calculates the "normal" difference in the outcome variable between the two groups (the difference that would still exist if neither group experienced the treatment), represented by the dotted line Q. (Notice that the slope from P1 to Q is the same as the slope from S1 to S2.) The treatment effect is the difference between the observed outcome (P2) and the "normal" outcome (the difference between P2 and Q).

4ece547ef4ac.sentence: In many applications including econometrics and biostatistics a fixed effects model refers to a regression model in which the group means are fixed (non-random) as opposed to a random effects model in which the group means are a random sample from a population.

3687045386bc.sentence: In statistics, econometrics, epidemiology and related disciplines, the quasi-experimental method of instrumental variables (IV) is used to estimate causal relationships when controlled experiments are not feasible or when a treatment is not successfully delivered to every unit in a randomized experiment.

e56ceef2ccfe.title: Instrumental variables
e56ceef2ccfe.sentence: Informally, in attempting to estimate the causal effect of some variable X ("covariate" or "explanatory variable") on another Y ("dependent variable"), an instrument is a third variable Z which affects Y only through its effect on X.

2cd239d720e7.title: Instrumental variables

fb6e8f7a2b6c.title: Instrumental variables
fb6e8f7a2b6c.sentence: When used, a valid instrument changes the explanatory variable (the variable correlated with the endogenous variable) but has no independent effect on the dependent variable and is not correlated with the error term, thus allowing a researcher or analyst to uncover the true causal effect of the explanatory variable on the dependent variable.

a2e77a95074c.title: Instrumental variables

eea4f5051a1a.sentence: Regression discontinuity designs (RDD) are a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design that attempts to determine the causal effects of interventions by assigning a cutoff or threshold above or below which an intervention is assigned.

cb97315d1a4d.title: Truncated regression model
cb97315d1a4d.sentence: Truncated regression models are a class of models in which the sample has been truncated for certain ranges of the dependent variable.

9d794bdb9b10.title: Truncated regression model

23a87b1f1d18.title: Truncated regression model

45713b721f1b.title: Truncated regression model
45713b721f1b.sentence: This is in contrast to censored regression models where only the value of the dependent variable is clustered at a lower threshold, an upper threshold, or both, while the value for independent variables is available.

a71613e28773.title: Truncated regression model

b0ad7e4db2e6.title: Logistic regression
b0ad7e4db2e6.sentence: In statistics, a logistic model (or logit model) is a statistical model that models the log-odds of an event as a linear combination of one or more independent variables.

4a2a745fc68c.title: Logistic regression

5a5164029056.title: Logistic regression

fdbdae7565fb.title: Propensity score matching
fdbdae7565fb.sentence: In the statistical analysis of observational data, propensity score matching (PSM) is a statistical matching technique that attempts to estimate the effect of a treatment, policy, or other intervention by accounting for the covariates that predict receiving the treatment.

b0b816316cc8.title: Propensity score matching
b0b816316cc8.sentence: The "propensity" describes how likely a unit is to have been treated, given its covariate values.

f7e7777f719b.title: Propensity score matching
f7e7777f719b.sentence: Paul R. Rosenbaum and Donald Rubin introduced the technique in 1983, defining the propensity score as the conditional probability of a unit (e.g., person, classroom, school) being assigned to the treatment, given a set of observed covariates.

d19dc6c00f24.title: Propensity score matching
d19dc6c00f24.sentence: Matching attempts to reduce the treatment assignment bias, and mimic randomization, by creating a sample of units that received the treatment that is comparable on all observed covariates to a sample of units that did not receive the treatment.

185bd0f8a7f6.title: Propensity score matching
185bd0f8a7f6.sentence: PSM employs a predicted probability of group membership—e.g., treatment versus control group—based on observed predictors, usually obtained from logistic regression to create a counterfactual group.

025fc4ba6333.title: Propensity score matching
025fc4ba6333.sentence: Match each participant to one or more nonparticipants on propensity score, using one of these methods:

4bc66ac05db6.title: Propensity score matching
4bc66ac05db6.sentence: Check that covariates are balanced across treatment and comparison groups within strata of the propensity score.

27136e98b42b.title: Propensity score matching
27136e98b42b.sentence: The key advantages of PSM were, at the time of its introduction, that by using a linear combination of covariates for a single score, it balances treatment and control groups on a large number of covariates without losing a large number of observations.

2b69fc2ca601.title: Propensity score matching
2b69fc2ca601.sentence: If units in the treatment and control were balanced on a large number of covariates one at a time, large numbers of observations would be needed to overcome the "dimensionality problem" whereby the introduction of a new balancing covariate increases the minimum necessary number of observations in the sample geometrically.

11d6bff21dc3.title: Propensity score matching
11d6bff21dc3.sentence: One disadvantage of PSM is that it only accounts for observed (and observable) covariates and not latent characteristics.

288b239bcca6.title: Propensity score matching
288b239bcca6.sentence: As the procedure only controls for observed variables, any hidden bias due to latent variables may remain after matching.

c7a1a487ac26.title: Propensity score matching
c7a1a487ac26.sentence: Another issue is that PSM requires large samples, with substantial overlap between treatment and control groups.

c7f559d5934c.title: Synthetic control method
c7f559d5934c.sentence: In causal inference, synthetic controls are a class of methods where the quasi-experimental control group is synthesized from a weighted average of potential control units.

f1a001700729.title: Synthetic control method
f1a001700729.sentence: A synthetic control is a weighted average of several units (such as regions or companies) combined to recreate the trajectory that the outcome of a treated unit would have followed in the absence of the intervention.

3a426adbfe43.title: Synthetic control method
3a426adbfe43.sentence: The method is often used to evaluate treatment effects in scenarios where only one or a small number of units are treated.

fbc7edb398f7.title: Synthetic control method
fbc7edb398f7.sentence: The weights are selected in a data-driven manner to ensure that the resulting synthetic control closely resembles the treated unit in terms of key predictors of the outcome variable.

fd30dcdda680.title: Synthetic control method
fd30dcdda680.sentence: It typically uses a relatively long time series of the outcome prior to the intervention and estimates weights in such a way that the control group mirrors the treatment group as closely as possible.

6d62f632ead2.title: Synthetic control method
6d62f632ead2.sentence: Unlike difference in differences approaches, this method can account for the effects of confounders changing over time, by weighting the control group to better match the treatment group before the intervention.

44ee998feeb1.title: Synthetic control method
44ee998feeb1.sentence: The synthetic control method combines elements from matching and difference-in-differences techniques.

9899e959a573.title: Synthetic control method
9899e959a573.sentence: The method was first proposed in a series of articles by Alberto Abadie and coauthors.

ca6f3a241a9d.title: Synthetic control method
ca6f3a241a9d.sentence: Synthetic controls have been used in a number of empirical applications, ranging from studies examining natural catastrophes and growth, or civil conflicts and growth, studies that examine the effect of vaccine mandates on childhood immunization, and studies linking political murders to house prices.

8251c5a5ad15.title: Synthetic control method
8251c5a5ad15.sentence: Recently, the synthetic control method is actively used in new drug development when evaluating the causal impact of a treatment or intervention, especially in situations where randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are not feasible.

b43af3d6220c.title: Soil

37fc265244c8.title: Soil

74ce4d15a381.title: Soil

a4ed88d3162f.title: Soil

995ab970d97a.title: Environmentalism

972b181eec0a.title: Environmentalism
972b181eec0a.sentence: Environmentalism advocates the preservation, restoration and improvement of the natural environment and critical earth system elements or processes such as the climate, and may be referred to as a movement to control pollution or protect plant and animal diversity.

a988e1e0863b.title: Environmentalism

d704e0c8117d.title: Autotroph
d704e0c8117d.sentence: Autotrophs produce complex organic compounds (such as carbohydrates, fats, and proteins) using carbon from simple substances such as carbon dioxide, generally using energy from light or inorganic chemical reactions.

e827cc835be0.title: Autotroph
e827cc835be0.sentence: Autotrophs do not need a living source of carbon or energy and are the producers in a food chain, such as plants on land or algae in water.

735f6d84fd26.title: Autotroph
735f6d84fd26.sentence: Thus, heterotrophs – all animals, almost all fungi, and most bacteria and protozoa – depend on autotrophs, or primary producers, for the raw materials and fuel they need.

376b4e5efefb.title: Autotroph
376b4e5efefb.sentence: Plants can only use a fraction (approximately 1%) of this energy for photosynthesis.

468b0b6783ff.title: Autotroph
468b0b6783ff.sentence: The term autotroph was coined by the German botanist Albert Bernhard Frank in 1892.

f2c649ac2a85.title: Autotroph
f2c649ac2a85.sentence: Instead, they consider that the first cells were autotrophs.

4ab0dd42f067.title: Autotroph
4ab0dd42f067.sentence: These autotrophs might have been thermophilic and anaerobic chemolithoautotrophs that lived at deep sea alkaline hydrothermal vents.

9bba8d0089a7.title: Primary production
9bba8d0089a7.sentence: In ecology, primary production is the synthesis of organic compounds from atmospheric or aqueous carbon dioxide.

7f1b280dce36.title: Primary production
7f1b280dce36.sentence: It principally occurs through the process of photosynthesis, which uses light as its source of energy, but it also occurs through chemosynthesis, which uses the oxidation or reduction of inorganic chemical compounds as its source of energy.

929643191ed9.title: Primary production
929643191ed9.sentence: Almost all life on Earth relies directly or indirectly on primary production.

3ee9bde84180.title: Primary production
3ee9bde84180.sentence: The organisms responsible for primary production are known as primary producers or autotrophs, and form the base of the food chain.

06a48e621d94.title: Primary production
06a48e621d94.sentence: In terrestrial ecoregions, these are mainly plants, while in aquatic ecoregions algae predominate in this role.

061f90d657d5.title: Primary production
061f90d657d5.sentence: The main source of such energy is sunlight, but a minute fraction of primary production is driven by lithotrophic organisms, using the chemical energy of inorganic molecules.

1313954eeeb6.title: Primary production
1313954eeeb6.sentence: Primary production on land is a function of many factors, but principally local hydrology and temperature (the latter covaries to an extent with light, specifically photosynthetically active radiation (PAR), the source of energy for photosynthesis).

98438b05d7fe.title: Primary production
98438b05d7fe.sentence: While plants cover much of the Earth's surface, they are strongly curtailed wherever temperatures are too extreme or where necessary plant resources (principally water and PAR) are limiting, such as deserts or polar regions.

dfa1e378991e.title: Primary production
dfa1e378991e.sentence: Using satellite-derived estimates of the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) for terrestrial habitats and sea-surface chlorophyll for the oceans, it is estimated that the total (photoautotrophic) primary production for the Earth was 104.9 petagrams of carbon per year (Pg C yr−1; equivalent to the non-SI Gt C yr−1).

de0ddc823a86.title: Primary production
de0ddc823a86.sentence: Of this, 56.4 Pg C yr−1 (53.8%), was the product of terrestrial organisms, while the remaining 48.5 Pg C yr−1, was accounted for by oceanic production.

d946a5de7881.title: Primary production
d946a5de7881.sentence: Human societies are part of the Earth's NPP cycle but disproportionately influence it.

54cebca39245.title: Biomass (ecology)
54cebca39245.sentence: Biomass is the total mass of living biological organisms in a given area or ecosystem at a specific time.

9d9deba3e033.title: Biomass (ecology)
9d9deba3e033.sentence: In some cases, biomass refers to the wet weight of organisms as they exist in nature.

e388227a7b92.title: Biomass (ecology)
e388227a7b92.sentence: In other contexts, it may refer to dry weight (excluding water content), or to the mass of organic carbon, excluding inorganic components such as bones, shells, or teeth.

48843221753f.title: Biomass (ecology)
48843221753f.sentence: In 2018, Bar-On et al. estimated Earth's total live biomass at approximately 550 billion tonnes of carbon, the majority of which is found in plants.

923e5ad41574.title: Biomass (ecology)
923e5ad41574.sentence: Animals represent less than 0.5% of the total biomass on Earth, with about 2 billion tonnes C in total.

9aa9a4c11930.title: Biomass (ecology)
9aa9a4c11930.sentence: By the year 2020, the mass of human-made materials or anthropogenic mass, defined as "the mass embedded in inanimate solid objects made by humans (that have not yet been demolished or taken out of service)", was projected to surpass that of all living biomass on Earth.

3cb4c6825f79.title: Biomass (ecology)
3cb4c6825f79.sentence: Terrestrial biomass generally decreases markedly at each higher trophic level (plants, herbivores, carnivores).

6f5704bc12ba.title: Biomass (ecology)
6f5704bc12ba.sentence: Ocean or marine biomass, in a reversal of terrestrial biomass, can increase at higher trophic levels.

12fe59cb2056.title: Biomass (ecology)
12fe59cb2056.sentence: However, there is a much more significant difference in standing stocks—while accounting for almost half of the total annual production, oceanic autotrophs account for only about 0.2% of the total biomass.

5eab845d5520.title: Biodiversity loss
5eab845d5520.section: Observations by type of life > Wild mammals
5eab845d5520.sentence: Nowadays, the total biomass of wild mammals on land is believed to be seven times lower than its prehistoric values, while the biomass of marine mammals had declined fivefold.

bb3d6162361c.title: Biodiversity loss
bb3d6162361c.section: Observations by type of life > Wild mammals
bb3d6162361c.sentence: At the same time, the biomass of humans is "an order of magnitude higher than that of all wild mammals", and the biomass of livestock mammals like pigs and cattle is even larger than that.

08d5fb88bf0f.title: Phytoplankton
08d5fb88bf0f.sentence: Phytoplankton (/ˌfaɪtoʊˈplæŋktən/) are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

263fcc81d3e8.title: Phytoplankton
263fcc81d3e8.sentence: Phytoplankton obtain their energy through photosynthesis, as trees and other plants do on land.

7de784f7f936.title: Phytoplankton
7de784f7f936.sentence: This means phytoplankton must receive sunlight, so they live in the well-lit surface layers (euphotic zone) of oceans and lakes.

4d134dd14603.title: Phytoplankton
4d134dd14603.sentence: They account for about half of global photosynthetic activity and at least half of the oxygen production, despite amounting to only about 1% of the global plant biomass.

5e6781fa90f3.title: Phytoplankton
5e6781fa90f3.sentence: Marine phytoplankton perform half of the global photosynthetic CO2 fixation (net global primary production of ~50 Pg C per year) and half of the oxygen production despite amounting to only ~1% of global plant biomass.

3ca20633ec8a.title: Phytoplankton
3ca20633ec8a.sentence: Phytoplankton form the base of marine and freshwater food webs and are key players in the global carbon cycle.

78621ccb13c9.title: Phytoplankton
78621ccb13c9.sentence: Phytoplankton are the key mediators of the biological pump.

ef8ea1b976fc.title: Phytoplankton
ef8ea1b976fc.sentence: At the same time, a certain fraction of this biomass is exported as sinking particles to the deep sea, where it is subject to ongoing transformation processes, e.g., remineralization.

0ab1823384a1.title: Phytoplankton
0ab1823384a1.sentence: Phytoplankton are very diverse, comprising photosynthesizing bacteria (cyanobacteria) and various unicellular protist groups (notably the diatoms).

fcaaa76d631b.title: Phytoplankton
fcaaa76d631b.sentence: There are about 5,000 known species of marine phytoplankton.

725aab311f79.title: Phytoplankton
725aab311f79.sentence: In comparison with terrestrial plants, marine phytoplankton are distributed over a larger surface area, are exposed to less seasonal variation, and have markedly faster turnover rates than trees (days versus decades).

7d2669fc5aa2.title: Phytoplankton
7d2669fc5aa2.sentence: Therefore, phytoplankton respond rapidly on a global scale to climate variations.

cb37f648e3ef.title: Phytoplankton
cb37f648e3ef.sentence: Increases in solar radiation, temperature and freshwater inputs to surface waters strengthen ocean stratification and consequently reduce transport of nutrients from deep water to surface waters, which reduces primary productivity.

be04b679dcfd.title: Phytoplankton
be04b679dcfd.sentence: Some studies indicate that global phytoplankton density has decreased over the past century.

20cca8376d33.title: Abiotic component
20cca8376d33.sentence: In ecology, abiotic components or abiotic factors are non-living chemical and physical parts of the environment that affect living organisms and the functioning of ecosystems.

f3a0a6ad5a6e.title: Abiotic component
f3a0a6ad5a6e.sentence: In biology, abiotic factors can include water, light, radiation, temperature, humidity, atmosphere, acidity, salinity, precipitation, altitude, minerals, tides, rain, dissolved oxygen nutrients, and soil.

b6a1ffa0fe63.title: Abiotic component
b6a1ffa0fe63.sentence: Humans can make or change abiotic factors in a species' environment.

154c322a6382.title: Abiotic component
154c322a6382.sentence: For instance, fertilizers can affect a snail's habitat, or the greenhouse gases which humans utilize can change marine pH levels.

6c00aff37317.title: Abiotic component
6c00aff37317.sentence: For example, there is a significant difference in access to both water and humidity between temperate rain forests and deserts.

e34df3ec20fd.title: Abiotic component
e34df3ec20fd.sentence: These differences in abiotic components alter the species present by creating boundaries of what species can survive within the environment and influencing competition between two species.

39b7505e4755.title: Abiotic component
39b7505e4755.sentence: Abiotic factors such as salinity can give one species a competitive advantage over another, creating pressures that lead to speciation and alteration of a species to and from generalist and specialist competitors.

94ff473587b2.title: Population (biology)
94ff473587b2.sentence: In qualitative terms, it is usually defined as "a group of organisms of the same species occupying a particular space at a particular time".

0999b9d278d1.title: Population (biology)
0999b9d278d1.sentence: Commonly, a population can be described by what individuals constitute the population, its size, a geographical area it occupies, and the time within which the population is examined.

b81d3264bf9c.title: Population (biology)
b81d3264bf9c.sentence: The two main approaches to define a population are ecological and evolutionary.

c03af17f3a0b.title: Population (biology)
c03af17f3a0b.sentence: From the ecological perspective, individuals are considered interacting and competing in a certain geographic area.

e3c4524ca689.title: Population (biology)
e3c4524ca689.sentence: From the evolutionary (genetic) perspective, genes and reproduction are considered the driving forces of a population.

cc6afe66ae37.title: Population (biology)
cc6afe66ae37.sentence: Such populations as a whole constitute a community.

c027d866ce87.title: Population (biology)
c027d866ce87.sentence: Each community consists of populations of animals and plants that live together, interacting and being dependent on each other.

21aa2bf0a8f9.title: Population (biology)
21aa2bf0a8f9.sentence: A census, being defined as a complete count of individuals, is rarely possible to conduct in large populations, but it can be useful in small populations that are easy to count, particularly in applied ecology.

4c2bc5885a45.title: Population (biology)
4c2bc5885a45.sentence: In ecology, the population of a certain species in a certain area can be estimated using the Lincoln index to calculate the total population of an area based on the number of individuals observed.

d258d8205202.title: Population (biology)
d258d8205202.sentence: Spatially separated populations of the same species can be called a metapopulation.

c4d5aa3af54d.title: Heterotroph
c4d5aa3af54d.sentence: A heterotroph (/ˈhɛtərəˌtroʊf, -ˌtrɒf/; from Ancient Greek ἕτερος (héteros), meaning "other", and τροφή (trophḗ), meaning "nourishment") is an organism that cannot produce its own food, instead taking nutrition from other sources of organic carbon, mainly matter from other organisms.

e87de18d84b3.title: Heterotroph
e87de18d84b3.sentence: Living organisms that are heterotrophic include most animals, all fungi, some bacteria and protists, and many parasitic plants.

04557b72f9b1.title: Heterotroph
04557b72f9b1.sentence: In the food chain, heterotrophs are primary, secondary and tertiary consumers, but not producers.

2b0fe8012bca.title: Heterotroph
2b0fe8012bca.sentence: Heterotrophs represent one of the two mechanisms of nutrition (trophic levels), the other being autotrophs (auto = self, troph = nutrition).

ae49c006c0f3.title: Heterotroph
ae49c006c0f3.sentence: Autotrophs use energy from sunlight (photoautotrophs) or oxidation of inorganic compounds (lithoautotrophs) to convert inorganic carbon dioxide to organic carbon compounds and energy to sustain their life.

a658530ef9f0.title: Heterotroph
a658530ef9f0.sentence: Detritivores are heterotrophs which obtain nutrients by consuming detritus (decomposing plant and animal parts as well as feces).

f3574dad2a73.title: Heterotroph
f3574dad2a73.sentence: Heterotrophic microbes' respiration and fermentation account for a large portion of the release of CO2 into the atmosphere, making it available for autotrophs as a source of nutrient and plants as a cellulose synthesis substrate.

69c591c4a024.title: Heterotroph
69c591c4a024.sentence: Respiration in heterotrophs is often accompanied by mineralization, the process of converting organic compounds to inorganic forms.

15e5e00864a9.title: Heterotroph
15e5e00864a9.sentence: Heterotrophs' ability to mineralize essential elements is critical to plant survival.

1f3d2bf879c0.title: Heterotroph
1f3d2bf879c0.sentence: By decomposing dead organic matter, they release essential elements like phosphorus through dephosphorylation, making these nutrients available for other organisms.

4917b6cbe9a9.title: Heterotroph
4917b6cbe9a9.sentence: This process is critical for maintaining soil fertility and supporting plant growth.

3b014d2d69c5.title: Population ecology
3b014d2d69c5.sentence: Population ecology is a field of ecology that deals with the dynamics of species populations and how these populations interact with the environment, such as birth and death rates, and by immigration and emigration.

4c7117e9aa97.title: Population ecology
4c7117e9aa97.sentence: The total number of individuals in a population is defined as a population size, and how dense these individuals are is defined as population density.

cf78dedca893.title: Population ecology
cf78dedca893.sentence: If N1 is the number of individuals at time 1 then N1=N0+B−D+I−E where N0 is the number of individuals at time 0, B is the number of individuals born, D the number that died, I the number that immigrated, and E the number that emigrated between time 0 and time 1.

279ef8a33854.title: Population ecology
279ef8a33854.sentence: In a population, carrying capacity is known as the maximum population size of the species that the environment can sustain, which is determined by resources available.

3cabc7c701e6.title: Population ecology
3cabc7c701e6.sentence: The discipline is important in conservation biology, especially in the development of population viability analysis which makes it possible to predict the long-term probability of a species persisting in a given patch of habitat.

ff5a096c9fa2.title: Population ecology
ff5a096c9fa2.sentence: In fisheries and wildlife management, population is affected by three dynamic rate functions.

f9d9564ce3cf.title: Population ecology
f9d9564ce3cf.sentence: - Natality or birth rate, often recruitment, which means reaching a certain size or reproductive stage.

5d7b098ceb45.title: Population ecology
5d7b098ceb45.sentence: - Mortality, which includes harvest mortality and natural mortality.

b71ac6c21d45.title: Population ecology
b71ac6c21d45.sentence: The beginning of population dynamics is widely regarded as the work of Malthus, formulated as the Malthusian growth model.

d9db822166e8.title: Population ecology
d9db822166e8.sentence: According to Malthus, assuming that the conditions (the environment) remain constant (ceteris paribus), a population will grow (or decline) exponentially.

2e3be2971457.title: Productivity (ecology)
2e3be2971457.sentence: In ecology, productivity is the rate of generation of biomass in an ecosystem, usually expressed in units of mass per volume (unit surface) per unit of time, such as grams per square metre per day (g m−2 d−1).

ce0dc0fd290c.title: Productivity (ecology)
ce0dc0fd290c.sentence: The productivity of autotrophs, such as plants, is called primary productivity, while the productivity of heterotrophs, such as animals, is called secondary productivity.

88de6e064933.title: Productivity (ecology)
88de6e064933.sentence: The productivity of an ecosystem is influenced by a wide range of factors, including nutrient availability, temperature, and water availability.

9d2110d33796.title: Productivity (ecology)
9d2110d33796.sentence: Increased nutrients can stimulate an algal bloom in waterbodies, increasing primary production but making the ecosystem less stable.

1330502c921c.title: Soil

7940666edd25.title: Soil
7940666edd25.sentence: Soil degradation involves acidification, contamination, desertification, erosion or salination.

665dd0b7d6d4.title: Soil

c130af1368cc.title: Soil
c130af1368cc.sentence: More than one kind of erosion can occur simultaneously.

8187296f324e.title: Soil
8187296f324e.sentence: Desertification, an environmental process of ecosystem degradation in arid and semi-arid regions, is often caused by badly adapted human activities such as overgrazing or excess harvesting of firewood.

4190b65b5519.title: Soil

057a8f14aaeb.title: Soil

6c35d6fb9a03.title: Soil
6c35d6fb9a03.sentence: Soil biota can treat waste by transforming it, mainly through microbial enzymatic activity.

94e9ebcafa98.sentence: Gross primary production (GPP) is the amount of chemical energy, typically expressed as carbon biomass, that primary producers create in a given length of time.

fdcfd3b08adf.sentence: Some fraction of this fixed energy is used by primary producers for cellular respiration and maintenance of existing tissues (i.e., "growth respiration" and "maintenance respiration").

32eafeae04e5.sentence: The remaining fixed energy (i.e., mass of photosynthate) is referred to as net primary production (NPP).

b34e1b1b3550.title: Primary production

b34e1b1b3550.sentence: Net primary production is available to be directed toward growth and reproduction of primary producers.

7244bd0502e2.sentence: Ecosystem ecology is the integrated study of living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) components of ecosystems and their interactions within an ecosystem framework.

110b4c49b267.title: Ecosystem
110b4c49b267.sentence: Ecosystem ecology is the "study of the interactions between organisms and their environment as an integrated system".

46952c188df8.sentence: Terrestrial ecosystems are ecosystems that are found on land.

d979918ac925.title: Terrestrial ecosystem
d979918ac925.sentence: Terrestrial ecosystems differ from aquatic ecosystems by the predominant presence of soil rather than water at the surface and by the extension of plants above this soil/water surface in terrestrial ecosystems.

f6b29884a12e.title: Terrestrial ecosystem

e46027b8ebd7.title: Terrestrial ecosystem
e46027b8ebd7.sentence: Because water buffers temperature fluctuations, terrestrial ecosystems usually experience greater diurnal and seasonal temperature fluctuations than do aquatic ecosystems in similar climates.

5a9118b1f626.title: Terrestrial ecosystem
