2e2831661615.title: Soil
2e2831661615.section: Chemistry > Cation and anion exchange > Cation exchange capacity (CEC)
2e2831661615.sentence: Cation exchange capacity is the soil's ability to remove cations from the soil water solution and sequester those to be exchanged later as the plant roots release hydrogen ions to the solution.

226eb4d6dad8.title: Soil
226eb4d6dad8.sentence: The negative or positive charges on colloid particles make them able to hold cations or anions, respectively, to their surfaces.

afc981abb05d.title: Soil
afc981abb05d.sentence: The cation exchange, that takes place between colloids and soil water, buffers (moderates) soil pH, alters soil structure, and purifies percolating water by adsorbing cations of all types, both useful and harmful.

e2cf1fe5c336.title: Soil
e2cf1fe5c336.section: Chemistry > Cation and anion exchange > Cation exchange capacity (CEC)
e2cf1fe5c336.sentence: CEC is the amount of exchangeable hydrogen cations (H+) that will combine with 100 grams dry weight of soil and whose measure is one milliequivalent per 100 grams of soil (1 meq/100 g).

a16a493aa597.title: Soil
a16a493aa597.sentence: The fraction of the negatively-charged soil colloid exchange sites (CEC) that are occupied by base-forming cations is called base saturation.

a3ccab778f94.title: Soil
a3ccab778f94.sentence: A typical soil is about 50% solids (45% mineral and 5% organic matter), and 50% voids (or pores) of which half is occupied by water and half by gas.

410c959f9ddd.title: Soil
410c959f9ddd.sentence: The percent soil mineral and organic content can be treated as a constant (in the short term), while the percent soil water and gas content is considered highly variable whereby a rise in one is simultaneously balanced by a reduction in the other.

57bd0fe38b4b.title: Soil
57bd0fe38b4b.sentence: The consumption of oxygen by microbes and plant roots, and their release of carbon dioxide, decreases oxygen and increases carbon dioxide concentration.

1285acd11fc3.title: Soil
1285acd11fc3.sentence: Atmospheric CO2 concentration is 0.04%, but in the soil pore space it may range from 10 to 100 times that level, thus potentially contributing to the inhibition of root respiration.

7f98582399bf.title: Soil
7f98582399bf.sentence: A horizontal layer of the soil, whose physical features, composition and age are distinct from those above and beneath, is referred to as a soil horizon.

acb176818ed9.title: Soil
acb176818ed9.sentence: Soil is said to be formed when organic matter has accumulated and colloids are washed downward, leaving deposits of clay, humus, iron oxide, carbonate, and gypsum, producing a distinct layer called the B horizon.

50193f725e23.title: Soil
50193f725e23.sentence: Soil reactivity is expressed in terms of pH and is a measure of the acidity or alkalinity of the soil.

7edb9c5c825a.title: Soil
7edb9c5c825a.sentence: More precisely, it is a measure of hydronium concentration in an aqueous solution and ranges in values from 0 to 14 (acidic to basic) but practically speaking for soils, pH ranges from 3.5 to 9.5, as pH values beyond those extremes are toxic to life forms.

b0a84907909e.title: Soil
b0a84907909e.sentence: The resistance of soil to change in pH, as a result of the addition of acid or basic material, is a measure of the buffering capacity of a soil and (for a particular soil type) increases as the CEC increases.

5b3ec31ff024.title: Soil
5b3ec31ff024.sentence: Hence, pure sand has almost no buffering ability, though soils high in colloids (whether mineral or organic) have high buffering capacity.

142a635329b6.title: Environmentalism
142a635329b6.sentence: Anti-environmentalism is a set of ideas and actions that oppose environmentalism as a whole or specific environmental policies or environmental initiatives.

214945f5822e.title: Environmentalism
214945f5822e.sentence: Oppositions can take the form of an organized countermovement, aimed at scientific claims about climate change, environmental policies and regulations, in both national or international spheres.

f0cc40e0c556.title: Environmentalism
f0cc40e0c556.sentence: Anti-environmentalist actors may include workers in industries and companies that are threatened by environmental policies, and anti-environmentalist think tanks.

1887b36d5551.title: Environmentalism
1887b36d5551.sentence: Free market environmentalism is a theory that argues that the free market, property rights, and tort law provide the best tools to preserve the health and sustainability of the environment.

033be4924219.title: Environmentalism
033be4924219.sentence: It considers environmental stewardship to be natural, as well as the expulsion of polluters and other aggressors through individual and class action.

9f19cc7364c2.title: Free-market environmentalism
9f19cc7364c2.sentence: Free-market environmentalists therefore argue that the best way to protect the environment is to clarify and protect property rights.

f02d29d1fd08.title: Free-market environmentalism
f02d29d1fd08.sentence: This allows parties to negotiate improvements in environmental quality.

1ab54a9e6ad3.title: Free-market environmentalism
1ab54a9e6ad3.sentence: It also allows them to use torts to stop environmental harm.

3ac3721a04df.title: Free-market environmentalism
3ac3721a04df.sentence: - The state encodes, provides and enforces laws which override or obscure property rights and thus fail to protect them adequately.

fbc090e22d84.title: Free-market environmentalism
fbc090e22d84.sentence: - Given the technological and legal context in which people operate, transaction costs are too high to allow parties to negotiate to a solution better for the environment.

e78d73fe8fb4.title: Free-market environmentalism
e78d73fe8fb4.sentence: Critics argue that free-market environmentalists have no method of dealing with collective problems like environmental degradation and natural resource depletion because of their rejection of collective regulation and control.

277386cf276e.title: Free-market environmentalism
277386cf276e.sentence: They see natural resources as too difficult to privatize (e.g. water), as well as legal responsibility for pollution and degrading biodiversity as too hard to trace.

293308857baa.title: Environmentalism
293308857baa.sentence: The concept of labor environmentalism refers to the efforts of trade unions to create environmental policies, advocate for environmental issues, and collaborate with environmental groups.

d46ec7460961.title: Environmentalism
d46ec7460961.sentence: Trade unions and international organizations such as the International Labour Organization face the dilemma of having to "navigate the structures of global capitalism and the economic growth paradigm, on the one hand, and the global ecological crisis on the other hand".

f0525d1e56a4.title: Environmentalism
f0525d1e56a4.sentence: To promote green jobs, trade unions developed the concept of a just transition.

317cf3fe8e3f.title: Primary production
317cf3fe8e3f.sentence: In a reversal of the pattern on land, in the oceans, almost all photosynthesis is performed by algae, with a small fraction contributed by vascular plants and other groups.

d9c82db9b5d6.title: Primary production
d9c82db9b5d6.sentence: The sunlit zone of the ocean is called the photic zone (or euphotic zone).

42161676eb09.title: Primary production
42161676eb09.sentence: This is a relatively thin layer (10–100 m) near the ocean's surface where there is sufficient light for photosynthesis to occur.

38ff48b6a542.title: Primary production
38ff48b6a542.sentence: Because of gravitational sinking of particulate material (such as plankton, dead or fecal material), nutrients are constantly lost from the photic zone, and are only replenished by mixing or upwelling of deeper water.

655963ec4001.title: Primary production
655963ec4001.sentence: A major source of iron to the oceans is dust from the Earth's deserts, picked up and delivered by the wind as aeolian dust.

bd0fb49392dc.title: Primary production
bd0fb49392dc.sentence: In regions of the ocean that are distant from deserts or that are not reached by dust-carrying winds (for example, the Southern and North Pacific oceans), the lack of iron can severely limit the amount of primary production that can occur.

72e0d48a8a62.title: Primary production
72e0d48a8a62.sentence: These areas are sometimes known as HNLC (High-Nutrient, Low-Chlorophyll) regions, because the scarcity of iron both limits phytoplankton growth and leaves a surplus of other nutrients.

a64e565d299a.title: Soil fertility
a64e565d299a.sentence: Nitrogen and potassium are also needed in substantial amounts.

01000ff56507.title: Soil fertility
01000ff56507.sentence: For this reason these three elements are always identified on a commercial fertilizer analysis.

7e72da5b1c80.title: Soil fertility
7e72da5b1c80.sentence: Bioavailable phosphorus (available to soil life) is the element in soil that is most often lacking, in particular in humid tropical soils.

fdde66b48e30.title: Soil fertility
fdde66b48e30.sentence: For example, a 10-10-15 fertilizer has 10 percent nitrogen, 10 percent available phosphorus (P2O5) and 15 percent water-soluble potassium (K2O).

6ad547e6eeff.title: Soil fertility
6ad547e6eeff.sentence: Inorganic fertilizers are generally less labour intensive and have higher concentrations of nutrients than organic fertilizers.

c9ab871716e4.title: Soil fertility
c9ab871716e4.sentence: Also, since nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium generally must be in the inorganic forms to be taken up by plants, inorganic fertilizers are generally immediately bioavailable to plants without modification.

74450c58097d.title: Soil fertility
74450c58097d.sentence: Soil depletion occurs when the components which contribute to fertility are removed and not replaced, and the conditions which support soil's fertility are not maintained.

7f4bdfb1521d.title: Soil fertility
7f4bdfb1521d.sentence: This leads to poor crop yields, now becoming a global problem.

cc01f90cc285.title: Soil fertility
cc01f90cc285.sentence: In agriculture, soil depletion can be due to excessively intensive cultivation and inadequate soil management.

9f3afe43cb0d.title: Soil fertility
9f3afe43cb0d.sentence: Depletion may occur through a variety of other effects, including over-tillage (which damages soil structure), overuse of nutrient inputs which leads to mining of the soil nutrient bank, and salinization of soil.

dcf95c05d6f2.title: Soil fertility
dcf95c05d6f2.sentence: Many countries in Africa also undergo a depletion of fertile soil, in particular in sub-Saharan Africa (Sahel) under high population pressure.

b92ea1716292.title: Autotroph
b92ea1716292.sentence: Chemolithotrophs produce biomass from the oxidation of inorganic chemical compounds.

c1c6b9e75bb4.title: Autotroph
c1c6b9e75bb4.sentence: They can sustain themselves entirely on atmospheric CO2 and inorganic chemicals without the need for light or organic compounds.

b5bc3b120a0e.title: Autotroph
b5bc3b120a0e.sentence: They are frequently found in hydrothermal vents in the deep ocean and include some archaea and bacteria (unicellular organisms).

ed2d1c1c1010.title: Autotroph
ed2d1c1c1010.sentence: These substrates primarily include hydrogen, iron, nitrogen, and sulfur.

8a6209eb12f7.title: Trophic level
8a6209eb12f7.sentence: An exception occurs in deep-sea hydrothermal ecosystems, where there is no sunlight.

1c0d373f9f37.title: Trophic level
1c0d373f9f37.sentence: Here primary producers manufacture food through a process called chemosynthesis.

bec77abfe4fb.title: Ecosystem diversity
bec77abfe4fb.sentence: Ecosystem diversity deals with the variations in ecosystems within a geographical location and its overall impact on human existence and the environment.

6a0ebdd6dd4f.title: Ecosystem diversity
6a0ebdd6dd4f.sentence: It is a variation in the ecosystems found in a region or the variation in ecosystems over the whole planet.

d25f12e5fbc9.title: Ecosystem diversity
d25f12e5fbc9.sentence: Ecosystem diversity addresses the combined characteristics of biotic properties which are living organisms (biodiversity) and abiotic properties such as nonliving things like water or soil (geodiversity).

a5b4f7aae4b3.title: Ecosystem diversity
a5b4f7aae4b3.sentence: Ecological diversity includes the variation in both terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.

4527d7e768de.title: Ecosystem diversity
4527d7e768de.sentence: An example of ecological diversity on a global scale would be the variation in ecosystems, such as deserts, forests, grasslands, wetlands and oceans.

6cb6cce84572.title: Ecosystem diversity
6cb6cce84572.sentence: Ecological diversity is the largest scale of biodiversity, and within each ecosystem, there is a great deal of both species and genetic diversity.

882b6f634245.title: Ecosystem diversity
882b6f634245.sentence: Ecosystem diversity boosts the availability of oxygen via the process of photosynthesis amongst plant organisms domiciled in the habitat.

afb049b59cf2.title: Ecosystem diversity
afb049b59cf2.sentence: Diversity in an aquatic environment helps in the purification of water by plant varieties for use by humans.

6aa4c2203018.title: Ecosystem diversity
6aa4c2203018.sentence: Diversity increases plant varieties which serve as a good source for medicines and herbs for human use.

237ecde17295.title: Ecosystem diversity
237ecde17295.section: Ecosystem diversity as a result of evolutionary pressure
237ecde17295.sentence: Crop pollinating insects are worth annually $14.6 billion to the US economy and the cost to hand pollinate over insect pollination is estimated to cost $5,715-$7,135 more per hectare.

95709afcfb11.title: Population ecology
95709afcfb11.sentence: Survivorship curves are graphs that show the distribution of survivors in a population according to age.

da679adc9b0e.title: Population ecology
da679adc9b0e.sentence: A Type I survivorship curve is characterized by the fact that death occurs in the later years of an organism's life (mostly mammals).

08ca10235a38.title: Population ecology
08ca10235a38.sentence: Typically, Type I survivorship curves characterize K-selected species.

2bf4cb2fd9a0.title: Population ecology
2bf4cb2fd9a0.sentence: Type II survivorship shows that death at any age is equally probable.

a45904cefc49.title: Population ecology
a45904cefc49.sentence: Type III curves indicate few surviving the younger years, but after a certain age, individuals are much more likely to survive.

f3c3b777537b.title: Productivity (ecology)
f3c3b777537b.sentence: The connection between plant productivity and biodiversity is a significant topic in ecology, although it has been controversial for decades.

89f9762b563f.title: Productivity (ecology)
89f9762b563f.sentence: According to some research on the correlation between plant diversity and ecosystem functioning is that productivity increases as species diversity increases.

c760ee7be383.title: Productivity (ecology)
c760ee7be383.sentence: One reasoning for this is that the likelihood of discovering a highly productive species increases as the number of species initially present in an ecosystem increases.

82163037f049.title: Productivity (ecology)
82163037f049.sentence: Other researchers believe that the relationship between species diversity and productivity is unimodal within an ecosystem.

3e000cbeee35.title: Productivity (ecology)
3e000cbeee35.sentence: More recently, a meta-analysis of 44 studies from various ecosystem types observed that the interaction between diversity and production was unimodal in all but one study.

d1c2f0e1708b.title: Productivity (ecology)
d1c2f0e1708b.sentence: A 1999 study on grassland ecosystems in Europe, for example, found that increasing species diversity initially increased productivity but gradually leveled off at intermediate levels of diversity.

eda687f5083e.title: Productivity (ecology)
eda687f5083e.sentence: Secondary production is the generation of biomass of heterotrophic (consumer) organisms in a system.

63b751a453f5.title: Productivity (ecology)
63b751a453f5.sentence: This is driven by the transfer of organic material between trophic levels, and represents the quantity of new tissue created through the use of assimilated food.

960bdd754e3a.title: Productivity (ecology)
960bdd754e3a.sentence: Secondary production can be estimated through a number of different methods including increment summation, removal summation, the instantaneous growth method and the Allen curve method.

579cc237661e.title: Conservation biology
579cc237661e.sentence: Conservation biology is the study of the conservation of nature and of Earth's biodiversity with the aim of protecting species, their habitats, and ecosystems from excessive rates of extinction and the erosion of biotic interactions.

732c0ec684be.title: Conservation biology
732c0ec684be.sentence: It is an interdisciplinary subject drawing on natural and social sciences, and the practice of natural resource management.

2314e27ab7c2.title: Ecological niche
2314e27ab7c2.sentence: Over time, two competing species can either coexist, through niche differentiation or other means, or compete until one species becomes locally extinct.

e1d30135d4d2.title: Conservation biology
e1d30135d4d2.sentence: The term conservation biology and its conception as a new field originated with the convening of "The First International Conference on Research in Conservation Biology" held at the University of California, San Diego in La Jolla, California, in 1978 led by American biologists Bruce A. Wilcox and Michael E. Soulé with a group of leading university and zoo researchers and conservationists including Kurt Benirschke, Sir Otto Frankel, Thomas Lovejoy, and Jared Diamond.

5a0d998dcdc2.title: Conservation biology
5a0d998dcdc2.sentence: The rapid decline of established biological systems around the world means that conservation biology is often referred to as a "Discipline with a deadline".

71d0fd8e2b2c.title: Conservation biology
71d0fd8e2b2c.sentence: Conservation may be classified as either in-situ conservation, which is protecting an endangered species in its natural habitat, or ex-situ conservation, which occurs outside the natural habitat.

5d6c3e9ab830.title: Conservation biology
5d6c3e9ab830.sentence: Ex-situ conservation, on the other hand, involves protection outside of an organism's natural habitat, such as on reservations or in gene banks, in circumstances where viable populations may not be present in the natural habitat.

9d5b009538c2.title: Conservation biology
9d5b009538c2.section: Concepts and foundations > Economic values and natural capital
9d5b009538c2.sentence: Conservation biologists have started to collaborate with leading global economists to determine how to measure the wealth and services of nature and to make these values apparent in global market transactions.

652584caebde.title: Conservation biology
652584caebde.section: Concepts and foundations > Economic values and natural capital
652584caebde.sentence: This system of accounting is called natural capital and would, for example, register the value of an ecosystem before it is cleared to make way for development.

61a8f5a12bcb.title: Conservation biology
61a8f5a12bcb.sentence: The global extinction rate may be approximately 1,000 times higher than the natural background extinction rate.

7c558d8efe94.title: Conservation biology
7c558d8efe94.section: Concepts and foundations > Ethics and values
7c558d8efe94.sentence: A conservationist may be inspired by the resource conservation ethic, which seeks to identify what measures will deliver "the greatest good for the greatest number of people for the longest time." In contrast, some conservation biologists argue that nature has an intrinsic value that is independent of anthropocentric usefulness or utilitarianism.

7eae5ccb77f8.title: Conservation biology
7eae5ccb77f8.section: Concepts and foundations > Strategic species concepts > Indicator species
7eae5ccb77f8.sentence: An indicator species has a narrow set of ecological requirements, therefore they become useful targets for observing the health of an ecosystem.

1358f5789e91.title: Conservation biology
1358f5789e91.section: Concepts and foundations > Strategic species concepts > Indicator species
1358f5789e91.sentence: Some animals, such as amphibians with their semi-permeable skin and linkages to wetlands, have an acute sensitivity to environmental harm and thus may serve as a miner's canary.

a1da53caa76b.title: Conservation biology
a1da53caa76b.section: Concepts and foundations > Strategic species concepts > Indicator species
a1da53caa76b.sentence: Indicator species are monitored in an effort to capture environmental degradation through pollution or some other link to proximate human activities.

0b1c7318c627.title: Conservation biology
0b1c7318c627.section: Concepts and foundations > Strategic species concepts > Indicator species
0b1c7318c627.sentence: Monitoring an indicator species is a measure to determine if there is a significant environmental impact that can serve to advise or modify practice, such as through different forest silviculture treatments and management scenarios, or to measure the degree of harm that a pesticide may impart on the health of an ecosystem.

cd1c2176f704.title: Conservation biology
cd1c2176f704.section: Concepts and foundations > Strategic species concepts > Indicator species
cd1c2176f704.sentence: It is generally recommended that multiple indicators (genes, populations, species, communities, and landscape) be monitored for effective conservation measurement that prevents harm to the complex, and often unpredictable, response from ecosystem dynamics (Noss, 1997).

75751be35b55.title: Conservation biology
75751be35b55.section: Concepts and foundations > Systematic conservation planning
75751be35b55.sentence: Systematic conservation planning is an effective way to seek and identify efficient and effective types of reserve design to capture or sustain the highest priority biodiversity values and to work with communities in support of local ecosystems.

0decc7e7de63.title: Conservation biology
0decc7e7de63.section: Concepts and foundations > Systematic conservation planning
0decc7e7de63.sentence: Margules and Pressey identify six interlinked stages in the systematic planning approach:

ec7a333178f7.title: Conservation biology
ec7a333178f7.section: Concepts and foundations > Systematic conservation planning
ec7a333178f7.sentence: - Compile data on the biodiversity of the planning region

6d687f91c6eb.title: Conservation biology
6d687f91c6eb.section: Concepts and foundations > Systematic conservation planning
6d687f91c6eb.sentence: - Identify conservation goals for the planning region

8987fc9f4014.title: Conservation biology
8987fc9f4014.section: Concepts and foundations > Systematic conservation planning

d865f06f47d3.title: Conservation biology
d865f06f47d3.section: Concepts and foundations > Systematic conservation planning
d865f06f47d3.sentence: - Maintain the required values of conservation areas

e112dbb94ba6.title: Conservation biology
e112dbb94ba6.section: Concepts and foundations > Systematic conservation planning
e112dbb94ba6.sentence: Systematic strategies generally employ the services of Geographic Information Systems to assist in the decision-making process.

71734b696b56.title: Habitat
71734b696b56.sentence: In ecology, habitat refers to the array of resources and biotic factors that are present in an area, such as to support the survival and reproduction of a particular species.

7d40ae9bf83b.title: Habitat
7d40ae9bf83b.sentence: A species' habitat can be seen as the physical manifestation of its ecological niche.

99346c53e6dd.title: Habitat
99346c53e6dd.sentence: The physical factors may include (for example): soil, moisture, range of temperature, and light intensity.

9fa3604f9be2.title: Habitat
9fa3604f9be2.sentence: Biotic factors include the availability of food and the presence or absence of predators.

7b4f89a3bc2e.title: Habitat
7b4f89a3bc2e.sentence: Every species has particular habitat requirements, habitat generalist species are able to thrive in a wide array of environmental conditions while habitat specialist species require a very limited set of factors to survive.

68c3951039c3.title: Habitat
68c3951039c3.sentence: The large blue butterfly Phengaris arion is much more specific in its requirements; it is found only in chalk grassland areas, its larvae feed on Thymus species, and because of complex life cycle requirements it inhabits only areas in which Myrmica ants live.

27906c18a51c.title: Habitat
27906c18a51c.sentence: Terrestrial habitat types include forests, grasslands, wetlands and deserts.

e06f609d6414.title: Habitat
e06f609d6414.sentence: Freshwater habitat types include rivers, streams, lakes, ponds, marshes and bogs.

f3eb3e967ee5.title: Habitat
f3eb3e967ee5.sentence: Loss of habitat is the single greatest threat to any species.

aef3a287d656.title: Habitat
aef3a287d656.sentence: Habitat destruction is in fact the leading cause of biodiversity loss and species extinction worldwide.

ea479ffa75b0.title: Habitat
ea479ffa75b0.sentence: The protection of habitat types is a necessary step in the maintenance of biodiversity because if habitat destruction occurs, the animals and plants reliant on that habitat suffer.

4c7eedad9a93.title: Habitat
4c7eedad9a93.sentence: This may take the form of the setting up of national parks, forest reserves and wildlife reserves, or it may restrict the activities of humans with the objective of benefiting wildlife.

d0adbf07f9bb.title: Afforestation
d0adbf07f9bb.sentence: One significant criticism of reforestation or afforestation efforts that rely on monocultures of - usually conifer - trees is that, while they may increase tree cover, they fail to provide the diverse and complex habitat needed by most woodland creatures.

f7954756fa96.title: Ecological niche
f7954756fa96.sentence: In ecology, a niche refers to the specific environmental condition occupied by a species or population.

d6528df51cf5.title: Ecological niche
d6528df51cf5.sentence: Different definitions have been proposed for the ecological niche, though they mainly revolve around describing the relationship between a species or population and its environment.

09dc5fc7d783.title: Ecological niche
09dc5fc7d783.sentence: The term was coined in 1910 by Roswell Hill Johnson, but the first conceptual work done in the context of ecology research was by Joseph Grinnell in 1917.

102eb1595852.title: Ecological niche
102eb1595852.sentence: The Grinnellian niche concept embodies the idea that the niche of a species is determined by the habitat in which it lives and its accompanying behavioral adaptations.

0b128839b737.title: Ecological niche
0b128839b737.sentence: In other words, the niche is the sum of the habitat requirements and behaviors that allow a species to persist and produce offspring.

479c4b513e33.title: Ecological niche
479c4b513e33.sentence: In 1927 Charles Sutherland Elton, a British ecologist, defined a niche as follows: "The 'niche' of an animal means its place in the biotic environment, its relations to food and enemies."

c87aec41a1e0.title: Ecological niche
c87aec41a1e0.sentence: The different dimensions, or plot axes, of a niche represent different biotic and abiotic variables.

5ac87d6d440d.title: Ecological niche
5ac87d6d440d.sentence: These factors may include descriptions of the organism's life history, habitat, trophic position (place in the food chain), and geographic range.

5fac84ec0410.title: Ecological niche
5fac84ec0410.sentence: Once a niche is left vacant, other organisms can fill that position.

b3d016a9ff22.title: Ecological niche
b3d016a9ff22.sentence: Also, when plants and animals are introduced into a new environment, they have the potential to occupy or invade the niche or niches of native organisms, often outcompeting the indigenous species.

8e8e3157a319.title: Biodiversity loss
8e8e3157a319.sentence: Every species has evolved to exist within a certain ecological niche, but climate change leads to changes of temperature and average weather patterns.

b25b41187786.title: Ecological niche
b25b41187786.sentence: The term was coined by the naturalist Roswell Hill Johnson but Joseph Grinnell was probably the first to use it in a research program in 1917, in his paper "The niche relationships of the California Thrasher".

2cb0af90b02f.title: Community (ecology)
2cb0af90b02f.sentence: In ecology, a community is a group or association of populations of multiple species occupying the same geographical area at the same time.

d0a831b2092b.title: Community (ecology)
d0a831b2092b.sentence: Such a grouping is also known as a biocoenosis, biotic community, biological community, ecological community, or life assemblage.

72fa393aed2b.title: Community (ecology)
72fa393aed2b.sentence: Community ecology or synecology is the study of the interactions between species in communities on many spatial and temporal scales, including the distribution, structure, abundance, demography, and interactions of coexisting populations.

0b48b043cfca.title: Community (ecology)
0b48b043cfca.sentence: Within the community, each species occupies a niche.

cc81e93f1406.title: Community (ecology)
cc81e93f1406.sentence: By having different niches species are able to coexist.

f652b52c5cfa.title: Community (ecology)
f652b52c5cfa.sentence: Certain species have a greater influence on the community through their direct and indirect interactions with other species.

f9a9420044a5.title: Community (ecology)
f9a9420044a5.sentence: The loss of these species results in large changes to the community, often reducing the stability of the community.

71eb94fef026.title: Community (ecology)
71eb94fef026.sentence: It is often measured through biological networks, such as food webs.

9a0097bbcfcf.title: Biome
9a0097bbcfcf.sentence: A biome (/ˈbaɪ.oʊm/, BY-ohm) is a distinct geographical region with specific climate, vegetation, and animal life.

17adc548e3e8.title: Biome
17adc548e3e8.sentence: It consists of a biological community that has formed in response to its physical environment and regional climate.

02f655175754.title: Biome
02f655175754.sentence: The International Biological Program (1964–74) projects popularized the concept of biome.

6ceb772f4de9.title: Biome
6ceb772f4de9.sentence: To divide the world into a few ecological zones is difficult, notably because of the small-scale variations that exist everywhere on earth and because of the gradual changeover from one biome to the other.

652adf16634a.title: Biome
652adf16634a.sentence: Their boundaries must therefore be drawn arbitrarily and their characterization made according to the average conditions that predominate in them.

42af3121ed3e.title: Biome
42af3121ed3e.sentence: Anthropogenic climate change has the potential to greatly alter the distribution of Earth's biomes.

69d404505e1f.title: Biome
69d404505e1f.sentence: More specifically, between 54% and 22% of global land area will experience climates that correspond to other biomes.

06929b7fa923.title: Biome
06929b7fa923.sentence: 3.6% of land area will experience climates that are completely new or unusual.

6bc29e2526ed.title: Biome
6bc29e2526ed.sentence: An example of a biome shift is woody plant encroachment, which can change grass savanna into shrub savanna.

0820f7ad54ba.title: Ecological succession
0820f7ad54ba.sentence: Ecological succession is the process of how species compositions change in an ecological community over time.

ab8551b4a4e4.title: Ecological succession
ab8551b4a4e4.sentence: The two main categories of ecological succession are primary succession and secondary succession.

d734178b9d06.title: Ecological succession
d734178b9d06.sentence: Primary succession occurs after the initial colonization of a newly created habitat with no living organisms.

5edf7af86c97.title: Ecological succession
5edf7af86c97.sentence: Secondary succession occurs after a disturbance such as fire, habitat destruction, or a natural disaster destroys a pre-existing community.

0a97bc2401b2.title: Ecological succession
0a97bc2401b2.sentence: Ecological succession is driven by feedbacks between plants and their environment.

1738bcdd4705.title: Ecological succession
1738bcdd4705.sentence: As plants grow following a disturbance, they change their environment, for example by creating shade, attracting seed dispersers, contributing organic matter to the soil, changing the availability of soil nutrients, creating microhabitats, and buffering temperature and moisture fluctuations.

ba702884d1cb.title: Ecological succession
ba702884d1cb.sentence: This creates opportunities for different plants to grow, which causes directional change in the ecosystem.

3b789ce0f691.title: Ecological succession
3b789ce0f691.sentence: Communities in early succession will be dominated by fast-growing, well-dispersed species (opportunist, fugitive, or r-selected life-histories).

ab04e16a3bfa.title: Ecological succession
ab04e16a3bfa.sentence: Species diversity, overall plant biomass, plant lifespans, the importance of decomposer organisms, and overall stability all increase as a community approaches a climax state, while the rate at which soil nutrients are consumed, rate of biogeochemical cycling, and rate of net primary productivity all decrease as a community approaches a climax state.

940e5586cf4e.title: Ecological succession
940e5586cf4e.section: Succession by habitat type > Grassland succession
940e5586cf4e.sentence: Rather, grasslands undergo a centuries-long process of succession, and a grassland that is tilled up for agriculture or otherwise destroyed is estimated to take a minimum of 100 years, and potentially on average 1,400 years, to recover to its previous level of biodiversity.

18bb2e6691a8.title: Ecological succession
18bb2e6691a8.section: Factors > Dispersal limitation vs. environmental filtering
18bb2e6691a8.sentence: Succession is impacted both by the ability of seeds to disperse to new sites, and the suitability of site conditions for those seeds to grow and survive.

283b62f264f5.title: Ecological succession
283b62f264f5.section: Factors > Dispersal limitation vs. environmental filtering
283b62f264f5.sentence: Dispersal limitation means that even though favorable sites for a plant to live might exist, the plant's seeds may be unable to reach those sites.

ca4c9aee67b6.title: Ecological succession
ca4c9aee67b6.section: Factors > Dispersal limitation vs. environmental filtering
ca4c9aee67b6.sentence: Environmental filtering, also called establishment limitation, implies that although seeds may be distributed to a site, those seeds may be unable to survive due to various characteristics of the site.

9f55448f14ef.title: Ecological succession
9f55448f14ef.sentence: Stotchastic events are succession is influenced partially by random chance, but it is debated how much random chance directs the trajectory of succession, as opposed to more deterministic factors.

23a5d2144176.title: Ecological succession
23a5d2144176.sentence: In 1916, Frederic Clements published a descriptive theory of succession and advanced it as a general ecological concept.

cfafabfeac9c.title: Ecological succession
cfafabfeac9c.sentence: Between 1899 and 1910, Henry Chandler Cowles, at the University of Chicago, developed a more formal concept of succession.

32969e83f5e8.title: Ecological succession
32969e83f5e8.sentence: In 1969, Eugene Odum published The Strategy of Ecosystem Development, a paper that was highly influential to conservation and environmental restoration.

e97c0ba0e861.title: Competition (biology)
e97c0ba0e861.sentence: Competition is an interaction between organisms or species in which both require one or more resources that are in limited supply (such as food, water, or territory).

9e153fb9f6dd.title: Competition (biology)
9e153fb9f6dd.sentence: Competition lowers the fitness of both organisms involved since the presence of one of the organisms always reduces the amount of the resource available to the other.

b507d6c5139a.title: Competition (biology)
b507d6c5139a.sentence: Competition among members of the same species is known as intraspecific competition, while competition between individuals of different species is known as interspecific competition.

369e14cb9dea.title: Competition (biology)
369e14cb9dea.sentence: Studies show that intraspecific competition can regulate population dynamics (changes in population size over time).

260d006544e8.title: Competition (biology)
260d006544e8.sentence: This occurs because individuals become crowded as the population grows.

010354f9cdf9.title: Competition (biology)
010354f9cdf9.sentence: Some individuals (typically small juveniles) eventually do not acquire enough resources and die or do not reproduce.

0f8291893df8.title: Competition (biology)
0f8291893df8.sentence: Competition is one of many interacting biotic and abiotic factors that affect community structure, species diversity, and population dynamics (shifts in a population over time).

8dc7194ea839.title: Competition (biology)
8dc7194ea839.sentence: To explain how species coexist, in 1934 Georgii Gause proposed the competitive exclusion principle which is also called the Gause principle: species cannot coexist if they have the same ecological niche.

b8a77742170a.title: Competition (biology)
b8a77742170a.sentence: An example among animals could be the case of cheetahs and lions; since both species feed on similar prey, they are negatively impacted by the presence of the other because they will have less food, however, they still persist together, despite the prediction that under competition one will displace the other.

6e1c6be52cf5.title: Wildlife conservation
6e1c6be52cf5.sentence: Wildlife conservation refers to the practice of protecting wild species and their habitats in order to maintain healthy wildlife species or populations and to restore, protect or enhance natural ecosystems.

da429313fc17.title: Wildlife conservation
da429313fc17.sentence: Major threats to wildlife include habitat destruction, degradation, fragmentation, overexploitation, poaching, pollution, climate change, and the illegal wildlife trade.

7c4b5c7c30ff.title: Wildlife conservation
7c4b5c7c30ff.sentence: According to the IUCN, out of all species assessed, over 42,100 are at risk of extinction and should be under conservation.

8a1ffa2dc9a5.title: Wildlife conservation
8a1ffa2dc9a5.sentence: Expanding to all existing species, a 2019 UN report on biodiversity put this estimate even higher at a million species.

759f8790c9a5.title: Wildlife conservation
759f8790c9a5.sentence: Deforestation causes many threats to wildlife as it not only causes habitat destruction for the many animals that survive in forests, as more than 80% of the world's species live in forests but also leads to further climate change.

74025dfc9079.title: Wildlife conservation
74025dfc9079.section: Threats to wildlife > Illegal wildlife trade
74025dfc9079.sentence: This illegal trading is worth an estimate of 7-23 billion and an annual trade of around 100 million plants and animals.

cdf5c0df3dbd.title: Wildlife conservation
cdf5c0df3dbd.sentence: In the US, the Endangered Species Act of 1973 was passed to protect US species deemed in danger of extinction.

245373ad3938.title: Wildlife conservation
245373ad3938.sentence: In the same year, the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Fauna and Flora (CITES) was passed as part of an international agreement to prevent the global trade of endangered wildlife.

de58c68005ad.title: Wildlife conservation
de58c68005ad.sentence: Habitat conservation is the practice of protecting a habitat in order to protect the species within it.

20900634bf3d.title: Wildlife conservation
20900634bf3d.sentence: This is sometimes preferable to focusing on a single species especially if the species in question has very specific habitat requirements or lives in a habitat with many other endangered species.

09ad8a8cf925.title: Wildlife conservation
09ad8a8cf925.sentence: Monitoring of wildlife populations is an important part of conservation because it allows managers to gather information about the status of threatened species and to measure the effectiveness of management strategies.

9fb63e8482e7.title: Ecosystem engineer
9fb63e8482e7.sentence: An ecosystem engineer is any species that creates, significantly modifies, maintains or destroys a habitat.

66b4166bcb25.title: Ecosystem engineer
66b4166bcb25.sentence: These organisms can have a large impact on species richness and landscape-level heterogeneity of an area.

1b249611afc8.title: Ecosystem engineer
1b249611afc8.sentence: Beavers are the original model for ecosystem engineers; in the process of clearcutting and damming, beavers alter their ecosystem extensively.

23718dc9d13d.title: Ecosystem engineer
23718dc9d13d.sentence: The addition of a dam will change both the distribution and the abundance of many organisms in the area.

4b89c61c539c.title: Ecosystem engineer
4b89c61c539c.sentence: In other words, they are identified as engineers because of their ability to modify resources, not because of their trophic effect.

a1b75a3367f2.title: Ecosystem engineer
a1b75a3367f2.sentence: Keystone species are typically essential because of their trophic effect, while ecosystem engineers are not.

4eb3c18d3d6b.title: Ecosystem engineer
4eb3c18d3d6b.sentence: By modifying the habitat, organisms like the beaver create more habitat heterogeneity and so can support species not found elsewhere.

066b4388f621.title: Ecosystem engineer
066b4388f621.sentence: Thoughts may be that similar to other umbrella species by conserving an ecosystem engineer you may be able to protect the overall diversity of a landscape.

6b614c95682b.title: Ecosystem engineer
6b614c95682b.sentence: Humans are thought to be the most dramatic ecosystem engineers.

5fbe5c872cad.title: Ecosystem engineer
5fbe5c872cad.sentence: Through urban development, agricultural practices, logging, damming and mining, humans have changed the way they interact with the environment.

9ff7aeb848dc.title: Ecosystem engineer
9ff7aeb848dc.sentence: Whales defecate at the surface and release nutrients that boost the growth of phytoplankton.

91e8b23598dc.title: Ecosystem engineer
91e8b23598dc.sentence: As whales migrate across the oceans, and move up and down the water column, they help to spread these nutrients in a process that is known as the "Whale Pump".

036f23bf60e8.title: Ecosystem engineer
036f23bf60e8.sentence: Introduced species, which may be invasive species, are often ecosystem engineers.

e486ff8b0929.title: Ecosystem engineer
e486ff8b0929.sentence: Kudzu, a leguminous plant introduced to the southeast U.S., changes the distribution and number of animal and bird species in the areas it invades.

299470252b51.title: Ecosystem engineer
299470252b51.sentence: The zebra mussel is an ecosystem engineer in North America.

50df6a544993.title: Nutrient cycle
50df6a544993.sentence: Ecosystem engineers can influence nutrient cycling efficiency rates through their actions.

49f2d9e135a7.title: Competitive exclusion principle
49f2d9e135a7.sentence: In ecology, the competitive exclusion principle, sometimes referred to as Gause's law, is a proposition that two species which compete for the same limited resource cannot coexist at constant population sizes.

4cff3abd3daf.title: Competitive exclusion principle
4cff3abd3daf.sentence: The principle has been paraphrased in the maxim "complete competitors cannot coexist".

fb69f1e822fa.title: Competitive exclusion principle
fb69f1e822fa.sentence: When one species has even the slightest advantage over another, the one with the advantage will dominate in the long term.

739699f9dcbc.title: Competitive exclusion principle
739699f9dcbc.sentence: This leads either to the extinction of the weaker competitor or to an evolutionary or behavioral shift toward a different ecological niche.

683f9f277e29.title: Biodiversity loss
683f9f277e29.sentence: Invasive species may drive local native species to extinction via competitive exclusion, niche displacement, or hybridisation with related native species.

7cda3fc15d61.title: Ecological niche
7cda3fc15d61.section: Segregation versus restriction > Relative significance of the mechanisms
7cda3fc15d61.sentence: However, Andrewartha and Birch (1954,1984) and others have pointed out that most natural populations usually don't even approach exhaustion of resources, and too much emphasis on interspecific competition is therefore wrong.

92fd42b11aac.title: Secondary succession
92fd42b11aac.sentence: As opposed to the first, primary succession, secondary succession is a process started by an event (e.g. forest fire, harvesting, hurricane, etc.) that reduces an already established ecosystem (e.g. a forest or a wheat field) to a smaller population of species, and as such secondary succession occurs on preexisting soil whereas primary succession usually occurs in a place lacking soil.

780baaafc579.title: Secondary succession
780baaafc579.sentence: Secondary succession is the ecological succession that occurs after the initial succession has been disrupted and some plants and animals still exist.

4a5633e6d768.title: Secondary succession
4a5633e6d768.sentence: It is usually faster than primary succession as soil is already present, and seeds, roots, and the underground vegetative organs of plants may still survive in the soil.

cf6094f23123.title: Secondary succession
cf6094f23123.sentence: A classic example of secondary succession occurs in oak and hickory forests cleared by wildfire.

87ad8e89bb26.title: Secondary succession
87ad8e89bb26.sentence: Thus, the first plants to grow back are usually annual plants followed within a few years by quickly growing and spreading grasses and other pioneer species.

68ff17d82961.title: Secondary succession
68ff17d82961.sentence: Due to, at least in part, changes in the environment brought on by the growth of the grasses and other species, over many years, shrubs will emerge along with small pine, oak, and hickory trees.

efe325b64a24.title: Secondary succession
efe325b64a24.sentence: Eventually, over 150 years, the forest will reach its equilibrium point where species composition is no longer changing and resembles the community before the fire.

120bb91cd2be.title: Secondary succession
120bb91cd2be.sentence: This equilibrium state is referred to as the climax community, which will remain stable until the next disturbance.

c939852a7a99.title: Secondary succession
c939852a7a99.sentence: Soil carbon stocks also increase upon secondary succession from Imperata grassland to secondary forest.

d683f3d0681f.title: Secondary succession
d683f3d0681f.sentence: Many species require fire events to reproduce, disperse, and establish.

b562457f051b.title: Secondary succession
b562457f051b.sentence: For example, the knobcone pine has closed cones that open for dispersal when exposed to heat caused by forest fires.

52ed5d4ec50f.title: Community (ecology)
52ed5d4ec50f.sentence: Species interact in various ways: competition, predation, parasitism, mutualism, commensalism, etc. The organization of a biological community with respect to ecological interactions is referred to as community structure.

1b3c77c36c86.title: Community (ecology)
1b3c77c36c86.sentence: Mutualism is an interaction between species in which both species benefit.

93414aaeb5a5.title: Community (ecology)
93414aaeb5a5.sentence: An example is Rhizobium bacteria growing in nodules on the roots of legumes.

3f4d75c39651.title: Community (ecology)
3f4d75c39651.sentence: Commensalism is a type of relationship among organisms in which one organism benefits while the other organism is neither benefited nor harmed.

d26c5b95d241.title: Community (ecology)
d26c5b95d241.sentence: For example, an epiphytic orchid attached to the tree for support benefits the orchid but neither harms nor benefits the tree.

1766f84956b4.title: Community (ecology)
1766f84956b4.sentence: The opposite of commensalism is amensalism, an interspecific relationship in which a product of one organism has a negative effect on another organism but the original organism is unaffected.

3a503d96a13e.title: Community (ecology)
3a503d96a13e.sentence: An example is an interaction between tadpoles of the common frog and a freshwater snail.

dd990847541a.title: Community (ecology)
dd990847541a.sentence: Making algae less abundant for the snail, the algae available for the snail is also of lower quality.

79a4fb75b60e.title: Community (ecology)
79a4fb75b60e.sentence: This is a positive-negative interaction, the predator species benefits while the prey species is harmed.

bb74cd1293b2.title: Community (ecology)
bb74cd1293b2.sentence: Parasitism is an interaction in which one organism, the host, is harmed while the other, the parasite, benefits.

1be8ca8d6785.title: Community (ecology)
1be8ca8d6785.sentence: Neutralism is where species interact, but the interaction has no noticeable effects on either species involved.

ab34541b60ff.title: Community (ecology)
ab34541b60ff.sentence: Due to the interconnectedness of communities, true neutralism is rare.

c71aad2fb8d4.title: Parasitism
c71aad2fb8d4.sentence: Parasitism is a close relationship between species, where one organism, the parasite, lives (at least some of the time) on or inside another organism, the host, causing it some harm, and is adapted structurally to this way of life.

0ea8510539de.title: Parasitism
0ea8510539de.sentence: Parasites include single-celled protozoans such as the agents of malaria, sleeping sickness, and amoebic dysentery; animals such as hookworms, lice, mosquitoes, and vampire bats; fungi such as honey fungus and the agents of ringworm; and plants such as mistletoe, dodder, and the broomrapes.

79d2111bd983.title: Parasitism
79d2111bd983.sentence: Unlike saprotrophs, parasites feed on living hosts, though some parasitic fungi, for instance, may continue to feed on hosts they have killed.

cd95d9fe6248.title: Parasitism
cd95d9fe6248.sentence: Parasitism is a major aspect of evolutionary ecology; for example, almost all free-living animals are host to at least one species of parasite.

efbad63cf07c.title: Parasitism
efbad63cf07c.sentence: Vertebrates, the best-studied group, are hosts to between 75,000 and 300,000 species of helminths and an uncounted number of parasitic microorganisms.

b8bec4fab1c9.title: Parasitism
b8bec4fab1c9.sentence: Parasitic plants make up about one per cent of angiosperms and are in almost every biome in the world.

c2628e953fa2.title: Parasitism
c2628e953fa2.sentence: A single parasite species usually has an aggregated distribution across host animals, which means that most hosts carry few parasites, while a few hosts carry the vast majority of parasite individuals.

aabdfef5118f.title: Parasitism
aabdfef5118f.sentence: Several groups of parasites, including microbial pathogens and parasitoidal wasps have been used as biological control agents in agriculture and horticulture.

c03287316082.title: Mutualism (biology)
c03287316082.sentence: Mutualism describes the ecological interaction between two or more species where each species has a net benefit.

e4bb6a5c26a6.title: Mutualism (biology)
e4bb6a5c26a6.sentence: - the nutrient exchange between vascular plants and mycorrhizal fungi,

5d661b24cb00.title: Mutualism (biology)
5d661b24cb00.sentence: - the fertilization of flowering plants by pollinators,

825721570dd9.title: Mutualism (biology)
825721570dd9.sentence: - the ways plants use fruits and edible seeds to encourage animal aid in seed dispersal, and

861ac45d665f.title: Mutualism (biology)
861ac45d665f.sentence: - the way corals become photosynthetic with the help of the microorganism zooxanthellae.

7706fd5db555.title: Mutualism (biology)
7706fd5db555.sentence: Mutualism can be contrasted with interspecific competition, in which each species experiences reduced fitness, and exploitation, and with parasitism, in which one species benefits at the expense of the other.

9331235b294f.title: Mutualism (biology)
9331235b294f.sentence: Mutualistic relationships can be thought of as a form of "biological barter" in mycorrhizal associations between plant roots and fungi, with the plant providing carbohydrates to the fungus in return for primarily phosphate but also nitrogenous compounds.

f84cee2a5be2.title: Mutualism (biology)
f84cee2a5be2.sentence: Other examples include rhizobia bacteria that fix nitrogen for leguminous plants (family Fabaceae) in return for energy-containing carbohydrates.

7b884d7c7461.title: Mutualism (biology)
7b884d7c7461.sentence: Three important types are pollination, cleaning symbiosis, and zoochory.

c16da61dc10c.title: Mutualism (biology)
c16da61dc10c.sentence: Mutualistic symbiosis can sometimes evolve from parasitism or commensalism.

2b7f81cc80db.title: Mutualism (biology)
2b7f81cc80db.sentence: Mutualisms are not static, and can be lost by evolution.

af11bebaaeb6.title: Mutualism (biology)
af11bebaaeb6.sentence: For example, beans may grow up cornstalks as a trellis, while fixing nitrogen in the soil for the corn, a phenomenon that is used in Three Sisters farming.

d6b0712396bb.title: Ecological niche
d6b0712396bb.sentence: In ecology, niche differentiation (also known as niche segregation, niche separation and niche partitioning) refers to the process by which competing species use the environment differently in a way that helps them to coexist.

6e0ae3c64135.title: Ecological niche
6e0ae3c64135.sentence: When two species differentiate their niches, they tend to compete less strongly, and are thus more likely to coexist.

f8e9e5f0af96.title: Ecological niche
f8e9e5f0af96.sentence: Resource partitioning is the phenomenon where two or more species divides out resources like food, space, resting sites etc. to coexist.

95f8de4b5472.title: Ecological niche
95f8de4b5472.sentence: For example, some lizard species appear to coexist because they consume insects of differing sizes.

f9ea1a71a26f.title: Ecological niche
f9ea1a71a26f.section: Niche differentiation > Development > Current competition (The Ghost of Competition Present)
f9ea1a71a26f.sentence: Niche differentiation can arise from current competition.

f12b0f5184fe.title: Ecological niche
f12b0f5184fe.section: Niche differentiation > Development > Via past extinctions (The Ghost of Competition Past)
f12b0f5184fe.sentence: Another way by which niche differentiation can arise is via the previous elimination of species without realized niches.

0d62b0e4d5e0.title: Ecological niche
0d62b0e4d5e0.sentence: In this case, two competing species will evolve different patterns of resource use so as to avoid competition.

f46d375bcbd8.title: Ecological niche
f46d375bcbd8.section: Coexistence without niche differentiation: exceptions to the rule
f46d375bcbd8.sentence: Some competing species have been shown to coexist on the same resource with no observable evidence of niche differentiation and in "violation" of the competitive exclusion principle.

89542f3707cb.title: Ecological niche
89542f3707cb.section: Coexistence without niche differentiation: exceptions to the rule
89542f3707cb.sentence: These beetle species, which eat the same food and occupy the same habitat, coexist without any evidence of segregation or exclusion.

4accf9ecd1da.title: Conservation biology
4accf9ecd1da.section: Context and trends > Threats to biodiversity
4accf9ecd1da.sentence: An acronym that can be used to express the top threats of present-day H.I.P.P.O stands for Habitat Loss, Invasive Species, Pollution, Human Population, and Overharvesting.

2f7431b5105d.title: Conservation biology
2f7431b5105d.section: Context and trends > Threats to biodiversity
2f7431b5105d.sentence: The primary threats to biodiversity are habitat destruction (such as deforestation, agricultural expansion, urban development), and overexploitation (such as wildlife trade).

7a636bdee62f.title: Conservation biology
7a636bdee62f.section: Concepts and foundations > Strategic species concepts > Umbrella and flagship species
7a636bdee62f.sentence: Any protections afforded to the monarch butterfly will at the same time umbrella many other species and habitats.

00b97c4e5173.title: Conservation biology
00b97c4e5173.section: Concepts and foundations > Strategic species concepts > Umbrella and flagship species
00b97c4e5173.sentence: The monarch migrates across North America, covering multiple ecosystems and so requires a large area to exist.

830f86f043d8.title: Conservation biology
830f86f043d8.section: Concepts and foundations > Strategic species concepts > Umbrella and flagship species
830f86f043d8.sentence: An umbrella species is often used as flagship species, which are species, such as the giant panda, the blue whale, the tiger, the mountain gorilla and the monarch butterfly, that capture the public's attention and attract support for conservation measures.

3f00f57d789d.title: Conservation biology
3f00f57d789d.section: Concepts and foundations > Strategic species concepts > Umbrella and flagship species
3f00f57d789d.sentence: Paradoxically, however, conservation bias towards flagship species sometimes threatens other species of chief concern.

4a469cd07012.title: Habitat
4a469cd07012.sentence: A microhabitat consists of the small-scale physical requirements of a particular organism or population.

07704685d66a.title: Habitat
07704685d66a.sentence: Every habitat includes large numbers of microhabitat types with subtly different exposure to light, humidity, temperature, air movement, and other factors.

22fb9a817fdb.title: Habitat
22fb9a817fdb.sentence: The lichens that grow on the north face of a boulder are different from those that grow on the south face, from those on the level top, and those that grow on the ground nearby; the lichens growing in the grooves and on the raised surfaces are different from those growing on the veins of quartz.

ee6cc9039bc8.title: Habitat
ee6cc9039bc8.sentence: The greater the structural diversity in the wood, the greater the number of microhabitat types that will be present.

fda98ae7590c.title: Habitat
fda98ae7590c.sentence: Many animals and plants have taken up residence in urban environments.

23b59f9e1861.title: Habitat
23b59f9e1861.sentence: They tend to be adaptable generalists and use the town's features to make their homes.

f83e4edb43a3.title: Habitat
f83e4edb43a3.sentence: About 2,000 coyotes are thought to live in and around Chicago.

0d646e76a3ef.title: Habitat
0d646e76a3ef.sentence: A survey of dwelling houses in northern European cities in the twentieth century found about 175 species of invertebrate inside them, including 53 species of beetle, 21 flies, 13 butterflies and moths, 13 mites, 9 lice, 7 bees, 5 wasps, 5 cockroaches, 5 spiders, 4 ants and a number of other groups.

3b38c1cf4089.title: Ecotone
3b38c1cf4089.sentence: An ecotone is a transitional area between two plant communities, where these meet and integrate.

2f51f14ee090.title: Ecotone
2f51f14ee090.sentence: Examples include estuary, lagoon, areas between grassland and forest, and areas between freshwater and sea water.

a0144ed5aafa.title: Ecotone
a0144ed5aafa.sentence: - General examples of ecotones include salt marshes and riparian zones.

28d92eed6483.title: Ecotone
28d92eed6483.sentence: An ecotone may be narrow or wide, and it may be local (the zone between a field and forest) or regional (the transition between forest and grassland ecosystems).

bc46c559d1f7.title: Ecotone
bc46c559d1f7.sentence: An ecotone may appear on the ground as a gradual blending of the two communities across a broad area, or it may manifest itself as a sharp boundary line.

61ef1a81bb03.title: Ecotone
61ef1a81bb03.sentence: Ecotones are particularly significant for mobile animals, as they can exploit more than one set of habitats within a short distance.

ee5853744b51.title: Ecotone
ee5853744b51.sentence: The phenomenon of increased variety of plants as well as animals at the community junction is called the edge effect and is essentially due to a locally broader range of suitable environmental conditions or ecological niches.

e35d27211ce3.title: Ecotone
e35d27211ce3.sentence: The word ecotone was coined (and its etymology given) in 1904 in "The Development and Structure of Vegetation" (Lincoln, Nebraska: Botanical Seminar) by Frederic E. Clements.

abfa6f01b72a.title: Biome
abfa6f01b72a.sentence: Whittaker classified biomes using two abiotic factors: precipitation and temperature.

45ec7b563d70.title: Biome
45ec7b563d70.sentence: The eponymously named Heinrich Walter classification scheme considers the seasonality of temperature and precipitation.

a12cf71cbdb5.title: Biome
a12cf71cbdb5.sentence: In 1947, the American botanist and climatologist Leslie Holdridge classified climates based on the biological effects of temperature and rainfall on vegetation under the assumption that these two abiotic factors are the largest determinants of the types of vegetation found in a habitat.

f18ef25f3c98.title: Biome
f18ef25f3c98.sentence: His scheme can be seen as a simplification of Holdridge's; more readily accessible, but missing Holdridge's greater specificity.

73233524fdca.title: Biome
73233524fdca.section: Classifications > Olson & Dinerstein (1998) biomes for WWF / Global 200
73233524fdca.sentence: A team of biologists convened by the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) developed a scheme that divided the world's land area into biogeographic realms (called "ecozones" in a BBC scheme), and these into ecoregions (Olson & Dinerstein, 1998, etc.).

00bb4b42d6f2.title: Biome
00bb4b42d6f2.section: Classifications > Olson & Dinerstein (1998) biomes for WWF / Global 200
00bb4b42d6f2.sentence: Each ecoregion is characterized by a main biome (also called major habitat type).

767a36880c58.title: Biome
767a36880c58.section: Classifications > Olson & Dinerstein (1998) biomes for WWF / Global 200
767a36880c58.sentence: This classification is used to define the Global 200 list of ecoregions identified by the WWF as priorities for conservation.

705052c733f2.title: Biome
705052c733f2.sentence: The number of classification schemes and the variety of determinants used in those schemes, however, should be taken as strong indicators that biomes do not fit perfectly into the classification schemes created.

af66c8176240.title: Anthropogenic biome
af66c8176240.sentence: Anthropogenic biomes, also known as anthromes, human biomes or intensive land-use biomes, describe the terrestrial biosphere in its contemporary, human-altered form using global ecosystem units (biomes) defined by global patterns of sustained direct human interaction with ecosystems.

ba995db0131e.title: Biome
ba995db0131e.sentence: Anthropogenic biomes provide an alternative view of the terrestrial biosphere based on global patterns of sustained direct human interaction with ecosystems, including agriculture, human settlements, urbanization, forestry and other uses of land.

b6861f24f59d.title: Biome
b6861f24f59d.sentence: As a result, vegetation forms predicted by conventional biome systems can no longer be observed across much of Earth's land surface as they have been replaced by crops and rangelands or cities.

f404ee098485.title: Anthropogenic biome
f404ee098485.section: Origin and evolution of the concept
f404ee098485.sentence: Anthromes were first named and mapped by Erle Ellis and Navin Ramankutty in their 2008 paper, "Putting People in the Map: Anthropogenic Biomes of the World".

93be74dd0377.title: Anthropogenic biome
93be74dd0377.section: Anthropogenic transformation of the biosphere > Agriculture (1700–present)
93be74dd0377.sentence: By the year 2000, over half of the Earth's ice free land was transformed into rangelands, croplands, villages and dense settlements, which left less than half of the Earth's land untouched.

13733884b2f1.title: Anthropogenic biome

13733884b2f1.sentence: While 23.4% of remote woodland anthrome is protected, only 2.3% of irrigated village anthrome is protected.

a9f81f2e9981.title: Community (ecology)

a9f81f2e9981.sentence: Holistic theory refers to the idea that a community is defined by the interactions between the organisms in it.

a60a1e37406a.title: Community (ecology)
a60a1e37406a.section: Theories of community structure > Individualistic theory
a60a1e37406a.sentence: Henry Gleason developed the individualistic (also known as open or continuum) concept of community, with the abundance of a population of a species changing gradually along complex environmental gradients.

70bb01d75410.title: Community (ecology)
70bb01d75410.section: Theories of community structure > Holistic theory
70bb01d75410.sentence: Frederic Clements developed the holistic (or organismic) concept of community, as if it were a superorganism or discrete unit, with sharp boundaries.

3d3324ddba03.title: Community (ecology)
3d3324ddba03.section: Theories of community structure > Individualistic theory
3d3324ddba03.sentence: Each species changes independently in relation to other species present along the gradient.

663cc8cc4f74.title: Community (ecology)

663cc8cc4f74.sentence: Association of species is random and due to coincidence.

2cb899f283f7.title: Ecological niche
2cb899f283f7.sentence: The Hutchinsonian niche is an "n-dimensional hypervolume", where the dimensions are environmental conditions and resources, that define the requirements of an individual or a species to practice its way of life, more particularly, for its population to persist.

42ce815996e0.title: Ecological niche
42ce815996e0.sentence: The niche concept was popularized by the zoologist G. Evelyn Hutchinson in 1957.

2b03c9d13204.title: Ecological niche
2b03c9d13204.sentence: Hutchinson inquired into the question of why there are so many types of organisms in any one habitat.

f4fde0c13648.title: Ecological niche
f4fde0c13648.sentence: His work inspired many others to develop models to explain how many and how similar coexisting species could be within a given community, and led to the concepts of 'niche breadth' (the variety of resources or habitats used by a given species), 'niche partitioning' (resource differentiation by coexisting species), and 'niche overlap' (overlap of resource use by different species).

2042ddb41470.title: Ecological niche
2042ddb41470.sentence: The mathematical representation of a species' fundamental niche in ecological space, and its subsequent projection back into geographic space, is the domain of niche modelling.

45c4300304f0.title: Parasitism
45c4300304f0.sentence: As hosts and parasites evolve together, their relationships often change.

6ac6646e218d.title: Parasitism
6ac6646e218d.sentence: When a parasite is in a sole relationship with a host, selection drives the relationship to become more benign, even mutualistic, as the parasite can reproduce for longer if its host lives longer.

105a16dac071.title: Parasitism
105a16dac071.section: Evolutionary ecology > Coevolution > Competition favouring virulence
105a16dac071.sentence: Competition between parasites can be expected to favour faster reproducing and therefore more virulent parasites, by natural selection.

d4a2b7155f8c.title: Parasitism
d4a2b7155f8c.sentence: Hosts have evolved a variety of defensive measures against their parasites, including physical barriers like the skin of vertebrates, the immune system of mammals, insects actively removing parasites, and defensive chemicals in plants.

4781cc1ed582.title: Parasitism
4781cc1ed582.sentence: There are six major parasitic strategies, namely parasitic castration; directly transmitted parasitism; trophically-transmitted parasitism; vector-transmitted parasitism; parasitoidism; and micropredation.

466e9b619f85.title: Parasitism
466e9b619f85.sentence: Vector-transmitted parasites rely on a third party, an intermediate host, where the parasite does not reproduce sexually, to carry them from one definitive host to another.

20ab0b566f1a.title: Parasitism
20ab0b566f1a.sentence: Parasitoids are insects which sooner or later kill their hosts, placing their relationship close to predation.

a2aaff7390f6.title: Parasitism
a2aaff7390f6.sentence: A micropredator attacks more than one host, reducing each host's fitness by at least a small amount, and is only in contact with any one host intermittently.

1f6c0e33680e.title: Parasitism
1f6c0e33680e.sentence: This behavior makes micropredators suitable as vectors, as they can pass smaller parasites from one host to another.

7db8657edc7b.title: Ecological succession
7db8657edc7b.sentence: According to classical ecological theory, succession stops when the sere has arrived at an equilibrium or steady state with the physical and biotic environment.

05a090fca497.title: Ecological succession
05a090fca497.sentence: Barring major disturbances, it will persist indefinitely.

de7dce22a43f.title: Ecological succession
de7dce22a43f.sentence: This end point of succession is called climax.

06aa3bd2d8de.title: Ecological succession
06aa3bd2d8de.sentence: - It has a wide diversity of species, a well-drained spatial structure, and complex food chains.

79c1ccf4f2cd.title: Ecological succession
79c1ccf4f2cd.sentence: There is equilibrium between gross primary production and total respiration, between energy used from sunlight and energy released by decomposition, between uptake of nutrients from the soil and the return of nutrient by litter fall to the soil.

fa761a9c3871.title: Ecological succession
fa761a9c3871.sentence: From about 1900 to 1960, however, understanding of succession was dominated by the theories of Frederic Clements, a contemporary of Cowles, who held that seres were highly predictable and deterministic and converged on a climatically determined stable climax community regardless of starting conditions.

59471a6ca0c5.title: Ecological succession
59471a6ca0c5.sentence: This idea has been largely abandoned by modern ecologists in favor of nonequilibrium ideas of ecosystems dynamics.

d75c236e21be.title: Ecological succession
d75c236e21be.sentence: A seral community is an intermediate stage found in an ecosystem advancing towards its climax community.

f59bb58203a5.title: Ecological succession
f59bb58203a5.sentence: The successional dynamics beginning with colonization of an area with little to no biotic factors is referred to as primary succession.

e8ef66e08e1d.title: Ecological succession
e8ef66e08e1d.sentence: This includes newly exposed rock or sand surfaces, lava flows, and newly exposed glacial tills.

5e53d958b979.title: Ecological succession
5e53d958b979.sentence: The stages of primary succession include pioneer species such as microorganisms, plants (lichens and mosses), grasses, smaller shrubs, and trees.

5498c9abf04c.title: Functional group (ecology)
5498c9abf04c.sentence: A functional group is a collection of organisms that share characteristics within a community.

3228f2d84e8c.title: Functional group (ecology)
3228f2d84e8c.sentence: Ideally, these would perform equivalent tasks based on domain forces, rather than a common ancestor or evolutionary relationship.

34c50f3287ba.title: Functional group (ecology)
34c50f3287ba.sentence: Groups that relate to vegetation science, or flora, are known as plant functional types.

aad0db9cf7b8.title: Functional group (ecology)
aad0db9cf7b8.sentence: In contrast, those within the animal science range are called guilds typically sharing feeding types.

8f2a4f1c8306.title: Functional group (ecology)
8f2a4f1c8306.sentence: Rather than being based in theory, functional groups are directly observed and determined by research specialists.

8b76b5853a6d.title: Functional group (ecology)
8b76b5853a6d.sentence: Behavior and overall contribution to others are common key points to look for.

062d448b6a78.title: Guild (ecology)
062d448b6a78.sentence: A guild (or ecological guild) is any group of species that exploit the same resources, or that exploit different resources in related ways.

4ab64ecfca12.title: Community (ecology)
4ab64ecfca12.sentence: A guild is a group of species in the community that utilize the same resources in a similar way.

4bd89427ad32.title: Community (ecology)
4bd89427ad32.sentence: Organisms in the same guild experience competition due to their shared resource.

4bdacac890af.title: Guild (ecology)
4bdacac890af.sentence: It is not necessary that the species within a guild occupy the same, or even similar, ecological niches.

e94d9b16ba3d.title: Community (ecology)
e94d9b16ba3d.sentence: However, guilds are not exclusively composed of closely related species.

6a3e8aaf6c73.title: Guild (ecology)
6a3e8aaf6c73.sentence: The number of guilds occupying an ecosystem is termed its disparity.

fcd4d819ba52.title: Competition (biology)
fcd4d819ba52.sentence: Competition can cause species to evolve differences in traits.

58af6d6feee9.title: Competition (biology)
58af6d6feee9.sentence: This occurs because the individuals of a species with traits similar to competing species always experience strong interspecific competition.

0597b4545ccf.title: Competition (biology)
0597b4545ccf.sentence: These individuals have less reproduction and survival than individuals with traits that differ from their competitors.

ecb11c7a86b9.title: Competition (biology)
ecb11c7a86b9.sentence: Consequently, they will not contribute many offspring to future generations.

1b8f404f8f33.title: Competition (biology)
1b8f404f8f33.sentence: For example, Darwin's finches can be found alone or together on the Galapagos Islands.

f6d4385f7629.title: Competition (biology)
f6d4385f7629.sentence: There are three major mechanisms of competition: interference, exploitation, and apparent competition (in order from most direct to least direct).

bd304a842d48.title: Competition (biology)
bd304a842d48.sentence: During interference competition, also called contest competition, organisms interact directly by fighting for scarce resources.

a73966adf3fa.title: Competition (biology)
a73966adf3fa.sentence: For example, large aphids defend feeding sites on cottonwood leaves by ejecting smaller aphids from better sites.

94335b6f8523.title: Competition (biology)
94335b6f8523.sentence: Exploitation competition, or scramble competition, occurs indirectly when organisms both use a common limiting resource or shared food item.

d0a6714711be.title: Competition (biology)
d0a6714711be.sentence: Instead of fighting or exhibiting aggressive behavior in order to win resources, exploitative competition occurs when resource use by one organism depletes the total amount available for other organisms.

19e1c11125d2.title: Competition (biology)
19e1c11125d2.sentence: Interference and exploitation competition can be classed as "real" forms of competition, while apparent competition is not, as organisms do not share a resource, but instead share a predator.

9f6dd1e4856d.title: Competition (biology)
9f6dd1e4856d.sentence: Apparent competition occurs when two otherwise unrelated prey species indirectly compete for survival through a shared predator.

7afc26ce6647.title: Mutualism (biology)
7afc26ce6647.sentence: In models of mutualisms, the terms "type I" and "type II" functional responses refer to the linear and saturating relationships, respectively, between the benefit provided to an individual of species 1 (dependent variable) and the density of species 2 (independent variable).

dacf43362681.sentence: In 1989, David Hamilton Wright modified the above Lotka–Volterra equations by adding a new term, βM/K, to represent a mutualistic relationship.

f8abb03544cb.title: Mutualism (biology)
f8abb03544cb.section: Mathematical modeling > Type II functional response
f8abb03544cb.sentence: Wright also considered the concept of saturation, which means that with higher densities, there is a decrease in the benefits of further increases of the mutualist population.

e2fbbe8c6ddd.title: Mutualism (biology)
e2fbbe8c6ddd.section: Mathematical modeling > Type II functional response
e2fbbe8c6ddd.sentence: Wright's mathematical theory is based on the premise of a simple two-species mutualism model in which the benefits of mutualism become saturated due to limits posed by handling time.

77645641d503.title: Mutualism (biology)
77645641d503.section: Mathematical modeling > Type II functional response
77645641d503.sentence: Without saturation, depending on the size of parameter α, species densities would increase indefinitely.

27bd70d254f2.title: Mutualism (biology)
27bd70d254f2.section: Mathematical modeling > Type II functional response
27bd70d254f2.sentence: Because that is not possible due to environmental constraints and carrying capacity, a model that includes saturation would be more accurate.

92f269c30030.title: Wildlife conservation
92f269c30030.sentence: Conservation genetics studies genetic phenomena that impact the conservation of a species.

a1d7f8ebf1e9.title: Wildlife conservation
a1d7f8ebf1e9.sentence: High genetic diversity increases survival because it means greater capacity to adapt to future environmental changes.

cbd8fe40adfd.title: Wildlife conservation
cbd8fe40adfd.sentence: Meanwhile, effects associated with low genetic diversity, such as inbreeding depression and loss of diversity from genetic drift, often decrease species survival by reducing the species' capacity to adapt or by increasing the frequency of genetic problems.

364082e26d21.title: Wildlife conservation
364082e26d21.sentence: In the early 1990s, only a single population with 20-25 individuals were left.

fe75e643cee4.title: Wildlife conservation
fe75e643cee4.sentence: The population had very low genetic diversity, was highly inbred, and suffered from several genetic issues including kinked tails, cardiac defects, and low fertility.

80ea0a5b2d26.title: Population ecology
80ea0a5b2d26.sentence: Metapopulation ecology is a simplified model of the landscape into patches of varying levels of quality.

f45f03ab14cc.sentence: An additional example may be that of woodpeckers or other birds who create holes in trees for them to nest in.

ba92bbb010a8.title: Ecosystem engineer
ba92bbb010a8.sentence: Once these birds are through with them, the holes are used by other species of birds or mammals for housing.

bf866cdf01dc.title: Ecosystem engineer
bf866cdf01dc.sentence: Examples include Sphagnum moss, which forms peatlands inhabited by species adapted to acidic, waterlogged conditions, and trees, whose trunks and branches serve as substrates and shelter for lichens, mosses, squirrels, birds and insects.

767af6d9a3a6.title: Ecotone
767af6d9a3a6.sentence: An ecotone system is often associated with an ecocline: a "physical transition zone" between two systems.

c56ab548ca83.title: Ecotone
c56ab548ca83.sentence: - an ecocline is a variation of the physicochemical environment dependent of one or two physico-chemical factors of life, and thus presence/absence of certain species.

13af9e9fed5a.title: Ecotone
13af9e9fed5a.sentence: An ecocline can be a thermocline, chemocline (chemical gradient), halocline (salinity gradient) or pycnocline (variations in density of water induced by temperature or salinity).
