a59dbd9af96d.title: Ecotone
a59dbd9af96d.sentence: - ecotone transitions are more clear-cut (distinct), conditions are less stable, hence they have a low species richness.

f0c7ec1dd2dc.title: Community (ecology)
f0c7ec1dd2dc.section: Theories of community structure > Neutral theory
f0c7ec1dd2dc.sentence: Stephen P. Hubbell introduced the neutral theory of ecology (not to be confused with the neutral theory of molecular evolution).

c869b0fbc8ee.title: Community (ecology)
c869b0fbc8ee.section: Theories of community structure > Neutral theory
c869b0fbc8ee.sentence: Within the community (or metacommunity), species are functionally equivalent, and the abundance of a population of a species changes by stochastic demographic processes (i.e., random births and deaths).

9b138f0e373f.title: Community (ecology)
9b138f0e373f.section: Theories of community structure > Neutral theory
9b138f0e373f.sentence: Equivalence of the species in the community leads to ecological drift.

c5034b5c3851.title: Community (ecology)
c5034b5c3851.section: Theories of community structure > Neutral theory
c5034b5c3851.sentence: Ecological drift leads to species' populations randomly fluctuating, whilst the overall number of individuals in the community remains constant.

4089ffaed836.title: Functional group (ecology)
4089ffaed836.sentence: Functional redundancy refers to the phenomenon that species in the same ecosystem fill similar roles, which results in a sort of "insurance" in the ecosystem.

9146869f2b07.title: Functional group (ecology)
9146869f2b07.sentence: Redundant species can easily do the job of a similar species from the same functional niche.

bb7410d448bf.title: Functional group (ecology)
bb7410d448bf.sentence: In ecosystems with high redundancy, losing a species (which lowers overall functional diversity) will not always lower overall ecosystem function due to high functional overlap, and thus in this instance it is most important to conserve a group, rather than an individual.

fc650b0e526f.title: Functional group (ecology)
fc650b0e526f.sentence: When conservation efforts begin, it is still up for debate whether preserving specific species or functional traits is a more beneficial approach for the preservation of ecosystem function.

d015491409fe.title: Functional ecology
d015491409fe.sentence: Functional ecology is a branch of ecology that focuses on the roles, or functions, that species play in the community or ecosystem in which they occur.

df6abb2d130b.title: Functional ecology
df6abb2d130b.sentence: In this approach, physiological, anatomical, and life history characteristics of the species are emphasized.

2cfe473af937.title: Functional ecology
2cfe473af937.sentence: In his influential 1927 work, Animal Ecology, Charles Elton proposed classifying an ecosystem based on the how its members utilize resources.

5f9b3596e4ae.title: Functional ecology
5f9b3596e4ae.sentence: By the 1950s, Elton's model of ecosystems was widely accepted, where organisms that shared similarities in resource use occupied the same 'guild' within an ecosystem.

48eaee18c643.title: Functional ecology
48eaee18c643.sentence: Beginning in the 1970s, an increased interest in functional classification revolutionized functional ecology. 'Guilds' would be re-termed 'functional groups', and classification schemes began to focus more on interactions between species and trophic levels.

da239d99f73c.title: Functional ecology
da239d99f73c.sentence: In the 1990s, biodiversity became better understood as the diversity of species' ecological functions within an ecosystem, rather than simply a great number of different species present.

e04b1e1866d7.title: Ecological restoration
e04b1e1866d7.sentence: The incorporation of functional ecology has shown that more functionally diverse restorations have lower levels of invasion.

0824b02349aa.title: Functional ecology
0824b02349aa.section: Applications of Functional Ecology > Functional traits
0824b02349aa.sentence: Under this paradigm, functional traits are defined as morpho-physiophenological traits which impact fitness indirectly via their effects on growth, reproduction and survival.

ed0eee62a1ee.title: Functional ecology
ed0eee62a1ee.section: Applications of Functional Ecology > Functional traits
ed0eee62a1ee.sentence: Considering more traits in a classification scheme will separate species into more specific functional groups, but may lead to an overestimation of total functional diversity in the environment.

97e01646ad9b.title: Functional ecology
97e01646ad9b.section: Applications of Functional Ecology > Functional traits
97e01646ad9b.sentence: However, considering too few traits runs the risk of classifying species as functionally redundant, when they are in fact vital to the health of the ecosystem.

f95881e2b673.title: Functional ecology
f95881e2b673.section: Applications of Functional Ecology > Functional traits
f95881e2b673.sentence: Individual organisms have Ecophysiological traits and life-history traits; populations have demographic traits; communities have response traits; and ecosystems have effect traits.

6565021712e2.title: Functional ecology
6565021712e2.sentence: Functional diversity is widely considered to be "the value and the range of those species and organismal traits that influence ecosystem functioning" In this sense, the use of the term "function" may apply to individuals, populations, communities, trophic levels, or evolutionary process (i.e. considering the function of adaptations).

c2c0a32b0ff2.title: Functional ecology
c2c0a32b0ff2.section: Functional Diversity > Impact on Ecosystem Health
c2c0a32b0ff2.sentence: Increased functional diversity increases both the capacity of the ecosystem to regulate the flux of energy and matter through the environment (Ecosystem Functions) as well as the ecosystem's ability to produce resources beneficial to humans such as air, water, and wood (Ecosystem Services).

c04ad8d7e05e.title: Functional ecology
c04ad8d7e05e.section: Functional Diversity > Impact on Ecosystem Health
c04ad8d7e05e.sentence: The greater an ecosystem's diversity, the more resilient it is to changes in species composition (e.g. extinction events or invasive species) and extraneous changes to environmental conditions (e.g. logging, farming, and pollution).

61b686769f45.title: Functional ecology
61b686769f45.section: Functional Diversity > Impact on Ecosystem Health
61b686769f45.sentence: Moreover, the benefits that diversity provides to an environment scale non-linearly with the amount of diversity.

50e017572583.title: Functional ecology
50e017572583.section: Functional Diversity > Impact on Ecosystem Health
50e017572583.sentence: The loss of diversity non-linearly disrupts ecosystems (even stable ones); this negative impact is especially detrimental when the loss is across trophic levels.

3de64973ba26.title: Functional ecology
3de64973ba26.section: Functional Diversity > Impact on Ecosystem Health
3de64973ba26.sentence: For, example, the loss of a single tertiary predator can have cascading effects on the food chain, resulting in reduction of plant biomass and genetic diversity.

ccbed6855c13.title: Functional ecology
ccbed6855c13.sentence: Functional extinction is defined as "the point at which a species fails to perform its historical functional role".

663afd608835.title: Functional ecology
663afd608835.sentence: Endangered species such as species of tigers, tuna and sea otters usually qualify for this threshold.

9358c3d1126f.title: Functional group (ecology)
9358c3d1126f.sentence: Traits of an organism that make it unique may include the way it moves, gathers resources, or reproduces, or the time of year it is active add to the overall diversity of an entire ecosystem, and therefore enhance the overall function, or productivity, of that ecosystem.

407807402e72.title: Functional group (ecology)
407807402e72.sentence: Functional diversity increases the overall productivity of an ecosystem by allowing for an increase in niche occupation.

236c420d9333.title: Functional group (ecology)
236c420d9333.sentence: Specifically, bee species, which we rely on for pollination services, have both lower functional diversity and species diversity in managed landscapes when compared to natural habitats, indicating that anthropogenic change can be detrimental for organismal functional diversity, and therefore overall ecosystem functional diversity.

a1015dcc57c2.title: Trophic level
a1015dcc57c2.sentence: The trophic level of an organism is the position it occupies in a food web.

e9e86d6cb8e0.title: Trophic level
e9e86d6cb8e0.sentence: The trophic level of an organism is the number of steps it is from the start of the chain.

6173b42c23c4.title: Trophic level
6173b42c23c4.sentence: A food web starts at trophic level 1 with primary producers such as plants, can move to herbivores at level 2, carnivores at level 3 or higher, and typically finish with apex predators at level 4 or 5.

1c5556dba263.title: Trophic level
1c5556dba263.sentence: The three basic ways in which organisms get food are as producers, consumers, and decomposers.

7485e88d84a4.title: Trophic level
7485e88d84a4.sentence: Herbivores eat plants and are called primary consumers.

d4128c132c98.title: Trophic level
d4128c132c98.sentence: Carnivores that eat herbivores are called secondary consumers.

d04cf37c9da7.title: Trophic level
d04cf37c9da7.sentence: Carnivores that eat other carnivores are called tertiary consumers.

0a73b9bce1d4.title: Trophic level
0a73b9bce1d4.sentence: The concept of trophic level was developed by Raymond Lindeman (1942), based on the terminology of August Thienemann (1926): "producers", "consumers", and "reducers" (modified to "decomposers" by Lindeman).

b913da3d70fb.title: Trophic level
b913da3d70fb.sentence: Consumers at each level convert on average only about 10% of the chemical energy in their food to their own organic tissue (the ten-per cent law).

17a082193128.title: Trophic level
17a082193128.sentence: For this reason, food chains rarely extend for more than 5 or 6 levels.

2650a1a367d4.title: Trophic level
2650a1a367d4.sentence: At the lowest trophic level (the bottom of the food chain), plants convert about 1% of the sunlight they receive into chemical energy.

99f6d2ab2a43.title: Trophic level
99f6d2ab2a43.sentence: It follows from this that the total energy originally present in the incident sunlight that is finally embodied in a tertiary consumer is about 0.001%

6271b4a6039c.title: Trophic level
6271b4a6039c.sentence: Fish at higher trophic levels usually have a higher economic value, which can result in overfishing at the higher trophic levels.

88a672cfbdff.title: Trophic level
88a672cfbdff.sentence: Humans have a mean trophic level of about 2.21, about the same as a pig or an anchovy.

da46f6185284.title: Herbivore
da46f6185284.sentence: A herbivore is an animal anatomically or physiologically evolved to feed on plants, especially upon vascular tissues such as foliage, fruits or seeds, as the main component of its diet.

b032ad2e284f.title: Herbivore
b032ad2e284f.sentence: Herbivores form an important link in the food chain because they consume plants to digest the carbohydrates photosynthetically produced by a plant.

78234d0277a6.title: Herbivore
78234d0277a6.sentence: Carnivores in turn consume herbivores for the same reason, while omnivores can obtain their nutrients from either plants or animals.

a7194e6a01e1.title: Herbivore
a7194e6a01e1.sentence: Due to a herbivore's ability to survive solely on tough and fibrous plant matter, they are termed the primary consumers in the food cycle (chain).

977c34b68341.title: Herbivore
977c34b68341.sentence: A large percentage of herbivores also have mutualistic gut flora made up of bacteria and protozoans that help to degrade the cellulose in plants, whose heavily cross-linking polymer structure makes it far more difficult to digest than the protein- and fat-rich animal tissues that carnivores eat.

34a9ba43d4a0.title: Herbivore
34a9ba43d4a0.sentence: Plant diversity and distribution is often driven by herbivory, and it is likely that trade-offs between plant competitiveness and defensiveness, and between colonization and mortality allow for coexistence between species in the presence of herbivores.

d5ae0aa43161.title: Herbivore
d5ae0aa43161.sentence: For example, increased abundance of herbivores such as deer decrease plant diversity and species richness, while other large mammalian herbivores like bison control dominant species which allows other species to flourish.

5f1bae1cf435.title: Herbivore
5f1bae1cf435.section: Impacts > Trophic cascades and environmental degradation
5f1bae1cf435.sentence: Often these effects are felt when predator populations decline and herbivore populations are no longer limited, which leads to intense herbivore foraging which can suppress plant communities.

7e67e625718f.title: Herbivore
7e67e625718f.section: Impacts > Trophic cascades and environmental degradation
7e67e625718f.sentence: Environmental degradation from white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus) in the US alone has the potential to both change vegetative communities through over-browsing and cost forest restoration projects upwards of $750 million annually.

4f1f662686ac.title: Herbivore
4f1f662686ac.sentence: Seed dispersal by herbivores and pollination are two forms of mutualistic herbivory in which the herbivore receives a food resource and the plant is aided in reproduction.

9b719dab3ff9.title: Food chain
9b719dab3ff9.sentence: A food chain is a linear network of links in a food web, often beginning with an autotroph (such as grass or algae), also called a producer, and typically ending at an apex predator (such as grizzly bears or killer whales), detritivore (such as earthworms and woodlice), or decomposer (such as fungi or bacteria).

f7bb886c4653.title: Food chain
f7bb886c4653.sentence: A food chain illustrates the associations between organisms according to the energy sources they consume in trophic levels, and the most common way to quantify them is in length: the number of links between a trophic consumer and the base of the chain.

00e31a9fd5c6.title: Food chain
00e31a9fd5c6.sentence: A food chain differs from a food web as a food chain follows a direct linear pathway of consumption and energy transfer.

447caf4de447.title: Food chain
447caf4de447.sentence: Natural interconnections between food chains make a food web, which are non-linear and depict interconnecting pathways of consumption and energy transfer.

23624720457d.title: Food chain
23624720457d.sentence: Thus, the foundation of the food chain typically consists of primary producers.

6c45b246ff56.title: Food chain
6c45b246ff56.sentence: Primary producers, or autotrophs, utilize energy derived from either sunlight or inorganic chemical compounds to create complex organic compounds, such as starch, for energy.

7fcbdab3e6bf.title: Food chain
7fcbdab3e6bf.sentence: All organisms in a food chain, except the first organism, are consumers.

02d8d92bc365.title: Food chain
02d8d92bc365.sentence: Chemosynthetic bacteria and archaea use hydrogen sulfide and methane from hydrothermal vents and cold seeps as an energy source (just as plants use sunlight) to produce carbohydrates; they form the base of the food chain in regions with little to no sunlight.

74537c2d9157.title: Food chain
74537c2d9157.sentence: For example, a food chain might start with a green plant as the producer, which is eaten by a snail, the primary consumer.

60478e03fd8b.title: Food chain
60478e03fd8b.sentence: The snail might then be the prey of a secondary consumer such as a frog, which itself may be eaten by a tertiary consumer such as a snake which in turn may be consumed by an eagle.

9b48b91f3188.title: Food chain
9b48b91f3188.sentence: When any trophic level dies, detritivores and decomposers consume their organic material for energy and expel nutrients into the environment in their waste.

d3b628e39ddc.title: Food chain
d3b628e39ddc.sentence: Decomposers and detritivores break down the organic compounds into simple nutrients that are returned to the soil.

23b92b1db9e7.title: Food chain
23b92b1db9e7.sentence: These are the simple nutrients that plants require to create organic compounds.

a5d0c0f146ab.title: Food chain
a5d0c0f146ab.sentence: Food chains are vital in ecotoxicology studies, which trace the pathways and biomagnification of environmental contaminants.

74aaa3969fb5.title: Food chain
74aaa3969fb5.sentence: Removing even one component from the food chain could result in extinction or significant decreases in a species' probability of surviving.

f1e3c2ded0a6.title: Food chain
f1e3c2ded0a6.sentence: Food chains were first discussed by al-Jahiz, a 10th century Arab philosopher.

fb23a7781423.title: Food web
fb23a7781423.sentence: A food web is the natural interconnection of food chains and a graphical representation of what-eats-what in an ecological community.

2fd5fe5fd74a.title: Food web
2fd5fe5fd74a.sentence: Links in food webs map the feeding connections (who eats whom) in an ecological community.

785a9fedec3f.title: Food web
785a9fedec3f.sentence: Position in the food web, or trophic level, is used in ecology to broadly classify organisms as autotrophs or heterotrophs.

606a5140f5b5.title: Food web
606a5140f5b5.sentence: Ecologists can broadly group all life forms into one of two trophic layers, the autotrophs and the heterotrophs.

97760ad322a2.title: Food web
97760ad322a2.sentence: There are different kinds of consumer–resource interactions that can be roughly divided into herbivory, carnivory, scavenging, and parasitism.

4b12d1409848.title: Food web
4b12d1409848.section: Taxonomy of a food web > Trophic levels
4b12d1409848.sentence: Basal species, such as plants, form the first level and are the resource-limited species that feed on no other living creature in the web.

4967fa47fec6.title: Food web
4967fa47fec6.section: Taxonomy of a food web > Trophic levels
4967fa47fec6.sentence: The top level has top (or apex) predators that no other species kills directly for their food resource needs.

dd91961b94eb.title: Food web
dd91961b94eb.section: Taxonomy of a food web > Energy flow and biomass
dd91961b94eb.sentence: Energy flow is directional, which contrasts against the cyclic flows of material through the food web systems.

c9b3c1748a75.title: Food web
c9b3c1748a75.section: Taxonomy of a food web > Ecological pyramids
c9b3c1748a75.sentence: Eventually, all the energy in a food chain is dispersed as heat.

e4acd9d0ea00.title: Food web
e4acd9d0ea00.section: Taxonomy of a food web > Ecological pyramids
e4acd9d0ea00.sentence: There is usually a maximum of four or five links in a food chain, although food chains in aquatic ecosystems are more often longer than those on land.

39eda5f587b9.title: Food web
39eda5f587b9.sentence: Charles Elton subsequently pioneered the concept of food cycles, food chains, and food size in his classical 1927 book "Animal Ecology"; Elton's 'food cycle' was replaced by 'food web' in a subsequent ecological text.

79148bfa38d5.title: Food web
79148bfa38d5.sentence: After Charles Elton's use of food webs in his 1927 synthesis, they became a central concept in the field of ecology.

0d46d614b35f.title: Biodiversity loss
0d46d614b35f.sentence: But even minor changes from a healthy stable state can have a dramatic influence on the food web and the food chain, because reductions in one species can adversely affect the entire chain (coextinction).

638dfbb0918b.title: Food web
638dfbb0918b.sentence: One of the earliest descriptions of a food chain was described by a medieval Afro-Arab scholar named Al-Jahiz: "All animals, in short, cannot exist without food, neither can the hunting animal escape being hunted in his turn." The earliest graphical depiction of a food web was by Lorenzo Camerano in 1880, followed independently by those of Pierce and colleagues in 1912 and Victor Shelford in 1913.

c611779d2923.title: Keystone species
c611779d2923.sentence: A keystone species is a species that has a disproportionately large effect on its natural environment relative to its abundance.

4ff6f5596eec.title: Keystone species
4ff6f5596eec.sentence: The concept was introduced in 1969 by the zoologist Robert T. Paine.

9d54bd579fa6.title: Keystone species
9d54bd579fa6.sentence: The role that a keystone species plays in its ecosystem is analogous to the role of a keystone in an arch.

99b96d0b7eb5.title: Keystone species
99b96d0b7eb5.sentence: Similarly, an ecosystem may experience a dramatic shift if a keystone species is removed, even though that species was a small part of the ecosystem by measures of biomass or productivity.

3f0af417b1ba.title: Keystone species
3f0af417b1ba.sentence: When Paine removed the ochre starfish, the mussels quickly outgrew the other species crowding them out.

0f9a22be1513.title: Keystone species
0f9a22be1513.sentence: At the start, the rock pools held 15 rock-clinging species.

d57765b0cbc1.title: Keystone species
d57765b0cbc1.sentence: Three years later there were 8 such species; and ten years later the pools were largely occupied by a single species, mussels.

d6c74ee88d5a.title: Keystone species
d6c74ee88d5a.section: Predators > Sea otters and kelp forests
d6c74ee88d5a.sentence: When the sea otters of the North American west coast were hunted commercially for their fur, their numbers fell to such low levels – fewer than 1000 in the north Pacific ocean – that they were unable to control the sea urchin population.

28f5d4236925.title: Keystone species
28f5d4236925.section: Predators > Sea otters and kelp forests
28f5d4236925.sentence: The urchins, in turn, grazed the holdfasts of kelp so heavily that the kelp forests largely disappeared, along with all the species that depended on them.

e35740143c1f.title: Keystone species
e35740143c1f.section: Predators > Sea otters and kelp forests
e35740143c1f.sentence: Reintroducing the sea otters has enabled the kelp ecosystem to be restored.

775c7a148157.title: Keystone species
775c7a148157.section: Predators > The wolf, Yellowstone's apex predator
775c7a148157.sentence: The elimination of the gray wolf from the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem had profound impacts on the trophic pyramid.

abd31c271cf3.title: Keystone species
abd31c271cf3.section: Predators > The wolf, Yellowstone's apex predator
abd31c271cf3.sentence: The removal of wolves had a direct effect on beaver populations, as their habitat became grazing territory.

2800e5af6e6e.title: Keystone species
2800e5af6e6e.section: Predators > The wolf, Yellowstone's apex predator
2800e5af6e6e.sentence: When wolves were reintroduced, the beaver population and the whole riparian ecosystem recovered dramatically within a few years.

fbdd5af94de3.title: Keystone species
fbdd5af94de3.sentence: Keystone mutualists are organisms that participate in mutually beneficial interaction, the loss of which would have a profound impact upon the ecosystem as a whole.

b30d02740dd6.title: Keystone species
b30d02740dd6.sentence: Some seeds will not grow unless they have been through a cassowary.

17a66e15fda2.title: Keystone species
17a66e15fda2.sentence: In this it overlaps with several other species conservation concepts such as flagship species (attracting support), indicator species (showing the health of the environment), and umbrella species (indirectly protecting many other species).

c11f19539fe1.title: Keystone species
c11f19539fe1.sentence: Although the concept is valued as a descriptor for particularly strong inter-species interactions, and has allowed easier communication between ecologists and conservation policy-makers, it has been criticized for oversimplifying complex ecological systems.

d179393f57c8.title: Keystone species
d179393f57c8.sentence: That stretching can be quantified: the researcher Ishana Shukla has listed 230 species identified as keystones in some 157 studies in the 50 years since Paine's paper.

e48c69c6e586.title: Keystone species
e48c69c6e586.sentence: The concept of the keystone species was introduced in 1969 by zoologist Robert T. Paine.

7825e1470302.title: Predation
7825e1470302.sentence: Predation is a biological interaction in which one organism, the predator, kills and eats another organism, its prey.

ba224c753ecb.title: Predation
ba224c753ecb.sentence: The predator-prey relationship is one of a family of common feeding behaviours that includes parasitism and micropredation (which usually do not kill the host) and parasitoidism (which always does, eventually).

4536cdbf6496.title: Predation
4536cdbf6496.sentence: It is distinct from scavenging on dead prey, though many predators also scavenge; it overlaps with herbivory, as seed predators and destructive frugivores are predators.

0602a54132e0.title: Predation
0602a54132e0.sentence: To feed, a predator must search for, pursue and kill its prey.

08a7ff7e5240.title: Predation
08a7ff7e5240.sentence: The decision depends on the costs and benefits involved.

1d58b25a1f7a.title: Predation
1d58b25a1f7a.sentence: Predators affect their ecosystems not only directly by eating their own prey, but by indirect means such as reducing predation by other species, or altering the foraging behaviour of a herbivore, as with the biodiversity effect of wolves on riverside vegetation or sea otters on kelp forests.

09cf4d55cd3e.title: Predation
09cf4d55cd3e.section: Role in ecosystems > Biodiversity maintained by apex predation
09cf4d55cd3e.sentence: Predators may increase the biodiversity of communities by preventing a single species from becoming dominant.

aea83f553d24.title: Predation
aea83f553d24.section: Role in ecosystems > Biodiversity maintained by apex predation
aea83f553d24.sentence: Such predators are known as keystone species and may have a profound influence on the balance of organisms in a particular ecosystem.

26a3c7280bb1.title: Predation
26a3c7280bb1.sentence: In the absence of predators, the population of a species can grow exponentially until it approaches the carrying capacity of the environment.

619bbd438791.title: Predation
619bbd438791.sentence: Predators limit the growth of prey both by consuming them and by changing their behavior.

51aef43c252d.title: Predation
51aef43c252d.sentence: This may explain population dynamics effects such as the cycles observed in lynx and snowshoe hares.

66e4977b77e6.title: Apex predator
66e4977b77e6.sentence: An apex predator, also known as a top predator, macropredator or superpredator, is a predator at the top of a food chain with few natural predators of their own, if any.

e909c17c72cf.title: Apex predator
e909c17c72cf.sentence: Apex predators are usually defined in terms of trophic dynamics, meaning that they occupy the highest trophic levels.

da6a47b2847a.title: Apex predator
da6a47b2847a.sentence: Food chains are often far shorter on land, usually limited to being secondary consumers – for example, wolves prey mostly upon large herbivores (primary consumers), which eat plants (primary producers).

36070c636442.title: Apex predator
36070c636442.sentence: They are central to the functioning of ecosystems, the regulation of disease, and the maintenance of biodiversity.

63a819604504.title: Apex predator
63a819604504.sentence: Predators that exert top-down control on organisms in their community are often considered keystone species.

998678b66fa9.title: Apex predator
998678b66fa9.sentence: Dramatic changes in the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem were recorded after the gray wolf, both an apex predator and a keystone species (one with a large effect on its ecosystem), was reintroduced to Yellowstone National Park in 1995 as a conservation measure.

27ab90192d68.title: Apex predator
27ab90192d68.sentence: Elk, the wolves' primary prey, became less abundant and changed their behavior, freeing riparian zones from constant grazing and allowing willows, aspens, and cottonwoods to flourish, creating habitats for beaver, moose, and scores of other species.

6459ad8bdeeb.title: Apex predator
6459ad8bdeeb.sentence: Humans have hunted many apex predators close to extinction, but in some parts of the world, these predators are now returning.

013b97aef1c9.title: Apex predator
013b97aef1c9.sentence: For example, the polar bear requires extensive areas of sea ice to hunt its prey, typically seals, but climate change is shrinking the sea ice of the Arctic, forcing polar bears to fast on land for increasingly long periods.

896e7c34b091.title: Apex predator
896e7c34b091.sentence: Ecotourism sometimes relies on apex predators to attract business.

190471784785.title: Apex predator
190471784785.sentence: These include interactions via ecotourism, such as with the tiger shark, and through rewilding efforts, such as the reintroduction of the Iberian lynx.

0cf38ff696c2.title: Apex predator
0cf38ff696c2.sentence: The reintroduction of large predators is controversial, in part because of concern among farmers for their livestock.

39ba551f0aa3.title: Trophic cascade
39ba551f0aa3.sentence: Trophic cascades are powerful indirect interactions that can control entire ecosystems, occurring when a trophic level in a food web is suppressed.

38ffb3d58df8.title: Trophic cascade
38ffb3d58df8.sentence: For example, a top-down cascade will occur if predators are effective enough in predation to reduce the abundance, or alter the behavior of their prey, thereby releasing the next lower trophic level from predation (or herbivory if the intermediate trophic level is a herbivore).

ce084bda9304.title: Trophic cascade
ce084bda9304.sentence: The removal of the top predator can alter the food web dynamics.

fc56958166d8.title: Trophic cascade
fc56958166d8.sentence: In this case, the primary consumers would overpopulate and exploit the primary producers.

0014e2c8f10f.title: Trophic cascade
0014e2c8f10f.sentence: Removal of piscivorous fish can change lake water from clear to green by allowing phytoplankton to flourish.

d79d14d0eb67.title: Trophic cascade
d79d14d0eb67.sentence: - In Pacific kelp forests, sea otters feed on sea urchins.

e45e902770f1.title: Trophic cascade
e45e902770f1.sentence: In areas where sea otters have been hunted to extinction, sea urchins increase in abundance and kelp populations are reduced.

d256103ecbc3.title: Trophic cascade
d256103ecbc3.sentence: - A similar cascade, also involving the Atlantic cod, occurred in the Baltic Sea at the end of the 1980s.

ff62e1e39651.title: Trophic cascade
ff62e1e39651.sentence: After a decline in Atlantic cod, the abundance of its main prey, the sprat (Sprattus sprattus), increased and the Baltic Sea ecosystem shifted from being dominated by cod into being dominated by sprat.

abeb20f4adf7.title: Trophic cascade
abeb20f4adf7.sentence: The next level of trophic cascade was a decrease in the abundance of Pseudocalanus acuspes, a copepod which the sprat prey on.

b8ba78da1a29.title: Trophic cascade
b8ba78da1a29.sentence: Aldo Leopold is generally credited with first describing the mechanism of a trophic cascade, based on his observations of overgrazing of mountain slopes by deer after human extermination of wolves.

3e48cf49b22b.title: Trophic cascade
3e48cf49b22b.sentence: - In popular media, the reintroduction of gray wolves (Canis lupus) to Yellowstone National Park is often celebrated as an example of a terrestrial trophic cascade in which the wolves "changed rivers" and "saved" the park.

f8e153f9a52a.title: Trophic cascade
f8e153f9a52a.sentence: In reality, the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem is too complex to serve as an example of a straightforward trophic cascade.

44888f1089f6.title: Trophic cascade
44888f1089f6.sentence: Although the existence of trophic cascades is not controversial, ecologists have long debated how ubiquitous they are.

ff87610b5134.title: Energy flow (ecology)
ff87610b5134.sentence: Energy flow is the flow of energy through living things within an ecosystem.

bfeab8a90c62.title: Energy flow (ecology)
bfeab8a90c62.sentence: Producers are important because they convert energy from the sun into a storable and usable chemical form of energy, glucose, as well as oxygen.

1a2146018d8e.title: Energy flow (ecology)
1a2146018d8e.sentence: The first step in energetics is photosynthesis, where in water and carbon dioxide from the air are taken in with energy from the sun, and are converted into oxygen and glucose.

8d822fee36b0.title: Energy flow (ecology)
8d822fee36b0.sentence: Cellular respiration is the reverse reaction, wherein oxygen and sugar are taken in and release energy as they are converted back into carbon dioxide and water.

be2738a47622.title: Energy flow (ecology)
be2738a47622.sentence: All living organisms can be organized into producers and consumers, and those producers and consumers can further be organized into a food chain.

a9960f6799e1.title: Energy flow (ecology)
a9960f6799e1.sentence: In order to more efficiently show the quantity of organisms at each trophic level, these food chains are then organized into trophic pyramids.

b6cd41d52872.title: Energy flow (ecology)
b6cd41d52872.sentence: Secondary production is the energy that herbivores and decomposers use and thus depends on primary productivity.

782e61302467.title: Energy flow (ecology)
782e61302467.sentence: Research has demonstrated that primary producers fix carbon at similar rates across ecosystems.

cee9834ffb17.title: Energy flow (ecology)
cee9834ffb17.sentence: Once carbon has been introduced into a system as a viable source of energy, the mechanisms that govern the flow of energy to higher trophic levels vary across ecosystems.

bf923db70de0.title: Energy flow (ecology)
bf923db70de0.section: Energy flow across ecosystems > Aquatic vs terrestrial ecosystems
bf923db70de0.sentence: In a general sense, the flow of energy is a function of primary productivity with temperature, water availability, and light availability.

f8a2572757e9.title: Marine food web
f8a2572757e9.sentence: A marine food web is a food web of marine life.

c794beb6f58a.title: Marine food web
c794beb6f58a.sentence: At the base of the ocean food web are single-celled algae and other plant-like organisms known as phytoplankton.

39991adb6377.title: Marine food web
39991adb6377.sentence: The second trophic level (primary consumers) is occupied by zooplankton which feed off the phytoplankton.

79ec1ef6ce7f.title: Marine food web
79ec1ef6ce7f.sentence: In the ocean, a food chain typically starts with energy from the sun powering phytoplankton, and follows a course such as:

5ac4eb1114b5.title: Marine food web
5ac4eb1114b5.sentence: > phytoplankton → herbivorous zooplankton → carnivorous zooplankton → filter feeder → predatory vertebrate

4a4d5f71b27d.title: Marine food web
4a4d5f71b27d.sentence: Forage fish occupy middle levels in the food web, serving as a dominant prey to higher level fish, seabirds and mammals.

04c31028502f.title: Marine food web
04c31028502f.sentence: They occupy about 8 per cent of the total ocean area and account for about half of all the ocean productivity.

0857fadd9995.title: Marine food web
0857fadd9995.sentence: There has been increasing recognition in recent years that marine microorganisms play much bigger roles in marine ecosystems than was previously thought.

679388ae0269.title: Marine food web
679388ae0269.sentence: Pteropods and brittle stars together form the base of the Arctic food webs and both are seriously damaged by acidification.

ed92ccbe9631.title: Marine food web
ed92ccbe9631.sentence: Acidification threatens to destroy Arctic food webs from the base up.

ebb050846925.title: Ecological pyramid
ebb050846925.sentence: An ecological pyramid (also trophic pyramid, Eltonian pyramid, energy pyramid, or sometimes food pyramid) is a graphical representation designed to show the biomass or bioproductivity at each trophic level in an ecosystem.

540fcba301e0.title: Ecological pyramid
540fcba301e0.sentence: Ecological pyramids begin with producers on the bottom (such as plants) and proceed through the various trophic levels (such as herbivores that eat plants, then carnivores that eat flesh, then omnivores that eat both plants and flesh, and so on).

1c21fa263cf1.title: Ecological pyramid
1c21fa263cf1.sentence: A pyramid of energy shows how much energy is retained in the form of new biomass from each trophic level, while a pyramid of biomass shows how much biomass (the amount of living or organic matter present in an organism) is present in the organisms.

3ae37b3eb483.title: Ecological pyramid
3ae37b3eb483.sentence: There is also a pyramid of numbers representing the number of individual organisms at each trophic level.

7150f9a2af66.title: Ecological pyramid
7150f9a2af66.sentence: Pyramids of energy are normally upright, but other pyramids can be inverted (pyramid of biomass for marine regions) or take other shapes (spindle shaped pyramid).

a8cd15c51b97.title: Ecological pyramid
a8cd15c51b97.sentence: For example, it will be inverted if beetles are feeding from the output of forest trees or parasites are feeding on large host animals.

49e61a9ec771.title: Ecological pyramid
49e61a9ec771.sentence: For example, in a pond ecosystem, the standing crop of phytoplankton, the major producers, at any given point will be lower than the mass of the heterotrophs, such as fish and insects.

aab0d2d2709c.title: Ecological pyramid

bf084fc7470a.title: Ecological pyramid

2c97672a2765.title: Ecological pyramid

f9309ea36e83.title: Ecological pyramid

1e2cb3e01f7a.title: Ecological pyramid
1e2cb3e01f7a.sentence: The idea of the pyramid of productivity or energy relies on the works of G. Evelyn Hutchinson and Raymond Lindeman (1942).

39b731217a93.title: Food web

39b731217a93.sentence: The basis of trophic dynamics is the transfer of energy from one part of the ecosystem to another.

d6f4c8bce5bf.title: Food web
d6f4c8bce5bf.section: Taxonomy of a food web > Trophic dynamics and multitrophic interactions
d6f4c8bce5bf.sentence: The trophic level concept was introduced in a historical landmark paper on trophic dynamics in 1942 by Raymond L. Lindeman.

b7cb179a0ba8.sentence: The trophic dynamic concept has served as a useful quantitative heuristic, but it has several major limitations including the precision by which an organism can be allocated to a specific trophic level.

73e1885127ea.title: Food web
73e1885127ea.section: Taxonomy of a food web > Trophic dynamics and multitrophic interactions
73e1885127ea.sentence: Omnivores, for example, are not restricted to any single level.

87838f7d5689.title: Food web
87838f7d5689.section: Taxonomy of a food web > Trophic dynamics and multitrophic interactions
87838f7d5689.sentence: Nonetheless, recent research has found that discrete trophic levels do exist, but "above the herbivore trophic level, food webs are better characterized as a tangled web of omnivores."

6be046e301f7.title: Ecological efficiency
6be046e301f7.sentence: Ecological efficiency is the efficiency with which energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.

69b513d14383.title: Ecological efficiency
69b513d14383.sentence: Energy transfer between trophic levels is generally inefficient, such that net production at one trophic level is generally only 10% of the net production at the preceding trophic level (the Ten percent law).

f56534aaed7b.title: Ecological efficiency
f56534aaed7b.sentence: Due to non-predatory death, egestion, and cellular respiration, a significant amount of energy is lost to the environment instead of being absorbed for production by consumers.

fe039bb7eb32.title: Ecological efficiency
fe039bb7eb32.sentence: The loss of energy by a factor of one half from each of the steps of non-predatory death, defecation, and respiration is typical of many living systems.

deeb7f620c71.title: Ecological efficiency
deeb7f620c71.sentence: Thus, the net production at one trophic level is 1/2∗1/2∗1/2=1/8 or approximately ten percent that of the trophic level before it.

66fb9538c3ee.title: Ecological efficiency
66fb9538c3ee.sentence: Ecological efficiency is a combination of several related efficiencies that describe resource utilization and the extent to which resources are converted into biomass.

b1cf91c24f2e.title: Ecological efficiency
b1cf91c24f2e.sentence: - Ecological efficiency is the exploitation efficiency multiplied by the assimilation efficiency multiplied by the net production efficiency, which is equivalent to the amount of consumer production divided by the amount of prey production (Pn/Pn−1)

fbeea673d725.title: Ecological efficiency
fbeea673d725.sentence: Edible kilocalories produced from kilocalories of energy required for cultivation are: 18.1% for chicken, 6.7% for grass-fed beef, 5.7% for farmed salmon, and 0.9% for shrimp.

262a85806699.title: Ecological efficiency
262a85806699.sentence: In contrast, potatoes yield 123%, corn produce 250%, and soy results in 415% of input calories converted to calories able to be utilized by humans.

c6d42fc7f97b.title: Ecological efficiency

d0781edb2e83.title: Ecological efficiency
d0781edb2e83.sentence: Thus, it is more energetically efficient to form a diet from lower trophic levels.

2eebb8d1811e.title: Ecological efficiency
2eebb8d1811e.sentence: Out of a total of 28,400 terawatt-hours (96.8×10^15 BTU) of energy used in the US in 1999, 10.5% was used in food production, with the percentage accounting for food from both producer and primary consumer trophic levels.

65b1d2af4d64.title: Predation
65b1d2af4d64.sentence: Predators have a choice of search modes ranging from sit-and-wait to active or widely foraging.

7cfa2a75ede8.title: Predation
7cfa2a75ede8.sentence: To capture prey, predators have a spectrum of pursuit modes that range from overt chase (pursuit predation) to a sudden strike on nearby prey (ambush predation).

3bfc5b02f69f.title: Predation
3bfc5b02f69f.sentence: The sit-and-wait method is most suitable if the prey are dense and mobile, and the predator has low energy requirements.

c8e5f0a707dd.title: Predation
c8e5f0a707dd.sentence: Wide foraging expends more energy, and is used when prey is sedentary or sparsely distributed.

3c0ed04052eb.title: Predation
3c0ed04052eb.sentence: In social predation, a group of predators cooperates to kill prey.

def86575b0ab.title: Predation
def86575b0ab.sentence: This makes it possible to kill creatures larger than those they could overpower singly; for example, hyenas, and wolves collaborate to catch and kill herbivores as large as buffalo, and lions even hunt elephants.

bbe07f9b736e.title: Predation
bbe07f9b736e.sentence: Predators are often highly specialized in their diet and hunting behaviour; for example, the Eurasian lynx only hunts small ungulates.

3e2bc6f9fc37.title: Predation
3e2bc6f9fc37.sentence: Others such as leopards are more opportunistic generalists, preying on at least 100 species.

2d08fd9d91a1.title: Predation
2d08fd9d91a1.sentence: Predators and prey are natural enemies, and many of their adaptations seem designed to counter each other.

3f9d0ee178d7.title: Predation
3f9d0ee178d7.sentence: For example, bats have sophisticated echolocation systems to detect insects and other prey, and insects have developed a variety of defences including the ability to hear the echolocation calls.

b03b0f2944bf.title: Predation
b03b0f2944bf.sentence: To counter predation, prey have evolved defences for use at each stage of an attack.

eff5d42be9f0.title: Predation
eff5d42be9f0.sentence: They can try to avoid detection, such as by using camouflage and mimicry.

6e34e2ef8704.title: Predation
6e34e2ef8704.sentence: They can detect predators and warn others of their presence.

d96b20327df5.title: Trophic level
d96b20327df5.sentence: But these trophic levels are not always simple integers, because organisms often feed at more than one trophic level.

3274d9bcf1af.title: Trophic level
3274d9bcf1af.sentence: That is, the consumer trophic level is one plus the weighted average of how much different trophic levels contribute to its food.

e1be9c4aca25.title: Trophic level
e1be9c4aca25.sentence: In the case of marine ecosystems, the trophic level of most fish and other marine consumers takes a value between 2.0 and 5.0.

55679454190b.title: Trophic level
55679454190b.sentence: The upper value, 5.0, is unusual, even for large fish, though it occurs in apex predators of marine mammals, such as polar bears and orcas.

527bcf2cc0bd.title: Trophic level
527bcf2cc0bd.sentence: In addition to observational studies of animal behavior, and quantification of animal stomach contents, trophic level can be quantified through stable isotope analysis of animal tissues such as muscle, skin, hair, bone collagen.

f21673d7ee89.title: Trophic level
f21673d7ee89.sentence: This is because there is a consistent increase in the nitrogen isotopic composition at each trophic level caused by fractionations that occur with the synthesis of biomolecules; the magnitude of this increase in nitrogen isotopic composition is approximately 3–4‰.

f1e973ba2c01.title: Trophic level

e438c3182589.sentence: where Yiy is the annual catch of the species or group i in year y, and TLi is the trophic level for species i as defined above.

8936bd9dd7cf.title: Trophic level
8936bd9dd7cf.sentence: Earlier reports found precipitous declines in mean trophic level of fisheries catch, in a process known as fishing down the food web.

ecda25ad3353.title: Trophic level
ecda25ad3353.sentence: However Pauly et al. note that trophic levels peaked at 3.4 in 1970 in the northwest and west-central Atlantic, followed by a subsequent decline to 2.9 in 1994.

805497e39c4c.title: Trophic level
805497e39c4c.sentence: They report a shift away from long-lived, piscivorous, high-trophic-level bottom fishes, such as cod and haddock, to short-lived, planktivorous, low-trophic-level invertebrates (e.g., shrimp) and small, pelagic fish (e.g., herring).

3dc42ae4ddfd.title: Trophic level
3dc42ae4ddfd.sentence: In 2000, this led Pauly and others to construct a "Fisheries in Balance" index, usually called the FiB index.

8bab579860aa.title: Trophic level
8bab579860aa.sentence: The FiB index is stable (zero) over periods of time when changes in trophic levels are matched by appropriate changes in the catch in the opposite direction.

3d4203c99276.title: Trophic level
3d4203c99276.sentence: One aspect of trophic levels is called tritrophic interaction.

9312dc13e061.title: Trophic level
9312dc13e061.sentence: Ecologists often restrict their research to two trophic levels as a way of simplifying the analysis; however, this can be misleading if tritrophic interactions (such as plant–herbivore–predator) are not easily understood by simply adding pairwise interactions (plant-herbivore plus herbivore–predator, for example).

24550c54eb81.title: Trophic level
24550c54eb81.sentence: Significant interactions can occur between the first trophic level (plant) and the third trophic level (a predator) in determining herbivore population growth, for example.

c4d3715e000f.title: Trophic level
c4d3715e000f.sentence: Simple genetic changes may yield morphological variants in plants that then differ in their resistance to herbivores because of the effects of the plant architecture on enemies of the herbivore.

690ec64ed037.title: Food web
690ec64ed037.section: Quantitative food webs > Complexity and stability
690ec64ed037.sentence: These concepts were derived and stimulated through the suggestion that complexity leads to stability in food webs, such as increasing the number of trophic levels in more species rich ecosystems.

a1607ee5ee1e.title: Food web
a1607ee5ee1e.section: Quantitative food webs > Complexity and stability
a1607ee5ee1e.sentence: Connectance is "the fraction of all possible links that are realized in a network".

bb55df5ec96a.title: Food web
bb55df5ec96a.section: Quantitative food webs > Complexity and stability
bb55df5ec96a.sentence: Sometimes in food web terminology, complexity is defined as product of the number of species and connectance., though there have been criticisms of this definition and other proposed methods for measuring network complexity.

7293e7dc5788.title: Food web
7293e7dc5788.section: Quantitative food webs > Complexity and stability
7293e7dc5788.sentence: This hypothesis was challenged through mathematical models suggesting otherwise, but subsequent studies have shown that the premise holds in real systems.

5e0eea1f3e9f.title: Herbivore
5e0eea1f3e9f.sentence: Two herbivore feeding strategies are grazing (e.g. cows) and browsing (e.g. moose).

4b0f10d08798.title: Herbivore
4b0f10d08798.sentence: For a terrestrial mammal to be called a grazer, at least 90% of the forage has to be grass, and for a browser at least 90% tree leaves and twigs.

3cbe2185b2e8.title: Herbivore
3cbe2185b2e8.sentence: An intermediate feeding strategy is called "mixed-feeding".

c1db3b9bece0.title: Herbivore
c1db3b9bece0.sentence: The latter especially is determined by the body mass of the herbivore, with small herbivores selecting for high-quality forage, and with increasing body mass animals are less selective.

edbd0de531ab.title: Herbivore
edbd0de531ab.sentence: Kleiber's law describes the relationship between an animal's size and its feeding strategy, saying that larger animals need to eat less food per unit weight than smaller animals.

a420a8709bb4.title: Herbivore
a420a8709bb4.sentence: A plant defense is a trait that increases plant fitness when faced with herbivory.

9c1d6bd7b02a.title: Herbivore
9c1d6bd7b02a.sentence: Plant defenses increase survival and/or reproduction (fitness) of plants under pressure of predation from herbivores.

ad5f7e314bb1.title: Herbivore
ad5f7e314bb1.sentence: Defense can be divided into two main categories, tolerance and resistance.

17ea5337b627.title: Herbivore
17ea5337b627.sentence: Tolerance is the ability of a plant to withstand damage without a reduction in fitness.

7818818da19e.title: Herbivore
7818818da19e.sentence: Resistance refers to the ability of a plant to reduce the amount of damage it receives from herbivores.

24be4452acf0.title: Herbivore
24be4452acf0.sentence: Herbivores have three primary strategies for dealing with plant defenses: choice, herbivore modification, and plant modification.

066f209f3171.title: Herbivore
066f209f3171.sentence: It has been suggested that many herbivores feed on a variety of plants to balance their nutrient uptake and to avoid consuming too much of any one type of defensive chemical.

30098fc48371.title: Food chain
30098fc48371.sentence: In its simplest form, the length of a chain is the number of links between a trophic consumer and the base of the web.

6a2778d73fc9.title: Food chain
6a2778d73fc9.sentence: Food chain length is important because the amount of energy transferred decreases as trophic level increases; generally only ten percent of the total energy at one trophic level is passed to the next, as the remainder is used in the metabolic process.

14df4ee50e03.title: Food chain
14df4ee50e03.sentence: There are usually no more than five tropic levels in a food chain.

19d5f82a84d9.title: Food chain
19d5f82a84d9.sentence: Humans are able to receive more energy by going back a level in the chain and consuming the food before, for example getting more energy per pound from consuming a salad than an animal which ate lettuce.

5faf8984b500.title: Food chain
5faf8984b500.sentence: Ecologists have formulated and tested hypotheses regarding the nature of ecological patterns associated with food chain length, such as length increasing with ecosystem volume, limited by the reduction of energy at each successive level, or reflecting habitat type.

6bfe650111bc.title: Ecosystem ecology
6bfe650111bc.sentence: Plants exert a "bottom-up" control on the energy structure of ecosystems by determining the total amount of energy that enters the system.

021ca087546a.title: Ecosystem ecology
021ca087546a.sentence: However, predators can also influence the structure of lower trophic levels from the top-down.

7f9a0d0b19bd.title: Ecosystem ecology
7f9a0d0b19bd.sentence: Trophic dynamics refers to process of energy and nutrient transfer between organisms.

15713b90f7ca.title: Ecosystem ecology
15713b90f7ca.sentence: Energy gained by primary producers (plants, P) is consumed by herbivores (H), which are consumed by carnivores (C), which are themselves consumed by "top- carnivores"(TC).

245b4614ac6c.title: Ecosystem ecology
245b4614ac6c.sentence: One of the most obvious patterns in Figure 3 is that as one moves up to higher trophic levels (i.e. from plants to top-carnivores) the total amount of energy decreases.

134e502e207d.title: Ecosystem ecology
134e502e207d.sentence: These influences can dramatically shift dominant species in terrestrial and marine systems The interplay and relative strength of top-down vs. bottom-up controls on ecosystem structure and function is an important area of research in the greater field of ecology.

8a622498f947.title: Ecosystem ecology
8a622498f947.sentence: For example, herbivory can increase litter decomposition and nutrient cycling via direct changes in litter quality and altered dominant vegetation.

84e4c04f452e.title: Population ecology
84e4c04f452e.section: Top-down and bottom-up controls > Top-down controls
84e4c04f452e.sentence: For example, the presence of top carnivores keep herbivore populations in check.

64709b524202.title: Population ecology
64709b524202.section: Top-down and bottom-up controls > Top-down controls
64709b524202.sentence: If there were no top carnivores in the ecosystem, then herbivore populations would rapidly increase, leading to all plants being eaten.

3f3edabed654.title: Population ecology
3f3edabed654.section: Top-down and bottom-up controls > Bottom-up controls
3f3edabed654.sentence: For example, if plant populations decreased significantly, the herbivore populations would decrease, which would lead to a carnivore population decreasing too.

61e4daa853e1.title: Population ecology
61e4daa853e1.section: Top-down and bottom-up controls > Do all ecosystems have to be either top-down or bottom-up?
61e4daa853e1.sentence: An ecosystem does not have to be either top-down or bottom-up.

4a7b110f745e.title: Population ecology
4a7b110f745e.section: Top-down and bottom-up controls > Do all ecosystems have to be either top-down or bottom-up?
4a7b110f745e.sentence: There are occasions where an ecosystem could be bottom-up sometimes, such as a marine ecosystem, but then have periods of top-down control due to fishing.

b9b7cf4d99a4.title: Competition (biology)
b9b7cf4d99a4.sentence: For example, suppose there are two species (species A and species B), which are preyed upon by food-limited predator species C. Scientists observe an increase in the abundance of species A and a decline in the abundance of species B. In an apparent competition model, this relationship is found to be mediated through predator C; a population explosion of species A increases the abundance of predator species C due to a greater total food source.

1355d81b5ad8.title: Competition (biology)
1355d81b5ad8.sentence: Since there are now more predators, species A and B would be hunted at higher rates than before.

d096be494833.title: Competition (biology)
d096be494833.sentence: This one-predator/two-prey model has been explored by ecologists as early as 1925, but the term apparent competition was coined by University of Florida ecologist Robert D. Holt in 1977.

5faf6eb9a54f.title: Competition (biology)
5faf6eb9a54f.section: Apparent competition > Apparent competition and realized niche
5faf6eb9a54f.sentence: A real-world example was studied in the late 1960s, when the introduction of snowshoe hares (Lepus americanus) to Newfoundland reduced the habitat range of native arctic hares (Lepus arcticus).

eb57f4d1ca61.title: Competition (biology)
eb57f4d1ca61.section: Apparent competition > Apparent competition and realized niche
eb57f4d1ca61.sentence: While some ecologists hypothesized that this was due to an overlap in the niche, other ecologists argued that the more plausible mechanism was that snowshoe hare populations led to an explosion in food-limited lynx populations, a shared predator of both prey species.

bb52dea38081.title: Competition (biology)
bb52dea38081.sentence: Human impacts on endangered prey species have been characterized by conservation scientists as an extreme form of asymmetric apparent competition, often through introducing predator species into ecosystems or resource subsidies.

a3d7407a9576.title: Competition (biology)
a3d7407a9576.sentence: An example of fully asymmetric apparent competition which often occurs near urban centers is subsidies in the form of human garbage or waste.

a003b9dfdf12.title: Mutualism (biology)
a003b9dfdf12.sentence: Mutualistic networks made up out of the interaction between plants and pollinators were found to have a similar structure in very different ecosystems on different continents, consisting of entirely different species.

669879b42cbe.title: Mutualism (biology)
669879b42cbe.sentence: Mathematical models that examine the consequences of this network structure for the stability of pollinator communities suggest that the specific way in which plant-pollinator networks are organized minimizes competition between pollinators, reduce the spread of indirect effects and thus enhance ecosystem stability and may even lead to strong indirect facilitation between pollinators when conditions are harsh.

3e7e50c2e851.title: Mutualism (biology)
3e7e50c2e851.sentence: This means that pollinator species together can survive under harsh conditions.

68dba4328313.title: Mutualism (biology)
68dba4328313.sentence: But it also means that pollinator species collapse simultaneously when conditions pass a critical point.

2f34e3298939.title: Pollination
2f34e3298939.sentence: Surprising similarities were found in the structure of networks consisting out of the interactions between plants and pollinators.

04c962dea56e.title: Pollination
04c962dea56e.sentence: This structure was found to be similar in very different ecosystems on different continents, consisting of entirely different species.

0812f07a2695.title: Pollination
0812f07a2695.sentence: The structure of plant-pollinator networks may have large consequences for the way in which pollinator communities respond to increasingly harsh conditions.

54a2f75ff3d2.title: Apex predator
54a2f75ff3d2.sentence: Ecologists have debated whether humans are apex predators.

2e937853a9f4.title: Apex predator
2e937853a9f4.sentence: For instance, Sylvain Bonhommeau and colleagues argued in 2013 that across the global food web, a fractional human trophic level (HTL) can be calculated as the mean trophic level of every species in the human diet, weighted by the proportion that that species forms in the diet.

f3c1afc123ef.title: Apex predator
f3c1afc123ef.sentence: This analysis gives an average HTL of 2.21, varying between 2.04 (for Burundi, with a 96.7% plant-based diet) and 2.57 (for Iceland, with 50% meat and fish, 50% plants).

1e73e438e589.title: Apex predator
1e73e438e589.sentence: These values are comparable to those of non-apex predators such as the anchovy or pig.

e40bd8137b9c.title: Apex predator
e40bd8137b9c.sentence: In 2014, Peter D. Roopnarine criticized Bonhommeau's approach, arguing that humans are apex predators and that the HTL was based on terrestrial farming where indeed humans have a low trophic level, mainly eating producers (crop plants at level 1) or primary consumers (herbivores at level 2), which as expected places humans at a level slightly above 2.

a8e8f4b28607.title: Apex predator
a8e8f4b28607.sentence: In these systems, humans mainly eat predatory fish and have a fractional trophic level of 4.65 and 4.5, respectively, which in Roopnarine's view makes those humans apex predators.

2097f96f7072.title: Apex predator
2097f96f7072.sentence: For example, a reduction in the population of sperm whales, apex predators with a fractional trophic level of 4.7, by hunting has caused an increase in the population of the large squid, with trophic level over 4 (carnivores that eat other carnivores).

6428c20c06f4.title: Apex predator
6428c20c06f4.sentence: This effect, called mesopredator release, occurs in terrestrial and marine ecosystems; for instance, in North America, the ranges of all apex carnivores have contracted whereas those of 60% of mesopredators have grown in the past two centuries.

173ea8c79ad3.title: Apex predator
173ea8c79ad3.sentence: Removal of badgers (in a trial investigating bovine tuberculosis) caused hedgehog densities to more than double.

da70206a1ee9.title: Trophic cascade
da70206a1ee9.sentence: The fact that the earliest documented trophic cascades all occurred in lakes and streams led a scientist to speculate that fundamental differences between aquatic and terrestrial food webs made trophic cascades primarily an aquatic phenomenon.

fef372a2cdf2.title: Trophic cascade
fef372a2cdf2.sentence: In 2002 a meta-analysis found trophic cascades to be generally weaker in terrestrial ecosystems, meaning that changes in predator biomass resulted in smaller changes in plant biomass.

f6a225dab5bb.title: Trophic cascade
f6a225dab5bb.sentence: In contrast, a study published in 2009 demonstrated that multiple species of trees with highly varying autecologies are in fact heavily impacted by the loss of an apex predator.

32aec977225f.title: Trophic cascade
32aec977225f.sentence: In real food webs, consumers often feed at multiple trophic levels (omnivory), organisms often change their diet as they grow larger, cannibalism occurs, and consumers are subsidized by inputs of resources from outside the local community, all of which blur the distinctions between trophic levels.

0771627303aa.title: Foundation species
0771627303aa.sentence: In ecology, the foundation species are species that have a strong role in structuring a community.

39c4b9d50ee5.title: Foundation species
39c4b9d50ee5.sentence: A foundation species can occupy any trophic level in a food web (i.e., they can be primary producers, herbivores or predators).

65aa076a3fc0.title: Foundation species
65aa076a3fc0.sentence: The term was coined by Paul K. Dayton in 1972, who applied it to certain members of marine invertebrate and algae communities.

02b0878fa56f.title: Foundation species
02b0878fa56f.sentence: Foundation species strongly facilitate the associated community by creating new habitat and alleviating physical stress.

e4bcb205bca2.title: Foundation species
e4bcb205bca2.sentence: In harsh coastal zones, corals, kelps, mussels, oysters, seagrasses, mangroves, and salt marsh plants facilitate organisms by attenuating currents and waves, providing aboveground structure for shelter and attachment, concentrating nutrients, and/or reducing desiccation stress during low tide exposure.

1dc739759f3f.title: Foundation species
1dc739759f3f.sentence: In more benign systems, foundation species such as the trees in a forest, shrubs and grasses in savannahs, and macrophytes in freshwater systems, have also been found to play a major habitat-structuring role.

ba088cca919c.title: Foundation species
ba088cca919c.section: Examples and outcomes of foundation species loss
ba088cca919c.sentence: The results of this hemlock study corroborated with those from the previous McKenzie Flats study discussed in that the loss of foundation species led to a proliferation of species diversity in the affected area.

bf96cce15941.title: Foundation species
bf96cce15941.section: Examples and outcomes of foundation species loss
bf96cce15941.sentence: These results seem to contradict a long-standing belief that foundation species play a vital role in communities and ecosystems by creating habitats for organisms, suggesting that in some circumstances they bottleneck species diversity.

e2aa1499899a.title: Green world hypothesis
e2aa1499899a.sentence: The green world hypothesis proposes that predators are the primary regulators of ecosystems: they are the reason the world is 'green', by regulating the herbivores that would otherwise consume all the greenery.

7965f645a2fc.title: Green world hypothesis
7965f645a2fc.sentence: It is also known as the HSS hypothesis, after Hairston, Smith and Slobodkin, the authors of the seminal paper on the subject.

bd3c96dd47fa.title: Green world hypothesis
bd3c96dd47fa.sentence: In 1960, Nelson Hairston, Smith, and Lawrence Slobodkin published a paper laying out the green world hypothesis.

641cd9e33a73.title: Green world hypothesis
641cd9e33a73.sentence: James Estes and John Palmisano did similar experiments with otters, sea urchins, and kelp, where otter presence increased kelp presence in a trophic cascade.

3483f7238ac6.title: Green world hypothesis
3483f7238ac6.sentence: The absence of sea otters in the ecosystem results in the near elimination of kelp forests, forming an ecological concept known as urchin barrens (Siliman and Angelini, 2012).

05739e9783a5.title: Green world hypothesis
05739e9783a5.sentence: The plant self-defense hypothesis proposes that plants are not entirely consumed by herbivores primarily because of their adaptations against it (thorns, toxicity, cellulose, etc.).

96d374032da2.title: Marine food web
96d374032da2.sentence: Marine environments can have inversions in their biomass pyramids.

667d0f17615c.title: Marine food web
667d0f17615c.sentence: In particular, the biomass of consumers (copepods, krill, shrimp, forage fish) is generally larger than the biomass of primary producers.

6a0b7862cec0.title: Marine food web
6a0b7862cec0.sentence: As primary consumers, zooplankton are the crucial link between the primary producers (mainly phytoplankton) and the rest of the marine food web (secondary consumers); the ocean's primary producers are mostly tiny phytoplankton which have r-strategist traits of growing and reproducing rapidly, so a small mass can have a fast rate of primary production.

1cf0f86f68d2.title: Marine food web
1cf0f86f68d2.sentence: Because of this inversion, it is the zooplankton that make up most of the marine animal biomass.

7420378f5ebd.title: Pelagic zone
7420378f5ebd.sentence: This happens because the ocean's primary producers are tiny phytoplankton which tend to have a fast life history (are r-strategists that grow and reproduce rapidly) so a small mass can have a fast rate of primary production.

cad4be396d23.title: Pelagic zone
cad4be396d23.sentence: In contrast, terrestrial primary producers, such as mature forests, often have a slow life history (are K-strategists that grow and reproduce slowly) so a much larger mass is needed to achieve the same rate of primary production.

08af2080d4a5.title: Pelagic zone
08af2080d4a5.sentence: Because of this inversion, it is the zooplankton that make up most of the marine animal biomass.

737366b19788.title: Pelagic zone
737366b19788.sentence: As primary consumers, they are the crucial link between the primary producers (mainly (phytoplankton) and the rest of the marine food web (secondary consumers).

fc769e61ab90.title: Marine food web
fc769e61ab90.sentence: In 2010, researchers found whales carry nutrients from the depths of the ocean back to the surface using a process they called the whale pump.

bec0846779c4.title: Marine food web
bec0846779c4.sentence: Whales feed at deeper levels in the ocean where krill is found, but return regularly to the surface to breathe.

1cc83d036c60.title: Whale feces
1cc83d036c60.section: Ecological significance > Nutrient cycling and carbon sequestration
1cc83d036c60.sentence: The fecal action of whales thus reverses the usual flow of nutrients of the ocean's "biological pump" due to the downward flow of "marine snow" and other detritus from surface to bottom.

baae21c52e92.title: Whale feces
baae21c52e92.sentence: > Whales transport more nitrogen through their feces in the Gulf of Maine than all of the rivers in that system combined.

d90cf350c9b1.title: Whale feces
d90cf350c9b1.section: Ecological significance > Nutrient cycling and carbon sequestration
d90cf350c9b1.sentence: Whale feces are up to 10 million times richer in iron than the surrounding sea water and plays a vital role in providing the iron required for maintaining phytoplankton biomass on the earth.

fa2598f62005.title: Whale feces
fa2598f62005.section: Ecological significance > Nutrient cycling and carbon sequestration
fa2598f62005.sentence: The Southern Ocean is amongst the largest ranges for phytoplankton and has the characteristic of being nutrient-rich in terms of phosphate, nitrate and silicate, while it is iron-deficient at the same time.

8801f03b102d.title: Cascade effect (ecology)
8801f03b102d.sentence: In ecology, a cascade effect is a series of secondary extinctions that are triggered by the primary extinction of a key species in an ecosystem.

1727b89f5fb4.title: Cascade effect (ecology)
1727b89f5fb4.sentence: Secondary extinctions are likely to occur when the threatened species are: dependent on a few specific food sources, mutualistic (dependent on the key species in some way), or forced to coexist with an invasive species that is introduced to the ecosystem.

2b9009faecfb.title: Cascade effect (ecology)
2b9009faecfb.sentence: However, the principal cause of cascade effects is the loss of top predators as the key species.

de99d35b0224.title: Cascade effect (ecology)
de99d35b0224.sentence: As a result of this loss, a dramatic increase (ecological release) of prey species occurs.

2eff258557fd.title: Cascade effect (ecology)
2eff258557fd.sentence: The prey is then able to overexploit its own food resources, until the population numbers decrease in abundance, which can lead to extinction.

63edef51e598.title: Cascade effect (ecology)
63edef51e598.sentence: Starting before the 17th century and not phased out until 1911 when an international treaty was signed to prevent their further exploitation, sea otters were hunted aggressively for their pelts, which caused a cascade effect through the kelp forest ecosystems along the Pacific Coast of North America.

a8fb2179db21.title: Cascade effect (ecology)
a8fb2179db21.sentence: The sea urchins then overexploited their main food source, kelp, creating urchin barrens where no life exists.

6d8f19d83353.title: Cascade effect (ecology)
6d8f19d83353.sentence: Also, since kelp forest ecosystems are homes to many other species, the loss of the kelp ultimately caused their extinction as well.

e9515d620400.title: Ecological efficiency
e9515d620400.section: Ecological efficiency in the marine environment
e9515d620400.sentence: Marine environments exhibit some differences from terrestrial environments, and transfer efficiencies between marine trophic levels are generally higher.

d0a7c2606400.title: Ecological efficiency
d0a7c2606400.section: Ecological efficiency in the marine environment
d0a7c2606400.sentence: Compared to the 10% transfer efficiency in the terrestrial environment suggested by the "ten percent law", the transfer efficiency between marine primary producers (phytoplankton) and primary consumers (herbivorous zooplankton) is estimated to be at about 20%.

87abcac337e5.title: Ecological efficiency
87abcac337e5.section: Ecological efficiency in the marine environment
87abcac337e5.sentence: In marine environments, phytoplankton grow quickly and are almost immediately grazed; this is evidenced by the fact that phytoplankton biomass can turn over 100–300 times per year.

b999fabbca70.title: Ecological efficiency
b999fabbca70.section: Ecological efficiency in the marine environment
b999fabbca70.sentence: Terrestrial plants, on the other hand, grow slowly and expend much of the energy derived from primary production on their own respiration, resulting in much smaller P/B ratios of between 0.5 and 2.0.

311503bc136f.title: Ecological efficiency
311503bc136f.section: Ecological efficiency in the marine environment
311503bc136f.sentence: Costal upwelling zones may have a little as three trophic levels and sustain top-level organisms as large as whales.

7899f90b5b93.title: Ecological efficiency
7899f90b5b93.section: Ecological efficiency in the marine environment
7899f90b5b93.sentence: Conversely, open ocean areas can have as many as six trophic levels and sustain small tuna and squid at the top of the food web.

66ea55fe2f84.title: Ecological efficiency
66ea55fe2f84.sentence: According to this law, during the transfer of organic food energy from one trophic level to the next higher level, only about ten percent of the transferred energy is stored as flesh.

7db00b26c2d5.title: Ecological efficiency
7db00b26c2d5.sentence: The remaining is lost during transfer, broken down in respiration, or lost to incomplete digestion by higher trophic level.

67e1ddc250b0.title: Ecological efficiency
67e1ddc250b0.sentence: The ten percent law of transfer of energy from one trophic level to the next can be attributed to Raymond Lindeman (1942), although Lindeman did not call it a "law" and cited ecological efficiencies ranging from 0.1% to 37.5%.

4998cf3083f3.title: Ecological efficiency
4998cf3083f3.sentence: For example, the sun releases 10,000 J of energy, then plants take only 100 J of energy from sunlight (exception- Only 1% of energy is taken up by plants from sun); thereafter, a deer would take 10 J (10% of energy) from the plant.

ab1f571dc709.title: Ecological efficiency
ab1f571dc709.sentence: A wolf eating the deer would only take 1 J (10% of energy from deer).

64cba6c92437.title: Ecological efficiency
64cba6c92437.sentence: A human eating the wolf would take 0.1J (10% of energy from wolf), etc.

13ec085b0564.title: Ecological stoichiometry
13ec085b0564.sentence: Ecological stoichiometry (more broadly referred to as biological stoichiometry) considers how the balance of energy and elements influences living systems.

a7042d353526.title: Ecological stoichiometry
a7042d353526.sentence: Similar to chemical stoichiometry, ecological stoichiometry is founded on constraints of mass balance as they apply to organisms and their interactions in ecosystems.

dc3ece292297.title: Ecological stoichiometry
dc3ece292297.sentence: The difference, or mismatch, between the elemental demands of organisms and the elemental composition of resources leads to an elemental imbalance.

5992c8abefea.title: Ecological stoichiometry
5992c8abefea.sentence: Consider termites, which have a tissue carbon:nitrogen ratio (C:N) of about 5 yet consume wood with a C:N ratio of 300–1000.

0856fc5f60c0.title: Ecological stoichiometry
0856fc5f60c0.sentence: The ability to maintain internal chemical composition despite changes in the chemical composition and availability of resources is referred to as "stoichiometric homeostasis".

6d7e9e5019dc.title: Ecological stoichiometry
6d7e9e5019dc.sentence: Photoautotrophic organisms, such as algae and vascular plants, can exhibit a very wide range of physiological plasticity in elemental composition and thus have relatively weak stoichiometric homeostasis.

736188faf6f7.title: Ecological stoichiometry
736188faf6f7.sentence: In contrast, other organisms, such as multicellular animals, have close to strict homeostasis and they can be thought of as having distinct chemical composition.

88b6362b375f.title: Ecological stoichiometry
88b6362b375f.sentence: For example, carbon to phosphorus ratios in the suspended organic matter in lakes (i.e., algae, bacteria, and detritus) can vary between 100 and 1000 whereas C:P ratios of Daphnia, a crustacean zooplankton, remain nearly constant at 80:1.

3afa77b6fd00.title: Ecological stoichiometry
3afa77b6fd00.sentence: For instance, in aquatic ecosystems, nitrogen and phosphorus pollution within streams, often due to agricultural activities, can increase the amount of N and P available to primary producers.

d1758e0f5704.title: Ecological stoichiometry
d1758e0f5704.sentence: This change in primary production can trickle through the food web via bottom-up processes and impact the stoichiometry of organisms, limiting elements, and biogeochemical cycling of streams.

9b6f2735833b.title: Phytoplankton
9b6f2735833b.sentence: In the early twentieth century, Alfred C. Redfield found the similarity of the phytoplankton's elemental composition to the major dissolved nutrients in the deep ocean.

9811477b0e1e.title: Phytoplankton
9811477b0e1e.sentence: Redfield proposed that the ratio of carbon to nitrogen to phosphorus (106:16:1) in the ocean was controlled by the phytoplankton's requirements, as phytoplankton subsequently release nitrogen and phosphorus as they are remineralized.

efa5997f1481.title: Phytoplankton
efa5997f1481.sentence: This so-called "Redfield ratio" in describing the stoichiometry of phytoplankton and seawater has become a fundamental principle for understanding marine ecology, biogeochemistry, and phytoplankton evolution.

216e57212819.title: Phytoplankton
216e57212819.sentence: However, the Redfield ratio is not a universal value and it may diverge due to the changes in exogenous nutrient delivery and microbial metabolisms in the ocean, such as nitrogen fixation, denitrification and anammox.

6c654ed39c1c.title: Decomposition
6c654ed39c1c.sentence: Decomposition is the process by which dead organic substances are broken down into simpler organic or inorganic matter such as carbon dioxide, water, simple sugars and mineral salts.

1db5175eed00.title: Decomposition
1db5175eed00.sentence: The process is a part of the nutrient cycle and is essential for recycling the finite matter that occupies physical space in the biosphere.

d26f6c3ef63f.title: Decomposition
d26f6c3ef63f.sentence: One can differentiate abiotic decomposition from biotic decomposition (biodegradation); the former means "the degradation of a substance by chemical or physical processes", e.g., hydrolysis; the latter means "the metabolic breakdown of materials into simpler components by living organisms", typically by microorganisms.

14631a9c9765.title: Decomposition
14631a9c9765.sentence: It begins with leaching by water; the most easily lost and soluble carbon compounds are liberated in this process.

d3bf70bbc584.title: Decomposition
d3bf70bbc584.sentence: Another early process is physical breakup or fragmentation of the plant material into smaller pieces, providing greater surface area for colonization and attack by decomposers.

acfd01ea9a2b.title: Decomposition
acfd01ea9a2b.sentence: Five general stages are typically used to describe the process of decomposition in vertebrate animals: fresh, bloat, active decay, advanced decay, and dry/remains.

5c86d6093f52.title: Carbon sequestration
5c86d6093f52.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Wetlands
5c86d6093f52.sentence: The waterlogged nature of the soil slows down the decomposition of organic material, resulting in the accumulation of carbon-rich sediments, that act as a long-term carbon sink.

70114c869d39.title: Biodiversity loss
70114c869d39.sentence: This in turn affects humans, because affected ecosystems can no longer provide the same quality of ecosystem services, such as crop pollination, cleaning air and water, decomposing waste, and providing forest products as well as areas for recreation and tourism.

cd90cd344b05.title: Soil organic matter
cd90cd344b05.sentence: Soil organic matter (SOM) is the organic matter component of soil, consisting of plant and animal detritus at various stages of decomposition, cells and tissues of soil microbes, and substances that soil microbes synthesize.

64141cba1f92.title: Soil organic matter
