64141cba1f92.sentence: The benefits of SOM result from several complex, interactive, edaphic factors; a non-exhaustive list of these benefits to soil function includes improvement of soil structure, aggregation, water retention, soil biodiversity, absorption and retention of pollutants, buffering capacity, and the cycling and storage of plant nutrients.

9189c0435b6a.title: Soil organic matter
9189c0435b6a.sentence: SOM increases soil fertility by providing cation exchange sites and being a reserve of plant nutrients, especially nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and sulfur (S), along with micronutrients, which the mineralization of SOM slowly releases.

23fed2e49c4b.title: Soil organic matter
23fed2e49c4b.sentence: Although the C content of SOM varies considerably, SOM is ordinarily estimated to contain 58% C, and "soil organic carbon" (SOC) is often used as a synonym for SOM, with measured SOC content often serving as a proxy for SOM, as it makes up a majority of SOM.

239ffa897c8e.title: Soil organic matter
239ffa897c8e.sentence: Soil microbes decompose it through enzymatic biochemical processes, obtain the necessary energy from the same matter, and produce the mineral compounds that plant roots are apt to absorb.

cdc9a038330d.title: Soil organic matter
cdc9a038330d.sentence: The decomposition of organic compounds specifically into mineral, i.e. inorganic, compounds, is denominated "mineralization".

9164e072967e.title: Soil organic matter
9164e072967e.sentence: A portion of organic matter is not mineralized and instead decomposed into stable organic matter that is denominated "humus".

4749898108ff.title: Soil organic matter
4749898108ff.sentence: Organic matter tends to accumulate under wet or cold conditions where decomposer activity is impeded by low temperature or excess moisture which results in anaerobic conditions.

670dbcd59763.title: Soil organic matter
670dbcd59763.sentence: Conversely, excessive rain and high temperatures of tropical climates enable rapid decomposition of organic matter and leaching of plant nutrients.

f7d0d4903836.title: Soil organic matter
f7d0d4903836.sentence: About 70% of global soil organic carbon occurs at depths below 20 cm.

b7fa9ecd8870.title: Soil biology
b7fa9ecd8870.sentence: Soil biology is the study of microbial and faunal activity and ecology in soil.

c4e7a98b8c04.title: Soil biology
c4e7a98b8c04.sentence: These organisms include earthworms, nematodes, protozoa, fungi, bacteria, different arthropods, as well as some reptiles (such as snakes), and species of burrowing mammals like gophers, moles and prairie dogs.

6bdbf1facaf6.title: Soil biology
6bdbf1facaf6.sentence: Soil organisms break down organic matter, making nutrients available for uptake by plants and other organisms.

ae167e3dd266.title: Soil biology
ae167e3dd266.sentence: The decomposition of organic matter by soil organisms has an immense influence on soil fertility, plant growth, soil structure, and carbon storage.

88862c37e1a6.title: Soil biology
88862c37e1a6.sentence: The nutrients stored in the bodies of soil organisms prevent nutrient loss by leaching, in particular for nitrogen and phosphorus.

e7fb956b04ad.title: Soil biology
e7fb956b04ad.sentence: Bacteria are single-cell organisms and the most numerous denizens of agricultural fields, with populations ranging from 100 million to 3 billion in a 'teaspoon' of productive soil.

51283fcd2423.title: Soil biology
51283fcd2423.sentence: A gram of garden soil can contain around one million fungi, such as yeasts and moulds, and around 700 km fungal hyphae can live in 1 g of soil.

92d394491588.title: Soil biology
92d394491588.sentence: Earthworms, ants and termites, known as ecosystem engineers, mix the soil as they burrow, significantly affecting soil formation and organic matter dynamics.

19c3fe496a9d.title: Soil biology
19c3fe496a9d.sentence: By aerating and stirring the soil, and by increasing the stability of soil aggregates, these organisms help to assure the ready infiltration of water.

b23e7b8eefef.title: Soil biology
b23e7b8eefef.sentence: Among these changes are increasing presence of the most essential elements like carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus, elements needed for plant growth.

adbc857db7f0.title: Soil biology
adbc857db7f0.sentence: Given these requirements and the development of a dense hyphal network (mycelium) they actively participate to the degradation of freshly deposited organic remains and their transformation in humus (humification) and carbon dioxide (mineralization).

2b530c49887a.title: Soil biology
2b530c49887a.sentence: In terms of soil and humus creation, the most important fungi tend to be saprotrophic; that is, they live on dead or decaying organic matter, thus breaking it down and converting it to mineral forms (e.g. nitrate, ammonium, phosphate) that are available to the higher plants.

7a989cbdb064.title: Soil biology
7a989cbdb064.sentence: As a relatively new science, much remains unknown about soil biology and its effect on soil ecosystems.

a515ee90ad13.title: Soil biology
a515ee90ad13.sentence: However, critical aspects about how these populations function and interact are unclear.

97d21dc45910.title: Decomposer
97d21dc45910.sentence: Decomposers are organisms that break down dead organisms and release the nutrients from the dead matter into the environment around them.

c6edee2e0b99.title: Decomposer
c6edee2e0b99.sentence: The term "decomposer" refers to a role in an ecosystem, not to a particular class or type of organism, or even to a specific capacity of those organisms.

45632e187a62.title: Decomposer
45632e187a62.sentence: At the center of this definition are the organisms that benefit most directly from the increase in nutrient availability that results from decomposition; plants and other non-mobile (sessile) autotrophs cannot travel to seek out nutrients, and most cannot digest other organisms themselves.

563d815dcb1d.title: Decomposer
563d815dcb1d.sentence: They must therefore rely on decomposers to free up nutrients from dead matter that they can then absorb.

7ec1d7d0a787.title: Decomposer
7ec1d7d0a787.sentence: "Decomposer" as a category, therefore, would include not just fungi and bacteria, which perform external digestion, but also invertebrates such as earthworms, woodlice, and sea cucumbers that digest dead matter internally and release nutrients locally via their feces.

1a81431dc343.title: Decomposer
1a81431dc343.sentence: Additionally, only wood-decay fungi have evolved lignin-modifying enzymes necessary to decompose lignin.

482d3eea91bf.title: Decomposer
482d3eea91bf.sentence: These two factors make fungi the primary decomposers in forests, where litter has high concentrations of lignin and often occurs in large pieces like fallen trees and branches.

24f4a0ca249c.title: Soil organic matter
24f4a0ca249c.sentence: Soil has a crucial function in the global carbon cycle, with the global soil carbon pool estimated to be 2,500 gigatons.

c015eab6631d.title: Soil organic matter
c015eab6631d.sentence: This is 3.3 times the amount of the atmospheric pool at 750 gigatons and 4.5 times the biotic pool at 560 gigatons.

4cc45799527f.title: Soil organic matter
4cc45799527f.sentence: The pool of organic carbon, which occurs primarily in the form of SOM, accounts for approximately 1,550 gigatons of the total global carbon pool, with soil inorganic carbon (SIC, mainly made of carbonates and bicarbonates) accounting for the remainder.

9b074364d4a9.title: Soil organic matter
9b074364d4a9.sentence: The pool of organic carbon exists in dynamic equilibrium between gains and losses; soil may therefore serve as either a sink or source of carbon through carbon sequestration or greenhouse gas emissions, respectively, depending on exogenous factors.

1f060bc0da35.title: Food web
1f060bc0da35.section: Kinds of food webs > Detrital web
1f060bc0da35.sentence: In a detrital web, plant and animal matter is broken down by decomposers, e.g., bacteria and fungi, and moves to detritivores and then carnivores.

08180660c351.title: Food web
08180660c351.section: Kinds of food webs > Detrital web
08180660c351.sentence: "Detritus can be broadly defined as any form of non-living organic matter, including different types of plant tissue (e.g. leaf litter, dead wood, aquatic macrophytes, algae), animal tissue (carrion), dead microbes, faeces (manure, dung, faecal pellets, guano, frass), as well as products secreted, excreted or exuded from organisms (e.g. extra-cellular polymers, nectar, root exudates and leachates, dissolved organic matter, extra-cellular matrix, mucilage).

f806d32f88fc.title: Food web
f806d32f88fc.section: Kinds of food webs > Detrital web
f806d32f88fc.sentence: Mushrooms produced by decomposers in the detrital web become a food source for deer, squirrels, and mice in the grazing web.

e1b030c1dc76.title: Food web
e1b030c1dc76.section: Kinds of food webs > Detrital web
e1b030c1dc76.sentence: Earthworms eaten by robins are detritivores consuming decaying leaves.

d550bd8de2b7.title: Soil fertility
d550bd8de2b7.sentence: Dark Earth is a type of soil found in the Amazon that has a darker color, higher organic carbon content, and higher fertility than soil in other regions of South America, which makes it highly coveted even today.

131b31cfc1ed.title: Soil fertility
131b31cfc1ed.sentence: Dark Earth deposits have been found, through ethnographic and archaeological studies, to have been created through ancient Indigenous practices by intentional soil management.

f455d70722ab.title: Soil fertility
f455d70722ab.sentence: While Dark Earth, and other anthropic soils, can be found all throughout the world, Amazonian Dark Earth is particularly significant because "it contrasts too sharply with the especially poor fertility of typical highly weathered tropical upland soils in the Amazon".

3b2f1bc49b39.title: Soil fertility
3b2f1bc49b39.sentence: In Ghana and Liberia, it is a long-standing practice to combine different types of waste to create fertile soil that is referred to as African Dark Earths.

7e2a13563396.title: Soil fertility
7e2a13563396.sentence: This soil contains high concentrations of calcium, phosphorus, and carbon.

d7f907a7becb.title: Soil fertility
d7f907a7becb.sentence: The details of Indigenous societies prior to European colonization in 1492 within the Amazonian regions of South America, particularly the size of the communities and the depth of interactions with the environment, are continually debated.

d0e4735a1eba.title: Soil fertility
d0e4735a1eba.sentence: Central to the debate is the influence of Dark Earth.

84903066ccae.title: Decomposition
84903066ccae.sentence: The rate of decomposition is governed by three sets of factors: the physical environment (temperature, moisture and soil properties), the quantity and quality of the dead material available to decomposers, and the nature of the microbial community itself.

8ae65d949b26.title: Decomposition
8ae65d949b26.sentence: Decomposition rates are highest in damp, moist conditions with adequate levels of oxygen.

0e9999ba9644.title: Decomposition
0e9999ba9644.sentence: Decomposition rates are low under very wet or very dry conditions.

f8a653e09be3.title: Decomposition
f8a653e09be3.sentence: Substances like sugars and amino acids decompose readily and are considered labile.

b621dd6dbb3b.title: Decomposition
b621dd6dbb3b.sentence: Compounds which are more resistant to decay, like lignin or cutin, are considered recalcitrant.

ad9136cd1377.title: Decomposition
ad9136cd1377.sentence: Consequently, dead animals decompose more rapidly than dead leaves, which themselves decompose more rapidly than fallen branches.

b2b6bb4b6abd.title: Decomposition
b2b6bb4b6abd.sentence: Soil disturbance like tilling increases decomposition by increasing the amount of oxygen in the soil and by exposing new organic matter to soil microbes.

00d34fb6d0d2.title: Ecosystem ecology
00d34fb6d0d2.sentence: Rates of plant litter decomposition are highly dependent on litter quality; high concentration of phenolic compounds, especially lignin, in plant litter has a retarding effect on litter decomposition.

b39be2ff1d77.title: Ecosystem ecology
b39be2ff1d77.sentence: Ecosystems dominated by plants with low-lignin concentration often have rapid rates of decomposition and nutrient cycling.

af8af7cff91a.title: Soil organic matter
af8af7cff91a.sentence: Humus refers to organic matter that has been decomposed by soil microflora and fauna to the point where it is resistant to further breakdown.

78b6b535726a.title: Soil organic matter
78b6b535726a.sentence: Humus usually constitutes only five percent of the soil or less by volume, but it is an essential source of nutrients and adds important textural qualities crucial to soil health and plant growth.

8155ecf69657.title: Soil organic matter
8155ecf69657.sentence: Humus has a high cation and anion exchange capacity that on a dry weight basis is many times greater than that of clay colloids.

68231dac6081.title: Soil organic matter
68231dac6081.sentence: Humic substances are classified into three genera based on their solubility in acids and alkalis, and also according to their stability:

b2421f081a38.title: Soil organic matter
b2421f081a38.sentence: - Fulvic acid is the genus that contains the matter that has the lowest molecular weight, is soluble in acids and alkalis, and is susceptible to microbial action.

56a8f4489197.title: Soil organic matter
56a8f4489197.sentence: - Humic acid is the genus that contains the intermediate matter that has medial molecular weight, is soluble in alkalis and insoluble in acids, and has some resistance to microbial action.

b85691bbceaa.title: Soil organic matter
b85691bbceaa.sentence: - Humin is the genus that contains the matter that has the greatest molecular weight, is the darkest in color, is insoluble in acids and alkalis, and has the greatest resistance to microbial action.

c794ccd5ad7e.title: Soil organic matter
c794ccd5ad7e.sentence: MAOM is thought to be low molecular weight compounds of plant and microbial origin that are associated with minerals through chemical bonds between SOM and charged mineral surfaces as well as occlusion in aggregates.

ec20f2c32cc2.title: Soil organic matter
ec20f2c32cc2.sentence: This mineral association acts as a protection for the SOM, as it is less accessible for decomposers.

16f27cf00697.title: Soil organic matter
16f27cf00697.sentence: MAOM is typically more persistent in the soil, staying there for centuries, compared to POM, which remains for only a few years to decades before being decomposed.

8f83ac7b8f68.title: Soil organic matter
8f83ac7b8f68.sentence: POM is thought to be made predominantly of fungal-colonized plant remains that have not experienced much decomposition.

21914b399ea8.title: Soil organic matter
21914b399ea8.sentence: This domination of mineral influences at depth, and also higher amount of SOC found in deeper soil has to do with mineral associated organic matter (MAOM or MAOC for mineral associated organic C) which is typically thought to be resistant to microbial degradation in comparison to particulate organic matter (POM or POC for organic C).

7dbbc6a3e19d.title: Soil biology
7dbbc6a3e19d.sentence: Those fungi that are able to live symbiotically with living plants, creating a relationship that is beneficial to both, are known as mycorrhizae (from myco meaning fungus and rhiza meaning root).

02ce8ce84297.title: Soil biology
02ce8ce84297.sentence: The mycorrhizal fungus obtains the carbohydrates that it requires from the root, in return providing the plant with nutrients, including nitrogen and phosphorus, and with moisture.

8c2499490f6d.title: Soil biology
8c2499490f6d.sentence: In mycorrhizae plant roots are invaded by the mycelium of the mycorrhizal fungus, which lives partly in the soil and partly in the root, and may either penetrate the root cortex without entering its cells (forming the Hartig net) and cover the root as a sheath (ectomycorrhizae) or be present in cortical cells in the form of arbuscules (arbuscular mycorrhizae).

e179737b38e8.title: Soil biology
e179737b38e8.sentence: Beneficial mycorrhizal associations (either ectomycorrhizae or arbuscular mycorrhizae) are to be found in many of our edible and flowering crops, to the exception of Brassicaceae (e.g. cabbage, turnip) as well as in the majority of tree species, especially in forests and woodlands, with Ericaceae (e.g. bracken, bilberry) harbouring a special type, called ericoid mycorrhizae.

3a9f7b00eefb.title: Soil biology
3a9f7b00eefb.sentence: Chemical signalling between plants through common mycorrhizal networks, although a beautiful concept, is still a matter of conjecture, more research being needed.

01d22d9d05de.title: Soil biology
01d22d9d05de.sentence: Nitrification is a vital part of the nitrogen cycle, wherein certain chemolithotrophic nitrifying bacteria (e.g. Nitrosomonas), called autotrophic nitrifiers (manufacturing their own carbohydrate supply without using the process of photosynthesis) are able to transform nitrogen in the form of ammonium, which is produced by the decomposition of proteins, into nitrates, available to growing plants and once again converted to proteins.

ee0d672d23c6.title: Nitrification
ee0d672d23c6.sentence: Nitrification is an important step in the nitrogen cycle in soil.

bf410560c91d.title: Nitrification
bf410560c91d.sentence: Nitrification is an aerobic process performed by small groups of autotrophic bacteria and archaea.

6959d3eaa841.title: Nitrogen cycle
6959d3eaa841.sentence: In the primary stage of nitrification, the oxidation of ammonium (NH+4) is performed by bacteria such as the Nitrosomonas species, which converts ammonia to nitrites (NO−2).

b95377ab692d.title: Nitrogen cycle
b95377ab692d.sentence: Other bacterial species such as Nitrobacter, are responsible for the oxidation of the nitrites (NO−2) into nitrates (NO−3).

60b941f18cb2.title: Nitrogen cycle
60b941f18cb2.sentence: It is important for the ammonia (NH3) to be converted to nitrates or nitrites because ammonia gas is toxic to plants.

00ed08354948.title: Soil biology
00ed08354948.sentence: While nitrogen fixation converts nitrogen from the atmosphere into organic compounds, a series of processes called denitrification returns some amount of nitrogen to the atmosphere.

1e88f41158fd.title: Soil biology
1e88f41158fd.sentence: The denitrification process caused by oxygen-free conditions converts nitrates and nitrites in soil into nitrogen gas or into gaseous compounds such as nitrous oxide or nitric oxide.

6fb40ecc150a.title: Soil biology
6fb40ecc150a.sentence: Denitrifying bacteria tend to be anaerobes, or facultatively anaerobes (can altern between the oxygen dependent and oxygen independent types of metabolisms), including Achromobacter and Pseudomonas.

b839fcdbea8b.title: Soil biology
b839fcdbea8b.sentence: In excess, denitrification can lead to overall losses of available soil nitrogen and subsequent loss of soil fertility.

ef65298d9246.title: Soil biology
ef65298d9246.sentence: An excess of nitrogen fertilizers may cause denitrification in addition to nitrate loss by percolation to the aquifer.

6db2d20ab4b6.title: Nitrogen cycle
6db2d20ab4b6.sentence: This process is performed by bacterial species such as Pseudomonas and Paracoccus, under anaerobic conditions.

64830f581189.title: Nitrogen cycle
64830f581189.sentence: Denitrification happens in anaerobic conditions e.g. waterlogged soils.

477a522e7bd0.title: Nitrogen cycle
477a522e7bd0.sentence: They use the nitrate as an electron acceptor in the place of oxygen during respiration.

962272471bbe.title: Denitrification
962272471bbe.sentence: Since denitrification can remove NO3−, reducing its leaching to groundwater, it can be strategically used to treat sewage or animal residues of high nitrogen content.

e8b4f5e1b96d.title: Soil biology
e8b4f5e1b96d.sentence: In another part of the nitrogen cycle, the process of nitrogen fixation constantly puts additional nitrogen into biological circulation.

2cd2b3c901e3.title: Soil biology
2cd2b3c901e3.sentence: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria are able to convert nitrogen from the atmosphere into nitrogen-containing organic substances, and thus play a decisive role in incipient soil formation.

a0abd52acc61.title: Soil biology
a0abd52acc61.sentence: This is carried out by free-living nitrogen-fixing (diazotroph) bacteria in the soil or water such as Azotobacter and heterocyst-bearing cyanobacteria (blue-green algae), or by those that live in close symbiosis with legumes, such as rhizobia, or with actinorhizal plants, such as Frankia.

5f69ef4b1885.title: Soil biology
5f69ef4b1885.sentence: These form colonies in nodules they create on the roots of peas, beans, Casuarina and related flowering plants.

612324e30b11.title: Nitrogen cycle
612324e30b11.sentence: Atmospheric nitrogen must be processed, or "fixed", into a usable form to be taken up by plants.

f460ac755ce0.title: Nitrogen cycle
f460ac755ce0.sentence: Between 5 and 10 billion kg per year are fixed by lightning strikes, but most fixation is done by free-living or symbiotic bacteria known as diazotrophs.

8e13c448c12d.title: Nitrogen fixation
8e13c448c12d.sentence: Biological nitrogen fixation was discovered by Jean-Baptiste Boussingault in 1838.

50370cf55021.title: Nitrogen fixation
50370cf55021.sentence: The discovery of the role of nitrogen-fixing bacteria by Herman Hellriegel and Herman Wilfarth in 1886–1888 would open a new era of soil science."

949fe1ccc2c4.title: Population dynamics
949fe1ccc2c4.sentence: Population dynamics is the type of mathematics used to model and study the size and age composition of populations as dynamical systems.

95d03d355fb4.title: Population dynamics
95d03d355fb4.sentence: Population dynamics is a branch of mathematical biology, and uses mathematical techniques such as differential equations to model behaviour.

3cd316686940.title: Population dynamics
3cd316686940.sentence: The beginning of population dynamics is widely regarded as the work of Malthus, formulated as the Malthusian growth model.

e38b68e024e9.title: Population dynamics
e38b68e024e9.sentence: According to Malthus, assuming that the conditions (the environment) remain constant (ceteris paribus), a population will grow (or decline) exponentially.

1234b3a7bc47.title: Population dynamics
1234b3a7bc47.sentence: Simplified population models usually start with four key variables (four demographic processes) including death, birth, immigration, and emigration.

d95047bd7990.title: Population dynamics
d95047bd7990.sentence: Models can be more mathematically complex where "...several competing hypotheses are simultaneously confronted with the data." For example, in a closed system where immigration and emigration does not take place, the rate of change in the number of individuals in a population can be described as: dNdt=B−D=bN−dN=(b−d)N=rN, where N is the total number of individuals in the specific experimental population being studied, B is the number of births and D is the number of deaths per individual in a particular experiment or model.

9d3b8bb0c077.title: Population dynamics
9d3b8bb0c077.sentence: This formula can be read as the rate of change in the population (dN/dt) is equal to births minus deaths (B − D).

367929b5fd3f.title: Population dynamics
367929b5fd3f.sentence: Using these techniques, Malthus' population principle of growth was later transformed into a mathematical model known as the logistic equation: dNdt=rN(1−NK), where N is the population size, r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase, and K is the carrying capacity of the population.

e3b322e8d627.title: Population dynamics
e3b322e8d627.sentence: The formula can be read as follows: the rate of change in the population (dN/dt) is equal to growth (rN) that is limited by carrying capacity (1 − N/K).

d16b53276616.title: Population dynamics
d16b53276616.sentence: The field of population ecology often uses data on life history and matrix algebra to develop projection matrices on fecundity and survivorship.

9c2980490714.title: Population dynamics
9c2980490714.sentence: This information is used for managing wildlife stocks and setting harvest quotas.

f91945d48fed.title: Biological dispersal
f91945d48fed.sentence: Biological dispersal refers to both the movement of individuals (animals, plants, fungi, bacteria, etc.) from their birth site to their breeding site ('natal dispersal') and the movement from one breeding site to another ('breeding dispersal').

ae8e7b3eaad3.title: Biological dispersal
ae8e7b3eaad3.sentence: The term also encompasses the movement of propagules such as seeds and spores.

315e8d35670e.title: Biological dispersal
315e8d35670e.sentence: Technically, dispersal is defined as any movement that has the potential to lead to gene flow.

003e222bb49a.title: Biological dispersal
003e222bb49a.sentence: The act of dispersal involves three phases: departure, transfer, and settlement.

6d4bd187e6ca.title: Biological dispersal
6d4bd187e6ca.sentence: In the broadest sense, dispersal occurs when the fitness benefits of movement outweigh its costs.

31fdd9a10a90.title: Biological dispersal
31fdd9a10a90.sentence: There are a number of benefits to dispersal, such as locating new resources, escaping unfavorable conditions, avoiding competition with siblings, and avoiding breeding with closely related individuals, which could lead to inbreeding depression.

9b99be5a8d7e.title: Biological dispersal
9b99be5a8d7e.sentence: There are also a number of costs associated with dispersal, which can be thought of in terms of four main currencies: energy, risk, time, and opportunity.

79948fbf55c0.title: Biological dispersal
79948fbf55c0.sentence: By simply moving from one habitat patch to another, an individual's dispersal can influence not only its own fitness but also broader processes such as population dynamics, population genetics, and species distribution.

f6a154236c53.title: Biological dispersal
f6a154236c53.sentence: An ecosystem depends critically on the ability of individuals and populations to disperse from one habitat patch to another.

ad5b835b5c59.title: Biological dispersal
ad5b835b5c59.sentence: Therefore, biological dispersal is critical for the stability of ecosystems.

3a6f9c70de09.title: Ecological goods and services
3a6f9c70de09.sentence: Examples of ecological services include purification of air and water, maintenance of biodiversity, decomposition of wastes, soil and vegetation generation and renewal, pollination of crops and natural vegetation, groundwater recharge through wetlands, seed dispersal, greenhouse gas mitigation, and aesthetically pleasing landscapes.

e66c4c41ab2b.title: Adaptive capacity
e66c4c41ab2b.sentence: Species' adaptive capacity is generally characterized by phenotypic plasticity, dispersal ability, and genetic diversity, which are foundational to the species' ability to acclimate in situ or track suitable climate across the landscape.

210496bb6398.title: R/K selection theory
210496bb6398.sentence: The r/K selection theory is an evolutionary hypothesis examining the selection of traits in an organism that trade off between quantity and quality of offspring.

6c4b232a09fa.title: R/K selection theory
6c4b232a09fa.sentence: Species which produce more offspring at the expense of reduced individual parental investment are termed r-strategists, while those which make greater parental investment at the expense of a reduced quantity of offspring are termed K-strategists.

532e6c96b53a.title: R/K selection theory
532e6c96b53a.sentence: These terms, r and K, are drawn from standard ecological formula as illustrated in the simplified Verhulst model of population dynamics:

63a59cba22e3.title: R/K selection theory
63a59cba22e3.sentence: where N is the population, r is the maximum growth rate, K is the carrying capacity of the local environment (from German Kapazitätsgrenze), and ⁠ dN /dt ⁠ (the derivative of population size N with respect to time t) is the rate of change in population with time.

a39e481624e2.title: R/K selection theory
a39e481624e2.sentence: In unstable or unpredictable environments, r-selection predominates due to the ability to reproduce rapidly.

a02a00db387d.title: R/K selection theory
a02a00db387d.sentence: Among the traits that are thought to characterize r-selection are high fecundity, small body size, early maturity onset, short generation time, and the ability to disperse offspring widely.

961e155b8d45.title: R/K selection theory
961e155b8d45.sentence: A typical r species is the dandelion (genus Taraxacum).

017ef027fcb1.title: R/K selection theory
017ef027fcb1.sentence: In stable or predictable environments, K-selection predominates as the ability to compete successfully for limited resources is crucial and populations of K-selected organisms typically are very constant in number and close to the maximum that the environment can bear (unlike r-selected populations, where population sizes can change much more rapidly).

b1a0758dfdcc.title: R/K selection theory
b1a0758dfdcc.sentence: Traits that are thought to be characteristic of K-selection include large body size, long life expectancy, and the production of fewer offspring, which often require extensive parental care until they mature.

f9a262f45246.title: R/K selection theory
f9a262f45246.sentence: Organisms with K-selected traits include large organisms such as elephants, sharks, humans, and whales, but also smaller long-lived organisms such as Arctic terns, parrots, and eagles.

6646b9cc5d03.title: R/K selection theory
6646b9cc5d03.sentence: Although some organisms are identified as primarily r- or K-strategists, the majority of organisms do not follow this pattern.

12eccddb0b4d.title: R/K selection theory
12eccddb0b4d.sentence: The r/K dichotomy can be re-expressed as a continuous spectrum using the economic concept of discounted future returns, with r-selection corresponding to large discount rates and K-selection corresponding to small discount rates.

959f9350b758.title: R/K selection theory
959f9350b758.sentence: The terminology of r/K-selection was coined by the ecologists Robert MacArthur and E. O. Wilson in 1967 based on their work on island biogeography; although the concept of the evolution of life history strategies has a longer history (see e.g. plant strategies).

23517bd90a67.title: R/K selection theory
23517bd90a67.sentence: The theory was popular in the 1970s and 1980s, when it was used as a heuristic device, but lost importance in the early 1990s, when it was criticized by several empirical studies.

5a0f62b84236.title: R/K selection theory
5a0f62b84236.sentence: The r- and K-selection paradigm was replaced by new paradigm that focused on age-specific mortality (Stearns, 1976; Charlesworth, 1980).

c08740cdec13.title: R/K selection theory
c08740cdec13.sentence: Some scientists now prefer to use the terms fast versus slow life history as a replacement for, respectively, r versus K reproductive strategy.

1b9c2149245e.title: Maximum sustainable yield
1b9c2149245e.section: Modelling MSY > Limitations of MSY approach > Orange roughy
1b9c2149245e.sentence: However, it was later discovered that the orange roughy lived a long time and had bred slowly (~30 years).

7b43169c0fee.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
7b43169c0fee.sentence: The Lotka–Volterra equations, also known as the Lotka–Volterra predator–prey model, are a pair of first-order nonlinear differential equations, frequently used to describe the dynamics of biological systems in which two species interact, one as a predator and the other as prey.

1a5ece42af11.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
1a5ece42af11.sentence: The prey are assumed to have an unlimited food supply and to reproduce exponentially, unless subject to predation; this exponential growth is represented in the equation above by the term αx.

fd92b4b657c9.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
fd92b4b657c9.sentence: The rate of predation on the prey is assumed to be proportional to the rate at which the predators and the prey meet; this is represented above by βxy.

70e83e2bf300.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
70e83e2bf300.sentence: The term δxy represents the growth of the predator population.

0b5cc2e8dda3.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
0b5cc2e8dda3.sentence: The term γy represents the loss rate of the predators due to either natural death or emigration; it leads to an exponential decay in the absence of prey.

0468a36eb0e5.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
0468a36eb0e5.sentence: In the model system, the predators thrive when prey is plentiful but, ultimately, outstrip their food supply and decline.

c054617b98a8.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
c054617b98a8.sentence: As the predator population is low, the prey population will increase again.

453d52356cbb.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
453d52356cbb.sentence: These dynamics continue in a population cycle of growth and decline.

fddc1de10cb0.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
fddc1de10cb0.sentence: Fluctuating numbers of predators and prey have been observed in natural populations, such as the lynx and snowshoe hare data of the Hudson's Bay Company and the moose and wolf populations in Isle Royale National Park.

062bec1ba7f9.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
062bec1ba7f9.sentence: This has as a consequence that an increase in, for instance, the prey growth rate, α, leads to an increase in the predator equilibrium density, but not the prey equilibrium density.

cba3abae5c02.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
cba3abae5c02.sentence: Making the environment better for the prey benefits the predator, not the prey (this is related to the paradox of the pesticides and to the paradox of enrichment).

6d519090d77e.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
6d519090d77e.sentence: The addition of iron typically leads to a short bloom in phytoplankton, which is quickly consumed by other organisms (such as small fish or zooplankton) and limits the effect of enrichment mainly to increased predator density, which in turn limits the carbon sequestration.

3d93f1119b74.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
3d93f1119b74.sentence: This is as predicted by the equilibrium population densities of the Lotka–Volterra predator-prey model, and is a feature that carries over to more elaborate models in which the restrictive assumptions of the simple model are relaxed.

83eef3f72d85.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
83eef3f72d85.sentence: The Lotka–Volterra predator–prey model was initially proposed by Alfred J. Lotka in the theory of autocatalytic chemical reactions in 1910.

a8b7763d6aca.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
a8b7763d6aca.sentence: The same set of equations was published in 1926 by Vito Volterra, a mathematician and physicist, who had become interested in mathematical biology.

aea06e4e5d72.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
aea06e4e5d72.sentence: Volterra developed his model to explain D'Ancona's observation and did this independently from Alfred Lotka.

e33fa48f8ac2.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
e33fa48f8ac2.sentence: It can be used to describe the dynamics in a market with several competitors, complementary platforms and products, a sharing economy, and more.

b0f18b8765a2.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
b0f18b8765a2.sentence: In economics, the Phillips curve, which shows the statistical relationship between unemployment and the rate of change in nominal wages, has been connected by the Goodwin model.

9e030587d14e.title: Lotka–Volterra equations
9e030587d14e.sentence: The Lotka–Volterra equations have a long history of use in economic theory; their initial application is commonly credited to Richard Goodwin in 1965 or 1967.

0864e9c63082.title: Minimum viable population
0864e9c63082.sentence: Minimum viable population (MVP) is a lower bound on the population of a species, such that it can survive in the wild.

9ba2f2b97c82.title: Minimum viable population
9ba2f2b97c82.sentence: MVP refers to the smallest possible size at which a biological population can exist without facing extinction from natural disasters or demographic, environmental, or genetic stochasticity.

9c1344a2e08c.title: Minimum viable population
9c1344a2e08c.sentence: Small populations are at a greater risk of extinction than larger populations due to small populations having less capacity to recover from adverse stochastic (i.e. random) events.

9cb911e95c82.title: Minimum viable population
9cb911e95c82.sentence: A set of random (stochastic) projections might be used to estimate the initial population size needed (based on the assumptions in the model) for there to be, (for example) a 95% or 99% probability of survival 1,000 years into the future.

17c3981fefd7.title: Minimum viable population
17c3981fefd7.sentence: These projections (population viability analyses, or PVA) use computer simulations to model populations using demographic and environmental information to project future population dynamics.

fa8ec1e77eec.title: Minimum viable population
fa8ec1e77eec.sentence: The probability assigned to a PVA is arrived at after repeating the environmental simulation thousands of times.

e5397d570bf4.title: Minimum viable population
e5397d570bf4.sentence: Small populations are vulnerable to genetic stochasticity, the random change in allele frequencies over time, also known as genetic drift.

d65ffa1fce53.title: Minimum viable population
d65ffa1fce53.sentence: In small populations, low genetic diversity can increase rates of inbreeding, which can result in inbreeding depression, in which a population made up of genetically similar individuals loses fitness.

86db8420b1e7.title: Minimum viable population
86db8420b1e7.sentence: The so-called "50/500 rule", where a population needs 50 individuals to prevent inbreeding depression, and 500 individuals to guard against genetic drift at-large, is an oft-used benchmark for an MVP, but 2014 guidance indicates this rule is not applicable across a wide diversity of taxa.

3fee0831962b.title: Minimum viable population
3fee0831962b.sentence: Based on a meta-analysis of reported values in the literature for many species, Traill et al. reported concerning vertebrates "a cross-species frequency distribution of MVP with a median of 4,169 individuals (95% CI = 3,577–5,129)."

8f36106555d7.title: Minimum viable population
8f36106555d7.sentence: Thus, it is useful for conservation managers and environmentalists; a population may be increased above the MVP using a captive breeding program or by bringing other members of the species in from other reserves.

9bdb5574c4b9.title: Species–area relationship
9bdb5574c4b9.sentence: The species–area relationship or species–area curve describes the relationship between the area of a habitat, or of part of a habitat, and the number of species found within that area.

3e57eca964b5.title: Species–area relationship
3e57eca964b5.sentence: Larger areas tend to contain larger numbers of species, and empirically, the relative numbers seem to follow systematic mathematical relationships.

6bf2173b72ed.title: Species–area relationship
6bf2173b72ed.sentence: Frank Preston advocated the power function based on his investigation of the lognormal species-abundance distribution.

769ad7d6bdc6.title: Species–area relationship
769ad7d6bdc6.sentence: If S is the number of species, A is the habitat area, and z is the slope of the species area relationship in log-log space, then the power function species–area relationship goes as:

263463c2da96.title: Species–area relationship
263463c2da96.sentence: The graph looks like a straight line on log–log axes, and can be linearized as:

e96d4ed4e3a0.title: Species–area relationship
e96d4ed4e3a0.sentence: In either case, the species–area relationship is almost always decelerating (has a negative second derivative) when plotted arithmetically.

53dd2be94b5c.title: Species–area relationship
53dd2be94b5c.sentence: These factors include the relative balance between immigration and extinction, rate and magnitude of disturbance on small vs. large areas, predator-prey dynamics, and clustering of individuals of the same species as a result of dispersal limitation or habitat heterogeneity.

97b9ddeacca5.title: Species–area relationship
97b9ddeacca5.sentence: Species–area relationships are often evaluated in conservation science in order to predict extinction rates in the case of habitat loss and habitat fragmentation.

45ceaed72aad.title: Species–area relationship
45ceaed72aad.sentence: Frank W. Preston, an early investigator of the theory of the species–area relationship, divided it into two types: samples (a census of a contiguous habitat that grows in the census area, also called "mainland" species–area relationships), and isolates (a census of discontiguous habitats, such as islands, also called "island" species–area relationships).

a619182dc4ae.title: Insular biogeography
a619182dc4ae.sentence: The theory was originally developed to explain the pattern of the species–area relationship occurring in oceanic islands.

1448b7941f45.title: Insular biogeography
1448b7941f45.sentence: The species-area relationship equation is: S=cAz.

21654e76920a.title: Insular biogeography
21654e76920a.sentence: This function can also be expressed as a logarithmic function: log(S)=log(c)+zlog(A) This expression of the function allows for the function to be drawn as a linear function.

28045bd6db16.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
28045bd6db16.sentence: The competitive Lotka–Volterra equations are a simple model of the population dynamics of species competing for some common resource.

9478f96a504a.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
9478f96a504a.sentence: For the competition equations, the logistic equation is the basis.

603e240ee46a.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
603e240ee46a.sentence: Given two populations, x1 and x2, with logistic dynamics, the Lotka–Volterra formulation adds an additional term to account for the species' interactions.

e90a46e5c2a3.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
e90a46e5c2a3.sentence: Here, α12 represents the effect species 2 has on the population of species 1 and α21 represents the effect species 1 has on the population of species 2.

ed194b454e43.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
ed194b454e43.sentence: Because this is the competitive version of the model, all interactions must be harmful (competition) and therefore all α-values are positive.

9063a94122a5.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
9063a94122a5.sentence: Also, note that each species can have its own growth rate and carrying capacity.

21293e3194f6.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
21293e3194f6.sentence: This model can be generalized to any number of species competing against each other.

51d3e3da4299.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
51d3e3da4299.sentence: One can think of the populations and growth rates as vectors, α's as a matrix.

12a7c425ae18.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
12a7c425ae18.sentence: So, Hirsch proved that competitive Lotka–Volterra systems cannot exhibit a limit cycle for N < 3, or any torus or chaos for N < 4.

8a5ca8800145.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
8a5ca8800145.sentence: This is still in agreement with Smale that any dynamics can occur for N ≥ 5.

3046f5b865bf.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
3046f5b865bf.sentence: For large-N systems Lotka–Volterra models are either unstable or have low connectivity.

721319432e31.title: Competitive Lotka–Volterra equations
721319432e31.sentence: Kondoh and Ackland and Gallagher have independently shown that large, stable Lotka–Volterra systems arise if the elements of αij (i.e. the features of the species) can evolve in accordance with natural selection.

e3d75c4ffa88.title: Allee effect
e3d75c4ffa88.sentence: The Allee effect is a phenomenon in biology characterized by a correlation between population size or density and the mean individual fitness (often measured as per capita population growth rate) of a population or species.

01b156f18d24.title: Allee effect
01b156f18d24.sentence: The generally accepted definition of Allee effect is positive density dependence, or the positive correlation between population density and individual fitness.

e2429a43ec41.title: Allee effect
e2429a43ec41.sentence: The classical view of population dynamics stated that due to competition for resources, a population will experience a reduced overall growth rate at higher density and increased growth rate at lower density.

1334611a98a9.title: Allee effect
1334611a98a9.sentence: However, the concept of the Allee effect introduced the idea that the reverse holds true when the population density is low.

a3f86f1e1014.title: Allee effect
a3f86f1e1014.sentence: Although the concept of Allee effect had no title at the time, it was first described in the 1930s by its namesake, Warder Clyde Allee.

ef952cc995f7.title: Allee effect
ef952cc995f7.sentence: Through experimental studies, Allee was able to demonstrate that goldfish have a greater survival rate when there are more individuals in the tank.

b0991d8b6f74.title: Allee effect
b0991d8b6f74.sentence: Although numerous ecological mechanisms for Allee effects exist, the list of most commonly cited facilitative behaviors that contribute to Allee effects in the literature include: mate limitation, cooperative defense, cooperative feeding, and environmental conditioning.

e1478d7bf188.title: Allee effect
e1478d7bf188.sentence: It is sometimes referred to as "undercrowding" and it is analogous (or even considered synonymous by some) to "depensation" in the field of fishery sciences.

2d243420fb9b.title: Allee effect
2d243420fb9b.sentence: Demographic and mathematical studies demonstrate that the existence of an Allee effect can reduce the speed of range expansion of a population and can even prevent biological invasions.

a6af02b89368.title: Alternative stable state
a6af02b89368.sentence: Also, Beisner et al. (2003) suggest that commercially exploited fish populations can be forced between alternative stable states by fishing pressure due to Allee effect that work at very low population sizes.

03210e495290.title: Population dynamics
03210e495290.sentence: Such populations grow in discrete reproductive periods between intervals of abstinence, as opposed to populations which grow without designated periods for reproduction.

8eaeacab1dbd.title: Population dynamics
8eaeacab1dbd.sentence: This equation means that the sequence (Nt) is geometric with first term N0 and common ratio 1 + R, which we define to be λ. λ is also called the finite rate of increase.

de6c33d8f1b1.title: Population dynamics
de6c33d8f1b1.sentence: Therefore, by induction, we obtain the expression of the population size at time t: Nt=λtN0 where λt is the finite rate of increase raised to the power of the number of generations.

79e86e0e39c9.title: Population dynamics
79e86e0e39c9.sentence: - If λ > 1, i.e. if R > 0, i.e. (with the assumption that both birth and death rate do not depend on time t) if b0 > d0, i.e. if the birth rate is strictly greater than the death rate, then the population size is increasing and tends to infinity.

fbc134598b7f.title: Population dynamics
fbc134598b7f.sentence: - If λ < 1, i.e. if R < 0, i.e. (with the assumption that both birth and death rate do not depend on time t) if b0 < d0, i.e. if the birth rate is strictly smaller than the death rate, then the population size is decreasing and tends to 0.

cb600a61fcb9.title: Population dynamics
cb600a61fcb9.sentence: - If λ = 1, i.e. if R = 0, i.e. (with the assumption that both birth and death rate do not depend on time t) if b0 = d0, i.e. if the birth rate is equal to the death rate, then the population size is constant, equal to the initial population N0.

02b01a9b9376.title: Population dynamics
02b01a9b9376.sentence: The doubling time (td) of a population is the time required for the population to grow to twice its size.

32f508386043.title: Population dynamics
32f508386043.sentence: The doubling time can be found by taking logarithms.

a56e2edb5e1c.title: Population dynamics
a56e2edb5e1c.sentence: Of course, in real life, a population cannot grow indefinitely: at some point the population lacks resources and so the death rate increases, which invalidates our core assumption because the death rate now depends on time.

681892786316.title: Population dynamics
681892786316.sentence: The rate at which a population increases in size if there are no density-dependent forces regulating the population is known as the intrinsic rate of increase.

df4662e9bcaf.title: Population dynamics
df4662e9bcaf.sentence: Thus r is the maximum theoretical rate of increase of a population per individual – that is, the maximum population growth rate.

b7a8febe2982.title: Population dynamics
b7a8febe2982.sentence: It is dNdt=rN where the derivative dN/dt is the rate of increase of the population, N is the population size, and r is the intrinsic rate of increase.

7436f8f0a673.title: Population dynamics
7436f8f0a673.sentence: The concept is commonly used in insect population ecology or management to determine how environmental factors affect the rate at which pest populations increase.

f35ce499114a.title: Population dynamics
f35ce499114a.section: Geometric populations > Mathematical relationship between geometric and logistic populations
f35ce499114a.sentence: To find the relationship between a geometric population and a logistic population, we assume the Nt is the same for both models, and we expand to the following equality: N0ert=N0λtert=λtrt=tln⁡(λ) Giving us r=ln⁡(λ) and λ=er.

70b6e82e396a.title: Recruitment (biology)
70b6e82e396a.sentence: In population dynamics, recruitment is the process by which new individuals are added to a population, whether by birth and maturation or by immigration.

abede8eec1de.title: Recruitment (biology)
abede8eec1de.section: Recruitment in population dynamics > Definition and importance
abede8eec1de.sentence: Successful recruitment is contingent on an individual surviving and integrating within the population; in some studies, individuals are only considered to have been recruited into a population once they've reached a certain size or life stage.

b68c9c56f89c.title: Recruitment (biology)
b68c9c56f89c.section: Recruitment in population dynamics > Definition and importance
b68c9c56f89c.sentence: Recruitment can be hard to assess due to the multitude of factors that affect it, such as predation, birth, and dispersal rates and environmental factors like temperature, precipitation, and natural disturbances.

b54591d6ccb7.title: Recruitment (biology)
b54591d6ccb7.section: Recruitment in population dynamics > Definition and importance
b54591d6ccb7.sentence: High recruitment may increase a species' current and future abundance within a system, whereas low recruitment can lead to reduced current and future abundance.

70ae363b78d6.title: Recruitment (biology)
70ae363b78d6.section: Recruitment in population dynamics > Common study systems > Aquatic systems
70ae363b78d6.sentence: For this reason, and due to their economic importance, recruitment has commonly been studied in fishery systems.

fe561504b5ac.title: Carrying capacity
fe561504b5ac.sentence: Because the population of a species which is brought below its carrying capacity due to fishing will find itself in the exponential phase of growth, as seen in the Verhulst model, the harvesting of an amount of fish at or below MSY is a surplus yield which can be sustainably harvested without reducing population size at equilibrium, keeping the population at its maximum recruitment.

ff686168331d.title: Logistic function
ff686168331d.section: Applications > In economics and sociology: diffusion of innovations
ff686168331d.sentence: The logistic function can be used to illustrate the progress of the diffusion of an innovation through its life cycle.

c0024712fa6f.title: Logistic function
c0024712fa6f.section: Applications > In economics and sociology: diffusion of innovations
c0024712fa6f.sentence: The ensuing situation halts or stabilizes the progress of the innovation, which approaches an asymptote.

0e2a0a020c1e.title: Logistic function
0e2a0a020c1e.section: Applications > In economics and sociology: diffusion of innovations
0e2a0a020c1e.sentence: In The Laws of Imitation (1890), Gabriel Tarde describes the rise and spread of new ideas through imitative chains.

58babbfec7ea.title: Logistic function
58babbfec7ea.section: Applications > In economics and sociology: diffusion of innovations
58babbfec7ea.sentence: In particular, Tarde identifies three main stages through which innovations spread: the first one corresponds to the difficult beginnings, during which the idea has to struggle within a hostile environment full of opposing habits and beliefs; the second one corresponds to the properly exponential take-off of the idea, with f(x)=2x; finally, the third stage is logarithmic, with f(x)=log⁡(x), and corresponds to the time when the impulse of the idea gradually slows down while, simultaneously new opponent ideas appear.

b555ae705584.title: Logistic function
b555ae705584.section: Applications > In economics and sociology: diffusion of innovations
b555ae705584.sentence: Historically, when new products are introduced there is an intense amount of research and development which leads to dramatic improvements in quality and reductions in cost.

15c6b31cdb85.title: Logistic function
15c6b31cdb85.section: Applications > In economics and sociology: diffusion of innovations
15c6b31cdb85.sentence: This leads to a period of rapid industry growth.

65a7d71760bb.title: Logistic function
65a7d71760bb.section: Applications > In economics and sociology: diffusion of innovations
65a7d71760bb.sentence: Some of the more famous examples are: railroads, incandescent light bulbs, electrification, cars and air travel.

6af58365bc94.title: Biological dispersal
6af58365bc94.sentence: A dispersal barrier may result in a dispersal range of a species much smaller than the species' distribution.

91c702ba5b94.title: Biological dispersal
91c702ba5b94.sentence: An artificial example is habitat fragmentation due to human land use.

692c74e6ccce.title: Biological dispersal
692c74e6ccce.sentence: By contrast, natural barriers to dispersal that limit species distribution include mountain ranges and rivers.

1dc4cd5d0699.title: Biological dispersal
1dc4cd5d0699.sentence: An example is the separation of the ranges of the two species of chimpanzee by the Congo River.

7e10e53d06df.title: Biological dispersal
7e10e53d06df.sentence: The formation of barriers to dispersal or gene flow between adjacent areas can isolate populations on either side of the emerging divide.

b41daa84f3a6.title: Biological dispersal
b41daa84f3a6.sentence: Geographic separation and subsequent genetic isolation of portions of an ancestral population can result in allopatric speciation.

4dafd6829e23.title: Biological dispersal
4dafd6829e23.sentence: The dispersal distance is usually described by a dispersal kernel which gives the probability distribution of the distance traveled by any individual.

233829e27023.title: Biological dispersal
233829e27023.sentence: Dispersal is most commonly quantified either in terms of rate or distance.

b80425c28b28.title: Biological dispersal
b80425c28b28.sentence: Dispersal rate (also called migration rate in the population genetics literature) or probability describes the probability that any individual leaves an area or, equivalently, the expected proportion of individuals who leave an area.

c5d7643320f0.title: Biological dispersal
c5d7643320f0.sentence: A number of different functions are used for dispersal kernels in theoretical models of dispersal including the negative exponential distribution, extended negative exponential distribution, normal distribution, exponential power distribution, inverse power distribution, and the two-sided power distribution.

e7b139a07f55.title: Biological dispersal
e7b139a07f55.sentence: The inverse power distribution and distributions with 'fat tails,' representing long-distance dispersal events (called leptokurtic distributions) are thought to best match empirical dispersal data.

ca30bcebc748.title: Biological dispersal
ca30bcebc748.sentence: There are two forms of human-mediated dispersal:

fc814135ddb2.title: Biological dispersal
fc814135ddb2.sentence: In Human-Vectored Dispersal, humans directly move the organism.

624bdab7efb4.title: Biological dispersal
624bdab7efb4.sentence: Human-Altered Dispersal signifies the effects that have occurred due to human interference with landscapes and animals.

c6afe96edbc0.title: Biological dispersal
c6afe96edbc0.sentence: This can occur deliberately, like for the usage of the animal in an agricultural setting, hunting, or more.

772204b5402e.title: Biological dispersal
772204b5402e.sentence: However, it can also occur accidentally, if the organism attaches itself to a person or vehicle.

1df77e176c00.title: Biological dispersal
1df77e176c00.sentence: Dispersal through a human can be many times more successful in distance compared to movement by wild or other environmental means.

6d6db16b385c.title: Biological dispersal
6d6db16b385c.sentence: On the other hand, human activities may also expand the dispersal range of a species by providing new dispersal methods (e.g., ballast water from ships).

8c292c58c959.title: Biological dispersal
8c292c58c959.section: Dispersal range > Urban Environments and Dispersal Range
8c292c58c959.sentence: While animals and physical factors (i.e. wind, water, etc.) have played a role in dispersal for centuries, motor vehicles have recently been considered major dispersal vectors.

28625f3da43f.title: Biological dispersal
28625f3da43f.section: Dispersal range > Urban Environments and Dispersal Range
28625f3da43f.sentence: This could lead to potential sources of invasive species on the urban-rural gradient.

15b4d525d571.title: Biological dispersal
15b4d525d571.sentence: Seed dispersal is the movement or transport of seeds away from the parent plant.

713943f77b88.title: Biological dispersal
713943f77b88.sentence: There are five main modes of seed dispersal: gravity, wind, ballistic, water, and animals.

020868a4fd02.title: Biological dispersal
020868a4fd02.sentence: The patterns of seed dispersal are determined in large part by the specific dispersal mechanism, and this has important implications for the demographic and genetic structure of plant populations, as well as their migration patterns and species interactions.

2a0f40b7309a.title: Biological dispersal
2a0f40b7309a.sentence: Transport by animals is especially effective, as it allows travel over far distances.

f996ce3ff385.title: Seed dispersal
f996ce3ff385.sentence: Plants have limited mobility and rely upon a variety of dispersal vectors to transport their seeds, including both abiotic vectors, such as wind and water, and living (biotic) vectors such as birds and mammals.

1326ef2e4284.title: R/K selection theory
1326ef2e4284.sentence: Because of their higher reproductive rates and ecological opportunism, primary colonisers typically are r-strategists and they are followed by a succession of increasingly competitive flora and fauna.

b3ca4d137908.title: R/K selection theory
b3ca4d137908.sentence: Eventually a new equilibrium is approached (sometimes referred to as a climax community), with r-strategists gradually being replaced by K-strategists which are more competitive and better adapted to the emerging micro-environmental characteristics of the landscape.

9f1610c8723a.title: R/K selection theory
9f1610c8723a.sentence: In areas of major ecological disruption or sterilisation (such as after a major volcanic eruption, as at Krakatoa or Mount St. Helens), r- and K-strategists play distinct roles in the ecological succession that regenerates the ecosystem.

85a2d63eeef4.title: R/K selection theory
85a2d63eeef4.sentence: However, the intermediate disturbance hypothesis posits that intermediate levels of disturbance in a landscape create patches at different levels of succession, promoting coexistence of colonizers and competitors at the regional scale.

a1acaee0c6a9.title: Leslie matrix
a1acaee0c6a9.sentence: The Leslie matrix is a discrete, age-structured model of population growth named after Patrick H. Leslie and used in population ecology.

060655def2e3.title: Leslie matrix
060655def2e3.sentence: In a Leslie model, the population is divided into groups based on age classes.

97cc762b9c4f.title: Leslie matrix
97cc762b9c4f.sentence: The Leslie matrix (also called the Leslie model) is one of the most well-known ways to describe the growth of populations (and their projected age distribution), in which a population is closed to migration, growing in an unlimited environment, and where only one sex, usually the female, is considered.

2625fdb6c5d7.title: Leslie matrix
2625fdb6c5d7.sentence: - nx, the count of individuals (n) of each age class x

948346d3b5d4.title: Leslie matrix
948346d3b5d4.sentence: - sx, the fraction of individuals that survives from age class x to age class x+1,

04d561ce5db5.title: Leslie matrix
04d561ce5db5.sentence: - fx, fecundity, the per capita average number of female offspring reaching n0 born from mother of the age class x.

ae0b54de9747.title: Leslie matrix
ae0b54de9747.sentence: At each time step, the population vector is multiplied by the Leslie matrix to generate the population vector for the subsequent time step.

43457a85e31b.title: Leslie matrix
43457a85e31b.sentence: The dominant eigenvalue of 𝐋, denoted λ, gives the population's asymptotic growth rate (growth rate at the stable age distribution).

d15224862069.title: Leslie matrix
d15224862069.sentence: The corresponding eigenvector provides the stable age distribution, the proportion of individuals of each age within the population, which remains constant at this point of asymptotic growth barring changes to vital rates.

1cb07ffc51f3.title: Allee effect
1cb07ffc51f3.sentence: However, when rare species are more desirable than common species, prices for rare species can exceed high harvest costs.

384014f7b8e0.title: Allee effect
384014f7b8e0.sentence: This phenomenon can create an "anthropogenic" Allee effect where rare species go extinct but common species are sustainably harvested.

9a73ab24576b.title: Allee effect
9a73ab24576b.sentence: Classic economic theory predicts that human exploitation of a population is unlikely to result in species extinction because the escalating costs to find the last few individuals will exceed the fixed price one achieves by selling the individuals on the market.

822f212b4e1a.title: Allee effect
822f212b4e1a.sentence: The anthropogenic Allee effect has become a standard approach for conceptualizing the threat of economic markets on endangered species.

b6578c44b521.title: Allee effect
b6578c44b521.sentence: It turns out that a two dimensional analysis yields an Allee curve in human exploiter and biological population space and that this curve separating species destined to extinction vs persistence can be complicated.

84856f0e638d.title: Allee effect
84856f0e638d.sentence: Even very high population sizes can potentially pass through the originally proposed Allee thresholds on predestined paths to extinction.

8df4b27f9892.title: Allee effect
8df4b27f9892.section: Definition > Strong vs. weak Allee effects
8df4b27f9892.sentence: The strong Allee effect is a demographic Allee effect with a critical population size or density.

cb8eac280b65.title: Allee effect
cb8eac280b65.section: Definition > Strong vs. weak Allee effects
cb8eac280b65.sentence: The weak Allee effect is a demographic Allee effect without a critical population size or density.

59fcf52ac05c.title: Allee effect
59fcf52ac05c.section: Definition > Strong vs. weak Allee effects
59fcf52ac05c.sentence: A population exhibiting a weak Allee effect will possess a reduced per capita growth rate (directly related to individual fitness of the population) at lower population density or size.

5bc20ef9189a.title: Allee effect
5bc20ef9189a.section: Definition > Strong vs. weak Allee effects
5bc20ef9189a.sentence: However, even at this low population size or density, the population will always exhibit a positive per capita growth rate.

69b35e497796.title: Allee effect
69b35e497796.section: Definition > Strong vs. weak Allee effects
69b35e497796.sentence: Meanwhile, a population exhibiting a strong Allee effect will have a critical population size or density under which the population growth rate becomes negative.

57b184701750.title: Allee effect
57b184701750.section: Definition > Strong vs. weak Allee effects
57b184701750.sentence: Therefore, when the population density or size hits a number below this threshold, the population will be destined for extinction without any further aid.

fa2aaa329d09.title: Allee effect
fa2aaa329d09.sentence: A simple mathematical example of an Allee effect is given by the cubic growth model.

c26f8f06c9de.title: Allee effect
c26f8f06c9de.sentence: where the population has a negative growth rate for 0<N<A, and a positive growth rate for A<N<K (assuming 0<A<K).

754720d1b0a5.title: Leslie matrix
754720d1b0a5.sentence: This age-structured growth model suggests a steady-state, or stable, age-structure and growth rate.

d4d84ab9fc98.title: Leslie matrix
d4d84ab9fc98.sentence: Regardless of the initial population size, N0, or age distribution, the population tends asymptotically to this age-structure and growth rate.

9fcdc4b5a8e0.title: Leslie matrix
9fcdc4b5a8e0.sentence: It also returns to this state following perturbation.

c616cf7401da.title: Leslie matrix
c616cf7401da.sentence: Once the stable age distribution has been reached, a population undergoes exponential growth at rate λ.

342d5e016706.title: Leslie matrix
342d5e016706.sentence: For example, a population with a large intrinsic growth rate will have a disproportionately “young” age-structure.

08977b21b3c7.title: Leslie matrix
08977b21b3c7.sentence: A population with high mortality rates at all ages (i.e. low survival) will have a similar age-structure.

673c33681fad.title: Photosynthesis
673c33681fad.sentence: Photosynthesis is a system of biological processes by which photopigment-bearing autotrophic organisms, such as most plants, algae and cyanobacteria, convert light energy—typically from sunlight—into the chemical energy necessary to fuel their metabolism.

b9e87269b5ee.title: Photosynthesis
b9e87269b5ee.sentence: The term photosynthesis usually refers to oxygenic photosynthesis, a process that releases oxygen as a byproduct of water splitting.

632d3708a515.title: Photosynthesis
632d3708a515.sentence: Photosynthetic organisms store the converted chemical energy within the bonds of intracellular organic compounds (complex compounds containing carbon), typically carbohydrates like sugars (mainly glucose, fructose and sucrose), starches, phytoglycogen and cellulose.

1b3dc2925def.title: Photosynthesis
1b3dc2925def.sentence: When needing to use this stored energy, an organism's cells then metabolize the organic compounds through cellular respiration.

75f9dcf678d1.title: Photosynthesis
75f9dcf678d1.sentence: Photosynthesis plays a critical role in producing and maintaining the oxygen content of the Earth's atmosphere, and it supplies most of the biological energy necessary for complex life on Earth.

6d22f4ca47f9.title: Photosynthesis
6d22f4ca47f9.sentence: The average rate of energy captured by global photosynthesis is approximately 130 terawatts, which is about eight times the total power consumption of human civilization.

2c5a4f039c5b.title: Photosynthesis
2c5a4f039c5b.sentence: Photosynthetic organisms also convert around 100–115 billion tons (91–104 Pg petagrams, or billions of metric tons), of carbon into biomass per year.

da60daff5ed3.title: Photosynthesis
da60daff5ed3.sentence: Cyanobacteria appeared later; the excess oxygen they produced contributed directly to the oxygenation of the Earth, which rendered the evolution of complex life possible.

94f5d77c47e2.title: Photosynthesis
94f5d77c47e2.section: Experimental history > Development of the concept
94f5d77c47e2.sentence: In 1893, the American botanist Charles Reid Barnes proposed two terms, photosyntax and photosynthesis, for the biological process of synthesis of complex carbon compounds out of carbonic acid, in the presence of chlorophyll, under the influence of light.

5afbc5d91182.title: Biogeochemical cycle
5afbc5d91182.sentence: A biogeochemical cycle, or more generally a cycle of matter, is the movement and transformation of chemical elements and compounds between living organisms, the atmosphere, and the Earth's crust.

93cde9d83607.title: Biogeochemical cycle
93cde9d83607.sentence: Major biogeochemical cycles include the carbon cycle, the nitrogen cycle and the water cycle.

c6c8861b6d12.title: Biogeochemical cycle
c6c8861b6d12.sentence: In each cycle, the chemical element or molecule is transformed and cycled by living organisms and through various geological forms and reservoirs, including the atmosphere, the soil and the oceans.

0eb05319c90d.title: Biogeochemical cycle
0eb05319c90d.sentence: Energy flows directionally through ecosystems, entering as sunlight (or inorganic molecules for chemoautotrophs) and leaving as heat during the many transfers between trophic levels.

03448e7156b6.title: Biogeochemical cycle
03448e7156b6.sentence: However, the matter that makes up living organisms is conserved and recycled.

0ce456d9fb8e.title: Biogeochemical cycle
0ce456d9fb8e.sentence: The six most common elements associated with organic molecules — carbon, nitrogen, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulfur — take a variety of chemical forms and may exist for long periods in the atmosphere, on land, in water, or beneath the Earth's surface.

052331d97f9c.title: Biogeochemical cycle
052331d97f9c.sentence: Geologic processes, such as weathering, erosion, water drainage, and the subduction of the continental plates, all play a role in this recycling of materials.

46b373b14d06.title: Biogeochemical cycle
46b373b14d06.sentence: Because geology and chemistry have major roles in the study of this process, the recycling of inorganic matter between living organisms and their environment is called a biogeochemical cycle.

a71d2c464018.title: Biogeochemical cycle
a71d2c464018.sentence: Microorganisms drive much of the biogeochemical cycling in the earth system.

5c2c5de60cc4.title: Biogeochemical cycle
5c2c5de60cc4.sentence: Climate change and human impacts are drastically changing the speed, intensity, and balance of these relatively unknown cycles, which include:

065e7c874d22.title: Carbon cycle
065e7c874d22.sentence: The carbon cycle is a part of the biogeochemical cycle where carbon is exchanged among the biosphere, pedosphere, geosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere of Earth.

69ca9a7f6c3c.title: Carbon cycle
69ca9a7f6c3c.sentence: Carbon is the main component of biological compounds as well as a major component of many rocks such as limestone.

24db643a7ce8.title: Carbon cycle
24db643a7ce8.sentence: It describes the movement of carbon as it is recycled and reused throughout the biosphere, as well as long-term processes of carbon sequestration (storage) to and release from carbon sinks.

99da588b5d18.title: Carbon cycle
99da588b5d18.sentence: The carbon cycle comprises a sequence of events that are key to making Earth capable of sustaining life.

0e5e20bade7e.title: Carbon cycle
0e5e20bade7e.sentence: Carbon in the Earth's atmosphere exists in two main forms: carbon dioxide and methane.

05c81a1658f3.title: Carbon cycle
05c81a1658f3.sentence: Both of these gases absorb and retain heat in the atmosphere and are partially responsible for the greenhouse effect.

3df60a53cc8e.title: Carbon cycle
3df60a53cc8e.sentence: Carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere primarily through photosynthesis and enters the terrestrial and oceanic biospheres.

49ae57dc1e4f.title: Carbon cycle
49ae57dc1e4f.sentence: About 500 gigatons of carbon are stored above ground in plants and other living organisms, while soil holds approximately 1,500 gigatons of carbon.

6c1d839cf9f5.title: Carbon cycle
6c1d839cf9f5.sentence: At 422.7 parts per million (ppm), the global average atmospheric carbon dioxide has set a new record high in 2024.

271748614eb6.title: Carbon cycle
271748614eb6.sentence: The carbon cycle was first described by Antoine Lavoisier and Joseph Priestley, and popularised by Humphry Davy.

27cdf0768154.title: Water cycle
27cdf0768154.sentence: The water cycle (or hydrologic cycle or hydrological cycle) is a biogeochemical cycle that involves the continuous change in form of water on, above and below the surface of the Earth across different reservoirs.

3b04974fe6b9.title: Water cycle
3b04974fe6b9.sentence: In doing so, the water goes through different phases: liquid, solid (ice) and vapor.

c9915cc1149f.title: Water cycle
c9915cc1149f.sentence: The mass of water on Earth remains fairly constant over time.

d28d72fea91d.title: Water cycle
d28d72fea91d.sentence: However, the partitioning of the water into the major reservoirs of ice, fresh water, salt water and atmospheric water is variable and depends on climatic variables.

f5a475f3a462.title: Water cycle
f5a475f3a462.sentence: The processes that drive these movements, or fluxes, are evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, sublimation, infiltration, surface runoff, and subsurface flow.

d2530f2072f3.title: Water cycle
d2530f2072f3.sentence: The water cycle is powered by the energy emitted from the sun.

f0c239139fe5.title: Water cycle
f0c239139fe5.sentence: The ocean plays a key role in the water cycle as it is the source of 86% of global evaporation.

dde4c3fa10e5.title: Water cycle
dde4c3fa10e5.sentence: Most water falls as rain back into the ocean or onto land, where the water flows over the ground as surface runoff.

012160e7afbc.title: Water cycle
012160e7afbc.sentence: Runoff is responsible for almost all of the transport of eroded sediment and phosphorus from land to waterbodies.

4c760cf8cb71.title: Water cycle
4c760cf8cb71.sentence: Both runoff and groundwater flow play significant roles in transporting nitrogen from the land to waterbodies.

5267c00cacd9.title: Water cycle
5267c00cacd9.section: Changes caused by humans > Water cycle intensification due to climate change
5267c00cacd9.sentence: The water cycle is essential to life on Earth and plays a large role in the global climate system and ocean circulation.

940255446a89.title: Nitrogen cycle
940255446a89.sentence: The nitrogen cycle is the biogeochemical cycle by which nitrogen is converted into multiple chemical forms as it circulates among atmospheric, terrestrial, and marine ecosystems.

e853011a8d9c.title: Nitrogen cycle
e853011a8d9c.sentence: Important processes in the nitrogen cycle include fixation, ammonification, nitrification, and denitrification.

9db1fa23758e.title: Nitrogen cycle
9db1fa23758e.sentence: The majority of Earth's atmosphere (78%) is atmospheric nitrogen, making it the largest source of nitrogen.

6905266c79ee.title: Nitrogen cycle
6905266c79ee.sentence: However, atmospheric nitrogen has limited availability for biological use, leading to a scarcity of usable nitrogen in many types of ecosystems.

e720fd75279c.title: Nitrogen cycle
e720fd75279c.sentence: The nitrogen cycle is of particular interest to ecologists because nitrogen availability can affect the rate of key ecosystem processes, including primary production and decomposition.

62981c6c5ed0.title: Nitrogen cycle
62981c6c5ed0.sentence: Many of these processes are carried out by microbes, either in their effort to harvest energy or to accumulate nitrogen in a form needed for their growth.

25bfa6a4c33e.title: Nitrogen cycle
25bfa6a4c33e.sentence: Plants can absorb nitrate or ammonium from the soil by their root hairs.

1c2208350177.title: Nitrogen cycle
1c2208350177.section: Human influences on the nitrogen cycle
1c2208350177.sentence: As a result of extensive cultivation of legumes (particularly soy, alfalfa, and clover), growing use of the Haber–Bosch process in the production of chemical fertilizers, and pollution emitted by vehicles and industrial plants, human beings have more than doubled the annual transfer of nitrogen into biologically available forms.

d9ff8dcc3d97.title: Evapotranspiration
d9ff8dcc3d97.sentence: Evapotranspiration (ET) refers to the combined processes that move water from the Earth's surface (open water and ice surfaces, bare soil and vegetation) into the atmosphere, including both evaporation and transpiration.

259b492d6f7e.title: Evapotranspiration
259b492d6f7e.sentence: - Evaporation: the movement of water directly to the air from sources such as the soil and water bodies.

48b3de843f77.title: Evapotranspiration
48b3de843f77.sentence: - Transpiration: the movement of water from root systems, through a plant, and exit into the air as water vapor.

310190dab0bd.title: Evapotranspiration
310190dab0bd.sentence: This exit occurs through stomata in the plant.

cc495efd21ee.title: Evapotranspiration
cc495efd21ee.sentence: Globally, it is estimated that on average between three-fifths and three-quarters of land precipitation is returned to the atmosphere via evapotranspiration.

f8a9e3779337.title: Evapotranspiration
f8a9e3779337.sentence: Evapotranspiration is typically measured in millimeters of water (i.e. volume of water moved per unit area of the Earth's surface) in a set unit of time.

99c2f952a470.title: Evapotranspiration
99c2f952a470.sentence: Levels of evapotranspiration in a given area are primarily controlled by three factors: Firstly, the amount of water present which includes the amount of available water in both the soil and in larger bodies of water.

2e143fcd95d5.title: Evapotranspiration
2e143fcd95d5.sentence: Secondly, the amount of energy present in the air and soil (e.g. heat, measured by the global surface temperature); and thirdly the ability of the atmosphere to take up water (humidity) which can cause the air temperature to vary from location to location and therefore lead to an increase of decrease in total evapotranspiration.

b7b71856d769.title: Evapotranspiration
b7b71856d769.sentence: This global warming has increased evapotranspiration over land.

2b399e16e30f.title: Evapotranspiration
2b399e16e30f.sentence: The increased evapotranspiration is one of the effects of climate change on the water cycle.

5caacdd0eb50.title: Evapotranspiration
5caacdd0eb50.sentence: Evapotranspiration is an important part of the local water cycle and climate, and measurement of it plays a key role in water resource management and agricultural irrigation.

bc50ad80c52c.title: Soil carbon
bc50ad80c52c.sentence: Soil carbon is the solid carbon stored in global soils.

1195b8ac727a.title: Soil carbon
1195b8ac727a.sentence: This includes both soil organic matter, derived from plant, animal, and microbial tissues, and inorganic carbon as carbonate minerals.

1f2f5cc507f8.title: Soil carbon
1f2f5cc507f8.sentence: Soil carbon contributes to vital functions of soil in ecosystems, including water holding capacity, nutrient retention, and soil structure.

57c1bd2f5a62.title: Soil carbon
57c1bd2f5a62.sentence: Of the 2,700 Gt of carbon stored in soils worldwide, 1550 GtC is organic and 950 GtC is inorganic carbon, which is approximately three times greater than the current atmospheric carbon and 240 times higher compared with the current annual fossil fuel emission.

99838dade3d5.title: Soil carbon
