99838dade3d5.sentence: While many environmental factors affect the total stored carbon in terrestrial ecosystems, photosynthesis, respiration, and decomposition are the main drivers in balancing the total amount of stored carbon on land.

683e0c5ed4ea.title: Soil carbon
683e0c5ed4ea.sentence: Soil carbon is a carbon sink in the global carbon cycle, playing a role in biogeochemistry, climate change mitigation.

2cf86e3f6a8f.title: Soil carbon
2cf86e3f6a8f.sentence: As such, data on soil carbon quality and change is important to constructing global climate models.

a02a510d20c9.title: Soil carbon
a02a510d20c9.sentence: Human activities have caused a massive loss of soil organic carbon; however, there is potential for human activity to intentionally divert carbon back to the soil.

15a7990988d5.title: Soil carbon
15a7990988d5.sentence: Microorganisms play an important role in breaking down carbon in the soil.

8c47f44cf2af.title: Soil carbon
8c47f44cf2af.sentence: Changes in their activity due to rising temperatures could possibly influence and even contribute to climate change.

a4f69a157c28.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
a4f69a157c28.sentence: Infiltration is the process by which water on the ground surface enters the soil.

6fbbdef3372b.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
6fbbdef3372b.sentence: The infiltration capacity is defined as the maximum rate of infiltration.

ae8272c55d3d.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
ae8272c55d3d.sentence: It is most often measured in meters per day but can also be measured in other units of distance over time if necessary.

91dce119591b.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
91dce119591b.sentence: If the precipitation rate exceeds the infiltration rate, runoff will usually occur unless there is some physical barrier.

594338e0fd16.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
594338e0fd16.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Soil characteristics
594338e0fd16.sentence: Soils that have smaller pore sizes, such as clay, have lower infiltration capacity and slower infiltration rates than soils that have large pore sizes, such as sands.

68751dfa2529.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
68751dfa2529.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Soil characteristics
68751dfa2529.sentence: Compaction of soils results in decreased porosity within the soils, which decreases infiltration capacity.

f2d779698121.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
f2d779698121.sentence: The infiltration capacity decreases as the soil moisture content of soils surface layers increases.

93be069c2a78.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
93be069c2a78.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Soil moisture content
93be069c2a78.sentence: Soil that is already saturated has no more capacity to hold more water, therefore infiltration capacity has been reached and the rate cannot increase past this point.

5befe53e3898.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
5befe53e3898.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Organic materials in soils
5befe53e3898.sentence: Vegetation contains roots that extend into the soil which create cracks and fissures in the soil, allowing for more rapid infiltration and increased capacity.

422dd923113b.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
422dd923113b.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Organic materials in soils
422dd923113b.sentence: Similarly to vegetation, animals that burrow in the soil also create cracks in the soil structure.

3cd152552103.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
3cd152552103.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Organic materials in soils
3cd152552103.sentence: When no vegetation is present infiltration rates can be very low, which can lead to excessive runoff and increased erosion levels.

d8daccec0989.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
d8daccec0989.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Land cover
d8daccec0989.sentence: If the land is covered by impermeable surfaces, such as pavement, infiltration cannot occur as the water cannot infiltrate through an impermeable surface.

0334673817ff.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
0334673817ff.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Land cover
0334673817ff.sentence: This relationship also leads to increased runoff.

403c444f268c.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
403c444f268c.sentence: When the slope of the land is higher runoff occurs more readily which leads to lower infiltration rates.

89fb19bfe2cd.title: Surface runoff
89fb19bfe2cd.sentence: Surface runoff (also known as overland flow or terrestrial runoff) is the unconfined flow of water over the ground surface, in contrast to channel runoff (or stream flow).

e9bc3b68d0ca.title: Surface runoff
e9bc3b68d0ca.sentence: It occurs when excess rainwater, stormwater, meltwater, or other sources, can no longer sufficiently rapidly infiltrate into the soil.

d47f599cc4d1.title: Surface runoff
d47f599cc4d1.sentence: This can occur when the soil is saturated by water to its full capacity, and the rain arrives more quickly than the soil can absorb it.

b1dce3e9e518.title: Surface runoff
b1dce3e9e518.sentence: Surface runoff often occurs because impervious areas (such as roofs and pavement) do not allow water to soak into the ground.

b6c75f09a505.title: Surface runoff
b6c75f09a505.sentence: Surface runoff is a major component of the water cycle.

64151c6b8413.title: Surface runoff
64151c6b8413.sentence: It is the primary agent of soil erosion by water.

a28090c932dc.title: Surface runoff
a28090c932dc.section: Effects of surface runoff > Environmental effects
a28090c932dc.sentence: The principal environmental issues associated with runoff are the impacts to surface water, groundwater and soil through transport of water pollutants to these systems.

75250ca00214.title: Surface runoff
75250ca00214.section: Effects of surface runoff > Environmental effects
75250ca00214.sentence: Some of the contaminants that create the greatest impact to surface waters arising from runoff are petroleum substances, herbicides and fertilizers.

6f1959e1d75e.title: Surface runoff
6f1959e1d75e.sentence: Increased runoff reduces groundwater recharge, thus lowering the water table and making droughts worse, especially for agricultural farmers and others who depend on the water wells.

1539fdee519b.title: Surface runoff
1539fdee519b.sentence: Flooding occurs when a watercourse is unable to convey the quantity of runoff flowing downstream.

53d267b000ce.title: Surface runoff
53d267b000ce.sentence: - Land use development controls aimed at minimizing impervious surfaces in urban areas

9494724785e3.title: Surface runoff
9494724785e3.sentence: - Erosion controls for farms and construction sites

753916466b1f.title: Surface runoff
753916466b1f.sentence: - Flood control and retrofit programs, such as green infrastructure

292afad1b8e0.title: Surface runoff
292afad1b8e0.sentence: - Chemical use and handling controls in agriculture, landscape maintenance, industrial use, etc.

17ed7b62dc4e.title: Soil erosion
17ed7b62dc4e.sentence: Soil erosion is the denudation or wearing away of the upper layer of soil.

b5d5de1e9b5b.title: Soil erosion
b5d5de1e9b5b.sentence: This natural process is caused by the dynamic activity of erosive agents, that is, water (e.g. landslide, flooding), ice (e.g. glaciers), snow (e.g. avalanches, snow gliding), air (e.g. wind), plants (e.g. tree uprooting), and animals (including humans).

1ae504c7fa9d.title: Soil erosion
1ae504c7fa9d.sentence: Soil erosion may be a slow process that continues relatively unnoticed, or it may occur at an alarming rate causing a serious loss of topsoil.

0488f3f13974.title: Soil erosion
0488f3f13974.sentence: The loss of soil from farmland may be reflected in reduced cropland area and production potential, lower surface water quality and damaged drainage networks.

dce693158a24.title: Soil erosion
dce693158a24.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Agricultural practices
dce693158a24.sentence: Unsustainable agricultural practices increase rates of erosion by one to two orders of magnitude over the natural rate and far exceed replacement by soil production.

32ee1bd97055.title: Soil erosion
32ee1bd97055.sentence: Each year, about 75 billion tons of soil is eroded from the land, a rate that is about 13–40 times as fast as the natural rate of erosion.

9aef934f5596.title: Soil erosion
9aef934f5596.sentence: Water and wind erosion are now the two primary causes of land degradation; combined, they are responsible for 84% of degraded acreage.

87438601e2b2.title: Soil erosion
87438601e2b2.sentence: Approximately 40% of the world's agricultural land is seriously degraded.

b5f9fbf40442.title: Soil erosion
b5f9fbf40442.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Soil structure and composition
b5f9fbf40442.sentence: Sediments containing more clay minerals tend to be more resistant to erosion than those with sand or silt, because the clay helps bind soil particles together.

44b3f6e65e44.title: Soil erosion
44b3f6e65e44.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Soil structure and composition
44b3f6e65e44.sentence: Soil containing high levels of organic matter are often more resistant to erosion, because the organic materials coagulate soil colloids and create a stronger, more stable soil structure.

18fe51d149a1.title: Soil erosion
18fe51d149a1.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Vegetative cover
18fe51d149a1.sentence: The roots of the plants bind the soil together, and interweave with other roots, forming a more solid mass that is less susceptible to both water and wind erosion.

885e5e7cb007.title: Soil erosion
885e5e7cb007.sentence: Longer, steeper slopes (especially those without adequate vegetative cover) are more susceptible to very high rates of erosion during heavy rains than shorter, less steep slopes.

6176262c2d0b.title: Soil erosion
6176262c2d0b.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Climate change
6176262c2d0b.sentence: Studies on soil erosion suggest that increased rainfall amounts and intensities will lead to greater rates of soil erosion.

20680ed603ef.title: Soil erosion
20680ed603ef.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Climate change
20680ed603ef.sentence: Thus, if rainfall amounts and intensities increase in many parts of the world as expected, erosion will also increase, unless amelioration measures are taken.

80f98b99edbb.title: Cellular respiration
80f98b99edbb.sentence: Cellular respiration is the process of oxidizing biological fuels using an inorganic electron acceptor, such as oxygen, to drive production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which stores chemical energy in a biologically accessible form.

730e5c650ef0.title: Cellular respiration
730e5c650ef0.sentence: Cellular respiration may be described as a set of metabolic reactions and processes that take place in the cells to transfer chemical energy from nutrients to ATP, with the flow of electrons to an electron acceptor, and then release waste products.

111ae674555a.title: Cellular respiration
111ae674555a.sentence: If the electron acceptor is oxygen, the process is more specifically known as aerobic cellular respiration.

28f2c0257b32.title: Cellular respiration
28f2c0257b32.sentence: If the electron acceptor is a molecule other than oxygen, this is anaerobic cellular respiration.

72e7ae15208d.title: Cellular respiration
72e7ae15208d.sentence: Although cellular respiration is technically a combustion reaction, it is an unusual one because of the slow, controlled release of energy from the series of reactions.

f3a0d3d2b005.title: Cellular respiration
f3a0d3d2b005.sentence: Mass balance of the global reaction: | C 6 H 12 O 6 (s) + 6 O 2 (g) → 6 CO 2 (g) + 6 H 2 O (l) + energy

aaef457bb313.title: Cellular respiration
aaef457bb313.sentence: The products of this process are carbon dioxide and water, and the energy transferred is used to make bonds between ADP and a third phosphate group to form ATP (adenosine triphosphate), by substrate-level phosphorylation, NADH and FADH2.

37ab694d0081.title: Cellular respiration
37ab694d0081.sentence: Biology textbooks often state that 38 ATP molecules can be made per oxidized glucose molecule during cellular respiration (2 from glycolysis, 2 from the Krebs cycle, and about 34 from the electron transport system).

0af66bf0f110.title: Cellular respiration
0af66bf0f110.sentence: However, this maximum yield is never quite reached because of losses due to leaky membranes as well as the cost of moving pyruvate and ADP into the mitochondrial matrix, and current estimates range around 29 to 30 ATP per glucose.

e8b5d78d98c0.title: Cellular respiration
e8b5d78d98c0.sentence: Aerobic metabolism is up to 15 times more efficient than anaerobic metabolism (which yields 2 molecules of ATP per 1 molecule of glucose).

b91c025c6caf.title: Cellular respiration
b91c025c6caf.sentence: Although plants are net consumers of carbon dioxide and producers of oxygen via photosynthesis, plant respiration accounts for about half of the CO2 generated annually by terrestrial ecosystems.

faa1350c7328.title: Ecological efficiency
faa1350c7328.sentence: The energy remaining after respiration is considered the net primary production.

ba78068666b2.title: Haber process
ba78068666b2.sentence: The Haber process, also called the Haber–Bosch process, is the main industrial method for making ammonia.

d1b02bbf81b2.title: Haber process
d1b02bbf81b2.sentence: It combines nitrogen from the air with hydrogen, using an iron catalyst, to form ammonia (NH3).

0d922783822f.title: Haber process
0d922783822f.sentence: Most of the ammonia is used to make nitrogen fertilizer, either directly or as ammonium nitrate and urea.

c186f2a8a7bc.title: Haber process
c186f2a8a7bc.sentence: Haber showed it working in the laboratory in 1909, and Bosch scaled it up for the German company BASF.

34482dae3335.title: Haber process
34482dae3335.sentence: During the 19th century, the demand rapidly increased for nitrates and ammonia for use as nitrogen fertilizers, which can supply plants with extra nitrogen compounds, and for industrial feedstocks.

3d9c2d2c5c5b.title: Haber process
3d9c2d2c5c5b.sentence: The main source was mining niter deposits and guano from tropical islands.

978cc0ac58af.title: Haber process
978cc0ac58af.sentence: At the beginning of the 20th century these reserves were thought insufficient to satisfy future demands, and research into new potential sources of ammonia increased.

5389ecc6dbf1.title: Haber process
5389ecc6dbf1.sentence: Hydrogen required for ammonia synthesis is most often produced through gasification of hydrocarbons, mostly natural gas, but other potential hydrogen sources include coal, petroleum, peat, biomass, or waste.

eabdccb42e43.title: Haber process
eabdccb42e43.sentence: As of 2012, the global production of ammonia produced from natural gas using the steam reforming process was 72%; however, in China as of 2022, natural gas and coal were responsible for 20% and 75% respectively.

7fbc66f4f617.title: Haber process
7fbc66f4f617.sentence: Combined with the energy needed to produce hydrogen and purified atmospheric nitrogen, ammonia production is energy-intensive, accounting for 1–2% of global energy consumption, 3% of global carbon emissions, and 3% to 5% of natural gas consumption.

b7478986c72b.title: Haber process
b7478986c72b.sentence: As of 2018, the Haber process produced 230 million tonnes of anhydrous ammonia per year.

e8037f124e10.title: Phosphorus cycle
e8037f124e10.sentence: The phosphorus cycle is the biogeochemical cycle that involves the movement of phosphorus through the lithosphere, hydrosphere, and biosphere.

81b24f04111d.title: Phosphorus cycle
81b24f04111d.sentence: Unlike many other biogeochemical cycles, the atmosphere does not play a significant role in the movement of phosphorus, because phosphorus and phosphorus-based materials do not enter the gaseous phase readily, as the main source of gaseous phosphorus, phosphine, is only produced in isolated and specific conditions.

b8b68daa1021.title: Phosphorus cycle
b8b68daa1021.sentence: Living organisms require phosphorus, a vital component of DNA, RNA, and ATP, for their proper functioning.

beab1686d534.title: Phosphorus cycle
beab1686d534.sentence: In animals, inorganic phosphorus in the form of apatite (Ca5(PO4)3(OH,F)) is also a key component of bones and teeth (tooth enamel).

529401b86e7a.title: Phosphorus cycle
529401b86e7a.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
529401b86e7a.sentence: Phosphates move quickly through plants and animals; however, the processes that move them through the soil or ocean are very slow, making the phosphorus cycle overall one of the slowest biogeochemical cycles.

6e71c9848e23.title: Phosphorus cycle
6e71c9848e23.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
6e71c9848e23.sentence: The global phosphorus cycle includes four major processes:

f7d7e067b748.title: Phosphorus cycle
f7d7e067b748.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
f7d7e067b748.sentence: (i) tectonic uplift and exposure of phosphorus-bearing rocks such as apatite to surface weathering;

8b3ce0820e6f.title: Phosphorus cycle
8b3ce0820e6f.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
8b3ce0820e6f.sentence: (ii) physical erosion, and chemical and biological weathering of phosphorus-bearing rocks to provide dissolved and particulate phosphorus to soils, lakes and rivers;

fe3849cb8021.title: Phosphorus cycle
fe3849cb8021.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
fe3849cb8021.sentence: (iii) riverine and subsurface transportation of phosphorus to various lakes and run-off to the ocean;

c86e7882a554.title: Phosphorus cycle
c86e7882a554.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
c86e7882a554.sentence: (iv) sedimentation of particulate phosphorus (e.g., phosphorus associated with organic matter and oxide/carbonate minerals) and eventually burial in marine sediments (this process can also occur in lakes and rivers).

fe0184462caa.title: Phosphorus cycle
fe0184462caa.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
fe0184462caa.sentence: The availability of phosphorus in an ecosystem is restricted by its rate of release during weathering.

afc970c35f51.title: Phosphorus cycle
afc970c35f51.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Ecological function
afc970c35f51.sentence: It can be a limiting nutrient for aquatic organisms.

8c77fc3754ae.title: Phosphorus cycle
8c77fc3754ae.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Ecological function
8c77fc3754ae.sentence: Phosphates which are found in fertilizers, sewage and detergents, can cause pollution in lakes and streams.

731296f6c904.title: Phosphorus cycle
731296f6c904.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Ecological function
731296f6c904.sentence: Freshwater algal blooms are generally caused by excess phosphorus, while those that take place in saltwater tend to result from excess nitrogen.

b4fcc36d746c.title: Nutrient pollution
b4fcc36d746c.sentence: Nutrient pollution is a form of water pollution caused by too many nutrients entering the water.

83a889678e64.title: Nutrient pollution
83a889678e64.sentence: It is a primary cause of eutrophication of surface waters (lakes, rivers and coastal waters), in which excess nutrients, usually nitrogen or phosphorus, stimulate algal growth.

342b33aaa701.title: Nutrient pollution
342b33aaa701.sentence: Sources of nutrient pollution include surface runoff from farms, waste from septic tanks, feedlots, and emissions from burning fuels.

c47d61f09835.title: Nutrient pollution
c47d61f09835.sentence: Raw sewage, which is rich in nutrients, is also a contributing factor when dumped in water bodies.

b207e55f2391.title: Nutrient pollution
b207e55f2391.sentence: When nitrogen and phosphorus are not fully used by the growing plants, they are lost from the farm fields and negatively impact air and downstream water quality.

1ae168274238.title: Nutrient pollution
1ae168274238.sentence: Excess nitrogen causes environmental problems such as harmful algal blooms, hypoxia, acid rain, nitrogen saturation in forests, and climate change.

c596bbba7adb.title: Nutrient pollution
c596bbba7adb.sentence: Nutrient pollution can have economic impacts due to increasing water treatment costs, commercial fishing, shellfish losses, recreational fishing losses, and reduced tourism income.

b827d097d2d9.title: Nutrient pollution
b827d097d2d9.sentence: Human health effects include excess nitrate in drinking water (blue baby syndrome) and disinfection by-products in drinking water.

ed8c46495080.title: Nutrient pollution
ed8c46495080.sentence: Swimming in water affected by a harmful algal bloom can cause skin rashes and respiratory problems.

686cd1e21636.title: Nutrient pollution
686cd1e21636.sentence: These include installing buffer zones of vegetation around farms or artificial wetlands to absorb excess nutrients.

21b114ed8560.title: Nutrient pollution
21b114ed8560.sentence: Additionally, better wastewater treatment and reducing sewage dumping can help limit nutrient discharge into water systems.

54372f85e54f.title: Nutrient pollution
54372f85e54f.sentence: Finally, countries can create a permit system under the polluter pays principle.

ef3198503619.title: Nutrient pollution
ef3198503619.sentence: Finally, by vegetating drainage ditches, there is another opportunity for excess nutrients to be captured.

360d4bcf0758.title: Nutrient pollution
360d4bcf0758.section: Reducing nutrient pollution > Nutrient source apportionment
360d4bcf0758.sentence: Agriculture is typically the principal source of nitrogen in water bodies in Europe, whereas in many countries households and industries tend to be the dominant contributors of phosphorus.

61595629d8fc.title: Eutrophication
61595629d8fc.sentence: Eutrophication is a general term describing a process in which nutrients accumulate in a body of water, resulting in an increased growth of organisms that may deplete the oxygen in the water; i.e. the process of too many plants growing on the surface of a river, lake, etc., often because chemicals that are used to help crops grow have been carried there by rain.

11ced5b84ee8.title: Eutrophication
11ced5b84ee8.sentence: Eutrophication is caused by excessive concentrations of nutrients, most commonly phosphates and nitrates, although this varies with location.

9eafca01e050.title: Eutrophication
9eafca01e050.sentence: Eutrophication may occur naturally or as a result of human actions.

a83f4f7ea683.title: Eutrophication
a83f4f7ea683.sentence: Manmade, or cultural, eutrophication occurs when sewage, industrial wastewater, fertilizer runoff, and other nutrient sources are released into the environment.

f28c2242dfec.title: Eutrophication
f28c2242dfec.sentence: Such nutrient pollution usually causes algal blooms and bacterial growth, resulting in the depletion of dissolved oxygen in water and causing substantial environmental degradation.

a66ba2430771.title: Eutrophication
a66ba2430771.sentence: Eutrophication can have the following ecological effects: increased biomass of phytoplankton, changes in macrophyte species composition and biomass, dissolved oxygen depletion, increased incidences of fish kills, loss of desirable fish species.

08bacd9a7956.title: Eutrophication
08bacd9a7956.sentence: Surveys showed that 54% of lakes in Asia are eutrophic; in Europe, 53%; in North America, 48%; in South America, 41%; and in Africa, 28%.

be1f96a41801.title: Eutrophication
be1f96a41801.sentence: The World Resources Institute has identified 375 hypoxic coastal zones in the world, concentrated in coastal areas in Western Europe, the Eastern and Southern coasts of the US, and East Asia, particularly Japan.

7636baca0ba3.title: Eutrophication
7636baca0ba3.sentence: The term "eutrophication" comes from the Greek eutrophos, meaning "well-nourished",.

d91e97085ffb.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
d91e97085ffb.sentence: Hypoxia refers to low oxygen conditions.

3e2735639df5.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
3e2735639df5.sentence: Hypoxia applies to many situations, but usually refers to the atmosphere and natural waters.

359359bbd797.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
359359bbd797.sentence: A system with low concentration—in the range between 1 and 30% saturation—is called hypoxic or dysoxic.

e8cd6a88507d.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
e8cd6a88507d.sentence: An aquatic system lacking dissolved oxygen (0% saturation) is termed anaerobic, reducing, or anoxic.

865c39ce619e.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
865c39ce619e.sentence: Most fish cannot live below 30% saturation since they rely on oxygen to derive energy from their nutrients.

bfd9a7828c60.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
bfd9a7828c60.sentence: A "healthy" aquatic environment should seldom experience less than 80% saturation.

06d0721124ef.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
06d0721124ef.sentence: Oxygen depletion can result from a number of natural factors, but is most often a concern as a consequence of pollution and eutrophication in which plant nutrients enter a river, lake, or ocean, and phytoplankton blooms are encouraged.

f107223f57fa.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
f107223f57fa.sentence: When phytoplankton cells die, they sink towards the bottom and are decomposed by bacteria, a process that further reduces DO in the water column.

45cafca8b79d.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
45cafca8b79d.sentence: Hypoxia may also occur in the absence of pollutants.

c788d40c4b99.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
c788d40c4b99.sentence: In estuaries, for example, because freshwater flowing from a river into the sea is less dense than salt water, stratification in the water column can result.

d982b77efd9c.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
d982b77efd9c.sentence: Vertical mixing between the water bodies is therefore reduced, restricting the supply of oxygen from the surface waters to the more saline bottom waters.

ab4db4dbe382.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
ab4db4dbe382.sentence: Hypoxia is problematic for air-breathing organisms, yet it is essential for many anaerobic organisms.

6e618eeddbac.title: Dead zone (ecology)
6e618eeddbac.sentence: Dead zones are hypoxic (low-oxygen) areas in the world's oceans and large lakes.

a81d05c8302f.title: Dead zone (ecology)
a81d05c8302f.sentence: With such a low concentration of DO, these bodies of water fail to support the aquatic life living there.

32a70699d88b.title: Dead zone (ecology)
32a70699d88b.sentence: Hypoxia occurs when dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration falls to or below 2 mg of O2/liter.

827dbd2b382d.title: Dead zone (ecology)
827dbd2b382d.sentence: Once DO declines below 0.5 mg O2/liter in a body of water, mass mortality occurs.

66e40b3bae97.title: Dead zone (ecology)
66e40b3bae97.sentence: Aquatic and marine dead zones can be caused by an increase in nutrients (particularly nitrogen and phosphorus) in the water, known as eutrophication.

1b61d86101d3.title: Dead zone (ecology)
1b61d86101d3.sentence: Exponential growth leads to rapid increases in the density of certain types of these phytoplankton, a phenomenon known as an algal bloom.

19c076c27614.title: Aquatic ecosystem
19c076c27614.sentence: Similar over-abundance of algae in coastal environments such as the Gulf of Mexico produces, upon decay, a hypoxic region of water known as a dead zone.

52f99d911f38.title: Dead zone (ecology)
52f99d911f38.sentence: A 2008 study counted 405 dead zones worldwide.

ea71c7879291.title: Dead zone (ecology)
ea71c7879291.sentence: - Permanent dead zones are deep water occurrences that rarely exceed 2 milligrams per liter.

70d9232c195b.title: Dead zone (ecology)
70d9232c195b.sentence: - Temporary dead zones are short lived dead zones lasting hours or days.

292a4bea4b75.title: Dead zone (ecology)
292a4bea4b75.sentence: - Seasonal dead zones are annually occurring, typically in warm months of summer and autumn.

abe5fb548ded.title: Dead zone (ecology)
abe5fb548ded.sentence: In the 1970s, marine dead zones were first noted in settled areas where intensive economic use stimulated scientific scrutiny: in the U.S. East Coast's Chesapeake Bay, in Scandinavia's strait called the Kattegat, which is the mouth of the Baltic Sea and in other important Baltic Sea fishing grounds, in the Black Sea, and in the northern Adriatic.

a72e4b846b84.title: Cover crop
a72e4b846b84.sentence: An example of this is in the Mississippi Valley Basin, where years of fertilizer nitrogen loading into the watershed from agricultural production have resulted in an annual summer hypoxic "dead zone" off the Gulf of Mexico that reached an area of over 22,000 square kilometres (8,500 sq mi) in 2017.

0f31834f3c8f.title: Climate change
0f31834f3c8f.sentence: Because oxygen is less soluble in warmer water, its concentrations in the ocean are decreasing, and dead zones are expanding.

e6eb5d829508.title: Dead zone (ecology)
e6eb5d829508.sentence: The recovery of benthic communities primarily depends upon the length and severity of hypoxic conditions inside the zone.

8e54722530e9.title: Dead zone (ecology)
8e54722530e9.sentence: Less severe conditions and temporary depletion of oxygen allow rapid recovery of benthic communities in the area due to reestablishment by benthic larvae from adjacent areas, with longer conditions of hypoxia and more severe oxygen depletion leading to longer reestablishment periods.

e895c2062b49.title: Atmospheric methane
e895c2062b49.sentence: Atmospheric methane is the methane present in Earth's atmosphere.

2f529bd9de4a.title: Atmospheric methane
2f529bd9de4a.sentence: The concentration of atmospheric methane is increasing due to methane emissions, and is causing climate change.

a116b4a20d1b.title: Atmospheric methane
a116b4a20d1b.sentence: Since the beginning of the Industrial Revolution (around 1750), the methane concentration in the atmosphere has increased by about 160%, and human activities almost entirely caused this increase.

045e91663427.title: Atmospheric methane
045e91663427.sentence: By 2025, global methane concentrations had risen from 722 parts per billion (ppb) in pre-industrial times to 1936 ppb.

937a36b05932.title: Atmospheric methane
937a36b05932.sentence: This is an increase by a factor of 2.6 and the highest value in at least 800,000 years.

16ac2436dbbc.title: Atmospheric methane
16ac2436dbbc.sentence: Since 1750 methane has contributed 3% of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in terms of mass but is responsible for approximately 23% of radiative or climate forcing.

0c6d42a3efad.title: Atmospheric methane
0c6d42a3efad.sentence: Methane (CH4) in the Earth's atmosphere is a powerful greenhouse gas with a global warming potential (GWP) 84 times greater than CO2 over a 20-year time frame.

774d284b5265.title: Atmospheric methane
774d284b5265.sentence: Methane is not as persistent as CO2, and tails off to about 28 times greater than CO2 over a 100-year time frame.

02ff1dd01df7.title: Atmospheric methane
02ff1dd01df7.sentence: Methane's radiative forcing (RF) of climate is direct, and it is the second largest contributor to human-caused climate forcing in the historical period.

d6eaaad61a8b.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
d6eaaad61a8b.sentence: Wetlands are the largest natural source of atmospheric methane in the world, and are therefore a major area of concern with respect to climate change.

831624c97988.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
831624c97988.sentence: Wetlands account for approximately 20–30% of atmospheric methane through emissions from soils and plants, and contribute an approximate average of 161 Tg of methane to the atmosphere per year.

ddab51ec6af0.title: Atmospheric methane
ddab51ec6af0.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane > Removal technologies
ddab51ec6af0.sentence: From 2010 to 2019, methane emissions caused 0.5 °C (about 30%) of observed global warming.

a30aaa20ee81.title: Atmospheric methane
a30aaa20ee81.sentence: Collins et al. said that CH4 mitigation that reduces atmospheric methane by the end of the century, could "make a substantial difference to the feasibility of achieving the Paris climate targets", and would provide us with more "allowable carbon emissions to 2100".

818d1afda8c8.title: Eutrophication
818d1afda8c8.sentence: Cultural or anthropogenic eutrophication is the process that causes eutrophication because of human activity.

6e73e1e8807f.title: Eutrophication
6e73e1e8807f.sentence: The problem became more apparent following the introduction of chemical fertilizers in agriculture (green revolution of the mid-1900s).

ed9f60b430fb.title: Eutrophication
ed9f60b430fb.sentence: Phosphorus and nitrogen are the two main nutrients that cause cultural eutrophication as they enrich the water, allowing for some aquatic plants, especially algae to grow rapidly and bloom in high densities.

324f65f36688.title: Eutrophication
324f65f36688.sentence: Prior to their being phasing out in the 1970's, phosphate-containing detergents contributed to eutrophication.

1e2267403055.title: Eutrophication
1e2267403055.sentence: Since then, sewage and agriculture have emerged as the dominant phosphate sources.

38538cab9172.title: Eutrophication
38538cab9172.sentence: The main sources of nitrogen pollution are from agricultural runoff containing fertilizers and animal wastes, from sewage, and from atmospheric deposition of nitrogen originating from combustion or animal waste.

de1a38add553.title: Carbon sink
de1a38add553.sentence: The same publication defines carbon pool as "a reservoir in the Earth system where elements, such as carbon [...], reside in various chemical forms for a period of time."

4c2dbc531e1d.title: Carbon cycle
4c2dbc531e1d.sentence: The global carbon cycle is now usually divided into the following major reservoirs of carbon (also called carbon pools) interconnected by pathways of exchange:

b521c3327228.title: Carbon cycle
b521c3327228.sentence: - Ocean, including dissolved inorganic carbon and living and non-living marine biota

d7606fe5974e.title: Carbon cycle
d7606fe5974e.sentence: - Sediments, including fossil fuels, freshwater systems, and non-living organic material.

0cded2453065.title: Carbon cycle
0cded2453065.sentence: The terrestrial biosphere includes the organic carbon in all land-living organisms, both alive and dead, as well as carbon stored in soils.

b004ae50ec68.title: Carbon cycle
b004ae50ec68.sentence: Most of the Earth's carbon is stored inertly in the Earth's lithosphere.

62bf04a36505.title: Carbon cycle
62bf04a36505.sentence: Partly because its concentration of DIC is about 15% higher but mainly due to its larger volume, the deep ocean contains far more carbon—it is the largest pool of actively cycled carbon in the world, containing 50 times more than the atmosphere—but the timescale to reach equilibrium with the atmosphere is hundreds of years: the exchange of carbon between the two layers, driven by thermohaline circulation, is slow.

303b6967fbba.title: Carbon cycle
303b6967fbba.sentence: Most carbon in the terrestrial biosphere is organic carbon, while about a third of soil carbon is stored in inorganic forms, such as calcium carbonate.

ca70759c285a.title: Carbon sink
ca70759c285a.sentence: Both carbon pools and carbon sinks are important concepts in understanding the carbon cycle, but they refer to slightly different things.

45b2a44e589e.title: Carbon sink
45b2a44e589e.sentence: A carbon pool can be thought of as the overarching term, and carbon sink is then a particular type of carbon pool: A carbon pool is all the places where carbon can be stored (for example the atmosphere, oceans, soil, plants, and fossil fuels).

d8a5a24b081a.title: Carbon sink
d8a5a24b081a.sentence: A carbon sink is a type of carbon pool that has the capability to take up more carbon from the atmosphere than it releases.

2a3722bd9c65.title: Carbon sink
2a3722bd9c65.sentence: A carbon sink is a natural or artificial carbon sequestration process that "removes a greenhouse gas, an aerosol or a precursor of a greenhouse gas from the atmosphere".

15e9db17aaa1.title: Carbon sink
15e9db17aaa1.sentence: These sinks form an important part of the natural carbon cycle.

c01aeccac8ef.title: Carbon sink
c01aeccac8ef.sentence: Globally, the two most important carbon sinks are vegetation and the ocean.

2d08a4f85bd9.title: Carbon sink
2d08a4f85bd9.sentence: Soils represent a short to long-term carbon storage medium and contain more carbon than all terrestrial vegetation and the atmosphere combined.

eec75adc04e2.title: Carbon sink
eec75adc04e2.sentence: Much organic carbon retained in many agricultural areas worldwide has been severely depleted due to intensive farming practices.

d8a78e6fa559.title: Carbon sink
d8a78e6fa559.sentence: In the case of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, sinks need not store the gas.

f18ae27c711f.title: Carbon sink
f18ae27c711f.sentence: Instead they can break it down into substances that have a reduced effect on global warming.

0f16362ba228.title: Carbon sink
0f16362ba228.sentence: For example, nitrous oxide can be reduced to harmless N2.

0b92d40c53bc.title: Carbon sink
0b92d40c53bc.sentence: Artificial carbon sinks are those that store carbon in building materials or deep underground (geologic carbon sequestration).

a695b2a9fd98.title: Carbon sink
a695b2a9fd98.sentence: No major artificial systems remove carbon from the atmosphere on a large scale yet.

7d71c393ef6e.title: Carbon sink
7d71c393ef6e.sentence: In the past, human practices like deforestation and industrial agriculture have depleted natural carbon sinks.

851f2217883e.title: Carbon sink
851f2217883e.sentence: This kind of land use change has been one of the causes of climate change.

1606a0df6ce2.title: Carbon sink
1606a0df6ce2.sentence: Public awareness of the significance of CO2 sinks has grown since passage of the 1997 Kyoto Protocol, which promotes their use as a form of carbon offset.

1e9937d08731.title: Carbon sink
1e9937d08731.section: Enhancing natural carbon sinks > Purpose in the context of climate change
1e9937d08731.sentence: This refers to the management of Earth's natural carbon sinks in a way that preserves or increases their capability to remove CO2 from the atmosphere and to store it durably.

8cab67a426d2.title: Carbon sink
8cab67a426d2.section: Enhancing natural carbon sinks > Purpose in the context of climate change
8cab67a426d2.sentence: An important mitigation measure is "preserving and enhancing carbon sinks".

99d6e2ac9c00.title: Carbon sink
99d6e2ac9c00.section: Enhancing natural carbon sinks > Purpose in the context of climate change
99d6e2ac9c00.sentence: To enhance the ability of ecosystems to sequester carbon, changes are necessary in agriculture and forestry.

74400fd8f489.title: Carbon sink
74400fd8f489.section: Enhancing natural carbon sinks > Purpose in the context of climate change
74400fd8f489.sentence: Examples are preventing deforestation and restoring natural ecosystems by reforestation.

389df9c166f3.title: Carbon sink
389df9c166f3.section: Enhancing natural carbon sinks > Purpose in the context of climate change
389df9c166f3.sentence: But ecosystem restoration and reduced conversion are among the mitigation tools that can yield the most emissions reductions before 2030.

6bc60243a235.title: Carbon sink
6bc60243a235.section: Enhancing natural carbon sinks > Purpose in the context of climate change
6bc60243a235.sentence: Land-based mitigation options are referred to as "AFOLU mitigation options" in the 2022 IPCC report on mitigation.

3ac70428c28e.title: Carbon sink
3ac70428c28e.section: Enhancing natural carbon sinks > Purpose in the context of climate change
3ac70428c28e.sentence: The abbreviation stands for "agriculture, forestry and other land use" The report described the economic mitigation potential from relevant activities around forests and ecosystems as follows: "the conservation, improved management, and restoration of forests and other ecosystems (coastal wetlands, peatlands, savannas and grasslands)".

010feb3b6760.title: Carbon sink
010feb3b6760.section: Enhancing natural carbon sinks > Carbon sequestration techniques in oceans
010feb3b6760.sentence: To enhance carbon sequestration processes in oceans the following technologies have been proposed but none have achieved large scale application so far: Seaweed farming, ocean fertilisation, artificial upwelling, basalt storage, mineralization and deep sea sediments, adding bases to neutralize acids.

2d46a533f915.title: Carbon sink
2d46a533f915.sentence: By removing the greenhouse gas CO2 from the air, forests function as terrestrial carbon sinks, meaning they store large amounts of carbon in the form of biomass, encompassing roots, stems, branches, and leaves.

58f3fcbdcfdb.title: Carbon sink
58f3fcbdcfdb.sentence: By doing so, forests sequester approximately 25% of human carbon emissions annually, playing a critical role in Earth's climate.

a9ad6ffb7b52.title: Carbon sink
a9ad6ffb7b52.sentence: An important consideration in such efforts is that forests can turn from sinks to carbon sources.

2123cbcb809d.title: Carbon sink
2123cbcb809d.sentence: In 2019 forests took up a third less carbon than they did in the 1990s, due to higher temperatures, droughts and deforestation.

23d5a4995d0f.title: Carbon sink
23d5a4995d0f.sentence: The typical tropical forest may become a carbon source by the 2060s.

9be210ba50e6.title: Carbon sink
9be210ba50e6.sentence: Researchers have found that, in terms of environmental services, it is better to avoid deforestation than to allow for deforestation to subsequently reforest, as the latter leads to irreversible effects in terms of biodiversity loss and soil degradation.

090cdf9d3974.title: Afforestation
090cdf9d3974.sentence: An important consideration in such efforts is that forests can turn from sinks to carbon sources.

d1e1dd011c2e.title: Afforestation
d1e1dd011c2e.sentence: In 2019 forests took up a third less carbon than they did in the 1990s, due to higher temperatures, droughts and deforestation.

b2c165185334.title: Afforestation
b2c165185334.sentence: It takes much longer − several decades − for the benefits for global warming to manifest to the same carbon sequestration benefits from mature trees in tropical forests and hence from limiting deforestation.

88ec3695c80b.title: Afforestation
88ec3695c80b.sentence: Therefore, scientists consider "the protection and recovery of carbon-rich and long-lived ecosystems, especially natural forests" to be "the major climate solution".

f47827bc9a07.title: Afforestation
f47827bc9a07.sentence: For this carbon sequestration process to succeed the carbon must not return to the atmosphere from biomass burning or rotting when the trees die.

0fc6b1a87250.title: Carbon cycle
0fc6b1a87250.sentence: There is a fast and a slow carbon cycle.

69debea301ed.title: Carbon cycle
69debea301ed.sentence: The fast cycle operates in the biosphere and the slow cycle operates in rocks.

7fc0c449e585.title: Carbon cycle
7fc0c449e585.sentence: The fast or biological cycle can complete within years, moving carbon from atmosphere to biosphere, then back to the atmosphere.

1b4e0cb3dae6.title: Carbon cycle
1b4e0cb3dae6.sentence: The slow or geological cycle may extend deep into the mantle and can take millions of years to complete, moving carbon through the Earth's crust between rocks, soil, ocean and atmosphere.

3cfe60bfbc3e.title: Biogeochemical cycle
3cfe60bfbc3e.sentence: The reactions of the fast carbon cycle to human activities will determine many of the more immediate impacts of climate change.

93629c0d594b.title: Carbon cycle
93629c0d594b.sentence: The geologic component of the carbon cycle operates slowly in comparison to the other parts of the global carbon cycle.

8afdf029dd31.title: Carbon cycle
8afdf029dd31.sentence: It is one of the most important determinants of the amount of carbon in the atmosphere, and thus of global temperatures.

9af06802679b.title: Carbon cycle
9af06802679b.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle
9af06802679b.sentence: Since the Industrial Revolution, and especially since the end of WWII, human activity has substantially disturbed the global carbon cycle by redistributing massive amounts of carbon from the geosphere.

bc9c82942904.title: Carbon cycle
bc9c82942904.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Climate change > Fossil carbon extraction and burning
bc9c82942904.sentence: The largest and one of the fastest growing human impacts on the carbon cycle and biosphere is the extraction and burning of fossil fuels, which directly transfer carbon from the geosphere into the atmosphere.

4615d8e177dd.title: Carbon cycle
4615d8e177dd.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Climate change > Fossil carbon extraction and burning
4615d8e177dd.sentence: As of 2020, about 450 gigatons of fossil carbon have been extracted in total; an amount approaching the carbon contained in all of Earth's living terrestrial biomass.

46325b65faa4.title: Carbon cycle
46325b65faa4.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Climate change > Fossil carbon extraction and burning
46325b65faa4.sentence: Carbon dioxide is also produced and released during the calcination of limestone for clinker production.

82963e563833.title: Carbon cycle
82963e563833.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Climate change > Fossil carbon extraction and burning
82963e563833.sentence: Clinker is an industrial precursor of cement.

6410b60451f6.title: Carbon cycle
6410b60451f6.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Land use changes
6410b60451f6.sentence: More directly, it often leads to the release of carbon from terrestrial ecosystems into the atmosphere.

340465d01d82.title: Carbon cycle
340465d01d82.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Land use changes
340465d01d82.sentence: Deforestation for agricultural purposes removes forests, which hold large amounts of carbon, and replaces them, generally with agricultural or urban areas.

0607fa71050c.title: Carbon cycle
0607fa71050c.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Land use changes
0607fa71050c.sentence: Over the past several centuries, direct and indirect human-caused land use and land cover change (LUCC) has led to the loss of biodiversity, which lowers ecosystems' resilience to environmental stresses and decreases their ability to remove carbon from the atmosphere.

f9daed52f902.title: Carbon cycle
f9daed52f902.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Climate change > Halocarbons
f9daed52f902.sentence: Nevertheless, the buildup of relatively small concentrations (parts per trillion) of chlorofluorocarbon, hydrofluorocarbon, and perfluorocarbon gases in the atmosphere is responsible for about 10% of the total direct radiative forcing from all long-lived greenhouse gases (year 2019); which includes forcing from the much larger concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane.

185e3860f3ca.title: Carbon cycle
185e3860f3ca.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Climate change
185e3860f3ca.sentence: The exchanges of carbon between the atmosphere and other components of the Earth system, collectively known as the carbon cycle, currently constitute important negative (dampening) feedbacks on the effect of anthropogenic carbon emissions on climate change.

5ec81cb2a4c4.title: Water cycle
5ec81cb2a4c4.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
5ec81cb2a4c4.sentence: Human activities can alter the water cycle at the local or regional level.

26d9aae47aad.title: Water cycle
26d9aae47aad.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
26d9aae47aad.sentence: This happens due to changes in land use and land cover.

404084edd036.title: Water cycle
404084edd036.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
404084edd036.sentence: Examples of common land use changes include urbanization, agricultural expansion, and deforestation.

5a8d04f04a93.title: Water cycle
5a8d04f04a93.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
5a8d04f04a93.sentence: Such changes affect "precipitation, evaporation, flooding, groundwater, and the availability of freshwater for a variety of uses".

b8ea7ad0446b.title: Water cycle
b8ea7ad0446b.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
b8ea7ad0446b.sentence: These changes can increase soil compaction and impervious surface cover which decrease the infiltration capacity of soils and result in greater surface runoff rates.

120297344af6.title: Water cycle
120297344af6.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
120297344af6.sentence: Deforestation has local and regional effects; at the local level it reduces soil moisture, evaporation, rainfall, and snowfall; at the regional level it can cause temperature changes that affect rainfall patterns.

e25de03c651f.title: Water cycle
e25de03c651f.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
e25de03c651f.sentence: Dams can alter natural flow rates, decrease water quality, and lead to a loss of habitat for aquatic species.

1f7e58824dc6.title: Afforestation
1f7e58824dc6.sentence: Water management can be improved afforestation, as trees regulate hydrological cycles, reduce soil erosion, and prevent water runoff.

920409660ca8.title: Water cycle
920409660ca8.section: Changes caused by humans > Water cycle intensification due to climate change
920409660ca8.sentence: The effects of climate change on the water cycle are profound and have been described as an intensification or a strengthening of the water cycle (also called the hydrologic cycle).

5e2055b9ea35.title: Water cycle
5e2055b9ea35.section: Changes caused by humans > Water cycle intensification due to climate change
5e2055b9ea35.sentence: This effect has been observed since at least 1980.

e6aefd94122a.title: Water cycle
e6aefd94122a.section: Changes caused by humans > Water cycle intensification due to climate change
e6aefd94122a.sentence: Since the middle of the 20th century, human-caused climate change has resulted in observable changes in the global water cycle.

42a59ede9154.title: Water cycle
42a59ede9154.section: Changes caused by humans > Water cycle intensification due to climate change
42a59ede9154.sentence: For example, a warmer atmosphere can contain more water vapor which has effects on evaporation and rainfall.

272cc8de8e9b.title: Water cycle
272cc8de8e9b.section: Changes caused by humans > Water cycle intensification due to climate change
272cc8de8e9b.sentence: One example is when heavy rain events become even stronger.

014f68957e91.title: Water cycle
014f68957e91.section: Changes caused by humans > Water cycle intensification due to climate change
014f68957e91.sentence: The effects of climate change on the water cycle have important negative effects on the availability of freshwater resources, as well as other water reservoirs such as oceans, ice sheets, the atmosphere, and soil moisture.

667015015858.title: Water cycle
667015015858.section: Changes caused by humans > Water cycle intensification due to climate change
667015015858.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report in 2021 predicted that these changes will continue to grow significantly at the global and regional level.

2ec2289b7763.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
2ec2289b7763.sentence: The oceanic carbon cycle (or marine carbon cycle) is composed of processes that exchange carbon between various pools within the ocean as well as between the atmosphere, Earth interior, and the seafloor.

4e1e04520b5a.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
4e1e04520b5a.sentence: The Oceanic carbon cycle is a central process to the global carbon cycle and contains both inorganic carbon (carbon not bound to other carbon) and organic carbon (carbon that is incorporated into molecules with carbon-carbon bonds).

78d06b4f9532.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
78d06b4f9532.sentence: Three main processes (or pumps) that make up the marine carbon cycle bring atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) into the ocean interior and distribute it through the oceans.

8e485a21a0c6.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
8e485a21a0c6.sentence: Before the Industrial Revolution, the ocean was a source of CO2 to the atmosphere balancing the impact of rock weathering and terrestrial particulate organic carbon; now it has become a sink for the excess atmospheric CO2.

17da6efc3a63.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
17da6efc3a63.sentence: Carbon dioxide is absorbed from the atmosphere at the ocean's surface at an exchange rate which varies locally and with time but on average, the oceans have a net absorption of around 2.9 Pg (equivalent to 2.9 billion metric tonnes) of carbon from atmospheric CO2 per year.

e81ca38391c0.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
e81ca38391c0.sentence: Oceans take up around 25 – 31% of anthropogenic CO2.

d19c578c5765.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
d19c578c5765.sentence: Because the solubility of carbon dioxide increases when temperature decreases, cold areas can contain more CO2 and still be in equilibrium with the atmosphere; In contrast, rising sea surface temperatures decrease the capacity of the oceans to take in carbon dioxide.

914a56e41083.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
914a56e41083.sentence: Inputs to the marine carbon cycle are numerous, but the primary contributions, on a net basis, come from the atmosphere and rivers.

515957d0fdaa.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
515957d0fdaa.sentence: Rivers contribute roughly equal amounts (~0.4 GtC/yr) of DIC and DOC to the oceans.

4332188a8a57.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
4332188a8a57.sentence: Sedimentation is a long-term sink for carbon in the ocean, as well as the largest loss of carbon from the oceanic system.

3fd10c5562eb.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
3fd10c5562eb.section: Outputs > Organic matter preservation > Fate of sinking organic carbon
3fd10c5562eb.sentence: 90% of organic carbon burial occurs in deposits of deltas and continental shelves and upper slopes; this is due partly to short exposure time because of a shorter distance to the seafloor and the composition of the organic matter that is already deposited in those environments.

efa8d02bd945.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
efa8d02bd945.sentence: Using data from the Global Reservoirs and Dams database, which contains approximately 7000 reservoirs that hold 77% of the total volume of water held back by dams (8000 km3), it is estimated that the delivery of carbon to the ocean has decreased by 13% since 1970 and is projected to reach 19% by 2030.

7c6d1775a260.title: Ocean acidification
7c6d1775a260.sentence: Ocean acidification is the ongoing decrease in the pH of the Earth's ocean.

5ef843517db1.title: Ocean acidification
5ef843517db1.sentence: CO2 from the atmosphere is absorbed by the oceans.

3c51c4848bbc.title: Ocean acidification
3c51c4848bbc.sentence: Carbon dioxide emissions from human activities are the primary cause of ocean acidification, with atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) levels exceeding 422 ppm (as of 2024).

e086e27516f8.title: Ocean acidification
e086e27516f8.sentence: This chemical reaction produces carbonic acid (H2CO3) which dissociates into a bicarbonate ion (HCO−3) and a hydrogen ion (H+).

5c90faada8d5.title: Ocean acidification
5c90faada8d5.sentence: The presence of free hydrogen ions (H+) lowers the pH of the ocean, increasing acidity (this does not mean that seawater is acidic yet; It is still alkaline, with a pH higher than 8).

afb1d50b0c37.title: Ocean acidification
afb1d50b0c37.section: Measured and estimated values > Present-day and recent history
afb1d50b0c37.sentence: Between 1950 and 2020, the average pH value of the ocean surface is estimated to have decreased from approximately 8.15 to 8.05.

9e592662c3aa.title: Ocean acidification
9e592662c3aa.section: Measured and estimated values > Present-day and recent history
9e592662c3aa.sentence: This represents an increase of around 26% in hydrogen ion concentration in the world's oceans (the pH scale is logarithmic, so a change of one in pH unit is equivalent to a tenfold change in hydrogen ion concentration).

f35f7f7f0ca2.title: Ocean acidification
f35f7f7f0ca2.sentence: Marine calcifying organisms, such as mollusks and corals, are especially vulnerable because they rely on calcium carbonate to build shells and skeletons.

5bed87462332.title: Ocean acidification
5bed87462332.sentence: This process, commonly referred to as "ocean acidification", is making it harder for marine calcifiers to build a shell or skeletal structure, endangering coral reefs and the broader marine ecosystems.

0543696f26b2.title: Ocean acidification
0543696f26b2.sentence: Importantly, the rate of change in ocean acidification is much higher than in the geological past.

e45499a8bf9f.title: Ocean acidification
e45499a8bf9f.sentence: This faster change prevents organisms from gradually adapting, and prevents climate cycle feedbacks from kicking in to mitigate ocean acidification.

b5ab95f7fef6.title: Ocean acidification
b5ab95f7fef6.section: Measured and estimated values > Geologic past
b5ab95f7fef6.sentence: It happened during the Capitanian mass extinction, at the end-Permian extinction, during the end-Triassic extinction, and during the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.

0d2e682be5f9.title: Ocean acidification
0d2e682be5f9.section: Other impacts on ecosystems > Compounded effects of acidification, warming, and deoxygenation
0d2e682be5f9.sentence: There is a substantial body of research showing that a combination of ocean acidification and elevated ocean temperature have a compounded effect on marine life and the ocean environment.

84c66407c874.title: Ocean acidification
84c66407c874.section: Other impacts on ecosystems > Compounded effects of acidification, warming, and deoxygenation
84c66407c874.sentence: This effect far exceeds the individual harmful impact of either.

630da2a05eed.title: Ocean acidification
630da2a05eed.sentence: Reducing carbon dioxide emissions (i.e. climate change mitigation measures) is the only solution that addresses the root cause of ocean acidification.

fa292c0cd66f.title: Ocean acidification
fa292c0cd66f.sentence: The removal of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere would also help to reverse ocean acidification.

c4b42e22a28a.title: Ocean acidification
c4b42e22a28a.sentence: The fundamental research really began with the creation of the pH scale by Danish chemist Søren Peder Lauritz Sørensen in 1909.

89c2994e6ec9.title: Biological pump
89c2994e6ec9.sentence: The biological pump (or marine biological carbon pump) is the ocean's biologically driven sequestration of carbon from the atmosphere and land runoff to the ocean interior and seafloor sediments.

9cb002a520d7.title: Biological pump
9cb002a520d7.sentence: In other words, it is a biologically mediated process which results in the sequestering of carbon in the deep ocean away from the atmosphere and the land.

9089461b0091.title: Biological pump
9089461b0091.sentence: The first step in the biological pump is the synthesis of both organic and inorganic carbon compounds by phytoplankton in the uppermost, sunlit layers of the ocean.

748c20fef581.title: Biological pump
748c20fef581.section: Processes in the biological pump > Key role of phytoplankton
748c20fef581.sentence: Marine phytoplankton perform half of all photosynthesis on Earth and directly influence global biogeochemical cycles and the climate, yet how they will respond to future global change is unknown.

8aee9b5f4093.title: Biological pump
8aee9b5f4093.sentence: Any unconsumed phytoplankton form aggregates, and along with zooplankton faecal pellets, sink rapidly and are exported out of the mixed layer (< 12 Gt C yr−1 14).

458287909cc4.title: Carbon cycle
458287909cc4.section: Processes within fast carbon cycle > Biological pump in the ocean
458287909cc4.sentence: The pump transfers about 11 billion tonnes of carbon every year into the ocean's interior.

e5f23d4ae724.title: Carbon cycle
e5f23d4ae724.section: Processes within fast carbon cycle > Biological pump in the ocean
e5f23d4ae724.sentence: An ocean without the biological pump would result in atmospheric CO2 levels about 400 ppm higher than the present day.

4c99540d5d0a.title: Biological pump
4c99540d5d0a.sentence: Climate change may affect the biological pump in the future by warming and stratifying the surface ocean.

66cb7c42d726.title: Biological pump
66cb7c42d726.sentence: It is believed that this could decrease the supply of nutrients to the euphotic zone, reducing primary production there.

318598c0d217.title: Biological pump
318598c0d217.section: Processes in the biological pump > Macroorganisms > Whale pump
318598c0d217.sentence: Whales and other marine mammals also enhance primary productivity in their feeding areas by concentrating nitrogen near the surface through the release of flocculent fecal plumes.

d5d1897b9a5b.title: Biological pump
d5d1897b9a5b.section: Processes in the biological pump > Macroorganisms > Whale pump
d5d1897b9a5b.sentence: This upward whale pump played a much larger role before industrial fishing devastated marine mammal stocks, when recycling of nitrogen was likely more than three times the atmospheric nitrogen input.

c861037db916.title: Ocean acidification
c861037db916.section: Impacts on the economy and societies > Fishing and tourism industry
c861037db916.sentence: The threat of acidification includes a decline in commercial fisheries and the coast-based tourism industry.

9687a3aa3aff.title: Ocean acidification
9687a3aa3aff.section: Impacts on the economy and societies > Fishing and tourism industry
9687a3aa3aff.sentence: Several ocean goods and services are likely to be undermined by future ocean acidification potentially affecting the livelihoods of some 470 to 870 million of the world's poorest people, depending upon the greenhouse gas emission scenario.

0ba06f83079b.title: Ocean acidification
0ba06f83079b.section: Impacts on the economy and societies > Fishing and tourism industry
0ba06f83079b.sentence: Some 1 billion people are completely or partially dependent on the fishing, tourism, and coastal management services provided by coral reefs.

116a20307a69.title: Ocean acidification
116a20307a69.section: Impacts on the economy and societies
116a20307a69.sentence: The increase of ocean acidity decelerates the rate of calcification in salt water, leading to smaller and slower growing coral reefs which supports approximately 25% of marine life.

adcaf50fc5fe.title: Ocean acidification
adcaf50fc5fe.section: Impacts on the economy and societies > Fishing and tourism industry > US commercial fisheries
adcaf50fc5fe.sentence: The value of fish caught from US commercial fisheries in 2007 was valued at $3.8 billion and of that 73% was derived from calcifiers and their direct predators.

45ecd3786bbc.title: Ocean acidification
45ecd3786bbc.section: Impacts on the economy and societies > Fishing and tourism industry > United Kingdom commercial fisheries
45ecd3786bbc.sentence: The direct potential loss ranges from 14 to 28 percent of fishery output.

439fcbe840fd.title: Ocean acidification
439fcbe840fd.section: Impacts on the economy and societies > Fishing and tourism industry > United Kingdom commercial fisheries
439fcbe840fd.sentence: That is a total loss of about 23 to 88 million pounds.

bbb8be01ee1d.title: Ocean acidification
bbb8be01ee1d.section: Impacts on the economy and societies > Fishing and tourism industry > Arctic
bbb8be01ee1d.sentence: In the Arctic, commercial fisheries are threatened because acidification harms calcifying organisms which form the base of the Arctic food webs (pteropods and brittle stars, see above).

bd631f591540.title: Ocean acidification
bd631f591540.section: Impacts on the economy and societies > Fishing and tourism industry > Arctic
bd631f591540.sentence: Arctic food webs are considered simple, meaning there are few steps in the food chain from small organisms to larger predators.

dba137412523.title: Solubility pump
dba137412523.sentence: In oceanic biogeochemistry, the solubility pump is a physicochemical process that transports carbon as dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) from the ocean's surface to its interior.

395ab7891b46.title: Solubility pump
395ab7891b46.sentence: - The solubility of carbon dioxide is a strong inverse function of seawater temperature (i.e. solubility is greater in cooler water)

cc3b2cd7169b.title: Solubility pump
cc3b2cd7169b.sentence: - The thermohaline circulation is driven by the formation of deep water at high latitudes where seawater is usually cooler and denser

e75dc484ee02.title: Solubility pump
e75dc484ee02.sentence: Consequently, these two processes act together to pump carbon from the atmosphere into the ocean's interior.

076e0ecbae40.title: Solubility pump
076e0ecbae40.sentence: One consequence of this is that when deep water upwells in warmer, equatorial latitudes, it strongly outgasses carbon dioxide to the atmosphere because of the reduced solubility of the gas.

3de571e2dfa2.title: Solubility pump
3de571e2dfa2.sentence: Presently, about one third (approximately 2 gigatons of carbon per year) of anthropogenic emissions of CO2 are believed to be entering the ocean.

982ebbe1e353.title: Solubility pump
982ebbe1e353.sentence: The solubility pump is the primary mechanism driving this flux, with the consequence that anthropogenic CO2 is reaching the ocean interior via high latitude sites of deep water formation (particularly the North Atlantic).

45f6cce2a95c.title: Solubility pump
45f6cce2a95c.sentence: Ocean warming decreases the solubility of CO2 in seawater, slowing the ocean's response to emissions.

f4133d76e901.title: Solubility pump
f4133d76e901.sentence: Warming also acts to increase ocean stratification, isolating the surface ocean from deeper waters.

09180933a3e4.title: Solubility pump
09180933a3e4.sentence: Additionally, changes in the ocean's thermohaline circulation (specifically slowing) may act to decrease transport of dissolved CO2 into the deep ocean.

f7f1f0434153.title: Solubility pump
f7f1f0434153.sentence: The solubility pump has a biological counterpart known as the biological pump.

161ea4dcd040.title: Solubility pump
161ea4dcd040.sentence: While ocean absorption of anthropogenic CO2 from the atmosphere acts to decrease climate change, it causes ocean acidification which is believed will have negative consequences for marine ecosystems.

0fbf800c8bd0.title: Soil erosion
0fbf800c8bd0.sentence: The most effective known method for erosion prevention is to increase vegetative cover on the land, which helps prevent both wind and water erosion.

adca2787a73c.title: Soil erosion
adca2787a73c.sentence: Terracing is an extremely effective means of erosion control, which has been practiced for thousands of years by people all over the world.

259ac57fa727.title: Soil erosion
259ac57fa727.sentence: Windbreaks (also called shelterbelts) are rows of trees and shrubs that are planted along the edges of agricultural fields, to shield the fields against winds.

978b7163c86b.title: Soil erosion
978b7163c86b.sentence: In addition to significantly reducing wind erosion, windbreaks provide many other benefits such as improved microclimates for crops (which are sheltered from the dehydrating and otherwise damaging effects of wind), habitat for beneficial bird species, carbon sequestration, and aesthetic improvements to the agricultural landscape.

47f33714734c.title: Soil erosion
47f33714734c.sentence: Traditional planting methods, such as mixed-cropping (instead of monocropping) and crop rotation, have also been shown to significantly reduce erosion rates.

fb69b4fbf43c.title: Soil erosion
fb69b4fbf43c.sentence: Crop residues play a role in the mitigation of erosion by conservation tillage methods, because they reduce the impact of raindrops breaking up the soil particles.

7a3118626a81.title: Soil erosion
7a3118626a81.sentence: Agroforestry, the mixing of agricultural crops with trees, is an efficient mean of mitigating soil erosion, in particular in tropical climates with heavy rains, but also everywhere land has been severely degraded by intensive agriculture activities (e.g. ravine lands).

e279b078becf.title: Soil erosion
e279b078becf.sentence: Their complex root structures are known to help reduce wave damage from storms and flood impacts while binding and building soils.

123558b85716.title: Soil erosion
123558b85716.sentence: These roots can slow down water flow, leading to the deposition of sediments and reduced erosion rates.

7b96c482fc0d.title: Afforestation
7b96c482fc0d.sentence: Public works programs under the New Deal saw the planting of 18,000 miles of windbreaks stretching from North Dakota to Texas to fight soil erosion (see Great Plains Shelterbelt).

c58904762c27.title: Erosion control
c58904762c27.sentence: Effective erosion controls handle surface runoff and are important techniques in preventing water pollution, soil loss, wildlife habitat loss and human property loss.

7ad5a4492993.title: Soil carbon
7ad5a4492993.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
7ad5a4492993.sentence: The exchange of carbon between soils and the atmosphere is a significant part of the global carbon cycle.

8f69b9467fae.title: Soil carbon
8f69b9467fae.sentence: Researchers are interested in discovering ways that human intervention can adequately restore carbon to the soils, through farming and other practices.

92fa3b1a3806.title: Soil carbon
92fa3b1a3806.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
92fa3b1a3806.sentence: Several factors affect the variation that exists in soil organic matter and soil carbon; the most significant has, in contemporary times, been the influence of humans and agricultural systems.

bcc896618359.title: Soil carbon
bcc896618359.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
bcc896618359.sentence: Although exact quantities are difficult to measure, human activities have caused substantial losses of soil organic carbon through land use changes, such as deforestation and other agricultural practices.

4afe9a31df82.title: Soil carbon
4afe9a31df82.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
4afe9a31df82.sentence: Also, fire removes soil cover and leads to immediate and continuing losses of soil organic carbon.

128aa0ef28be.title: Soil carbon
128aa0ef28be.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
128aa0ef28be.sentence: Additionally, tillage and drainage both expose soil organic matter to oxygen and oxidation.

0bb975e9467f.title: Soil carbon
0bb975e9467f.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
0bb975e9467f.sentence: In the Netherlands, East Anglia, Florida, and the California Delta, subsidence of peat lands from oxidation has been severe as a result of tillage and drainage.

70e4788c9a8a.title: Soil carbon
70e4788c9a8a.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon > Carbon catchment health
70e4788c9a8a.sentence: - Reduced erosion, sedimentation: increased soil aggregate stability means greater resistance to erosion; mass movement is less likely when soils are able to retain structural strength under greater moisture levels.

3b4e1ad87ade.title: Soil carbon
3b4e1ad87ade.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon > Carbon catchment health
3b4e1ad87ade.sentence: - Greater productivity: healthier and more productive soils can contribute to positive socio-economic circumstances.

024d5f2d01ee.title: Soil carbon
024d5f2d01ee.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon > Carbon catchment health
024d5f2d01ee.sentence: - Cleaner waterways, nutrients and turbidity: nutrients and sediment tend to be retained by the soil rather than leach or wash off, and are so kept from waterways.

7d0194327547.title: Soil carbon
7d0194327547.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon > Carbon catchment health
7d0194327547.sentence: - Water balance: greater soil water holding capacity reduces overland flow and recharge to groundwater; the water saved and held by the soil remains available for use by plants.

5c1767c9996f.title: Carbon dioxide removal
5c1767c9996f.sentence: Land-based methods include afforestation, reforestation, agricultural practices that sequester carbon in soils (carbon farming), bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS), and direct air capture combined with storage.

3cb5fa253edf.title: Carbon accounting
3cb5fa253edf.section: Frameworks and standards > Project accounting standards > Gold Standard
3cb5fa253edf.sentence: Allowable project categories include renewable energy supply, energy efficiency, afforestation/reforestation, and agriculture (the latter can be difficult - for example soil carbon measurements are depth sensitive).

7514b677b648.title: Nutrient pollution
7514b677b648.sentence: Nutrient trading is a type of water quality trading, a market-based policy instrument used to improve or maintain water quality.

28cb9884d26f.title: Nutrient pollution
28cb9884d26f.sentence: Water quality trading involves the voluntary exchange of pollution reduction credits from sources with low costs of pollution control to those with high costs of pollution control, and the same principles apply to nutrient water quality trading.

7fd145d64f97.title: Nutrient pollution
7fd145d64f97.sentence: The concept of water quality trading is based on the fact that different pollution sources in a watershed can face very different costs to control the same pollutant.

53dcbc5b645d.title: Nutrient pollution
53dcbc5b645d.sentence: The underlying principle is "polluter pays", usually linked with a regulatory requirement for participating in the trading program.

b03f8acf7aeb.title: Nutrient pollution
b03f8acf7aeb.sentence: A 2013 Forest Trends report summarized water quality trading programs and found three main types of funders: beneficiaries of watershed protection, polluters compensating for their impacts and "public good payers" that may not directly benefit, but fund the pollution reduction credits on behalf of a government or NGO.

a9d7655006d9.title: Nutrient pollution
a9d7655006d9.sentence: As of 2013, payments were overwhelmingly initiated by public good payers like governments and NGOs.

fb0981bf246f.title: Sulfur cycle
fb0981bf246f.sentence: The sulfur cycle is a biogeochemical cycle in which the sulfur moves between rocks, waterways and living systems.

34c02873ce4d.title: Sulfur cycle
34c02873ce4d.sentence: It is important in geology as it affects many minerals and in life because sulfur is an essential element (CHNOPS), being a constituent of many proteins and cofactors, and sulfur compounds can be used as oxidants or reductants in cellular respiration.

a76bc38ee7f5.title: Sulfur cycle
a76bc38ee7f5.sentence: The global sulfur cycle involves the transformations of sulfur species through different oxidation states, which play an important role in both geological and biological processes.

025dbea544f7.title: Sulfur cycle
025dbea544f7.sentence: Sulfur is found in oxidation states ranging from +6 in SO2− 4 to −2 in sulfides.

03278ee65da4.title: Sulfur cycle
03278ee65da4.sentence: - Mineralization of organic sulfur into inorganic forms, such as hydrogen sulfide (H2S), elemental sulfur, as well as sulfide minerals.

8ae677b311bb.title: Sulfur cycle
8ae677b311bb.sentence: - Oxidation of hydrogen sulfide, sulfide, and elemental sulfur (S) to sulfate (SO2− 4).

e3a2a8194428.title: Sulfur cycle
e3a2a8194428.sentence: - Reduction of sulfate and sulfite to sulfide.

aa7630b4edba.title: Sulfur cycle
aa7630b4edba.sentence: Aerobic sulfide oxidation is usually performed by autotrophs that use sulfide or elemental sulfur to fix carbon dioxide.

de0809b792fe.title: Sulfur cycle
de0809b792fe.sentence: Earth's main sulfur sink is the oceans SO2− 4 available as electron acceptor for microorganisms in anoxic waters.

11ab7f4dbded.title: Sulfur cycle
11ab7f4dbded.sentence: Dissimilatory sulfate reduction is driven by the degradation of buried organic matter and anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) both of which produce carbon dioxide.

01b861f9bc19.title: Sulfur cycle
01b861f9bc19.sentence: At depths where sulfate is depleted, methanogenesis is prevalent.

c32026579c75.title: Sulfur cycle
c32026579c75.sentence: Sulfur is intimately involved in the production of fossil fuels and most metal deposits because it acts as an oxidizing or reducing agent.

94a358e0c15a.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
94a358e0c15a.sentence: The permafrost carbon cycle or Arctic carbon cycle is a sub-cycle of the larger global carbon cycle.

95963f4fc29e.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
95963f4fc29e.sentence: The permafrost carbon cycle deals with the transfer of carbon from permafrost soils to terrestrial vegetation and microbes, to the atmosphere, back to vegetation, and, finally, back to permafrost soils through burial and sedimentation due to cryogenic processes.

89f948681b15.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
89f948681b15.sentence: Permafrost is defined as subsurface material that remains below 0o C (32o F) for at least two consecutive years.

14422e6aaee7.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
14422e6aaee7.sentence: Permafrost affected soils cover nearly 9% of the Earth's land area, yet store between 25 and 50% of the soil organic carbon.

4363ba398567.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
4363ba398567.sentence: It is estimated that the total soil organic carbon (SOC) stock in northern circumpolar permafrost region equals around 1,460–1,600 Pg.

b187d7ce947a.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
b187d7ce947a.sentence: This estimation of the amount of carbon stored in permafrost soils is more than double the amount currently in the atmosphere.

a8f1d9bbdaae.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
a8f1d9bbdaae.sentence: Radiocarbon dating techniques reveal that carbon within permafrost is often thousands of years old.

d509b7b4bf09.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
d509b7b4bf09.sentence: - The first process that captures carbon and stores it is syngenetic permafrost growth.

2cf8d8b4de18.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
2cf8d8b4de18.sentence: This aggradation of soil is the result of aeolian or fluvial sedimentation and/or peat formation.

177986e182dc.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
177986e182dc.sentence: As this process occurs, the organic and mineral soil that is deposited is incorporated into the permafrost as the permafrost surface rises.

624915ce6935.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
624915ce6935.sentence: Permafrost represents a large carbon reservoir, one which was often neglected in the initial research determining global terrestrial carbon reservoirs.

00a12d4129cd.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
00a12d4129cd.sentence: Since the start of the 2000s, however, far more attention has been paid to the subject, with an enormous growth both in general attention and in the scientific research output.

33e895089f7c.title: Net ecosystem production
33e895089f7c.sentence: Net ecosystem production (NEP) in ecology, limnology, and oceanography, is the difference between gross primary production (GPP) and net ecosystem respiration.

823a4e4eb0ba.title: Net ecosystem production
823a4e4eb0ba.sentence: - NEP = GPP - respiration [by plants] - respiration [by animals and other heterotrophs]

22479f273e99.title: Net ecosystem production
22479f273e99.sentence: Net ecosystem production describes the total carbon in an ecosystem that can be stored, exported, or oxidized back into carbon dioxide gas.

1923bc449d7e.title: Net ecosystem production
1923bc449d7e.sentence: NEP is written in units of mass of carbon per unit area per time, for example, grams carbon per square meter per year (g C m−2 yr−1).

a71bac5d02b2.title: Net ecosystem production
