a71bac5d02b2.sentence: In a given ecosystem, carbon quantified as net ecosystem production can eventually end up: oxidized by fire or ultraviolet radiation, accumulated as biomass, exported as organic carbon to another system, or accumulated in sediments or soils.

f7540d286321.title: Net ecosystem production
f7540d286321.section: Net ecosystem production vs. net primary production
f7540d286321.sentence: In contrast, net primary production (NPP) is all the carbon taken up by plants (autotrophs) minus the carbon that the plants themselves respire through cellular respiration.

91286b474f2f.title: Net ecosystem production
91286b474f2f.section: Net ecosystem production vs. net primary production
91286b474f2f.sentence: Net ecosystem production is all the carbon not respired, including respiration by plants and heterotrophic organisms such as animals and microbes.

8caeb5f5bbc2.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
8caeb5f5bbc2.sentence: Net ecosystem production (NEP) and climate changes are the all encompassing factors that have been shown to have a direct relationship with methane emissions from wetlands.

ee4a72ca4e8f.title: Photosynthesis
ee4a72ca4e8f.sentence: In the light-dependent reactions, one molecule of the pigment chlorophyll absorbs one photon and loses one electron.

e5757f7358d6.title: Photosynthesis
e5757f7358d6.sentence: In plants, light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplasts where they drive the synthesis of ATP and NADPH.

f9f8fdcf7499.title: Photosynthesis
f9f8fdcf7499.sentence: This electron is taken up by a modified form of chlorophyll called pheophytin, which passes the electron to a quinone molecule, starting the flow of electrons down an electron transport chain that leads to the ultimate reduction of NADP to NADPH.

92c51841658c.title: Photosynthesis
92c51841658c.sentence: The chlorophyll molecule ultimately regains the electron it lost when a water molecule is split in a process called photolysis, which releases oxygen.

c2df0b36ce6b.title: Photosynthesis
c2df0b36ce6b.sentence: In the light-independent (or "dark") reactions, the enzyme RuBisCO captures CO2 from the atmosphere and, in a process called the Calvin cycle, uses the newly formed NADPH and releases three-carbon sugars, which are later combined to form sucrose and starch.

455a6fcbeb16.title: Photosynthesis
455a6fcbeb16.sentence: Using the ATP and NADPH produced by the light-dependent reactions, the resulting compounds are then reduced and removed to form further carbohydrates, such as glucose.

cf84e09b1647.title: Photosynthesis
cf84e09b1647.sentence: The simple carbon sugars photosynthesis produces are then used to form other organic compounds, such as the building material cellulose, the precursors for lipid and amino acid biosynthesis, or as a fuel in cellular respiration.

0e716c012237.title: Photosynthesis
0e716c012237.section: Experimental history > C3: C4 photosynthesis research
0e716c012237.sentence: In the late 1940s at the University of California, Berkeley, the details of photosynthetic carbon metabolism were sorted out by the chemists Melvin Calvin, Andrew Benson, James Bassham and a score of students and researchers utilizing the carbon-14 isotope and paper chromatography techniques.

1dfbcc48b26b.title: Photosynthesis
1dfbcc48b26b.section: Experimental history > C3: C4 photosynthesis research
1dfbcc48b26b.sentence: For that original and ground-breaking work, a Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Melvin Calvin in 1961.

eb266e17b2b4.title: Photosynthesis
eb266e17b2b4.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
eb266e17b2b4.sentence: Some plants have evolved mechanisms to increase the CO2 concentration in the leaves under these conditions.

f2ed19636c67.title: Photosynthesis
f2ed19636c67.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > In water
f2ed19636c67.sentence: Cyanobacteria possess carboxysomes, which increase the concentration of CO2 around RuBisCO to increase the rate of photosynthesis.

48cdf82b48d0.title: Photosynthesis
48cdf82b48d0.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
48cdf82b48d0.sentence: In hot and dry conditions, plants close their stomata to prevent water loss.

8b071773cb1f.title: Photosynthesis
8b071773cb1f.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
8b071773cb1f.sentence: Under these conditions, CO2 will decrease and oxygen gas, produced by the light reactions of photosynthesis, will increase, causing an increase of photorespiration by the oxygenase activity of ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (RuBisCO) and decrease in carbon fixation.

e15bb1fb7b7d.title: Photosynthesis
e15bb1fb7b7d.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
e15bb1fb7b7d.sentence: Plants that use the C4 carbon fixation process chemically fix carbon dioxide in the cells of the mesophyll by adding it to the three-carbon molecule phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), a reaction catalyzed by an enzyme called PEP carboxylase, creating the four-carbon organic acid oxaloacetic acid.

e5d05c4f7cc3.title: Abiotic component
e5d05c4f7cc3.sentence: C3 plants have no mechanisms to manage photorespiration, whereas C4 and CAM plants utilize a separate PEP carboxylase enzyme to prevent photorespiration, thus increasing the yield of photosynthesis processes in certain high energy environments.

47886383e050.title: Photosynthesis
47886383e050.sentence: Total photosynthesis is limited by a range of environmental factors.

83f1a429409f.title: Photosynthesis
83f1a429409f.sentence: These include the amount of light available, the amount of leaf area a plant has to capture light (shading by other plants is a major limitation of photosynthesis), the rate at which carbon dioxide can be supplied to the chloroplasts to support photosynthesis, the availability of water, and the availability of suitable temperatures for carrying out photosynthesis.

370f64d4c203.title: Photosynthesis
370f64d4c203.section: Factors > Carbon dioxide levels and photorespiration

6e9989afaf31.sentence: When the concentration of carbon dioxide is high, RuBisCO will fix carbon dioxide.

7d5c580e6d65.title: Photosynthesis

ff7d2948ee63.title: Photosynthesis

1e4bef35a7d1.title: Photosynthesis

0fb904853cb8.sentence: The other context of agricultural issues involves the transport of agricultural chemicals (nitrates, phosphates, pesticides, herbicides, etc.) via surface runoff.

af7517cb533d.title: Surface runoff
af7517cb533d.section: Effects of surface runoff > Environmental effects > Agricultural issues
af7517cb533d.sentence: This result occurs when chemical use is excessive or poorly timed with respect to high precipitation.

7bb4da6f6446.title: Surface runoff
7bb4da6f6446.section: Effects of surface runoff > Environmental effects > Agricultural issues
7bb4da6f6446.sentence: The resulting contaminated runoff represents not only a waste of agricultural chemicals, but also an environmental threat to downstream ecosystems.

1db3d5bb3ed2.title: Agricultural pollution
1db3d5bb3ed2.sentence: Nitrate fertilizers are much more likely to be lost to the soil profile through runoff because of its high solubility and like charges between the molecule and negatively charged clay particles.

8710422e0f1e.title: Agricultural pollution
8710422e0f1e.sentence: Once in the environment these pollutants can have both direct effects in surrounding ecosystems, e.g. killing local wildlife or contaminating drinking water, and downstream effects such as dead zones caused by agricultural runoff is concentrated in large water bodies.

676633f4a500.title: Surface runoff
676633f4a500.sentence: This occurs when the rate of rainfall on a surface exceeds the rate at which water can infiltrate the ground, and any depression storage has already been filled.

dad6b6d336d8.title: Surface runoff
dad6b6d336d8.sentence: When the soil is saturated and the depression storage filled, and rain continues to fall, the rainfall will immediately produce surface runoff.

f1b817ba6073.title: Surface runoff
f1b817ba6073.sentence: This is also called Hortonian overland flow (after Robert E. Horton), or unsaturated overland flow.

30b4c4367e5c.title: Surface runoff
30b4c4367e5c.sentence: This more commonly occurs in arid and semi-arid regions, where rainfall intensities are high and the soil infiltration capacity is reduced because of surface sealing, or in urban areas where pavements prevent water from infiltrating.

0d8293f29aeb.title: Surface runoff
0d8293f29aeb.sentence: This runoff is called saturation excess overland flow, saturated overland flow, or Dunne runoff.

0f19d9c286b8.title: Surface runoff
0f19d9c286b8.sentence: The higher the level of antecedent soil moisture, the more quickly the soil becomes saturated.

ed289ca2c2fd.title: Surface runoff
ed289ca2c2fd.sentence: Once the soil is saturated, runoff occurs.

55b44434f6bd.title: Surface runoff
55b44434f6bd.sentence: After water infiltrates the soil on an up-slope portion of a hill, the water may flow laterally through the soil, and exfiltrate (flow out of the soil) closer to a channel.

aa9de25f5e1c.title: Surface runoff
aa9de25f5e1c.sentence: This is called subsurface return flow or throughflow.

183d83c67ed9.title: Surface runoff
183d83c67ed9.sentence: Mitigation of adverse impacts of runoff can take several forms:

90006c360261.title: Surface runoff
90006c360261.sentence: Erosion controls have appeared since medieval times when farmers realized the importance of contour farming to protect soil resources.

f5011333bf8b.title: Surface runoff
f5011333bf8b.sentence: This included such techniques as: use of straw bales and barriers to slow runoff on slopes, installation of silt fences, programming construction for months that have less rainfall and minimizing extent and duration of exposed graded areas.

edcbb7b93dc3.title: Surface runoff
edcbb7b93dc3.sentence: Some of the techniques commonly applied are: provision of holding ponds (also called detention basins or balancing lakes) to buffer riverine peak flows, use of energy dissipators in channels to reduce stream velocity and land use controls to minimize runoff.

082c1bffef00.title: Surface runoff
082c1bffef00.sentence: The U.S. Clean Water Act (CWA) requires that local governments in urbanized areas (as defined by the Census Bureau) obtain stormwater discharge permits for their drainage systems.

7a2700eb01cf.title: Surface runoff
7a2700eb01cf.sentence: Essentially this means that the locality must operate a stormwater management program for all surface runoff that enters the municipal separate storm sewer system ("MS4").

9c5865d15b32.title: Surface runoff
9c5865d15b32.sentence: Urban runoff is surface runoff of rainwater, landscape irrigation, and car washing created by urbanization.

afa0e44e2539.title: Surface runoff
afa0e44e2539.sentence: Impervious surfaces (roads, parking lots and sidewalks) are constructed during land development.

a4a9b2d90643.title: Surface runoff
a4a9b2d90643.sentence: During rain, storms, and other precipitation events, these surfaces (built from materials such as asphalt and concrete), along with rooftops, carry polluted stormwater to storm drains, instead of allowing the water to percolate through soil.

53c887d92043.title: Surface runoff
53c887d92043.sentence: This causes lowering of the water table (because groundwater recharge is lessened) and flooding since the amount of water that remains on the surface is greater.

b87dde217739.title: Surface runoff
b87dde217739.sentence: Most municipal storm sewer systems discharge untreated stormwater to streams, rivers, and bays.

e9eb715eccb5.title: Surface runoff
e9eb715eccb5.sentence: Many municipalities have produced guidelines and codes (zoning and related ordinances) for land developers that encourage minimum width sidewalks, use of pavers set in earth for driveways and walkways and other design techniques to allow maximum water infiltration in urban settings.

8c84813e5988.title: Carbon sink
8c84813e5988.sentence: Broad-base adoption of mass timber and their role in substituting steel and concrete in new mid-rise construction projects over the next few decades has the potential to turn timber buildings into carbon sinks, as they store the carbon dioxide taken up from the air by trees that are harvested and used as mass timber.

2815ff452948.title: Carbon sink
2815ff452948.sentence: This could result in storing between 10 million tons of carbon per year in the lowest scenario and close to 700 million tons in the highest scenario.

3402864afd67.title: Carbon sink
3402864afd67.sentence: For this to happen, the harvested forests would need to be sustainably managed and wood from demolished timber buildings would need to be reused or preserved on land in various forms.

1209baba027f.title: Carbon sink
1209baba027f.sentence: Using rapidly renewable plant materials like bamboo, straw or hempcrete can further carbon sinks.

f1f4b0ada804.title: Eutrophication
f1f4b0ada804.section: Causes and effects for different types of water bodies > Coastal waters
f1f4b0ada804.sentence: Eutrophication is a common phenomenon in coastal waters, where nitrogenous sources are the main culprit.

0350eabdd69f.title: Eutrophication
0350eabdd69f.section: Causes and effects for different types of water bodies > Coastal waters
0350eabdd69f.sentence: In coastal waters, nitrogen is commonly the key limiting nutrient of marine waters (unlike the freshwater systems where phosphorus is often the limiting nutrient).

a1d7723cc60f.title: Eutrophication
a1d7723cc60f.section: Causes and effects for different types of water bodies > Coastal waters
a1d7723cc60f.sentence: Therefore, nitrogen levels are more important than phosphorus levels for understanding and controlling eutrophication problems in salt water.

56741262142b.title: Eutrophication
56741262142b.section: Causes and effects for different types of water bodies > Coastal waters > Effects of coastal eutrophication
56741262142b.sentence: These pressures vary geographically depending on the catchment activities and associated nutrient load.

e570161810a3.title: Eutrophication
e570161810a3.section: Causes and effects for different types of water bodies > Coastal waters > Effects of coastal eutrophication
e570161810a3.sentence: The geographical setting of the coastal zone is another important factor as it controls dilution of the nutrient load and oxygen exchange with the atmosphere.

8c43781d825a.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
8c43781d825a.sentence: Over the last century the annual riverine inputs of nitrogen and phosphorus to the oceans have increased from 19 to 37 megatonnes of nitrogen and from 2 to 4 megatonnes of phosphorus.

854b53316bb8.title: Eutrophication
854b53316bb8.sentence: Some harmful algal blooms resulting from eutrophication, are toxic to plants and animals.

056f2e9cd6bb.title: Eutrophication
056f2e9cd6bb.sentence: When the algae die or are eaten, neuro- and hepatotoxins are released which can kill animals and may pose a threat to humans.

d7d444b0b078.title: Eutrophication
d7d444b0b078.sentence: An example of algal toxins working their way into humans is the case of shellfish poisoning.

55c3b860eab5.title: Eutrophication
55c3b860eab5.section: Causes and effects for different types of water bodies > Freshwater systems
55c3b860eab5.sentence: In freshwater ecosystems, the formation of floating algal blooms are commonly nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria (blue-green algae).

ab1ca53be9e1.title: Eutrophication
ab1ca53be9e1.section: Causes and effects for different types of water bodies > Freshwater systems
ab1ca53be9e1.sentence: This outcome is favored when soluble nitrogen becomes limiting and phosphorus inputs remain significant.

fbe87d7ce34e.title: Eutrophication
fbe87d7ce34e.sentence: Eutrophication and harmful algal blooms can have economic impacts due to increasing water treatment costs, commercial fishing and shellfish losses, recreational fishing losses (reductions in harvestable fish and shellfish), and reduced tourism income (decreases in perceived aesthetic value of the water body and decreases in safety due to high bacteria levels from decomposition).

d111f4b5ab38.title: Eutrophication
d111f4b5ab38.sentence: Water treatment costs can be increased due to decreases in water transparency (increased turbidity).

fe71d7d29460.title: Eutrophication
fe71d7d29460.sentence: There can also be issues with color and smell during drinking water treatment.

e2baae45a4d9.title: Eutrophication
e2baae45a4d9.sentence: However, controlled eutrophication can potentially be used to increase production in fisheries, which in turn increases community income.

9b3a82ede88b.title: Eutrophication
9b3a82ede88b.sentence: Notably, there is a delicate line where eutrophication can become damaging very quickly, and as such is not recommended currently due to high eutrophication rates.

ab33817f4ee9.title: Eutrophication
ab33817f4ee9.sentence: Eutrophication can be a natural process and occurs naturally through the gradual accumulation of sediment and nutrients.

c6533948cfad.title: Eutrophication
c6533948cfad.sentence: Naturally, eutrophication is usually caused by the natural accumulation of nutrients from dissolved phosphate minerals and dead plant matter in water.

d934a32fee58.title: Phosphorus cycle
d934a32fee58.sentence: It does occur naturally, as when lakes age they become more productive due to increases in major limiting reagents such as nitrogen and phosphorus.

7e18a6714492.title: Eutrophication
7e18a6714492.sentence: Paleolimnologists now recognise that climate change, geology, and other external influences are also critical in regulating the natural productivity of lakes.

a8dfa8b545f3.title: Eutrophication
a8dfa8b545f3.sentence: Nutrient bioextraction or bioharvesting is the practice of farming and harvesting shellfish and seaweed to remove nitrogen and other nutrients from natural water bodies.

b751a94df991.title: Eutrophication
b751a94df991.section: Reversal and remediation > Nutrient bioextraction > Shellfish in estuaries
b751a94df991.sentence: Several studies have shown that oysters and mussels can dramatically impact nitrogen levels in estuaries.

02034aebfebe.title: Eutrophication
02034aebfebe.section: Reversal and remediation > Nutrient bioextraction > Shellfish in estuaries
02034aebfebe.sentence: It has been suggested that nitrogen removal by oyster reefs could generate net benefits for sources facing nitrogen emission restrictions, similar to other nutrient trading scenarios.

7f70649c91d8.title: Eutrophication
7f70649c91d8.section: Reversal and remediation > Nutrient bioextraction > Shellfish in estuaries
7f70649c91d8.sentence: Specifically, if oysters maintain nitrogen levels in estuaries below thresholds, then oysters effectively stave off an enforcement response, and compliance costs parties responsible for nitrogen emission would otherwise incur.

62b35cf38f06.title: Eutrophication
62b35cf38f06.section: Reversal and remediation > Nutrient bioextraction > Seaweed farming
62b35cf38f06.sentence: Seaweed, such as kelp, also absorbs phosphorus and nitrogen and is thus helpful to remove excessive nutrients from polluted parts of the sea.

0743cc25258b.title: Eutrophication
0743cc25258b.sentence: There are multiple different ways to fix cultural eutrophication with raw sewage being a point source of pollution.

35d8b8d1e442.title: Eutrophication
35d8b8d1e442.section: Prevention > Minimizing nutrient pollution by agriculture
35d8b8d1e442.sentence: There are many ways to help fix cultural eutrophication caused by agriculture.

77aa4143bd2b.title: Eutrophication
77aa4143bd2b.sentence: For example, sewage treatment plants can be upgraded for biological nutrient removal so that they discharge much less nitrogen and phosphorus to the receiving water body.

6aed634f10d5.title: Eutrophication
6aed634f10d5.sentence: However, even with good secondary treatment, most final effluents from sewage treatment works contain substantial concentrations of nitrogen as nitrate, nitrite or ammonia.

2ae1fbceed11.title: Eutrophication
2ae1fbceed11.section: Prevention > Minimizing nutrient pollution by agriculture
2ae1fbceed11.sentence: - Nutrient management techniques - Anyone using fertilizers should apply fertilizer in the correct amount, at the right time of year, with the right method and placement.

98305e324f5b.title: Eutrophication
98305e324f5b.sentence: SDG 14 specifically has a target to: "by 2025, prevent and significantly reduce marine pollution of all kinds, in particular from land-based activities, including marine debris and nutrient pollution".

31391228f986.title: Eutrophication
31391228f986.sentence: Reducing nutrient inputs is a crucial precondition for restoration.

26f4e913d751.title: Eutrophication
26f4e913d751.sentence: Still, there are two caveats: Firstly, it can take a long time, mainly because of the storage of nutrients in sediments.

b4515e31d4af.title: Eutrophication
b4515e31d4af.sentence: Secondly, restoration may need more than a simple reversal of inputs since there are sometimes several stable but very different ecological states.

b99e7f8d7bff.title: Eutrophication
b99e7f8d7bff.section: Reversal and remediation > Chemical removal of phosphorus
b99e7f8d7bff.sentence: Of the several phosphate sorbents, alum (aluminium sulfate) is of practical interest.) Many materials have been investigated.

e1e4e9d9447b.title: Eutrophication
e1e4e9d9447b.section: Reversal and remediation > Chemical removal of phosphorus
e1e4e9d9447b.sentence: The phosphate sorbent is commonly applied in the surface of the water body and it sinks to the bottom of the lake reducing phosphate, such sorbents have been applied worldwide to manage eutrophication and algal bloom (for example under the commercial name Phoslock).

689e93bddad4.title: Eutrophication
689e93bddad4.section: Reversal and remediation > Chemical removal of phosphorus
689e93bddad4.sentence: Finnish phosphorus removal measures started in the mid-1970s and have targeted rivers and lakes polluted by industrial and municipal discharges.

21536da3e149.title: Eutrophication
21536da3e149.section: Reversal and remediation > Chemical removal of phosphorus
21536da3e149.sentence: These efforts have had a 90% removal efficiency.

1e87aa2d64f6.title: Ocean acidification
1e87aa2d64f6.section: Possible responses > Carbon removal technologies which add alkalinity > Ocean alkalinity enhancement
1e87aa2d64f6.sentence: Ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) is a proposed "carbon dioxide removal (CDR) method that involves deposition of alkaline minerals or their dissociation products at the ocean surface".

d27ab5dcbe48.title: Ocean acidification
d27ab5dcbe48.section: Possible responses > Carbon removal technologies which add alkalinity
d27ab5dcbe48.sentence: Some carbon removal techniques add alkalinity to the ocean and therefore immediately buffer pH changes which might help the organisms in the region that the extra alkalinity is added to.

d0b25580d5e3.title: Ocean acidification
d0b25580d5e3.section: Possible responses > Carbon removal technologies which add alkalinity > Electrochemical methods
d0b25580d5e3.sentence: Electrochemical methods, or electrolysis, can strip carbon dioxide directly from seawater.

efea1542f66c.title: Ocean acidification
efea1542f66c.section: Possible responses > Carbon removal technologies which add alkalinity > Electrochemical methods
efea1542f66c.sentence: Electrochemical process are a type of ocean alkalinity enhancement, too.

1131cb49dab9.title: Ocean acidification
1131cb49dab9.sentence: These strategies are under investigation, but generally have a low technology readiness level and many risks.

f433475169aa.title: Carbon cycle
f433475169aa.sentence: Slow or deep carbon cycling is an important process, though it is not as well-understood as the relatively fast carbon movement through the atmosphere, terrestrial biosphere, ocean, and geosphere.

513c8df498cc.title: Carbon cycle
513c8df498cc.sentence: The deep carbon cycle is intimately connected to the movement of carbon in the Earth's surface and atmosphere.

2e896fc4bc46.title: Carbon cycle
2e896fc4bc46.section: Processes within slow carbon cycle > Carbon in the lower mantle
2e896fc4bc46.sentence: Carbon principally enters the mantle in the form of carbonate-rich sediments on tectonic plates of ocean crust, which pull the carbon into the mantle upon undergoing subduction.

214f97cb87c9.title: Carbon cycle
214f97cb87c9.sentence: If the process did not exist, carbon would remain in the atmosphere, where it would accumulate to extremely high levels over long periods of time.

974ef3ddb7c6.title: Carbon cycle
974ef3ddb7c6.sentence: Therefore, by allowing carbon to return to the Earth, the deep carbon cycle plays a critical role in maintaining the terrestrial conditions necessary for life to exist.

311e42c1b085.title: Carbon cycle
311e42c1b085.section: Processes within slow carbon cycle > Carbon in the lower mantle
311e42c1b085.sentence: For instance, a 2011 study demonstrated that carbon cycling extends all the way to the lower mantle.

413d09905258.title: Carbon cycle
413d09905258.section: Processes within slow carbon cycle > Carbon in the lower mantle
413d09905258.sentence: The study analyzed rare, super-deep diamonds at a site in Juina, Brazil, determining that the bulk composition of some of the diamonds' inclusions matched the expected result of basalt melting and crystallisation under lower mantle temperatures and pressures.

daae677913a2.title: Water cycle
daae677913a2.section: Historical interpretations > Discovery of the correct theory
daae677913a2.sentence: The first published thinker to assert that rainfall alone was sufficient for the maintenance of rivers was Bernard Palissy (1580 CE), who is often credited as the discoverer of the modern theory of the water cycle.

6ab99d9a2988.title: Water cycle
6ab99d9a2988.sentence: In ancient times, it was widely thought that the land mass floated on a body of water, and that most of the water in rivers has its origin under the earth.

6351661405e9.title: Water cycle
6351661405e9.sentence: By roughly 500 BCE, Greek scholars were speculating that much of the water in rivers can be attributed to rain.

7c1bdb788e4e.title: Water cycle
7c1bdb788e4e.section: Historical interpretations > Discovery of the correct theory
7c1bdb788e4e.sentence: Palissy's theories were not tested scientifically until 1674, in a study commonly attributed to Pierre Perrault.

15d24688de74.title: Water cycle
15d24688de74.section: Historical interpretations > Discovery of the correct theory
15d24688de74.sentence: Even then, these beliefs were not accepted in mainstream science until the early nineteenth century.

0847d06c8722.title: Soil erosion
0847d06c8722.section: Global environmental effects > Sedimentation of aquatic ecosystems
0847d06c8722.sentence: Soil erosion (especially from agricultural activity) is considered to be the leading global cause of diffuse water pollution, due to the effects of the excess sediments flowing into the world's waterways.

01f3f40fed87.title: Soil erosion
01f3f40fed87.section: Global environmental effects > Sedimentation of aquatic ecosystems
01f3f40fed87.sentence: The sediments themselves act as pollutants, as well as being carriers for other pollutants, such as attached pesticide molecules or heavy metals.

b5426f025fc1.title: Soil erosion
b5426f025fc1.section: Global environmental effects > Sedimentation of aquatic ecosystems
b5426f025fc1.sentence: Silt can smother the spawning beds of fish, by filling in the space between gravel on the stream bed.

74343c509d93.title: Soil erosion
74343c509d93.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Roads and human impact
74343c509d93.sentence: Much of the sediment carried in runoff from urban areas (especially roads) is highly contaminated with fuel, oil, and other chemicals.

c7aa2efbc3ed.title: Soil erosion
c7aa2efbc3ed.sentence: Tillage erosion occurs in cultivated fields due to the movement of soil by tillage.

c3741a4272cf.title: Soil erosion
c3741a4272cf.sentence: There is growing evidence that tillage erosion is a major soil erosion process in agricultural land, surpassing water and wind erosion in many fields all around the world, especially on sloping and hilly lands.

c7aaff49c0da.title: Soil erosion
c7aaff49c0da.sentence: Eroded hilltops are actually caused by tillage erosion as water erosion mainly causes soil losses in the midslope and lowerslope segments of a slope, not the hilltops.

3e1cbbe94e58.title: Soil erosion
3e1cbbe94e58.sentence: Tillage erosion results in soil degradation, which can lead to significant reduction in crop yield and, therefore, economic losses for the farm.

06cf1906534a.title: Soil erosion
06cf1906534a.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
06cf1906534a.sentence: Rainfall, and the surface runoff which may result from rainfall, produce four main types of soil erosion: splash erosion, sheet erosion, rill erosion, and gully erosion.

dbaa6beb3e08.title: Soil erosion
dbaa6beb3e08.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
dbaa6beb3e08.sentence: Splash erosion is generally seen as the first and least severe stage in the soil erosion process, which is followed by sheet erosion, then rill erosion and finally gully erosion (the most severe of the four).

e3a50167b4dd.title: Soil erosion
e3a50167b4dd.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
e3a50167b4dd.sentence: In splash erosion, the impact of a falling raindrop creates a small crater in the soil, ejecting soil particles.

1caca018c7a2.title: Soil erosion
1caca018c7a2.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
1caca018c7a2.sentence: The distance the ejected soil particles travel can be as much as 0.6 m (two feet) vertically and 1.5 m (five feet) horizontally on level ground and in the absence of wind.

a0f2ebe48696.title: Soil erosion
a0f2ebe48696.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
a0f2ebe48696.sentence: Sheet erosion is the transport of loosened soil particles by overland flow.

15b1cf864283.title: Soil erosion
15b1cf864283.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
15b1cf864283.sentence: Rill erosion refers to the development of small, ephemeral concentrated flow paths which function as both sediment sources and sediment delivery systems for erosion on hillslopes.

d8da2ed8c46a.title: Soil erosion
d8da2ed8c46a.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
d8da2ed8c46a.sentence: Flow depths in rills are typically of the order of a few centimeters (about an inch) or less and along-channel slopes may be quite steep.

2412a342a6b9.title: Soil erosion
2412a342a6b9.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
2412a342a6b9.sentence: Gully erosion occurs when runoff water accumulates and rapidly flows in narrow channels during or immediately after heavy rains or melting snow, removing soil to a considerable depth.

a21033c51898.title: Soil erosion
a21033c51898.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
a21033c51898.sentence: The most commonly used model for predicting soil loss from water erosion is the Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE).

0ad055c1f9cf.title: Soil erosion
0ad055c1f9cf.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
0ad055c1f9cf.sentence: It estimates the average annual soil loss A on a plot-sized area as:

db310249f2c0.title: Soil erosion
db310249f2c0.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
db310249f2c0.sentence: where R is the rainfall erosivity factor, K is the soil erodibility factor, L and S are topographic factors representing length and slope, respectively, C is the cover and management factor and P is the support practices factor.

2fe1434c5fe8.title: Soil erosion
2fe1434c5fe8.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
2fe1434c5fe8.sentence: This was developed in the 1960s and 1970s.

cd0468771e7f.title: Soil erosion
cd0468771e7f.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
cd0468771e7f.sentence: Global studies continue to be based on the USLE.

121f3279aeec.title: Soil erosion
121f3279aeec.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
121f3279aeec.sentence: One major problem is that the USLE cannot simulate gully erosion, and so erosion from gullies is ignored in any USLE-based assessment of erosion.

3b63c6d6223f.title: Soil erosion
3b63c6d6223f.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
3b63c6d6223f.sentence: Yet erosion from gullies can be a substantial proportion (10–80%) of total erosion on cultivated and grazed land.

0359fd07598e.title: Soil erosion
0359fd07598e.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
0359fd07598e.sentence: But because of the complexity of soil erosion and its constituent processes, all erosion models can only roughly approximate actual erosion rates when validated i.e. when model predictions are compared with real-world measurements of erosion.

62525345c547.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
62525345c547.sentence: The USLE was developed in the U.S., based on soil erosion data collected beginning in the 1930s by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Soil Conservation Service (now the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service).

a38b20b8cb8d.title: Soil erosion
a38b20b8cb8d.sentence: Wind erosion is a major geomorphological force, especially in arid and semi-arid regions.

85e81d546019.title: Soil erosion
85e81d546019.sentence: It is also a major source of land degradation, evaporation, desertification, harmful airborne dust, and crop damage—especially after being increased far above natural rates by human activities such as deforestation, urbanization, and agriculture.

6c8298f69e7f.title: Soil erosion
6c8298f69e7f.sentence: Wind erosion is of two primary varieties: deflation, where the wind picks up and carries away loose particles; and abrasion, where surfaces are worn down as they are struck by airborne particles carried by wind.

314ead511caf.title: Soil erosion
314ead511caf.section: Global environmental effects > Airborne dust pollution
314ead511caf.sentence: Soil particles picked up during wind erosion of soil are a major source of air pollution, in the form of airborne particulates called dust.

f6fb0d963de1.title: Soil erosion
f6fb0d963de1.section: Global environmental effects > Airborne dust pollution
f6fb0d963de1.sentence: Dust events have been linked to a decline in the health of coral reefs across the Caribbean and Florida, primarily since the 1970s.

3a8a2eb8464e.title: Evapotranspiration
3a8a2eb8464e.sentence: Potential evapotranspiration (PET) or potential evaporation (PE) is the amount of water that would be evaporated and transpired by a specific crop, soil or ecosystem if there was sufficient water available.

89015ffbb81c.title: Evapotranspiration
89015ffbb81c.sentence: If the actual evapotranspiration (AET) is considered the net result of atmospheric demand for moisture from a surface and the ability of the surface to supply moisture, then PET is a measure of the demand side (also called evaporative demand).

88142d19ea96.title: Evapotranspiration
88142d19ea96.sentence: Evapotranspiration can never be greater than potential evapotranspiration, but can be lower if there is not enough water to be evaporated or plants are unable to transpire maturely and readily.

58294ca073d7.title: Evapotranspiration
58294ca073d7.sentence: A dryland is a place where annual potential evaporation exceeds annual precipitation.

313e3b5efe53.title: Evapotranspiration
313e3b5efe53.sentence: Potential evapotranspiration is higher in the summer, on clearer and less cloudy days, and closer to the equator, because of the higher levels of solar radiation that provides the energy (heat) for evaporation.

552ba2a4ff74.title: Evapotranspiration
552ba2a4ff74.sentence: Potential evapotranspiration is also higher on windy days because the evaporated moisture can be quickly moved from the ground or plant surface before it precipitates, allowing more evaporation to fill its place.

6a407f8e2088.title: Evapotranspiration
6a407f8e2088.sentence: Because atmospheric vapor flux is difficult or time-consuming to measure directly, evapotranspiration is typically estimated by one of several different methods that do not rely on direct measurement.

a06462eecca6.sentence: In the equation, the change in water stored within the basin (ΔS) is related to precipitation (P) (water going into the basin), and evapotranspiration (ET), streamflow (Q), and groundwater recharge (D) (water leaving the basin).

124c8462a3f2.title: Evapotranspiration

c92d711d4d5a.title: Evapotranspiration
c92d711d4d5a.sentence: This allows for both actual and potential evapotranspiration to be calculated on a pixel-by-pixel basis.

6d0fdd7a2a4c.title: Evapotranspiration

6d0fdd7a2a4c.sentence: The most general and widely used equation for calculating reference ET is the Penman equation.

a75979ce794e.sentence: Evapotranspiration can be measured directly with a weighing or pan lysimeter.

7091b4b7d7d2.title: Evapotranspiration
7091b4b7d7d2.sentence: When used properly, this allows for precise measurement of evapotranspiration over small areas.

ccd43adbd19e.title: Evapotranspiration
ccd43adbd19e.section: Influencing factors > Secondary factors > Vegetation type
ccd43adbd19e.sentence: Vegetation type impacts levels of evapotranspiration.

51871d2607fc.title: Evapotranspiration
51871d2607fc.section: Influencing factors > Secondary factors > Vegetation coverage
51871d2607fc.sentence: The density of vegetation coverage can control different environmental conditions of varying ecosystems and the way that water moves through the system.

b9693c923590.title: Evapotranspiration
b9693c923590.section: Influencing factors > Secondary factors > Vegetation coverage
b9693c923590.sentence: As a result, denser vegetation, like forests, may increase evapotranspiration and reduce water yield.

f1a0ed1d4b95.title: Evapotranspiration
f1a0ed1d4b95.section: Influencing factors > Secondary factors > Vegetation coverage
f1a0ed1d4b95.sentence: In rainforests, water yield is increased (compared to cleared, unforested land in the same climatic zone) as evapotranspiration increases humidity within the forest (a portion of which condenses and returns quickly as precipitation experienced at ground level as rain).

7d213de61359.title: Evapotranspiration
7d213de61359.section: Influencing factors > Secondary factors > Vegetation coverage
7d213de61359.sentence: The density of the vegetation blocks sunlight and reduces temperatures at ground level (thereby reducing losses due to surface evaporation), and reduces wind speeds (thereby reducing the loss of airborne moisture).

dc98792db23e.title: Evapotranspiration
dc98792db23e.section: Influencing factors > Secondary factors > Vegetation coverage
dc98792db23e.sentence: The combined effect results in increased surface stream flows and a higher ground water table whilst the rainforest is preserved.

4bb58a88fd96.title: Evapotranspiration
4bb58a88fd96.section: Influencing factors > Secondary factors > Vegetation coverage
4bb58a88fd96.sentence: Clearing of rainforests frequently leads to desertification as ground level temperatures and wind speeds increase, vegetation cover is lost or intentionally destroyed by clearing and burning, soil moisture is reduced by wind, and soils are easily eroded by high wind and rainfall events.

129a3c8203f0.title: Deforestation
129a3c8203f0.section: Impacts > On the environment > Changes to the water cycle
129a3c8203f0.sentence: Deforestation also contributes to decreased evapotranspiration, which lessens atmospheric moisture which in some cases affects precipitation levels downwind from the deforested area, as water is not recycled to downwind forests, but is lost in runoff and returns directly to the oceans.

b96fa8190ed8.title: Nitrogen fixation
b96fa8190ed8.section: Biological > Root nodule symbioses > Legume family
b96fa8190ed8.sentence: Plants that contribute to nitrogen fixation include those of the legume family—Fabaceae— with taxa such as kudzu, clover, soybean, alfalfa, lupin, peanut and rooibos.

2d74f6a9f259.title: Nitrogen fixation
2d74f6a9f259.section: Biological > Root nodule symbioses > Legume family
2d74f6a9f259.sentence: They contain symbiotic rhizobia bacteria within nodules in their root systems, producing nitrogen compounds that help the plant to grow and compete with other plants.

a361eda15b3a.title: Nitrogen fixation
a361eda15b3a.section: Biological > Root nodule symbioses > Legume family
a361eda15b3a.sentence: When the plant dies, the fixed nitrogen is released, making it available to other plants; this helps to fertilize the soil.

589a63ff4267.title: Nitrogen fixation
589a63ff4267.section: Biological > Root nodule symbioses > Legume family
589a63ff4267.sentence: In many traditional farming practices, fields are rotated through various types of crops, which usually include one consisting mainly or entirely of clover.

1c1c9d0fb707.title: Agroforestry
1c1c9d0fb707.sentence: Agroforestry can also utilise nitrogen-fixing plants such as legumes to restore soil nitrogen fertility.

8bdeec80cf3b.title: Nitrogen fixation
8bdeec80cf3b.sentence: Nitrogen can be fixed by lightning converting nitrogen gas (N 2) and oxygen gas (O 2) in the atmosphere into nitrogen oxides (NOx).

60ba4df2e106.title: Nitrogen fixation
60ba4df2e106.sentence: Lightning produces enough energy and heat to break this bond allowing nitrogen atoms to react with oxygen, forming NOx.

28070efc2d99.title: Nitrogen fixation
28070efc2d99.sentence: These compounds cannot be used by plants, but as this molecule cools, it reacts with oxygen to form nitrogen dioxide (NO 2), which in turn reacts with water to produce nitrous acid (HNO 2) or nitric acid (HNO 3).

61b6490017b2.title: Nitrogen fixation
61b6490017b2.sentence: When these acids seep into the soil, they produce nitrate (NO3−), which is of use to plants.

baee837fce9f.title: Nitrogen fixation
baee837fce9f.sentence: A method for nitrogen fixation was first described by Henry Cavendish in 1784 using electric arcs reacting nitrogen and oxygen in air.

23a9f7f9e2ee.title: Nitrogen fixation
23a9f7f9e2ee.sentence: The fixation of nitrogen by lightning is a very similar natural occurring process.

14f0f54ea68f.title: Biological pump
14f0f54ea68f.section: Processes in the biological pump > Microbial loop > Bacterial lysis
14f0f54ea68f.sentence: The microbial loop describes a trophic pathway in the marine microbial food web where dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is returned to higher trophic levels via its incorporation into bacterial biomass, and then coupled with the classic food chain formed by phytoplankton-zooplankton-nekton.

2f28fe466e4c.title: Biological pump
2f28fe466e4c.section: Processes in the biological pump > Microbial loop > Bacterial lysis
2f28fe466e4c.sentence: The term microbial loop was coined by Farooq Azam, Tom Fenchel et al. in 1983 to include the role played by bacteria in the carbon and nutrient cycles of the marine environment.

fced2db28cd2.title: Biological pump
fced2db28cd2.section: Processes in the biological pump > Microbial loop > Bacterial lysis
fced2db28cd2.sentence: In general, dissolved organic carbon is introduced into the ocean environment from bacterial lysis, the leakage or exudation of fixed carbon from phytoplankton (e.g., mucilaginous exopolymer from diatoms), sudden cell senescence, sloppy feeding by zooplankton, the excretion of waste products by aquatic animals, or the breakdown or dissolution of organic particles from terrestrial plants and soils.

1f9b5e137b9f.title: Soil carbon
1f9b5e137b9f.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Measuring data on soil organic carbon
1f9b5e137b9f.sentence: Under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), countries must estimate and report GHG emissions and removals, including changes in carbon stocks in all five pools (above- and below-ground biomass, dead wood, litter, and soil carbon) and associated emissions and removals from land use, land-use change and forestry activities, according to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change's good practice guidance.

efd44e6f7978.title: Soil carbon
efd44e6f7978.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Measuring data on soil organic carbon
efd44e6f7978.sentence: For these reasons, reliable estimates of soil organic carbon stock and stock changes are needed for Reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation and GHG reporting under the UNFCCC.

0c8e46d8db2a.title: Soil carbon
0c8e46d8db2a.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Measuring data on soil organic carbon > Europe
0c8e46d8db2a.sentence: Finally, a new proposed model for estimation of soil organic carbon in agricultural soils has estimated current top SOC stock of 17.63 Gt in EU agricultural soils.

ef8620986be6.title: Soil carbon
ef8620986be6.sentence: Soil inorganic carbon consists of mineral forms of carbon, either from weathering of parent material, or from reaction of soil minerals with atmospheric CO2.

ecc2459e9dca.title: Soil carbon
ecc2459e9dca.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Inorganic Carbon
ecc2459e9dca.sentence: In arid and semi-arid environments, a majority of soil carbon occurs in the form of inorganic carbonates, such as the minerals calcite and dolomite.

e70d79b71b29.title: Soil carbon

e70d79b71b29.sentence: Carbonates can originate from the bedrock or parent material from which the soil forms, or can form in situ as pedogenic carbonate.

df1ff4a5d05b.title: Soil carbon

15ddd6ed294f.title: Soil carbon
15ddd6ed294f.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
15ddd6ed294f.sentence: In humid environments, the majority of soil carbon is organic.

0b042c18f45a.title: Soil carbon

0b042c18f45a.sentence: Soil organic carbon is part of soil organic matter, which contains approximately 50% carbon by dry weight, with the remaining mass made up primarily of hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur.

bf418ab870c0.title: Soil carbon
bf418ab870c0.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
bf418ab870c0.sentence: Detritus resulting from plant senescence is the major source of soil organic carbon, as organic matter is added to soil in the form of plant roots, fallen leaves, and crop residue.

47f0ca9c7079.title: Soil carbon

47f0ca9c7079.sentence: Root exudates are another source of soil carbon.

45e1c3bc3c55.title: Soil carbon

45e1c3bc3c55.sentence: Some plant compounds, such as cellulose, starches, proteins, and lipids, are readily degraded by microbes, resulting in short residence times, while more persistent forms of organic C include lignin, humus, organic matter encapsulated in soil aggregates and charcoal.

df9b9ed25a89.title: Soil carbon

df9b9ed25a89.sentence: These resist alteration and have long residence times.

a51f99c7bff0.sentence: Soil organic carbon increased the cation exchange capacity (CEC), a measure of soil fertility, in sandy soils.

bcc7db87a7fd.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
bcc7db87a7fd.sentence: As climate change increases mean annual air temperatures throughout the Arctic, it extends permafrost thaw and deepens the active layer, exposing old carbon that has been in storage for decades to millennia to biogenic processes which facilitate its entrance into the atmosphere.

7b48beb563e2.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
7b48beb563e2.sentence: Carbon emissions from permafrost thaw contribute to the same warming which facilitates the thaw, making it a positive climate change feedback.

336227941771.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
336227941771.sentence: In general, the volume of permafrost in the upper 3 m of ground is expected to decrease by about 25% per 1 °C (1.8 °F)of global warming.

0e2865ebec2e.sentence: Most of the permafrost soil are oxic and provide a suitable environment for aerobic microbial respiration.

1fbd9f74435b.sentence: As such, carbon dioxide emissions account for the overwhelming majority of permafrost emissions and of the Arctic emissions in general.

8c519e5475d6.sentence: On the other hand, former permafrost areas consistently see increased vegetation growth, or primary production, as plants can set down deeper roots in the thawed soil and grow larger and uptake more carbon.

b7c6a54581ab.title: Permafrost carbon cycle

b7c6a54581ab.sentence: This is generally the main counteracting feedback on permafrost carbon emissions.

8829ff1866f4.sentence: Since methanogenesis requires anaerobic environments, it is frequently associated with Arctic lakes, where the emergence of bubbles of methane can be observed.

a770558baa2c.sentence: Lakes produced by the thaw of particularly ice-rich permafrost are known as thermokarst lakes.

c4a2350f03e0.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
c4a2350f03e0.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Cumulative
c4a2350f03e0.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report estimates that carbon dioxide and methane released from permafrost could amount to the equivalent of 14–175 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide per 1 °C (1.8 °F) of warming.

2c28c2d41d51.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
2c28c2d41d51.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Cumulative
2c28c2d41d51.sentence: For comparison, by 2019, annual anthropogenic emission of carbon dioxide alone stood around 40 billion tonnes.

f4bc7138bb05.title: Cellular respiration

cbca09cb0732.sentence: During winter, ice and snow cover can attenuate light, and therefore reduce rates of photosynthesis.

43a5f66149e6.sentence: The freezing over of a lake also prevents air-water interactions that allow the exchange of oxygen.

70fa610f7c86.title: Hypoxia (environmental)
70fa610f7c86.sentence: This creates a lack of oxygen while respiration continues.

3c85a422c28e.title: Dead zone (ecology)
3c85a422c28e.sentence: The influence of dead zones on fisheries and other marine commercial activities varies by the length of occurrence and location.

733776466aac.title: Dead zone (ecology)
733776466aac.sentence: Dead zones are often accompanied by a decrease in biodiversity and collapse in benthic populations, lowering the diversity of yield in commercial fishing operations, but in cases of eutrophication-related dead zone formations, the increase in nutrient availability can lead to temporary rises in select yields among pelagic populations, such as anchovies.

810d73b763a1.title: Dead zone (ecology)
810d73b763a1.sentence: However, studies estimate that the increased production in the surrounding areas do not offset the net decrease in productivity resulting from the dead zone.

9de24ec107e3.title: Dead zone (ecology)
