9de24ec107e3.sentence: It is reported that the Gulf of Mexico dead zone is costing the U.S. seafood and tourism industries about $82 million a year.

9e5f4576b378.title: Dead zone (ecology)
9e5f4576b378.section: Locations > Gulf of Mexico 'dead zone' > Economic impact
9e5f4576b378.sentence: Scientists are not in universal agreement that nutrient loading has a negative impact on fisheries.

bb19a9e19211.title: Dead zone (ecology)
bb19a9e19211.section: Locations > Gulf of Mexico 'dead zone' > Economic impact
bb19a9e19211.sentence: Grimes makes a case that nutrient loading enhances the fisheries in the Gulf of Mexico.

9c260dc4d508.title: Dead zone (ecology)
9c260dc4d508.section: Locations > Gulf of Mexico 'dead zone' > Economic impact
9c260dc4d508.sentence: Courtney et al. hypothesize that nutrient loading may have contributed to the increases in red snapper in the northern and western Gulf of Mexico.

5bd4e170d8da.title: Biological pump
5bd4e170d8da.sentence: The carbonate pump is sometimes referred to as the "hard tissue" component of the biological pump.

1825b02bc564.title: Biological pump
1825b02bc564.sentence: Some surface marine organisms, like coccolithophores, produce hard structures out of calcium carbonate, a form of particulate inorganic carbon, by fixing bicarbonate.

8cbe4844996d.title: Biological pump
8cbe4844996d.sentence: This biologically fixed carbon is used as a protective coating for many planktonic species (coccolithophores, foraminifera) as well as larger marine organisms (mollusk shells).

418465892366.title: Biological pump
418465892366.sentence: Three main processes (or pumps) that make up the marine carbon cycle bring atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) into the ocean interior and distribute it through the oceans.

00341bb9c5ff.title: Biological pump
00341bb9c5ff.sentence: These three pumps are: (1) the solubility pump, (2) the carbonate pump, and (3) the biological pump.

44da3f4dac0b.title: Biological pump
44da3f4dac0b.sentence: Also, changes in the ecological success of calcifying organisms caused by ocean acidification may affect the biological pump by altering the strength of the hard tissues pump.

305ad81e00bf.title: Biological pump
305ad81e00bf.sentence: This may then have a "knock-on" effect on the soft tissues pump because calcium carbonate acts to ballast sinking organic material.

980cb7daae07.title: Biological pump
980cb7daae07.section: Oceanic carbon cycle > Continental shelf pump
980cb7daae07.sentence: The continental shelf pump is proposed as operating in the shallow waters of the continental shelves as a mechanism transporting carbon (dissolved or particulate) from the continental waters to the interior of the adjacent deep ocean.

28a3502d59ff.title: Biological pump
28a3502d59ff.section: Oceanic carbon cycle > Continental shelf pump
28a3502d59ff.sentence: As originally formulated, the pump is thought to occur where the solubility pump interacts with cooler, and therefore denser water from the shelf floor which feeds down the continental slope into the neighbouring deep ocean.

fb03c1bda640.title: Biological pump
fb03c1bda640.section: Oceanic carbon cycle > Continental shelf pump
fb03c1bda640.sentence: The shallowness of the continental shelf restricts the convection of cooling water, so the cooling can be greater for continental shelf waters than for neighbouring open ocean waters.

b4ecb325b56b.title: Biological pump
b4ecb325b56b.section: Processes in the biological pump > Marine snow
b4ecb325b56b.sentence: The deep ocean gets most of its nutrients from the higher water column when they sink down in the form of marine snow.

956425bc8e8a.title: Biological pump
956425bc8e8a.section: Processes in the biological pump > Marine snow
956425bc8e8a.sentence: This is made up of dead or dying animals and microbes, fecal matter, sand and other inorganic material.

c75bdd976f9b.title: Biological pump
c75bdd976f9b.section: Processes in the biological pump > Biomineralization > Ballast minerals
c75bdd976f9b.sentence: Formation and sinking of these aggregates drive the biological carbon pump via export and sedimentation of organic matter from the surface mixed layer to the deep ocean and sediments.

70a45d1a8761.title: Deep sea
70a45d1a8761.sentence: Organisms can survive in the deep sea through a number of feeding methods including scavenging, predation and filtration, with a number of organisms surviving by feeding on marine snow.

371d5cb04d72.title: Deep sea
371d5cb04d72.sentence: Organisms in the deep sea are almost entirely reliant upon sinking living and dead organic matter which falls at approximately 100 meters per day.

426932a7d4da.title: Deep sea
426932a7d4da.sentence: In addition, only about 1 to 3% of the production from the surface reaches the seabed, mostly in the form of marine snow.

8e6c3949a7a3.title: Biological pump
8e6c3949a7a3.section: Processes in the biological pump > Biomineralization > Remineralisation
8e6c3949a7a3.sentence: Remineralisation refers to the breakdown or transformation of organic matter (those molecules derived from a biological source) into its simplest inorganic forms.

5a19cc7003f7.title: Biological pump
5a19cc7003f7.section: Processes in the biological pump > Biomineralization > Remineralisation
5a19cc7003f7.sentence: These transformations form a crucial link within ecosystems as they are responsible for liberating the energy stored in organic molecules and recycling matter within the system to be reused as nutrients by other organisms.

034ebd932f8a.title: Biological pump
034ebd932f8a.section: Processes in the biological pump > Biomineralization > Remineralisation
034ebd932f8a.sentence: What fraction does escape remineralisation varies depending on the location.

8cf3e173c889.title: Biological pump
8cf3e173c889.section: Processes in the biological pump > Vertical migrations
8cf3e173c889.sentence: Diel vertically migrating krill, salps, smaller zooplankton and fish can actively transport carbon to depth by consuming POC in the surface layer at night, and metabolising it at their daytime, mesopelagic residence depths.

c8c7d4fb5578.title: Biological pump
c8c7d4fb5578.section: Processes in the biological pump > Vertical migrations
c8c7d4fb5578.sentence: Without vertical migration the biological pump wouldn't be nearly as efficient.

ddf6b0095a62.title: Biological pump
ddf6b0095a62.section: Processes in the biological pump > Vertical migrations > Lipid pump
ddf6b0095a62.sentence: The lipid pump sequesters carbon from the ocean's surface to deeper waters via lipids associated with overwintering vertically migratory zooplankton.

8f746a171477.title: Biological pump
8f746a171477.section: Processes in the biological pump > Microbial loop > Viral shunt
8f746a171477.sentence: The viral shunt is a mechanism whereby marine viruses prevent microbial particulate organic matter (POM) from migrating up trophic levels by recycling them into dissolved organic matter (DOM), which can be readily taken up by microorganisms.

5b4ec2d2cafe.title: Biological pump
5b4ec2d2cafe.section: Processes in the biological pump > Microbial loop > Viral shunt
5b4ec2d2cafe.sentence: As much as 25% of the primary production from phytoplankton in the global oceans may be recycled within the microbial loop through viral shunting.

5ac46f8f2cff.title: Carbon cycle
5ac46f8f2cff.section: Processes within fast carbon cycle > Viruses as regulators
5ac46f8f2cff.sentence: The average contribution of viruses to the Earth ecosystem carbon cycle is 8.6%, of which its contribution to marine ecosystems (1.4%) is less than its contribution to terrestrial (6.7%) and freshwater (17.8%) ecosystems.

a6b16dea1a1d.title: Phosphorus cycle
a6b16dea1a1d.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Dust Storms
a6b16dea1a1d.sentence: Although phosphorus does not have a major atmospheric component, phosphorus sediments can be moved during dust storms.

6c30182d0a59.title: Phosphorus cycle
6c30182d0a59.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Dust Storms
6c30182d0a59.sentence: Most of Earth's phosphorus is in rocks, and dust contains weathered rock particles from this parent material.

3c15f6aa7c0c.title: Phosphorus cycle
3c15f6aa7c0c.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Dust Storms
3c15f6aa7c0c.sentence: Large dust events can counteract natural imbalances where P occurs and allow for production in areas that would otherwise be P-limited.

56d5ba7573f8.title: Phosphorus cycle
56d5ba7573f8.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Dust Storms
56d5ba7573f8.sentence: Dust also carries other nutrients such as potassium, calcium, and magnesium, making these storms of high importance to biogeochemical cycling.

8150b093636b.title: Phosphorus cycle
8150b093636b.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Dust Storms
8150b093636b.sentence: Phosphorus carried in by wind from Northern Africa to the Amazon basin is thought to play a significant role supporting the rich biodiversity of the Amazon rainforest.

71a5f388d41a.title: Phosphorus cycle
71a5f388d41a.sentence: Humans have greatly influenced the phosphorus cycle by mining phosphate rock.

1fb951111f71.title: Phosphorus cycle
1fb951111f71.sentence: Most of this mining is done to produce fertilizers which can be used on a global scale.

830e3e6ccfed.title: Phosphorus cycle
830e3e6ccfed.sentence: Since the 1840s, when the technology to mine and extract phosphorus became more prevalent, approximately 110 teragrams of phosphorus has been added to the environment.

bb36e2117302.title: Phosphorus cycle
bb36e2117302.sentence: This trend appears to be continuing, as from 1900 to 2022, the amount of phosphorus mined globally has increased 72-fold, with an expected annual increase of 4%.

2a0430b324bf.title: Phosphorus cycle
2a0430b324bf.sentence: However, at the rate humans are mining, the geological system can not quickly restore what is lost.

9ce8bf9a318d.title: Phosphorus cycle
9ce8bf9a318d.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Eutrophication > Saltwater
9ce8bf9a318d.sentence: Due to a dramatic rise in mining for phosphorus, it is estimated that humans have increased the net storage of phosphorus in soil and ocean systems by 75%.

963a2614d318.title: Phosphorus cycle
963a2614d318.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Eutrophication > Saltwater
963a2614d318.sentence: This increase in phosphorus has led to more eutrophication in ocean waters manifested as phytoplankton blooms.

d4812d538e78.title: Phosphorus cycle
d4812d538e78.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Interaction with nitrogen
d4812d538e78.sentence: Human activity has resulted in an imbalance of normal N:P ratios, impacting the speed at which organisms synthesize proteins and DNA.

2e82b666020a.title: Phosphorus cycle
2e82b666020a.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Interaction with nitrogen
2e82b666020a.sentence: Both N and P are widely used in agricultural fertilizers, as they are essential nutrients for plants.

c0e79e5cc686.title: Phosphorus cycle
c0e79e5cc686.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Interaction with nitrogen
c0e79e5cc686.sentence: In the last 40 years, the N:P ratio has increased from 19:1 to 30:1, meaning P is less available to ecosystems.

cb334f11d2eb.title: Phosphorus cycle
cb334f11d2eb.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Interaction with nitrogen
cb334f11d2eb.sentence: This imbalance is not only caused by more N pollution, but also because P is more likely to get trapped after water has been treated, preventing its release into ecosystems.

b0bd50205939.title: Phosphorus cycle
b0bd50205939.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Interaction with nitrogen
b0bd50205939.sentence: As this ratio increases, it is harder for organisms to grow.

92d12e85eb09.title: Phosphorus cycle
92d12e85eb09.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Eutrophication > Wetland
92d12e85eb09.sentence: Wetlands are frequently applied to solve the issue of eutrophication.

4867938a7990.title: Phosphorus cycle
4867938a7990.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Eutrophication > Wetland
4867938a7990.sentence: Therefore, wetlands could help to reduce the concentration of nitrogen and phosphorus to remit eutrophication.

7c3c8307d040.title: Phosphorus cycle
7c3c8307d040.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Eutrophication > Wetland
7c3c8307d040.sentence: Nitrate is transformed in wetlands to free nitrogen and discharged to the air.

c72609a35828.title: Phosphorus cycle
c72609a35828.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Eutrophication > Wetland
c72609a35828.sentence: Phosphorus is adsorbed by wetland soils which are taken up by the plants.

f31ca99b6549.title: Phosphorus cycle
f31ca99b6549.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Eutrophication > Wetland
f31ca99b6549.sentence: However, wetland soils can only hold a limited amount of phosphorus.

7ac48076fdcd.title: Phosphorus cycle
7ac48076fdcd.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Eutrophication > Wetland
7ac48076fdcd.sentence: To remove phosphorus continually, it is necessary to add more new soils within the wetland from remnant plant stems, leaves, root debris, and undecomposable parts of dead algae, bacteria, fungi, and invertebrates.

2cfdc34abbcc.title: Atmospheric methane
2cfdc34abbcc.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane
2cfdc34abbcc.sentence: The amount of methane in the atmosphere is the result of a balance between the production of methane on the Earth's surface—its source—and the destruction or removal of methane, mainly in the atmosphere—its sink— in an atmospheric chemical process.

684011babe95.title: Atmospheric methane
684011babe95.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane
684011babe95.sentence: This atmospheric chemical process is the most effective methane sink, as it removes 90% of atmospheric methane.

26c6680e7947.title: Atmospheric methane
26c6680e7947.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane
26c6680e7947.sentence: Another major natural sink is through oxidation by methanotrophic or methane-consuming bacteria in Earth's soils.

c85676009576.title: Atmospheric methane
c85676009576.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane > Methanotrophs in soils and sediments
c85676009576.sentence: Methane oxidation allows methanotrophic bacteria to use methane as a source of energy, reacting methane with oxygen and as a result producing carbon dioxide and water.

22e8ed4132cc.title: Atmospheric methane
22e8ed4132cc.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane > Methanotrophs in soils and sediments
22e8ed4132cc.sentence: Forest soils act as good sinks for atmospheric methane because soils are optimally moist for methanotroph activity, and the movement of gases between soil and atmosphere (soil diffusivity) is high.

8f6c0006344f.title: Atmospheric methane
8f6c0006344f.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane > Methanotrophs in soils and sediments
8f6c0006344f.sentence: Wetland soils, however, are often sources of atmospheric methane rather than sinks because the water table is much higher, and the methane can be diffused fairly easily into the air without having to compete with the soil's methanotrophs.

f3066eeef746.title: Atmospheric methane
f3066eeef746.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane > Mean lifespan
f3066eeef746.sentence: The average time that a physical methane molecule is in the atmosphere is estimated to be around 9.6 years.

ea733d252ad1.title: Atmospheric methane
ea733d252ad1.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane > Mean lifespan
ea733d252ad1.sentence: However, the average time that the atmosphere will be affected by the emission of that molecule before reaching equilibrium – known as its 'perturbation lifetime' – is approximately twelve years.

37f8dfe1a217.title: Atmospheric methane
37f8dfe1a217.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane > Removal technologies
37f8dfe1a217.sentence: Atmospheric methane removal is a category of potential approaches being researched to accelerate the breakdown of methane that is in the atmosphere, for mitigating some of the impacts of climate change.

e30da09d5d57.title: Atmospheric methane
e30da09d5d57.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane > Removal technologies
e30da09d5d57.sentence: Since methane is a more powerful greenhouse gas, removing smaller amounts of atmospheric methane compared to carbon dioxide from the atmosphere would result in a similar climate impact.

a7f0fbef9cb5.title: Atmospheric methane
a7f0fbef9cb5.section: Natural sinks or removal of atmospheric methane > Removal technologies
a7f0fbef9cb5.sentence: With background levels of atmospheric carbon dioxide being approximately 420 ppm and background levels of atmospheric methane being approximately 1.92 ppm, lower concentrations of methane result in an increase in difficulty in methane capture compared to carbon dioxide.

d3f9e1ed9f8c.title: Reactive nitrogen
d3f9e1ed9f8c.sentence: Reactive nitrogen ("Nr"), also known as fixed nitrogen, refers to all forms of nitrogen present in the environment except for molecular nitrogen (N 2).

98c7b6108794.title: Reactive nitrogen
98c7b6108794.sentence: Common Nr species include nitrogen oxides (NO x), ammonia (NH 3), nitrous oxide (N 2O), as well as the anion nitrate (NO− 3).

b4017858bda9.title: Reactive nitrogen
b4017858bda9.sentence: However, just over half of all reactive nitrogen entering the biosphere is attributable to anthropogenic activity such as industrial fertilizer production.

5cd6b2add4f3.title: Nitrogen cycle
5cd6b2add4f3.section: Human influences on the nitrogen cycle
5cd6b2add4f3.sentence: Generation of Nr, reactive nitrogen, has increased over 10 fold in the past century due to global industrialisation.

9ff82e2e79af.title: Nitrogen cycle
9ff82e2e79af.section: Human influences on the nitrogen cycle
9ff82e2e79af.sentence: This form of nitrogen follows a cascade through the biosphere via a variety of mechanisms, and is accumulating as the rate of its generation is greater than the rate of denitrification.

c922e2431ca7.title: Reactive nitrogen
c922e2431ca7.sentence: While reactive nitrogen is eventually converted back into molecular nitrogen via denitrification, an excess of reactive nitrogen can lead to problems such as eutrophication in marine ecosystems.

8745b8de4612.title: Haber process
8745b8de4612.sentence: In combination with advances in breeding, herbicides, and pesticides, these fertilizers have helped to increase the productivity of agricultural land:

d70ba1a2647d.title: Haber process
d70ba1a2647d.sentence: The energy-intensity of the process contributes to climate change and other environmental problems such as the leaching of nitrates into groundwater, rivers, ponds, and lakes; expanding dead zones in coastal ocean waters, resulting from recurrent eutrophication; atmospheric deposition of nitrates and ammonia affecting natural ecosystems; higher emissions of nitrous oxide (N2O), now the third most important greenhouse gas following CO2 and CH4.

0ec0b4ee9f6c.title: Haber process
0ec0b4ee9f6c.sentence: > With average crop yields remaining at the 1900 level the crop harvest in the year 2000 would have required nearly four times more land and the cultivated area would have claimed nearly half of all ice-free continents, rather than under 15% of the total land area that is required today.

fe36834ca9df.title: Haber process
fe36834ca9df.sentence: — Vaclav Smil, Nitrogen cycle and world food production, Volume 2, pages 9–13

1c6d4f376ce1.title: Haber process
1c6d4f376ce1.sentence: Thus, the Haber process serves as the "detonator of the population explosion", enabling the global population to increase from 1.6 billion in 1900 to 7.7 billion by November 2018.

337db5e6f716.title: Haber process
337db5e6f716.sentence: Nearly 50% of the nitrogen found in human tissues originated from the Haber–Bosch process.

b3ed5f00cdd6.title: Carrying capacity
b3ed5f00cdd6.sentence: Without the Haber-Bosch process for fixing nitrogen, modern agriculture could not support 8 billion people.

f4c4d98aed13.title: Haber process
f4c4d98aed13.sentence: The Haber–Bosch process is one of the largest contributors to a buildup of reactive nitrogen in the biosphere, causing an anthropogenic disruption to the nitrogen cycle.

595f13c862ed.title: Haber process
595f13c862ed.sentence: Since nitrogen use efficiency is typically less than 50%, farm runoff from heavy use of fixed industrial nitrogen disrupts biological habitats.

5744accf8c12.title: Climate-smart agriculture
5744accf8c12.sentence: For example, the manufacture and use of nitrogen fertilizer contributes around 5% of all global greenhouse gas emissions.

6e9dddde5b61.title: Haber process
6e9dddde5b61.sentence: The use of synthetic nitrogen fertilisers reduces the incentive for farmers to use more sustainable crop rotations which include legumes for their natural nitrogen-fixing ability.

4ae6917f0b25.title: Carbon tariff
4ae6917f0b25.sentence: Examples of imports which are high-carbon and so may be subject to a carbon tariff are electricity generated by coal-fired power stations, iron and steel from blast furnaces, and fertilizer from the Haber process.

3400437fea63.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
3400437fea63.sentence: Agricultural and industrial nitrogen (N) inputs to the environment currently exceed inputs from natural N fixation.

c504a52d1fd0.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
c504a52d1fd0.sentence: This is largely attributed to the widespread use of synthetic fertilizers produced via the Haber-Bosch process, and the expansion of fossil fuel combustion following the Industrial Revolution.

b044c95d6f88.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
b044c95d6f88.sentence: As a consequence of anthropogenic inputs, the global nitrogen cycle has been significantly altered over the past century, leading to increased nitrogen deposition and disruption of natural biogeochemical processes.

f0253a83f71a.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
f0253a83f71a.sentence: Global atmospheric nitrous oxide (N2O) mole fractions have increased from a pre-industrial value of ~270 nmol/mol to ~319 nmol/mol in 2005, a concerning trend given that N2O is both a greenhouse gas and an ozone-depleting substance (ODS).

225955d7480b.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
225955d7480b.sentence: Human activities account for over one-third of N2O emissions (35% of total global N2O emissions), with about 20% originating from agricultural sources such as fertilizer use, manure management, and aquaculture.

8bd184c8e893.title: Nitrogen cycle
8bd184c8e893.section: Human influences on the nitrogen cycle
8bd184c8e893.sentence: Nitrous oxide is also a greenhouse gas and is currently the third largest contributor to global warming, after carbon dioxide and methane.

91c13e901998.title: Nitrogen cycle
91c13e901998.section: Human influences on the nitrogen cycle
91c13e901998.sentence: While not as abundant in the atmosphere as carbon dioxide, it is, for an equivalent mass, nearly 300 times more potent in its ability to warm the planet.

beb907c729f8.title: Nitrogen cycle
beb907c729f8.section: Human influences on the nitrogen cycle
beb907c729f8.sentence: The very high temperature of lightning naturally produces small amounts of NO x, NH 3, and HNO 3, but high-temperature combustion has contributed to a 6- or 7-fold increase in the flux of NO x to the atmosphere.

954f327f3069.title: Nitrogen cycle
954f327f3069.section: Human influences on the nitrogen cycle
954f327f3069.sentence: They are precursors of tropospheric (lower atmosphere) ozone production, which contributes to smog and acid rain, damages plants and increases nitrogen inputs to ecosystems.

fd8da80b1486.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
fd8da80b1486.sentence: As of 2020, the top five countries in anthropogenic N2O emissions were China (16.7%), India (10.9%), United States (5.7%), Brazil (5.3%), and Russia (4.6%).

d3fd997d33c8.title: Nitrogen cycle
d3fd997d33c8.section: Consequence of human modification of the nitrogen cycle > Impacts on human health: nitrate accumulation in drinking water
d3fd997d33c8.sentence: Leakage of Nr (reactive nitrogen) from human activities can cause nitrate accumulation in the natural water environment, which can create harmful impacts on human health.

f22e9ebc57b1.title: Nitrogen cycle
f22e9ebc57b1.section: Consequence of human modification of the nitrogen cycle > Impacts on human health: nitrate accumulation in drinking water
f22e9ebc57b1.sentence: Excessive use of N-fertilizer in agriculture has been a significant source of nitrate pollution in groundwater and surface water.

bfa06b4b2d7c.title: Nitrogen cycle
bfa06b4b2d7c.section: Consequence of human modification of the nitrogen cycle > Impacts on human health: nitrate accumulation in drinking water
bfa06b4b2d7c.sentence: Due to its high solubility and low retention by soil, nitrate can easily escape from the subsoil layer to the groundwater, causing nitrate pollution.

70791c5ff823.title: Nitrogen cycle
70791c5ff823.section: Consequence of human modification of the nitrogen cycle > Impacts on human health: nitrate accumulation in drinking water
70791c5ff823.sentence: Some other non-point sources for nitrate pollution in groundwater originate from livestock feeding, animal and human contamination, and municipal and industrial waste.

83b3c8471bef.title: Eutrophication
83b3c8471bef.sentence: Human health effects of eutrophication derive from two main issues excess nitrate in drinking water and exposure to toxic algae.

6d9579ba7438.title: Eutrophication
6d9579ba7438.sentence: Nitrates in drinking water can cause Blue baby syndrome in infants and can react with chemicals used to treat water to create disinfection by-products in drinking water.

d1831dd7af88.title: Eutrophication
d1831dd7af88.sentence: Getting direct contact with toxic algae through swimming or drinking can cause rashes, stomach or liver illness, and respiratory or neurological problems.

31874028007f.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
31874028007f.sentence: Iron fertilization is a facet of geoengineering, which purposefully manipulates the Earth's climate system, typically in aspects of the carbon cycle or radiative forcing.

8342f90f0b53.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
8342f90f0b53.sentence: Of current geoengineering interest is the possibility of accelerating the biological pump to increase export of carbon from the surface ocean.

f5ae1d5f3475.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
f5ae1d5f3475.sentence: This increased export could theoretically remove excess carbon dioxide from the atmosphere for storage in the deep ocean.

0d0dfcb76d92.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
0d0dfcb76d92.sentence: Due to the scale of the ocean and the fast response times of heterotrophic communities to increases in primary production, it is difficult to determine whether limiting-nutrient fertilization results in an increase in carbon export.

196a310b62e9.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
196a310b62e9.sentence: However, the majority of the community does not believe this is a reasonable or viable approach.

3da808c13365.title: Iron fertilization
3da808c13365.sentence: Approximately 25 percent of the ocean surface contains ample macronutrients but little plant biomass (as defined by the presence of chlorophyll).

ae77e5caffba.title: Iron fertilization
ae77e5caffba.sentence: The production in these high-nutrient low-chlorophyll (HNLC) waters is primarily limited by micronutrients, especially iron.

68191d31e0d7.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
68191d31e0d7.sentence: Carbon compounds can be distinguished as either organic or inorganic, and dissolved or particulate, depending on their composition.

cd1362c4d441.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
cd1362c4d441.sentence: Marine carbon is further separated into particulate and dissolved phases.

262a60b3b7ae.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
262a60b3b7ae.sentence: Dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) is made up of bicarbonate (HCO3−), carbonate (CO32−) and carbon dioxide (including both dissolved CO2 and carbonic acid H2CO3).

d2012ee14b91.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
d2012ee14b91.sentence: Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is defined operationally as any organic molecule that can pass through a 0.2 μm filter.

de3e224167ee.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
de3e224167ee.sentence: Those organic carbon molecules being captured on a filter are defined as particulate organic carbon (POC).

a733742d3bb6.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
a733742d3bb6.sentence: DIC can also be converted to particulate organic carbon (POC) through photosynthesis and chemoautotrophy (i.e. primary production).

a35b240b6b95.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
a35b240b6b95.sentence: DIC can be converted to particulate inorganic carbon (PIC) through precipitation of CaCO3 (biologically or abiotically).

992364d5d99c.title: Solubility pump
992364d5d99c.sentence: However, unlike many other gases (oxygen for instance), it reacts with water and forms a balance of several ionic and non-ionic species (collectively known as dissolved inorganic carbon, or DIC).

cd2c7b011cf3.title: Solubility pump
cd2c7b011cf3.sentence: These are dissolved free carbon dioxide (CO2(aq)), carbonic acid (H2CO3), bicarbonate (HCO−3) and carbonate (CO2−3), and they interact with water as follows:

c602705f56f8.title: Solubility pump

84754b4a4f5b.title: Solubility pump
84754b4a4f5b.sentence: In carbonate chemistry terms, this imbalance is referred to as alkalinity.

bd1ab8b605aa.title: Solubility pump

40c881fd7833.title: Solubility pump
40c881fd7833.sentence: In terms of measurement, four basic parameters are of key importance: Total inorganic carbon (TIC, TCO2 or CT), Total alkalinity (TALK or AT), pH, and pCO2.

7f92c27615f8.title: Solubility pump
7f92c27615f8.sentence: Measuring any two of these parameters allows for the determination of a wide range of pH-dependent species (including the above-mentioned species).

f4e610d22b78.title: Ocean acidification
f4e610d22b78.section: Main effects > Decrease in saturation state
f4e610d22b78.sentence: The saturation state (known as Ω) of seawater for a mineral is a measure of the thermodynamic potential for the mineral to form or to dissolve, and for calcium carbonate is described by the following equation:

ee739cc933d0.title: Ocean acidification
ee739cc933d0.section: Main effects > Decrease in saturation state
ee739cc933d0.sentence: Here Ω is the product of the concentrations (or activities) of the reacting ions that form the mineral (Ca+2 and CO2−3), divided by the apparent solubility product at equilibrium (Ksp), that is, when the rates of precipitation and dissolution are equal.

e19000090aa3.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
e19000090aa3.sentence: The rise in dissolved carbon dioxide reduces the availability of the carbonate ion, reducing CaCO3 saturation state, thus making it thermodynamically harder to make CaCO3 shell.

964420bfa453.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
964420bfa453.sentence: CaCO3 is supersatured in the great majority of ocean surface waters and undersaturated at depth, meaning the shells are more likely to dissolve as they sink to ocean depths.

b40673d49b60.title: Ocean acidification
b40673d49b60.section: Main effects > Decrease in saturation state
b40673d49b60.sentence: In seawater, dissolution boundary is formed as a result of temperature, pressure, and depth, and is known as the saturation horizon.

6c26378e14f7.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
6c26378e14f7.sentence: The Revelle Factor is a ratio of the change of carbon dioxide to the change in dissolved inorganic carbon, which serves as an indicator of carbon dioxide dissolution in the mixed layer considering the solubility pump.

d0b4dfa110c7.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
d0b4dfa110c7.sentence: The lower the Revelle factor, the higher the capacity for ocean water to take in carbon dioxide.

a9a23f7fadbc.title: Oceanic carbon cycle
a9a23f7fadbc.sentence: Because the Revelle factor increases with increasing CO2, a smaller fraction of the anthropogenic flux will be taken up by the ocean in the future.

f2394a683bb5.title: Sulfur cycle
f2394a683bb5.sentence: The burning of coal, natural gas, and other fossil fuels has greatly increased the amount of sulfur in the atmosphere and ocean and depleted the sedimentary rock sink.

ae776ce7e870.title: Sulfur cycle
ae776ce7e870.sentence: Without human impact sulfur would stay tied up in rocks for millions of years until it was uplifted through tectonic events and then released through erosion and weathering processes.

f30f04b4abf8.title: Sulfur cycle
f30f04b4abf8.sentence: Humans are mining coal and extracting petroleum from the Earth's crust at a rate that mobilizes 150 × 10^12 gS/yr, which is more than double the rate of 100 years ago.

6e970f55e565.title: Sulfur cycle
6e970f55e565.sentence: Therefore, human activities do not cause a major change in the global pools of sulfur, but they do produce massive changes in the annual flux of sulfur through the atmosphere.

2f2ca71021bb.title: Sulfur cycle
2f2ca71021bb.sentence: When SO2 is emitted as an air pollutant, it forms sulfuric acid through reactions with water in the atmosphere.

2866568c591b.title: Sulfur cycle
2866568c591b.sentence: Over the most polluted areas there has been a 30-fold increase in sulfate deposition.

06b585ce2d75.title: Sulfur cycle
06b585ce2d75.sentence: Recently sulfur deficiency has become widespread in many countries in Europe.

7376a5544c20.title: Sulfur cycle
7376a5544c20.sentence: Because of actions taken to limit acid rains atmospheric inputs of sulfur continue to decrease, As a result, the deficit in the sulfur input is likely to increase unless sulfur fertilizers are used.

2ee3393db01c.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
2ee3393db01c.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
2ee3393db01c.sentence: Subsea permafrost occurs beneath the seabed and exists in the continental shelves of the polar regions.

c71e1c36ba5c.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
c71e1c36ba5c.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
c71e1c36ba5c.sentence: Thus, it can be defined as "the unglaciated continental shelf areas exposed during the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM, ~26 500 BP) that are currently inundated".

66d5b09d2f3d.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
66d5b09d2f3d.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
66d5b09d2f3d.sentence: The size of today's subsea permafrost has been estimated at 2 million km2 (~1/5 of the terrestrial permafrost domain size), which constitutes a 30–50% reduction since the LGM.

284b845f78f8.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
284b845f78f8.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
284b845f78f8.sentence: Containing around 560 GtC in OM and 45 GtC in CH4, with a current release of 18 and 38 MtC per year respectively, which is due to the warming and thawing that the subsea permafrost domain has been experiencing since after the LGM (~14000 years ago).

422f07a95f6e.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
422f07a95f6e.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
422f07a95f6e.sentence: In fact, because the subsea permafrost systems responds at millennial timescales to climate warming, the current carbon fluxes it is emitting to the water are in response to climatic changes occurring after the LGM.

1c9eac55cbe8.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
1c9eac55cbe8.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
1c9eac55cbe8.sentence: Therefore, human-driven climate change effects on subsea permafrost will only be seen hundreds or thousands of years from today.

cfa0975e3d9b.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
cfa0975e3d9b.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
cfa0975e3d9b.sentence: According to predictions under a business-as-usual emissions scenario RCP 8.5, by 2100, 43 GtC could be released from the subsea permafrost domain, and 190 GtC by the year 2300.

02787608ed7e.title: Net ecosystem production
02787608ed7e.sentence: Net community production (NCP) is the difference between net primary production and respiration by animals and heterotrophs only.

c78a75216424.title: Net ecosystem production
c78a75216424.sentence: - NCP = NPP - respiration [by animals and other heterotrophs]

5c9f8e9cc169.title: Net ecosystem production
5c9f8e9cc169.sentence: Net ecosystem production is equal to net community production, and is only calculated differently.

b89486596770.title: Net ecosystem production
b89486596770.sentence: For example, annual net community production in the tropical South Pacific Ocean can be very close to zero, meaning that basically all carbon produced is respired by heterotrophs.

b4468ef92800.title: Net ecosystem production
b4468ef92800.sentence: In the rest of the Pacific Ocean, annual net community production can range from 2.0 to 2.4 mol C m−2 yr−1, meaning that carbon produced by phytoplankton (minus what the phytoplankton respire themselves) is greater during a given year than what gets respired by heterotrophs

4ea236334904.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
4ea236334904.sentence: This sequential transfer between ecosystems is termed the nitrogen cascade.

f12941c65270.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
f12941c65270.sentence: Most Nr applied to global agroecosystems cascades through the atmosphere and aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems until it is converted to N2, primarily through denitrification.

b17dcc5e8f3d.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
b17dcc5e8f3d.sentence: The above system responses to reactive nitrogen (Nr) inputs are almost all exclusively studied separately; however, research increasingly indicates that nitrogen loading problems are linked by multiple pathways transporting nutrients across system boundaries.

fdc42e024019.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
fdc42e024019.sentence: During the cascade, some systems accumulate Nr, which results in a time lag in the cascade and enhanced effects of Nr on the environment in which it accumulates.

21a5415f3332.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
21a5415f3332.sentence: Ultimately, anthropogenic inputs of Nr are either accumulated or denitrified; however, little progress has been made in determining the relative importance of Nr accumulation and denitrification, which has been mainly due to a lack of integration among scientific disciplines.

5f8add80b656.title: Beaver dam
5f8add80b656.sentence: Some scientists [weasel words] believe that the nitrogen cascade – the production of more fixed nitrogen than the natural cycles can turn back into nitrogen gas – may be as much of a problem to Earth's ecology as carbon dioxide production.

44a93b7a87ad.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
44a93b7a87ad.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere
44a93b7a87ad.sentence: Terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems receive Nr inputs from the atmosphere through wet and dry deposition.

88410623e385.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
88410623e385.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere
88410623e385.sentence: Atmospheric Nr species can be deposited to ecosystems in precipitation (e.g., NO3−, NH4+, organic N compounds), as gases (e.g., NH3 and gaseous nitric acid [HNO3]), or as aerosols (e.g., ammonium nitrate [NH4NO3]).

ac0bdb827e6a.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
ac0bdb827e6a.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle
ac0bdb827e6a.sentence: During this period, atmospheric emissions of Nr species reportedly increased 250% and deposition to marine and terrestrial ecosystems increased over 200%.

77ec4afacd31.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

77ec4afacd31.sentence: Increased N deposition can acidify soils, streams, and lakes and alter forest and grassland productivity.

7afeb7c3ca0b.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
7afeb7c3ca0b.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere
7afeb7c3ca0b.sentence: In grassland ecosystems, N inputs have produced initial increases in productivity followed by declines as critical thresholds are exceeded.

6987f40be540.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

6987f40be540.sentence: Several nutrient addition studies have shown that increased N inputs lead to dominance of fast-growing plant species, with associated declines in species richness.

c94aeb0ef541.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
c94aeb0ef541.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on plant species diversity
c94aeb0ef541.sentence: Heathlands are characterized by N-poor soils, which exclude N-demanding grasses; however, with increasing N deposition and soil acidification, invading grasslands replace lowland heath.

90ffeab1e54e.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
90ffeab1e54e.sentence: While much research has been done on how plants, free-living microbial decomposers, and soil minerals affect this pool of carbon, it is recently coming to light that mycorrhizal fungi—symbiotic fungi that associate with roots of almost all living plants—may play an important role in maintaining this pool as well.

03b61726ff47.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
03b61726ff47.sentence: Soil contains more carbon than plants and the atmosphere combined.

8e0b23c32454.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
8e0b23c32454.sentence: Measurements of plant carbon allocation to mycorrhizal fungi have been estimated to be 5 to 20% of total plant carbon uptake, and in some ecosystems the biomass of mycorrhizal fungi can be comparable to the biomass of fine roots.

fad0fc88fc0b.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
fad0fc88fc0b.sentence: Recent research has shown that mycorrhizal fungi hold 50 to 70 percent of the total carbon stored in leaf litter and soil on forested islands in Sweden.

66938d607259.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
66938d607259.sentence: The mechanism presented is that ectomycorrhizal fungi can compete with free-living decomposers for nutrients, and thereby limit the rate of total decomposition.

f234f580febe.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
f234f580febe.sentence: Since then there have been several other reports of ectomycorrhizal fungi reducing activity and decomposition rates of free-living decomposers and thereby increasing soil carbon storage.

16c56f592e57.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
16c56f592e57.sentence: Since arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi are thought to lack the ability to produce the enzymes to catalyze this decomposition it is generally thought that they stimulate free-living decomposer communities to increase activity by exuding labile energy substrates, a process termed priming.

e3309618f897.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
e3309618f897.sentence: Recent lab experiments have shown that the presence of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi increases losses of soil carbon compared to soils where arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi are excluded, and that the difference is greater under elevated CO2 when the abundance of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi is greater.

b7336a7648c0.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
b7336a7648c0.sentence: The evidence for ectomycorrhizal priming is so far inconclusive.

5c4d5edb7721.title: Climate change

9e24402f69aa.title: Climate change

ceb017987b14.title: Climate change

c82d2bad2746.title: Climate change

ae4e7eb22fde.title: Greenhouse effect
ae4e7eb22fde.sentence: The greenhouse effect occurs when heat-trapping gases in a planet's atmosphere prevent the planet from losing heat to space, raising its surface temperature.

e4ac0360192f.title: Greenhouse effect
e4ac0360192f.sentence: In the case of Earth, the Sun emits shortwave radiation (sunlight) that passes through greenhouse gases to heat the Earth's surface.

683b049fb7e2.title: Greenhouse effect
683b049fb7e2.sentence: In response, the Earth's surface emits longwave radiation that is mostly absorbed by greenhouse gases, reducing the rate at which the Earth can cool off.

090c2488c828.title: Greenhouse effect
090c2488c828.sentence: Without this absorption, Earth's surface would have an average temperature of −18 °C (−0.4 °F).

a3634d5560ac.title: Greenhouse gas
a3634d5560ac.sentence: Without greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, the average temperature of Earth's surface would be about −18 °C (0 °F), rather than the present average of 15 °C (59 °F).

408559c21e2d.title: Greenhouse effect
408559c21e2d.sentence: Strengthening of the greenhouse effect through additional greenhouse gases from human activities is known as the enhanced greenhouse effect.

a90586d76086.title: Greenhouse effect
a90586d76086.sentence: The enhanced greenhouse effect describes the fact that by increasing the concentration of GHGs in the atmosphere (due to human action), the natural greenhouse effect is increased.

a0490c8966dc.title: Greenhouse effect
a0490c8966dc.sentence: As well as being inferred from measurements by ARGO, CERES and other instruments throughout the 21st century, this increase in radiative forcing from human activity has been observed directly, and is attributable mainly to increased atmospheric carbon dioxide levels.

f781c126a7fd.title: Greenhouse effect
f781c126a7fd.sentence: The existence of the greenhouse effect, while not named as such, was proposed as early as 1824 by Joseph Fourier.

0709a41b4ba2.title: Greenhouse effect
0709a41b4ba2.sentence: In 1856 Eunice Newton Foote demonstrated that the warming effect of the sun is greater for air with water vapour than for dry air, and the effect is even greater with carbon dioxide.

e30eaf135f0f.title: Greenhouse effect
e30eaf135f0f.sentence: The term greenhouse effect comes from an analogy to greenhouses.

117724c60043.title: Greenhouse effect
117724c60043.sentence: Greenhouses retain heat mainly by blocking convection (the movement of air).

15c08b2190da.title: Greenhouse gas

9d624d713e44.title: Greenhouse gas
9d624d713e44.sentence: Unlike other gases, greenhouse gases absorb the radiations that a planet emits, resulting in the greenhouse effect.

9ec9b08cca3c.title: Greenhouse gas
9ec9b08cca3c.sentence: 99% of the Earth's dry atmosphere (excluding water vapor) is made up of nitrogen (N 2) (78%) and oxygen (O 2) (21%).

988db4cd4c09.title: Greenhouse gas

6ec549ce0680.title: Greenhouse gas

4bbe28fc593f.sentence: Water vapor is the most important greenhouse gas overall, being responsible for 41–67% of the greenhouse effect, but its global concentrations are not directly affected by human activity.

ebfd926454b3.title: Greenhouse gas

9c265695f288.title: Effects of climate change
9c265695f288.sentence: Effects of climate change are well documented and growing for Earth's natural environment and human societies.

44560b78906e.title: Effects of climate change
44560b78906e.sentence: Changes to the climate system include an overall warming trend, changes to precipitation patterns, and more extreme weather.

de47be380225.title: Effects of climate change
de47be380225.sentence: As the climate changes it impacts the natural environment with effects such as more intense forest fires, thawing permafrost, and desertification.

6c8110105167.title: Effects of climate change

4210aa6dc030.title: Effects of climate change
4210aa6dc030.sentence: Ice sheets and oceans absorb the vast majority of excess heat in the atmosphere, delaying effects there but causing them to accelerate and then continue after surface temperatures stabilize.

c5c3c5785544.title: Effects of climate change

08f0e68c9404.title: Effects of climate change

0898eb9255ad.title: Effects of climate change

06e9c1076a88.title: Effects of climate change

9a3484dfb1e6.title: Effects of climate change

497b39362a93.title: Effects of climate change

75d391532c9b.title: Effects of climate change

d669843c2c40.title: Effects of climate change

8d829e6487d5.title: Effects of climate change

86781ab8b61c.title: Effects of climate change

35c172cb20a5.title: Effects of climate change

1f14b13a2314.title: Effects of climate change

7474fb6720b4.title: Effects of climate change

2b50966d9168.title: Extreme weather
2b50966d9168.sentence: The main types of extreme weather include heat waves, cold waves, droughts, and heavy precipitation or storm events, such as tropical cyclones.

238a24c48aa4.title: Extreme weather

0cfdc4ce2c31.title: Extreme weather
0cfdc4ce2c31.sentence: Definitions of 'rare' vary, but an extreme weather event would normally be as rare as or rarer than the 10th or 90th percentile of a probability density function estimated from observations."Aside from being rare, extreme weather can also be determined by the severity, rate or effects of a specific weather episode.

e3d1e4486e6c.title: Extreme weather
e3d1e4486e6c.sentence: Severe weather is a particular type of extreme weather which poses risks to life and property.

f7300ecb0f54.title: Extreme weather

5a6a86b75ac4.title: Extreme weather

a02d31d2a30e.title: Extreme weather
a02d31d2a30e.sentence: However, certain system wide changes to global weather systems can lead to increased frequency or intensity of extreme weather events.

a9a56c537963.title: Extreme weather

a9a56c537963.sentence: Storms such as hurricanes or tropical cyclones may experience greater rainfall, causing major flooding events or landslides by saturating soil.

b5b2703b082a.title: Extreme weather

b5b2703b082a.sentence: This is because warmer air is able to 'hold' more moisture due to the water molecules having increased kinetic energy, and precipitation occurs at a greater rate because more molecules have the critical speed needed to fall as rain drops.

4b418365b7dc.title: Radiative forcing
4b418365b7dc.sentence: Radiative forcing (or climate forcing) is a concept used to quantify a change to the balance of energy flowing through a planetary atmosphere.

f5bfe7ec56eb.title: Radiative forcing
f5bfe7ec56eb.sentence: Various factors contribute to this change in energy balance, such as concentrations of greenhouse gases and aerosols, and changes in surface albedo and solar irradiance.

75c79ff427cd.title: Radiative forcing
75c79ff427cd.sentence: It is quantified in units of watts per square meter, and often summarized as an average over the total surface area of the globe.

c0892072bdf3.title: Radiative forcing
c0892072bdf3.sentence: A planet in radiative equilibrium with its parent star and the rest of space can be characterized by net zero radiative forcing and by a planetary equilibrium temperature.

39a18958158e.title: Radiative forcing

d81f88985830.title: Global warming potential
d81f88985830.sentence: Global warming potential (GWP) is a measure of how much heat a greenhouse gas (GHG) traps in the atmosphere over a specific time period, relative to carbon dioxide (CO2).

000f1fad21a4.title: Global warming potential
000f1fad21a4.sentence: Therefore, by definition CO2 has a GWP of 1.

4a113f71da98.title: Global warming potential

00f6273c76a9.title: Global warming potential
00f6273c76a9.sentence: For example, methane (CH4) has a GWP over 20 years (GWP-20) of 81.2 meaning that, a leak of a tonne of methane is equivalent to emitting 81.2 tonnes of CO2, both measured over 20 years.

1f62e5aa25ac.title: Global warming potential

5ebb694ced23.title: Global warming potential

41adbcc78d3a.title: Global warming potential

An estimated value of λ~≈0.8 gives an increase in global temperature of about 1.6 K above the 1750 reference temperature due to the increase in CO2 over that time (278 to 405 ppm, for a forcing of 2.0 W/m2), and predicts a further warming of 1.4 K above present temperatures if the CO2 mixing ratio in the atmosphere were to become double its pre-industrial value.
