d80196e4a9f4.title: Human impact on the environment
d80196e4a9f4.sentence: Human impact on the environment (or anthropogenic environmental impact) refers to changes to biophysical environments and to ecosystems, biodiversity, and natural resources caused directly or indirectly by humans.

54835550a39e.title: Human impact on the environment
54835550a39e.sentence: Modifying the environment to fit the needs of society (as in the built environment) is causing severe effects including global warming, environmental degradation (such as ocean acidification), mass extinction, and biodiversity loss, ecological crisis, and ecological collapse.

ba37d3d40f02.title: Human impact on the environment
ba37d3d40f02.sentence: Some human activities that cause damage (either directly or indirectly) to the environment on a global scale include population growth, neoliberal economic policies, and rapid economic growth.

8439a36c91fe.title: Human impact on the environment
8439a36c91fe.sentence: Overconsumption, overexploitation, pollution, and deforestation are also contributing to this problem.

1f7730e0d7e8.title: Human impact on the environment
1f7730e0d7e8.sentence: Human-caused impacts on the global environment have increased significantly since the start of the Industrial Revolution in the 1700s, but humans have been impacting their surroundings since they began populating the Earth.

e106ab8ddb22.title: Human impact on the environment
e106ab8ddb22.sentence: According to a 2018 study in Nature, 87% of the oceans and 77% of land (excluding Antarctica) have been altered by anthropogenic activity, and 23% of the planet's landmass remains as wilderness.

84b9c9a63a85.title: Human impact on the environment
84b9c9a63a85.sentence: Estimates by the Global Footprint Network indicate that humanity's current demand is 70% higher than the regeneration rate of all of the planet's ecosystems combined.

ba653eb87140.title: Human impact on the environment
ba653eb87140.sentence: The world's chickens weigh three times as much as all wild birds combined, while domesticated cattle and pigs outweigh all wild mammals by 14 to 1.

1fba62db0577.title: Human impact on the environment
1fba62db0577.section: Human activities > Fishing and farming > Fishing
1fba62db0577.sentence: According to the 2019 Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services report, overfishing is the main driver of mass species extinction in the oceans.

50cf19f9d6bc.title: Habitat destruction
50cf19f9d6bc.sentence: Habitat destruction (also termed habitat loss) occurs when a natural habitat is no longer able to support its native species.

237d160f01ad.title: Habitat destruction
237d160f01ad.sentence: The organisms once living there have either moved elsewhere, or are dead, leading to a decrease in biodiversity and species numbers.

7a261e9b44fb.title: Habitat destruction
7a261e9b44fb.sentence: Habitat destruction is in fact the leading cause of biodiversity loss and species extinction worldwide.

7cf904bacdf5.title: Habitat destruction
7cf904bacdf5.sentence: Humans contribute to habitat destruction through the use of natural resources, agriculture, industrial production and urbanization (urban sprawl).

014ebddd7241.title: Habitat destruction
014ebddd7241.sentence: Other activities include mining, logging, and trawling.

b63bb05ab035.title: Habitat destruction
b63bb05ab035.sentence: Habitat degradation, fragmentation, and pollution are aspects of habitat destruction caused by humans that do not necessarily involve over destruction of habitat, yet result in habitat collapse.

1e5ffc8a0f7a.title: Habitat destruction
1e5ffc8a0f7a.sentence: From the approximately 16 million square kilometers of tropical rainforest habitat that originally existed worldwide, less than 9 million square kilometers remain today.

f568c062d566.title: Habitat destruction
f568c062d566.sentence: When a habitat is destroyed, the carrying capacity for indigenous plants, animals, and other organisms is reduced so that populations decline, sometimes up to the level of extinction.

e0f9623372ab.title: Habitat destruction
e0f9623372ab.sentence: Endemic organisms with limited ranges are most affected by habitat destruction, mainly because these organisms are not found anywhere else in the world, and thus have less chance of recovering.

df1572cc8662.title: Habitat destruction
df1572cc8662.sentence: Probably the most profound impact that habitat destruction has on people is the loss of many valuable ecosystem services.

59ccc9b44841.title: Habitat destruction
59ccc9b44841.sentence: Other ecosystem services that are diminished or lost altogether as a result of habitat destruction include watershed management, nitrogen fixation, oxygen production, pollination (see pollinator decline), waste treatment (i.e., the breaking down and immobilization of toxic pollutants), and nutrient recycling of sewage or agricultural runoff.

0d45a0317df9.title: Habitat destruction
0d45a0317df9.sentence: Across the globe, poor people suffer the most when natural habitat is destroyed, because less natural habitat means fewer natural resources per capita, yet wealthier people and countries can simply pay more to continue to receive more than their per capita share of natural resources.

46f96e0c551b.title: Deforestation
46f96e0c551b.sentence: Deforestation or forest clearance is the removal and destruction of a forest or stand of trees from land that is then converted to non-forest use.

1588631b95cb.title: Deforestation
1588631b95cb.sentence: Deforestation can involve conversion of forest land to farms, ranches, or urban use.

4ff4890b2b10.title: Deforestation
4ff4890b2b10.sentence: About 31% of Earth's land surface is covered by forests at present.

6a7bae0ac4b4.title: Deforestation
6a7bae0ac4b4.sentence: This is one-third less than the forest cover before the expansion of agriculture, with half of that loss occurring in the last century.

5f8f9402a59a.title: Deforestation
5f8f9402a59a.sentence: Between 2015 and 2020, the rate of deforestation was estimated at 10 million hectares per year, down from 16 million hectares per year in the 1990s.

ff44c2ab782d.title: Deforestation
ff44c2ab782d.sentence: By far, the direct cause of most deforestation is agriculture.

fb448ad4aad4.title: Deforestation
fb448ad4aad4.sentence: In 2025 nearly 90% of global deforestation was caused by agriculture, with cropland expansion and pasture creation the primary drivers, this is up from more than 80% in 2012.

fb373f9721ef.title: Deforestation
fb373f9721ef.sentence: Further drivers are the wood industry (logging), urbanization and mining.

75c5c082b021.title: Deforestation
75c5c082b021.sentence: The effects of climate change are another cause via the increased risk of wildfires (see deforestation and climate change).

cf03258a735c.title: Deforestation
cf03258a735c.sentence: Deforestation results in habitat destruction which in turn leads to biodiversity loss.

382388eb041a.title: Deforestation
382388eb041a.sentence: Deforestation also leads to extinction of animals and plants, changes to the local climate, and displacement of indigenous people who live in forests.

67f65631ea89.title: Deforestation
67f65631ea89.sentence: Another problem is that deforestation reduces the uptake of carbon dioxide (carbon sequestration) from the atmosphere.

95636f5bfe66.title: Deforestation
95636f5bfe66.sentence: This reduces the potential of forests to assist with climate change mitigation.

74f4e0d87f35.title: Deforestation
74f4e0d87f35.sentence: Deforested regions often also suffer from other environmental problems such as desertification and soil erosion.

b604db903596.title: Deforestation
b604db903596.section: Impacts > On the economy and agriculture
b604db903596.sentence: Economic losses due to deforestation in Brazil could reach around 317 billion dollars per year, approximately 7 times higher in comparison to the cost of all commodities produced through deforestation.

a84e63d6b51e.title: Extinction
a84e63d6b51e.sentence: Extinction is the termination of a species via the death of its last member.

c3778a96ebab.title: Extinction
c3778a96ebab.sentence: A species is extinct when the last existing member dies.

70d675490106.title: Extinction
70d675490106.sentence: A taxon may become functionally extinct before the death of its last member if it loses the capacity to reproduce and recover.

5748947f7eed.title: Extinction
5748947f7eed.sentence: A species may become functionally extinct when only a handful of individuals survive, which cannot reproduce due to poor health, age, sparse distribution over a large range, a lack of individuals of both sexes (in sexually reproducing species), or other reasons.

a946b0f11cd3.title: Extinction
a946b0f11cd3.sentence: It is estimated that over 99.9% of all species that ever lived are extinct.

76b63f12ea6f.title: Extinction
76b63f12ea6f.sentence: The average lifespan of a species is 1–10 million years, although this varies widely between taxa.

d86c87a1a875.title: Extinction
d86c87a1a875.sentence: Habitat degradation is currently the main anthropogenic cause of species extinctions.

10385a3b36fd.title: Extinction
10385a3b36fd.sentence: The main cause of habitat degradation worldwide is agriculture, with urban sprawl, logging, mining, and some fishing practices close behind.

53f16842504a.title: Extinction
53f16842504a.sentence: Recently in geological time, humans have become an additional cause of extinction of some species, either as a new mega-predator or by transporting animals and plants from one part of the world to another.

1859167fce31.title: Extinction
1859167fce31.sentence: Extinction as a result of climate change has been confirmed by fossil studies.

0f5c19d8d726.title: Extinction
0f5c19d8d726.sentence: A 2003 review across 14 biodiversity research centers predicted that, because of climate change, 15–37% of land species would be "committed to extinction" by 2050.

ae1293b87c75.title: Extinction
ae1293b87c75.sentence: There have been at least five mass extinctions in the history of life on earth, and four in the last 350 million years in which many species have disappeared in a relatively short period of geological time.

060ba63ea793.title: Extinction
060ba63ea793.sentence: A 2014 special edition of Science declared there is widespread consensus on the issue of human-driven mass species extinctions.

7800d8352685.title: Extinction
7800d8352685.sentence: As a species' potential range may be very large, determining this moment is quite difficult, and is usually done retrospectively.

dc90a6d7b033.title: Biodiversity loss
dc90a6d7b033.sentence: Biodiversity loss happens when species disappear completely from Earth (extinction) or when there is a decrease or disappearance of species in a specific area.

960fafcbc567.title: Biodiversity loss
960fafcbc567.sentence: The decrease can be temporary or permanent.

33e6099e38f1.title: Biodiversity loss
33e6099e38f1.sentence: It is temporary if the damage that led to the loss is reversible in time, for example through ecological restoration.If this is not possible, then the decrease is permanent.

0c1e0009a662.title: Biodiversity loss
0c1e0009a662.sentence: The current rate of global biodiversity loss is estimated to be 100 to 1000 times higher than the (naturally occurring) background extinction rate, faster than at any other time in human history, and is expected to grow in the upcoming years.

341b707342a6.title: Biodiversity loss
341b707342a6.sentence: In any case, all contemporary biodiversity loss has been attributed to human activities.

422489ceac35.title: Biodiversity loss
422489ceac35.sentence: Still, it is the general habitat destruction (often for expansion of agriculture), not climate change, that is currently the bigger driver of biodiversity loss.

5d472918d628.title: Biodiversity loss
5d472918d628.sentence: To measure biodiversity loss rates for a particular location, scientists record the species richness and its variation over time in that area.

6cce01844a0d.title: Biodiversity loss
6cce01844a0d.section: Observations by type of life > Wildlife in general
6cce01844a0d.sentence: In 2022, the World Wildlife Fund reported an average population decline of 68% between 1970 and 2016 for 4,400 animal species worldwide, encompassing nearly 21,000 monitored populations.

c7e2e1f00918.title: Biodiversity loss
c7e2e1f00918.sentence: For example, of the 20 biodiversity goals laid out by the Aichi Biodiversity Targets in 2010, only six were "partially achieved" by 2020.

60c1fee14aa2.title: Invasive species
60c1fee14aa2.sentence: An invasive species is an introduced species that harms its new environment.

07da41380ae4.title: Invasive species
07da41380ae4.sentence: Invasive species are the subset of established non-native species that pose a threat to native species and biodiversity.

fa5b6c107d22.title: Invasive species
fa5b6c107d22.sentence: Invasion of long-established ecosystems by organisms is a natural phenomenon, but human-facilitated introductions have greatly increased the rate, scale, and geographic range of invasion.

99197750cfd6.title: Invasive species
99197750cfd6.sentence: Biotic invasion is one of the five top drivers for global biodiversity loss, and is increasing because of tourism and globalization.

c9f6aedada61.title: Invasive species
c9f6aedada61.sentence: Common invasive species traits include fast growth and rapid reproduction, such as vegetative reproduction in plants; association with humans; and prior successful invasions.

654836abfd9a.title: Invasive species
654836abfd9a.sentence: Typically, an introduced species must persist at low population densities before it can become invasive in a new environment.

ecba630a3cfc.title: Invasive species
ecba630a3cfc.sentence: At low densities, introduced species often face difficulties in reproducing and sustaining a viable population—sometimes requiring multiple introductions before establishment occurs.

d780c22bfd46.title: Invasive species
d780c22bfd46.sentence: The consensus of the scientific community is that the effects of invasive species on biodiversity are primarily negative, despite the potential for some favorable impacts.

d1c55ea071a6.title: Invasive species
d1c55ea071a6.sentence: Some invasive species can provide a suitable habitat or food source for other organisms.

63c39abeaf4c.title: Invasive species
63c39abeaf4c.sentence: The term "invasive" is poorly defined and often very subjective.

e395c74a443a.title: Nature conservation
e395c74a443a.sentence: Nature conservation is the ethical/moral philosophy and conservation movement focused on protecting species from extinction, maintaining and restoring habitats, enhancing ecosystem services, and protecting biological diversity.

09f8335da142.title: Nature conservation
09f8335da142.sentence: Conservation goals include conserving habitat, preventing deforestation, maintaining soil organic matter, halting species extinction, reducing overfishing, and mitigating climate change.

0a6df98b66aa.title: Nature conservation
0a6df98b66aa.sentence: As of 2018 15% of land and 7.3% of the oceans were protected.

3a2dda423975.title: Nature conservation
3a2dda423975.sentence: Many environmentalists set a target of protecting 30% of land and marine territory by 2030.

82f6bd298eb1.title: Nature conservation
82f6bd298eb1.sentence: Protected areas in developing countries, where probably as many as 70–80 percent of the species of the world live, still enjoy very little effective management and protection.

0e975530ce30.title: Nature conservation
0e975530ce30.sentence: Nowadays, officially more than 10 percent of the world is legally protected in some way or the other, and in practice, private fundraising is insufficient to pay for the effective management of so much land with protective status.

c8f59e037349.title: Nature conservation
c8f59e037349.sentence: The term "conservation" was coined by Gifford Pinchot in 1907.

c89b33252ff4.title: Nature conservation
c89b33252ff4.sentence: The historian Al Runte described how they first were set up and emphasized the role of "worthless lands", i.e. that mainly land of low commercial interest is protected, such as alpine and dry habitats.

f3a4c623c3e8.title: Overexploitation
f3a4c623c3e8.sentence: Overexploitation, also called overharvesting or ecological overshoot, refers to harvesting a renewable resource to the point of diminishing returns.

5350902e2ac6.title: Overexploitation
5350902e2ac6.sentence: Continued overexploitation can lead to the destruction of the resource, as it will be unable to replenish itself.

7905004640b0.title: Overexploitation
7905004640b0.sentence: In ecology, "overexploitation" describes one of the five main activities threatening global biodiversity.

6c4856bc195d.title: Overexploitation
6c4856bc195d.sentence: Ecologists use the term to describe populations that are harvested at an unsustainable rate, given their natural rates of mortality and capacities for reproduction.

0efd7137a51f.title: Overexploitation
0efd7137a51f.sentence: Such practices can result in extinction at the population level and even extinction of whole species.

db5a7eda4a49.title: Overexploitation
db5a7eda4a49.sentence: Overexploitation can lead to resource destruction, including extinctions; however, it can also be sustainable, as discussed below in the section on fisheries.

b63e804e22ee.title: Overexploitation
b63e804e22ee.sentence: Overexploitation may not destroy the resource, and it can be sustainable.

fc85b83e57cc.title: Overexploitation
fc85b83e57cc.sentence: Overexploitation occurs if a water resource, such as the Ogallala Aquifer, is mined or extracted at a rate that exceeds the recharge rate, that is, at a rate that exceeds the practical sustained yield.

aab9cd8ae6f0.title: Overexploitation
aab9cd8ae6f0.sentence: An aquifer that has been overexploited is said to be overdrafted or depleted.

5061dcc36b86.title: Overexploitation
5061dcc36b86.sentence: Forests are considered overexploited when logging occurs at a rate that exceeds the rate of reforestation.

55a5d6c8d200.title: Overexploitation
55a5d6c8d200.sentence: Overexploitation threatens one-third of endangered vertebrates, as well as other groups.

a6bece08fb74.title: Overexploitation
a6bece08fb74.section: Endangered and extinct species > Vertebrates > Birds
a6bece08fb74.sentence: Overexploitation has affected 50 bird species that have become extinct since 1500 (approximately 40% of the total), including:

1897ffb12a33.title: Overexploitation
1897ffb12a33.sentence: Excluding edible fish, the illegal trade in wildlife is valued at $10 billion per year.

2ed124596d45.title: Overexploitation
2ed124596d45.sentence: It was based on a parable that William Forster Lloyd published in 1833 to explain how individuals innocently acting in their own self-interest can overexploit and destroy a resource that they all share.

c209565abd0d.title: Overexploitation
c209565abd0d.sentence: However, all herders reach the same rational decision to buy additional cows and graze them on the common, which eventually destroys it.

d6239b446c7e.title: Habitat fragmentation
d6239b446c7e.sentence: Habitat fragmentation is the emergence of discontinuities (fragmentation) in an organism's preferred environment (habitat), causing population fragmentation and ecosystem decay.

ace2007ee153.title: Habitat fragmentation
ace2007ee153.sentence: More specifically, habitat fragmentation is a process by which large and contiguous habitats get divided into smaller, isolated patches of habitats.

df888a76f10a.title: Habitat fragmentation
df888a76f10a.sentence: - Reduction in the total area of the habitat

a9f97a57b4e4.title: Habitat fragmentation
a9f97a57b4e4.sentence: - Decrease of the interior: edge ratio

c1c68bfe4f7a.title: Habitat fragmentation
c1c68bfe4f7a.sentence: - Isolation of one habitat fragment from other areas of habitat

c823c69036a1.title: Habitat fragmentation
c823c69036a1.sentence: - Breaking up of one patch of habitat into several smaller patches

ecc4e33222cb.title: Habitat fragmentation
ecc4e33222cb.sentence: - Decrease in the average size of each patch of habitat

5873f8908c60.title: Habitat fragmentation
5873f8908c60.sentence: Habitat fragmentation is frequently caused by humans when native plants are cleared for human activities such as agriculture, rural development, urbanization and the creation of hydroelectric reservoirs.

2043760c85bd.title: Habitat fragmentation
2043760c85bd.sentence: Habitat fragmentation consistently reduces biodiversity by 13 to 75% and impairs key ecosystem functions by decreasing biomass and altering nutrient cycles.

0a80fb05b59f.title: Habitat fragmentation
0a80fb05b59f.sentence: Generally a 10% remnant contiguous habitat will result in a 50% biodiversity loss.

e5c734633292.title: Habitat fragmentation
e5c734633292.sentence: Minor fluctuations in climate, resources, or other factors that would be unremarkable and quickly corrected in large populations can be catastrophic in small, isolated populations.

4f3c188114b4.title: Habitat fragmentation
4f3c188114b4.sentence: Thus fragmentation of habitat is an important cause of species extinction.

35dc9a2dc476.title: Habitat fragmentation
35dc9a2dc476.sentence: Aquatic species' habitats have been fragmented by dams and water diversions.

b8ed3a2fad0e.title: Habitat fragmentation
b8ed3a2fad0e.sentence: The effects of current fragmentation will continue to emerge for decades.

2211af960118.title: Habitat fragmentation
2211af960118.sentence: Indeed, the experiments here reveal ongoing losses of biodiversity and ecosystem functioning two decades or longer after fragmentation occurred.

96def634574c.title: Habitat fragmentation
96def634574c.sentence: One solution to the problem of habitat fragmentation is to link the fragments by preserving or planting corridors of native vegetation.

0259e69e673a.title: Habitat fragmentation
0259e69e673a.sentence: In some cases, a bridge or underpass may be enough to join two fragments.

5cfa93611c75.title: Habitat fragmentation
5cfa93611c75.sentence: This has the potential to mitigate the problem of isolation but not the loss of interior habitat.

05a1a6216df4.title: Land degradation
05a1a6216df4.sentence: Land degradation is a process in which land becomes less healthy and productive due to a combination of human activities or natural conditions.

7b7ceda2dc60.title: Land degradation
7b7ceda2dc60.sentence: Human activities are often the main cause, such as unsustainable land management practices.

c40abc5ee62a.title: Land degradation
c40abc5ee62a.sentence: In the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment of 2005, land degradation is defined as "the reduction or loss of the biological or economic productivity of drylands".

d434bba5b1cd.title: Land degradation
d434bba5b1cd.sentence: The United Nations estimates that about 30% of land is degraded worldwide, and about 3.2 billion people live in these degrading areas, giving a high rate of environmental pollution.

d3910d94f492.title: Land degradation
d3910d94f492.sentence: Approximately 120,000 km2 of productive land—which roughly equals the size of Greece—is degraded every year.

3309c89ebe9f.title: Land degradation
3309c89ebe9f.sentence: By 2025, unsustainable farming and management practices has led to the degradation of 9.96 million km2 of agricultural lands; this accounts for over 60% of human-induced land degradation, which affects a total area of more than 16.6 million km2.

2d34c112deb1.title: Land degradation
2d34c112deb1.sentence: They include lower crop yields, less diverse ecosystems, more vulnerability to natural disasters like floods and droughts, people losing their homes, less food available, and economic problems.

3d8eaa06166a.title: Land degradation
3d8eaa06166a.sentence: Degraded land also releases greenhouse gases, making climate change worse.

6145df483d3a.title: Land degradation
6145df483d3a.sentence: Land that is degraded becomes less resilient than undegraded land, which can lead to even further degradation through shocks to the landscape.

de4455cfe8a7.title: Land degradation
de4455cfe8a7.sentence: Reversing just 10% of human-induced degradation of croplands could restore production sufficient to feed an additional 154 million people annually.

4ca03bdd0e4a.title: Desertification
4ca03bdd0e4a.sentence: Desertification is a type of gradual land degradation of fertile land into arid desert due to a combination of natural processes and human activities.

3ec5cd7de12b.title: Desertification
3ec5cd7de12b.sentence: Desertification has been defined in the text of the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) as "land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid regions resulting from various factors, including climatic variations and human activities."

e8c0b4138162.title: Desertification
e8c0b4138162.sentence: The immediate cause of desertification is the loss of most vegetation.

d65e3587e8d3.title: Desertification
d65e3587e8d3.sentence: This is driven by a number of factors, alone or in combination, such as drought, climatic shifts, tillage for agriculture, overgrazing and deforestation for fuel or construction materials.

7b275dbff710.title: Desertification
7b275dbff710.sentence: Unprotected, dry soil surfaces blow away with the wind or are washed away by flash floods, leaving infertile lower soil layers that bake in the sun and become an unproductive hardpan.

662ca7c6ad57.title: Desertification
662ca7c6ad57.sentence: Drylands occupy approximately 40–41% of Earth's land area and are home to more than 2 billion people.

f520e20d5194.title: Desertification
f520e20d5194.sentence: At least 90% of the inhabitants of drylands live in developing countries, where they also suffer from poor economic and social conditions.

8838077c16f8.title: Desertification
8838077c16f8.sentence: It has been estimated that some 10–20% of drylands are already degraded, the total area affected by desertification being between 6 and 12 million square kilometers, that about 1–6% of the inhabitants of drylands live in desertified areas, and that a billion people are under threat from further desertification.

20c6d7409121.title: Desertification
20c6d7409121.sentence: However, more intense climate change is still expected to increase the current extent of drylands on the Earth's continents: from 38% in late 20th century to 50% or 56% by the end of the century, under the "moderate" and high-warming Representative Concentration Pathways 4.5 and 8.5.

5d19b5c51e28.title: Desertification
5d19b5c51e28.sentence: One proposed barrier is that the costs of adopting sustainable agricultural practices sometimes exceed the benefits for individual farmers, even while they are socially and environmentally beneficial.

548ec249db32.title: Desertification
548ec249db32.sentence: Fixating the soil is often done through the use of shelter belts, woodlots and windbreaks.

80f84944b8c8.title: Desertification
80f84944b8c8.sentence: Windbreaks are made from trees and bushes and are used to reduce soil erosion and evapotranspiration.

7588cc81f08d.title: Genetic diversity
7588cc81f08d.sentence: Genetic diversity is the total number of genetic characteristics in the genetic makeup of a species.

a1dc1c58547f.title: Genetic diversity
a1dc1c58547f.sentence: Genetic diversity serves as a way for populations to adapt to changing environments.

87ed19006c4f.title: Genetic diversity
87ed19006c4f.sentence: With more variation, it is more likely that some individuals in a population will possess variations of alleles that are suited for the environment.

9f4be6b6370f.title: Genetic diversity
9f4be6b6370f.section: Evolutionary importance of genetic diversity > Adaptation
9f4be6b6370f.sentence: Conversely, the vulnerability of a population to changes, such as climate change or novel diseases will increase with reduction in genetic diversity.

67fbad8860db.title: Genetic diversity
67fbad8860db.section: Evolutionary importance of genetic diversity > Adaptation
67fbad8860db.sentence: For example, the inability of koalas to adapt to fight Chlamydia and the koala retrovirus (KoRV) has been linked to the koala's low genetic diversity.

ca8e78330195.title: Genetic diversity
ca8e78330195.section: Evolutionary importance of genetic diversity > Small populations
ca8e78330195.sentence: Small populations are more likely to experience the loss of diversity over time by random chance, which is an example of genetic drift.

4713c7a6732f.title: Genetic diversity
4713c7a6732f.section: Evolutionary importance of genetic diversity > Small populations
4713c7a6732f.sentence: In small population sizes, inbreeding, or mating between individuals with similar genetic makeup, is more likely to occur, thus perpetuating more common alleles to the point of fixation, thus decreasing genetic diversity.

e02eba979e94.title: Genetic diversity
e02eba979e94.section: Evolutionary importance of genetic diversity > Small populations
e02eba979e94.sentence: A genetic bottleneck can occur when a population goes through a period of low number of individuals, resulting in a rapid decrease in genetic diversity.

daabe376f10a.title: Genetic diversity
daabe376f10a.sentence: A study conducted by the National Science Foundation in 2007 found that genetic diversity (within-species diversity) and biodiversity are dependent upon each other — i.e. that diversity within a species is necessary to maintain diversity among species, and vice versa.

52fc5b003bdf.title: Genetic diversity
52fc5b003bdf.sentence: Loss of genetic diversity in domestic animal populations has also been studied and attributed to the extension of markets and economic globalization.

7b8f8a34b3ba.title: Genetic diversity
7b8f8a34b3ba.section: Evolutionary importance of genetic diversity > Mutation
7b8f8a34b3ba.sentence: Random mutations consistently generate genetic variation.

76e11902733c.title: Genetic diversity
76e11902733c.section: Evolutionary importance of genetic diversity > Gene flow
76e11902733c.sentence: Gene flow, often by migration, is the movement of genetic material (for example by pollen in the wind, or the migration of a bird).

4328c192cda5.title: Genetic diversity
4328c192cda5.section: Evolutionary importance of genetic diversity > Gene flow
4328c192cda5.sentence: Gene flow can introduce novel alleles to a population.

d1a115973c14.title: Species richness
d1a115973c14.sentence: Species richness is the number of different species represented in an ecological community, landscape, or region.

c334c5157db9.title: Species richness
c334c5157db9.sentence: Species richness is simply a count of species, and it does not take into account the abundance of each species or its abundance relative to other species (known as relative species abundance).

c2152fc6ff70.title: Species richness
c2152fc6ff70.sentence: Species richness and species diversity are sometimes erroneously used as synonyms, but species diversity is a scientific assessment of both species richness and species evenness.

45ae4b4ac232.title: Species richness
45ae4b4ac232.sentence: For this reason, sets with many individuals can be expected to contain more species than sets with fewer individuals.

f6bc357d5cb9.title: Species richness
f6bc357d5cb9.sentence: If species richness of the obtained sample is taken to represent species richness of the underlying habitat or other larger unit, values are only comparable if sampling efforts are standardised in an appropriate way.

c51e19b6f3a9.title: Species richness
c51e19b6f3a9.sentence: Many organism groups have most species in the tropics, which leads to latitudinal gradients in species richness.

63767232fbf6.title: Species richness
63767232fbf6.sentence: Species richness is often used as a criterion when assessing the relative conservation values of habitats or landscapes.

d75c9d9b56bd.title: Species richness
d75c9d9b56bd.sentence: However, species richness is blind to the identity of the species.

845accb9f69d.title: Species richness
845accb9f69d.sentence: An area with many endemic or rare species is generally considered to have higher conservation value than another area where species richness is similar, but all the species are common and widespread.

5c777b8b5ef2.title: Wildlife corridor
5c777b8b5ef2.sentence: A wildlife corridor, also known as a habitat corridor or green corridor, is an area that connects wildlife populations that have been separated by human activities or structures such as industrialization, expansion of agriculture, urbanization, road infrastructure, land clearings, and other development.

e73dfb6b6d08.title: Wildlife corridor
e73dfb6b6d08.sentence: Corridors mitigate the impacts of habitat fragmentation, meaning the division of habitat areas and restriction of movement, which has been caused by rapid urbanization and transport network expansion.

3ec4146ac062.title: Wildlife corridor
3ec4146ac062.sentence: Habitat fragmentation from human development poses a significant threat to biodiversity, and wildlife corridors help to reduce the harmful effects of fragmentation and habitat degradation.

988889c66122.title: Wildlife corridor
988889c66122.sentence: By enabling the movement of individuals and populations, wildlife corridors help to prevent the negative effects of inbreeding and reduced genetic diversity that occur in isolated populations.

3076484fef77.title: Wildlife corridor
3076484fef77.sentence: Wildlife corridors also have effects on plant populations by increasing pollen and seed dispersal through animal movement between isolated habitat patches.

5e43bf7b8dee.title: Wildlife corridor
5e43bf7b8dee.sentence: With climate change, corridors can also serve the purpose of connecting cooler areas of habitat with warmer areas of habitat, helping individuals and populations by facilitating movement as specie ranges shift with climate change.

b416a0c270cf.title: Wildlife corridor
b416a0c270cf.section: Types of corridors > Size and continuity
b416a0c270cf.sentence: Continuous corridors are uninterrupted strips of habitat, while "stepping stone" corridors consist of small, separate patches of suitable habitat.

256cb2c22460.title: Wildlife corridor
256cb2c22460.sentence: Wildlife corridors also include aquatic habitats, or riparian zones.

a03adb8ef863.title: Wildlife corridor
a03adb8ef863.sentence: Corridors can include wildlife crossings, such an underpasses or overpasses.

18dacb2985c3.title: Wildlife corridor
18dacb2985c3.sentence: In a corridor ecology experiment in South Carolina, in the United States, five remnant areas of land were monitored for butterfly movement and plant reproduction.

697a80b9ba35.title: Wildlife corridor
697a80b9ba35.sentence: Butterflies that were placed in the central habitat area were two to four times more likely to move to the patch connected by the wildlife corridor than to the disconnected habitat patches.

8d3bb6c3e87c.title: Wildlife corridor
8d3bb6c3e87c.sentence: In order to successfully implement wildlife corridors, a shared goal and vision between these stakeholders and partners is important.

61b7d829a635.title: Wildlife corridor
61b7d829a635.sentence: A clear set of rules and regulations governing the wildlife corridor, incentive programs for encouraging the private sector to support the corridor, in addition to research that outlines priority areas for corridors (including areas of high-quality habitat and areas near other corridors) is important for habitat connectivity implementation.

977816a003bf.title: Wildlife corridor
977816a003bf.sentence: Corridors can coincide with areas of human settlements, which can produce conflict between wildlife and people.

781cd747d031.title: Wildlife corridor
781cd747d031.sentence: Human-wildlife conflict, caused by the degradation of wildlife habitat and resource competition, can take the form of road mortality, crop raiding, livestock predation, as well as human injury and death.

bde0593bfad5.title: Abundance (ecology)
bde0593bfad5.sentence: In ecology, local abundance is the relative representation of a species in a particular ecosystem.

30bd1a6b7f52.title: Abundance (ecology)
30bd1a6b7f52.sentence: It is usually measured as the number of individuals found per sample.

f6c4460a8a60.title: Abundance (ecology)
f6c4460a8a60.sentence: The ratio of abundance of one species to one or multiple other species living in an ecosystem is referred to as relative species abundances.

1476c9c4cec6.title: Abundance (ecology)
1476c9c4cec6.sentence: Both indicators are relevant for computing biodiversity.

1e4eb72407ab.title: Abundance (ecology)
1e4eb72407ab.sentence: For larger animals, these may include spotlight counts, track counts and roadkill counts, as well as presence at monitoring stations.

62f34c34778b.title: Abundance (ecology)
62f34c34778b.sentence: In many plant communities the abundances of plant species are measured by plant cover, i.e. the relative area covered by different plant species in a small plot.

087ab0b7a535.title: Abundance (ecology)
087ab0b7a535.sentence: In most ecosystems in which abundance has been calculated, most often only a small number of species are abundant, while a large number are pretty rare.

73f7a206382d.title: Abundance (ecology)
73f7a206382d.sentence: These abundant species are often generalists, with many rare species being specialists.

c376c8877e24.title: Abundance (ecology)
c376c8877e24.sentence: Species with high abundance are likely to have more offspring, and these offspring in turn are more likely to colonize a new sector of the ecosystem than a species which is less abundant.

364315e95804.title: Abundance (ecology)
364315e95804.sentence: Thus begins a positive feedback loop leading to a species distribution in which a few "core species" are wide spread, and the other species are restricted and scarce known as satellite species.

3f10b3e7d23d.title: Endemism
3f10b3e7d23d.sentence: Endemism is the state of a species being found only in a singular defined geographic location, such as an island, state, nation, country or other defined zone; organisms that are indigenous to a place are not endemic to it if they are also found elsewhere.

1fbe166d22e5.title: Endemism
1fbe166d22e5.sentence: Endemism is an important concept in conservation biology for measuring biodiversity in a particular place and evaluating the risk of extinction for species.

0a31b16fdf2f.title: Endemism
0a31b16fdf2f.sentence: The extreme opposite of an endemic species is one with a cosmopolitan distribution, having a global or widespread range.

512f80b63782.title: Endemism
512f80b63782.sentence: Endemics are not necessarily rare; some might be common where they occur.

91c7d92c4ff6.title: Endemism
91c7d92c4ff6.sentence: Likewise, not all rare species are endemics; some may have a large range but be rare throughout this range.

bcc23e442746.title: Endemism
bcc23e442746.sentence: In isolated areas where there is little possibility for organisms to disperse to new places or to receive new gene flow from outside, the rate of endemism is particularly high.

ece76843df29.title: Endemism
ece76843df29.sentence: For example, many endemic species are found on remote islands, such as Hawaii, the Galápagos Islands and Socotra.

14338796b99c.title: Endemism
14338796b99c.sentence: In 1872, it was Charles Darwin who first used endemic to mean a species restricted to a specific location, although, as already mentioned, it now can apply to a genus, family, or even a higher taxonomic rank.

bbfa54ba3118.title: Endemism
bbfa54ba3118.sentence: Endemics might more easily become endangered or extinct because they are already restricted in distribution.

89a0debb8fa3.title: Endemism
89a0debb8fa3.sentence: This puts endemic plants and animals at greater risk than widespread species during the rapid climate change of this century.

cb4bf5c3d2ae.title: Endemism

6d7e2e68fdfc.title: Endemism

e1dd9c4458fd.title: Endemism

e8e9e2d90e22.title: Deforestation and climate change
e8e9e2d90e22.sentence: Land use change, especially in the form of deforestation, is the second largest source of carbon dioxide emissions from human activities, after the burning of fossil fuels.

3a9f9bd60036.title: Deforestation and climate change
3a9f9bd60036.sentence: Greenhouse gases are emitted from deforestation during the burning of forest biomass and decomposition of remaining plant material and soil carbon.

3228e8a350cb.title: Deforestation and climate change

75e1f8adad93.title: Deforestation and climate change

3f9a03341bba.sentence: By doing so, forests sequester approximately 25% of human carbon emissions annually, playing a critical role in Earth's climate.

3a92f508b8cb.title: Deforestation and climate change

82b6732d62bd.title: Deforestation and climate change
82b6732d62bd.sentence: The more trees that are removed, the greater the effect of climate change which then results in the loss of more trees.

9d9faedbc8ab.title: Deforestation and climate change
9d9faedbc8ab.sentence: Some of the effects of climate change, such as more wildfires, invasive species, and extreme weather events can lead to more forest loss.

c64c03b78870.title: Deforestation and climate change
c64c03b78870.section: Effects of deforestation from climate change
c64c03b78870.sentence: Moreover, it suggests that standing tropical forests help cool the average global temperature by more than 1 °C or 1.8 °F.

9b858a2df31f.title: Deforestation and climate change

9b858a2df31f.sentence: In 2019 forests took up a third less carbon than they did in the 1990s, due to higher temperatures, droughts and deforestation.

e7d7a27b7e86.title: Deforestation and climate change
e7d7a27b7e86.section: Effects of deforestation from climate change
e7d7a27b7e86.sentence: Deforestation of tropical forests may risk triggering tipping points in the climate system and of forest ecosystem collapse which would also have effects on climate change.

19882f1e1637.title: Poaching
19882f1e1637.sentence: Poaching is the illegal hunting or capturing of wild animals, usually associated with land use rights.

6a57578008bc.title: Poaching
6a57578008bc.sentence: Since the 1980s, the term "poaching" has also been used to refer to the illegal harvesting of wild plants.

05346979bbef.title: Poaching
05346979bbef.sentence: Wildlife biologists and conservationists consider poaching to have a detrimental effect on biodiversity both within and outside protected areas as wildlife populations decline, species are depleted locally, and the functionality of ecosystems is disturbed.

5f58da9b3a8d.title: Poaching

3eb1a91d75eb.title: Poaching

4f59ee2b4560.title: Poaching

e9880ffa5d92.title: Poaching

d1eca813695a.title: Poaching

c8e37735d742.title: Poaching

5bb452b5731a.sentence: The Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services is a report by the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services, on the global state of biodiversity.

fc63a2730edb.title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services

282fd8b16322.title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
282fd8b16322.sentence: The Global Assessment Report is a global-level assessment of changes in Earth's biodiversity that have occurred over the past 50 years.

934e62e8822e.title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
934e62e8822e.sentence: The Global Assessment Report comprises some 1,700 pages evaluating over 15,000 scientific publications and reports from indigenous peoples.

f8c1b0fdd216.title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
f8c1b0fdd216.sentence: It is the first United Nations report on the global state of biodiversity since the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment published in 2005.

765bce59d365.sentence: Out of those 8 million species, 1 million are threatened with extinction, including 40 percent of amphibians, almost a third of reef-building corals, more than a third of marine mammals, and 10 percent of all insects.

60cbd96d2c09.title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
60cbd96d2c09.sentence: The drivers of these extinctions are, in descending order: (1) changes in land and sea use; (2) direct exploitation of organisms; (3) climate change; (4) pollution and (5) invasive alien species.

680957482c47.title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
680957482c47.sentence: The total biomass of wild mammals has decreased by 82 percent, while humans and their farm animals now make up 96 percent of all mammalian biomass on Earth.

05ae7b7e0aad.title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
05ae7b7e0aad.sentence: In the past 50 years, the world's human population has doubled, per capita gross domestic product has quadrupled, and biodiversity has suffered a catastrophic decline.

6a3928b2637d.title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
6a3928b2637d.sentence: Socioeconomic consequences include threatened loss of food production, due to loss of pollinator insects, valued at between $235 and $577 billion a year; and anticipated loss of the livelihoods of up to 300 million people, due to loss of coastal areas such as mangrove forests.

9f3ba91298fe.title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
9f3ba91298fe.sentence: The Report warned that society should not fixate on economic growth, and that countries should "base their economies on an understanding that nature is the foundation for development." It also suggests that countries reduce their subsidies to industries that are harmful to nature, and increase subsidies and funding to environmentally beneficial programs.

e824fed38558.title: Diversity index
e824fed38558.sentence: A diversity index is a method of measuring how many different types (e.g. species) there are in a dataset (e.g. a community).

8409cbcdc2e5.title: Diversity index
8409cbcdc2e5.sentence: Diversity indices are statistical representations of different aspects of biodiversity (e.g. richness, evenness, and dominance), which are useful simplifications for comparing different communities or sites.

af55584bd915.title: Diversity index
af55584bd915.sentence: The entities of interest are usually individual organisms (e.g. plants or animals), and the measure of abundance can be, for example, number of individuals, biomass or coverage.

95605cc49004.title: Diversity index

2d045ee7715e.title: Diversity index
2d045ee7715e.sentence: Richness is a simple measure, so it has been a popular diversity index in ecology, where abundance data are often not available.

2bc04bb5983c.title: Diversity index

e81763783d00.title: Diversity index

a97e9b77810e.title: Diversity index

e6a0db41a5ff.title: Diversity index

d1039b7d8668.title: Biodiversity hotspot
d1039b7d8668.sentence: A biodiversity hotspot is a biogeographic region with significant levels of biodiversity that is threatened by human habitation.

d324c7a860d4.title: Biodiversity
d324c7a860d4.sentence: A biodiversity hotspot is a region with a high level of endemic species that have experienced great habitat loss.

0f684cf2ce16.title: Biodiversity hotspot
0f684cf2ce16.sentence: Norman Myers wrote about the concept in two articles in The Environmentalist in 1988 and 1990, after which the concept was revised following thorough analysis by Myers and others into "Hotspots: Earth's Biologically Richest and Most Endangered Terrestrial Ecoregions" and a paper published in the journal Nature, both in 2000.

095e6ea8e6db.title: Biodiversity hotspot
095e6ea8e6db.sentence: To qualify as a biodiversity hotspot on Myers' 2000 edition of the hotspot map, a region must meet two strict criteria: it must contain at least 1,500 species of vascular plants (more than 0.5% of the world's total) as endemics, and it has to have lost at least 70% of its primary vegetation.

6e3ac53d8678.title: Biodiversity hotspot
6e3ac53d8678.sentence: Globally, 36 zones qualify under this definition.

ce3fdebb1998.title: Biodiversity hotspot
ce3fdebb1998.sentence: Biodiversity hotspots host their diverse ecosystems on just 2.4% of the planet's surface.

3c037c3e3729.title: Biodiversity hotspot
3c037c3e3729.sentence: These sites support nearly 60% of the world's plant, bird, mammal, reptile, and amphibian species, with a high share of those species as endemics.

d3461c09e212.title: Biodiversity hotspot

7c8c37b6c606.title: Biodiversity hotspot
7c8c37b6c606.sentence: Only a small percentage of the total land area within biodiversity hotspots is now protected.

01b9e1ddd7d7.title: Biodiversity hotspot

b1855ebc3de3.title: Bushmeat
b1855ebc3de3.sentence: Bushmeat is meat from wildlife hunted for human consumption, particularly in Africa.

a847daf0ac2b.title: Bushmeat
a847daf0ac2b.sentence: Bushmeat represents a primary source of animal protein and a source of income in poor and rural communities of humid tropical forest regions of the world.

e5ef0a0f62f0.title: Bushmeat
e5ef0a0f62f0.sentence: As of 2016, 301 terrestrial mammals were threatened with extinction due to hunting for bushmeat including non-human primates, even-toed ungulates, bats, diprotodont marsupials, rodents and carnivores occurring in developing countries.

d9a0eda558ac.title: Bushmeat
d9a0eda558ac.sentence: The 301 mammal species threatened by hunting for bushmeat comprise 126 primates, 65 even-toed ungulates, 27 bats, 26 diprotodont marsupials, 21 rodents, 12 carnivores and all pangolin species.

ee6fa95fad7b.title: Bushmeat
ee6fa95fad7b.sentence: The volume of the bushmeat trade in West and Central Africa was estimated at 1–5 million tonnes (980,000–4,920,000 long tons; 1,100,000–5,500,000 short tons) per year at the turn of the 21st century.

b898349b3989.title: Bushmeat
b898349b3989.sentence: It can be sustainable when carried out by traditional hunter-gatherers in large landscapes for their own consumption.

c6399e221c04.title: Bushmeat

b5146ac0e26f.title: Bushmeat

a1f9ab32f6ba.title: Bushmeat

57e9c992bac9.title: Habitat conservation
57e9c992bac9.sentence: Habitat conservation is a management practice that seeks to conserve, protect and restore habitats and prevent species extinction, fragmentation or reduction in range.

4b0bda780fb2.title: Habitat conservation
4b0bda780fb2.sentence: Natural habitats can provide Ecosystem services to humans, which are "any positive benefit that wildlife or ecosystems provide to people." The natural environment is a source for a wide range of resources that can be exploited for economic profit, for example timber is harvested from forests and clean water is obtained from natural streams.

3a88e18d8dff.title: Habitat conservation

578405a4d3d1.title: Habitat conservation

f08d7669a7ea.title: Habitat conservation

6ac77fdfb635.title: Habitat conservation
