6c4cea3b66e5.sentence: Wildlife trade refers to the exchange of products derived from non-domesticated animals or plants usually extracted from their natural environment or raised under controlled conditions.

5d0094984544.title: Wildlife trade
5d0094984544.sentence: It can involve the trade of living or dead individuals, tissues such as skins, bones or meat, or other products.

74b374082b7a.title: Wildlife trade
74b374082b7a.sentence: Legal wildlife trade is regulated by the United Nations' Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which currently has 184 member countries called Parties.

5048b18cfb5a.title: Wildlife trade
5048b18cfb5a.section: Ineffective monitoring of international wildlife trade
5048b18cfb5a.sentence: According to an analysis on the 2012 Harmonized System customs statistics, global import of wildlife products amounted to US$187 billion, of which fisheries commodities accounted for $113 billion; plants and forestry products for $71 billion; non-fishery animal for $3 billion including live animals, parts and derivatives.

b1867f341742.title: Wildlife trade
b1867f341742.sentence: Illegal wildlife trade is widespread and constitutes one of the major illegal economic activities, comparable to the traffic of drugs and weapons.

edb7ba030223.title: Wildlife trade
edb7ba030223.sentence: Interpol has estimated the extent of the illegal wildlife trade between $10 billion and $20 billion per year.

b972feb75529.title: Wildlife trade
b972feb75529.sentence: Different forms of wildlife trade or use (utilization, hunting, trapping, collection or over-exploitation) are the second major threat to endangered mammals and it also ranks among the first ten threats to birds, amphibians and cycads.

88ccea705c6d.title: Wildlife trade
88ccea705c6d.sentence: Outbreaks of zoonotic diseases including COVID-19, H5N1 avian flu, severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), and monkeypox have been traced to live wildlife markets where the potential for zoonotic transmission is greatly increased.

764169af92c0.title: Wildlife trade
764169af92c0.section: Ineffective monitoring of international wildlife trade
764169af92c0.sentence: However, the global trade of wildlife commodities is ineffectively monitored and accounted for due to the constraint of the HS Code System used by the customs worldwide.

f54d7a6c68db.title: Wildlife trade
f54d7a6c68db.section: Ineffective monitoring of international wildlife trade
f54d7a6c68db.sentence: The majority of international imports of wildlife are only recorded in extremely basic and general categories, such as 'plant' or 'animal products', with no further taxonomic detail.

bc8287ad0481.title: Wildlife trade
bc8287ad0481.section: Legal wildlife trade > Examples of successful wildlife trade > North America > Alligator
bc8287ad0481.sentence: The use of legal trade and quotas have allowed management of a species as well as economic incentive for sustaining habitat with greater ecological benefits.

96ef1d7f6845.title: Insular biogeography
96ef1d7f6845.sentence: Insular biogeography or island biogeography is a field within biogeography that examines the factors that affect the species richness and diversification of isolated natural communities.

366ab80ade10.title: Insular biogeography
366ab80ade10.sentence: The field was started in the 1960s by the ecologists Robert H. MacArthur and E. O. Wilson, who coined the term island biogeography in their inaugural contribution to Princeton's Monograph in Population Biology series, which attempted to predict the number of species that would exist on a newly created island.

ba0b7ec9e053.title: Insular biogeography
ba0b7ec9e053.sentence: The theory of insular biogeography proposes that the number of species found in an undisturbed insular environment ("island") is determined by immigration and extinction.

8e85c1716cea.title: Insular biogeography
8e85c1716cea.sentence: Over time, the countervailing forces of extinction and immigration result in an equilibrium level of species richness.

311adb960fdf.title: Insular biogeography
311adb960fdf.sentence: Islands that are more isolated are less likely to receive immigrants than islands that are less isolated.

362422deda03.title: Insular biogeography
362422deda03.sentence: Larger islands contain larger habitat areas and opportunities for more different varieties of habitat.

203e5a3473e3.title: Insular biogeography
203e5a3473e3.sentence: Larger habitat size reduces the probability of extinction due to chance events.

136a576b202f.title: Insular biogeography
136a576b202f.sentence: For biogeographical purposes, an insular environment or "island" is any area of habitat suitable for a specific ecosystem, surrounded by an expanse of unsuitable habitat.

5c7eeda38ce9.title: Insular biogeography
5c7eeda38ce9.sentence: While this may be a traditional island—a mass of land surrounded by water—the term may also be applied to many nontraditional "islands", such as the peaks of mountains, isolated springs or lakes, and non-contiguous woodlands.

b5524cd9b532.title: Insular biogeography
b5524cd9b532.sentence: The concept is often applied to natural habitats surrounded by human-altered landscapes, such as expanses of grassland surrounded by highways or housing tracts, and national parks.

1a4d3b8d30a3.title: Insular biogeography
1a4d3b8d30a3.sentence: The theory of island biogeography was experimentally tested by E. O. Wilson and his student Daniel Simberloff in the mangrove islands in the Florida Keys.

ae7bbdb184eb.title: Insular biogeography
ae7bbdb184eb.sentence: Within a year the islands had been recolonized to pre-fumigation levels.

85245e11f1bf.title: Insular biogeography
85245e11f1bf.sentence: Islands closer to the mainland recovered faster as predicted by the Theory of Island Biogeography.

a11561b28773.title: Insular biogeography
a11561b28773.sentence: The idea that reserves and national parks formed islands inside human-altered landscapes (habitat fragmentation), and that these reserves could lose species as they 'relaxed towards equilibrium' (that is they would lose species as they achieved their new equilibrium number, known as ecosystem decay) caused a great deal of concern.

4ec40b7b0b9a.title: Insular biogeography
4ec40b7b0b9a.sentence: This led to the debate known as single large or several small (SLOSS), described by writer David Quammen in The Song of the Dodo as "ecology's own genteel version of trench warfare".

e9633cc3e88f.title: Insular biogeography
e9633cc3e88f.sentence: Island biogeography theory also led to the development of wildlife corridors as a conservation tool to increase connectivity between habitat islands.

11339060e2b1.title: Defaunation
11339060e2b1.sentence: Defaunation is the global, local, or functional extinction of animal populations or species from ecological communities.

073506d46081.title: Defaunation
073506d46081.sentence: Defaunation differs from extinction; it includes both the disappearance of species and declines in abundance.

48ce019f688f.title: Defaunation
48ce019f688f.sentence: The growth of the human population, combined with advances in harvesting technologies, has led to more intense and efficient exploitation of the environment.

845ee755817a.title: Defaunation
845ee755817a.sentence: This has resulted in the depletion of large vertebrates from ecological communities, creating what has been termed "empty forest".

d00ee7b9d9ea.title: Defaunation
d00ee7b9d9ea.sentence: It is estimated that more than 50 percent of all wildlife has been lost in the last 40 years.

1f38ca47d161.title: Defaunation
1f38ca47d161.sentence: Large mammals are often more vulnerable to extinction than smaller animals because they require larger home ranges and thus are more prone to suffer the effects of deforestation.

c4bd47e1aa07.title: Defaunation
c4bd47e1aa07.sentence: In extinct animal species for which the cause of extinction is known, over 50% were affected by invasive species.

c7f3da072165.title: Defaunation
c7f3da072165.sentence: Tropical regions are the most heavily impacted by defaunation.

7784b29a4017.title: Defaunation
7784b29a4017.sentence: These regions, which include the Brazilian Amazon, the Congo Basin of Central Africa, and Indonesia, experience the greatest rates of overexploitation and habitat degradation.

a61acb2ca873.title: Defaunation
a61acb2ca873.sentence: According to a 2022 study published in Science, terrestrial mammal food web links have declined by 53% over the past 130,000 years as a result of human population expansion and accompanying defaunation.

eda15eea9d0b.title: Defaunation
eda15eea9d0b.sentence: Changes in predation dynamics, seed predation, seed dispersal, carrion removal, dung removal, vegetation trampling, and other ecosystem processes as a result of defaunation can affect ecosystem supporting and regulatory services, such as nutrient cycling and decomposition, crop pollination, pest control, and water quality.

d2f010e79366.title: Defaunation
d2f010e79366.sentence: Defaunation effects were first implied at the Symposium of Plant-Animal Interactions at the University of Campinas, Brazil in 1988 in the context of Neotropical forests.

81e80c49254c.title: Conservation status
81e80c49254c.sentence: The conservation status of a group of organisms (for example, a species) indicates whether the group still exists and how likely it is to become extinct in the near future.

39709bc7a964.title: Conservation status
39709bc7a964.sentence: Many factors are taken into account when assessing conservation status—not simply the number of individuals remaining, but the overall increase or decrease in the population over time, breeding success rates, and known threats.

924b7b770d69.title: Conservation status
924b7b770d69.sentence: The two international systems are by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).

71b7c21dfe4d.title: Conservation status
71b7c21dfe4d.sentence: Various systems of conservation status are in use at international, multi-country, national and local levels, as well as for consumer use such as sustainable seafood advisory lists and certification.

3e48a5d8f66d.title: Conservation status
3e48a5d8f66d.section: International systems > IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
3e48a5d8f66d.sentence: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species by the International Union for Conservation of Nature is the best known worldwide conservation status listing and ranking system.

906389d23020.title: Conservation status
906389d23020.section: International systems > IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
906389d23020.sentence: Species are classified by the IUCN Red List into nine groups set through criteria such as rate of decline, population size, area of geographic distribution, and degree of population and distribution fragmentation.

865a96350e9d.title: Conservation status
865a96350e9d.section: International systems > IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
865a96350e9d.sentence: When discussing the IUCN Red List, the official term "threatened" is a grouping of three categories: critically endangered, endangered, and vulnerable.

7808d73dff4e.title: Conservation status
7808d73dff4e.section: International systems > IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
7808d73dff4e.sentence: - Extinct (EX) – There are no known living individuals

90360202b8e8.title: Conservation status
90360202b8e8.section: International systems > IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
90360202b8e8.sentence: - Extinct in the wild (EW) – Known only to survive in captivity, or as a naturalized population outside its historic range

f07f2d6cbcae.title: Conservation status
f07f2d6cbcae.section: International systems > IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
f07f2d6cbcae.sentence: - Near Threatened (NT) – Likely to become endangered in the near future

c7eaed7201b9.title: Conservation status
c7eaed7201b9.section: International systems > IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
c7eaed7201b9.sentence: - Least concern (LC) – Very low risk; does not qualify for a higher risk category and not likely to be threatened in the near future.

b4be1a4802f1.title: Conservation status
b4be1a4802f1.section: International systems > IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
b4be1a4802f1.sentence: - Data deficient (DD) – Not enough data to make an assessment of its risk of extinction

868b5f99bd2f.title: Conservation status
868b5f99bd2f.section: International systems > The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora
868b5f99bd2f.sentence: The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) went into force in 1975.

c4ce783cc2ee.title: Conservation status
c4ce783cc2ee.section: International systems > The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora
c4ce783cc2ee.sentence: It aims to ensure that international trade in specimens of wild animals and plants does not threaten their survival.

5d2395706221.title: Conservation status
5d2395706221.sentence: Some consumer guides for seafood, such as Seafood Watch, divide fish and other sea creatures into three categories, analogous to conservation status categories:

c5025c77ad0c.title: Conservation status
c5025c77ad0c.sentence: The categories do not simply reflect the imperilment of individual species, but also consider the environmental impacts of how and where they are fished, such as through bycatch or ocean bottom trawlers.

09c1d4153cde.title: Endangered species
09c1d4153cde.sentence: An endangered species is a species having a very high risk of extinction in the near future, either worldwide or in a particular region.

55b2d9c6e387.title: Endangered species
55b2d9c6e387.sentence: Species become endangered mainly due to habitat depletion and loss of genetic variation.

95b8f03e2ce4.title: Endangered species
95b8f03e2ce4.sentence: Unlike their more general use elsewhere, the List uses the terms "endangered species" and "threatened species" with particular meanings: "Endangered" (EN) species lie between "Vulnerable" (VU) and "Critically Endangered" (CR) species.

80501db04608.title: Endangered species
80501db04608.sentence: A species is endangered when its population declines by 20% within five years and there are fewer than 2,500 mature individuals remaining.

54d6a83b03e0.title: Endangered species
54d6a83b03e0.sentence: A species is endangered when its population diminishes by 50% to 70%, an assessment made over 10 years or three generations, whichever is longer.

eb364a562d60.title: Endangered species
eb364a562d60.sentence: In 2026, the IUCN Red List named 49,500 species worldwide as threatened for extinction.

07c8a2824157.title: Endangered species
07c8a2824157.sentence: Many nations have laws that protect conservation-reliant species which, for example, forbid hunting or harvesting, restrict land development, or create protected areas.

15fb40f9a673.title: Endangered species
15fb40f9a673.section: Conservation > Success stories > American bald eagle
15fb40f9a673.sentence: Once on the brink of extinction in the contiguous United States with only 417 known nesting pairs in 1963 due to pesticide use and habitat destruction, the bald eagle population has made a remarkable recovery.

bd45bcad9b7c.title: Endangered species
bd45bcad9b7c.section: Conservation > Success stories > American bald eagle
bd45bcad9b7c.sentence: By 2020, the number of nesting pairs had surged to 71,400.

a5cfadb55834.title: Endangered species
a5cfadb55834.section: Conservation > Success stories > American bald eagle
a5cfadb55834.sentence: Thanks to habitat protection, legal protection, and DDT ban efforts, the bald eagle was removed from the list of threatened and endangered species.

34ab976a6c28.title: Threatened species
34ab976a6c28.sentence: A threatened species is any species (including animals, plants and fungi) which is vulnerable to extinction in the near future.

f8ed13aae006.title: Threatened species
f8ed13aae006.sentence: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) is the foremost authority on threatened species, and treats threatened species not as a single category, but as a group of three categories, depending on the degree to which they are threatened:

7c6b2f60e4c1.title: Threatened species
7c6b2f60e4c1.sentence: Although threatened and vulnerable may be used interchangeably when discussing IUCN categories, the term threatened is generally used to refer to the three categories (critically endangered, endangered, and vulnerable), while vulnerable is used to refer to the least at risk of those three categories.

568a4a0558a7.title: Threatened species
568a4a0558a7.sentence: Less-than-threatened categories are near threatened, least concern, and the no longer assigned category of conservation dependent.

ea0424e9f7ef.title: Threatened species
ea0424e9f7ef.sentence: Species that have not been evaluated (NE), or do not have sufficient data (data deficient) also are not considered "threatened" by the IUCN.

b801c865e410.title: Threatened species
b801c865e410.sentence: Threatened species are also referred to as a red-listed species, as they are listed in the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.

85e7863e00bd.title: Biodiversity
85e7863e00bd.sentence: About 40 percent of the 40,177 species assessed using the IUCN Red List criteria are now listed as threatened with extinction—a total of 16,119.

fcad3ed85558.title: Threatened species
fcad3ed85558.sentence: Subspecies, populations and stocks may also be classified as threatened.

40e4eee96190.title: Background extinction rate
40e4eee96190.sentence: Background extinction rate (BER), also known as the normal extinction rate, refers to the standard rate of extinction in Earth's geological and biological history, excluding major extinction events, such as the current human-induced Holocene extinction.

28977c28eaf7.title: Background extinction rate
28977c28eaf7.sentence: Extinctions are a normal part of the evolutionary process, and the background extinction rate is a measurement of "how often" they naturally occur.

ff38c17b1318.title: Background extinction rate
ff38c17b1318.sentence: Normal extinction rates are often used as a comparison to present day extinction rates, to illustrate the higher frequency of extinction today than in all periods of non-extinction events before it.

ab971c30e06d.title: Background extinction rate
ab971c30e06d.sentence: For example, there is approximately one extinction estimated per million species years.

5bf5e6e6ff4f.title: Background extinction rate
5bf5e6e6ff4f.sentence: For example, at the background rate one species of bird will go extinct every estimated 400 years.

bf6373a2e4c7.title: Background extinction rate
bf6373a2e4c7.sentence: For example, given normal extinction rates species typically exist for 5–10 million years before going extinct.

221319cf1c41.title: Background extinction rate
221319cf1c41.sentence: - Mammals: These species' average lifespan is 1 million years.

ee51d08ca3b4.title: Background extinction rate
ee51d08ca3b4.sentence: There has been a decline in background extinction rates over the Phanerozoic eon, particularly from the middle of the Palaeozoic era, which has been attributed to increased oxygenation of the oceans.

1f271ad44ee4.title: Extinction event
1f271ad44ee4.sentence: An extinction event (also known as a mass extinction or biotic crisis) is a widespread and rapid decrease in the biodiversity on Earth.

3049f48a0285.title: Extinction event
3049f48a0285.sentence: Such an event is identified by a sharp fall in the diversity and abundance of multicellular organisms.

4e1ba5f84b0d.title: Extinction event
4e1ba5f84b0d.sentence: It occurs when the rate of extinction increases with respect to the background extinction rate and the rate of speciation.

0f00ab47cb75.title: Extinction event
0f00ab47cb75.sentence: Estimates of the number of major mass extinctions in the last 540 million years range from as few as five to more than twenty.

6a98e0583dd7.title: Extinction event
6a98e0583dd7.section: The "Big Five" mass extinction events > Permian–Triassic extinction event, 252 Ma
6a98e0583dd7.sentence: The End Permian extinction, or the "Great Dying", occurred at the Permian–Triassic transition.

5f1404b8fee9.title: Extinction event
5f1404b8fee9.section: The "Big Five" mass extinction events > Permian–Triassic extinction event, 252 Ma
5f1404b8fee9.sentence: It was the Phanerozoic Eon's largest extinction: 53% of marine families died, 84% of marine genera, about 81% of all marine species and an estimated 70% of terrestrial vertebrate species.

7b2b6b4d7244.title: Extinction event
7b2b6b4d7244.sentence: In general, large extinctions may result when a biosphere under long-term stress undergoes a short-term shock.

5d07c77fea35.title: Extinction event
5d07c77fea35.sentence: Research completed after the seminal 1982 paper (Sepkoski and Raup) has concluded that a sixth mass extinction event due to human activities is currently underway.

53d25af2203a.title: Extinction event
53d25af2203a.sentence: Extinctions have occurred at over 1,000 times the background extinction rate since 1900, and the rate is increasing.

12146c6c4bd9.title: Extinction event
12146c6c4bd9.sentence: The mass extinction is a result of human activity (an ecocide) driven by population growth, economic growth, and overconsumption of the Earth's natural resources.

a9bbd6a23fd8.title: Extinction event
a9bbd6a23fd8.sentence: After a major extinction event, usually only weedy species survive due to their ability to live in diverse habitats.

f6dfdfd798a3.title: Extinction event
f6dfdfd798a3.sentence: When dominance of particular ecological niches passes from one group of organisms to another, it is rarely because the newly dominant group is "superior" to the old but usually because an extinction event eliminates the old, dominant group and makes way for the new one, a process known as adaptive radiation.

8b5881cdb597.title: Extinction event
8b5881cdb597.sentence: In a landmark paper published in 1982, Jack Sepkoski and David M. Raup identified five particular geological intervals with excessive diversity loss.

5b81cdf7a200.title: Holocene extinction
5b81cdf7a200.sentence: The Holocene or Anthropocene extinction is an ongoing extinction event caused by human activity during the current geological epoch, impacting diverse families of plants and animals, including mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish, and invertebrates, as well as both terrestrial and marine species.

4735191fdae1.title: Holocene extinction
4735191fdae1.sentence: It is sometimes also called the sixth extinction (though this can also describe the Capitanian).

bde3cf5647ab.title: Holocene extinction
bde3cf5647ab.sentence: The abundance of species extinctions considered anthropogenic, or due to human activity, has sometimes (especially when referring to hypothesized future events) been collectively called the "Anthropocene extinction".

cb2bbda1e60e.title: Holocene extinction
cb2bbda1e60e.sentence: The contemporary rate of extinction is estimated at 100 to 1,000 times higher than the natural background extinction rate—the typical rate of species loss through natural evolutionary processes.

44547be4a1a3.title: Holocene extinction
44547be4a1a3.sentence: The Holocene extinction continues into the 21st century, driven by anthropogenic climate change, destruction of wetlands, deforestation, overfishing, ocean acidification, human population growth, economic growth, and increasing consumption, particularly among affluent societies.

ac96a78cf9d4.title: Holocene extinction
ac96a78cf9d4.sentence: There is widespread consensus among scientists that human activities—especially habitat destruction, resource consumption, and the elimination of species—are the main drivers of the current extinction crisis.

1fb3f62bebbe.title: Holocene extinction
1fb3f62bebbe.sentence: The 2019 Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services, published by the United Nations IPBES, estimated that about one million species are currently at risk of extinction within decades because of human activities.

3f37c93fff53.title: Holocene extinction
3f37c93fff53.sentence: According to a 2023 study published in PNAS, at least 73 genera of animals have gone extinct since 1500.

00a7ca6c0a39.title: Holocene extinction
00a7ca6c0a39.sentence: If humans had never existed, the study estimates it would have taken 18,000 years for the same genera to have disappeared naturally, leading the authors to conclude that "the current generic extinction rates are 35 times higher than expected background rates prevailing in the last million years under the absence of human impacts" and that human civilization is causing the "rapid mutilation of the tree of life".

164b60909b86.title: Holocene extinction
164b60909b86.sentence: Contemporary human overpopulation and continued population growth, along with economic growth and per-capita consumption growth, prominently in the past two centuries, are regarded as the underlying causes of extinction.

7c45b48c6381.title: Holocene extinction
7c45b48c6381.sentence: Stabilizing and gradually reducing human populations; reining in capitalism, decreasing economic demands, and shifting them to economic activities with low impacts on biodiversity; transitioning to plant-based diets; and increasing the number and size of terrestrial and marine protected areas have been suggested to avoid or limit biodiversity loss and a possible sixth mass extinction.

b04bcc0264be.title: Extinction debt
b04bcc0264be.sentence: In ecology, extinction debt is the future extinction of species due to events in the past.

23630525a6f4.title: Extinction debt
23630525a6f4.sentence: Extinction debt occurs because of time delays between impacts on a species, such as destruction of habitat, and the species' ultimate disappearance.

c006dd66f852.title: Extinction debt
c006dd66f852.sentence: For instance, long-lived trees may survive for many years even after reproduction of new trees has become impossible, and thus they may be committed to extinction.

f119434d58c7.title: Extinction debt
f119434d58c7.sentence: The most well-known drivers of extinction debt are habitat fragmentation and habitat destruction.

235e8505021a.title: Extinction debt
235e8505021a.sentence: These cause extinction debt by reducing the ability of species to persist via immigration to new habitats.

3c00528d1247.title: Extinction debt
3c00528d1247.sentence: However, as other patches have been destroyed or rendered inaccessible due to fragmentation, this "insurance" effect is reduced and the species may ultimately become extinct.

cec570391970.title: Extinction debt
cec570391970.sentence: It is most likely to be found in long-lived species and species with very specific habitat requirements (specialists).

c7c51e90bde7.title: Extinction debt
c7c51e90bde7.sentence: The term extinction debt was first used in 1994 in a paper by David Tilman, Robert May, Clarence Lehman and Martin Nowak, although Jared Diamond used the term "relaxation time" to describe a similar phenomenon in 1972.

283b9d7efa28.title: Extinction debt
283b9d7efa28.sentence: In discussions of threats to biodiversity, extinction debt is analogous to the "climate commitment" in climate change, which states that inertia will cause the earth to continue to warm for centuries even if no more greenhouse gasses are emitted.

d06b5187306c.title: Extinction debt
d06b5187306c.sentence: Of extinction from past deforestation in the Amazon, 80–90% has yet to occur, based on modeling based on species-area relationships.

b311c36e292e.title: Extinction debt
b311c36e292e.sentence: On the islands of the Azores Archipelago, more than 95% of native forests have been destroyed in the past 600 years.

aecdaf0d8f87.title: Extinction debt
aecdaf0d8f87.sentence: As a result, more than half of arthropods on these islands are believed to be committed to extinction, with many islands likely to lose more than 90% of species.

416f422dc84e.title: Extinction debt
416f422dc84e.sentence: Protection of existing habitats may not be sufficient to protect species from extinction.

158eef93122b.title: Extinction debt
158eef93122b.sentence: However, the long time scales of extinction debt may allow for habitat restoration in order to prevent extinction, as occurred in the slowing of extinction in Amazon forest birds above.

ae49277b594c.title: Climate change and infectious diseases
ae49277b594c.sentence: Climate change is influencing the transmission and burden of many infectious diseases worldwide.

ed78d42d0651.title: Climate change and infectious diseases
ed78d42d0651.sentence: Warmer and wetter conditions expand suitable habitats for vectors, enabling them to survive in areas that were previously too cold or dry.

4c159cd9a065.title: Climate change and infectious diseases
4c159cd9a065.section: Mechanisms and pathways > Environmental change and zoonotic disease emergence
4c159cd9a065.sentence: Consequently, diseases including dengue fever and Lyme disease have been reported in regions where they were previously uncommon, particularly at higher latitudes and elevations.

61d452b70b62.title: Climate change and infectious diseases
61d452b70b62.sentence: Warmer waters and increased flooding promote the growth and spread of bacteria such as Vibrio cholerae, which causes cholera, and other pathogens responsible for gastroenteritis and wound infections.

dbd1479dd026.title: Climate change and infectious diseases
dbd1479dd026.sentence: Drought and poor access to clean water increase the risk of contamination and exposure to diarrheal diseases, typhoid, and hepatitis A.

b5cd18e3fac0.title: Climate change and infectious diseases
b5cd18e3fac0.section: Mechanisms and pathways > Environmental change and zoonotic disease emergence
b5cd18e3fac0.sentence: Environmental changes associated with climate change, including deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and biodiversity loss, further contribute to zoonotic disease risk.

71edd56b12df.title: Climate change and infectious diseases
71edd56b12df.section: Mechanisms and pathways > Environmental change and zoonotic disease emergence
71edd56b12df.sentence: Alterations in ecosystems may favor species that serve as efficient reservoirs for infectious agents, while increased human encroachment into natural habitats can facilitate pathogen transmission between species.

4997a1e6eae6.title: Climate change and infectious diseases
4997a1e6eae6.sentence: Low-income countries and communities with high socio-economic constraints and limited healthcare, infrastructure and sanitation are the most vulnerable.

1a4b056a8892.title: Climate change and infectious diseases
1a4b056a8892.sentence: Additionally, when countries are forced to contend with a disease like malaria (for example), their prospects for self-sufficiency and prosperity are slowed.

856504e8d753.title: Climate change and infectious diseases

4bdf6b615edc.sentence: Agricultural biodiversity or agrobiodiversity is a subset of general biodiversity pertaining to agriculture.

f76d4f51debd.title: Agricultural biodiversity
f76d4f51debd.sentence: It can be defined as "the variety and variability of animals, plants and micro-organisms at the genetic, species and ecosystem levels that sustain the ecosystem structures, functions and processes in and around production systems, and that provide food and non-food agricultural products." It is managed by farmers, pastoralists, fishers and forest dwellers, agrobiodiversity provides stability, adaptability and resilience and constitutes a key element of the livelihood strategies of rural communities throughout the world.

5e73c83e4257.title: Agricultural biodiversity
5e73c83e4257.sentence: The use of agricultural biodiversity can contribute to food security, nutrition security, and livelihood security, and it is critical for climate adaptation and climate mitigation.

2b7cd820db0a.title: Agricultural biodiversity

697d8d1d084b.title: Agricultural biodiversity

af9872e48d82.title: Agricultural biodiversity
af9872e48d82.sentence: Agrobiodiversity loss leads to genetic erosion, the loss of genetic diversity, including the loss of individual genes, and the loss of particular combinations of genes (or gene complexes) such as those manifested in locally adapted landraces or breeds.

9e7b8b6c9d6b.title: Economics of biodiversity

38bd7a700276.title: Agricultural biodiversity

11d811a7c66a.title: Agricultural biodiversity

4d6442fe559a.title: Agricultural biodiversity

c040c7f3baa2.title: Agricultural biodiversity

5bd8fd6479f0.sentence: Philosophers have attached intrinsic value to different aspects of nature, whether this is individual organisms (biocentrism) or ecological wholes such as species or ecosystems (ecoholism).

472f2560f7dd.title: Nature conservation
472f2560f7dd.sentence: More utilitarian schools of conservation have an anthropocentric outlook and seek a proper valuation of local and global impacts of human activity upon nature in their effect upon human wellbeing, now and to posterity.

f80c7441f285.title: Nature conservation
f80c7441f285.sentence: How such values are assessed and exchanged among people determines the social, political and personal restraints and imperatives by which conservation is practiced.

a66e31dff9c5.title: Nature conservation
a66e31dff9c5.sentence: There is increasing interest in extending the responsibility for human wellbeing to include the welfare of sentient animals.

b12815325ab0.title: Nature conservation
b12815325ab0.sentence: Branches of conservation ethics focusing on sentient individuals include ecofeminism and compassionate conservation.

7a2417bd75b9.title: Desertification

da53d5b2cf93.title: Desertification
da53d5b2cf93.sentence: Drought in the Sahel region is now thought to be principally the result of seasonal variability in rainfall caused by large-scale sea surface temperature variations, largely driven by natural variability and anthropogenic emissions of aerosols (reflective sulphate particles) and greenhouse gases.

139c73b447e9.title: Desertification

00bbe149e78b.title: Desertification

f95aa7f9c3f1.title: Desertification

b0a515dbd7ed.title: Habitat fragmentation
b0a515dbd7ed.sentence: Forest fragmentation is a form of habitat fragmentation where forests are reduced (either naturally or man-made) to relatively small, isolated patches of forest known as forest fragments or forest remnants.

636b4685b786.title: Habitat fragmentation
636b4685b786.sentence: The intervening matrix that separates the remaining woodland patches can be natural open areas, farmland, or developed areas.

279221c4e26b.title: Habitat fragmentation
279221c4e26b.sentence: Forest fragmentation is one of the greatest threats to biodiversity in forests, especially in the tropics.

7a070de1614d.title: Habitat fragmentation
7a070de1614d.sentence: Following the principles of island biogeography, remnant woodlands act like islands of forest in a sea of pastures, fields, subdivisions, shopping malls, etc. These fragments will then begin to undergo the process of ecosystem decay.

5bc7261ebf97.title: Habitat fragmentation
5bc7261ebf97.sentence: Forest patches that are smaller or more isolated will lose species faster than those that are larger or less isolated.

fde2b83e13f2.title: Habitat fragmentation
fde2b83e13f2.sentence: Small populations are at an increased risk of a variety of genetic consequences that influence their long-term survival.

2b2f6c907b63.title: Habitat fragmentation
2b2f6c907b63.sentence: Remnant populations often contain only a subset of the genetic diversity found in the previously continuous habitat.

c429de9d4407.title: Habitat fragmentation
c429de9d4407.section: Implications > Genetic risks > Gene Flow and Inbreeding
c429de9d4407.sentence: When a habitat becomes fragmented and reduced in area, gene flow and migration are typically reduced.

dfa2936d4de7.title: Habitat fragmentation
dfa2936d4de7.sentence: Genetic drift is random changes to the genetic makeup of populations and leads to reductions in genetic diversity.

354b27ec70ef.title: Habitat fragmentation
354b27ec70ef.sentence: The smaller the population is, the more likely genetic drift will be a driving force of evolution rather than natural selection.

9f4ef6932c0f.title: Defaunation
9f4ef6932c0f.sentence: Inbreeding lowers reproduction and survival rates.

13a46e067d5b.title: Defaunation
13a46e067d5b.sentence: It is suggested that these genetic factors contribute to the extinction risk in threatened/endangered species.

1eceb0517ad6.title: Land degradation
1eceb0517ad6.sentence: In high-income countries with intensive agricultural systems, the per hectare production losses from degradation are particularly severe, though often masked by heavy application of synthetic fertilizers and other inputs.

5a91b2184ade.title: Land degradation
5a91b2184ade.sentence: This compensatory strategy creates a troubling paradox: while maintaining high yields in the short term, it generates diminishing returns, increases production costs, and often exacerbates the underlying degradation through soil acidification, nutrient imbalances and pollution.

8d2fd7f8250c.title: Land degradation
8d2fd7f8250c.sentence: Farmers, as private actors, make decisions primarily based on productivity and profitability.

899b1db2d937.title: Land degradation
899b1db2d937.sentence: Land degradation on farms is shaped by local choices and global drivers such as trade, climate change and demographic transitions.

174d4fa12a46.title: Land degradation
174d4fa12a46.sentence: Threshold effects associated with land degradation may lead to land abandonment in areas with a long history of intensive agricultural systems.

508429b80954.title: Land degradation
508429b80954.section: Prevention and reversal > Prevention > Sustainable land management
508429b80954.sentence: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 15 has a target to restore degraded land and soil and achieve a land degradation-neutral world by 2030.

d98ceaae5995.title: Land degradation
d98ceaae5995.section: Prevention and reversal > Prevention > Sustainable land management
d98ceaae5995.sentence: The full title of Target 15.3 is: "By 2030, combat desertification, restore degraded land and soil, including land affected by desertification, drought and floods, and strive to achieve a land degradation-neutral world."

ed06bf217273.title: Land degradation
ed06bf217273.sentence: Second, the estimates exclude impacts on pasturelands and the broader ecosystem services that benefit society at large, making land degradation a challenge requiring collective action for the provision of these public goods.

50558fb490e5.title: Rio Convention
50558fb490e5.section: Goals of the Three Rio Conventions > The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)
50558fb490e5.sentence: Legislatively, the UNCCD is committed to achieving Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) and combat pressing environmental issues of Desertification, land degradation and drought (DLDD) through a newly created 2018-2030 Strategic Framework, consistent with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development This framework follows the 10-year strategic plan and framework for 2008-2018 that aimed to establish global partnerships in working toward the reversal and prevention of desertification and land degradation.

08a2eb5eb61b.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
08a2eb5eb61b.sentence: Its objectives include improving affected ecosystems, combating desertification and land degradation, supporting land degradation neutrality, improving the living conditions of affected populations, strengthening drought resilience, generating global environmental benefits and mobilizing resources for implementation.

2d9ab2bac4c2.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
2d9ab2bac4c2.sentence: These include the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and, under it, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the Strategic Plan for Biodiversity 2020 and its Aichi Biodiversity Targets, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and Paris Agreement, the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification and its target of Land Degradation Neutrality, the Ramsar Convention, and the United Nations Strategic Plan on Forests 2017 – 2030.

1699e202c1a4.title: SLOSS debate
1699e202c1a4.sentence: The SLOSS debate was a debate in ecology and conservation biology during the 1970's and 1980's as to whether a single large or several small (SLOSS) reserves were a superior means of conserving biodiversity in a fragmented habitat.

581e2496f55d.title: Habitat fragmentation
581e2496f55d.sentence: A review of empirical studies found that, of the 381 reported significant effect of habitat fragmentation per se on species occurrences, abundances or diversity in the scientific literature, 76% were positive whereas 24% were negative.

c3ebf6397732.title: Habitat fragmentation
c3ebf6397732.sentence: Positive effects of habitat fragmentation per se imply that several small patches of habitat can have higher conservation value than a single large patch of equivalent size.

641491923849.title: Habitat fragmentation
641491923849.sentence: A large number of small forest "islands" typically cannot support the same biodiversity that a single contiguous forest would hold, even if their combined area is much greater than the single forest.

02e8ef51eca9.title: Habitat fragmentation
02e8ef51eca9.sentence: Land sharing strategies could therefore have more positive impacts on species than land sparing strategies.

ba4496a8af7b.title: Genetic diversity
ba4496a8af7b.section: Coping with low genetic diversity > Human intervention
ba4496a8af7b.sentence: Attempts to increase the viability of a species by increasing genetic diversity is called genetic rescue.

88fe3533faf9.title: Genetic diversity
88fe3533faf9.section: Coping with low genetic diversity > Human intervention
88fe3533faf9.sentence: For example, eight panthers from Texas were introduced to the Florida panther population, which was declining and suffering from inbreeding depression.

a67befe87ae7.title: Genetic diversity
a67befe87ae7.section: Coping with low genetic diversity > Human intervention
a67befe87ae7.sentence: Genetic variation was thus increased and resulted in a significant increase in population growth of the Florida panther.

840edfe786d8.title: Genetic diversity
840edfe786d8.section: Coping with low genetic diversity > Human intervention
840edfe786d8.sentence: Creating or maintaining high genetic diversity is an important consideration in species rescue efforts, in order to ensure the longevity of a population.

a03695888718.title: Genetic diversity
a03695888718.sentence: Selective breeding leads to monocultures: entire farms of nearly genetically identical plants.

eca59416a5b6.title: Genetic diversity
eca59416a5b6.sentence: Little to no genetic diversity makes crops extremely susceptible to widespread disease; bacteria morph and change constantly and when a disease-causing bacterium changes to attack a specific genetic variation, it can easily wipe out vast quantities of the species.

c1b5d320d96b.title: Genetic diversity
c1b5d320d96b.sentence: If the genetic variation that the bacterium is best at attacking happens to be that which humans have selectively bred to use for harvest, the entire crop will be wiped out.

a201f6f91760.title: Genetic diversity
a201f6f91760.sentence: The nineteenth-century Great Famine in Ireland was caused in part by a lack of biodiversity.

ca102b8dd9c9.title: Genetic diversity
ca102b8dd9c9.sentence: Since new potato plants do not come as a result of reproduction, but rather from pieces of the parent plant, no genetic diversity is developed, and the entire crop is essentially a clone of one potato, it is especially susceptible to an epidemic.

5bc5b28b4bde.title: Genetic diversity
5bc5b28b4bde.sentence: Genetic diversity of a population can be assessed by some simple measures.

728d3795bbd3.title: Genetic diversity
728d3795bbd3.sentence: - Gene diversity is the proportion of polymorphic loci across the genome.

592d37852bef.title: Genetic diversity
592d37852bef.sentence: - Heterozygosity is the fraction of individuals in a population that are heterozygous for a particular locus.

3632f9397acf.title: Genetic diversity
3632f9397acf.sentence: - Alleles per locus is also used to demonstrate variability.

30c619202c4a.title: Genetic diversity
30c619202c4a.sentence: - Nucleotide diversity is the extent of nucleotide polymorphisms within a population, and is commonly measured through molecular markers such as micro- and minisatellite sequences, mitochondrial DNA, and single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs).

7a67ec900b6c.title: Genetic diversity
7a67ec900b6c.sentence: Furthermore, stochastic simulation software is commonly used to predict the future of a population given measures such as allele frequency and population size.

40822df59f10.title: Wildlife corridor
40822df59f10.sentence: These structures allow animals to cross human infrastructure (i.e. a highway, canal) which helps to reduce road mortality.

cb3aecbbd71f.title: Wildlife corridor
cb3aecbbd71f.sentence: Wildlife overpasses and underpasses are able to facilitate the movement of different kinds of species, because species exhibit preferences for different types of wildlife crossing infrastructure.

ae8dfd0256aa.title: Wildlife corridor
ae8dfd0256aa.sentence: For example, in Banff National Park, black bears and mountain lions have been observed to prefer wildlife underpasses, which provide a darker, visually protected way to cross the Trans-Canada Highway.

ab2287fa0f35.title: Wildlife corridor
ab2287fa0f35.sentence: The network includes six overpasses and 38 underpasses.

70c0867c7dde.title: Wildlife corridor
70c0867c7dde.sentence: Created by Parks Canada, the project spans over 180 kilometres along the Trans-Canada Highway, and has reduced wildlife collisions by 80%.

cc1276252ca8.title: Wildlife corridor
cc1276252ca8.sentence: Fencing is something to be considered in the design of wildlife corridor infrastructure, as a tool that often complements overpasses and underpasses along road corridors, thereby reducing road mortality.

e536b79bf0d7.title: Abundance (ecology)
e536b79bf0d7.sentence: The two Semi-Quantitive Abundance ratings used are known as the D.A.F.O.R, and the A.C.F.O.R.

0cb6a8c9ee1a.title: Abundance (ecology)
0cb6a8c9ee1a.sentence: - D - Species observed is "Dominant" in a given area.

4f63b7c55166.title: Abundance (ecology)
4f63b7c55166.sentence: - R - Species observed is "Rare" in a given area.

50978272cdb0.title: Abundance (ecology)
50978272cdb0.sentence: These are measurement methods which involve estimation based on viewing a specific area of a designated size.

68a21e1ef19e.title: Abundance (ecology)
68a21e1ef19e.sentence: These methods are useful for getting a rough estimate of the species abundance in a designated area (quadrant), but they are not exact or objective measurements.

682c79e34ee5.title: Abundance (ecology)
682c79e34ee5.sentence: Therefore, if another method of measuring abundance is available, it should be used, as this will lead to more useful and quantifiable data.

7f7c5b37b785.title: Abundance (ecology)
7f7c5b37b785.sentence: SAD is a measurement of how common, or rare species are within an ecosystem.

22fc0a6c0935.title: Abundance (ecology)
22fc0a6c0935.sentence: SAD is one of the most basic measurements in ecology and is used very often, therefore many different methods of measurement and analysis have developed.

74e324e88ed9.title: Abundance (ecology)
74e324e88ed9.sentence: It is common for the distribution of species to be skewed so that a few species take up the bulk of individuals collected.

f7dbafecd542.title: Endemism
f7dbafecd542.sentence: Paleoendemism refers to species that were formerly widespread but are now restricted to a smaller area.

b5322cede42a.title: Endemism
b5322cede42a.sentence: Neoendemism refers to species that have recently arisen, such as through divergence and reproductive isolation or through hybridization and polyploidy in plants, and have not dispersed beyond a limited range.

34d3a370dfe0.title: Endemism
34d3a370dfe0.sentence: Using this work, Ledyard Stebbins and Jack Major then introduced the concepts of neoendemics and paleoendemics in 1965 to describe the endemics of California.

c12830f389cd.title: Endemism
c12830f389cd.sentence: The ginkgo tree, Ginkgo biloba, is one example of a paleoendemic species.

c6415e5ba545.title: Endemism
c6415e5ba545.sentence: The concept of phylogenetic endemism has also been used to measure the relative uniqueness of the species endemic to an area.

8f043f4b81d8.title: Endemism
8f043f4b81d8.sentence: This captures not only the total number of taxa endemic to the area (taxonomic endemism) but also how distant those species are from their living relatives.

0c1ccb1e8de2.title: Endemism
0c1ccb1e8de2.sentence: Different categorizations of endemism also capture the uniqueness and irreplaceability of biodiversity hotspots differently and impact how those hotspots are defined, affecting how resources for conservation are allocated.

b6d982eb4dff.title: Species evenness
b6d982eb4dff.sentence: Species evenness describes the commonness or rarity of a species; it requires knowing the abundance of each species relative to those of the other species within the community.

7d0fd2bfae9c.title: Species diversity
7d0fd2bfae9c.sentence: Species evenness quantifies how equal the abundances of the species are.

669ab67fec01.title: Species evenness
669ab67fec01.sentence: Species evenness is combined with species richness, (the number of species in the community), in order to determine species diversity, which is an important measure of community structure.

82308d3b95c1.title: Species evenness
82308d3b95c1.sentence: In community A, one of the species constitutes 80% of the individuals in the community, while the remaining three species comprise only 20% of the individuals in the community.

38dd46b26f74.title: Species evenness
38dd46b26f74.sentence: In community B, the number of individuals are evenly divided among the four species, (25% each).

1a30eb8155de.title: Species evenness
1a30eb8155de.sentence: Therefore, community A has lower species evenness than community B. When comparing the two communities, even though each has the same species richness of four species, community B has the higher species diversity because it has higher species evenness.

5f5cc33c42e6.title: Species evenness
5f5cc33c42e6.sentence: Area-based counts, distance methods, and mark and recapture studies are the three general categories of methods for estimating abundance.

d8ea71d375f6.title: Species diversity
d8ea71d375f6.sentence: Species diversity is the number of different species that are represented in a given community (a dataset).

e569fe8d79d1.title: Species diversity
e569fe8d79d1.sentence: Meanings of species diversity may include species richness, taxonomic or phylogenetic diversity, and/or species evenness.

0fcf5991f4ce.title: Species diversity
0fcf5991f4ce.sentence: The effective number of species refers to the number of equally abundant species needed to obtain the same mean proportional species abundance as that observed in the dataset of interest (where all species may not be equally abundant).

c86d83c3c2e3.title: Species diversity
c86d83c3c2e3.sentence: Such indices include species richness, the Shannon index, the Simpson index, and the complement of the Simpson index (also known as the Gini-Simpson index).

582269515fe9.title: Species diversity
582269515fe9.sentence: When interpreted in ecological terms, each one of these indices corresponds to a different thing, and their values are therefore not directly comparable.

0d0e1bf976ee.title: Species diversity
0d0e1bf976ee.sentence: Extrapolation from the sample to the underlying population of interest is not straightforward, because the species diversity of the available sample generally gives an underestimation of the species diversity in the entire population.

a57fcb09b7c5.title: Species diversity
a57fcb09b7c5.sentence: When species diversity values are compared among sets, sampling efforts need to be standardised in an appropriate way for the comparisons to yield ecologically meaningful results.

611a1bb74c6a.title: Species diversity
611a1bb74c6a.sentence: Increasing the area sampled increases observed species diversity both because more individuals get included in the sample and because large areas are environmentally more heterogeneous than small areas.

dffcecc66d38.title: Alpha diversity
dffcecc66d38.sentence: In ecology, alpha diversity (α-diversity) is the mean species diversity in a site at a local scale.

a797292c9fd2.title: Alpha diversity
a797292c9fd2.sentence: The term was introduced by R. H. Whittaker together with the terms beta diversity (β-diversity) and gamma diversity (γ-diversity).

b26b984515df.title: Alpha diversity
b26b984515df.sentence: Whittaker's idea was that the total species diversity in a landscape (gamma diversity) is determined by two different things, the mean species diversity in sites at a more local scale (alpha diversity) and the differentiation among those sites (beta diversity).

8ce698a9af20.title: Alpha diversity
8ce698a9af20.sentence: Both the area and landscape of interest and the sites within it may be of very different sizes in different situations, and no consensus has been reached on what spatial scales are appropriate to quantify alpha diversity.

60b6d1bef23f.title: Alpha diversity
60b6d1bef23f.sentence: It has therefore been proposed that the definition of alpha diversity does not need to be tied to a specific spatial scale: alpha diversity can be measured for an existing dataset that consists of subunits at any scale.

a278b8943493.title: Alpha diversity
a278b8943493.sentence: Often researchers use the values given by one or more diversity indices, such as species richness (which is simply a count of species), the Shannon index or the Simpson index (which take into account also species proportional abundances).

d905d1dde1b6.title: Measurement of biodiversity
d905d1dde1b6.sentence: A variety of objective means exist to empirically measure biodiversity.

b58bf971d981.title: Measurement of biodiversity
b58bf971d981.sentence: Biodiversity is commonly measured in terms of taxonomic richness of a geographic area over a time interval.

1f6b0d26d8b2.title: Measurement of biodiversity
1f6b0d26d8b2.sentence: In order to calculate biodiversity, species evenness, species richness, and species diversity are to be obtained first.

7ec4280e0390.title: Measurement of biodiversity
7ec4280e0390.sentence: Species diversity is the relationship between species evenness and species richness.

4163b1b9a950.title: Measurement of biodiversity
4163b1b9a950.sentence: However, the two most popular are Shannon-Weaver diversity index, commonly referred to as Shannon diversity index, and the other is Simpsons diversity index.

4357d8b29a29.title: Measurement of biodiversity
4357d8b29a29.sentence: - Alpha diversity refers to diversity within a particular area, community or ecosystem, and is measured by counting the number of taxa within the ecosystem (usually species)

fb790b440a65.title: Measurement of biodiversity
fb790b440a65.sentence: - Beta diversity is species diversity between ecosystems; this involves comparing the number of taxa that are unique to each of the ecosystems.

e81ed2956ddb.title: Measurement of biodiversity
e81ed2956ddb.sentence: - Gamma diversity is a measurement of the overall diversity for different ecosystems within a region.

94f1b45b7f31.title: Measurement of biodiversity
94f1b45b7f31.sentence: Each measure of biodiversity relates to a particular use of the data.

ff82775a7c88.title: Measurement of biodiversity
ff82775a7c88.sentence: For others, a more economically defensible definition should allow the ensuring of continued possibilities for both adaptation and future use by humans, assuring environmental sustainability.

5245fdb71bd7.title: Measurement of biodiversity
5245fdb71bd7.sentence: Since it cannot always be said which genes are more likely to prove beneficial, the best choice for conservation is to assure the persistence of as many genes as possible.

d279025f6f04.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
d279025f6f04.sentence: The diversity of species and genes in ecological communities affects the functioning of these communities.

e4a091d8b47a.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
e4a091d8b47a.sentence: The two main areas where the effect of biodiversity on ecosystem function have been studied are the relationship between diversity and productivity, and the relationship between diversity and community stability.

56eec87714c2.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
56eec87714c2.sentence: More biologically diverse communities appear to be more productive (in terms of biomass production) than are less diverse communities, and they appear to be more stable in the face of perturbations.

02a4aa72bbea.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
02a4aa72bbea.sentence: It is generally measured by taking the total aboveground biomass of all plants in an area.

c9e274ce5cc2.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
c9e274ce5cc2.section: Effects on community productivity > Review of data
c9e274ce5cc2.sentence: Field experiments to test the degree to which diversity affects community productivity have had variable results, but many long-term studies in grassland ecosystems have found that diversity does indeed enhance the productivity of ecosystems.

a7264e72c4fd.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
a7264e72c4fd.section: Effects on community productivity > Review of data
a7264e72c4fd.sentence: Specifically, a diversity in the functional roles of the species may be a more important quality for predicting productivity than the diversity in species number.

18e0fe790ea7.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
18e0fe790ea7.section: Productivity and stability as indicators of ecosystem health
18e0fe790ea7.sentence: Thus, if there is indeed a link between diversity and stability, it is likely that losses of diversity could feedback on themselves, causing even more losses of species.

a3a31c4f880e.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
a3a31c4f880e.section: Productivity and stability as indicators of ecosystem health
a3a31c4f880e.sentence: Losing species means losing potential foods, medicines, industrial products, and tourism, all of which have a direct economic effect on peoples lives.

63eb0003dc89.title: Habitat fragmentation
63eb0003dc89.sentence: Furthermore, habitat fragmentation alters relationships between biodiversity and ecosystem functioning across multiple scales, affecting both the local loss of biodiversity and the local loss of function.

a50c5c322345.title: Rescue effect
a50c5c322345.sentence: This populational process explains how the migration of individuals can increase the persistence of small isolated populations by helping to stabilize a metapopulation, thus reducing the chances of extinction.

6104599083b8.title: Rescue effect
6104599083b8.sentence: In other words, immigration can lead to the recolonization of previously extinct patches, promoting the long-term persistence of the network of populations.

273e7caeb529.title: Rescue effect
273e7caeb529.sentence: The rescue effect is a phenomenon which was first described by Brown and Kodric-Brown, and is commonly used in metapopulation dynamics and many other disciplines in ecology.

35f2f2981465.title: Habitat fragmentation
35f2f2981465.sentence: In an unfragmented landscape a declining population can be "rescued" by immigration from a nearby expanding population.

e8de070d19c3.title: Habitat fragmentation
e8de070d19c3.sentence: In fragmented landscapes, the distance between fragments may prevent this from happening.

20f631e0c056.sentence: Deforestation changes the landscape and reflectivity of earth's surface, i.e. decreasing Albedo.

c08acc9b23d9.section: Effects of deforestation from climate change

36c15c2430d8.sentence: As a consequence of reduced evapotranspiration, precipitation is also reduced.

9fbafceb4570.sentence: This implies having a hotter and drier climate, and a longer dry season.

5b2dcdb7bc84.sentence: This change in climate has drastic ecological and global impacts including increases in severity and frequency of fires, and disruption in the pollination process that will likely spread beyond the area of deforestation.

489248653599.sentence: A 2025 study using statistical models to separate the effects of deforestation and global climate change across 29 areas in the Brazilian Legal Amazon estimated that deforestation accounted for approximately 74% of the decline in dry-season precipitation over 1985–2020.

a98db078a804.section: Effects of deforestation from climate change > Changes in rainfall
a98db078a804.sentence: By the year 2100, researchers anticipate that deforestation in the Congo will diminish regional precipitation levels by up to 8-10%.

613c5772fae9.sentence: Frederick Chen has stated that there are two main solutions to attack the supply side of poaching to reduce its effects: enforcing and enacting more policies and laws for conservation, and encouraging local communities to protect the wildlife around them by giving them more land rights.

5caf4e4188f6.title: Poaching
5caf4e4188f6.sentence: While approaches to dilute mitigate poaching from a supply-side may not be the best option as people can become more willing to purchase rarer items, especially in countries gaining more wealth and therefore higher demand for illicit goods—Frederick Chen still advocates that we should also focus on exploring ways to reduce the demand for these goods to better stop the problem of poaching.

5c9aacce6665.title: Poaching
5c9aacce6665.sentence: The former deals with people desiring a product due to many other people buying it, while the latter is similar but with one distinct difference: people will clamour to buy something if it denotes wealth that only a few elites could possibly afford.

a361d82f2546.title: Poaching
a361d82f2546.sentence: Therefore, the snob effect would offset some of the gains made by anti-poaching laws, regulations, or practices: if a portion of the supply is cut off, the rarity and price of the object would increase, and only a select few would have the desire and purchasing power for it.

4175651b25cc.title: Poaching
4175651b25cc.sentence: Indeed, there is some evidence that interventions to reduce consumer demand may be more effective for combatting poaching than continually increased policing to catch poachers.

902ad2fccadc.title: Poaching
902ad2fccadc.sentence: However, almost no groups deploying interventions that attempt to reduce consumer demand evaluate the impact of their actions.

7f2260a1ceba.title: CITES
7f2260a1ceba.section: Shortcomings and concerns > Approach to biodiversity conservation
7f2260a1ceba.sentence: Listing the species on Appendix I increased the price of rhino horn (which fueled more poaching), but the species survived wherever there was adequate on-the-ground protection.

734f1b4d5539.title: Flagship species
734f1b4d5539.sentence: In conservation biology, a flagship species is a species chosen to raise support for biodiversity conservation in a given place or social context.

9b82aba56f21.title: Flagship species
9b82aba56f21.sentence: The species need to be popular, to work as symbols or icons, and to stimulate people to provide money or support.

12d0ce0fa9c5.title: Flagship species
12d0ce0fa9c5.sentence: Definitions have varied, but they have tended to focus on the strategic goals and the socio-economic nature of the concept, to support the marketing of a conservation effort.

de9a3e5a83e8.title: Flagship species
de9a3e5a83e8.sentence: Most of the latest definitions focus on the strategic, socio-economic, and marketing character of the concept.

2bf6dd19b8f0.title: Flagship species
2bf6dd19b8f0.sentence: Chosen flagship species are often charismatic, well-known species: see the Bengal tiger (Panthera tigris), the giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), the Golden lion tamarin (Leontopithecus rosalia), the African elephant (Loxodonta sp.) and Asian elephant (Elephas maximus).

8ba3560fab11.title: Flagship species
8ba3560fab11.sentence: - They can skew the management and conservation priorities in their favour, to the detriment of more threatened but less charismatic species.

c92cda3825c3.title: Flagship species
c92cda3825c3.sentence: Leaving aside the impact on other species, charisma does not seem to protect even charismatic species against extinction.

769f52b1474a.title: Flagship species
769f52b1474a.sentence: All ten of the most charismatic groups of animal identified in a 2018 study, namely tiger, lion, elephant, giraffe, leopard, panda, cheetah, polar bear, wolf, and gorilla, are currently endangered; only the giant panda shows a demographic growth from an extremely small population.

6bc9101acaa7.title: Flagship species
6bc9101acaa7.sentence: A major challenge for the utilization of several flagship species in non-Western contexts is that they may come into conflict with local communities, thereby jeopardizing well-intended conservation actions.

7b1e625918b6.title: Flagship species
7b1e625918b6.sentence: This has been termed "flagship mutiny", and is exemplified by the Asian elephant in countries where there is human-elephant conflict.

15b4ba835ab1.title: Extinction event

25ed0de21971.title: Extinction event
25ed0de21971.section: The "Big Five" mass extinction events > Late Devonian mass extinction, 372 Ma
25ed0de21971.sentence: The Late Devonian was an epoch with high diversity loss, concentrated into two major extinction events.

b95d6ce749be.title: Extinction event
b95d6ce749be.section: The "Big Five" mass extinction events > Triassic–Jurassic extinction event, 201.3 Ma
b95d6ce749be.sentence: The End Triassic extinction marks the Triassic–Jurassic transition.

1b92e2ea4eed.title: Extinction event
1b92e2ea4eed.section: The "Big Five" mass extinction events > Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, 66 Ma
1b92e2ea4eed.sentence: The End Cretaceous extinction, or the K–Pg extinction (formerly K–T extinction), occurred at the Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) – Paleogene (Danian) transition.

cacb4ff0b45b.title: Extinction event
cacb4ff0b45b.section: The "Big Five" mass extinction events > Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, 66 Ma
cacb4ff0b45b.sentence: About 17% of all families, 50% of all genera and 75% of all species became extinct.

fbb165b92239.title: Extinction
fbb165b92239.sentence: The Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event (K–Pg) occurred 66 million years ago, at the end of the Cretaceous period; it is best known for having wiped out non-avian dinosaurs, among many other species.

a173cbd9c714.title: Extinction event
a173cbd9c714.sentence: The "Big Five" cannot be so clearly defined, but rather appear to represent the largest (or some of the largest) of a relatively smooth continuum of extinction events.

7c081ec4d1e9.title: Extinction event
7c081ec4d1e9.section: The "Big Five" mass extinction events > Discussion of the five extinction events
7c081ec4d1e9.sentence: Despite the common presentation focusing only on these five events, no measure of extinction shows any definite line separating them from the many other Phanerozoic extinction events that appear only slightly lesser catastrophes; further, using different methods of calculating an extinction's impact can lead to other events featuring in the top five.

934058da009e.title: Extinction risk from climate change
934058da009e.section: Extinction risk estimates for all species > Fossil-based estimates
934058da009e.sentence: 2021 research found that the "Big Five" mass extinctions were associated with a warming of around 5.2 °C (9.4 °F).

868253aa6487.title: Alpha diversity
868253aa6487.sentence: The effective number of species is the number of equally-abundant species needed to obtain the same mean proportional species abundance as that observed in the dataset of interest (where all species may not be equally abundant).

aa6a13424c46.title: Diversity index
aa6a13424c46.section: Effective number of species or Hill numbers
aa6a13424c46.sentence: True diversity, or the effective number of types, refers to the number of equally abundant types needed for the average proportional abundance of the types to equal that observed in the dataset of interest (where all types may not be equally abundant).

28af46799146.title: Alpha diversity
28af46799146.sentence: However, it has been argued that it would be better to use the effective number of species as the universal measure of species diversity.

7b58b13de282.title: Alpha diversity
7b58b13de282.sentence: This measure allows weighting rare and abundant species in different ways, just as the diversity indices collectively do, but its meaning is intuitively easier to understand.

9d657241dac1.title: Diversity index
9d657241dac1.section: Effective number of species or Hill numbers
9d657241dac1.sentence: The numbers qD are called Hill numbers of order q or effective number of species.

bc8612d0ba48.title: Diversity index
bc8612d0ba48.section: Sensitivity of the diversity value to rare vs. abundant species
bc8612d0ba48.sentence: It defines the sensitivity of the true diversity to rare vs. abundant species by modifying how the weighted mean of the species' proportional abundances is calculated.

5f6ea60afda0.title: Diversity index
5f6ea60afda0.section: Sensitivity of the diversity value to rare vs. abundant species
5f6ea60afda0.sentence: At q = 0, the effective number of species, 0D, hence equals the actual number of species R. In the context of diversity, q is generally limited to non-negative values.

6f0716af57bd.title: Diversity index
6f0716af57bd.section: Sensitivity of the diversity value to rare vs. abundant species
6f0716af57bd.sentence: This leads to obtaining a larger Mq−1 value and a smaller true diversity (qD) value with increasing q.

6a2d40f6777c.title: Diversity index
6a2d40f6777c.sentence: The most commonly used diversity indices are simple transformations of the effective number of types (also known as 'true diversity'), but each diversity index can also be interpreted in its own right as a measure corresponding to some real phenomenon (but a different one for each diversity index).

e04834c77dc7.title: Species diversity
e04834c77dc7.sentence: Species diversity in a dataset can be calculated by first taking the weighted average of species proportional abundances in the dataset, and then taking the inverse of this.

c4fb5adcc0fd.title: Species diversity
c4fb5adcc0fd.sentence: The denominator equals mean proportional species abundance in the dataset as calculated with the weighted generalized mean with exponent q - 1.

d97c89933fd4.title: Species diversity
d97c89933fd4.sentence: The value of q determines which mean is used. q = 0 corresponds to the weighted harmonic mean, which is 1/S because the pi values cancel out, with the result that 0D is equal to the number of species or species richness, S. q = 1 is undefined, except that the limit as q approaches 1 is well defined:

01379b9cea25.title: Species diversity
01379b9cea25.sentence: which is the exponential of the Shannon entropy.

0b89372c15c0.title: Species diversity
0b89372c15c0.sentence: In practice, q modifies species weighting, such that increasing q increases the weight given to the most abundant species, and fewer equally abundant species are hence needed to reach mean proportional abundance.

3b38d613eda4.title: Species diversity
3b38d613eda4.sentence: Consequently, large values of q lead to smaller species diversity than small values of q for the same dataset.

07af0afdddde.title: Species diversity
07af0afdddde.sentence: If all species are equally abundant in the dataset, changing the value of q has no effect, but species diversity at any value of q equals species richness.

9f2522285e18.title: Diversity index
9f2522285e18.sentence: Then the Shannon entropy quantifies the uncertainty in predicting the species identity of an individual that is taken at random from the dataset.

5866628bba21.title: Diversity index
5866628bba21.sentence: The measure was originally proposed by Claude Shannon in 1948 to quantify the entropy (hence Shannon entropy, related to Shannon information content) in strings of text.

3c923c800ab7.title: Diversity index
3c923c800ab7.sentence: The idea is that the more letters there are, and the closer their proportional abundances in the string of interest, the more difficult it is to correctly predict which letter will be the next one in the string.

27a3a37c2685.title: Diversity index
27a3a37c2685.sentence: Each log base corresponds to a different measurement unit, which has been called binary digits (bits), decimal digits (decits), and natural digits (nats) for the bases 2, 10 and e, respectively.

bc3738b38a12.title: Diversity index
bc3738b38a12.section: Effective number of species or Hill numbers
bc3738b38a12.sentence: which is the exponential of the Shannon entropy calculated with natural logarithms (see above).

4b47907e75fe.title: Diversity index
4b47907e75fe.sentence: The Simpson index was introduced in 1949 by Edward H. Simpson to measure the degree of concentration when individuals are classified into types.

685d49f335d6.title: Diversity index
685d49f335d6.sentence: The measure equals the probability that two entities taken at random from the dataset of interest represent the same type.

5b981fa84a95.title: Diversity index
5b981fa84a95.sentence: As a result, the same measure is usually known as the Simpson index in ecology, and as the Herfindahl index or the Herfindahl–Hirschman index (HHI) in economics.

15234bd43b77.title: Diversity index
15234bd43b77.sentence: Its transformation 1 − λ, therefore, equals the probability that the two entities represent different types.

17a0ef3c06e0.title: Diversity index
17a0ef3c06e0.sentence: This simply equals true diversity of order 2, i.e. the effective number of types that is obtained when the weighted arithmetic mean is used to quantify average proportional abundance of types in the dataset of interest.

426094737396.title: Biodiversity hotspot

eddd5051ebd3.title: Biodiversity hotspot

e3754edbcfdd.title: Biodiversity hotspot

625ec15d0b88.title: Bushmeat

1fc500cda485.title: Bushmeat
1fc500cda485.sentence: Over 30 years of data link sharp declines in both mammal populations and the biomass of 41 wildlife species with a decreased supply of fish.

36e196b2b1b7.title: Bushmeat

16e6860d9258.title: Bushmeat
16e6860d9258.section: Role in spread of diseases > HIV
16e6860d9258.sentence: It is likely that HIV was initially transferred to humans after having come into contact with infected bushmeat.

53a5e97b32fe.title: Bushmeat
53a5e97b32fe.sentence: Outbreaks of the Ebola virus in the Congo Basin and in Gabon in the 1990s have been associated with the butchering and consumption of chimpanzees and bonobos.

b268ed832489.title: Bushmeat
b268ed832489.sentence: The emergence of disease is influenced by environmental and socioeconomic factors, including deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and expanding human activity in wildlife habitats.

c43bbc535f52.title: Bushmeat

6f3bd6722b86.title: Bushmeat

195534a5f11f.title: Deforestation

195534a5f11f.sentence: Deforestation eliminates a great number of species of plants and animals which also often results in exposure of people to zoonotic diseases.

9fb463ed29e8.title: Deforestation
9fb463ed29e8.section: Impacts > On human health > Infectious diseases
9fb463ed29e8.sentence: Forest-associated diseases include malaria, Chagas disease (also known as American trypanosomiasis), African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness), leishmaniasis, Lyme disease, HIV and Ebola.

98e3a0f05e5f.title: Deforestation
98e3a0f05e5f.section: Impacts > On human health > Infectious diseases
98e3a0f05e5f.sentence: The majority of new infectious diseases affecting humans, including the SARS-CoV-2 virus that caused the COVID-19 pandemic, are zoonotic and their emergence may be linked to habitat loss due to forest area change and the expansion of human populations into forest areas, which both increase human exposure to wildlife.

8b54f5c02878.title: Deforestation

8b54f5c02878.sentence: In Malaysia, thousands of acres of forest have been cleared for pig farms.

8a01ba7c8b72.title: Deforestation
8a01ba7c8b72.section: Impacts > On human health > Infectious diseases
8a01ba7c8b72.sentence: This has resulted in an increase in the spread of the Nipah virus.

60e8a879c001.title: Habitat conservation
60e8a879c001.sentence: Pearce and Moran outlined the following method for classifying environmental uses:

07ec2d43cf46.title: Habitat conservation
07ec2d43cf46.sentence: - Direct extractive uses: e.g. timber from forests, food from plants and animals

fda321f27152.title: Habitat conservation
fda321f27152.sentence: - Indirect uses: e.g. ecosystem services like flood control, pest control, erosion protection

a0ec773639fa.title: Habitat conservation
a0ec773639fa.sentence: - Optional uses: future possibilities e.g. unknown but potential use of plants in chemistry/medicine

f5df8981939a.title: Habitat conservation
f5df8981939a.sentence: - Bequest value (benefit of an individual who knows that others may benefit from it in future)

1b850f578f69.title: Habitat conservation

945da4d775d3.title: Habitat conservation
945da4d775d3.sentence: Habitat restoration is a subset of habitat conservation and its goals include improving the habitat and resources ranging from one species to several species The Society for Ecological Restoration's International Science and Policy Working Group define restoration as "the process of assisting the recovery of an ecosystem that has been degraded, damaged, or destroyed." The scale of habitat restoration efforts can range from small to large areas of land depending on the goal of the project.

e20ec68eb4fa.title: Habitat conservation
e20ec68eb4fa.sentence: Elements of habitat restoration include developing a plan and embedding goals within that plan, and monitoring and evaluating species.

f3d5b50ee1fa.title: Habitat conservation
f3d5b50ee1fa.sentence: Efforts to restore habitats that have been altered by anthropogenic activities has become a global endeavor, and is used to counteract the effects of habitat destruction by humans.

a5da4fc0a3f8.title: Habitat conservation
a5da4fc0a3f8.sentence: Miller and Hobbs state three constraints on restoration: "ecological, economic, and social" constraints.
