785eaa34f944.sentence: Legalising the trade of products derived from endangered species is highly controversial.

efc0f335142a.title: Wildlife trade
efc0f335142a.section: Legal wildlife trade > Legalising trade for endangered species
efc0f335142a.sentence: Many researchers have proposed that a well regulated legal market could benefit some endangered species by either flooding the market with products that drive down the price of illegal products, decreasing the incentive to illegally harvest, or by providing revenue that could fund the species's conservation.

abf274933f1c.title: Wildlife trade
abf274933f1c.section: Legal wildlife trade > Legalising trade for endangered species
abf274933f1c.sentence: However, laundering and corruption pose a major obstacle to implementing such policies, as illegal harvesters attempt to disguise illegal product as legal when trade is legalized.

1c11fcc4c8b4.title: Wildlife trade
1c11fcc4c8b4.section: Legal wildlife trade > Legalising trade for endangered species
1c11fcc4c8b4.sentence: Under the Convention on International Trade of Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), species listed under Appendix I are threatened with extinction, and commercial trade in wild-caught specimens, or products derived from them, is prohibited.

6c398243b629.title: Wildlife trade
6c398243b629.section: Legal wildlife trade > Legalising trade for endangered species
6c398243b629.sentence: Commercial trade of endangered species listed under Appendix II and III is not prohibited, although Parties must provide non-detriment finding to show that the species in the wild is not being unsustainably harvested for the purpose of trade.

fd31ac1f10ed.title: Defaunation
fd31ac1f10ed.sentence: Defaunation in the ocean has occurred later and less intensely than on land.

4bf556253d24.title: Defaunation

4b90fa6612dd.title: Defaunation
4b90fa6612dd.sentence: A relatively small number of marine species have been driven to extinction.

3efb81c2a955.title: Defaunation

551036a97f1a.title: Defaunation

2cb135ba0243.title: Crop wild relative
2cb135ba0243.sentence: A crop wild relative (CWR) is a wild plant closely related to a domesticated plant.

ba64cc2f259d.title: Crop wild relative
ba64cc2f259d.sentence: It may be a wild ancestor of the domesticated (cultivated) plant or another closely related taxon.

03723ad1f9f6.title: Crop wild relative
03723ad1f9f6.sentence: Their natural selection in the wild accumulates a rich set of useful traits that can be introduced into crop plants by crossing.

f324df2695a3.title: Crop wild relative
f324df2695a3.sentence: CWRs have contributed many useful genes to crop plants, and modern varieties of most major crops now contain genes from their wild relatives.

b346acff4042.title: Crop wild relative
b346acff4042.sentence: It was Nikolai Vavilov, the Russian botanist who first realized the importance of crop wild relatives in the early 20th century.

5855ea480854.title: Crop wild relative
5855ea480854.sentence: With the advent of anthropogenic climate change and greater ecosystem instability CWRs are likely to prove a critical resource in ensuring food security for the new millennium.

4c0bf5495fc8.title: Crop wild relative
4c0bf5495fc8.sentence: In 2016, 29% of wild relative plant species were completely missing from the world’s genebanks, with a further 24% represented by fewer than 10 samples.

dbee1620a963.title: Empty forest
dbee1620a963.sentence: An "empty forest" refers to an ecosystem that is void of large mammals.

d62934aaa64a.title: Empty forest
d62934aaa64a.sentence: Empty forests are characterized by an otherwise excellent habitat, and often have large, fully grown trees, although they lack large mammals as a result of human impact.

a4c095ecb0d9.title: Empty forest
a4c095ecb0d9.sentence: Empty forest is a term coined by Kent H. Redford's article "The Empty Forest" (1992), which was published in BioScience.

0d8877ab7643.title: Empty forest
0d8877ab7643.sentence: Even though certain animals may not have become completely extinct, they may have declined in numbers to the point that they have suffered an ecological extinction.

6e3e270e6d63.title: Empty forest

78384aea087a.title: Empty forest
78384aea087a.sentence: In areas with heavy hunting, the biomass of mammalian game species can decrease by 93.7%.

8afd88bed6d4.title: Empty forest

e658cbaad4d7.title: Empty forest

6bcb27ac8479.title: Empty forest
6bcb27ac8479.sentence: An absence of large predators seems to result in uneven densities of prey species.

94e0555fac86.title: Key Biodiversity Area
94e0555fac86.sentence: Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs) are geographical regions that have been determined to be of international importance in terms of biodiversity conservation, using globally standardized criteria published by the IUCN as part of a collaboration between scientists, conservation groups, and government bodies across the world.

204265493a3b.title: Key Biodiversity Area
204265493a3b.sentence: The purpose of Key Biodiversity Areas is to identify regions that are in need of protection by governments or other agencies.

25b615ef4770.title: Key Biodiversity Area
25b615ef4770.sentence: KBAs extend the Important Bird Area (IBA) concept to other taxonomic groups and are now being identified in many parts of the world.

35b7de9ae427.title: Key Biodiversity Area
35b7de9ae427.sentence: The determination of KBAs often brings sites onto the conservation agenda that hadn't previously been identified as needing protection due to the nature of the two non-exclusive criteria used to determine them; vulnerability; and irreplaceability.

812ba1208753.title: Key Biodiversity Area
812ba1208753.sentence: The KBA global standard was published in 2016.

1e19b52aed48.title: Key Biodiversity Area
1e19b52aed48.sentence: The KBA standard has been applied around the globe to over 16,000 areas with a total 21,000,000 km2, which can be viewed in map form.

2d628a58d556.title: Key Biodiversity Area
2d628a58d556.sentence: Criteria may also be too broad, as one analysis found that between 26% and 68% of all terrestrial land on Earth could be classified as a KBA.

76be65d1ddf6.title: Extinction debt

5c22d7793fe0.title: Extinction debt

82ce523fd57e.title: Extinction debt

564d04bf9a92.title: In-situ conservation

5eae94b51cd5.sentence: Since 2004, and 30 years following the invention of the biosphere reserve concept, there have been about 459 conservation areas developed in 97 countries.

80ec179f06e6.title: In-situ conservation
80ec179f06e6.sentence: It includes both biosphere reserves as well as national parks.

c92f5d732f99.title: In-situ conservation
c92f5d732f99.sentence: In agriculture, in situ conservation techniques are an effective way to improve, maintain, and use traditional or native varieties of agricultural crops.

0bcb46adfafa.title: In-situ conservation
0bcb46adfafa.sentence: Such methodologies link the positive output of scientific research with farmers' experience and field work.

86a5e0c9f6da.title: In-situ conservation
86a5e0c9f6da.sentence: First, the accessions of a variety stored at a germplasm bank and those of the same variety multiplied by farmers are jointly tested in the producers field and in the laboratory, under different situations and stresses.

c4e1f48e6af4.title: In-situ conservation
c4e1f48e6af4.sentence: Later, the best tested accessions are crossed, mixed, and multiplied under replicable situations.

682a1747be59.title: In-situ conservation
682a1747be59.sentence: At last, these improved accessions are supplied to the producers.

7dcfc6c9bd5e.title: In-situ conservation
7dcfc6c9bd5e.sentence: Thus, farmers are enabled to crop improved selections of their own varieties, instead of being lured to substitute their own varieties with commercial ones or to abandon their crop.

c1318ab73ba7.title: In-situ conservation
c1318ab73ba7.sentence: This technique of conservation of agricultural biodiversity is more successful in marginal areas, where commercial varieties are not expedient, due to climate and soil fertility constraints, or where the taste and cooking characteristics of traditional varieties compensate for their lower yields.

3e63d9152797.title: Extinction risk from climate change
3e63d9152797.sentence: Assisted migration is the act of moving plants or animals to a different habitat.

598ceccfc046.title: Extinction risk from climate change
598ceccfc046.sentence: A more radical approach is the assisted migration of species endangered by climate change to new habitats, whether passively (through measures like the creation of wildlife corridors to allow them to move to a new area unimpeded), or their active transport to new areas.

4af76e43b7b2.title: Extinction risk from climate change
4af76e43b7b2.sentence: It has been proposed as a way to rescue species which may not be able to disperse easily, have long generation times or have small populations.

0232872416de.title: Extinction risk from climate change
0232872416de.sentence: This strategy has already been implemented to save multiple tree species in North America.

81553634018f.title: Extinction risk from climate change
81553634018f.sentence: This is approach is more controversial, since some of the rescued species may end up invasive in their new locations.

92dc2c49fe3a.title: Global biodiversity
92dc2c49fe3a.sentence: There are several indicators used that describe trends in global biodiversity.

842b548a11dd.title: Global biodiversity
842b548a11dd.sentence: The Living Planet Index (LPI) is a population-based indicator that combines data from individual populations of many vertebrate species to create a single index.

58c71a00dc1f.title: Global biodiversity
58c71a00dc1f.sentence: The Global LPI for 2012 decreased by 28%.

d0874225e5d7.title: Global biodiversity
d0874225e5d7.sentence: The Red List Index is based on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species and measures changes in conservation status over time and currently includes taxa that have been completely categorized: mammals, birds, amphibians and corals.

3c65a3d6cd08.title: Global biodiversity
3c65a3d6cd08.sentence: However, there is no single indicator for all extant species as not all have been described and measured over time.

5a90e3cbb1ad.title: Global biodiversity
5a90e3cbb1ad.sentence: Challenges to these indices due to data availability are taxonomic gaps and the length of time of each index.

85bb5ee620fa.title: Measurement of biodiversity
85bb5ee620fa.sentence: The Biodiversity Intactness Index (BII) measures biodiversity change using abundance data on plants, fungi and animals worldwide.

6d59589a8276.title: Measurement of biodiversity
6d59589a8276.sentence: The BII shows how local terrestrial biodiversity responds to human pressures such as land use change and intensification.

8b004ee7ed63.title: Measurement of biodiversity
8b004ee7ed63.sentence: The Mean Species Abundance Index (MSA) calculates the trend in population size of a cross section of the species.

128482787aa6.title: Biodiversity
128482787aa6.sentence: Northern Africa, southern Australia, coastal Brazil, Madagascar and South Africa, are also identified as areas with striking losses in biodiversity intactness.

063577f366d3.title: Measurement of biodiversity
063577f366d3.sentence: - phylogenetic diversity measures, include information on phylogenetic relationships among species

c3d4fef1c6fb.title: Measurement of biodiversity
c3d4fef1c6fb.sentence: - functional diversity measures, include information on functional traits among species

c254158b7394.title: Measurement of biodiversity
c254158b7394.sentence: - functional group richness (FGR); e.g., Tilman et al. (1997)

7fe6847fb8db.title: Measurement of biodiversity
7fe6847fb8db.sentence: These different types of diversity may not be independent.

1d4b1a1ee241.title: Measurement of biodiversity
1d4b1a1ee241.sentence: There is, for example, a close link between vertebrate taxonomic and ecological diversity.

c265a04dbeb9.title: Agricultural biodiversity
c265a04dbeb9.sentence: Over the past 50 years, there has been a major decline in two components of crop diversity; genetic diversity within each crop and the number of species commonly grown.

88909611447c.title: Agricultural biodiversity
88909611447c.sentence: Crop diversity loss threatens global food security, as the world's human population depends on a diminishing number of varieties of a diminishing number of crop species.

db3e302b2b24.title: Agricultural biodiversity
db3e302b2b24.sentence: - The Irish potato blight of 1846 was a major factor in the deaths of one million people and the emigration of about two million.

2a8bfdc745c2.title: Agricultural biodiversity
2a8bfdc745c2.sentence: It was the result of planting only two potato varieties, both vulnerable to the blight, Phytophthora infestans, which arrived in 1845

3da47d7c6337.title: Agricultural biodiversity
3da47d7c6337.sentence: - When rice grassy stunt virus struck rice fields from Indonesia to India in the 1970s, 6,273 varieties were tested for resistance.

4e962ab55b14.title: Agricultural biodiversity
4e962ab55b14.sentence: Only one was resistant, an Indian variety and known to science only since 1966.

7e59a28c8d3c.title: Agricultural biodiversity
7e59a28c8d3c.sentence: Animal genetic resources for food and agriculture (AnGR), also known as farm animal genetic resources or livestock biodiversity, are genetic resources (i.e., genetic material of actual or potential value) of avian and mammalian species, which are used for food and agriculture purposes.

4bd3f81d579a.title: Agricultural biodiversity
4bd3f81d579a.sentence: Known are currently 8,800 different breeds of birds and mammals within 38 species used for food and agriculture.

d6c6bdc43c59.title: Agricultural biodiversity
d6c6bdc43c59.sentence: AnGR could be embodied in live populations or in conserved genetic materials such as cryoconserved semen or embryos.

ab39f745d849.title: Island restoration
ab39f745d849.sentence: The ecological restoration of islands, or island restoration, is the application of the principles of ecological restoration to islands and island groups.

a15b190135c4.title: Island restoration
a15b190135c4.sentence: The principal components of island restoration are the removal of introduced species and the reintroduction of native species.

1042c1ff048b.title: Island restoration
1042c1ff048b.sentence: Islands, due to their isolation, are home to many of the world's endemic species, as well as important breeding grounds for seabirds and some marine mammals.

d33c3b70bd3a.title: Island restoration
d33c3b70bd3a.sentence: Their ecosystems are also very vulnerable to human disturbance and particularly to introduced species, due to their small size.

78ffaa7debd4.title: Invasive species
78ffaa7debd4.section: Control, eradication, and study > Reestablishing species
78ffaa7debd4.sentence: A 2019 study suggests that if eradications of invasive animals were conducted on just 169 islands, the survival prospects of 9.4% of the Earth's most highly threatened terrestrial insular vertebrates would be improved.

10812d13dada.title: Invasive species
10812d13dada.section: Control, eradication, and study > Taxon substitution
10812d13dada.sentence: Non-native species can be introduced to fill an ecological engineering role that previously was performed by a native species now extinct.

9ecb8df69918.title: Invasive species
9ecb8df69918.section: Control, eradication, and study > Taxon substitution
9ecb8df69918.sentence: The procedure is known as taxon substitution.

714103a59c85.title: Invasive species
714103a59c85.section: Control, eradication, and study > Taxon substitution
714103a59c85.sentence: Introduction of the non-native Aldabra giant tortoises (Aldabrachelys gigantea) on two islets in 2000 and 2007 has begun to restore ecological equilibrium.

412908b64af4.title: Invasive species
412908b64af4.section: Control, eradication, and study > Taxon substitution
412908b64af4.sentence: The introduced tortoises are dispersing seeds of several native plants and are selectively grazing invasive plant species.

98f706cd050d.title: Decline in insect populations
98f706cd050d.section: Countermeasures > Wildflower strips and buffer zones
98f706cd050d.sentence: A wildflower strip is a strip of land sown with seeds of biodiverse insect- and pollinator-friendly flowering plant species, usually at the edge of an agricultural field, intended to sustain local biodiversity, conserve insects, restore farmland birds and counteract the negative consequences of agricultural intensification.

d51262b1b99f.title: Decline in insect populations
d51262b1b99f.section: Countermeasures > Wildflower strips and buffer zones
d51262b1b99f.sentence: Buffer zones around nature reserves where pesticide use is drastically reduced has been proposed for inclusion in the countermeasures.

de0f8ef0c907.title: Decline in insect populations
de0f8ef0c907.section: Countermeasures > Wildflower strips and buffer zones
de0f8ef0c907.sentence: Scientists who proposed the measure conducted a Germany-wide field study and found that insect samples in these areas are contaminated with ~16 pesticides on average, proportionate to the agricultural production area in a radius of 2 km.

1fea9f89cd15.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
1fea9f89cd15.sentence: By complementarity, a more diverse plant community should be able to use resources more completely, and thus be more productive.

88b54c70a339.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
88b54c70a339.sentence: - Facilitation Facilitation is a mechanism whereby certain species help or allow other species to grow by modifying the environment in a way that is favorable to a co-occurring species.

a64834a1a0fc.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
a64834a1a0fc.sentence: - The Sampling Effect The sampling effect of diversity can be thought of as having a greater chance of including a species of greatest inherent productivity in a plot that is more diverse.

c8b8b040f78c.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
c8b8b040f78c.sentence: - Complementarity Plant species coexistence is thought to be the result of niche partitioning, or differences in resource requirements among species.

e4df4a9c2e70.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
e4df4a9c2e70.sentence: Some examples of facilitation include large desert perennials acting as nurse plants, aiding the establishment of young neighbors of other species by alleviating water and temperature stress, and nutrient enrichment by nitrogen-fixers such as legumes.

c5a99ebf2738.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
c5a99ebf2738.sentence: This provides for a composition effect on productivity, rather than diversity being a direct cause.

8f48eed94963.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
8f48eed94963.sentence: - Averaging Effect If all species have differential responses to changes in the ecosystem over time, then the averaging of these responses will cause a more temporally stable ecosystem if more species are in the ecosystem.

f237a7ac4749.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
f237a7ac4749.sentence: - Negative Covariance Effect If some species do better when other species are not doing well, then when there are more species in the ecosystem, their overall variance will be lower than if there were fewer species in the system.

11320233791e.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
11320233791e.sentence: - Insurance Effect If an ecosystem contains more species then it will have a greater likelihood of having redundant stabilizing species, and it will have a greater number of species that respond to perturbations in different ways.

824db98918f5.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
824db98918f5.sentence: This effect is a statistical effect due to summing random variables.

5adfa8d5c8af.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
5adfa8d5c8af.sentence: This effect is a consequence of competition as highly competitive species will negatively covary.

db6c677f09ab.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
db6c677f09ab.sentence: This will enhance an ecosystem's ability to buffer perturbations.

07f568f2242a.title: Ecological effects of biodiversity
07f568f2242a.section: Effects on community stability > Review of resistance and resilience stability data
07f568f2242a.sentence: Some experimenters have seen a correlation between diversity and reduced invasibility, though many have also seen the opposite.

02cf527968d6.title: Beta diversity
02cf527968d6.sentence: In ecology, beta diversity (β-diversity or true beta diversity) is the ratio between regional and local species diversity.

995420b0bf10.title: Beta diversity
995420b0bf10.sentence: The idea was that the total species diversity in a landscape (γ) is determined by two different things: the mean species diversity at the local level (α) and the differentiation among local sites (β).

b13a342a50f0.title: Beta diversity
b13a342a50f0.sentence: The term was introduced by R. H. Whittaker together with the terms alpha diversity (α-diversity) and gamma diversity (γ-diversity).

40a5418ea648.title: Beta diversity
40a5418ea648.sentence: Beta diversity quantifies how many subunits there would be if the total species diversity of the dataset and the mean species diversity per subunit remained the same, but the subunits shared no species.

bb28093bce8b.title: Beta diversity
bb28093bce8b.sentence: Other formulations for beta diversity include "absolute species turnover", "Whittaker's species turnover" and "proportional species turnover".

0c1eb85bc824.title: Beta diversity
0c1eb85bc824.sentence: As a result, there are now many defined types of beta diversity.

646f78e13ab6.title: Beta diversity
646f78e13ab6.sentence: Kitching et al. sampled moths in primary and logged forests of Danum valley, Borneo to show that β-diversity in primary forests was higher than logged forests.

1fa2f25ec0d4.title: Beta diversity
1fa2f25ec0d4.sentence: Contrastingly, Berry et al. sampled trees in the same study area to show that β-diversity in logged forests was higher than primary forests.

83d126a2cea5.title: Beta diversity
83d126a2cea5.sentence: Therefore, there is a clear lack of consensus on β-diversity patterns among studies.

1b85b3a19ed0.title: Biodiversity
1b85b3a19ed0.section: Biodiversity changes (other than losses) > Introduced and invasive species
1b85b3a19ed0.sentence: Invasive species seem to increase local (alpha diversity) diversity, which decreases turnover of diversity (beta diversity).

360b317138e3.title: Gamma diversity
360b317138e3.sentence: In ecology, gamma diversity (γ-diversity) is the total species diversity in a landscape.

283e993f58d8.title: Gamma diversity
283e993f58d8.sentence: The term was introduced by R. H. Whittaker together with the terms alpha diversity (α-diversity) and beta diversity (β-diversity).

7602f23d1b8b.title: Gamma diversity
7602f23d1b8b.sentence: Whittaker's idea was that the total species diversity in a landscape (γ) is determined by two different things, the mean species diversity in sites at a more local scale (α) and the differentiation among those sites (β).

d67c7e0e8f25.title: Gamma diversity
d67c7e0e8f25.sentence: The area or landscape of interest may be of very different sizes in different situations, and no consensus has been reached on what spatial scales are appropriate to quantify gamma diversity.

c19c4024fbf5.title: Gamma diversity
c19c4024fbf5.sentence: If results are extrapolated beyond the actual observations, it needs to be taken into account that the species diversity in the dataset generally gives an underestimation of the species diversity in a larger area.

36eed9eb6cff.title: Gamma diversity
36eed9eb6cff.sentence: The degree of underestimation can be estimated from a species-area curve.

dcd5ad9e1497.title: Beta diversity
dcd5ad9e1497.sentence: This quantifies how much more species diversity the entire dataset contains than an average subunit within the dataset.

965d163f0cf3.title: Beta diversity
965d163f0cf3.sentence: This can also be interpreted as the total amount of species turnover among the subunits in the dataset.

98773238e0ac.title: Beta diversity
98773238e0ac.sentence: Some researchers have preferred to partition gamma diversity into additive rather than multiplicative components.

471e040bacdc.title: Beta diversity
471e040bacdc.sentence: If absolute species turnover is divided by alpha diversity, a measure is obtained that quantifies how many times the species composition changes completely among the subunits of the dataset.

2838a7369e28.title: Beta diversity
2838a7369e28.sentence: When there are two subunits, and presence-absence data are used, this equals the one-complement of the Sørensen similarity index.

49a57d1ad013.title: Beta diversity
49a57d1ad013.sentence: If absolute species turnover is divided by gamma diversity, a measure is obtained that quantifies what proportion of the species diversity in the dataset is not contained in an average subunit.

303a7046dc62.title: Beta diversity
303a7046dc62.sentence: When there are two subunits, and presence-absence data are used, this measure as ranged to the interval [0, 1] equals the one-complement of the Jaccard similarity index.

c15a14c5681b.title: Biotic homogenization
c15a14c5681b.sentence: Biotic homogenization is the process by which two or more spatially distributed ecological communities become increasingly similar over time.

b3b27e9d6c97.title: Biotic homogenization
b3b27e9d6c97.sentence: This process may be genetic, taxonomic, or functional, and it leads to a loss of beta (β) diversity.

a4c997422982.title: Biotic homogenization
a4c997422982.sentence: This phenomenon stems primarily from two sources: extinctions of native and invasions of nonnative species.

2c02a0a53e8b.title: Biotic homogenization
2c02a0a53e8b.sentence: While this process pre-dates human civilization, as evidenced by the fossil record, and still occurs due to natural impacts, it has recently been accelerated due anthropogenic pressures.

b6944d0329f0.title: Biotic homogenization
b6944d0329f0.sentence: A common misconception with taxonomic homogenization is that it represents a loss in α diversity, or that it leads to decreased species richness.

acb5de51508b.title: Biotic homogenization
acb5de51508b.sentence: However, assemblages under taxonomic homogenization may actually display an increase in α diversity, a phenomenon that has been observed in plant, animal, and microbial groups.

9cbfea7af130.title: Biotic homogenization
9cbfea7af130.sentence: In a comparison of 201 watersheds that analyzed changes in similarities over 200 years, approximately 65% of comparisons demonstrate that the watersheds are undergoing homogenization.

3eac11b8e35d.title: Biotic homogenization
3eac11b8e35d.sentence: However, as ecosystems become increasingly similar and simplified, there is concern that the resilience of the assemblages against stressful events will be limited.

9714b081594e.title: Carrying capacity
9714b081594e.sentence: The carrying capacity of an ecosystem is the maximum population size of a living biological species that can be sustained by that specific environment, given the food, habitat, water, and other resources available, over a fixed amount of time.

3f3e1ae35806.title: Carrying capacity
3f3e1ae35806.sentence: The carrying capacity is defined as the environment's maximal load, which in population ecology corresponds to the population equilibrium, when the number of deaths in a population equals the number of births (as well as immigration and emigration).

80761c84571d.title: Carrying capacity
80761c84571d.sentence: If the population of a given organism is below the carrying capacity of a given environment, this environment could support a positive natural increase; should it find itself above that threshold the population typically decreases.

68626be991a2.title: Carrying capacity
68626be991a2.sentence: Population size decreases above carrying capacity due to a range of factors depending on the species concerned, but can include insufficient space, food supply, or sunlight.

3433cca0e9a6.title: Carrying capacity
3433cca0e9a6.sentence: The specific reason why a population stops growing is known as a limiting or regulating factor.

85c8bb10460f.title: Carrying capacity
85c8bb10460f.sentence: What determines a specific system's carrying capacity involves a limiting factor; this may be available supplies of food or water, nesting areas, space, or the amount of waste that can be absorbed without degrading the environment and decreasing carrying capacity.

8ac3cc0e1074.title: Carrying capacity
8ac3cc0e1074.sentence: Carrying capacity of the environment implies that the resources extraction is not above the rate of regeneration of the resources and the wastes generated are within the assimilating capacity of the environment.

1060bf0a256d.title: Carrying capacity
1060bf0a256d.sentence: Carrying capacity is applied to the maximum population an environment can support in ecology, agriculture and fisheries.

20909ae5e8fe.title: Carrying capacity
20909ae5e8fe.sentence: It then became a term used generally in biology in the 1870s, being most developed in wildlife and livestock management in the early 1900s.

ba38b4f1be0a.title: Carrying capacity
ba38b4f1be0a.sentence: It had become a staple term in ecology used to define the biological limits of a natural system related to population size in the 1950s.

e5c7a236e434.title: Carrying capacity
e5c7a236e434.sentence: Numerous authors have questioned the usefulness of the term when applied to actual wild populations.

4bf8fff8e801.title: Carrying capacity
4bf8fff8e801.sentence: Although useful in theory and in laboratory experiments, carrying capacity as a method of measuring population limits in the environment is less useful as it sometimes oversimplifies the interactions between species.

909481e2bfde.title: Carrying capacity
909481e2bfde.sentence: A 2008 review finds the first use of the term in English was an 1845 report by the US Secretary of State to the US Senate.

90213c27b2a3.title: Carrying capacity
90213c27b2a3.sentence: It was first used in the context of wildlife management by the American Aldo Leopold in 1933, and a year later by the American Paul Lester Errington, a wetlands specialist.

67cc2bbf4ebf.title: Feedback
67cc2bbf4ebf.sentence: Feedback occurs when outputs of a system are routed back as inputs as part of a chain of cause and effect that forms a circuit or loop.

02420c3ebe43.title: Feedback
02420c3ebe43.sentence: > Simple causal reasoning about a feedback system is difficult because the first system influences the second and second system influences the first, leading to a circular argument.

ecb4ad242e71.title: Feedback
ecb4ad242e71.sentence: This makes reasoning based upon cause and effect tricky, and it is necessary to analyze the system as a whole.

0185db363d0d.title: Feedback
0185db363d0d.sentence: The first ever known artificial feedback device was a float valve, for maintaining water at a constant level, invented in 270 BC in Alexandria, Egypt.

d505e4a96474.title: Feedback
d505e4a96474.sentence: Self-regulating mechanisms have existed since antiquity, and the idea of feedback started to enter economic theory in Britain by the 18th century, but it was not at that time recognized as a universal abstraction and so did not have a name.

80b24a9cba84.title: Feedback
80b24a9cba84.sentence: In biological systems such as organisms, ecosystems, or the biosphere, most parameters must stay under control within a narrow range around a certain optimal level under certain environmental conditions.

b86ab5df4b66.title: Feedback
b86ab5df4b66.sentence: The climate system is characterized by strong positive and negative feedback loops between processes that affect the state of the atmosphere, ocean, and land.

aa7035b7b3e9.title: Feedback
aa7035b7b3e9.section: Types > Positive and negative feedback > Limitations of negative and positive feedback
aa7035b7b3e9.sentence: While simple systems can sometimes be described as one or the other type, many systems with feedback loops cannot be shoehorned into either type, and this is especially true when multiple loops are present.

788d0456ab64.title: Disturbance (ecology)
788d0456ab64.sentence: In ecology, a disturbance is a change in environmental conditions that causes a pronounced change in an ecosystem.

372f89a14e75.title: Disturbance (ecology)
372f89a14e75.sentence: Ecological disturbances include fires, flooding, storms, insect outbreaks, trampling, human presence, earthquakes, plant diseases, infestations, volcanic eruptions, impact events, etc.

53828098f5b6.title: Disturbance (ecology)
53828098f5b6.sentence: The scale of disturbance ranges from events as small as a single tree falling, to as large as a mass extinction.

194246cbc435.title: Disturbance (ecology)
194246cbc435.sentence: Ecosystems that form under these conditions are often maintained by regular disturbance.

a4c07ad5353f.title: Disturbance (ecology)
a4c07ad5353f.sentence: Wetland ecosystems, for example, can be maintained by the movement of water through them and by periodic fires.

ecca84d4bff1.title: Disturbance (ecology)
ecca84d4bff1.sentence: Immediately after a disturbance there is a pulse of recruitment or regrowth under conditions of little competition for space or other resources.

fca04d71ffbf.title: Disturbance (ecology)
fca04d71ffbf.sentence: Biological diversity is dependent on natural disturbance.

981eb33f87ae.title: Disturbance (ecology)
981eb33f87ae.sentence: As an example, many shade-intolerant plant species rely on disturbances for successful establishment and to limit competition.

aed2e071724c.title: Disturbance (ecology)
aed2e071724c.sentence: A good example of this role of disturbance is in ponderosa pine (Pinus ponderosa) forests in the western United States, where surface fires frequently thin existing vegetation allowing for new growth.

cbd6edb72789.title: Disturbance (ecology)
cbd6edb72789.sentence: If fire is suppressed, douglas fir (Pesudotsuga menziesii), a shade tolerant species, eventually replaces the pines.

c2f626651da6.title: Disturbance (ecology)
c2f626651da6.sentence: As the diversity of surface plants decreases, animal species that rely on them diminish as well.

bfb1d4f1f5ac.title: Disturbance (ecology)
bfb1d4f1f5ac.section: Importance > Relationship to climate change adaptation
bfb1d4f1f5ac.sentence: Disturbance in ecosystems can form a way of modeling future ability of ecosystems to adapt to climate change.

891487b829d6.title: Disturbance (ecology)
891487b829d6.section: Importance > Relationship to climate change adaptation
891487b829d6.sentence: Likewise, adaptation of a species to disturbance may be a predictor of its future ability to survive the current biodiversity crisis.

06ca9f3cd40b.title: Ecological resilience
06ca9f3cd40b.sentence: In ecology, resilience is the capacity of an ecosystem to respond to a perturbation or disturbance by resisting damage and subsequently recovering.

b0aadef7654e.title: Ecological resilience
b0aadef7654e.sentence: Such perturbations and disturbances can include stochastic events such as fires, flooding, windstorms, insect population explosions, and human activities such as deforestation, fracking of the ground for oil extraction, pesticide sprayed in soil, and the introduction of exotic plant or animal species.

81760a0e6d06.title: Ecological resilience
81760a0e6d06.sentence: Disturbances of sufficient magnitude or duration can profoundly affect an ecosystem and may force an ecosystem to reach a threshold beyond which a different regime of processes and structures predominates.

a1b0adbef55e.title: Ecological resilience
a1b0adbef55e.sentence: Human activities that adversely affect ecological resilience such as reduction of biodiversity, exploitation of natural resources, pollution, land use, and anthropogenic climate change are increasingly causing regime shifts in ecosystems, often to less desirable and degraded conditions.

00980bc512d2.title: Ecological resilience
00980bc512d2.sentence: The concept of resilience in ecological systems was first introduced by the Canadian ecologist C.S. Holling in order to describe the persistence of natural systems in the face of changes in ecosystem variables due to natural or anthropogenic causes.

6b850c580334.title: Ecological resilience
6b850c580334.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report defines resilience as, “not just the ability to maintain essential function, identity and structure, but also the capacity for transformation.” The IPCC considers resilience both in terms of ecosystem recovery as well as the recovery and adaptation of human societies to natural disasters.

10366c83a048.title: Ecological resilience
10366c83a048.sentence: In addition, generally, the resilience of a forest system allows recovery from a relatively small scale of damage (such as lightning or landslide) of up to 10 percent of its area.

cbe9c36bf218.title: Ecological resilience
cbe9c36bf218.sentence: The larger the scale of damage, the more difficult it is for the forest ecosystem to restore and maintain its balance.

395d620fb9a3.title: Ecological resilience
395d620fb9a3.sentence: Sustainable use of environmental goods and services requires understanding and consideration of the resilience of the ecosystem and its limits.

b2b618b5c2c3.title: Ecological resilience
b2b618b5c2c3.sentence: Interdisciplinary discourse on resilience now includes consideration of the interactions of humans and ecosystems via socio-ecological systems, and the need for shift from the maximum sustainable yield paradigm to environmental resource management and ecosystem management, which aim to build ecological resilience through "resilience analysis, adaptive resource management, and adaptive governance".

6420a1393ade.title: Ecological stability
6420a1393ade.sentence: In ecology, an ecosystem is said to possess ecological stability (or equilibrium) if it is capable of returning to its equilibrium state after a perturbation (a capacity known as resilience) or does not experience unexpected large changes in its characteristics across time.

525ece55e4a6.title: Ecological stability
525ece55e4a6.sentence: It is possible for an ecosystem or a community to be stable in some of their properties and unstable in others.

5639e05ae045.title: Ecological stability
5639e05ae045.sentence: For example, a vegetation community in response to a drought might conserve biomass but lose biodiversity.

fd3abb118a75.title: Ecological stability
fd3abb118a75.sentence: In 1997, Grimm and Wissel made an inventory of 167 definitions used in the literature and found 70 different stability concepts.

329734d1aa1e.title: Ecological stability
329734d1aa1e.sentence: One of the strategies that these two authors proposed to clarify the subject is to replace ecological stability with more specific terms, such as constancy, resilience and persistence.

8101d633cd84.title: Ecological stability
8101d633cd84.sentence: Nevertheless, it is important to mention that not every community or ecosystem in nature is stable (for example, wolves and moose on Isle Royale).

4ff21f7b33bb.title: Ecological stability
4ff21f7b33bb.sentence: The concept of ecological stability emerged in the first half of the 20th century.

1b00a9e115fc.title: Ecological stability
1b00a9e115fc.sentence: With the advancement of theoretical ecology in the 1970s, the usage of the term has expanded to a wide variety of scenarios.

176776fce5d6.title: Ecosystem health
176776fce5d6.sentence: Ecosystem health is a metaphor used to describe the condition of an ecosystem.

fa2c3043db6d.title: Ecosystem health
fa2c3043db6d.sentence: Ecosystem condition can vary as a result of fire, flooding, drought, extinctions, invasive species, climate change, mining, fishing, farming or logging, chemical spills, and a host of other reasons.

29b9773d524d.title: Ecosystem health
29b9773d524d.sentence: There is no universally accepted benchmark for a healthy ecosystem, rather the apparent health status of an ecosystem can vary depending upon which health metrics are employed in judging it and which societal aspirations are driving the assessment.

ca5dfad17662.title: Ecosystem health
ca5dfad17662.sentence: Advocates of the health metaphor argue for its simplicity as a communication tool.

783fd0f53b9f.title: Ecosystem health
783fd0f53b9f.sentence: "Policy-makers and the public need simple, understandable concepts like health." Some critics worry that ecosystem health, a "value-laden construct", can be "passed off as science to unsuspecting policy makers and the public." However, this term is often used in portraying the state of ecosystems worldwide and in conservation and management.

48ca418626f5.title: Ecosystem health
48ca418626f5.sentence: The health metaphor applied to the environment has been in use at least since the early 1800s and the great American conservationist Aldo Leopold (1887–1948) spoke metaphorically of land health, land sickness, mutilation, and violence when describing land use practices.

4618fe01ca8e.title: Ecosystem health
4618fe01ca8e.sentence: A suite of 80 lake health indicators was developed for the Great Lakes Basin including monitoring native fish species, exotic species, water levels, phosphorus levels, toxic chemicals, phytoplankton, zooplankton, fish tissue contaminants, etc.

f392598ab7ee.title: Ecosystem health
f392598ab7ee.sentence: Also, fossil and pollen records indicate that the species that occupy an ecosystem reshuffle through time, so it is difficult to identify one snapshot in time as optimum or "healthy.".

a13f708afff5.title: Ecosystem health
a13f708afff5.section: Criticism of the concept and proposed alternatives
a13f708afff5.sentence: Alternatives have been proposed for the term ecosystem health, including more neutral language such as ecosystem status, ecosystem prognosis, and ecosystem sustainability.

db98db2d958d.title: Overshoot (population)
db98db2d958d.sentence: In environmental science, a population overshoots its local carrying capacity—the maximum population size that an ecosystem can sustainably support—when it exceeds the availability of resources needed for survival.

271d6fdc2df6.title: Overshoot (population)
271d6fdc2df6.sentence: This can lead to a population crash if resources are depleted faster than they can regenerate.

29335548cd37.title: Overshoot (population)
29335548cd37.sentence: The path taken by such a population is referred to as 'overshoot-and-collapse'.

a0ad08386562.title: Overshoot (population)
a0ad08386562.sentence: Overshoot can happen as a result of delayed impacts, where reproduction rates persistently surpass the death rate.

6f276796c82c.title: Overshoot (population)
6f276796c82c.sentence: In 1944, 29 reindeer were introduced to the island, which by 1963 had grown to a peak population of roughly 6000 individuals — well past the estimated carrying capacity.

f58eced85ca1.title: Overshoot (population)
f58eced85ca1.sentence: At next count, in 1965, the population had plummeted and only 42 reindeer were left alive.

a23fa00db513.title: Overshoot (population)
a23fa00db513.sentence: An instance of this phenomenon took place in the Horn of Africa when smallpox was eradicated, causing a sudden increase in the population that exceeded the region's carrying capacity.

c5cfb2d629fc.title: Overshoot (population)
c5cfb2d629fc.sentence: For centuries, the land had sustained approximately 1 million pastoralists, but with the elimination of the disease, the population suddenly grew to 14 million people.

381e29810f1b.title: Overshoot (population)
381e29810f1b.sentence: Consequently, overgrazing occurred, leading to soil erosion.

ea2ed88c0904.title: Overshoot (population)
ea2ed88c0904.sentence: This can lead to significant consequences, with entire ecosystems being profoundly impacted and sometimes simplified due to prolonged overshoot.

187411cc02f7.title: Hysteresis
187411cc02f7.sentence: Hysteresis is the dependence of the state of a system on its history.

3deba2fc93ef.title: Hysteresis
3deba2fc93ef.sentence: Plots of a single component of the moment often form a loop or hysteresis curve, where there are different values of one variable depending on the direction of change of another variable.

348193959659.title: Hysteresis
348193959659.sentence: The term "hysteresis" is derived from ὑστέρησις, an Ancient Greek word meaning "deficiency" or "lagging behind".

860e200c42b2.title: Hysteresis
860e200c42b2.sentence: It was coined in 1881 by Sir James Alfred Ewing to describe the behaviour of magnetic materials.

f16092f6e712.title: Hysteresis
f16092f6e712.sentence: Hysteresis is a commonly encountered phenomenon in ecology and epidemiology, where the observed equilibrium of a system can not be predicted solely based on environmental variables, but also requires knowledge of the system's past history.

188e6626fb1b.title: Hysteresis
188e6626fb1b.sentence: Notable examples include the theory of spruce budworm outbreaks and behavioral-effects on disease transmission.

6ba12d5824f9.title: Hysteresis
6ba12d5824f9.sentence: For example, a thermostat controlling a heater may switch the heater on when the temperature drops below A, but not turn it off until the temperature rises above B. (For instance, if one wishes to maintain a temperature of 20 °C then one might set the thermostat to turn the heater on when the temperature drops to below 18 °C and off when the temperature exceeds 22 °C).

2d09aff9f4a3.title: Hysteresis
2d09aff9f4a3.sentence: For example, agar melts at 85 °C (185 °F) and solidifies from 32 to 40 °C (90 to 104 °F).

bb206296dff4.title: Carrying capacity
bb206296dff4.sentence: Human carrying capacity is a function of how people live and the technology at their disposal.

f8e1c49589d2.title: Carrying capacity
f8e1c49589d2.sentence: But human carrying capacity is always a function of a certain number of people living a certain way.

bd9dc4fb4ef2.title: Carrying capacity
bd9dc4fb4ef2.sentence: The two great economic revolutions that marked human history up to 1900—the agricultural and industrial revolutions—greatly increased the Earth's human carrying capacity, allowing human population to grow from 5 to 10 million people in 10,000 BCE to 1.5 billion in 1900.

84eccd33adb8.title: Carrying capacity
84eccd33adb8.sentence: Recent technological successes, however, have come at grave environmental costs.

72996db33717.title: Carrying capacity
72996db33717.sentence: Climate change, ocean acidification, and the huge dead zones at the mouths of many of world's great rivers, are a function of the scale of contemporary agriculture and the many other demands 8 billion people make on the planet.

47b9ede85440.title: Carrying capacity
47b9ede85440.sentence: Humanity's unprecedented ecological impacts threaten to degrade the ecosystem services that people and the rest of life depend on—potentially decreasing Earth's human carrying capacity.

eb3c9797a90d.title: Carrying capacity
eb3c9797a90d.sentence: The fact that degrading Earth's essential services is obviously possible, and happening in some cases, suggests that 8 billion people may be above Earth's human carrying capacity.

72bbda65591b.title: Carrying capacity
72bbda65591b.sentence: Another issue to consider when applying carrying capacity, especially to humans, is that measuring food resources is arbitrary.

7e8933da4c30.title: Carrying capacity
7e8933da4c30.sentence: Measuring water resources carrying capacity is likewise highly arbitrary: choices in temporal resolution (e.g., monthly versus annual), spatial resolution (e.g., how subbasins are delineated), and whether to include human activities such as inter-basin water transfers and reservoir storage in the assessment can all lead to vastly different WRCC results.

4755e47af680.title: Carrying capacity
4755e47af680.sentence: They also assume that the populations in the region only rely on that region's resources even though humans exchange resources with others from other regions and there are few, if any, isolated populations.

27b11fce20de.title: Carrying capacity
27b11fce20de.section: Recent warnings that humanity may have exceeded Earth's carrying capacity > Millennium ecosystem assessment
27b11fce20de.sentence: The Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (MEA) of 2005 was a massive, collaborative effort to assess the state of Earth's ecosystems, involving more than 1,300 experts worldwide.

71f2ed4ec772.title: Carrying capacity
71f2ed4ec772.section: Recent warnings that humanity may have exceeded Earth's carrying capacity > Millennium ecosystem assessment
71f2ed4ec772.sentence: According to the MEA, these unprecedented environmental changes threaten to reduce the Earth's long-term human carrying capacity.

b82b915cdfd4.title: Carrying capacity
b82b915cdfd4.section: Recent warnings that humanity may have exceeded Earth's carrying capacity > Planetary boundaries framework
b82b915cdfd4.sentence: By itself, crossing one of the planetary boundaries does not prove humanity has exceeded Earth's human carrying capacity; perhaps technological improvements or clever management might reduce this stressor and bring us back within the biosphere's safe operating space.

942ea2e6f15a.title: Carrying capacity
942ea2e6f15a.section: Recent warnings that humanity may have exceeded Earth's carrying capacity > Planetary boundaries framework
942ea2e6f15a.sentence: But when several boundaries are crossed, it becomes harder to argue that carrying capacity has not been breached.

a08b8365e6f7.title: Human overpopulation
a08b8365e6f7.sentence: A 2004 meta-analysis of 69 such studies from 1694 until 2001 found the average predicted maximum number of people the Earth would ever have was 7.7 billion people, with lower and upper meta-bounds at 0.65 and 98 billion people, respectively.

9aa53f93e2c8.sentence: However, as population size nears carrying capacity, the growth decreases and reaches zero at K.

(Note that decrease is negative growth.) The choice of the letter K came from the German Kapazitätsgrenze (capacity limit).

d3a8d6efa289.title: Carrying capacity
d3a8d6efa289.sentence: In terms of population dynamics, the term 'carrying capacity' was not explicitly used in 1838 by the Belgian mathematician Pierre François Verhulst when he first published his equations based on research on modelling population growth.

b75868a4c0ee.title: Systems thinking
b75868a4c0ee.sentence: Systems thinking is a way of making sense of the complexity of the world by looking at it in terms of wholes and relationships rather than by splitting it down into its parts.

56ff2b177458.title: Systems thinking
56ff2b177458.sentence: It has been used as a way of exploring and developing effective action in complex contexts, enabling systems change.

d517ab83b858.title: Systems thinking
d517ab83b858.sentence: A system is a set of things... interconnected in such a way that they produce their own pattern of behavior over time....

383a8e0b0207.title: Systems thinking
383a8e0b0207.sentence: Systems thinking, born from the visionary contributions of theoretical biologist Ludwig von Bertalanffy, computer scientist Jay Forrester, and their contemporaries, reached its zenith in the 1990s with the release of Peter Senge’s seminal work, The Fifth Discipline, a landmark in intellectual exploration.

373a896840a2.title: Systems thinking
373a896840a2.sentence: MIT’s Jay Forrester likes to say that the average manager can... guess with great accuracy where to look for leverage points—places in the system where a small change could lead to a large shift in behavior".— Donella Meadows, (2008) Thinking In Systems: A Primer p.145

719ec92a1e8b.title: Systems thinking
719ec92a1e8b.sentence: - System dynamics of stocks, flows, and internal feedback loops.

174fd26e5640.title: Ecological threshold
174fd26e5640.sentence: Ecological threshold is the point at which a relatively small change or disturbance in external conditions causes a rapid change in an ecosystem.

cd48ac94d640.title: Ecological threshold
cd48ac94d640.sentence: When an ecological threshold has been passed, the ecosystem may no longer be able to return to its state by means of its inherent resilience.

d19908d19e5b.title: Ecological threshold
d19908d19e5b.sentence: Ecological threshold represent a non-linearity of the responses in ecological or biological systems to pressures caused by human activities or natural processes.

92d444e35e39.title: Ecological threshold
92d444e35e39.sentence: Thresholds can be characterized as points or as zones.

6dd1df111cc2.title: Ecological threshold
6dd1df111cc2.sentence: Zone-type thresholds imply a gradual shift or transition from one state to another rather than an abrupt change at a specific point.

0be95711ef62.title: Ecological threshold
0be95711ef62.sentence: Ecological thresholds have caught attention because many cases of catastrophic worsening of conditions have proved to be difficult or nearly impossible to remedy (also known as points of no return).

5e5b22863dea.title: Ecological threshold
5e5b22863dea.sentence: Ecological extinction is an example of a definitive point of no return.

90652ac5f335.title: Ecological threshold
90652ac5f335.sentence: Ecological thresholds are often characterized by hysteresis, which means the dependence of the state of a system on the history of its state.

3fa058fa1023.title: Ecological threshold
3fa058fa1023.sentence: Even when the change is not irreversible, the return path from altered to original state can be drastically different from the development leading to the altered state.

23c2971a7414.title: Ecological threshold
23c2971a7414.sentence: There are many different types of thresholds and detecting the occurrence of a threshold is not always straightforward.

2d831a0f2b3e.title: Ecological threshold
2d831a0f2b3e.sentence: One approach is to process time series which are thought to display a shift in order to identify a possible jump.

16afa85998b5.title: Ecological threshold
16afa85998b5.sentence: Some examples of ecological thresholds, such as clear lakes turning into turbid ones, are well documented but many more probably exist.

8bf522059893.title: Ecological threshold
8bf522059893.sentence: The thresholds database by Resilience Alliance and Santa Fe Institute includes over one hundred examples.

ef86af1c4a2a.title: Ecological threshold
ef86af1c4a2a.sentence: Critical load, regime shift, critical transition and tipping point are examples of other closely related terms.

11e260a5dc2a.title: Planetary boundaries
11e260a5dc2a.sentence: Planetary boundaries are a framework to describe limits to the impacts of human activities on the Earth system.

960dc6906029.title: Planetary boundaries
960dc6906029.sentence: Beyond these limits, the environment may not be able to continue to self-regulate.

48f26b7edd6a.title: Planetary boundaries
48f26b7edd6a.sentence: This would mean the Earth system would leave the period of stability of the Holocene, in which human society developed.

4023df1df286.title: Planetary boundaries
4023df1df286.sentence: These nine boundaries are climate change, ocean acidification, stratospheric ozone depletion, biogeochemical flows in the nitrogen cycle, excess global freshwater use, land system change, the erosion of biosphere integrity, chemical pollution and atmospheric aerosol loading.

923e94f7a88e.title: Planetary boundaries
923e94f7a88e.sentence: According to the framework, "transgressing one or more planetary boundaries may be deleterious or even catastrophic due to the risk of crossing thresholds that will trigger non-linear, abrupt environmental change within continental-scale to planetary-scale systems."

053ee4b3c5b7.title: Planetary boundaries
053ee4b3c5b7.sentence: The authors of this framework was a group of Earth System and environmental scientists in 2009 led by Johan Rockström from the Stockholm Resilience Centre and Will Steffen from the Australian National University.

cda3d324e46e.title: Planetary boundaries
cda3d324e46e.sentence: In 2009, according to Rockström and others, three boundaries were already crossed (biodiversity loss, climate change and nitrogen cycle), while others were in imminent danger of being crossed.

13060082db64.title: Planetary boundaries
13060082db64.sentence: According to this update, four of the boundaries were crossed: climate change, loss of biosphere integrity, land-system change, altered biogeochemical cycles (phosphorus and nitrogen).

9dbad646a85e.title: Planetary boundaries
9dbad646a85e.sentence: In 2022, based on the available literature, the introduction of novel entities was concluded to be the 5th transgressed planetary boundary.

357f2737f7ab.title: Planetary boundaries
357f2737f7ab.sentence: Freshwater change was concluded to be the 6th transgressed planetary boundary in 2023 before ocean acidification was documented to be the 7th crossed limit in 2025.

7cc6dcd6bb37.title: Planetary boundaries
7cc6dcd6bb37.section: Subsequent developments > Boundaries related to agriculture and food consumption
7cc6dcd6bb37.sentence: Human activities related to agriculture and nutrition globally contribute to the transgression of four out of nine planetary boundaries.

70d70037c413.title: Planetary boundaries
70d70037c413.section: Subsequent developments > Boundaries related to agriculture and food consumption
70d70037c413.sentence: Surplus nutrient flows (N, P) into aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems are of highest importance, followed by excessive land-system change and biodiversity loss.

b92f19491b84.title: Planetary boundaries
b92f19491b84.section: Usage at international policy level > United Nations
b92f19491b84.sentence: The United Nations secretary general Ban Ki-moon endorsed the concept of planetary boundaries on 16 March 2012, when he presented the key points of the report of his High Level Panel on Global Sustainability to an informal plenary of the UN General Assembly.

770ff2fdc2dd.title: Planetary boundaries
770ff2fdc2dd.section: Usage at international policy level > United Nations
770ff2fdc2dd.sentence: However, the use of the concept was subsequently withdrawn from the text of the conference, "partly due to concerns from some poorer countries that its adoption could lead to the sidelining of poverty reduction and economic development.

9778909ead9a.title: Planetary boundaries
9778909ead9a.sentence: In 2015, several of the scientists in the original group published an update, bringing in new co-authors and new model-based analysis.

357d58fbac86.title: Tipping points in the climate system
357d58fbac86.sentence: In climate science, a tipping point is a critical threshold that, when crossed, leads to large, accelerating and often irreversible changes in the climate system.

12c25f402e55.title: Tipping points in the climate system
12c25f402e55.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report defines a tipping point as a "critical threshold beyond which a system reorganizes, often abruptly and/or irreversibly".

15ab82dabc0d.title: Tipping points in the climate system
15ab82dabc0d.sentence: It can be brought about by a small disturbance causing a disproportionately large change in the system.

21b57be3e79f.title: Tipping points in the climate system
21b57be3e79f.sentence: It can also be associated with self-reinforcing feedbacks, which could lead to changes in the climate system irreversible on a human timescale.

9d04290dfbc5.title: Tipping points in the climate system
9d04290dfbc5.sentence: Tipping behavior is found across the climate system, for example in ice sheets, mountain glaciers, circulation patterns in the ocean, in ecosystems, and the atmosphere.

377fc4d5d2af.title: Tipping points in the climate system
377fc4d5d2af.sentence: At that time the IPCC concluded they would only be likely in the event of global warming of 4 °C (7.2 °F) or more above preindustrial times, and another early assessment placed most tipping point thresholds at 3–5 °C (5.4–9.0 °F) above 1980–1999 average warming.

3a7aa89c7193.title: Tipping points in the climate system
3a7aa89c7193.sentence: As of 2021 tipping points are considered to have significant probability at today's warming level of just over 1 °C (1.8 °F), with high probability above 2 °C (3.6 °F) of global warming.

9fcc744dd5ca.title: Tipping points in the climate system
9fcc744dd5ca.sentence: If tipping points are crossed, they are likely to have severe impacts on human society and may accelerate global warming.

f00db77b9a84.title: Ecosystem collapse
f00db77b9a84.sentence: Yet, if destabilizing processes become strong enough or fast enough to cross a critical threshold within that ecosystem, often described as an ecological 'tipping point', then an ecosystem collapse (sometimes also termed ecological collapse) occurs.

eee86c468904.title: Ecosystem collapse
eee86c468904.sentence: Ecosystem collapse does not mean total disappearance of life from the area, but it does result in the loss of the original ecosystem's defining characteristics, typically including the ecosystem services it may have provided.

86a0a7acfd7e.title: Ecosystem collapse
86a0a7acfd7e.sentence: Ecosystem collapse has also been described as "an analogue of species extinction", and in many cases, it is irreversible, with a new ecosystem appearing instead, which may retain some characteristics of the previous ecosystem, yet has a greatly altered structure and function.

8995176348b5.title: Ecosystem collapse
8995176348b5.sentence: Collapse of an ecosystem is effectively irreversible more often than not, and even if the reversal is possible, it tends to be slow and difficult.

6e9ac3698bcf.title: Ecosystem collapse
6e9ac3698bcf.sentence: There are exceptions where an ecosystem can be recovered past the point of a collapse, but by definition, will always be far more difficult to reverse than allowing a disturbed yet functioning ecosystem to recover, requiring active intervention and/or a prolonged period of time even if it can be reversed.

4252a2d88e82.title: Ecosystem collapse
4252a2d88e82.sentence: Some behaviors that induce transformation are: human intervention in the balance of local diversity (through introduction of new species or overexploitation), alterations in the chemical balance of environments through pollution, modifications of local climate or weather with anthropogenic climate change, and habitat destruction or fragmentation in terrestrial/marine systems.

bec39628737f.title: Ecosystem collapse
bec39628737f.sentence: The collapse can happen when the ecosystem's distribution decreases below a minimal sustainable size, or when key biotic processes and features disappear due to environmental degradation or disruption of biotic interactions.

585814ada674.title: Ecosystem collapse
585814ada674.sentence: Updated 2022 estimates show that even at a global average increase of 1.5 °C (2.7 °F) over pre-industrial temperatures, only 0.2% of the world's coral reefs would still be able to withstand marine heatwaves, as opposed to 84% being able to do so now, with the figure dropping to 0% by 2 °C (3.6 °F) and beyond.

566623c915ed.title: Ecosystem collapse
566623c915ed.section: Contemporary risk > Early detection and monitoring
566623c915ed.sentence: Another indicated that large ecosystem disruptions will occur earlier under more intense climate change: under the high-emissions RCP8.5 scenario, ecosystems in the tropical oceans would be the first to experience abrupt disruption before 2030, with tropical forests and polar environments following by 2050.

1f320d089f2d.title: Ecosystem collapse
1f320d089f2d.sentence: As of now, there is not much information on effective conservation or reversal methods for ecosystem collapse.

36a6cff1faf4.title: Regime shift
36a6cff1faf4.sentence: Regime shifts are large, abrupt, persistent changes in the structure and function of ecosystems, the climate, financial systems or other complex systems.

3f8c2943f925.title: Regime shift
3f8c2943f925.sentence: A regime is a characteristic behaviour of a system which is maintained by mutually reinforced processes or feedbacks.

c60c1ad7ebcf.title: Regime shift
c60c1ad7ebcf.sentence: Regime shifts are triggered either by the weakening of stabilizing internal processes – feedbacks – or by external shocks which exceed the stabilizing capacity of a system.

7d7f940cd52f.title: Regime shift
7d7f940cd52f.sentence: Although such non-linear changes have been widely studied in different disciplines ranging from atoms to climate dynamics, regime shifts have gained importance in ecology because they can substantially affect the flow of ecosystem services that societies rely upon, such as provision of food, clean water or climate regulation.

d7722e197d85.title: Regime shift
d7722e197d85.sentence: Regime shifts are hard to reverse and in some cases irreversible.

7aefb8d8cd96.title: Regime shift
7aefb8d8cd96.sentence: In short, regime shifts describe dynamics characterized by the possibility that a small disturbance can produce big effects.

4231567ebce4.title: Regime shift
4231567ebce4.sentence: In such situations the common notion of proportionality between inputs and outputs of a system is incorrect.

d55065f5ff9e.title: Regime shift
d55065f5ff9e.sentence: Moreover, regime shift occurrence is expected to increase as human influence on the planet increases – the Anthropocene – including current trends on human induced climate change and biodiversity loss.

306d05383448.title: Regime shift
306d05383448.sentence: However, by the 1990s more substantial evidence of regime shifts was collected for kelp forest, coral reefs, drylands and shallow lakes.

c01c337578a4.title: Regime shift
c01c337578a4.sentence: At the regional scale, rainforest areas in the Amazon and East Asia are thought to be at risk of shifting towards savanna regimes given the weakening of the moisture recycling feedback driven by deforestation.

68a15a2ada7c.title: Regime shift
68a15a2ada7c.sentence: The shift from forest to savanna potentially affects the provision of food, fresh water, climate regulation and support for biodiversity.

c6558984b891.section: Nine boundaries > Thresholds and tipping points
c6558984b891.sentence: The control variables were chosen because together they provide an effective way to track the human-caused shift away from Holocene conditions.

b5e3d73aec3a.section: Nine boundaries > Thresholds and tipping points
b5e3d73aec3a.sentence: The quantification of individual planetary boundaries is based on the observed dynamics of the interacting Earth system processes included in the framework.

0fdbbcd9e80d.section: Nine boundaries > Thresholds and tipping points
0fdbbcd9e80d.sentence: The 2009 study identified nine planetary boundaries with quantifications for seven of them, eight of them are now being quantified in 2025.

0bac5bb0d2d0.title: Alternative stable state

bdcb57fa9af8.title: Tipping points in the climate system
bdcb57fa9af8.sentence: Three types of tipping points have been identified—bifurcation, noise-induced and rate-dependent.

3dc26a96d123.title: Tipping points in the climate system
3dc26a96d123.sentence: Bifurcation-induced tipping happens when a particular parameter in the climate (for instance a change in environmental conditions or forcing), passes a critical level – at which point a bifurcation takes place – and what was a stable state loses its stability or simply disappears.

5faf4c312384.title: Tipping points in the climate system
5faf4c312384.sentence: Noise-induced tipping is the transition from one state to another due to random fluctuations or internal variability of the system.

90abdcd66fbf.title: Tipping points in the climate system
90abdcd66fbf.sentence: Noise-induced transitions do not show any of the early warning signals which occur with bifurcations.

17dec14676e9.title: Tipping points in the climate system
17dec14676e9.sentence: This means they are unpredictable because the underlying potential does not change.

2e1d51b80280.title: Tipping points in the climate system

e6e179fe004c.title: Tipping points in the climate system
e6e179fe004c.sentence: In peatlands, for instance, after years of relative stability, rate-induced tipping can lead to an "explosive release of soil carbon from peatlands into the atmosphere" – sometimes known as "compost bomb instability".

8044cfa5727b.title: Ecosystem collapse
8044cfa5727b.sentence: There are two tools commonly used together to assess risks to ecosystems and biodiversity: generic risk assessment protocols and stochastic simulation models.

5e00063c3351.title: Ecosystem collapse
5e00063c3351.sentence: The most notable of the two tactics is risk assessment protocol, particularly because of the IUCN Red List of Ecosystems (RLE), which is widely applicable to many ecosystems even in data-poor circumstances.

0e6ec5422c22.title: Ecosystem collapse
0e6ec5422c22.sentence: The IUCN RLE is a global standard that was developed to assess threats to various ecosystems on local, regional, national, and global scales, as well as to prompt conservation efforts in the face of the unparalleled decline of natural systems in the last decade.

370baddf41b8.title: Ecosystem collapse
370baddf41b8.sentence: The concept of ecosystem collapse is used in the framework to establish categories of risk for ecosystems, with the category Collapsed used as the end-point of risk assessment.

71d631c43efd.title: Ecosystem collapse
71d631c43efd.sentence: Other categories of threat (Vulnerable, Endangered and Critically Endangered) are defined in terms of the probability or risk of collapse.

73d735afce37.title: Ecosystem collapse
73d735afce37.sentence: However, because using this tool is essentially comparing systems to a list of criteria, it is often limited in its ability to look at ecosystem decline holistically; and is thus often used in conjunction with simulation models that consider more aspects of decline such as ecosystem dynamics, future threats, and social-ecological relationships.

6fe720dbbfc9.title: Ecosystem collapse
6fe720dbbfc9.sentence: The Rapa Nui subtropical broadleaf forests in Easter Island, formerly dominated by an endemic palm, are considered collapsed due to the combined effects of overexploitation, climate change and introduced exotic rats.

5a5814b8a1eb.title: Ecosystem collapse
5a5814b8a1eb.sentence: It was once considered one of the largest lakes in the world but has been shrinking since the 1960s after the rivers that fed it were diverted for large scale irrigation.

1baa2a7b64d6.title: Ecosystem collapse

e80eab276dba.title: Ecosystem collapse
e80eab276dba.sentence: Another notable example is the collapse of the Grand Banks cod in the early 1990s, when overfishing reduced fish populations to 1% of their historical levels.

6361467f106f.title: Ecosystem collapse

2415ab6b58af.title: Ecological stability
2415ab6b58af.sentence: This multitude of trends can be labeled by different types of ecological stability.

6130608bb643.title: Ecological stability
6130608bb643.sentence: Resistance is a measure of how little the variable of interest changes in response to external pressures.

1f19ace82e2d.title: Ecological stability
1f19ace82e2d.sentence: Inertia (or persistence) implies that the living system is able to resist external fluctuations.

c961da22d236.title: Ecological stability
c961da22d236.sentence: Resilience is the tendency of a system to retain its functional and organizational structure and the ability to recover after a perturbation or disturbance.

06d40e548471.title: Ecological stability
06d40e548471.sentence: Elasticity is the speed with which a system returns to its original/previous state.

9dcd7ad717c1.title: Ecological stability
9dcd7ad717c1.sentence: Amplitude measures how far a system can be moved from the previous state and still return.

bea791cd1788.title: Ecological stability
bea791cd1788.section: Types > Dynamical stability > Local and global stability
bea791cd1788.sentence: In the sense of perturbation amplitude, local stability indicates that a system is stable over small short-lived disturbances, while global stability indicates a system highly resistant to change in species composition and/or food web dynamics.

895077022513.title: Ecological stability
895077022513.sentence: The relationship between diversity and stability has been widely studied.

a91174a2ea82.title: Ecological stability
a91174a2ea82.sentence: Charles Elton argued in 1958 that complex, diverse communities tended to be more stable.

6f4ae7d01b7a.title: Ecological stability
6f4ae7d01b7a.sentence: After much progress made with experimental studies in the 60's, Robert May advanced the field of theoretical ecology and refuted the idea that diversity begets stability.

11175f004bcb.title: Ecological stability
11175f004bcb.sentence: Diversity can enhance the stability of ecosystem functions at various ecological scales.

3f6b59df782c.title: Ecological stability
3f6b59df782c.sentence: For example, genetic diversity can enhance resistance to environmental perturbations.

c0c00a6bfb95.title: Ecological stability
c0c00a6bfb95.sentence: The effect of diversity on stability in food-web models can be either positive or negative, depending on the trophic coherence of the network.

5af2dc05cb2e.title: Ecological stability

5af2dc05cb2e.sentence: This result is known as the May stability criterion.

7936f9d0650f.sentence: Therefore, the system will lose stability when,S>1σ.
