fe982b614d1e.title: Ecosystem health
fe982b614d1e.sentence: Ecosystem assessments employ two kinds of indicators, descriptive indicators and normative indicators.

29afb7e0670c.title: Ecosystem health
29afb7e0670c.sentence: "Indicators can be used descriptively for a scientific purpose or normatively for a political purpose."

cab63991b686.title: Ecosystem health
cab63991b686.sentence: An indicator is a variable, such as a chemical or biological property, that when measured, is used to infer trends in another (unmeasured) environmental variable or cluster of unmeasured variables (the indicandum).

1118046f7937.title: Ecosystem health
1118046f7937.sentence: Rising chlorophyll-a levels in a lake may signal eutrophication.

99eb7bf6dc23.title: Ecosystem health
99eb7bf6dc23.sentence: A high chlorophyll-a level in a natural successional wetland might be viewed as healthy whereas a human-impacted wetland with the same indicator value may be judged unhealthy.

05785af78f58.title: Ecosystem health
05785af78f58.sentence: A health indicator is a normative indicator, and if conflated with descriptive indicators "implies that normative values can be measured objectively, which is certainly not true.

ea8482006279.title: Ecosystem health
ea8482006279.sentence: The very act of selecting indicators of any kind is biased by the observer's perspective and separation of goals from descriptions has been advocated as a step toward transparency: "A separation of descriptive and normative indicators is essential from the perspective of the philosophy of science...

745f246c3c55.title: Ecosystem health
745f246c3c55.section: Relationship to human health: the health paradox
745f246c3c55.sentence: A trade-off between human health and the "health" of nature has been termed the "health paradox" and it illuminates how human values drive perceptions of ecosystem health.

3c1065b1212e.title: Ecosystem health
3c1065b1212e.section: Relationship to human health: the health paradox
3c1065b1212e.sentence: Human health has benefited by sacrificing the "health" of wild ecosystems, such as dismantling and damming of wild valleys, destruction of mosquito-bearing wetlands, diversion of water for irrigation, conversion of wilderness to farmland, timber removal, and extirpation of tigers, whales, ferrets, and wolves.

8318ae40df42.title: Ecosystem health
8318ae40df42.section: Relationship to human health: the health paradox
8318ae40df42.sentence: These two perspectives have been characterized as utilitarian vs protectionist.

845dceca73f7.title: Ecosystem health
845dceca73f7.section: Relationship to human health: the health paradox
845dceca73f7.sentence: The utilitarian view treats human health and well-being as criteria of ecosystem health.

51ab1aeac07a.title: Ecosystem health
51ab1aeac07a.section: Relationship to human health: the health paradox
51ab1aeac07a.sentence: For example, destruction of wetlands to control malaria mosquitoes "resulted in an improvement in ecosystem health." The protectionist view treats humans as an invasive species: "If there was ever a species that qualified as an invasive pest, it is Homo sapiens."

349980b9d85c.title: Ecosystem health
349980b9d85c.section: Relationship to human health: the health paradox
349980b9d85c.sentence: Proponents of the utilitarian view argue that "healthy ecosystems are characterized by their capability to sustain healthy human populations," and "healthy ecosystems must be economically viable," as it is "unhealthy" ecosystems that are likely to result in increases in contamination, infectious diseases, fires, floods, crop failures and fishery collapse.

81c30491b77c.title: Overshoot (population)
81c30491b77c.sentence: British scholar Thomas Malthus, in his seminal work published in 1798 titled An Essay on the Principle of Population, forecast the potential depletion of the world's food resources due to the growth of human population.

8c487de0f6d0.title: Overshoot (population)
8c487de0f6d0.sentence: In 1968, Paul R. Ehrlich revived Malthus' argument in his book The Population Bomb, wherein he anticipated an impending global famine of catastrophic proportions.

8ad660a963be.title: Overshoot (population)
8ad660a963be.sentence: The predictions of Ehrlich and other neo-Malthusians were challenged by a number of economists, notably Julian Lincoln Simon, who said advances in agriculture, collectively known as the Green Revolution, forestalled any potential global famine in the late 20th century.

caa20c69f217.title: Overshoot (population)
caa20c69f217.sentence: Notably, between 1950 and 1984, the Green Revolution transformed agriculture around the world and grain production increased by over 250%.

066368f1cf65.title: Overshoot (population)
066368f1cf65.sentence: However, neo-Malthusians point out that fossil fuels provided the energy for the Green Revolution, in the form of natural gas-derived fertilizers, oil-derived pesticides, and hydrocarbon-fueled irrigation, and that many crops have become so genetically uniform that a crop failure in any one country could potentially have global repercussions.

5ad009b3a03a.title: Overshoot (population)
5ad009b3a03a.sentence: According to a 2009 report by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the world will have to produce 70% more food by 2050 to feed a projected extra 2.3 billion people.

13365355830a.title: Hysteresis
13365355830a.sentence: This causes hysteresis: the unemployment becomes permanently higher after negative shocks.

70495ea1c947.title: Hysteresis
70495ea1c947.sentence: For example, export performance is subject to strong hysteresis effects: because of the fixed transportation costs it may take a big push to start a country's exports, but once the transition is made, not much may be required to keep them going.

7abfee9f01bf.title: Hysteresis
7abfee9f01bf.sentence: According to theories based on hysteresis, severe economic downturns (recession) and/or persistent stagnation (slow demand growth, usually after a recession) cause unemployed individuals to lose their job skills (commonly developed on the job) or to find that their skills have become obsolete, or become demotivated, disillusioned or depressed or lose job-seeking skills.

9eae3f7e3fe9.title: Hysteresis
9eae3f7e3fe9.sentence: Then, in times of an economic upturn, recovery, or "boom", the affected workers will not share in the prosperity, remaining unemployed for long periods (e.g., over 52 weeks).

15a4591bc9d3.title: Hysteresis
15a4591bc9d3.sentence: Hysteresis has been invoked by Olivier Blanchard among others to explain the differences in long run unemployment rates between Europe and the United States.

e9929c4b84ba.title: Regime shift
e9929c4b84ba.section: Detection of whether a regime shift has occurred
e9929c4b84ba.sentence: Using current well-known statistical methods such as average standard deviates, principal component analysis, or artificial neural networks one can detect whether a regime shift has occurred.

3a5bb17e8379.title: Regime shift
3a5bb17e8379.section: Detection of whether a regime shift has occurred
3a5bb17e8379.sentence: Such analyses require long term data series and that the threshold under study has to be crossed.

e3baef9cd4a8.title: Regime shift
e3baef9cd4a8.section: Detection of whether a regime shift has occurred
e3baef9cd4a8.sentence: In other words, evidence that data does not exhibit multiple regimes does not rule out the possibility a system could shift to an alternative regime in the future.

d87ce10c930a.title: Regime shift
d87ce10c930a.section: Detection of whether a regime shift has occurred
d87ce10c930a.sentence: Moreover, in management decision making, it can be risky to assume that a system has only one regime, when plausible alternative regimes have highly negative consequences.

c54c7d161f45.title: Regime shift
c54c7d161f45.sentence: Systems prone to regime shifts can show three different types of change: smooth, abrupt or discontinuous, depending on the configuration of processes that define a system – in particular the interaction between a system's fast and slow processes.

8491b77711a1.title: Regime shift
8491b77711a1.sentence: Smooth change can be described by a quasi-linear relationship between fast and slow processes; abrupt change shows a non-linear relationship among fast and slow variables, while discontinuous change is characterized by the difference in the trajectory on the fast variable when the slow one increases compared to when it decreases.

317596cccd6e.title: Regime shift
317596cccd6e.sentence: In other words, the point at which the system flips from one regime to another is different from the point at which the system flips back.

8d265ba8bc1e.title: Regime shift
8d265ba8bc1e.sentence: Systems that exhibit this last type of change demonstrate hysteresis.

bb3ca3fb8c8f.title: Regime shift
bb3ca3fb8c8f.sentence: For example, at the local scale, one of the best documented examples is woody plant encroachment, which is thought to follow a smooth change dynamic.

df2ee46ffaee.title: Regime shift
df2ee46ffaee.sentence: Woody encroachment refers to small changes in herbivory rates that can shift drylands from grassy dominated regimes towards woody dominated savannas.

cf2e811cd5de.title: Complex adaptive system
cf2e811cd5de.sentence: A complex adaptive system (CAS) is a system that is complex in that it is a dynamic network of interactions, but the behavior of the ensemble may not be predictable according to the behavior of the components.

1c7030554f3d.title: Complex adaptive system
1c7030554f3d.sentence: John H. Holland said that CAS "are systems that have a large numbers of components, often called agents, that interact and adapt or learn."

159589e49161.title: Complex adaptive system
159589e49161.sentence: Typical examples of complex adaptive systems include: climate; cities; firms; markets; governments; industries; ecosystems; social networks; power grids; animal swarms; traffic flows; social insect (e.g. ant) colonies; the brain and the immune system; and the cell and the developing embryo.

fe58b5c84ae2.title: Complex adaptive system
fe58b5c84ae2.sentence: - The interactions are non-linear: small changes in inputs, physical interactions or stimuli can cause large effects or very significant changes in outputs.

5546a994336e.title: Complex adaptive system
5546a994336e.sentence: - Any interaction can feed back onto itself directly or after a number of intervening stages.

d0f81a97925a.title: Complex adaptive system
d0f81a97925a.sentence: CAS can be hierarchical, but more often exhibit aspects of "self-organization".

58873660aae2.title: Complex adaptive system
58873660aae2.sentence: Complex adaptive systems feature a high degree of adaptive capacity, giving them resilience in the face of perturbation.

3b1469e09980.title: Complex adaptive system
3b1469e09980.sentence: - Complex systems operate under far from equilibrium conditions.

ce750847f1e3.title: Complex adaptive system
ce750847f1e3.sentence: There has to be a constant flow of energy to maintain the organization of the system

64e484f30473.title: Complex adaptive system
64e484f30473.sentence: The term complex adaptive system was coined in 1968 by sociologist Walter F. Buckley who proposed a model of cultural evolution which regards psychological and socio-cultural systems as analogous with biological species.

7a1c40687dda.title: Complex adaptive system
7a1c40687dda.sentence: CAS is increasingly applied to analyze political-economic development and institutional change, where outcomes emerge from interactions among adaptive agents, and may be influenced but not precisely controlled.

2dfdb380555c.title: Complex adaptive system
2dfdb380555c.sentence: CAS are occasionally modelled by means of agent-based models and complex network-based models.

fe19d749773b.title: Socio-ecological system
fe19d749773b.sentence: A social-ecological system consists of 'a bio-geo-physical' unit and its associated social actors and institutions.

7ce53d6bd385.title: Socio-ecological system
7ce53d6bd385.sentence: The socio-ecological system consists of a bio-geophysical (the built and natural environment) unit and the social actors (the individual people, the organization, the governance) and institutions.

d3436f8a72b4.title: Socio-ecological system
d3436f8a72b4.sentence: Social-ecological systems are based on the concept that humans are a part of—not separate from—nature.

bd0b78e66b50.title: Socio-ecological system
bd0b78e66b50.sentence: This concept, which holds that the delineation between social systems and natural systems is arbitrary and artificial, was first put forth by Berkes and Folke, and its theory was further developed by Berkes et al.

ac8355737aa1.title: Socio-ecological system
ac8355737aa1.sentence: While resilience has somewhat different meaning in social and ecological context, the SES approach holds that social and ecological systems are linked through feedback mechanisms, and that both display resilience and complexity.

6759e4c1ecd2.title: Socio-ecological system
6759e4c1ecd2.sentence: Social-ecological systems are complex and adaptive and delimited by spatial or functional boundaries surrounding particular ecosystems and their context problems.

079482e57d7b.title: Socio-ecological system
079482e57d7b.sentence: It generates path dependency, which refers to local rules of interaction that change as the system evolves and develops.

eb98ed776844.title: Socio-ecological system
eb98ed776844.sentence: A consequence of path dependency is the existence of multiple basins of attraction in ecosystem development and the potential for threshold behaviour and qualitative shifts in system dynamics under changing environmental influences.

2e6c7339430c.title: Socio-ecological system
2e6c7339430c.sentence: In a complex system many subsystems can be distinguished; and since many complex systems are hierarchic, each subsystem is nested in a larger subsystem etc.

67cba1af6087.title: Socio-ecological system
67cba1af6087.sentence: Therefore, complex systems should always be analysed or managed simultaneously at different scales.

ffe97d4ad9ee.title: Socio-ecological system
ffe97d4ad9ee.sentence: It is thus the communities which interact with ecosystems on the daily basis and over long periods of time that possess the most relevant knowledge of resource and ecosystem dynamics, together with associated management practices.

5d5b349a53e5.title: Socio-ecological system
5d5b349a53e5.sentence: The adaptive cycle, originally conceptualised by Holling (1986) interprets the dynamics of complex ecosystems in response to disturbance and change.

f65067f9fcd0.title: Socio-ecological system
f65067f9fcd0.sentence: In terms of its dynamics, the adaptive cycle has been described as moving slowly from exploitation (r) to conservation (K), maintaining and developing very rapidly from K to release (Omega), continuing rapidly to reorganisation (alpha) and back to exploitation (r).

a659671d0609.title: Socio-ecological system
a659671d0609.sentence: Depending on the particular configuration of the system, it can then begin a new adaptive cycle or alternatively it may transform into a new configuration, shown as an exit arrow.

44548dec8ca4.title: Socio-ecological system
44548dec8ca4.sentence: The two main dimensions that determine changes in an adaptive cycle are connectedness and potential.

311a882f584d.title: Socio-ecological system
311a882f584d.sentence: The adaptive cycle thus predicts that the four phases of the cycle can be distinguished based on distinct combinations of high or low potential and connectedness.

98dec97e3336.title: Socio-ecological system
98dec97e3336.sentence: Adaptability is the capacity of a social-ecological system to learn and adjust to both internal and external processes.

b0f7d4ce6618.title: Socio-ecological system
b0f7d4ce6618.sentence: Transformability is the capacity of a system to transform into a completely new system, when ecological, economic, or social structures make the current system unsustainable.

2a039cc18f49.title: Socio-ecological system
2a039cc18f49.sentence: Adaptability and transformability are prerequisites for resilience.

61c8038cca60.title: Socio-ecological system
61c8038cca60.sentence: The concept of resilience is a promising tool for analysing adaptive change towards sustainability because it provides a way for analysing how to manipulate stability in the face of change.

b991b66a5d09.title: Socio-ecological system
b991b66a5d09.sentence: Such an arrangement in governance creates the opportunity for institutional learning to take place, allowing for a successful period of reorganisation and growth.

bf727f341edf.title: Socio-ecological system
bf727f341edf.sentence: In order to emphasise the key requirements of a social-ecological system for successful adaptive governance, Folke and colleagues contrasted case studies from the Florida Everglades and the Grand Canyon.

635293f4e000.title: Socio-ecological system
635293f4e000.sentence: Both are complex social-ecological systems that have experiences unwanted degradation of their ecosystem services, but differ substantially in terms of their institutional make-up.

b3fb0e2efeab.title: Socio-ecological system
b3fb0e2efeab.sentence: The governance structure in the Everglades is dominated by the interests of agriculture and environmentalists who have been in conflict over the need to conserve the habitat at the expense of agricultural productivity throughout history.

f4c55624c2be.title: Socio-ecological system
f4c55624c2be.sentence: Here, a few feedbacks between the ecological system and the social system exist, and the SES is unable to innovate and adapt (the α-phase of reorganisation and growth).

59f6b67ff2ce.title: Socio-ecological system
59f6b67ff2ce.sentence: In contrast, different stakeholders have formed an adaptive management workgroup in the case of Grand Canyon, using planned management interventions and monitoring to learn about changes occurring in the ecosystem including the best ways to subsequently manage them.

c5dc40c43c15.title: Climate governance
c5dc40c43c15.sentence: A relatively new approach to governing climate impacts upon social systems is to use the flexible technique of adaptive governance, introduced by Holling in 1978 as opposed to the more mitigation-focused approaches which have generally dominated efforts thus far.

0bb77343d495.title: Socio-ecological system
0bb77343d495.sentence: Elinor Ostrom and her many co-researchers developed a comprehensive "Social-Ecological Systems (SES) framework", which includes much of the theory of common-pool resources and collective self-governance.

9eac6fca87e5.title: Socio-ecological system
9eac6fca87e5.sentence: It draws heavily on systems ecology and complexity theory.

ccbaac104248.title: Socio-ecological system
ccbaac104248.sentence: The studies of SES include some central societal concerns (e.g. equity and human wellbeing) that have traditionally received little attention in complex adaptive systems theory, and there are areas of complexity theory (e.g. quantum physics) that have little direct relevance for understanding SES.

ac7aecc4f81d.title: Socio-ecological system
ac7aecc4f81d.sentence: While SES theory draws on a range of discipline-specific theories, such as island biogeography, optimal foraging theory, and microeconomic theory, it is much broader than any of these individual theories alone.

b81b06b6466f.title: Alternative stable state
b81b06b6466f.sentence: State shifts are often illustrated heuristically by the ball-in-cup model (Holling, C.S. et al., 1995) Biodiversity in the functioning of ecosystems: an ecological synthesis.

1da14d332574.title: Alternative stable state
1da14d332574.sentence: A ball, representing the ecosystem, exists on a surface where any point along the surface represents a possible state.

6d385d6d7a4f.title: Alternative stable state
6d385d6d7a4f.sentence: In the simplest model, the landscape consists of two valleys separated by a hill.

6c4de4f73985.title: Alternative stable state
6c4de4f73985.sentence: When the ball is in a valley, or a "domain of attraction", it exists in a stable state and must be perturbed to move from this state.

0acfa6e11ca6.title: Alternative stable state
0acfa6e11ca6.sentence: In the ball-and-cup model, this would be the energy required to push the ball up and over a hill, where it would fall downhill into a different valley.

48f782837a3b.title: Alternative stable state
48f782837a3b.sentence: In the ball-and-cup model, a valley with steep sides has greater resilience than a shallow valley, since it would take more force to push the ball up the hill and out of the valley.

034f876f87a7.title: Alternative stable state
034f876f87a7.sentence: Ecosystems can shift from one state to another via a significant perturbation directly to state variables.

4a621bcc3f80.title: Alternative stable state
4a621bcc3f80.sentence: This perspective requires a change in environmental parameters that affect the behavior of state variables.

3de32abdefd3.title: Alternative stable state
3de32abdefd3.sentence: State variables are quantities that change quickly (in ecologically-relevant time scales) in response to feedbacks from the system (i.e., they are dependent on system feedbacks), such as population densities.

7bef012b6bf6.title: Alternative stable state
7bef012b6bf6.sentence: Ecosystem parameters are quantities that are unresponsive (or respond very slowly) to feedbacks from the system (i.e., they are independent of system feedbacks).

255ecab76fbd.title: Alternative stable state
255ecab76fbd.sentence: The community perspective requires the existence of alternative stable states (i.e., more than one valley) before the perturbation, since the landscape is not changing.

450f223b2776.title: Alternative stable state
450f223b2776.sentence: Changing the landscape can modify the number, location, and resilience of stable states, as well as the unstable intermediate states.

7cd63fe566b9.title: Alternative stable state
7cd63fe566b9.sentence: Often, humans influence stable states by reducing the resilience of basins of attraction.

77786049bd39.title: Alternative stable state
77786049bd39.sentence: There are at least three ways in which anthropogenic forces reduce resilience (Folke et al. 2004): (1) Decreasing diversity and functional groups, often by top-down effects (e.g., overfishing); (2) altering the physico-chemical environment (e.g., climate change, pollution, fertilization); or (3) modifying disturbance regimes to which organisms are adapted (e.g., bottom trawling, coral mining, etc.).

607bb91fb434.title: Alternative stable state
607bb91fb434.sentence: When the resilience is decreased, ecosystems can be pushed into alternative, and often less-desirable, stable states with only minor perturbations.

4cf928948b6d.title: Alternative stable state
4cf928948b6d.sentence: Shifts to less-desirable states often entail a loss of ecosystem service and function, and have been documented in an array of terrestrial, marine, and freshwater environments (reviewed in Folke et al. 2004).

1b1835d46a6c.title: Resistance (ecology)
1b1835d46a6c.sentence: English ecologist Charles Elton applied the term resistance to the ecosystem properties which limit the ability of introduced species to successfully invade communities.

fc67bfedda7e.title: Resistance (ecology)
fc67bfedda7e.sentence: These properties include both abiotic factors like temperature and drought, and biotic factors including competition, parasitism, predation and the lack of necessary mutualists.

5373da95ab93.title: Resistance (ecology)
5373da95ab93.sentence: Higher species diversity and lower resource availability can also contribute to resistance.

e61e37f4a1de.title: Coupled human–environment system
e61e37f4a1de.sentence: - Telecoupling provides guidance for research on two systems that are spatially distant from each other.

faad5d054cb2.title: Coupled human–environment system
faad5d054cb2.sentence: - Intracoupling is for research within one coupled system

b761376b5d92.title: Coupled human–environment system
b761376b5d92.sentence: - Pericoupling is used to analyze two coupled systems that are geographically adjacent from each other.

f6e97619f357.title: Coupled human–environment system
f6e97619f357.sentence: - Metacoupling uses all three previous frameworks (intracoupling, pericoupling, and telecoupling) at the same time.

4457f0640579.title: Coupled human–environment system
4457f0640579.sentence: - Sending system: a sending system is a system that sends a flow to another system, either adjacent or distant.

5a717151aec9.title: Coupled human–environment system
5a717151aec9.sentence: - Receiving system: a receiving system is a system that receives a flow to another system, either adjacent or distant.

855e5bdca40f.title: Coupled human–environment system
855e5bdca40f.sentence: - Spillover: A spillover system is a separate system affected by the interactions within the focal system.

c90386344af6.sentence: The measurement of "critical slowing down" (CSD) is one approach for developing early warning signals for a potential or likely onset of approaching collapse.

1b86fb8ceed5.sentence: This, in turn, may lead to an increase in (spatial or temporal) autocorrelation and variance, while variance spectra tend to lower frequencies, and the 'direction of critical slowing down' in a system's state space may be indicative of a system's future state when delayed negative feedbacks leading to oscillatory or other complex dynamics are weak.

2ece60bddf35.title: Tipping points in the climate system

2ece60bddf35.sentence: These systems display critical slowing down, with an increased memory (rising autocorrelation) and variance.

5f4f2d895d2a.title: Ecosystem collapse
5f4f2d895d2a.sentence: In 2022, research found that more than three-quarters of the Amazon rainforest has been losing resilience due to deforestation and climate change since the early 2000s as measured by recovery-time from short-term perturbations (the critical slowing down), reinforcing the theory that it is approaching a critical transition.

40d2ac33a252.title: Tipping points in the climate system
40d2ac33a252.section: Mathematical theory > Bifurcation-induced tipping > Early warning signals
40d2ac33a252.sentence: Using early warning signals (increased autocorrelation and variance of the melt rate time series), it has been suggested that the Greenland ice sheet is currently losing resilience, consistent with modelled early warning signals of the ice sheet.

6b1dfe62edcd.title: Regime shift

b4ed3c09d329.section: Mathematical theory > Bifurcation-induced tipping > Early warning signals
b4ed3c09d329.sentence: Human-induced changes in the climate system may be too fast for early warning signals to become evident, especially in systems with inertia.

49e773d19bcd.sentence: Panarchy views coupled human-natural systems as a cross-scale set of adaptive cycles that reflect the dynamic nature of human and natural structures across time and space.

89663ee8a98d.title: Ecological resilience
89663ee8a98d.sentence: - Panarchy: the degree to which a certain hierarchical level of an ecosystem is influenced by other levels.

d3baa05d9bbd.title: C. S. Holling
d3baa05d9bbd.sentence: He has introduced important ideas in the application of ecology and evolution, including resilience, adaptive management, the adaptive cycle, and panarchy.

1625bfa39323.title: C. S. Holling
1625bfa39323.sentence: This work resulted in the 2002 book Panarchy: understanding transformations in human and natural systems.

ba475f67b946.title: Socio-ecological system
ba475f67b946.sentence: The notion of panarchy and adaptive cycles has become an important theoretical lens to describe the resilience of ecological systems and, more recently, social-ecological systems.

c0b1787d3033.title: Socio-ecological system
c0b1787d3033.sentence: Although panarchy theory originates in ecology, it has found widespread applications in other disciplines.

56c21b090aab.title: Socio-ecological system
56c21b090aab.sentence: For example, in management, Wieland (2021) describes a panarchy that represents the planetary, political-economic, and supply chain levels.

5f8db879b332.title: Ecological resilience
5f8db879b332.sentence: Ecologists Brian Walker, C S Holling and others describe four critical aspects of resilience: latitude, resistance, precariousness, and panarchy.

72926bb81046.title: Ecological resilience
72926bb81046.sentence: - Latitude: the maximum amount a system can be changed before losing its ability to recover (before crossing a threshold which, if breached, makes recovery difficult or impossible).

833a21ab4844.title: Ecological resilience
833a21ab4844.sentence: - Resistance: the ease or difficulty of changing the system; how “resistant” it is to being changed.

de21bf985e27.title: Ecological resilience
de21bf985e27.sentence: - Precariousness: how close the current state of the system is to a limit or “threshold.”.

96bf3d02e467.title: Ecological resilience

7dd99fb4e3e0.title: Forest
7dd99fb4e3e0.sentence: A forest is an ecosystem characterized by a dense community of trees.

0e1fea61de0c.title: Forest
0e1fea61de0c.sentence: Hundreds of definitions of forest are used throughout the world, incorporating factors such as tree density, tree height, land use, legal standing, and ecological function.

df9e2d36f456.title: Forest
df9e2d36f456.sentence: The United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) defines a forest as, "Land spanning more than 0.5 hectares with trees higher than 5 meters and a canopy cover of more than 10 percent, or trees able to reach these thresholds in situ.

c44675378065.title: Forest
c44675378065.sentence: It does not include land that is predominantly under agricultural or urban use." Using this definition, Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025 found that forests covered 4.14 billion hectares (10.2 billion acres; 41.4 million square kilometres; 16.0 million square miles), or approximately 31 percent of the world's land area in 2025.

55fed4acb3ec.title: Forest
55fed4acb3ec.sentence: The world has a total forest area of 4.14 billion hectares (ha), which is 32% of the global land area and equivalent to 0.50 ha of forest per person.

4d838df8477a.title: Forest
4d838df8477a.sentence: The tropical domain has the largest proportion of the world’s forests (45%), followed by the boreal, temperate and subtropical domains.

36786ec0fa03.title: Forest
36786ec0fa03.sentence: Forests account for 75% of the gross primary production of the Earth's biosphere, and contain 80% of the Earth's plant biomass.

bcac67920dba.title: Forest
bcac67920dba.sentence: - Converting carbon dioxide into oxygen and biomass.

a8d1e1fbcf51.title: Forest
a8d1e1fbcf51.sentence: For example, research from 2017 shows that forests induce rainfall.

73daeeb2780e.title: Forest
73daeeb2780e.sentence: - Mitigating natural hazards such as floods.

e2a605965940.title: Forest
e2a605965940.sentence: - Serving as a source of woodlands and trees for millions of people dependent almost entirely on forests for subsistence for their essential fuelwood, food, and fodder needs.

585eede70a2e.title: Forest
585eede70a2e.sentence: An important consideration regarding carbon sequestration is that forests can turn from a carbon sink to a carbon source if plant diversity, density or forest area decreases, as has been observed in different tropical forests The typical tropical forest may become a carbon source by the 2060s.

5cf631833178.title: Forest

f6fb99a78a7c.title: Forest

4989f17f006c.title: Aquatic ecosystem
4989f17f006c.sentence: An aquatic ecosystem is an ecosystem found in and around a body of water, in contrast to land-based terrestrial ecosystems.

307b4071a25c.title: Aquatic ecosystem
307b4071a25c.sentence: Aquatic ecosystems contain communities of organisms—aquatic life—that are dependent on each other and on their environment.

c576c717a5f5.title: Aquatic ecosystem
c576c717a5f5.sentence: The two main types of aquatic ecosystems are marine ecosystems and freshwater ecosystems.

5b4cd74190c0.title: Aquatic ecosystem
5b4cd74190c0.sentence: Freshwater ecosystems may be lentic (slow moving water, including pools, ponds, and lakes); lotic (faster moving water, for example streams and rivers); and wetlands (areas where the soil is saturated or inundated for at least part of the time).

aa591ad2629e.title: Aquatic ecosystem
aa591ad2629e.sentence: Aquatic environments have relatively low oxygen levels, forcing adaptation by the organisms found there.

b5e11df14061.title: Aquatic ecosystem
b5e11df14061.sentence: For example, many wetland plants must produce aerenchyma to carry oxygen to roots.

7e8b0b05fc71.title: Aquatic ecosystem
7e8b0b05fc71.sentence: Algae use solar energy to generate biomass from carbon dioxide and are possibly the most important autotrophic organisms in aquatic environments.

8f86e0e341cd.title: Aquatic ecosystem
8f86e0e341cd.sentence: The more shallow the water, the greater the biomass contribution from rooted and floating vascular plants.

bfbe7f1bce7e.title: Aquatic ecosystem
bfbe7f1bce7e.sentence: These two sources combine to produce the extraordinary production of estuaries and wetlands, as this autotrophic biomass is converted into fish, birds, amphibians and other aquatic species.

2f86457d8e9c.title: Wetland
2f86457d8e9c.sentence: A wetland is a distinct semi-aquatic ecosystem whose groundcovers are flooded or saturated in water, either permanently, for years or decades, or only seasonally.

dc8bafb3a383.title: Wetland
dc8bafb3a383.sentence: Wetlands form a transitional zone between waterbodies and dry lands, and are different from other terrestrial or aquatic ecosystems due to their vegetation's roots having adapted to oxygen-poor waterlogged soils.

93158e2b5b4e.title: Wetland
93158e2b5b4e.sentence: Flooding results in oxygen-poor (anoxic) processes taking place, especially in the soils.

c8d193cd6bdb.title: Wetland
c8d193cd6bdb.sentence: They are considered among the most biologically diverse of all ecosystems, serving as habitats to a wide range of aquatic and semi-aquatic plants and animals, with often improved water quality due to plant removal of excess nutrients such as nitrates and phosphorus.

25278621d7e2.title: Wetland
25278621d7e2.sentence: Wetlands exist on every continent, except Antarctica.

4b38f65ef03b.title: Wetland
4b38f65ef03b.sentence: The water in wetlands is either freshwater, brackish or saltwater.

8e32c272b4da.title: Wetland
8e32c272b4da.sentence: For example, marshes are wetlands dominated by emergent herbaceous vegetation such as reeds, cattails, and sedges.

c650901120ce.title: Wetland
c650901120ce.sentence: Swamps are dominated by woody vegetation, such as trees and shrubs (although reed swamps in Europe are dominated by reeds, not trees).

9cf99ccc7c78.title: Wetland
9cf99ccc7c78.sentence: Peatlands are a unique kind of wetland where lush plant growth and slow decay of dead plants (under anoxic conditions) results in organic peat accumulating; bogs, fens, and mires are different names for peatlands.

8e05068a60a0.title: Wetland
8e05068a60a0.sentence: The most important factor producing wetlands is hydrology, or flooding.

966e22226ebb.title: Wetland
966e22226ebb.sentence: The duration of flooding or prolonged soil saturation by groundwater determines whether the resulting wetland has aquatic, marsh or swamp vegetation.

386ce9684431.title: Wetland
386ce9684431.sentence: Wetlands contribute many ecosystem services that benefit people.

69618d06a58b.title: Wetland
69618d06a58b.sentence: These include for example water purification, stabilization of shorelines, storm protection and flood control.

4ee768caf6af.title: Wetland

3abf8d3f7dea.title: Wetland
3abf8d3f7dea.sentence: The world's largest wetlands include the Amazon River basin, the West Siberian Plain, the Pantanal in South America, and the Sundarbans in the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta.

193398444b34.title: Mangrove

a4ed730a1cf1.title: Mangrove
a4ed730a1cf1.sentence: The term is also used for tropical coastal vegetation consisting of such species.

953ac104e171.title: Mangrove
953ac104e171.sentence: They occur worldwide in tropical and subtropical coastal areas, mainly between latitudes 30° N and 30° S, with the greatest mangrove area within 5° of the equator.

2bedb6c0c6aa.title: Mangrove

300a335420ec.title: Mangrove

9567356eea96.title: Mangrove

779039f1beaf.title: Mangrove
779039f1beaf.sentence: Among countries and areas, Indonesia has the world's largest extent of mangroves, at 3.40 million ha, followed by Brazil (1.39 million ha), Australia (1.11 million ha), Nigeria (976,000 ha) and Mexico (947,000 ha).

efaf661ed1ef.title: Mangrove
efaf661ed1ef.sentence: Collectively, these five countries host almost half (49%) of the global mangrove area.

2d65fd141fc2.title: Mangrove

03a6bbf528a2.title: Mangrove

277b13d8f3d9.title: Mangrove

a24df1fc351d.title: Mangrove
a24df1fc351d.sentence: They protect nearby areas from tsunamis and extreme weather events.

ac288bbf823d.title: Mangrove
ac288bbf823d.sentence: Mangrove forests are also effective at carbon sequestration and storage.

2fd802e3fd65.title: Mangrove
2fd802e3fd65.sentence: However, a given mangrove swamp typically features only a small number of tree species.

40fdd5ec4489.title: Mangrove

5f95a5e6b762.title: Grassland

3c31c27424d8.title: Grassland

30afe32d040a.title: Grassland

ff9b349c7d31.sentence: - "...terrestrial ecosystems dominated by herbaceous and shrub vegetation, and maintained by fire, grazing, drought and/or freezing temperatures." (Pilot Assessment of Global Ecosystems, 2000)

d2ae2b955a96.title: Grassland
d2ae2b955a96.sentence: Grasslands support the greatest aggregations of large animals on Earth, including jaguars, African wild dogs, pronghorn, black-footed ferret, plains bison, mountain plover, African elephant, Sunda tiger, black rhino, white rhino, savanna elephant, greater one-horned rhino, Indian elephant and swift fox.

e4530199ec62.title: Grassland
e4530199ec62.sentence: Grasslands provide a range of marketed and non-marketed ecosystem services that are fundamental to the livelihoods of an estimated one billion people globally.

65cd89b8bd7d.title: Grassland
65cd89b8bd7d.sentence: Grasslands hold about twenty percent of global soil carbon stocks.

15d0bba2ef7b.title: Grassland
15d0bba2ef7b.sentence: Grasslands are among the most threatened ecosystems, and have been described as the most imperiled terrestrial biome.

da8861420908.title: Grassland
da8861420908.sentence: Grasslands have experienced a far greater rate of global conversion than forests, yet receive relatively little federal or international protection.

5bd01963e47a.title: Peatland
5bd01963e47a.sentence: A peatland is a type of wetland whose soils consist of organic matter from decaying plants, forming layers of peat.

1e7dd8a7c4d2.title: Peatland
1e7dd8a7c4d2.sentence: Peatlands arise because of incomplete decomposition of organic matter, usually litter from vegetation, due to water-logging and subsequent anoxia.

64c3d412b74f.title: Peatland
64c3d412b74f.sentence: Covering around 3 million km2 globally, they sequester 0.37 gigatons (Gt) of carbon dioxide (CO2) a year.

69a7bc81c656.title: Peatland
69a7bc81c656.sentence: Peatlands are the largest natural carbon store on land.

76a49ee066cf.title: Peatland
76a49ee066cf.sentence: Peat soils store over 600 Gt of carbon, more than the carbon stored in all other vegetation types, including forests.

ebf384a42b3f.title: Peatland
ebf384a42b3f.sentence: In their natural state, peatlands provide a range of ecosystem services, including minimising flood risk and erosion, purifying water and regulating climate.

15a51f92f554.title: Peatland
15a51f92f554.sentence: Peatlands are under threat by commercial peat harvesting, drainage and conversion for agriculture (notably palm oil in the tropics) and fires, which are predicted to become more frequent with climate change.

3729443cc871.title: Peatland
3729443cc871.sentence: The destruction of peatlands results in release of stored greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, further exacerbating climate change.

338450ce8051.title: Peatland
338450ce8051.sentence: Peatlands are found around the globe, although are at their greatest extent at high latitudes in the Northern Hemisphere.

75ee8581da58.title: Wetland
75ee8581da58.sentence: Depending on a wetland's geographic and topographic location, the functions it performs can support multiple ecosystem services, values, or benefits.

a237b50d3f54.title: Wetland
a237b50d3f54.sentence: United Nations Millennium Ecosystem Assessment and Ramsar Convention described wetlands as a whole to be of biosphere significance and societal importance in the following areas:

aef3a87c7eaa.title: Wetland
aef3a87c7eaa.sentence: > The economic worth of the ecosystem services provided to society by intact, naturally functioning wetlands is frequently much greater than the perceived benefits of converting them to 'more valuable' intensive land use – particularly as the profits from unsustainable use often go to relatively few individuals or corporations, rather than being shared by society as a whole.

0a56621c2044.title: Wetland
0a56621c2044.sentence: To replace these wetland ecosystem services, enormous amounts of money would need to be spent on water purification plants, dams, levees, and other hard infrastructure, and many of the services are impossible to replace.

7d7d4888ff8e.title: Wetland
7d7d4888ff8e.section: Ecosystem services > Shoreline stabilization and storm protection
7d7d4888ff8e.sentence: One analysis using the impact of hurricanes versus storm protection provided naturally by wetlands projected the value of this service at US$33,000/hectare/year.

6597e695952a.title: Wetland
6597e695952a.sentence: Many wetlands are directly linked to groundwater and they can be a crucial regulator of both the quantity and quality of water found below the ground.

411fb2bec49d.title: Wetland
411fb2bec49d.sentence: Substrates that are porous allow water to filter down through the soil and underlying rock into aquifers which are the source of much of the world's drinking water.

d533777f958c.title: Wetland
d533777f958c.section: Ecosystem services > Shoreline stabilization and storm protection
d533777f958c.sentence: Tidal and inter-tidal wetland systems protect and stabilize coastal zones.

c23c29e221b2.title: Wetland
c23c29e221b2.section: Ecosystem services > Shoreline stabilization and storm protection
c23c29e221b2.sentence: The main conservation benefit these systems have against storms and storm surges is the ability to reduce the speed and height of waves and floodwaters.

dc44594e8930.title: Wetland
dc44594e8930.section: Ecosystem services > Additional services and uses of wetlands
dc44594e8930.sentence: Pollination services are supported by many wetlands which may provide the only suitable habitat for pollinating insects, birds, and mammals in highly developed areas.

156131ab10cd.title: Tropical forest
156131ab10cd.sentence: Tropical forests are forested ecoregions with tropical climates – that is, land areas approximately bounded by the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, but possibly affected by other factors such as prevailing winds.

e91ded06070b.title: Tropical forest
e91ded06070b.sentence: The tropical domain has the largest proportion of the world's forests (45 percent), followed by the boreal, temperate and subtropical domains.

0fe283ef552d.title: Biodiversity
0fe283ef552d.sentence: About 60 percent of all vascular plants are found in tropical forests.

0267bf2a1b51.title: Tropical forest
0267bf2a1b51.sentence: Tropical forests are often thought of as evergreen rainforests and moist forests, but these account for only a portion of them (depending on how they are defined – see maps).

bbd57ba6ac1d.title: Tropical forest
bbd57ba6ac1d.sentence: The remaining tropical forests are a diversity of many different forest types including: Eucalyptus open forest, tropical coniferous forests, savanna woodland (e.g. Sahelian forest), and mountain forests (the higher elevations of which are cloud forests).

111ec7173df8.title: Tropical forest
111ec7173df8.sentence: There is no single scheme that defines what a forest is, in tropical regions or elsewhere.

b02118930b44.title: Tropical forest
b02118930b44.sentence: Because of these difficulties, information on the extent of tropical forests varies between sources.

6e3e376d1108.title: Tropical forest
6e3e376d1108.sentence: Current deforestation in the biodiversity hotspots of North and South America, sub-Saharan Africa, South-East Asia and the Pacific, can be attributed to export of commodities such as: beef, soy, coffee, cacao, palm oil, and timber; there is a requirement for "strong transnational efforts... by improving supply chain transparency [and] public–private engagement".

5c43807a04b0.title: Tropical forest
5c43807a04b0.sentence: A widely-held view is that placing a value on the ecosystem services these forests provide may bring about more sustainable policies.

7748835bf18c.title: Tropical forest
7748835bf18c.sentence: However, clear monitoring and evaluation mechanisms for environmental, social and economic outcomes are needed.

0511229361ca.title: Tropical forest
0511229361ca.sentence: The tropical forest was originally identified as a specific type of biome in 1949.

6dabebbea8ea.title: Tropical rainforest
6dabebbea8ea.sentence: A tropical rainforest is a dense and warm rainforest with high rainfall, typically found between 10° north and south of the Equator.

bbacb5434a4f.title: Tropical rainforest
bbacb5434a4f.sentence: True rainforests usually occur in tropical rainforest climates where no dry season occurs; all months have an average precipitation of at least 60 mm (2.4 in).

2d34768551c6.title: Tropical rainforest
2d34768551c6.sentence: Mean monthly temperatures exceed 18 °C (64 °F) during all months of the year.

d66e0382b07e.title: Tropical rainforest
d66e0382b07e.sentence: This high level of precipitation often results in poor soils due to leaching of soluble nutrients in the ground.

18986a49b00b.title: Tropical rainforest
18986a49b00b.sentence: Most of the nutrients within the soil of a tropical rainforest occur near the surface because of the rapid turnover time and decomposition of organisms and leaves.

b3c52b0a6201.title: Tropical rainforest
b3c52b0a6201.sentence: Rain forests play an important role in maintaining biological diversity, sequestering and storing carbon, global climate regulation, disease control, and pollination.

09434a0e062b.title: Tropical rainforest
09434a0e062b.sentence: Half of the rainfall in the Amazon area is produced by the forests.

ed116ae57a72.title: Deforestation
ed116ae57a72.section: Impacts > On the environment > Changes to the water cycle
ed116ae57a72.sentence: Tropical rainforests produce about 30% of Earth's fresh water.

3bf47bafa428.title: Energy flow (ecology)
3bf47bafa428.section: Energy flow across ecosystems > Aquatic vs terrestrial ecosystems
3bf47bafa428.sentence: Among terrestrial ecosystems, marshes, swamps, and tropical rainforests have the highest primary production rates, whereas tundra and alpine ecosystems have the lowest.

d8b2bba7fce9.title: Tropical rainforest
d8b2bba7fce9.section: Human dimensions > Resources > Cultivated foods and spices
d8b2bba7fce9.sentence: Yam, coffee, chocolate, banana, mango, papaya, macadamia, avocado, and sugarcane all originally came from tropical rainforest and are still mostly grown on plantations in regions that were formerly primary forest.

c3046abaaeb7.title: Tropical rainforest
c3046abaaeb7.section: Conservation > Threats > Deforestation > Mining and drilling
c3046abaaeb7.sentence: These resources are important to developing nations and their extraction is often given priority to encourage economic growth.

c8123355c594.title: Tropical rainforest
c8123355c594.section: Conservation > Threats > Deforestation > Mining and drilling
c8123355c594.sentence: Mining and drilling can require large amounts of land development, directly causing deforestation.

29cd58823edc.title: Tropical rainforest
29cd58823edc.section: Conservation > Threats > Deforestation > Conversion to agricultural land
29cd58823edc.sentence: With the invention of agriculture, humans were able to clear sections of rainforest to produce crops, converting it to open farmland.

8f11fb4d4d91.title: Tropical rainforest
8f11fb4d4d91.sentence: International policy has also introduced a market incentive program called Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) for companies and governments to outset their carbon emissions through financial investments into rainforest conservation.

69ceef073822.title: Old-growth forest
69ceef073822.sentence: An old-growth forest is a forest that has developed over a long period of time without disturbance.

b6cec0aa872f.title: Old-growth forest
b6cec0aa872f.sentence: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations defines primary forests as naturally regenerated forests of native tree species where there are no clearly visible indications of human activity and the ecological processes are not significantly disturbed.

e1e6634de193.title: Old-growth forest
e1e6634de193.sentence: One-third (34%) of the world's forests are primary forests.

904df1b1f80e.title: Old-growth forest
904df1b1f80e.sentence: Old-growth forests tend to have large trees and standing dead trees, multilayered canopies with gaps that result from the deaths of individual trees, and coarse woody debris on the forest floor.

0a84c944c20d.title: Old-growth forest
0a84c944c20d.sentence: A forest regenerated after a severe disturbance, such as wildfire, insect infestation, or harvesting, is often called second-growth or 'regeneration' until enough time passes for the effects of the disturbance to be no longer evident.

1b0c440901fb.title: Old-growth forest
1b0c440901fb.sentence: Depending on the forest, this may take from a century to several millennia.

b26626779b51.title: Old-growth forest
b26626779b51.sentence: As old-growth forest is structurally diverse, it provides higher-diversity habitat than forests in other stages.

671b52886f98.title: Old-growth forest
671b52886f98.sentence: Old-growth forests are often biologically diverse, and home to many rare species, threatened species, and endangered species of plants and animals, such as the northern spotted owl, marbled murrelet and fisher, making them ecologically significant.

60c4b60b01c6.title: Old-growth forest
60c4b60b01c6.sentence: Old-growth forests provide ecosystem services that may be far more important to society than their use as a source of raw materials.

d80ef775c00f.title: Old-growth forest
d80ef775c00f.sentence: These services include making breathable air, making pure water, carbon storage, regeneration of nutrients, maintenance of soils, pest control by insectivorous bats and insects, micro- and macro-climate control, and the storage of a wide variety of genes.

34bed0747240.title: Old-growth forest
34bed0747240.sentence: However, evidence from analysis of carbon stored above ground and in the soil has shown old-growth forests are more productive at storing carbon than younger forests.

b896cc309e4a.title: Old-growth forest
b896cc309e4a.sentence: According to the World Resources Institute, as of January 2009, only 21% of the original old-growth forests that once existed on Earth are remaining.

31c1ba290c68.title: Old-growth forest
31c1ba290c68.sentence: An estimated one-half of Western Europe's forests were cleared before the Middle Ages, and 90% of the old-growth forests that existed in the contiguous United States in the 1600s have been cleared.

a154b30ca14d.title: Old-growth forest
a154b30ca14d.sentence: Primary forests were lost at a rate of 1.61 million ha per year between 2015 and 2025, which was less than half the rate in 2000–2015, when it was 3.92 million ha per year.

37b55b421b1f.title: Taiga
37b55b421b1f.sentence: Taiga or tayga (/ˈtaɪ.ɡə/, TY-gə; Russian: тайга́, IPA: [tɐjˈɡa]), also known as boreal forest or snow forest, is a biome characterized by coniferous forests consisting mostly of pines, spruces, and larches.

342698ee3bfe.title: Taiga
342698ee3bfe.sentence: The taiga is found throughout the high northern latitudes, between the tundra and the temperate forest, from about 50°N to 70°N, but with considerable regional variation.

a725e2f475ec.title: Taiga
a725e2f475ec.sentence: Taiga covers 17 million square kilometres (6.6 million square miles) or 11.5% of the Earth's land area, second only to deserts and xeric shrublands.

7c32094813fe.title: Taiga
7c32094813fe.sentence: The largest areas are located in Russia and Canada.

dfe1a39aa3d7.title: Taiga
dfe1a39aa3d7.sentence: After the permanent ice caps and tundra, taiga is the terrestrial biome with the lowest annual average temperatures, with mean annual temperature generally varying from −5 to 5 °C (23 to 41 °F).

b9d5c7092c9b.title: Taiga
b9d5c7092c9b.sentence: This climate is classified as Dfc, Dwc, Dsc, Dfd and Dwd in the Köppen climate classification scheme, meaning that the short summers (24 h average 10 °C (50 °F) or more), although generally warm and humid, only last 1–3 months, while winters, with average temperatures below freezing, last 5–7 months.

8112ad6a0605.title: Taiga
8112ad6a0605.sentence: Taiga soil tends to be young, with poor nutrient availability, lacking the deep, organically enriched profile present in temperate deciduous forests.

4b7b6ec9c6ff.title: Taiga
4b7b6ec9c6ff.sentence: The colder climate hinders development of soil, and the ease with which plants can use its nutrients.

d04cf9b3c276.title: Taiga
d04cf9b3c276.sentence: The taiga stores enormous quantities of carbon, more than the world's temperate and tropical forests combined, much of it in wetlands and peatland.

8275cbcef5b2.title: Taiga
8275cbcef5b2.sentence: In fact, current estimates place boreal forests as storing twice as much carbon per unit area as tropical forests.

b975ae25cf2c.title: Taiga
b975ae25cf2c.sentence: Wildfires could use up a significant part of the global carbon budget, so fire management at about 12 dollars per tonne of carbon not released is very cheap compared to the social cost of carbon.

4103a6833a1e.title: Taiga
4103a6833a1e.sentence: During the last quarter of the twentieth century, the zone of latitude occupied by the boreal forest experienced some of the greatest temperature increases on Earth.

0baef2606688.title: Taiga
0baef2606688.sentence: The number of days with extremely cold temperatures (e.g., −20 to −40 °C; −4 to −40 °F) has decreased irregularly but systematically in nearly all the boreal region, allowing better survival for tree-damaging insects.

47b0173cb8ea.title: Bog
47b0173cb8ea.sentence: A bog or bogland is a wetland that accumulates peat as a deposit of dead plant materials – often mosses, typically sphagnum moss.

d1f128139fb5.title: Bog
d1f128139fb5.sentence: It is one of the four main types of wetlands.

07ab24e785ee.title: Bog
07ab24e785ee.sentence: Other names for bogs include mire, mosses, quagmire, and muskeg; alkaline mires are called fens.

04e8e6cdc6c2.title: Bog
04e8e6cdc6c2.sentence: Bogs occur where the water at the ground surface is acidic and low in nutrients.

7ad024547510.title: Bog
7ad024547510.sentence: They are generally found in cooler northern climates and are formed in poorly draining lake basins.

3b993dcaf139.title: Bog
3b993dcaf139.sentence: In general, the low fertility and cool climate result in relatively slow plant growth, but decay is even slower due to low oxygen levels in saturated bog soils.

e91d7c5fb70f.title: Bog
e91d7c5fb70f.sentence: Large areas of the landscape can be covered many meters deep in peat.

28a4187c556a.title: Bog
28a4187c556a.sentence: - The wetland receives most of its water and nutrients from precipitation (ombrotrophic) rather than surface or groundwater (minerotrophic).

931adc79ab00.title: Bog
931adc79ab00.sentence: - Peat is present, usually thicker than 30 centimetres (12 in).

3d2e68e0c05b.title: Bog
3d2e68e0c05b.sentence: The world's largest wetland is the peat bogs of the Western Siberian Lowlands in Russia, which cover more than a million square kilometres.

a3c08460ef4e.title: Bog
a3c08460ef4e.sentence: There are many highly specialized animals, fungi, and plants associated with bog habitat.

2f9112dd5a9c.title: Bog
2f9112dd5a9c.sentence: Carnivorous plants such as sundews (Drosera) and pitcher plants (for example Sarracenia purpurea) have adapted to the low-nutrient conditions by using invertebrates as a nutrient source.

a558ecda5902.title: Bog
a558ecda5902.sentence: The gradual accumulation of decayed plant material in a bog functions as a carbon sink.

794317dbe6b9.title: Tundra
794317dbe6b9.sentence: In physical geography, a tundra (/ˈtʌndrə, ˈtʊn-/) is a type of biome where tree growth is hindered by frigid temperatures and short growing seasons.

1e3d71a3150f.title: Tundra
1e3d71a3150f.sentence: There are three regions and associated types of tundra: Arctic, Alpine, and Antarctic.

a3a3596568d6.title: Tundra
a3a3596568d6.sentence: Tundra vegetation is composed of dwarf shrubs, sedges, grasses, mosses, and lichens.

bc6287af4a68.title: Tundra
bc6287af4a68.sentence: The ecotone (or ecological boundary region) between the tundra and the forest is known as the tree line or timberline.

42a083885502.title: Tundra
42a083885502.sentence: It is also a polar desert, with only about 150–250 mm (6–10 in) of precipitation falling per year (the summer is typically the season of maximum precipitation).

f2abb7adff8c.title: Tundra
f2abb7adff8c.sentence: During the winter it is very cold, dark, and windy with the average temperature around −28 °C (−18 °F), sometimes dipping as low as −50 °C (−58 °F).

f5ee340aa0fc.title: Tundra
f5ee340aa0fc.sentence: The biodiversity of tundras is low: 1,700 species of vascular plants and only 48 species of land mammals can be found, although millions of birds migrate there each year for the marshes.

e9c8c4eb253b.title: Tundra
e9c8c4eb253b.sentence: The soil also contains large amounts of biomass and decomposed biomass that has been stored as methane and carbon dioxide in the permafrost, making the tundra soil a carbon sink.

1746e08e6b98.title: Tundra
1746e08e6b98.sentence: Due to the harsh climate of Arctic tundra, regions of this kind have seen little human activity, even though they are sometimes rich in natural resources such as petroleum, natural gas, and uranium.

1c567a62e342.title: Tundra
1c567a62e342.sentence: In recent times this has begun to change in Alaska, Russia, and some other parts of the world: for example, the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug produces 90% of Russia's natural gas.

622c3ed51916.title: Forest
622c3ed51916.sentence: The transition of a region from forest loss to net gain in forested land is referred to as the forest transition.

1c8886c9876d.title: Forest
1c8886c9876d.sentence: This change occurs through a few main pathways, including increase in commercial tree plantations, adoption of agroforestry techniques by small farmers, or spontaneous regeneration when former agricultural land is abandoned.

d9ae364afedc.title: Forest
d9ae364afedc.sentence: It can be motivated by the economic benefits of forests, the ecosystem services forests provide, or cultural changes where people increasingly appreciate forests for their spiritual, aesthetic, or otherwise intrinsic value.

6880402f0193.title: Forest
6880402f0193.sentence: While deforestation is taking place in some areas, new forests are being established through natural expansion or deliberate efforts in other areas.

6f6754a4e80e.title: Forest
6f6754a4e80e.sentence: As a result, the net loss of forest area is less than the rate of deforestation; and it, too, is decreasing: from 7.8 million hectares (19 million acres) per year in the 1990s to 4.7 million hectares (12 million acres) per year during 2010–2020.

081f17131d8e.title: Forest
081f17131d8e.sentence: In addition, ambitious tree-planting programmes in countries such as China, India, the United States, and Vietnam – combined with natural expansion of forests in some regions – have added more than 7 million hectares (17 million acres) of new forests annually.

2fbd56916cf8.title: Forest
2fbd56916cf8.sentence: China instituted a ban on logging, beginning in 1998, due to the erosion and flooding that it caused.

079a1f191340.title: Forest
079a1f191340.sentence: New forests are not equivalent to old growth forests in terms of species diversity, resilience, and carbon capture.

3f977b4708bb.title: Forest
3f977b4708bb.sentence: In 2025 the area of forest in legally established protected areas worldwide was estimated at 813 million ha, which is around 20% of the total forest area.

3eff32579c19.title: Forest transition
3eff32579c19.sentence: Changes in forest area (like deforestation) may follow a pattern suggested by the forest transition (FT) theory, whereby at early stages in its development a country is characterized by high forest cover and low deforestation rates (HFLD countries).

8d8e21d1171d.title: Forest transition
8d8e21d1171d.sentence: Then deforestation rates accelerate (HFHD, high forest cover – high deforestation rate), and forest cover is reduced (LFHD, low forest cover – high deforestation rate), before the deforestation rate slows (LFLD, low forest cover – low deforestation rate), after which forest cover stabilizes and eventually starts recovering.

99d5ba2a8ed7.title: Forest transition
99d5ba2a8ed7.sentence: FT is not a "law of nature", and the pattern is influenced by national context (for example, human population density, stage of development, structure of the economy), global economic forces, and government policies.

f344b13c4eab.title: Wetland
f344b13c4eab.sentence: Humans are disturbing and damaging wetlands for example by oil and gas extraction, building infrastructure, overgrazing of livestock, overfishing, alteration of wetlands including dredging and draining, nutrient pollution and water pollution.

780699e5cef3.title: Wetland
780699e5cef3.sentence: The disturbances (sometimes termed stressors or alterations) can be human-associated or natural, direct or indirect, reversible or not, and isolated or cumulative.

1f0b8f8f16ea.title: Wetland
1f0b8f8f16ea.sentence: Since 1900, 65–70% of the world's wetlands have been lost.

4b3fb7406b53.title: Wetland
4b3fb7406b53.section: Disturbances and human impacts > Conversion to dry land
4b3fb7406b53.sentence: To increase economic productivity, wetlands are often converted into dry land with dykes and drains and used for agricultural purposes.

631f07d8b42c.title: Wetland
631f07d8b42c.sentence: Some of the world's most important agricultural areas were wetlands that have been converted to farmland.

48b26321d82b.title: Wetland
48b26321d82b.section: Disturbances and human impacts > Conversion to dry land
48b26321d82b.sentence: Once settlements are constructed and protected by dykes, the settlements then become vulnerable to land subsidence and ever increasing risk of flooding.

568908b958eb.title: Wetland
568908b958eb.section: Disturbances and human impacts > Conversion to dry land
568908b958eb.sentence: Since wetlands tend to retain water with less influx or efflux compared to other bodies of water, they can quickly concentrate toxicants that originate from pollutants.

c96b3056fba6.title: Wetland
c96b3056fba6.section: Disturbances and human impacts > Conversion to dry land
c96b3056fba6.sentence: This accumulation of toxicants will cause the biodiversity of a wetland to change, particularly since toxicants will be harmful to native aquatic species.

b2813c38ba4a.title: Wetland
b2813c38ba4a.sentence: Some aquaculture has eliminated massive areas of wetland through practices such as the shrimp farming industry's destruction of mangroves.

5e1c83bab42d.title: Wetland
5e1c83bab42d.sentence: Also burgeoning demand for shrimp globally has provided a large and ready market.

f8c9c7ad1d2d.title: Wetland
f8c9c7ad1d2d.section: Ecosystem services > Shoreline stabilization and storm protection
f8c9c7ad1d2d.sentence: In East Asia, reclamation of coastal wetlands has resulted in widespread transformation of the coastal zone, and up to 65% of coastal wetlands have been destroyed by coastal development.

d478cc98d3ee.title: Wetland
d478cc98d3ee.sentence: - Minor disturbance: Stress that maintains ecosystem integrity.

81f4e3d7d0e0.title: Wetland
81f4e3d7d0e0.sentence: - Moderate disturbance: Ecosystem integrity is damaged but can recover in time without assistance.

1d18dcaebe1d.title: Wetland
1d18dcaebe1d.sentence: - Impairment or severe disturbance: Human intervention may be needed in order for ecosystem to recover.

798ae8c22912.title: Wetland
798ae8c22912.sentence: Since the 1970s, more focus has been put on preserving wetlands for their natural functions.

60ff60c1e7e0.title: Wetland
60ff60c1e7e0.sentence: In order to maintain wetlands and sustain their functions, alterations and disturbances that are outside the normal range of variation should be minimized.

09a5febec641.title: Wetland
09a5febec641.sentence: Since 1971, work under an international treaty seeks to identify and protect "wetlands of international importance."

94890970b555.title: Wetland
94890970b555.sentence: The Ramsar Convention (full title: Convention on Wetlands of International Importance, especially as Waterfowl Habitat), is an international treaty designed to address global concerns regarding wetland loss and degradation.

eaa042582181.title: Wetland
eaa042582181.sentence: The primary purposes of the treaty are to list wetlands of international importance and to promote their wise use, with the ultimate goal of preserving the world's wetlands.

583625b2ba2d.title: Wetland
583625b2ba2d.sentence: Methods include restricting access to some wetland areas, as well as educating the public to combat the misconception that wetlands are wastelands.

edeeb92a1da2.title: Wetland
edeeb92a1da2.section: Conservation > Balancing wetland conservation with the needs of people
edeeb92a1da2.sentence: Studies have shown that it is possible to conserve wetlands while improving the livelihoods of people living among them.

46fba36fb0e8.title: Wetland
46fba36fb0e8.section: Conservation > Balancing wetland conservation with the needs of people
46fba36fb0e8.sentence: Case studies conducted in Malawi and Zambia looked at how dambos – wet, grassy valleys or depressions where water seeps to the surface – can be farmed sustainably.

2a527b309927.title: Wetland conservation
2a527b309927.sentence: Wetlands cover at least six percent of the Earth and have become a focal issue for conservation due to the ecosystem services they provide.

7e24cf52c805.title: Wetland conservation
7e24cf52c805.sentence: More than three billion people, around half the world's population, obtain their basic water needs from inland freshwater wetlands.

8f20788d7f10.title: Wetland conservation
8f20788d7f10.section: Wetland functions and value > Floodwater storage and filtration
8f20788d7f10.sentence: Coastal wetlands have been estimated to have saved a median of US$447 billion in damages and 4,620 lives annually from storms.

e8db7771b205.title: Wetland conservation
e8db7771b205.section: Wetland functions and value > Climate change mitigation
e8db7771b205.sentence: The term used by scientists to categorize carbon absorbed by coastal wetlands which is then stored in the soil and organic material is blue carbon.According to an article published by A.M. Nahlik and M.S. Fennesy, worldwide, wetlands retain around 700 billion tons of carbon, mainly in peat soils, with an annual sequestration rate of 96 million tons.

d1aa43476e00.title: Ramsar Convention
d1aa43476e00.sentence: It is named after the city of Ramsar in Iran, where the convention was signed in 1971.

41df0a83b121.title: Wetland
41df0a83b121.sentence: Restoration and restoration ecologists intend to return wetlands to their natural trajectory by aiding directly with the natural processes of the ecosystem.

652f1833c61d.title: Wetland
652f1833c61d.sentence: There is no one way to restore a wetland and the level of restoration required will be based on the level of disturbance although, each method of restoration does require preparation and administration.

4feb925eeded.title: Wetland
4feb925eeded.sentence: Factors influencing selected approach may include budget, time scale limitations, project goals, level of disturbance, landscape and ecological constraints, political and administrative agendas and socioeconomic priorities.

f72ff1fe0084.title: Wetland
f72ff1fe0084.section: Restoration > Levels of restoration > Prescribed natural or assisted regeneration
f72ff1fe0084.sentence: For this strategy, there is no biophysical manipulation and the ecosystem is left to recover based on the process of succession alone.

dfe57f97f22c.title: Wetland
dfe57f97f22c.section: Restoration > Levels of restoration > Prescribed natural or assisted regeneration
dfe57f97f22c.sentence: This is likely to be the first method of approach since it is the least intrusive and least expensive although some biophysical non-intrusive manipulation may be required to enhance the rate of succession to an acceptable level.

af598689c61b.title: Wetland
af598689c61b.section: Restoration > Levels of restoration > Partial reconstruction
af598689c61b.sentence: For this strategy, a mixture of natural regeneration and manipulated environmental control is used.

315f29dd927f.title: Wetland
315f29dd927f.section: Restoration > Levels of restoration > Partial reconstruction
315f29dd927f.sentence: This may require some engineering, and more intensive biophysical manipulations including ripping of subsoil, agrichemical applications of herbicides or insecticides, laying of mulch, mechanical seed dispersal, and tree planting on a large scale.

97ce922fdc44.title: Wetland
97ce922fdc44.section: Restoration > Levels of restoration > Complete reconstruction
97ce922fdc44.sentence: This most expensive and intrusive method of reconstruction requires engineering and ground up reconstruction.

05672ea76ba7.title: Wetland
05672ea76ba7.section: Restoration > Levels of restoration > Traditional knowledge
05672ea76ba7.sentence: The ideas from traditional ecological knowledge can be applied as a holistic approach to the restoration of wetlands.

b30cd7cd73a4.title: Wetland
b30cd7cd73a4.section: Restoration > Levels of restoration > Traditional knowledge
b30cd7cd73a4.sentence: Applying these practices on specific locations of wetlands increase productivity, biodiversity, and improve its resilience.

c48e0ba60ebe.title: Wetland
c48e0ba60ebe.sentence: The value of a wetland to local communities typically involves first mapping a region's wetlands, then assessing the functions and ecosystem services the wetlands provide individually and cumulatively, and finally evaluating that information to prioritize or rank individual wetlands or wetland types for conservation, management, restoration, or development.

7b46c34a6b49.title: Wetland
7b46c34a6b49.sentence: Over the longer term, it requires keeping inventories of known wetlands and monitoring a representative sample of the wetlands to determine changes due to both natural and human factors.

4747a74dd2ab.title: Wetland
4747a74dd2ab.sentence: Rapid assessment methods are used to score, rank, rate, or categorize various functions, ecosystem services, species, communities, levels of disturbance, and/or ecological health of a wetland or group of wetlands.

4a82ecc57cbd.title: Wetland
4a82ecc57cbd.sentence: Assessments are typically considered to be "rapid" when they require only a single visit to the wetland lasting less than one day, which in some cases may include interpretation of aerial imagery and geographic information system (GIS) analyses of existing spatial data, but not detailed post-visit laboratory analyses of water or biological samples.

30fa5c67b96a.title: Wetland
30fa5c67b96a.sentence: This is often done to prioritize particular wetlands for conservation (avoidance) or to determine the degree to which loss or alteration of wetland functions should be compensated, such as by restoring degraded wetlands elsewhere or providing additional protections to existing wetlands.

40f3581a8da9.title: Wetland
40f3581a8da9.sentence: A need for wetland assessments to be rapid arises mainly when government agencies set deadlines for decisions affecting a wetland or when the number of wetlands needing information on their functions or condition is large.

2c09aa0e7f31.title: Wetland
2c09aa0e7f31.sentence: Remote sensing such as aerial imagery and satellite imaging provides effective tools to map and monitor wetlands across large geographic regions and over time.

64da9cae14d6.title: Wetland
64da9cae14d6.sentence: The integration of multi-sourced data such as LiDAR and aerial photos proves more effective at mapping wetlands than the use of aerial photos alone, especially with the aid of modern machine learning methods (e.g., deep learning).

c26ae6a8118c.title: Wetland
c26ae6a8118c.sentence: Wetlands can act as a sink or a source of carbon, depending on the specific wetland.

2fc283520616.title: Wetland
2fc283520616.sentence: However, wetlands can also be a significant source of methane emissions due to anaerobic decomposition of soaked detritus, and some are also emitters of nitrous oxide.

ccc3d9f1bca8.title: Wetland
ccc3d9f1bca8.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
ccc3d9f1bca8.sentence: Wetlands are the largest natural source of atmospheric methane in the world, and are therefore a major area of concern with respect to climate change.

a6fcab5647e1.title: Wetland
a6fcab5647e1.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
a6fcab5647e1.sentence: Wetlands account for approximately 20–30% of atmospheric methane through emissions from soils and plants, and contribute an approximate average of 161 Tg of methane to the atmosphere per year.

156a5b7ea8cb.title: Wetland
156a5b7ea8cb.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
156a5b7ea8cb.sentence: This high level of water saturation creates conditions conducive to methane production.

e5a30b12d195.title: Wetland
e5a30b12d195.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
e5a30b12d195.sentence: Most methanogenesis, or methane production, occurs in oxygen-poor environments.

aaf4e8aba316.title: Wetland
aaf4e8aba316.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
aaf4e8aba316.sentence: While peatlands constitute only 3% of the world's land area, their degradation produces 7% of all CO2 emissions.

f1a252a995e4.title: Wetland
f1a252a995e4.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
f1a252a995e4.sentence: As a result of peat drainage, the organic carbon that had built up over thousands of years and is normally under water is suddenly exposed to the air.

8bd4ebc59dd6.title: Wetland
8bd4ebc59dd6.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
8bd4ebc59dd6.sentence: The peat decomposes and is converted into carbon dioxide (CO2), which is then released into the atmosphere.

dd8865413c0d.title: Wetland
dd8865413c0d.section: Climate change aspects > Climate change mitigation
dd8865413c0d.sentence: In salt marshes and mangrove swamps in particular, the average carbon sequestration rate is 210 g CO2 m−2 y−1 while peatlands sequester approximately 20–30 g CO2 m−2 y−1.

f801aaf91813.title: Wetland
f801aaf91813.section: Climate change aspects > Climate change mitigation
f801aaf91813.sentence: However, CO2 removal using coastal blue carbon restoration has questionable cost-effectiveness when considered only as a climate mitigation action, either for carbon-offsetting or for inclusion in Nationally Determined Contributions.

b3ad76810206.title: Wetland
b3ad76810206.section: Climate change aspects > Climate change adaptation
b3ad76810206.sentence: A warming climate makes extremely wet and very dry occurrences more severe, causing more severe floods and droughts.

1aaa0052d5dc.title: Wetland
1aaa0052d5dc.section: Climate change aspects > Climate change adaptation
1aaa0052d5dc.sentence: For this reason, some of the ecosystem services that wetlands provide (e.g. water storage and flood control, groundwater replenishment, shoreline stabilization and storm protection) are important for climate change adaptation measures.

d9dad38c5809.title: Drylands
d9dad38c5809.sentence: Drylands are defined by a scarcity of water.

3f278c192cf3.title: Drylands
3f278c192cf3.sentence: Drylands are zones where precipitation is balanced by evaporation from surfaces and by evapotranspiration by plants.

344cdc670647.title: Drylands
344cdc670647.sentence: The United Nations Environment Program defines drylands as tropical and temperate areas with an aridity index of less than 0.65.

af37f5772f34.title: Drylands
af37f5772f34.sentence: Drylands cover 41.3% of the Earth's land surface, including 15% of Latin America, 66% of Africa, 40% of Asia, and 24% of Europe.

eeb2a9461924.title: Drylands
eeb2a9461924.sentence: Drylands are home to more than 2 billion people.

0b1d9e0b340d.title: Drylands
0b1d9e0b340d.sentence: There is a significantly greater proportion of drylands in developing countries (72%), and the proportion increases with aridity: almost 100% of all hyper-arid lands are in the developing world.

fbe4f37dbc0c.title: Desertification
fbe4f37dbc0c.sentence: Drylands cover 41% of the earth's land surface and include 45% of the world's agricultural land.

a7d421762519.title: Drylands
a7d421762519.sentence: Drylands are complex ecosystems, whose characteristics and dynamic properties depend on many interrelated interactions between climate, soil, and vegetation.

834b0a519760.title: Drylands
834b0a519760.sentence: Drylands, unlike more humid biomes, rely mostly on above ground water runoff for redistribution of water.

c8376720ed9f.title: Drylands
c8376720ed9f.sentence: Drylands are highly vulnerable to climate change due to changing rainfall patterns and land degradation.

b858154c305d.title: Agroecosystem
b858154c305d.sentence: Agroecosystems, or cultivated ecosystem, are natural ecosystems that have been modified and is managed by humans for the purposes of agricultural production, whether plant or animal.

a4ed074d60c5.title: Agroecosystem
a4ed074d60c5.sentence: Like other ecosystems, agroecosystems consists of the physical environment (soil, water, climate), living organisms (crops, animals, micro-organisms and wildlife) and the ecological interactions that link them.

58be16c0b407.title: Agroecosystem
58be16c0b407.sentence: As such they are the basic unit of study in Agroecology, and Regenerative Agriculture using ecological approaches.

fbebd4df079c.title: Agroecosystem
fbebd4df079c.sentence: An agroecosystem can be seen as not restricted to the immediate site of agricultural activity (e.g. the farm).

2659aef8589a.title: Agroecosystem
2659aef8589a.sentence: That is, it includes the region that is impacted by this activity, usually by changes to the complexity of species assemblages and energy flows, as well as to the net nutrient balance.

b446b78d8e33.title: Agroecosystem
b446b78d8e33.sentence: Agroecosystems, particularly those managed intensively, are characterized as having simpler species composition, energy and nutrient flows than "natural" ecosystems.

08e59ecf3399.title: Agroecosystem
08e59ecf3399.sentence: Likewise, agroecosystems are often associated with elevated nutrient input, much of which exits the farm leading to eutrophication of connected ecosystems not directly engaged in agriculture.

1490f526a5c5.title: Agroecosystem
