1490f526a5c5.sentence: On the other hand, an increased plant diversity in sustainable agroecosystems provides a range of benefits, both ecologically and economically.

668447e98c00.title: Agroecosystem
668447e98c00.sentence: Forest gardens are probably the world's oldest and most resilient agroecosystem.

c37571f189f3.title: Agroecosystem
c37571f189f3.sentence: According to a report by the International Water Management Institute and the United Nations Environment Programme, there is not enough water to continue farming using current practices; therefore how critical water, land, and ecosystem resources are used to boost crop yields must be reconsidered.

ae10cd0de05d.title: Agroecosystem
ae10cd0de05d.sentence: The report suggested assigning value to ecosystems, recognizing environmental and livelihood tradeoffs, and balancing the rights of a variety of users and interests, as well addressing inequities that sometimes result when such measures are adopted, such as the reallocation of water from poor to rich, the clearing of land to make way for more productive farmland, or the preservation of a wetland system that limits fishing rights.

f0ab196ec5e0.title: Agroecosystem
f0ab196ec5e0.sentence: One of the major efforts of disciplines such as agroecology is to promote management styles that blur the distinction between agroecosystems and "natural" ecosystems, both by decreasing the impact of agriculture (increasing the biological and trophic complexity of the agricultural system as well as decreasing the nutrient inputs/outflow) and by increasing awareness that "downstream" effects extend agroecosystems beyond the boundaries of the farm (e.g. the Corn Belt agroecosystem includes the hypoxic zone in the Gulf of Mexico).

9d40b7af3271.title: Agroecosystem
9d40b7af3271.sentence: In the first case, polyculture or buffer strips for wildlife habitat can restore some complexity to a cropping system, while organic farming can reduce nutrient inputs.

850e25200d16.title: Mangrove
850e25200d16.sentence: Mangrove swamps protect coastal areas from erosion, storm surge (especially during tropical cyclones), and tsunamis.

b0d9773b6f10.title: Mangrove
b0d9773b6f10.sentence: The mangroves' massive root systems are efficient at dissipating wave energy.

f34a84ee3d31.title: Mangrove
f34a84ee3d31.sentence: They limit high-energy wave erosion mainly during events such as storm surges and tsunamis.

638246453eef.title: Mangrove
638246453eef.sentence: Likewise, they slow down tidal water so that its sediment is deposited as the tide comes in, leaving all except fine particles when the tide ebbs.

c9c15ae61662.title: Mangrove
c9c15ae61662.sentence: In this way, mangroves build their environments.

21c6e7ea3479.title: Mangrove
21c6e7ea3479.sentence: Once established, mangrove roots provide an oyster habitat and slow water flow, thereby enhancing sediment deposition in areas where it is already occurring.

146808fccad2.title: Mangrove
146808fccad2.sentence: Globally, mangroves have been shown to provide measurable economic protections to coastal communities affected by tropical storms.

ea68803bce6b.title: Mangrove
ea68803bce6b.sentence: Because of the uniqueness of mangrove ecosystems and the protection against erosion they provide, they are often the object of conservation programs, including national biodiversity action plans.

c859c41c3de9.title: Mangrove
c859c41c3de9.sentence: The fine, anoxic sediments under mangroves act as sinks for a variety of heavy (trace) metals which colloidal particles in the sediments have concentrated from the water.

98d40d8afadd.title: Mangrove
98d40d8afadd.sentence: Mangrove removal disturbs these underlying sediments, often creating problems of trace metal contamination of seawater and organisms of the area.

992174c927f9.title: Ecological values of mangroves
992174c927f9.section: Ecological values > Endangered mangrove coastlines and human development
992174c927f9.sentence: Wave energy may be reduced by 75 per cent in the wave's passage through 200 meters of mangrove forests, a very substantial amount once the mangrove has been removed.

4b14752d50fa.title: Ecological values of mangroves
4b14752d50fa.section: Ecological values > Endangered mangrove coastlines and human development
4b14752d50fa.sentence: Mangrove covered shorelines are less likely to erode, or will erode significantly more slowly, than unvegetated shorelines during periods of high wave energy.

df5a5d8eac32.title: Ecological values of mangroves
df5a5d8eac32.section: Ecological values > Endangered mangrove coastlines and human development
df5a5d8eac32.sentence: Maintaining a healthy mangrove forest sustains natural protection and is less expensive than seawalls and similar erosion control structures, which can increase erosion in front of the structure and at adjacent properties due to coastal currents.

74832e231dd8.title: Forest ecology
74832e231dd8.sentence: Forest ecology is the scientific study of the interrelated patterns, processes, flora, fauna, funga, and ecosystems in forests.

0da638ad5326.title: Forest ecology
0da638ad5326.sentence: A forest ecosystem is a natural woodland unit consisting of all plants, animals, and micro-organisms (biotic components) in that area functioning together with all of the non-living physical (abiotic) factors of the environment.

dac97a587bdb.title: Forest ecology
dac97a587bdb.sentence: However, as the term forest connotes an area inhabited by more than one organism, forest ecology most often concentrates on the level of the population, community or ecosystem.

447854032199.title: Forest ecology
447854032199.sentence: Since trees can grow larger than other plant life-forms, there is the potential for a wide variety of forest structures (or physiognomies).

3bca715c3fbd.title: Forest ecology
3bca715c3fbd.sentence: Thus, forests are often highly heterogeneous environments compared to other terrestrial plant communities.

776dfaa9a472.title: Forest ecology
776dfaa9a472.sentence: This heterogeneity in turn can enable great biodiversity of species of both plants and animals.

d55a35735f52.title: Forest ecology
d55a35735f52.sentence: Forests have an enormously important role to play in the global ecosystem, as they cover almost a third of all land.

47fe551bab8c.title: Forest ecology
47fe551bab8c.sentence: Forest ecology therefore has a great impact upon the whole biosphere and human activities that are sustained by it.

77113ef5a387.title: Forest ecology
77113ef5a387.sentence: The management of forests is known as forestry, silviculture, and forest management.

531b3290f5c8.title: Forest ecology
531b3290f5c8.sentence: The emergence of machine learning(ML) has allowed for new methods of approaching forest ecology, as it can process larger and more complex data.

ebeb660a0533.title: Aquatic ecosystem
ebeb660a0533.sentence: Aquatic ecosystems perform many important environmental functions.

9701d8d30e8f.title: Aquatic ecosystem
9701d8d30e8f.sentence: For example, they recycle nutrients, purify water, attenuate floods, recharge ground water and provide habitats for wildlife.

6309d1d2d2fa.title: Aquatic ecosystem
6309d1d2d2fa.sentence: The biota of an aquatic ecosystem contribute to its self-purification, most notably microorganisms, phytoplankton, higher plants, invertebrates, fish, bacteria, protists, aquatic fungi, and more.

1a5166782786.title: Aquatic ecosystem
1a5166782786.sentence: These organisms are actively involved in multiple self-purification processes, including organic matter destruction and water filtration.

58bcef635670.title: Aquatic ecosystem
58bcef635670.sentence: In addition to environmental functions, aquatic ecosystems are also used for human recreation, and are very important to the tourism industry, especially in coastal regions.

a39029eabda5.title: Aquatic ecosystem
a39029eabda5.sentence: They are also used for religious purposes, such as religious tourism to the Jordan River by Christians, and educational purposes, such as the usage of lakes for ecological study.

02728be08b13.title: Aquatic ecosystem
02728be08b13.sentence: Freshwater ecosystems are a subset of Earth's aquatic ecosystems that include the biological communities inhabiting freshwater waterbodies such as lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, springs, bogs, and wetlands.

1cc465f6b4fb.title: Aquatic ecosystem
1cc465f6b4fb.sentence: They can be contrasted with marine ecosystems, which have a much higher salinity.

c4bf2cf59d6b.title: Aquatic ecosystem
c4bf2cf59d6b.sentence: Freshwater habitats can be classified by different factors, including temperature, light penetration, nutrients, and vegetation.

8720a1c5ba23.title: Aquatic ecosystem
8720a1c5ba23.sentence: Lentic ecosystems can be compared with lotic ecosystems, which involve flowing terrestrial waters such as rivers and streams.

bcc3c59d6a98.title: Aquatic ecosystem
bcc3c59d6a98.sentence: Together, these two ecosystems are examples of freshwater ecosystems.

fdbc05525c83.title: Aquatic ecosystem
fdbc05525c83.sentence: Organisms in marine ecosystems tolerate salinity, while many freshwater organisms are intolerant of salt.

46de67beff7a.title: Aquatic ecosystem
46de67beff7a.sentence: Freshwater used for irrigation purposes often absorbs levels of salt that are harmful to freshwater organisms.

cce866a03463.title: Freshwater ecosystem
cce866a03463.sentence: They can be contrasted with marine ecosystems, which have a much higher salinity.

dee90076be69.title: Freshwater ecosystem
dee90076be69.sentence: There are three basic types of freshwater ecosystems: lentic (slow moving water, including pools, ponds, and lakes), lotic (faster moving streams, for example creeks and rivers) and wetlands (semi-aquatic areas where the soil is saturated or inundated for at least part of the time).

7a14a97851bf.title: Freshwater ecosystem
7a14a97851bf.sentence: Freshwater ecosystems contain 41% of the world's known fish species.

1357bdc30202.title: Biomass (ecology)
1357bdc30202.sentence: Terrestrial freshwater ecosystems generate about 1.5% of the global net primary production.

68973c3d7097.title: Freshwater ecosystem
68973c3d7097.sentence: Five broad threats to freshwater biodiversity include overexploitation, water pollution, flow modification, destruction or degradation of habitat, and invasion by exotic species.

273cba93140f.title: Freshwater ecosystem
273cba93140f.sentence: The World Wide Fund for Nature's Living Planet Index noted an 83% decline in the populations of freshwater vertebrates between 1970 and 2014.

686fb3b571bd.title: Aquatic ecosystem
686fb3b571bd.sentence: Marine ecosystems are the largest of Earth's aquatic ecosystems and exist in waters that have a high salt content.

2bd92ea2e9f9.title: Aquatic ecosystem
2bd92ea2e9f9.sentence: Marine waters cover more than 70% of the surface of the Earth and account for more than 97% of Earth's water supply and 90% of habitable space on Earth.

78585356aaca.title: Aquatic ecosystem
78585356aaca.sentence: Seawater has an average salinity of 35 parts per thousand.

c108783221f0.title: Aquatic ecosystem
c108783221f0.sentence: Actual salinity varies among different marine ecosystems.

35a890a71956.title: Aquatic ecosystem
35a890a71956.sentence: Marine ecosystems can be divided into many zones depending upon water depth and shoreline features.

1bf2dad09ac2.title: Aquatic ecosystem
1bf2dad09ac2.sentence: The oceanic zone is the vast open part of the ocean where animals such as whales, sharks, and tuna live.

e04edc1a4ecb.title: Aquatic ecosystem
e04edc1a4ecb.sentence: The benthic zone consists of substrates below the surface where many invertebrates live.

039d82b6a618.title: Marine ecosystem
039d82b6a618.sentence: Seawater has an average salinity of 35 parts per thousand.

201f7c536f91.title: Marine ecosystem
201f7c536f91.sentence: Actual salinity varies among different marine ecosystems.

144d7f1f1118.title: Marine ecosystem
144d7f1f1118.sentence: Marine ecosystems can be divided into many zones depending upon water depth and shoreline features.

1adbc26ed048.title: Marine ecosystem
1adbc26ed048.section: Types or locations > Marine coastal ecosystems > Coral reefs
1adbc26ed048.sentence: Coral reefs are one of the most well-known marine ecosystems in the world, with the largest being the Great Barrier Reef.

e2985f12c15b.title: Marine ecosystem
e2985f12c15b.sentence: Organisms that live freely at the surface, termed neuston, include keystone organisms like the golden seaweed Sargassum that makes up the Sargasso Sea, floating barnacles, marine snails, nudibranchs, and cnidarians.

4e711bb45a8c.title: Marine ecosystem
4e711bb45a8c.section: Types or locations > Deep sea and sea floor
4e711bb45a8c.sentence: The deep sea contains up to 95% of the space occupied by living organisms.

f6ae5c42ee64.title: Marine ecosystem
f6ae5c42ee64.sentence: Pelagic marine systems regulate the global climate, contribute to the water cycle, maintain biodiversity, provide food and energy resources, and create opportunities for recreation and tourism.

4a858272c009.title: Marine ecosystem
4a858272c009.sentence: Economically, marine systems support billions of dollars' worth of capture fisheries, aquaculture, offshore oil and gas, and trade and shipping.

f5ee3034f7f8.title: Marine ecosystem
f5ee3034f7f8.sentence: For example, coastal capture fisheries from mangroves and coral reef habitats are estimated to be worth a minimum of $34 billion per year.

27fd5c2e4f33.title: Estuary
27fd5c2e4f33.sentence: An estuary is a partially enclosed coastal body of brackish water where freshwater from rivers or streams meets and mixes with saltwater from the open sea.

06a64d583265.title: Estuary
06a64d583265.sentence: Estuaries form transition zones between riverine and marine environments and are classified as ecotones, areas where different ecosystems overlap.

d7ba923b9ea6.title: Estuary
d7ba923b9ea6.sentence: They are influenced by both marine processes (such as tides, waves, and saline water intrusion) and fluvial processes (including freshwater flow and sediment input).

459a86dfd544.title: Estuary
459a86dfd544.sentence: The mixing of seawater and freshwater provides high levels of nutrients both in the water column and in sediment, making estuaries among the most productive natural habitats in the world.

61f8ec90ac75.title: Estuary
61f8ec90ac75.sentence: Most existing estuaries originated during the Holocene epoch with the flooding of river-eroded or glacially scoured valleys when the sea level began to rise about 10,000–12,000 years ago.

bc911efc2df7.title: Estuary
bc911efc2df7.sentence: There is extreme spatial variability in salinity, with a range of near-zero at the tidal limit of tributary rivers to 3.4% at the estuary mouth.

788e37c02712.title: Estuary
788e37c02712.sentence: At any one point, the salinity will vary considerably over time and seasons, making it a harsh environment for organisms.

ba8cafaa761e.title: Estuary
ba8cafaa761e.sentence: Of the thirty-two largest cities in the world in the early 1990s, twenty-two were located on estuaries.

f624085a910c.title: Pelagic zone
f624085a910c.sentence: The pelagic zone consists of the water column of the open ocean and can be further divided into regions by depth.

50e28bd9851c.title: Pelagic zone
50e28bd9851c.sentence: The pelagic zone refers to the open, free waters away from the shore, where marine life can swim freely in any direction unhindered by topographical constraints.

b722c616933f.title: Pelagic zone
b722c616933f.sentence: Conditions in the water column change with depth: pressure increases; temperature and light decrease; salinity, oxygen, micronutrients (such as iron, magnesium and calcium) all change.

19a1fa6188b2.title: Pelagic zone
19a1fa6188b2.sentence: The pelagic ecosystem is based on phytoplankton.

62f26702ee98.title: Pelagic zone
62f26702ee98.sentence: Because they need sunlight, they inhabit the upper, sunlit epipelagic zone, which includes the coastal or neritic zone.

a4dc78df9bee.title: Pelagic zone
a4dc78df9bee.sentence: Biodiversity diminishes markedly in the deeper zones below the epipelagic zone as dissolved oxygen diminishes, water pressure increases, temperatures become colder, food sources become scarce, and light diminishes and finally disappears.

44a6ce188667.title: Pelagic zone
44a6ce188667.sentence: Pelagic fish are often migratory forage fish, which feed on plankton, and the larger predatory fish that follow and feed on the forage fish.

1f313c636891.title: Pelagic zone
1f313c636891.sentence: Examples of migratory forage fish are herring, anchovies, capelin, and menhaden.

efbaa9d77d31.title: Pelagic zone
efbaa9d77d31.sentence: Examples of larger pelagic fish which prey on the forage fish are billfish, tuna, and oceanic sharks.

7ee8407000b5.title: Biological pump
7ee8407000b5.sentence: The majority of this carbon fixation (~80%) is carried out in the open ocean while the remaining amount occurs in the very productive upwelling regions of the ocean.

cc53439e9d79.title: Biological pump
cc53439e9d79.sentence: Despite these productive regions producing 2 to 3 times as much fixed carbon per area, the open ocean accounts for greater than 90% of the ocean area and therefore is the larger contributor.

f46c3ae97d51.title: Deep sea
f46c3ae97d51.sentence: The deep sea is broadly defined as the ocean depth where light begins to fade, at an approximate depth of 200 m (660 ft) or the point of transition from continental shelves to continental slopes.

13e7d9b35ce2.title: Deep sea
13e7d9b35ce2.sentence: Conditions within the deep sea are a combination of low temperatures, darkness, and high pressure.

0f31b84c84e9.title: Deep sea
0f31b84c84e9.sentence: The deep sea is considered the least explored Earth biome as the extreme conditions make the environment difficult to access and explore.

1694a61b6a19.title: Deep sea
1694a61b6a19.sentence: Pressure increases at approximately one atmosphere for every 10 meters meaning that some areas of the deep sea can reach pressures of above 1,000 atmospheres.

b64b47e1c541.title: Deep sea
b64b47e1c541.sentence: Since photosynthesis is not possible, plants and phytoplankton cannot live in this zone, and as these are the primary producers of almost all of earth's ecosystems, life in this area of the ocean must depend on energy sources from elsewhere.

1522bfd54a05.title: Deep sea
1522bfd54a05.sentence: Except for the areas close to the hydrothermal vents, this energy comes from organic material drifting down from the photic zone.

f057b26e8fb5.title: Deep sea
f057b26e8fb5.sentence: At any given depth, the temperature is practically unvarying over long periods of time, without seasonal changes and with very little interannual variability.

8ced689c074e.title: Deep sea
8ced689c074e.sentence: No other habitat on earth has such a constant temperature.

085350bd527b.title: Deep sea
085350bd527b.sentence: Salinity is remarkably constant throughout the deep sea, at about 35 parts per thousand.

209e1964fd70.title: Deep sea
209e1964fd70.sentence: In 1960, the bathyscaphe Trieste descended to the bottom of the Mariana Trench near Guam, at 10,911 m (35,797 ft; 6.780 mi), the deepest known spot in any ocean.

00e66710d762.title: Deep sea
00e66710d762.sentence: The midwater fish have special adaptations to cope with these conditions—they are small, usually being under 25 centimetres (10 in); they have slow metabolisms and unspecialized diets, preferring to sit and wait for food rather than waste energy searching for it.

9b88d343b7b2.title: Deep sea
9b88d343b7b2.sentence: The two main methods by which this is achieved are reduction in the area of their shadow by lateral compression of the body, and counter illumination via bioluminescence.

c5507f120076.title: Estuary
c5507f120076.sentence: Estuaries provide a wide range of ecosystem services that sustain both ecological productivity and human well-being.

3c7f410fc0ee.title: Estuary
3c7f410fc0ee.sentence: They function as nursery habitats, supporting the early life stages of many marine fish and shellfish, while also maintaining mangroves, seagrasses, salt marshes, and seaweeds that recycle nutrients and support productive fisheries.

3a0119875d34.title: Estuary
3a0119875d34.section: Implications of eutrophication on estuaries > Effects of eutrophication on human activities
3a0119875d34.sentence: The commercial fishing industry relies upon estuaries for approximately 68 percent of their catch by value because of the great biodiversity of this ecosystem.

62e36df6c03d.title: Estuary
62e36df6c03d.sentence: Water draining from upland areas carries sediments, nutrients, and pollutants into estuaries, where wetlands such as swamps and salt marshes naturally filter these materials improving water clarity and quality for both marine organisms and coastal communities.

69fb29482fcd.title: Estuary
69fb29482fcd.sentence: Vegetation, such as salt marsh grasses, also stabilize shorelines and help reduce erosion, providing a natural buffer against storm impacts and sea-level rise, thereby protecting coastal environments and human infrastructure.

3a6efee29d10.title: Estuary
3a6efee29d10.sentence: These ecosystems serve as critical migration corridors for anadromous and catadromous fish.

b16720ecb238.title: Estuary
b16720ecb238.sentence: In addition, estuaries offer habitat for migratory birds and endangered species, enhancing biodiversity and supporting ecotourism opportunities.

845835c0ec1a.title: Grassland
845835c0ec1a.sentence: Herbaceous (non-wooded) vegetation dominates grasslands and carbon is stored in the roots and soil underground.

c0f5451af95f.title: Grassland
c0f5451af95f.sentence: Above-ground biomass carbon is relatively short-lived due to grazing, fire, and senescence.

f8aee2104c18.title: Grassland
f8aee2104c18.sentence: For this reason, soil carbon accounts for about 81% of the total ecosystem carbon in grasslands.

8233fa4977bd.title: Grassland
8233fa4977bd.sentence: Because plant productivity is limited by grassland precipitation, carbon stocks are highest in regions where precipitation is heaviest, such as the high grass prairie in the humid temperate region of the United States.

26d923a49e33.title: Grassland
26d923a49e33.sentence: Similarly, as annual temperatures rise, grassland carbon stocks decrease due to increased evapotranspiration.

4079ecb9a2fc.title: Grassland
4079ecb9a2fc.sentence: Grasslands have suffered large losses of organic carbon due to soil disturbances, vegetation degradation, fires, erosion, nutrient deficiencies, and water shortages.

eaf9d59e17e5.title: Grassland
eaf9d59e17e5.sentence: Good grassland management can reverse historical soil carbon losses.

c627af84437a.title: Grassland
c627af84437a.sentence: There is a lack of agreement on the amount of carbon that can be stored in grassland ecosystem.

1b53599d5302.title: Grassland
1b53599d5302.sentence: This is partly caused by different methodologies applied to measure soil organic carbon and limited respective datasets.

93ecc46bb8c7.title: Grassland
93ecc46bb8c7.sentence: According to the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN), the most significant threat to grasslands is human land use, especially agriculture and mining.

a7939c3c1205.title: Grassland
a7939c3c1205.sentence: Global losses from grassland degradation are estimated to be over $7 billion per year.

aeeda708f53e.title: Grassland
aeeda708f53e.sentence: A global analysis of 70 grassland ecoregions found that 21 are less than 20% intact, while only 14 retain at least 60% intactness; moreover, 47 of 70 regional grasslands have been in decline since 2000.

94792c84a51d.title: Grassland
94792c84a51d.sentence: To feed a growing human population, most of the world's grasslands are converted from natural landscapes to fields of corn, wheat or other crops.

d7bf1008f174.title: Grassland
d7bf1008f174.sentence: The vulnerability of grasslands stems from a range of factors, such as misclassification, poor protection and cultivation.

27f3922a0ff8.title: Grassland
27f3922a0ff8.section: Degradation > Causes > Afforestation or introduction of invasive species
27f3922a0ff8.sentence: It is expected that non-native grasses will continue to outperform native species under warmer and drier conditions that occur in many grasslands due to climate change.

98a36a0035df.title: Grassland
98a36a0035df.sentence: Despite growing recognition of the importance of grasslands, understanding of restoration options remains limited.

e0bb59122d7d.title: Grassland
e0bb59122d7d.sentence: Only seven large, continuous grassland regions have been identified as remaining relatively intact on Earth: the Selenge-Altai and surrounding steppes and the Mongolian-Manchurian and Daurian grasslands in Asia, the Wyoming Basin steppe and the Nebraska Sand Hills in North America, the Central Andean wet Puna in South America, the Mitchell grasslands in Australia, and the Maloti-Drakensberg grasslands in Africa.

1c6b04dbfd69.title: Grassland
1c6b04dbfd69.sentence: Cost of grassland restoration is highly variable and respective data is scarce.

26e1ccfbf6e3.title: Grassland
26e1ccfbf6e3.sentence: - appropriate management of livestock and wild herbivores: in light of land use intensification caused by global food demand, grassland land use practices may need to be adjusted to better support key ecosystem services.

f290913d9337.title: Grassland
f290913d9337.sentence: - reintroduction of native grasses and forbs via seeding or transplant: a main challenge for grassland restoration is how to overcome seed limitation.

42d5e3959e34.title: Grassland
42d5e3959e34.sentence: Successful grassland restoration has several dimensions, including recognition in policy, standardisation of indicators of degradation, scientific innovation, knowledge transfer and data sharing.

35c880305839.title: Grassland
35c880305839.sentence: For the period 2021–2030 the United Nations General Assembly has proclaimed the UN Decade on Restoration, involving a joint resolution by over 70 countries.

5e4cbab27f16.title: Grassland
5e4cbab27f16.sentence: It is led by the United Nations Environment Programme and the Food and Agriculture Organization.

abaa0a55a5cd.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
abaa0a55a5cd.sentence: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands of concern consist primarily of methane and nitrous oxide emissions.

da6790f76cb3.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
da6790f76cb3.sentence: This high level of water saturation creates conditions conducive to methane production.

9c05ce76fb41.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
9c05ce76fb41.sentence: Because the microbes that live in warm, moist environments consume oxygen more rapidly than it can diffuse in from the atmosphere, wetlands are the ideal anaerobic environments for fermentation as well as methanogen activity.

4c18c3c31dd6.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
4c18c3c31dd6.sentence: A warmer, more anaerobic environment with soil rich in organic matter would allow for more efficient methanogenesis.

8b564d8a4896.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
8b564d8a4896.sentence: Some wetlands are a significant source of methane emissions and some are also emitters of nitrous oxide.

e7c8746d2234.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
e7c8746d2234.sentence: Nitrous oxide is a greenhouse gas with a global warming potential 300 times that of carbon dioxide and is the dominant ozone-depleting substance emitted in the 21st century.

efdf8b89492c.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
efdf8b89492c.sentence: Excess nutrients mainly from anthropogenic sources have been shown to significantly increase the N2O fluxes from wetland soils through denitrification and nitrification processes (see table below).

c5d0bdaa788d.title: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands
c5d0bdaa788d.sentence: Wetlands can also act as a sink for greenhouse gases.

405e70050177.title: Carbon sequestration
405e70050177.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Wetlands
405e70050177.sentence: Wetland soil is an important carbon sink; 14.5% of the world's soil carbon is found in wetlands, while only 5.5% of the world's land is composed of wetlands.

bed148a1c22a.title: Peatland
bed148a1c22a.sentence: Generally, whenever the inputs of carbon into the soil from dead organic matter exceed the carbon outputs via organic matter decomposition, peat is formed.

aab06bdb534a.title: Peatland
aab06bdb534a.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
aab06bdb534a.sentence: Despite accounting for just 3% of Earth's land surfaces, peatlands are collectively a major carbon store containing between 500 and 700 billion tonnes of carbon.

1657324a4d1b.title: Peatland
1657324a4d1b.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
1657324a4d1b.sentence: Carbon stored within peatlands equates to over half the amount of carbon found in the atmosphere.

131668c14a21.title: Peatland
131668c14a21.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
131668c14a21.sentence: In their natural state, mires are a small atmospheric carbon dioxide sink through the photosynthesis of peat vegetation, which outweighs their release of greenhouse gases.

7cc6ae2ff1f9.title: Peatland
7cc6ae2ff1f9.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
7cc6ae2ff1f9.sentence: On the other hand, most mires are generally net emitters of methane and nitrous oxide.

39748d3bfe9a.title: Peatland
39748d3bfe9a.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
39748d3bfe9a.sentence: The water table position of a peatland is the main control of its carbon release to the atmosphere.

a15155f9e39c.title: Peatland
a15155f9e39c.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
a15155f9e39c.sentence: Carbon dioxide release increases when the water table falls lower, such as during a drought, as this increases the availability of oxygen to the aerobic microbes thus accelerating peat decomposition.

7ff864bffffe.title: Peatland
7ff864bffffe.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
7ff864bffffe.sentence: Due to the continued CO2 sequestration over millennia, and because of the longer atmospheric lifespan of the CO2 molecules compared with methane and nitrous oxide, peatlands have had a net cooling effect on the atmosphere.

3b50de97ea77.title: Peatland
3b50de97ea77.sentence: This involves cutting drainage ditches to lower the water table with the intended purpose of enhancing the productivity of forest cover or for use as pasture or cropland.

9fcb1d8f1647.title: Peatland
9fcb1d8f1647.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry
9fcb1d8f1647.sentence: As such, drainage of mires for agriculture transforms them from net carbon sinks to net carbon emitters.

18f996541dbb.title: Peatland
18f996541dbb.sentence: Peatlands are used by humans in modern times for a range of purposes, the most dominant being agriculture and forestry, which accounts for around a quarter of global peatland area.

f0a69451c543.title: Peatland
f0a69451c543.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry
f0a69451c543.sentence: By allowing oxygen to enter the peat column within a mire, drainage disrupts the balance between peat accumulation and decomposition, and the subsequent oxidative degradation results in the release of carbon into the atmosphere.

666472e49c51.title: Peatland
666472e49c51.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry
666472e49c51.sentence: The drainage of peatlands for agriculture and forestry has resulted in the emission of extensive greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, most notably carbon dioxide and methane.

e4d06845d3a3.title: Carbon sequestration
e4d06845d3a3.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Wetlands > Peatlands, mires and peat bogs
e4d06845d3a3.sentence: These degraded peatlands account for 5-10% of global carbon emissions from human activities.

e9e130a3a2d7.title: Peatland
e9e130a3a2d7.sentence: Upon extreme drying, the ecosystem can undergo a state shift, turning the mire into a barren land with lower biodiversity and richness.

8c0c56c8abc5.title: Peatland
8c0c56c8abc5.sentence: Often, restoration is done by blocking drainage channels in the peatland, and allowing natural vegetation to recover.

e0838103fb37.title: Peatland
e0838103fb37.sentence: Rehabilitation projects undertaken in North America and Europe usually focus on the rewetting of peatlands and revegetation of native species.

c6685c2bca68.title: Peatland
c6685c2bca68.sentence: This acts to mitigate carbon release in the short term before the new growth of vegetation provides a new source of organic litter to fuel the peat formation in the long term.

33da8b2ff8bc.title: Peatland
33da8b2ff8bc.sentence: According to the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report, the conservation and restoration of wetlands and peatlands has large economic potential to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions, providing benefits for adaptation, mitigation and biodiversity.

bdfda036ed48.title: Peatland
bdfda036ed48.sentence: The United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity highlights peatlands as key ecosystems to be conserved and protected.

491e1835a2b1.title: Peatland
491e1835a2b1.sentence: Wetlands are also protected under the 1971 Ramsar Convention.

c13def23e5dc.title: Peatland
c13def23e5dc.section: Management and rehabilitation > Global Peatlands Initiative
c13def23e5dc.sentence: The Global Peatlands Initiative is an effort made by leading experts and institutions formed in 2016 by 13 founding members at the UNFCCC COP in Marrakech, Morocco.

c83a6d6155d2.title: Peatland
c83a6d6155d2.section: Management and rehabilitation > Global Peatlands Initiative
c83a6d6155d2.sentence: The mission of the Initiative is to protect and conserve peatlands as the world's largest terrestrial organic carbon stock and to prevent it from being emitted into the atmosphere.

c7f4397bac51.title: Peatland restoration
c7f4397bac51.sentence: This landscape globally occupies 400 million hectares or 3% of land surface on Earth.

994e20f0af8e.title: Peatland restoration
994e20f0af8e.sentence: Historically, peatlands have been drained for several main reasons; peat extraction, creation of agricultural land, and forestry usage.

397d1842f44c.title: Peatland restoration
397d1842f44c.sentence: However, this activity has caused degradation affecting this landscape's structure through damage to habitats, hydrology, nutrients cycle, carbon balance and more.

f8f3345ffba5.title: Peatland restoration
f8f3345ffba5.section: Targets of restoration > Climate change mitigation and adaptation
f8f3345ffba5.sentence: Peatlands store carbon from dead plants and hence help mitigate climate change.

5473e4d9947c.title: Peatland restoration
5473e4d9947c.section: Targets of restoration > Climate change mitigation and adaptation
5473e4d9947c.sentence: However, draining and degrading peatlands release large amounts of greenhouse gases.

2cd10f482185.title: Peatland restoration
2cd10f482185.sentence: A peatland as an intact ecosystem is a natural water purifier, it filters and stores organic substances, metals or other toxic matter and retains nutrients.

1665d824f453.title: Peatland restoration
1665d824f453.sentence: These pollutants are stored in the peat for long periods of time, improving the quality of drinking water.

a53714ddd67e.title: Bog
a53714ddd67e.sentence: The peat in bogs is an important place for the storage of carbon.

8b91126fafa0.title: Bog
8b91126fafa0.sentence: Peat bogs are also important in storing fresh water, particularly in the headwaters of large rivers.

cf66bd9edeef.title: Bog
cf66bd9edeef.sentence: If the peat decays, carbon dioxide would be released to the atmosphere, contributing to global warming.

a96a2e2b26f4.title: Bog
a96a2e2b26f4.sentence: Undisturbed, bogs function as a carbon sink.

431558427f8f.title: Bog
431558427f8f.sentence: As one example, the peatlands of the former Soviet Union were calculated to be removing 52 Tg of carbon per year from the atmosphere.

11858ef15f02.title: Bog
11858ef15f02.sentence: Therefore, the rewetting of drained peatlands may be one of the most cost-effective ways to mitigate climate change.

e7c3b9ba1a5d.title: Bog
e7c3b9ba1a5d.sentence: Even the enormous Yangtze River arises in the Ruoergai peatland near its headwaters in Tibet.

cd6ef7cd9ff3.title: Bog
cd6ef7cd9ff3.sentence: Blueberries, cranberries, cloudberries, huckleberries, and lingonberries are harvested from the wild in bogs.

2c7f6e2cf58b.title: Bog
2c7f6e2cf58b.sentence: Sphagnum bogs are also used for outdoor recreation, with activities including ecotourism and hunting.

6e24c61c8881.title: Fen
6e24c61c8881.sentence: A fen is a type of peat-accumulating wetland fed by mineral-rich ground or surface water.

6b041330e86e.title: Fen
6b041330e86e.sentence: It is one of the main types of wetland along with marshes, swamps, and bogs.

49b3b1e982c7.title: Fen
49b3b1e982c7.sentence: Bogs and fens, both peat-forming ecosystems, are also known as mires.

cbfb475e099a.title: Fen
cbfb475e099a.sentence: The unique water chemistry of fens is a result of the ground or surface water input.

824a1c48c00c.title: Fen
824a1c48c00c.sentence: Typically, this input results in higher mineral concentrations and a more basic pH than found in bogs.

7eb87286e569.title: Fen
7eb87286e569.section: Ecosystem services > Carbon sequestration and global warming
7eb87286e569.sentence: Fens, as peat-forming ecosystems, sequester large quantities of carbon as peat, preventing its release into the atmosphere as carbon dioxide.

bc2f1c040b54.title: Fen
bc2f1c040b54.section: Ecosystem services > Carbon sequestration and global warming
bc2f1c040b54.sentence: Destruction of the peat layer in fens can release carbon stores into the atmosphere.

c4a18c17ecc1.title: Fen
c4a18c17ecc1.sentence: One major application of this is treatment of agricultural runoff rich in nitrogen.

79056b98a8ef.title: Fen
79056b98a8ef.sentence: Fens accepting this agricultural runoff can discharge water containing lower levels of nitrogen and other pollutants, improving water quality in nearby aquatic environments.

a768de547e33.title: Fen
a768de547e33.section: Threats and conservation > Threats to fens
a768de547e33.sentence: Historically, a major cause of fen loss has been conversion to agricultural lands.

97500b1e39f3.title: Fen
97500b1e39f3.section: Threats and conservation > Conservation of fens
97500b1e39f3.sentence: Significant losses of fens, particularly via conversion to agricultural lands, has reduced their prevalence, especially across Europe and North America.

06831b97e6d3.title: Fen
06831b97e6d3.section: Threats and conservation > Conservation of fens
06831b97e6d3.sentence: There is also interest in restoring fens that have been damaged or degraded.

e73143e3bda8.title: Fen
e73143e3bda8.section: Threats and conservation > Conservation of fens
e73143e3bda8.sentence: Often, this is attempted by altering or restoring the hydrological conditions at a site (e.g., blocking of drains or ditches).

4f57ba151c4e.title: Boreal ecosystem
4f57ba151c4e.sentence: A boreal ecosystem is an ecosystem with a subarctic climate located in the Northern Hemisphere, approximately between 50° and 70°N latitude.

a6775dd0da02.title: Boreal ecosystem
a6775dd0da02.sentence: These ecosystems are commonly known as taiga and are located in parts of North America, Europe, and Asia.

b125431e9927.title: Boreal ecosystem
b125431e9927.sentence: Boreal ecosystems are filled with a multitude of flora species from black and white spruce, to willows, wildflowers, and alders.

8bc3db9a3e85.title: Boreal ecosystem
8bc3db9a3e85.sentence: Caribou, although not there year round, come down and into these regions during the winter to forage for lichen.

6278d93ad405.title: Boreal ecosystem
6278d93ad405.sentence: However, despite not being as biodiverse as tropical systems, this area has a variety of species.

c6fc326e1cf0.title: Boreal ecosystem
c6fc326e1cf0.sentence: Secondary succession consists of varied events: wildfires, flooding, mudslides and even excessive insect foraging act in this progression and cycle of boreal forests.

bc3983f31ff5.title: Boreal ecosystem
bc3983f31ff5.sentence: Boreal ecosystems contain approximately 338 Pg (petagrams) of carbon in their soil, this is comparable to the amount which is stored in biomass in tropical ecosystems.

507fe2417e05.title: Boreal ecosystem
507fe2417e05.sentence: Boreal ecosystems are some of the most vulnerable to climate change.

06af72f1a04b.title: Wetland
06af72f1a04b.sentence: Wetlands naturally produce an array of vegetation and other ecological products that can be harvested for personal and commercial use.

49ede813196c.title: Wetland
49ede813196c.sentence: Many fishes have all or part of their life-cycle occurring within a wetland system.

e697d5a768ec.title: Wetland
e697d5a768ec.sentence: Fresh and saltwater fish are the main source of protein for about one billion people and comprise 15% of an additional 3.5 billion people's protein intake.

5393f8f122cc.title: Wetland
5393f8f122cc.sentence: Another food staple found in wetland systems is rice, a popular grain that is consumed at the rate of one fifth of the total global calorie count.

4f51f1f64a00.title: Wetland
4f51f1f64a00.sentence: Other mangrove-derived products include fuelwood, salt (produced by evaporating seawater), animal fodder, traditional medicines (e.g. from mangrove bark), fibers for textiles and dyes and tannins.

a3d45cab0802.title: Wetland
a3d45cab0802.sentence: A good example is the Lower Mekong basin which runs through Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam, supporting over 55 million people.

824706767b22.title: Wetland
824706767b22.sentence: Water purification can be provided by floodplains, closed-depression wetlands, mudflat, freshwater marsh, salt marsh, mangroves.

4fe5f8592dca.title: Wetland
4fe5f8592dca.sentence: A natural function of wetland vegetation is the up-take, storage, and (for nitrate) the removal of nutrients found in runoff water from the surrounding landscapes.

dddb29d178ef.title: Wetland
dddb29d178ef.sentence: Wetland vegetation acts as a physical barrier to slow water flow and then trap sediment for both short or long periods of time.

5674c644506b.title: Wetland
5674c644506b.sentence: Suspended sediment can contain heavy metals that are also retained when wetlands trap the sediment.

42a436802111.title: Wetland
42a436802111.sentence: The ability of wetland systems to store or remove nutrients and trap sediment is highly efficient and effective but each system has a threshold.

8d0b3d8175dc.title: Wetland
8d0b3d8175dc.sentence: An overabundance of nutrient input from fertilizer run-off, sewage effluent, or non-point pollution will cause eutrophication.

fc645911076d.title: Wetland
fc645911076d.sentence: Upstream erosion from deforestation can overwhelm wetlands making them shrink in size and cause dramatic biodiversity loss through excessive sedimentation load.

3e42812e70c5.title: Wetland
3e42812e70c5.sentence: Constructed wetlands are built for wastewater treatment.

77f8461a5fdc.title: Wetland
77f8461a5fdc.sentence: A constructed wetland is an artificial wetland to treat sewage, greywater, stormwater runoff or industrial wastewater.

d4c504ba0981.title: Wetland
d4c504ba0981.sentence: Constructed wetlands are engineered systems that use the natural functions of vegetation, soil, and organisms to provide secondary treatment to wastewater.

1fb1799cb5b4.title: Wetland
1fb1799cb5b4.sentence: Constructed wetlands are designed to remove water pollutants such as suspended solids, organic matter and nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus).

fd8bbebc9e3c.title: Wetland
fd8bbebc9e3c.sentence: All types of pathogens (i.e., bacteria, viruses, protozoans and helminths) are expected to be removed to some extent in a constructed wetland.

f518d5dcb25b.title: Wetland
f518d5dcb25b.sentence: An example of how a natural wetland is used to provide some degree of sewage treatment is the East Kolkata Wetlands in Kolkata, India.

a5e89b296d67.title: Wetland
a5e89b296d67.sentence: The wetlands cover 125 square kilometres (48 sq mi), and are used to treat Kolkata's sewage.

f6fb7ce39e3b.title: Wetland
f6fb7ce39e3b.sentence: The nutrients contained in the wastewater sustain fish farms and agriculture.

75dbae381856.sentence: They can be used in developments as part of water-sensitive urban design systems and have benefits such as flood mitigation, removing pollutants, carbon sequestration, providing habitat for wildlife and biodiversity in often highly urbanised and fragmented landscapes.

d253465cb209.title: Temperate forest
d253465cb209.sentence: A temperate forest is a forest found between the tropical and boreal regions, located in the temperate zone.

05bfdd26d441.title: Temperate forest
05bfdd26d441.sentence: It is the second largest terrestrial biome, covering 25% of the world's forest area, only behind the boreal forest, which covers about 33%.

fd051bf1ad0d.title: Temperate forest
fd051bf1ad0d.sentence: These forests cover both hemispheres at latitudes ranging from 25 to 50 degrees, wrapping the planet in a belt similar to that of the boreal forest.

73cda74a6d81.title: Temperate forest
73cda74a6d81.sentence: Due to its large size spanning several continents, there are several main types: deciduous, coniferous, mixed forest, and rainforest.

8dbddc8ce63f.title: Temperate forest
8dbddc8ce63f.sentence: Temperate forests are located in the middle latitudes where much of the planet's population is.

9d1844df5ea8.title: Temperate forest
9d1844df5ea8.sentence: Not only were these forests cut down to build cities (i.e. New York City, Seattle, London, Tokyo, Paris), they have also been "cut down long ago to make way for cultivation." This biome has been subject to mining, logging, hunting, pollution, deforestation and habitat loss.

d8a3ff44e71e.title: Temperate forest
d8a3ff44e71e.section: Types of temperate forest > Temperate rainforest
d8a3ff44e71e.sentence: Adding to its rarity is that most of the temperate rainforests outside protected areas have been cut down and no longer exist.

6f0dd88abeb8.title: Urban ecosystem
6f0dd88abeb8.sentence: In ecology, urban ecosystems are considered an ecosystem functional group within the intensive land-use biome.

971ebd69da12.title: Urban ecosystem
971ebd69da12.sentence: They are structurally complex ecosystems with highly heterogeneous and dynamic spatial structure that is created and maintained by humans.

5af3c843abad.title: Urban ecosystem
5af3c843abad.sentence: They include cities, smaller settlements and industrial areas, that are made up of diverse patch types (e.g. buildings, paved surfaces, transport infrastructure, parks and gardens, refuse areas).

2216f365bc6d.title: Urban ecosystem
2216f365bc6d.sentence: Urban ecosystems rely on large subsidies of imported water, nutrients, food and other resources.

8c1bc18fdc32.title: Urban ecosystem
8c1bc18fdc32.sentence: Compared to other natural and artificial ecosystems human population density is high, and their interaction with the different patch types produces emergent properties and complex feedbacks among ecosystem components.

e86ac2e9a0aa.title: Urban ecosystem
e86ac2e9a0aa.sentence: In socioecology, urban areas are considered part of a broader social-ecological system in which urban landscapes and urban human communities interact with other landscape elements.

a7447e3dffd6.title: Urban ecosystem
a7447e3dffd6.section: Difficulties and opportunities > Difficulties > Population growth
a7447e3dffd6.sentence: Cities are home to more than half of the world's population, and the number of people living in urban areas is expected to continue to grow in the coming decades.

afcf34819c71.title: Urban ecosystem
afcf34819c71.section: Difficulties and opportunities > Difficulties > Population growth
afcf34819c71.sentence: On the one hand, cities can provide economic opportunities, access to healthcare and education, and a high quality of life for residents.

ba51efbf24a6.title: Urban ecosystem
ba51efbf24a6.section: Difficulties and opportunities > Difficulties > Population growth
ba51efbf24a6.sentence: On the other, increased urbanization exacerbates the struggles of pollution, loss of green spaces, loss of biodiversity, and more.

e925e011a798.title: Urban ecosystem
e925e011a798.sentence: Urbanization has large impacts on human and environmental health, and the study of urban ecosystems has led to proposals for sustainable urban designs and approaches to development of city fringe areas that can help reduce negative impact on surrounding environments and promote human well-being.

1afbf4d61a93.sentence: Demonstrating convergent evolution, many of these species found similar solutions to the tropical conditions of variable salinity, tidal range (inundation), anaerobic soils, and intense sunlight.

ae5df16cbda5.title: Mangrove

3df2b07d18c5.title: Mangrove

e35bb1881b85.title: Mangrove

beb12b718915.title: Mangrove

579b88739354.title: Mangrove

098f8ec199ed.title: Mangrove

9e6a0ed224bd.title: Mangrove

1e5401b63611.title: Mangrove

b48ba90aea3b.title: Mangrove

dbad857f0979.title: Mangrove

b9604c8eb389.title: Mangrove

1dc5e00517e9.title: Mangrove

a43d9aafa59d.title: Mangrove

a1d2f8bf0d64.sentence: As one of the largest biomes, the taiga provides an exceptional amount of value to human populations including lumber and paper production.

0d5d0b4b94bb.sentence: A significant threat to forest ecology is deforestation as it removes large areas of forest for timber and land development.

6a6887f296af.sentence: Climate change has an effect on forests from wildfires, droughts, soil erosion, and heat stress effects on vegetation.

d51a988ff092.title: Forest ecology
d51a988ff092.sentence: As trees are cleared, forest habitat become fragmented into smaller patches, making it harder for forest-dependent species to find resources such as food, shelter and mates.

ec0c756767c3.title: Forest ecology

569c555d5507.title: Forest ecology

bf351fb5cba3.title: Forest ecology

1c7a52fff490.title: Forest ecology

49d31220f197.title: Forest ecology

11c70002ce81.title: Forest ecology

a68188b61cc2.title: Peat swamp forest

f48b7665cdb7.title: Peat swamp forest

f9d84d830717.title: Peat swamp forest

da11f89a516a.title: Peat swamp forest

6644f0e17b56.title: Peat swamp forest

5e5f778b05d1.title: Estuary

4f4c3cd16c81.title: Estuary
4f4c3cd16c81.section: Classification based on geomorphology > Drowned river valleys
4f4c3cd16c81.sentence: In places where the sea level is rising relative to the land, sea water progressively penetrates into river valleys and the topography of the estuary remains similar to that of a river valley.

c2aa847a3e17.title: Estuary
c2aa847a3e17.section: Classification based on geomorphology > Drowned river valleys
c2aa847a3e17.sentence: This is the most common type of estuary in temperate climates.

32620d910a43.title: Estuary
32620d910a43.section: Classification based on geomorphology > Lagoon-type or bar-built
32620d910a43.sentence: Bar-built estuaries are found in a place where the deposition of sediment has kept pace with rising sea levels so that the estuaries are shallow and separated from the sea by sand spits or barrier islands.

f139d7b1d2d1.title: Estuary
f139d7b1d2d1.section: Classification based on geomorphology > Lagoon-type or bar-built
f139d7b1d2d1.sentence: They are relatively common in tropical and subtropical locations.

593363389260.title: Estuary
593363389260.sentence: Fjord-type estuaries are formed in deeply eroded valleys formed by glaciers.

8e33271169f4.title: Estuary
8e33271169f4.section: Classification based on geomorphology > Tectonically produced
8e33271169f4.sentence: These estuaries are formed by subsidence or land cut off from the ocean by land movement associated with faulting, volcanoes, and landslides.

2f806f173956.title: Estuary
2f806f173956.section: Classification based on geomorphology > Tectonically produced
2f806f173956.sentence: There are only a small number of tectonically produced estuaries; one example is the San Francisco Bay, which was formed by the crustal movements of the San Andreas Fault system causing the inundation of the lower reaches of the Sacramento and San Joaquin rivers.

a93b355b7183.title: Estuary
a93b355b7183.section: Classification based on water circulation > Salt wedge
a93b355b7183.sentence: In this type of estuary, river output greatly exceeds marine input and tidal effects have minor importance.

5ae35cd55621.title: Estuary
5ae35cd55621.section: Classification based on water circulation > Salt wedge
5ae35cd55621.sentence: Freshwater floats on top of the seawater in a layer that gradually thins as it moves seaward.

d1e0630fc968.title: Estuary
d1e0630fc968.section: Classification based on water circulation > Salt wedge
d1e0630fc968.sentence: The denser seawater moves landward along the bottom of the estuary, forming a wedge-shaped layer that is thinner as it approaches land.

5d38a52d5084.title: Estuary
5d38a52d5084.section: Classification based on water circulation > Partially mixed
5d38a52d5084.sentence: As tidal forcing increases, river output becomes less than the marine input.

13790bf948ee.title: Estuary
13790bf948ee.section: Classification based on water circulation > Well-mixed
13790bf948ee.sentence: Tidal mixing forces exceed river output, resulting in a well-mixed water column and the disappearance of the vertical salinity gradient.

68efb9a3fd60.title: Estuary
68efb9a3fd60.section: Classification based on water circulation > Inverse
68efb9a3fd60.sentence: Inverse estuaries occur in dry climates where evaporation greatly exceeds the inflow of freshwater.

4d0dd1ced415.sentence: Nitrogen is often the lead cause of eutrophication in estuaries in temperate zones.

d841a44bf4b6.sentence: A decrease in production within this industry can affect any of the 1.7 million people the fishing industry employs yearly across the United States.
