b10384ea1687.sentence: Most reefs grow best in warm, shallow, clear, sunny, and agitated water.

e084ef27d697.title: Coral reef
e084ef27d697.sentence: Coral reefs flourish in ocean waters that provide few nutrients.

99c609e7bad3.title: Coral reef
99c609e7bad3.sentence: Over 4,000 species of fish inhabit coral reefs.

7c9da758acd5.title: Coral reef
7c9da758acd5.sentence: Fringing reefs just below low tide level have a mutually beneficial relationship with mangrove forests at high tide level and sea grass meadows in between: the reefs protect the mangroves and seagrass from strong currents and waves that would damage them or erode the sediments in which they are rooted, while the mangroves and sea grass protect the coral from large influxes of silt, fresh water and pollutants.

09016cbbda21.title: Coral reef
09016cbbda21.sentence: Shallow tropical coral reefs have declined by 50% since 1950, partly because they are sensitive to water conditions.

e07538f51a10.title: Coral reef
e07538f51a10.sentence: Coral reefs first appeared 485 million years ago, at the dawn of the Early Ordovician, displacing the microbial and sponge reefs of the Cambrian.

37197e8453c4.title: Coral reef
37197e8453c4.sentence: Most coral reefs are less than 10,000 years old.

c5d69a2f5581.title: Seagrass
c5d69a2f5581.sentence: Seagrasses are the only embryophytes (commonly referred to as "land plants") which grow in marine environments.

a9c72621c017.title: Seagrass
a9c72621c017.sentence: Like all autotrophic plants, seagrasses photosynthesize, in the submerged photic zone, and most occur in shallow and sheltered coastal waters anchored in sand or mud bottoms.

92796fab7c24.title: Seagrass
92796fab7c24.sentence: The name seagrass stems from the many species with long and narrow leaves, which grow by rhizome extension and often spread across large "meadows" resembling grassland; many species superficially resemble terrestrial grasses of the family Poaceae.

c5fbb3120188.title: Seagrass
c5fbb3120188.sentence: There are about 60 species of fully marine seagrasses which belong to four families (Posidoniaceae, Zosteraceae, Hydrocharitaceae and Cymodoceaceae), all in the order Alismatales (in the clade of monocotyledons).

759575f31ad5.title: Seagrass
759575f31ad5.sentence: Seagrasses evolved from terrestrial plants which recolonised the ocean 70 to 100 million years ago.

8621a62a8b7b.title: Seagrass
8621a62a8b7b.sentence: Most species undergo submarine pollination and complete their life cycle underwater.

f264625aa984.title: Seagrass
f264625aa984.sentence: These meadows account for more than 10% of the ocean's total carbon storage.

344475c3f444.title: Seagrass
344475c3f444.sentence: Per hectare, it holds twice as much carbon dioxide as rain forests and can sequester about 27.4 million tons of CO2 annually.

5723492a94de.title: Seagrass
5723492a94de.sentence: Many seagrass species produce an extensive underground network of roots and rhizome which stabilizes sediment and reduces coastal erosion.

554d696fc555.title: Seagrass
554d696fc555.sentence: The long blades of seagrasses slow the movement of water which reduces wave energy and offers further protection against coastal erosion and storm surge.

3a586da075f2.title: Seagrass
3a586da075f2.sentence: Sea turtles, manatees, parrotfish, surgeonfish, sea urchins and pinfish feed on seagrasses.

5f970ea04788.title: Seagrass
5f970ea04788.sentence: These habitats also act as a nursery grounds for commercially and recreationally valued fishery species, including the gag grouper (Mycteroperca microlepis), red drum, common snook, and many others.

9d68c824aea4.title: Seagrass
9d68c824aea4.sentence: Furthermore, many commercially important invertebrates also reside in seagrass habitats including bay scallops (Argopecten irradians), horseshoe crabs, and shrimp.

f07ba30ee07d.title: Seagrass
f07ba30ee07d.sentence: Despite only covering 0.1 - 0.2% of the ocean's surface, seagrasses form critically important ecosystems.

becae6049a19.title: Seagrass
becae6049a19.sentence: Since the late 19th century, over 20% of the global seagrass area has been lost, with seagrass bed loss occurring at a rate of 1.5% each year.

d7307584d990.title: Seagrass
d7307584d990.sentence: Of the 72 global seagrass species, approximately one quarter (15 species) could be considered at a Threatened or Near Threatened status on the IUCN's Red List of Threatened Species.

e76270cc6206.title: Salt marsh
e76270cc6206.sentence: A salt marsh, saltmarsh or salting, also known as a coastal marsh, is a tidal wetland in the upper coastal intertidal zone between land and sea that is regularly flooded by tides of seawater or brackish water.

af8392e95c40.title: Salt marsh
af8392e95c40.sentence: It is a unique marine coastal ecosystem dominated by dense stands of salt-tolerant plants such as herbs, grasses, or low shrubs.

5d29d96cffb5.title: Salt marsh
5d29d96cffb5.sentence: Salt marshes occur on low-energy shorelines in temperate and high-latitudes which can be stable, emerging, or submerging depending if the sedimentation is greater, equal to, or lower than relative sea level rise (subsidence rate plus sea level change), respectively.

fc18d8277673.title: Salt marsh
fc18d8277673.sentence: These typically include sheltered environments such as embankments, estuaries and the leeward side of barrier islands and spits.

93ec992b4751.title: Salt marsh
93ec992b4751.sentence: In the tropics and sub-tropics they are replaced by mangroves; an area that differs from a salt marsh in that instead of herbaceous plants, they are dominated by salt-tolerant trees.

4f94c0c6a386.title: Salt marsh
4f94c0c6a386.sentence: These plants are terrestrial in origin and are essential to the stability of the salt marsh in trapping and binding sediments.

1bd77ea1d09a.title: Salt marsh
1bd77ea1d09a.sentence: Salt marshes play a large role in the aquatic food web and the delivery of nutrients to coastal waters.

38b4f82682f8.title: Salt marsh
38b4f82682f8.sentence: They also support terrestrial animals and provide coastal protection.

e66f37654fef.title: Salt marsh
e66f37654fef.sentence: Salt marshes are ecologically important, providing habitats for native migratory fish and acting as sheltered feeding and nursery grounds.

cdfb486fc93f.title: Salt marsh
cdfb486fc93f.section: Human impacts > Urban development and nitrogen loading
cdfb486fc93f.sentence: They are highly productive ecosystems, and when net productivity is measured in g m−2 yr−1 they are equalled only by tropical rainforests.

07500548a92f.title: Salt marsh
07500548a92f.sentence: A later study conservatively estimated global saltmarsh extent as 90,800 km2 (9,080,000 hectares).

7afbd32a70d3.title: Salt marsh
7afbd32a70d3.sentence: The most extensive saltmarshes worldwide are found outside the tropics, notably including the low-lying, ice-free coasts, bays and estuaries of the North Atlantic which are well represented in their global polygon dataset.

864057d4cc32.title: Coral reef
864057d4cc32.sentence: Coral reefs deliver ecosystem services to tourism, fisheries, and coastline protection.

375554b957e5.title: Coral reef
375554b957e5.sentence: About 500 million people benefit from ecosystem services provided by coral reefs.

e4b7d2bb0f08.title: Coral reef
e4b7d2bb0f08.sentence: The global economic value of coral reefs has been estimated to be between US$29.8 billion and $375 billion per year.

7048531ddbbd.title: Coral reef
7048531ddbbd.sentence: The economic cost of destroying one square kilometre of coral reef over 25 years has been estimated at between $137,000 and $1,200,000.

84a305828354.title: Coral reef
84a305828354.sentence: About six million tons of fish are taken each year from coral reefs.

6e3e7dfd6aa7.title: Coral reef
6e3e7dfd6aa7.sentence: Well-managed reefs have an average annual yield of 15 tons of seafood per square kilometre.

68c6a880a219.title: Coral reef
68c6a880a219.sentence: Southeast Asia's coral reef fisheries alone yield about $2.4 billion in seafood annually.

f39ec87576cd.title: Coral reef
f39ec87576cd.sentence: To improve the management of coastal coral reefs, the World Resources Institute (WRI) developed and published tools to calculate the value of coral reef-related tourism, shoreline protection, and fisheries, partnering with five Caribbean countries.

9db9822fcd8b.title: Coral reef
9db9822fcd8b.sentence: The WRI was "making sure that the study results support improved coastal policies and management planning".

bd470fc83118.title: Coral reef
bd470fc83118.sentence: The Belize study estimated the value of reef and mangrove services at $395–559 million annually.

199e851c6691.title: Coral reef
199e851c6691.sentence: Bermuda's coral reefs provide economic benefits to the Island worth, on average, $722 million per year, based on six key ecosystem services, according to Sarkis et al. (2010).

e0b265a914df.title: Kelp forest
e0b265a914df.sentence: Kelp forests are underwater areas with a high density of kelp, which covers a large part of the world's coastlines.

7245e358cb41.title: Kelp forest
7245e358cb41.sentence: Smaller areas of anchored kelp are called kelp beds.

bf293cfce9e1.title: Kelp forest
bf293cfce9e1.sentence: Physically formed by brown macroalgae, kelp forests provide a unique habitat for marine organisms and are a source for understanding many ecological processes.

e5e1b88caecb.title: Kelp forest
e5e1b88caecb.sentence: They are recognized as one of the most productive and dynamic ecosystems on Earth.

340378081013.title: Kelp forest
340378081013.sentence: Although algal kelp forest combined with coral reefs only cover 0.1% of Earth's total surface, they account for 0.9% of global primary productivity.

0a860607962d.title: Kelp forest
0a860607962d.sentence: Kelp forests occur worldwide throughout temperate and polar coastal oceans.

fabc9261e643.title: Kelp forest
fabc9261e643.sentence: In 2007, kelp forests were also discovered in tropical waters near Ecuador.

aa88aa924d1d.title: Kelp forest
aa88aa924d1d.sentence: Frequently considered an ecosystem engineer, kelp provides a physical substrate and habitat for kelp forest communities.

dca04aec1abe.title: Kelp forest
dca04aec1abe.sentence: A wide range of sea life uses kelp forests for protection or food, including fish.

3c4adf344117.title: Kelp forest
3c4adf344117.sentence: Many marine mammals and birds are also found, including seals, sea lions, whales, sea otters, gulls, terns, snowy egrets, great blue herons, and cormorants, as well as some shore birds.

bcceb4442d58.title: Kelp forest
bcceb4442d58.sentence: For example, kelp forests can influence coastal oceanographic patterns and provide many ecosystem services.

e6ce009a02db.title: Kelp forest
e6ce009a02db.sentence: Already due to the combined effects of overfishing and climate change, kelp forests have all but disappeared in many especially vulnerable places, such as Tasmania's east coast and the coast of Northern California.

64f51a3bcddd.title: Seagrass meadow
64f51a3bcddd.sentence: A seagrass meadow or seagrass bed is an underwater ecosystem formed by seagrasses.

e615ef426e99.title: Seagrass meadow
e615ef426e99.sentence: Seagrasses are marine (saltwater) plants found in shallow coastal waters and in the brackish waters of estuaries.

6a940fdcb9eb.title: Seagrass meadow
6a940fdcb9eb.sentence: Seagrasses are flowering plants with stems and long green, grass-like leaves.

757d4dbcd640.title: Seagrass meadow
757d4dbcd640.sentence: Seagrasses form dense underwater meadows which are among the most productive ecosystems in the world.

4500532461ee.title: Seagrass meadow
4500532461ee.sentence: They provide habitats and food for a diversity of marine life comparable to that of coral reefs.

d1a46575a87d.title: Seagrass meadow
d1a46575a87d.sentence: They evolved from terrestrial plants which migrated back into the ocean about 75 to 100 million years ago.

5d9aeac00e22.title: Seagrass meadow
5d9aeac00e22.sentence: Seagrass meadows are found in the shallow seas of the continental shelves of all continents except Antarctica.

8f8c15c67e56.title: Seagrass meadow
8f8c15c67e56.sentence: Seagrasses can survive to maximum depths of about 60 metres.

30b7405aeab5.title: Seagrass meadow
30b7405aeab5.sentence: They prefer sheltered places, such as shallow bays, lagoons, and estuaries (sheltered areas where rivers flow in to the sea), where waves are limited and light and nutrient levels are high.

72ba8d839855.title: Seagrass meadow
72ba8d839855.sentence: They provide refuges for endangered species such as seahorses, turtles, and dugongs.

09e5c7a3f246.title: Seagrass meadow
09e5c7a3f246.sentence: They function as nursery habitats for shrimps, scallops and many commercial fish species.

691da0b312e9.title: Seagrass meadow
691da0b312e9.sentence: However, today seagrass meadows are being damaged by human activities such as pollution from land runoff, fishing boats that drag dredges or trawls across the meadows uprooting the grass, and overfishing which unbalances the ecosystem.

82ead4dddd05.title: Seagrass meadow
82ead4dddd05.sentence: Seagrass meadows are currently being destroyed at a rate of about 3 square metres per second (1,900 sq ft/min).

28d58587245e.title: Coral reef
28d58587245e.sentence: Coral reefs protect shorelines by absorbing wave energy, and many small islands would not exist without reefs.

5c22bc20450d.title: Coral reef
5c22bc20450d.sentence: Coral reefs can reduce wave energy by 97%, helping to prevent loss of life and property damage.

ddf2d1219a7a.title: Coral reef
ddf2d1219a7a.sentence: Reefs can attenuate waves as well as, or better than, artificial structures designed for coastal defence, such as breakwaters.

c9ae22f8681b.title: Coral reef
c9ae22f8681b.sentence: Restoring reefs is significantly cheaper than building artificial breakwaters in tropical environments.

ab674b713e1e.title: Coral reef
ab674b713e1e.sentence: An estimated 197 million people who live both below 10 m elevation and within 50 km of a reef consequently may receive risk reduction benefits from reefs.

ee120e031da2.title: Coral reef
ee120e031da2.sentence: Expected damages from flooding would double, and costs from frequent storms would triple without the topmost meter of reefs.

484b9b9c18a1.title: Coral reef
484b9b9c18a1.sentence: For 100-year storm events, flood damages would increase by 91% to $US 272 billion without the top meter.

d8d3e034c074.title: Coral reef
d8d3e034c074.sentence: They are under threat from excess nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus), rising ocean heat content and acidification, overfishing (e.g., from blast fishing, cyanide fishing, spearfishing on scuba), sunscreen use, and harmful land-use practices, including runoff and seeps (e.g., from injection wells and cesspools).

c3a6130d30f8.title: Coral reef
c3a6130d30f8.sentence: From 2009 to 2018, coral reefs worldwide declined 14%.

43fe687239a7.title: Coral reef
43fe687239a7.sentence: Human activities that threaten coral include coral mining, bottom trawling, and the digging of canals and accesses into islands and bays, all of which can damage marine ecosystems if not done sustainably.

1704196b7424.title: Coral reef
1704196b7424.sentence: Other localized threats include blast fishing, overfishing, coral overmining, and marine pollution, including use of the banned anti-fouling biocide tributyltin; although absent in developed countries, these activities continue in places with few environmental protections or poor regulatory enforcement.

ef336643bf10.title: Coral reef
ef336643bf10.sentence: Greenhouse gas emissions present a broader threat through sea temperature rise and sea level rise, resulting in widespread coral bleaching and loss of coral cover.

2e3568c0c468.title: Coral reef
2e3568c0c468.sentence: Ocean acidification also affects corals by decreasing calcification rates and increasing dissolution rates, although corals can adapt their calcifying fluids to changes in seawater pH and carbonate levels to mitigate the impact.

1531e48ba60d.title: Coral reef
1531e48ba60d.sentence: Overfishing and excess nutrient supply from onshore can enable algae to outcompete and kill the coral.

3627fd7f1efe.title: Biodiversity loss
3627fd7f1efe.sentence: But 70–90% of today's warm-water coral reefs will disappear even if warming is kept to 1.5 °C (2.7 °F).

710e5741789c.title: Coral reef
710e5741789c.sentence: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are areas designated because they provide various kinds of protection to ocean and/or estuarine areas.

1044e6be9d96.title: Coral reef
1044e6be9d96.sentence: They are intended to promote responsible fishery management and habitat protection.

8cab7c34b5f1.title: Coral reef
8cab7c34b5f1.sentence: MPAs can also encompass social and biological objectives, including reef restoration, aesthetics, biodiversity, and economic benefits.

484d5aad3539.title: Coral reef
484d5aad3539.sentence: The effectiveness of MPAs is still debated.

1ae66dcedf8c.title: Coral reef
1ae66dcedf8c.sentence: For example, a study investigating the success of a small number of MPAs in Indonesia, the Philippines, and Papua New Guinea found no significant differences between the MPAs and unprotected sites.

78462e94e058.title: Coral reef
78462e94e058.sentence: Furthermore, in some cases they can generate local conflict, due to a lack of community participation, clashing views of the government and fisheries, effectiveness of the area and funding.

fb39d8dce9c0.title: Coral reef
fb39d8dce9c0.sentence: In some situations, as in the Phoenix Islands Protected Area, MPAs provide revenue to locals.

7c98ac42565a.title: Coral reef
7c98ac42565a.sentence: The level of income provided is similar to the income they would have generated without controls.

22069af229ab.title: Coral reef
22069af229ab.sentence: Overall, it appears the MPAs can protect local coral reefs, but that clear management and sufficient funds are required.

4053220ba9f1.title: Coral reef
4053220ba9f1.sentence: The report shows that healthier Caribbean reefs are those with large, healthy populations of parrotfish.

6ba901971c23.title: Coral reef
6ba901971c23.sentence: These occur in countries that protect parrotfish and other species, like sea urchins.

d466a2f29bab.title: Coral reef
d466a2f29bab.sentence: They also often ban fish trapping and spearfishing.

f9a6ab50f4f1.title: Coral reef
f9a6ab50f4f1.sentence: Protecting networks of diverse and healthy reefs, not only climate refugia, helps ensure the greatest chance of genetic diversity, which is critical for coral to adapt to new climates.

2af1cecc2958.title: Salt marsh
2af1cecc2958.sentence: In the past, salt marshes were perceived as coastal 'wastelands,' causing considerable loss and change of these ecosystems through land reclamation for agriculture, urban development, salt production and recreation.

b62364187010.title: Salt marsh
b62364187010.sentence: As of 2002, over half of the world's population was estimated to being living within 60 km of the coastal shoreline, making coastlines highly vulnerable to human impacts from daily activities that put pressure on these surrounding natural environments.

a6b77c3021bd.title: Salt marsh
a6b77c3021bd.sentence: A study published in 2022 estimates that 22% of saltmarsh loss from 1999 to 2019 was due to direct human drivers, defined as observable activities occurring at the location of the detected change, such as conversion to aquaculture, agriculture, coastal development, or other physical structures.

18f4b4474108.title: Salt marsh
18f4b4474108.sentence: Additionally, 30% of saltmarsh gain over this same time period were also due to direct drivers, such as restoration activities or coastal modifications to promote tidal exchange.

06f545517fd5.title: Salt marsh
06f545517fd5.section: Human impacts > Urban development and nitrogen loading
06f545517fd5.sentence: Urban development of salt marshes has slowed since about 1970 owing to growing awareness by environmental groups that they provide beneficial ecosystem services.

b8b675558cfd.title: Salt marsh
b8b675558cfd.sentence: Additionally, sea level rise caused by climate change is endangering other marshes, through erosion and submersion of otherwise tidal marshes.

f0bbc0dab5f8.title: Salt marsh
f0bbc0dab5f8.sentence: As with all coastlines, this rise in water levels is predicted to negatively affect salt marshes, by flooding and eroding them.

3a9286682646.title: Salt marsh
3a9286682646.sentence: While salt marshes are susceptible to threats concerning sea level rise, they are also an extremely dynamic coastal ecosystem.

721d984626f6.title: Salt marsh
721d984626f6.sentence: The sea level rise causes more open water zones within the salt marsh.

40455350fa02.title: Salt marsh
40455350fa02.sentence: These zones cause erosion along their edges, further eroding the marsh into open water until the whole marsh disintegrates.

f46f247f4925.title: Salt marsh
f46f247f4925.sentence: Salt marsh vegetation helps to increase sediment settling because it slows current velocities, disrupts turbulent eddies, and helps to dissipate wave energy.

d28cf55c4983.title: Salt marsh
d28cf55c4983.sentence: Salt marsh vegetation captures sediment to stay in the system which in turn allows for the plants to grow better and thus the plants are better at trapping sediment and accumulate more organic matter.

69a882493e17.title: Salt marsh
69a882493e17.sentence: This positive feedback loop potentially allows for salt marsh bed level rates to keep pace with rising sea level rates.

f58737bee1b7.title: Salt marsh
f58737bee1b7.sentence: The salt marsh's resilience depends upon its increase in bed level rate being greater than that of sea levels' increasing rate, otherwise the marsh will be overtaken and drowned.

c4b19945ffc5.title: Salt marsh
c4b19945ffc5.sentence: Salt marshes may in fact have the capability to keep pace with a rising sea level, by 2100, mean sea level could see increases between 0.6m to 1.1m.

7118170b344f.title: Salt marsh
7118170b344f.sentence: Accommodation space is the land available for additional sediments to accumulate and marsh vegetation to colonize laterally.

7abc7d8ce302.title: Salt marsh
7abc7d8ce302.sentence: This lateral accommodation space is often limited by anthropogenic structures such as coastal roads, sea walls and other forms of development of coastal lands.

b217d43aab5f.title: Kelp forest
b217d43aab5f.sentence: All of these are examples of ecosystem services provided specifically by kelp forests.

9d3abc9d242f.title: Kelp forest
9d3abc9d242f.sentence: Kelp forests have been important to human existence for thousands of years.

7f46349bcfee.title: Kelp forest
7f46349bcfee.sentence: Modern economies are based on fisheries of kelp-associated species such as lobster and rockfish.

1201cd4cee31.title: Kelp forest
1201cd4cee31.sentence: Humans can also harvest kelp directly to feed aquaculture species such as abalone and to extract the compound alginic acid, which is used in products like toothpaste and antacids.

f84239dad3ad.title: Kelp forest
f84239dad3ad.sentence: Kelp forests are valued for recreational activities such as SCUBA diving and kayaking; the industries that support these sports represent one benefit related to the ecosystem and the enjoyment derived from these activities represents another.

6302e2435cc9.title: Kelp forest
6302e2435cc9.sentence: Indeed, many now theorise that the first colonisation of the Americas was due to fishing communities following the Pacific kelp forests during the last ice age.

b302471d8ff7.title: Kelp forest
b302471d8ff7.sentence: Besides these benefits, researchers believe that the kelp forests might have helped early boaters navigate, acting as a type of "kelp highway".

a66d54ff33d1.title: Kelp forest
a66d54ff33d1.sentence: In a well-studied example from Alaskan kelp forests, sea otters (Enhydra lutris) control populations of herbivorous sea urchins through predation.

9bdbbe72def2.title: Kelp forest
9bdbbe72def2.sentence: When sea otters are removed from the ecosystem (for example, by human exploitation), urchin populations are released from predatory control and grow dramatically.

1a9d7b51c59f.title: Kelp forest
1a9d7b51c59f.sentence: This leads to increased herbivore pressure on local kelp stands.

52d9c666983b.title: Kelp forest
52d9c666983b.sentence: In Alaskan kelp forest ecosystems, sea otters are the keystone species that mediates this trophic cascade.

4ce8d43556be.title: Kelp forest
4ce8d43556be.sentence: Deterioration of the kelp itself results in the loss of physical ecosystem structure and subsequently, the loss of other species associated with this habitat.

59d56d413add.title: Kelp forest
59d56d413add.sentence: In Southern California, kelp forests persist without sea otters and the control of herbivorous urchins is instead mediated by a suite of predators including lobsters and large fishes, such as the California sheephead.

6f6700e3bf54.title: Kelp forest
6f6700e3bf54.sentence: The effect of removing one predatory species in this system differs from Alaska because redundancy exists in the trophic levels and other predatory species can continue to regulate urchins.

3f17fcd39912.title: Kelp forest
3f17fcd39912.sentence: The transition from macroalgal (i.e. kelp forest) to denuded landscapes dominated by sea urchins (or 'urchin barrens') is a widespread phenomenon, often resulting from trophic cascades like those described above; the two phases are regarded as alternative stable states of the ecosystem.

f353ee3e48c7.title: Kelp forest
f353ee3e48c7.sentence: The recovery of kelp forests from barren states has been documented following dramatic perturbations, such as urchin disease or large shifts in thermal conditions.

adf23e0db1a3.title: Kelp forest
adf23e0db1a3.sentence: Bottom-up processes are generally driven by the abiotic conditions required for primary producers to grow, such as availability of light and nutrients, and the subsequent transfer of energy to consumers at higher trophic levels.

e36f74321057.title: Kelp forest
e36f74321057.sentence: For example, the occurrence of kelp is frequently correlated with oceanographic upwelling zones, which provide unusually high concentrations of nutrients to the local environment.

b4bbbd179ab8.title: Kelp forest
b4bbbd179ab8.sentence: This allows kelp to grow and subsequently support herbivores, which in turn support consumers at higher trophic levels.

87db63f7d026.title: Kelp forest
87db63f7d026.sentence: Major issues of concern include marine pollution and water quality, kelp harvesting and fisheries, invasive species, and climate change.

a1926070bb9b.title: Kelp forest
a1926070bb9b.sentence: The most pressing threat to kelp forest preservation may be the overfishing of coastal ecosystems, which by removing higher trophic levels facilitates their shift to depauperate urchin barrens.

7a22ca9d0451.title: Kelp forest
7a22ca9d0451.sentence: More recently, the 2022 IPCC report states that kelp and other seaweeds in most regions are undergoing mass mortalities from high temperature extremes and range shifts from warming, as they are stationary and cannot adapt quick enough to deal with the rapidly increasing temperature of the Earth and thus, the ocean.

c75e57c2e1c9.title: Kelp forest
c75e57c2e1c9.section: Threats and management > Kelp forest restoration in California
c75e57c2e1c9.sentence: In the 2010s, Northern California lost 95% of its kelp ecosystems due to marine heatwaves.

558144b8aef6.title: Kelp forest
558144b8aef6.sentence: - Acute and chronic pollution events have been shown to impact southern California kelp forests, though the intensity of the impact seems to depend on both the nature of the contaminants and duration of exposure.

c041a673fd87.title: Kelp forest
c041a673fd87.sentence: Pollution can include sediment deposition and eutrophication from sewage, industrial byproducts and contaminants like PCBs and heavy metals (for example, copper, zinc), runoff of organophosphates from agricultural areas, anti-fouling chemicals used in harbors and marinas (for example, TBT and creosote) and land-based pathogens like fecal coliform bacteria.

41b8aa611499.title: Kelp forest

03b37c7c976f.title: Seagrass meadow

668dcf210e3b.title: Seagrass meadow

6582f0ef5a50.title: Seagrass meadow

5c9a6c7251f2.title: Seagrass meadow

fde170c6af79.title: Seagrass meadow

384366e35e4b.title: Seagrass meadow

414b9f29507b.title: Seagrass meadow

8d678c147f39.title: Seagrass meadow

66e800a92af3.title: Seagrass meadow

f6bc8ff93ef1.title: Seagrass meadow

ed0f6905bcd9.title: Seagrass meadow

0a57eff0565e.title: Seagrass meadow

a76066bc5c6b.title: Seagrass meadow

e87f6aae31e2.title: Seagrass meadow

e9ced2cd2819.title: Seagrass meadow

6137123dc6a3.title: Seagrass meadow

06abeb50c2ef.title: Seagrass meadow

e8cabe1b8ed1.title: Seagrass meadow

db6d891f0525.title: Seagrass meadow

742c1825af7a.title: Seagrass meadow

b792379f2dd2.title: Coral reef

243e627cec03.title: Coral reef

f74a92f46eb9.title: Coral reef

38e2010aaa66.title: Coral reef

7fadeddb18ca.title: Coral reef
7fadeddb18ca.sentence: Barrier reefs are separated from a mainland or island shore by a deep channel or lagoon.

1653e210b076.title: Coral reef
1653e210b076.sentence: Atolls or atoll reefs are a more or less circular or continuous barrier reef that extends all the way around a lagoon without a central island.

5da18ee84699.title: Coral reef

8249ceca3f91.title: Coral reef
8249ceca3f91.sentence: Platform reefs, variously called bank or table reefs, can form on the continental shelf, as well as in the open ocean, in fact anywhere where the seabed rises close enough to the surface of the ocean to enable the growth of zooxanthemic, reef-forming corals.

34a56d331ebb.title: Riparian zone

44282f913b00.title: Riparian zone

516c93da7ab0.title: Riparian zone

4153f89a4216.title: Floodplain

5c0cb301a74f.title: Floodplain

d704fdc32b46.title: Floodplain

1d0c2956fefc.sentence: Mid-latitude grasslands, including the prairie and Pacific grasslands of North America, the Pampas of Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay, calcareous downland, and the steppes of Europe.

9c5ead9d92b3.title: Grassland
9c5ead9d92b3.section: Types of grasslands > General grasslands types > Flooded
9c5ead9d92b3.sentence: Grasslands that are flooded seasonally or year-round, like the Everglades of Florida, the Pantanal of Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay or the Esteros del Ibera in Argentina, are classified with flooded savannas as the flooded grasslands and savannas biome and occur mostly in the tropics and subtropics.

fd168ab2bc8f.title: Grassland
fd168ab2bc8f.section: Types of grasslands > General grasslands types > Tropical and subtropical
fd168ab2bc8f.sentence: The rainfall level for that grassland type is between 90 and 150 centimeters per year.

20cfe140d30b.title: Grassland
20cfe140d30b.section: Types of grasslands > General grasslands types > Tropical and subtropical
20cfe140d30b.sentence: Grasses and scattered trees are common for that ecoregion, as well as large mammals, such as wildebeest (Connochaetes taurinus) and zebra (Equus zebra).

c62d013fe66a.title: Grassland
c62d013fe66a.section: Types of grasslands > General grasslands types > Temperate
c62d013fe66a.sentence: Temperate grasslands are the home to many large herbivores, such as bison, gazelles, zebras, rhinoceroses, and wild horses.

d2463254772e.title: Grassland
d2463254772e.section: Types of grasslands > General grasslands types > Tundra grasslands
d2463254772e.sentence: However, during the Pleistocene glacial periods (commonly referred to as ice ages), a grassland known as steppe-tundra or mammoth steppe occupied large areas of the Northern Hemisphere.

1a01c666e490.title: Riparian zone
1a01c666e490.sentence: Pollutants are filtered from surface runoff, enhancing water quality via biofiltration.

679b81c656bd.title: Riparian zone
679b81c656bd.sentence: From a social aspect, riparian zones contribute to nearby property values through amenity and views, and they improve enjoyment for footpaths and bikeways through supporting foreshoreway networks.

a1d19dbbc9e7.title: Riparian zone
a1d19dbbc9e7.sentence: The meandering curves of a river, combined with vegetation and root systems, slow the flow of water, which reduces soil erosion and flood damage.

578fc59fb879.title: Riparian zone
578fc59fb879.sentence: Sediment is trapped, reducing suspended solids to create less turbid water, replenish soils, and build stream banks.

97027069f7b9.title: Riparian zone
97027069f7b9.sentence: The riparian zones also provide wildlife habitat, increased biodiversity, and wildlife corridors, enabling aquatic and riparian organisms to move along river systems avoiding isolated communities.

623066b71a63.title: Riparian zone
623066b71a63.sentence: Thinning of riparian zones has been observed to cause increased maximum temperatures, higher fluctuations in temperature, and elevated temperatures being observed more frequently and for longer periods of time.

99c43da8c011.title: Riparian zone
99c43da8c011.sentence: Extreme changes in water temperature can have lethal effects on fish and other organisms in the area.

528a9e78aa4e.title: Riparian zone
528a9e78aa4e.sentence: Space is created for riparian sports such as fishing, swimming, and launching for vessels and paddle craft.

1c2ce409d273.title: Riparian zone
1c2ce409d273.sentence: The protection of riparian zones is often a consideration in logging operations.

3fb41685d2c8.title: Riparian zone
3fb41685d2c8.sentence: The undisturbed soil, soil cover, and vegetation provide shade, plant litter, and woody material and reduce the delivery of soil eroded from the harvested area.

fbd04a9f73bc.title: Riparian zone
fbd04a9f73bc.sentence: Factors such as soil types and root structures, climatic conditions, and vegetative cover determine the effectiveness of riparian buffering.

48cbe111020f.title: Riparian zone
48cbe111020f.sentence: Activities associated with logging, such as sediment input, introduction or removal of species, and the input of polluted water all degrade riparian zones.

46ce011400df.title: Riparian zone
46ce011400df.sentence: Riparian zones can be restored through relocation (of human-made products), rehabilitation, and time.

0b72791ee504.title: Riparian zone
0b72791ee504.sentence: Land clearing followed by floods can quickly erode a riverbank, taking valuable grasses and soils downstream, and later allowing the sun to bake the land dry.

afac52d0db38.title: Riparian zone
afac52d0db38.sentence: When riparian zones are damaged by construction, agriculture or silviculture, biological restoration can take place, usually by human intervention in erosion control and revegetation.

dc1113f6cbba.title: Riparian zone
dc1113f6cbba.sentence: There are several other techniques used by government and non-government agencies to address riparian and streambed degradation, ranging from the installation of bed control structures such as log sills to the use of pin groynes or rock emplacement.

6ceb83d59ff9.title: Riparian zone
6ceb83d59ff9.sentence: Other possible approaches include control of invasive species, monitoring of herbivore activity, and cessation of human activity in a particular zone followed by natural re-vegetation.

1b45e86aa914.title: Riparian zone
1b45e86aa914.sentence: Another technique is to quickly establish ecological succession by encouraging fast-growing plants such as "weeds" (pioneer species) to grow.

ce54c40655eb.title: Riparian zone
ce54c40655eb.sentence: These may spread along the watercourse and cause environmental degradation, but may stabilize the soil, place carbon into the ground, and protect the land from drying.

315180448ae3.title: Riparian zone
315180448ae3.sentence: The weeds will improve the streambeds so trees and grasses can return and, ideally, replace the weeds.

c00017445bea.title: Riparian zone
c00017445bea.sentence: Conservation efforts have also encouraged incorporating the value of ecosystem services provided by riparian zones into management plans, as these benefits have traditionally been absent in the consideration and designing of these plans.

f6ad370bfa2d.title: Tropical rainforest
f6ad370bfa2d.sentence: Rainforests are divided into different strata, or layers, with vegetation organized into a vertical pattern from the top of the soil to the canopy.

fa9cd55cfc08.title: Tropical rainforest
fa9cd55cfc08.sentence: Each layer is a unique biotic community containing different plants and animals adapted for life in that particular strata.

40e191bef9fd.title: Tropical rainforest
40e191bef9fd.sentence: The forest floor, the bottom-most layer, receives only 2% of the sunlight.

3e6f41622b39.title: Tropical rainforest
3e6f41622b39.sentence: Only plants adapted to low light can grow in this region.

a54e2829e855.title: Tropical rainforest
a54e2829e855.sentence: The canopy is the primary layer of the forest, forming a roof over the two remaining layers.

3b57b1c930be.title: Tropical rainforest
3b57b1c930be.sentence: It contains the majority of the largest trees, typically 30–45 m in height.

d11d10f409e0.title: Tropical rainforest
d11d10f409e0.sentence: The emergent layer contains a small number of very large trees, called emergents, which grow above the general canopy, reaching heights of 45–55 m, although on occasion a few species will grow to 70–80 m tall.

92c170bd01eb.title: Tropical rainforest
92c170bd01eb.sentence: Only the emergent layer is unique to tropical rainforests, while the others are also found in temperate rainforests.

9a5ebd27f8e4.title: Floodplain
9a5ebd27f8e4.sentence: The US government also sponsors flood hazard mitigation efforts to reduce flood impacts.

72b2c316e8f9.title: Floodplain
72b2c316e8f9.sentence: Excluding famines and epidemics, some of the worst natural disasters in history (measured by fatalities) have been river floods, particularly in the Yellow River in China – see list of deadliest floods.

4ecbf391f56c.title: Floodplain
4ecbf391f56c.sentence: The worst of these, and the worst natural disaster (excluding famine and epidemics), was the 1931 China floods, estimated to have killed millions.

d9bad1499a9a.title: Floodplain
d9bad1499a9a.sentence: The extent of floodplain inundation depends partly on flood magnitude, defined by the return period.

9a798e62900c.title: Floodplain
9a798e62900c.sentence: Another commonly encountered term is the Special Flood Hazard Area, which is any area subject to inundation by a 100-year flood.

1ab8417705e1.title: Floodplain
1ab8417705e1.sentence: In the United States, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) manages the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP).

6542b5390eed.title: Floodplain
6542b5390eed.sentence: The NFIP offers insurance to properties located within a flood-prone area, as defined by the Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM), which depicts various flood risks for a community.

db2ef4bb5a7f.title: Floodplain
db2ef4bb5a7f.sentence: A large shopping center and parking lot, for example, may raise the levels of 5-year, 100-year, and other floods, but the maps are rarely adjusted and are frequently rendered obsolete by subsequent development.

daef03b083d8.title: Floodplain
daef03b083d8.sentence: A number of whole towns such as English, Indiana, have been completely relocated to remove them from the floodplain.

11b7a395a277.title: Floodplain
11b7a395a277.sentence: In some floodplains, such as the Inner Niger Delta of Mali, annual flooding events are a natural part of the local ecology and rural economy, allowing for the raising of crops through recessional agriculture.

f0780c7af86e.title: Floodplain
f0780c7af86e.sentence: Most floodplains are formed by deposition on the inside of river meanders and by overbank flow.

51f70d143a22.title: Floodplain
51f70d143a22.sentence: Wherever the river meanders, the flowing water erodes the river bank on the outside of the meander.

efc42465bf27.title: Floodplain
efc42465bf27.sentence: At the same time, sediments are simultaneously deposited in a bar on the inside of the meander.

02f8b4d6d3a6.title: Floodplain
02f8b4d6d3a6.sentence: The overall effect is that, as the river meanders, it creates a level floodplain composed mostly of point bar deposits.

39e885d62300.title: Floodplain
39e885d62300.sentence: Flow over the banks of the river deposits a thin veneer of sediments that is coarsest and thickest close to the channel.

0c6b2800e6dd.title: Floodplain
0c6b2800e6dd.sentence: Natural levees are ridges along river banks that form from rapid deposition from the overbank flow.

460a29d79356.title: Floodplain
460a29d79356.sentence: In undisturbed river systems, overbank flow is frequent, typically occurring every one to two years, regardless of climate or topography.

88c802fee58f.title: Floodplain
88c802fee58f.section: Floodplain soils > Phosphorus cycling in floodplain soils
88c802fee58f.sentence: Floodplains have high buffering capacity for phosphorus to prevent nutrient loss to river outputs.

8cb2a1d194d3.title: Floodplain
8cb2a1d194d3.section: Floodplain soils > Phosphorus cycling in floodplain soils
8cb2a1d194d3.sentence: Phosphorus nutrient loading is a problem in freshwater systems.

23eb36191761.title: Floodplain
23eb36191761.section: Floodplain soils > Phosphorus cycling in floodplain soils
23eb36191761.sentence: Much of the phosphorus in freshwater systems comes from municipal wastewater treatment plants and agricultural runoff.

7116b661ce3a.title: Floodplain
7116b661ce3a.section: Floodplain soils > Phosphorus cycling in floodplain soils
7116b661ce3a.sentence: In either phosphorus form, floodplain forests are beneficial as phosphorus sinks, and the human-caused disconnect between floodplains and rivers exacerbates the phosphorus overload.

9bbc51deecd9.title: Salt marsh
9bbc51deecd9.sentence: Earlier in the 20th century, it was believed that draining salt marshes would help reduce mosquito populations, such as Aedes taeniorhynchus, the black salt marsh mosquito.

f617add0f71e.title: Salt marsh
f617add0f71e.sentence: In many locations, particularly in the northeastern United States, residents and local and state agencies dug straight-lined ditches deep into the marsh flats.

2060e535b69d.title: Salt marsh
2060e535b69d.sentence: The result, however, was a depletion of killifish habitat.

1aa910666dde.title: Salt marsh
1aa910666dde.sentence: The killifish is a mosquito predator, so the loss of habitat actually led to higher mosquito populations, and adversely affected wading birds that preyed on the killifish.

f22c88ce48f9.title: Salt marsh
f22c88ce48f9.sentence: These ditches can still be seen, despite some efforts to refill the ditches.

1fe795ee8e7c.title: Salt marsh
1fe795ee8e7c.section: Human impacts > Urban development and nitrogen loading
1fe795ee8e7c.sentence: Nitrogen loading through human-use indirectly affects salt marshes causing shifts in vegetation structure and the invasion of non-native species.

0907746361ba.title: Salt marsh
0907746361ba.section: Human impacts > Urban development and nitrogen loading
0907746361ba.sentence: Human impacts such as sewage, urban run-off, agricultural and industrial wastes are running into the marshes from nearby sources.

8ebcc3bbeff4.title: Salt marsh
8ebcc3bbeff4.section: Human impacts > Urban development and nitrogen loading
8ebcc3bbeff4.sentence: Salt marshes are nitrogen limited and with an increasing level of nutrients entering the system from anthropogenic effects, the plant species associated with salt marshes are being restructured through change in competition.

c69835a71dc2.title: Salt marsh
c69835a71dc2.section: Human impacts > Urban development and nitrogen loading
c69835a71dc2.sentence: Additionally, in the same marshes, the reed Phragmites australis has been invading the area expanding to lower marshes and becoming a dominant species.

282b5d456c0a.title: Salt marsh
282b5d456c0a.section: Human impacts > Urban development and nitrogen loading
282b5d456c0a.sentence: P. australis is an aggressive halophyte that can invade disturbed areas in large numbers outcompeting native plants.

bb1118133c38.title: Salt marsh
bb1118133c38.section: Human impacts > Urban development and nitrogen loading
bb1118133c38.sentence: This loss in biodiversity is not only seen in flora assemblages but also in many animals such as insects and birds as their habitat and food resources are altered.

36470e9a6279.title: Salt marsh
36470e9a6279.sentence: The formation begins as tidal flats gain elevation relative to sea level by sediment accretion, and subsequently the rate and duration of tidal flooding decreases so that vegetation can colonize on the exposed surface.

ba3f413fbd76.title: Salt marsh
ba3f413fbd76.sentence: When rivers and streams arrive at the low gradient of the tidal flats, the discharge rate reduces and suspended sediment settles onto the tidal flat surface, helped by the backwater effect of the rising tide.

5f01ae730968.title: Salt marsh
5f01ae730968.sentence: These species retain sediment washed in from the rising tide around their stems and leaves and form low muddy mounds which eventually coalesce to form depositional terraces, whose upward growth is aided by a sub-surface root network which binds the sediment.

836174b4e453.title: Salt marsh
836174b4e453.sentence: Once vegetation is established on depositional terraces further sediment trapping and accretion can allow rapid upward growth of the marsh surface such that there is an associated rapid decrease in the depth and duration of tidal flooding.

3625ea545cfd.title: Salt marsh
3625ea545cfd.sentence: As a result, competitive species that prefer higher elevations relative to sea level can inhabit the area and often a succession of plant communities develops.

16921c7aa5be.title: Salt marsh
16921c7aa5be.sentence: Reclamation of land for agriculture by converting marshland to upland was historically a common practice.

6357a26610ec.title: Salt marsh
6357a26610ec.sentence: Dikes were often built to allow for this shift in land change and to provide flood protection further inland.

7581d50ab547.title: Salt marsh
7581d50ab547.sentence: Land reclamation for agriculture has resulted in many changes such as shifts in vegetation structure, sedimentation, salinity, water flow, biodiversity loss and high nutrient inputs.

ee72301deba8.title: Salt marsh
ee72301deba8.sentence: In the Blyth estuary in Suffolk in eastern England, the mid-estuary reclamations (Angel and Bulcamp marshes) that were abandoned in the 1940s have been replaced by tidal flats with compacted soils from agricultural use overlain with a thin veneer of mud.

9026bdadf5cf.title: Salt marsh
9026bdadf5cf.sentence: Little vegetation colonisation has occurred in the last 60–75 years and has been attributed to a combination of surface elevations too low for pioneer species to develop, and poor drainage from the compacted agricultural soils acting as an aquiclude.

8aab77da3022.title: Salt marsh
8aab77da3022.sentence: However, recent acknowledgment by both environmentalists and larger society for the importance of saltwater marshes for biodiversity, ecological productivity and other ecosystem services, such as carbon sequestration, have led to an increase in salt marsh restoration and management since the 1980s.

444c4a34a9c8.title: Salt marsh
444c4a34a9c8.sentence: With the impacts of this habitats and their importance now realised, a growing interest in restoring salt marshes through managed retreat or the reclamation of land has been established.

267f7d6af985.title: Salt marsh
267f7d6af985.sentence: The perception of bay salt marshes as a coastal 'wasteland' has since changed, acknowledging that they are one of the most biologically productive habitats on earth, rivalling tropical rainforests.

6a15020f39aa.title: Salt marsh
6a15020f39aa.sentence: They are now protected by legislation in many countries to prevent the loss of these ecologically important habitats.

255dd90d0203.title: Salt marsh
255dd90d0203.sentence: In the United States and Europe, they are now accorded a high level of protection by the Clean Water Act and the Habitats Directive respectively.

5d4fadb4ca70.title: Salt marsh
5d4fadb4ca70.sentence: The first is to abandon all human interference and leave the salt marsh to complete its natural development.

a15c9bcd70af.title: Salt marsh
a15c9bcd70af.sentence: The second option suggested by Bakker et al. (1997) is to restore the destroyed habitat into its natural state either at the original site or as a replacement at a different site.

417ec01b5ee9.title: Salt marsh
417ec01b5ee9.sentence: Under natural conditions, recovery can take 2–10 years or even longer depending on the nature and degree of the disturbance and the relative maturity of the marsh involved.

3c04a3373a5e.title: Salt marsh
3c04a3373a5e.sentence: Restoration can often be sped up through the replanting of native vegetation.

5e35450ae03c.title: Salt marsh
5e35450ae03c.sentence: This last approach is often the most practiced and generally more successful than allowing the area to naturally recover on its own.

284b73605c0c.title: Salt marsh
284b73605c0c.sentence: This example highlights that considerable time and effort is needed to effectively restore salt marsh systems.

340a6e1c9c12.title: Salt marsh
340a6e1c9c12.sentence: There are many setbacks and problems associated with marsh restoration that require careful long-term monitoring.

8cf0b1048b09.title: Salt marsh
8cf0b1048b09.sentence: However, many Asian countries such as China still need to recognise the value of marshlands.

da18b33c7378.title: Salt marsh
da18b33c7378.sentence: With their ever-growing populations and intense development along the coast, the value of salt marshes tends to be ignored and the land continues to be reclaimed.

99efd17c9140.title: Salt marsh
99efd17c9140.sentence: In salt marshes, microbes play the main role in nutrient cycling and biogeochemical processing.

3163105ba04a.title: Salt marsh
3163105ba04a.sentence: The variable salinity, climate, nutrient levels and anaerobic conditions of salt marshes provide strong selective pressures on the microorganisms inhabiting them.

4b481852c5d5.title: Salt marsh
4b481852c5d5.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Chemo(litho)autotrophs in salt marshes > Why are sulfate-reducing bacteria in salt marshes?
4b481852c5d5.sentence: Salt marshes are the ideal environment for sulfate-reducing bacteria.

875ef8856233.title: Salt marsh
875ef8856233.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Chemo(litho)autotrophs in salt marshes > Abundance and diversity of sulfate-reducing chemolithoautotrophs
875ef8856233.sentence: In these ecosystems, up to 50% of sedimentary remineralization can be attributed to sulfate reduction.

b70b66227883.title: Salt marsh
b70b66227883.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Chemo(litho)autotrophs in salt marshes > Significance of sulfate-reducing bacteria
b70b66227883.sentence: Sulfate-reducing bacteria play a significant role in nutrient recycling and in reducing nitrate pollution levels.

70aef4b840a1.title: Salt marsh
70aef4b840a1.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Photoautotrophic bacteria > Cyanobacteria in salt marshes
70aef4b840a1.sentence: Cyanobacteria are important nitrogen fixers in salt marshes, and provide nitrogen to organisms like diatoms and microalgae.

3bbc887a931a.title: Old-growth forest
3bbc887a931a.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
3bbc887a931a.sentence: From a forest dynamics perspective, old-growth forest is in a stage that follows an understory reinitiation stage.

7513a489e042.title: Old-growth forest
7513a489e042.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
7513a489e042.sentence: - Stand-replacing: Disturbance hits the forest and kills most of the living trees.

b8a5c6a376b6.title: Old-growth forest
b8a5c6a376b6.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
b8a5c6a376b6.sentence: - Stand-initiation: A population of new trees becomes established.

8a50e229172f.title: Old-growth forest
8a50e229172f.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
8a50e229172f.sentence: - Stem-exclusion: Trees grow higher and enlarge their canopy, thus competing for the light with neighbors; light competition mortality kills slow-growing trees and reduces forest density, which allows surviving trees to increase in size.

24c6fcaf1bd6.title: Old-growth forest
24c6fcaf1bd6.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
24c6fcaf1bd6.sentence: - Understory reinitiation: Trees die from low-level mortality, such as windthrow and diseases.

e4c828ed6e53.title: Old-growth forest
e4c828ed6e53.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
e4c828ed6e53.sentence: Eventually, the canopies of neighboring trees touch each other and drastically lower the amount of light that reaches lower layers.

69a83d2247c9.title: Old-growth forest
69a83d2247c9.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
69a83d2247c9.sentence: Due to that, the understory dies and only very shade-tolerant species survive.

30cbcdd8b1c1.title: Old-growth forest
30cbcdd8b1c1.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
30cbcdd8b1c1.sentence: Individual canopy gaps start to appear and more light can reach the forest floor.

2d4e134e60db.title: Old-growth forest
2d4e134e60db.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
2d4e134e60db.sentence: Hence, shade-tolerant species can establish in the understory.

71074ec6ae6b.title: Old-growth forest
71074ec6ae6b.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
71074ec6ae6b.sentence: - Old-growth: Main canopy trees become older and more of them die, creating even more gaps.

38b3425a04da.title: Old-growth forest
38b3425a04da.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
38b3425a04da.sentence: Since the gaps appear at different times, the understory trees are at different growth stages.

1eba41c1b95c.title: Old-growth forest
1eba41c1b95c.section: Definitions > Ecological definitions > Forest dynamics definition
1eba41c1b95c.sentence: Thus, each understory tree grows at a different rate.

9a5cc5492a92.title: Old-growth forest
9a5cc5492a92.sentence: A climax stand that is uniformly aged becomes senescent and degrades within a relatively short time to result in a new cycle of forest succession.

427b8f53388f.title: Old-growth forest
427b8f53388f.sentence: Thus, uniformly aged stands are less stable ecosystems.

d6e723b1b400.title: Old-growth forest
d6e723b1b400.sentence: In logging terms, old-growth stands are past the economic optimum for harvesting—usually between 80 and 150 years, depending on the species.

3707bd7f4827.title: Old-growth forest
3707bd7f4827.sentence: Old-growth forests were often given harvesting priority because they had the most commercially valuable timber, they were considered to be at greater risk of deterioration through root rot or insect infestation, and they occupied land that could be used for more productive second-growth stands.

e530dda08a0b.title: Old-growth forest
e530dda08a0b.sentence: The large trees in old-growth forests are economically valuable and have been subject to aggressive logging throughout the world.

08febd10979e.title: Old-growth forest
08febd10979e.sentence: This has led to many conflicts between logging companies and environmental groups.

cd4055d204bc.title: Old-growth forest
cd4055d204bc.sentence: In some regions, old growth is not the most commercially viable timber—in British Columbia, Canada, harvesting in the coastal region is moving to younger second-growth stands.

cd4b1fa658b0.title: Taiga
cd4b1fa658b0.sentence: Fire has been one of the most important factors shaping the composition and development of boreal forest stands; it is the dominant stand-renewing disturbance through much of the Canadian boreal forest.

669bc9e556b1.title: Taiga
669bc9e556b1.sentence: The fire history that characterizes an ecosystem is its fire regime, which has 3 elements: (1) fire type and intensity (e.g., crown fires, severe surface fires, and light surface fires), (2) size of typical fires of significance, and (3) frequency or return intervals for specific land units.

bbac9600f346.title: Taiga
bbac9600f346.sentence: The dominant fire regime in the boreal forest is high-intensity crown fires or severe surface fires of very large size, often more than 10,000 ha (100 km2), and sometimes more than 400,000 ha (4000 km2).

def1af46b910.title: Taiga
def1af46b910.sentence: The average time within a fire regime to burn an area equivalent to the total area of an ecosystem is its fire rotation (Heinselman 1973) or fire cycle (Van Wagner 1978).

744997db6aef.title: Taiga
744997db6aef.sentence: However, as Heinselman (1981) noted, each physiographic site tends to have its own return interval, so that some areas are skipped for long periods, while others might burn two-times or more often during a nominal fire rotation.

fd738e1d366f.title: Taiga
fd738e1d366f.sentence: The recurrent cycle of large, damaging fire occurs approximately every 70 to 100 years.

4df418a4d55f.title: Peatland
4df418a4d55f.sentence: A peatland that is still capable of forming new peat is called a mire, while drained and converted peatlands might still have a peat layer but are not considered mires as the formation of new peat has ceased.

42804e03be2c.title: Peatland
42804e03be2c.sentence: There are two types of mire: bog and fen.

adc5633f47ce.title: Peatland
adc5633f47ce.sentence: Botanists and ecologists use the word "peatland" as a general term for any terrain dominated by peat to a depth of at least 30 cm (12 in), even if it has been completely drained (i.e. a peatland can be dry).

99b7e1673aac.title: Peatland
99b7e1673aac.sentence: A bog is a mire that, due to its raised location relative to the surrounding landscape, obtains all its water solely from precipitation (ombrotrophic).

60be39fd40c1.title: Peatland
60be39fd40c1.sentence: A fen is located on a slope, flat, or in a depression and gets most of its water from the surrounding mineral soil or from groundwater (minerotrophic).

08426c5e5490.title: Peatland
08426c5e5490.sentence: Water passing through peat declines in nutrients and pH.

f665d18c6336.title: Peatland
f665d18c6336.sentence: Therefore, mires are typically nutrient-poor and acidic unless the inflow of groundwater (bringing in supplementary cations) is high.

ddf80c42c319.title: Peatland
ddf80c42c319.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry > Palm oil plantations
ddf80c42c319.sentence: Palm oil plantations have replaced much of the forested peatlands in Southeast Asia.

da68776f0790.title: Peatland
da68776f0790.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry > Palm oil plantations
da68776f0790.sentence: To create viable soil for plantation, the mires in tropical regions of Indonesia and Malaysia are drained and cleared.

1765c01026d9.title: Peatland
1765c01026d9.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry > Palm oil plantations
1765c01026d9.sentence: In comparison to alternatives, palm oil is considered to be among the most efficient sources of vegetable oil and biofuel, requiring only 0.26 hectares of land to produce 1 ton of oil.

0205af5e80a4.title: Peatland
0205af5e80a4.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry > Palm oil plantations
0205af5e80a4.sentence: With palm oil as a leading export in countries such as Indonesia and Malaysia, many smallholders have found economic success in palm oil plantations.

6b7cdb85a3f3.title: Peatland
6b7cdb85a3f3.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry > Palm oil plantations
6b7cdb85a3f3.sentence: Estimates now state that 12.9 Mha or about 47% of peatlands in Southeast Asia were deforested by 2006.

3ef01cc8c873.title: Peatland
3ef01cc8c873.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry > Palm oil plantations
3ef01cc8c873.sentence: Greenhouse gas emissions for palm oil planted on peatlands is estimated to be between the equivalent of 12.4 (best case) to 76.6 t CO2/ha (worst case).

feee8ed6ca5c.title: Peatland
feee8ed6ca5c.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry > Palm oil plantations
feee8ed6ca5c.sentence: Tropical peatland converted to palm oil plantation can remain a net source of carbon to the atmosphere after 12 years.

0a6c2b70f1c9.title: Peatland
0a6c2b70f1c9.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry > Palm oil plantations
0a6c2b70f1c9.sentence: Drainage of peatlands for palm oil plantations creates a dry layer of flammable peat.

04b0474f4dd0.title: Peatland
04b0474f4dd0.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry > Palm oil plantations
04b0474f4dd0.sentence: These fires add to greenhouse gas emissions while also causing thousands of deaths every year.

ac31f2c65432.title: Peatland
ac31f2c65432.section: Tropical peatlands > Greenhouse gases and fires
ac31f2c65432.sentence: Burning events in tropical peatlands are becoming more frequent due to large-scale drainage and land clearance and in the past ten years, more than 2 million hectares was burnt in Southeast Asia alone.

6553c5c35cf1.title: Peatland
6553c5c35cf1.section: Tropical peatlands > Greenhouse gases and fires
6553c5c35cf1.sentence: The tropical peatlands in Southeast Asia only cover 0.2% of Earth's land area but CO2 emissions are estimated to be 2 Gt per year, equal to 7% of global fossil fuel emissions.

48a9007582de.title: Peatland
48a9007582de.section: Tropical peatlands > Greenhouse gases and fires
48a9007582de.sentence: These emissions get bigger with drainage and burning of peatlands and a severe fire can release up to 4,000 t of CO2/ha.

14bfc98463b1.title: Peatland
14bfc98463b1.section: Tropical peatlands > Greenhouse gases and fires
14bfc98463b1.sentence: These fires last typically for 1–3 months and release large amounts of CO2.

f672e031d5d4.title: Wetland
f672e031d5d4.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
f672e031d5d4.sentence: Peat fires cause the same process to occur rapidly and in addition create enormous clouds of smoke that cross international borders, which now happens almost yearly in Southeast Asia.

6a86eafb63c7.title: Kelp forest
6a86eafb63c7.sentence: Kelp forests grow in rocky places along the shore that are constantly eroding carrying material out to the deep sea.

2774d1754e84.title: Kelp forest
2774d1754e84.sentence: The kelp then sinks to the ocean floor and store the carbon where is it unlikely to be disturbed by human activity.

e1e6a2017144.title: Kelp forest
e1e6a2017144.sentence: Every year 200 million tons of carbon dioxide are being sequestered by macroalgae such as kelp.

84561ae12475.title: Kelp forest
84561ae12475.sentence: Researchers from the University of Western Australia estimated kelp forest around Australia sequestered 1.3-2.8 teragrams of carbon per year which is 27–34% of the total annual blue carbon sequestered in the Australian continent by tidal marshes, mangrove forests and seagrass beds.

1ea7b76b5a9c.title: Kelp forest
1ea7b76b5a9c.sentence: The architecture of a kelp forest ecosystem is based on its physical structure, which influences the associated species that define its community structure.

6df11baba40f.title: Kelp forest
6df11baba40f.sentence: Structurally, the ecosystem includes three guilds of kelp and two guilds occupied by other algae:

bbf74616b156.title: Kelp forest
bbf74616b156.sentence: - Canopy kelps include the largest species and often constitute floating canopies that extend to the ocean surface (e.g., Macrocystis and Alaria).

303021e88810.title: Kelp forest
303021e88810.sentence: - Stipitate kelps generally extend a few meters above the sea floor and can grow in dense aggregations (e.g., Eisenia and Ecklonia).

f27709258174.title: Kelp forest
f27709258174.sentence: - Prostrate kelps lie near and along the sea floor (e.g., Laminaria).

87d813c20ff1.title: Kelp forest
87d813c20ff1.sentence: Multiple kelp species often co-exist within a forest; the term understory canopy refers to the stipitate and prostrate kelps.

c1b4832fede3.title: Kelp forest
c1b4832fede3.sentence: - The benthic assemblage is composed of other algal species (e.g., filamentous and foliose functional groups, articulated corallines) and sessile organisms along the ocean bottom.

770e4c8a0de6.title: Bog
770e4c8a0de6.sentence: After drying, peat is used as a fuel, and it has been used that way for centuries.

bd306e79210f.title: Bog
bd306e79210f.sentence: The other major use of dried peat is as a soil amendment (sold as moss peat or sphagnum peat) to increase the soil's capacity to retain moisture and enrich the soil.

383201259476.title: Bog
383201259476.sentence: More than 20% of home heat in Ireland comes from peat, and it is also used for fuel in Finland, Scotland, Germany, and Russia.

30d1ba94b3bd.title: Bog
30d1ba94b3bd.sentence: Russia is the leading exporter of peat for fuel, at more than 90 million metric tons per year.

fe80cf21106e.title: Bog
fe80cf21106e.sentence: Once the peat has been extracted it can be difficult to restore the wetland, since peat accumulation is a slow process.

ea9b17ce718f.title: Bog
ea9b17ce718f.sentence: More than 90% of the bogs in England have been damaged or destroyed.

efe9724774d1.title: Bog
efe9724774d1.sentence: In 2011 plans for the elimination of peat in gardening products were announced by the UK government.

593c7033d111.title: Bog
593c7033d111.sentence: Bogs are fragile ecosystems, and have been deteriorating quickly, as archaeologists and scientists have been recently finding.

5f5c7a375146.title: Bog
5f5c7a375146.sentence: Since bogs take thousands of years to form and create the rich peat that is used as a resource, once they are gone they are extremely hard to recover.

bbf00c7826de.title: Bog
bbf00c7826de.sentence: Sphagnum bogs were widespread in northern Europe but have often been cleared and drained for agriculture.

5bf6f1ddc484.title: Bog
5bf6f1ddc484.sentence: A paper led by Graeme T. Swindles in 2019 showed that peatlands across Europe have undergone rapid drying in recent centuries owing to human impacts including drainage, peat cutting and burning.

c637fd33f5e5.title: Bog
c637fd33f5e5.sentence: Arctic and sub-Arctic circles where many bogs are warming at 0.6 °C per decade, an amount twice as large as the global average.

883330d97e6a.title: Bog
883330d97e6a.sentence: Because bogs and other peatlands are carbon sinks, they are releasing large amounts of greenhouse gases as they warm up.

52f60a4ecc42.title: Bog
52f60a4ecc42.sentence: These changes have resulted in a severe decline of biodiversity and species populations of peatlands throughout Northern Europe.

a67791c84382.title: Bog
a67791c84382.sentence: Bogs are recognized as a significant/specific habitat type by a number of governmental and conservation agencies.

2d408afba710.title: Bog
2d408afba710.sentence: The United Kingdom in its Biodiversity Action Plan establishes bog habitats as a priority for conservation.

b8788b756850.title: Bog
b8788b756850.section: Types > By location and water source
b8788b756850.sentence: Bogs may be classified on their topography, proximity to water, method of recharge, and nutrient accumulation.

7831cd1988fe.title: Bog
7831cd1988fe.section: Types > By location and water source > Valley bog
7831cd1988fe.sentence: These develop in gently sloping valleys or hollows.

75213fb2ab92.title: Bog
75213fb2ab92.section: Types > By location and water source > Valley bog
75213fb2ab92.sentence: Valley bogs may develop in relatively dry and warm climates, but because they rely on ground or surface water, they only occur on acidic substrates.

63c28f38dda0.title: Bog
63c28f38dda0.section: Types > By location and water source > Raised bog
63c28f38dda0.sentence: Over centuries there is a progression from open lake, to a marsh, to a fen (or, on acidic substrates, valley bog), to a carr, as silt or peat accumulates within the lake.

adbfc3156c3c.title: Bog
adbfc3156c3c.section: Types > By location and water source > Raised bog
adbfc3156c3c.sentence: The bog continues to form peat, and over time a shallow dome of bog peat develops into a raised bog.

48f2f433be03.title: Bog
48f2f433be03.section: Types > By location and water source > Raised bog
48f2f433be03.sentence: The dome is typically a few meters high in the center and is often surrounded by strips of fen or other wetland vegetation at the edges or along streamsides where groundwater can percolate into the wetland.

791a6eefd5ad.title: Bog
791a6eefd5ad.section: Types > By location and water source > Blanket bog
791a6eefd5ad.sentence: In cool climates with consistently high rainfall (on more than c. 235 days a year), the ground surface may remain waterlogged for much of the time, providing conditions for the development of bog vegetation.

26bac1fdfcb5.title: Bog
26bac1fdfcb5.section: Types > By location and water source > Blanket bog
26bac1fdfcb5.sentence: In these circumstances, bog develops as a layer "blanketing" much of the land, including hilltops and slopes.

e9346a1a36e3.title: Bog
e9346a1a36e3.section: Types > By location and water source > Quaking bog
e9346a1a36e3.sentence: A quaking bog, schwingmoor, or swingmoor is a form of floating bog occurring in wetter parts of valley bogs and raised bogs and sometimes around the edges of acidic lakes.

47cfc65a2db5.title: Bog
47cfc65a2db5.section: Types > By location and water source > Quaking bog
47cfc65a2db5.sentence: The bog vegetation, mostly sphagnum moss anchored by sedges (such as Carex lasiocarpa), forms a floating mat approximately half a meter thick on the surface of water or above very wet peat.

863b856f6b20.title: Bog
863b856f6b20.section: Types > By location and water source > Quaking bog
863b856f6b20.sentence: Walking on the surface causes it to move – larger movements may cause visible ripples on the surface, or they may even make trees sway.

d46c196f81f5.title: Seagrass meadow
d46c196f81f5.sentence: The long blades of seagrasses slow the movement of water which reduces wave energy and offers further protection against coastal erosion and storm surge.

fdfa42e2d1a2.title: Seagrass meadow
fdfa42e2d1a2.sentence: Many seagrass species produce an extensive underground network of roots and rhizome which stabilizes sediment and reduces coastal erosion.

2095ebe45599.title: Seagrass meadow
2095ebe45599.sentence: Seagrasses are also ecosystem engineers, which means they alter the ecosystem around them, adjusting their surroundings in both physical and chemical ways.

5fa8ef301509.title: Seagrass meadow
5fa8ef301509.sentence: The leaves, extending toward the sea surface, slow down the water currents.

36673c13a920.title: Seagrass meadow
36673c13a920.sentence: The slower current is not able to carry the particles of sediment, so the particles drop down and become part of the seafloor, eventually building it up.

8fe4a54359a2.title: Seagrass meadow
8fe4a54359a2.sentence: When seagrasses are not present, the sea current has no obstacles and carries the sediment particles away, lifting them and eroding the seafloor.

a07b095eb357.title: Seagrass meadow
a07b095eb357.sentence: Seagrasses reduce erosion of the coast and protect houses and cities from both the force of the sea and from sea-level rise caused by global warming.

d28e68cd3565.title: Seagrass meadow
d28e68cd3565.sentence: They do this by reducing the wave energy with their leaves, and helping sediment transported in the seawater to accumulate on the seafloor.

c5641a93d816.title: Seagrass meadow
c5641a93d816.section: Ecosystem services > Nursery habitats for fisheries
c5641a93d816.sentence: Seagrass meadows provide nursery habitats for many commercially important fish species.

97cf4ff9a1cd.title: Seagrass meadow
97cf4ff9a1cd.section: Ecosystem services > Nursery habitats for fisheries
97cf4ff9a1cd.sentence: It's estimated that about half of the global fisheries get their start because they are supported by seagrass habitats.

7042cac9e10e.title: Seagrass meadow
7042cac9e10e.section: Ecosystem services > Nursery habitats for fisheries
7042cac9e10e.sentence: If the seagrass habitats are lost, then the fisheries are lost as well.

6a12f36f56c0.title: Seagrass meadow
6a12f36f56c0.section: Ecosystem services > Nursery habitats for fisheries
6a12f36f56c0.sentence: They argue that: (1) Seagrass meadows provide valuable nursery habitat to over 1/5th of the world's largest 25 fisheries, including walleye pollock, the most landed species on the planet.

47e2d8eea2fc.title: Seagrass meadow
47e2d8eea2fc.section: Ecosystem services > Nursery habitats for fisheries
47e2d8eea2fc.sentence: According to a 2019 paper by Unsworth et al, the significant role seagrass meadows play in supporting fisheries productivity and food security across the globe is not adequately reflected in the decisions made by authorities with statutory responsibility for their management.

41903b3ae8bf.title: Seagrass meadow
41903b3ae8bf.section: Ecosystem services > Nursery habitats for fisheries
41903b3ae8bf.sentence: Invertebrate gleaning (walking) fisheries are common within intertidal seagrass meadows globally, contributing to the food supply of hundreds of millions of people, but understanding of these fisheries and their ecological drivers are extremely limited.

5f07e91cc5d1.title: Seagrass meadow
5f07e91cc5d1.section: Ecosystem services > Nursery habitats for fisheries
5f07e91cc5d1.sentence: In 2022, Jones et al showed seagrass associated small-scale fisheries can provide a safety net for the poor, and are used more commonly than reef-associated fisheries across the Indo-Pacific.

e766d2012b25.title: Seagrass meadow
e766d2012b25.sentence: Seagrass propagules are materials that help propagate seagrass.

603a1ef87b12.title: Seagrass meadow
603a1ef87b12.sentence: Seagrass restoration has primarily involved using asexual material (e.g., cuttings, rhizome fragments or cores) collected from donor meadows.

981851a13456.title: Seagrass meadow
981851a13456.sentence: In various locations, communities are attempting to restore seagrass beds that were lost to human action, including in the US states of Virginia, Florida and Hawaii, as well as the United Kingdom.

77cf66566619.title: Seagrass meadow
77cf66566619.sentence: Such reintroductions have been shown to improve ecosystem services.

7a946135f0bd.title: Seagrass meadow
7a946135f0bd.sentence: Relatively few seagrass restoration efforts have used sexually derived propagules.

af51180d487b.title: Seagrass meadow
af51180d487b.sentence: Restoration using seagrass propagules has so far demonstrated low and variable outcomes, with more than 90% of propagules failing to survive.

02d82b9fee92.title: Seagrass meadow
02d82b9fee92.sentence: In Chesapeake Bay several million Zostera marina seeds have been collected each year during the peak reproductive season using a mechanical harvester.

1bb0e8d09e4d.title: Seagrass meadow
1bb0e8d09e4d.sentence: Seagrass Wasting Disease is (SWD) is a marine illness that affects eelgrass (Zostera marina), which is the most widely distributed of all seagrasses.

6a5420a6216d.title: Seagrass meadow
6a5420a6216d.sentence: SWD is caused by the pathogen Labyrinthula zosterae, which is a pathogenic species commonly known as marine slime mold.

ee12ca2c9b6a.title: Seagrass meadow
ee12ca2c9b6a.sentence: The pathogen invades healthy eelgrass leaf tissue, impairs photosynthesis, and causes enzymatic degradation of eelgrass cells.

9530a097e641.title: Seagrass meadow
9530a097e641.sentence: Symptoms of SWD on eelgrass include blackened or brown spots, streaks, and or patches on eelgrass leaves.

4dc7cba51313.title: Seagrass meadow
4dc7cba51313.sentence: One study found that that warmer sea surface temperatures fueled summer epidemics of eelgrass wasting disease during and after the 2015–2016 northeast Pacific marine heatwave, with disease prevalence rising from 5–70% in 2013 to 60–90% by 2017 and severity roughly doubling each year from 2015 to 2017.

ede1ea78c49a.title: Seagrass meadow
ede1ea78c49a.sentence: Over the same period, eelgrass shoot density declined by 60%.

6962aa2d88cf.title: Seagrass meadow
6962aa2d88cf.sentence: Low or absent wasting disease can serve as a practical signal of climate-resilient refugia, helping managers prioritize eelgrass meadows that are more likely to persist under warming and pathogen pressure.

e7e7f0149b06.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
e7e7f0149b06.sentence: Intertidal zones are the areas that are visible and exposed to air during low tide and covered up by saltwater during high tide.

705b2b27c73d.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
705b2b27c73d.sentence: There are four physical divisions of the intertidal zone with each one having its distinct characteristics and wildlife.

c944a5b9337e.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
c944a5b9337e.sentence: These divisions are the Spray zone, High intertidal zone, Middle Intertidal zone, and Low intertidal zone.

dfd9c7eb130e.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
dfd9c7eb130e.sentence: The high intertidal zone is submerged at high tide but remains dry for long periods between high tides.

5ac0a2f71491.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
5ac0a2f71491.sentence: Due to the large variance of conditions possible in this region, it is inhabited by resilient wildlife that can withstand these changes such as barnacles, marine snails, mussels and hermit crabs.

8d56ba14f22a.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
8d56ba14f22a.sentence: The low intertidal zone is submerged nearly all the time except during the lowest tides and life is more abundant here due to the protection that the water gives.

da1804ed2af8.title: Mangrove forest
da1804ed2af8.sentence: Mangrove forests, also called mangrove swamps, mangrove thickets or mangals, are productive wetlands located in tropical and subtropical intertidal zones.

1969470428e8.title: Mangrove forest
1969470428e8.sentence: Approximately 80 mangrove species exist, all adapted to areas where slow-moving water allows for the deposition of fine sediment and low-oxygen soil conditions.

21e0299122e3.title: Mangrove forest
21e0299122e3.sentence: These trees cannot endure freezing temperatures, which restricts their distribution to warmer climates.

ce4f15c11032.title: Mangrove forest
ce4f15c11032.sentence: Their distinct, stilt-like roots allow the trees to slow the movement of tidal waters, causing the settlement of suspended sediments and acting as a protective barrier to reduce coastal erosion from storm surge and waves.

f155cbd717b3.title: Mangrove forest
f155cbd717b3.sentence: These roots also provide a habitat for many species and act as nurseries for juvenile fish, including species that are recreationally and commercially important.

46f243ff80bb.title: Mangrove forest
46f243ff80bb.sentence: Mangrove forests are amongst the world's most productive marine ecosystems, with net primary productivity (NPP) in the order of 208 Tg C yr−1.

7569e26e1c62.title: Mangrove forest
7569e26e1c62.sentence: Mangrove ecosystems generally act as a net sink of carbon, although they release organic matter to the sea in the form of dissolved refractory macromolecules, leaves, branches and other debris.

afabbe0e7df8.title: Mangrove forest
afabbe0e7df8.section: Exploitation and conservation > Biogeochemical implications of conservation
afabbe0e7df8.sentence: Mangroves sequester over 25 million tons of carbon annually.

edd2603a0d35.title: Mangrove forest
