edd2603a0d35.section: Exploitation and conservation > Biogeochemical implications of conservation
edd2603a0d35.sentence: Mangrove loss has been associated with reduced carbon storage and altered carbon export dynamics.

76f30f2be697.title: Mangrove forest
76f30f2be697.sentence: However, of those areas for which data has been collected, it appears that 35% of the mangroves have been destroyed.

82193c56a217.title: Mangrove forest
82193c56a217.sentence: Since the 1980s, around 2% of mangrove area is estimated to be lost each year.

2266451624bb.title: Mangrove forest
2266451624bb.sentence: Shrimp farming causes approximately a quarter of the destruction of mangrove forests.

435daa39b654.title: Mangrove forest
435daa39b654.section: Exploitation and conservation > Biogeochemical implications of conservation
435daa39b654.sentence: Mangrove areas have declined globally over recent decades due to the expansion of aquaculture, and oil and timber production.

41585d78fc88.title: Mangrove forest
41585d78fc88.sentence: The largest mangrove forest in the world is in the Sundarbans.

a9a5a125315b.title: Mangrove forest
a9a5a125315b.sentence: The forest covers 10,000 km2 (3,900 mi2) of which about 6,000 km2 (2,300 mi2) are in Bangladesh.

bcedfd8d9b95.title: Mudflat
bcedfd8d9b95.sentence: Mudflats or mud flats, also known as tidal flats or, in Ireland, slob or slobs, are coastal wetlands that form in intertidal areas where sediments have been deposited by tides or rivers.

38d8bc5b8cff.title: Mudflat
38d8bc5b8cff.sentence: A global analysis published in 2019 suggested that tidal flat ecosystems are as extensive globally as mangroves, covering at least 127,921 km2 (49,391 mi2) of the Earth's surface.

6ffcee77ecfe.title: Mudflat
6ffcee77ecfe.sentence: A recent global remote sensing analysis estimated that approximately 50% of the global extent of tidal flats occurs within eight countries (Indonesia, China, Australia, United States, Canada, India, Brazil, and Myanmar) and that 44% of the world's tidal flats occur within Asia (56,051 km2 or 21,641 mi2).

c4ff646200be.title: Mudflat
c4ff646200be.sentence: They support a large population of wildlife, and are a key habitat that allows tens of millions of migratory shorebirds to migrate from breeding sites in the northern hemisphere to non-breeding areas in the southern hemisphere.

629c49dcf8a6.title: Mudflat
629c49dcf8a6.sentence: In the past tidal flats were considered economically unimportant areas and were often dredged and developed into agricultural land.

62f2f41962ed.title: Mudflat
62f2f41962ed.sentence: It is estimated that up to 16% of the world tidal flats have disappeared since the mid-1980s.

064d6d79170a.title: Mudflat
064d6d79170a.sentence: For example, around the Yellow Sea region of East Asia, more than 65% of mudflats present in the early 1950s had been destroyed by the late 2000s.

6d47eee800f5.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
6d47eee800f5.sentence: Seagrass beds are found from cold polar waters to the tropics.

687cf96b76ca.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
687cf96b76ca.sentence: Mangrove forests are confined to tropical and sub-tropical areas, while tidal marshes are found in all regions, but most commonly in temperate areas.

df10d3650573.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
df10d3650573.sentence: Combined, these ecosystems cover about 50 million hectares and provide a diverse array of ecosystem services such as fishery production, coastline protection, pollution buffering, as well as high rates of carbon sequestration.

58ea179ad974.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
58ea179ad974.sentence: Vegetated coastal ecosystems typically reside over organic-rich sediments that may be several meters deep and effectively lock up carbon due to low-oxygen conditions and other factors that inhibit decomposition at depth.

6697d22a148f.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
6697d22a148f.sentence: These carbon stocks can exceed those of terrestrial ecosystems, including forests, by several times.

266970c2e5d4.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
266970c2e5d4.sentence: When coastal habitats are degraded or converted to other land uses, the sediment carbon is destabilised or exposed to oxygen, and subsequent increased microbial activity releases large amounts of greenhouse gasses to the atmosphere or water column.

091f3cc71795.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
091f3cc71795.sentence: Rapid loss of vegetated coastal ecosystems through land-use change has occurred for centuries, and has accelerated in recent decades.

d3b981db4659.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
d3b981db4659.sentence: Causes of habitat conversion vary globally and include conversion to aquaculture, agriculture, forest over-exploitation, industrial use, upstream dams, dredging, eutrophication of overlying waters, urban development, and conversion to open water due to accelerated sea-level rise and subsidence.

f1b3fc65b927.title: Seagrass meadow
f1b3fc65b927.sentence: Blue carbon refers to carbon dioxide removed from the atmosphere by the world's coastal marine ecosystems, mostly mangroves, salt marshes, seagrasses and potentially macroalgae, through plant growth and the accumulation and burial of organic matter in the sediment.

1ac2dff072c1.title: Seagrass meadow
1ac2dff072c1.sentence: They keep coastal waters healthy by absorbing bacteria and nutrients, and slow the speed of climate change by sequestering carbon dioxide into the sediment of the ocean floor.

340d17420e1f.title: Seagrass meadow
340d17420e1f.sentence: Although seagrass meadows occupy only 0.1% of the area of the ocean floor, they account for 10–18% of the total oceanic carbon burial.

120a0cb485a4.title: Seagrass meadow
120a0cb485a4.sentence: Per hectare, they hold twice as much carbon dioxide as rain forests and can sequester about 27 million tons of CO2 annually.

3947d67758cc.title: Seagrass meadow
3947d67758cc.sentence: Currently global seagrass meadows are estimated to store as much as 19.9 Pg (petagrams or gigatons, equals a billion tons) of organic carbon.

3171477ce7ae.title: Seagrass meadow
3171477ce7ae.sentence: Carbon primarily accumulates in marine sediments, which are anoxic and thus continually preserve organic carbon from decadal-millennial time scales.

e3de9d5f6419.title: Seagrass meadow
e3de9d5f6419.sentence: High accumulation rates, low oxygen, low sediment conductivity and slower microbial decomposition rates all encourage carbon burial and carbon accumulation in these coastal sediments.

c57312296af0.title: Seagrass meadow
c57312296af0.sentence: Compared to terrestrial habitats that lose carbon stocks as CO2 during decomposition or by disturbances like fires or deforestation, marine carbon sinks can retain C for much longer time periods.

65f9fe712da1.title: Seagrass meadow
65f9fe712da1.sentence: Carbon sequestration rates in seagrass meadows vary depending on the species, characteristics of the sediment, and depth of the habitats, but on average the carbon burial rate is about 140 g C m−2 yr−1.

f4dfd45de253.title: Blue carbon
f4dfd45de253.section: Carbon storage by type of biome > Seagrass meadows
f4dfd45de253.sentence: Restored seagrass meadows were found to start sequestering carbon in sediment within about four years.

774e627dae72.title: Mangrove forest
774e627dae72.sentence: The outwelling hypothesis argues that export of locally derived POC and DOC is an important ecosystem function of mangroves, which drives detrital based food webs in adjacent coastal habitats.

914080ef515c.title: Mangrove forest
914080ef515c.sentence: The theory of outwelling is supported by mass balance evaluations that show the amount of carbon fixed by mangroves normally greatly exceeds the amount stored within the forest, although the scale of outwelling varies considerably between forests, due to differences in coastal geomorphology, tidal regimes, freshwater flow and productivity.

e6a3af81f00c.title: Mangrove forest
e6a3af81f00c.sentence: Mangrove forests achieve a steady state once the forest reaches maximum biomass at around 20–30 years through a constant process of mortality and renewal so, assuming the living biomass is not becoming more carbon dense, then carbon has to be lost at a rate equal to the amount of carbon fixed as NPP.

a77e1a1fb24a.title: Mangrove forest
a77e1a1fb24a.sentence: Hence this productivity is either retained within the mangrove forest, as a standing stock of live material such as wood, buried in sediments, or exported to neighbouring habitats as litter, particulate and dissolved organic carbon (POC and DOC) and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), or lost to the atmosphere.

0ebf3574c0b2.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
0ebf3574c0b2.sentence: Coral reefs, seagrasses, and mangroves buffer habitats further inland from storms and wave damage as well as participate in a tri-system exchange of mobile fish and invertebrates.

7e4c7dc8eb64.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
7e4c7dc8eb64.sentence: Mangroves and seagrasses are critical in regulating sediment, freshwater, and nutrient flows to coral reefs.

2a622f8a0e99.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
2a622f8a0e99.sentence: The ecosystem services provided by intact reefs, seagrasses, and mangroves are both highly valuable and mutually enhance each other.

acfadce15d63.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
acfadce15d63.sentence: Fisheries are characterized by migratory species, and therefore, protecting fisheries in one ecosystem increases fish biomass in others.

eea4fc44136b.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
eea4fc44136b.sentence: Tourism benefits from coastal protection and healthy fisheries from multiple ecosystems.

7c9a7ddc7015.title: Pelagic zone
7c9a7ddc7015.sentence: The pelagic zone is subdivided into five vertical regions.

c783a5d00e2c.title: Pelagic zone
c783a5d00e2c.sentence: In a manner analogous to stratification in the Earth's atmosphere, the water column can be divided vertically into up to five different layers (illustrated in the diagram), with the number of layers depending on the depth of the water.

bb02bc6aaf85.title: Pelagic zone
bb02bc6aaf85.sentence: The illuminated zone at the surface of the sea, and the only zone with sufficient light for photosynthesis.

672fe0b85161.title: Pelagic zone
672fe0b85161.sentence: Nearly all primary production in the ocean occurs here, and about 90% marine life is concentrated in this zone, including: plankton, floating seaweed, jellyfish, tuna, whales, sharks, dolphins, and many more diverse species.

5251a8995882.title: Pelagic zone
5251a8995882.sentence: This zone contains a very trace amount of sunlight and has a pressure of about 20 - 100 atm.

d46738fbfa17.title: Pelagic zone
d46738fbfa17.sentence: Many organisms living here have evolved adaptations, such as bioluminescence, due to the lack of sunlight.

bb6b075ac251.title: Pelagic zone
bb6b075ac251.sentence: Some mesopelagic creatures rise to the epipelagic zone at night to feed.

89cf280be191.title: Pelagic zone
89cf280be191.sentence: In this zone, the environment is pitch black at this depth and contains no trace of sunlight, apart from occasional bioluminescent organisms, such as anglerfish.

6633a6b3728c.title: Pelagic zone
6633a6b3728c.sentence: Most creatures survive on detritus known as "marine snow" falling from the zones above or, like the marine hatchetfish, by preying on other inhabitants of this zone.

3a660f8fd569.title: Pelagic zone
3a660f8fd569.sentence: This is the deepest part of the ocean at more than 6,000 m (20,000 ft).

e5fa65800d00.title: Pelagic zone
e5fa65800d00.sentence: The deepest trenches stretch to 10,935 m deep (at Challenger Deep, deepest point on earth), while average trenches are usually 5–10 kilometers deep.

15d330cd2a0a.title: Pelagic zone
15d330cd2a0a.sentence: This zone can have an atmospheric pressure of 1,100 atm.

36332f29e9a1.title: Tundra
36332f29e9a1.sentence: As global warming heats the ecosystem and causes soil thawing, the permafrost carbon cycle accelerates and releases much of these soil-contained greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, creating a feedback cycle that contributes to climate change.

2614a85cd455.title: Tundra
2614a85cd455.sentence: Carbon emissions from permafrost thaw contribute to the same warming which facilitates the thaw, making it a positive climate change feedback.

76052f5e6c61.title: Tundra
76052f5e6c61.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report estimates that carbon dioxide and methane released from permafrost could amount to the equivalent of 14–175 billion tonnes (1.4×10^10–1.72×10^11 long tons; 1.5×10^10–1.93×10^11 short tons) carbon dioxide per 1 °C (1.8 °F) of warming.

52d09fa72faa.title: Tundra
52d09fa72faa.sentence: For comparison, by 2019, annual anthropogenic emission of carbon dioxide alone stood around 40 billion tonnes (3.9×10^10 long tons; 4.4×10^10 short tons).

0e2d6594d287.title: Tundra
0e2d6594d287.sentence: A 2018 perspectives article discussing tipping points in the climate system activated around 2 °C (3.6 °F) of global warming suggested that at this threshold, permafrost thaw would add a further 0.09 °C (0.16 °F) to global temperatures by 2100, with a range of 0.04–0.16 °C (0.07–0.29 °F)

d883bb59ddb9.title: Tundra
d883bb59ddb9.sentence: It also represents a significant risk to infrastructure built on top of permafrost, such as roads and pipelines.

7841debdd8b1.title: Fen
7841debdd8b1.sentence: Bogs and fens can be thought of as two ecosystems on a gradient from poor to rich, with bogs at the poor end, extremely rich fens at the rich end, and poor fens in between.

c265bba02bb0.title: Fen
c265bba02bb0.sentence: In this context, "rich" and "poor" refer to the species richness, or how biodiverse a fen or bog is.

80cc611052e5.title: Fen
80cc611052e5.sentence: The richness of these species is strongly influenced by pH and concentrations of calcium and bicarbonate.

255c35f3bae5.title: Fen
255c35f3bae5.sentence: These factors assist in identifying where along the gradient a particular fen falls.

a6c150c2dc21.title: Fen
a6c150c2dc21.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Rich fens
a6c150c2dc21.sentence: Rich fens are strongly minerotrophic; that is, a large proportion of their water comes from mineral-rich ground or surface water.

a05b827cabcb.title: Fen
a05b827cabcb.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Rich fens
a05b827cabcb.sentence: This water is dominated by calcium and bicarbonate, resulting in a slightly acidic to slightly basic pH characteristic of rich fens.

469d63bab8a9.title: Fen
469d63bab8a9.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Rich fens

543fe53e4b93.title: Fen
543fe53e4b93.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Poor fens
543fe53e4b93.sentence: They are much more acidic than their rich counterparts, with a pH of approximately 5.5 to 4.

e83200e9a2cf.title: Fen
e83200e9a2cf.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Poor fens
e83200e9a2cf.sentence: Peat in poor fens tends to be thicker than that of rich fens, which cuts off vegetation access to the mineral-rich soil underneath.

d4a6ec1cb950.title: Drylands
d4a6ec1cb950.sentence: However, some researchers raise criticism against the dominant desertification narrative.

c93e592c38e0.title: Drylands
c93e592c38e0.sentence: Desertification is a major problem threatening ecosystems and human lives with the most affected regions being Western Asia and South America.

f392cfa8b435.title: Drylands
f392cfa8b435.sentence: The Sahel region is often falsely perceived as drying at a higher rate than other places.

a9f47c33e7aa.title: Drylands
a9f47c33e7aa.sentence: Critics argue that desertification in the Sahel region originates from a colonial understanding of the land use/land cover.

10c1778a70b1.title: Drylands
10c1778a70b1.sentence: In reality, the region has experienced a greening during the last decades.

15194480833f.title: Drylands
15194480833f.sentence: The livelihoods of millions of people in developing countries depend highly on dryland ecosystems to ensure their food security and their well-being.

bb0f81b86084.title: Drylands
bb0f81b86084.sentence: Drylands also provide significant global economic value through the provision of ecosystem services and biodiversity conservation.

e16a87a6d51c.title: Drylands
e16a87a6d51c.sentence: Dryland inhabitants' lifestyles provide global environmental benefits such as contributing to halting climate change through carbon sequestration and species conservation.

14ab87b3ce97.title: Drylands
14ab87b3ce97.sentence: The UN Conference on Sustainable Development, Rio+20 held in Brazil in June 2012, stressed the intrinsic value of drylands' biodiversity and recognized the severity of biodiversity loss and degradation in these ecosystems.

8d97df08e5b4.title: Drylands
8d97df08e5b4.sentence: Drylands can be classified into four sub-types:

74761e9af0b4.title: Drylands
74761e9af0b4.section: Four sub-types > Dry and sub-humid lands
74761e9af0b4.sentence: These areas produce a large amount the world's crops and livestock.

de1231b79227.title: Drylands
de1231b79227.sentence: One measure based on precipitation considers semi-arid lands as places where the annual rainfall ranges between 500 and 800mm.

05a0651b0914.title: Drylands
05a0651b0914.sentence: Arid lands make up about 10% of the world's land and are home to 20% of the world's people.

1efd6be45578.title: Drylands
1efd6be45578.sentence: The UNCCD defined them as having an aridity index between ~0.05-0.20.

56d99cd5b312.title: Drylands
56d99cd5b312.sentence: These lands cover ~8% of the world and consist of areas of little to no vegetation.

b3ed5d2ca294.title: Drylands
b3ed5d2ca294.sentence: They receive irregular rainfall that barely surpasses 100 mm, and in some cases, they may not receive rainfall for several years.

ec5e5c681551.title: Drylands
ec5e5c681551.sentence: The UNCCD excludes hyper-arid zones from its definition of drylands.

3149028b2eb2.title: Drylands
3149028b2eb2.sentence: Climate change and human activities are causing land degradation in drylands.

b1e21fb3485f.title: Drylands
b1e21fb3485f.sentence: These factors have led to increasing droughts, desertification and soil erosion, which decreases biodiversity, soil fertility and carbon sequestration in these regions.

df8dd28985c2.title: Drylands
df8dd28985c2.sentence: From 1982 to 2015, 12.6% of the world's drylands have degraded due to anthropogenic climate change.

ef8c4593843f.title: Drylands
ef8c4593843f.sentence: In recent decades, about 7.6% of global land (an area larger than Canada) has transitioned into drier conditions, either becoming more arid or shifting from non-drylands to drylands.

caf0cb4ad1db.title: Drylands
caf0cb4ad1db.sentence: Drylands' vulnerability to land degradation and desertification is affecting 213 million people of which the vast majority live in the Global South.

da9078480869.title: Drylands
da9078480869.sentence: This has negative impacts on local agriculture and food security.

00d5bfa6095e.title: Drylands
00d5bfa6095e.sentence: Sustainable land management practices (such as mobile pastoralism), restoring degraded lands, and climate-smart agriculture can mitigate these impacts.

dc624ac1b4e5.title: Drylands
dc624ac1b4e5.section: Four sub-types > Semi-arid lands > Adaptation and resilience
dc624ac1b4e5.sentence: In semi-arid lands where pastoralism is the principal activity, the main adaptation measures are an earlier movement of herds, the reduction of the size of the herd, a change in the management of water, and diversification of paths of transhumance.

844e016ae1d0.title: Drylands
844e016ae1d0.sentence: Restoration is defined by IPBES as 'any intentional activities that initiates or accelerates the recovery of an ecosystem from a degraded state.' It is one of the three pillars of nature-based solutions defined by the IUCN as "actions to protect, sustainably manage, and restore natural or modified ecosystems, that address societal challenges effectively and adaptively, simultaneously providing human well-being and biodiversity benefits".

ece8e0e6d2dd.title: Drylands
ece8e0e6d2dd.sentence: Dryland restoration is often understood in two ways; either to restore a dryland to its previous functionality or to avoid further degradation.

a2463aab365c.title: Drylands
a2463aab365c.sentence: Ecosystem restoration in general is also emphasized as a tool for climate mitigation and adaptation by IUCN and IPCC.

4a72c6d5515a.title: Drylands
4a72c6d5515a.sentence: Restoration efforts in dryland areas are particularly challenging because of rare and variable precipitation, high temperatures, low soil fertility, and invasive species.

0776c15f659a.title: Drylands
0776c15f659a.sentence: A defining feature of dryland ecosystems is the patchiness of its vegetation, where isolated vegetated patches are scattered within largely bare areas.

91f3e222a2a8.title: Drylands
91f3e222a2a8.sentence: Restoration techniques addressing this patchiness are restoration islands (also known as assisted nucleation or nucleation plantings), the use of soil fauna, as well as techniques such as afforestation, exclosures, and silvopastoralism.

ee095ab8aba1.title: Drylands
ee095ab8aba1.sentence: Smaller scale techniques such as semicircular bunds have also shown promising results.

4e4e509f37dd.title: Drylands
4e4e509f37dd.sentence: FAO provides 10 practice principles to guide ecosystem restoration.

35bfb83aa477.title: Drylands
35bfb83aa477.section: Dryland restoration > Indigenous knowledge and community engagement
35bfb83aa477.sentence: Indigenous or local knowledge plays an important role in protecting and restoring drylands.

c381be33f190.title: Drylands
c381be33f190.section: Dryland restoration > Indigenous knowledge and community engagement
c381be33f190.sentence: Several case studies have found that the inclusion of indigenous knowledge and local communities has increased restoration success.

335b5e89e41f.title: Drylands
335b5e89e41f.section: Dryland restoration > Indigenous knowledge and community engagement
335b5e89e41f.sentence: Approaches such as silvopastoralism/agroforestry have been applied for centuries in dryland communities with great success.

b1aa08e9a3d8.title: Drylands
b1aa08e9a3d8.section: Dryland restoration > Indigenous knowledge and community engagement
b1aa08e9a3d8.sentence: One technique that studies have shown to be successful is the use of indigenous fire ecology to lower the fuel load in ecosystems and help prevent the large devastating fires.

a7d93ccb7e85.title: Drylands
a7d93ccb7e85.section: Dryland restoration > Restoration techniques > Restoration islands
a7d93ccb7e85.sentence: Restoration islands use small, strategically located plantings (islands) to make use of limited resources.

5faaa0a1114e.title: Drylands
5faaa0a1114e.section: Dryland restoration > Restoration techniques > Restoration islands
5faaa0a1114e.sentence: Once established, the island plantations proliferate (nucleate) into neighboring areas.

527b033bde5a.title: Drylands
527b033bde5a.section: Dryland restoration > Restoration techniques > Restoration islands
527b033bde5a.sentence: This strategy is best suited to address the patchiness of dryland vegetation, because restoration islands can be placed in the most promising locations and are less resource-intensive than large-scale plantations.

7d906110ca76.title: Drylands
7d906110ca76.section: Dryland restoration > Restoration techniques > Restoration islands
7d906110ca76.sentence: Other benefits include reduced fire risk, lower soil erosion, weed control, seed sources for long-term restoration, and habitat for wildlife.

303becc06d5f.title: Drylands
303becc06d5f.section: Dryland restoration > Restoration techniques > Restoration islands
303becc06d5f.sentence: Compared to humid ecosystems, vegetation patches in drylands take more time to nucleate as extensively.

f140564b03dd.title: Drylands
f140564b03dd.sentence: With its carbon sequestration potential, rangeland restoration is considered a climate mitigation option.

7ce3897164a1.title: Drylands
7ce3897164a1.sentence: Rangeland restoration can also improve livelihood opportunities for local pastoralists and can help combat desertification.

c928ab6b8f0d.title: Drylands
c928ab6b8f0d.sentence: Rangelands cover about 25% of drylands globally.

071a359484c6.title: Drylands
071a359484c6.sentence: Ecological, economic, political, institutional and socio-cultural factors can support or limit the adaptation of restoration practices.

5c89230ecc0d.title: Drylands
5c89230ecc0d.sentence: The adoption of a sustainable rangeland practice is highly context specific and cannot be generalized.

4a074a012953.title: Intact forest landscape
4a074a012953.sentence: An intact forest landscape (IFL) is an unbroken natural landscape of a forest ecosystem and its habitat–plant community components, in an extant forest zone.

dd48931b9969.title: Intact forest landscape
dd48931b9969.sentence: An IFL is a natural environment with no signs of significant human activity or habitat fragmentation, and of sufficient size to contain, support, and maintain the complex of indigenous biodiversity of viable populations of a wide range of genera and species, and their ecological effects.

7ddee9d8a51f.title: Intact forest landscape
7ddee9d8a51f.sentence: Technically, an IFL is defined as an area which contains forest and non-forest ecosystems minimally influenced by human economic activity, with an area of at least 500 km2 (50,000 ha) and a minimal width of 10 km (measured as the diameter of a circle that is entirely inscribed within the boundaries of the territory).

9c9f26c53b77.title: Intact forest landscape
9c9f26c53b77.sentence: IFLs are estimated to cover 23 percent of forest ecosystems (13.1 million km2).

3cebbbfb7071.title: Intact forest landscape
3cebbbfb7071.sentence: Two biomes hold almost all of these IFLs: dense tropical and subtropical forests (45 percent) and boreal forests (44 percent), while the proportion of IFLs in temperate broadleaf and mixed forests is very small.

4094b0defae1.title: Intact forest landscape
4094b0defae1.sentence: Nineteen percent of the global IFL area is under some form of protection, but only 10 percent is strictly protected, i.e., belongs to IUCN protected areas categories I–III.

e39038076371.title: Intact forest landscape
e39038076371.sentence: It is estimated that the planet has lost seven percent of its IFLs since 2000.

87c0037f86da.title: Intact forest landscape
87c0037f86da.sentence: At the same time the cost of conserving large unpopulated areas is often low.

f7c9ac7d369d.title: Intact forest landscape
f7c9ac7d369d.sentence: The same factors that have kept them from being developed, such as remoteness and low economic value, also help to reduce the cost of protecting them.

c5f6fe8be78f.title: Intact forest landscape
c5f6fe8be78f.sentence: The first regional IFL map was presented by Greenpeace Russia in 2001, covering northern European Russia.

2ae6262b3b57.title: River ecosystem
2ae6262b3b57.section: Community patterns and diversity > River continuum concept
2ae6262b3b57.sentence: The River continuum concept (RCC) was an attempt to construct a single framework to describe the function of temperate lotic ecosystems from the headwaters to larger rivers and relate key characteristics to changes in the biotic community.

2844569e530b.title: River ecosystem
2844569e530b.section: Community patterns and diversity > River continuum concept
2844569e530b.sentence: The physical basis for RCC is size and location along the gradient from a small stream eventually linked to a large river.

2d769a17dd92.title: River ecosystem
2d769a17dd92.section: Community patterns and diversity > River continuum concept
2d769a17dd92.sentence: Stream order (see characteristics of streams) is used as the physical measure of the position along the RCC.

3d8eef24ff5c.title: River ecosystem
3d8eef24ff5c.section: Community patterns and diversity > River continuum concept
3d8eef24ff5c.sentence: According to the RCC, low ordered sites are small shaded streams where allochthonous inputs of CPOM are a necessary resource for consumers.

9985f3a5a0c2.title: River ecosystem
9985f3a5a0c2.section: Community patterns and diversity > River continuum concept
9985f3a5a0c2.sentence: Ample sunlight should reach the bottom in these systems to support significant periphyton production.

6d2978329cc5.title: River ecosystem
6d2978329cc5.section: Community patterns and diversity > River continuum concept
6d2978329cc5.sentence: Thus, allochthonous inputs are expected to be the primary energy source for large rivers.

4d1dd61931c4.title: River ecosystem
4d1dd61931c4.section: Community patterns and diversity > River continuum concept
4d1dd61931c4.sentence: Biota should change with this change in energy from the headwaters to the mouth of these systems.

e7eb3dc1509c.title: River ecosystem
e7eb3dc1509c.section: Community patterns and diversity > River continuum concept
e7eb3dc1509c.sentence: Namely, shredders should prosper in low-ordered systems and grazers in mid-ordered sites.

06d2af20846c.title: Flood pulse concept
06d2af20846c.sentence: However, Junk et al. argue that the river continuum concept is not sufficient because it is based on research done on small temperate streams and has mistakenly been applied to all water systems; furthermore, the river continuum concept does not explain habitats that fluctuate between lotic and lentic states, whereas the flood pulse concept adequately covers these systems.

f76ecd9d275d.title: Forest ecology
f76ecd9d275d.section: Matter and energy flows > Death and regeneration
f76ecd9d275d.sentence: Woody material, often referred to as coarse woody debris, decays relatively slowly in many forests in comparison to most other organic materials, due to a combination of environmental factors and wood chemistry (see lignin).

cb4a0ccd94d4.title: Forest ecology
cb4a0ccd94d4.section: Matter and energy flows > Death and regeneration
cb4a0ccd94d4.sentence: Thus, tree trunks and branches can remain on the forest floor for long periods, affecting such things as wildlife habitat, fire behaviour, and tree regeneration processes.

6246e671df16.title: Forest ecology
6246e671df16.section: Matter and energy flows > Death and regeneration
6246e671df16.sentence: Trees growing in arid and/or cold environments do so especially slowly.

c19cff5da818.title: Deep sea
c19cff5da818.sentence: Regions below the epipelagic are divided into further zones, beginning with the bathyal zone (also considered the continental slope) which spans from 200 to 3,000 meters (660 to 9,840 ft) below sea level and is essentially transitional, containing elements from both the shelf above and the abyss below.

7e50e18130d6.title: Deep sea
7e50e18130d6.sentence: Below this zone, the deep sea consists of the abyssal zone (ocean depth between 3–6 km; 1.9–3.7 mi) and the hadal zone (6–11 km; 3.7–6.8 mi).

1be92f07ade4.title: Forest ecology
1be92f07ade4.sentence: Forests accumulate large amounts of standing biomass, and many are capable of accumulating it at high rates, i.e. they are highly productive.

13a4066797c4.title: Forest ecology
13a4066797c4.sentence: The world's forests contain about 606 gigatonnes of living biomass (above- and below-ground) and 59 gigatonnes of dead wood.

47df9d381d6c.title: Forest ecology
47df9d381d6c.sentence: Such high levels of biomass and tall vertical structures represent large stores of potential energy that can be converted to kinetic energy under the right circumstances.

7d9962feac6f.title: Forest ecology
7d9962feac6f.sentence: Two such conversions of great importance are fires and treefalls, both of which radically alter forest structure and ecosystem processes and the physical environment where they occur.

fc9e25786e5e.title: Deep sea
fc9e25786e5e.sentence: These species and communities are found at hydrothermal vents at sea-floor spreading zones.

d20e3fb5fb3c.title: Deep sea
d20e3fb5fb3c.sentence: It is this chemosynthesis that supports the complex communities that can be found around hydrothermal vents.

7719cc56b2be.title: Deep sea
7719cc56b2be.sentence: These complex communities are one of the few ecosystems on the planet that do not rely upon sunlight for their supply of energy.

050cabe88b8b.title: Deep sea
050cabe88b8b.sentence: One example is the symbiotic relationship between the tube worm Riftia and chemosynthetic bacteria.

5e3169587312.title: Deep sea
5e3169587312.sentence: In hydrothermal vents the temperature of the water as it emerges from the "black smoker" chimneys may be as high as 400 °C (752 °F), being kept from boiling by the high hydrostatic pressure – thus being superheated water.

d17f146c02c9.title: Forest ecology
d17f146c02c9.sentence: An important interaction in forest ecosystems is the mycorrhizal network, which consists of fungi and plants that share symbiotic relationships.

a786e7793b36.title: Forest ecology
a786e7793b36.sentence: Mycorrhizal networks have been shown to increase the uptake of important nutrients, especially ones which disperse slowly into the soil like phosphorus.

d07ed1b2a0c7.title: Forest ecology
d07ed1b2a0c7.sentence: The fine hypha of the mycelium is able to reach farther into the soil than the roots of the plant, allowing it to better access phosphorus and water.

fd75cf983598.title: Forest ecology
fd75cf983598.sentence: The mycorrhizal network can also transport water and nutrients between plants.

01767f1bee53.title: Forest ecology
01767f1bee53.sentence: These interactions can help provide drought resistance to their symbiotic plants, helping protect them through the progression of climate change.

47ae9c704ddc.title: Forest ecology
47ae9c704ddc.section: Types of forest ecosystems > Coniferous forests
47ae9c704ddc.sentence: Because of the types of leaves possessed by conifers, they face the problem of soil nutrient loss; this problem is solved through mycorrhizal symbiosis with fungi that help transport the limited nutrients to the trees in exchange for sugars.

9c142b785e74.title: Forest ecology
9c142b785e74.section: Types of forest ecosystems > Coniferous forests
9c142b785e74.sentence: Some conifers are incapable of surviving without mycorrhizal fungi.

4101ab51352a.title: Forest ecology
4101ab51352a.sentence: However, it's been shown that the benefit of mycorrhizal networks vary greatly depending on the species of plant and nutrient availability.

6670ef7992b1.title: Forest ecology
6670ef7992b1.sentence: The plants' benefit from mycorrhizal fungus decreases as nutrient density increases, because the plants' loss of sugars costs more than the benefit they receive.

dfd3930c40ef.title: Lake ecosystem
dfd3930c40ef.sentence: One common system divides lakes into three zones.

ad04f23f5fda.title: Lake ecosystem
ad04f23f5fda.sentence: The first, the littoral zone, is the shallow zone near the shore.

4d820d2c9b8a.title: Lake ecosystem
4d820d2c9b8a.sentence: The offshore is divided into two further zones, an open water zone and a deep water zone.

f4e0e6a87f5c.title: Lake ecosystem
f4e0e6a87f5c.sentence: This is where rooted wetland plants occur.

903955a60cc3.title: Lake ecosystem
903955a60cc3.sentence: In the open water zone (or photic zone) sunlight supports photosynthetic algae and the species that feed upon them.

8022ed0de945.title: Lake ecosystem
8022ed0de945.sentence: In the deep water zone, sunlight is not available and the food web is based on detritus entering from the littoral and photic zones.

0781ab348bee.title: Lake ecosystem
0781ab348bee.sentence: The off shore areas may be called the pelagic zone, the photic zone may be called the limnetic zone and the aphotic zone may be called the profundal zone.

f221fa0e72c5.section: Management and policy > Land use change decisions
f221fa0e72c5.sentence: Often it is the combination of the best science combined with the stakeholder values, estimates and opinions that drive the process.

6e8c726fd5e4.title: Ecosystem service
6e8c726fd5e4.section: Management and policy > Land use change decisions
6e8c726fd5e4.sentence: One analytical study modeled the stakeholders as agents to support water resource management decisions in the Middle Rio Grande basin of New Mexico.

73e999bba218.title: Ecosystem service
73e999bba218.section: Management and policy > Land use change decisions
73e999bba218.sentence: Another study used Monte Carlo methods to exercise econometric models of landowner decisions in a study of the effects of land-use change.

cae80dea0137.title: Ecosystem service
cae80dea0137.section: Management and policy > Land use change decisions
cae80dea0137.sentence: Here the stakeholder inputs were modeled as random effects to reflect the uncertainty.

22c81a57f228.title: Ecosystem service
22c81a57f228.section: Management and policy > Land use change decisions
22c81a57f228.sentence: A third study used a Bayesian decision support system to both model the uncertainty in the scientific information Bayes Nets and to assist collecting and fusing the input from stakeholders.

f66b07b2d4aa.title: Ecosystem service
f66b07b2d4aa.section: Management and policy > Land use change decisions
f66b07b2d4aa.sentence: Remote sensing data and analyses can be used to assess the health and extent of land cover classes that provide ecosystem services, which aids in planning, management, monitoring of stakeholders' actions, and communication between stakeholders.

7aeae432b073.title: Ecological goods and services
7aeae432b073.sentence: Such benefits accrue to all living organisms, including animals and plants, rather than to humans alone.

cc4518f648f1.title: Payment for ecosystem services
cc4518f648f1.sentence: In the case of private contracts, the beneficiaries of the ecosystem services are willing to pay a price that can be expected to be lower than their welfare gain due to the services.

1253a46dfb3b.title: Ecological goods and services
1253a46dfb3b.sentence: What has emerged is the notion that rural landowners who provide ecological goods and services to society through good stewardship practices on their land should be duly compensated.

95af38eb1f4b.title: Gretchen Daily
95af38eb1f4b.sentence: Nature's Services: Societal Dependence on Natural Ecosystems was published in 1997 by Island Press.

a8e25826e99a.title: Gretchen Daily
a8e25826e99a.sentence: During her time as a research scientist, Daily served as the editor of Nature's Services: Societal Dependence on Natural Ecosystems, a foundational book that lays out the framework used widely today for understanding the benefits of nature to people, with numerous examples and ways of considering their value.

41930014745f.title: Gretchen Daily
41930014745f.sentence: Nature's Services starts off with an introduction from Daily titled "What are Ecosystem Services" and another introductory piece by Harold Mooney and Paul Ehrlich that seeks to detail the "fragmentary history" of ecosystem services.

01caf5181622.title: Nutrient cycle
01caf5181622.sentence: A nutrient cycle (or ecological recycling) is the movement and exchange of inorganic and organic matter back into the production of matter.

3fb128f99910.title: Nutrient cycle
3fb128f99910.sentence: The nutrient cycle is nature's recycling system.

48256a484523.title: Nutrient cycle
48256a484523.sentence: Energy flow is a unidirectional and noncyclic pathway, whereas the movement of mineral nutrients is cyclic.

0c62b9eb8f74.title: Nutrient cycle
0c62b9eb8f74.sentence: Mineral cycles include the carbon cycle, sulfur cycle, nitrogen cycle, water cycle, phosphorus cycle, oxygen cycle, among others that continually recycle along with other mineral nutrients into productive ecological nutrition.

8052d00ce46c.title: Nutrient cycle
8052d00ce46c.sentence: Recycling in ecology is regulated to a large extent during the process of decomposition.

e91d8328fd54.title: Nutrient cycle
e91d8328fd54.sentence: Ecosystems employ biodiversity in the food webs that recycle natural materials, such as mineral nutrients, which includes water.

efa1d1cb1305.title: Nutrient cycle
efa1d1cb1305.sentence: Recycling in natural systems is one of the many ecosystem services that sustain and contribute to the well-being of human societies.

6800bede2220.title: Nutrient cycle
6800bede2220.sentence: There are regional and spatial differences in the rates of growth and exchange of materials, where some ecosystems may be in nutrient debt (sinks) where others will have extra supply (sources).

dc06ee74837f.title: Nutrient cycle
dc06ee74837f.sentence: These differences relate to climate, topography, and geological history leaving behind different sources of parent material.

ecb20c4e1a39.title: Nutrient cycle
ecb20c4e1a39.sentence: Most textbooks integrate the two and seem to treat them as synonymous terms.

7c9f9a30ed76.title: Nutrient cycle
7c9f9a30ed76.sentence: The nutrient cycle is more often used in direct reference to the idea of an intra-system cycle, where an ecosystem functions as a unit.

654675fcac09.title: Nutrient cycle
654675fcac09.sentence: Even earlier, in 1749, Carl Linnaeus wrote: "the economy of nature we understand the all-wise disposition of the creator in relation to natural things, by which they are fitted to produce general ends, and reciprocal uses", in reference to the balance of nature in his book Oeconomia Naturae.

c9d3371b4708.title: Nutrient cycle
c9d3371b4708.sentence: In this book, he captured the notion of ecological recycling: "The 'reciprocal uses' are the key to the whole idea, for 'the death, and destruction of one thing should always be subservient to the restitution of another;' thus mould spurs the decay of dead plants to nourish the soil, and the earth then 'offers again to plants from its bosom, what it has received from them.'" The basic idea of a balance of nature, however, can be traced back to the Greeks: Democritus, Epicurus, and their Roman disciple Lucretius.

63109d553964.title: Nutrient cycle
63109d553964.sentence: In 1926, Vernadsky coined the term biogeochemistry as a sub-discipline of geochemistry.

20f95d93004d.title: Pollination
20f95d93004d.sentence: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther of a plant to the stigma of a plant, later enabling fertilisation and the production of seeds.

2051bc57d1d2.title: Pollination
2051bc57d1d2.sentence: Pollinating agents can be animals such as insects, for example bees, beetles or butterflies; birds, and bats; water; wind; and even plants themselves.

4442053f82b7.title: Pollination
4442053f82b7.sentence: Between 100,000 and 200,000 species of animal act as pollinators of the world's 250,000 species of flowering plant.

49d4b0a08405.title: Pollination
49d4b0a08405.sentence: The majority of these pollinators are insects, but about 1,500 species of birds and mammals visit flowers and may transfer pollen between them.

f8ee6b733a87.title: Pollination
f8ee6b733a87.sentence: About 80% of angiosperms rely on biotic pollination.

26abcc24423a.title: Pollination
26abcc24423a.sentence: Adding natural habitat areas into farm systems generally improves pollination, as farms that are closer to natural habitat have higher crop yield because they are visited by more pollinators.

9f1c2323b4e2.title: Pollination
9f1c2323b4e2.section: Environmental impacts > Food security and pollinator decline
9f1c2323b4e2.sentence: Pollination is necessary for plants to continue their populations and 3/4 of the plant species that contribute to the world's food supply are plants that require pollinators.

eeab900d6533.title: Pollination
eeab900d6533.section: Environmental impacts > Food security and pollinator decline
eeab900d6533.sentence: Insect pollinators, like bees, are large contributors to crop production, over 200 billion dollars' worth of crop species are pollinated by these insects.

865e23009280.title: Pollination
865e23009280.sentence: Pollination by animals aids in the genetic variability and diversity within plants because it allows for out-crossing instead for self-crossing.

8ad74740201d.title: Food security
8ad74740201d.sentence: Food security is the state of having reliable access to a sufficient quantity of affordable, healthy food.

7352c03c9621.title: Food security
7352c03c9621.sentence: Food security, as defined by the World Food Summit in 1996, is "when all people, at all times, have physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food that meets their dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy life".

43b0eb8d5264.title: Food security
43b0eb8d5264.sentence: Close to 12% of the global population was severely food insecure in 2020, representing 928 million people -148 million more than in 2019.

59181d2d6003.title: Food security
59181d2d6003.sentence: The UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights noted that the causes of hunger and malnutrition are often not a scarcity of food but an inability to access available food, usually due to poverty.

cd01073ac015.title: Food security
cd01073ac015.section: Causes of food insecurity > Environmental degradation and overuse > Land degradation
cd01073ac015.sentence: Intensive farming often leads to a vicious cycle of exhaustion of soil fertility and a decline of agricultural yields.

e47d67512d31.title: Food security
e47d67512d31.section: Causes of food insecurity > Environmental degradation and overuse > Land degradation
e47d67512d31.sentence: Other causes of land degradation include for example deforestation, overgrazing, and over-exploitation of vegetation for use.

098b1ac2f982.title: Food security
098b1ac2f982.section: Causes of food insecurity > Environmental degradation and overuse > Overfishing
098b1ac2f982.sentence: The overexploitation of fish stocks can pose serious risks to food security.

01b21008e3c9.title: Pollination
01b21008e3c9.section: Environmental impacts > Food security and pollinator decline
01b21008e3c9.sentence: Besides the imbalance of the ecosystem caused by the decline in pollinators, it may jeopardise food security.

1cbb8038cefd.title: Groundwater recharge
1cbb8038cefd.sentence: Groundwater recharge or deep drainage or deep percolation is a hydrologic process, where water moves downward from surface water to groundwater.

a2f4748dbe8f.title: Groundwater recharge
a2f4748dbe8f.sentence: Recharge is the primary method through which water enters an aquifer.

e013bcf0e171.title: Groundwater recharge
e013bcf0e171.sentence: Water is recharged naturally by rain and snow melt and to a smaller extent by surface water (rivers and lakes).

e5353380e0ef.title: Groundwater recharge
e5353380e0ef.sentence: Recharge occurs both naturally (through the water cycle) and through anthropogenic processes (i.e., "artificial groundwater recharge"), where rainwater and/or reclaimed water is routed to the subsurface.

5a4e55ded96d.title: Groundwater recharge
5a4e55ded96d.sentence: Recharge may be impeded somewhat by human activities including paving, development, or logging.

934e059dd8fb.title: Groundwater recharge
934e059dd8fb.sentence: These activities can result in loss of topsoil resulting in reduced water infiltration, enhanced surface runoff and reduction in recharge.

1c1bdc00e1b3.title: Groundwater recharge
1c1bdc00e1b3.sentence: Tree roots increase water saturation into groundwater reducing water runoff.

711359714440.title: Groundwater recharge
711359714440.sentence: Wetlands help maintain the level of the water table and exert control on the hydraulic head.

16481cc28e57.title: Groundwater recharge
16481cc28e57.sentence: Researchers have discovered groundwater recharge of up to 20% of wetland volume per season.

bf6a47f1ddb7.title: Groundwater recharge
bf6a47f1ddb7.sentence: Groundwater recharge is an important process for sustainable groundwater management, since the volume-rate abstracted from an aquifer in the long term should be less than or equal to the volume-rate that is recharged.

8a33b2ab7ffd.title: Groundwater recharge
8a33b2ab7ffd.section: Factors affecting groundwater recharge > Climate change
8a33b2ab7ffd.sentence: Direct redistribution of water by human activities amounting to ~24,000 km3 per year is about double the global groundwater recharge each year.

505db541ffa2.title: Groundwater recharge
505db541ffa2.sentence: Rates of groundwater recharge are difficult to quantify.

8f676ac8c108.title: Groundwater recharge
8f676ac8c108.sentence: This is because other related processes, such as evaporation, transpiration (or evapotranspiration) and infiltration processes must first be measured or estimated to determine the balance.

357081eedb1f.title: Aquifer
357081eedb1f.sentence: Recharge occurs both naturally (through the water cycle) and through anthropogenic processes (i.e., "artificial groundwater recharge"), where rainwater and/or reclaimed water is routed to the subsurface.

39815a50dbc0.title: Storm surge
39815a50dbc0.sentence: A storm surge is a coastal flood or tsunami-like phenomenon of rising water (tropical wave) commonly associated with low-pressure weather systems, such as tropical cyclones.

6f1abd0e78a7.title: Storm surge
6f1abd0e78a7.sentence: It is measured as the rise in water level above the normal tidal level, and does not include waves.

4fab05394082.title: Storm surge
4fab05394082.sentence: The main meteorological factor contributing to a storm surge is high-speed wind pushing water towards the coast over a long fetch.

2101bd5562c0.title: Storm surge
2101bd5562c0.sentence: This effect is estimated at a 10 mm (0.39 in) increase in sea level for every millibar (hPa) drop in atmospheric pressure.

91b3443f6982.title: Storm surge
91b3443f6982.sentence: The deadliest storm surge on record was the 1970 Bhola cyclone, which killed up to 500,000 people in the area of the Bay of Bengal.

907c703ebf61.title: Storm surge
907c703ebf61.sentence: Storm surge both destroys built infrastructure, like roads, and undermines foundations and building structures.

c7f84f8b1dca.title: Storm surge
c7f84f8b1dca.sentence: Additionally, storm surge can cause or transform human-utilized land through other processes, hurting soil fertility, increasing saltwater intrusion, hurting wildlife habitat, and spreading chemical or other contaminants from human storage.

583d2754e644.title: Storm surge
583d2754e644.sentence: As extreme weather becomes more intense and the sea level rises due to climate change, storm surges are expected to cause more risk to coastal populations.

27c2b7d30f0f.title: Blue carbon
27c2b7d30f0f.section: Carbon storage by type of biome > Tidal marshes
27c2b7d30f0f.sentence: Marshes provide valuable habitat for plants, birds, and juvenile fish, protect coastal habitat from storm surge and flooding, and can reduce nutrient loading to coastal waters.

e11b615f5d0b.title: Biological pest control
e11b615f5d0b.sentence: Biological control or biocontrol is a method of controlling pests, whether animals, weed plants, or pathogens of animals or of plants by using other organisms.

052be1849a3f.title: Biological pest control
052be1849a3f.sentence: It relies on predation, parasitism, and herbivory, but typically involves an active human management role.

59f571df1a10.title: Biological pest control
59f571df1a10.sentence: It can be a component of integrated pest management (IPM) programs.

71393d5d705d.title: Biological pest control
71393d5d705d.sentence: The first report of the use of an insect species to control an insect pest comes from "Nanfang Caomu Zhuang" (南方草木狀 Plants of the Southern Regions) (c. 304 AD), attributed to Western Jin dynasty botanist Ji Han (嵇含, 263–307), in which it is mentioned that "Jiaozhi people sell ants and their nests attached to twigs looking like thin cotton envelopes, the reddish-yellow ant being larger than normal.

362f358f9d5f.title: Biological pest control
362f358f9d5f.sentence: Without such ants, southern citrus fruits will be severely insect-damaged".

d5dc2a3e0fed.title: Biological pest control
d5dc2a3e0fed.sentence: Modern biological control techniques started to emerge in the US in the 1870s, when the Missouri State entomologist C. V. Riley and the Illinois State entomologist W. LeBaron began distributing parasitoids to control crop pests in their states.

7961312505bb.title: Biological pest control
7961312505bb.sentence: Lady beetles, and in particular their larvae which are active between May and July in the northern hemisphere, are voracious predators of aphids, and also consume mites, scale insects and small caterpillars.

cd253ee54a7a.title: Biological pest control
cd253ee54a7a.sentence: Most insect parasitoids are wasps or flies, and many have a very narrow host range.

a9ba6fadd59d.title: Biological pest control
a9ba6fadd59d.sentence: Pathogenic micro-organisms include bacteria, fungi, and viruses.

1e41eea5710a.title: Biological pest control
1e41eea5710a.sentence: Bacillus thuringiensis, a soil-dwelling bacterium, is the most widely applied species of bacteria used for biological control, with at least four sub-species used against Lepidopteran (moth, butterfly), Coleopteran (beetle) and Dipteran (true fly) insect pests.

115085172007.title: Biological pest control
115085172007.sentence: Genes from B. thuringiensis have also been incorporated into transgenic crops, making the plants express some of the bacterium's toxins, which are proteins.

3a9b58755a62.title: Economics of biodiversity
3a9b58755a62.section: Agriculture and food > Biological pest control
3a9b58755a62.sentence: Biological pest control can reduce economic losses incurred as a result of pests, disease vectors, and invasive species.

7fd4cde19046.title: Agricultural pollution
7fd4cde19046.section: Biotic sources > Introduced species > Biological control
7fd4cde19046.sentence: The use of biological pest control agents, or using predators, parasitoids, parasites, and pathogens to control agricultural pests, has the potential to reduce agricultural pollution associated with other pest control techniques, such as pesticide use.

c7c405a4c785.title: Biological pest control
c7c405a4c785.sentence: The first international shipment of an insect as a biological control agent was made by Charles V. Riley in 1873, shipping the predatory mites Tyroglyphus phylloxera to France to help fight phylloxera that was destroying grapevines there.

cec889d205cc.title: Water purification
cec889d205cc.sentence: Water purification is the process of removing undesirable chemicals, biological contaminants, suspended solids, and gases from water.

e636221de75c.title: Water purification
e636221de75c.sentence: The goal is to produce water that is fit for specific purposes.

5cb45b63e88d.title: Water purification
5cb45b63e88d.sentence: Soil and rock layers naturally filter the ground water to a high degree of clarity and often, it does not require additional treatment besides adding chlorine or chloramines as secondary disinfectants.

abafee21cdb8.title: Water purification
abafee21cdb8.sentence: In bank filtration, natural sediments in a riverbank are used to provide the first stage of contaminant filtration.

d43d8eec866a.title: Water purification
d43d8eec866a.sentence: These filters rely on biological treatment processes for their action rather than physical filtration.

6e6524ecb700.title: Water purification
6e6524ecb700.sentence: The methods used include physical processes such as filtration, sedimentation, and distillation; biological processes such as slow sand filters or biologically active carbon; chemical processes such as flocculation and chlorination; and the use of electromagnetic radiation such as ultraviolet light.

20992af3e14d.title: Water purification
20992af3e14d.sentence: According to a 2007 World Health Organization report, 1.1 billion people lack access to an improved drinking water supply; 88% of the 4 billion annual cases of diarrheal disease are attributed to unsafe water and inadequate sanitation and hygiene, while 1.8 million people die from diarrhoeal disease each year.

bce345669696.title: Water purification
bce345669696.sentence: This method was refined in the following two decades by engineers working for private water companies, and it culminated in the first treated public water supply in the world, installed by engineer James Simpson for the Chelsea Waterworks Company in London in 1829.

344b0b73094a.title: Microclimate
344b0b73094a.sentence: A microclimate (or micro-climate) refers to localized atmospheric conditions in the near-surface layer, which includes the air immediately above a surface as well as the shallow soil and water environments below it.

71b20e833c4e.title: Microclimate
71b20e833c4e.sentence: It is characterized by a set of persistent, measurable differences in the climate conditions from those in the adjacent surrounding areas.

c9098063d086.title: Microclimate
c9098063d086.sentence: A microclimate can range in size from a few meters to at most a few kilometers across.

a1c619c0ff76.title: Microclimate
a1c619c0ff76.sentence: A Macroclimate is the climate of a large region, typically covering an area defined as hundred to thousands of kilometers.

4740a02d84de.title: Microclimate
4740a02d84de.sentence: Mesoclimates range in size between tens to hundreds of kilometers.

b421ef9ae7fa.title: Microclimate
b421ef9ae7fa.sentence: Microclimates are present at much smaller scales, mostly controlled by the properties of the area and energy exchanges.

bcda95d876d1.title: Microclimate
bcda95d876d1.sentence: These processes can be shaped or influenced by contributing factors, such as topography, soil composition, vegetation structure and plant diversity as well as the mass of nearby objects, natural or human made.

30b899ba25cd.title: Microclimate
30b899ba25cd.sentence: These localized atmospheric conditions arise from differences in sunlight, heat, wind, and moisture near the surface.

7d3d32832a53.title: Microclimate
7d3d32832a53.sentence: The area in a developed industrial park may vary greatly from a wooded park nearby, as natural flora in parks absorb light and heat in leaves that a building roof or parking lot radiates back into the air.

8f8ce2c79282.title: Microclimate
8f8ce2c79282.sentence: Microclimate management involves the modification of conditions to those which are optimized for growth and crop yield, such as the practices of irrigation, shading, windbreaks, and vegetation management, These modifications can help buffer crops from environmental extremes, such as heat and drought.

4030b3147e03.title: Microclimate
4030b3147e03.sentence: As climate change increases the frequency and intensity of temperature extremes, microclimate management will play an important role in agriculture management.

59b046b00c03.title: Clearcutting
59b046b00c03.section: Effects on the environment > Positive perspectives
59b046b00c03.sentence: Generally, a harvest area wider than double the height of the adjacent trees will no longer be subject to the moderating influence of the woodland on the microclimate.

8c9e58729896.title: Habitat fragmentation
8c9e58729896.sentence: Moreover, fragmentation can change the microclimate at both local and regional scales, influencing biodiversity through interactions with anthropogenic climate change.

144d01864dc5.title: Bioprospecting
144d01864dc5.sentence: Bioprospecting (also known as biodiversity prospecting) is the exploration of natural sources for small molecules, macromolecules and biochemical and genetic information that could be developed into commercially valuable products for the agricultural, aquaculture, bioremediation, cosmetics, nanotechnology, or pharmaceutical industries.

113176a216b4.title: Bioprospecting
113176a216b4.sentence: In the pharmaceutical industry, for example, almost one third of all small-molecule drugs approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) between 1981 and 2014 were either natural products or compounds derived from natural products.

e765719ace0a.title: Bioprospecting
e765719ace0a.sentence: Many of the antibacterial drugs in current clinical use were discovered through bioprospecting including the aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, amphenicols, polymyxins, cephalosporins and other β-lactam antibiotics, macrolides, pleuromutilins, glycopeptides, rifamycins, lincosamides, streptogramins, and phosphonic acid antibiotics.

fe92c932ad2c.title: Bioprospecting
fe92c932ad2c.sentence: The aminoglycoside antibiotic streptomycin, for example, was discovered from the soil bacterium Streptomyces griseus, the fusidane antibiotic fusidic acid was discovered from the soil fungus Acremonium fusidioides, and the pleuromutilin antibiotics (eg. lefamulin) were discovered and developed from the basidiomycete fungi Omphalina mutila and Clitopilus passeckerianus.

152b4f6a6e28.title: Bioprospecting
152b4f6a6e28.sentence: Other examples of bioprospecting-derived anti-infective drugs include the antifungal drug griseofulvin (discovered from the soil fungus Penicillium griseofulvum), the antifungal and antileishmanial drug amphotericin B (discovered from the soil bacterium Streptomyces nodosus), the antimalarial drug artemisinin (discovered from the plant Artemisia annua), and the antihelminthic drug ivermectin (developed from the soil bacterium Streptomyces avermitilis).

7db517c892c7.title: Bioprospecting
7db517c892c7.section: Bioprospecting as a discovery strategy > Strengths
7db517c892c7.sentence: Bioprospecting-derived small molecules (also known as natural products) are more structurally complex than synthetic chemicals, and therefore show greater specificity towards biological targets.

b94589314775.title: Bioprospecting
b94589314775.sentence: Terrestrial plants, fungi and actinobacteria have been the focus of many past bioprospecting programs, but interest is growing in less explored ecosystems (e.g. seas and oceans, caves and polar regions) and organisms (e.g. extremophiles, tropical corals and necrophages) as a means of identifying new molecules with novel biological activities.

a54b895d22c7.title: Bioprospecting
a54b895d22c7.section: Bioprospecting pitfalls > Collection of source material
a54b895d22c7.sentence: Environmental impacts must also be considered as the over-harvesting of desirable species can put them at risk of extinction.

0044eaaae434.title: Bioprospecting
0044eaaae434.section: Criticism of bioprospecting > Criticism of ethnobotanical bioprospecting
0044eaaae434.sentence: Bioprospecting has been promoted by the United Nations, environmental nongovernmental organizations (NGOs), World Trade Organization and World Intellectual Property Organization as an ethical and sustainable form of economic development that is based on the protection of biodiversity.

c987e7e77e79.title: Bioprospecting
c987e7e77e79.section: Criticism of bioprospecting > Criticism of ethnobotanical bioprospecting
c987e7e77e79.sentence: According to Isla, the creation of "conservation areas" for ecotourism, biodiversity research and bioprospecting denies local communities access to common lands where they previously hunted and fished.

d3d9df3685fd.title: Medicinal plants
d3d9df3685fd.sentence: Medicinal plants, also called medicinal herbs, have been discovered and used in traditional medicine practices since prehistoric times.

8d806a55e219.title: Medicinal plants
8d806a55e219.sentence: Medicinal plants are used with the intention of maintaining health, to be administered for a specific condition, or both, whether in modern medicine or in traditional medicine.

2228d6acc8b4.title: Medicinal plants
2228d6acc8b4.sentence: Plants synthesize hundreds of chemical compounds for various functions, including defense and protection against insects, fungi, diseases, against parasites and herbivorous mammals.

d50627412416.title: Medicinal plants
d50627412416.sentence: These phytochemicals have potential for use as drugs, and the content and known pharmacological activity of these substances in medicinal plants is the scientific basis for their use in modern medicine, if scientifically confirmed.

3d53343c064b.title: Medicinal plants
3d53343c064b.sentence: The Food and Agriculture Organization estimated in 2002 that over 50,000 medicinal plants are used across the world.

6117d3c1efe6.title: Medicinal plants
6117d3c1efe6.sentence: In modern medicine, around a quarter of the drugs prescribed to patients are derived from medicinal plants, and they are rigorously tested.

ba21506cdffb.title: Medicinal plants
ba21506cdffb.sentence: As of 2023 by one estimate, the global market was US$68 billion per year, growing by 10-20% annually.

e0db7b73e411.title: Medicinal plants
e0db7b73e411.sentence: China and India are the leading producers of natural products, and are also the leading exporters and domestic consumers.

f6357541ed0e.title: Medicinal plants
f6357541ed0e.sentence: In most of the developing world, especially in rural areas, local traditional medicine, including herbalism, is the only source of health care for people, while in the developed world, alternative medicine including use of dietary supplements is marketed aggressively using the claims of traditional medicine.

72706e615ddb.title: Medicinal plants
72706e615ddb.sentence: General threats include climate change and habitat loss to development and agriculture.

33dca921d8d8.title: Medicinal plants
33dca921d8d8.sentence: A specific threat is over-collection to meet rising demand for medicines.

67639f3b988b.title: Medicinal plants
67639f3b988b.sentence: As of 2015, most products made from medicinal plants had not been tested for their safety and efficacy, and products that were marketed in developed economies and provided in the undeveloped world by traditional healers were of uneven quality, sometimes containing dangerous contaminants.

2fc24a8a9abd.title: Medicinal plants
2fc24a8a9abd.sentence: There is no reason to presume that because a product comes from nature it must be safe: the existence of powerful natural poisons like atropine and nicotine shows this to be untrue.

caadf39cfb3d.title: Medicinal plants

99c8c1fa4b59.title: Soil formation
99c8c1fa4b59.sentence: Soil formation, also known as pedogenesis, is the process of soil genesis as regulated by the effects of place, environment, and history.

dd865a62602d.title: Soil formation
dd865a62602d.sentence: The starting point is weathering of freshly accumulated parent material.

f09c1f37d82a.title: Soil formation
f09c1f37d82a.sentence: A variety of soil microbes (bacteria, archaea, fungi) feed on simple compounds (nutrients) released by weathering and produce organic acids and specialized proteins which contribute in turn to mineral weathering.

5259f12aec9c.title: Soil formation
5259f12aec9c.sentence: They also leave behind organic residues which contribute to humus formation.

eb5a99aa3a48.title: Soil formation
eb5a99aa3a48.sentence: These alterations lead to the development of layers, termed soil horizons, distinguished by differences in color, structure, texture, and chemistry.

0ea980ac3259.title: Soil formation

d4da131c96a9.title: Soil formation
