80a2d03af9ab.title: Land degradation
80a2d03af9ab.sentence: Soil erosion from agricultural fields is estimated to be currently 11 to 20 times (no-tillage) to more than 100 times (conventional tillage) higher than the soil formation rate (medium confidence)."

742b080d9697.title: Food system
742b080d9697.sentence: Food systems are highly dependent on a multitude of ecosystem services, such as soil formation, nutrient cycling, microorganisms providing nitrogen-fixation, natural pest regulation, water supply and pollinators.

43898becbc13.title: Soil formation
43898becbc13.sentence: Russian geologist Vasily Dokuchaev, commonly regarded as the father of pedology, determined in 1883 that soil formation occurs over time under the influence of climate, vegetation, topography, and parent material.

21122c326b30.title: Pollinator decline
21122c326b30.sentence: Pollinator decline is the reduction in abundance of insect and other animal pollinators in many ecosystems worldwide that began being recorded at the end of the 20th century.

1e1f07a12c74.title: Pollinator decline
1e1f07a12c74.sentence: Multiple lines of evidence exist for the reduction of wild pollinator populations at the regional level, especially within Europe and North America.

f457a6631efe.title: Pollinator decline
f457a6631efe.sentence: Similar findings from studies in South America, China and Japan make it reasonable to suggest that declines are occurring around the globe.

0f7adfc42dd7.title: Pollinator decline
0f7adfc42dd7.sentence: Although the number of managed honey bee colonies in Europe and North America declined by 25% and 59% between 1985-2005 and 1947-2005 respectively, overall global stocks increased due to major hive number increases in countries such as China and Argentina.

a89ffb512c4c.title: Pollinator decline
a89ffb512c4c.sentence: Nevertheless, in the time managed honeybee hives increased by 45% the demand for animal pollinated crops tripled, highlighting the danger of relying on domesticated populations for pollination services.

6a92c56f4d98.title: Pollinator decline
6a92c56f4d98.sentence: A 2021 study described as the "first long-term assessment of global bee decline", which analyzed GBIF-data of over a century, found that the number of bee species declined steeply worldwide after the 1990s, shrinking by a quarter in 2006–2015 compared to before 1990.

c66318e830b0.title: Pollinator decline
c66318e830b0.sentence: Nonetheless, an estimated 87.5% of the world's flowering plant species are animal-pollinated, and 60% of crop plant species use animal pollinators.

3bc883aff18e.title: Pollinator decline
3bc883aff18e.sentence: This includes the majority of fruits, many vegetables, and also fodder.

7a262e1597ad.title: Pollinator decline
7a262e1597ad.sentence: The expected direct reduction in total agricultural production in the US in the absence of animal pollination is expected to be 3 to 8%, with smaller impacts on agricultural production diversity.

1bc599043794.title: Pollinator decline
1bc599043794.sentence: In 2009 another study calculated the worldwide value of the 100 crops that need pollinators at €153 billion (not including production costs).

e2933cf3d792.title: Pollinator decline
e2933cf3d792.sentence: Despite the dire predictions, the theorised decline in pollinators has had no effect on food production, with yields of both animal-pollinated and non-animal-pollinated crops increasing at the same rate, over the period of supposed pollinator decline.

0d69df65bf37.title: Pollination
0d69df65bf37.sentence: Since the early 1900s, beekeepers in the United States started renting out their colonies to farmers to increase the farmer's crop yields, earning additional revenue from providing privatized pollination.

de19c99f1285.title: Pollination
de19c99f1285.sentence: While there are 200,000 – 350,000 different species of animals that help pollination, honeybees are responsible for majority of the pollination for consumed crops, providing between $235 and $577 US billion of benefits to global food production.

bf237401cc81.title: Pollination
bf237401cc81.sentence: As of 2016, 41% of an average US beekeeper's revenue comes from providing such pollination service to farmers, making it the biggest proportion of their income, with the rest coming from sales of honey, beeswax, government subsidy, etc.

cf6b5dbb8ddd.title: Pollination
cf6b5dbb8ddd.sentence: This is an example of how a positive externality, pollination of crops from beekeeping and honey-making, was successfully accounted for and incorporated into the overall market for agriculture.

f51b6ea3fd99.title: Pollination
f51b6ea3fd99.sentence: Almond industry uses up to 82% of the services in the pollination market.

cdbb106c7bb1.title: Pollination
cdbb106c7bb1.sentence: Each February, around 60% of the all bee colonies in the US are moved to California's Central Valley.

ba2902a612c7.title: Pollination
ba2902a612c7.sentence: Almond pollinating bees, approximately 60% of the bees in the US as mentioned above, will be mixed with bees from thousands of other hives provided by different beekeepers, making them exponentially susceptible to diseases and mites that any of them could be carrying.

743248e9c135.title: Pollination
743248e9c135.sentence: The deaths do not stop at commercial honeybees as there is evidence of significant pathogen spillover to other pollinators including wild bumble bees, infecting up to 35–100% of wild bees within 2 km radius of commercial pollination.

91e7d8559bc2.title: Pollination
91e7d8559bc2.sentence: The negative externality of private pollination services is the decline of biodiversity through the deaths of commercial and wild bees.

fe1b9e080865.title: Pollination
fe1b9e080865.sentence: In 2016, a colony rented out for almond pollination gave beekeepers an income of $165 per colony rented, around three times from average of other crops that use the pollination rental service.

5965880e8fc9.title: Pollination
5965880e8fc9.sentence: However, a recent study published in Oxford Academic's Journal of Economic Entomology found that once the costs for maintaining bees specifically for almond pollination, including overwintering, summer management, and the replacement dying bees are considered, almond pollination is barely or not profitable for average beekeepers.

bc35c928f675.title: Firewood
bc35c928f675.sentence: Firewood is any wooden material that can be used for fuel.

022930ccef6c.title: Firewood
022930ccef6c.sentence: The term usually refers to wood fuel that is not industrially processed, such as wood pellets, and instead takes the form of a recognizable log or branch.

6a693a23529d.title: Firewood
6a693a23529d.sentence: Firewood is a renewable resource, although demand for this fuel can quickly outpace its ability to regenerate on a local or regional level.

59586a7b9eb5.title: Firewood
59586a7b9eb5.sentence: For most of human history, firewood was the main fuel, until the use of coal spread during the Industrial Revolution.

a781e4ef9475.title: Firewood
a781e4ef9475.sentence: As such, access to firewood was a valued resource, with wood botes, or the right to gather firewood, being a significant aspect of many medieval leases.

ed81a252f673.title: Firewood
ed81a252f673.sentence: Along with clearance for agriculture firewood is a cause of deforestation.

74662dacf52b.title: Firewood
74662dacf52b.sentence: Burning firewood can cause respiratory issues and other illnesses.

d4c5ec9ab1db.title: Firewood
d4c5ec9ab1db.sentence: Transporting firewood long distances can also spread plant pests, diseases, and invasive species.

09f2848c886e.title: Food security
09f2848c886e.sentence: The WHO states that three pillars that determine food security: food availability, food access, and food use and misuse.

9b4e10c04e1a.title: Food security
9b4e10c04e1a.sentence: The FAO added a fourth pillar: the stability of the first three dimensions of food security over time.

5fa6235c08da.title: Food security
5fa6235c08da.sentence: Food availability relates to the supply of food through production, distribution, and exchange.

e96fc45b93d7.title: Food security
e96fc45b93d7.sentence: Food access refers to the affordability and allocation of food, as well as the preferences of individuals and households.

e46353261abd.title: Food security
e46353261abd.sentence: Food stability refers to the ability to obtain food over time.

ecd9f544085d.title: Food security
ecd9f544085d.sentence: Food insecurity can be transitory, seasonal, or chronic.

f13f4628cb57.title: Food security
f13f4628cb57.sentence: Sustainability refers to the long-term ability of food systems to provide food security and nutrition in a way that does not compromise the economic, social, and environmental bases that generate food security and nutrition for future generations.

5c463010924a.title: Nutrient cycle
5c463010924a.sentence: Complete recycling means that 100% of the waste material can be reconstituted indefinitely.

5a0ce90f4b44.title: Nutrient cycle
5a0ce90f4b44.sentence: This idea was captured by Howard T. Odum when he penned that "it is thoroughly demonstrated by ecological systems and geological systems that all the chemical elements and many organic substances can be accumulated by living systems from background crustal or oceanic concentrations without limit as to concentration so long as there is available solar or another source of potential energy" In 1979 Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen proposed the fourth law of entropy stating that complete recycling is impossible.

cfbad89743ca.title: Nutrient cycle
cfbad89743ca.sentence: Despite Georgescu-Roegen's extensive intellectual contributions to the science of ecological economics, the fourth law has been rejected in line with observations of ecological recycling.

0bcd9b92ac3e.title: Nutrient cycle
0bcd9b92ac3e.sentence: However, some authors state that complete recycling is impossible for technological waste.

514d1be2c8f0.title: Nutrient cycle
514d1be2c8f0.section: Recycling in novel ecosystems > Technological recycling
514d1be2c8f0.sentence: Recycling in human industrial systems (or technoecosystems) differs from ecological recycling in scale, complexity, and organization.

a5bc4bfe2023.title: Nutrient cycle
a5bc4bfe2023.section: Recycling in novel ecosystems > Technological recycling
a5bc4bfe2023.sentence: Industrial recycling systems do not focus on the employment of ecological food webs to recycle waste back into different kinds of marketable goods, but primarily employ people and technodiversity instead.

173741611e71.title: Nutrient cycle
173741611e71.sentence: Only 7% of total plastic waste (adding up to millions upon millions of tons) is being recycled by industrial systems; the 93% that never makes it into the industrial recycling stream is presumably absorbed by natural recycling systems In contrast and over extensive lengths of time (billions of years) ecosystems have maintained a consistent balance with production roughly equaling respiratory consumption rates.

9b58bc78249f.title: Nutrient cycle
9b58bc78249f.section: Recycling in novel ecosystems > Technological recycling
9b58bc78249f.sentence: Many technoecosystems are competitive and parasitic toward natural ecosystems.

d48d0c43308b.title: Groundwater recharge
d48d0c43308b.sentence: Managed aquifer recharge (MAR) strategies to augment freshwater availability include streambed channel modification, bank filtration, water spreading and recharge wells.

a06e8e9e3b8d.title: Groundwater recharge
a06e8e9e3b8d.sentence: A facility in Orange County, California cleans and injects 100 million gallons per day; or 90 billion gallons per year.

9aa74207e462.title: Groundwater recharge
9aa74207e462.sentence: Artificial groundwater recharge is becoming increasingly important in India, where over-pumping of groundwater by farmers has led to underground resources becoming depleted.

b460e94fd812.title: Groundwater recharge
b460e94fd812.sentence: In 2007, on the recommendations of the International Water Management Institute, the Indian government allocated ₹1,800 crore (equivalent to ₹59 billion or US$630 million in 2026) to fund dug-well recharge projects (a dug-well is a wide, shallow well, often lined with concrete) in 100 districts within seven states where water stored in hard-rock aquifers had been over-exploited.

f84c2cc74808.title: Pollination
f84c2cc74808.sentence: Biotic pollination relies on living pollinators to move the pollen from one flower to another.

50ea61609e6c.title: Pollination
50ea61609e6c.sentence: Abiotic pollination relies on wind, water or even rain.

0c313dee4ff8.title: Pollination
0c313dee4ff8.sentence: Some 98% of abiotic pollination is anemophily, i.e., pollination by wind.

40f620845b03.title: Pollination
40f620845b03.sentence: This allows the plant to spend energy directly on pollen rather than on attracting pollinators with flowers and nectar.

95d37de974d4.title: Pollination
95d37de974d4.sentence: It is possible for a plant to have varying pollination methods, including both biotic and abiotic pollination.

cdcdaca6d8ee.title: Pollination
cdcdaca6d8ee.sentence: The orchid Oeceoclades maculata uses both rain and butterflies, depending on its environmental conditions.

a7fa244a199f.title: Pollination
a7fa244a199f.sentence: The most essential staple food crops on the planet, like wheat, maize, rice, soybeans and sorghum are wind pollinated or self pollinating.

a07bf0c9d47f.title: Pollination
a07bf0c9d47f.sentence: When considering the top 15 crops contributing to the human diet globally in 2013, slightly over 10% of the total human diet of plant crops (211 out of 1916 kcal/person/day) is dependent upon insect pollination.

d9ac9659192f.title: Pollination
d9ac9659192f.section: In agriculture > Improving pollination in areas with suboptimal bee densities
d9ac9659192f.sentence: The number of managed beehives in the US has steadily declined from close to 6 million after WWII, to less than 2.5 million today.

f05acc682609.title: Pollination
f05acc682609.section: In agriculture > Improving pollination in areas with suboptimal bee densities
f05acc682609.sentence: In contrast, the area dedicated to growing bee-pollinated crops has grown over 300% in the same time period.

281a63110598.title: Pollination
281a63110598.sentence: The largest managed pollination event in the world is in California almond orchards, where nearly half (about one million hives) of the US honey bees are trucked to the almond orchards each spring.

9bfa86ba88eb.title: Storm surge
9bfa86ba88eb.sentence: Communities and governments can adapt by building hard infrastructure, like flood barriers, soft infrastructure, like coastal dunes or mangroves, improving coastal construction practices and building social strategies such as early warning, education and evacuation plans.

e8f952f33f71.title: Storm surge
e8f952f33f71.sentence: A prophylactic method introduced after the North Sea flood of 1953 is the construction of dams and storm-surge barriers (flood barriers).

8e23d25e4bf7.title: Storm surge
8e23d25e4bf7.sentence: They are open and allow free passage, but close when the land is under threat of a storm surge.

fffe83bf6fb2.title: Storm surge
fffe83bf6fb2.sentence: Major storm surge barriers are the Oosterscheldekering and Maeslantkering in the Netherlands, which are part of the Delta Works project; the Thames Barrier protecting London; and the Saint Petersburg Dam in Russia.

f091d4b10f4d.title: Storm surge
f091d4b10f4d.sentence: Similarly educating coastal communities and developing local evacuation plans can reduce the relative impact on people.

c6b6120b721b.title: Seed dispersal
c6b6120b721b.sentence: Seed dispersal is sometimes split into autochory (when dispersal is attained using the plant's own means) and allochory (when obtained through external means).

9d1aeb5a56b5.title: Seed dispersal
9d1aeb5a56b5.sentence: Autochorous plants disperse their seed without any help from an external vector.

6019f57c0e8d.title: Seed dispersal
6019f57c0e8d.sentence: This limits considerably the distance they can disperse their seed.

7ec644b3634d.title: Seed dispersal

6f3e0231365a.title: Seed dispersal

2cae62112250.title: Seed dispersal

2cae62112250.sentence: Animals can disperse plant seeds in several ways, all named zoochory.

eede6f942555.title: Seed dispersal
eede6f942555.section: Types > Allochory > Animals: epi- and endozoochory
eede6f942555.sentence: Seeds can be transported on the outside of vertebrate animals (mostly mammals), a process known as epizoochory.

610c9bc78cd1.title: Seed dispersal
610c9bc78cd1.sentence: Examples are: dispersal on human clothes (up to 250 m), on shoes (up to 5 km), or by cars (regularly ~ 250 m, single cases > 100 km).

1b4c85683f77.title: Biological pest control
1b4c85683f77.sentence: There are three basic biological pest control strategies: importation, augmentation and conservation.

8947d2629b47.title: Biological pest control
8947d2629b47.sentence: Importation or classical biological control is the introduction of a pest's natural enemies to a new locale where they do not occur naturally.

e1f96f5ce6df.title: Biological pest control
e1f96f5ce6df.sentence: Augmentation involves the supplemental release of natural enemies that occur in a particular area, boosting the naturally occurring populations there.

902cf71fb180.title: Biological pest control
902cf71fb180.sentence: In inoculative release, small numbers of the control agents are released at intervals to allow them to reproduce, in the hope of setting up longer-term control and thus keeping the pest down to a low level, constituting prevention rather than cure.

58dc2f0320f8.title: Biological pest control
58dc2f0320f8.sentence: In inundative release, in contrast, large numbers are released in the hope of rapidly reducing a damaging pest population, correcting a problem that has already arisen.

0e2a5253c14c.title: Biological pest control
0e2a5253c14c.sentence: Early instances were often unofficial and not based on research; some introduced species subsequently became serious pests themselves.

19fb68112d3a.title: Integrated pest management
19fb68112d3a.sentence: Augmentative biocontrol involves increasing natural enemies and pathogens such as predators, parasitoids or microbes, so that they can fight pests and diseases in an area on a timely basis.

01b5ab1b6998.title: Biological pest control
01b5ab1b6998.sentence: The conservation of existing natural enemies in an environment is the third method of biological pest control.

1286d9fae9df.title: Biological pest control
1286d9fae9df.sentence: Natural enemies are already adapted to the habitat and to the target pest, and their conservation can be simple and cost-effective, as when nectar-producing crop plants are grown in the borders of rice fields.

c2a8001f8103.title: Biological pest control
c2a8001f8103.sentence: These provide nectar to support parasitoids and predators of planthopper pests and have been demonstrated to be so effective (reducing pest densities by 10- or even 100-fold) that farmers sprayed 70% less insecticides and enjoyed yields boosted by 5%.

859724f41b7b.title: Biological pest control
859724f41b7b.sentence: Cropping systems can be modified to favor natural enemies, a practice sometimes referred to as habitat manipulation.

56b7c2ab457c.title: Biological pest control
56b7c2ab457c.sentence: Providing a suitable habitat, such as a shelterbelt, hedgerow, or beetle bank where beneficial insects such as parasitoidal wasps can live and reproduce, can help ensure the survival of populations of natural enemies.

dd476f9f5a66.title: Biological pest control
dd476f9f5a66.sentence: Predators of aphids were similarly found to be present in tussock grasses by field boundary hedges in England, but they spread too slowly to reach the centers of fields.

cf00f565c81a.title: Biological pest control
cf00f565c81a.sentence: Control was improved by planting a meter-wide strip of tussock grasses in field centers, enabling aphid predators to overwinter there.

853b536bc5ec.title: Biological pest control
853b536bc5ec.sentence: Biological control can affect biodiversity through predation, parasitism, pathogenicity, competition, or other attacks on non-target species.

ee47b3fe5ffa.title: Biological pest control
ee47b3fe5ffa.sentence: An introduced control does not always target only the intended pest species; it can also target native species.

8641482f64db.title: Biological pest control
8641482f64db.sentence: Vertebrate animals tend to be generalist feeders, and seldom make good biological control agents; many of the classic cases of "biocontrol gone awry" involve vertebrates.

34808cded6ec.title: Biological pest control
34808cded6ec.sentence: 102 toads were obtained from Hawaii and bred in captivity to increase their numbers until they were released into the sugar cane fields of the tropic north in 1935.

5fdcb953ebf9.title: Biological pest control
5fdcb953ebf9.sentence: It was later discovered that the toads could not jump very high and so were unable to eat the cane beetles which stayed on the upper stalks of the cane plants.

37d51c138246.title: Biological pest control
37d51c138246.sentence: However, the toad thrived by feeding on other insects and soon spread very rapidly; it took over native amphibian habitat and brought foreign disease to native toads and frogs, dramatically reducing their populations.

d141aab8e3ba.title: Nursery habitat
d141aab8e3ba.sentence: In marine environments, a nursery habitat is a subset of all habitats where juveniles of a species occur, having a greater level of productivity per unit area than other juvenile habitats.

a6d74cf54939.title: Nursery habitat
a6d74cf54939.sentence: The nursery habitat hypothesis states that the contribution per unit area of a nursery habitat is greater than for other habitats used by juveniles for the species.

c6f6f01cbb5e.title: Nursery habitat
c6f6f01cbb5e.sentence: Mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass are typical nursery habitats for a range of marine species.

cbd9f262cb4f.title: Nursery habitat
cbd9f262cb4f.sentence: If we are unable to preserve nursery habitats, recruitment of juveniles into adult populations may decline, reducing population numbers and compromising the survival of species for biodiversity and human harvesting.

217e43ea7960.title: Nursery habitat
217e43ea7960.sentence: While density may be an indicator of productivity, it is suggested that alone, density does not adequately provide evidence of the role of a habitat as a nursery.

7cb03bfdab72.title: Nursery habitat
7cb03bfdab72.sentence: Recruitment biomass from juvenile to adult population is the best measure of movement between the two habitats.

ac6ff9359ee4.title: Bioprospecting
ac6ff9359ee4.section: Legal and political aspects > Bioprospecting contracts
ac6ff9359ee4.sentence: Bioprospecting contracts lay down the rules of benefit sharing between researchers and countries, and can bring royalties to lesser-developed countries.

af1c48cfb0d2.title: Bioprospecting
af1c48cfb0d2.section: Legal and political aspects > Convention on Biological Diversity
af1c48cfb0d2.sentence: The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) came into force in 1993.

31254af12b69.title: Bioprospecting
31254af12b69.section: Legal and political aspects > Convention on Biological Diversity
31254af12b69.sentence: It secured rights to control access to genetic resources for the countries in which those resources are located.

95a8908f6617.title: Bioprospecting
95a8908f6617.section: Legal and political aspects > Bioprospecting contracts
95a8908f6617.sentence: The requirements for bioprospecting as set by CBD has created a new branch of international patent and trade law, bioprospecting contracts.

433f05374d6c.title: Bioprospecting
433f05374d6c.section: Legal and political aspects > Bioprospecting contracts
433f05374d6c.sentence: However, although these contracts are based on prior informed consent and compensation (unlike biopiracy), every owner or carrier of an indigenous knowledge and resources are not always consulted or compensated, as it would be difficult to ensure every individual is included.

c66f20935e82.title: Biodiversity
c66f20935e82.sentence: Biodiverse countries that allow bioprospecting or collection of natural products, expect a share of the benefits rather than allowing the individual or institution that discovers/exploits the resource to capture them privately.

cd46349c4d3e.title: Soil formation
cd46349c4d3e.sentence: They are: parent material, climate, topography (relief), soil organisms, and time.

13d006c8c23d.title: Soil formation
13d006c8c23d.sentence: When reordered to climate, organisms, relief, parent material, and time, they form the acronym CLORPT.

638bc4dcc703.title: Soil formation
638bc4dcc703.sentence: Climate is the dominant factor in soil formation, and soils show the distinctive characteristics of the climate zones in which they form, with a feedback to climate through transfer of carbon stocked in soil horizons back to the atmosphere.

db81ae67921d.title: Soil formation
db81ae67921d.sentence: Steep slopes encourage rapid soil loss by erosion and allow less rainfall to enter the soil before running off and hence, little mineral deposition in lower profiles (illuviation).

22da4bb26fe7.title: Soil formation
22da4bb26fe7.sentence: Therefore, soils on steep terrain tend to have rather shallow, poorly developed profiles in comparison to soils on nearby, more level sites.

39b4b22cd004.title: Soil formation
39b4b22cd004.sentence: Plants hold soil against erosion, and accumulated plant material build soil humus levels.

05f0569f7bd3.title: Soil formation
05f0569f7bd3.sentence: Animals serve to decompose plant materials and mix soil through bioturbation.

aaab0ae4baa1.title: Soil formation
aaab0ae4baa1.sentence: Soil is the most speciose (species-rich) ecosystem on Earth, but the vast majority of organisms in soil are microbes, a great many of which have not been described so far.

3455a2d45ecd.title: Soil formation
3455a2d45ecd.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
3455a2d45ecd.sentence: American soil scientist Hans Jenny published in 1941 a state equation for the factors influencing soil formation:

c0eac27a0cab.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
c0eac27a0cab.sentence: Jenny's state equation in Factors of Soil Formation differs from Vasily Dokuchaev's equation, treating time (t) as a factor, adding topographic relief (r), and pointedly leaving the ellipsis open for more factors (state variables) to be added as our understanding becomes more refined.

d80e798fedef.title: Soil formation
d80e798fedef.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
d80e798fedef.sentence: The empirical method is still mostly employed today, and soil formation can be defined by varying a single factor and keeping the other factors constant.

8e2ebfdd131a.title: Soil formation
8e2ebfdd131a.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
8e2ebfdd131a.sentence: This had led to the development of empirical models to describe pedogenesis, such as climofunctions, biofunctions, topofunctions, lithofunctions, and chronofunctions.

271ddae48874.title: Soil formation
271ddae48874.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
271ddae48874.sentence: Since Jenny published his formulation in 1941, it has been used by innumerable soil surveyors all over the world as a qualitative list for understanding the factors that may be important for producing the soil pattern within a region.

993901f74f66.title: Pollination management
993901f74f66.sentence: Pollination management is the horticultural practice that accomplishes or enhances pollination of a crop, to improve yield or quality, by understanding of the particular crop's pollination needs, and by knowledgeable management of pollenizers, pollinators, and pollination conditions.

9d73aa10a211.title: Pollination management
9d73aa10a211.sentence: Other insects are commercially available that are more efficient, like the blue orchard bee for fruit and nut trees; local bumblebees better specialized for some other crops; hand pollination that is essential for production of hybrid seeds and some greenhouse situations; and even pollination machines.

ec7d560274e6.title: Pollination management
ec7d560274e6.sentence: This has been called pollination limitation (PL) and may lead to a reduction in yield due to insufficient or inefficient pollination.

d55d6e0072d1.title: Pollination management
d55d6e0072d1.sentence: However, PL has declined by 50% between 1950 and the 2010s, apparently mainly because of pollination management, that is, because many fields are now supplemented with managed pollinators.

298bb6baf2c1.title: Pollination management
298bb6baf2c1.sentence: The increasing size of fields and orchards (monoculture) increases the importance of pollination management.

bb30ab12d4f9.title: Pollination management
bb30ab12d4f9.sentence: While honeybees may visit dozens of different kinds of flowers, diluting the orchard pollen they carry, the Blue orchard bee will visit only the intended tree, producing a much higher fertilization rate.

a732634fc5a0.title: Pollination management
a732634fc5a0.sentence: The focus on the specific tree also makes the orchard bee 100 times more efficient at pollinating, per bee.

f4a12cbdcfe1.title: Pollination management
f4a12cbdcfe1.sentence: In the 1950s when the woods were full of wild bee trees, and beehives were normally kept on most South Carolina farms, a farmer who grew ten acres (4.0 hectares) of watermelons would be a large grower and probably had all the pollination needed.

bedcb6fd3e06.title: Pollination management
bedcb6fd3e06.sentence: But today's grower may grow 200 acres (81 hectares), and, if lucky, there might be one bee tree left within range.

29ddb297ff08.title: Pollination management
29ddb297ff08.sentence: The only option in the current economy is to bring beehives to the field during blossom time.

f5b28e19ee57.title: Pollinator decline
f5b28e19ee57.sentence: Although the existence of pollinator decline can be difficult to determine, a number of possible reasons for the theoretical concept have been proposed, such as exposure to pathogens, parasites, and pesticides; habitat destruction; climate change; market forces; intra- and interspecific competition with native and invasive species; and genetic alterations.

645b1ca80a26.title: Pollinator decline
645b1ca80a26.sentence: - Pesticides: Synthetic pesticides are a primary driver of pollinator decline, with neonicotinoids the most widespread and found to act as a major toxin and cause neurological and immune disorders in bees and other insect pollinator species, as well as insectivorous birds, thereby contributing to pollinator declines.

6c0bd949b8fe.title: Pollinator decline
6c0bd949b8fe.sentence: Pollutants such as ozone, hydroxyl, and nitrate radicals bond quickly with volatile scent molecules of flowers, which consequently travel shorter distances intact.

fe1c3cfd80bf.title: Pollinator decline
fe1c3cfd80bf.sentence: Pollinators must thus travel longer distances to find flowers.

d9a43729b1ab.title: Pollinator decline
d9a43729b1ab.sentence: Climate change can cause bees to emerge at times in the year when flowering plants were not available.

36259fb0e86e.title: Pollinator decline
36259fb0e86e.sentence: A 2021 global assessment of the drivers of pollinator decline found that "global policy responses should focus on reducing pressure from changes in land cover and configuration, land management and pesticides, as these were considered very important drivers in most regions".

63e99d5f0e5e.title: Pollinator decline
63e99d5f0e5e.sentence: According to their model, the size of the effect that pollinator decline had on a population depends on the local diet, and vitamin A is the most likely nutrient to become deficient, as it is already deficient.

1ab487cf9c28.title: Pollinator decline
1ab487cf9c28.sentence: One study estimated that 70% of dietary vitamin A worldwide is found in crops that are animal pollinated, as well as 55% of folate.

d61b05f16627.title: Pollinator decline
d61b05f16627.sentence: Another 2015 study also modeled what would happen should 100% of pollinators die off.

64b415f704fc.title: Pollinator decline
64b415f704fc.sentence: In that scenario, 71 million people in low-income countries would become deficient in vitamin A, and the vitamin A intake of 2.2 billion people who are already consuming less than the recommended amount would further decline.

161dc4aef9cb.title: Pollinator decline

baa1db39c83d.title: Pollinator decline
baa1db39c83d.sentence: In a less extreme scenario wherein only 50% of pollinators die off, 700,000 additional deaths would occur each year, as well as 13.2 million disability-adjusted years.

60b73edbbcdf.title: Ecological values of mangroves
60b73edbbcdf.sentence: Mangrove ecosystems represent natural capital capable of producing a wide range of goods and services for coastal environments and communities and society as a whole.

3652033dfc9b.title: Ecological values of mangroves
3652033dfc9b.sentence: Some of these outputs, such as timber, are freely exchanged in formal markets.

e4467fbda2b9.title: Ecological values of mangroves
e4467fbda2b9.sentence: Value is determined in these markets through exchange and quantified in terms of price.

ead536189d68.title: Ecological values of mangroves
ead536189d68.sentence: Mangroves provide nursery habitat for many wildlife species, including commercial fish and crustaceans, and thus contribute to sustaining the local abundance of fish and shellfish populations.

bb6928bce254.title: Ecological values of mangroves
bb6928bce254.sentence: An estimated 75 percent of the commercially caught prawns and fish in Queensland, Australia, depend on mangroves for part of their life cycles and on nutrients exported from the mangroves to other ecosystems.

b8a88ca8390d.title: Ecological values of mangroves
b8a88ca8390d.sentence: They also help to maintain water quality via nutrient cycling.

3c5be90fddfa.title: Ecological values of mangroves
3c5be90fddfa.sentence: Furthermore, they slow water, encouraging sediment to settle down, and also serve as breakwaters in storms or tsunamis, protecting the coasts.

db852291b509.title: Ecological values of mangroves
db852291b509.sentence: Mangrove forests absorb carbon from the atmosphere and store it in their biomass and in the waterlogged soils in which they grow, contributing to coastal blue carbon stocks.

1a2f419777c4.title: Ecological values of mangroves
1a2f419777c4.section: Ecological values > Endangered mangrove coastlines and human development
1a2f419777c4.sentence: In just the last decade, at least 35 percent of the world's mangroves have been destroyed, exceeding the rate of the disappearance of tropical rainforests.

fc3c6c9d392c.title: Ecological values of mangroves
fc3c6c9d392c.sentence: Economic arguments carry the greatest weight in conservation and management of mangroves.

10ca3abe814c.title: Ecological values of mangroves
10ca3abe814c.sentence: However, the true economic value of mangrove diversity and natural resources is difficult to measure and important ecological processes and functions undervalued.

3c884844df63.title: Biodiversity
3c884844df63.section: Role and benefits of biodiversity > Ecosystem services
3c884844df63.sentence: - Regulating services which are those that lessen environmental change (e.g.: climate regulation, pest/disease control)

1d7868a85550.title: Mangrove restoration
1d7868a85550.sentence: In most of these regions mangroves provide many services including; shelter, climate regulation through carbon sequestration, decrease coastal erosion, create a link between terrestrial and marine ecosystems, and maintain water quality along the coast.

0a2a5cf3f325.title: Tropical rainforest
0a2a5cf3f325.sentence: They are crucial for global ecological functions, including carbon sequestration and climate regulation.

dfd5c564c227.title: Marine coastal ecosystem
dfd5c564c227.sentence: These coastal seas are highly productive systems, providing an array of ecosystem services to humankind, such as processing of nutrient effluents from land and climate regulation.

961b7c0fdc34.title: Urban forestry
961b7c0fdc34.sentence: Trees are important in regulating ecosystem processes; they contribute to filtering air pollution, microclimate regulation, carbon dioxide sequestration, and reducing climate change.

76b06c63438e.title: Corporate sustainability
76b06c63438e.sentence: Natural capital not only includes the responsible consumption of renewable and non-renewable resources, but also the preservation of vital ecosystem services such as climate regulation and water purification, which have no viable substitutes.

66b7d9864203.title: Regime shift
66b7d9864203.sentence: On the global realm, the faster retreating of the arctic ice sheet in summer time is reinforcing climate warming through the albedo feedback, potentially affecting sea water levels and climate regulation worldwide.

45837c5f40df.title: Gross ecosystem product
45837c5f40df.sentence: GEP addresses this oversight by providing a summary monetary measure of the contributions of ecosystem services using both market and non-market valuation, including material services like livestock and fishery products, regulating services such as climate regulation or pollination, and cultural services like tourism.

01ab81fed37b.title: Ecological values of mangroves
01ab81fed37b.section: Ecological values > Improving coastal water quality
01ab81fed37b.sentence: Mangroves maintain coastal water quality by abiotic and biotic retention, removal, and cycling of nutrients, pollutants, and particulate matter from land-based sources, filtering these materials from water before they reach seaward coral reef and seagrass habitats.

d16a5e45bd52.title: Ecological values of mangroves
d16a5e45bd52.section: Ecological values > Improving coastal water quality
d16a5e45bd52.sentence: Mangrove root systems slow water flow, facilitating the deposition of sediment.

20217b649ec3.title: Ecological values of mangroves
20217b649ec3.section: Ecological values > Improving coastal water quality
20217b649ec3.sentence: Toxins and nutrients can be bound to sediment particles or within the molecular lattice of clay particles and are removed during sediment deposition.

44b3dffe3ba0.title: Ecological values of mangroves
44b3dffe3ba0.section: Ecological values > Improving coastal water quality
44b3dffe3ba0.sentence: Compared with the expense of constructing a wastewater treatment plant, mangroves are commonly selected as receiving areas of effluent.

6a783f31fa64.title: Ecological values of mangroves
6a783f31fa64.section: Ecological values > Improving coastal water quality
6a783f31fa64.sentence: Increasingly the notion of specifically constructed mangrove wetlands is being adopted and used for treatment of aquaculture and sewage effluents.

65b0288a21cc.title: Ecological values of mangroves
65b0288a21cc.section: Ecological values > Improving coastal water quality
65b0288a21cc.sentence: For instance, terrigenous sediments and nutrients carried by freshwater runoff are first filtered by coastal forests, then by mangrove wetlands, and finally by seagrass beds before reaching coral reefs.

c6dbc62f46f0.title: Ecological values of mangroves
c6dbc62f46f0.section: Ecological values > Improving coastal water quality
c6dbc62f46f0.sentence: The existence and health of coral reefs are dependent on the buffering capacity of these shoreward ecosystems, which support the oligotrophic conditions needed by coral reefs to limit overgrowth by algae.

34bffad3fb42.title: Forest restoration
34bffad3fb42.sentence: - environmental protection particularly watershed services (e.g. reduced soil erosion, lower landslide risk, flood/drought mitigation etc.),

13ea43d13900.title: Payment for ecosystem services
13ea43d13900.sentence: These are climate change mitigation, watershed services and biodiversity conservation, and demand for these services in particular is predicted to continue to grow as time goes on.

bb0a853770a9.title: Payment for ecosystem services
bb0a853770a9.section: Examples > Central and South America > Costa Rica
bb0a853770a9.sentence: It explicitly recognized four environmental services: mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions, hydrological services, biodiversity protection, and provision of scenic beauty.

25f44a40cfe4.title: Reduced-impact logging
25f44a40cfe4.sentence: As international markets for carbon, hydrological services, and biodiversity continue to develop, forests managed with RIL techniques may gain recognition and financial incentives for their conservation efforts.

044a302f3f51.title: Well-being
044a302f3f51.sentence: Well-being is what is intrinsically good for a person.

ab5449667c38.title: Well-being
ab5449667c38.sentence: Also called welfare and quality of life, it is a measure of how well life is going for someone.

2bc2be60686b.title: Well-being
2bc2be60686b.sentence: In the broadest sense, it covers the balance of all positive and negative aspects of a person's life.

5e5ba0bc547e.title: Well-being
5e5ba0bc547e.sentence: More narrowly, it refers only to positive degrees and contrasts with ill-being, which denotes negative ones.

c7157c75f957.title: Well-being
c7157c75f957.sentence: For example, money and medicine can contribute to well-being as external causes but are not themselves forms of well-being.

37008db5a902.title: Well-being
37008db5a902.sentence: For example, there is wide agreement that positive emotions, achievements, interpersonal relationships, and health typically contribute to well-being in some form, despite academic disagreement about their precise roles.

cdffcb93b478.title: Well-being
cdffcb93b478.sentence: Individual well-being concerns the quality of life of a particular person and is the main focus of disciplines such as psychology and some schools of philosophy.

713f1b61ed77.title: Well-being
713f1b61ed77.sentence: Community well-being applies the concept of well-being to a group of people.

e9e0cb34df0d.title: Well-being
e9e0cb34df0d.sentence: It encompasses a broad range of economic, social, environmental, and cultural aspects that influence how the community functions and thrives while ensuring that the community's needs are fulfilled.

aabe27e9eb4b.title: Well-being
aabe27e9eb4b.sentence: Welfare economics studies the influence of economic activity on well-being.

7da8f9e02633.title: Well-being
7da8f9e02633.sentence: One of its primary goals is to develop standards for evaluating and choosing between competing policy proposals based on their potential benefit to well-being.

aea270d28568.title: Well-being
aea270d28568.sentence: This field uses metrics such as distribution of income, gross domestic product, consumer surplus, and compensating variation.

35198846e955.title: Anthropocentrism
35198846e955.sentence: Indeed, defenders of anthropocentrism concerned with the ecological crisis contend that the maintenance of a healthy, sustainable environment is necessary for human well-being as opposed to for its own sake.

4d1fd1a3323c.title: Well-being
4d1fd1a3323c.sentence: The study of well-being originated in antiquity, often in the form of discussions on how to lead a good life.

0c7f91d2b4fe.title: Recreation
0c7f91d2b4fe.sentence: Recreation is an activity of leisure, often done for enjoyment, amusement, or pleasure and are considered to be "fun".

c774ffcbf495.title: Recreation
c774ffcbf495.sentence: The "need to do something for recreation" is an essential element of human biology and psychology.

85f6b6a9bb6d.title: Recreation
85f6b6a9bb6d.sentence: People spend their time on activities of daily living, work, sleep, social duties and leisure, the latter time being free from prior commitments to physiologic or social needs, a prerequisite of recreation.

3182d086aaf9.title: Recreation
3182d086aaf9.sentence: Other factors that account for an increased role of recreation are affluence, population trends, and increased commercialization of recreational offerings.

e78a4002a1bf.title: Recreation
e78a4002a1bf.sentence: Public space such as parks and beaches are essential venues for many recreational activities and Tourism has recognized that many visitors are specifically attracted by recreational offerings.

e839962ab69f.title: Ecosystem service
e839962ab69f.sentence: Lastly, their cultural services include recreation and tourism.

229a50aab645.title: Recreation
229a50aab645.sentence: Leisure is a human right under the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

4a6c493acc17.title: Outdoor recreation
4a6c493acc17.sentence: Outdoor recreation or outdoor activity refers to recreation done outside, most commonly in natural settings.

ff828c2b0974.title: Outdoor recreation
ff828c2b0974.sentence: These activities can include fishing, hunting, backpacking, walking and horseback riding — and can be completed individually or collectively.

80684348e894.title: Outdoor recreation
80684348e894.sentence: Other traditional examples of outdoor recreational activities include hiking, camping, mountaineering, cycling, dog walking, canoeing, caving, kayaking, rafting, rock climbing, running, sailing, skiing, sky diving and surfing.

354aee85b8c5.title: Outdoor recreation
354aee85b8c5.sentence: Outdoor recreation is typically pursued for purposes of physical exercise, general wellbeing, and spiritual renewal.

c23b57ae9407.title: Outdoor recreation
c23b57ae9407.sentence: Competition generally is less stressed than in organized individual or team sports.

2a55fbe6c0dc.title: Outdoor recreation
2a55fbe6c0dc.sentence: Outdoor recreation often occurs in sparsely populated areas with mountains, lakes, rivers, scenic views, and rugged terrain.

5d0101e160e5.title: Outdoor recreation
5d0101e160e5.sentence: According to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, outdoor recreation accounted for $696.7 billion in current-dollar value added, or 2.4 percent of U.S. gross domestic product (GDP), in 2024.

7760428952ea.title: Outdoor recreation
7760428952ea.section: Education > Outdoor education in the United States
7760428952ea.sentence: Studies have shown that outdoor recreation programs can be beneficial to a student's well-being and stress levels in terms of calming and soothing the mind.

fc6b5d200425.title: Forest management
fc6b5d200425.sentence: Foresters manage forests to provide a variety of objectives including direct extraction of raw material, outdoor recreation, conservation, hunting and aesthetics.

224f6581a983.title: Biophilia hypothesis
224f6581a983.sentence: The biophilia hypothesis (also called BET) suggests that humans possess an innate tendency to seek connections with nature and other forms of life.

3b41bb94db4e.title: Biophilia hypothesis
3b41bb94db4e.sentence: Edward O. Wilson introduced and popularized the hypothesis in his book, Biophilia (1984).

d24a845ab793.title: Biophilia hypothesis
d24a845ab793.sentence: The term was first used by Erich Fromm to describe a psychological orientation of being attracted to all that is alive and vital.

0058f9f5b538.title: Biophilia hypothesis
0058f9f5b538.sentence: The hypothesis has since been developed as part of theories of evolutionary psychology.

b5c3cc122564.title: Biophilia hypothesis
b5c3cc122564.sentence: One possible explanation is that our ancestors who had stronger connections to nature would hold an evolutionary advantage over less connected people as they would have better knowledge and therefore access to food, water, and shelter.

82d5ee7d503d.title: Biophilia hypothesis
82d5ee7d503d.sentence: In a broader and more general sense research has suggested that our modern urban environments are not suited for minds that evolved in natural environments.

72b18a7d1349.title: Biophilia hypothesis
72b18a7d1349.sentence: Similarly, the hypothesis helps explain why ordinary people care for and sometimes risk their lives to save domestic and wild animals, and keep plants and flowers in and around their homes.

073f074ecb9a.title: Biophilia hypothesis
073f074ecb9a.sentence: The concern for a lack of connection with the rest of nature outside of us, is that a stronger disregard for other plants, animals and less appealing wild areas could lead to further ecosystem degradation and species loss.

86c42d5eed99.title: Biophilia hypothesis
86c42d5eed99.sentence: Therefore, reestablishing a connection with nature has become more important in the field of conservation.

6a52b03ae610.title: Biophilia hypothesis
6a52b03ae610.sentence: Examples would be more available green spaces in and around cities, more classes that revolve around nature and implementing smart design for greener cities that integrate ecosystems into them such as biophilic cities.

7d8d1eb7c2aa.title: Biophilia hypothesis
7d8d1eb7c2aa.sentence: These cities can also become part of wildlife corridors to help with migrational and territorial needs of other animals.

96fcb1091631.title: Biophilic design
96fcb1091631.sentence: Fromm's approach was that of a psychoanalyst (a person who studies the unconscious mind) and presented a broad spectrum as he called biophilia a biologically normal instinct.

285b0ca57683.title: Biophilic design
285b0ca57683.sentence: The term has been used since by many scientists, and philosophers overall being adapted to several different areas of study.

4a483dc30d6b.title: Biophilic design
4a483dc30d6b.sentence: While biophilia refers to the inherent need to experience and love nature, biophobia is human's inherited fear of nature and animals.

9e519c797fae.title: Biophilic design
9e519c797fae.sentence: Some anxieties of the natural environment are inherited from threats seen in anthropocentric evolution: this includes fear of snakes, spiders, and blood.

10fa98ae9489.title: Biophilic design
10fa98ae9489.sentence: The word "biophilia" was first introduced by a psychoanalyst named Erich Fromm who stated that biophilia is the "passionate love of life and of all that is alive...whether in a person, a plant, an idea, or a social group" in his book The Anatomy of Human Destructiveness in 1973.

686dd461180d.title: Subjective well-being
686dd461180d.sentence: Subjective well-being (SWB) is a concept of well-being (happiness) that focuses on evaluations from the perspective of the people whose lives are being evaluated rather than from an objective viewpoint.

6bc683111231.title: Subjective well-being
6bc683111231.sentence: Ed Diener defined SWB in terms of three indicators of subjective well-being: frequent positive affect, infrequent negative affect, and cognitive evaluations such as life satisfaction.

2aca9a31414d.title: Subjective well-being
2aca9a31414d.sentence: There are three components of SWB: affect (hedonic measures), life satisfaction (cognitive measures), and eudaimonia (a sense of meaning and purpose).

aff02f7bcc5c.title: Subjective well-being
aff02f7bcc5c.sentence: - Life satisfaction is generally measured using a self-report method.

1e882040669e.title: Subjective well-being
1e882040669e.sentence: A common measurement for life satisfaction is questionnaires.

1b3b3a428fe4.title: Subjective well-being
1b3b3a428fe4.sentence: In SWB research, evaluating life satisfaction is the most common practice.

a73ec675f4bd.title: Subjective well-being
a73ec675f4bd.sentence: Due to the specific focus on the subjective aspects of well-being, definitions of SWB typically exclude objective conditions such as material conditions or health, although these can influence ratings of SWB.

7273cae8af7f.title: Subjective well-being
7273cae8af7f.sentence: In the top-down view, global features of personality influence the way a person perceives events.

677cdb0e4ca1.title: Subjective well-being
677cdb0e4ca1.sentence: From a bottom-up perspective, happiness is created from happy experiences.

4a6fd798f230.title: Subjective well-being
4a6fd798f230.sentence: Bottom-up approaches are based on the idea that there are universal basic human needs and that happiness results from their fulfilment.

74c29d600f56.title: Subjective well-being
74c29d600f56.sentence: Quality of social connections has a much stronger effect on SWB than the quantity of those connections.

4e61c93afe1e.title: Subjective well-being
4e61c93afe1e.sentence: Research shows that nature relatedness directly impacts an individual's SWB.

8dbc9c4eb617.title: Subjective well-being
8dbc9c4eb617.sentence: Greater nature relatedness in people reflects greater affect and life satisfaction when evaluating the impact of nature relatedness on the components of subjective well-being, and also reflects a strong correlation between nature relatedness and eudaimonic perspectives when environmental attitudes are part of the control group.

559b15138cc1.title: Subjective well-being
559b15138cc1.sentence: SWB is often used in appraising the wellbeing of populations.

7e8cdb9b0b2c.title: Aesthetics of nature
7e8cdb9b0b2c.sentence: Aesthetics of nature is a sub-field of philosophical ethics, and refers to the study of natural objects from their aesthetical perspective.

751a1d6c2087.title: Aesthetics of nature
751a1d6c2087.sentence: In the 18th and 19th century, the aesthetics of nature advanced the concepts of disinterestedness, the pictures, and the introduction of the idea of positive aesthetics.

d0a3632459ea.title: Aesthetics of nature
d0a3632459ea.sentence: Anthony Ashley-Cooper introduced the concept as a way of characterizing the notion of the aesthetic, later magnified by Francis Hutcheson, who expanded it to exclude personal and utilitarianism interests and associations of a more general nature from aesthetic experience.

5dd522102b6f.title: Aesthetics of nature
5dd522102b6f.sentence: Andrew Lothian's The Science of Scenery (2017) measures scenic beauty by having members of the public rate photographs of landscapes.

2189ea8aa30c.title: Aesthetics of nature
2189ea8aa30c.sentence: In a review, Rudi van Etteger objected that the method favours the picturesque over the sublime, and argued from the work of Allen Carlson, Arnold Berleant and Yuriko Saito that static photographs leave out bodily engagement with the environment and the value of everyday places.

aab2efd119e1.title: Aesthetics of nature

aab2efd119e1.sentence: According to Leopold, the three features of ecosystems that generate land ethic are integrity, stability and beauty.

3988ae7b0656.sentence: Fractal patterns offer the chance to enhance man-made spaces by introducing visually soothing natural designs.

16ea796aa689.sentence: Research indicates a preference for specific fractal complexities that resemble nature's patterns.

b0b2721ad5eb.title: Environmental philosophy
b0b2721ad5eb.sentence: It asks crucial questions about human environmental relations such as "What do we mean when we talk about nature?" "What is the value of the natural, that is non-human environment to us, or in itself?" "How should we respond to environmental challenges such as environmental degradation, pollution and climate change?" "How can we best understand the relationship between the natural world and human technology and development?" and "What is our place in the natural world?" Environmental philosophy includes environmental ethics, environmental aesthetics, ecofeminism, environmental hermeneutics, and environmental theology.

041f6fdff366.title: Nature connectedness
041f6fdff366.sentence: Nature connectedness is the extent to which individuals include nature as part of their identity.

c932da11f311.title: Nature connectedness
c932da11f311.sentence: Characteristics of nature connectedness are similar to those of a personality trait: nature connectedness is stable over time and across various situations.

0dacae77c893.title: Nature connectedness
0dacae77c893.section: Implications of feeling connected to nature
0dacae77c893.sentence: Although nature relatedness is a stable individual trait, it can change based on one's experience with nature, so that people feel more connected to nature (and are more concerned about nature) after exposure to nature Spending time in nature (and feeling connected to nature) may be one way to motivate environmentally friendly behaviours.

270b0bfeccdd.title: Nature connectedness
270b0bfeccdd.sentence: Schultz describes three components that make up the nature connectedness construct:

c85a7629ee5d.title: Nature connectedness
c85a7629ee5d.sentence: - The cognitive component is the core of nature connectedness and refers to how integrated one feels with nature.

03421cda01f3.title: Nature connectedness
03421cda01f3.sentence: - The affective component is an individual's sense of care for nature.

3957a58bf194.title: Nature connectedness
3957a58bf194.sentence: - The behavioral component is an individual's commitment to protect the natural environment.

fdb103812517.title: Nature connectedness
fdb103812517.sentence: This means that individuals who are highly connected to nature also report higher psychological well-being (i.e., greater acceptance of self), and social well-being (i.e., socially integrated).

8b8776e66698.title: Nature connectedness
8b8776e66698.sentence: So far, research has provided support for the assertion that nature connectedness (at a subjective level) is a reliable predictor of environmental behaviors.

d8fdd90a0392.title: Nature connectedness
d8fdd90a0392.sentence: For instance, nature relatedness was found to relate to concern for the environment, as people who scored high on nature relatedness were also more likely to belong to environmental organizations, and declare themselves environmentalists.

0028e04e5bbf.title: Nature connectedness
0028e04e5bbf.section: Implications of feeling connected to nature
0028e04e5bbf.sentence: As these authors and Kaplan explain, motivating ecological behaviours by increasing the connection to the natural environment may be more effective than establishing laws and rules that people have to follow.

87e9dbccc4ee.title: Nature connectedness
87e9dbccc4ee.section: Implications of feeling connected to nature
87e9dbccc4ee.sentence: - Increasing nature exposure and the accessibility to green space in cities may increase the well-being and ecological behaviors of individuals.
