8c4329cbdd2e.sentence: This highlights the importance of green space for policymakers and city planners.

99bc83e4fae9.title: Nature tourism
99bc83e4fae9.sentence: Nature tourism is tourism based on the natural attractions of an area, including its flora and fauna.

47722ca578ac.title: Nature tourism
47722ca578ac.sentence: It can overlap with wildlife tourism, and adventure tourism, and includes ecotourism, which specifically focuses environmental education and environmental conservation.

24607bde2a97.title: Nature tourism
24607bde2a97.sentence: It includes tourism for stargazing purposes, and many other variants, for example cycling tourism and birdwatching tourism.

985f970cc4ef.title: Nature tourism
985f970cc4ef.sentence: National parks has become closely associated with nature tourism.

79b6dbdc3e78.title: Nature tourism
79b6dbdc3e78.sentence: Nature tourism can have negative impacts on the environment, and practices exist for minimizing this.

d6de80967b03.title: Nature tourism
d6de80967b03.sentence: It can help promote conservation by making remaining natural areas more valuable to local communities and landowners.

5e8dfbb0e539.title: Sustainable tourism
5e8dfbb0e539.sentence: Sustainable tourism is a concept that covers the complete tourism experience, including concern for economic, social, and environmental issues as well as attention to improving tourists' experiences and addressing the needs of host communities.

10b34a43d926.title: Sustainable tourism
10b34a43d926.sentence: It has its roots in sustainable development and there can be some confusion as to what "sustainable tourism" means.

787358a60de8.title: Sustainable tourism
787358a60de8.sentence: Sustainable tourism is "an exceedingly complex concept with varied definitions due to different interpretations of the meaning and use of the concept".

f3bf51e1ba0d.title: Sustainable tourism
f3bf51e1ba0d.section: Background > Comparison with conventional tourism and mass tourism
f3bf51e1ba0d.sentence: As one of the world's largest and fastest-growing industries, this continuous growth will place great stress on remaining biologically diverse habitats and Indigenous cultures.

f2580321298a.title: Sustainable tourism
f2580321298a.sentence: Local communities benefit from sustainable tourism through economic development, job creation, and infrastructure development.

ef34d0822a12.title: Sustainable tourism
ef34d0822a12.sentence: One important factor to consider in any ecologically sensitive or remote area or an area new to tourism is that of carrying capacity.

16ffda9095ea.title: Sustainable tourism
16ffda9095ea.sentence: Without travel there is no tourism, so the concept of sustainable tourism is tightly linked to a concept of sustainable transport.

8f16d2f4d651.title: Sustainable tourism
8f16d2f4d651.sentence: Two relevant considerations are tourism's reliance on fossil fuels and tourism's effect on climate change.

6a9457c3155d.title: Sustainable tourism
6a9457c3155d.sentence: GSTC launched the GSTC Criteria, a global standard for sustainable travel and tourism, which includes criteria and performance indicators for destinations, tour operators and hotels.

86605a99ea5e.title: Sustainable tourism
86605a99ea5e.sentence: The GSTC Criteria serve as the international standard for certification agencies (the organizations that would inspect a tourism product, and certify them as a sustainable company).

d2c01e67e51c.title: Sustainable tourism
d2c01e67e51c.sentence: Many critics view the extractive nature of "sustainable tourism" as an oxymoron, as it is fundamentally unable to continue indefinitely.

b37cf0ac5177.title: Sustainable tourism
b37cf0ac5177.sentence: Historically, the movement toward sustainable tourism through responsible tourism emerged following the environmental awareness that rose out of the 1960s and 1970s amid a growing phenomenon of "mass tourism".

5123e68381e8.title: Sustainable tourism
5123e68381e8.sentence: In 1973, the European Travel Commission initiated a multilateral effort to advance environmentally sound tourism and development.

57bf95406fe1.title: Ecotourism
57bf95406fe1.sentence: Ecotourism is a form of nature-oriented tourism intended to contribute to the conservation of the natural environment, generally defined as being minimally impactful, and contributing to both conservation and environmental education.

910afa86114e.title: Ecotourism
910afa86114e.sentence: The definition sometimes also includes being financially beneficial to the host community or making conservation financially possible.

f2b16db80102.title: Ecotourism
f2b16db80102.sentence: Ecotourism is a sub-component of the field of sustainable tourism.

31149592fc1a.title: Ecotourism
31149592fc1a.sentence: In contrast to nature tourism and sustainable tourism in general, ecotourism is also usually intended to foster a greater appreciation in tourists of natural habitats and threats they experience, as well as local culture.

85b42aa3227e.title: Ecotourism
85b42aa3227e.section: Risks and benefits > Benefits > Potential economic benefits
85b42aa3227e.sentence: - Generates revenue (related to visitor expenditures) and creates employment that is directly related to the sector

53b692c8bb43.title: Ecotourism
53b692c8bb43.section: Risks and benefits > Benefits > Direct benefits
53b692c8bb43.sentence: - Provides funds to manage and expand protected areas.

408ebb3b4bf9.title: Ecotourism
408ebb3b4bf9.section: Risks and benefits > Benefits > Direct benefits

49911914150f.title: Ecotourism
49911914150f.section: Risks and benefits > Benefits > Direct benefits
49911914150f.sentence: - Incentive to rehabilitate modified environments and lands

e1ab25d67d48.title: Ecotourism
e1ab25d67d48.section: Risks and benefits > Benefits > Potential socio-cultural benefits
e1ab25d67d48.sentence: For example, 70% of the money made at national parks in South Africa comes directly from tourism revenue.

dda451ac5507.title: Ecotourism
dda451ac5507.sentence: Ecological risk: Ecotourism activities, or merely the presence of travelers in a particular region or location, may negatively impact the ecological integrity of protected areas.

aadee4f6d31f.title: Ecotourism
aadee4f6d31f.sentence: For example, like other forms of tourism, ecotourism may result in friction between tourists and local community members, and may increase the cost of rent, rates, and property values, thereby marginalizing local community members.

9c3f1f761755.title: Ecotourism
9c3f1f761755.sentence: Health risks: Ecotourism carries known health risks for both tourists and local people, along with wildlife and ecosystems.

e65eb862a3a0.title: Ecotourism
e65eb862a3a0.sentence: Most forms of ecotourism are owned by foreign investors and corporations that provide few benefits to the local people.

21d1daf81695.title: Ecotourism
21d1daf81695.sentence: An overwhelming majority of profits are put into the pockets of investors instead of reinvestment into the local economy or environmental protection leading to further environmental degradation.

45b15bdec01b.title: Ecotourism
45b15bdec01b.sentence: Like most long-distance travel, ecotourism often depends on air transportation, which contributes to climate change.

5dc35d50fe89.title: Ecotourism
5dc35d50fe89.sentence: However (according to Buckley), very few organizations make a net-positive impact on the environment overall.

f7b7afc7ad28.title: Ecotourism
f7b7afc7ad28.sentence: Because the regulations of ecotourism may be poorly implemented, ecologically destructive greenwashed operations like underwater hotels and helicopter tours can be categorized as ecotourism along with canoeing, camping, photography, and wildlife observation.

650f31dcffd5.title: Ecotourism
650f31dcffd5.sentence: According to the Oxford English Dictionary, ecotour was first recorded in 1973 and ecotourism, "probably after ecotour", in 1982.

d41b81f0eb41.title: Ecotourism
d41b81f0eb41.section: Improving sustainability > Small scale, slow growth, and local control
d41b81f0eb41.sentence: The theory of underdevelopment tourism describes the behavior of multinational corporations that control the development of ecotourism and reap the main benefits, which may lead to a loss of development ownership by local communities.

a2cb950af719.title: Ecotourism
a2cb950af719.section: Improving sustainability > Small scale, slow growth, and local control
a2cb950af719.sentence: This may limit the control of local communities over natural resources and raise discussions about the unequal distribution of ownership and benefits of tourism resources.

185bda99ac16.title: Ecotourism
185bda99ac16.section: Improving sustainability > Small scale, slow growth, and local control
185bda99ac16.sentence: These corporations finance and profit from the development of large-scale ecotourism that causes excessive environmental degradation, loss of traditional culture and way of life, and exploitation of local labor.

20f8fe44e648.title: Well-being
20f8fe44e648.sentence: A traditionally influential approach categorizes theories of well-being into hedonism, desire theories, and objective list theories.

c8c4cfd0d29a.title: Well-being
c8c4cfd0d29a.sentence: Hedonism about well-being, also called prudential hedonism, holds that pleasure and pain are the only factors of well-being.

c25a6324886c.title: Well-being
c25a6324886c.sentence: According to desire theories, the satisfaction of desires is the only source of well-being.

93d853639e65.title: Well-being
93d853639e65.sentence: This means that individuals have well-being when they get what they want.

2ce7bb0683dd.title: Well-being
2ce7bb0683dd.section: Theories of well-being > Objective list theories
2ce7bb0683dd.sentence: These factors can include subjective components, like pleasure and desire-satisfaction, but also encompass objective factors that enhance a person's well-being independent of whether they subjectively care about them.

663d98382629.title: Well-being
663d98382629.section: Theories of well-being > Objective list theories
663d98382629.sentence: Objective list theorists have proposed diverse lists of items to cover a wide variety of elements contributing to well-being, such as health, friendship, achievement, knowledge, and autonomy.

e5a3a517f27d.title: Well-being
e5a3a517f27d.sentence: As the father of classical utilitarianism, Jeremy Bentham (1748–1832) proposed the felicific calculus as a method to measure, compare, and aggregate degrees of pleasure and pain, considering factors such as their intensity and duration.

3e92f887ee6c.title: Nature exposure and mental health
3e92f887ee6c.sentence: Nature exposure and mental health refers to the association between an individual interacting with natural environments and its effect on the individual's mental health.

c4ed763004ce.title: Nature exposure and mental health
c4ed763004ce.sentence: Most studies consider any interaction with nature as exposure, such as a hike, being in a forest or a place with water (e.g. lake, beach), going on a walk in a park, etc.

1e1e4a735cfe.title: Nature exposure and mental health
1e1e4a735cfe.sentence: Research on the exposure to natural environments show that nature strengthens our mental health in multiple ways, such as lowering stress and improving mood.

8d97f7992533.title: Nature exposure and mental health
8d97f7992533.sentence: Moreover, there is evidence that demonstrates that the contact with nature is associated with increases in happiness, subjective well-being, positive affect, positive social interactions and a sense of meaning and purpose in life, as well as decreases in mental distress.

a6ec9abd66cd.title: Nature exposure and mental health
a6ec9abd66cd.sentence: In regards to children, in Denmark there was a study done throughout eighteen years that analyzed the comparison between children ages 0–10 years old that lived in neighborhoods with more green space and children from lower levels of exposure to green space.

9080deacd3a5.title: Nature exposure and mental health
9080deacd3a5.sentence: It was found that the children from the higher level of green space had 55% less risk of developing multiple psychiatric disorders, such as depression, schizophrenia, substance disorder, eating disorders, and mood disorders.

f4f075440f83.title: Nature exposure and mental health
f4f075440f83.sentence: A 10-year UK study found that both the greeness of people's home surroundings (within 300m of their home) and their access to green and blue spaces nearby (such as parks, lakes and beaches) both reduced people's risk of anxiety and depression.

17b65ad6845e.title: Nature exposure and mental health
17b65ad6845e.sentence: Some of the main benefits that studies have found are improvement on working memory performance, improved attention, cognitive flexibility, and attentional-control tasks.

38e0b054fb9c.title: Nature exposure and mental health
38e0b054fb9c.sentence: In contrast, exposure to urban environments has been linked to attention deficits.

32e11777d37a.title: Nature exposure and mental health
32e11777d37a.sentence: Short periods of nature exposure can also cause cognitive benefits, including exposure just through images.

d305c5f9c124.title: Nature exposure and mental health
d305c5f9c124.sentence: Midway through the task participants had micro-breaks of 40 seconds in which they would see either a city scene with a flowering meadow green roof or a bare concrete roof.

13a488e831a5.title: Nature exposure and mental health
13a488e831a5.sentence: The participants that viewed the green roof made significantly less omission errors and showed more consistent responding to the task compared to participants who viewed the concrete roof according to the study.

dfac9771c159.title: Nature exposure and mental health
dfac9771c159.sentence: Studies show that the contact of human beings with nature has decreased with the contemporary lifestyle of being most of the time indoors and with increasing time spent on screens.

aab78cc2727d.title: Nature exposure and mental health
aab78cc2727d.sentence: As a consequence, therapists use nature in their treatments to improve mental or physical health.

f89ef3137347.title: Nature exposure and mental health
f89ef3137347.sentence: These treatments and techniques are called ecotherapy.

3152d3e98400.title: Attention restoration theory
3152d3e98400.sentence: Attention Restoration Theory (ART) proposes that spending time in natural settings or even viewing natural scenes helps people recover from directed attention fatigue (mental tiredness that occurs when sustaining deliberate focus on tasks).

fc7c2cb90211.title: Attention restoration theory
fc7c2cb90211.sentence: Within ART, Stephen and Rachel Kaplan argue that directed attention is often taxed in stimulating modern environments.

213ae4ccd5df.title: Nature connectedness
213ae4ccd5df.sentence: The constant demand of the inhibitory control may cause that directed attention to become depleted and result in attention fatigue.

c0fbe78dfe15.title: Attention restoration theory
c0fbe78dfe15.sentence: Soft fascination facilitates restoration and involves effortless attention on gentle, interesting stimuli in the environment, similar to mind-wandering but still directed outward.

e4bcf0d3376e.title: Attention restoration theory
e4bcf0d3376e.sentence: Common examples of what encourages soft fascination include watching clouds drift, leaves rustle, or water flow.

bd1e889ba45d.title: Attention restoration theory
bd1e889ba45d.sentence: The Kaplans also describe four properties that together characterize a restorative setting: being away (psychological or physical distance from routine demands), extent (sufficient scope and coherence to invite exploration), compatibility (a good fit between what the setting affords and the person's purposes), and fascination (interest without effort).

0a8f2ee1f247.title: Attention restoration theory
0a8f2ee1f247.sentence: Attention in ART draws on William James' distinction between voluntary and involuntary attention.

444515f2f20b.title: Attention restoration theory
444515f2f20b.sentence: James defined voluntary attention as effortful, deliberate, goal-oriented focus, and involuntary attention is automatic and is captured by engaging stimuli.

a54e0445b518.title: Attention restoration theory
a54e0445b518.sentence: Following the introduction of ART, Roger Ulrich put forth a competing theoretical nature framework known as Stress Reduction Theory (SRT).

24f89f36e77c.title: Attention restoration theory
24f89f36e77c.sentence: SRT claimed that nature-related benefits were not in fact due to cognitive benefits but, instead, emotional and physiological responses.

1b783bb1c0e0.title: Nature therapy
1b783bb1c0e0.sentence: Nature therapy, sometimes referred to as ecotherapy, grounding, or earthing, is a practice that describes a broad group of techniques or treatments using nature to improve mental or physical health.

81a138814339.title: Nature therapy
81a138814339.sentence: Various types of nature therapy include forest therapy, forest bathing, shinrin-yoku, and Sami Lok.

7c74a1a3d1d5.title: Nature therapy
7c74a1a3d1d5.sentence: "Forest bathing" and Shrinrin-yoku was popularized in Japan by the former head of the Japanese Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, and Fisheries, Tomohide Akiyama, in 1982 to encourage more people to visit forests.

e527083e5d87.title: Nature therapy
e527083e5d87.sentence: These effects are usually linked to the body's natural stress recovery process, in which contact with nature decreases cortisol levels and heart rate.

662e6b1d5989.title: Nature therapy
662e6b1d5989.sentence: Beginning in 2005, Qing Li ran a series of small, random controlled trials that reported that spending a few hours/day walking in a forest over several days increased the number of natural killer cells, by roughly 50 percent, while levels of perforin, granzymes, and granulysin, had all risen sharply.

804931f178e7.title: Nature therapy
804931f178e7.sentence: Repeating the experiment in an urban area had no such effects.

038ab468867c.title: Nature therapy
038ab468867c.sentence: Interaction with nature is associated with lower stress and depressive symptoms.

4c57dbcc2495.title: Nature therapy
4c57dbcc2495.sentence: Nature therapy is relatively accessible and low-cost, since it can be practiced in parks, community gardens, or other public outdoor spaces without equipment.

4974bbea09bd.title: Nature therapy
4974bbea09bd.sentence: Recent reviews have noted that results often vary depending on study design and population, which makes it difficult to measure long-term effects of nature-based therapies with consistency.

c4a06bc703e7.title: Nature therapy
c4a06bc703e7.sentence: A 2024 review claimed that many studies rely on self-reported feelings instead of objective measurements.

5ea733c4c4b8.title: Nature therapy
5ea733c4c4b8.sentence: Spending time in forests demonstrated positive health effects, but not enough to generate clinical practice guidelines or demonstrate causality.

63c97a16a53a.title: Sense of place
63c97a16a53a.sentence: The term sense of place refers to a multidimensional, complex construct used to characterize the relationship between people and spatial settings.

ca85c5a4e16e.title: Sense of place
ca85c5a4e16e.sentence: It is often used in relation to those characteristics that make a place special or unique, as well as to those that foster a sense of authentic human attachment and belonging.

82660085f883.title: Sense of place
82660085f883.sentence: It is a characteristic that some geographic places have and some do not, while to others it is a feeling or perception held by people (not by the place itself).

54101d335018.title: Sense of place
54101d335018.sentence: Others, such as geographer Yi-Fu Tuan, have pointed to senses of place that are not "positive", such as fear.

19c1a870f90e.title: Sense of place
19c1a870f90e.sentence: Places said to have a strong "sense of place" have a strong identity that is deeply felt by inhabitants and visitors.

713e0e89b121.title: Sense of place
713e0e89b121.sentence: Codes aimed at protecting, preserving and enhancing places felt to be of value include "World Heritage Site" designations, the British "Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty" controls and the American "National Historic Landmark" designation.

970b7d4eef9c.title: Sense of place
970b7d4eef9c.sentence: The special bond which develops between children and their childhood environments has been called a "primal landscape" by human geographers.

66b5b4cf84a8.title: Sense of place
66b5b4cf84a8.sentence: This childhood landscape forms part of an individual's identity and constitutes a key point of comparison for considering subsequent places later in life.

65079146280f.title: Sense of place
65079146280f.sentence: As people move around as adults, they tend to consider new places in relation to this baseline landscape experienced during childhood.

70654c25bebb.title: Sense of place
70654c25bebb.sentence: In the context of climate change, sense of place and then the awareness of the changes and disaster related destruction of place is leading to emotional experiences of grief and solastalgia.

948594fbfd5f.title: Sense of place
948594fbfd5f.sentence: Many indigenous cultures are losing their sense of place because of climate change and "ancestral homeland, land rights and retention of sacred places".

3c4029a53b87.title: Nature therapy
3c4029a53b87.sentence: [unreliable medical source?] Interactions with nature environments enhance social connections, stewardship, sense of place, and increase environmental participation.

d5841e693a3d.title: Cultural landscape
d5841e693a3d.sentence: Cultural landscape is a term used in the fields of geography, ecology, and heritage studies, to describe a symbiosis of human activity and environment.

0653fb5f5258.title: Cultural landscape
0653fb5f5258.sentence: As defined by the World Heritage Committee, it is the "cultural properties [that] represent the combined works of nature and of man" and falls into three main categories:

213e97c341ef.title: Cultural landscape
213e97c341ef.sentence: - "a landscape designed and created intentionally by man"

e208359d61fb.title: Cultural landscape
e208359d61fb.sentence: - an "organically evolved landscape" which may be a "relict (or fossil) landscape" or a "continuing landscape"

c1581906ada3.title: Cultural landscape
c1581906ada3.sentence: - an "associative cultural landscape" which may be valued because of the "religious, artistic or cultural associations of the natural element."

0e20e55a9c6e.title: Cultural landscape
0e20e55a9c6e.sentence: Geographer Otto Schlüter is credited with having first formally used “cultural landscape” as an academic term in the early 20th century.

1ffbfb9431f8.title: Cultural landscape
1ffbfb9431f8.sentence: He defined two forms of landscape: the Urlandschaft (transl. original landscape) or landscape that existed before major human induced changes and the Kulturlandschaft (transl. 'cultural landscape') a landscape created by human culture.

b4cd4beea906.title: Cultural landscape
b4cd4beea906.sentence: > The cultural landscape is fashioned from a natural landscape by a cultural group.

37e864e12905.title: Cultural landscape
37e864e12905.sentence: Culture is the agent, the natural area is the medium, the cultural landscape is the result

245277902e59.title: Cultural landscape
245277902e59.sentence: By 1992, the World Heritage Committee elected to convene a meeting of the 'specialists' to advise and assist redraft the Committee's Operational Guidelines to include 'cultural landscapes' as an option for heritage listing properties that were neither purely natural nor purely cultural in form (i.e. 'mixed' heritage).

0299cd21673d.title: Cultural landscape
0299cd21673d.section: Examples > Tongariro National Park, New Zealand (1993)
0299cd21673d.sentence: > "In 1993 Tongariro National Park, became the first property to be inscribed on the World Heritage List under the revised criteria describing cultural landscapes.

cd6cfb18ca6f.title: Cultural landscape
cd6cfb18ca6f.section: Examples > Tongariro National Park, New Zealand (1993)
cd6cfb18ca6f.sentence: The mountains at the heart of the park have cultural and religious significance for the Maori people and symbolize the spiritual links between this community and its environment.

cab504e1d9c2.title: Cultural landscape
cab504e1d9c2.sentence: The concept of cultural landscape is useful for the sustainable management and conservation of heritage.

ba1cc84b2bc8.title: Cultural landscape
ba1cc84b2bc8.sentence: Adopting a cultural landscape perspective can interlink individual aspects of cultural heritage, such as historic buildings, regional material resources, and vernacular construction techniques, into a unified notion of identity and place.

25363e63a833.title: Cultural landscape
25363e63a833.sentence: This can unify tangible and intangible heritage, expose risks within complex system dynamics, and draw the focus of conservation from the protection of past fabric towards the management of future change.

9ed87ef03a5f.title: Cultural landscape
9ed87ef03a5f.sentence: This landscape was struck from the World Heritage list in 2009, due to the construction of a four lane highway across the Elbe.

c08c27e7b5dc.title: Recreation
c08c27e7b5dc.sentence: Recreation has many health benefits, and, accordingly, Therapeutic Recreation has been developed to take advantage of this effect.

b566b031946a.title: Recreation
b566b031946a.sentence: Such therapy is applied in rehabilitation, psychiatric facilities for youth and adults, and in the care of the elderly, disabled people, or people with chronic diseases.

bb75bd58c189.title: Recreation
bb75bd58c189.sentence: The National Council for Therapeutic Recreation Certification (NCTRC) is the nationally recognized credentialing organization for the profession of Therapeutic Recreation.

77e4539b08d0.title: Recreation
77e4539b08d0.sentence: Professionals in the field of Therapeutic Recreation who are certified by the NCTRC are called "Certified Therapeutic Recreation Specialists".

f2893a0f65ee.title: Sustainable tourism
f2893a0f65ee.section: Related similar concepts > Nature Positive Tourism
f2893a0f65ee.sentence: Nature positive tourism recognises that tourism should do more than leave no trace.

1671f1aefd2c.title: Sustainable tourism
1671f1aefd2c.section: Related similar concepts > Nature Positive Tourism
1671f1aefd2c.sentence: It should leave behind positive benefits for the natural world.

3af82fe6666d.title: Sustainable tourism
3af82fe6666d.section: Related similar concepts > Nature Positive Tourism
3af82fe6666d.sentence: A form of regenerative tourism, nature positive tourism is a way for the tourism industry to address the global biodiversity crisis by committing to a nature-positive approach.

fa6f08756d83.title: Sustainable tourism
fa6f08756d83.section: Related similar concepts > Nature Positive Tourism
fa6f08756d83.sentence: This requires change across the sector to arrest and reverse declines in nature by 2030, and to achieve full recovery by 2050.

05fbd0035578.title: Sustainable tourism
05fbd0035578.section: Related similar concepts > Nature Positive Tourism
05fbd0035578.sentence: According to the World Travel and Tourism Council, 80% of good and services in the industry are highly dependent on nature.

b28ea3789beb.title: Sustainable tourism
b28ea3789beb.section: Related similar concepts > Nature Positive Tourism
b28ea3789beb.sentence: This could be through supporting reforestation or regeneration initiatives, making space for nature in urban hotels, or changing operating procedures to eradicate light and water pollution.

f224adfcfabe.title: Sustainable tourism
f224adfcfabe.sentence: While "sustainable tourism" is a concept, the term "responsible tourism" refers to the behaviors and practices that can lead to sustainable tourism.

b9160b1c80be.title: Sustainable tourism
b9160b1c80be.sentence: According to the Center for Responsible Tourism, responsible tourism is "tourism that maximizes the benefits to local communities, minimizes negative social or environmental impacts, and helps local people conserve fragile cultures and habitats or species." Responsible tourism incorporates not only being responsible for interactions with the physical environment, but also of the economic and social interactions.

e90d146576cf.title: Sustainable tourism
e90d146576cf.sentence: All stakeholders are responsible for the kind of tourism they develop or engage in.

d31a1b9f70a0.title: Sustainable tourism
d31a1b9f70a0.sentence: Both service providers and purchasers or consumers are held accountable.

8ca601a85649.title: Sustainable tourism
8ca601a85649.sentence: Some argue that it actually detracts attention from the wider issues surrounding tourism that are in need of regulation, such as the number of visitors and environmental impact.

d9b4037314a9.title: Biophilia hypothesis
d9b4037314a9.section: Natural affinity for living systems > Physiological responses: fractal fluency
d9b4037314a9.sentence: Fractal fluency is a neuroscience model that proposes that, through exposure to nature's fractal scenery, people's visual systems have adapted to efficiently process fractals with ease.

9df49d7d67de.title: Biophilia hypothesis
9df49d7d67de.section: Natural affinity for living systems > Physiological responses: fractal fluency
9df49d7d67de.sentence: Fractals are patterns that repeat at different scales.

71f4d3f636b6.title: Biophilia hypothesis
71f4d3f636b6.section: Natural affinity for living systems > Physiological responses: fractal fluency
71f4d3f636b6.sentence: Examples in natural scenery include clouds, mountains and trees.

bccb5b3944b5.title: Biophilia hypothesis
bccb5b3944b5.section: Natural affinity for living systems > Physiological responses: fractal fluency
bccb5b3944b5.sentence: Humans appear to be especially well-adapted to processing fractal patterns with fractal dimension between 1.3 and 1.5.

3e0c46264a41.title: Biophilia hypothesis
3e0c46264a41.section: Natural affinity for living systems > Physiological responses: fractal fluency
3e0c46264a41.sentence: When humans view fractal patterns with fractal dimensions in this range, these fractals reduce physiological stress and boost cognitive abilities.

8fe0173aff53.title: Biophilia hypothesis
8fe0173aff53.section: Natural affinity for living systems > Physiological responses: fractal fluency
8fe0173aff53.sentence: Designers and architects incorporate biophilic fractals into the built environment to counter the fact that people spend 92% of their time indoors and away from nature's scenery.

a9de99918603.title: Biophilia hypothesis
a9de99918603.section: Indigenous perspectives on the human-nature connection
a9de99918603.sentence: Many Indigenous cultures do not draw a sharp distinction between humans and nature.

eeb5f975a53e.title: Biophilia hypothesis

6dae233a8a43.title: Sacred natural site

4bdd2309f4f3.title: Tourism carrying capacity
4bdd2309f4f3.sentence: "Tourism Carrying Capacity" is defined by the World Tourism Organization as "The maximum number of people that may visit a tourist destination at the same time, without causing destruction of the physical, economic, socio-cultural environment and an unacceptable decrease in the quality of visitors' satisfaction".

30a32bf933f8.title: Tourism carrying capacity

8f9901393b84.title: Tourism carrying capacity
8f9901393b84.sentence: Although it is challenging to pinpoint a specific number of visitors beyond which damage begins, even an imperfect estimate of the TCC can guide policies that cap the number of visitors and reduce the environmental impact of tourism.

6b758cce9af0.title: Tourism carrying capacity
6b758cce9af0.sentence: For example, the government of Peru limits the number of hikers on the Inca Trail to 500 per day, because geologists warned that a larger number could cause serious erosion.

5f3dbbad0c9b.title: Tourism carrying capacity

833a5d765fe1.title: Tourism carrying capacity
833a5d765fe1.sentence: In the case of an individual tourist attraction it is the maximum number that can fit on the site at any given time and still allow people to be able to move.

bb681cde9c0d.title: Tourism carrying capacity

3eee391633d0.title: Tourism carrying capacity

ab37f568bc04.title: Tourism carrying capacity

637148efaf65.title: Tourism carrying capacity

88b10021db14.title: Tourism carrying capacity

1412b009f89e.title: Tourism carrying capacity

2b335927b6a5.title: Tourism carrying capacity

26a9d801d93d.sentence: Remote sensing is the acquisition of information about an object or area from a distance, without touching it, as opposed to measuring it on-site observation.

089f1c29deb8.title: Remote sensing

e6bb082b70e5.title: Remote sensing

778b146e09a9.title: Remote sensing

d8073bd0dd9b.title: Remote sensing

3880539e2d7c.title: Geographic information system
3880539e2d7c.sentence: A geographic information system (GIS) consists of integrated computer hardware and software that store, manage, analyze, edit, output, and visualize geographic data.

286af1ce9f61.title: Geographic information system
286af1ce9f61.sentence: GIS provides the ability to relate previously unrelated information, through the use of location as the "key index variable".

1a3149ea3ddf.title: Geographic information system
1a3149ea3ddf.section: Geospatial data management > Aspects of geographic data
1a3149ea3ddf.sentence: Just as a relational database containing text or numbers can relate many different tables using common key index variables, GIS can relate otherwise unrelated information by using location as the key index variable.

48cdc7c2fe70.title: Geographic information system
48cdc7c2fe70.sentence: The core of any GIS is a database that contains representations of geographic phenomena, modeling their geometry (location and shape) and their properties or attributes.

3860dd3f9d97.title: Geographic information system
3860dd3f9d97.sentence: While digital GIS dates to the mid-1960s, when Roger Tomlinson first coined the phrase "geographic information system", many of the geographic concepts and methods that GIS automates date back decades earlier.

03c2d588b251.title: Geographic information system
03c2d588b251.sentence: GIS data acquisition includes several methods for gathering spatial data into a GIS database, which can be grouped into three categories: primary data capture, the direct measurement phenomena in the field (e.g., remote sensing, the global positioning system); secondary data capture, the extraction of information from existing sources that are not in a GIS form, such as paper maps, through digitization; and data transfer, the copying of existing GIS data from external sources such as government agencies and private companies.

bc22c7933538.title: Geographic information system
bc22c7933538.sentence: The condition of the Earth's surface, atmosphere, and subsurface can be examined by feeding satellite data into a GIS.

eae57d348ed7.title: Geographic information system
eae57d348ed7.sentence: GIS technology gives researchers the ability to examine the variations in Earth processes over days, months, and years through the use of cartographic visualizations.

b9ca0dd6bdab.title: Geographic information system
b9ca0dd6bdab.sentence: Geographic information system (GIS) is a commonly used tool for environmental management, modelling and planning.

3f07627ef3ab.title: Landscape ecology
3f07627ef3ab.sentence: Landscape ecology is the science of studying and improving relationships between ecological processes in the environment and particular ecosystems.

0257643fd524.title: Landscape ecology
0257643fd524.sentence: The most salient characteristics of landscape ecology are its emphasis on the relationship among pattern, process and scales, and its focus on broad-scale ecological and environmental issues.

0bcf9454f00a.title: Landscape ecology
0bcf9454f00a.sentence: Landscapes are spatially heterogeneous geographic areas characterized by diverse interacting patches or ecosystems, ranging from relatively natural terrestrial and aquatic systems such as forests, grasslands, and lakes to human-dominated environments including agricultural and urban settings.

e95c4f3bbba9.title: Landscape ecology
e95c4f3bbba9.sentence: The main difference from traditional ecological studies, which frequently assume that systems are spatially homogenous, is the consideration of spatial patterns.

31c5562083ec.title: Landscape ecology
31c5562083ec.sentence: Heterogeneity is the measure of how parts of a landscape differ from one another.

626b20a25418.title: Landscape ecology
626b20a25418.sentence: The German term Landschaftsökologie – thus landscape ecology – was coined by German geographer Carl Troll in 1939.

f21cfa03b2f9.title: Landscape ecology
f21cfa03b2f9.sentence: He developed this terminology and many early concepts of landscape ecology as part of his early work, which consisted of applying aerial photograph interpretation to studies of interactions between environment and vegetation.

367555f87f35.title: Landscape ecology
367555f87f35.sentence: Landscape ecology consists of four main principles: the development and dynamics of spatial heterogeneity, interactions and exchanges across heterogeneous landscapes, influences of spatial heterogeneity on biotic and abiotic processes, and the management of spatial heterogeneity.

50486b1baf13.title: Landscape ecology
50486b1baf13.sentence: Landscape ecology explicitly includes humans as entities that cause functional changes on the landscape.

02e7f0d90c05.title: Landscape ecology
02e7f0d90c05.sentence: It also proposes ways for restoring degraded landscapes.

6d3d5b5ee68f.title: Landscape ecology
6d3d5b5ee68f.sentence: Recent growth of landscape ecology owes much to the development of geographic information systems (GIS) and the availability of large-extent habitat data (e.g. remotely sensed datasets).

8141e763b190.title: Landscape ecology
8141e763b190.sentence: By 1980, landscape ecology was a discrete, established discipline.

3da361078d84.title: Landscape ecology
3da361078d84.sentence: Landscape ecology developed in Europe from historical planning on human-dominated landscapes.

2fcf0b3553f5.title: System dynamics
2fcf0b3553f5.sentence: System dynamics (SD) is an approach to understanding the nonlinear behaviour of complex systems over time using stocks, flows, internal feedback loops, table functions and time delays.

73398e4baba0.title: System dynamics
73398e4baba0.section: Topics in systems dynamics > Stock and flow diagrams
73398e4baba0.sentence: A stock is the term for any entity that accumulates or depletes over time.

899b7ea9f52e.title: System dynamics
899b7ea9f52e.section: Topics in systems dynamics > Stock and flow diagrams
899b7ea9f52e.sentence: A flow is the rate of change in a stock.

d48007da1028.title: System dynamics
d48007da1028.sentence: It is a property of complex systems that the structure of any system, with many circular, interlocking, sometimes time-delayed relationships among its components, is often just as important in determining its behavior as the individual components themselves.

4b651009bd71.title: System dynamics
4b651009bd71.sentence: System dynamics was created during the mid-1950s by Professor Jay Forrester of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

dac7803912d8.title: System dynamics
dac7803912d8.sentence: From hand simulations (or calculations) of the stock-flow-feedback structure of the GE plants, which included the existing corporate decision-making structure for hiring and layoffs, Forrester was able to show how the instability in GE employment was due to the internal structure of the firm and not to an external force such as the business cycle.

1f7ef5937c0f.title: System dynamics

3192b7888fd5.title: System dynamics

7ee0e4549c7c.title: System dynamics
7ee0e4549c7c.sentence: SD models solve the problem of simultaneity (mutual causation) by updating all variables in small time increments with positive and negative feedbacks and time delays structuring the interactions and control.

42e136802450.title: Ecosystem model
42e136802450.sentence: An ecosystem model is an abstract, usually mathematical, representation of an ecological system (ranging in scale from an individual population, to an ecological community, or even an entire biome), which is studied to better understand the real system.

9078b16876d7.title: Ecosystem model
9078b16876d7.sentence: Using data gathered from the field, ecological relationships—such as the relation of sunlight and water availability to photosynthetic rate, or that between predator and prey populations—are derived, and these are combined to form ecosystem models.

c648a8c9f837.title: Ecosystem model
c648a8c9f837.sentence: These model systems are then studied in order to make predictions about the dynamics of the real system.

fa20170f82cb.title: Ecosystem model
fa20170f82cb.sentence: Models enable researchers to simulate large-scale experiments that would be too costly or unethical to perform on a real ecosystem.

74a9db79ff8f.title: Ecosystem model
74a9db79ff8f.sentence: They also enable the simulation of ecological processes over very long periods of time (i.e. simulating a process that takes centuries in reality, can be done in a matter of minutes in a computer model).

cb4b263f5aad.title: Ecosystem model
cb4b263f5aad.sentence: There are two major types of ecological models, which are generally applied to different types of problems: (1) analytic models and (2) simulation / computational models.

f2b1920da315.title: Ecosystem model
f2b1920da315.sentence: Analytic models are typically relatively simple (often linear) systems, that can be accurately described by a set of mathematical equations whose behavior is well-known.

f6b3f238e4be.title: Ecosystem model
f6b3f238e4be.sentence: Simulation models on the other hand, use numerical techniques to solve problems for which analytic solutions are impractical or impossible.

5af29b341c19.title: Ecosystem model
5af29b341c19.sentence: Simulation models tend to be more widely used, and are generally considered more ecologically realistic, while analytic models are valued for their mathematical elegance and explanatory power.

39432437d78c.title: Ecosystem model
39432437d78c.sentence: Because of this complexity, ecosystem models typically simplify the systems they are studying to a limited number of components that are well understood, and deemed relevant to the problem that the model is intended to solve.

ce110f7e12f8.title: Ecosystem model
ce110f7e12f8.sentence: The process of simplification typically reduces an ecosystem to a small number of state variables and mathematical functions that describe the nature of the relationships between them.

b4c14401f6a8.title: Ecosystem model
b4c14401f6a8.sentence: The number of ecosystem components that are incorporated into the model is limited by aggregating similar processes and entities into functional groups that are treated as a unit.

79088677476c.title: Ecosystem model
79088677476c.sentence: Spatially explicit models (also called "spatially distributed" or "landscape" models) attempt to incorporate a heterogeneous spatial environment into the model.

e6c3dde90dd0.title: Ecosystem model
e6c3dde90dd0.sentence: However, for many ecological problems spatial dynamics are an important part of the problem, with different spatial environments leading to very different outcomes.

b7cea9cde580.title: Ecosystem model
b7cea9cde580.sentence: One method is to test the model with multiple sets of data that are independent of the actual system being studied.

45bfb0f8bf47.title: Ecosystem model
45bfb0f8bf47.sentence: Another method of validation is to compare the model's output with data collected from field observations.

c79ffc54d2df.title: Ecosystem model
c79ffc54d2df.sentence: Researchers frequently specify beforehand how much of a disparity they are willing to accept between parameters output by a model and those computed from field data.

98c114505389.title: Ecosystem model
98c114505389.sentence: Often, the study of inaccuracies in the model (when compared to empirical observations) will lead to the generation of hypotheses about possible ecological relations that are not yet known or well understood.

2078a3300ea6.title: Ecosystem model
2078a3300ea6.sentence: Ecopath is a powerful software system which uses simulation and computational methods to model marine ecosystems.

16bb942e3d3d.title: Ecosystem model
16bb942e3d3d.sentence: It is widely used by marine and fisheries scientists as a tool for modelling and visualising the complex relationships that exist in real world marine ecosystems.

7393ffa69b38.title: Agent-based model
7393ffa69b38.sentence: An agent-based model (ABM) is a computational model for simulating the actions and interactions of an autonomous agent (both individual or collective entities such as organizations or groups) to understand the behavior of a system and what governs its outcomes.

52664183840d.title: Agent-based model
52664183840d.sentence: Particularly within ecology, an ABM is also called an individual-based model (IBM).

5790d8caecfe.title: Agent-based model
5790d8caecfe.sentence: The three ideas central to agent-based models are agents as objects, emergence, and complexity.

edfe8436358b.title: Agent-based model
edfe8436358b.sentence: Agent-based modeling, however, using simple rules, can result in different sorts of complex and interesting behavior.

ef133fbfdabe.title: Agent-based model
ef133fbfdabe.sentence: One of the earliest agent-based models in concept was Thomas Schelling's segregation model, which was discussed in his paper "Dynamic Models of Segregation" in 1971.

cfa6aff763c9.title: Agent-based model
cfa6aff763c9.sentence: Though Schelling originally used coins and graph paper rather than computers, his models embodied the basic concept of agent-based models as autonomous agents interacting in a shared environment with an observed aggregate, emergent outcome.

fd9f2dde02fa.title: Agent-based model
fd9f2dde02fa.sentence: The idea of agent-based modeling was developed as a relatively simple concept in the late 1940s.

ac5daa39601e.title: Agent-based model
ac5daa39601e.sentence: Since it requires computation-intensive procedures, it did not become widespread until the 1990s.

dbbf61b96381.title: Agent-based model
dbbf61b96381.section: Applications > In economics and social sciences
dbbf61b96381.sentence: ABMs do not assume the economy can achieve equilibrium and "representative agents" are replaced by agents with diverse, dynamic, and interdependent behavior including herding.

07f23fb90462.title: Agent-based model
07f23fb90462.section: Applications > In economics and social sciences
07f23fb90462.sentence: ABMs can represent unstable systems with crashes and booms that develop out of non-linear (disproportionate) responses to proportionally small changes.

4cf35deef6cf.title: Agent-based model
4cf35deef6cf.section: Implementation > Integration with other modeling forms
4cf35deef6cf.sentence: For instance, agent-based models have also been combined with Geographic Information Systems (GIS).

d732e63f8e51.title: Agent-based model
d732e63f8e51.section: Implementation > Integration with other modeling forms
d732e63f8e51.sentence: This provides a useful combination where the ABM serves as a process model and the GIS system can provide a model of pattern.

dd5aa2de2f60.title: Agent-based model
dd5aa2de2f60.sentence: ABMs have also been applied in water resources planning and management, particularly for exploring, simulating, and predicting the performance of infrastructure design and policy decisions, and in assessing the value of cooperation and information exchange in large water resources systems.

877fa37a2d32.title: Agent-based model
877fa37a2d32.sentence: Verification involves making sure the implemented model matches the conceptual model, whereas validation ensures that the implemented model has some relationship to the real-world.

69d4b729cb60.title: Agent-based model
69d4b729cb60.sentence: Face validation, sensitivity analysis, calibration, and statistical validation are different aspects of validation.

cbb7a9db9908.title: Land cover
cbb7a9db9908.sentence: Land cover is the physical material at the land surface of Earth.

b1be1baf2428.title: Land cover
b1be1baf2428.sentence: Land covers include flora, concrete, built structures, bare ground, and temporary water.

8e6d938367a6.title: Land cover
8e6d938367a6.sentence: "Land cover" is distinct from "land use", despite the two terms often being used interchangeably.

e3cc7ef1b6c1.title: Land cover
e3cc7ef1b6c1.sentence: Land use is a description of how people utilize the land and of socio-economic activity.

5d096b4b6d6a.title: Land cover
5d096b4b6d6a.sentence: There are two primary methods for capturing information on land cover: field survey, and analysis of remotely sensed imagery.

beecb9bc2eaa.title: Land cover
beecb9bc2eaa.sentence: One of the major land cover issues (as with all natural resource inventories) is that every survey defines similarly named categories in different ways.

26b6d198fe9f.title: Land cover
26b6d198fe9f.sentence: For instance, there are many definitions of "forest"—sometimes within the same organisation—that may or may not incorporate a number of different forest features (e.g., stand height, canopy cover, strip width, inclusion of grasses, and rates of growth for timber production).

e5c39cf8c325.title: Land cover
e5c39cf8c325.sentence: [6970] | Artificial surfaces (including urban and associated areas) | 26.04 | 34.33 | 55.40 | 0.37% | 29.35

bb34e2ed0612.title: Land cover
bb34e2ed0612.sentence: Land cover change detection using remote sensing and geospatial data provides baseline information for assessing the climate change impacts on habitats, biodiversity, and natural resources in the target areas.

1069bba718d0.title: Land use
1069bba718d0.sentence: Human activity is the most significant cause of land cover change, and humans are also directly impacted by the environmental consequences of these changes.

2dbea1f30ee8.title: Land use
2dbea1f30ee8.sentence: For example, deforestation (the systematic and permanent conversion of previously forested land for other uses) has historically been a primary facilitator of land use and land cover change.

f49e54e7870f.title: Scenario planning
f49e54e7870f.sentence: Scenario planning, scenario thinking, scenario analysis, scenario prediction and the scenario method all describe a strategic planning method that some organizations use to make flexible long-term plans.

fd6b8dfabf6c.title: Scenario planning
fd6b8dfabf6c.section: Scenario planning compared to other techniques > Scenario analysis
fd6b8dfabf6c.sentence: Scenario analysis is a process of analyzing future events by considering alternative possible outcomes (sometimes called "alternative worlds").

206b80dc4965.title: Scenario planning
206b80dc4965.section: Scenario planning compared to other techniques > Scenario analysis
206b80dc4965.sentence: Thus, scenario analysis, which is one of the main forms of projection, does not try to show one exact picture of the future.

927332c3cb1a.title: Scenario planning
927332c3cb1a.section: Scenario planning compared to other techniques > Scenario analysis
927332c3cb1a.sentence: Instead, it presents several alternative future developments.

426b20685790.title: Scenario planning
426b20685790.section: Scenario planning compared to other techniques > Scenario analysis
426b20685790.sentence: In contrast to prognoses, the scenario analysis is not based on extrapolation of the past or the extension of past trends.

2bc4f697cdf3.title: Scenario planning
2bc4f697cdf3.section: Scenario planning compared to other techniques > Scenario analysis
2bc4f697cdf3.sentence: It does not rely on historical data and does not expect past observations to remain valid in the future.

7cc7b992689c.title: Scenario planning
7cc7b992689c.sentence: Scenario planning may involve aspects of systems thinking, specifically the recognition that many factors may combine in complex ways to create sometimes surprising futures (due to non-linear feedback loops).

b27a872fb820.title: Scenario planning
b27a872fb820.sentence: However, futures studies analysts select scenario features so they are both possible and uncomfortable.

a7306e8cfcfc.title: Scenario planning
a7306e8cfcfc.sentence: Scenario planning helps policy-makers and firms anticipate change, prepare responses, and create more robust strategies.

53346424fce7.title: Scenario planning
53346424fce7.section: History of use by academic and commercial organizations
53346424fce7.sentence: Most authors attribute the introduction of scenario planning to Herman Kahn through his work for the US Military in the 1950s at the RAND Corporation where he developed a technique of describing the future in stories as if written by people in the future.

7de11a4740f8.title: Scenario planning
7de11a4740f8.section: History of use by academic and commercial organizations
7de11a4740f8.sentence: Though Kahn is often cited as the father of scenario planning, at the same time Kahn was developing his methods at RAND, Gaston Berger was developing similar methods at the Centre d'Etudes Prospectives which he founded in France.

d60cca0d9cf0.title: Scenario planning
d60cca0d9cf0.section: Critique > Critique of Shell's use of scenario planning
d60cca0d9cf0.sentence: In the 1970s, many energy companies were surprised by both environmentalism and the OPEC cartel, and thereby lost billions of dollars of revenue by misinvestment.

35891ac90db9.title: Scenario planning
35891ac90db9.section: Critique > Critique of Shell's use of scenario planning
35891ac90db9.sentence: The dramatic financial effects of these changes led at least one organization, Royal Dutch Shell, to implement scenario planning.

07227bd3c097.title: Scenario planning
07227bd3c097.sentence: In business applications, the emphasis on understanding the behavior of opponents has been reduced while more attention is now paid to changes in the natural environment.

5216fa5c8d9a.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
5216fa5c8d9a.sentence: The normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) is a widely used metric for quantifying the health and density of vegetation using sensor data.

d4e4347f59d6.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
d4e4347f59d6.sentence: It is calculated from spectrometric data at two specific bands: red and near-infrared.

d16fee61f4d8.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
d16fee61f4d8.sentence: The pigment in plant leaves, chlorophyll, strongly absorbs visible light (from 400 to 700 nm) for use in photosynthesis.

37324418e8c3.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
37324418e8c3.sentence: The cell structure of the leaves, on the other hand, strongly reflects near-infrared light (from 700 to 1100 nm).

f6fb0ed6b69f.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
f6fb0ed6b69f.sentence: Hence, live green plants appear relatively dark in the PAR and relatively bright in the near-infrared.

47c88c42ce23.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
47c88c42ce23.sentence: The index is easy to interpret: NDVI will be a value between -1 and 1, where values close to zero will indicate little to no vegetation, negative values are associated with non-land surfaces or water, and higher values correspond to healthy, dense vegetation.

4040684f6df9.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
4040684f6df9.sentence: It can be seen from its mathematical definition that the NDVI of an area containing a dense vegetation canopy will tend to positive values (say 0.3 to 0.8) while clouds and snow fields will be characterized by negative values of this index.

104516fda5d6.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
104516fda5d6.sentence: - soils which generally exhibit a near-infrared spectral reflectance somewhat larger than the red, and thus tend to also generate rather small positive NDVI values (say 0.1 to 0.2).

1eb0e855a168.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
1eb0e855a168.sentence: With the assistance of a resident mathematician (Dr. John Schell), they studied solutions to this dilemma and subsequently developed the ratio of the difference of the red and infrared radiances over their sum as a means to adjust for or "normalize" the effects of the solar zenith angle.

ac41ae2d1878.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
ac41ae2d1878.sentence: The earliest reported use of NDVI in the Great Plains study was in 1973 by Rouse et al.

260cb1b69d13.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
260cb1b69d13.sentence: Thus, NDVI was one of the most successful of many attempts to simply and quickly identify vegetated areas and their "condition," and it remains the most well-known and used index to detect live green plant canopies in multispectral remote sensing data.

4a10fc37d141.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
4a10fc37d141.sentence: Within precision agriculture, NDVI data is used to assess crop health.

d968982f1560.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
d968982f1560.sentence: This includes being able to identify plant stress much sooner than it can be seen.

0ef6ae5a82cb.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
0ef6ae5a82cb.sentence: Since there is a prediction aspect to NDVI, it has been able to be used in yield prediction models since higher NDVI is more often linked to greater productivity/biomass.

461358a9ca10.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
461358a9ca10.sentence: For example, NDVI can be used to monitor drought by tracking changes in vegetation green over time, where lower values can indicate plant stress due to reduced water availability.

667df46d6611.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
667df46d6611.sentence: It also has applications in detecting deforestation and land cover damage since decreases in values often point to vegetation loss or degradation.

fe4436b9e543.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
fe4436b9e543.sentence: Whether the missing information is relevant or valuable is for the user to judge, but it is important to understand that an NDVI product carries only a fraction of the information available in the original spectral reflectance data.

f5e6b649b9f1.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
f5e6b649b9f1.sentence: Also, the calculation of the NDVI value is sensitive to a number of factors such as atmospheric effects, differences between sensors, soil, ice, or snow conditions, and spatial inconsistency in the data

ce8f0a395aeb.title: Spatial analysis
ce8f0a395aeb.sentence: Spatial analysis is any of the formal techniques which study entities using their topological, geometric, or geographic properties, primarily used in urban design.

8d80493fbad0.title: Spatial analysis
8d80493fbad0.sentence: Spatial analysis includes a variety of techniques using different analytic approaches, especially spatial statistics.

b0baf79a85f9.title: Spatial analysis
b0baf79a85f9.sentence: In a more restricted sense, spatial analysis is geospatial analysis, the technique applied to structures at the human scale, most notably in the analysis of geographic data.

45c9af055d42.title: Spatial analysis
45c9af055d42.sentence: Geospatial and hydrospatial analysis, or just spatial analysis, is an approach to applying statistical analysis and other analytic techniques to data which has a geographical or spatial aspect.

839d8da1a925.title: Spatial analysis
839d8da1a925.sentence: Such analysis would typically employ software capable of rendering maps processing spatial data, and applying analytical methods to terrestrial or geographic datasets, including the use of geographic information systems and geomatics.

8bdb72fcae73.title: Spatial analysis
8bdb72fcae73.section: Geospatial and hydrospatial analysis > Geographical information system usage > Basic applications
8bdb72fcae73.sentence: Geospatial and Hydrospatial analysis, using GIS, was developed for problems in the environmental and life sciences, in particular ecology, geology and epidemiology.

dda84dcbc4db.title: Spatial analysis
dda84dcbc4db.section: Geospatial and hydrospatial analysis > Geographical information system usage > Basic applications
dda84dcbc4db.sentence: It has extended to almost all industries including defense, intelligence, utilities, Natural Resources (i.e. Oil and Gas, Forestry... etc.), social sciences, medicine and Public Safety (i.e. emergency management and criminology), disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM), and climate change adaptation (CCA).

27e4562e5716.title: Spatial analysis
27e4562e5716.section: Geospatial and hydrospatial analysis > Geographical information system usage > Basic operations
27e4562e5716.sentence: Vector-based GIS is typically related to operations such as map overlay (combining two or more maps or map layers according to predefined rules), simple buffering (identifying regions of a map within a specified distance of one or more features, such as towns, roads or rivers) and similar basic operations.

4ad92b107bc0.title: Spatial analysis
4ad92b107bc0.sentence: Spatial interaction or "gravity models" estimate the flow of people, material or information between locations in geographic space.

cb46917e8000.title: Spatial analysis
cb46917e8000.sentence: The most fundamental of these is the problem of defining the spatial location of the entities being studied.

92cad5c05d11.title: Spatial analysis
92cad5c05d11.section: Fundamental issues > Common errors in spatial analysis > Ecological fallacy
92cad5c05d11.sentence: The ecological fallacy describes errors due to performing analyses on aggregate data when trying to reach conclusions on the individual units.

8b5b3fc1da42.title: Spatial analysis
8b5b3fc1da42.sentence: Spatial analysis began with early attempts at cartography and surveying.

05ab2f952899.title: Spatial analysis
05ab2f952899.sentence: Land surveying goes back to at least 1,400 B.C in Egypt: the dimensions of taxable land plots were measured with measuring ropes and plumb bobs.

db1ab8c57b85.title: Species distribution modelling
db1ab8c57b85.sentence: Species distribution modelling (SDM), also known as environmental (or ecological) niche modelling (ENM), habitat suitability modelling, predictive habitat distribution modelling, and range mapping uses ecological models to predict the distribution of a species across geographic space and time using environmental data.

bda4e738a611.title: Species distribution modelling
bda4e738a611.sentence: The environmental data are most often climate data (e.g. temperature, precipitation), but can include other variables such as soil type, water depth, and land cover.

8c54063fcde9.title: Species distribution modelling
8c54063fcde9.sentence: Predictions from an SDM may be of a species' future distribution under climate change, a species' past distribution in order to assess evolutionary relationships, or the potential future distribution of an invasive species.

7b77bbef9562.title: Species distribution modelling
7b77bbef9562.sentence: A primary application of SDMs lies in biodiversity conservation and reserve design.

efa50ea19a62.title: Species distribution modelling
efa50ea19a62.sentence: Models are used to identify areas of high habitat suitability, helping to prioritise sites for protection and restoration.

e7b0c2ac4bde.title: Species distribution modelling
e7b0c2ac4bde.sentence: In many cases, SDMs guide the expansion of protected area networks by predicting potential habitats for rare, endemic, or threatened species, even in regions where field data are scarce.

6c724d71fcd8.title: Species distribution modelling
6c724d71fcd8.sentence: In addition, SDMs support the identification of climate refugia, areas likely to remain suitable under future climatic conditions, which are crucial for long-term conservation planning.

1a0a41ec66ef.title: Species distribution modelling
1a0a41ec66ef.sentence: Correlative SDMs, also known as climate envelope models, bioclimatic models, or resource selection function models, model the observed distribution of a species as a function of environmental conditions.

b68b2eee5e26.title: Species distribution modelling
b68b2eee5e26.sentence: Mechanistic SDMs, also known as process-based models or biophysical models, use independently derived information about a species' physiology to develop a model of the environmental conditions under which the species can exist.

42c673164e6e.title: Species distribution modelling
42c673164e6e.section: Correlative vs mechanistic models > Correlative SDMs
42c673164e6e.sentence: Since correlative SDMs are models of a species' observed distribution, they are models of the realized niche (the environments where a species is found), as opposed to the fundamental niche (the environments where a species can be found, or where the abiotic environment is appropriate for the survival).

867f7eb6ac2a.title: Species distribution modelling
867f7eb6ac2a.section: Correlative vs mechanistic models > Correlative SDMs
867f7eb6ac2a.sentence: Correlative SDMs are easier and faster to implement than mechanistic SDMs, and can make ready use of available data.

92cb0c933b43.title: Species distribution modelling
92cb0c933b43.section: Correlative vs mechanistic models > Correlative SDMs
92cb0c933b43.sentence: Since they are correlative however, they do not provide much information about causal mechanisms and are not good for extrapolation.

c4c04035d587.title: Species distribution modelling
c4c04035d587.section: Correlative vs mechanistic models > Mechanistic SDMs
c4c04035d587.sentence: Mechanistic SDMs incorporate causal mechanisms and are better for extrapolation and non-equilibrium situations.

042189b98a83.title: Species distribution modelling
042189b98a83.section: Correlative vs mechanistic models > Mechanistic SDMs
042189b98a83.sentence: However, they are more labor-intensive to create than correlational models and require the collection and validation of a lot of physiological data, which may not be readily available.

03db9ca0e780.title: Species distribution modelling
03db9ca0e780.sentence: MaxEnt is the most widely used method/software uses presence only data and performs well when there are few presence records available.

0ace60ada471.title: Species distribution modelling
0ace60ada471.sentence: The expansion of remote sensing and the development of GIS-based environmental modelling increase the amount of environmental information available for model-building and made it easier to use.

f40dde005b2f.title: Land change modeling
f40dde005b2f.sentence: Land change models (LCMs) describe, project, and explain changes in and the dynamics of land use and land-cover.

68d1ea45ab61.title: Land change modeling
68d1ea45ab61.sentence: LCMs are a means of understanding ways that humans change the Earth's surface in the past, present, and future.

a8a34bb21b1f.title: Land change modeling
a8a34bb21b1f.sentence: Land change models are valuable in development policy, helping guide more appropriate decisions for resource management and the natural environment at a variety of scales ranging from a small piece of land to the entire spatial extent.

8aa04adc68d6.title: Landscape ecology
8aa04adc68d6.sentence: Land change modeling is an application of landscape ecology designed to predict future changes in land use.

f280857b0c2d.title: Land change modeling
f280857b0c2d.sentence: Land change modeling is a key component of land change science, which uses LCMs to assess long-term outcomes for land cover and climate.

52ff4662d428.title: Land change modeling
52ff4662d428.section: Approaches > Machine learning and statistical models
52ff4662d428.sentence: A machine-learning approach uses land-cover data from the past to try to assess how land will change in the future, and works best with large datasets.

ab21121ba4ce.title: Land change modeling
ab21121ba4ce.sentence: A cellular land change model uses maps of suitability for various types of land use, and compares areas that are immediately adjacent to one another to project changes into the future.

e13c1a4b02af.title: Land change modeling
e13c1a4b02af.section: Approaches > Sector-based and spatially disaggregated economic models
e13c1a4b02af.sentence: Economic models are built on principles of supply and demand.

b853c60b856e.title: Land change modeling
b853c60b856e.sentence: Agent-based models try to simulate the behavior of many individuals making independent choices, and then see how those choices affect the landscape as a whole.

0f77fa5dad71.title: Land change modeling
0f77fa5dad71.sentence: Many models do not limit themselves to one of the approaches above - they may combine several in order to develop a fully comprehensive and accurate model.

4caf1fc67280.title: Land change modeling
4caf1fc67280.section: Approaches > Machine learning and statistical models
4caf1fc67280.sentence: There are multiple types of machine-learning and statistical models - a study in western Mexico from 2011 found that results from two outwardly similar models were considerably different, as one used a neural network and the other used a simple weights-of-evidence model.

f509a1bf053b.title: Land change modeling
f509a1bf053b.sentence: A notable property of all land change models is that they have some irreducible level of uncertainty in the model structure, parameter values, and/or input data.

b5dcfa70e2ac.title: Land change modeling
b5dcfa70e2ac.sentence: For instance, one uncertainty within land change models is a result from temporal non-stationarity that exists in land change processes, so the further into the future the model is applied, the more uncertain it is.

b4192c1bc467.title: Land change modeling
b4192c1bc467.section: Improvement and advancement > Aligning model choices with model goals
b4192c1bc467.sentence: For example, when someone needs to design a model with policy and policy actors in mind, they may choose an agent-based model.

d9f1b2533976.title: Land change modeling
d9f1b2533976.section: Improvement and advancement > Aligning model choices with model goals
d9f1b2533976.sentence: When one needs to grasp the early stages of problem identification, and thus needs to understand the scientific patterns and trend of land change, machine learning and cellular approaches are useful.

a999b8f2ee5c.title: Land change modeling
a999b8f2ee5c.sentence: The practical disciplines use LCMs to analyze current land change trends and explore future outcomes from policies or actions in order to set appropriate guidelines, limits and principles for policy and action.

44f0f08fb561.title: Land change modeling
44f0f08fb561.sentence: Research and practitioner communities may study land change to address topics related to land-climate interactions, water quantity and quality, food and fiber production, and urbanization, infrastructure, and the built environment.

2c6771b16ab7.title: Land use
2c6771b16ab7.sentence: LCMs can be used to predict how land use and land cover may change under alternate circumstances, which is useful for risk assessment, in that it allows for the prediction of potential impacts and can be used to inform policy decisions, albeit with some uncertainty.

811029545707.title: Remote sensing
811029545707.sentence: Remote sensing methods are generally classed as passive or active.

5cc02293f0b8.title: Remote sensing
5cc02293f0b8.sentence: Passive sensors record natural energy that an object or scene emits or reflects; sunlight reflected by the surface is the source they most often measure.

4e4b563cb8f2.title: Remote sensing
4e4b563cb8f2.sentence: Active sensors supply their own energy: they direct radiation at a target, and then detect and measure what is reflected or scattered back from the target.

9f30a68328fe.title: Remote sensing
9f30a68328fe.sentence: Common passive instruments include photography, both film and digital, as well as radiometers and spectrometers.

f2a60474b201.title: Remote sensing
f2a60474b201.sentence: Radar and lidar are active systems that time the interval between sending a pulse and receiving its return, which can give the distance to the target.

f9797d7ce06c.title: Lidar
f9797d7ce06c.sentence: Lidar (/ˈlaɪdɑːr/, an acronym of light detection and ranging or laser imaging, detection, and ranging, often stylized LiDAR) is a method for determining ranges by targeting an object or a surface with a laser and measuring the time for the reflected light to return to the optical receiver.

1fb83e575a39.title: Lidar
1fb83e575a39.sentence: Lidar uses active sensors that supply their own illumination source.

891b5253dcd0.title: Lidar
891b5253dcd0.sentence: Distance to the object is determined by recording the time between transmitted and backscattered pulses and by using the speed of light to calculate the distance traveled.

7d3fc4b0aac5.title: Lidar
7d3fc4b0aac5.sentence: A narrow laser beam can map physical features with very high resolutions; for example, an aircraft can map terrain at 30-centimetre (12 in) resolution or better.

c1d8c56d2b68.title: Lidar
c1d8c56d2b68.sentence: Measurements are used to take inventory in forest plots as well as calculate individual tree heights, crown width and crown diameter.

bdf16ff761ba.title: Lidar
bdf16ff761ba.sentence: Other statistical analysis use lidar data to estimate total plot information such as canopy volume, mean, minimum and maximum heights, vegetation cover, biomass, and carbon density.
