e90506c57001.sentence: Use-value (German: Gebrauchswert; Nutzwert) or value in use is a concept in classical political economy and Marxist economics.

e7b712219216.title: Use value
e7b712219216.sentence: It refers to the tangible features of a commodity (a tradeable object) which can satisfy some human requirement, want or need, or which serves a useful purpose.

e66d16d5b902.title: Use value
e66d16d5b902.sentence: For example, gold may be used as a means of exchange, as a decorative object, or one of the most efficient electrical conductors (and used extensively in electronic components for that reason).

9acdb9f45e03.title: Use value
9acdb9f45e03.sentence: Smith recognized that commodities may have an exchange-value but may satisfy no use-value, such as diamonds, while a commodity with a very high use-value may have a very low exchange-value, such as water.

ef01485abdc3.title: Use value
ef01485abdc3.sentence: In Karl Marx's critique of political economy, any commodity has an exchange value and is a use-value — the former manifestly appearing as exchange-value in any exchange-relation in which bearers of commodities mutually alienate and appropriate each-others commodities on the market, it's foremost the proportion in which any commodity is exchangeable for any commodities, its form as the money form within money economies.

6f6f57c40c75.title: Use value
6f6f57c40c75.sentence: The transformation of a use-value into a social use-value and into a commodity (the process of commodification) is not automatic or spontaneous, but has technical, social and political preconditions.

10881287049a.title: Use value
10881287049a.sentence: For example, it must be possible to trade it, and to transfer ownership or access rights to it from one person or organization to another in a secure way.

28284e1cd052.title: Use value
28284e1cd052.sentence: There must also be a real market demand for it.

17362bec850a.title: Classical economics
17362bec850a.sentence: Its theory of value was largely displaced by marginalist schools of thought which sees "use value" as deriving from the marginal utility that consumers find in a good, and "exchange value" (i.e. natural price) as determined by the marginal opportunity- or disutility-cost of the inputs that make up the product.

16b2d49f3e1a.title: Commodification of nature
16b2d49f3e1a.sentence: Most researchers who employ a commodification of nature framing invoke a Marxian conceptualization of commodities as "objects produced for sale on the market" that embody both use and exchange value.

d9ea74775a70.title: Exchange value
d9ea74775a70.sentence: In political economy and especially Marxian economics, exchange value (German: Tauschwert) refers to one of the four major attributes of a commodity, i.e., an item or service produced for, and sold on the market, the other three attributes being use value, economic value, and price.

cc82e6a56932.title: Exchange value
cc82e6a56932.sentence: - an exchange value, which is the proportion at which a commodity can be exchanged for other entities;

538253663355.title: Exchange value
538253663355.section: Exchange value and price according to Marx
538253663355.sentence: For Marx, exchange-value is not identical to the money price of a commodity.

0a8c2e6c03e7.title: Exchange value
0a8c2e6c03e7.section: Exchange value and price according to Marx
0a8c2e6c03e7.sentence: Actual money prices (or even equilibrium prices) will only ever roughly correspond to exchange-values.

9951b1b773b8.title: Exchange value
9951b1b773b8.section: Exchange value and price according to Marx
9951b1b773b8.sentence: The value of a good is determined by the socially necessary labour time required to produce it.

984a47e199bc.title: Exchange value
984a47e199bc.sentence: - the existence of a social need for it (a market demand) that must be met through trade, or at any event cannot be met otherwise;

d1b9dc77cc22.title: Exchange value
d1b9dc77cc22.sentence: - the legally sanctioned assertion of private ownership rights to the commodity and the right to trade it;

a7532b52c914.title: Exchange value
a7532b52c914.sentence: - the transferability of these private rights from one owner to another;

90a3fbd68b26.title: Exchange value
90a3fbd68b26.sentence: - the imposition of exclusivity of access to the commodity;

6ef1d5820303.title: Exchange value
6ef1d5820303.sentence: In modern neoclassical economics, exchange value itself is no longer explicitly theorised.

4330ea9fd68d.title: Exchange value
4330ea9fd68d.sentence: Exchange value thus becomes simply the price for which a good will trade in a given market which is identical to what Marx refers to as price.

659b92f49bd7.title: Commodification of nature
659b92f49bd7.sentence: By taking on a general quality of exchange value, they become commensurable.

3b161c4f51e5.title: Commodification of nature
3b161c4f51e5.sentence: Valuation is the manifestation of all expressions of worth (aesthetic, practical, ethical, et cetera) through a single exchange value.

10f382e0131a.title: Environmental philosophy
10f382e0131a.sentence: Environmental philosophy is the branch of philosophy that is concerned with the natural environment and humans' place within it.

b1dd80c50807.title: Environmental philosophy
b1dd80c50807.sentence: Environmental philosophy emerged as a branch of philosophy in 1970s.

9e42da3b8ee2.title: Environmental philosophy
9e42da3b8ee2.sentence: Early environmental philosophers include Seyyed Hossein Nasr, Richard Routley, Arne Næss, and J. Baird Callicott.

9ca9946f8bfb.title: Environmental philosophy
9ca9946f8bfb.sentence: A major debate arose in the 1970s and 80s was that of whether nature has intrinsic value in itself independent of human values or whether its value is merely instrumental, with ecocentric or deep ecology approaches emerging on the one hand versus consequentialist or pragmatist anthropocentric approaches on the other.

d0cc69b29015.title: Environmental philosophy
d0cc69b29015.sentence: Modern issues within environmental philosophy include but are not restricted to the concerns of environmental activism, questions raised by science and technology, environmental justice, and climate change.

38e1fb7153e5.title: Environmental philosophy
38e1fb7153e5.sentence: These include issues related to the depletion of finite resources and other harmful and permanent effects brought on to the environment by humans, as well as the ethical and practical problems raised by philosophies and practices of environmental conservation, restoration, and policy in general.

22506caad409.title: Environmental philosophy
22506caad409.sentence: Another debate that arose at this time was the debate over whether there really is such a thing as wilderness or not, or whether it is merely a cultural construct with colonialist implications as suggested by William Cronon.

b41eda618a28.title: Environmental philosophy
b41eda618a28.sentence: Another question that has settled on the minds of modern environmental philosophers is "Do rivers have rights?" At the same time environmental philosophy deals with the value human beings attach to different kinds of environmental experience, particularly how experiences in or close to non-human environments contrast with urban or industrialized experiences, and how this varies across cultures with close attention paid to indigenous people.

f8ea997605cf.title: Paradox of value
f8ea997605cf.sentence: The paradox of value, also known as the diamond–water paradox, is the paradox that, although water is on the whole more useful in terms of survival than diamonds, diamonds command a higher price in the market.

0df34374ccb8.title: Paradox of value
0df34374ccb8.sentence: The philosopher Adam Smith is often considered to be the classic presenter of this paradox, although it had already appeared as early as Plato's Euthydemus.

b8557805a8ed.title: Paradox of value
b8557805a8ed.sentence: The one may be called "value in use;" the other, "value in exchange." The things which have the greatest value in use have frequently little or no value in exchange; on the contrary, those which have the greatest value in exchange have frequently little or no value in use.

24464123fb0c.title: Paradox of value
24464123fb0c.sentence: Nothing is more useful than water: but it will purchase scarcely anything; scarcely anything can be had in exchange for it.

69613eea9f3d.title: Paradox of value
69613eea9f3d.sentence: Furthermore, Smith explains the value in exchange as being determined by labor, stating: "The real price of every thing, what every thing really costs to the man who wants to acquire it, is the toil and trouble of acquiring it." Hence, Smith denied a necessary relationship between price and utility.

c9656d31b45a.title: Paradox of value
c9656d31b45a.sentence: Proponents of the labor theory of value see that as the resolution of the paradox.

39f7fadfad81.title: Paradox of value
39f7fadfad81.sentence: In explaining the diamond-water paradox, marginalists explain that it is not the total usefulness of diamonds or water that determines price, but the usefulness of each unit of water or diamonds.

fed6e66141fc.title: Paradox of value
fed6e66141fc.sentence: It is true that the total utility of water to people is tremendous because they need it to survive; however, since water is in such large supply in the world, the marginal utility of water is low.

286b519705a6.title: Paradox of value
286b519705a6.sentence: They are of such low supply that the usefulness of one additional diamond is greater than the usefulness of one additional glass of water, which is in abundant supply.

a0fd6c095d2e.title: Paradox of value
a0fd6c095d2e.sentence: Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk illustrated this with the example of a farmer having five sacks of grain.

4ce44a732bc7.title: Paradox of value
4ce44a732bc7.sentence: Thus, the value of the fifth bag of grain is equal to the satisfaction he gets from feeding the pigeons.

0d971d2f6d9b.title: Paradox of value
0d971d2f6d9b.sentence: Conversely, a man dying of thirst in a desert would have greater marginal use for water than for diamonds so would pay more for water, perhaps up to the point at which he was no longer dying.

9df1cf0ad445.title: Marginal utility

9df1cf0ad445.sentence: Smith suggested that there was an irrational divide between the 'use value' of something and the 'exchange value'.

8aac5c6209ce.sentence: Nothing is more useful than water: but it will purchase scarcely anything.

28c01e7800a1.title: Instrumental and intrinsic value
28c01e7800a1.sentence: In moral philosophy, instrumental and intrinsic value are the distinction between what is a means to an end and what is as an end in itself.

1971314b191a.title: Instrumental and intrinsic value
1971314b191a.sentence: A tool or appliance, such as a hammer or washing machine, has instrumental value because it helps one pound in a nail or clean clothes, respectively.

63b031eb126a.title: Instrumental and intrinsic value
63b031eb126a.sentence: Happiness and pleasure are typically considered to have intrinsic value insofar as asking why someone would want them makes little sense: they are desirable for their own sake irrespective of their possible instrumental value.

b59151ff4f1d.title: Instrumental and intrinsic value
b59151ff4f1d.sentence: The classic names instrumental and intrinsic were coined by sociologist Max Weber, who spent years studying good meanings people assigned to their actions and beliefs.

10bcb20682b6.title: Instrumental and intrinsic value
10bcb20682b6.sentence: John Dewey thought that belief in intrinsic value was a mistake.

7560b10d543a.title: Instrumental and intrinsic value
7560b10d543a.sentence: Although the application of instrumental value is easily contaminated, it is the only means humans have to coordinate group behaviour efficiently and legitimately.

76306a951d8c.title: Instrumental and intrinsic value
76306a951d8c.section: J. Fagg Foster > Revised definition of 'instrumental value'
76306a951d8c.sentence: This definition stresses the condition that instrumental success is never short term; it must not lead down a dead-end street.

ce1bc080dcb4.title: Instrumental and intrinsic value
ce1bc080dcb4.section: J. Fagg Foster > Revised definition of 'instrumental value'
ce1bc080dcb4.sentence: The same point is made by the currently popular concern for sustainability—a synonym for instrumental value.

363724fc82ee.title: Anthropocentrism
363724fc82ee.sentence: Anthropocentrism (from Ancient Greek ἄνθρωπος (ánthrōpos) 'human' and κέντρον (kéntron) 'center') is the belief that human beings are the central or most important entity on the planet.

81a6b3d410eb.title: Anthropocentrism
81a6b3d410eb.sentence: From an anthropocentric perspective, humankind is seen as separate from nature and superior to it, and other entities (animals, plants, minerals, etc.) are viewed as resources for humans to use.

142ff04f6877.title: Anthropocentrism
142ff04f6877.sentence: It is a major concept in the field of environmental ethics and environmental philosophy, where it is often considered to be the root cause of problems created by human action within the ecosphere.

b6ae9154bd3c.title: Anthropocentrism
b6ae9154bd3c.sentence: However, many proponents of anthropocentrism state that this is not necessarily the case: they argue that a sound long-term view acknowledges that the global environment must be made continually suitable for humans and that the real issue is shallow anthropocentrism.

819aac261c2b.title: Anthropocentrism
819aac261c2b.sentence: According to William Grey, the problem with a "shallow" viewpoint is not that it is human-centred: "What's wrong with shallow views is not their concern about the well-being of humans, but that they do not really consider enough in what that well-being consists.

7228c3a2cedc.title: Anthropocentrism
7228c3a2cedc.sentence: According to this view, we need to develop an enriched, fortified anthropocentric notion of human interest to replace the dominant short-term, sectional and self-regarding conception." In turn, Plumwood in Environmental Culture: The Ecological Crisis of Reason argued that Grey's anthropocentrism is inadequate.

ad2936100fc5.title: Anthropocentrism
ad2936100fc5.sentence: Val Plumwood argued that anthropocentrism plays an analogous role in green theory to androcentrism in feminist theory and ethnocentrism in anti-racist theory.

456391b68792.title: Anthropocentrism
456391b68792.sentence: The use of the word "dominion" in the Genesis has been used to justify an anthropocentric worldview, but recently some have found it controversial, viewing it as possibly a mistranslation from the Hebrew.

25ef4c81fee6.title: Anthropocentrism
25ef4c81fee6.sentence: In his follow-up exhortation, Laudate Deum (2023) he refers to a preferable understanding of "the unique and central value of the human being amid the marvellous concert of all God's creatures" as a "situated anthropocentrism".

5438a1392d90.title: Anthropocentrism
5438a1392d90.section: Moral status of animals > Early critiques
5438a1392d90.sentence: Later, J. Howard Moore, in The Universal Kinship (1906), expanded on this critique, asserting that Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species (1859) "sealed the doom" of anthropocentrism.

8b8021dfba9e.title: Intrinsic value (ethics)
8b8021dfba9e.sentence: In ethics, intrinsic value is a property of anything that is valuable on its own.

d30eb4bbeae8.title: Intrinsic value (ethics)
d30eb4bbeae8.sentence: Intrinsic value is always something that an object has "in itself" or "for its own sake", and is an intrinsic property.

81c6d793299a.title: Intrinsic value (ethics)
81c6d793299a.sentence: Intrinsic value is in contrast to instrumental value (also known as extrinsic value), which is a property of anything that derives its value from a relation to another intrinsically valuable thing.

4135378c340f.title: Intrinsic value (ethics)
4135378c340f.sentence: All major normative ethical theories identify something as being intrinsically valuable.

15c71fd7cfe7.title: Intrinsic value (ethics)
15c71fd7cfe7.sentence: For instance, for a virtue ethicist, eudaimonia (human flourishing, sometimes translated as "happiness") has intrinsic value, whereas things that bring you happiness (such as having a family) may be merely instrumentally valuable.

89e0d54408d9.title: Intrinsic value (ethics)
89e0d54408d9.sentence: Similarly, consequentialists may identify pleasure, the lack of pain, and/or the fulfillment of one's preferences as having intrinsic value, making actions that produce them merely instrumentally valuable.

490b72216f97.title: Environmental ethics
490b72216f97.sentence: Norwegian environmentalist and philosopher Arne Næss's "Deep Ecology", coined in 1972, was extremely influential in advocating for an environmental ethic that provided all non-human entities with intrinsic value.

353b72a14d8f.title: Decline in insect populations
353b72a14d8f.sentence: According to the Zoological Society of London, in addition to such loss of instrumental value, the decline also represents a loss of the declining species' intrinsic value.

61c02a9f16ce.title: Intrinsic value (ethics)
61c02a9f16ce.section: Types of intrinsic value > Absolute and relative
61c02a9f16ce.sentence: There is an ongoing discussion on whether an absolute intrinsic value exists at all, for instance in pragmatism.

23459a037680.title: Intrinsic value (ethics)
23459a037680.section: Types of intrinsic value > Absolute and relative
23459a037680.sentence: In other words, he only believed in relative intrinsic value, but not any absolute intrinsic value.

29f933d3a506.title: Deep ecology
29f933d3a506.sentence: Deep ecology is an environmental philosophy that promotes the inherent worth of all living beings regardless of their instrumental utility to human needs, and argues that modern human societies should be restructured in accordance with such ideas.

ddab8640f17e.title: Deep ecology
ddab8640f17e.sentence: Deep ecology's core principle is the belief that the living environment as a whole should be respected and regarded as having certain basic moral and legal rights to live and flourish, independent of its instrumental benefits for human use.

ad3fbe3684d1.title: Deep ecology
ad3fbe3684d1.sentence: The phrase "Deep Ecology" first appeared in a 1973 article by the Norwegian philosopher Arne Næss.

a33c31fde44a.title: Deep ecology
a33c31fde44a.sentence: When Arne Næss coined the term deep ecology, he compared it favourably with shallow ecology which he criticized for its utilitarian and anthropocentric attitude to nature and for its materialist and consumer-oriented outlook, describing its "central objective" as "the health and affluence of people in the developed countries." William D. Grey believes that developing a non-anthropocentric set of values is "a hopeless quest".

44d9424b9025.title: Deep ecology
44d9424b9025.sentence: Proponents of deep ecology oppose the narrative that man is separate from nature, is in charge of nature, or is the steward of nature, or that nature exists as a resource to be freely exploited.

e9f6fa5a7a33.title: Deep ecology
e9f6fa5a7a33.sentence: They believe that the current materialist paradigm must be replaced – as Næss pointed out, this involves more than merely getting rid of capitalism and the concept of economic growth, or "progress", that is critically endangering the biosphere.

76e3d841b2e9.title: Deep ecology
76e3d841b2e9.sentence: Sessions considers the publication of Carson's 1962 seminal book Silent Spring as the beginning of the contemporary deep ecology movement.

8377e39b263f.title: Deep ecology
8377e39b263f.sentence: First, because deep ecologists believe that environmental movements must shift from an anthropocentric to an ecocentric approach, they fail to recognize the two most fundamental ecological crises facing the world: overconsumption in the global north and increasing militarization.

cade5176683b.title: Deep ecology
cade5176683b.sentence: Social ecologist Murray Bookchin interpreted deep ecology as being misanthropic, due in part to the characterization of humanity by David Foreman, of the environmental advocacy group Earth First!, as a "pathological infestation on the Earth".

d1e8e03d4e64.title: Ecosystem valuation

d1e8e03d4e64.sentence: Arguments about the non-market valuation of ecosystem can be found by referring to environmental ethics and deep ecology.

0b6a77fc0433.title: Ecocentrism
0b6a77fc0433.sentence: Ecocentrism (/ˌɛkoʊˈsɛntrɪzəm/; from Greek: οἶκος /ˈoi.kos/ oikos, 'house' and κέντρον /ˈken.tron/ kentron, 'center') is a term used by environmental philosophers and ecologists to denote a nature-centered, as opposed to human-centered (i.e., anthropocentric), system of values.

de86de70f82c.title: Ecocentrism
de86de70f82c.sentence: The ontological belief denies that there are any existential divisions between human and non-human nature sufficient to claim that humans are either (a) the sole bearers of intrinsic value or (b) possess greater intrinsic value than non-human nature.

106103c896cd.title: Ecocentrism
106103c896cd.sentence: Thus the subsequent ethical claim is for an equality of intrinsic value across human and non-human nature, or biospherical egalitarianism.

f2a320a42c39.title: Ecocentrism
f2a320a42c39.sentence: The ecocentric ethic was conceived by Aldo Leopold and recognizes that all species, including humans, are the product of a long evolutionary process and are inter-related in their life processes.

0796db7f3b87.title: Ecocentrism
0796db7f3b87.sentence: The writings of Aldo Leopold and his idea of the land ethic and good environmental management are a key element to this philosophy.

5c03d0845c91.title: Ecocentrism
5c03d0845c91.sentence: Ecocentrism focuses on the biotic community as a whole and strives to maintain ecosystem composition and ecological processes.

66c2b421c162.title: Ecocentrism
66c2b421c162.section: Relationship to other similar philosophies > Biocentrism
66c2b421c162.sentence: Ecocentrism recognizes Earth's interactive living and non-living systems rather than just the Earth's organisms (biocentrism) as central in importance.

345269f9af1a.title: Ecocentrism
345269f9af1a.section: Relationship to other similar philosophies > Anthropocentrism
345269f9af1a.sentence: Anthropocentrism is alleged to leave the case for the protection of non-human nature subject to the demands of human utility, and thus never more than contingent on the demands of human welfare.

5bdaecdb8a71.title: Ecocentrism
5bdaecdb8a71.section: Relationship to other similar philosophies > Anthropocentrism
5bdaecdb8a71.sentence: An ecocentric ethic, by contrast, is believed to be necessary in order to develop a non-contingent basis for protecting the natural world.

4bf421864692.title: Ecocentrism
4bf421864692.section: Relationship to other similar philosophies > Anthropocentrism
4bf421864692.sentence: Critics of ecocentrism have argued that it opens the doors to an anti-humanist morality that risks sacrificing human well-being for the sake of an ill-defined 'greater good'.

317f3a9f46fb.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
317f3a9f46fb.sentence: In environmental ethics, biocentrism (from Greek βίος bios, "life" and κέντρον kentron, "center") is a view that extends equal inherent value to all living things.

6815127856fe.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
6815127856fe.sentence: It stands in contrast to anthropocentrism, which centers on the value of humans, and to sentientism, which places value in sentient beings (those capable of having valenced experiences like pleasure or pain).

9cd100c3cf3f.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
9cd100c3cf3f.sentence: The related ecocentrism extends inherent value to the whole of nature.

de3a9373f544.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
de3a9373f544.sentence: The four main pillars of a biocentric outlook are:

52b7606687cf.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
52b7606687cf.sentence: - Humans and all other species are members of Earth's community.

291510df44cc.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
291510df44cc.sentence: - All species are part of a system of interdependence.

3d783593c3f7.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
3d783593c3f7.sentence: - All living organisms pursue their own "good" in their own ways.

744abcf5059e.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
744abcf5059e.sentence: - Human beings are not inherently superior to other living things.

2e978501fc88.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
2e978501fc88.sentence: Biocentric ethics includes Albert Schweitzer's ethics of "Reverence for Life", Peter Singer's ethics of Animal Liberation and Paul W. Taylor's ethics of biocentric egalitarianism.

ce831f910a97.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
ce831f910a97.sentence: Advocates of biocentrism often promote the preservation of biodiversity, animal rights, and environmental protection.

e01ea26b5c45.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
e01ea26b5c45.sentence: Some of this criticism grows out of the concern that biocentrism is an anti-human paradigm and that it will not hesitate to sacrifice human well-being for the greater good.

41719ec9c04b.title: Biocentrism (ethics)
41719ec9c04b.sentence: Biocentrism has also been criticized for its individualism; emphasizing too much on the importance of individual life and neglecting the importance of collective groups, such as an ecosystem.

848ea831350d.title: Endangered Species Act of 1973
848ea831350d.section: Challenges and controversies > The biocentric focus of listing and recovery
848ea831350d.sentence: A law review article published in 2024 states, "Alone among major environmental laws, the ESA explicitly prioritizes the protection and conservation of non-human species and constrains the ability of government agencies to consider trade-offs." 2b5f320b0bfa.title: Environmental philosophy
2b5f320b0bfa.sentence: The values of nature encompass the various ways societies perceive and attribute importance to the non-human world, spanning extrinsic, intrinsic, and relational dimensions.

0b5f54c6f552.title: Environmental philosophy
0b5f54c6f552.sentence: Extrinsic (Instrumental) values: Refer to nature's utility to humans, such as the provision of timber, purification of water and air, carbon sequestration or pollination—often called ecosystem services for which comprehensive classifications have been made.

1c2a6f5bf714.title: Environmental philosophy
1c2a6f5bf714.sentence: Many can be described with an economic value, leading to inclusion in environmental impact assessments, cost-benefit analyses, and systems of national accounts.

1938595f4433.title: Environmental philosophy
1938595f4433.sentence: Intrinsic values: the philosophical stance that all living things and natural systems have value or inherent worth, regardless of any utility to humans.

17a33295c55f.title: Environmental philosophy
17a33295c55f.sentence: Relational values: the diverse meaningful relationships, responsibilities, and cultural connections between humans and nature, have been expressed over the centuries.

5694e136ae66.title: Environmental philosophy
5694e136ae66.sentence: Building on the work of the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment, the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES), advocates for such a broad articulation of nature's values to guide policy decision making and ecological restoration.

1b579fc39102.title: Ecocentrism
1b579fc39102.section: Relationship to other similar philosophies > Technocentrism
1b579fc39102.sentence: Ecocentrism is also contrasted with technocentrism (meaning values centred on technology) as two opposing perspectives on attitudes towards human technology and its ability to affect, control and even protect the environment.

d0a653bbe3c2.sentence: Technocentrics, including imperialists, have absolute faith in technology and industry and firmly believe that humans have control over nature.

a24f474cf0e8.title: Ecocentrism
a24f474cf0e8.section: Relationship to other similar philosophies > Technocentrism
a24f474cf0e8.sentence: Although technocentrics may accept that environmental problems do exist, they do not see them as problems to be solved by a reduction in industry.

675576a99466.title: Ecocentrism
675576a99466.section: Relationship to other similar philosophies > Technocentrism
675576a99466.sentence: Indeed, technocentrics see that the way forward for developed and developing countries and the solutions to our environmental problems today lie in scientific and technological advancement.

68e3e79a88df.title: Ecocentrism
68e3e79a88df.section: Relationship to other similar philosophies > Technocentrism
68e3e79a88df.sentence: Ecocentrics, including "deep green" ecologists, see themselves as being subject to nature, rather than in control of it.

7897dca29db6.title: Ecocentrism
7897dca29db6.section: Relationship to other similar philosophies > Technocentrism
7897dca29db6.sentence: Ecocentrics will argue that the natural world should be respected for its processes and products, and that low impact technology and self-reliance is more desirable than technological control of nature.

b388fe4b29e9.title: Environmental philosophy
b388fe4b29e9.sentence: In 1982, Murray Bookchin described his philosophy of Social Ecology which provides a framework for understanding nature, our relationship with nature, and our relationships to each other.

753d90e84aa6.title: Environmental philosophy
753d90e84aa6.sentence: Instead, social ecology defines nature as a tendency in healthy ecosystems toward greater levels of diversity, complementarity, and freedom.

d88ce5289179.title: Environmental philosophy

3ba711c947d6.title: Best–worst scaling

e881059d2c18.title: Cheap talk

0a3341b0b01e.title: Cheap talk

8f5a42afa5b8.sentence: In statistics, a latent class model (LCM) is a model for clustering multivariate discrete data.

f78086b565a2.title: Latent class model
f78086b565a2.sentence: It is called a latent class model because the class to which each data point belongs is unobserved (or latent).

82d4e4371c1c.title: Latent class model
82d4e4371c1c.sentence: It assumes that the data arise from a mixture of discrete distributions, within each of which the variables are independent.

adb427659725.title: Latent class model

39a782a6e685.title: Meta-regression
39a782a6e685.sentence: Meta-regression is a meta-analysis that uses regression analysis to combine, compare, and synthesize research findings from multiple studies while adjusting for the effects of available covariates on a response variable.

1a36eede67af.title: Meta-regression
1a36eede67af.sentence: A meta-regression analysis aims to reconcile conflicting studies or corroborate consistent ones; a meta-regression analysis is therefore characterized by the collated studies and their corresponding data sets—whether the response variable is study-level (or equivalently aggregate) data or individual participant data (or individual patient data in medicine).

fde3ea919526.title: Meta-regression

95ed69278236.title: Meta-regression
95ed69278236.sentence: Mixed-effect meta-regression includes a random-effect term in addition to the fixed effects, suggesting that the studies are heterogeneous.

71cbf3b0255b.title: Meta-regression

71cbf3b0255b.sentence: The mixed effects model allows for within-study variation and between-study variation and is therefore taken as the most flexible model to choose in many applications.

4d7f70a1a0f0.title: Meta-regression

c8c0e3656d75.title: Meta-regression
c8c0e3656d75.sentence: Recent applications include quantitative reviews of the empirical literature in economics, business, energy and water policy.

7dbb9c0ed314.title: Meta-regression
7dbb9c0ed314.sentence: Examples include own price elasticities for alcohol, tobacco, water and energy.

b9b5da17a230.title: Meta-regression
b9b5da17a230.sentence: Meta-regression is an increasingly popular tool to evaluate the available evidence in cost-benefit analysis studies of a policy or program spread across multiple studies.

53a57a821522.title: Net present value
53a57a821522.sentence: Net present value (NPV), also known as net present worth (NPW) is a method for assessing whether future amounts of money are worth more or less than the cost of an investment made today.

069df8da6c98.title: Net present value
069df8da6c98.sentence: Net Present Value measures the value of an asset that has cashflow by adding up the present value of all future cash flows that asset will generate.

a22ca990d7c0.title: Net present value
a22ca990d7c0.sentence: NPV works by converting future cash flows into their “present value,” recognising that money available now is more valuable than the same amount received later.

45d3e01838d7.title: Net present value
45d3e01838d7.sentence: A cash flow today is more valuable than an identical cash flow in the future because a present flow can be invested immediately and begin earning returns, while a future flow cannot.

0c5f02db8f62.title: Net present value
0c5f02db8f62.sentence: After the cash flow for each period is calculated, the present value (PV) of each one is achieved by discounting its future value (see Formula) at a periodic rate of return (the rate of return dictated by the market).

9cf776cc3473.title: Net present value
9cf776cc3473.sentence: - i is the discount rate, i.e. the return that could be earned per unit of time on an investment with similar risk

32cfbdc4a2b2.title: Net present value
32cfbdc4a2b2.sentence: NPV is the sum of all the discounted future cash flows.

a81fcd16b425.title: Net present value
a81fcd16b425.sentence: For example, a lender may offer 99 cents for the promise of receiving $1.00 a month from now, but the promise to receive that same dollar 20 years in the future would be worth much less today to that same person (lender), even if the payback in both cases was equally certain.

9284a4387bb5.title: Net present value
9284a4387bb5.sentence: A positive net present value indicates that the projected earnings generated by a project or investment (in present dollars) exceeds the anticipated costs (also in present dollars).

d12e812e917e.title: Net present value
d12e812e917e.sentence: This concept is the basis for the Net Present Value Rule, which dictates that the only investments that should be made are those with positive NPVs.

df57d63e2d41.title: Net present value
df57d63e2d41.section: Advantages and disadvantages of using Net Present Value > Disadvantages > Relies on input parameters such as knowledge of future cash flows
df57d63e2d41.sentence: The NPV is heavily dependent on knowledge of future cash flows, their timing, the length of a project, the initial investment required, and the discount rate.

b648166bc906.title: Net present value

b648166bc906.sentence: Hence, it can only be accurate if these input parameters are correct; although, sensitivity analyzes can be undertaken to examine how the NPV changes as the input variables are changed, thus reducing the uncertainty of the NPV.

eca9910674fb.title: Net present value

eca9910674fb.sentence: The accuracy of the NPV method relies heavily on the choice of a discount rate and hence discount factor, representing an investment's true risk premium.

9c50532883f4.sentence: The NPV calculation is purely financial and thus does not consider non-financial metrics that may be relevant to an investment decision.

632772876753.title: Net present value

a1c6b824c784.title: Cost–benefit analysis
a1c6b824c784.sentence: Cost–benefit analysis (CBA), sometimes also called benefit–cost analysis, is a systematic approach to estimating the strengths and weaknesses of alternatives.

08671d8781c0.title: Cost–benefit analysis
08671d8781c0.sentence: A CBA may be used to compare completed or potential courses of action, and to estimate or evaluate the value against the cost of a decision, project, or policy.

67cd1816b4ef.title: Cost–benefit analysis
67cd1816b4ef.sentence: - To determine if an investment (or decision) is sound, ascertaining if – and by how much – its benefits outweigh its costs.

9237172c12b9.title: Cost–benefit analysis
9237172c12b9.sentence: - To provide a basis for comparing investments (or decisions), comparing the total expected cost of each option with its total expected benefits.

82645e235ed3.title: Cost–benefit analysis
82645e235ed3.sentence: - Convert all costs and benefits into a common currency.

bdf766b8c2b4.title: Cost–benefit analysis
bdf766b8c2b4.sentence: - Apply a discount rate (usually a specific social discount rate).

e615ddfe8d58.title: Cost–benefit analysis
e615ddfe8d58.sentence: - Calculate the net present value of actions under consideration.

412f996b7b9f.title: Cost–benefit analysis
412f996b7b9f.sentence: The guiding principle of evaluating benefits is to list all parties affected by an intervention and add the positive or negative value (usually monetary) that they ascribe to its effect on their welfare.

149e5b5c9bf7.title: Cost–benefit analysis
149e5b5c9bf7.sentence: Costs tend to be most thoroughly represented in cost–benefit analyses due to relatively-abundant market data.

b3e2abb56fd8.title: Cost–benefit analysis
b3e2abb56fd8.sentence: Another metric is valuing the environment, which in the 21st century is typically assessed by valuing ecosystem services to humans (such as air and water quality and pollution).

f1e0f0abe4cd.title: Cost–benefit analysis

3606651d79f6.title: Cost–benefit analysis
3606651d79f6.sentence: The Flood Control Act of 1939 was instrumental in establishing CBA as federal policy, requiring that "the benefits to whomever they accrue [be] in excess of the estimated costs."

6b217e7dff8a.title: Shadow price
6b217e7dff8a.sentence: A shadow price is the monetary value assigned to an abstract or intangible commodity which is not traded in the marketplace.

e0939707a91f.title: Shadow price
e0939707a91f.sentence: Shadow prices are the real economic prices given to goods and services after they have been appropriately adjusted by removing distortionary market instruments and incorporating the societal impact of the respective good or service.

5979a7d88765.title: Shadow price
5979a7d88765.sentence: The need for shadow prices arises as a result of “externalities” and the presence of distortionary market instruments.

249bb34cf672.title: Shadow price
249bb34cf672.sentence: Shadow prices are also known as the recalculation of known market prices in order to account for the presence of distortionary market instruments (e.g. quotas, tariffs, taxes or subsidies).

51c68d29514f.title: Shadow price
51c68d29514f.sentence: A shadow price is often calculated based on a group of assumptions and estimates because it lacks reliable data, so it is subjective and somewhat inaccurate.

fd8992748df4.title: Shadow price
fd8992748df4.sentence: Although shadow pricing may be inaccurate, it is still often used in cost-benefit analyses.

2455d4a6b1ce.title: Shadow price
2455d4a6b1ce.sentence: Shadow pricing is frequently used to figure out the monetary values of intangibles which are hard to quantify factors during cost-benefit analyses.

c2708e1ef9a2.title: Shadow price

805ee48c5c23.title: Value of a statistical life
805ee48c5c23.sentence: The value of a statistical life (VSL) is an economic value used to quantify the benefit of avoiding a fatality.

1594f5bf01c2.title: Value of a statistical life
1594f5bf01c2.sentence: As such, it is a statistical term, the value of reducing the average number of deaths by one.

aff690728111.title: Value of a statistical life
aff690728111.section: Treatment in economics and methods of calculation
aff690728111.sentence: This again emphasizes that VSL is more of an estimate of willingness to pay for small reductions in mortality risks rather than how much a human life is worth.

7c84b75a8269.title: Value of a statistical life
7c84b75a8269.section: Treatment in economics and methods of calculation
7c84b75a8269.sentence: The VSL is very different from the value of an actual life.

0c59e1df67a9.title: Value of a statistical life
0c59e1df67a9.section: Treatment in economics and methods of calculation
0c59e1df67a9.sentence: It is the value placed on changes in the likelihood of death, not the price someone would pay to avoid certain death.

28527716359d.title: Value of a statistical life
28527716359d.section: Treatment in economics and methods of calculation
28527716359d.sentence: > Suppose each person in a sample of 100,000 people were asked how much he or she would be willing to pay for a reduction in their individual risk of dying by 1 in 100,000, or 0.001%, over the next year.

e95135fca2f1.title: Value of a statistical life
e95135fca2f1.section: Treatment in economics and methods of calculation
e95135fca2f1.sentence: Then the total dollar amount that the group would be willing to pay to save one statistical life in a year would be $100 per person × 100,000 people, or $10 million.

b9346383110a.title: Value of a statistical life
b9346383110a.section: Treatment in economics and methods of calculation
b9346383110a.sentence: This is what is meant by the "value of a statistical life".

a66df8e4d1cd.sentence: Similarly, compensating differentials, which are the reduced or additional wage payments that are intended to compensate workers for conveniences or downsides of a job, can be used for VSL calculations.

80156b0757be.title: Value of a statistical life
80156b0757be.section: Treatment in economics and methods of calculation
80156b0757be.sentence: Economists might estimate the VSL by simply asking people (e.g. through questionnaires) how much they would be willing to pay for a reduction in the likelihood of dying, perhaps by purchasing safety improvements.

258558884faa.title: Value of a statistical life

dafbd5451105.section: Treatment in economics and methods of calculation
dafbd5451105.sentence: All of these methods might result in a VSL that is overstated or understated.

ac52a5ba27dd.title: Value of a statistical life
ac52a5ba27dd.sentence: The motivation for placing a monetary value on life is to enable policy and regulatory analysts to allocate the limited supply of resources, infrastructure, labor, and tax revenue.

f56fbaf629ef.sentence: Knowing the value of life is helpful when performing a cost-benefit analysis, especially in regard to public policy.

08e702a8f744.sentence: Another health-based predictor of environmental use value is the value of a statistical life (VSL), which provides an estimate of how much people are willing to pay for small reductions in their risk of dying from environmental hazards.

ca18de0f2dfa.section: Estimates of the value of life > European Union > Sweden

070ccf46142b.sentence: As of 2013, the value of preventing a fatal casualty was £1.7m (2013 prices) in UK.

ee96468166f7.sentence: Elizabeth Anderson and other philosophers have argued that the methods for measuring the value of a statistical life are insufficiently accurate as they rely on wage studies that are conducted in non-competitive labor markets where workers have insufficient information about their working conditions to accurately determine the risk of death from taking a particular job.

7984d7273028.title: Value of a statistical life
7984d7273028.sentence: Further these philosophers contend that some goods (including mortality risk, as well as environmental goods) are simply incommensurate, it is impossible to compare them, and therefore impossible to monetize them and put them on a single scale, making the very practice of valuing a statistical life problematic.

f877c80b0e37.title: Value of a statistical life
f877c80b0e37.sentence: In health economics and in the pharmaceutical sector, however, the value of a quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) is used more often than the VSL.

c68c02d98487.title: Value of a statistical life
c68c02d98487.sentence: While QALY measures the quality of life ranging from 0–1, VSL monetizes the values using willingness-to-pay.

622036ad17ab.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis
622036ad17ab.sentence: Cost-effectiveness analysis (CEA) is a form of economic analysis that compares the relative costs and outcomes (effects) of different courses of action.

6aa0c4e4290d.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis
6aa0c4e4290d.sentence: Cost-effectiveness analysis is distinct from cost–benefit analysis, which assigns a monetary value to the measure of effect.

21644623f084.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis
21644623f084.sentence: Cost-effectiveness analysis is often used in the field of health services, where it may be inappropriate to monetize health effect.

72c3fc748f62.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis
72c3fc748f62.sentence: Typically the CEA is expressed in terms of a ratio where the denominator is a gain in health from a measure (years of life, premature births averted, sight-years gained) and the numerator is the cost associated with the health gain.

2c202a940f55.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis
2c202a940f55.sentence: The most commonly used outcome measure is quality-adjusted life years (QALY).

636fe592ec97.title: Cost–benefit analysis
636fe592ec97.sentence: For some environmental effects, cost–benefit analysis can be replaced by cost-effectiveness analysis.

3c558585835d.title: Cost–benefit analysis
3c558585835d.sentence: This is especially true when one type of physical outcome is sought, such as a reduction in energy use by an increase in energy efficiency.

e684a7d9a6c9.title: Cost–benefit analysis
e684a7d9a6c9.sentence: Using cost-effectiveness analysis is less laborious and time-consuming, since it does not involve the monetization of outcomes (which can be difficult in some cases).

ead1e8285134.title: Economic analysis of climate change
ead1e8285134.sentence: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis (CEA) is preferable to CBA when the benefits of impacts, adaptation and mitigation are difficult to estimate in monetary terms.

4f228dc9b175.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis
4f228dc9b175.sentence: Cost-effectiveness analysis focuses on maximising the average level of an outcome, distributional cost-effectiveness analysis extends the core methods of CEA to incorporate concerns for the distribution of outcomes as well as their average level and make trade-offs between equity and efficiency, these more sophisticated methods are of particular interest when analysing interventions to tackle health inequality.

f2358a9fc163.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis
f2358a9fc163.sentence: A 1995 study of the cost-effectiveness of reviewed over 500 life-saving interventions found that the median cost-effectiveness was $42,000 per life-year saved.

cc526ac6368a.title: Quality-adjusted life year
cc526ac6368a.sentence: The quality-adjusted life year (QALY) is a generic measure of disease burden, including both the quality and the quantity of life lived.

2e209998d870.title: Quality-adjusted life year
2e209998d870.sentence: One QALY equates to one year in perfect health.

1605752d1cf7.title: Quality-adjusted life year
1605752d1cf7.sentence: QALY scores range from 1 (perfect health) to 0 (dead).

1a7b842f8078.title: Quality-adjusted life year
1a7b842f8078.sentence: For example, 1 year of life lived in a situation with utility 0.5 yields 0.5 QALYs—a person experiencing this state is getting only 50% of the possible value of that year.

940534bbf678.title: Quality-adjusted life year
940534bbf678.sentence: The QALY calculation is simple: the change in utility value induced by the treatment is multiplied by the duration of the treatment effect to provide the number of QALYs gained.

57ae335897a5.title: Quality-adjusted life year
57ae335897a5.sentence: - Time-trade-off (TTO): Respondents are asked to choose between remaining in a state of ill health for a period of time, or being restored to perfect health but having a shorter life expectancy.

e11427037c2f.title: Quality-adjusted life year
e11427037c2f.sentence: - Standard gamble (SG): Respondents are asked to choose between remaining in a state of ill health for a period of time, or choosing a medical intervention which has a chance of either restoring them to perfect health or killing them.

f7aa8537dc4a.title: Quality-adjusted life year
f7aa8537dc4a.sentence: - Visual analogue scale (VAS): Respondents are asked to rate a state of ill health on a scale from 0 to 100, with 0 representing being dead, and 100 representing perfect health.

5cc9d73fc532.title: Wellbeing economy

316452b025f1.sentence: The economics of happiness or happiness economics is the theoretical, qualitative and quantitative study of happiness and quality of life, including positive and negative affects, well-being, life satisfaction and related concepts – typically tying economics more closely than usual with other social sciences, like sociology and psychology, as well as physical health.

60df13b9113b.title: Happiness economics
