be67518e4278.sentence: For instance, in the case of a manufactured product, environmental impacts are assessed from raw material extraction and processing (cradle), through the product's manufacture, distribution and use, to the recycling or final disposal of the materials composing it (grave).

0c5724508960.title: Life-cycle assessment
0c5724508960.sentence: An LCA study involves a thorough inventory of the energy and materials that are required across the supply chain and value chain of a product, process or service, and calculates the corresponding emissions to the environment.

8f9bd3909f16.title: Carbon footprint
8f9bd3909f16.section: Underlying concepts for calculations > Combination with life cycle analysis (LCA)
8f9bd3909f16.sentence: It is not limited to the greenhouse gas emissions.

6276250b5fc6.title: Carbon footprint
6276250b5fc6.section: Underlying concepts for calculations > Combination with life cycle analysis (LCA)
6276250b5fc6.sentence: It includes water pollution, air pollution, ecotoxicity and similar types of pollution.

6be8e3c3227e.title: Life-cycle assessment
6be8e3c3227e.sentence: LCA was primarily used as a comparison tool, providing informative information on the environmental impacts of a product and comparing it to available alternatives.

a8ec08901832.title: Life-cycle assessment
a8ec08901832.sentence: Its potential applications expanded to include marketing, product design, product development, strategic planning, consumer education, ecolabeling and government policy.

84a485fa189b.title: Life-cycle assessment
84a485fa189b.sentence: A life cycle analysis is only as accurate and valid as is its basis set of data.

199c18be734f.title: Life-cycle assessment
199c18be734f.sentence: There are two fundamental types of LCA data–unit process data, and environmental input-output (EIO) data.

42e70ced7095.title: Life-cycle assessment
42e70ced7095.sentence: Not every factor, however, can be reduced to a number and inserted into a model.

3828e7207695.title: Life-cycle assessment
3828e7207695.sentence: Rigid system boundaries make accounting for changes in the system difficult.

458b5f762601.title: Emission intensity
458b5f762601.sentence: An emission intensity (also carbon intensity or C.I.) is the emission rate of a given pollutant relative to the intensity of a specific activity, or an industrial production process; for example grams of carbon dioxide released per megajoule of energy produced, or the ratio of greenhouse gas emissions produced to gross domestic product (GDP).

87f690407280.title: Emission intensity
87f690407280.sentence: Emission intensities are used to derive estimates of air pollutant or greenhouse gas emissions based on the amount of fuel combusted, the number of animals in animal husbandry, on industrial production levels, distances traveled or similar activity data.

6a88adcdbf2b.title: Emission intensity
6a88adcdbf2b.sentence: Emission intensities may also be used to compare the environmental impact of different fuels or activities.

4dc81256ac3c.title: Emission intensity
4dc81256ac3c.sentence: One commonly used figure is carbon intensity per kilowatt-hour (CIPK), which is used to compare emissions from different sources of electrical power.

9baf771e5f68.title: Emission intensity
9baf771e5f68.sentence: Coal, being mostly carbon, emits a lot of CO2 when burnt: it has a high CO2 emission intensity.

e826ba542496.title: Emission intensity
e826ba542496.sentence: Natural gas, being methane (CH4), has 4 hydrogen atoms to burn for each one of carbon and thus has medium CO2 emission intensity.

8b573edb0eda.title: Emission intensity
8b573edb0eda.section: Carbon intensity of regions > Carbon intensity in Europe
8b573edb0eda.sentence: Total CO2 emissions per unit of GDP, the “CO2 intensity”, decreased more rapidly than energy intensity: by 2.3%/year and 1.4%/year, respectively, on average between 1990 and 2007.

611ad69a422d.title: Emission intensity
611ad69a422d.sentence: - The whole life-cycle assessment (LCA): this includes not only the carbon emissions due to a specific process, but also those due to the production and end-of-life of materials, plants and machineries used for the considered process.

963a96eafff9.title: Emission intensity
963a96eafff9.sentence: - Methods not considering LCA aspects but only the emissions occurring during a specific process; i.e. just the combustion of a fuel in a power plant, without considering the Upstream emissions.

9db760caf202.title: Emission intensity
9db760caf202.sentence: Different calculation methods can lead to different results.

35aed837a0c1.title: Greenhouse gas emissions
35aed837a0c1.sentence: The terms "carbon intensity" and "emissions intensity" are also sometimes used.

ccd6f4b947d3.title: Kaya identity
ccd6f4b947d3.section: Current trend and future projections > Emission intensity of energy (F/E)
ccd6f4b947d3.sentence: However, the carbon intensity of the global energy supply has declined by 13%, from 66.3 kg CO2/GJ in 1978 to 58.0 kg CO2/GJ in 2018.

396a1052be75.title: Kaya identity
396a1052be75.section: Current trend and future projections > Emission intensity of energy (F/E)
396a1052be75.sentence: This reduction is largely attributed to the increased use of renewable energy and nuclear power in the global energy mix.

b0809981e3b2.title: Biocapacity
b0809981e3b2.sentence: The biocapacity or biological capacity of an ecosystem is an estimate of its production of certain biological materials such as natural resources, and its absorption and filtering of other materials such as carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

a868f75c65f3.title: Biocapacity
a868f75c65f3.sentence: Biocapacity is used together with ecological footprint as a method of measuring human impact on the environment.

fff285310c60.title: Biocapacity
fff285310c60.sentence: In general, biocapacity is the amount of resources available to people at a specific moment in time to a specific population (supply) and to differentiate between ecological footprint – which is the environmental demand of a regional ecosystem.

a0b4d307a33c.title: Biocapacity
a0b4d307a33c.sentence: For example, there were roughly 12.2 billion hectares of biologically productive land and water areas on this planet in 2016.

d6d2629edc62.title: Biocapacity
d6d2629edc62.sentence: Dividing by the number of people alive in that year, 7.4 billion, gives a biocapacity for the Earth of 1.6 global hectares per person.

fc1d5906a74a.title: Biocapacity
fc1d5906a74a.sentence: These 1.6 global hectares include the areas for wild species that compete with people for space.

496f7191f672.title: Biocapacity
496f7191f672.sentence: The biocapacity of an area is calculated by multiplying the actual physical area by the yield factor with the appropriate equivalence factor.

c497ccf5ce41.title: Biocapacity
c497ccf5ce41.sentence: Biocapacity is also affected by the technology used during the year.

d289f8644060.title: Biocapacity
d289f8644060.sentence: Hence what is considered "useful" can change from year to year (e.g. use of corn (maize) stover for cellulosic ethanol production would result in corn stover becoming a useful material, and thus increase the biocapacity of maize cropland).

8b9df78759a9.title: Biocapacity
8b9df78759a9.sentence: An increase in global population can result in a decrease in biocapacity.

de34a1257aa9.title: Biocapacity
de34a1257aa9.sentence: This is usually because the Earth's resources have to be shared; therefore, there becomes little to supply the increasing demand of the increasing population.

018a883ba597.title: Ecological footprint
018a883ba597.sentence: The ecological footprint measures human demand on natural capital, i.e. the quantity of nature it takes to support people and their economies.

0a2215bbdb04.title: Ecological footprint
0a2215bbdb04.sentence: The simplest way to define an ecological footprint is the amount of environmental resources necessary to produce the goods and services that support an individual's lifestyle, a nation's prosperity, or the economic activity of humanity as a whole.

c5d5c9a6403b.title: Ecological footprint
c5d5c9a6403b.sentence: The accounts contrast the biologically productive area people use to satisfy their consumption to the biologically productive area available within a region, nation, or the world (biocapacity).

3ba7245b7a20.title: Ecological footprint
3ba7245b7a20.sentence: It can be calculated at any scale: for an activity, a person, a community, a city, a region, a nation, or humanity as a whole.

22c10cf49b72.title: Ecological footprint
22c10cf49b72.sentence: Footprints can be split into consumption categories: food, housing, and goods and services.

264c558ea849.title: Ecological footprint
264c558ea849.sentence: Such applications translate the consumption of energy, biomass (food, fiber), building material, water and other resources into normalized land areas called global hectares (gha) needed to provide these inputs.

d1527ae3f774.title: Ecological footprint
d1527ae3f774.sentence: For 2023 Global Footprint Network estimated humanity's ecological footprint as 1.71 planet Earths.

70084d598494.title: Ecological footprint
70084d598494.sentence: According to their calculations this means that humanity's demands were 1.71 times more than what the planet's ecosystems renewed.

dfb42bbd7152.title: Ecological footprint
dfb42bbd7152.sentence: Humanity's ecological footprint was 7.0 billion gha in 1961 and increased to 20.6 billion gha in 2014, a function of higher per capita resource use and population increase.

932cf31ebfe4.title: Ecological footprint
932cf31ebfe4.sentence: The carbon footprint is the fastest growing part of the ecological footprint and accounts currently for about 60% of humanity's total ecological footprint.

c24b54d21df4.title: Ecological footprint
c24b54d21df4.sentence: The average per country ranges from 14.3 (Qatar) to 0.5 (Yemen) global hectares per person.

7754d635c0cd.title: Ecological footprint
7754d635c0cd.sentence: The ecological footprint concept and calculation method was developed as the PhD dissertation of Mathis Wackernagel, in collaboration with his supervisor William Rees at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver, Canada, from 1990 to 1994.

cfdf9d8eddd6.title: Ecological footprint
cfdf9d8eddd6.sentence: To make the idea more accessible, Rees came up with the term "ecological footprint", inspired by a computer technician who praised his new computer's "small footprint on the desk".

0cc9e6c2ec45.title: Ecological footprint
0cc9e6c2ec45.sentence: The first academic publication about ecological footprints was written by William Rees in 1992.

cd751c8b88de.title: Ecological footprint
cd751c8b88de.sentence: In 1996, Wackernagel and Rees published the book Our Ecological Footprint: Reducing Human Impact on the Earth.

7ab18c1a366e.title: Carbon footprint
7ab18c1a366e.sentence: A carbon footprint (or greenhouse gas footprint) is a calculated value or index that allows the comparison of the total amount of greenhouse gases that an activity, product, company or country adds to the atmosphere.

3846191fe79d.title: Carbon footprint
3846191fe79d.sentence: Carbon footprints are usually reported in tonnes of emissions (CO2-equivalent) per unit of comparison.

b58519136b1d.title: Carbon footprint
b58519136b1d.sentence: Such units can be, for example, tonnes CO2-eq per year, per kilogram of protein for consumption, per kilometer travelled, per piece of clothing and so forth.

632cbeff02d8.title: Carbon footprint
632cbeff02d8.sentence: The carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2eq) emissions per unit of comparison sums up all greenhouse gas emissions.

a7734be2af44.title: Carbon footprint
a7734be2af44.sentence: It includes all greenhouse gases—not just carbon dioxide—and it looks at emissions from economic activities, events, organizations and services.

d9ce7ae58427.title: Carbon footprint
d9ce7ae58427.sentence: So the carbon footprint concept allows everyone to make comparisons between the climate impacts of individuals, products, companies and countries.

7376f424b517.title: Carbon footprint
7376f424b517.sentence: It also helps people devise strategies and priorities for reducing the carbon footprint.

87ad1cde2856.title: Carbon footprint
87ad1cde2856.sentence: According to the World Bank, the global average carbon footprint in 2014 was about 5 tonnes of CO2 per person, measured on a production basis.

6526a61402ee.title: Carbon footprint
6526a61402ee.sentence: Assuming a global population of around 9–10 billion by 2050, a carbon footprint of about 2–2.5 tonnes CO2e per capita is needed to stay within a 2 °C target.

0c1449af3e9c.title: Carbon footprint
0c1449af3e9c.sentence: The term carbon footprint was first used in a BBC vegetarian food magazine in 1999, though the broader concept of ecological footprint, which encompasses the carbon footprint, had been used since at least 1992, as also chronicled by journalist William Safire in the New York Times.

858c20acf725.title: Carbon footprint
858c20acf725.section: Problems > Relationship with other environmental impacts
858c20acf725.sentence: A focus on carbon footprints can lead people to ignore or even exacerbate other related environmental issues of concern.

1a2250089fb7.title: Carbon footprint
1a2250089fb7.section: Problems > Relationship with other environmental impacts
1a2250089fb7.sentence: These include biodiversity loss, ecotoxicity, and habitat destruction.

bed2ce2658c5.title: IUCN Red List
bed2ce2658c5.sentence: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List of Threatened Species, also known as the IUCN Red List or Red Data Book, founded in 1964, is an inventory of the global conservation status and extinction risk of biological species.

c3fdc8485421.title: IUCN Red List
c3fdc8485421.sentence: The goals of the Red List are to provide scientifically based information on the status of species and subspecies at a global level, to draw attention to the magnitude and importance of threatened biodiversity, to influence national and international policy and decision-making, and to provide information to guide actions to conserve biological diversity.

1d81a38cdeec.title: IUCN Red List
1d81a38cdeec.sentence: As of 2023, of 150,388 species surveyed, 42,108 are considered at risk of extinction because of human activity, in particular overfishing, hunting, and land development.

ddd73b0464fa.title: IUCN Red List
ddd73b0464fa.sentence: The IUCN aims to have the category of every species re-evaluated at least every ten years, and every five years if possible.

5f773390623e.title: IUCN Red List
5f773390623e.sentence: This is done in a peer reviewed manner through IUCN Species Survival Commission Specialist Groups (SSC), which are Red List Authorities (RLA) responsible for a species, group of species or specific geographic area, or in the case of BirdLife International, an entire class (Aves).

0c2787004f43.title: IUCN Red List
0c2787004f43.sentence: At threat are 41% of amphibian species, 33% of reef-building corals, 30% of conifers, 25% of mammals, and 13% of birds.

4b67acff0206.title: IUCN Red List
4b67acff0206.sentence: The first two volumes of Red Lists were published in 1966 by conservationist Noel Simon, one for mammals and one for birds.

35a5036b4eb5.title: IUCN Red List
35a5036b4eb5.sentence: In the November 2016 issue of Science Advances, a research article claims there are serious inconsistencies in the way species are classified by the IUCN.

3091a89f840d.title: IUCN Red List
3091a89f840d.sentence: They believe that combining geographical data can significantly increase the number of species that need to be reclassified to a higher risk category.

638156b1f7e0.title: Water footprint
638156b1f7e0.sentence: A water footprint shows the extent of water use in relation to consumption by people.

1cc195d278de.title: Water footprint
1cc195d278de.sentence: The water footprint of an individual, community, or business is defined as the total volume of fresh water used to produce the goods and services consumed by the individual or community or produced by the business.

352946daf6fe.title: Water footprint
352946daf6fe.sentence: Water use is measured in water volume consumed (evaporated) and/or polluted per unit of time.

947bdcaf7c7b.title: Water footprint
947bdcaf7c7b.sentence: The concept of a water footprint was coined in 2002, by Arjen Hoekstra, Professor in water management at the University of Twente, Netherlands, and co-founder and scientific director of the Water Footprint Network, whilst working at the UNESCO-IHE Institute for Water Education, as a metric to measure the amount of water consumed and polluted to produce goods and services along their full supply chain.

d3130e57f5c4.title: Water footprint
d3130e57f5c4.sentence: In 2002, the water footprint concept was introduced in order to have a consumption-based indicator of water use, that could provide useful information in addition to the traditional production-sector-based indicators of water use.

3596a9d33565.title: Water footprint
3596a9d33565.sentence: It is analogous to the ecological footprint concept introduced in the 1990s.

bebce44ef1f7.title: Water footprint
bebce44ef1f7.sentence: The water footprint is a geographically explicit indicator, not only showing volumes of water use and pollution, but also the locations.

6528907f2ca6.title: Water footprint
6528907f2ca6.sentence: The average global water footprint of an individual is 1,385 m3 per year.

3b533e03b780.title: Water footprint
3b533e03b780.section: Definition and measures > Calculation for different factors
3b533e03b780.sentence: That of a product is the whole footprint (sum) of processes in its complete supply chain divided by the number of product units.

f58ef8f160c3.title: Water footprint
f58ef8f160c3.sentence: In July 2014, the International Organization for Standardization issued ISO 14046:2014, Environmental management—Water footprint—Principles, requirements and guidelines, to provide practical guidance to practitioners from various backgrounds, such as large companies, public authorities, non-governmental organizations, academic and research groups as well as small and medium enterprises, for carrying out a water footprint assessment.

536297e97302.title: Water footprint
536297e97302.sentence: The ISO standard is based on life-cycle assessment (LCA) principles and can be applied for different sorts of assessment of products and companies.

c842a5effd62.title: Water footprint
c842a5effd62.section: Criticism > Regional water scarcity should be taken into account when interpreting water footprint
c842a5effd62.sentence: For example, the 140 litres required for coffee production for one cup might be of no harm to water resources if its cultivation occurs mainly in humid areas, but could be damaging in more arid regions.

c7b06a709981.title: Sustainability measurement
c7b06a709981.sentence: Sustainability measurement is a set of frameworks or indicators used to measure how sustainable something is.

af22b7a7fc66.title: Sustainability measurement
af22b7a7fc66.sentence: This includes processes, products, services and businesses.

8a5e715daffa.title: Sustainability measurement
8a5e715daffa.sentence: Sustainability is difficult to quantify and it may even be impossible to measure as there is no fixed definition.

0cf299a5ba2c.title: Sustainability measurement
0cf299a5ba2c.sentence: To measure sustainability, frameworks and indicators consider environmental, social and economic domains.

cb0a8a12dbae.title: Sustainability measurement
cb0a8a12dbae.sentence: They include indicators, benchmarks and audits.

53192f256797.title: Sustainability measurement
53192f256797.section: Metrics at the global scale > Benchmarks, indicators, indexes, auditing etc.
53192f256797.sentence: In the last couple of decades, there has arisen a crowded toolbox of quantitative methods used to assess sustainability — including measures of resource use like life cycle assessment, measures of consumption like the ecological footprint and measurements of quality of environmental governance like the Environmental Performance Index.

bafe7f758fb2.title: Sustainability measurement
bafe7f758fb2.section: Metrics at the global scale > United Nations indicators
bafe7f758fb2.sentence: The UN Commission on Sustainable Development (CSD) has published a list of 140 indicators which covers environmental, social, economical and institutional aspects of sustainable development.

673f01d5a199.title: Sustainability measurement
673f01d5a199.section: Metrics at the global scale > Benchmarks, indicators, indexes, auditing etc.
673f01d5a199.sentence: A benchmark is a point of reference for a measurement.

2d9f66cd82dc.title: Sustainability measurement
2d9f66cd82dc.section: Metrics at the global scale > Benchmarks, indicators, indexes, auditing etc.
2d9f66cd82dc.sentence: Once a benchmark is established it is possible to assess trends and measure progress.

ff2ab9a18da7.title: Sustainability measurement
ff2ab9a18da7.sentence: - Global indicators- Due to differences in social, economical, and environmental conditions of countries, each country has its own indicators and indexes to measure sustainability, which can lead to improper and varying interpretation at the global level.

73ba4e52a2e5.title: Sustainability measurement
73ba4e52a2e5.sentence: Hence, there common indexes and measuring parameters would allow comparisons among countries.

f8681a7a9b3c.title: Input–output model
f8681a7a9b3c.sentence: In economics, an input–output model is a quantitative economic model that represents the interdependencies between different sectors of a national economy or different regional economies.

7740ac651219.title: Input–output model
7740ac651219.sentence: The model depicts inter-industry relationships within an economy, showing how output from one industrial sector may become an input to another industrial sector.

1a6c99b644e2.title: Input–output model
1a6c99b644e2.sentence: In the inter-industry matrix, column entries typically represent inputs to an industrial sector, while row entries represent outputs from a given sector.

ce05d6757a3b.title: Input–output model
ce05d6757a3b.sentence: Each column of the input–output matrix shows the value of inputs to each sector and each row represents the value of each sector's outputs, typically in monetary values.

cb75dc563e08.title: Input–output model
cb75dc563e08.sentence: Wassily Leontief (1906–1999) is credited with developing this type of analysis and was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics for his development of this model.

e22945f1c8f8.title: Input–output model
e22945f1c8f8.sentence: Francois Quesnay had developed a cruder version of this technique called Tableau économique, and Léon Walras's work Elements of Pure Economics on general equilibrium theory also was a forerunner and made a generalization of Leontief's seminal concept.

b2c2d47877fd.title: Input–output model
b2c2d47877fd.sentence: These models are often used by national statistics offices for their system of national accounts, including the quantification of Gross domestic product.

31661d6000f9.title: Input–output model
31661d6000f9.sentence: Furthermore, they have been used increasingly in recent years to quantify Environmental footprints, enabling a consumption-based accounting of environmental impacts.

93e908df4680.title: Input–output model
93e908df4680.sentence: For example, information on fossil fuel inputs to each sector can be used to investigate flows of embodied carbon within and between different economies.

236d29e6fe3f.title: Input–output model
236d29e6fe3f.sentence: Because they are linear in nature, computing input-output models is computationally cheap.

3a02d0781797.title: Input–output model
3a02d0781797.sentence: Because the data collection and preparation process for the input–output accounts is necessarily labor and computer intensive, input–output tables are often published long after the year in which the data were collected—typically as much as 5–7 years after.

b0f71e3bdc98.title: Input–output model
b0f71e3bdc98.sentence: Since most input-output models are quantified in monetary units, environmental intensities are typically expressed in damage per dollar, meaning that every dollar spent in an industry is assumed to have the same impact.

496cee715ae8.title: Input–output model
496cee715ae8.sentence: This can lead to bias in the estimations, since price does not always reflect environmental damage (e.g., in Co2 or water use) well.

8187543c61a4.title: Environmental indicator
8187543c61a4.sentence: Environmental indicators are simple measures that tell us what is happening in the environment.

cbf8638544e5.title: Environmental indicator
cbf8638544e5.sentence: Indicators are developed based on quantitative measurements or statistics of environmental condition that are tracked over time.

daf85caad27b.title: Environmental indicator
daf85caad27b.sentence: Since the environment is very complex, indicators provide a more practical and economical way to track the state of the environment than if we attempted to record every possible variable in the environment.

f76fadaaa0c6.title: Environmental indicator
f76fadaaa0c6.sentence: For example, concentrations of ozone depleting substances (ODS) in the atmosphere, tracked over time, is a good indicator with respect to the environmental issue of stratospheric ozone depletion.

e01840723707.title: Environmental indicator
e01840723707.sentence: It can be considered, for example, that there are major subsets of environmental indicators in-line with the Pressure-State-Response model developed by the OECD.

2cfa2fea195a.title: Environmental indicator
2cfa2fea195a.sentence: These are also referred to as “state” indicators as their focus is on the state of the environment or conditions in the environment.

1462a9258a9e.title: Environmental indicator
1462a9258a9e.sentence: These are also referred to as “pressure” indicators.

aa54205cb9a3.title: Environmental indicator
aa54205cb9a3.sentence: Finally, there are indicators, such as the number of people serviced by sewage treatment, which track societal responses to environmental issues.

46e3ad2e93f9.title: Environmental indicator
46e3ad2e93f9.sentence: Environmental indicators, in turn, should be considered as a subset of sustainable development indicators which are meant to track the overall sustainability of a society with respect to its environmental, social and economic integrity and health.

5257caf42bbd.title: Environmental indicator
5257caf42bbd.sentence: Criteria tend to focus on three key areas – scientific credibility, policy/social relevance and practical monitoring and data requirements.

7e018c2ca16d.title: Environmental indicator
7e018c2ca16d.sentence: Finally, the general public responds to indicators that have clear and simple messages and are meaningful to them, such as the UV index and the air quality index.

9b10ba90a5bd.title: Environmental indicator
9b10ba90a5bd.sentence: In general these methods can be categorized as numerical aggregation (e.g. indices), short selections of indicators (e.g. core set or headline indicators), short visual assessments (e.g. arrows, traffic signals), and compelling presentations (e.g. maps or the dashboard of sustainability).

af86dd7aff6d.title: Embedded emissions
af86dd7aff6d.sentence: One way of attributing greenhouse gas emissions is to measure the embedded emissions of goods that are being consumed (also referred to as "embodied emissions", "embodied carbon emissions", or "embodied carbon").

7ff9ad642623.title: Embedded emissions
7ff9ad642623.sentence: The UNFCCC measures emissions according to production, rather than consumption.

886706398e04.title: Embedded emissions
886706398e04.sentence: Consequently, embedded emissions on imported goods are attributed to the exporting, rather than the importing, country.

3abd07d18367.title: Embedded emissions
3abd07d18367.sentence: The question of whether to measure emissions on production instead of consumption is partly an issue of equity, i.e., who is responsible for emissions.

49e7afb0b4af.title: Embedded emissions
49e7afb0b4af.sentence: 2010 research confirmed that, in 2004, 23% of global emissions were embedded in goods traded internationally, mostly flowing from China and developing countries, such as Russia and South Africa, to the US, Europe and Japan.

0e0125a93e6f.title: Embedded emissions
0e0125a93e6f.sentence: In a briefing note, Wang and Watson (2007) asked the question, "who owns China's carbon emissions?".

9557b29ff28b.title: Embedded emissions
9557b29ff28b.sentence: In their study, they suggested that nearly a quarter of China's CO2 emissions might be a result of its production of goods for export, primarily to the US but also to Europe.

252ae37f08e8.title: Embedded emissions
252ae37f08e8.sentence: In Western Europe the difference in the import and export of emissions is particularly pronounced, with imported emissions making up 20-50% of consumed emissions.

2f98f06fc2d7.title: Carbon tariff
2f98f06fc2d7.sentence: A carbon tariff or border carbon adjustment (BCA) is an eco-tariff on embedded carbon.

5b8c04cf75aa.title: Greenhouse gas emissions
5b8c04cf75aa.sentence: Emissions are usually measured according to production, rather than consumption.

4f798ca96e07.title: Greenhouse gas emissions
4f798ca96e07.sentence: For example, in the main international treaty on climate change (the UNFCCC), countries report on emissions produced within their borders, e.g. the emissions produced from burning fossil fuels.

fa95ed1e455e.title: Greenhouse gas emissions
fa95ed1e455e.sentence: A substantial proportion of CO2 emissions is traded internationally.

09c717c7970b.title: Earth Overshoot Day
09c717c7970b.sentence: Earth Overshoot Day (EOD) is the calculated calendar date on which humanity's resource consumption for the year exceeds Earth's capacity to regenerate those resources that year.

489544697920.title: Earth Overshoot Day
489544697920.sentence: Earth Overshoot Day is calculated by dividing the world biocapacity (the amount of natural resources regenerated by Earth that year), by the world ecological footprint (humanity's consumption of Earth's natural resources for that year), and multiplying by 365 (366 in leap years), the number of days in a year:

c952236cf7c4.title: Earth Overshoot Day
c952236cf7c4.sentence: When viewed through an economic perspective, the annual Earth Overshoot Day represents the day by which the planet's annual regenerative budget is spent, and humanity enters environmental deficit spending.

1e2962f95c29.title: Earth Overshoot Day
1e2962f95c29.sentence: Andrew Simms of UK think tank New Economics Foundation originally developed the concept of Earth Overshoot Day.

ae4fc55b2be1.title: Earth Overshoot Day
ae4fc55b2be1.sentence: Earth Overshoot Day is calculated by Global Footprint Network and is a campaign supported by dozens of other nonprofit organizations.

87c8be04ebad.title: Earth Overshoot Day
87c8be04ebad.sentence: But by the early 1970s, that critical threshold had been crossed: Human consumption began outstripping what the planet could reproduce.

42cffdb3c76d.title: Earth Overshoot Day
42cffdb3c76d.sentence: In 2020 the calculated overshoot day fell on 22 August (more than three weeks later than 2019) due to coronavirus-induced lockdowns around the world.

5e1cef2fc97b.title: Carrying capacity
5e1cef2fc97b.section: Recent warnings that humanity may have exceeded Earth's carrying capacity > Ecological footprint accounting
5e1cef2fc97b.sentence: > In 2024, [Earth Overshoot Day] fell on August 1.

86067c23a245.title: Earth Overshoot Day
86067c23a245.sentence: Hence, EOD does a poor job at measuring water and land mismanagement (e.g., soil erosion) and only highlights the excess of carbon dioxide that humanity releases above what the ecosystem can absorb.

6827222e700f.title: Earth Overshoot Day
6827222e700f.sentence: In 2017, the ecomodernist Breakthrough Institute dismissed the idea of Earth Overshoot Day by calling it "a nice publicity stunt".

213a9e92a1bb.title: Carbon footprint
213a9e92a1bb.section: Underlying concepts for calculations > Consumption-based emission accounting based on input-output analysis
213a9e92a1bb.sentence: Consumption-based emission accounting traces the impacts of demand for goods and services along the global supply chain to the end-consumer.

159c018ff3d2.title: Carbon footprint
159c018ff3d2.section: Underlying concepts for calculations > Consumption-based emission accounting based on input-output analysis
159c018ff3d2.sentence: It is also called consumption-based carbon accounting.

0824b244d3f5.title: Carbon footprint
0824b244d3f5.section: Underlying concepts for calculations > Consumption-based emission accounting based on input-output analysis
0824b244d3f5.sentence: The production-based approach includes only impacts physically produced in the country in question.

8454898a6e76.title: Carbon footprint
8454898a6e76.sentence: The GHG emissions listed in those national inventories are only from activities in the country itself.

5ee0c910323b.title: Carbon footprint
5ee0c910323b.sentence: This approach is called territorial-based accounting or production-based accounting.

930bafe77bdc.title: Carbon footprint
930bafe77bdc.sentence: Consumption-based accounting does reflect emissions from goods and services imported from other countries.

f6e1be11515c.title: Carbon footprint
f6e1be11515c.sentence: Consumption-based accounting is therefore more comprehensive.

2be5a252ac63.title: Carbon footprint
2be5a252ac63.section: Underlying concepts for calculations > Consumption-based emission accounting based on input-output analysis
2be5a252ac63.sentence: Consumer-based accounting is based on input-output analysis.

8c3cc69f0855.title: Carbon footprint
8c3cc69f0855.section: Underlying concepts for calculations > Consumption-based emission accounting based on input-output analysis
8c3cc69f0855.sentence: Input-output analysis has been extended globally to multi-regional input-output analysis (MRIO).

160005efa77d.title: Carbon footprint
160005efa77d.sentence: Consumption-based emissions reflect the lifestyle choices of a country's citizens.

3992df6db949.title: Greenhouse gas inventory
3992df6db949.section: Greenhouse gas emissions accounting > Emissions embodied in international trade
3992df6db949.sentence: Thus, including international trade (i.e. the methodology of consumption-based accounting) reverses the apparent decreasing trend in emissions in developed countries, changing a 2% decrease (as calculated by production-based accounting) into a 7% increase across the time period.

81878d8a215e.title: Greenhouse gas inventory
81878d8a215e.section: Disadvantages of consumption-based accounting > Greater uncertainty and complexity
81878d8a215e.sentence: Uncertainty derives from three main reasons: production-based accounting is much closer to statistical sources and GDP which are more assured; the methodology behind consumption-based accounting requires an extra step over production-based accounting, this step inherently incurring further doubt; and consumption-based accounting includes data from all trading partners of a particular country which will contain different levels of accuracy.

e25960705ff7.title: Greenhouse gas inventory
e25960705ff7.sentence: However, because of its key disadvantage of omitting emissions embodied in international trade, it is clear that consumption-based accounting provides invaluable information and should at least be used as a ‘shadow’ to production-based accounting.

f71a01bdf710.title: Carbon footprint
f71a01bdf710.sentence: The greenhouse gas protocol is a set of standards for tracking greenhouse gas emissions.

8cbbcfc9d0cf.title: Carbon footprint
8cbbcfc9d0cf.sentence: The standards divide emissions into three scopes (Scope 1, 2 and 3) within the value chain.

193806bd68be.title: Carbon footprint
193806bd68be.sentence: Greenhouse gas emissions caused directly by the organization such as by burning fossil fuels are referred to as Scope 1.

275b69817a7e.title: Carbon footprint
275b69817a7e.section: Types of greenhouse gas emissions > Direct carbon emissions (Scope 1)
275b69817a7e.sentence: An example for industry would be the emissions from burning a fuel on site.

85c8046c7013.title: Carbon footprint
85c8046c7013.section: Types of greenhouse gas emissions > Direct carbon emissions (Scope 1)
85c8046c7013.sentence: On the individual level, emissions from personal vehicles or gas-burning stoves are Scope 1.

7201265ba758.title: Carbon footprint
7201265ba758.sentence: Emissions caused indirectly by an organization, such as by purchasing secondary energy sources like electricity, heat, cooling or steam are called Scope 2.

e9e28f6986fc.title: Carbon footprint
e9e28f6986fc.section: Types of greenhouse gas emissions > Other indirect carbon emissions (Scope 3)
e9e28f6986fc.sentence: Scope 3 emissions are all other indirect emissions derived from the activities of an organization.

53bc4fb7cead.title: Carbon footprint
53bc4fb7cead.section: Types of greenhouse gas emissions > Other indirect carbon emissions (Scope 3)
53bc4fb7cead.sentence: But they are from sources they do not own or control.

dc08dfb92ab1.title: Carbon footprint
dc08dfb92ab1.section: Types of greenhouse gas emissions > Other indirect carbon emissions (Scope 3)
dc08dfb92ab1.sentence: Scope 3 emission sources include emissions from suppliers and product users.

aa52da350100.title: Carbon footprint
aa52da350100.section: Types of greenhouse gas emissions > Other indirect carbon emissions (Scope 3)
aa52da350100.sentence: In 2022 about 30% of US companies reported Scope 3 emissions.

4bc756fc9ddb.title: Carbon footprint
4bc756fc9ddb.sentence: The term carbon footprint has been applied to limited calculations that do not include Scope 3 emissions or the entire supply chain.

b326971d1d2b.title: Carbon footprint
b326971d1d2b.sentence: This can lead to claims of misleading customers with regards to the real carbon footprints of companies or products.

5a9e82888314.title: Net-zero emissions
5a9e82888314.sentence: - Scope 1 covers all direct GHG emissions within a corporate boundary (owned or controlled by a company).

f4d3e2a507bb.title: Net-zero emissions
f4d3e2a507bb.sentence: It includes fuel burned by the company, use of company vehicles, and fugitive emissions.

86f47a159125.title: Net-zero emissions
86f47a159125.sentence: - Scope 3 emission sources include emissions from suppliers and product users (also known as the "value chain").

2d11c646bf10.title: Net-zero emissions
2d11c646bf10.sentence: Scope 3 emissions were estimated to represent 75% of all emissions reported to the Carbon Disclosure Project, though that percentage varies widely amongst business sectors.

f4135f5e747f.title: Net-zero emissions
f4135f5e747f.sentence: Some oil companies, for instance, claim that their operations (Scopes 1 and 2) produce net-zero emissions.

c74e86474275.title: Net-zero emissions
c74e86474275.sentence: These claims do not cover the emissions produced when the oil is burned by its customers, which are 70 - 90% of oil-related emissions.

a30129221089.title: Net-zero emissions
a30129221089.sentence: This is because they count as Scope 3 emissions.

88aababa3eb1.title: Life-cycle assessment
88aababa3eb1.sentence: According to standards in the ISO 14040 and 14044, an LCA is carried out in four distinct phases, as illustrated in the figure shown at the above right (at opening of the article).

75a60120cef4.title: Life-cycle assessment
75a60120cef4.section: Main ISO phases of LCA > Goal and scope
75a60120cef4.sentence: An LCA study begins with a goal and scope definition phase, which includes the product function, functional unit, product system and its boundaries, assumptions, data categories, allocation procedures, and review method to be employed in the analysis.

44401328c696.title: Life-cycle assessment
44401328c696.section: Main ISO phases of LCA > Life cycle inventory (LCI)
44401328c696.sentence: Life cycle inventory (LCI) analysis involves creating an inventory of flows from and to nature (ecosphere) for a product system.

e33693501cee.title: Life-cycle assessment
e33693501cee.section: Main ISO phases of LCA > Life cycle inventory (LCI)
e33693501cee.sentence: It is the process of quantifying raw material and energy requirements, atmospheric emissions, land emissions, water emissions, resource uses, and other releases over the life cycle of a product or process.

0582171ed107.title: Life-cycle assessment
0582171ed107.section: Main ISO phases of LCA > Life cycle impact assessment (LCIA)
0582171ed107.sentence: Life cycle inventory analysis is followed by a life cycle impact assessment (LCIA).

71066de72f65.title: Life-cycle assessment
71066de72f65.section: Main ISO phases of LCA > Life cycle impact assessment (LCIA)
71066de72f65.sentence: This phase of LCA is aimed at evaluating the potential environmental and human health impacts resulting from the elementary flows determined in the LCI.

693b3ee78274.title: Life-cycle assessment
693b3ee78274.section: Main ISO phases of LCA > Interpretation
693b3ee78274.sentence: The results from the inventory analysis and impact assessment are summarized during the interpretation phase.

5294f657e990.title: Life-cycle assessment
5294f657e990.section: Main ISO phases of LCA > Interpretation
5294f657e990.sentence: The outcome of the interpretation phase is a set of conclusions and recommendations for the study.

ad3e9133140e.title: Life-cycle assessment
ad3e9133140e.sentence: The phases are often interdependent, in that the results of one phase will inform how other phases are completed.

949ab2e036a4.title: Life-cycle assessment
949ab2e036a4.sentence: Therefore, none of the stages should be considered finalized until the entire study is complete.

56f12621ee23.title: Ecological indicator
56f12621ee23.sentence: Ecological indicators are used to communicate information about ecosystems and the impact human activity has on ecosystems to groups such as the public or government policy makers.

3b9fd0b5f25e.title: Ecological indicator
3b9fd0b5f25e.sentence: Ecosystems are complex and ecological indicators can help describe them in simpler terms that can be understood and used by non-scientists to make management decisions.

edc6c20b7fd1.title: Ecological indicator
edc6c20b7fd1.sentence: For example, the number of different beetle taxa found in a field can be used as an indicator of biodiversity.[1][2][3]

430a0c6960fb.title: Ecological indicator
430a0c6960fb.sentence: Using ecological indicators is a pragmatic approach since direct documentation of changes in ecosystems as related to management measures, is cost and time intensive.[5][6] For example, it would be expensive and time-consuming to count every bird, plant and animal in a newly restored wetland to see if the restoration was a success.

e72995bdab66.title: Ecological indicator
e72995bdab66.sentence: Instead, a few indicator species can be monitored to determine the success of the restoration.

913cd5a38f82.title: Ecological indicator
913cd5a38f82.sentence: However, ecological indicators are actually a sub-set of environmental indicators.

294a35140552.title: Ecological indicator
294a35140552.sentence: Ecological indicators refer only to ecological processes; however, sustainability indicators are seen as increasingly important for managing humanity's coupled human-environmental systems.

f52434e90807.title: Ecological indicator
f52434e90807.sentence: - Variable availability of data and information on local, regional and national scales.

d4e47e67bba5.title: Ecological indicator
d4e47e67bba5.sentence: - Lack of methodological standards on an international scale.

ec35d175bdcf.title: Ecological indicator
ec35d175bdcf.sentence: - Lack of reference levels, therefore it is unknown if trends in environmental change are strong or weak.

97737b7072b0.title: Ecological indicator
97737b7072b0.sentence: - Attention to more easily handled measurable indicators distracts from indicators less quantifiable such as aesthetics, ethics or cultural values.

376cd0ff834d.title: Living Planet Index
376cd0ff834d.sentence: The Living Planet Index (LPI) is an indicator of the state of global biodiversity, based on trends in vertebrate populations of species from around the world.

a223f4d4d3ba.title: Living Planet Index
a223f4d4d3ba.sentence: The index was originally developed in 1997 by the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) in collaboration with the World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC), the biodiversity assessment and policy implementation arm of the United Nations Environment Programme.

3864d9e9dda1.title: Living Planet Index
3864d9e9dda1.sentence: Since 2006, the Zoological Society of London (ZSL) manages the index in cooperation with WWF.

6c89b2779635.title: Living Planet Index
6c89b2779635.sentence: As of 2022, the index is statistically created from journal studies, online databases and government reports for 31,821 populations of 5,230 species of mammal, bird, reptile, amphibian and fish.

e89804033e66.title: Living Planet Index
e89804033e66.sentence: According to the 2024 report, monitored wildlife populations showed a 73% average decline in size between 1970 and 2020, compared with a 69% average decline over 1970–2018 reported in the 2022 edition, suggesting that natural ecosystems are degrading at a rate unprecedented in human history Many trends are consistent with broader global assessments that identify biodiversity loss as one of the most significant environmental challenges currently affecting ecosystems worldwide.

7ef9cc681308.title: Living Planet Index
7ef9cc681308.sentence: The extent of declines varies with geographic region, with monitored vertebrate populations in Latin America and the Caribbean experiencing average declines of 94%.

e414c406696b.title: Living Planet Index
e414c406696b.sentence: One of the key drivers of declines has been identified as land-use change and the associated habitat loss and degradation, often linked to unsustainable agriculture, logging, or other development.

b35aa9eb7a29.title: Living Planet Index
b35aa9eb7a29.sentence: The index is limited to vertebrate species, largely because long-term population data for invertebrates and plants are less widely available.

b78ed6a0e816.title: Living Planet Index
b78ed6a0e816.sentence: The index is often misinterpreted in the media, with incorrect suggestions that it shows we have lost 69% of all animals or species since 1970.

8faa6dd98b46.title: Living Planet Index
8faa6dd98b46.sentence: In 2020, a re-analysis of the baseline data by McGill University showed that the overall estimated trend of a decline by 60% since 1970 was driven by less than 3% of the studied populations; when some outliers of extreme decline are removed, the decline still exists but is considerably less catastrophic, and when more outliers (roughly amounting to 2.4% of the populations) are removed, the trend shifts to that of a decline between the 1980s and 2000s, but a roughly positive trend after 2000.

3259b25890c2.title: Living Planet Index
3259b25890c2.sentence: A 2024 study by Charles University focused on calculation method, found that calculation of the Living Planet Index is biased by several mathematical issues, leading to overestimation of vertebrate population declines.

2df0e8208e31.title: Living Planet Index
2df0e8208e31.sentence: The LPI played a pivotal role in measuring progress towards the CBD's 2010 target.

c08093a998d5.title: Living Planet Index
c08093a998d5.sentence: It has also been adopted by the CBD as an indicator of progress towards its Nagoya Protocol 2011-2020 targets 5, 6, and 12 (part of the Aichi Biodiversity Targets).

4b2f0fa55ada.title: IUCN Red List
4b2f0fa55ada.sentence: Species are classified by the IUCN Red List into nine groups, specified through criteria such as rate of decline, population size, area of geographic distribution, and degree of population and distribution fragmentation.

88cfcaa97b06.title: IUCN Red List
88cfcaa97b06.sentence: - Extinct (EX) – beyond reasonable doubt that the species is no longer extant.

5e94757e19f4.title: IUCN Red List
5e94757e19f4.sentence: - Extinct in the wild (EW) – survives only in captivity, cultivation and/or outside native range, as presumed after exhaustive surveys.

db24374c5ac3.title: IUCN Red List
db24374c5ac3.sentence: In the IUCN Red List, "threatened" embraces the categories of Critically Endangered, Endangered, and Vulnerable.

432294eadede.title: IUCN Red List
432294eadede.sentence: - Near Threatened (NT) – close to being endangered in the near future.

72d0d473b12c.title: IUCN Red List
72d0d473b12c.sentence: - Least Concern (LC) – widespread and abundant in the wild.

3d33972e4406.title: IUCN Red List
3d33972e4406.sentence: - Data Deficient (DD) – inadequate information to assess extinction risk.

c2f01bde7f52.title: IUCN Red List
c2f01bde7f52.sentence: - Not Evaluated (NE) – has not yet been assessed.

09579a71ef70.title: IUCN Red List
09579a71ef70.sentence: All new IUCN assessments since 2001 have used version 3.1 of the categories and criteria.

3c48492c0b9a.title: Red List Index
3c48492c0b9a.sentence: The Red List Index (RLI), based on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, is an indicator of the changing state of global biodiversity.

86ac63e4a792.title: Red List Index
86ac63e4a792.sentence: It defines the conservation status of major species groups, and measures trends in extinction risk over time.

b87bdbad5fdb.title: Red List Index
b87bdbad5fdb.sentence: By conducting conservation assessments at regular intervals, changes in the threat status of species in a taxonomic group can be used to monitor trends in extinction risk.

7a5bc74600a0.title: Red List Index
7a5bc74600a0.sentence: As well as taxonomic groups, RLIs can show trends in extinction risk according to biogeographic realm, habitat type, and dominant threat process.

f122734c492c.title: Red List Index
f122734c492c.sentence: The Red List Index can also be disaggregated by specific taxonomic orders to evaluate and compare long-term trends in aggregate extinction risk.

83003bbeb5cd.title: Red List Index
83003bbeb5cd.sentence: Assessing every species in the larger and lesser known groups which comprise the majority of the world's biodiversity, such as fungi, invertebrates (particularly insects) and plants, is not practical.

8aa951d9c515.title: Red List Index
8aa951d9c515.sentence: The Red List Index (sampled approach) (SRLI) has been developed in order to determine the threat status and also trends of lesser-known and less charismatic species groups.

6946ea261105.title: Red List Index
6946ea261105.sentence: The SRLI is based on a representative sample of species selected from taxonomic groups within animals (invertebrates and vertebrates), fungi and plants.

a7db242b6343.title: Red List Index
a7db242b6343.sentence: As the journal "Ecological erosion and expanding extinction risk of sharks and rays" presents, the shark and ray Red List Index has diminished by 19% on the Red List index since the 1970s due to overfishing.

abfad20bca1e.title: Red List Index
abfad20bca1e.sentence: A national Red List Index (RLI) spanning three decades (1990 to 2020) was calculated for Australia's birds, revealing that the national score fell from 0.927 to 0.896, dropping below the global avian RLI in 2020.

54aba2c6af63.title: Red List Index
54aba2c6af63.sentence: This national application demonstrated that the index is highly sensitive to specific events, capturing both deteriorations from the 2019–2020 wildfires and measurable improvements from targeted conservation interventions like invasive predator eradications.

93ad6420ec5c.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
93ad6420ec5c.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 15.5: Protect biodiversity and natural habitats
93ad6420ec5c.sentence: This target has one indicator: Indicator 15.5.1 is the "Red List Index".

8e26efb29093.title: Red List Index
8e26efb29093.sentence: In April 2002 at the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), 188 Nations committed themselves to actions to: "... achieve, by 2010, a significant reduction of the current rate of biodiversity loss at the global, regional and national levels..." The RLI has been adopted by the CBD as one of the indicators to measure progress towards this important target, and specifically to monitor changes in threat status of species.

3109ce3e4dab.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
3109ce3e4dab.sentence: The IUCN Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) is a global framework for monitoring and documenting the status of ecosystems.

96e51c1f163d.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
96e51c1f163d.sentence: The Red List of Ecosystem was developed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), the same entity that created the Red List of Threatened Species, a global framework to monitor the level of risk of animal and plant species.

8a79c7012920.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
8a79c7012920.sentence: The Red List of Ecosystems was created to carry out assessments of biodiversity at a level of biological organization above species.

4ebeb41f2c17.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
4ebeb41f2c17.sentence: Existing protocols developed by national or subnational authorities differed in focus and implementation, were often not comparable, and did not distinguish between strict risk analysis and the process of setting conservation priorities.

aa5fa6fbaf2f.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
aa5fa6fbaf2f.sentence: In 2008, during the IV World Conservation Congress (Barcelona, Spain), the process of developing criteria to estimate their risk status was activated and the IUCN laid the foundations for the creation of a Red List of Ecosystems (RLE).

76c57fb01892.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
76c57fb01892.sentence: In 2013, the process of creating The Categories and Criteria of the IUCN Red List Ecosystems, was finalized.

01a0b335ed4f.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
01a0b335ed4f.sentence: The RLE was officially recognized by IUCN in 2014, to be managed as a Thematic Group under the IUCN Commission on Ecosystem Management (CEM).

d4babf965036.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
d4babf965036.sentence: Its main objectives are to support conservation, resource use, and management decisions by evaluating all the world's ecosystems by 2025.

1bf335f4b84a.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
1bf335f4b84a.section: The Red List of Ecosystems as a tool
1bf335f4b84a.sentence: It contributes to better management of the limited resources devoted to conservation.

3cef5605f2d4.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
3cef5605f2d4.section: The Red List of Ecosystems as a tool
3cef5605f2d4.sentence: It prioritizes ecosystems with the most imminent chances of disappearing, focussing on them the greatest efforts to mitigate environmental threats, and create effective protected areas to safeguard them.

91af7c78092c.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
91af7c78092c.sentence: Some countries, like Finland, have adopted these guidelines as an official system to assess risk to ecosystems.

61ede692d439.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
61ede692d439.sentence: Some arguments against the wide adoption of the RLE are the lack of consistent means to classify ecosystems for assessing conservation status, technical difficulties with the concept of ecosystem collapse and lack of scientific basis for the criteria and thresholds.

76e63ff7dca4.title: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
76e63ff7dca4.sentence: The concept of ecosystem collapse is still a major point of debate.

14f81dc306d1.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
14f81dc306d1.sentence: Sustainability metrics and indices are measures of sustainability, using numbers to quantify environmental, social and economic aspects of the world.

d6ba9faa34ce.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
d6ba9faa34ce.sentence: There are multiple perspectives on how to measure sustainability as there is no universal standard.

37d0db36c0cf.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
37d0db36c0cf.sentence: Instead, different disciplines and international organizations have offered measures or indicators of how to measure the concept.

fcda1854acba.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
fcda1854acba.sentence: Some examples include: the Ecological Footprint, the UN's Human Development Index (HDI), the Genuine Progress Index (GPI), and the Environmental Sustainability Index (ESI).

e9e722d80c28.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
e9e722d80c28.sentence: Alternative aggregate measures for sustainability offer a more detailed view of development than traditional indicators like Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

f66fd61ba19d.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
f66fd61ba19d.sentence: Since the 2010s, there has been an expansion of interest in Sustainable Development Index (SDI) systems, both in industrialized and, albeit to a lesser extent, in developing countries.

1ce4bc030f00.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
1ce4bc030f00.sentence: While sustainability indicators, indices and reporting systems gained growing popularity in both the public and private sectors, their effectiveness in influencing actual policy and practices often remains limited.

f1c2f9b8f88f.title: Water footprint
f1c2f9b8f88f.sentence: Blue water footprint refers to groundwater or surface water usage, green water footprint refers to rainwater, and grey water footprint refers to the amount of water needed to dilute pollutants.

65930cdf9459.title: Water footprint
65930cdf9459.section: Definition and measures > Blue water footprint
65930cdf9459.sentence: A blue water footprint refers to the volume of water that has been sourced from surface or groundwater resources (lakes, rivers, wetlands and aquifers) and has either evaporated (for example while irrigating crops), or been incorporated into a product or taken from one body of water and returned to another, or returned at a different time.

722e0863d97d.title: Water footprint
722e0863d97d.section: Definition and measures > Green water footprint
722e0863d97d.sentence: A green water footprint refers to the amount of water from precipitation that, after having been stored in the root zone of the soil (green water), is either lost by evapotranspiration or incorporated by plants.

a369d97525b5.title: Water footprint
a369d97525b5.section: Definition and measures > Green water footprint
a369d97525b5.sentence: It is particularly relevant for agricultural, horticultural and forestry products.

50e3f3858b08.title: Water footprint
50e3f3858b08.section: Definition and measures > Grey water footprint
50e3f3858b08.sentence: A grey water footprint refers to the volume of water that is required to dilute pollutants (industrial discharges, seepage from tailing ponds at mining operations, untreated municipal wastewater, or nonpoint source pollution such as agricultural runoff or urban runoff) to such an extent that the quality of the water meets agreed water quality standards.

7662f2b0c79c.title: Human impact on the environment
7662f2b0c79c.section: Human activities > Fishing and farming > Meat production
7662f2b0c79c.sentence: For example, "green water" use is evapotranspirational use of soil water that has been provided directly by precipitation; and "green water" has been estimated to account for 94% of global beef cattle production's "water footprint", and on rangeland, as much as 99.5% of the water use associated with beef production is "green water".

136a9a703bce.title: Water footprint
136a9a703bce.section: Criticism > Disproportionality in Measuring the Effects of Grey Water
136a9a703bce.sentence: The effects of contamination are not considered to be different from that of scarcity, though the two have different effects on both human life and the environment.

cef15cfe306d.title: Sustainability measurement
cef15cfe306d.sentence: The principal objective of sustainability indicators is to inform public policy-making as part of the process of sustainability governance.

b262d5c48dfb.title: Sustainability measurement
b262d5c48dfb.sentence: Sustainability indicators can provide information on any aspect of the interplay between the environment and socio-economic activities.

68994ea2ac8a.title: Sustainability measurement
68994ea2ac8a.sentence: Building strategic indicator sets generally deals with just a few simple questions: what is happening?

c3b2d0e4f45a.title: Sustainability measurement
c3b2d0e4f45a.sentence: (descriptive indicators), does it matter and are we reaching targets?

1a4d451e852a.title: Sustainability measurement
1a4d451e852a.section: Sustainability indicators and their function > Politics
1a4d451e852a.sentence: A study concluded that social indicators and, therefore, sustainable development indicators, are scientific constructs whose principal objective is to inform public policy-making.

a47552d860b6.title: Environmentally extended input–output analysis
a47552d860b6.sentence: Environmentally extended input–output analysis (EEIOA) is used in environmental accounting as a tool which reflects production and consumption structures within one or several economies.

9928404c04d2.title: Environmentally extended input–output analysis

fc0371207fe6.title: Environmentally extended input–output analysis

1fe4b21f57bd.title: Environmentally extended input–output analysis

4b31b252cfd6.title: Environmentally extended input–output analysis
4b31b252cfd6.sentence: In order to consider variations in production structures across different economies or regions, national input-output tables are combined to form so-called multi-regional input-output (MRIO) models.

8d247bcc9dc6.title: Environmentally extended input–output analysis

72297d8788c8.title: Happy Planet Index
72297d8788c8.sentence: The Happy Planet Index (HPI) is an index of human well-being and environmental impact that was introduced by the New Economics Foundation in 2006.

ebfad57fdff6.title: Happy Planet Index
ebfad57fdff6.sentence: The HPI is best conceived as a measure of the environmental efficiency of supporting well-being in a given country.

2b6b59bdd25e.title: Happy Planet Index
2b6b59bdd25e.sentence: Each country's HPI value is a function of its average subjective life satisfaction, life expectancy at birth, and ecological footprint per capita.

a76e5c50bf79.title: Happy Planet Index
a76e5c50bf79.sentence: The exact function is a little more complex, but conceptually it approximates multiplying life satisfaction and life expectancy and dividing that by the ecological footprint.

99693f5781d1.title: Happy Planet Index
99693f5781d1.sentence: The index is designed to challenge well-established indices of countries' development, such as the gross domestic product (GDP) and the Human Development Index (HDI), which are seen as not taking sustainability into account.

84a735bce067.title: Happy Planet Index
84a735bce067.sentence: In 2009, Costa Rica was the best scoring country among the 143 analyzed, followed by the Dominican Republic, Jamaica, Guatemala and Vietnam.

1d4765fe8a13.title: Happy Planet Index
1d4765fe8a13.sentence: For the 2012 ranking, 151 countries were compared, and the best scoring country for the second time in a row was Costa Rica, followed by Vietnam, Colombia, Belize and El Salvador.

e6b8fe35533d.title: Happy Planet Index
e6b8fe35533d.sentence: In 2016, out of 140 countries, Costa Rica topped the index for the third time in a row.

8512e2c24365.title: Happy Planet Index
8512e2c24365.sentence: The ranking was led by Costa Rica with an HPI score of 62.1, with its lead considered to be due to its very high life expectancy of 77 years.

e04c8ab941b1.title: Happy Planet Index
e04c8ab941b1.sentence: As such, the HPI is not a measure of which are the happiest countries in the world.

3cf6d9bf96d2.title: Happy Planet Index
3cf6d9bf96d2.sentence: Countries with relatively high levels of life satisfaction, as measured in surveys, are found from the very top (Colombia in 3rd place) to the very bottom (the US in 108th place) of the rank order.

c44af884a906.title: Happy Planet Index
c44af884a906.sentence: The index has been criticized for weighting the carbon footprint too heavily, to the point that the US would have had to be universally happy and would have had to have a life expectancy of 439 years to equal Vanuatu's score in the 2006 index.

93b79c3648ef.title: Happy Planet Index
93b79c3648ef.sentence: In the HPI Report of 2006 (by nef) they emphasized that they "were forced to estimate data on Footprint and life satisfaction for several countries".

4a0999fc52e6.title: Environmental Performance Index
4a0999fc52e6.sentence: The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) is a method of quantifying and numerically marking the environmental performance of a state's policies, highlighting the degradation of the planet's life-supporting systems on which humanity depends.

01cad66dd3ed.title: Environmental Performance Index
01cad66dd3ed.sentence: The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) was started in 2002 by World Economic Forum in association with the Yale Center for Environmental Law & Policy (Yale University) and Center for International Earth Science Information Network Earth Institute (Columbia University).

a886365b6a53.title: Environmental Performance Index
a886365b6a53.sentence: The biennial EPI report harnesses the latest data sets, science, and technology to provide the most comprehensive assessment of the state of sustainability around the world.

3ea68ba38b51.title: Environmental Performance Index
3ea68ba38b51.sentence: In total, the 2024 EPI report incorporates 58 indicators to rank 180 countries on their progress at mitigating climate change, safeguarding ecosystem vitality, and promoting environmental health.

d7d2e8ad1110.title: Environmental Performance Index
d7d2e8ad1110.section: List of countries by 2024 EPI scores
d7d2e8ad1110.sentence: The top five countries are Estonia, Luxembourg, Germany, Finland and the United Kingdom, while the last ones are India, Myanmar, Laos, Pakistan and Vietnam.

3536aa83b213.title: Environmental Performance Index
3536aa83b213.section: EPI scores vs. GDP per capita, 2024
3536aa83b213.sentence: EPI scores are positively correlated with a country's wealth, although after a point, increasing wealth yields diminishing returns.

01619f3b70e8.title: Environmental Performance Index
01619f3b70e8.section: EPI scores vs. GDP per capita, 2024
01619f3b70e8.sentence: In this regard, factors other than wealth, such as investments in human development, rule of law, and regulatory quality, are stronger predictors of environmental performance.

0665bea92584.title: Environmental Performance Index
0665bea92584.section: EPI scores vs. GDP per capita, 2024
0665bea92584.sentence: Wealth allows countries to make investments in the infrastructure required to provide clean drinking water, safely manage waste, and rapidly expand renewable energy.

a94f61f3ce77.title: Environmental Performance Index
a94f61f3ce77.section: EPI scores vs. GDP per capita, 2024
a94f61f3ce77.sentence: But wealth also leads to higher material consumption and its associated environmental impacts, such as higher rates of waste generation, GHG emissions, and ecosystem degradation.

d8ab4d55996d.title: Environmental Performance Index
d8ab4d55996d.sentence: Over time, the methodology for the EPI has been criticized for its arbitrary choice of metrics which could introduce bias, and its poor performance as an indicator for environmental sustainability.

3f7fb5309aef.title: Environmental Performance Index
3f7fb5309aef.sentence: Additional criticisms center on the EPI's lack of specific policy suggestions, and the index's weighting biases against data deficient countries that has led to the overlooking of ecological progress in developing countries.

7466a47ed9a2.title: Environmental Performance Index
7466a47ed9a2.sentence: In 2024, India was ranked at 176 in the list and rejected the low ranking.

cdcbce4b7c1e.title: DPSIR
cdcbce4b7c1e.sentence: DPSIR (drivers, pressures, state, impact, and response model of intervention) is a causal framework used to describe the interactions between society and the environment.

6040a22a0074.title: DPSIR
6040a22a0074.sentence: First, the indicators are categorized into "drivers" which put "pressures" in the "state" of the system, which in turn results in certain "impacts" that will lead to various "responses" to maintain or recover the system under consideration.

52ac8c4d7b4e.title: DPSIR
52ac8c4d7b4e.sentence: Driver refers to the social, demographic, and economic developments which influence the human activities that have a direct impact on the environment.

f40927e853f5.title: DPSIR
f40927e853f5.sentence: Primary driving forces refer to technological and societal actors that motivate human activities like population growth and distribution of wealth.

132f3fc8e73f.title: DPSIR
132f3fc8e73f.sentence: Pressure represents the consequence of the driving force, which in turn affects the state of the environment.

a4200d5c8951.title: DPSIR
a4200d5c8951.sentence: They can be both human-induced, like emissions, fuel extraction, and solid waste generation, and natural processes, like solar radiation and volcanic eruptions.

e4d7e7c5299e.title: DPSIR
e4d7e7c5299e.sentence: Impact refers to how changes in the state of the system affect human well-being.

44e47fb635e5.title: DPSIR
44e47fb635e5.sentence: Response refers to actions taken to correct the problems of the previous stages, by adjusting the drivers, reducing the pressure on the system, bringing the system back to its initial state, and mitigating the impacts.

16274ea2c490.title: DPSIR
16274ea2c490.sentence: Responses are mostly designed and/or implemented as political actions of protection, mitigation, conservation, or promotion.

da18274d10c9.title: DPSIR
da18274d10c9.sentence: The Driver-Pressure-State-Impact-Response framework was developed by the European Environment Agency (EEA) in 1999.

8b0ebf28ed39.title: DPSIR
8b0ebf28ed39.sentence: It was built upon several existing environmental reporting frameworks, like the Pressure-State-Response (PSR) framework developed by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) in 1993, which itself was an extension of Rapport and Friend's Stress-Response (SR) framework (1979).

c58b212522e0.title: DPSIR
c58b212522e0.sentence: However, several notable authors have mentioned that it lacks a well-defined set of categories, which undermines the comparability between studies, even if they are similar.

dfde0cc83484.title: DPSIR
dfde0cc83484.sentence: A wastewater treatment plant is considered a response while dealing with water pollution, but a pressure when effluent runoff leading to eutrophication is taken into account.

e3adf04e2de7.title: DPSIR
e3adf04e2de7.sentence: Another criticism is the misguiding simplicity of the framework, which ignores the complex synergy between the categories.

7779cfe0b160.title: DPSIR
7779cfe0b160.sentence: This undermines valuable indigenous knowledge about various components of the framework in a particular region, since the inclusion of the knowledge is almost exclusively left at the discretion of the "developers".

4892db2e6515.title: Ecological footprint
4892db2e6515.sentence: In 2022, the top ten countries in total ecological footprint were: China (5.54 billion global hectares), United States (2.66 billion), India (1.64 billion), Russian Federation (774 million), Japan (586 million), Brazil (542 million), Indonesia (460 million), Germany (388 million), Republic of Korea (323 million) and Mexico (301 million).

c75caadd8ee4.title: Ecological footprint

3a93fc6e6fe2.sentence: Since this metric tracks biocapacity, the replacement of original ecosystems with high-productivity agricultural monocultures can lead to attributing a higher biocapacity to such regions.

e1caecf107f1.title: Ecological footprint

f7def88a12d5.title: Carbon footprint

fab7a8732761.title: Life-cycle assessment
fab7a8732761.section: Variants > Economic input–output life cycle assessment
fab7a8732761.sentence: Economic input–output LCA (EIOLCA) involves use of aggregate sector-level data on how much environmental impact can be attributed to each sector of the economy and how much each sector purchases from other sectors.

784754a15e70.title: Life-cycle assessment
784754a15e70.section: Variants > Economic input–output life cycle assessment
784754a15e70.sentence: Such analysis can account for long chains (for example, building an automobile requires energy, but producing energy requires vehicles, and building those vehicles requires energy, etc.), which somewhat alleviates the scoping problem of process LCA; however, EIOLCA relies on sector-level averages that may or may not be representative of the specific subset of the sector relevant to a particular product and therefore is not suitable for evaluating the environmental impacts of products.

17657e04e441.title: Life-cycle assessment
17657e04e441.section: Variants > Economic input–output life cycle assessment
17657e04e441.sentence: Additionally, the translation of economic quantities into environmental impacts is not validated.

52ca845a906c.title: Life-cycle assessment
52ca845a906c.section: Variants > Cradle-to-grave or life cycle assessment
52ca845a906c.sentence: Cradle-to-grave is the full life cycle assessment from resource extraction ('cradle'), to manufacturing, usage, and maintenance, all the way through to its disposal phase ('grave').

81d84a03ed89.title: Life-cycle assessment
81d84a03ed89.sentence: Cradle-to-gate is an assessment of a partial product life cycle from resource extraction (cradle) to the factory gate (i.e., before it is transported to the consumer).

1add2e7e4a87.title: Life-cycle assessment
1add2e7e4a87.sentence: Gate-to-gate is a partial LCA looking at only one value-added process in the entire production chain.

b8674e9f0c30.title: Life-cycle assessment
b8674e9f0c30.sentence: The use phase and disposal phase of the product are omitted in this case.

6eec15ae9b84.title: Life-cycle assessment
6eec15ae9b84.section: Variants > Cradle-to-cradle or closed loop production
6eec15ae9b84.sentence: Cradle-to-cradle is a specific kind of cradle-to-grave assessment, where the end-of-life disposal step for the product is a recycling process.

1b7bb2680100.title: Life-cycle assessment
1b7bb2680100.section: Variants > Cradle-to-cradle or closed loop production
1b7bb2680100.sentence: From the recycling process originate new, identical products (e.g., asphalt pavement from discarded asphalt pavement, glass bottles from collected glass bottles), or different products (e.g., glass wool insulation from collected glass bottles).

7564976db5ae.title: Life-cycle assessment
7564976db5ae.sentence: Well-to-wheel (WtW) is the specific LCA used for transport fuels and vehicles.

fa05dfb937ce.title: Life-cycle assessment
fa05dfb937ce.sentence: Life cycle energy analysis (LCEA) is an approach in which all energy inputs to a product are accounted for, not only direct energy inputs during manufacture, but also all energy inputs needed to produce components, materials and services needed for the manufacturing process.

dc3c268ae017.title: Life-cycle assessment
dc3c268ae017.section: Life cycle energy analysis > Energy production
dc3c268ae017.sentence: Net energy content is the energy content of the product minus energy input used during extraction and conversion, directly or indirectly.

87a04155c9d3.title: Life-cycle assessment

22855153198b.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
22855153198b.sentence: University of Maryland School of Public Policy professor and former Chief Economist for the World Bank Herman E. Daly (working from theory initially developed by Romanian economist Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen and laid out in his 1971 opus "The Entropy Law and the Economic Process") suggested the following three operational rules defining the condition of ecological (thermodynamic) sustainability:

78ab7676eeb0.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
78ab7676eeb0.sentence: - Renewable resources such as fish, soil, and groundwater must be used no faster than the rate at which they regenerate.

8869eb6fbd50.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
8869eb6fbd50.sentence: - Nonrenewable resources such as minerals and fossil fuels must be used no faster than renewable substitutes for them can be put into place.

d92f4f6cf9c7.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
d92f4f6cf9c7.sentence: - Pollution and wastes must be emitted no faster than natural systems can absorb them, recycle them, or render them harmless.

e05bdd7ab1e2.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
e05bdd7ab1e2.sentence: In this view, the Bruntland Definition and the Daly Rules can be seen as complementary—Bruntland provides the ethical goal of non-depletion of natural capital, Daly details parsimoniously how this ethic is operationalized in physical terms.

fa2f94ef662f.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
fa2f94ef662f.section: Metrics and indices > Circles of Sustainability approach
fa2f94ef662f.sentence: A number of agencies including the UN Global Compact Cities Programme, World Vision and Metropolis have since 2010 begun using the Circles of Sustainability approach that sets up a four-domain framework for choosing appropriate indicators.

1f6f676c113f.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
1f6f676c113f.section: Metrics and indices > Circles of Sustainability approach
1f6f676c113f.sentence: The framework is arranged around four domains - economics, ecology, politics and culture - which are then subdivided into seven analytically derived sub-domains for each domain.

48e92dfab505.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
48e92dfab505.section: Metrics and indices > Circles of Sustainability approach
48e92dfab505.sentence: Rather than designating the indicators that have to be used like most other approaches, it provides a framework to guide decision-making on what indicators are most useful.

167219fd5fdb.title: Sustainability metrics and indices
167219fd5fdb.section: Metrics and indices > Circles of Sustainability approach
167219fd5fdb.sentence: Indicators are linked to each sub-domain.

7292d9de9d29.title: Emission inventory
7292d9de9d29.sentence: An emission inventory (or emissions inventory) is an accounting of the amount of pollutants discharged into the atmosphere.

5d5a42ae6e61.title: Emission inventory
5d5a42ae6e61.sentence: An emission inventory usually contains the total emissions for one or more specific greenhouse gases or air pollutants, originating from all source categories in a certain geographical area and within a specified time span, usually a specific year.

db7ca6820829.title: Water footprint
db7ca6820829.section: By region > Water footprint of nations
db7ca6820829.sentence: The water footprint of a nation is the amount of water used to produce the goods and services consumed by the inhabitants of that nation.

9bc1214c59d7.section: By region > Water footprint of nations > Internal or external
9bc1214c59d7.sentence: The internal water footprint is the amount of water used from domestic water resources; the external water footprint is the amount of water used in other countries to produce goods and services imported and consumed by the inhabitants of the country.

f61332a114c6.sentence: When taking the use of domestic water resources as a starting point for calculating a nation's water footprint, one should subtract the virtual water flows that leave the country and add the virtual water flows that enter the country.
