4bf5cd4dd2c9.title: Porter hypothesis
4bf5cd4dd2c9.sentence: According to the Porter hypothesis, strict environmental regulations can induce efficiency and encourage innovations that help improve commercial competitiveness.

b6ef8420ca08.title: Porter hypothesis
b6ef8420ca08.sentence: The hypothesis was formulated by the Harvard University economist Michael Porter in an article in 1991.

2c0c32a3968c.title: Porter hypothesis
2c0c32a3968c.sentence: Porter and Claas van der Linde, of the University of St. Gallen, detailed the hypothesis in the 1995 journal article "Toward a New Conception of the Environment-Competitiveness Relationship."

50e813991452.title: Porter hypothesis
50e813991452.sentence: The hypothesis suggests that strict environmental regulation triggers the discovery and introduction of cleaner technologies and environmental improvements, the innovation effect, making production processes and products more efficient.

5208dda9501e.title: Porter hypothesis
5208dda9501e.sentence: The cost savings that can be achieved are sufficient to overcompensate for both the compliance costs directly attributed to new regulations and the innovation costs.

9f655b513445.title: Porter hypothesis

8519b0c36186.title: Porter hypothesis

2fa2398cbf72.title: Porter hypothesis
2fa2398cbf72.sentence: There is mixed evidence whether stricter regulation enhances business performance, the "strong" version of Porter hypothesis.

51847339c320.title: Porter hypothesis

e4479eedffa1.title: Regulation and monitoring of pollution

b3ff24665097.title: Regulation and monitoring of pollution

9bffdb5dc2f9.title: Pigouvian tax
9bffdb5dc2f9.sentence: A Pigouvian tax (also spelled Pigovian tax) is a tax on a market activity that generates negative externalities, that is, costs incurred by third parties.

f687b2b0d8e0.title: Pigouvian tax
f687b2b0d8e0.sentence: Ideally, the tax is set equal to the external marginal cost of the negative externalities, in order to correct an undesirable or inefficient market outcome (a market failure).

855fc632b57b.title: Pigouvian tax
855fc632b57b.sentence: In the presence of negative externalities, parties who did not consent to the transaction or activity, and did not receive payment, nevertheless incur some of the costs, so the total cost is not covered by the private cost of the activity.

42ff5bd41d0b.title: Pigouvian tax
42ff5bd41d0b.sentence: In such a case, the market outcome is not efficient and may lead to a harmful excess of the activity.

c9d21a980531.title: Pigouvian tax
c9d21a980531.sentence: Pigouvian taxes are named after the English economist Arthur Cecil Pigou (1877–1959), who developed the concept of economic externalities.

ea851e3d8d3f.title: Pigouvian tax
ea851e3d8d3f.sentence: In 1920, the British economist Arthur Cecil Pigou published The Economics of Welfare.

c985f1fdf31b.title: Pigouvian tax
c985f1fdf31b.sentence: To deal with over-production, Pigou recommends a tax placed on the offending producer.

30320238797f.title: Pigouvian tax
30320238797f.sentence: A tax shifts the marginal private cost curve up by the amount of the externality.

a347e110b387.title: Pigouvian tax
a347e110b387.sentence: If the tax is placed on the quantity of emissions from the factory, the producers have an incentive to reduce output to the socially optimum level.

7f9c6634c293.title: Pigouvian tax

4b96072a7c6b.title: Pigouvian tax
4b96072a7c6b.sentence: Taxing proxies for the negative externalities, such as taxing production as a proxy for emissions, has been argued to sometimes fail to deliver efficient market outcomes.

f23bbc0b5587.title: Pigouvian tax

98cfbef441ca.title: Pigouvian tax
98cfbef441ca.sentence: Examples are a subsidy for flu vaccines, for research and development, and for public goods such as education and national defense.

f962bf7a1d33.title: Pigouvian tax
f962bf7a1d33.sentence: The Pigouvian tax is a method commonly used by governments as it has relatively low transaction costs associated with implementation.

b3fd9ec70059.title: Pigouvian tax
b3fd9ec70059.sentence: Other methods such as command and control regulations or subsidies assume that the government has complete knowledge of the market, which is almost never the case, and can often lead to inefficiencies and market failure through rent-seeking behavior by individuals and firms.

3da0c9fdc38d.sentence: The environmental tax, including carbon taxes, fuel taxes, severance taxes, land value taxes (LVT) on the unimproved value of land, etc., is a classic example of the Pigouvian tax.

0a32ee3b3368.title: Environmental tax

3976c9dc4fa5.title: Environmental tax

5bd2d2ae3aef.title: Environmental tax

99afe093136d.title: Environmental tax

71037d032cbe.sentence: An excise, or excise tax, is any duty on a category of goods that is normally levied by a government at the moment of manufacture for domestic consumption.

6afa55718e8a.title: Excise

b73ebe897928.title: Excise

aaac9210e05f.title: Congestion pricing
aaac9210e05f.sentence: Congestion pricing or congestion charges is a system of charging users of public goods that are subject to congestion through excess demand, such as through higher peak charges for use of bus services, electricity, metros, railways, telephones, and road pricing to reduce traffic congestion; airlines and shipping companies may be charged higher fees for slots at airports and through canals at busy times.

28e65eb508f3.title: Congestion pricing

dc7b60dc250c.title: Congestion pricing
dc7b60dc250c.sentence: According to the economic theory behind congestion pricing, the objective of this policy is to use the price mechanism to cover the social cost of an activity where users otherwise do not pay for the negative externalities they create (such as driving in a congested area during peak demand).

576fdf5059a4.title: Pigouvian tax

24336f7b39ca.title: Congestion pricing
24336f7b39ca.sentence: According to the economic theory behind congestion pricing, the objective of this policy is the use of the price mechanism to make users more aware of the costs that they impose upon one another when consuming during the peak demand, and that they should pay for the additional congestion they create, thus encouraging the redistribution of the demand in space or in time, or shifting it to the consumption of a substitute public good; for example, switching from private transport to public transport.

8f47ba3510de.title: Congestion pricing

61f0b82f4788.title: Carbon tax

be97cd1fa3fe.title: Emissions trading
be97cd1fa3fe.section: Economics > Prices versus quantities, and the safety valve
be97cd1fa3fe.sentence: Uncertainty in future supply and demand conditions (market volatility) coupled with a fixed number of pollution permits creates an uncertainty in the future price of pollution permits, and the industry must accordingly bear the cost of adapting to these volatile market conditions.

62bb47a3ff6f.sentence: The burden of a volatile market thus lies with the industry rather than the controlling agency, which is generally more efficient.

2b43880980c8.sentence: A major drawback of an emission tax is that the environmental outcome (e.g. a limit on the amount of emissions) is not guaranteed.

554d83d8f526.sentence: An advantage is that, given a uniform tax rate and a volatile market, the taxing entity will not be in a position to pick "winners and losers" and the opportunity for corruption will be less.

b9205841ce8b.sentence: A tax is a price control, while a cap-and-trade system is a quantity control instrument.

6500a55b9aaf.sentence: That is, a tax is a unit price for pollution that is set by authorities, and the market determines the quantity emitted; in cap and trade, authorities determine the amount of pollution, and the market determines the price.

a5d6848f8893.sentence: Responsiveness to inflation: Cap-and-trade has the advantage that it adjusts to inflation (changes to overall prices) automatically, while emissions fees must be changed by regulators.

bea965ed2200.title: Emissions trading

bea965ed2200.sentence: Under cap and trade, the emissions cost automatically decreases, so a cap-and-trade scheme adds another automatic stabilizer to the economy—in effect, an automatic fiscal stimulus.

de06ca8572a5.title: Pigouvian tax

f502fa3d2e85.title: Carbon fee and dividend
f502fa3d2e85.sentence: A carbon fee and dividend or climate income is a system to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and address climate change.

60c16943524a.title: Carbon fee and dividend
60c16943524a.sentence: The system imposes a carbon tax on the sale of fossil fuels, and then distributes the revenue of this tax over the entire population (equally, on a per-person basis) as a monthly income or regular payment.

00e6e1c973a7.title: Carbon fee and dividend
00e6e1c973a7.sentence: - A fee is levied on fuels at their point of origin into the economy, such as the well, mine, or port of entry.

20737f2c4e21.title: Carbon fee and dividend
20737f2c4e21.sentence: - The fee is progressively increased, providing a steady, predictable price signal and incentivizing early transition to low-carbon energy sources and products.

0ac596b15a65.title: Carbon fee and dividend
0ac596b15a65.sentence: - A border tax adjustment is levied on imports from nations that lack their own equivalent fee on carbon.

efe6970d52af.title: Carbon fee and dividend
efe6970d52af.sentence: Returning 100% of net fees results in a revenue-neutral carbon fee-and-dividend system; this revenue neutrality often appeals to conservatives, such as former Secretary of State George Shultz, who want to reduce emissions without increasing the size and funding of the federal government.

5a89a194956a.title: Carbon fee and dividend
5a89a194956a.sentence: While there is broad scientific consensus that a carbon tax is the most powerful way to reduce emissions, such a tax necessarily increases prices and the cost of living.

64a966c89f84.title: Carbon fee and dividend
64a966c89f84.sentence: By handing out the revenue of this tax as a universal climate income, the price rise is largely compensated.

1947d962aa3a.title: Carbon fee and dividend
1947d962aa3a.sentence: As of July 2022, there were eight jurisdictions globally implementing a form of carbon fee and dividend: Switzerland, Austria and Alberta, Ontario, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Yukon and British Columbia in Canada.

682bb2ec5777.title: Carbon fee and dividend

23b1a13d0053.title: Carbon fee and dividend

2a016bfe56c3.title: Carbon fee and dividend

d12f7115e348.title: Carbon fee and dividend

0f34badabe7b.title: Carbon fee and dividend
0f34badabe7b.sentence: The Swiss carbon tax and dividend scheme commenced in 2008 when voluntary measures failed to meet intermediate targets linked to Switzerland's Kyoto Protocol commitments, as legislated under its Federal Act on the Reduction of CO2 Emissions ("CO2 Act").

f399199d59be.title: British Columbia carbon tax

e3bb202abc9c.title: British Columbia carbon tax
e3bb202abc9c.sentence: It was a British Columbia policy that added additional carbon taxes to fossil fuels burned for transportation, home heating, and electricity and reduces personal income taxes and corporate taxes by a roughly equal amount.

dc158aac31b6.title: British Columbia carbon tax

ef3056debc85.title: British Columbia carbon tax

0c076d4e180a.title: British Columbia carbon tax

d0323e32bfcf.title: British Columbia carbon tax

070c9d058433.title: British Columbia carbon tax

1121e389835d.title: British Columbia carbon tax

a0613458b531.title: Hypothecated tax
a0613458b531.sentence: The hypothecation of a tax (also known as the ring-fencing or earmarking of a tax) is the dedication of the revenue from a specific tax for a particular expenditure purpose.

7e5d1679bf41.title: Hypothecated tax
7e5d1679bf41.sentence: This approach differs from the classical method according to which all government spending is done from a consolidated fund.

469b2a401147.title: Hypothecated tax
469b2a401147.sentence: Strong hypothecation means that the revenues from the tax go only to financing the particular service and the service is financed only through the revenues from this tax.

04cdf8fe37c6.title: Hypothecated tax
04cdf8fe37c6.sentence: If at least one of the two conditions is not met, we say that the hypothecation is weak.

cbfb5bd637a1.title: Hypothecated tax
cbfb5bd637a1.sentence: - Transparency – Hypothecated taxation makes the link between revenues from taxes and government spending more visible and consumers may be better able to decide how much they are willing to pay.

3ebfa021854b.title: Hypothecated tax
3ebfa021854b.sentence: - Public support – The knowledge that the money paid on taxes will go directly to some needed service (e.g. health care) can help to reduce the dissatisfaction of the population with an increase in taxes.

8941384bc55a.title: Hypothecated tax
8941384bc55a.sentence: Firstly, public spending should be determined by policies and not by the amount of the revenue raised.

83dc1ed3deba.title: Hypothecated tax
83dc1ed3deba.sentence: Secondly, the flexibility of fiscal policy and thus the ability to influence the economic situation is reduced when hypothecation is used.

d67ea08af2e7.title: Landfill tax

07d0e85a3856.title: Per unit tax

4dfc395f44df.title: Per unit tax

82a5adff39ce.title: Per unit tax

5d129de8e6d7.title: Per unit tax
5d129de8e6d7.sentence: Using specific taxes has proved to be one of the most effective ways to reduce consumption, whereas ad valorem tax which is based on a per cent of product value may lead to substitution to cheaper brands.

c0eefbf0d4be.title: Steering tax
c0eefbf0d4be.sentence: A steering tax or ecological incentive tax is a tax which aims to change the behaviour of the tax payer, as defined by lawmakers, and not particularly to increase tax revenue.

96f8338ab513.title: Steering tax
96f8338ab513.sentence: The Pigovian tax is a special case of a steering tax to avoid negative externality.

48ef677c786e.title: Steering tax
48ef677c786e.sentence: If the aim of steering the payer's behaviour is successful, this means that the aim to increase tax revenues will be unsuccessful.

77ae41a3df77.title: Steering tax
77ae41a3df77.sentence: The yield of tax revenue is reduced if the tax payers behave in the targeted way.

f368984902e9.title: Steering tax

f368984902e9.sentence: There are also steering taxes like the de:Swiss VOC-fee (Incentive Tax on Volatile Organic Compounds), which will be completely distributed amongst the population.

228aaf7ec505.title: Steering tax

228aaf7ec505.sentence: The ideal goal of such a refund is the creation of positive incentives: People will be rewarded when they behave in the wanted way.

2b830930d224.title: Pass-through (economics)
2b830930d224.sentence: In economics, cost pass-through (also known as price transmission or simply pass-through) is a process (or result) of a business changing pricing of its output (products or services) to reflect a change in costs of its own input (materials, labor, etc.).

37d13c82bef7.title: Pass-through (economics)
37d13c82bef7.sentence: The effect of passthrough is quantified as passthrough rate, a ratio between the change in costs and the change in prices.

7a5d5422a4b9.title: Pass-through (economics)
7a5d5422a4b9.sentence: Depending on circumstances, a business might choose to absorb part of the cost changes (resulting in ratio below 1.0) or amplify them (ratio above 1.0).

3a63d28a56bd.title: Pass-through (economics)
3a63d28a56bd.sentence: For example, in the perfectly inelastic demand case (consumers have to have the good whatever the price is), a cost shock will be passed to consumers in its entirety (full pass-through, passthrough rate will be equal to 1.0).

100b84d855e5.title: Pass-through (economics)
100b84d855e5.sentence: In the case of a perfectly elastic demand (consumers ready to abandon the market if faced with any price increase), producers will be forced to fully absorb the shock (pass-through rate 0.0).

d8d4baf63b8a.title: Pass-through (economics)
d8d4baf63b8a.sentence: The cost pass-through in a perfectly competitive market is higher with less elastic demand and more elastic supply.

fb7751026502.title: Road pricing
fb7751026502.sentence: Road pricing are direct charges levied for the use of roads, including road tolls, distance or time-based fees, congestion charges and charges designed to discourage the use of certain classes of vehicle, fuel sources or more polluting vehicles.

2d11d9217a51.title: Road pricing
2d11d9217a51.sentence: These charges may be used primarily for revenue generation, usually for road infrastructure financing, or as a transportation demand management tool to reduce peak hour private vehicle travel and the associated traffic congestion or other social and environmental negative externalities associated with road travel such as air pollution, greenhouse gas emissions, visual intrusion, noise pollution and road traffic collisions.

b40ae77402c1.title: Road pricing
b40ae77402c1.sentence: Nobel-laureate William Vickrey then built on the ideas of the economist Arthur Pigou, outlining a theoretical case for road pricing in a major work on the subject of 1955 proposing in 1959 that drivers should be charged by electronic means for use of busy urban roads.

fa450616a48b.title: Road pricing

26e64530c515.title: Road pricing

1a64b753f567.title: Road pricing

93bd5f0ece12.title: Feebate
93bd5f0ece12.sentence: A feebate is a policy mechanism that imposes fees on products or activities associated with negative externalities while providing rebates for alternatives that produce fewer or no such externalities.

29df1a9ecde4.title: Feebate

95ea9e2d6770.title: Feebate

9f90cb8487d9.title: Feebate

38f92d83b1f2.title: Feebate
38f92d83b1f2.sentence: A feebate can internalize that cost into the initial purchase price, thereby requiring the buyer to prepay for the taking of public and private environmental goods.

a39ecca04dfc.title: User fee

c9fc742c7b55.title: User fee

8c13b1f55a06.title: User fee

2ef0c22846ef.sentence: Water quality trading (WQT) is a market-based approach, implemented on a watershed-scale, used to improve or maintain water quality.

a05f35fd20ab.title: United States regulation of point source water pollution
a05f35fd20ab.section: Other emerging regulatory approaches > Water quality trading > Background
a05f35fd20ab.sentence: Most of the water quality trading markets currently in operation are focused on the trading of nutrients such as phosphorus and nitrogen.

45a99f7f9225.title: United States regulation of point source water pollution
45a99f7f9225.section: Regulatory framework > Related programs > EPA water quality trading policy
45a99f7f9225.sentence: EPA issued its Water Quality Trading Policy in 2003.

7d0c77bd1273.title: United States regulation of point source water pollution
7d0c77bd1273.section: Regulatory framework > Related programs > EPA water quality trading policy
7d0c77bd1273.sentence: All water quality trading programs are subject to the requirements of the Clean Water Act.

c0dea4a540c3.title: White certificates
c0dea4a540c3.sentence: In environmental policy, white certificates are documents certifying that a certain reduction of energy consumption has been attained.

de782ec6c998.title: White certificates
de782ec6c998.sentence: In most applications, the white certificates are tradable and combined with an obligation to achieve a certain target of energy savings.

b549639ea0e8.title: White certificates
b549639ea0e8.sentence: Under such a system, producers, suppliers or distributors of electricity, gas and oil are required to undertake energy efficiency measures for the final user that are consistent with a pre-defined percentage of their annual energy deliverance.

d7b82583b4bd.title: White certificates
d7b82583b4bd.sentence: If energy producers do not meet the mandated target for energy consumption they are required to pay a penalty.

de0c478a9f62.title: White certificates
de0c478a9f62.sentence: Quite analogous to the closely related concept of emissions trading, the tradability in theory guarantees that the overall energy saving is achieved at least cost, while the certificates guarantee that the overall energy saving target is achieved.

2f11669ca863.title: White certificates
2f11669ca863.sentence: Great Britain started in 2002, Italy in January 2005; France and Denmark a year later.

31aa0dbceff9.title: Carbon retirement
31aa0dbceff9.sentence: Carbon retirement is the permanent removal of emission allowances or carbon credits from circulation within carbon emission trading systems.

ca095de2b3cd.title: Carbon retirement
ca095de2b3cd.sentence: A retired allowance or credit can no longer be sold or used, so retirement is meant either to cut the total amount of emissions allowed under a cap or to record that a credit has been used to offset emissions.

ef742c77a0be.title: Carbon retirement
ef742c77a0be.sentence: Removing allowances from the market reduces the overall supply, which raises their scarcity and price.

ab6d3f7e95a8.title: Carbon retirement
ab6d3f7e95a8.sentence: By then, more than 3 billion allowances had been invalidated under the mechanism.

e2aa952cb0a9.title: Carbon retirement
e2aa952cb0a9.sentence: Companies retire credits to offset emissions they can't yet eliminate, often as part of net-zero commitments.

058d5cb25d93.title: Carbon retirement
058d5cb25d93.sentence: - In 2023, a record 164 million credits were retired, up 6% from 154 million in 2022, according to BloombergNEF.

8d4ab5347512.title: Acid Rain Program
8d4ab5347512.sentence: Citizens and groups can purchase sulfur dioxide emissions allowances alongside electric utilities and other producers of air pollution in annual auctions conducted by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and on the Chicago Board of Trade.

5a908364d185.title: Acid Rain Program
5a908364d185.sentence: No national environmental group has ever bid in the annual EPA Auction, but a small number of local groups have participated for many years, apparently on the theory that reducing the supply of allowances may someday drive up the price of acquiring them.

9a253bafba9b.title: Transferable development rights
9a253bafba9b.sentence: Transferable development rights (TDR) is a method by which developers can purchase the development rights of certain parcels within a designated "sending district" and transfer the rights to another "receiving district" to increase the density of their new development.

e1e28f6c368e.title: Transferable development rights
e1e28f6c368e.sentence: The underlying legal concept of a transfer of development rights programme is the notion that all land has a bundle of property rights.

20cca12e1d40.title: Transferable development rights
20cca12e1d40.sentence: TDR is based on the concept that with land ownership comes the right of use of land, or land development.

bd6a40509de9.title: Transferable development rights
bd6a40509de9.sentence: Sending districts are commonly made up of areas with desirable traits that are at risk of being developed such as agricultural lands or wilderness areas, but may also be newly designated historic sites.

3e814971e217.title: Transferable development rights
3e814971e217.sentence: Receiving districts are generally areas more suited for higher density developments and sending districts are areas with environmental, heritage or agricultural values that the county, city or town wishes to preserve.

b184c8aef69a.title: Transferable development rights
b184c8aef69a.sentence: The procedure offers landowners financial incentives or bonuses for the conservation and maintenance of the environmental, heritage or agricultural values of their land.

a32d32c06c80.title: Transferable development rights
a32d32c06c80.sentence: The TDR process can be considered a tool for controlling urban sprawl by concentrating development.

1c057405c245.title: Transferable development rights
1c057405c245.sentence: TDR programs have been implemented in over 200 U.S. communities, in several states, including Colorado, Massachusetts, Virginia and Washington.

4e4a467d88f6.title: Subsidy
4e4a467d88f6.sentence: A subsidy, subvention or government incentive is a type of government expenditure which redistributes from tax payers to individuals, households, or businesses.

7fa7024fdfa1.title: Subsidy
7fa7024fdfa1.sentence: Subsidies take various forms, such as direct government expenditures, tax incentives, soft loans, price support, and government provision of goods and services.

05e6bea6fd6a.title: Subsidy
05e6bea6fd6a.sentence: Although commonly extended from the government, the term subsidy can relate to any type of support – for example from NGOs, or international organizations.

764f99c78915.title: Subsidy
764f99c78915.sentence: For instance, the government may distribute direct payment subsidies to individuals and households during an economic downturn in order to help its citizens pay their bills and to stimulate economic activity.

a20d52c9599a.title: Subsidy
a20d52c9599a.sentence: Evidence from recent studies suggests that government expenditures on subsidies remain high in many countries, often amounting to several percentage points of GDP.

1afe9d6e2839.title: Subsidy
1afe9d6e2839.sentence: Some governments subsidise transport, especially rail and bus transport, which decrease congestion and pollution compared to cars.

f62958639895.title: Subsidy
f62958639895.sentence: Although subsidies can be important, many create perverse incentives and adverse unintended consequences.

955fbdfe72eb.title: Precautionary principle
955fbdfe72eb.sentence: The precautionary principle (or precautionary approach) is a broad epistemological, philosophical and legal approach to innovations with potential for causing harm when extensive scientific knowledge on the matter is lacking.

fb8a65f200ce.title: Precautionary principle
fb8a65f200ce.sentence: It emphasizes caution, pausing and review before leaping into new innovations that may prove disastrous.

f47f1f842d94.title: Precautionary principle
f47f1f842d94.sentence: The principle is often used by policy makers in situations where there is the possibility of harm from making a certain decision (e.g. taking a particular course of action) and conclusive evidence is not yet available.

641a5df45fc6.title: Precautionary principle
641a5df45fc6.sentence: The concept "precautionary principle" is generally considered to have arisen in English from a translation of the German term Vorsorgeprinzip in the 1970s in response to forest degradation and sea pollution, where German lawmakers adopted clean air act banning use of certain substances suspected in causing the environmental damage even though evidence of their impact was inconclusive at that time.

20355e69d17e.title: Precautionary principle
20355e69d17e.sentence: Within this element lies an implicit reversal of the onus of proof: under the precautionary principle it is the responsibility of an activity-proponent to establish that the proposed activity will not (or is very unlikely to) result in significant harm.

2aeaa2cea852.title: Precautionary principle
2aeaa2cea852.sentence: - The concept of proportionality of the risk and the cost and feasibility of a proposed action.

ddf819ebcd03.title: Precautionary principle
ddf819ebcd03.sentence: Various interests being represented by various groups proposing the principle resulted in great variability of its formulation: one study identified 14 different formulations of the principle in treaties and non-treaty declarations.

d4600375483c.title: Precautionary principle
d4600375483c.section: Application > International agreements and declarations > European Union
d4600375483c.sentence: It shall be based on the precautionary principle and on the principles that preventive action should be taken, that environmental damage should as a priority be rectified at source and that the polluter should pay.

d5d7b1753767.title: Precautionary principle
d5d7b1753767.sentence: - Global warming or abrupt climate change in general

726694be583b.title: Precautionary principle
726694be583b.sentence: - Introduction of new products into the environment, with potential impact on biodiversity (e.g., genetically modified organisms)

5da03ca8fed0.title: Precautionary principle
5da03ca8fed0.sentence: - Threats to public health, due to new diseases and techniques (e.g., HIV transmitted through blood transfusion)

0683179132af.title: Precautionary principle
0683179132af.sentence: Critics argue that it is vague, self-cancelling, unscientific and an obstacle to progress.

415123aef6f3.title: Precautionary principle
415123aef6f3.sentence: The precautionary principle was promulgated in philosophy by Hans Jonas in his 1979 text, The Imperative of Responsibility, wherein Jonas argued that technology had altered the range of the impact of human action and, as such, ethics must be modified so that the far distant effects of one's actions should now be considered.

653a1b4331c1.title: Precautionary principle
653a1b4331c1.section: Application > International agreements and declarations > "Principle" vs. "approach"
653a1b4331c1.sentence: Principle 15 of the Rio Declaration 1992 states that: "in order to protect the environment, the precautionary approach shall be widely applied by States according to their capabilities.

203d05f6ab9c.title: Ecolabel
203d05f6ab9c.sentence: Ecolabels (also "eco-Labels") and Green Stickers are labeling systems for food and consumer products.

b36898e8a92f.title: Ecolabel
b36898e8a92f.sentence: They are a form of sustainability measurement directed at consumers, intended to make it easy to take environmental concerns into account when shopping.

c26d643b7c03.title: Ecolabel
c26d643b7c03.sentence: The use of ecolabels is voluntary, whereas green stickers are mandated by law; for example, in North America major appliances and automobiles use Energy Star.

38ca0d03ec98.title: Ecolabel
38ca0d03ec98.sentence: There are currently 456 eco-labels in 199 countries, across 25 industry sectors according Ecolabel Index, the largest global directory of eco-labels.

f33830713e45.title: Ecolabel
f33830713e45.sentence: Some labels quantify pollution or energy consumption by way of index scores or units of measurement, while others assert compliance with a set of practices or minimum requirements for sustainability or reduction of harm to the environment.

2e3990e4cd62.title: Ecolabel
2e3990e4cd62.sentence: Through a verification process, usually referred to as "certification", a farm, forest, fishery, or mine can show that it complies with a standard and earn the right to sell its products as certified through the supply chain, often resulting in a consumer-facing ecolabel.

bb1d3a351d9e.title: Ecolabel
bb1d3a351d9e.sentence: Label trust is an issue for consumers because some manufacturers and manufacturing associations have set up "rubber stamp" labels to greenwash their products with fake ecolabels.

901775f92cab.title: Ecolabel
901775f92cab.sentence: Green Stickers on consumer goods have been evolving since the late 1970s, when the German Blue Angel (Der Blaue Engel) certification became the first ecolabel worldwide in 1978.

3363bdacd6c1.title: Ecolabel
3363bdacd6c1.sentence: They provide a verifiable link between products and informed consumer wishes.

769f7e0b1593.title: Ecolabel
769f7e0b1593.sentence: This approach applies market pressure on industries to minimize their environmental impact; this is evidenced by the growth in the population of informed consumers.

1a083fca1ca6.title: Ecolabel
1a083fca1ca6.sentence: The EU Ecolabel was established in 1992 by the European Commission.

39fcd6c0e45e.title: Sustainability standards and certification
39fcd6c0e45e.sentence: Sustainability standards and certifications are voluntary guidelines used by producers, manufacturers, traders, retailers, and service providers to demonstrate their commitment to good environmental, social, ethical, and food safety practices.

a15b19893f28.title: Sustainability standards and certification
a15b19893f28.sentence: There are over 400 such standards across the world.

57ac2e9f67ce.title: Sustainability standards and certification
57ac2e9f67ce.sentence: A standard is normally developed by a broad range of stakeholders and experts in a particular sector and includes a set of practices or criteria for how a crop should be sustainably grown or a resource should be ethically harvested.

ce904091a6ad.title: Sustainability standards and certification
ce904091a6ad.sentence: Normally sustainability standards are accompanied by a verification process – often referred to as "certification" – to evaluate that an enterprise complies with a standard, as well as a traceability process for certified products to be sold along the supply chain, often resulting in a consumer-facing label.

3dd8a62aa092.title: Sustainability standards and certification
3dd8a62aa092.sentence: - Weak legislation and strong demand for action: Sustainability standards emerged in areas where weak national and global legislation existed but where the consumer and NGO movements around the globe demanded action.

43744ebb89b9.title: Sustainability standards and certification
43744ebb89b9.sentence: Some standards set the bar high for a sector, promoting strong social and environmental practices and working with the top performers to constantly push up sustainability expectations.

4a437d1acf03.title: Sustainability standards and certification
4a437d1acf03.sentence: Other standards are more focused on eliminating the worst practices and operate at more of an entry level to get a large proportion of an industry working incrementally towards better practices.

4343b41390d4.title: Sustainability standards and certification
4343b41390d4.sentence: Additional differences between standards might relate to the certification process and whether it is conducted by a first, second or third party; the traceability system in place and whether it allows for the segregation or mixing of certified and non-certified materials; and the types of sustainability claims that are made on products.

612bb9efe101.title: Sustainability standards and certification
612bb9efe101.section: International and private standards supporting sustainability
612bb9efe101.sentence: The most widely established and adopted standards are in agriculture, with 40% of global coffee production certified to one of the main schemes, and approximately 15–20% of cocoa and tea production being compliant with major international standards.

0e98b433a944.title: Sustainability standards and certification
0e98b433a944.sentence: Recent academic research has also examined individual certification schemes within the broader ecosystem of sustainability standards, including B Corp certification, highlighting both their potential benefits and ongoing debates about their effectiveness and governance.

8c68fd216af9.title: Sustainability standards and certification
8c68fd216af9.sentence: The trend started in the late 1980s and 1990s with the introduction of Ecolabels and standards for organic food and other products.

ff31ea66f007.title: Fair trade
ff31ea66f007.sentence: Fair trade is a trade arrangement designed to help producers in developing countries achieve sustainable and equitable conditions.

14865783515a.title: Fair trade
14865783515a.sentence: The fair trade movement advocates paying higher prices to exporters and improving social and environmental standards.

c52c53860af0.title: Fair trade
c52c53860af0.sentence: The movement focuses in particular on commodities, or products that are typically exported from developing countries to developed countries but are also used in domestic markets (e.g., Brazil, the United Kingdom and Bangladesh), most notably for handicrafts, coffee, cocoa, wine, sugar, fruit, flowers and gold.

0bb171cab21e.title: Fair trade
0bb171cab21e.sentence: The current fair trade movement was shaped in Europe in the 1960s.

f9f1eb41b487.title: Fair trade
f9f1eb41b487.sentence: Sales of fair trade products only took off with the arrival of the first Fairtrade certification initiatives.

8867046a9c5b.title: Fair trade
8867046a9c5b.sentence: Overseen by a standard-setting body (Fairtrade International) and a certification body (FLO-CERT), the system involves independent auditing of producers and traders to ensure the standards are met.

a6e174a288c9.title: Sustainability standards and certification
a6e174a288c9.sentence: The most distinguishing feature of the Fairtrade label is the guarantee of a minimum price and a social premium that goes to the cooperative and not to the producers directly.

a794b7f20e9a.title: Fair trade
a794b7f20e9a.sentence: In 2011, more than 1.2 million farmers and workers in more than 60 countries participated in Fairtrade International's fair trade system, which included €65 million in fairtrade premium paid to producers for use developing their communities.

b59b2f3042a5.title: Fair trade
b59b2f3042a5.sentence: Coffee is the most well-established fair trade commodity.

466e613b792c.title: Fair trade
466e613b792c.sentence: A proposed alternative to fair trade is direct trade, which eliminates the overhead costs of the fair trade certification and allows suppliers to receive higher prices closer to the retail value of the end product.

400e94f7d346.title: Fair trade
400e94f7d346.sentence: On 6 June 2008, Wales became the world's first Fair Trade Nation; followed by Scotland in February 2013.

87877a1be35d.title: Energy subsidy
87877a1be35d.sentence: Energy subsidies are measures that keep prices for customers below market levels, or for suppliers above market levels, or reduce costs for customers and suppliers.

b3a81035fc72.title: Energy subsidy
b3a81035fc72.sentence: The International Renewable Energy Agency tracked some $634 billion in energy-sector subsidies in 2020, and found that around 70% were fossil fuel subsidies.

ff94cf1fb37b.title: Energy subsidy
ff94cf1fb37b.sentence: About 20% went to renewable power generation, 6% to biofuels and just over 3% to nuclear.

f540bed66c30.title: Energy subsidy
f540bed66c30.section: Overview of all sources of energy
f540bed66c30.sentence: - Energy-related services provided by government at less than full cost – direct investment in energy infrastructure; public research and development.

97dae10d2d8c.title: Energy subsidy
97dae10d2d8c.section: Overview of all sources of energy
97dae10d2d8c.sentence: - Regulation of the energy sector – demand guarantees and mandated deployment rates; price controls; market-access restrictions; preferential planning consent and controls over access to resources.

b17f82de655f.title: Energy subsidy
b17f82de655f.section: Overview of all sources of energy
b17f82de655f.sentence: - Failure to impose external costs – environmental externality costs; energy security risks and price volatility costs.

8ca9114bae6f.title: Energy subsidy
8ca9114bae6f.section: Overview of all sources of energy
8ca9114bae6f.sentence: If governments choose to subsidize one particular source of energy more than another, that choice can impact the environment.

1bdd31428615.title: Energy subsidy
1bdd31428615.sentence: Early support of solar power by the United States and Germany greatly helped renewable energy commercialization to reduce greenhouse gas emissions worldwide, but may not have helped local manufacturing.

4877d7b364d6.title: Energy subsidy
4877d7b364d6.section: Overview of all sources of energy
4877d7b364d6.sentence: Overall, energy subsidies require coordination and integrated implementation, especially in light of globalization and increased interconnectedness of energy policies, thus their regulation at the World Trade Organization is often seen as necessary.

7a6623893cb9.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
7a6623893cb9.sentence: Fossil fuel subsidies are energy subsidies on fossil fuels.

34288aa5af06.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
34288aa5af06.sentence: Fossil fuel subsidies have been described as "any government action that lowers the cost of fossil fuel energy production, raises the price received by energy producers, or lowers the price paid by energy consumers." Including negative externalities such as health costs results in a much larger total.

452d3996d600.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
452d3996d600.sentence: Under a narrow definition, fossil fuel subsidies totalled around $725 billion (0.6% of global GDP) to $900 billion in 2024.

922e3690cc69.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
922e3690cc69.sentence: Under a more expansive definition, they totalled $6.7 trillion (5.8% of GDP).

56be68e10613.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
56be68e10613.sentence: Most subsidy is for oil and natural gas.

00071fb914e6.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
00071fb914e6.sentence: Subsidies are mainly on consumption, such as a lower sales tax on natural gas for residential heating; or subsidies on production, such as tax breaks on exploration for oil.

b7f586c7293c.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
b7f586c7293c.sentence: Or they may be free or cheap negative externalities; such as air pollution or climate change due to burning gasoline, diesel and jet fuel.

af6380c1472f.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
af6380c1472f.sentence: Fossil fuel subsidies are a negative carbon price and use government money that could be spent on other things.

324c7910a280.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
324c7910a280.sentence: The consensus among economists is that the rich get most absolute benefit from fossil fuel subsidies, for example the poorest people do not usually own cars.

156e7dd2d7ab.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
156e7dd2d7ab.sentence: Subsidies are estimated to cause hundreds of thousands of deaths from air pollution each year.

3ac623c564a6.title: Fossil fuel subsidies
3ac623c564a6.sentence: Eliminating fossil fuel subsidies would reduce the health risks of air pollution, and would greatly reduce global carbon emissions thus helping to limit climate change.

7aec711c0dde.title: Sustainable procurement
7aec711c0dde.sentence: Sustainable procurement is a process whereby organizations meet their needs for goods, services, works and utilities in a way that achieves value for money on a life-cycle basis while addressing equity principles for sustainable development, therefore benefiting societies and the economy across time and geographies while remaining within the carrying capacity of the environment.

8029ce7cd1cd.title: Sustainable procurement
8029ce7cd1cd.sentence: Procurement – the letting of contracts for goods, works and services on the best possible terms – has historically been based on two criteria, price and quality, with a view to maximizing benefits for the procuring organization.

9a39382031e8.title: Sustainable procurement
9a39382031e8.sentence: Sustainable procurement broadens this framework to take account of third-party consequences of procurement decisions, forming a "triple baseline" of external concerns which the procuring organization must fulfill.

b853eec0d369.title: Sustainable procurement
b853eec0d369.sentence: Sustainable procurement aims to promote conservation and responsible management of resources by using renewable or recycled materials wherever possible and reducing waste.

61c9f10784b0.title: Sustainable procurement
61c9f10784b0.sentence: Sustainable procurement also involves looking at production practices and making sure there are not any negative impacts to the environment such as pollution, biodiversity loss or habitat disruption.

ae7fb86348ad.title: Sustainable procurement
ae7fb86348ad.section: Sustainable procurement policy and development > Central government
ae7fb86348ad.sentence: Public spending, which accounts for an average of 12% of GDP in OECD countries, and up to 30% in developing countries, wields enormous purchasing power.

e35e90dd276d.title: Sustainable procurement
e35e90dd276d.section: Sustainable procurement policy and development > Private sector
e35e90dd276d.sentence: Acquisition of goods and services may account for over 50% of the company's expenses, and may exceed 80% in sectors such as in retailing, electronic and automotive industries - with all this purchasing power, the private sector has a great ability to influence markets.

93f93a7ec9e4.title: Sustainable procurement
93f93a7ec9e4.sentence: Often differences in the purchase price between a non-sustainable and sustainable alternative are negligible.

43e929e7ad6f.title: Sustainable procurement
43e929e7ad6f.sentence: Yet even where the sustainable option costs more upfront, savings of energy, water and waste over the lifetime of the product or service can provide significant financial savings.

bdb46ddafe76.title: Extended producer responsibility
bdb46ddafe76.sentence: Extended producer responsibility (EPR) is a strategy to add all of the estimated environmental costs associated with a product throughout the product life cycle to the market price of that product, contemporarily mainly applied in the field of waste management.

fd805391f2f2.title: Extended producer responsibility
fd805391f2f2.sentence: In subsequent reports prepared for the Ministry, the following definition emerged: "[EPR] is an environmental protection strategy to reach an environmental objective of a decreased total environmental impact of a product, by making the manufacturer of the product responsible for the entire life-cycle of the product and especially for the take-back, recycling and final disposal."

099303dc31e7.title: Extended producer responsibility
099303dc31e7.sentence: The concept was first formally introduced in Sweden by Thomas Lindhqvist in a 1990 report to the Swedish Ministry of the Environment.

3c459f0473a4.title: Extended producer responsibility
3c459f0473a4.sentence: Extended producer responsibility uses financial incentives to encourage manufacturers to design environmentally friendly products by holding producers responsible for the costs of managing their products at end of life.

868b76304e3a.title: Extended producer responsibility
868b76304e3a.sentence: EPR is based on the principle that manufacturers (usually brand owners) have the greatest control over product design and marketing and have the greatest ability and responsibility to reduce toxicity and waste.

db2057c25cf8.title: Extended producer responsibility
db2057c25cf8.sentence: EPR may take the form of a reuse, buyback, or recycling program.

a65d36ede88a.title: Extended producer responsibility
a65d36ede88a.sentence: The producer may also choose to delegate this responsibility to a third party, a so-called producer responsibility organization (PRO), which is paid by the producer for used-product management.

36bbc81b6e69.title: Extended producer responsibility
36bbc81b6e69.sentence: This policy approach differs from product stewardship, which shares responsibility across the chain of custody of a product, in that it attempts to relieve local governments of the costs of managing certain priority products by requiring manufacturers to internalize the cost of recycling within the product price.

8b6ebdb6f4ff.title: Extended producer responsibility
8b6ebdb6f4ff.sentence: In Germany, since the adoption of EPR, "between 1991 and 1998, the per capita consumption of packaging was reduced from 94.7 kg to 82 kg, resulting in a reduction of 13.4%".

822e2090ae4b.title: Extended producer responsibility
822e2090ae4b.sentence: One frequently discussed concern is the administrative burden created by the variation of regulatory frameworks across countries and waste streams.

79d07e8ed311.title: Extended producer responsibility
79d07e8ed311.sentence: Because EPR requirements often differ between jurisdictions, producers operating in multiple markets may face complex compliance obligations.

106dd0226381.title: Extended producer responsibility
106dd0226381.sentence: The OECD published a guidance manual about EPR in 2001 after several years of discussion by experts in this field, and updated it in 2016 to include developing countries' perspectives, based on experiences and policy changes.

65e3e6afe5fb.title: Polluter pays principle
65e3e6afe5fb.sentence: This is a concept that was probably first described by Thomas Lindhqvist for the Swedish government in 1990.

fcf123d9931f.title: Nudge theory
fcf123d9931f.sentence: Nudge theory is a concept in behavioral economics, decision making, behavioral policy, social psychology, consumer behavior, and related behavioral sciences that proposes adaptive designs of the decision environment (choice architecture) as ways to influence the behavior and decision-making of groups or individuals.

7b0d18ba4718.title: Nudge theory
7b0d18ba4718.sentence: Nudging contrasts with other ways to achieve compliance, such as education, legislation or enforcement.

c2b34711b907.title: Nudge theory
c2b34711b907.sentence: The nudge concept was popularized in the 2008 book Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth, and Happiness, by behavioral economist Richard Thaler and legal scholar Cass Sunstein, two American scholars at the University of Chicago.

50305165849c.title: Nudge theory
50305165849c.sentence: A nudge attempts to make it more likely that an individual will make a particular choice, or behave in a particular way, by altering the environment so that automatic cognitive processes are triggered to favour the desired outcome.

5e5c61a60076.title: Nudge theory
5e5c61a60076.sentence: Nudges are small changes in the environment that are easy and inexpensive to implement.

12e6a4158bc3.title: Nudge theory
12e6a4158bc3.sentence: Several different techniques exist for nudging, including defaults, social-proof heuristics, and increasing the salience of the desired option.

4dbc22f1e881.title: Nudge theory
4dbc22f1e881.sentence: For instance, tourists consumed more ethical foods, selected more sustainable hotels, reused towels and bed linen during hotel stays, increased their intentions to reduce their energy consumption, increased the adoption of tourists' voluntary carbon offsetting and many other examples.

14c37e0b8425.title: Nudge theory
14c37e0b8425.sentence: Several nudge units exist around the world at the national level (UK, Germany, Japan, and others) as well as at the international level (e.g. World Bank, UN, and the European Commission).

137ec7b2c7af.title: Nudge theory
137ec7b2c7af.sentence: In 2010, the British Behavioural Insights Team, or "Nudge Unit," was established at the British Cabinet Office and headed by psychologist David Halpern.

d1aa84a4a031.title: Nudge theory
d1aa84a4a031.sentence: They found that nudging is effective but there is a moderate publication bias.

02de0eaab86e.title: Nudge theory
02de0eaab86e.sentence: Later, Maier and colleagues found that, after correcting for this publication bias appropriately, there is no evidence that nudging would have any effect.

6e9362d4d1a1.title: Common Agricultural Policy
6e9362d4d1a1.sentence: The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) is the agricultural policy of the European Commission.

d986ad513dba.title: Common Agricultural Policy
d986ad513dba.sentence: It implements a system of agricultural subsidies, risk management instruments and other programmes.

33d082d787da.title: Common Agricultural Policy
33d082d787da.sentence: The CAP was introduced in 1962 and has since then undergone several changes to reduce the EEC budget cost (from 73% in 1985, to 37% in 2017) and consider rural development in its aims.

07e4f8ed4361.title: Common Agricultural Policy
07e4f8ed4361.section: Origins and history > Modern reforms > Agenda 2000 (1999)
07e4f8ed4361.sentence: The 'Agenda 2000' reforms divided the CAP into two 'Pillars': production support and rural development.

393ec972b1e6.title: Common Agricultural Policy
393ec972b1e6.sentence: CAP price intervention has been criticised for creating artificially high food prices throughout the EU.

c298ea5ed93d.title: Common Agricultural Policy
c298ea5ed93d.sentence: High import tariffs (estimated at 18–28%) have the effect of keeping prices high by restricting competition by non-EU producers.

b4d040fdbcf7.title: Common Agricultural Policy
b4d040fdbcf7.sentence: This leads to the European Union purchasing millions of tons of surplus output every year at the stated guaranteed market price, and storing this produce in large quantities (leading to what critics have called 'butter mountains' and 'wine lakes'), before selling the produce wholesale to developing nations.

8a64e49c899a.title: Common Agricultural Policy
8a64e49c899a.sentence: Because the CAP has traditionally rewarded farmers who produce more, larger farms have benefited much more from subsidies than smaller farms.

8739ac82b9a7.title: Common Agricultural Policy
8739ac82b9a7.sentence: A study reported in 2024 that 80% of the CAP's subsidies in 2013 supported emissions-intensive animal products, a ratio that hasn't significantly changed since.

fa17f6473d31.title: Common Agricultural Policy
fa17f6473d31.section: Origins and history > Modern reforms > The MacSharry reforms (1992)
fa17f6473d31.sentence: In 1992, the MacSharry reforms (named after the European Commissioner for Agriculture, Ray MacSharry) were created to limit rising production, while at the same time adjusting to the trend toward a more free agricultural market.

c9f616eaf5dd.title: Common Agricultural Policy
c9f616eaf5dd.section: Origins and history > Modern reforms > European Commission Report and decoupling (2003)
c9f616eaf5dd.sentence: On 26 June 2003, EU farm ministers adopted a fundamental reform of the CAP, based on "decoupling" subsidies from particular crops.

cbc446bcf6ea.title: Subsidy
cbc446bcf6ea.sentence: The effect of a subsidy is to shift the supply or demand curve to the right (i.e. increases the supply or demand) by the amount of the subsidy.

46fb92dc8855.title: Subsidy
46fb92dc8855.sentence: Assuming the market is in a perfectly competitive equilibrium, a subsidy increases the supply of the good beyond the equilibrium competitive quantity.

f6a676973ee7.title: Subsidy
f6a676973ee7.sentence: Deadweight loss from a subsidy is the amount by which the cost of the subsidy exceeds the gains of the subsidy.

8f9840d8a21a.title: Subsidy
8f9840d8a21a.sentence: The magnitude of the deadweight loss is dependent on the size of the subsidy.

ef73b06fbcc8.title: Subsidy
ef73b06fbcc8.sentence: A demand subsidy tends to increase prices, while supply subsidy can reduce the subsidized prices.

10b0bf9a997d.title: Subsidy
10b0bf9a997d.sentence: A subsidized product sold in the world market lowers the price of the good in other countries.

f7dee1e9448a.title: Subsidy
f7dee1e9448a.sentence: Since subsidies result in lower revenues for producers of foreign countries, they are a source of tension between the United States, Europe and poorer developing countries.

9e67feb006c4.title: Subsidy
9e67feb006c4.sentence: In its July 2019 report, "Going for Growth 2019: The time for reform is now", the OECD suggests that countries make better use of environmental taxation, phase out agricultural subsidies and environmentally harmful tax breaks.

8b4b422e0957.title: Subsidy
8b4b422e0957.sentence: To be "perverse", subsidies must exert effects that are demonstrably and significantly adverse both economically and environmentally.

8c556e463e87.title: Subsidy
8c556e463e87.sentence: A subsidy rarely, if ever, starts perverse, but over time a legitimate efficacious subsidy can become perverse or illegitimate if it is not withdrawn after meeting its goal or as political goals change.

535fb53cac8d.title: Subsidy
535fb53cac8d.sentence: Directly, they are expensive to governments by directing resources away from other legitimate should priorities (such as environmental conservation, education, health, or infrastructure), ultimately reducing the fiscal health of the government.

9dbb0cddcae9.title: Subsidy
9dbb0cddcae9.sentence: Indirectly, they cause environmental degradation (exploitation of resources, pollution, loss of landscape, misuse and overuse of supplies) which, as well as its fundamental damage, acts as a further brake on economies; tend to benefit the few at the expense of the many, and the rich at the expense of the poor; lead to further polarization of development between the Northern and Southern hemispheres; lower global market prices; and undermine investment decisions reducing the pressure on businesses to become more efficient.

391cbd3dcd7f.title: Subsidy
391cbd3dcd7f.sentence: Principally, this is because they become "locked" into society, causing bureaucratic roadblocks and institutional inertia.

0b4a6c192282.title: Subsidy
0b4a6c192282.sentence: In 2005, US farmers received $14 billion and EU farmers $47 billion in agricultural subsidies.

e1cd165e3c2c.title: Command and control regulation
e1cd165e3c2c.sentence: Empirical data suggests that CAC regulations, especially government subsidies in agriculture, often fuel environmental damage, deforestation and overfishing in particular.

48eb60c28f83.title: Tax incentive
48eb60c28f83.sentence: A tax incentive is an aspect of a government's taxation policy designed to incentivize or encourage a particular economic activity by reducing tax payments.

8040c70f86be.title: Tax incentive
8040c70f86be.sentence: Individual tax incentives are a prominent form of incentive and include deductions, exemptions, and credits.

84f6b2f2611a.title: Tax incentive
84f6b2f2611a.sentence: Specific examples include the mortgage interest deduction, individual retirement account, and hybrid tax credit.

af335c7a3c59.title: Tax incentive
af335c7a3c59.sentence: Tax incentives that target individual companies are generally seen as inefficient, economically costly, and distortionary, as well as having regressive economic effects.

5f2f21c8e17f.title: Tax incentive
5f2f21c8e17f.sentence: According to a 2020 study, tax competition "primarily reduces taxes for mobile firms and is unlikely to substantially affect the efficiency of business location." A 2020 NBER paper found some evidence that state and local business tax incentives in the United States led to employment gains but no evidence that the incentives increased broader economic growth at the state and local level.

c0be2459ff3c.title: Tax incentive
c0be2459ff3c.sentence: Tax incentives can cause negative effects on a government's financial condition, among other negative effects, if they are not properly designed and implemented.

1599e69c2825.title: Conservation finance
1599e69c2825.sentence: Conservation projects have traditionally relied on philanthropic donations and foundation grants, alongside government funding such as tax incentives, ballot measures, bonds, and agency appropriations.

250ae39ae2f8.title: Feed-in tariff
250ae39ae2f8.sentence: A feed-in tariff (FIT, FiT, standard offer contract, advanced renewable tariff, or renewable energy payments) is a policy mechanism designed to accelerate investment in renewable energy technologies by offering long-term contracts to renewable energy producers.

d0fb9b3425f8.title: Feed-in tariff
d0fb9b3425f8.sentence: This means promising renewable energy producers an above-market price and providing price certainty and long-term contracts that help finance renewable energy investments.

b6f68339a2aa.title: Feed-in tariff
b6f68339a2aa.sentence: FITs typically include three key provisions:

1ec10665b2f6.title: Feed-in tariff
1ec10665b2f6.sentence: FITs typically offer a guaranteed purchase agreement for long periods (15–25 years) and give incentives to producers to maximize output and efficiency.

8bf5167a67e6.title: Feed-in tariff
8bf5167a67e6.sentence: FITs often include a "digression": a gradual decrease of the price or tariff in order to follow and encourage technological cost reductions.

fa5907ea66c5.title: Feed-in tariff
fa5907ea66c5.sentence: Typically, FITs award different prices to different sources of renewable energy in order to encourage the development of one technology over another.

f422174da96e.title: Feed-in tariff
f422174da96e.sentence: For example, technologies such as wind power and solar PV are awarded a higher price per kWh than tidal power.

e57dc1832d01.title: Feed-in tariff
e57dc1832d01.sentence: In 2008, a detailed analysis by the European Commission concluded that "well-adapted feed-in tariff regimes are generally the most efficient and effective support schemes for promoting renewable electricity." This conclusion was supported by other analyses, including by the International Energy Agency, the European Federation for Renewable Energy, and by the Deutsche Bank.

cde744c83068.title: Feed-in tariff
cde744c83068.sentence: Increases in electricity rates occurred when the funding for the feed-in tariff scheme is provided by ratepayers via a surcharge in their electricity bills.

1636a282e435.title: Feed-in tariff
1636a282e435.sentence: In Germany, this approach to funding the feed-in tariff added 6.88 cents/kWh to the electricity rate for residential consumers in 2017.

1aac52488c88.title: Feed-in tariff
1aac52488c88.sentence: However, renewable energy can reduce spot market prices via the merit order effect, the practice of using higher-cost fossil fuel facilities only when demand exceeds the capacity of lower-cost facilities.

a509a2a7044e.title: Feed-in tariff
a509a2a7044e.sentence: This has led to electricity price reductions in Spain, Denmark, and Germany.

02873f15e7cb.title: Feed-in tariff
02873f15e7cb.sentence: As of 2019, over 50 countries had enacted FIT policies.

43bc6689c959.title: Feed-in tariff
43bc6689c959.sentence: The first form of feed-in tariff (under another name ) was implemented in the US in 1978 under President Jimmy Carter, who signed the National Energy Act (NEA).

e96eb56c0d9f.title: Feed-in tariff
e96eb56c0d9f.sentence: In 1990, Germany adopted its "Stromeinspeisungsgesetz" (StrEG), or "Law on Feeding Electricity into the Grid".

ae60843c790e.title: Feed-in tariff
ae60843c790e.section: History > Germany's Renewable Energy Sources Act
ae60843c790e.sentence: Germany's feed-in law underwent a major restructuring in 2000 to become the Renewable Energy Sources Act (2000) (German: Erneuerbare-Energien-Gesetz or EEG).

f9e1436dc325.title: Pollutant release and transfer register
f9e1436dc325.sentence: A pollutant release and transfer register (PRTR) is a system for collecting and disseminating information about environmental releases and transfers of hazardous substances from industrial and other facilities.

9fe75abe5d07.title: Pollutant release and transfer register
9fe75abe5d07.sentence: PRTRs were established in several countries after the 1984 Bhopal Disaster and the 1992 United Nations Conference on Environment and Development in Rio de Janeiro, which affirmed communities' and workers' right to know about toxic chemicals and other substances of concern.

f422cdb53318.title: Pollutant release and transfer register
f422cdb53318.sentence: Companies and civilians living near to the facilities generally have quite different levels of understanding and information on the processes and the environmental impact.

44c14607d009.title: Pollutant release and transfer register
44c14607d009.sentence: In a democratic context however a level playing field for all actors involved in permitting decisions is paramount to acceptance of the decisions.

080df9f1ee26.title: Pollutant release and transfer register
080df9f1ee26.sentence: Against this background, a protocol to the Aarhus Convention requires the parties to this convention to set up PRTRs as a tool to provide the general public this type of information.

91e437ba01c4.title: Aarhus Convention
91e437ba01c4.sentence: The Kyiv Protocol is the first legally binding international instrument on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers (PRTRs).

b1074dbcc470.title: Pollutant release and transfer register
b1074dbcc470.sentence: PRTR data collection methods for individual facility emissions typically utilize questionnaires sent to individual facilities or firms.

6aecae87a889.title: Pollutant release and transfer register
6aecae87a889.sentence: Despite the validation by competent authorities, the data remain essentially the facilities' estimates and data quality control essentially depends on data users asking questions.

cd79b40ff68d.title: Aarhus Convention
cd79b40ff68d.sentence: The Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers to the Aarhus Convention was adopted at an extraordinary meeting of the Parties on 21 May 2003, in Kyiv, Ukraine.

9e3d9611aa4a.title: Environmental certification
9e3d9611aa4a.sentence: Environmental certification is a form of environmental regulation and development where a company can voluntarily choose to comply with predefined processes or objectives set forth by the certification service.

1bed853f1c90.title: Environmental certification
1bed853f1c90.sentence: Most certification services have a logo (commonly known as an ecolabel) which can be applied to products certified under their standards.

36c42a343fa9.title: Environmental certification
36c42a343fa9.sentence: This is seen as a form of corporate social responsibility allowing companies to address their obligation to minimise the harmful impacts to the environment by voluntarily following a set of externally set and measured objectives.

eb76faf132d9.title: Environmental certification
eb76faf132d9.sentence: The primary motivations for many companies who choose to implement environmental certification schemes are, to provide an ethical product for the consumers, increase sustainable development, improve the image of the company, gain a better relationship with stakeholders and to make a higher profit.

ca0275803fd6.title: Environmental certification
ca0275803fd6.sentence: This also means that if environmental marketing strategies such as environmental certification are to work there must be consumers willing to purchase the resulting green products.

3d201b50a945.title: Environmental certification
3d201b50a945.sentence: As a result of the ethical production, consumers may be willing to pay an additional price as a way of promoting and sustaining ethical production.

f9150d3d4d71.title: Greenwashing
f9150d3d4d71.sentence: Companies may pursue environmental certification to avoid greenwashing through independent verification of their green claims.

edf67f4e0aab.title: ISO 14000 family
edf67f4e0aab.sentence: The ISO 14000 family is a set of international standards for environment management systems.

d46c148f5522.title: ISO 14000 family
d46c148f5522.sentence: It was developed in March 1996 by International Organization for Standardization.

e6aef8c45be5.title: ISO 14000 family
e6aef8c45be5.sentence: The goal of these standards is to help organizations (a) minimize how their operations (processes, etc.) negatively affect the environment (i.e. cause adverse changes to air, water, or land); (b) comply with applicable laws, regulations, and other environmentally oriented requirements; and (c) continually improve in the above.

5b6e41aeb80a.title: ISO 14000 family
5b6e41aeb80a.sentence: ISO 14000 is similar to ISO 9000 quality management in that both pertain to the process of how a service/product is rendered, rather than to the service/product itself.

f8ea477fda45.title: ISO 14000 family
f8ea477fda45.sentence: The ISO 14000 family includes most notably the ISO 14001 standard, which represents the core set of standards used by organizations for designing and implementing an effective environmental management system (EMS).

6b2290f53647.title: ISO 14000 family
6b2290f53647.sentence: It does not state requirements for environmental performance but maps out a framework that a company or organization can follow to set up an effective EMS.

822c809ef2b3.title: ISO 14000 family
822c809ef2b3.sentence: The ISO 14000 series is based on a voluntary approach to environmental regulation.

49cbb701dba9.title: ISO 14000 family
49cbb701dba9.sentence: As with ISO 9001, certification is performed by third-party organizations rather than being awarded by ISO directly.

664da2d0b714.title: ISO 14000 family
664da2d0b714.sentence: As of 2017, more than 300,000 certifications to ISO 14001 can be found in 171 countries.

7badc0835fa7.title: ISO 14000 family
7badc0835fa7.sentence: By minimizing the risk of regulatory and environmental liability fines and improving an organization's efficiency, benefits can include a reduction in waste, consumption of resources, and operating costs.

c120eedacedc.title: ISO 14000 family
c120eedacedc.sentence: This can provide them with a competitive advantage against companies that do not adopt the standard (Potoki & Prakash, 2005).

8c89b2da2ce2.title: ISO 14000 family
8c89b2da2ce2.sentence: In March 1992, BSI published the world's first environmental management systems standard, BS 7750, as part of a response to growing concerns about the environment.

71c8dfde1d62.title: ISO 14000 family
71c8dfde1d62.sentence: BS 7750 supplied the template for the development of the ISO 14000 series in March 1996, by ISO.

8a11384638e3.title: Certified wood
8a11384638e3.sentence: Certified wood and paper products come from responsibly managed forests – as defined by a particular standard.

60f2b4dcd391.title: Certified wood
60f2b4dcd391.sentence: Forest certification is a voluntary process.

06a0e7e7d6c8.title: Certified wood
06a0e7e7d6c8.sentence: With third-party forest certification, an independent standards setting organization (SSO) develops standards for good forest management, and independent auditing companies issue certificates to forest operations that comply with those standards.

28ba3528ed6b.title: Certified wood
28ba3528ed6b.sentence: - Protection of biodiversity, species at risk and wildlife habitat; sustainable harvest levels; protection of water quality; and prompt regeneration (e.g., replanting and reforestation).

6f0e9a979b5f.title: Certified wood
6f0e9a979b5f.sentence: Third-party forest certification was pioneered in the early 1990s by the FSC, a collaboration between environmental NGOs, forest product companies and social interests.

773ea5a1e0b7.title: Certified wood
773ea5a1e0b7.sentence: Without a single international standard for forestry management certification, there are a proliferation of private standards, with more than 50 scheme owners offering certification programs worldwide addressing the many types of forests and tenures around the world.

d18c7210cd33.title: Certified wood
d18c7210cd33.sentence: The two largest international forest certification programs are the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) and the Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification (PEFC).

03a2dbda844e.title: Certified wood
03a2dbda844e.sentence: The PEFC is the largest certification framework in terms of forest area, with approximately two-thirds of the total certified area.

9f618cdf5df9.title: Certified wood
9f618cdf5df9.sentence: About 10% of the world's forest under at least one certification program.

bb46dedd18ee.title: Certified wood
bb46dedd18ee.sentence: Some commentators, including Jared Diamond, have suggested that many competing private standards were set up by logging companies specifically aiming to confuse consumers with less rigorously enforced but similarly named competing standards.

6dc8b33284b8.title: Certified wood
6dc8b33284b8.sentence: - Paper, publishing, printing and packaging – commitments to increase the use of responsible paper sources by large publishers such as Time Inc. has probably been the most significant factor driving growth in forest and chain-of-custody certification.

75a1bd7f3f2c.title: Certified wood
75a1bd7f3f2c.sentence: - Green public procurement – governments such as the UK and the Netherlands have adopted green timber procurement policies, including recognition of FSC and PEFC endorsed programs.

93f552df0b8b.title: Certified wood
93f552df0b8b.sentence: - Green building – standards for green building incentivize and reward the use of certified wood products.

290c4960032b.title: Certified wood
290c4960032b.sentence: - Illegal logging – new legislation designed to minimize the risk of illegal wood entering supply chains such as the amended Lacey Act in the United States has created a strong incentive to demand independently certified wood that can address illegal logging concerns.

a882592ce2f3.title: Subsidy
a882592ce2f3.sentence: Fishing subsidies include "direct assistant to fishers; loan support programs; tax preferences and insurance support; capital and infrastructure programs; marketing and price support programs; and fisheries management, research, and conservation programs." They promote the expansion of fishing fleets, the supply of larger and longer nets, larger yields and indiscriminate catch, as well as mitigating risks which encourages further investment into large-scale operations to the disfavour of the already struggling small-scale industry.

d8624272f655.title: Subsidy
d8624272f655.sentence: Today, much of the world's major fisheries are overexploited; in 2002, the WWF estimate this at approximately 75%.

804896fe54a3.title: Subsidy
804896fe54a3.sentence: Collectively, these result in the continued overcapitalization and overfishing of marine fisheries.

bba24b9c5030.title: Subsidy
bba24b9c5030.sentence: The first important classification of subsidies are direct and indirect subsidies.

13aa61c98f02.title: Subsidy
13aa61c98f02.sentence: Another important classification of subsidies are producer/production subsidies and consumer/consumption subsidies.

f9fe5c5afd00.title: Subsidy
f9fe5c5afd00.sentence: These various subsidies can be divided into broad and narrow.

078bac5c8d48.title: Subsidy
078bac5c8d48.sentence: Subsidies are categorised as direct when it involves actual cash outlays targeted towards a specified individual or household.

252019bca2ea.title: Subsidy
252019bca2ea.sentence: Popular examples includes cash grants and interest-free loans.

004dda0a790f.title: Subsidy
004dda0a790f.sentence: Subsidies come in various forms including: direct (cash grants, interest-free loans) and indirect (tax breaks, insurance, low-interest loans, accelerated depreciation, rent rebates).

481a90a2491c.title: Subsidy
481a90a2491c.sentence: A production subsidy encourages suppliers to increase the output of a particular product by partially offsetting the production costs or losses.

3026fa90d741.title: Subsidy
3026fa90d741.sentence: Consumption subsidies benefit consumers typically through a reduction in the market price of goods and services.

d99d80eec5c7.title: Subsidy
d99d80eec5c7.sentence: This type of subsidies are most common in developing countries where governments subsidise such things as food, water, electricity and education on the basis that no matter how impoverished, all should be allowed those most basic requirements.

d28b95065be5.title: Subsidy
d28b95065be5.sentence: Conversely broad subsidies include both monetary and non-monetary subsidies and is often difficult to identify.

0e82c65e61f4.title: Subsidy
0e82c65e61f4.sentence: Environmental externalities are the most common type of broad subsidy.

f7761feeb294.title: Eco-Management and Audit Scheme
f7761feeb294.sentence: Eco-Management and Audit Scheme or Environmental Management and Audit Scheme (EMAS) is an international standard for environmental management systems.

9bd749894941.title: Eco-Management and Audit Scheme
9bd749894941.sentence: It was developed in March 1993 by European Commission.

e267e8654f3a.title: Eco-Management and Audit Scheme
e267e8654f3a.sentence: The goal of the standard is to enable organizations to assess, manage and continuously improve their environmental performance.

672f8cb098e4.title: Environmental certification
672f8cb098e4.sentence: The Eco-Management and Audit Scheme (EMAS) is the EU's voluntary environmental resources management instrument.

9e76b60122b7.title: Eco-Management and Audit Scheme
9e76b60122b7.sentence: The scheme is globally applicable and open to all types of private and public organizations.

a4fa31a24983.title: Eco-Management and Audit Scheme
a4fa31a24983.sentence: In order to register with EMAS an organisation must comply with the following implementation steps (Article 4 of the EMAS Regulation):

c876f2ff9341.title: Eco-Management and Audit Scheme
c876f2ff9341.sentence: - Environmental review: initial comprehensive analysis of the organization's activities, products and services and their environmental impact; cataloging applicable environmental law, etc.

90cf900901fe.title: Eco-Management and Audit Scheme
90cf900901fe.sentence: - Environmental statement: comprehensive, regular reports to the public on the organisation's structure and activities; environmental policy and management system; environmental aspects and impacts; environmental programme, objectives and targets; environmental performance and compliance with applicable environmental law etc.

2251fa351a86.title: Environmental certification
2251fa351a86.sentence: Only independent environmental verifiers that are accredited/licensed and supervised by government authorities (Accreditation or Licensing Bodies) are authorised to validate EMAS environmental statements.

de1b5d9dc4c4.title: Eco-Management and Audit Scheme
de1b5d9dc4c4.section: Implementation > Key performance indicators > An indicator set according to EMAS
de1b5d9dc4c4.sentence: Entered into force in January 2010, EMAS III requires registered organisations to report on key performance indicators in six key environmental areas.

797fe7fb6815.title: Green industrial policy
797fe7fb6815.sentence: Green industrial policy (GIP) is strategic government policy that attempts to accelerate the development and growth of green industries to transition towards a low-carbon economy.

ca96b89a0de4.title: Green industrial policy
ca96b89a0de4.sentence: Green industrial policy seeks to address market failures and protect the environment.

b94fd755f706.title: Green industrial policy
b94fd755f706.sentence: Green industrial policy is necessary because green industries such as renewable energy and low-carbon public transportation infrastructure face high costs and many risks in terms of the market economy.

3fa5a551dd51.title: Green industrial policy
3fa5a551dd51.sentence: Therefore, they need support from the public sector in the form of industrial policy until they become commercially viable.

8e9a91b0aa33.title: Green industrial policy
8e9a91b0aa33.sentence: Subsidies for a targeted sector are the most common form of GIP.

f52e9d40a53b.title: Green industrial policy
f52e9d40a53b.sentence: Both use similar policy approaches, like research and development subsidies and tax credits.

23bdeffcf2d4.title: Green industrial policy
23bdeffcf2d4.sentence: New, sustainable technologies cannot immediately compete on the market with existing, unsustainable technologies due to path dependency.

324622849f68.title: Green industrial policy
324622849f68.sentence: Thus, governments must create technological niches and use forms of GIP to subsidize and nurture technological niches to ensure that green innovations develop.

fe9a6af6a3bc.title: Green industrial policy
fe9a6af6a3bc.sentence: GIP led to a booming German renewable energy industry that employs over 371,000 people, which is double the number of jobs that were available in 2004.

3a5ab88af9f3.title: Green industrial policy
3a5ab88af9f3.sentence: Without government intervention in the economy, it is unlikely that the current market will transition towards a low-carbon economy.

260c80f7ee0c.title: Inflation Reduction Act
260c80f7ee0c.sentence: The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (IRA), Pub.

12ad9b5daef3.section: Projected impacts > Energy and climate change > Climate action's fiscal impact
12ad9b5daef3.sentence: The Inflation Reduction Act is the largest piece of federal legislation ever to address climate change.
