c073ac45c1fa.sentence: According to the CBO and JCT, it will invest $783 billion in provisions relating to energy security and climate change.

b105671ed604.title: Inflation Reduction Act

b105671ed604.sentence: Measures include $9 billion in home energy rebate programs that focus on improving access to energy efficient technologies, and 10 years of consumer tax credits for the use of heat pumps, rooftop solar, and high-efficiency electric heating, ventilation, air conditioning and water heating.

e5572e1570a3.title: Inflation Reduction Act

e5572e1570a3.sentence: One $27 billion competitive grant program is a green bank called the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund, intended to capitalize smaller regional green banks.

1ec4cce5f9fd.title: Inflation Reduction Act
1ec4cce5f9fd.sentence: The Rhodium Group's expectations for GHG emissions reductions by the year 2030, relative to the level of 2005, moved from 17–30% to 29–42%, and to a 32–51% decline by the year 2035.

4807903b6692.title: Inflation Reduction Act
4807903b6692.sentence: On January 20–23, 2025, the Trump administration issued executive direction leading federal agencies to pause disbursements and payments of funds appropriated under the IRA and the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

de2bc44c0aae.sentence: The Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) is a publicly available database containing information on toxic chemical releases and other waste management activities in the United States.

a9cdd9c9dd4d.title: Precautionary principle
a9cdd9c9dd4d.sentence: Strong precaution holds that regulation is required whenever there is a possible risk to health, safety, or the environment, even if the supporting evidence is speculative and even if the economic costs of regulation are high.

4aefb8876669.title: Precautionary principle
4aefb8876669.sentence: Weak precaution holds that lack of scientific evidence does not preclude action if damage would otherwise be serious and irreversible.

c5a082e9315c.title: Precautionary principle
c5a082e9315c.sentence: Strong precaution can also be termed as a "no-regrets" principle, where costs are not considered in preventative action.

a19937f5a514.title: Precautionary principle
a19937f5a514.sentence: In 1982, the United Nations World Charter for Nature gave the first international recognition to the strong version of the principle, suggesting that when "potential adverse effects are not fully understood, the activities should not proceed".

43004ef89552.title: Precautionary principle
43004ef89552.sentence: Weak formulations do not preclude weighing benefits against the costs.

702702da463b.title: Precautionary principle
702702da463b.sentence: Factors other than scientific uncertainty, including economic considerations, may provide legitimate grounds for postponing action.

7cb2833db839.title: Precautionary principle

a7dbd0dc3127.title: Precautionary principle

3ec640c43346.title: Precautionary principle
3ec640c43346.sentence: This maintains that, of the two available interpretations of the principle, neither are plausible: weak formulations (which hold that precaution in the face of uncertain harms is permissible) are trivial, while strong formulations (which hold that precaution in the face of uncertain harms is required) are incoherent.

ff1fb86c6f25.title: Precautionary principle

636ed92892a2.sentence: Prior to implementing ISO 14001, an initial review or gap analysis of the organization's processes and products is recommended, to assist in identifying all elements of the current operation, and if possible, future operations, that may interact with the environment, termed "environmental aspects".

3a797829586b.title: ISO 14000 family

3a797829586b.sentence: During the "check" stage, performance is monitored and periodically measured to ensure that the organization's environmental targets and objectives are being met.

a1e3fd28cbcd.sentence: In addition, internal audits are conducted at planned intervals to ascertain whether the EMS meets the user's expectations and whether the processes and procedures are being adequately maintained and monitored.

40702222ab9f.title: ISO 14000 family

40702222ab9f.sentence: After the checking stage, a management review is conducted to ensure that the objectives of the EMS are being met, the extent to which they are being met, and that communications are being appropriately managed.

3eaab2057d59.title: ISO 14000 family

64b9c6d623a6.title: Carbon emission label

e853b7d4f137.title: Carbon emission label

805823f2aefe.sentence: Sustainable seafood advisory lists and certification programs are public policies designed to support transparent seafood supply chains and to help consumers make informed purchasing decisions that reflect resource stewardship and sustainable seafood considerations.

beebeb2549ef.title: Environmental certification
beebeb2549ef.sentence: There are various negative aspects associated with environmental certification one of which is the perception from markets that it is a reactive rather than a proactive investment, meaning that the certification as a standard is initiated as a response to institutional pressure rather than a self-regulation standard showing a desire to move towards a more environmentally sound system.

150095fa9813.title: Environmental certification
150095fa9813.sentence: The implementation of environmental certification is expensive, the burden of which is usually felt by the supplier rather than the retailer who must pay for the certification fees and the increased cost of production.

833940401356.title: Environmental certification

fe68d54e2fc9.title: Environmental certification

af0e3f95c6aa.title: Environmental certification
af0e3f95c6aa.sentence: In many cases the profit a supplier can expect to gain for their product does not compensate for the implementation cost.

a0b020ea3668.title: Environmental certification

0188d9552ec9.title: Environmental certification

3ad5492ad7fa.title: Green industrial policy
3ad5492ad7fa.sentence: Local content requirements (LCRs) mean that in the production process, producers must obtain a certain minimum percentage of goods, labour, or services from local sources.

b388ea02c43b.title: Green industrial policy
b388ea02c43b.sentence: Ontario, Canada passed legislation with local content requirements in 2009 called the Green Energy and Green Economy Act.

720794aed000.title: Green industrial policy
720794aed000.sentence: The Act required Ontario-made content in renewable electricity generators, such as wind and solar farms, for the generators to be eligible for government subsidies.

021991d6ee61.title: Green industrial policy
021991d6ee61.sentence: It created many jobs, lowered GHG emissions, and vastly expanded the renewable energy industry in Ontario.

d9d6fbec3774.title: Green industrial policy
d9d6fbec3774.sentence: Arguments against GIP state that governments cannot make practical choices about which firms or industries to support, and subsequently, they will make mistakes and waste valuable resources.

c1e2457138ea.title: Green industrial policy
c1e2457138ea.sentence: Additionally, GIP raises concerns about rent-seeking and regulatory capture.

23ca0d25198c.title: Green industrial policy
23ca0d25198c.sentence: Subsidies are particularly prone to rent-seeking as special interests may lobby intensely to maintain subsidies, even when they are no longer needed, while taxpayers who may want to abolish subsidies have fewer resources for lobbying.

3cbe90d0cc93.title: Green industrial policy
3cbe90d0cc93.sentence: Government intervention in markets can create rent-seeking behaviour - or the manipulation of policy to increase profits - so GIP may become driven by political concerns rather than economic ones.

c23ad68fd505.title: Green industrial policy
c23ad68fd505.sentence: While proponents of GIP discuss several ways to mitigate risks, some instances of targeting the wrong firms or industries are inevitable because some degree of failure is inherent in GIP effort.

4e7609b448c6.title: Green industrial policy

6886feb282be.title: Environmental policy
6886feb282be.sentence: Environmental policy is the pledge by governments or organizations to adopt laws, regulations, and other mechanisms concerning environmental issues.

ff4dd7954a23.title: Environmental policy
ff4dd7954a23.sentence: These typically involve air and water pollution, waste management, ecosystem management, biodiversity conservation, the management of natural resources, and safeguarding wildlife and endangered species.

f8235e1caee9.title: Environmental policy
f8235e1caee9.sentence: This policy can be deliberately taken to influence human activities and thereby prevent undesirable effects on the biophysical environment and natural resources, as well as to make sure that changes in the environment do not have unacceptable effects on humans.

712dbc91332f.title: Environmental policy
712dbc91332f.sentence: In 1863, in the United Kingdom, health problems arising from the release of harmful chemicals led to the adoption of the Alkali Act and the creation of the Alkali Inspectorate.

1572b0721f80.title: Environmental policy
1572b0721f80.sentence: The rationale for governmental involvement in the environment is often attributed to market failure in the form of forces beyond the control of one person, including the free rider problem and the tragedy of the commons.

614a5d95fdfd.title: Environmental policy
614a5d95fdfd.sentence: Ultimately, the environmental effectiveness of policies is measured by the extent to which they reduce or resolve environmental problems (ecological destruction and degradation, resource degradation and depletion, and adverse effects on humans by environmental modification, including by urban development and pollution).

a878200caff3.title: Environmental policy
a878200caff3.sentence: Whether environmental policies have addressed environmental problems more or less effectively remains a topic of debate.

d11ea844a4dc.title: Environmental policy
d11ea844a4dc.sentence: Environmental degradation tends to motivate action more than the threat of global warming does, since air and water pollution cause immediate health problems, and because pollutants can damage natural resources, hampering economic potential.

6634ac90a774.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
6634ac90a774.sentence: In environmental law and policy, market-based instruments (MBIs) are policy instruments that use markets, price, and other economic variables to provide incentives for polluters to reduce or eliminate negative environmental externalities.

54c128b152b2.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
54c128b152b2.sentence: MBIs seek to address the market failure of externalities (such as pollution) by incorporating the external cost of production or consumption activities through taxes or charges on processes or products, or by creating property rights and facilitating the establishment of a proxy market for the use of environmental services.

43c06ebd3ed1.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
43c06ebd3ed1.sentence: Market-based instruments are also referred to as economic instruments, price-based instruments, new environmental policy instruments (NEPIs) or new instruments of environmental policy.

5bb523300b36.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
5bb523300b36.sentence: Examples include environmentally related taxes, charges and subsidies, emissions trading and other tradeable permit systems, deposit-refund systems, environmental labeling laws, licenses, and economic property rights.

586d7dd33c83.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
586d7dd33c83.sentence: For instance, the European Union Emission Trading Scheme is an example of a market-based instrument to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

761abfe054eb.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
761abfe054eb.sentence: However, implementing an MBI also commonly requires some form of regulation.

85774ed87802.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
85774ed87802.sentence: For example, although the use of new environmental policy instruments only grew significantly in Britain in the 1990s, David Lloyd George may have introduced the first market-based instrument of environmental policy in the UK when a Fuel tax was levied in 1909-1910 during his ministry.

6d4c3aaea513.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
6d4c3aaea513.sentence: For a variety of reasons, environmental advocates initially opposed the use of market-based instruments except under very constrained conditions.

aea2603383a6.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
aea2603383a6.sentence: However, after the successful use of freely traded credits in the lead phasedown in the U.S. environmental advocates recognized that trading markets have benefits for the environment as well.

d22d44fa8da1.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
d22d44fa8da1.sentence: Thereafter, beginning with the proposal of the acid rain allowance market, environmental advocates have supported the use of trading in a variety of contexts.

15a1f6c23d1c.title: Public choice
15a1f6c23d1c.sentence: Public choice, or public choice theory, is a formal theory of political and social science that applies economic methods—namely, rational choice theory, game theory, decision theory, and social choice theory—to study political agents (e.g. officials, bureaucrats, and voters) and their interactions.

692dd59d6e36.title: Public choice
692dd59d6e36.sentence: Researchers emphasise the applicability of markets in the political system, the self-interested nature of agents, and the nature of decisions as a combination of individual choices rather than as an aggregate whole.

9b924f068cd2.title: Public choice
9b924f068cd2.sentence: Public choice theory is rooted in skepticism of treating government as though it attempts "to maximize some kind sort of welfare function for society", and as distinct from characterizations of self-interested economic agents, such as those in business.

4a845cdf3edc.title: Public choice
4a845cdf3edc.sentence: By contrast, public choice theory models government as made up of officials who, besides pursuing the public interest, may act to benefit themselves, for example in the budget-maximizing model of bureaucracy, possibly at the cost of efficiency.

f3d7f7415249.title: Public choice
f3d7f7415249.sentence: James Buchanan has suggested that public choice theory be interpreted as "politics without romance", a critical approach to a pervasive earlier notion of idealized politics set against market failure.

9c7c61f62752.title: Public choice
9c7c61f62752.sentence: Modern public-choice theory, and especially election theory, has been dated to the work of Duncan Black, sometimes called "the founding father of public choice".

b250e0d27ce4.title: Public choice
b250e0d27ce4.sentence: In a series of papers from 1948, which culminated in The Theory of Committees and Elections (1958), Black outlined a program of unification toward a more general "Theory of Economic and Political Choices" based on common formal methods, developed underlying concepts of what became median voter theory, and rediscovered earlier work on voting theory.

4a1b46c1684f.title: Public choice
4a1b46c1684f.sentence: Several notable public choice scholars have been awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics, including Kenneth Arrow (1972), James M. Buchanan (1986), George Stigler (1982), Gary Becker (1992), Amartya Sen (1998), Vernon Smith (2002), and Elinor Ostrom (2009).

1592a7c80ead.title: Public choice
1592a7c80ead.section: Theory and methods > Validity and efficacy
1592a7c80ead.sentence: Steven Pressman offers a critique of the public choice approach, arguing that public choice fails to explain political behavior in a number of central areas, including politicians’ behavior and voting behavior.

dd0e36bb5548.title: Public choice
dd0e36bb5548.section: Theory and methods > Validity and efficacy
dd0e36bb5548.sentence: These include why politicians vote against their constituents' interests, why they advocate for higher taxation, fewer benefits, and smaller government, and why wealthy people seek office.

515f0d35ea77.title: Environmental policy
515f0d35ea77.sentence: In practice, governments have adopted a wide range of approaches to the development and implementation of environmental policies.

fdfa022e61ad.title: Environmental policy
fdfa022e61ad.sentence: Regulation has been a traditional and predominant approach to policymaking in many policy areas and countries.

12770b19f087.title: Environmental policy
12770b19f087.sentence: Economic instruments involve the imposition or use of economic incentives, including (environmental) taxes, tax exemptions, fees, subsidies, and the creation of markets and rights for trading in substances, pollutants, resources, or activities, such as for SO2, CO2 (carbon or greenhouse gas emissions), water, and tradeable fisheries quota.

7cd8ce361a8b.title: Environmental policy
7cd8ce361a8b.sentence: Normative ("hortatory") instruments ("sermons") rely on persuasion and information.

c538e854fa99.title: Environmental policy
c538e854fa99.sentence: It relies foremost on adopting rules (often backed up by legislation), to prohibit, impose or circumscribe human behaviour and practices.

dbf17af289df.title: Environmental policy
dbf17af289df.sentence: In the environmental policy area, this includes, for instance, the imposition of limits or standards for air and water pollution, car emissions, the regulation or banning of the use of hazardous substances, the phasing out of ozone-depleting substances, waste disposal, and laws to protect endangered species and natural areas.

d7ea9634fc74.title: Environmental policy
d7ea9634fc74.sentence: Regulation is often derogatorily referred to by detractors as a top-down, "command and control" approach as it leaves target groups with little if any control over the way(s) environmental activities or goals must be pursued.

e5a8e96ea2f7.title: Environmental policy
e5a8e96ea2f7.sentence: They are based on the assumption that behaviour and practices are foremost driven by rationality, self-interest and economic considerations and that these motivations can be harnessed for environmental purposes.

6fff6106618c.title: Environmental policy
6fff6106618c.sentence: Decision-making studies cast doubt on these premises.

47075ffe7783.title: Environmental policy
47075ffe7783.sentence: There has been much debate about the relative merits of the various kinds of policy instruments.

9dcae3e0b822.title: Environmental policy
9dcae3e0b822.sentence: Market instruments are often held up and used as a more efficient and cost-effective, alternative to regulation.

02b0de1784f4.title: Environmental policy
02b0de1784f4.sentence: Yet, many analysts have pointed out that regulation, economic incentives, "market" instruments, and environmental taxation and subsidies can achieve the same results.

7f6a81c68796.title: Environmental policy
7f6a81c68796.sentence: For instance, as Kemp and Pontoglio argue, policy instruments cannot be usefully ranked with regard to their effects on eco-innovation, "the often expressed view that market-based approaches such as pollution taxes and emission trading systems are better for promoting eco-innovation is not brought out by the case study literature or by survey analysis", and there is actually more evidence that regulations stimulate radical innovation more than market-based instruments.

4ac9d8894c87.title: Environmental policy
4ac9d8894c87.sentence: More generally, the performance of economic instruments in dealing with environmental problems has been a mixed bag, referred to by Hahn as "not very impressive", and has led Tietenberg to conclude that they are "no panacea".

00ffdc5bee07.title: Environmental policy
00ffdc5bee07.sentence: However, although regulation, taxation and market instruments can be equally (in-) effective, they may differ significantly in the allocation and distribution of (potential) costs and benefits, with the allocation of tradeable ("property") rights potentially generating significant profits to those who receive such rights.

7ca07095e997.title: Environmental policy
7ca07095e997.sentence: This has led analysts to point out that there are many other important aspects to the choice of policy instruments than their efficiency and cost-effectiveness, such as distributional, ethical and political aspects, and their appropriateness for addressing environmental problems.

ba6701ddf67a.title: Environmental policy
ba6701ddf67a.sentence: They are, therefore, generally much preferred by affected resource users and industries, which explains their popularity since the rise of neoliberalism.

4baf4fa554d9.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
4baf4fa554d9.sentence: A market-based tax approach determines a maximum cost for control measures.

d51ec2e9d3d3.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
d51ec2e9d3d3.sentence: A market-based transferable permit sets a maximum level of pollution (a 'cap'), but is likely to achieve that level at a lower cost than other means, and, importantly, may reduce below that level due to technological innovation.

d85a7d5791ae.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
d85a7d5791ae.sentence: There is no cap; the quantity of pollution reduced depends on the chosen tax rate.

6c4e758aabd6.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
6c4e758aabd6.sentence: A tax approach is more flexible than permits, as the tax rate can be adjusted until it creates the most effective incentive.

2f81124877a1.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
2f81124877a1.sentence: Taxes also have lower compliance costs than permits.

06aaf4d9874a.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
06aaf4d9874a.sentence: However, taxes are less effective at achieving reductions in target quantities than permits.

a266835dd3dc.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
a266835dd3dc.sentence: There can also be a conflict between objectives with a tax: less pollution means less revenue.

9d9f2b61a286.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
9d9f2b61a286.sentence: Another important aspect of transferable permits is whether they are auctioned or allocated via grandfathering.

b7f79076804d.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
b7f79076804d.sentence: An argument against permits is that formalising emission rights is effectively giving people a license to pollute, which is believed to be socially unacceptable.

0765160ba3f1.title: Induced innovation
0765160ba3f1.sentence: Induced innovation is a microeconomic hypothesis first proposed in 1932 by John Hicks in his work The Theory of Wages.

87a4952a02af.title: Induced innovation
87a4952a02af.sentence: He proposed that "a change in the relative prices of the factors of production is itself a spur to invention, and to invention of a particular kind—directed to economizing the use of a factor which has become relatively expensive."

3044d165870e.title: Induced innovation
3044d165870e.sentence: Considerable literature has been produced on this hypothesis, which is often presented in terms of the effects of wage increases as an encouragement to labor-saving innovation.

17b514b0a900.title: Induced innovation
17b514b0a900.sentence: The hypothesis has also been applied to viewing increases in energy costs as a motivation for a more rapid improvement in energy efficiency of goods than would normally occur.

4c6342c5bfec.title: Induced innovation
4c6342c5bfec.sentence: Global GDP and CO2 emissions were growing at a corresponding rate in the until the 1970s.

4a6b70a6ed84.title: Induced innovation
4a6b70a6ed84.sentence: It was then that oil prices have increased greatly causing people to reduce its consumption.

24139c398ffb.title: Induced innovation
24139c398ffb.sentence: Following the oil shock significant investments were made in alternative sources of energy, more efficient cars and heating systems to mitigate oil consumption.

b0e518258954.title: Induced innovation
b0e518258954.sentence: As a result, CO2 emissions started growing at a slower rate than GDP per capita.

08d4914d3e0a.title: Induced innovation
08d4914d3e0a.sentence: Although petrol prices then dropped in the 1980s, CO2 emissions have continued to grow more slowly than GDP.

f6a80459325b.title: Induced innovation
f6a80459325b.sentence: In other words, when demand for their products increases, farmers are lured by changes in relative prices to seek for technological alternatives that substitute the increasingly scarce factors of production.

79be28df142b.sentence: Innovation is assumed to be exogenous; As such, the model is a pre-ITC model (it does not yet include Induced Technological Change).

b3b66c64e81b.title: Environmental policy
b3b66c64e81b.sentence: How environmental policies are made, how effective they are, and how they can or should be improved, has become the subject of considerable research and debate.

e7578f3fe989.title: Environmental policy
e7578f3fe989.sentence: In the academic realm, these questions are commonly addressed under the label of environmental policy analysis.

be2662d8536c.title: Environmental policy
be2662d8536c.section: Policy analysis > The analycentric or rational approach
be2662d8536c.sentence: The analycentric approach to environmental policy analysis, which focuses on particular issues and uses mostly quantitative methods to identify "optimal" (cost-effective or efficient) solutions, has been the prevalent way to address environmental problems, both by governments and businesses.

808d20a1e106.title: Environmental policy
808d20a1e106.section: Policy analysis > The analycentric or rational approach
808d20a1e106.sentence: Technological innovation, more efficient management, and economic instruments such as cost-benefit analysis, environmental taxes, and tradeable permit schemes (market creation) have been among the preferred means in this approach.

8e89dd072fac.title: Environmental policy
8e89dd072fac.section: Policy analysis > The policy process approach
8e89dd072fac.sentence: The policy process approach emphasises the role and importance of politics and power in policy development.

539a680b0f23.title: Environmental policy
539a680b0f23.section: Policy analysis > The policy process approach
539a680b0f23.sentence: It commonly involves identifying a variable number of steps, including problem definition and agenda setting, the formulation and selection of policy options, implementation, and evaluation.

32ce96e4007d.title: Environmental policy
32ce96e4007d.sentence: Meta-policy research focuses on the ways policy development is influenced or shaped by contextual factors, including political institutions and systems, socio-cultural patterns, economic systems, knowledge frameworks, discourses, and the changes therein.

a327e3576271.title: Environmental policy
a327e3576271.sentence: In the environmental field, it is often called environmental policy integration.

30c3f6cd93ed.title: Environmental policy
30c3f6cd93ed.sentence: The main idea is that policies in one area (or domain) should consider their effects on other areas.

fa23682673ae.title: Environmental policy
fa23682673ae.sentence: The concept of policy integration has been discussed since the 1980s under various terms, such as policy mainstreaming, policy coordination, and holistic governance.

38c300731158.title: Implicit carbon prices
38c300731158.sentence: Implicit carbon prices arise from measures which impact on the marginal cost of emitting greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions without targeting GHG emissions or the carbon content of fuel directly.

80cf9959ab32.title: Implicit carbon prices
80cf9959ab32.sentence: In contrast to implicit carbon prices, explicit carbon prices are measures designed specifically to target GHG emissions or the carbon content of fuel.

0047f4f83ec1.title: Implicit carbon prices
0047f4f83ec1.sentence: Measures such as carbon taxes or emissions trading schemes put an explicit price on GHG emissions.

76fdf51122ab.title: Implicit carbon prices
76fdf51122ab.sentence: The sum of implicit and explicit carbon prices is referred to as the effective carbon price.

58312c80d9f9.title: Implicit carbon prices

6150d5ebb60b.title: Public choice

990359513a51.title: Public choice

1e639c13e9e5.title: Public choice

f3d1635af442.title: Public choice

bc3aafa2eb8a.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments
bc3aafa2eb8a.sentence: Command and control regulatory instruments include emissions standards, process/equipment specifications, limits on input/output/discharges, requirements to disclose information, and audits.

fa3fc5f52321.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments

1cfece9b4ae5.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments

657ab12d8529.title: Market-based environmental policy instruments

f5242b2d714d.title: Rent-seeking
f5242b2d714d.sentence: Rent-seeking is the act of growing one's existing wealth by manipulating public policy or economic conditions without creating new wealth.

7d5011dd50dd.title: Rent-seeking
7d5011dd50dd.sentence: They lead to reduced economic efficiency due to misallocation of resources, stifled competition, lower wealth creation, a loss of government revenue, increased income inequality, increased debt levels, the risk of increased corruption and cronyism, the decline in public trust in institutions, and potential socioeconomic and institutional decline.

ebf663886473.title: Rent-seeking
ebf663886473.sentence: The classic example of rent-seeking, according to Robert Shiller, is that of a property owner who installs a chain across a river that flows through their land and then hires a collector to charge passing boats a fee to lower the chain.

741b8b1660ac.title: Rent-seeking
741b8b1660ac.sentence: There is nothing productive about the chain or the collector, nor do passing boats get anything in return.

1786c55da77f.title: Rent-seeking
1786c55da77f.sentence: The owner has made no improvements to the river and is not adding value in any way, directly or indirectly, except for themselves.

92fc60245082.title: Rent-seeking
92fc60245082.sentence: Rent-seeking is distinguished in theory from profit-seeking, in which entities seek to extract value by engaging in mutually beneficial transactions.

698a6e796989.title: Rent-seeking
698a6e796989.sentence: Profit-seeking in this sense is the creation of wealth, while rent-seeking is "profiteering" by using social institutions, such as but not limited to the power of the state, to redistribute wealth among different groups without creating new wealth.

7391bce012b7.title: Rent-seeking
7391bce012b7.sentence: "Rent-seeking" is an attempt to obtain economic rent (i.e., the portion of income paid to a factor of production in excess of what is needed to keep it employed in its current use) by manipulating the social or political environment in which economic activities occur, rather than by creating new wealth.

3473bc6b1ca4.title: Rent-seeking

51d66876e672.title: Rent-seeking
51d66876e672.sentence: An example of rent-seeking in a modern economy is spending money on lobbying to obtain government subsidies or a share of wealth that has already been created, or to impose regulations on competitors in order to increase one's own market share.

1b556a96de9b.title: Rent-seeking

947a9995ad1c.title: Rent-seeking

0941e5aae864.sentence: In the social sciences, path dependence is the phenomenon of past events or decisions constraining or defining later events or decisions.

e97c42813b1d.title: Path dependence

fed97fd146b8.title: Path dependence

4a4964011dad.title: Path dependence

fcb300d89a9a.title: Path dependence

a6c7729bd485.title: Regulatory capture
a6c7729bd485.sentence: In politics, regulatory capture (also called agency capture) is a form of corruption of authority that occurs when a political entity, policymaker, or regulator is co-opted to serve the commercial, ideological, or political interests of a minor constituency, such as a particular geographic area, industry, profession, or ideological group.

3e02ae847b06.title: Regulatory capture
3e02ae847b06.sentence: When regulatory capture occurs, a special interest is prioritized over the general interests of the public, leading to a net loss for society.

8847ea941ab5.title: Regulatory capture
8847ea941ab5.sentence: For public choice theorists, regulatory capture occurs because groups or individuals with high-stakes interests in the outcome of policy or regulatory decisions can be expected to focus their resources and energies to gain the policy outcomes they prefer, while members of the public, each with only a tiny individual stake in the outcome, will ignore it altogether.

73cb58519b56.title: Regulatory capture
73cb58519b56.sentence: Regulatory capture has an economic basis: vested interests in an industry have the greatest financial stake in regulations affecting them, and so are more likely to try to influence the regulator than relatively dispersed individual consumers, each with little incentive.

b1f488887cee.title: Regulatory capture
b1f488887cee.sentence: The theory of regulatory capture is associated with Nobel laureate economist George Stigler, one of its major developers.

ec8512eab4c6.title: Regulatory capture
ec8512eab4c6.sentence: A captured regulator is often worse than no regulation, because it wields the authority of government.

9bbf58693f9c.title: Regulatory capture

3b74ee312e2b.title: Regulatory capture
3b74ee312e2b.sentence: There is substantial academic literature suggesting that smaller government units are easier for small, concentrated industries to capture than large ones.

d8588042c845.title: Regulatory capture
d8588042c845.sentence: For example, a group of states or provinces with a large timber industry might have their legislature and/or their delegation to the national legislature captured by lumber companies.

14870ecf767e.title: Regulatory capture

2b4db9ad1cde.title: Median voter theorem
2b4db9ad1cde.sentence: In political science and social choice, Black's median voter theorem says that if voters and candidates are distributed along a one-dimensional political spectrum, any Condorcet consistent voting method will elect the candidate preferred by the median voter.

caf1dd860bee.title: Median voter theorem
caf1dd860bee.section: Statement and proof of the theorem
caf1dd860bee.sentence: Voters rank candidates by proximity, i.e. the closest candidate is their first preference, the second-closest is their second preference, and so on.

d890cc790d68.title: Median voter theorem
d890cc790d68.section: Statement and proof of the theorem
d890cc790d68.sentence: Then, the median voter theorem says that the candidate closest to the median voter is a majority-preferred (or Condorcet) candidate.

4806943e35a2.title: Median voter theorem
4806943e35a2.section: Statement and proof of the theorem
4806943e35a2.sentence: In other words, this candidate is preferred to any one of their opponents by a majority of voters.

a2af9d27f593.title: Median voter theorem
a2af9d27f593.sentence: The theorem was first derived by Duncan Black in 1948, and independently by Kenneth Arrow.

7ae8365419c3.title: The Logic of Collective Action
7ae8365419c3.sentence: The Logic of Collective Action: Public Goods and the Theory of Groups is a book by Mancur Olson Jr. published in 1965.

e9a9bbfaf04e.title: The Logic of Collective Action
e9a9bbfaf04e.sentence: Its central argument is that concentrated minor interests will be overrepresented and diffuse majority interests trumped, due to a free-rider problem that is stronger when a group becomes larger.

e7da95fccb6d.title: The Logic of Collective Action
e7da95fccb6d.sentence: It argues instead that individuals in any group attempting collective action will have incentives to "free ride" on the efforts of others if the group is working to provide public goods.

144819eaa548.title: The Logic of Collective Action
144819eaa548.sentence: Without selective incentives to motivate active participation, collective action is unlikely to occur even when large groups of people with common interests exist.

20143d94a881.title: The Logic of Collective Action
20143d94a881.sentence: The book notes that large groups will face relatively high costs when attempting to organize for collective action while small groups will face relatively low costs, and individuals in large groups will gain marginally less per capita.

17b918f8ed06.title: The Logic of Collective Action
17b918f8ed06.sentence: Hence, in the absence of selective incentives, the incentive for group action diminishes as group size increases, so that large groups are less able to act in their common interest than small ones.

2fb07b315e9a.title: The Logic of Collective Action
2fb07b315e9a.sentence: The book concludes that, not only is collective action by large groups difficult to achieve even when they have interests in common, but situations could occur where the minority (bound together by concentrated selective incentives) can dominate the majority.

ec820aef8c31.title: The Logic of Collective Action

dc444322c36d.title: Bootleggers and Baptists

fda4821d976b.title: Environmental mitigation
fda4821d976b.sentence: Environmental mitigation refers to the process by which measures to avoid, minimise, or compensate for adverse impacts on the environment are applied.

e8edad30d79e.title: Environmental mitigation
e8edad30d79e.sentence: In the context of planning processes like Environmental Impact Assessments, this process is often guided by applying conceptual frameworks like the "mitigation hierarchy" or "mitigation sequence".

5667fa9e615b.title: Environmental mitigation
5667fa9e615b.sentence: This generally includes the steps avoid, reduce, restore, and offset.

060b2c85ea73.title: Environmental mitigation
060b2c85ea73.sentence: In practice, environmental mitigation measures might be implemented by establishing new habitat, restoring degraded habitat, and preserving or enhancing existing habitats to offset impacts that cannot be avoided or reduced.

a87b9371570c.title: Environmental mitigation
a87b9371570c.sentence: Climate change mitigation focuses specifically on actions to limit climate change by reducing net greenhouse gas emissions, while the scope of environmental mitigation is broader.

a747c50d4dd7.title: Environmental mitigation
a747c50d4dd7.sentence: A growing awareness of this has led to the expansion of legal requirements for environmental mitigation globally - 191 of the United Nations member states have Environment Impact Assessment legislation and more than 108 countries now have policies for biodiversity offsetting, a form of environmental mitigation.

f4114e2e7a3b.title: Environmental mitigation
f4114e2e7a3b.section: Environmental mitigation in the United States
f4114e2e7a3b.sentence: The Fish and Wildlife Coordination Act in 1934 included the first legal expressions of the duty to minimise and compensate for negative environmental impacts.

df614a458703.title: Environmental mitigation
df614a458703.sentence: Environmental mitigation is often applied with the aim of achieving a specific goal such as "no net loss" (NNL) or a "net positive impact" (NPI) by using frameworks like the mitigation hierarchy.

c7e9a94114ce.title: No net loss
c7e9a94114ce.sentence: "No net loss" (NNL) is an environmental policy approach that aims to counterbalance the negative impacts of development projects on the environment by using environmental mitigation measures.

be6ef8488467.title: No net loss
be6ef8488467.sentence: No net loss originated in 1980s in the United States, where it was developed as a policy goal for wetland conservation by the National Wetlands Policy Forum.

a8fbf91067b0.title: No net loss
a8fbf91067b0.sentence: During his campaign for the 1988 United States presidential election, George H. W. Bush promised "no net loss of wetlands" as a national goal.

ca908b3737e7.title: No net loss
ca908b3737e7.sentence: It is now used in many countries as an objective for biodiversity offsetting, such as in Colombia, France, and Uganda.

c0fb4b0c605a.title: No net loss
c0fb4b0c605a.sentence: No net loss policies have become widespread - by 2018, they were in place in at least 69 countries.

6ba25454b2fa.title: No net loss
6ba25454b2fa.sentence: NNL is implemented in planning processes via Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs), which assess the potential for significant adverse impacts on the environment resulting from proposed developments and determine how environmental mitigation can be used to reach no net loss.

290e67a27645.title: No net loss
290e67a27645.sentence: The mitigation hierarchy is generally used as a sequential framework to guide the implementation of measures to achieve NNL.

3f715990edda.title: No net loss
3f715990edda.sentence: Some lending institutions, such as the International Finance Corporation, also require no net loss on projects they co-finance.

e59d4a218d5f.title: No net loss

897a4fc8dc12.title: No net loss
897a4fc8dc12.sentence: A study to evaluate the impact of the NVMF found that up to 86% of offsets under the scheme did not compensate for impacts to native vegetation in the state, suggesting that the NNL goal was not achieved.

dd282e378f05.title: No net loss

2e6ce8dd0ff3.title: Environmental mitigation
2e6ce8dd0ff3.sentence: The mitigation hierarchy is a tool that is commonly used to guide the application of environmental mitigation measures.

7586f9557d13.title: Biodiversity offsetting
7586f9557d13.sentence: The mitigation hierarchy describes a series of measures that should be applied in sequence to reduce impacts on biodiversity to the point where no adverse effects remain, often including the steps avoid, reduce, restore/rehabilitate, and offset.

53362b8750a4.title: Environmental mitigation
53362b8750a4.sentence: - Avoid - measures taken to avoid creating impacts.

e262e665f256.title: Environmental mitigation
e262e665f256.sentence: This step is widely regarded as the most important.

9000a5e33923.title: Environmental mitigation
9000a5e33923.sentence: - Minimise - measures to reduce impacts that cannot be avoided.

a6b65c0a693b.title: Environmental mitigation
a6b65c0a693b.sentence: - Restore/rehabilitate - measures to restore or rehabilitate ecosystems that have been cleared or degraded, following a development project/activity that caused impacts that could not be avoided or minimised.

952df4a48773.title: Environmental mitigation
952df4a48773.sentence: - Offset - measures to compensate for residual negative impacts that cannot be avoided, minimised, or restored/rehabilitated, generally with the aim of no net loss or net gain of biodiversity.

7a4259caaa5d.title: Biodiversity offsetting
7a4259caaa5d.sentence: Offsetting is often regarded as the "final resort" in the mitigation hierarchy.

8d6bb458b8e0.title: Environmental mitigation
8d6bb458b8e0.sentence: Requirements for compliance with the mitigation hierarchy are often embedded within regulations to govern Environmental Impact Assessments and environmental licensing systems to evaluate and mitigate the environmental impacts of economic development.

3d41f4a6823a.title: Environmental mitigation
3d41f4a6823a.sentence: In some jurisdictions, the application of the mitigation hierarchy is required by law.

8b7b14a5dba9.title: No net loss
8b7b14a5dba9.sentence: As a framework for achieving no net loss, the mitigation hierarchy is part of France's Environmental Impact Assessment laws, referred to as the ERC sequence (Avoid-Reduce-Compensate, French: éviter-réduire-compenser).

8a9760c916a2.title: Environmental mitigation
8a9760c916a2.sentence: In addition to its use for biodiversity, alternate versions of the mitigation hierarchy have been proposed for different sectors, such as waste, food waste, energy, and carbon.

50de37d92a51.title: Environmental mitigation
50de37d92a51.sentence: Variations to the classical mitigation hierarchy have been proposed, like the Mitigation and Conservation Hierarchy and the Science Based Target Network's AR3T framework.

d543a3db0b2d.title: Biodiversity offsetting
d543a3db0b2d.sentence: Biodiversity offsetting is a system used predominantly by planning authorities and developers to fully compensate for biodiversity impacts associated with economic development, through the planning process.

92781a0a9f4b.title: Biodiversity offsetting
92781a0a9f4b.sentence: Biodiversity offsets are defined by the Business and Biodiversity Offsets Programme as "measurable conservation outcomes of actions designed to compensate for significant residual adverse biodiversity impacts arising from project development after appropriate prevention and mitigation measures have been taken."

cb7d73d653aa.title: Biodiversity offsetting
cb7d73d653aa.sentence: The definition also states that the goal of biodiversity offsets is to achieve no net loss of biodiversity, or ideally, a net gain.

9ad86f93d39a.title: Biodiversity offsetting
9ad86f93d39a.sentence: Offsetting is generally considered the final stage in a mitigation hierarchy, whereby predicted biodiversity impacts must first be avoided, minimised and reversed by developers, before any remaining impacts are offset.

4b59d072e91f.title: Biodiversity offsetting
4b59d072e91f.sentence: Individuals or companies involved in arranging biodiversity offsets will use quantitative measures to determine the amount, type and quality of habitat that is likely to be affected by a proposed project.

241bcab8be0f.title: Biodiversity offsetting
241bcab8be0f.sentence: Then, they will establish a new location or locations (often called receptor sites) where it would be possible to re-create the same amount, type and quality of habitat.

ebf36764760d.title: Biodiversity offsetting

408423adddab.sentence: However, there is so far mixed evidence that biodiversity offsets successfully counteract the biodiversity losses caused by associated developments, with evidence that offsets are generally more successful in less structurally-complex and more rapidly-recovering habitats such as loss of biodiversity simplified wetland habitats.

cf56b135ff33.sentence: A review of research conducted to determine the success of no net loss policies found that around one-third of NNL policies and individual biodiversity offsets reported achieving no net loss.

27a94063573c.title: Biodiversity offsetting
27a94063573c.sentence: For example, it has been argued that biodiversity offsetting legitimises ongoing habitat destruction and promotes the "bulldozing of biodiversity".

612c9c9df50a.title: Biodiversity offsetting
612c9c9df50a.sentence: Further concerns have been expressed over substitution of biodiversity in a specific place for efforts to conserve biodiversity elsewhere, given that biodiversity can have a place-based cultural and spiritual value for humans but also because of a view of biodiversity as having an intrinsic value outside of benefits to humans.

5a64f552dfd0.title: Biodiversity banking
5a64f552dfd0.sentence: Biodiversity banking, also known as biodiversity trading, conservation banking, mitigation banking, habitat banking, compensatory habitat, or set-asides, describes a market-based framework for biodiversity offsetting where offsets can be traded in the form of credits to offset negative environmental impacts of development projects or activities.

074f381c9e66.title: Biodiversity banking

7131fffbe11e.title: Biodiversity banking
7131fffbe11e.sentence: To generate credits, conservation activities must be carried out at the site of a potential biodiversity bank so that the credits represent improved outcomes for biodiversity that would not have otherwise happened.

6d1ab453fedf.title: Biodiversity banking
6d1ab453fedf.sentence: On a practical level, this might involve reintroducing native plant species that had disappeared from the area, removing invasive species, or removing ditches and levees to restore a swamp.

6be6e49b0775.title: Biodiversity banking
6be6e49b0775.sentence: Biodiversity banking generally turns offsets into assets that can be stored or traded, through the creation of biodiversity credits that quantify the value of projects undertaken to restore, create, or enhance biodiversity in advance of a development and away from its potential site.

904e7ec0d184.title: Biodiversity banking
904e7ec0d184.sentence: When establishing a biodiversity bank, a legal arrangement, such as a conservation easement (also known as a conservation covenant) might be required to set aside the land for conservation and prevent the use of the land for development, either in perpetuity or for a specified time period.

8330a85ac828.title: Biodiversity banking

60410799ed96.title: Biodiversity banking

74304de07b56.title: Mitigation banking
74304de07b56.sentence: Mitigation banking is a market-based system of debits and credits (used primarily in the United States as part of its "no net loss" policy) that involves restoration, creation, or enhancement of wetlands to compensate for unavoidable impacts to a wetland in another location.

2fe5cee7a040.title: Mitigation banking
2fe5cee7a040.sentence: It involves a system of mitigation banks, sites where projects to restore, create, or enhance wetlands can be carried out in advance of impacts.

80f79cb4263b.title: Mitigation banking
80f79cb4263b.sentence: The outcomes of these projects are valued through the creation of compensatory mitigation credits that can be purchased from mitigation banks to offset the negative impacts of developments or agriculture expansion on wetlands and aquatic habitats.

46d4712829de.title: Mitigation banking

a4205021c5e1.title: Mitigation banking

6a112eea6c1f.title: Mitigation banking
6a112eea6c1f.sentence: The public interest is served when enforcement agencies require more habitat as mitigation, often referred to as a mitigation ratio, than is adversely impacted by management or development of nearby acreage.

24777fc23bfc.title: Conservation banking
24777fc23bfc.sentence: Conservation banks are permanently protected parcels of land with inherent abilities to harbor, preserve, and manage the survival of endangered and threatened species, along with their critical habitat.

e7765a0d49ae.title: Conservation banking
e7765a0d49ae.sentence: Purchasing “credits” through a conservation bank is one such mitigation measure to remedy the loss.

6392293fc8a0.title: Conservation banking
6392293fc8a0.sentence: Rather than have developments offset their effects by conserving small areas of habitat, conservation banking allows pooling multiple mitigation resources into a larger reserve.

3a6a82909981.title: Conservation banking
3a6a82909981.sentence: Banks are often considered to be the more ecologically efficient option for mitigation because they generally incorporate larger tracts of land that enables higher quality habitat and range connectivity, thereby creating a stronger chance of survival and sustainability for the species.

822d90663ecb.title: Conservation banking
822d90663ecb.sentence: Comparatively, conservation banks are more cost effective as they are able to maintain larger blocks of land with greater functionality for a species, such as allowing habitat connectivity.

f3f042ed9b19.title: Conservation banking

be775f172486.title: Conservation banking
be775f172486.sentence: Collectively, the nation’s 130 conservation banks is equivalent to over 160,000 acres of permanently protected land.

8e55aa9f2e91.title: Conservation banking
8e55aa9f2e91.sentence: Additionally, the market forces of supply and demand largely dictate the price of any given credit, and the value may fluctuate based on many other economic factors such as land value, competition, and speculation about development in a certain habitat area.

85d242428112.title: Biodiversity Impact Credit
85d242428112.sentence: A Biodiversity Impact Credit (BIC) is a transferable biodiversity credit designed to reduce global species extinction risk.

493962d98b89.title: Biodiversity Impact Credit
493962d98b89.sentence: The underlying BIC metric, developed by academics working at Queen Mary University of London and Bar-Ilan University, is given by a simple formula that quantifies the positive and negative effects that interventions in nature have on the mean long-term survival probability of species.

89d4664d063d.title: Biodiversity Impact Credit
89d4664d063d.sentence: As a simple interpretation, the BIC metric measures the equivalent number of endangered species whose populations have been restored or (for negative BIC) the number of species that should be restored to achieve net zero biodiversity impact.

1db19c11f9b5.title: Biodiversity Impact Credit
1db19c11f9b5.section: Biodiversity Impact Credits in practice > Rationale
1db19c11f9b5.sentence: BICs are designed to address Target 4 of this framework ("to halt extinction of known threatened species... and significantly reduce extinction risk" and Target 15: "[Take measures] to ensure that large transnational companies and financial institutions [...] transparently disclose their risks, dependencies and impacts on biodiversity... in order to progressively reduce negative impacts."

913c91a07102.title: Biodiversity Impact Credit

913c91a07102.sentence: The Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures via their LEAP methodology recommends use of BICs to quantify impacts on species extinction risk in version 1.1 of their disclosure recommendations.

75a16d46c7d9.title: Biodiversity Impact Credit
75a16d46c7d9.sentence: Biodiversity credits have been criticised by some who say that putting a monetary value on nature can oversimplify its ecological complexity and intrinsic value, making quantification unreliable or inappropriate.

3418df13f666.title: Biodiversity Impact Credit

be6a4f694891.title: Biodiversity Impact Credit
be6a4f694891.sentence: Biodiversity credits have also been criticised as a way for companies to make false sustainability claims, a practice called greenwashing.

fecfe7dc3a90.title: Biodiversity offsetting
fecfe7dc3a90.sentence: However, also viable are so-called "averted loss" biodiversity offsets, in which measures are taken to prevent ecological degradation from occurring where it almost certainly would have happened otherwise.

3c9287b3ec43.title: Biodiversity offsetting
3c9287b3ec43.sentence: Averted loss offsets might involve the creation of new protected areas (to conserve fauna species that would otherwise have disappeared), the removal of invasive species from areas of habitat (which otherwise would have reduced or displaced populations of native species), or positive measures to reduce extensive natural resource use (e.g. the offer of alternative livelihood creation to prevent activities leading to deforestation).

87d56d82ab18.title: Biodiversity offsetting
87d56d82ab18.sentence: Any activities that do not result in a positive and measurable gain for biodiversity would not generally be counted as part of a biodiversity offset.

395126f45b10.title: Biodiversity offsetting
395126f45b10.sentence: For instance, if a developer funds ecological conservation research in a region that they are impacting through a project, would not count as an offset (unless it could be shown quantitatively how specific fauna and flora would benefit). instead, this would be a more general form of compensation.

804a3807072d.title: Biodiversity offsetting
804a3807072d.sentence: Poorly designed offset policies may also create perverse incentives that lower conservation standards and unintentionally encourage further biodiversity decline.

8a93be057d52.title: Biodiversity offsetting
8a93be057d52.sentence: The cost of re-creating an area of habitat affected by a development proposal (impact site) can be calculated and represented as a number of conservation credits that a developer could purchase in order to offset their biodiversity impact.

3d64f2de1f7f.title: Biodiversity offsetting
3d64f2de1f7f.sentence: Land put forward for investment to re-create impacted biodiversity (receptor site) is also calculated in conservation credits (to account for the cost of creating or restoring biodiversity at that particular site and to cover the cost of its long-term conservation management).

ba98ffa1424b.title: Biodiversity offsetting
ba98ffa1424b.sentence: This situation enables the buying (by developers) and selling (by landowners) of conservation credits.

f1b781f8cd4f.title: Biodiversity offsetting

3a59db0d002a.title: Biodiversity offsetting

f14a9527e680.title: Biodiversity offsetting

746a4bd72bb9.title: Biodiversity offsetting

c48e1c0dcf15.title: Mitigation banking

7ca1a5799403.title: Mitigation banking
7ca1a5799403.sentence: It includes the steps avoid, minimise, and compensate, requiring that avoidance and minimisation measures should be exercised before compensation.

73659cc560f6.title: Mitigation banking
73659cc560f6.sentence: It is a form of environmental mitigation and can include both on-site (on or adjacent to the site of impacts) and off-site mitigation.

13a3e66669f7.title: Conservation banking

d6ac31f3dcf7.title: Conservation banking
d6ac31f3dcf7.sentence: In-Lieu fee programs allows a permittee to contribute money into a United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) approved fund in lieu of implementing their own mitigation.

202655af9279.title: Conservation banking
202655af9279.sentence: The second alternative form of mitigation is the Permittee-Responsible program, which allows the permittee takes on implementation and assumes liability for their own mitigation project to offset effects.

d6dfe4f1fe44.title: Mitigation banking
d6dfe4f1fe44.sentence: In 2008, the regulations for compensatory mitigation (which includes mitigation banking) were revised by the USACE and USEPA under the 'Compensatory Mitigation Rule'.

9ec504d3d90b.title: Mitigation banking
9ec504d3d90b.sentence: These new federal regulations established mitigation banks as the preferred method for compensatory mitigation and also introduced ecosystem services into the standards for mitigation banking.

d928a909a2bf.title: Mitigation banking
d928a909a2bf.sentence: This is a voluntary legal arrangement between a landowner and a government agency or conservation organisation to restrict future commercial or residential development on a site, permanently setting it aside to be managed for conservation purposes.

f93c1044ee51.title: Mitigation banking

ae6950bc9e56.title: Environmental mitigation

2d25384250b2.title: Environmental mitigation
2d25384250b2.sentence: Examples of such systems include biodiversity banking (a way to carry out biodiversity offsetting) and its various forms, including mitigation banking, habitat banking, species banking, or conservation banking, dependent on region or the goals of the system for conservation.

42dad007680f.title: Environmental mitigation
42dad007680f.sentence: Determining the currency that a system will be based on and ensuring that debits and credits are ecologically equivalent are considered challenging issues for environmental crediting systems.

215807482fc4.title: Environmental mitigation
215807482fc4.sentence: Ensuring that the outcomes of conservation projects used to generate credits are better for biodiversity than if the projects had not happened (a concept called additionality) is another challenge.

00ef10189919.title: Environmental mitigation
00ef10189919.sentence: - Net positive impact - a goal for the outcomes of a development project where the aim is for the negative environmental impacts of the project to be outweighed by the positive impacts of environmental mitigation measures; the goal is for the level of biodiversity to be greater than it was before the project.

9ec9088ad41b.title: No net loss
9ec9088ad41b.sentence: Where the aim is for biodiversity levels to exceed their previous state, a goal of "net gain" (NG) or "net positive impact" (NPI) might be used instead of "no net loss".

95a85d776f8e.title: No net loss

65fbe2fa682b.title: No net loss

3d2579a33f5a.title: Nature-positive

3d2579a33f5a.sentence: NNL and NPI differ because NNL focuses on preventing losses, while NPI focuses on aiming for a net gain in biodiversity.

c0ef1caa6d55.title: Carbon offsets and credits
c0ef1caa6d55.sentence: A carbon credit is a tradable instrument (typically a virtual certificate) that conveys a claim to have avoided greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions or to have enhanced removal of GHG from the atmosphere.

13939fc898b3.title: Carbon offsets and credits
13939fc898b3.sentence: One carbon credit represents the avoided or enhanced removal of one metric ton of carbon dioxide or its carbon dioxide-equivalent (CO2e).

69a815feaeb9.title: Carbon offsets and credits
69a815feaeb9.sentence: Carbon offsetting is the practice of using carbon credits to offset or counter an entity's greenhouse gas inventory emissions in line with reporting programs or institutional emissions targets/goals.

44f846cfcaa9.title: Carbon offsets and credits
44f846cfcaa9.sentence: Carbon credit trading mechanisms (i.e., crediting programs), enable project developers to implement projects that mitigate GHGs and receive carbon credits which can be sold to interested buyers who may use the credits to claim they have offset their inventory GHG emissions.

04aadbd67a3e.title: Carbon offsets and credits
04aadbd67a3e.sentence: Carbon credits are a form of carbon pricing, along with carbon taxes, and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanisms (CBAM).

e643e22f87fc.sentence: In the 1990s, regulatory frameworks for the US Clean Water Act enabled mitigation banking and wetlands offsetting, which set the procedural and conceptual precedent for carbon offsetting.

a1df7db2224f.sentence: In 1997, the original international compliance carbon markets emerged from the Kyoto Protocol, which established three mechanisms that enable countries or operators in developed countries to acquire offset credits.

3d3f9db5cd72.title: Carbon offsets and credits
3d3f9db5cd72.sentence: In November 2024, after years of deadlock, governments attending the COP29 conference in Baku, Azerbaijan agreed to rules on creating, trading and registering emission reductions and removals as carbon credits that higher-emission countries can buy, thus providing funding for low-emission technologies.

025537d07cda.title: Clean Development Mechanism
025537d07cda.sentence: The Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) is a United Nations-run carbon offset scheme allowing countries to fund greenhouse gas emissions-reducing projects in other countries and claim the saved emissions as part of their own efforts to meet international emissions targets.

1df5d8a73cb5.title: Clean Development Mechanism
1df5d8a73cb5.sentence: It is one of the three Flexible Mechanisms defined in the Kyoto Protocol.

7679078476b1.title: Clean Development Mechanism
7679078476b1.sentence: The CDM, defined in Article 12 of the Protocol, was intended to assist non-Annex I countries (predominantly developing nations) achieve sustainable development and reduce their carbon footprints, and to assist Annex I countries (predominantly industrialized nations) achieve compliance with greenhouse gas emissions reduction commitments.

cc1b8eba0209.title: Clean Development Mechanism
cc1b8eba0209.sentence: The IPCC has projected GDP losses for OECD Europe with full use of CDM and Joint Implementation to between 0.13% and 0.81% of GDP versus 0.31% to 1.50% with only domestic action.

a95de0580c2b.title: Clean Development Mechanism
a95de0580c2b.sentence: The revenues of the CDM constitutes the largest source of mitigation finance to developing countries to date (World Bank, 2010, p. 261-262).

e13102edd0f0.title: Clean Development Mechanism
e13102edd0f0.sentence: The CDM is the main source of income for the UNFCCC Adaptation Fund, which was established in 2007 to finance concrete adaptation projects and programmes in developing countries that are parties to the Kyoto Protocol (World Bank, 2010, p. 262-263).

772b702fbd9d.title: REDD+
772b702fbd9d.sentence: It aims to encourage developing countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, and to promote conservation, sustainable forest management, and enhancement of forest carbon stocks through financial incentives and policy support.

f05293db1327.title: REDD+
f05293db1327.sentence: The acronym is commonly expanded as "reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation in developing countries", and the "+" denotes the additional forest conservation and enhancement activities included in the UNFCCC scope.

e828205450de.title: REDD+

a00ebf7ec133.title: REDD+

39f978a672a2.title: REDD+
39f978a672a2.sentence: In 2019, the IPCC estimated net emissions from the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector at about 13 GtCO2-eq (about 22% of global net anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions), and reported that about half of net AFOLU emissions were net CO2 emissions from land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF), predominantly from deforestation.

2ad492f356b4.title: REDD+
2ad492f356b4.sentence: UNFCCC decisions describe a set of core elements for developing countries undertaking REDD+ activities, including a national strategy or action plan; a forest reference emission level and/or forest reference level (FREL/FRL) as a benchmark; a national forest monitoring system to support MRV; and a system for providing information on how safeguards are addressed and respected.

c5d60e74cb40.title: REDD+
c5d60e74cb40.sentence: Because the main drivers of deforestation and forest degradation often sit outside the forest sector (especially agricultural expansion, infrastructure and extractive activities), effective REDD+ strategies typically combine forest-sector measures (for example, improved forest governance, protected-area management, or improved logging practices) with cross-sector reforms such as land-use planning and agricultural policy.

f89179a68b96.title: Forest reference emission level
f89179a68b96.sentence: Forest reference emission levels (FRELs) and related forest reference levels (FRLs) are benchmarks used under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) for assessing performance in REDD+ implementation.

c46adcffa9de.title: Forest reference emission level
c46adcffa9de.sentence: They are expressed as tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) per year for a reference period and compared with emissions and removals reported for a results period.

8468f8bd861f.title: Forest reference emission level
8468f8bd861f.sentence: In broad terms, reference levels draw on historical information, combining data on changes in forest area with estimates of emissions and removals.

50573f0205f3.title: Forest reference emission level
50573f0205f3.sentence: For results-based payments, each submission is subject to a technical assessment coordinated by the UNFCCC secretariat under decision 13/CP.19, part of the Warsaw Framework for REDD-plus.

e65fb69e6613.title: Forest reference emission level
e65fb69e6613.sentence: Parties may update reference levels over time using a stepwise approach that incorporates improved data and methodologies, while maintaining consistency with national greenhouse gas inventories.

7b6b1c229d35.title: Forest reference emission level
7b6b1c229d35.sentence: Because reported REDD+ results are assessed relative to the submitted benchmark, choices about the reference period, data sources, scope (activities and carbon pools), and any adjustments can affect the quantity of results calculated against a reference level, which has made transparency and documentation central themes in UNFCCC technical discussions.

78d5afdbee6d.title: Forest reference emission level
78d5afdbee6d.sentence: For example, a study comparing alternative approaches for setting reference emission levels argued that if reference levels are constructed by simple extrapolation of historical forest-area change, countries could behave strategically during the reference period to improve their starting position, creating perverse incentives (for example, higher deforestation rates during the reference period could make it easier to generate credits later).

ac1a3fe670e6.title: Forest reference emission level

b211f1519faa.title: Carbon offsets and credits

970f76f2b0ef.title: Carbon offsets and credits

a01b1db72b9b.title: Gold Standard (carbon offset standard)
a01b1db72b9b.sentence: The Gold Standard (GS), or Gold Standard for the Global Goals, is a standard and logo certification mark program, for non-governmental emission reductions projects in the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), the voluntary carbon market and other climate and development interventions.

36dc8491bb90.title: Gold Standard (carbon offset standard)
36dc8491bb90.sentence: The Gold Standard for CDM (GS-CER) was developed in 2003 by World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), South-North, and Helio International.

7278bc688b6c.title: Gold Standard (carbon offset standard)
7278bc688b6c.sentence: It was designed with an intent to ensure that carbon credits are real, verifiable, and that projects make measurable contributions to sustainable development.

d4b9332f5633.title: Gold Standard (carbon offset standard)

94560b87e4b9.title: Gold Standard (carbon offset standard)

fc108e02b98a.title: Gold Standard (carbon offset standard)

a3f2fdc0dcf5.title: Gold Standard (carbon offset standard)

a2e341b6cd44.title: REDD+

a2e341b6cd44.sentence: Another option would be some form of reduced-impact logging in commercial logging, under the REDD+ eligible activity of sustainable management of forests.

5714eb82cd56.title: REDD+
5714eb82cd56.sentence: UNFCCC decisions describe REDD+ as a phased approach, beginning with "readiness" activities (planning, capacity-building and institutional development), moving to implementation of national policies and measures, and evolving toward results-based actions that are fully measured, reported and verified.

8bed461dc82e.title: REDD+
8bed461dc82e.sentence: Decision 1/CP.16, paragraph 73, suggests that national capacity for implementing REDD+ is built up in phases, "beginning with the development of national strategies or action plans, policies and measures, and capacity-building, followed by the implementation of national policies and measures and national strategies or action plans that could involve further capacity-building, technology development and transfer and results-based demonstration activities, and evolving into results-based actions that should be fully measured, reported and verified".

cb41ecaed7b3.title: REDD+
cb41ecaed7b3.sentence: The initial phase of developing national strategies, action, and capacity building is typically referred to as the "readiness phase".

d196d2e75ac1.title: REDD+
d196d2e75ac1.sentence: REDD+ readiness (often described as phase 1) refers to early institutional and technical work needed before results-based implementation, including developing national strategies or action plans, building MRV capacity, establishing forest reference levels, and putting in place safeguard-related processes and stakeholder participation arrangements.

03c0d2bca15d.title: REDD+

0900299a3b0b.title: National forest monitoring system
0900299a3b0b.sentence: A national forest monitoring system (NFMS) is a country's institutional and technical arrangement for monitoring forests and producing information for decision-making and reporting, as described by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO).

aa2599cf1f86.title: National forest monitoring system
aa2599cf1f86.sentence: In the context of REDD+, Decision 11/CP.19 under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), adopted as part of the Warsaw Framework for REDD+, encourages developing countries undertaking REDD+ activities to establish NFMSs that are transparent and consistent and that draw on both remote sensing and ground-based forest inventory approaches, as appropriate to national circumstances.

34dee96ab36e.title: National forest monitoring system
34dee96ab36e.sentence: NFMSs can produce outputs such as time series of forest area and change, maps, and estimates of biomass or carbon stocks, with accompanying documentation and uncertainty information.

0f4d18e99b21.title: National forest monitoring system

6de7551f4bcc.title: National forest monitoring system

69c5def5ebd9.title: Forest Carbon Partnership Facility
69c5def5ebd9.sentence: The Forest Carbon Partnership Facility (FCPF) is a World Bank facility that supports developing countries in preparing for and implementing REDD+.

3aec91700638.title: Forest Carbon Partnership Facility

7838186235f4.title: New York Declaration on Forests

10e2c40c174a.title: New York Declaration on Forests

56110beb24c8.title: Time value of carbon
56110beb24c8.sentence: The time value of carbon is a conjecture that there is a greater benefit from reducing carbon dioxide or other greenhouse gas reduction immediately than reducing the same amount of emissions (or rate of emissions) in the future.

6b8a5cf33c2c.title: Time value of carbon
6b8a5cf33c2c.sentence: According to this conjecture, carbon emissions are subject to a discount rate, similar to money, which means that the timing of carbon emissions is important to consider alongside their magnitude.

7da617b53b97.title: Time value of carbon
7da617b53b97.sentence: This is not to be confused with the monetary discount rate applied to carbon emission or carbon sequestration projects.

bef187cf5405.title: Time value of carbon
bef187cf5405.sentence: Rather, it is a discount rate applied to the physical carbon itself.

5abb0ae4aea9.title: Time value of carbon
5abb0ae4aea9.sentence: Even though each of the three scenarios start and end at the same place, and in the same amount of time, the total amount of carbon emitted will be different in each pathway.

bb5f0c61cfd3.title: Time value of carbon
bb5f0c61cfd3.sentence: The area under the curve -- which represents the total amount of CO2 emitted -- is smallest in Scenario 1, and largest in Scenario 3.

51a8a63f2fe1.title: Time value of carbon
51a8a63f2fe1.sentence: A high discount rate on emissions reductions or carbon sequestration incentivizes cutting emissions earlier.

0d8226aa9201.title: Time value of carbon
0d8226aa9201.sentence: A low discount rate means that carbon emissions have similar value across time, and so there is less incentive to take immediate action towards reducing emissions.

f76fef93203c.title: Time value of carbon
f76fef93203c.section: Additional implications of carbon discount rates
f76fef93203c.sentence: If the time value of carbon is positive -- that is, if carbon not emitted now is more valuable than carbon not emitted later -- then carbon sequestration projects, even those that are known to be temporary, have positive value.

6bc0bb4f70b4.title: Time value of carbon
6bc0bb4f70b4.section: Additional implications of carbon discount rates
6bc0bb4f70b4.sentence: Storing carbon in trees or soil delays its introduction to the atmosphere to a point where it is less impactful, meaning that these projects can have a tangible benefit, even if the total amount of carbon emitted is exactly the same.

9319d202f388.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
9319d202f388.sentence: - Corresponding adjustment: the accounting adjustment used to prevent double claiming between Parties by ensuring a transferred outcome is reflected in only one Party’s NDC accounting, consistent with CMA guidance.

aba9075c1ed0.title: Paris Agreement
aba9075c1ed0.section: Content > Mitigation provisions and carbon markets
aba9075c1ed0.sentence: A mechanism, the "corresponding adjustment", was established to avoid double counting for emission offsets.

78b3e20e3b81.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
78b3e20e3b81.sentence: Double claiming (between Parties) | Both the transferring Party and the acquiring Party treat the same mitigation outcome as contributing to their NDC achievement. | Apply a corresponding adjustment linked to authorization/first transfer, and disclose it through Article 6 reporting under the Article 13 transparency framework.

e2eb13da9776.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
e2eb13da9776.sentence: Such bilateral arrangements are intended to pair transfers with corresponding adjustments and transparency reporting so that a transferred mitigation outcome is not counted toward both Parties’ NDCs.

baf2f002c0dd.title: Paris Agreement
baf2f002c0dd.section: Content > Mitigation provisions and carbon markets > Linkage of carbon trading systems and ITMOs
baf2f002c0dd.sentence: This provision requires the "linkage" of carbon emissions trading systems – because measured emissions reductions must avoid "double counting", transferred mitigation outcomes must be recorded as a gain of emission units for one party and a reduction of emission units for the other, a so-called "corresponding adjustment".

94421d081da6.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
94421d081da6.sentence: The CMA guidance adopted at COP26 (CMA.3) includes requirements on “corresponding adjustments” and reporting intended to apply these accounting and integrity principles in practice.

842fe0d3eb69.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
842fe0d3eb69.section: Implementation and early use cases > Relationship to voluntary carbon markets
842fe0d3eb69.sentence: Voluntary and compliance credit markets can overlap, including when host governments authorize credits from independent programmes for use under Article 6, which can require an authorization decision and, where relevant, a corresponding adjustment so the same outcome is not claimed more than once.

2cc4d4a242bd.title: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
2cc4d4a242bd.sentence: Market commentary and academic analysis have described recurring integrity concerns, including information asymmetries between project developers and credit buyers, heterogeneous methodologies across standards, and perverse incentives that can reward over-crediting when demand is driven by headline "tons" of carbon dioxide equivalent rather than robust impact.

f01891d6beee.title: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
f01891d6beee.section: Reception and criticism > Criticism > Stringency and additionality
f01891d6beee.sentence: In a 2022 public comment submission on draft CCP materials, Barbara Haya argued that high-level integrity concepts such as additionality, conservative quantification, and permanence were already used by existing programs, yet over-crediting had still occurred in practice.

089cd0a4e94e.title: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
089cd0a4e94e.section: Reception and criticism > Criticism > Stringency and additionality
089cd0a4e94e.sentence: She argued that a principles-based benchmark would need rigorous, credit-type-specific assessment and resourcing to reliably screen out over-crediting, and she raised concerns about baseline setting and other methodological choices that could systematically inflate credited reductions.

84b55a612baa.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
84b55a612baa.sentence: The impacts of Article 6 remain debated, particularly around environmental integrity, governance capacity and the risk of over-crediting.

6ecb92ac1e6f.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
6ecb92ac1e6f.section: Approaches under Article 6 > Article 6.2: Cooperative approaches
