6ecb92ac1e6f.sentence: Commentators debate whether Article 6.2 transfers primarily lower costs and mobilize finance or risk undermining environmental integrity through over-crediting, unambitious baselines (“hot air”), or weak governance; assessments emphasize that outcomes depend on ambition and the strength of accounting, transparency and review safeguards.

2ddd5cacf495.title: Bond (finance)
2ddd5cacf495.sentence: In finance, a bond is a type of security under which the issuer (debtor) owes the holder (creditor) a debt, and is obliged to provide cash flow to the creditor.

23c944adea61.title: Bond (finance)
23c944adea61.sentence: Thus, a bond is a form of loan or IOU.

6b0f9dd6e8cc.title: Bond (finance)
6b0f9dd6e8cc.sentence: This usually consists of as interest over a specified amount of time, and repaying the principal at the maturity date.

4080e4cd6502.title: Bond (finance)
4080e4cd6502.sentence: The interest is usually payable at fixed intervals: semiannual, annual, and less often at other periods.

fb13ae61d5fe.title: Bond (finance)
fb13ae61d5fe.sentence: Bonds provide the borrower with external funds to finance long-term investments or, in the case of government bonds, to finance current expenditure.

338db74f4518.title: Bond (finance)
338db74f4518.sentence: Bonds and stocks are both securities, but the major difference between the two is that (capital) stockholders have an equity stake in a company (i.e. they are owners), whereas bondholders have a creditor stake in a company (i.e. they are lenders).

86e70bccb922.title: Bond (finance)
86e70bccb922.sentence: As creditors, bondholders have priority over stockholders.

134b3046dc26.title: Bond (finance)
134b3046dc26.sentence: Another difference is that bonds usually have a defined term, or maturity, after which the bond is redeemed, whereas stocks typically remain outstanding indefinitely.

aaedb90f6eb1.title: Bond (finance)
aaedb90f6eb1.sentence: Most bonds have a term shorter than 30 years.

867748ac3c0d.title: Bond (finance)
867748ac3c0d.sentence: Bonds are issued by public authorities, credit institutions, companies and supranational institutions in the primary markets.

d32db0f1dec9.title: Bond (finance)
d32db0f1dec9.sentence: Bonds are bought and traded mostly by institutions like central banks, sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, insurance companies, hedge funds, and banks.

ddded8e7161e.title: Bond (finance)
ddded8e7161e.sentence: The coupon is the interest rate that the issuer pays to the holder.

69d280374a5a.title: Bond (finance)
69d280374a5a.sentence: For fixed rate bonds, the coupon is fixed throughout the life of the bond.

315d097dc5cb.title: Bond (finance)
315d097dc5cb.sentence: For floating rate notes, the coupon varies throughout the life of the bond and is based on the movement of a money market reference rate (historically this was generally LIBOR, but with its discontinuation the market reference rate has transitioned to SOFR).

a33e90f44af7.title: Return on investment
a33e90f44af7.sentence: Return on investment (ROI) or return on costs (ROC) is the ratio between net income or profit to investment (costs resulting from an investment of some resources).

98b18c0e8c3e.title: Return on investment
98b18c0e8c3e.sentence: A high ROI means the investment's gains compare favorably to its cost.

d868e16f65bd.title: Return on investment
d868e16f65bd.sentence: As a performance measure, ROI is used to evaluate the efficiency of an investment or to compare the efficiencies of several different investments.

03594306ac1f.title: Return on investment
03594306ac1f.sentence: The investment with the largest ROI is usually prioritized, even though the spread of ROI over the time period of an investment should also be taken into account.

488f7349f490.title: Return on investment
488f7349f490.sentence: return on investment = (gain from investment − cost of investment) / cost of investment

640744293465.title: Return on investment
640744293465.sentence: For example, you invested $10,000 in stocks (initial investment) and paid $200 in brokerage fees (other expenses).

7d030ef5729e.title: Return on investment
7d030ef5729e.sentence: After one year, the current value of your investment is $12,500, not yet sold.

9bee431618af.title: Return on investment
9bee431618af.sentence: During the year, you received $300 in dividends (income from the investment).

8e63a5b0861c.title: Return on investment
8e63a5b0861c.sentence: As the duration of this investment is 1 year, this ROI is annual.

2ea6417098dc.title: Return on investment
2ea6417098dc.sentence: ROI is not time-adjusted (unlike e.g. net present value): most textbooks describe it with a "Year 0" investment and two to three years' income.

2e25af0598ed.title: Return on investment
2e25af0598ed.sentence: For long-term investments, the need for a Net Present Value adjustment is great and without it the ROI is incorrect.

b100dba944d9.title: Return on investment
b100dba944d9.sentence: Similar to discounted cash flow, a Discounted ROI should be used instead.

5ea8dfe8fd51.title: Return on investment
5ea8dfe8fd51.sentence: One limitation associated with the traditional ROI calculation is that it does not fully "capture the short-term or long-term importance, value, or risks associated with natural and social capital", because it does not account for the environmental, social, and governance performance of an organization.

b7900748d253.title: Stock
b7900748d253.sentence: Stocks (also capital stock, or sometimes interchangeably, shares) consist of all the shares by which ownership of a corporation or company is divided.

9b6dca9171e1.title: Stock
9b6dca9171e1.sentence: A single share of the stock means fractional ownership of the corporation in proportion to the total number of shares.

c9ebd07bdad7.title: Stock
c9ebd07bdad7.sentence: This typically entitles the shareholder (stockholder) to that fraction of the company's earnings, proceeds from liquidation of assets (after discharge of all senior claims such as secured and unsecured debt), or voting power, often dividing these up in proportion to the number of like shares each stockholder owns.

a8c420f24c20.title: Stock
a8c420f24c20.sentence: As a unit of ownership, common stock typically carries voting rights that can be exercised in corporate decisions.

74563a40671b.title: Stock
74563a40671b.sentence: Preferred stock differs from common stock in that it typically does not carry voting rights but is legally entitled to receive a certain level of dividend payments before any dividends can be issued to other shareholders.

5b7c277677fc.title: Stock
5b7c277677fc.sentence: They can achieve these goals by selling shares in the company to the general public, through a sale on a stock exchange.

70602eca6ad6.title: Stock
70602eca6ad6.sentence: This process is called an initial public offering, or IPO.

62710b58a081.title: Stock
62710b58a081.sentence: Financing a company through the sale of stock in a company is known as equity financing.

af68332d6f06.title: Stock
af68332d6f06.sentence: Alternatively, debt financing (for example issuing bonds) can be done to avoid giving up shares of ownership of the company.

e9936041ba69.title: Stock
e9936041ba69.sentence: At any given moment, an equity's price is strictly a result of supply and demand.

45bd8e066e5f.title: Stock
45bd8e066e5f.sentence: The price of the stock moves in order to achieve and maintain equilibrium.

ccb2c8cb498b.title: Stock
ccb2c8cb498b.sentence: However, shareholder's rights to a company's assets are subordinate to the rights of the company's creditors.

630d71c33ced.title: Environmental finance
630d71c33ced.sentence: Environmental finance is a field within finance that employs market-based environmental policy instruments to improve the ecological impact of investment strategies.

e1844f901826.title: Environmental finance
e1844f901826.sentence: The primary objective of environmental finance is to regress the negative impacts of climate change through pricing and trading schemes.

d15ac9db3400.title: Environmental finance
d15ac9db3400.sentence: Environmental finance aims to reallocate business resources to improve the sustainability of investments whilst also retaining profit margins.

637edca30c91.title: Environmental finance
637edca30c91.sentence: In 1992, Richard L. Sandor proposed a new course outlining emission markets at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, that would later be known as the course, Environmental Finance.

5d4bb6c2d78a.title: Environmental finance
5d4bb6c2d78a.sentence: Inspired by the theory of social cost, Sandor focused on cap-and-trade strategies such as emission trading schemes and more flexible mechanisms including taxes and subsidies to manage environmental crisis.

6bad976ba301.title: Environmental finance
6bad976ba301.sentence: Cap-and-trade mechanisms limit the total amount of emissions a particular region or country can emit.

b97c8803ffb8.title: Environmental finance
b97c8803ffb8.sentence: Firms are issued with tradeable permits which they can buy or sell.

69100d7e045c.title: Environmental finance
69100d7e045c.sentence: This acts as a financial incentive to reduce emissions and as a disincentive to exceed emission caps.

2d4cca62674f.title: Environmental finance
2d4cca62674f.sentence: In 1999, the Dow Jones Sustainability Index was introduced to evaluate the ecological and social impact of stocks so shareholders could invest more sustainably.

e3a0526f7a90.title: Environmental finance
e3a0526f7a90.sentence: Mitigation finance is investment that aims to reduce global carbon emissions.

fdbaec47a1c5.title: Environmental finance
fdbaec47a1c5.sentence: Adaptation finance aims to respond to the consequences of climate change.

116ff123babb.title: Environmental finance
116ff123babb.sentence: Globally, there is a much greater focus on mitigation, accounting for over 90% of spending on climate.

ad2c75283898.title: Official development assistance
ad2c75283898.sentence: Official development assistance (ODA) is a category used by the Development Assistance Committee (DAC) of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) to measure foreign aid.

330b3cee4a7c.title: Official development assistance
330b3cee4a7c.sentence: It refers to material resources given by the governments of richer countries to promote the economic development of poorer countries and the welfare of their people.

58fccb0d162b.title: Official development assistance
58fccb0d162b.sentence: The DAC first adopted the concept in 1969.

8af39b7d4cc9.title: Official development assistance
8af39b7d4cc9.sentence: Most ODA is in the form of grants, but some is measured as the concessional value in soft (low-interest) loans.

f669e4baa4a5.title: Official development assistance
f669e4baa4a5.sentence: - at concessional financial terms (if a loan, having a grant element of at least 25 per cent).

b12f48208d35.title: Official development assistance
b12f48208d35.sentence: In 2019, the annual amount of state donor aid counted as ODA was US$168 billion, of which US$152 billion came from DAC donors.

4475f82dfbb5.title: Official development assistance
4475f82dfbb5.sentence: In 2019, 28% of all ODA was multilateral.

200a1f27558a.title: Official development assistance
200a1f27558a.sentence: The main organizations for multilateral ODA were the European Union, the IDA (the concessional lending branch of the World Bank), regional development banks and UN agencies.

def7f20bbf00.title: Official development assistance
def7f20bbf00.sentence: In 2025, aid from OECD Development Assistance Committee donor countries dropped by 23% after adjusting for inflation, the biggest annual decline on record.

9de63fa4256b.title: Official development assistance
9de63fa4256b.section: Problem areas and alternatives > Problem areas
9de63fa4256b.sentence: ODA is widely acknowledged to be an untidy and somewhat arbitrary category of aid, its definition having been agreed by the DAC members only with difficulty and awkward compromises.

7de949e9acd9.title: Official development assistance
7de949e9acd9.section: Problem areas and alternatives > Problem areas
7de949e9acd9.sentence: Seen as a measure of donor countries' contribution to a common effort or to altruistic purposes, ODA is criticized for including expenditures that may mostly benefit the donor country or that are already included in that country's international legal obligations.

2d38244317b3.title: Conservation finance
2d38244317b3.section: Sources of capital and actors > International public and multilateral finance
2d38244317b3.sentence: International public finance for conservation is commonly provided through Official development assistance (ODA) and related official flows, including grants and concessional lending as well as technical assistance and other support intended to promote development and welfare objectives in recipient countries.

7216233bd673.title: Economics of biodiversity
7216233bd673.sentence: Biodiversity plays an essential role in the global economy.

d38a98ecfdee.title: Economics of biodiversity
d38a98ecfdee.section: Impact of economic activity on biodiversity
d38a98ecfdee.sentence: Despite the role of biodiversity in underpinning the economy, economic activities often cause harm to biodiversity and the economic incentives they provide mean that they are often favoured over conservation and restoration activities.

0184c95c01ad.title: Economics of biodiversity
0184c95c01ad.sentence: This includes its role in providing ecosystem services - the benefits that humans get from ecosystems.

61036d702314.title: Economics of biodiversity
61036d702314.sentence: Biodiversity plays a major role in the productivity and functioning of ecosystems, affects their ability to provide ecosystem services.

ebabf456a0be.title: Economics of biodiversity
ebabf456a0be.sentence: For example, biodiversity is a source of food, medication, and materials used in industry.

a2814ab03b2f.title: Economics of biodiversity
a2814ab03b2f.sentence: Recreation and tourism are also examples of human economic activities that rely on these benefits.

6fe65a58d93f.title: Economics of biodiversity
6fe65a58d93f.sentence: Examples of some of the raw materials that originate from biodiversity include wood, plant fibers (such as cotton), animal fibers (such as wool and silk).

3d5bd6bb2875.title: Economics of biodiversity
3d5bd6bb2875.sentence: In 2018, the WWF Living Planet Report argues that the whole global economy of US$125 trillion ultimately relies on nature.

af71d320c936.title: Economics of biodiversity
af71d320c936.sentence: The majority of species have yet to be evaluated for their current or future economic importance.

1ebe06441f51.title: Economics of biodiversity
1ebe06441f51.sentence: The benefits of biodiversity are often evaluated in an anthropocentric way and the inherent value of biodiversity, outside of its benefits to humanity, has been debated by economists.

971c218417ff.title: Economics of biodiversity
971c218417ff.sentence: The field of biomimetics is dedicated to the emulation of models, systems, and elements from nature to solve complex human problems.

ee4f5e01b064.title: Economics of biodiversity
ee4f5e01b064.sentence: For example, the ridges on pectoral fins of humpback whales have inspired the shape of wind turbine blades.

32e9dd40c3e0.title: Conservation finance
32e9dd40c3e0.sentence: Conservation finance is the practice of raising and managing capital to support land, water, and resource conservation.

d11fbb2e9f5f.title: Conservation finance
d11fbb2e9f5f.sentence: It draws on public, private, and nonprofit funding sources, and can use instruments ranging from loans and grants to tax incentives and market-based mechanisms, at scales from local to national.

94978958fdbc.title: Conservation finance
94978958fdbc.sentence: Conservationists have traditionally relied upon private, philanthropic capital in the form of solicited donations and foundation grants, and public, governmental funds in the form of tax incentives, ballot measures, bonds, and agency appropriations, to fund conservation projects and initiatives.

943d99dcbcd8.title: Conservation finance
943d99dcbcd8.sentence: In this usage, fundraising and funding refer to raising and distributing non-repayable support, such as donations, foundation grants, and government appropriations, to pay for conservation work, while conservation finance refers to using a broader set of financial tools and capital sources to mobilise and manage capital for conservation outcomes.

5cbc0fb25919.title: Conservation finance
5cbc0fb25919.sentence: Proponents of conservation finance often argue that existing public and philanthropic funding flows are far below estimated global conservation needs; one widely cited estimate compared annual needs of hundreds of billions of dollars with much lower annual flows directed to conservation finance.

48aa1605b989.title: Conservation finance
48aa1605b989.sentence: Analyses of conservation finance commonly describe a gap between estimated conservation funding needs and the scale of finance that is mobilised and tracked for nature-related outcomes, alongside methodological challenges in classifying and aggregating biodiversity-related expenditures and investments.

769095f286be.title: Conservation finance
769095f286be.sentence: In response, conservation finance has been described as leveraging philanthropic and government resources with other sources of capital, including capital markets, through tools such as debt financing, tax benefits, private equity investments, and project finance.

abb1cb433ea6.title: Conservation finance
abb1cb433ea6.sentence: In response, conservation finance is sometimes framed as expanding the set of tools and capital sources used for conservation, including approaches that seek to leverage philanthropic and government resources with capital from financial markets, such as debt financing, tax benefits, private equity, and project finance.

662c7e1c1318.title: Conservation finance
662c7e1c1318.sentence: Early examples include debt-for-nature swaps (developed in the 1980s) and the later growth of incentive-based approaches such as payments for ecosystem services.

2fd059e6af51.title: Conservation finance
2fd059e6af51.sentence: By the mid-2000s, conservation finance was increasingly described as a distinct field, with reference works cataloguing instruments ranging from land-protection tools and dedicated funds to market-based mechanisms and investment structures.

57f5d0247f40.title: Conservation finance
57f5d0247f40.sentence: More recent policy and market analyses emphasise mobilising larger volumes of private capital for nature-related outcomes, including through labelled bond markets and blended finance structures that combine public or philanthropic capital with private investment to improve project risk–return characteristics.

7ea0d664fad6.title: Conservation finance
7ea0d664fad6.sentence: Conservation finance transactions are typically structured around an identifiable source of cash flow or budget authority that can support conservation activities over time.

09fd7f2ff233.title: Debt-for-nature swap
09fd7f2ff233.sentence: Debt-for-nature swaps are financial transactions in which a portion of a developing nation's foreign debt is forgiven in exchange for local investments in environmental conservation measures.

c0ff2db3a21d.title: Conservation finance
c0ff2db3a21d.sentence: A debt-for-nature swap is a transaction in which a portion of a country's external debt is purchased or forgiven--often at a discount--and the debtor government commits local-currency funding and/or policy measures for conservation.

dcabf33fd231.title: Debt-for-nature swap
dcabf33fd231.sentence: The debt-for-nature swaps concept was first given birth by Thomas Lovejoy of the World Wildlife Fund in 1987 as an opportunity to deal with the problems of developing-nation indebtedness and its consequent deleterious effect on the environment.

a9b7ac10c8d9.title: Debt-for-nature swap
a9b7ac10c8d9.sentence: In the wake of the Latin American debt crisis that resulted in steep reductions to the environmental conservation ability of highly indebted nations, Lovejoy suggested that ameliorating debt and promoting conservation could be done at the same time.

956c97e6b58c.title: Conservation finance
956c97e6b58c.sentence: A widely cited early swap was agreed in 1987 between the Government of Bolivia and Conservation International (CI), under which CI acquired US$650,000 of Bolivian external debt for US$100,000.

9ee685019652.title: Conservation finance
9ee685019652.sentence: Bolivia undertook conservation policy actions and committed local-currency funding for management activities in the Beni Biosphere Reserve and adjacent protected areas.

3e5537e84ac3.title: Debt-for-nature swap
3e5537e84ac3.sentence: Participation in debt-for-nature swaps has been restricted primarily to countries where the risk of default on debt payments is high.

ddae8b0349b1.title: Debt-for-nature swap
ddae8b0349b1.sentence: In these circumstances, the funder can purchase the debt at well below its face value.

19d7f6e0a34f.title: Debt-for-nature swap
19d7f6e0a34f.sentence: The national government of the indebted country agrees to a payment schedule on the amount of the debt forgiven, usually paid through the nation’s central bank, in local currency or ponds.

09d7fad10c20.title: Debt-for-nature swap
09d7fad10c20.sentence: Most swaps occur in tropical countries, which contain many diverse species of flora and fauna.

44ac00122f34.title: Debt-for-nature swap
44ac00122f34.sentence: Also, countries that have engaged in debt-for-nature swaps typically have several threatened or endangered species, experience rapid deforestation, and have relatively stable, often democratic, political systems.

804b524d081a.title: Debt-for-nature swap
804b524d081a.sentence: Since 1987, debt-for-nature agreements have generated over US$1 billion for conservation in developing countries.

17e5a0b137ac.title: Debt-for-nature swap
17e5a0b137ac.sentence: During this period, conservation organizations and national governments negotiated swaps at a rate of approximately five agreements per year.

8d2d8404f640.title: Debt-for-nature swap
8d2d8404f640.sentence: Since 2000, the number of swap agreements has dropped to about two per year.

c220393d8333.title: Debt-for-nature swap
c220393d8333.sentence: The decline in the number of debt-for-nature swaps in recent years likely results in part from the higher prices of commercial debt in secondary markets.

ecdf85268620.title: Conservation finance
ecdf85268620.sentence: Because swaps convert external debt obligations into domestically managed conservation spending commitments, analyses describe governance and implementation capacity as important for effectiveness, and note that swap experience has informed later conservation financing approaches such as conservation trust funds.

6e2895a0bf10.title: Debt-for-nature swap
6e2895a0bf10.sentence: Since the first swap occurred between Conservation International and Bolivia in 1987, many national governments and conservation organizations have engaged in debt-for-nature swaps.

ebaf821e838b.title: Blended finance
ebaf821e838b.sentence: Blend finance is defined as "the strategic use of development finance and philanthropic funds to mobilize private capital flows to emerging and frontier markets", resulting in positive results for both investors and communities.

2e568b40241c.title: Conservation finance
2e568b40241c.sentence: Blended finance refers to the strategic use of development or public finance to mobilise additional private finance towards sustainable development objectives, including by improving project risk-return characteristics (for example, through concessional capital, guarantees, or other structuring mechanisms).

dc933ee2d77e.title: Blended finance
dc933ee2d77e.sentence: The term blended finance implies the mixing of both public and private funds through a common investment scheme or deal, with each party using their expertise in a complementary way.

cd1636a5878d.title: Blended finance
cd1636a5878d.sentence: As such, blended finance is designed to support progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) set forth by the United Nations.

b1617c3ff80b.title: Blended finance
b1617c3ff80b.sentence: Meeting the SDGs will require an additional $2.5 trillion in private and public financing per year as of 2017 estimates, and an additional $13.5 trillion to implement the COP21 Paris climate accord.

085985400416.title: Blended finance
085985400416.sentence: Philanthropic and concessional funds are placed in subordinate or first-loss positions to absorb initial risk.

59afce48d102.title: Blended finance
59afce48d102.sentence: This reassures commercial investors that their principal is protected, allowing them to participate in projects they would otherwise avoid.

7853f4b3a51b.title: Blended finance
7853f4b3a51b.sentence: Each dollar of concessional capital can attract multiple dollars of private investment—often 3× to 10× leverage depending on the structure.

184f8e3ad694.title: Blended finance
184f8e3ad694.sentence: The classic example involves a $2 million philanthropic first-loss layer drawing $10 million in private capital for a village electrification project, thus achieving a 5× multiplier.

6fa3f492f91a.title: Blended finance
6fa3f492f91a.sentence: In 2018, blended finance principles were adopted by the OECD's Development Assistance Committee to guide the design and implementation of the concept.

005d934756f3.title: Blended finance
005d934756f3.sentence: Building upon evidence from a previous survey done on behalf of the World Economic Forum, the OECD released recent findings which identified 180 blended finance funds and facilities, with $60.2 billion in assets invested across 111 developing countries and impacting over 177 million lives, demonstrating the potential of blended finance to close the funding gap required to finance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and deliver development outcomes.

a24e58721ba4.title: Blended finance
a24e58721ba4.sentence: Critics argue that these financial arrangements often shift profits to private actors - mostly in the Global North - while placing financial risks on Southern governments.

e0cd9641a839.title: Blended finance
e0cd9641a839.sentence: The complexity of these financial structures can undermine transparency and accountability, as commercial confidentiality limits public oversight.

679d9e3a9f74.title: Conservation finance
679d9e3a9f74.sentence: Nature-related blended finance structures are discussed as one way to address barriers to private investment, such as risk, small deal sizes, and transaction costs, by combining private capital with public or philanthropic capital in a single structure.

e5ae4020c4df.title: Diversification (finance)
e5ae4020c4df.sentence: In finance, diversification is the process of allocating capital in a way that reduces the exposure to any one particular asset or risk.

ea0f3cffaba3.title: Diversification (finance)
ea0f3cffaba3.sentence: A common path towards diversification is to reduce risk or volatility by investing in a variety of assets.

df41bba30613.title: Diversification (finance)
df41bba30613.sentence: The simplest example of diversification is provided by the proverb "Don't put all your eggs in one basket".

a7f8a83b5bd8.title: Diversification (finance)
a7f8a83b5bd8.sentence: There is more risk of losing one egg, but less risk of losing all of them.

187d42260530.title: Diversification (finance)
187d42260530.sentence: If asset prices do not change in perfect synchrony, a diversified portfolio will have less variance than the weighted average variance of its constituent assets, and often less volatility than the least volatile of its constituents.

0fef86c7257d.title: Diversification (finance)
0fef86c7257d.sentence: The return on a diversified portfolio can never exceed that of the top-performing investment, and indeed will always be lower than the highest return (unless all returns are identical).

a9e703caeb9e.title: Diversification (finance)
a9e703caeb9e.sentence: Conversely, the diversified portfolio's return will always be higher than that of the worst-performing investment.

a7f492cd4d4c.title: Diversification (finance)
a7f492cd4d4c.sentence: That is the role of diversification: it narrows the range of possible outcomes.

6e7035af9f22.title: Diversification (finance)
6e7035af9f22.sentence: In finance, an example of an undiversified portfolio is to hold only one stock.

c04015d543fb.title: Diversification (finance)
c04015d543fb.sentence: This is risky; it is not unusual for a single stock to go down 50% in one year.

012cd7b25a0d.title: Diversification (finance)
012cd7b25a0d.section: An empirical example relating diversification to risk reduction
012cd7b25a0d.sentence: In 1977 Edwin Elton and Martin Gruber worked out an empirical example of the gains from diversification.

965410c6c657.title: Diversification (finance)
965410c6c657.section: An empirical example relating diversification to risk reduction
965410c6c657.sentence: The result for n=30 is close to n=1,000, and even four stocks provide most of the reduction in risk compared with one stock.

12799fc58d36.title: Diversification (finance)
12799fc58d36.sentence: Longin and Solnik (1995) showed that correlations among major international equity markets changed over time, while later studies found that correlations tend to increase during periods of market stress, reducing diversification benefits when investors may need them most.

10de08761afc.title: Trophy hunting
10de08761afc.sentence: Trophy hunting is a form of hunting for sport in which parts of the hunted wild animals are kept and displayed as trophies.

6429edf4812b.title: Trophy hunting
6429edf4812b.sentence: The parts most commonly kept vary by species but often include the head, hide, tusks, horns, or antlers.

552fd80122d6.title: Trophy hunting
552fd80122d6.sentence: Trophy hunting can provide economic incentives to conserve areas for wildlife: 'if it pays it stays'; there are research studies corroborating this in Conservation Biology, Journal of Sustainable Tourism, Wildlife Conservation by Sustainable Use, and Animal Conservation.

98779add41f6.title: Trophy hunting
98779add41f6.section: Influence in conservation > In Africa > Financial support of conservation efforts
98779add41f6.sentence: The International Union for Conservation of Nature recognizes that trophy hunting, when well-managed, can generate significant economic incentives for the conservation of target species and their habitats outside of protected areas.

eef4c9fdf35c.title: Trophy hunting
eef4c9fdf35c.section: Influence in conservation > In Africa > Effects on habitat loss
eef4c9fdf35c.sentence: A 2005 paper by Nigel Leader-Williams and colleagues in the Journal of International Wildlife Law and Policy asserted that the legalization of white rhinoceros hunting in South Africa motivated private landowners to reintroduce the species onto their lands.

f15674092dad.title: Trophy hunting
f15674092dad.section: Influence in conservation > In Africa > Effects on habitat loss
f15674092dad.sentence: As a result, white rhinos increased from fewer than one hundred individuals to more than 11,000.

448789597c4c.title: Trophy hunting
448789597c4c.section: Influence in conservation > In Africa > Effects of trophy hunting on animal populations
448789597c4c.sentence: When poorly managed, trophy hunting can cause negative ecological impacts for the target species such as altered age/sex structures, social disruption, deleterious genetic effects, and even population declines in the event of excessive off-takes, as well as threaten the conservation and influence the behavior of non-target species.

84175e426a30.title: Trophy hunting
84175e426a30.sentence: Similarly, a 2017 report by the Australian-based Economists at Large says that trophy hunting amounted to less than one percent of tourism revenue in eight African countries.

0673bd514701.title: Trophy hunting
0673bd514701.sentence: Economists at Large, an NGO promoting social justice, animal welfare and sustainability, claim that little of this 190 million reaches communities.

24bc39794379.title: Fiduciary
24bc39794379.sentence: A fiduciary is a person who holds a legal or ethical relationship of trust with one or more other parties (legal person or group of persons).

bee120c82bed.title: Fiduciary
bee120c82bed.sentence: Typically, a fiduciary prudently takes care of money or other assets for another person.

c83a663193c4.title: Fiduciary
c83a663193c4.sentence: In such a relation, good conscience requires the fiduciary to act at all times for the sole benefit and interest of the one who trusts.

cbea77845b35.title: Fiduciary
cbea77845b35.sentence: Likewise, financial advisers, financial planners, and asset managers, including managers of pension plans, endowments, and other tax-exempt assets, are considered fiduciaries under applicable statutes and laws.

7b095fb3be16.title: Fiduciary
7b095fb3be16.sentence: The most common circumstance where a fiduciary duty will arise is between a trustee, whether real or juristic, and a beneficiary.

6e23460dcdd9.title: Fiduciary
6e23460dcdd9.section: Fiduciary duties under Delaware corporate law
6e23460dcdd9.sentence: The corporate law of Delaware is the most influential in the United States, as more than 50% of publicly traded companies in the United States, including 64% of the Fortune 500, have chosen to incorporate in that state.

64a116a7c75e.title: Fiduciary
64a116a7c75e.section: Fiduciary duties under Delaware corporate law
64a116a7c75e.sentence: Under Delaware law, officers, directors and other control persons of corporations and other entities owe three primary fiduciary duties, (1) the duty of care, (2) the duty of loyalty and (3) the duty of good faith.

cd22febc066f.title: Fiduciary
cd22febc066f.sentence: Therefore, it is said the fiduciary has a duty not to be in a situation where personal interests and fiduciary duty conflict, a duty not to be in a situation where his fiduciary duty conflicts with another fiduciary duty, and not to profit from his fiduciary position without express knowledge and consent.

0a45b122def9.title: Fiduciary
0a45b122def9.sentence: A fiduciary must not profit from the fiduciary position.

49bdee584241.title: Economics of biodiversity
49bdee584241.section: Impact of economic activity on biodiversity
49bdee584241.sentence: This contributes to the loss of biodiversity observed on a global scale with numerous causes, such as habitat loss, land-use change, pollution, and overexploitation.

5d1d365dced2.title: Economics of biodiversity
5d1d365dced2.section: Impact of economic activity on biodiversity
5d1d365dced2.sentence: According to an estimate from BCG, more than 90% of the anthropogenic drivers of biodiversity loss result from economic activities linked to agriculture, infrastructure, fashion, and energy.

80254e82ee91.title: Economics of biodiversity
80254e82ee91.section: Impact of economic activity on biodiversity
80254e82ee91.sentence: In addition, the IUCN estimates that 79% of threatened species are impacted by agriculture, infrastructure, and energy and mining activities.

50f57298e2e8.title: Economics of biodiversity
50f57298e2e8.section: Impact of economic activity on biodiversity
50f57298e2e8.sentence: The failure to halt terrestrial biodiversity loss between 2000 and 2010 was estimated to cost the global economy $500 billion.

16af42b6bd59.title: Economics of biodiversity
16af42b6bd59.section: Impact of economic activity on biodiversity
16af42b6bd59.sentence: Continued biodiversity loss and environmental degradation poses a long-term risk to society and the economy, such as by increasing the risk of pandemics, floods, and droughts.

bba8a670416e.title: Bond (finance)
bba8a670416e.sentence: The quality of the issue refers to the probability that the bondholders will receive the amounts promised at the due dates.

8b2a4dd8b0ff.title: Bond (finance)
8b2a4dd8b0ff.sentence: In other words, credit quality tells investors how likely the borrower is going to default.

70d801175fbe.title: Bond (finance)
70d801175fbe.sentence: High-yield bonds are bonds that are rated below investment grade by the credit rating agencies.

103447aa1c1b.title: Bond (finance)
103447aa1c1b.sentence: As these bonds are riskier than investment grade bonds, investors expect to earn a higher yield.

d2dbea4d7dbd.title: Bond (finance)
d2dbea4d7dbd.sentence: The yield is the rate of return received from investing in the bond.

20feb0bea1e8.title: Bond (finance)
20feb0bea1e8.sentence: - The current yield, or running yield: the annual interest payment divided by the current market price of the bond (often the clean price).

0cb2091ab433.title: Bond (finance)
0cb2091ab433.sentence: - The yield to maturity (or redemption yield, as it is termed in the United Kingdom) is an estimate of the total rate of return anticipated to be earned by an investor who buys a bond at a given market price, holds it to maturity, and receives all interest payments and the capital redemption on schedule.

6fa2965048f3.title: Bond (finance)
6fa2965048f3.sentence: It is a more useful measure of the return on a bond than current yield because it takes into account the present value of future interest payments and principal repaid at maturity.

4afae3902292.title: Bond (finance)
4afae3902292.sentence: The yield and price of a bond are inversely related so that when market interest rates rise, bond prices fall and vice versa.

aacd8af07730.title: Bond (finance)
aacd8af07730.sentence: Bonds can be categorised in several ways, such as the type of issuer, the currency, the term of the bond (length of time to maturity) and the conditions applying to the bond.

b25831cc0ace.title: Bond (finance)
b25831cc0ace.section: Types > The nature of the issuer and the security offered
b25831cc0ace.sentence: - Government bonds, often also called treasury bonds, are issued by a sovereign national government.

35cc059b1016.title: Bond (finance)
35cc059b1016.section: Types > The nature of the issuer and the security offered
35cc059b1016.sentence: Risk-free bonds are the safest bonds, with the lowest interest rate.

2a0b618acf78.title: Bond (finance)
2a0b618acf78.section: Types > The term of the bond
2a0b618acf78.sentence: Typically, a bond with term to maturity of under five years would be called a short bond; 5 to 15 years would be "medium", and over 15 years would be "long"; but the numbers may vary in different markets.

c27fa5e45d5c.title: Bond (finance)
c27fa5e45d5c.section: Types > The conditions applying to the bond
c27fa5e45d5c.sentence: - Fixed rate bonds have interest payments ("coupon"), usually semi-annual, that remains constant throughout the life of the bond.

5caa880254c8.title: Bond (finance)
5caa880254c8.section: Types > The conditions applying to the bond
5caa880254c8.sentence: - Floating rate notes (FRNs, floaters) have a variable coupon that is linked to a reference rate of interest, such as Libor or Euribor.

67af8c8d5c68.title: Bond (finance)
67af8c8d5c68.section: Types > Bonds with embedded options for the holder
67af8c8d5c68.sentence: - Convertible bonds let a bondholder exchange a bond to a number of shares of the issuer's common stock.

4b6686e433de.title: Bond (finance)
4b6686e433de.section: Types > Bonds with embedded options for the holder
4b6686e433de.sentence: These are known as hybrid securities, because they combine equity and debt features.

6b6e055007ae.title: Conservation finance
6b6e055007ae.section: Challenges and criticism > Additionality, leakage and permanence
6b6e055007ae.sentence: A recurring critique of performance-based and market-based conservation mechanisms is whether financed actions are additional--that is, whether they achieve conservation outcomes that would not have occurred in the absence of the payment or financing arrangement.

93d3ec889baa.title: Conservation finance
93d3ec889baa.section: Challenges and criticism > Additionality, leakage and permanence
93d3ec889baa.sentence: Related concerns include leakage (or spillovers), where conservation in one location may displace environmentally damaging activity to another area, reducing net benefits.

f0ede9e90ec0.title: Conservation finance
f0ede9e90ec0.section: Challenges and criticism > Additionality, leakage and permanence
f0ede9e90ec0.sentence: Critics also raise permanence concerns, particularly where outcomes depend on continued compliance over long time horizons.

e0b1820bd667.title: Conservation finance
e0b1820bd667.section: Challenges and criticism > Additionality, leakage and permanence
e0b1820bd667.sentence: Analyses of conservation incentive programmes note that durability of effects can depend on contract length, enforcement capacity, land-use pressures, and whether conservation behaviours persist after payments end.

f280a615d353.title: Conservation finance
f280a615d353.section: Challenges and criticism > Additionality, leakage and permanence
f280a615d353.sentence: Reviews of PES design and evidence have noted practical difficulties in establishing baselines and counterfactuals, which can affect claims about additionality and impact.

9d2e68694318.title: Conservation finance
9d2e68694318.sentence: Reporting may distinguish between outputs (such as funded activities or area under management) and outcomes (such as changes in ecological condition), but attribution can be difficult because conservation results may depend on baselines, counterfactuals, and long time horizons.

8c0209533102.title: Return on investment
8c0209533102.sentence: To address the lack of integration of the short and long term importance, value and risks associated with natural and social capital into the traditional ROI calculation, companies are valuing their environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance through an integrated management approach to reporting that expands ROI to Return on Integration.

e30ea7b8dde0.title: Return on investment
e30ea7b8dde0.sentence: This allows companies to value their investments not just for their financial return but also the long term environmental and social return of their investments.

94c8b47d6a00.title: Return on investment
94c8b47d6a00.sentence: The social cost of carbon is one value that can be incorporated into Return on Integration calculations to encompass the damage to society from greenhouse gas emissions that result from an investment.

6d66d9fb48ec.title: Return on investment
6d66d9fb48ec.sentence: This is an integrated approach to reporting that supports Integrated Bottom Line (IBL) decision making, which takes triple bottom line (TBL) a step further and combines financial, environmental and social performance reporting into one balance sheet.

3d243b80c3de.title: Return on investment
3d243b80c3de.sentence: For example, social return on investment (SROI) is a principles-based method for measuring extra-financial value (i.e., environmental and social value not currently reflected in conventional financial accounts) relative to resources invested.

807050a2f41e.title: Conservation easement
807050a2f41e.sentence: Landowners in the United States who donate a "qualifying" conservation easement to a "qualified" land protection organization under § 170(h) of the Internal Revenue Code may be eligible for a federal income tax deduction equal to the value of their donation.

75bf38b7328e.title: Conservation easement
75bf38b7328e.sentence: The landowner who grants a conservation easement continues to manage and otherwise privately own the land and may receive significant state and federal tax advantages for having donated and/or sold the conservation easement.

47da42401daf.title: Conservation easement
47da42401daf.sentence: The value of the easement donation, as determined by a qualified appraiser, equals the difference between the fair market value of the property before and after the easement takes effect.

240c3b8cdbf3.title: Conservation easement
240c3b8cdbf3.sentence: To qualify for this income tax deduction, the easement must be: a) perpetual; b) held by a qualified governmental or non-profit organization; and, c) serve a valid "conservation purpose", meaning the property must have an appreciable natural, scenic, historic, scientific, recreational, or open space value.

4ed6f80e7686.title: Conservation easement
4ed6f80e7686.sentence: For landowners who will leave sizable estates upon their death, the most important financial impact of a conservation easement may be a significant reduction in estate taxes.

58d048d575e5.title: Conservation easement
58d048d575e5.sentence: In other words, heirs will only have to pay estate taxes on preserved farmland values, and not full development values.

12d96eeb9aca.title: Conservation easement
12d96eeb9aca.sentence: Some states have granted credits that can be used to pay state income tax to donors of qualified conservation easements.

957262719f44.title: Conservation easement
957262719f44.sentence: For this reason, some states, including Colorado and Virginia, have made the state tax credit transferable; the landowner can sell their credit to someone else.

e8ade2d4a981.title: Conservation easement
e8ade2d4a981.sentence: Many conservation easements are purchased with funds from federal, state, and local governments, nonprofit organizations, or private donors.

d7f5181d6961.title: Conservation easement
d7f5181d6961.sentence: In these cases, landowners are paid directly for the purchase of the conservation easement.

6d3cdb2e7a70.title: Conservation easement
6d3cdb2e7a70.sentence: The Farm Bill, updated every five or more years, provides an important source of funds for conservation easement purchase.

b2d2f900b762.title: Conservation easement
b2d2f900b762.sentence: The 2014 Farm Bill created the Agricultural Conservation Easement Program (ACEP) by consolidating the Farm and Ranch Lands Protection Program, the Grassland Reserve Program, and the Wetlands Reserve Program.

29f4421be07e.title: Conservation easement
29f4421be07e.sentence: Commonly used funding sources include real estate transfer tax, legislative bonds, and lottery proceeds.

29ffaba8c582.title: Conservation easement
29ffaba8c582.sentence: Many states and counties have programs for the purchase of agricultural conservation easements (PACE) to protect productive farmland from non-agricultural development.

0bcbbf3a0ddf.title: Official development assistance
0bcbbf3a0ddf.sentence: The target of spending 0.7% of gross national income on ODA is the best known international aid target.

c6f294662848.title: Official development assistance
c6f294662848.sentence: It was formalised on 24 October 1970, when the UN General Assembly adopted a resolution which included the goal that "Each economically advanced country will progressively increase its official development assistance to the developing countries and will exert its best efforts to reach a minimum net amount of 0.7% of its gross national product at market prices by the middle of the Decade [by 1975]." Sweden and the Netherlands were the first countries to meet the target, in 1974, but it has been met by few other countries since.

bccb04215dee.title: Official development assistance
bccb04215dee.section: Concept and definition > ODA as a proportion of donor national incomes
bccb04215dee.sentence: After that, while donors' incomes continued to grow, the level of ODA remained around 0.3 - 0.35%, except when it dipped below that level in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

c1aca29ad700.title: Official development assistance
c1aca29ad700.section: Concept and definition > Donor countries by percentage of gross national income
c1aca29ad700.sentence: In 2019 six countries met the longstanding UN target for an ODA/GNI ratio of 0.7%.

4f9c116037bd.title: Official development assistance
4f9c116037bd.section: Concept and definition > Donor countries by percentage of gross national income
4f9c116037bd.sentence: In 2021, the UK reduced its annual aid budget from 0.7% of gross national income to 0.5%.

506256944f9d.title: Official development assistance
506256944f9d.sentence: Tied aid is aid given on condition that the money is used to buy things from the donor country or a severely limited group of countries.

3c8a8171e59c.title: Official development assistance
3c8a8171e59c.sentence: The legitimacy of tied ODA has long been a point of contention within the DAC.

b5ca33e5bcef.title: Official development assistance
b5ca33e5bcef.sentence: Targets have been set to reduce tying: for example in the 2005 Paris Declaration and the DAC's "Recommendation" on untying, first agreed in 1998 and subsequently maintained in revised forms.

79a71f0c7af3.title: Official development assistance
79a71f0c7af3.sentence: A major review of the Paris Declaration targets found that, in 2009, 51% (by value) of contracts was spent in the country of the donor, even though donors were reporting only 14% of their aid as tied.

1624ac9c7a0d.title: Debt-for-nature swap
1624ac9c7a0d.sentence: Debt-for-nature swaps produce only minor debt reductions and generate far less funding than the face value of the debt purchased in the secondary market.

a9cb0778e5cc.title: Debt-for-nature swap
a9cb0778e5cc.sentence: Critics of debt-for-nature swaps argue that they do not generate funds where the needs are greatest.

88e88d3ab4ac.title: Debt-for-nature swap
88e88d3ab4ac.sentence: Debt for nature swaps are usually actioned by an indebted nation's elite, not the peasantry who may traditionally have owned or at least used the land in question.

51e91bf3d05b.title: Debt-for-nature swap
51e91bf3d05b.sentence: The amount of public debt relieved by debt-for-nature swaps, even in the countries that participate in swaps regularly, accounts for less than 1% of total external debt.

2a84beebb464.title: Debt-for-nature swap
2a84beebb464.sentence: Early in the history of debt-for-nature swaps, nearly three-quarters of the total funds generated went to Costa Rica, while other countries with needs equal to or exceeding those of Costa Rica did not receive any.

12c9f20f5789.title: Debt-for-nature swap
12c9f20f5789.sentence: Brazil, for example, has had limited involvement in debt-for-nature swaps though it has experienced rapid deforestation.

bf9c382195f7.title: Debt-for-nature swap
bf9c382195f7.sentence: Some early debt-for-nature swaps tended to overlook the people living on the land set aside for conservation.

b6e336b3a8bc.title: Debt-for-nature swap
b6e336b3a8bc.section: Criticism > Meddling in the internal affairs
b6e336b3a8bc.sentence: This kind of intervention was labeled as environmental or eco-colonialism.

a44dcba95f4c.title: Debt-for-nature swap
a44dcba95f4c.sentence: Debt for nature swaps have often been described as agreements in which all parties benefit and that there are no disadvantages.

165d86d7131e.title: Debt-for-nature swap
165d86d7131e.sentence: In a commercial debt-for-nature swap or three-party debt-for-nature swap, a non-governmental organization (NGO) acts as the funder/donor and purchases debt titles from commercial banks on the secondary market.

48e356d067e2.title: Debt-for-nature swap
48e356d067e2.sentence: Bilateral debt-for-nature swaps take place between two governments.

48ce7996620a.title: Debt-for-nature swap
48ce7996620a.sentence: Multilateral debt-for-nature swaps are similar to bilateral swaps but involve international transactions of more than two national governments.

35e3b193208f.title: Debt-for-nature swap
35e3b193208f.sentence: The NGO transfers the debt title to the debtor country, and in exchange the country agrees to either enact certain environmental policies or endow a government bond in the name of a conservation organization, with the aim of funding conservation programs.

3301705aacc6.title: Debt-for-nature swap
3301705aacc6.sentence: In a bilateral swap, a creditor country forgives a portion of the public bilateral debt of a debtor nation in exchange for environmental commitments from that country.

533f8b746290.title: Debt-for-nature swap
533f8b746290.sentence: In total, recorded third-party debt-for-nature swaps have generated nearly US$140 million in conservation funding from 1987-2010 (see Table 1).

7a9dd2141801.title: Debt-for-nature swap
7a9dd2141801.sentence: Recorded bilateral and multilateral debt-for-nature swaps have generated nearly US$900 million in total conservation funding from 1987-2010 (see Table 1).

0bfffc7ab016.title: Economics of biodiversity
0bfffc7ab016.sentence: Agricultural biodiversity (agrobiodiversity) refers to all the components of biodiversity that are relevant to food and agriculture, and that make up agricultural ecosystems.

cbd9c7ee4512.title: Economics of biodiversity
cbd9c7ee4512.sentence: Biodiversity plays an essential economic role in agriculture as the origin of all crops and domesticated livestock, contributing both to food security and to livelihoods.

adceda1b6535.title: Economics of biodiversity
adceda1b6535.sentence: Around 25% of the global population is estimated to work in agriculture.

88fb4f9f97c2.title: Economics of biodiversity
88fb4f9f97c2.sentence: Estimating the economic value of biodiversity (and the costs of its continued loss) in agriculture and through the use of wild species for food is both challenging and controversial.

cd81d20971fe.title: Economics of biodiversity
cd81d20971fe.section: Agriculture and food > Aquaculture and fishing
cd81d20971fe.sentence: By 2006, over 3 billion people were dependent on marine and coastal biodiversity for their livelihoods and 38 million people were estimated to be directly employed by fishing.

cdf658130cb8.title: Economics of biodiversity
cdf658130cb8.sentence: Biodiversity plays a vital role in the maintenance of human health and a wide variety of products derived from plants, animals, and fungi are used in medicine.

d29c09a673d4.title: Economics of biodiversity
d29c09a673d4.sentence: Biodiversity acts as a source of medicinal compounds, impacts the provision of ecosystem services that improve health and protect against disease, and as an inspiration for biomedical techniques that could be utilised to cure diseases (such as CRISPR/Cas9).

6acf53cceb59.title: Economics of biodiversity
6acf53cceb59.sentence: Over 40% of pharmaceutical products are derived from nature, identified through indigenous knowledge and scientific methods, and 70% of all cancer drugs are natural or bioinspired products.

f87c1d09279a.title: Economics of biodiversity
f87c1d09279a.sentence: Wild plant species have been used for medicinal purposes since pre-historic times and over 60% of the world's population still depends on herbal medicine as their primary source of healthcare.

c93b7cfaf711.title: Economics of biodiversity
c93b7cfaf711.sentence: For example, quinine, derived from the bark of South American Cinchona trees is used as an anti-malarial.

48068857d920.title: Economics of biodiversity
48068857d920.sentence: Artemisinin, another anti-malarial, was isolated from sweet wormwood by Tu Youyou.

0fd044e041dd.title: Economics of biodiversity
0fd044e041dd.sentence: Through cultural ecosystem services, biodiversity provides economic benefits in the form of recreation and tourism, while also benefitting human wellbeing.

2c1391e1260f.title: Economics of biodiversity
2c1391e1260f.sentence: This includes outdoor recreation, such as hiking, hunting, fishing, and wildlife watching.

45bd77f36291.title: Economics of biodiversity
45bd77f36291.sentence: The revenue generated through tourism is vital to many economies worldwide and accounts for 10% of the global job market.

7bd9632fa44c.title: Economics of biodiversity
7bd9632fa44c.sentence: In 2023, the global ecotourism market was estimated to be worth US$216.49 billion.

9a06ea4e9985.title: Economics of biodiversity
9a06ea4e9985.sentence: Despite the economic benefits from biodiversity through tourism, the tourism industry has negative impacts on biodiversity.

78fcd542b9ef.title: Economics of biodiversity
78fcd542b9ef.sentence: For example, through habitat destruction and pollution.

eacbcf4967bb.title: Economics of biodiversity
eacbcf4967bb.sentence: As a result, sustainable tourism emerged with the aim of reducing the negative impacts of tourism on the environment.

6b966782bf91.title: Economics of biodiversity
6b966782bf91.section: Agriculture and food > Biological pest control
6b966782bf91.sentence: An important ecosystem function associated with biodiversity is pest control.

91a04f9b816b.title: Economics of biodiversity
91a04f9b816b.section: Agriculture and food > Biological pest control
91a04f9b816b.sentence: Control species can suppress pest populations and reduce loss of crop yields without the negative impacts of chemical pesticides.

671654080e03.title: Economics of biodiversity
671654080e03.section: Agriculture and food > Biological pest control
671654080e03.sentence: This has economic benefits and maintaining natural pest control is important to humanity's ability to grow crops.

17a2fdc47fd7.title: Economics of biodiversity
17a2fdc47fd7.section: Agriculture and food > Biological pest control
17a2fdc47fd7.sentence: However, its use can have unintended effects where control species are introduced without adequate research.

cf095640ad80.title: Economics of biodiversity
cf095640ad80.section: Agriculture and food > Biological pest control
cf095640ad80.sentence: For example, the cane toad was introduced to Queensland, Australia in 1935 to control cane beetles that attack sugarcane roots but are now regarded as an invasive species through their damaging impacts on native species.

c6ed621c0ad1.title: Blended finance
c6ed621c0ad1.sentence: Supporting mechanisms have been traditionally used by development funders in a Blended Finance package to attract and support private sector investors by managing risks and reducing transaction costs.

736ebe9b7447.title: Blended finance
736ebe9b7447.sentence: - Technical Assistance, or grant funds to supplement the capacity of investees and lower transaction costs.

38aa81d3e865.title: Blended finance
38aa81d3e865.sentence: - Risk Underwriting, to fully or partially protect the investor against risk through appropriate risk mitigation

21dfe0691175.title: Blended finance
21dfe0691175.sentence: - Market Incentives, guaranteed payments contingent on performance of future pricing and/or payment in exchange for upfront investment in new or distressed markets.

5b26fa4ab6ad.title: Blended finance
5b26fa4ab6ad.sentence: Through guarantees, insurance, or concessional tranches, blended finance reduces perceived and actual risks such as currency volatility, political instability, or credit default.

aa2e8d6f14d9.title: Blended finance
aa2e8d6f14d9.sentence: Because concessional capital is used catalytically rather than continuously, it can be recycled into new projects once investor confidence and repayment are established, multiplying development outcomes without expanding public budgets.

eaf520963692.title: Economics of biodiversity
eaf520963692.sentence: The illegal wildlife trade profits from biodiversity through the sale of products derived from non-domesticated animals, including those classed as endangered by the IUCN.

9bd838844de2.title: Economics of biodiversity
9bd838844de2.sentence: According to the Zoological Society of London, the illegal wildlife trade is estimated to be worth $23 billion a year.

7ae1d36b9364.title: Economics of biodiversity
7ae1d36b9364.sentence: Cultural demand (such as for bushmeat or use in traditional medicine) is one factor motivating the illegal wildlife trade, however, terrorist and criminal organisations engage in illicit trafficking of plants and animals to fund the purchase of weapons, fund civil conflicts, and other illegal activities.

74f847a41281.title: Economics of biodiversity
74f847a41281.sentence: Exploitation of biodiversity through wildlife smuggling has a negative impact on biodiversity itself, including by driving population declines, species extinctions, and the loss of genetic diversity.

506d92fb6fc7.title: Economics of biodiversity
506d92fb6fc7.sentence: It can also impact biodiversity through biosecurity risks, including the potential to spread diseases that native populations may not be resistant to and through the introduction of alien species.

f6ad299f28f9.title: Diversification (finance)
f6ad299f28f9.sentence: The capital asset pricing model introduced the concepts of diversifiable and non-diversifiable risk.

600dea6aeb71.title: Diversification (finance)
600dea6aeb71.sentence: Synonyms for diversifiable risk are idiosyncratic risk, unsystematic risk, and security-specific risk.

3ed9cd6925a5.title: Diversification (finance)
3ed9cd6925a5.sentence: Synonyms for non-diversifiable risk are systematic risk, beta risk and market risk.

17260d473f1d.title: Diversification (finance)
17260d473f1d.sentence: If one buys all the stocks in the S&P 500 one is obviously exposed only to movements in that index.

71bb6e852e23.title: Diversification (finance)
71bb6e852e23.sentence: If one buys a single stock in the S&P 500, one is exposed both to index movements and movements in the stock based on its underlying company.

8b801fbac502.title: Diversification (finance)
8b801fbac502.sentence: The second risk is called "diversifiable", because it can be reduced by diversifying among stocks.

39195b3d8399.title: Diversification (finance)
39195b3d8399.sentence: One simple measure of financial risk is variance of the return on the portfolio.

7cd64f797470.title: Diversification (finance)
7cd64f797470.sentence: Diversification can lower the variance of a portfolio's return below what it would be if the entire portfolio were invested in the asset with the lowest variance of return, even if the assets' returns are uncorrelated.

b2fa26e45610.title: Diversification (finance)
b2fa26e45610.sentence: If the fraction q of a one-unit (e.g. one-million-dollar) portfolio is placed in asset X and the fraction 1−q is placed in Y, the stochastic portfolio return is qx+(1−q)y.

6fed91ece328.title: Diversification (finance)
6fed91ece328.sentence: If x and y are uncorrelated, the variance of portfolio return is var(qx+(1−q)y)=q2σx2+(1−q)2σy2.

c2d4edb6d85a.title: Diversification (finance)
c2d4edb6d85a.sentence: The variance-minimizing value of q is q=σy2/[σx2+σy2], which is strictly between 0 and 1.

8d3206ae7e06.title: Diversification (finance)
8d3206ae7e06.sentence: Using this value of q in the expression for the variance of portfolio return gives the latter as σx2σy2/[σx2+σy2], which is less than what it would be at either of the undiversified values q=1 and q=0 (which respectively give portfolio return variance of σx2 and σy2).

0567d7a199bb.title: Diversification (finance)
0567d7a199bb.sentence: In the mean–variance framework developed by Harry Markowitz (Markowitz, 1952), portfolio risk depends not only on the variance of individual assets but also on the covariance among asset returns.

afccd7928aed.title: Land trust
afccd7928aed.sentence: Land trusts are nonprofit organizations which own and manage land, and sometimes waters.

28d32b0c1305.title: Land trust
28d32b0c1305.sentence: There are three common types of land trust, distinguished from one another by the ways in which they are legally structured and by the purposes for which they are organized and operated:

935c1b9b4f3c.title: Land trust
935c1b9b4f3c.sentence: - A community land trust (CLT) is a private, nonprofit corporation that acquires, manages, and develops land for a variety of purposes, primarily for the production and stewardship of affordable housing, although many CLTs are also engaged in non-residential buildings and uses.

f1b248859407.title: Land trust
f1b248859407.sentence: - A conservation land trust is a private, non-profit corporation in the US that acquires land or conservation easements for the purpose of limiting commercial development and preserving open space, natural areas, waterways, and/or productive farms and forests.

d2758e0c8bea.title: Land trust
d2758e0c8bea.sentence: Land trusts have been around at least since Roman times but their clearest history is from the time of King Henry VIII in England.

1e0e56d8fedd.title: Land trust
1e0e56d8fedd.sentence: In Australia, Aboriginal land trusts are a type of non-profit organisation that holds the freehold title to an area of land on behalf of a community of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

62eb39978493.title: Conservation land trust
62eb39978493.sentence: Conservation land trusts are nonprofit organizations that acquire and steward land or conservation easements for the purpose of achieving environmental, agricultural, recreational, and/or species conservation goals.

8cafbdd9ef6e.title: Land trust
8cafbdd9ef6e.sentence: Many different strategies are used to provide this protection, including outright acquisition of the land by the trust.

9e1bf40b19cb.title: Land trust
9e1bf40b19cb.sentence: In other cases, the land will remain in private hands, but the trust will purchase a conservation easement on the property to prevent development, or purchase any mining, logging, drilling, or development rights on the land.

1eb91e3cd74f.title: Land trust
1eb91e3cd74f.sentence: As non-profit organizations, land trusts rely on donations, grants and public land acquisition programs for operating expenses and for acquiring land and easements.

4168bf93ca7f.title: Land trust
4168bf93ca7f.sentence: Donors often provide monetary support, but it is common for conservation-minded landowners to donate an easement on their land, or the land itself.

2771eafa4389.title: Conservation land trust
2771eafa4389.sentence: Funding can be limited for the work of these organizations, such that many rely on volunteer labor.

8a1af094cf40.title: Land trust
8a1af094cf40.sentence: According to the 2005 National Land Trust Census, 31% of land trusts reported having at least one full-time staff member, 54% are all volunteer, and 15% have only part-time staff.

706e0ce1a010.title: Conservation land trust
706e0ce1a010.section: Regional land trusts > Land trusts in North America
706e0ce1a010.sentence: In the United States, the first conservation land trust organization was the Massachusetts Trustees of Reservations, founded in 1891.

ccdec4f663fe.title: Conservation land trust
ccdec4f663fe.section: Regional land trusts > Land trusts in North America
ccdec4f663fe.sentence: As of 2021, there were over 1,300 conservation land trusts in the United States, with 446 of these accredited by the Land Trust Accreditation Commission.

4cbdf976b1c7.title: Conservation land trust
4cbdf976b1c7.sentence: Although there are some global conservation land trust organizations that work across multiple continents, such as the World Land Trust and The Nature Conservancy, most land trusts focus on smaller regional areas.

82df3d87f470.title: Land trust
82df3d87f470.sentence: The last Census, conducted in 2003, reported that these trusts have protected almost 9.4 million acres (38,000 km2) of land in the United States, double the 4.7 million acres (19,000 km2) recorded in the 1998 survey.

7cdf230b8f75.title: Natural Asset Company
7cdf230b8f75.sentence: Natural Asset Companies, abbreviated as NACs, are designed to mobilize private investment for ecological conservation, nature-based solutions, and regenerative land management.

ab0785cda458.title: Natural Asset Company
ab0785cda458.sentence: Each NAC holds the rights to, and manages the productivity and ecological benefits of, natural assets such as forests, working ranches and farms, grasslands, or marine areas.

4e0af3c65cb8.title: Natural Asset Company
4e0af3c65cb8.sentence: NACs, which are managed by a board of directors and management team, are operated to maximize the ecological value of a designated area under management.

6ed46a1ca7f0.title: Natural Asset Company
6ed46a1ca7f0.sentence: They produce two types of reports: traditional financial statements (GAAP/IFRS) and Ecological Performance Reports (EPRs) to account for non-traditional natural asset and ecosystem services value.

6ac6bfb85686.title: Natural Asset Company
6ac6bfb85686.sentence: NACs assign value to ecosystem services, such as carbon retention, freshwater generation, groundwater storage, and erosion prevention.

6a3924b915f0.title: Natural Asset Company
6a3924b915f0.sentence: In 2021, IEG and ICE-owned New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) announced plans to introduce NACs as a publicly listed asset class designed to finance natural capital.

cf8791363e31.title: Natural Asset Company
cf8791363e31.sentence: The NYSE filed a listing proposal with the SEC, intending to allow NACs to be traded publicly, but withdrew the proposal in January 2024 amid political backlash and concerns about management of public lands in the U.S.

353672326d80.title: Natural Asset Company
353672326d80.sentence: From the right, critics argue NACs could be used to lock up public lands, enable land speculation, or result in unintended regulatory control over private land.

81d091c7972a.title: Natural Asset Company
81d091c7972a.sentence: Opposition from the left reflects concerns that market-based solutions are not a responsible mode of stewardship for natural assets.

3f2552a2c3ac.title: Conservation finance
3f2552a2c3ac.section: Instruments and mechanisms > Conservation trust funds
3f2552a2c3ac.sentence: Conservation trust funds (CTFs) are long-term financing mechanisms that provide grants to conservation projects and programmes, and are often structured as sinking funds or endowments intended to support conservation over extended time horizons.

b5d92d370fb8.title: Conservation finance
b5d92d370fb8.section: Instruments and mechanisms > Conservation trust funds
b5d92d370fb8.sentence: CTFs have been used to help fund protected area management and other conservation interventions, including by covering recurrent costs that can be difficult to sustain through short-term grants alone.

923bf67be3b0.title: Conservation finance
923bf67be3b0.sentence: Conservation finance arrangements often include requirements to monitor and report both the use of funds and the ecological results that financing is intended to support.

d76a75ba353e.title: Conservation finance
d76a75ba353e.sentence: The Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) has published recommendations that include disclosure of nature-related dependencies and impacts, as well as suggested approaches to metrics and targets, while noting that data availability and methodological differences can limit consistency across organisations.

8715c71d6942.title: Conservation finance
8715c71d6942.section: Challenges and criticism > Distributional equity and social concerns
8715c71d6942.sentence: Mechanisms used in conservation finance can raise distributional and participation questions, including who is eligible to receive payments or benefits, how programmes interact with land tenure and local livelihoods, and whether public funding disproportionately benefits wealthier landholders.

3352cc638f90.title: Conservation finance
3352cc638f90.sentence: The mix of sources that can contribute to nature-related outcomes includes domestic public expenditures, international public finance (including official development assistance), and private expenditures and investments.

899591a01fbb.title: Conservation finance
899591a01fbb.sentence: Market-rate capital can come from private investors as well as from public and philanthropic investors operating through development finance institutions and multilateral development banks.

c44141a29a39.title: Conservation finance
c44141a29a39.sentence: Intermediary and implementing organisations can include conservation non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and foundations.

0c70c4d943a0.title: Conservation finance
0c70c4d943a0.sentence: Large conservation NGOs can have significant expenditures, and NGOs may receive substantial revenue from governments and philanthropic foundations, which can complicate accounting for flows and risks double counting when estimating total finance.

6da67cfe5c2d.title: Conservation finance
6da67cfe5c2d.section: Sources of capital and actors > International public and multilateral finance
6da67cfe5c2d.sentence: Some analyses describe public and philanthropic capital as playing a catalytic role in conservation finance, for example by covering early-stage costs or sharing risk in ways intended to help mobilise private investment alongside public funding.

6d38b350202b.title: Conservation finance
6d38b350202b.section: Challenges and criticism > Transaction costs and complexity
6d38b350202b.sentence: Transaction costs and deal complexity are frequently cited barriers to scaling conservation finance, especially where projects are small, heterogeneous, or require intensive monitoring and verification.

ec71c8aad8d7.title: Conservation finance
ec71c8aad8d7.section: Challenges and criticism > Transaction costs and complexity
ec71c8aad8d7.sentence: Analyses of private finance for nature describe costs associated with project origination, aggregation, due diligence, contracting, and ongoing monitoring, which can limit investability and raise the cost of capital.

7e80180b16a9.title: Conservation finance
7e80180b16a9.section: Challenges and criticism > Transaction costs and complexity
7e80180b16a9.sentence: Debt-for-nature swaps, for example, require coordination among debtor governments, creditors, and third-party organisations such as NGOs to convert external debt obligations into domestic conservation spending and management structures.

5bba4a62a6da.title: Catastrophe bond
5bba4a62a6da.sentence: Catastrophe bonds (also known as cat bonds) are a subset of insurance-linked securities (ILS) that transfer a specified set of risks from a sponsor to investors.

223b9f6440fb.title: Catastrophe bond
223b9f6440fb.sentence: If a specified catastrophe occurs, the bond pays the invested principal to the sponsors as a way of funding the recovery from the disaster; otherwise, the principal is returned at maturity to the investors, who are also paid a coupon over the lifetime of the bond.

c8a4e540352b.title: Catastrophe bond
c8a4e540352b.sentence: They were created and first used in the mid-1990s in the aftermath of Hurricane Andrew and the Northridge earthquake.

5284d3e332bd.title: Catastrophe bond
5284d3e332bd.sentence: Though present since the 1990s, the increases in disaster risk related to climate change caused many governments and insurance companies to turn to cat bonds when reinsurance is not available or too expensive.

3bce66e468b8.title: Catastrophe bond
3bce66e468b8.sentence: Investors choose to invest in catastrophe bonds because their return is largely uncorrelated with the return on other investments in fixed income or in equities, so cat bonds help investors achieve diversification.

85c7c66a4688.title: Catastrophe bond
85c7c66a4688.sentence: At year end 2023, Swiss Re Capital Markets estimates the market size is $43.1 billion with a record $15.4 billion issued in 2023 alone.

4dd1fff470a0.title: Catastrophe bond
4dd1fff470a0.sentence: Most catastrophe bonds are rated below investment grade (B and BB category ratings), and the various rating agencies have adopted moved the view that securities generally must require multiple events before an occurrence of a loss in order to be rated investment grade.

91facb50b662.title: Catastrophe bond
91facb50b662.sentence: A catastrophe bond is rated based on its probability of default due to a qualifying catastrophe triggering loss of principal (attachment probability).

c660d34331aa.title: Catastrophe bond
c660d34331aa.sentence: Cat bonds can be categorized into four basic cover types.

5979d8d2e272.title: Catastrophe bond
5979d8d2e272.sentence: Indemnity: triggered by the issuer's actual losses, so the sponsor is indemnified, as if they had purchased traditional catastrophe reinsurance.

6bd906e7450a.title: Catastrophe bond
6bd906e7450a.sentence: Modeled loss: instead of dealing with the company's actual claims, an exposure portfolio is constructed for use with catastrophe modeling software, and then when there is a large event, the event parameters are run against the exposure database in the cat model.

8a38233b90d2.title: Catastrophe bond
8a38233b90d2.sentence: Industry toss: instead of adding up the insurer's claims, the cat bond is triggered when the insurance industry loss from a certain peril reaches a specified threshold, say $30 billion.

dc6630d929e9.title: Catastrophe bond
dc6630d929e9.sentence: The cover types listed first are more correlated to the actual losses of the insurer sponsoring the cat bond.

e164b87b272a.title: Catastrophe bond
e164b87b272a.sentence: The cover types listed farther down the list are not as highly correlated to the insurer's actual losses, so the cat bond has to be structured carefully and properly calibrated, but investors would not have to worry about the insurer's claims adjustment practices.

ff3a69551cf8.title: Catastrophe bond
ff3a69551cf8.sentence: Aggregate: the sum of losses over a time period (commonly one year, a so-called Annual Aggregate) breach a threshold (the attachment level) to trigger the bond payout.

a05bbac24e06.title: Catastrophe bond
a05bbac24e06.sentence: Per occurrence: the loss from a single event must breach a threshold (the attachment level) to trigger the bond payout.

36248eacad48.title: Catastrophe bond
36248eacad48.sentence: In this case, if the attachment of the note was set to $90 billion, the bond would pay out as the sum of the insured losses are $100 billion = $20 billion + $20 billion + $20 billion + $40 billion.

06d66b88467d.title: Parametric insurance
06d66b88467d.sentence: Parametric insurance (also called index-based insurance) is a non-traditional insurance product that offers pre-specified payouts based upon a trigger event.

2b5eab4163d5.title: Parametric insurance
2b5eab4163d5.sentence: Trigger events depend on the nature of the parametric policy and can include environmental triggers such as wind speed and rainfall measurements, business-related triggers such as foot traffic, and more.

b3710bc33699.title: Parametric insurance
b3710bc33699.sentence: Traditional indemnity insurance is structured so that after an event that leads to a loss, such as a fire, flood, storm, or car accident, the insurer reimburses the insured for the total value of the loss, subject to any limits and deductibles are included in the insurance policy.

6bab6aea6b10.title: Parametric insurance
6bab6aea6b10.sentence: In a parametric insurance policy, insurance companies need to verify that the loss event exceeded the trigger event(s) specified in the policy.

482a1089f68e.title: Parametric insurance
482a1089f68e.sentence: For weather-based parameters, this involves researching measurements from trusted third-party weather services or collecting sensor and satellite data to verify the magnitude of the weather event.

e3216b5095d9.title: Parametric insurance
e3216b5095d9.sentence: The main benefit of parametric insurance policies is that they offer faster payouts than traditional insurance based on the nature of the trigger event.

4f2cf9b06ca6.title: Parametric insurance
4f2cf9b06ca6.sentence: These quick payouts are especially beneficial for the liquidity to successfully recover after a disaster strikes.

6f6ffed51c38.title: Parametric insurance
