9a3be4b8d029.title: Intensive farming
9a3be4b8d029.sentence: Intensive agriculture, also known as intensive farming (as opposed to extensive farming), or conventional agriculture, is a type of agriculture, both of crop plants and of animals, with higher levels of input and output per unit of agricultural land area.

c8987ec46ebe.title: Intensive farming
c8987ec46ebe.sentence: It is characterized by a low fallow ratio, higher use of inputs such as capital, labour, agrochemicals and water, and higher crop yields per unit land area.

56d7eee3c8ff.title: Intensive farming
56d7eee3c8ff.sentence: Most of the meat, dairy products, eggs, fruits, and vegetables available in supermarkets are produced by such farms.

944110ba0e6f.title: Intensive farming
944110ba0e6f.sentence: Sustainably increasing agricultural productivity, especially on smallholdings, is an important way to decrease the amount of land needed for farming and slow and reverse environmental degradation caused by processes such as deforestation.

fc694949d6b1.title: Intensive farming
fc694949d6b1.sentence: Industrial agricultural practices are one of the main drivers of global warming, accounting for 14–28% of net greenhouse gas emissions.

317bc66edcdd.title: Intensive farming
317bc66edcdd.sentence: Many of the negative effects of industrial agriculture may emerge at some distance from fields and farms.

ab1d710a0e64.title: Intensive farming

f758b8dc212f.title: Intensive farming

12059c5f8d1e.sentence: These risks include too much water (flood), too little water (drought and water scarcity), and poor quality (polluted) water.

ab6d872336de.title: Water security

75c0f0e7b387.sentence: A food system is made up of all the interconnected people, institutions, policies and infrastructure involved in feeding a population.

a5a5aaaa194b.title: Food system
a5a5aaaa194b.sentence: It covers every stage from food production (sowing, growing, breeding and harvesting) to processing, packaging, distributing, marketing and consuming food, and disposing of food-related waste.

14f869516cd6.title: Food system
14f869516cd6.sentence: Conventional food systems are characterised by operating on economies of scale.

65afd6e0ae42.title: Food system
65afd6e0ae42.sentence: These food systems are often oriented towards increasing productivity and reducing unit costs through maximizing efficiency in order to lower consumer costs and increase overall production.

a23569d7c2f8.title: Food system
a23569d7c2f8.sentence: They utilize economic models such as vertical integration, economic specialization and standardization, increasingly extended supply chains and global trade.

b10ebabddc24.title: Food system
b10ebabddc24.sentence: These systems have contributed to substantial increases in agricultural productivity and food availability.

aeab8b5e6c83.title: Food system
aeab8b5e6c83.sentence: However, they have also been associated with soil degradation, biodiversity loss and greenhouse gas emissions, as well as with the concentration of agri-food production and distribution, leading to deepening inequities in access to food.

360d0ddfd848.title: Food system
360d0ddfd848.section: Conventional food systems > Impacts of conventional food systems
360d0ddfd848.sentence: Since 1961, food supply per capita has increased by more than 30%.

520c7f0b00ff.title: Food system

a608281602e1.title: Food system
a608281602e1.section: Conventional food systems > Impacts of conventional food systems
a608281602e1.sentence: However, conventional food systems are largely based on the availability of inexpensive fossil fuels, which is necessary for mechanized agriculture, the manufacture or collection of chemical fertilizers, the processing of food products, and the packaging of the foods.

ed2e7c23716c.sentence: Silviculture is the practice of controlling the growth, composition/structure, as well as quality of forests to meet values and needs, specifically timber production.

1945d46c8135.title: Silviculture
1945d46c8135.sentence: The distinction between forestry and silviculture is that silviculture is applied at the stand-level, while forestry is a broader concept.

1bb9fd992c25.title: Silviculture
1bb9fd992c25.sentence: Generally, silviculture is the commercial business of growing and cultivating forest crops based on a knowledge of silvics, the study of the life history and general characteristics of forest trees and stands, with reference to local/regional factors.

08b49168863c.title: Silviculture
08b49168863c.sentence: Regeneration can take place through self-sown seed ("natural regeneration"), by artificially sown seed, or by planted seedlings.

45c1d1443d65.title: Silviculture

2e5795786f44.title: Silviculture

fbb0630dfeb9.title: Silviculture

0f78a43d4c86.title: Silviculture

1f33385e028d.sentence: Overall, about one-third of the world's food is thrown away, and a huge amount of resources used in food production are wasted.

d11d244761b1.title: Food loss and waste
d11d244761b1.sentence: Global food waste amounts to 931 million tonnes annually (about 121 kg per person) across three sectors: 61 percent from households, 26 percent from food service and 13 percent from retail.

be87cd066038.title: Food loss and waste
be87cd066038.sentence: Wasted food is a major part of the impact of agriculture on climate change (it amounts to 3.3 billion tons of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions annually) and other environmental issues, such as land use, water use and loss of biodiversity.

5b9dec0b4eeb.title: Food loss and waste
5b9dec0b4eeb.sentence: Discarding food in landfills is to be avoided because it is a major source of the greenhouse gas methane.

171bcb63e8da.title: Food loss and waste
171bcb63e8da.sentence: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations defines food loss and waste as the decrease in quantity or quality of food along the food supply chain.

246000343366.title: Food loss and waste
246000343366.sentence: Definitions of what constitutes food loss versus food waste or what parts of foods (i.e., inedible parts) exit the food supply chain are considered lost or wasted vary.

97371e308151.title: Food loss and waste
97371e308151.sentence: According to FAO's The State of Food and Agriculture 2019, the case for reducing food loss and waste includes gains that society can reap but which individual actors may not take into account, namely: (i) increased productivity and economic growth; (ii) improved food security and nutrition; and (iii) mitigation of environmental impacts of losing and wasting food, in particular terms of reducing greenhouse gas (GHG emissions as well as lowering pressure on land and water resources.

7f82a9db191d.title: Food loss and waste
7f82a9db191d.sentence: The UN's Sustainable Development Goals seek to "halve global per capita food waste at the retail and consumer levels and reduce food losses along production and supply chains, including post-harvest losses" by 2030.

0c32557c7741.title: Clearcutting
0c32557c7741.sentence: Clearcutting, clearfelling or clearcut logging is a practice in forestry and logging, in which most or all of the trees in an area are uniformly cut down.

1bed40bd17f5.title: Clearcutting
1bed40bd17f5.sentence: Clearcutting is the most economically efficient method of logging.

1aff012235f6.title: Clearcutting
1aff012235f6.sentence: In addition to the purpose of harvesting wood, clearcutting is used to create land for farming.

9551059f5d4e.title: Clearcutting
9551059f5d4e.sentence: Clearcutting is a forestry practice that mimics the stand initiation stage of forest succession after a natural disturbance such as stand replacing fire or windthrow, and is successful for regeneration of fast growing, sun tolerant tree species and wildlife species that readily regenerate in post-stand replacing sites.

30a54bef7c70.title: Clearcutting
30a54bef7c70.sentence: Many variations of clearcutting exist; the most common professional practices are:

d50df4d1ae3e.title: Clearcutting
d50df4d1ae3e.sentence: - Standard (uniform) clearcut – removal of every stem (whether commercially viable or not), so no canopy remains.

d4ffc8165b29.title: Clearcutting
d4ffc8165b29.sentence: - Patch clearcut – removal of all the stems in a limited, predetermined area (patch).

abfe09951855.title: Clearcutting
abfe09951855.sentence: - Strip clearcut – removal of all the stems in a row (strip), usually placed perpendicular to the prevailing winds in order to minimize the possibility of windthrow.

2343f6eb698a.title: Clearcutting
2343f6eb698a.sentence: A clearcut is distinguished from selective logging where typically only a few trees per hectare are harvested in proportions dictated by management objectives.

8e7d30c9623b.title: Clearcutting
8e7d30c9623b.sentence: Removal or damage of the biota reduces the local capacity to retain water, which can exacerbate flooding and lead to increased leaching of nutrients from the soil.

35de68913d02.title: Clearcutting
35de68913d02.section: Effects on the environment > Negative impacts
35de68913d02.sentence: A study from the University of Oregon found that in certain zones, areas that were clear cut had nearly three times the amount of erosion due to slides.

7c71f84ceaec.title: Clearcutting
7c71f84ceaec.section: Effects on the environment > Negative impacts
7c71f84ceaec.sentence: When the roads required by the clearcutting were factored in, the increase in slide activity appeared to be about 5 times greater compared to nearby forested areas.

9dfa7461b0bf.title: Clearcutting
9dfa7461b0bf.sentence: Ultimately, the effects of clearcutting on the land will depend on how well or poorly the forest is managed, and whether it is converted to non-forest land uses after clearcuts.

fe53f81c043d.title: Pastoralism
fe53f81c043d.sentence: Pastoralism is a form of animal husbandry where domesticated animals (known as "livestock") are released onto large vegetated outdoor lands (pastures) for grazing, historically by nomadic people who moved around with their herds.

c797d3732725.title: Pastoralism
c797d3732725.sentence: Pastoralism is practised in various ways around the world, generally where environmentally affected characteristics such as aridity, poor soils, cold or hot temperatures, and lack of water make crop-growing difficult or impossible.

7fdc4ebecd27.title: Pastoralism
7fdc4ebecd27.sentence: As of 2019, between 200 million and 500 million people globally practiced pastoralism, and 75% of all countries had pastoral communities.

d5774447a143.title: Pastoralism
d5774447a143.sentence: The African Union estimated that Africa has about 268 million pastoralists—over a quarter of the total population—living on about 43 percent of the continent's total land mass." Pastoralists manage rangelands covering about a third of the Earth's terrestrial surface and are able to produce food where crop production is not possible.

07287f7fd12e.title: Pastoralism
07287f7fd12e.sentence: Mobile pastoralism includes moving herds locally across short distances in search of fresh forage and water (something that can occur daily or even within a few hours); as well as transhumance, where herders routinely move animals between different seasonal pastures across regions; and nomadism, where nomadic pastoralists and their families move with the animals in search for any available grazing-grounds—without much long-term planning.

a4d3cf3bd156.title: Pastoralism
a4d3cf3bd156.sentence: The enclosure of common lands has led to sedentary pastoralism becoming more common as the hardening of political borders, land tenures, expansion of crop farming, and construction of fences and dedicated agricultural buildings all reduce the ability to move livestock around freely, leading to the rise of pastoral farming on established grazing-zones (sometimes called "ranches").

72d2ae975f3e.title: Pastoralism
72d2ae975f3e.sentence: Pastoralism has been shown, "based on a review of many studies, to be between 2 and 10 times more productive per unit of land than the capital intensive alternatives that have been put forward".

9e7362d51aef.title: Pastoralism
9e7362d51aef.sentence: However, many of these benefits go unmeasured and are frequently squandered by policies and investments that seek to replace pastoralism with more capital intensive modes of production.

a950f53ea39b.title: Pastoralism
a950f53ea39b.sentence: In many places, grazing herds on savannas and in woodlands can help maintain the biodiversity of such landscapes and prevent them from evolving into dense shrublands or forests.

affa99ab5fc9.title: Pastoralism
affa99ab5fc9.sentence: Operating in more extreme environments with more marginal lands means that pastoral communities are very vulnerable to the effects of global warming.

e398e1a4398d.title: Shifting cultivation
e398e1a4398d.sentence: Shifting cultivation is an agricultural system in which plots of land are cultivated temporarily, then abandoned while post-disturbance fallow vegetation is allowed to freely grow while the cultivator moves on to another plot.

5b9a78bc535e.title: Shifting cultivation
5b9a78bc535e.sentence: The period of cultivation is usually terminated when the soil shows signs of exhaustion or, more commonly, when the field is overrun by weeds.

42aabf6ab8d6.title: Shifting cultivation
42aabf6ab8d6.sentence: The period of time during which the field is cultivated is usually shorter than the period over which the land is allowed to regenerate by lying fallow.

9d87dabda50e.title: Shifting cultivation
9d87dabda50e.sentence: Land is often cleared by slash-and-burn methods—trees, bushes and forests are cleared by slashing, and the remaining vegetation is burnt.

643ffd867225.title: Shifting cultivation
643ffd867225.sentence: In shifting agriculture, after two or three years of producing vegetable and grain crops on cleared land, the migrants abandon it for another plot.

2b62d04d96ab.title: Shifting cultivation
2b62d04d96ab.sentence: During the fallow period, shifting cultivators use the successive vegetation species widely for timber for fencing and construction, firewood, thatching, ropes, clothing, tools, carrying devices and medicines.

b6405ac97e02.title: Shifting cultivation
b6405ac97e02.sentence: Fallows commonly contain plants that attract birds and animals and are important for hunting.

032f4586a381.title: Shifting cultivation
032f4586a381.sentence: But perhaps most importantly, tree fallows protect soil against physical erosion and draw nutrients to the surface from deep in the soil profile.

572b8b6fec9b.title: Shifting cultivation
572b8b6fec9b.sentence: Shifting cultivation was one of the first forms of agriculture practiced by humans and its survival into the modern world suggests that it is a flexible and highly adaptive means of production.

255c4e9c4c2a.title: Shifting cultivation
255c4e9c4c2a.sentence: In the tropical developing world, shifting cultivation in its many diverse forms, remains a pervasive practice.

3fe799938f75.title: Shifting cultivation
3fe799938f75.sentence: Nevertheless, shifting cultivation systems are particularly susceptible to rapid increases in population and to economic and social change in the larger world around them.

8519c178aea2.title: Shifting cultivation
8519c178aea2.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
8519c178aea2.sentence: Increased cash incomes often are spent on chain saws, which have enabled larger areas to be cleared for cultivation.

0d78a1b145c9.title: Shifting cultivation
0d78a1b145c9.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
0d78a1b145c9.sentence: Fallow periods have been reduced and cropping periods extended.

55f153596fc6.title: Shifting cultivation
55f153596fc6.sentence: The blame for the destruction of forest resources is often laid on shifting cultivators.

547db5998ff9.title: Shifting cultivation
547db5998ff9.sentence: But the forces bringing about the rapid loss of tropical forests at the end of the 20th century are the same forces that led to the destruction of the forests of Europe, urbanization, industrialization, increased affluence, populational growth and geographical expansion and the application the latest technology to extract ever more resources from the environment in pursuit of wealth and political power by competing groups.

4df485fd3ad8.title: Shifting cultivation
4df485fd3ad8.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
4df485fd3ad8.sentence: Shifting cultivation was assessed by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) to be one of the causes of deforestation while logging was not.

088c64ca5c19.title: Shifting cultivation
088c64ca5c19.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
088c64ca5c19.sentence: The apparent discrimination against shifting cultivators caused a confrontation between FAO and environmental groups, who saw the FAO supporting commercial logging interests against the rights of indigenous people (Potter 1993, 108).

426ffb89ebe9.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
426ffb89ebe9.sentence: Slash-and-burn agriculture is a form of shifting cultivation in agriculture that involves the cutting and burning of plants in a forest or woodland to create a field called a swidden.

69ff14d73db9.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
69ff14d73db9.sentence: The downed vegetation, or "slash", is left out to dry, usually right before the rainiest part of the year.

d493fad06afb.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
d493fad06afb.sentence: The biomass is then burned, resulting in a nutrient-rich layer of ash which increases soil fertility and temporarily eliminates weeds and pests.

b0ceb8f4a3fb.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
b0ceb8f4a3fb.sentence: After about three to five years, the plot's productivity decreases due to depletion of nutrients along with weed and pest invasion, causing farmers to abandon the plot and move to a new area.

e6bd4f5bf879.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
e6bd4f5bf879.sentence: The time it takes for a swidden to recover depends on the location and can be as little as five years to more than twenty years, after which the plot can be slashed and burned again, repeating the cycle.

995647d33c6c.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
995647d33c6c.sentence: A rough estimate says that about 200–300 million people worldwide use slash-and-burn agricultural techniques.

5dc8cf05307a.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
5dc8cf05307a.sentence: Thus, since Neolithic times, slash-and-burn agriculture has been widely used to clear land to make it suitable for crops and livestock.

80c0a47badf7.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
80c0a47badf7.sentence: Because the leached soil in many tropical regions, such as the Amazon, are nutritionally extremely poor, slash-and-burn is one of the only types of agriculture which can be practiced in these areas.

f5191542c163.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
f5191542c163.sentence: It has been ecologically sustainable for thousands of years.

c663920dcdd6.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
c663920dcdd6.sentence: A huge amount of land, or a low density of people, is required for sustainable slash-and-burn.

9da25cbbe56e.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
9da25cbbe56e.sentence: This technique is most unsuitable for the production of cash crops.

57b5d3bc9fb0.title: Deforestation
57b5d3bc9fb0.sentence: Another prevalent method of agricultural deforestation is slash-and-burn agriculture, which was primarily used by subsistence farmers in tropical regions but has now become increasingly less sustainable.

7cf66e6fb499.title: Carbon farming
7cf66e6fb499.section: Methods used in agriculture > Working with biochar and terra preta
7cf66e6fb499.sentence: Globally up to 12% of the anthropogenic carbon emissions from land use change (0.21 gigatonnes) can be off-set annually in soil, if slash-and-burn is replaced by slash-and-char.

bee8c550f2ea.title: Groundwater depletion
bee8c550f2ea.sentence: Groundwater depletion or groundwater overdrafting is the process of extracting groundwater beyond the equilibrium yield of an aquifer.

867e3b349bac.title: Groundwater depletion
867e3b349bac.sentence: The primary cause of groundwater depletion is the excessive pumping of groundwater up from underground aquifers.

25dbd4ecde3a.title: Groundwater depletion
25dbd4ecde3a.sentence: Insufficient recharge can lead to depletion, reducing the usefulness of the aquifer for humans.

019cb6073f85.title: Groundwater depletion
019cb6073f85.sentence: Safe yield is the amount of groundwater that can be withdrawn over a period of time without exceeding the long-term recharge rate or affecting the aquifer integrity.

83de9299449c.title: Groundwater depletion
83de9299449c.sentence: Sustainable yield is the amount of water extraction that can be sustained indefinitely without negative hydrological impacts, taking into account both recharge rate and surface water impacts.

6fa11ae0c1fa.title: Groundwater depletion
6fa11ae0c1fa.sentence: When groundwater is extracted from an aquifer, a cone of depression is created around the well.

bd2530c9350d.title: Groundwater depletion
bd2530c9350d.sentence: As the drafting of water continues, the cone increases in radius.

08570555719c.title: Groundwater depletion
08570555719c.sentence: Extracting too much water (overdrafting) can lead to negative impacts such as a drop of the water table, land subsidence, and loss of surface water reaching the streams.

e97bcbd21792.title: Groundwater depletion
e97bcbd21792.sentence: The lowering water table can diminish streamflow and reduce water level in other water bodies such as wetlands and lakes.

4f1d63442292.title: Groundwater depletion
4f1d63442292.sentence: Overdrafting in coastal regions can lead to the reduction of water pressure in an aquifer, allowing saltwater intrusion.

7966f7e518dd.title: Groundwater depletion
7966f7e518dd.sentence: Roughly 40% of global irrigation is supported by groundwater, and irrigation is the primary activity causing groundwater storage loss across the U.S.

991788ecfb81.title: Groundwater depletion
991788ecfb81.sentence: In the U.S., an estimated 800 km3 of groundwater was depleted during the 20th century.

6cb8acfaedf0.title: Groundwater depletion
6cb8acfaedf0.sentence: Since recharge is the natural replenishment of water, artificial recharge is the man-made replenishment of groundwater, though there is only a limited amount of suitable water available for replenishing.

85d9a84ea7ba.title: Groundwater depletion
85d9a84ea7ba.sentence: These include improving governance to ensure proper water management, incentivizing water conservation, improving agriculture techniques to ensure water use is efficient, changing diets to crops that require less water, and investing in infrastructure that uses water sustainably.

42f273127b35.title: Land value tax
42f273127b35.sentence: A land value tax (LVT) is a levy on the value of land without regard to buildings, personal property and other improvements upon it.

1820aa69a8f9.title: Land value tax
1820aa69a8f9.sentence: Many economists favor LVT, arguing it does not cause economic inefficiency, and helps reduce economic inequality.

8560cb9d6562.title: Land value tax
8560cb9d6562.sentence: Most taxes distort economic decisions and discourage beneficial economic activity.

54b7013c2dcb.title: Land value tax
54b7013c2dcb.sentence: For example, property taxes discourage construction, maintenance, and repair because taxes increase with improvements.

33f0b83bec42.title: Land value tax
33f0b83bec42.sentence: A land value tax has progressive tax effects, in that it is paid by the owners of valuable land who tend to be the rich, and since the amount of land is fixed, the tax burden cannot be passed on as higher rents or lower wages to tenants, consumers, or workers.

ceb9b503930c.title: Land value tax
ceb9b503930c.sentence: LVT removes financial incentives to hold unused land solely for price appreciation, making more land available for productive uses.

0c6e21224958.title: Land value tax
0c6e21224958.sentence: LVT is less vulnerable to tax evasion, since land cannot be concealed or moved overseas and titles are easily identified, as they are registered with the public.

d898fe2a9334.title: Land value tax
d898fe2a9334.sentence: The value of land generally owes nothing to the landowner and everything to the surroundings.

a94435b798d7.title: Land value tax
a94435b798d7.sentence: Adam Smith, in his 1776 book The Wealth of Nations, first rigorously analyzed the effects of a land value tax, pointing out that it would not harm economic activity or raise contract rents.

22aa02d82a8e.title: Land value tax
22aa02d82a8e.sentence: A journalist, politician, and political economist, he advocated a "single tax" on land that would eliminate the need for all other taxes.

985ed5a77f56.title: Land value tax
985ed5a77f56.sentence: Levying an LVT requires an assessment and a title register.

d2d41ba49617.title: Land value tax
d2d41ba49617.sentence: In some countries, LVT is impractical due to uncertainty about land titles and tenure.

389d49f547df.title: Land value tax
389d49f547df.sentence: An LVT was implemented beginning in 1873.

67e87e0ba684.title: Forest product
67e87e0ba684.sentence: A forest product is any material derived from forestry for direct consumption or commercial use, such as lumber, paper, or fodder for livestock.

838569d3a7de.title: Forest product
838569d3a7de.sentence: Wood, by far the dominant product of forests, is used for many purposes, such as wood fuel (e.g. in form of firewood or charcoal) or the finished structural materials used for the construction of buildings, or as a raw material, in the form of wood pulp, that is used in the production of paper.

844f5c0e3b3a.title: Forest product
844f5c0e3b3a.sentence: All other non-wood products derived from forest resources, comprising a broad variety of other forest products, are collectively described as non-timber forest products (NTFP).

432a8e8ca305.title: Forest product
432a8e8ca305.sentence: Non-timber forest products are viewed to have fewer negative effects on forest ecosystem when providing income sources for local community.

14e41773baf2.title: Forest product
14e41773baf2.sentence: In 2023, the global export value of wood and paper products reached US$482 billion.

d184dac546a5.title: Forest product
d184dac546a5.sentence: Industrial roundwood removals amounted to 1.92 billion cubic meters.

ea1b8375a6e9.title: Forest product
ea1b8375a6e9.sentence: Global sawnwood production totaled 445 million cubic meters.

aa7a46091a52.title: Forest product
aa7a46091a52.section: Forest products in sustainability > Climate action
aa7a46091a52.sentence: One core idea is that forest products themselves are storage for carbon dioxide.

b3c4f29ef7ae.title: Forest product
b3c4f29ef7ae.section: Forest products in sustainability > Climate action
b3c4f29ef7ae.sentence: Second, timbers from forest can be sustainable construction materials.

9c40d3126fa7.title: Forest product
9c40d3126fa7.section: Forest products in sustainability > Climate action
9c40d3126fa7.sentence: Rather than concrete that is hard for degradation and recycled, structural timbers can be recycled for re-use or for biodegradation.

f539b3fc9c54.title: Forest product
f539b3fc9c54.section: Forest products in sustainability > Climate action
f539b3fc9c54.sentence: First, as mentioned above, bioenergy can replace fossil energy and reduce the greenhouse gas emissions although its combustion initially produces more GHG than fossil fuels per unit of produced energy: it takes several decades or even centuries for new trees to re-absorb the carbon emitted by burning their predecessors.

c9328c469de4.title: Forest product
c9328c469de4.sentence: Many forest management policies have been implemented that impact forest product economics, including forest access restrictions, harvesting fees, and harvest limits.

61b02e79e283.title: Non-timber forest product
61b02e79e283.sentence: Non-timber forest products (NTFPs) are useful foods, substances, materials and/or commodities obtained from forests other than timber.

a976bddeaf28.title: Non-timber forest product
a976bddeaf28.sentence: They typically include game animals, fur-bearers, nuts, seeds, berries, mushrooms, oils, sap, foliage, pollarding, medicinal plants, peat, mast, fuelwood, fish, insects, spices, and forage.

a50013084916.title: Non-timber forest product
a50013084916.sentence: Harvest ranges from wild collection to farming.

a5fa1c104b26.title: Non-timber forest product
a5fa1c104b26.sentence: Non-wood forest products (NWFPs) are a subset of NTFP; they exclude woodfuel and wood charcoal.

ec2b8cd8fe08.title: Non-timber forest product
ec2b8cd8fe08.sentence: On a global scale, FAO estimates that NWFPs generated US$88 billion in 2011.

985b522e9ab9.title: Non-timber forest product
985b522e9ab9.sentence: Worldwide, around 1 billion people depend to some extent on wild foods such as wild meat, edible insects, edible plant products, mushrooms and fish, which often contain high levels of key micronutrients.

437b284fa72d.title: Non-timber forest product
437b284fa72d.sentence: Several million households world-wide depend on NWFPs for income, and these products may be particularly important for local economies.

39c0d04abe7a.title: Non-timber forest product
39c0d04abe7a.sentence: More than 28,000 plant species are currently recorded as being of medicinal use; many of them are found in forest ecosystems.

47723759a464.title: Non-timber forest product
47723759a464.sentence: Estimating the contribution of NTFPs to national or regional economies is difficult, broad-based systems for tracking the combined value of the hundreds of products that make up various NTFP industries are lacking.

42938f291d64.title: Non-timber forest product
42938f291d64.sentence: All research promotes forest products as valuable commodities and tools that can promote the conservation of forests.

4193407bb9de.title: Non-timber forest product
4193407bb9de.sentence: In some contexts, the gathering and use of NTFPs can be a mechanism for poverty alleviation and local development.

af6b88bfe717.title: Community forestry
af6b88bfe717.sentence: Community forestry is a branch of forestry that deals with the communal management of forests for generating income from timber and non-timber forest products on one hand, and managing for ecosystem services such as watershed conservation, carbon sequestration and aesthetic values on the other hand.

5e3611b214ec.title: Illegal logging
5e3611b214ec.sentence: Illegal logging is the harvest, transportation, purchase, or sale of timber in violation of laws.

e2e11fb2a783.title: Illegal logging
e2e11fb2a783.sentence: The harvesting procedure itself may be illegal, including using corrupt means to gain access to forests; extraction without permission, or from a protected area; the cutting down of protected species; or the extraction of timber in excess of agreed limits.

09eb69e44301.title: Illegal logging
09eb69e44301.sentence: Illegality may also occur during transport, such as illegal processing and export (through fraudulent declaration to customs); the avoidance of taxes and other charges, and fraudulent certification.

72ad472546a4.title: Illegal logging
72ad472546a4.sentence: These acts are often referred to as "wood laundering".

e493990d8084.title: Illegal logging
e493990d8084.sentence: Illegal logging is driven by a number of economic forces, such as demand for raw materials, land grabbing and demand for pasture for cattle.

9ad330fbd4b1.title: Illegal logging
9ad330fbd4b1.sentence: It is estimated that illegal logging on public land alone causes losses in assets and revenue in excess of US$10 billion annually.

a9c3539e15fc.title: Illegal logging
a9c3539e15fc.sentence: Although exact figures are difficult to calculate, given the illegal nature of the activity, decent estimates show that more than half of the logging that takes place globally is illegal, especially in open and vulnerable areas, such as the Amazon Basin, Central Africa, Southeast Asia and the Russian Federation.

1acad81e33f9.title: Illegal logging
1acad81e33f9.sentence: Available figures and estimates must be treated with caution.

ddf5aa31c4e9.title: Illegal logging
ddf5aa31c4e9.sentence: Governments tend to underestimate the situation, given that high estimates of illegal logging may cause embarrassment as these to suggest ineffective enforcement of legislation or, even worse, bribery and corruption.

5e05f98f69c0.title: Illegal logging
5e05f98f69c0.sentence: On the other hand, environmental NGOs publish alarming figures to raise awareness and emphasize the need for stricter conservation measures.

074cabbb373b.title: Illegal logging
074cabbb373b.sentence: Illegal logging has detrimental impacts, including deforestation and, consequently, global warming.

bb2a226fefba.title: Illegal logging
bb2a226fefba.sentence: It leads to biodiversity loss, weakens the rule of law, and hampers responsible forest management.

7b7c3a478561.title: Illegal logging
7b7c3a478561.sentence: Moreover, it fosters corruption, tax evasion, and diminishes revenue for producer countries, limiting their capacity to invest in sustainable development.

f8cf1839ebd0.title: Illegal logging
f8cf1839ebd0.sentence: In May 2003, the European Commission presented the EU Forest Law Enforcement, Governance and Trade Action Plan (EU FLEGT).

8e112bcb5114.title: Illegal logging
8e112bcb5114.sentence: The primary means of implementing the Plan is through Voluntary Partnership Agreements with timber producing countries.

706c0bb4812b.title: Water right
706c0bb4812b.sentence: In water law, water right is the right of a user to use water from a water source, e.g., a river, stream, pond or source of groundwater.

25f8d9c6e6e0.title: Water right
25f8d9c6e6e0.sentence: In areas with plentiful water and few users, such systems are generally not complicated or contentious.

99911aaf9fdb.title: Water right
99911aaf9fdb.sentence: In other areas, especially arid areas where irrigation is practiced, such systems are often the source of conflict, both legal and physical.

0faf72090ae4.title: Water right
0faf72090ae4.section: Types > Utilization of water as an element > Based on ownership of the land
0faf72090ae4.sentence: Often, water rights are based on ownership of the land upon which the water rests or flows.

53d6642b46c3.title: Water right
53d6642b46c3.section: Types > Utilization of water as an element > Based on ownership of the land
53d6642b46c3.sentence: On streams and rivers, these are referred to as riparian rights or littoral rights, which are protected by property law.

7c0e95917fcc.title: Water right
7c0e95917fcc.section: Types > Utilization of water as an element > Based on ownership of the land
7c0e95917fcc.sentence: Under riparian law, water rights are subject to the test of "reasonable use".

48dadebdf709.title: Water right
48dadebdf709.section: Types > Utilization of water as an element > Based on previous use or prior appropriation
48dadebdf709.sentence: Where water is more scarce (like in the Western United States), allocation of flowing water is premised upon prior appropriation.

eb3601f82a3e.title: Water right

06512a02c459.sentence: Food-driven investments, which comprise roughly 37% of land investments worldwide, are undertaken primarily by two sets of actors: agribusinesses trying to expand their holdings and react to market incentives, and government-backed investments, especially from the Gulf states, as a result of fears surrounding national food security.

44438cddb20e.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
44438cddb20e.sentence: In the American legal system, prior appropriation water rights is the doctrine that the first person to take a quantity of water from a water source for "beneficial use" (agricultural, industrial or household) has the right to continue to use that quantity of water for that purpose.

347c59836911.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
347c59836911.sentence: The doctrine is sometimes summarized, "first in time, first in right".

396e52060652.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
396e52060652.sentence: Subsequent users can take the remaining water for their own use if they do not impinge on the rights of previous users.

2f21ee20264e.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
2f21ee20264e.sentence: Prior appropriation rights do not constitute a full ownership right in the water, merely the right to withdraw it, and can be abrogated if not used for an extended period of time.

f11161101675.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
f11161101675.sentence: Under the prior appropriation system, the right is initially allotted to those who are "first in time of use"; these rights of withdrawal can then trade on the open market, like other property.

2ecb34409495.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
2ecb34409495.sentence: Each year, the user with the earliest appropriation date (known as the "senior appropriator") may use up to their full allocation (provided the water source can supply it).

1cfcf7ef5b9f.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
1cfcf7ef5b9f.sentence: Then the user with the next earliest appropriation date may use their full allocation and so on.

532e943153fb.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
532e943153fb.sentence: In cases of water shortages, prior-appropriation does not require a senior user to utilize less water than usual.

cf2ec1f662fc.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
cf2ec1f662fc.sentence: The appropriation doctrine originated in Gold-Rush–era California, when miners sought to acquire water for mining operations.

6aeb49ca0062.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
6aeb49ca0062.sentence: An appropriator who uses water inefficiently retains the right to the full allotment, but an appropriator who uses only a portion risks losing the right to the rest, and water right markets remain too illiquid to purchase any excess.

6ec96ead5984.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
6ec96ead5984.sentence: As a result, the vast majority of water in the West still is allocated to agricultural uses despite cries for additional water from growing cities.

4e4034e36e30.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
4e4034e36e30.sentence: High demand can cause an over-appropriation of the waters, in which there are more water rights for a particular stream than water actually available.

933f4efb7af0.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
933f4efb7af0.sentence: This leads to an apparent inefficiency: if a water source is over-appropriated, the latest users will almost never see water from their claims.

3fa2436a3651.title: Prior-appropriation water rights
3fa2436a3651.sentence: The doctrine has historically excluded ecological purposes, such as maintaining a natural body of water and the wildlife that depends on it, but some jurisdictions now accept such claims.

dc391b0ac3c1.title: Riparian water rights
dc391b0ac3c1.sentence: Riparian water rights (or simply riparian rights) is a system for allocating water among those who possess land along its path.

0ef14a1c0d6c.title: Riparian water rights
0ef14a1c0d6c.sentence: It has its origins in English common law.

3508aa432668.title: Riparian water rights
3508aa432668.sentence: Riparian water rights exist in many jurisdictions with a common law heritage, such as Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and states in the eastern United States.

6dc42aff8fbf.title: Riparian water rights
6dc42aff8fbf.sentence: Under the riparian principle, all landowners whose properties adjoin a body of water have the right to make reasonable use of it as it flows through or over their properties.

3e02be419496.title: Riparian water rights
3e02be419496.sentence: If there is not enough water to satisfy all users, allotments are generally fixed in proportion to frontage on the water source.

3b3f1d791e8a.title: Riparian water rights
3b3f1d791e8a.sentence: These rights cannot be sold or transferred other than with the adjoining land and only in reasonable quantities associated with that land.

c5a6142d2f5d.title: Riparian water rights
c5a6142d2f5d.sentence: The water cannot be transferred out of the watershed without due consideration as to the rights of the downstream riparian landowners.

3debb615d026.title: Riparian water rights
3debb615d026.sentence: The reasonable use of the water by a riparian owner is subject to the downstream riparian owner's "riparian right" to receive waters undiminished in flow and quality.

1491e1b0c042.title: Riparian water rights
1491e1b0c042.sentence: Although use and overlap varies over time and by state, the western arid states that were once under Mexico and Spain generally follow the doctrine of prior appropriation, also known as "first-come, first-served", but water rights for the eastern states follow riparian law.

603a074f9e7d.sentence: Proforestation refers specifically to enabling continuous forest growth uninterrupted by active management or timber harvesting, a term coined by scientists William Moomaw, Susan Masino, and Edward Faison.

2569e1c7b2c9.sentence: However, soils containing clay can be almost impermeable and therefore rainfall on clay soils will run off and contribute to flood volumes.

ca41bab71ecb.title: Drainage basin
ca41bab71ecb.sentence: For example, rainfall on roofs, pavements, and roads will be collected by rivers with almost no absorption into the groundwater.

1ba92e103a5c.title: Drainage basin
1ba92e103a5c.section: Major drainage basins of the world > Endorheic drainage basins
1ba92e103a5c.sentence: Endorheic basin are inland basins that do not drain to an ocean.

45e8e4898997.title: Drainage basin
45e8e4898997.section: Major drainage basins of the world > Endorheic drainage basins
45e8e4898997.sentence: Endorheic basins cover around 18% of the Earth's land.

721c5524dd59.title: Drainage basin
721c5524dd59.section: Major drainage basins of the world > Endorheic drainage basins
721c5524dd59.sentence: In endorheic bodies of water where evaporation is the primary means of water loss, the water is typically more saline than the oceans.

9dc55b995cc4.title: Drainage basin
9dc55b995cc4.section: Major drainage basins of the world > Endorheic drainage basins
9dc55b995cc4.sentence: An extreme example of this is the Dead Sea.

b6e627ec8163.title: Drainage basin
b6e627ec8163.section: Major drainage basins of the world > Endorheic drainage basins
b6e627ec8163.sentence: The largest endorheic basins are in Central Asia, including the Caspian Sea, the Aral Sea, and numerous smaller lakes.

e191f507e687.title: Water pricing
e191f507e687.sentence: Water pricing is a term that covers various processes to assign a price to water.

8fe2647e6146.title: Water pricing
8fe2647e6146.sentence: Key to effective and efficient water pricing is a systematic process to understand: (i) the value of water in alternative uses; (ii) the private and external costs of supplying water services; and (iii) the multiple options to determine an appropriate water tariff.

247f46986298.title: Water pricing
247f46986298.sentence: Within the four dimensions of water pricing (uniform versus variable tariff and flat charge versus volumetric pricing), there is an almost infinite number of possible pricing combinations.

46caf74e2f0e.title: Water pricing
46caf74e2f0e.sentence: Prices for piped water supply provided by utilities, be they publicly or privately managed, are determined administratively (see water tariffs).

959dd3a6e94d.title: Water pricing
959dd3a6e94d.sentence: They vary from US$0.01 to almost US$8 per cubic meter (including sewer tariffs).

ca7bc6275e1d.title: Water pricing
ca7bc6275e1d.sentence: Prices for irrigation water that is being provided by a public agency are also typically determined administratively, usually using a flat rate, since metering is not common in agriculture in most countries of the world.

6ed2761cb3df.title: Water pricing
6ed2761cb3df.section: Institutional and behavioural factors in agricultural water pricing
6ed2761cb3df.sentence: Increasing irrigation water prices does not necessarily lead to proportional reductions in water consumption, particularly when farmers face financial constraints, limited access to efficient irrigation technologies, or insufficient opportunities to diversify their livelihoods.

ffab95441bfc.title: Water pricing
ffab95441bfc.sentence: Some countries allow water rights to be traded, so that the price for water itself is formed in the market.

023dcd2dce5d.title: Water pricing
023dcd2dce5d.sentence: Such water trading exist in parts of Australia, Chile and the Southwestern United States).

36edcfce91f5.title: Forestry
36edcfce91f5.sentence: Genetic diversity is the differences in DNA sequence between individuals as distinct from variation caused by environmental influences.

90af13057dc7.title: Forestry
90af13057dc7.sentence: Genetic diversity is needed to maintain the vitality of forests and to provide resilience to pests and diseases.

f7d28bd7f862.title: Forestry
f7d28bd7f862.sentence: Genetic diversity also ensures that forest trees can survive, adapt and evolve under changing environmental conditions.

06baca9a98ff.title: Forestry
06baca9a98ff.sentence: Genetic diversity in forests is threatened by forest fires, habitat fragmentation, pests and diseases, poor silvicultural practices and inappropriate use of forest reproductive material.

d64613ec4db0.title: Aquifer
d64613ec4db0.sentence: An unconfined aquifer has no impermeable barrier immediately above it, such that the water level can rise in response to recharge.

cac37fe95180.title: Aquifer
cac37fe95180.sentence: A confined aquifer has an overlying impermeable barrier that prevents the water level in the aquifer from rising any higher.

9a1e93c26579.title: Aquifer
9a1e93c26579.sentence: Unconfined aquifers are sometimes also called water table or phreatic aquifers, because their upper boundary is the water table or phreatic surface (see Biscayne Aquifer).

996e89279ad4.title: Aquifer
996e89279ad4.sentence: An aquifer in the same geologic unit may be confined in one area and unconfined in another.

854c97ea02af.title: Forestry law
854c97ea02af.sentence: Forestry laws govern activities in designated forest lands, most commonly with respect to forest management and timber harvesting.

82ce29768d6d.title: Forestry law
82ce29768d6d.sentence: Forestry laws generally adopt management policies for public forest resources, such as multiple use and sustained yield.

45165022c235.title: Forestry law
45165022c235.sentence: Forestry laws are intended to protect resources and prevent forest clearing, logging, hunting, and collecting vegetation.

35ab6031a931.title: Forestry law
35ab6031a931.sentence: However, there are no clear limitations set within these laws in regards to allowable cuts, harvesting rotations, and minimum harvesting diameters.

12d397358d97.title: Forestry law
12d397358d97.sentence: Public provisions referring to forest uses over more than one generation are among the oldest forms of long-term environmental policies.

fd1df6f467fc.title: Forestry law
fd1df6f467fc.sentence: Forestry management dates back to customary law codified in the 14th century.

481492740bf8.title: Forestry law
481492740bf8.sentence: Due to the Kyoto Protocol, the mitigation of climate change has become an objective of forest law and policy, complementing broader climate policies and programs.

7531ea461a33.title: Intensive farming
7531ea461a33.section: Techniques and technologies > Livestock > Concentrated animal feeding operations
7531ea461a33.sentence: Intensive livestock farming or "factory farming", is the process of raising livestock in confinement at high stocking density.

06395f7ec7a9.title: Intensive farming
06395f7ec7a9.section: Techniques and technologies > Livestock > Concentrated animal feeding operations
06395f7ec7a9.sentence: "Concentrated animal feeding operations" (CAFO), or "intensive livestock operations", can hold large numbers (some up to hundreds of thousands) of cows, hogs, turkeys, or chickens, often indoors.

1cd7a54e9441.title: Intensive farming
1cd7a54e9441.section: Techniques and technologies > Livestock > Concentrated animal feeding operations
1cd7a54e9441.sentence: The aim is to provide maximum output at the lowest possible cost and with the greatest level of food safety.

ee085a8a705b.title: Intensive farming
ee085a8a705b.section: Techniques and technologies > Livestock > Concentrated animal feeding operations
ee085a8a705b.sentence: CAFOs have dramatically increased the production of food from animal husbandry worldwide, both in terms of total food produced and efficiency.

43d0af6d03e6.title: Water security
43d0af6d03e6.sentence: Water conflict typically refers to violence or disputes associated with access to, or control of, water resources, or the use of water or water systems as weapons or casualties of conflicts.

98f5f2fd8d6b.title: Water security
98f5f2fd8d6b.sentence: A wide range of water conflicts appear throughout history, though they are rarely traditional wars waged over water alone.

e41dd0d6ebfe.title: Water security
e41dd0d6ebfe.sentence: Instead, water has long been a source of tension and one of the causes for conflicts.

34ac0fe53c13.title: Water security
34ac0fe53c13.sentence: Water conflicts can occur on the intrastate and interstate levels.

62de6cb48308.title: Water security
62de6cb48308.sentence: Interstate conflicts occur between two or more countries that share a transboundary water source, such as a river, sea, or groundwater basin.

8ea52f4b2e4b.title: Water security
8ea52f4b2e4b.sentence: Intrastate conflicts take place between two or more parties in the same country, such as conflicts between farmers and urban water users.

4a379e8f20ea.title: Water security
4a379e8f20ea.sentence: For example, the Middle East has only 1% of the world's fresh water shared among 5% of the world's population and most of the rivers cross international borders.

6502ae3fa52e.title: Water security
6502ae3fa52e.sentence: Water risk refers to the possibility of problems to do with water.

0bb22673b6f2.title: Water security
0bb22673b6f2.sentence: Examples are water scarcity, water stress, flooding, infrastructure decay and drought.

bd636b01b3c0.title: Water security
bd636b01b3c0.sentence: There exists an inverse relationship between water risk and water security.

f470b1f828f2.title: Water security
f470b1f828f2.sentence: This means as water risk increases, water security decreases.

b655ad1073a5.title: Water security
b655ad1073a5.sentence: Risk is a combination of hazard, exposure and vulnerability.

3f3779dec113.title: Water security
3f3779dec113.sentence: Examples are the food and beverage sector, agriculture, oil and gas and utilities.

6139da8b5068.title: Water security
6139da8b5068.sentence: Agriculture uses 69% of total freshwater in the world.

a4ba16b7915e.title: Water resources
a4ba16b7915e.sentence: Some human water users have an intermittent need for water.

7191880162f1.title: Water resources
7191880162f1.sentence: Other users have a continuous need for water, such as a power plant that requires water for cooling.

5b77264c5d89.title: Water resources
5b77264c5d89.sentence: It is estimated that 22% of worldwide water is used in industry.

d7fba9080035.title: Water resources
d7fba9080035.sentence: Major industrial users include hydroelectric dams, thermoelectric power plants, which use water for cooling, ore and oil refineries, which use water in chemical processes, and manufacturing plants, which use water as a solvent.

dec974371fea.title: Water resources
dec974371fea.section: Water uses > Drinking water and domestic use (households)
dec974371fea.sentence: It is estimated that 8% of worldwide water use is for domestic purposes.

403e26fcf0a3.title: Water resources
403e26fcf0a3.section: Water uses > Drinking water and domestic use (households)
403e26fcf0a3.sentence: These include drinking water, bathing, cooking, toilet flushing, cleaning, laundry and gardening.

eae442b2e753.title: Water resources
eae442b2e753.sentence: Water withdrawal can be very high for certain industries, but consumption is generally much lower than that of agriculture.

c2b7fc1aed88.title: Water resources
c2b7fc1aed88.section: Water uses > Agriculture and other irrigation
c2b7fc1aed88.sentence: Irrigation has been a key aspect of agriculture for over 5,000 years and has been developed by many cultures worldwide.

51077240dbeb.title: Water resources
51077240dbeb.sentence: Water resource management is the activity of planning, developing, distributing and managing the optimum use of water resources.

820c196344b8.title: Water resources
820c196344b8.sentence: Ideally, water resource management planning has regard to all the competing demands for water and seeks to allocate water on an equitable basis to satisfy all uses and demands.

154560acc28e.title: Water resources
154560acc28e.sentence: As with other resource management, this is rarely possible in practice so decision-makers must prioritise issues of sustainability, equity and factor optimisation (in that order!) to achieve acceptable outcomes.

4b8808e64fe1.title: Water resources
4b8808e64fe1.sentence: With the growing uncertainties of global climate change and the long-term impacts of past management actions, this decision-making will be even more difficult.

302403425fb8.title: Water resources
302403425fb8.sentence: As a result, alternative management strategies, including participatory approaches and adaptive capacity are increasingly being used to strengthen water decision-making.

fc1903f44013.title: Water resources
fc1903f44013.sentence: Sustainable Development Goal 6 has a target related to water resources management: "Target 6.5: By 2030, implement integrated water resources management at all levels, including through transboundary cooperation as appropriate."

46e3a20ccddb.title: Water resources
46e3a20ccddb.section: Water resource management > Sustainable water management
46e3a20ccddb.sentence: Further challenges to sustainable and equitable water resources management include the fact that many water bodies are shared across boundaries which may be international (see water conflict) or intra-national (see Murray-Darling basin).

9bfab6b9e889.title: Water resources
9bfab6b9e889.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
9bfab6b9e889.sentence: Integrated water resources management (IWRM) has been defined by the Global Water Partnership (GWP) as "a process which promotes the coordinated development and management of water, land and related resources, in order to maximize the resultant economic and social welfare in an equitable manner without compromising the sustainability of vital ecosystems".

d3439888ec8d.title: Water resources
d3439888ec8d.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
d3439888ec8d.sentence: In the International Water Association definition, IWRM rests upon three principles that together act as the overall framework:

14148432bae5.title: Water resources
14148432bae5.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
14148432bae5.sentence: - Social equity: ensuring equal access for all users (particularly marginalized and poorer user groups) to an adequate quantity and quality of water necessary to sustain human well-being.

64caa84c3b87.title: Water resources
64caa84c3b87.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
64caa84c3b87.sentence: - Economic efficiency: bringing the greatest benefit to the greatest number of users possible with the available financial and water resources.

553cc8fb51b3.title: Water resources
553cc8fb51b3.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
553cc8fb51b3.sentence: - Ecological sustainability: requiring that aquatic ecosystems are acknowledged as users and that adequate allocation is made to sustain their natural functioning.

71838a97a072.title: Water resources
71838a97a072.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
71838a97a072.sentence: IWRM is a paradigm that emerged at international conferences in the late 1900s and early 2000s, although participatory water management institutions have existed for centuries.

5032b226593f.title: Water resources
5032b226593f.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
5032b226593f.sentence: The development of IWRM was particularly recommended in the final statement of the ministers at the International Conference on Water and the Environment in 1992, known as the Dublin Statement.

6046073b5003.title: Water resources
6046073b5003.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
6046073b5003.sentence: Some scholars say that IWRM is complementary to water security because water security is a goal or destination, whilst IWRM is the process necessary to achieve that goal.

a4fb9c8d70a8.title: Water resources
a4fb9c8d70a8.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
a4fb9c8d70a8.sentence: In addition, in light of contributing the achievement of Sustainable Development goals (SDGs), IWRM has been evolving into more sustainable approach as it considers the Nexus approach, which is a cross-sectoral water resource management.

4bab9205f477.title: Water resources
4bab9205f477.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
4bab9205f477.sentence: The Nexus approach is based on the recognition that "water, energy and food are closely linked through global and local water, carbon and energy cycles or chains."

0b2a345f5571.title: Water resources
0b2a345f5571.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
0b2a345f5571.sentence: There is not one correct administrative model.

69aa699a09de.title: Water resources
69aa699a09de.section: Water resource management > Integrated water resources management
69aa699a09de.sentence: IWRM practices depend on context; at the operational level, the challenge is to translate the agreed principles into concrete action.

261c0d2bdf0d.title: Virtual water
261c0d2bdf0d.sentence: The virtual water trade is the hidden flow of water in food or other commodities that are traded from one place to another.

480f245950de.title: Virtual water
480f245950de.sentence: The virtual water trade is the idea that virtual water is exchanged along with goods and services.

fd0b948c8203.title: Virtual water
fd0b948c8203.sentence: Other terms for it are embedded or embodied water.

43da8c7651ac.title: Virtual water
43da8c7651ac.sentence: The virtual water concept, also known as embodied water, was coined by John Anthony Allan (Tony Allan) in 1993.

a55c9e6f01ce.title: Virtual water
a55c9e6f01ce.sentence: He received the Stockholm Water Prize for the concept in 2008.

9e5c7a648037.title: Virtual water
9e5c7a648037.sentence: When a country imports one tonne of wheat instead of producing it domestically, it is saving about 1,300 cubic meters of real indigenous water.

e0bd3a9929ff.title: Virtual water
e0bd3a9929ff.sentence: For example, cereal grains have been major carriers of virtual water in countries where water resources are scarce.

a07ba7391873.title: Virtual water
a07ba7391873.sentence: So cereal imports can compensate for local water deficits.

50e4359a00a1.title: Virtual water
50e4359a00a1.sentence: However, low-income countries may not be able to afford such imports in the future.

4c54df7484e7.title: Virtual water
4c54df7484e7.sentence: Water-scarce countries like Israel discourage the export of oranges (relatively water intensive crops) precisely to prevent large quantities of water from being exported to different parts of the world.

5b01b4cc735f.title: Virtual water
5b01b4cc735f.sentence: The data that underlie the concept of virtual water can readily be used to construct water satellite accounts, and brought into economic models of international trade such as the GTAP Computable General Equilibrium Model.

0ea3143d4a3b.title: Virtual water
0ea3143d4a3b.sentence: Such a model can be used to study the economic implications of changes in the water supply or water policy, as well as the water resource implications of economic development and trade liberalization.

b9d9aeeaabd5.title: Virtual water
b9d9aeeaabd5.section: Virtual water content of selected products

241a9def0ee6.title: Virtual water
241a9def0ee6.section: Virtual water content of selected products

fa0034be0594.title: Environmental flow
fa0034be0594.sentence: Environmental flows describe the quantity, timing, and quality of water flows required to sustain freshwater and estuarine ecosystems and the human livelihoods and well being that depend on these ecosystems.

1de3c43f5e74.title: Environmental flow
1de3c43f5e74.sentence: Through implementation of environmental flows, water managers strive to achieve a flow regime, or pattern, that provides for human uses and maintains the essential processes required to support healthy river ecosystems.

ba9b99004996.title: Environmental flow
ba9b99004996.sentence: Environmental flows do not necessarily require restoring the natural, pristine flow patterns that would occur absent human development, use, and diversion but, instead, are intended to produce a broader set of values and benefits from rivers than from management focused strictly on water supply, energy, recreation, or flood control.

2f18467fa14f.title: Environmental flow
2f18467fa14f.sentence: More than half of the world's large rivers are dammed, a figure that continues to increase.

77fd9c4ea01a.title: Environmental flow
77fd9c4ea01a.sentence: Dams and other river structures change the downstream flow patterns and consequently affect water quality, temperature, sediment movement and deposition, fish and wildlife, and the livelihoods of people who depend on healthy river ecosystems.

665507dde73e.title: Environmental flow
665507dde73e.section: Evolution of environmental flow concepts and recognition
665507dde73e.sentence: During the 1970s, the ecological and economic effects of these projects prompted scientists to seek ways to modify dam operations to maintain certain fish species.

03447c5151f7.title: Environmental flow
03447c5151f7.section: Evolution of environmental flow concepts and recognition
03447c5151f7.sentence: The initial focus was on determining the minimum flow necessary to preserve an individual species, such as trout, in a river.

67c62135fe71.title: Environmental flow
67c62135fe71.section: Evolution of environmental flow concepts and recognition
67c62135fe71.sentence: Environmental flows evolved from this concept of "minimum flows" and, later, "instream flows", which emphasized the need to keep water within waterways.

ffb66222db48.title: Environmental flow
ffb66222db48.section: Evolution of environmental flow concepts and recognition
ffb66222db48.sentence: By the 1990s, scientists came to realize that the biological and social systems supported by rivers are too complicated to be summarized by a single minimum flow requirement.

5ca433482f42.title: Environmental flow
5ca433482f42.section: Evolution of environmental flow concepts and recognition
5ca433482f42.sentence: In 2007, the Brisbane Declaration on Environmental Flows was endorsed by more than 750 practitioners from more than 50 countries.

43d26bf0a212.title: Environmental flow
43d26bf0a212.sentence: More than 200 methods are used worldwide to prescribe river flows needed to maintain healthy rivers.

9d4fd5e6d046.title: Environmental flow
9d4fd5e6d046.sentence: Such comprehensive approaches include DRIFT (Downstream Response to Imposed Flow Transformation), BBM (Building Block Methodology), and the "Savannah Process" for site-specific environmental flow assessment, and ELOHA (Ecological Limits of Hydrologic Alteration) for regional-scale water resource planning and management.

2fd42be5db52.title: Environmental flow
2fd42be5db52.sentence: Dam reoperation to release environmental flows, in combination with floodplain restoration, has in some instances increased the water available for hydropower production while reducing flood risk.

693413d9f159.title: Water scarcity
693413d9f159.sentence: One is the water use to availability ratio.

58d28d84d43f.title: Water scarcity
58d28d84d43f.sentence: One way to measure water scarcity is to calculate the amount of water resources available per person each year.

9d2cb49bbc6e.title: Water scarcity
9d2cb49bbc6e.sentence: One example is the "Falkenmark Water Stress Indicator".

332850423d37.title: Water scarcity
332850423d37.sentence: This indicator says a country or region experiences "water stress" when annual water supplies drop below 1,700 cubic meters per person per year.

4ef2752a165d.title: Water scarcity
4ef2752a165d.sentence: When water supplies drop below 1,000 cubic meters per person per year the country faces "water scarcity".

5d87b465b7eb.title: Water scarcity
5d87b465b7eb.sentence: It described it as "the ratio between total freshwater withdrawn (TFWW) by all major sectors and total renewable freshwater resources (TRWR), after taking into account environmental flow requirements (EFR)".

7bd8913c9e4d.title: Water scarcity
7bd8913c9e4d.sentence: This means that the value for TFWW is divided by the difference between TRWR minus EFR.

12ea0ae583ee.title: Water scarcity
12ea0ae583ee.sentence: Below 10% is low stress; 10-20% is low-to-medium; 20-40% medium-to-high; 40-80% high; above 80% very high.

0af94de8deba.title: Water scarcity
0af94de8deba.section: Challenges > Simple indicators > Renewable freshwater resources
0af94de8deba.sentence: This metric has a drawback because it is an average.

5cbfdf06e568.title: Water scarcity
5cbfdf06e568.section: Challenges > Simple indicators > Renewable freshwater resources
5cbfdf06e568.sentence: This metric does not describe how easy it is for individuals, households, industries or government to access water.

104583e6bba1.title: Water scarcity
104583e6bba1.section: Challenges > Simple indicators > Renewable freshwater resources
104583e6bba1.sentence: Lastly this metric gives a description of a whole country.

ebc2301fb902.title: Water resources
ebc2301fb902.section: Water resource management > Sustainable water management
ebc2301fb902.sentence: The four Dublin Principles, promulgated in the Dublin Statement are:

08643310616a.title: Water resources
08643310616a.section: Water resource management > Sustainable water management
08643310616a.sentence: Sustainable water management requires a holistic approach based on the principles of Integrated Water Resource Management, originally articulated in 1992 at the Dublin (January) and Rio (July) conferences.

14e5a7120ccb.title: Water resources
14e5a7120ccb.section: Water resource management > Sustainable water management
14e5a7120ccb.sentence: - Fresh water is a finite and vulnerable resource, essential to sustain life, development and the environment;

18bb80b0281c.title: Water resources
18bb80b0281c.section: Water resource management > Sustainable water management
18bb80b0281c.sentence: - Water development and management should be based on a participatory approach, involving users, planners and policy-makers at all levels;

52840d3ada3f.title: Water resources
52840d3ada3f.section: Water resource management > Sustainable water management
52840d3ada3f.sentence: - Women play a central part in the provision, management and safeguarding of water;

6f68f1bf6c2f.title: Water resources
6f68f1bf6c2f.section: Water resource management > Sustainable water management
6f68f1bf6c2f.sentence: - Water has an economic value in all its competing uses and should be recognized as an economic good.

3f339246340d.title: Water resources
3f339246340d.section: Water resource management > Sustainable water management
3f339246340d.sentence: Implementation of these principles has guided reform of national water management law around the world since 1992.

594725b7006f.title: Reduced-impact logging
594725b7006f.sentence: Reduced-Impact Logging (RIL) is a set of forestry practices which enable sustainability within tropical selective felling forestry.

e46ac8e9aeea.title: Reduced-impact logging
e46ac8e9aeea.sentence: RIL is intensively planned and carefully controlled timber harvesting conducted by trained workers in ways that minimize the deleterious impacts of logging.

694cec77359b.title: Reduced-impact logging
694cec77359b.sentence: Selective logging is a widely common timber-harvesting practice that involves the removal of few timbers species trees above a minimum diameter cutting limit.

3cd016c19e21.title: Reduced-impact logging
3cd016c19e21.sentence: Unlike clearcutting, where all trees in an area are felled, selective logging leaves the remaining trees in the stand.

2a2dca0ae763.title: Reduced-impact logging
2a2dca0ae763.sentence: It is estimated that selective logging worldwide concerns 1 billion hectares of forests including 680 million hectares of tropical forests species.

a2b0c411cfde.title: Reduced-impact logging
a2b0c411cfde.sentence: Where forests are selectively logged by untrained and poorly supervised workers at intensities and frequencies that do not sustain timber yields, this causes high damage to the forest stand, hydrological functions and biodiversity.

3c7b7c2c8da1.title: Reduced-impact logging
3c7b7c2c8da1.sentence: However, the term 'Reduced Impact' better known now under its acronym RIL was raised only in the late 1990s.

f1d329175a59.title: Reduced-impact logging
f1d329175a59.sentence: By the early 1990s, it became evident that mechanized logging posed serious threats to long-term sustainability, particularly when considering non-timber values.

4c0749f815da.title: Reduced-impact logging
4c0749f815da.sentence: In response, the concept of RIL emerged to mitigate environmental damage while meeting timber needs.

fb4630297a92.title: Reduced-impact logging
fb4630297a92.sentence: The FAO advocated for broader adoption of RIL by producing a model code of forest harvesting practice, which emphasizes several standard measures: defining a minimum cutting cycle of 20 years, limiting the removal of stand basal area to one-third, directional felling to facilitate log yarding, and limiting the size of log landings.

797a6fc28d85.title: Reduced-impact logging
797a6fc28d85.sentence: Use of RIL practices results in fewer trees and less soil being damaged, but its benefits can be lost at very high logging intensities.

5815b1e138b3.title: Reduced-impact logging
5815b1e138b3.sentence: In Southeast Asia, researchers have provided evidence that when more than 8 trees per hectare are logged, the benefits of RIL are diminished and the impacts become similar to those from conventional logging.

298a67124d7f.title: Reduced-impact logging
298a67124d7f.sentence: Whether it imposes a financial burden on loggers remains a contentious issue, with concerns about reduced income and increased operational costs apparently hindering widespread adoption.

b589bff6f9fa.title: Reduced-impact logging
b589bff6f9fa.sentence: Studies have produced mixed results, with some showing RIL to be financially favorable due to reduced timber wastage, while others highlight potential losses, especially in areas with restrictions on harvesting.

13acc76d38c4.title: Reduced-impact logging
13acc76d38c4.sentence: Despite challenges, there are potential economic benefits to RIL, including increased carbon retention and eligibility for environmental service payments.

5dd1b667796f.title: Faustmann's formula
5dd1b667796f.sentence: Faustmann's formula, or the Faustmann model, gives the present value of the income stream for forest rotation.

27a3e11209c0.title: Faustmann's formula

0e934ea3fb79.sentence: Water bankruptcy is a condition caused by an overuse of water resource for an extended period to the extent that leads to irreversible ecosystem damages, resulting in systems losing their ability to restore historical ecosystem service baselines.

3b405986bdf0.title: Water bankruptcy
3b405986bdf0.sentence: Water bankruptcy is used in water policy and environmental governance discourse to describe a condition in which a water system, such as a river basin, aquifer, lake system, or watershed, has been so overexploited or degraded that it can no longer return to its historical balance under existing climatic, ecological, and institutional conditions.

5901ba7a9b72.title: Water bankruptcy
5901ba7a9b72.sentence: In that article, Madani proposed a framework combining two essential elements: 1) hydrological insolvency, meaning that withdrawals exceed renewable inflows and safe depletion limits, and 2) irreversibility, meaning that resulting damages cannot be reversed without disproportionate economic, social, or environmental cost.

f161dd315ee6.title: Water bankruptcy
f161dd315ee6.sentence: The term has been used to distinguish severe and potentially irreversible human-water systems' failure from more familiar concepts such as water scarcity, water stress, or water crisis.

b7af790636ce.title: Water bankruptcy
b7af790636ce.sentence: - Water crisis usually refers to acute or chronic disruption that may still be reversible.

43f458187a78.title: Water bankruptcy
43f458187a78.sentence: The concept therefore emphasizes not only shortage, but also systemic insolvency, ecological degradation, and irreversible loss of recoverability.

951c5e3b3fd5.title: Water bankruptcy
951c5e3b3fd5.sentence: The term has been developed and formally defined in the scientific literature by environmental scientist Kaveh Madani and was adopted by the United Nations system in 2026, with the publication of the "Global Water Bankruptcy" report.

fe5d662d455b.title: Water bankruptcy
fe5d662d455b.sentence: On 20 January, 2026 the United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health (UNU-INWEH), known as the UN's Think Tank on Water, published a flagship report titled Global Water Bankruptcy: Living Beyond Our Hydrological Means in the Post-Crisis Era.

97a3d3d18109.title: Water bankruptcy
97a3d3d18109.sentence: The report officially declared that as of 2026, the world has entered the 'Global Water Bankruptcy' era, characterized by the growing number of river basins and aquifers that are unable to return to historical hydrological norms because of long-term overuse, ecosystem degradation, and changing climatic conditions.

eb75ae0147e6.sentence: The four components that make up restoration benefits are the conservation of biodiversity, the effectiveness of reducing climate change, climate change adaptation, and improving human water security.

8db09e51832f.title: Water resource policy

8db09e51832f.sentence: The human right to water and sanitation (HRWS) is a principle stating that clean drinking water and sanitation are a universal human right because of their high importance in sustaining every person's life.

7603c7440304.title: Water resource policy
7603c7440304.sentence: Water resource policy, sometimes called water resource management or water management, encompasses the policy-making processes and legislation that affect the collection, preparation, use, disposal, and protection of water resources.

72f1403cc759.title: Water resource policy

6c0e0ad4a8d4.title: Water resource policy

0979ce1ed602.title: Water resource policy

b5367f31d8d8.title: Water resource policy
b5367f31d8d8.sentence: Green water is rainwater that was precipitated on soil that can be used naturally for plants and agriculture.

d244d91261af.title: Water resource policy

2a7e46441d79.title: Water resource policy

f932dcf2f403.title: Water resource policy

9faee2610e09.title: Water resource policy

f4757a397342.title: Water resource policy

bb1299c02b52.title: Water resource policy

297f86d570ea.title: Water-energy nexus
297f86d570ea.sentence: The water-energy nexus is the relationship between the water used for energy production, including both electricity and sources of fuel such as oil and natural gas, and the energy consumed to extract, purify, deliver, heat/cool, treat and dispose of water (and wastewater) sometimes referred to as the energy intensity (EI).

876891227405.title: Water-energy nexus
876891227405.sentence: The relationship is not truly a closed loop as the water used for energy production need not be the same water that is processed using that energy, but all forms of energy production require some input of water making the relationship inextricable.

03830f4e223e.title: Water-energy nexus
03830f4e223e.sentence: Energy is needed in every stage of the water cycle from producing, moving, treating and heating water to collecting and treating wastewater.

5291b372ddb0.title: Water-energy nexus
5291b372ddb0.section: Water used in the energy sector
5291b372ddb0.sentence: Water is considered used if it does not reduce the supply of water to downstream users, i.e. water that is taken and returned to the same source (instream use), such as in thermoelectric plants that use water for cooling and are by far the largest users of water.

06e13994a660.title: Water-energy nexus
06e13994a660.section: Water used in the energy sector
06e13994a660.sentence: Water is consumed when it is removed completely from the system, such as by evaporation or consumption by crops or humans.

b3c6170a5e59.title: Water-energy nexus
b3c6170a5e59.sentence: Renewable energy methods, such as biofuels, concentrating solar power (CSP), carbon capture, utilization and storage or nuclear power, are quite water intensive.

8eaa72206e08.title: Water-energy nexus

635a22fa045b.title: Water-energy nexus

f33b2429715f.title: Natural resource management
f33b2429715f.sentence: Natural resource management (NRM) is the management of natural resources such as land, water, soil, plants and animals, with a particular focus on how management affects the quality of life for both present and future generations (stewardship).

c4aa37e33629.title: Natural resource management
c4aa37e33629.sentence: Natural resource management deals with managing the way in which people and natural landscapes interact.

ce8ab4ca1d93.title: Natural resource management
ce8ab4ca1d93.sentence: It recognizes that people and their livelihoods rely on the health and productivity of our landscapes, and their actions as stewards of the land play a critical role in maintaining this health and productivity.

7a6db197b5f2.title: Natural resource management
7a6db197b5f2.sentence: It brings together natural heritage management, land use planning, water management, bio-diversity conservation, and the future sustainability of industries like agriculture, mining, tourism, fisheries and forestry.

e8ed2c22eaa4.title: Natural resource management

0ee4d278fa44.title: Natural resource management

251baf4cf047.title: Natural resource management

0de3ff96e935.title: Commons
