f0a22d15bcd0.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
f0a22d15bcd0.sentence: Ecosystem-based adaptation (EbA) encompasses a broad set of approaches to adapt to climate change.

958b86d8d239.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
958b86d8d239.sentence: The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) defines EBA as "the use of biodiversity and ecosystem services as part of an overall adaptation strategy to help people to adapt to the adverse effects of climate change".

b6828ba05270.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
b6828ba05270.sentence: EbA involves the conservation, sustainable management and restoration of ecosystems, such as forests, grasslands, wetlands, mangroves or coral reefs to reduce the harmful impacts of climate hazards including shifting patterns or levels of rainfall, changes in maximum and minimum temperatures, stronger storms, and increasingly variable climatic conditions.

1859127772cd.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
1859127772cd.sentence: EbA measures can be implemented on their own or in combination with engineered approaches (such as the construction of water reservoirs or dykes), hybrid measures (such as artificial reefs) and approaches that strengthen the capacities of individuals and institutions to address climate risks (such as the introduction of early warning systems).

d6d2a0c8370a.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
d6d2a0c8370a.section: Overview > Making active use of biodiversity and ecosystem services
d6d2a0c8370a.sentence: For example, EbA measures include coastal habitat restoration in ecosystems such as; coral reefs, mangrove forests, and marshes to protect communities and infrastructure from storm surges; agroforestry to increase resilience of crops to droughts or excessive rainfall; integrated water resource management to cope with consecutive dry days and change in rainfall patterns; and sustainable forest management interventions to stabilise slopes, prevent landslides, and regulate water flow to prevent flash flooding (see Table 1 and Figure 2).

30081ca9bc50.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation

b9052b23b408.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation

ac24cb622e45.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation

17061b1053a3.title: Howard T. Odum
17061b1053a3.sentence: Ecological engineering, he wrote, is "those cases where the energy supplied by man is small relative to the natural sources but sufficient to produce large effects in the resulting patterns and processes." Ecological engineering as a practical field was developed by his former graduate student Bill Mitsch, who started and continues to edit the standard journal in the field and helped to start both international and U.S. societies devoted to ecological engineering, and has written two textbooks on the subject One of Odum's last papers was his assessment of ecological engineering that was published in the journal Ecological Engineering in 2003, a year after Odum died.

2acca6723cc5.sentence: Mitsch and Jorgensen summarized five basic concepts that differentiate ecological engineering from other approaches to addressing problems to benefit society and nature: 1) it is based on the self-designing capacity of ecosystems; 2) it can be the field (or acid) test of ecological theories; 3) it relies on system approaches; 4) it conserves non-renewable energy sources; and 5) it supports ecosystem and biological conservation.

01cd32f5f3e9.sentence: With these principals in mind, the world's first B.S. Ecological Engineering program was formalized in 2009 at Oregon State University.

dcc25fc5d98b.title: Nature-based solutions
dcc25fc5d98b.sentence: The Indigenous Environmental Network has stated that "Nature-based solutions (NBS) is a greenwashing tool that does not address the root causes of climate change." and "The legacy of colonial power continues through nature-based solutions." For example, NBS activities can involve converting non-forest land into forest plantations (for climate change mitigation) but this carries risks of climate injustice through taking land away from smallholders and pastoralists.

a9c186adf75b.title: Nature-based solutions
a9c186adf75b.sentence: However, the IPCC pointed out that the term is "the subject of ongoing debate, with concerns that it may lead to the misunderstanding that NbS on its own can provide a global solution to climate change".

45d663bc5efe.title: Nature-based solutions
45d663bc5efe.sentence: To clarify this point further, the IPCC also stated that "nature-based systems cannot be regarded as an alternative to, or a reason to delay, deep cuts in GHG emissions".

6265245cdac2.title: Nature-based solutions
6265245cdac2.sentence: A global evidence map of natural climate solutions identified 257,266 relevant papers across 22 pathways.

eae4ada9bcb4.title: Nature-based solutions
eae4ada9bcb4.sentence: Fewer than 2% of the papers explicitly mentioned cost, equity, or information about Indigenous peoples and local communities in their abstracts.

ee428dd94fe6.title: Nature-based solutions
ee428dd94fe6.sentence: The majority of case studies and examples of NBS are from the Global North, resulting in a lack of data for many medium- and low-income nations.

44c716834c3b.title: Nature-based solutions
44c716834c3b.sentence: Consequently, many ecosystems and climates are excluded from existing studies as well as cost analyses in these locations.

c544c4a086ee.title: Nature-based solutions
c544c4a086ee.sentence: It is crucial that grey infrastructures continue to be used with green infrastructure.

4e526d53730c.title: Nature-based solutions
4e526d53730c.sentence: Using green infrastructure alone or grey infrastructure alone are less effective than when the two are used together.

bb5ff0175c85.title: Nature-based solutions
bb5ff0175c85.sentence: Multiple studies recognise that while NBS is very effective and improves flood resilience, it is unable to act alone and must be in coordination with grey infrastructure.

483cd06cae7e.title: Nature-based solutions
483cd06cae7e.sentence: When NBS is used alongside grey infrastructure the benefits transcend flood management and improve social conditions, increase carbon sequestration and prepare cities for planning for resilience.

c370eefaabaf.title: Nature-based solutions
c370eefaabaf.sentence: Researchers have pointed out that "instead of framing NBS as an alternative to engineered approaches, we should focus on finding synergies among different solutions".

fa0e26d75508.title: Nature-based solutions
fa0e26d75508.sentence: Scientists have proposed a typology to characterise NBS along two gradients:

f926bd82aec4.title: Nature-based solutions
f926bd82aec4.sentence: - "How much engineering of biodiversity and ecosystems is involved in NBS", and

69552ee295d2.title: Nature-based solutions
69552ee295d2.sentence: - "How many ecosystem services and stakeholder groups are targeted by a given NBS".

450ba3bdbc9f.title: Nature-based solutions
450ba3bdbc9f.section: Types > Type 1 – Minimal intervention in ecosystems
450ba3bdbc9f.sentence: Type 1 consists of no or minimal intervention in ecosystems, with the objectives of maintaining or improving the delivery of a range of ecosystem services both inside and outside of these conserved ecosystems.

ddd66836e502.title: Nature-based solutions
ddd66836e502.section: Types > Type 1 – Minimal intervention in ecosystems
ddd66836e502.sentence: Examples include the protection of mangroves in coastal areas to limit risks associated with extreme weather conditions; and the establishment of marine protected areas to conserve biodiversity within these areas while exporting fish and other biomass into fishing grounds.

814677ef900b.title: Nature-based solutions
814677ef900b.section: Types > Type 2 – Some interventions in ecosystems and landscapes
814677ef900b.sentence: Type 2 corresponds to management approaches that develop sustainable and multifunctional ecosystems and landscapes (extensively or intensively managed).

bc7bd02db78e.title: Nature-based solutions
bc7bd02db78e.section: Types > Type 2 – Some interventions in ecosystems and landscapes
bc7bd02db78e.sentence: Examples include innovative planning of agricultural landscapes to increase their multi-functionality; using existing agrobiodiversity to increase biodiversity, connectivity, and resilience in landscapes; and approaches for enhancing tree species and genetic diversity to increase forest resilience to extreme events.

7c468a8b8408.title: Nature-based solutions
7c468a8b8408.section: Types > Type 2 – Some interventions in ecosystems and landscapes
7c468a8b8408.sentence: This type of NBS is strongly connected to concepts like agroforestry.

cf61ae5e7ccc.title: Nature-based solutions
cf61ae5e7ccc.section: Types > Type 3 – Managing ecosystems in extensive ways
cf61ae5e7ccc.sentence: Type 3 consists of managing ecosystems in very extensive ways or even creating new ecosystems (e.g., artificial ecosystems with new assemblages of organisms for green roofs and walls to mitigate city warming and clean polluted air).

23820ceb732c.title: Nature-based solutions
23820ceb732c.section: Types > Type 3 – Managing ecosystems in extensive ways
23820ceb732c.sentence: Constructed wetlands are one example for a Type 3 NBS.

04117005977a.title: Nature-based solutions
04117005977a.sentence: The typology highlights that NBS can involve very different actions on ecosystems (from protection, to management, or even the creation of new ecosystems) and is based on the assumption that the higher the number of services and stakeholder groups targeted, the lower the capacity to maximise the delivery of each service and simultaneously fulfil the specific needs of all stakeholder groups.

8847ddf88885.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
8847ddf88885.section: Implementation and examples > Principles and standards for implementing EBA > Challenges
8847ddf88885.sentence: Although interest in Ecosystem-based Adaptation has grown, and meta-analyses of case studies are demonstrating the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of EbA interventions, there are recognized challenges that should be addressed or considered to increase adoption of the approach.

4af004f740ea.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
4af004f740ea.section: Implementation and examples > Principles and standards for implementing EBA > Challenges > Potential limitations of ecosystem services under a changing climate.
4af004f740ea.sentence: One challenge facing EbA is the identification of limits and thresholds beyond which EbA might not deliver adaptation benefits and the extent ecosystems can provide ecosystem services under a changing climate.

5db59bf21127.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
5db59bf21127.section: Implementation and examples > Principles and standards for implementing EBA > Challenges > Difficulty in monitoring, evaluation, and establishing the evidence base for effective EbA
5db59bf21127.sentence: Confusion around what Ecosystem-based Adaptation means has led to an array of different methodologies used for assessments, and the lack of consistent and comparable quantitative measures of EbA success and failure makes it difficult to argue the case for EbA in socio-economic terms.

845d0f5e07e5.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
845d0f5e07e5.section: Implementation and examples > Principles and standards for implementing EBA > Challenges > Governance and institutional constraints
845d0f5e07e5.sentence: Because EbA is a multi-sectoral policy issue, the challenges of governing and planning are immense.

ff97af337a67.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
ff97af337a67.section: Implementation and examples > Principles and standards for implementing EBA > Challenges > Governance and institutional constraints
ff97af337a67.sentence: This is due in part to the fact that EbA involves both the sectors that manage ecosystems and those that benefit from ecosystem services.

b7bbd8ec29ed.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
b7bbd8ec29ed.section: Implementation and examples > Principles and standards for implementing EBA > Challenges > Economic and financial constraints
b7bbd8ec29ed.sentence: Broad macroeconomic considerations such as economic development, poverty, and access to financial capital to implement climate adaptation options are contributing factors to constraints impeding greater uptake of EbA.

4fe5db864871.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
4fe5db864871.section: Implementation and examples > Principles and standards for implementing EBA > Challenges > Social and cultural barriers
4fe5db864871.sentence: A clear factor constraining EbA is varying perceptions of risks and cultural preferences for particular types of management approaches such as cultural preferences for what a particular landscape should look like.

760a8b5e8a87.title: Ecological engineering
760a8b5e8a87.section: Design guidelines, functional classes, and design principles
760a8b5e8a87.sentence: Mitsch and Jorgensen identified five Functional Classes for ecological engineering designs:

d3f16cf4abed.title: Ecological engineering
d3f16cf4abed.section: Design guidelines, functional classes, and design principles
d3f16cf4abed.sentence: - Ecosystem utilized to reduce/solve pollution problem.

0b00f93998ad.title: Ecological engineering
0b00f93998ad.section: Design guidelines, functional classes, and design principles
0b00f93998ad.sentence: Example: phytoremediation, wastewater wetland, and bioretention of stormwater to filter excess nutrients and metals pollution

469e61b707bf.title: Ecological engineering
469e61b707bf.section: Design guidelines, functional classes, and design principles
469e61b707bf.sentence: - Ecosystem imitated or copied to address resource problem.

536fd8df2eb3.title: Ecological engineering
536fd8df2eb3.section: Design guidelines, functional classes, and design principles
536fd8df2eb3.sentence: Example: forest restoration, replacement wetlands, and installing street side rain gardens to extend canopy cover to optimize residential and urban cooling

5d37a32fbe62.title: Ecological engineering
5d37a32fbe62.section: Design guidelines, functional classes, and design principles

0873136400d6.title: Ecological engineering
0873136400d6.section: Design guidelines, functional classes, and design principles
0873136400d6.sentence: Example: mine land restoration, lake restoration, and channel aquatic restoration with mature riparian corridors

e4d3e1ae7d18.title: Ecological engineering
e4d3e1ae7d18.section: Design guidelines, functional classes, and design principles
e4d3e1ae7d18.sentence: - Ecosystem modified in ecologically sound way.

58b41c5953eb.title: Ecological engineering
58b41c5953eb.section: Design guidelines, functional classes, and design principles
58b41c5953eb.sentence: - Ecosystems used for benefit without destroying balance.

64524616adc7.title: Ecological engineering
64524616adc7.section: Design guidelines, functional classes, and design principles
64524616adc7.sentence: Example: sustainable agro-ecosystems, multispecies aquaculture, and introducing agroforestry plots into residential property to generate primary production at multiple vertical levels.

5ee0f85256cf.title: Ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction
5ee0f85256cf.sentence: Ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction (Eco-DRR) is based on disaster risk reduction (DRR) and the purpose of Eco-DRR is to prevent and reduce disasters by utilizing ecosystems.

de04b8b71519.title: Ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction
de04b8b71519.sentence: Eco-DRR is to maintain ecosystems and ecosystem services, to use them as buffer zones and buffers for dangerous natural phenomena, and to provide humans and local communities with functions such as food and water supply.

707b17ddcf86.title: Ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction
707b17ddcf86.sentence: Eco-DRR is closely related to Ecosystem-based adaptation (EbA), approaches to adapt to climate change.

3a7ada2f54cb.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
3a7ada2f54cb.section: Policy frameworks > Disaster risk reduction policy
3a7ada2f54cb.sentence: Measures and interventions applied as part of EbA are often closely linked or similar to those employed under ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction (Eco-DRR).

57189b9e80d0.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
57189b9e80d0.section: Policy frameworks > Disaster risk reduction policy
57189b9e80d0.sentence: The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction acknowledges that in order to strengthen disaster risk governance and manage disaster risk and risk reduction at global and regional levels, it is important "to promote transboundary cooperation to enable policy and planning for the implementation of ecosystem-based approaches with regard to shared resources, such as within river basins and along coastlines, to build resilience and reduce disaster risk, including epidemic and displacement risk".

83050a90c9a6.title: Ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction
83050a90c9a6.sentence: However, disaster risk reduction research has tended to focus on urban areas of the Global North.

688d1090fa88.title: Ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction
688d1090fa88.sentence: More research is needed in coastal, dryland and watershed areas and the Global South.

028cf0797bee.title: Conservation International
028cf0797bee.sentence: CI-affiliated scientists have also contributed to work quantifying the climate-mitigation potential of natural climate solutions, including conservation, restoration and improved land-management actions that increase carbon storage or avoid greenhouse-gas emissions.

00226d0e1268.title: Carbon farming
00226d0e1268.sentence: The Canadian government has allocated CAD$885M to spend between 2021-31 on adopting climate solutions in agriculture as part of the CAD$2B Natural Climate Solutions Fund.

6c6a8a24b8cd.title: Stormwater
6c6a8a24b8cd.sentence: Stormwater, also written storm water, is water that originates from precipitation (storm), including heavy rain and meltwater from hail and snow.

6e7a6bca5a2b.title: Stormwater
6e7a6bca5a2b.sentence: Stormwater can soak into the soil (infiltrate) and become groundwater, be stored on depressed land surface in ponds and puddles, evaporate back into the atmosphere, or contribute to surface runoff.

db3c4807737f.title: Stormwater
db3c4807737f.sentence: In natural landscapes, such as forests, soil absorbs much of the stormwater.

63f7cedb6a1f.title: Stormwater
63f7cedb6a1f.sentence: Plants also reduce stormwater by improving infiltration, intercepting precipitation as it falls, and by taking up water through their roots.

a544b762254a.title: Stormwater
a544b762254a.sentence: In developed environments, such as cities, unmanaged stormwater can create two major issues: one related to the volume and timing of runoff (flooding) and the other related to potential contaminants the water is carrying (water pollution).

5b090d711c23.title: Stormwater
5b090d711c23.sentence: With less vegetation and more impervious surfaces (parking lots, roads, buildings, compacted soil), developed areas allow less rain to infiltrate into the ground, and more runoff is generated than in undeveloped conditions.

b7f42e0f65ff.title: Stormwater
b7f42e0f65ff.sentence: This greatly increases the volume of water in waterways and the discharge of those waterways, leading to erosion and flooding.

aa2152779e53.title: Stormwater
aa2152779e53.sentence: Because the water is flushed out of the watershed during the storm event, little infiltrates the soil, replenishes groundwater, or supplies stream baseflow in dry weather.

ec090ef81f41.title: Stormwater
ec090ef81f41.sentence: Most runoff is conveyed directly as surface water to nearby streams, rivers or other large water bodies (wetlands, lakes and oceans) without treatment.

8c64450c06d0.title: Stormwater
8c64450c06d0.sentence: The effect of phosphorus, either dissolved from (fertilizers) or bound to sediment particles from construction or agriculture runoff, causes algae and toxic cyanobacteria (aka Blue-green algae) blooms in receiving lakes.

59e54ba4f903.title: Stormwater
59e54ba4f903.sentence: Stormwater is a major cause of urban flooding, which is the inundation of land or property in a built-up environment caused by stormwater overwhelming the capacity of drainage systems, such as storm sewers.

ceb5bb048499.title: Flood management
ceb5bb048499.sentence: Flood management or flood control are methods used to reduce or prevent the detrimental effects of flood waters.

d13ddf344fdf.title: Flood management
d13ddf344fdf.sentence: Flooding can be caused by a mix of both natural processes, such as extreme weather upstream, and human changes to waterbodies and runoff.

52295808b3c6.title: Flood management
52295808b3c6.sentence: Flood management methods can be either of the structural type (i.e. flood control) and of the non-structural type.

3560828dd891.title: Flood management
3560828dd891.sentence: Structural methods hold back floodwaters physically, while non-structural methods do not.

c1ba596d8e0e.title: Flood management
c1ba596d8e0e.section: Causes of flooding > Precipitation, absorption, and runoff
c1ba596d8e0e.sentence: Flooding can be exacerbated by increased amounts of impervious surface or by other natural hazards such as wildfires, which reduce the supply of vegetation that can absorb rainfall.

3038481c0046.title: Flood management
3038481c0046.sentence: Natural flooding has many beneficial environmental effects.

1d8a6b581626.title: Flood management
1d8a6b581626.sentence: This kind of flooding is usually a seasonal occurrence where floods help replenish soil fertility, restore wetlands and promote biodiversity.

480a3f7f0ed2.title: Flood management
480a3f7f0ed2.sentence: The costs of flood protection rise as more people and property are to be protected.

40be50cbe8b4.title: Flood management
40be50cbe8b4.sentence: The US FEMA, for example, estimates that for every $1.00 spent on mitigation, $4.00 is saved.

07e0a6e3cd5f.title: Flood management
07e0a6e3cd5f.sentence: Wetlands are effective for flood management strategies, particularly in coastal regions, because they are able to hold excess water that flows towards inland regions.

a8d9495162ed.title: Flood management
a8d9495162ed.sentence: For example, the communities of multiple bays and river deltas, including the Chesapeake Bay, the Mississippi River delta, and the Yangtze River delta, benefit from local wetlands with respect to flood management, specifically because wetlands are able to protect inland communities from storm surges that these regions often face.

8b6cbbf54d21.title: Green infrastructure
8b6cbbf54d21.sentence: Green infrastructure or blue-green infrastructure refers to a network that provides the "ingredients" for solving urban and climatic challenges by building with nature.

93d6d03c5379.title: Green infrastructure
93d6d03c5379.sentence: When nature is harnessed by people and used as an infrastructural system it is called "green infrastructure".

3ccca0740226.title: Green infrastructure
3ccca0740226.sentence: Nature can be used to provide important services for communities by protecting them against flooding or excessive heat, or helping to improve air, soil and water quality.

e11dd1e16cd8.title: Green infrastructure
e11dd1e16cd8.sentence: The main components of this approach include stormwater management, climate adaptation, the reduction of heat stress, increasing biodiversity, food production, better air quality, sustainable energy production, clean water, and healthy soils, as well as more human centered functions, such as increased quality of life through recreation and the provision of shade and shelter in and around towns and cities.

e529f2ce933a.title: Green infrastructure
e529f2ce933a.sentence: However, the term does not have a widely recognized definition.

867357278e06.title: Green infrastructure
867357278e06.sentence: The term "green infrastructure" is sometimes expanded to "multifunctional" green infrastructure.

46b19cf1f6cd.title: Green infrastructure
46b19cf1f6cd.sentence: Multifunctionality in this context refers to the integration and interaction of different functions or activities on the same piece of land.

613f145512b5.title: Green infrastructure
613f145512b5.sentence: Green infrastructure concepts originated in mid-1980s proposals for best management practices that would achieve more holistic stormwater quantity management goals for runoff volume reduction, erosion prevention, and aquifer recharge.

b3cf3e1cad3b.title: Green infrastructure
b3cf3e1cad3b.sentence: Green infrastructure as a term did not appear until the early 1990s, although ideas of green infrastructure had been used long before that.

20e96e26a7c4.title: Green infrastructure
20e96e26a7c4.sentence: The first coined use of the term was seen in a 1994 report by Buddy MacKay, chair of the Florida Greenways Commission, to Florida governor Lawton Chiles about an infrastructure project undertaken in 1991: Florida Greenways Project.

8a1c3f54142c.title: Green infrastructure
8a1c3f54142c.section: Types of green infrastructure > Urban forests
8a1c3f54142c.sentence: They are an important component of urban green infrastructure systems.

bd2dcd3aa532.title: Green infrastructure
bd2dcd3aa532.section: Types of green infrastructure > Constructed wetlands
bd2dcd3aa532.sentence: Constructed wetlands are manmade wetlands, which work as a bio-filtration system.

118eb2d2ca30.title: Green infrastructure
118eb2d2ca30.section: Types of green infrastructure > Green and blue roofs
118eb2d2ca30.sentence: Green roofs improve air and water quality while reducing energy cost.

5295acd8fd0c.title: Green infrastructure
5295acd8fd0c.section: Types of green infrastructure > Rain gardens
5295acd8fd0c.sentence: Rain gardens are a form of stormwater management using water capture.

5c095a063ac1.title: Green infrastructure
5c095a063ac1.section: Types of green infrastructure > Stormwater basins
5c095a063ac1.sentence: Stormwater basins collect rainwater in vegetated depressions in order to reduce runoff loads to sewers, reduce erosion, filter rainwater, and prevent flooding.

514b0788c248.title: Green infrastructure
514b0788c248.sentence: Bioswales are stormwater runoff systems providing an alternative to traditional storm sewers.

113f00bf1dcf.title: Urban flooding
113f00bf1dcf.sentence: Urban flooding is the inundation of land or property in cities or other built environment, caused by rainfall or coastal storm surges overwhelming the capacity of drainage systems, such as storm sewers.

12d51998163e.title: Urban flooding
12d51998163e.sentence: Urban flooding can occur regardless of whether or not affected communities are located within designated floodplains or near any body of water.

ad8c7adc9a2a.title: Urban flooding
ad8c7adc9a2a.sentence: Any activities that enlarge the impermeable surface areas in a city can increase the flood risk.

5b67985d4de7.title: Urban flooding
5b67985d4de7.sentence: Impermeable surface areas are generated through soil sealing as this reduces drainage options of floodwaters.

8c069147b0bc.title: Urban flooding
8c069147b0bc.sentence: Many of the common causes of urban flooding, including storm surges, heavy precipitation, and river overflow, are expected to increase in frequency and severity as climate change intensifies and causes increases in ocean and river levels.

95e6ba64e2a7.title: Urban flooding
95e6ba64e2a7.sentence: In 2020, floods caused an estimated 6,000 deaths and caused US$51.3B in damages globally.

9423a293ad50.title: Stormwater
9423a293ad50.sentence: Where properties are built with basements, urban flooding is the primary cause of basement and sewer backups.

4ba2d0ac8a07.title: Stormwater
4ba2d0ac8a07.sentence: Although the number of casualties from urban flooding is usually limited, the economic, social and environmental consequences can be considerable: in addition to direct damage to property and infrastructure (highways, utilities and services), chronically wet houses are linked to an increase in respiratory problems and other illnesses.

4cb736a5f2c7.title: Urban flooding
4cb736a5f2c7.section: Mitigation and management > Building gray infrastructure
4cb736a5f2c7.sentence: One traditional urban flooding management strategy is building gray infrastructure, which is a set of infrastructure types (including dams and seawalls) traditionally constructed of concrete or other impervious materials and designed to prevent the flow of water.

6cd9c2872a5c.title: Urban flooding
6cd9c2872a5c.section: Mitigation and management > Using green infrastructure
6cd9c2872a5c.sentence: An alternative to gray infrastructure is green infrastructure, which refers to a set of strategies for absorbing and storing stormwater at or close to the location where it falls.

358bced46d04.title: Urban flooding
358bced46d04.section: Mitigation and management > Improving drainage systems
358bced46d04.sentence: One way urban flooding is commonly mitigated is via urban drainage systems, which transport storm water away from streets and businesses and into appropriate storage and drainage areas.

5816b76065cd.title: Urban flooding
5816b76065cd.section: Mitigation and management > Understanding and altering land use
5816b76065cd.sentence: In particular, increasing the percent of land dedicated to open, vegetated space can be helpful in providing an absorption and storage area for storm runoff.

e15fa21fd993.title: Constructed wetland
e15fa21fd993.sentence: A constructed wetland is an artificial wetland to treat sewage, greywater, stormwater runoff or industrial wastewater.

2d08fea974dc.title: Constructed wetland
2d08fea974dc.sentence: Constructed wetlands are engineered systems that use the natural functions of vegetation, soil, and organisms to provide secondary treatment to wastewater.

d1d58dcec221.title: Constructed wetland
d1d58dcec221.sentence: Vegetation in a wetland provides a substrate (roots, stems, and leaves) upon which microorganisms can grow as they break down organic materials.

ff2bc07dec64.title: Constructed wetland
ff2bc07dec64.sentence: Physical, chemical, and biological processes combine in wetlands to remove contaminants from wastewater.

32464c3722a2.title: Constructed wetland
32464c3722a2.sentence: Constructed wetlands have been used extensively for the removal of dissolved metals and metalloids.

2a23256d041d.title: Constructed wetland
2a23256d041d.sentence: Constructed wetlands mimic the functions of natural wetlands to capture stormwater, reduce nutrient loads, and create diverse wildlife habitat.

be1195b6806b.title: Constructed wetland
be1195b6806b.sentence: Since constructed wetlands are self-sustaining their lifetime costs are significantly lower than those of conventional treatment systems.

07aa38cdf1f7.title: Constructed wetland
07aa38cdf1f7.sentence: Often their capital costs are also lower compared to conventional treatment systems.

3999de1cd93a.title: Constructed wetland
3999de1cd93a.sentence: They do take up significant space, and are therefore not preferred where real estate costs are high.

053eb38bf759.title: Constructed wetland
053eb38bf759.sentence: Typhas and Phragmites are the main species used in constructed wetland due to their effectiveness, even though they can be invasive outside their native range.

dc52029fc56a.title: Constructed wetland
dc52029fc56a.sentence: Stormwater wetlands provide habitat for amphibians but the pollutants they accumulate can affect the survival of larval stages, potentially making them function as "ecological traps".

ddc38102fe35.title: Bioswale
ddc38102fe35.sentence: Bioswales are channels designed to concentrate and convey stormwater runoff while removing debris and pollution.

f3cc1fcab95c.title: Bioswale
f3cc1fcab95c.sentence: Bioswales are typically vegetated, mulched, or xeriscaped.

1904b402500e.title: Bioswale
1904b402500e.sentence: They consist of a swaled drainage course with gently sloped sides (less than 6%).

2907ca6777bd.title: Bioswale
2907ca6777bd.sentence: Bioswale design is intended to safely maximize the time water spends in the swale, which aids the collection and removal of pollutants, silt and debris.

4fe788cfa84e.title: Bioswale
4fe788cfa84e.sentence: The longer the runoff stays within the bioswale, the better the pollutant removal outcome.

c3b2ce38cbeb.title: Bioswale
c3b2ce38cbeb.sentence: As the storm water runoff flows through the bioswale, the pollutants are captured and settled by the leaves and stems of the plants.

475fbbe1562d.title: Bioswale
475fbbe1562d.sentence: The pollutants then enter the soil where they decompose or can be broken down by bacteria in healthy soil.

bc83536bc914.title: Bioswale
bc83536bc914.sentence: Bioswales can also be beneficial in recharging groundwater, reducing flooding and erosion, and creating a valuable habitat for pollinators.

10812315852d.title: Bioswale
10812315852d.sentence: Bioswales are commonly applied along streets and around parking lots, where substantial automotive pollution settles on the pavement and is flushed by the first instance of rain, known as the first flush.

b7e33849735e.title: Bioswale
b7e33849735e.sentence: There are four types of bioswales that can be constructed based on the needs of the location.

5f95395ad181.title: Bioswale
5f95395ad181.sentence: - Low grass bioswales utilize low growing grass that can be landscaped, similar to lawns.

e86247e2e514.title: Bioswale
e86247e2e514.sentence: - Vegetated bioswales are created with taller growing plants, ornamental vegetations, shrubs, and even trees.

da8e791f3898.title: Bioswale
da8e791f3898.sentence: - Low water use bioswales are helpful in areas that tend to be drier with hotter climate.

22ec4c2f9c10.title: Bioswale
22ec4c2f9c10.sentence: - Wet bioswales are similar to wetlands in which they retain water for a much longer period of time that allows for infiltration of stormwater instead of simply emptying the water at the end of the bioswale into storm drain inlets.

b35024f29de7.title: Bioswale
b35024f29de7.sentence: Improper maintenance can lead to high restoration costs to address inefficient bioswales.

dcb834f8575e.title: Bioswale
dcb834f8575e.sentence: Time and frequency of inspections vary based on different local governments, but should occur at least once a year.

6ba33ccb474c.title: Bioswale
6ba33ccb474c.sentence: In 1996, for Willamette River Park in Portland, Oregon, a total of 2330 lineal feet of bioswale was designed and installed to capture and prevent pollutant runoff from entering the Willamette River.

dc582dc313ed.title: Bioswale
dc582dc313ed.sentence: Intermittent check dams were installed to further abet silt capture, which reduced by 50% suspended solids entering the river system.

c2d04e789a34.title: Sustainable drainage system
c2d04e789a34.sentence: Sustainable drainage systems (also known as SuDS, SUDS, or sustainable urban drainage systems) are a collection of water management practices that aim to align modern drainage systems with natural water processes and are part of a larger green infrastructure strategy.

30ca172e0b05.title: Sustainable drainage system
30ca172e0b05.sentence: These efforts hope to mitigate the effect human development has had or may have on the natural water cycle, particularly surface runoff and water pollution trends.

884efdfc2c80.title: Sustainable drainage system
884efdfc2c80.sentence: As areas of vegetation are replaced by concrete, asphalt, or roofed structures, leading to impervious surfaces, the area loses its ability to absorb rainwater.

d67a315631d5.title: Sustainable drainage system
d67a315631d5.sentence: This rain is instead directed into surface water drainage systems, often overloading them and causing floods.

96dd6f7dbb74.title: Sustainable drainage system
96dd6f7dbb74.sentence: Many of these issues are addressed by SuDS systems by bypassing traditional drainage systems altogether and returning rainwater to natural water sources or streams as soon as possible.

78023017ff0e.title: Sustainable drainage system
78023017ff0e.sentence: The following are examples generally accepted as components in a SuDS system:

7aa47b37e8ac.title: Sustainable drainage system
7aa47b37e8ac.sentence: Bioswales are channels designed to concentrate and convey stormwater runoff while removing debris and pollution.

598859db4349.title: Sustainable drainage system
598859db4349.sentence: Permeable paving surfaces are made of either a porous material that enables stormwater to flow through it or nonporous blocks spaced so that water can flow between the gaps.

8a093d96d301.title: Sustainable drainage system
8a093d96d301.sentence: Artificial wetlands can be constructed in areas that see large volumes of storm water surges or runoff.

8e1d78d7f49e.title: Sustainable drainage system
8e1d78d7f49e.sentence: A retention basin, sometimes called a retention pond, wet detention basin, or storm water management pond (SWMP), is an artificial pond with vegetation around the perimeter and a permanent pool of water in its design.

08869fb03d17.title: Sustainable drainage system
08869fb03d17.sentence: A green roof or living roof is a roof of a building that is partially or completely covered with vegetation and a growing medium, planted over a waterproofing membrane.

c7eecdfc110f.title: Sustainable drainage system
c7eecdfc110f.sentence: Rain gardens are a form of stormwater management using water capture.

b5e22c0a62d2.title: Sustainable drainage system
b5e22c0a62d2.sentence: Downspout disconnection is a form of green infrastructure that separates roof downspouts from the sewer system and redirects roof water runoff into permeable surfaces.

a18b7b1dbca4.title: Sustainable drainage system
a18b7b1dbca4.sentence: Vegetation and soil help capture and remove pollutants from stormwater in many ways like adsorption, filtration, and plant uptake.

d808d0a07b02.title: Sustainable drainage system
d808d0a07b02.section: Benefits for stormwater management > Increased water supply
d808d0a07b02.sentence: More than half of the rain that falls in urban areas covered mostly by impervious surfaces ends up as runoff.

4c749a7a129f.title: Sustainable drainage system
4c749a7a129f.section: Benefits for stormwater management > Reduced costs
4c749a7a129f.sentence: The expenses for implementing green infrastructure are often smaller, planting a rain garden to deal with drainage costs less than digging tunnels and installing pipes.

554bc5614ff1.title: Sustainable drainage system
554bc5614ff1.sentence: Drainage systems have been found in ancient cities over 5,000 years old, including Minoan, Indus, Persian, and Mesopotamian civilizations.

5e3f6bfeaba7.title: Sustainable drainage system
5e3f6bfeaba7.sentence: Modern drainage systems did not appear until the 19th century in Western Europe, although most of these systems were primarily built to deal with sewage issues rising from rapid urbanization.

a72cbeb0bc2f.title: Water-sensitive urban design
a72cbeb0bc2f.sentence: Water-sensitive urban design (WSUD) is a land planning and engineering design approach which integrates the urban water cycle, including stormwater, groundwater, and wastewater management and water supply, into urban design to minimise environmental degradation and improve aesthetic and recreational appeal.

9b378e625452.title: Water-sensitive urban design
9b378e625452.sentence: WSUD is a term used in the Middle East and Australia and is similar to low-impact development (LID), a term used in the United States; and Sustainable Drainage System (SuDS), a term used in the United Kingdom.

31ef4b01a84e.title: Water-sensitive urban design
31ef4b01a84e.section: Differences from conventional urban stormwater management
31ef4b01a84e.sentence: WSUD regards urban stormwater runoff as a resource rather than a nuisance or liability.

25ea72906953.title: Water-sensitive urban design
25ea72906953.sentence: This resulted in a strong focus on the design of stormwater management systems that rapidly convey stormwater runoff directly to streams with little or no focus on ecosystem preservation.

e4081898c247.title: Water-sensitive urban design
e4081898c247.sentence: - Protecting and enhancing creeks, rivers, and wetlands within urban environments

f5a7458699a8.title: Water-sensitive urban design
f5a7458699a8.sentence: - Protecting and improving the water quality of water draining from urban environments into creeks, rivers, and wetlands

642569b4dcea.title: Water-sensitive urban design
642569b4dcea.sentence: - Restoring the urban water balance by maximizing the reuse of stormwater, recycled water, and grey water

5b05872d0df4.title: Water-sensitive urban design
5b05872d0df4.section: Common WSUD practices > Road layout and streetscape > Bioretention systems
5b05872d0df4.sentence: Bioretention systems involve the treatment of water by vegetation prior to filtration of sediment and other solids through prescribed media.

22d890f6ac11.title: Water-sensitive urban design
22d890f6ac11.section: Common WSUD practices > Road layout and streetscape > Infiltration trenches and systems
22d890f6ac11.sentence: Infiltration trenches are shallow excavated structures filled with permeable materials such as gravel or rock to create an underground reservoir.

e4407b83fbed.title: Water-sensitive urban design
e4407b83fbed.section: Common WSUD practices > Road layout and streetscape > Porous paving
e4407b83fbed.sentence: Porous paving (or pervious paving) is an alternative to conventional impermeable pavement and allows infiltration of runoff water to the soil or to a dedicated water storage reservoir below it In reasonably flat areas such as car parks, driveways, and lightly used roads, it decreases the volume and velocity of stormwater runoff and can improve water quality by removing contaminants through filtering, interception, and biological treatment.

bd912e9f940f.title: Water-sensitive urban design
bd912e9f940f.section: Common WSUD practices > Public open space > Sedimentation basins
bd912e9f940f.sentence: Sedimentation basins (otherwise known as sediment basins) are used to remove (by settling) coarse to medium-sized sediments and to regulate water flows and are often the first element in a WSUD treatment system.

dc141cc0ec09.title: Water-sensitive urban design
dc141cc0ec09.section: Common WSUD practices > Public open space > Constructed wetlands
dc141cc0ec09.sentence: Constructed wetlands are designed to remove stormwater pollutants associated with fine to colloidal particles and dissolved contaminants.

6c10337a1cb2.title: Water-sensitive urban design
6c10337a1cb2.section: Common WSUD practices > Public open space > Swales and buffer strips
6c10337a1cb2.sentence: Swales and buffer strips are used to convey stormwater in lieu of pipes and provide a buffer strip between receiving waters (e.g. creek or wetland) and impervious areas of a catchment.

f445290b69f7.title: Water-sensitive urban design
f445290b69f7.section: Common WSUD practices > Water re-use > Rainwater tanks
f445290b69f7.sentence: Rainwater tanks (see also Rainwater Harvesting) are designed to conserve potable water by harvesting rain and stormwater to partially meet domestic water demands (e.g. during drought periods).

59def07c797a.title: Nature-based solutions
59def07c797a.sentence: Another framework called "Water Sensitive Urban Design" (WSUD) came out of Australia in the 1990s while Low Impact Development (LID) came out of the U.S.

84897e2de7ba.title: Water-sensitive urban design
84897e2de7ba.section: Policy, planning, and legislation > State legislation and policy > Victoria
84897e2de7ba.sentence: New residential developments are subject to a permeability standard that at least 20 percent of sites should not be covered by impervious surfaces.

088158680698.title: Water-sensitive urban design
088158680698.section: Issues affecting decision-making in WSUD > Impediments to the adoption of WSUD
088158680698.sentence: Major issues affecting the adoption of WSUD include:

7eb91b59cd0c.title: Water-sensitive urban design
7eb91b59cd0c.section: Issues affecting decision-making in WSUD > Impediments to the adoption of WSUD
7eb91b59cd0c.sentence: - Regulatory framework barriers and institutional fragmentation at state and local government levels

145a67fa8ec4.title: Bioretention
145a67fa8ec4.sentence: Bioretention is the process in which contaminants and sedimentation are removed from stormwater runoff.

48d26a3ee58f.title: Bioretention
48d26a3ee58f.sentence: The main objective of the bioretention cell is to attenuate peak runoff as well as to remove stormwater runoff pollutants.

ec3d5deb4f0b.title: Bioretention
ec3d5deb4f0b.sentence: Stormwater is firstly directed into the designed treatment area, which conventionally consists of a sand bed (which serves as a transition to the actual soil), a filter media layer (which consists of layered materials of various composition), and plants atop the filter media.

17d66c7d8a42.title: Bioretention
17d66c7d8a42.sentence: Stored water in the bioretention area planting soil exfiltrates over a period of days into the underlying soils.

27b07ff2d94d.title: Bioretention
27b07ff2d94d.sentence: The term "Bioretention" refers to the fact that the biomass in the treatment media, such as plants and bacteria, retains, absorbs, breaks down, and cycles contaminants found in runoff.

6b4a0feea7b5.title: Bioretention
6b4a0feea7b5.sentence: Filtration, adsorption, chemical transformation, and biological degradation are the main methods of pollutant treatment in bioretention.

401bdd6c4ca6.title: Bioretention
401bdd6c4ca6.sentence: If left untreated, these nutrients contribute to eutrophication in downstream aquatic systems, leading to algal blooms and oxygen depletion.

7be531f7f0de.title: Bioretention
7be531f7f0de.sentence: Bioretention media designed with optimal soil and organic content can significantly reduce both total and dissolved forms of nitrogen and phosphorus.

48c87ca63adc.title: Bioretention
48c87ca63adc.sentence: In laboratory experiments, bioretention cells removed 94%, 88%, 95%, and >95% of zinc, copper, lead, and cadmium, respectively from water with metal concentrations typical of stormwater runoff.

c6ab15ca93bb.title: Bioretention
c6ab15ca93bb.sentence: While this is a great benefit for water quality improvement, bioretention systems have a finite capacity for heavy metal removal.

27175d013bff.title: Bioretention
27175d013bff.sentence: Therefore, removal and replacement of the bioretention layer will become necessary in areas with heavy metal pollutants in stormwater runoff to extend the life of the treatment system.

b7486e6d259d.title: Bioretention
b7486e6d259d.sentence: An unstable surrounding soil stratum and soils with a clay content greater than 25 percent may preclude the use of bioretention, as would a site with slopes greater than 20 percent or a site with mature trees that would be removed during construction of the best management practices.

0fa9d241ed78.title: Rain garden
0fa9d241ed78.sentence: Rain gardens, also called bioretention facilities, are one of a variety of practices designed to increase reabsorption of rain runoff by the soil.

c28cc4dc7b54.title: Green infrastructure
c28cc4dc7b54.section: Types of green infrastructure > Rain gardens
c28cc4dc7b54.sentence: Rain gardens are shallow depressed areas in the landscape, planted with shrubs and plants that are used to collect rainwater from roofs or pavement and allows for the stormwater to slowly infiltrate into the ground.

be12a4039d13.title: Rain garden
be12a4039d13.sentence: Rain gardens are designed landscape sites that reduce the flow rate, total quantity, and pollutant load of runoff from impervious urban areas like roofs, driveways, walkways, parking lots, and compacted lawn areas.

e3828d7c4942.title: Rain garden
e3828d7c4942.sentence: Rain gardens rely on plants and natural or engineered soil medium to retain stormwater and increase the lag time of infiltration, while remediating and filtering pollutants carried by urban runoff.

75aa0e8974c6.title: Rain garden
75aa0e8974c6.section: Purpose > Urban runoff mitigation > Urban hydrology
75aa0e8974c6.sentence: In contrast, central urban areas are filled with impervious surfaces, which can account for about 90–100 percent of the land cover.

ca2f301a5679.title: Rain garden
ca2f301a5679.section: Purpose > Urban runoff mitigation > Urban hydrology
ca2f301a5679.sentence: In suburban areas, impervious surfaces typically only cover 5–10 percent of the land.

5146eb02f53d.title: Rain garden
5146eb02f53d.sentence: The bioretention soil mixture should typically contain 60% sand, 20% compost, and 20% topsoil.

72b69f89c5c9.title: Rain garden
72b69f89c5c9.sentence: Native and adapted plants are commonly selected for rain gardens because they are more tolerant of the local climate, soil, and water conditions; have deep and variable root systems for enhanced water infiltration and drought tolerance; increase habitat value, diversity for local ecological communities, and overall sustainability once established.

0736675d66c3.title: Rain garden
0736675d66c3.sentence: The rain gardens for residential use were developed in 1990 in Prince George's County, Maryland, when Dick Brinker, a developer building a new housing subdivision had the idea to replace the traditional best management practices (BMP) pond with a bioretention area.

a4bc5259c23b.title: Rain garden
a4bc5259c23b.sentence: This system proved to be highly cost-effective.

75fea3fdbc0a.title: Rain garden
75fea3fdbc0a.sentence: Ponding beyond 48 hours or channelization may indicate clogging which is one of the most common challenges associated with rain gardens.

8d3c176fa43a.title: Rain garden
8d3c176fa43a.sentence: This study showed that over four years, there were 28 large storm events in Xi'an.

fd34036d034c.title: Rain garden
fd34036d034c.sentence: Within these 28 storms, the rain garden was able to retain the rainfall from a majority of the storms.

33f3bd6d0732.title: Rain garden
33f3bd6d0732.sentence: Only 5 of these storms caused the rain garden to overflow.

4935d182fba2.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
4935d182fba2.sentence: Low-impact development (LID) is a term used in Canada and the United States to describe a land planning and engineering design approach to manage stormwater runoff as part of green infrastructure.

f37061fad874.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
f37061fad874.sentence: This approach implements engineered small-scale hydrologic controls to replicate the pre-development hydrologic regime of watersheds through infiltrating, filtering, storing, evaporating, and detaining runoff close to its source.

4918360a13e5.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
4918360a13e5.sentence: Broadly equivalent terms used elsewhere include Sustainable drainage systems (SuDS) in the United Kingdom (where LID has a different meaning), water-sensitive urban design (WSUD) in Australia, natural drainage systems in Seattle, Washington, "Environmental Site Design" as used by the Maryland Department of the Environment, and "Onsite Stormwater Management", as used by the Washington State Department of Ecology.

20dbb40094ac.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
20dbb40094ac.section: Alternative to conventional stormwater management practices
20dbb40094ac.sentence: A concept that began in Prince George's County, Maryland in 1990, LID began as an alternative to traditional stormwater best management practices (BMPs) installed at construction projects.

09460b7b99cf.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
09460b7b99cf.section: Alternative to conventional stormwater management practices
09460b7b99cf.sentence: Officials found that the traditional practices such as detention ponds and retention basins were not cost-effective and the results did not meet water quality goals.

04fb4bf86644.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
04fb4bf86644.sentence: - Conserve natural areas wherever possible (don't pave over the whole site if you don't need to).

53bedc154998.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
53bedc154998.sentence: - Minimize the development impact on hydrology.

322f9e6f39db.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
322f9e6f39db.sentence: - Maintain runoff rate and duration from the site (don't let the water leave the site).

c61c83164cfc.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
c61c83164cfc.sentence: - Scatter integrated management practices (IMPs) throughout your site – IMPs are decentralized, microscale controls that infiltrate, store, evaporate, and/or detain runoff close to the source.

85b9ed183f0b.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
85b9ed183f0b.sentence: - Implement pollution prevention, proper maintenance and public education programs.

bf1785ba5b74.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
bf1785ba5b74.sentence: - Bioretention cells, also known as rain gardens

1afa711d0ec1.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
1afa711d0ec1.sentence: - Pervious concrete, also called "porous pavement", similar to permeable paving

d72bbd0b19e0.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
d72bbd0b19e0.sentence: - Grassed swales, also known as bioswales.

26c4c5e40223.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
26c4c5e40223.section: Designing for low-impact development > Storage and reuse
26c4c5e40223.sentence: Rainwater harvesting is an LID practice that facilitates the reuse of stormwater.

abd3aeaac94b.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
abd3aeaac94b.sentence: His data indicated that LID rain gardens can hold up to 90% of water after a major rain event and release this water over a time scale of up to two weeks.

f968f02abb8b.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
f968f02abb8b.sentence: LID can also be used to eliminate the need for stormwater ponds, which occupy expensive land.

e88f7ef9b98c.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
e88f7ef9b98c.sentence: Incorporating LID into designs enables developers to build more homes on the same plot of land and maximize their profits.

441b227048f8.title: Low-impact development (U.S. and Canada)
441b227048f8.sentence: In some municipalities, LID can be a cost-effective way to reduce the incidence of combined sewer overflows (CSO).

079312c7c59a.title: Permeable paving
079312c7c59a.sentence: Permeable paving surfaces are made of either a porous material that enables stormwater to flow through it or nonporous blocks spaced so that water can flow between the gaps.

f952076954f8.title: Permeable paving
f952076954f8.sentence: Permeable pavement surfaces may be composed of; pervious concrete, porous asphalt, paving stones, or interlocking pavers.

ddc89e21a56d.title: Permeable paving
ddc89e21a56d.sentence: In addition to reducing surface runoff, permeable paving systems can trap suspended solids, thereby filtering pollutants from stormwater.

d2c826824f56.title: Permeable paving
d2c826824f56.sentence: They can reduce downstream flooding and stream bank erosion, and maintain base flows in rivers to keep ecosystems self-sustaining.

fc24d8a90bef.title: Permeable paving
fc24d8a90bef.sentence: In areas where infiltration is not possible due to unsuitable soil conditions, permeable pavements are used in the attenuation mode where water is retained in the pavement and slowly released to surface water systems between storm events.

462bd78f84df.title: Permeable paving
462bd78f84df.sentence: Some estimates put the cost of permeable paving at about one third more expensive than that of conventional impervious paving.

71935260e619.title: Permeable paving
71935260e619.sentence: Using permeable paving, however, can reduce the cost of providing larger or more stormwater BMPs on site, and these savings should be factored into any cost analysis.

bb6f80c7d9e4.title: Permeable paving
bb6f80c7d9e4.sentence: If maintenance is not carried out on a regular basis, the porous pavements can begin to function more like impervious surfaces.

8ee67f047021.title: Permeable paving
8ee67f047021.sentence: These "hot spots" include commercial plant nurseries, recycling facilities, fueling stations, industrial storage, marinas, some outdoor loading facilities, public works yards, hazardous materials generators (if containers are exposed to rainfall), vehicle service, washing, and maintenance areas, and steam cleaning facilities.

f009e42c342a.title: Permeable paving
f009e42c342a.sentence: Since porous pavement is an infiltration practice, it should not be applied at stormwater hot spots due to the potential for groundwater contamination.

6cb6f8f33548.title: Stormwater
6cb6f8f33548.sentence: Managing the quantity and quality of stormwater is termed, "Stormwater Management." The term Best Management Practice (BMP) or stormwater control measure (SCM) is often used to refer to both structural or engineered control devices and systems (e.g. retention ponds) to treat or store polluted stormwater, as well as operational or procedural practices (e.g. street sweeping).

fe2bd62120b4.title: Stormwater
fe2bd62120b4.sentence: - control of hazardous materials to prevent release of pollutants into the environment (source control);

3493e0cbd35f.title: Stormwater
3493e0cbd35f.sentence: - planning and construction of stormwater systems like retention basins, buried vaults with various kinds of media filters, and vortex separators to remove coarse solids before they pollute surface waters or groundwater resources;

b938f9cfe134.title: Stormwater
b938f9cfe134.sentence: - acquisition and protection of natural waterways or rehabilitation;

16174edc2545.title: Stormwater
16174edc2545.sentence: - building nature-based solutions such as ponds, swales, constructed wetlands or green infrastructure solutions to work with existing or "hard" drainage structures, such as pipes and concrete channels (constructed wetlands built for stormwater treatment can also serve as habitat for plants, amphibians and fish)

774a0cd1dcfe.title: Stormwater
774a0cd1dcfe.section: Stormwater management > Institutional and policy aspects
774a0cd1dcfe.sentence: - development of funding approaches to stormwater programs potentially including stormwater user fees and the creation of a stormwater utility;

3ced693df863.title: Stormwater

3ced693df863.sentence: - development of long-term asset management programs to repair and replace aging infrastructure;

5727d2f18ad2.title: Stormwater
5727d2f18ad2.section: Stormwater management > Institutional and policy aspects
5727d2f18ad2.sentence: - revision of current stormwater regulations to address comprehensive stormwater needs;

97bc4640631b.title: Stormwater
97bc4640631b.section: Stormwater management > Institutional and policy aspects
97bc4640631b.sentence: - education of a community about how its actions affect water quality, and about what it can do to improve water quality.

570886c05d8e.title: Stormwater
570886c05d8e.sentence: Stormwater management facilities (SWMF) are generally designed using Stokes' law to allow rudimentary treatment through the settling particulate matter larger than 40 micron in size and to impound water to reduce downstream flooding.

7a0f94f7ad7a.title: Stormwater
7a0f94f7ad7a.sentence: Stormwater infrastructure is an expensive long-term investment that is difficult to replace when the underlying circumstances change.

d1cbe6b6e703.title: Stormwater

bdbb082004e1.title: Stormwater
bdbb082004e1.section: Regulations > United States > Nonpoint source pollution management
bdbb082004e1.sentence: Agricultural runoff (except for concentrated animal feeding operations, or "CAFO") is classified as nonpoint source pollution under the CWA.

97228ef57f6e.title: Stormwater
97228ef57f6e.section: Regulations > United States > Nonpoint source pollution management
97228ef57f6e.sentence: It is not included in the CWA definition of "point source" and therefore not subject to NPDES permit requirements.

c521c205a1d5.title: Flood management
c521c205a1d5.sentence: - Structural flood management (i.e.: flood control) is the reduction of the effects of a flood using physical solutions, such as reservoirs, levees, dredging and diversions.

9887be0f625c.title: Flood management
9887be0f625c.sentence: Some methods of flood control have been practiced since ancient times.

3749469b7a7a.title: Flood management
3749469b7a7a.sentence: These methods include planting vegetation to retain extra water, terracing hillsides to slow flow downhill, and the construction of floodways (man-made channels to divert floodwater).

93b3300495af.title: Flood management
93b3300495af.sentence: Many large dams have flood-control reservations in which the level of a reservoir must be kept below a certain elevation before the onset of the rainy/summer melt season to allow a certain amount of space in which floodwaters can fill.

fbe5ec8b6ae0.title: Flood management
fbe5ec8b6ae0.sentence: Defenses such as levees, bunds, reservoirs, and weirs are used to prevent rivers from bursting their banks.

26b4d85652fe.title: Flood management
26b4d85652fe.sentence: Coastal flooding is addressed with coastal defenses, such as sea walls, beach nourishment, and barrier islands.

ce26cc98c2ab.title: Flood management
ce26cc98c2ab.section: Structural methods > Floodplains and groundwater replenishment
ce26cc98c2ab.sentence: Excess water can be used for groundwater replenishment by diversion onto land that can absorb the water.

972630eee511.title: Flood management
972630eee511.section: Structural methods > Floodplains and groundwater replenishment
972630eee511.sentence: This technique can reduce the impact of later droughts by using the ground as a natural reservoir.

c3ef692b43fb.title: Flood management
c3ef692b43fb.sentence: There are several methods of non-structural flood management that form part of flood risk management strategies.

e963488e14b5.title: Flood management
e963488e14b5.sentence: These can involve policies that reduces the amount of urban structures built around floodplains or flood prone areas through land zoning regulations.

e50bb4d335f6.title: Flood management
e50bb4d335f6.sentence: Stakeholder engagement is a useful tool for flood risk management that allows enhanced public engagement for agreements to be reached on policy discussions.

77966fad3db1.title: Flood management
77966fad3db1.sentence: Different management considerations can be taken into account, including emergency management and disaster risk reduction goals, interactions of land-use planning with the integration of flood risks and required policies.

a89a899a097e.title: Flood management
a89a899a097e.sentence: Property owners may fit their homes to stop water entering by blocking doors and air vents, waterproofing important areas and sandbagging the edges of the building.

d94f04fcb7aa.title: Flood management
d94f04fcb7aa.sentence: Private precautionary measures are increasingly important in flood risk management.

1b76a5d5bb8a.title: Flood management
1b76a5d5bb8a.sentence: Buildings and other urban infrastructure can be designed so that even if a flood does happen, the city can recover quickly and costs are minimized.

97dceab14b6b.title: Flood management
97dceab14b6b.sentence: For example, homes can be put on stilts or build on an elevated level.

b6527935d020.title: Green infrastructure
b6527935d020.sentence: Green infrastructure is often cheaper than other conventional water management strategies.

a4ec5eb608e9.title: Green infrastructure
a4ec5eb608e9.sentence: A comprehensive green infrastructure in Philadelphia is planned to cost just $1.2 billion over the next 25 years, compared to over $6 billion for "grey" infrastructure (concrete tunnels created to move water).

b0eceb7e33aa.title: Green infrastructure
b0eceb7e33aa.sentence: A 2012 study focusing on 479 green infrastructure projects across the United States found that 44% of green infrastructure projects reduced costs, compared to the 31% that increased the costs.

72711243412a.title: Green infrastructure
72711243412a.sentence: The most notable cost savings were due to reduced stormwater runoff and decreased heating and cooling costs.

83709d39882c.title: Green infrastructure
83709d39882c.sentence: The city of Philadelphia, for example, discovered that a new green infrastructure plan would cost $1.2 billion over a 25-year period, compared to the $6 billion that would have been needed to finance a grey infrastructure plan.

25eec09079b3.title: Green infrastructure
25eec09079b3.sentence: - The new greenery will increase property values by $390 million over 45 years, also boosting the property taxes the city takes in.

8dd947acafd7.title: Green infrastructure
8dd947acafd7.sentence: A green infrastructure plan in New York City is expected to cost $1.5 billion less than a comparable grey infrastructure approach.

fefb76b67e75.title: Green infrastructure
fefb76b67e75.sentence: In addition to ambitious infrastructure plans and layouts offering economical and health benefits with the investment of green infrastructure, a study conducted in 2016 within the United Kingdom analyzed the "willingness-to-pay" capacity held by residents in response to green infrastructure.

daf5f341e1be.title: Green infrastructure
daf5f341e1be.sentence: Their findings concluded that, "investment in urban [green infrastructure] that is visibly greener, that facilitates access to [green infrastructure] and other amenities, and that is perceived to promote multiple functions and benefits on a single site (i.e. multi-functionality) generate higher [willingness-to-pay] values." The "willingness-to-pay" obligation is pronounced with the idea that the locations of some living spaces with functionality and aesthetics are more likely to wield larger amounts of social and economical capital.

ad542beb5543.title: Green infrastructure
ad542beb5543.sentence: Upfront construction costs for GI were up to 8% higher than non-green infrastructure projects.

55f61fdb62be.title: Green infrastructure
55f61fdb62be.sentence: This often happens when urban green spaces added in lower income communities attract wealthier residents, which causes the property values to increase and displace the current residence of lower income communities.

2f8869874105.title: Green infrastructure
2f8869874105.sentence: In cities such as Chicago, green infrastructure projects are aimed at enhancing the environment through sustainability and livability, but often they create more social justice concerns like gentrification.

e3741851cf9c.title: Green infrastructure
e3741851cf9c.sentence: However, the benefits of such projects are often unevenly distributed, typically serving wealthier, whiter neighborhoods.

248491851ac4.title: Green infrastructure
248491851ac4.sentence: Additionally, a statistical analysis of the correlation between green infrastructure and its environmental effects on housing prices in Los Angeles led by Junsik Kim, Reid Ewing, and Alessandro Rigolon demonstrates how green infrastructure often leads to "green climate gentrification," as the inequity gap increases between quality and quantity of green installations, housing prices, air pollution, and extreme heat for minority communities.

77a339324908.title: Green infrastructure
77a339324908.sentence: Green infrastructure like increased green spaces or walkability in cities can potentially improve the well-being of individuals living within the communities, but more often at the expense of dispelling homeless populations or those with decreased housing accessibility living in the future project areas for urban improvement.

6200d5c7ca60.title: Green infrastructure
6200d5c7ca60.sentence: The impacts of green gentrification upon local communities can ultimately contradict the positives brought by sustainable and green infrastructure initially.

f05236fc69dc.title: Green infrastructure
f05236fc69dc.sentence: The planning process of infrastructure should consider the environmental outcomes while also integrating social equity considerations.

77a412a2f415.title: Green infrastructure
77a412a2f415.sentence: The success of implementing green infrastructure within communities that have experienced environmental injustice, like excess exposure to pollution or affordable housing, is dependent on the interaction and collaboration of project managers overseeing green infrastructure sites alongside community residents.

7379ac726c05.title: Environmental gentrification
7379ac726c05.sentence: Green amenities include green spaces, parks, green roofs, gardens and green and energy efficient building materials.

b5c84f14317f.title: Environmental gentrification
b5c84f14317f.sentence: More specifically, in certain cases the introduction of green amenities might lead to (1) the physical displacement of low income households due to soaring housing costs, and/or (2) the cultural, social, and political displacement of long-time residents.

91c76f73550f.title: Environmental gentrification
91c76f73550f.sentence: First coined by Sieg et al. (2004), environmental gentrification is a relatively new concept, although it can be considered as a new hybrid of the older and wider topics of gentrification and environmental justice.

b54e713b5f28.title: Sponge city
b54e713b5f28.sentence: Sponge city (Chinese: 海绵城市) is a nature-based urban planning model originated in China that emphasizes the implementation of ecological infrastructures in urban hydrological management.

16afefabe199.title: Sponge city
16afefabe199.sentence: Sponge cities focus on flood prevention and stormwater management via utilization of green infrastructure instead of purely relying on drainage systems.

ece4bb0cdfdf.title: Sponge city
ece4bb0cdfdf.sentence: The name comes from the analogy that greened landscapes can store, slow down and "soak up" surface water like sponges, thus helping other developed/settled areas stay dry.

d28c4c2619b1.title: Sponge city
d28c4c2619b1.sentence: The Sponge City philosophy is to distribute and retain water at its source, slow down water as it flows away from its source, clean water naturally, and adapt to water at the sink when water accumulates.

547678222619.title: Sponge city
547678222619.sentence: This is in stark contrast to the conventional solution of grey infrastructure, which is to centralize and accumulate water using big reservoirs, speed up the flow by pipes and channelized drains, and fight against water at the end by higher and stronger flood walls and dams.

58a9cb1615b3.title: Sponge city
58a9cb1615b3.sentence: Because of this, surface flow increases from 10% to 60%, while infiltration is drastically reduced, even to zero.

b0efb88992ec.title: Sponge city
b0efb88992ec.sentence: First proposed by landscape architect Kongjian Yu, the urban planning model has been accepted by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and the State Council as a nationwide urban development policy in 2014.

cb2a6706be88.title: Sponge city
cb2a6706be88.sentence: Though the concept had been published and practiced since early 2000, it was the Beijing flood on July 21, 2012 which caused 79 deaths that prompted the top Chinese authorities to accept the Sponge City concept and make it a nationwide policy.

d3db4a9712b7.title: Sponge city
d3db4a9712b7.sentence: In 2015, China initiated a pilot initiative in 16 districts.

1bdffe4c0a16.title: Sponge city
1bdffe4c0a16.sentence: Four batches were selected by 2017, consisting of a total of 87 cities.

2e9b9ab2d9cf.title: Sponge city
2e9b9ab2d9cf.sentence: Under the guideline, cities in China will collect and utilize 70 percent of the rainwater, with 20 percent of urban areas meeting the target by 2020, and the proportion will increase to 80 percent by 2030.

13b399283673.title: Sponge city
13b399283673.sentence: Studies have shown that sponge cities are highly effective in reducing stormwater runoff and improving water quality.

8ed0e370f91e.title: Sponge city
8ed0e370f91e.sentence: Monitoring data has been difficult to obtain due to the lack of monitoring data and evaluation standards published by the government.

4a428d382803.title: Sponge city
4a428d382803.sentence: Nineteen of the thirty pilot cities has experienced flooding since implementation.

9c138b1ac49f.title: Beaver dam
9c138b1ac49f.sentence: A beaver dam, or beaver impoundment, is a dam built by beavers; it creates a pond which protects against predators and holds food during winter.

5f6c478dc01d.title: Beaver dam
5f6c478dc01d.sentence: These structures modify the natural environment in such a way that the overall ecosystem builds upon the change, making beavers a keystone species and ecosystem engineers.

8c348038c11a.title: Beaver dam
8c348038c11a.sentence: In native regions, these dams reduce downstream flooding, clean water, help restore and maintain wetlands and provide important firebreaks in fire-prone regions.

e24b9c19edab.title: Beaver dam
e24b9c19edab.sentence: Afterward the dam gradually releases the extra stored water, thus somewhat reducing the height of the flood wave moving down the river.

5c881ebd3c13.title: Beaver dam
5c881ebd3c13.sentence: This may also help in reducing flood waves, and increasing water flow when there is no rain.

a1457e711995.title: Beaver dam
a1457e711995.sentence: Bacteria in the dirt and the plant debris, which collects at the dams, turns nitrates into nitrogen gas.

0f0e5a0dba18.title: Beaver dam
0f0e5a0dba18.sentence: Some of these toxicants are metabolized and decomposed by the bacteria in the cellulose-rich bottom of a beaver dam.

366c9d750f72.title: Beaver dam
366c9d750f72.sentence: A study in Alberta, Canada, showed that "Pitfall traps on beaver ponds captured 5.7 times more newly metamorphosed wood frogs, 29 times more western toads and 24 times more boreal chorus frogs than on nearby free-flowing streams."

abaab1dc79f3.title: Beaver dam
abaab1dc79f3.sentence: Beaver dams typically range in length from a few meters to about 100 metres (328 ft 1 in).

fd34a5900c2c.title: Beaver dam
fd34a5900c2c.sentence: The largest known beaver dam is in Wood Buffalo National Park in Alberta, Canada, and is 775 metres (2,542 ft 8 in) long.

d449f9a65079.title: Beaver dam
d449f9a65079.sentence: Beaver dams can be disruptive; the flooding can cause extensive property damage, and, when the flooding occurs next to a railroad roadbed, it can cause derailments by washing out the tracks.

6a8c6f906d5f.title: Beaver dam
6a8c6f906d5f.sentence: Introduced to an area without its natural predators, as in Tierra del Fuego, beavers have flooded thousands of acres of land and are considered a plague.

4a97bb5eb89c.title: Beaver dam
4a97bb5eb89c.sentence: If a beaver pond becomes too shallow due to sediment accumulation, or the tree supply is depleted, beavers will abandon the site, leaving a wetland behind.

9be3273194fa.title: Beaver dam
9be3273194fa.sentence: As the wetland fills up with plant debris and dries out, pasture species colonize it and the wetland may eventually become a meadow suitable for grazing in a previously forested area.

93c039683d68.title: Beaver dam
93c039683d68.sentence: Finally, the meadow will be colonized by riverine trees, typically aspens, willows and such species which are favoured by the beaver.

777bef911cfc.title: Beaver dam
777bef911cfc.sentence: Each time the stream life cycle repeats itself another layer of organic soil is added to the bottom of the valley.

d12a93f720a2.title: Flood management
d12a93f720a2.section: Causes of flooding > Flood levels: blunting the peak
d12a93f720a2.sentence: The peak flood level occurs as a very steep, short spike; a quick spurt of water.

322d0666998a.title: Flood management
322d0666998a.section: Causes of flooding > Flood levels: blunting the peak
322d0666998a.sentence: Anything that slows the surface runoff (marshes, meanders, vegetation, porous materials, turbulent flow, the river spreading over a floodplain) will slow some of the flow more than other parts, spreading the flow over time and blunting the spike.

e6ee927095ec.title: Flood management
e6ee927095ec.section: Causes of flooding > Flood levels: blunting the peak
e6ee927095ec.sentence: Water levels during a flood tend to rise, then fall, very abruptly.

3280acc22a14.title: Flood management
3280acc22a14.sentence: Flood mapping is a tool used by governments and policy makers to delineate the borders of potential flooding events, allowing educated decisions to prevent extreme flooding events.

6d420a17cdea.title: Flood management
6d420a17cdea.sentence: Flood maps are useful to create documentation that allows policy makers to make informed decisions about flood hazards.

788077d0eae1.title: Flood management
788077d0eae1.section: Purposes > Protection of wider areas such as towns or cities
788077d0eae1.sentence: The most effective way of reducing the risk to people and property is through the production of flood risk maps.

e753691d1299.title: Flood management
e753691d1299.section: Purposes > Protection of wider areas such as towns or cities
e753691d1299.sentence: Most countries have produced maps which show areas prone to flooding based on flood data.

0da0d0ee4fa5.title: Flood management
0da0d0ee4fa5.sentence: Flood modelling is a tool used to model flood hazard and the effects on humans and the physical environment.

8213c57b9f30.title: Flood management
8213c57b9f30.sentence: Flood modelling takes into consideration how flood hazards, external and internal processes and factors, and the main drivers of floods interact with each other.

b1285a762e02.title: Flood management
b1285a762e02.sentence: As an example, in Bangladesh, where nearly 80% of the population lives in low-lying floodplains, such a map aids in identifying areas prone to recurring or severe flooding caused by seasonal monsoon rains and river overflows.

0e7d3ea3ce2a.title: Flood management
0e7d3ea3ce2a.sentence: One way of reducing the damage caused by flooding is to remove buildings from flood-prone areas, leaving them as parks or returning them to wilderness.

7c312dcab877.title: Flood management
7c312dcab877.sentence: Floodplain buyout programs have been operated in places like New Jersey (both before and after Hurricane Sandy), Charlotte, North Carolina, and Missouri.

563915fc4427.title: Flood management
563915fc4427.sentence: A flood barrier, surge barrier or storm surge barrier is a specific type of floodgate, designed to prevent a storm surge or spring tide from flooding the protected area behind the barrier.

cbf0b8ab44c9.title: Flood management
cbf0b8ab44c9.sentence: A surge barrier is almost always part of a larger flood protection system consisting of floodwalls, levees (also known as dikes), and other constructions and natural geographical features.

cdbd074ccebd.title: Flood management
cdbd074ccebd.section: Examples by country > Europe > United Kingdom
cdbd074ccebd.sentence: London is protected from flooding by Thames Barrier, a huge mechanical barrier across the River Thames, which is raised when the water level reaches a certain point.

2aaf4bbf3b02.title: Flood management
2aaf4bbf3b02.section: Examples by country > Europe > United Kingdom
2aaf4bbf3b02.sentence: This project has been operational since 1982 and was designed to protect against a surge of water such as the North Sea flood of 1953.

1e8ae4532ae3.title: Coastal management
1e8ae4532ae3.section: Construction techniques > Hard engineering methods > Floodgates
1e8ae4532ae3.sentence: Storm surge barriers, or floodgates, were introduced after the North Sea Flood of 1953 and prevent damage from storm surges or any other type of natural disaster that could harm the area they protect.

d3b928e94065.title: Coastal management
d3b928e94065.sentence: Storm surge warnings can help determine when to close floodgates.

6d2e1d7dd7a4.title: Green infrastructure
6d2e1d7dd7a4.sentence: Lack of funding is consistently cited as a barrier to the implementation of green infrastructure.

dd5cafbad248.title: Green infrastructure
