dd5cafbad248.sentence: One advantage that green infrastructure projects offer, however, is that they generate so many benefits that they can compete for a variety of diverse funding sources.

1418fc073a21.title: Green infrastructure
1418fc073a21.sentence: Some tax incentive programs administered by federal agencies can be used to attract financing to green infrastructure projects.

dee729395e09.title: Green infrastructure
dee729395e09.sentence: Climate Finance was not adequately captured by Fragile states for GI investments, and governance issues may further hinder capability to take full advantage.

28eb5368e85c.title: Green infrastructure
28eb5368e85c.sentence: GI Investments needed strong government participation as well as institutional capacities and capabilities that fragile states may not possess.

371c05613e3f.title: Green infrastructure
371c05613e3f.sentence: "Blue infrastructure" refers to urban infrastructure relating to water.

1a0abafe73ee.title: Green infrastructure
1a0abafe73ee.sentence: Rivers, streams, ponds, and lakes may exist as natural features within cities, or be added to an urban environment as an aspect of its design.

0c8d1910b272.title: Green infrastructure
0c8d1910b272.sentence: Blue infrastructure is commonly associated with green infrastructure in urban environments and may be referred to as "blue-green infrastructure" when being viewed in combination.

031dee46db66.title: Green infrastructure
031dee46db66.sentence: Blue infrastructure can support unique aquatic biodiversity in urban areas, including aquatic insects, amphibians, and water birds.

c1f3853a7cc8.title: Green infrastructure
c1f3853a7cc8.sentence: Accessible blue infrastructure in urban areas is also referred as to blue spaces.

8cd7c7e67d61.title: Green infrastructure
8cd7c7e67d61.sentence: There may considerable co-benefits to the health and wellbeing of populations with access to blue spaces in the urban context.

0c2aa186354c.title: Green infrastructure
0c2aa186354c.section: Types of green infrastructure > Constructed floating wetlands
0c2aa186354c.sentence: Constructed Floating Wetlands (CFWs) are built to float on the water surface and sustain vegetation compatible with the environment, whether naturally freshwater (lakes and rivers) or saline (estuaries and coastal locations).

0bbb6bacc24e.title: Green infrastructure
0bbb6bacc24e.section: Types of green infrastructure > Constructed floating wetlands > Benefits
0bbb6bacc24e.sentence: The vegetation in CFWs can improve water quality by effectively removing heavy metals (copper, lead, zinc) and harmful nutrients (phosphorus, nitrogen), and, depending on the subtrate, can sequester carbon.

afd10251ce5d.title: Green infrastructure
afd10251ce5d.section: Types of green infrastructure > Constructed floating wetlands > Benefits
afd10251ce5d.sentence: The CFWs also provide habitat to insects and other wildlife and have an added social benefit of improving landscape aesthetics, particularly in urban areas with hardened shorelines, and engage community members in understanding local ecology, such as Boston's Charles River Floating Wetland.

a360086eadf6.title: Green infrastructure
a360086eadf6.section: Types of green infrastructure > Downspout disconnection
a360086eadf6.sentence: Downspout disconnection is a form of green infrastructure that separates roof downspouts from the sewer system and redirects roof water runoff into permeable surfaces.

e67918442c43.title: Green infrastructure
e67918442c43.section: Types of green infrastructure > Downspout disconnection
e67918442c43.sentence: With high volumes of rain, downspouts on buildings can send 12 gallons of water a minute into the sewer system, which increases the risk of basement backups and sewer overflows.

2e59f3cea07c.title: Green infrastructure
2e59f3cea07c.section: Types of green infrastructure > Downspout disconnection
2e59f3cea07c.sentence: Downspout disconnection is especially beneficial in cities with combined sewer systems.

a8460dc9b6c6.title: Green infrastructure
a8460dc9b6c6.section: Types of green infrastructure > Green and blue roofs
a8460dc9b6c6.sentence: The plants and soil provide more green space and insulation on roofs.

0610bbe5e0e7.title: Green infrastructure
0610bbe5e0e7.section: Types of green infrastructure > Green and blue roofs
0610bbe5e0e7.sentence: Blue roofs, not technically being green infrastructure, collect and store rainfall, reducing the inrush of runoff water into sewer systems.

d4ad1dd3e03a.title: Green infrastructure
d4ad1dd3e03a.section: Types of green infrastructure > Green and blue roofs
d4ad1dd3e03a.sentence: Forty to eighty percent of the total volume of rain that falls on green roofs are able to be reserved.

bdba0aa78bae.title: Green infrastructure
bdba0aa78bae.section: Types of green infrastructure > Green and blue roofs
bdba0aa78bae.sentence: The water released from the roofs flow at a slow pace, reducing the amount of runoff entering the watershed at once.

85bc10f04262.title: Green infrastructure
85bc10f04262.section: Types of green infrastructure > Green and blue roofs
85bc10f04262.sentence: Blue roofs use detention ponds, or detention basins, for collecting the rainfall before it gets drained into waterways and sewers at a controlled rate.

adbdd4415ac2.title: Green infrastructure
adbdd4415ac2.sentence: Since 1991, the city of Zürich has had a law stating all flat roofs (unless used as terraces) must be greened roofed surfaces.

dcd6c041032c.title: Green infrastructure
dcd6c041032c.sentence: The Green Infrastructure approach analyses the natural environment in a way that highlights its function and subsequently seeks to put in place, through regulatory or planning policy, mechanisms that safeguard critical natural areas.

dea41dafb2c6.title: Green infrastructure
dea41dafb2c6.sentence: Where life support functions are found to be lacking, plans may propose how these can be put in place through landscaped and/or engineered improvements.

c4ae1b3377f1.title: Green infrastructure
c4ae1b3377f1.sentence: In the United Kingdom, Green infrastructure planning is increasingly recognised as a valuable approach for spatial planning and is now seen in national, regional and local planning and policy documents and strategies, for example in the Milton Keynes and South Midlands Growth area.

2932e6eb8eb8.title: Green infrastructure
2932e6eb8eb8.sentence: Green infrastructure programs managed by EPA and partner organizations are intended to improve water quality generally through more extensive management of stormwater runoff.

60df82ad36d9.title: Green infrastructure
60df82ad36d9.sentence: The practices are expected to reduce stress on traditional water drainage infrastructure--storm sewers and combined sewers—which are typically extensive networks of underground pipes and/or surface water channels in U.S. cities, towns and suburban areas.

74bd6292c10a.title: Green infrastructure
74bd6292c10a.section: Types of green infrastructure > Stormwater basins
74bd6292c10a.sentence: Newer designs incorporate more robust vegetation rather than mowed grasses to grant a more sustainable solution with distinct advantages.

406b4ef70458.title: Green infrastructure
406b4ef70458.section: Types of green infrastructure > Stormwater basins
406b4ef70458.sentence: These newer designs, often referred to as bioretention basins, are especially proficient at reduction of organics and pollutants and absorption of sediments.

a94dda1162ec.title: Green infrastructure
a94dda1162ec.section: Types of green infrastructure > Stormwater basins
a94dda1162ec.sentence: Stormwater basins are an important component of the sponge city concept for flood management.

608bdcd16fcf.title: Floodplain restoration
608bdcd16fcf.sentence: Floodplain restoration is the process of fully or partially restoring a river's floodplain to its original conditions before having been affected by the construction of levees (dikes) and the draining of wetlands and marshes.

0f76180162b7.title: Floodplain restoration
0f76180162b7.sentence: The objectives of restoring floodplains include the reduction of the incidence of floods, the provision of habitats for aquatic species, the improvement of water quality and the increased recharge of groundwater.

c5d112a593a0.title: Floodplain restoration
c5d112a593a0.sentence: Anthropogenic impacts on floodplain mostly target the lateral connectivity between rivers and their floodplains, so many restoration methods focus on removing human-made structures that disrupt connectivity.

c4514fdd2a79.title: Floodplain restoration
c4514fdd2a79.sentence: One type of floodplain restoration are levee setbacks and dam removal, either full or partial, to allow for rivers to migrate within a space that is closer to the natural floodplain.

b01f87e17218.title: Floodplain restoration
b01f87e17218.sentence: The removal of levees and/or weirs can allow for the reconnection of river channels to their floodplain.

74ec626ff024.title: Floodplain restoration
74ec626ff024.sentence: Restoring drained or degraded wetlands can help increase floodplain connectivity.

3412a234ca86.title: Floodplain restoration
3412a234ca86.section: Description > Types/methods > Floodplain and wetland restoration as Nature-Based Solutions
3412a234ca86.sentence: Floodplain and wetland restoration are nature-based solutions (NbS) that reduce flood risk by increasing the natural ecosystem's service to attenuate water.

e21632942549.title: Floodplain restoration
e21632942549.section: Description > Types/methods > Floodplain and wetland restoration as Nature-Based Solutions
e21632942549.sentence: Increased flora biodiversity provides surface roughness that can reduce wave energy by approximately 70% in salt marshes and 65% in mangrove fields during floods.

7a11a74d1675.title: Floodplain restoration
7a11a74d1675.section: Description > Types/methods > Floodplain and wetland restoration as Nature-Based Solutions
7a11a74d1675.sentence: They are most effective for frequent, low- to moderate- intensity floods, and have limited benefit for extreme flooding events when applied autonomously.

4fc4728b6a35.title: Floodplain restoration
4fc4728b6a35.section: Description > Types/methods > Floodplain and wetland restoration as Nature-Based Solutions > Coastal floodplain protection and restoration
4fc4728b6a35.sentence: While there is high confidence in coastal wetland's capacity to act as large carbon sinks, the improvement of their carbon sequestration rates through restoration is debated, and the long-term permanence under climate change is uncertain.

62baf684c2a1.title: Floodplain restoration
62baf684c2a1.section: Description > Types/methods > Floodplain and wetland restoration as Nature-Based Solutions > Inland floodplain protection and restoration
62baf684c2a1.sentence: While NbS can improve floodplain ecosystem functioning to store large amounts of carbon dioxide, the magnitude of their sink capacity is variable and difficult to determine; however, their primary role in flood risk reduction and adaptation is well supported with medium to high confidence in literature.

00b81bcc298d.title: Floodplain restoration
00b81bcc298d.sentence: There is also the potential for a higher value or desire placed into immediate flood-defense and current land-use practices rather than the ecological or environmental benefits, which can stall or prevent floodplain restoration.

b84d6535fd9b.title: Floodplain restoration
b84d6535fd9b.section: Examples of existing projects > Europe > Waal River Project (Netherlands)
b84d6535fd9b.sentence: Instead of further hard engineering, the project restored floodplain capacity by relocating the Lent dike 350 metres inland and creating a 3-km-long side channel.

068bf6ed1abe.title: Floodplain restoration
068bf6ed1abe.section: Examples of existing projects > Europe > Waal River Project (Netherlands)
068bf6ed1abe.sentence: This widened the extent of the river width in winter, lowered peak water levels by approximately 35 cm, and significantly reduced flood risk for both Nijmegen and Lent.

ccf5558e2c32.title: Stream restoration
ccf5558e2c32.sentence: Stream restoration or river restoration, also sometimes referred to as river reclamation, is work conducted to improve the environmental health of a river or stream, in support of biodiversity, recreation, flood management and/or landscape development.

357127b388ac.title: Stream restoration
357127b388ac.sentence: Stream restoration approaches can be divided into two broad categories: form-based restoration, which relies on physical interventions in a stream to improve its conditions; and process-based restoration, which advocates the restoration of hydrological and geomorphological processes (such as sediment transport or connectivity between the channel and the floodplain) to ensure a stream's resilience and ecological health.

107b6555d072.title: Stream restoration
107b6555d072.sentence: - river engineering, a term which typically refers to physical alterations of a water body, for purposes that include navigation, flood control or water supply diversion and are not necessarily related to ecological restoration;

04ef1e29fcc7.title: Stream restoration
04ef1e29fcc7.sentence: Stream restoration activities may range from the simple improvement or removal of a structure that inhibits natural stream functions (e.g. repairing or replacing a culvert, or removing barriers to fish passage such as weirs), to the stabilization of stream banks, or other interventions such as riparian zone restoration or the installation of stormwater-management facilities like constructed wetlands.

5323d4ce2eb7.title: Stream restoration
5323d4ce2eb7.sentence: Stream-restoration projects normally begin with an assessment of a focal stream system, including climatic data, geology, watershed hydrology, stream hydraulics, sediment transport patterns, channel geometry, historical channel mobility, and flood records.

bb2a19f87297.title: Stream restoration
bb2a19f87297.sentence: In the 2000s, a study of stream restoration efforts in the U.S. led to the creation of the National River Restoration Science Synthesis (NRRSS) database, which included information on over 35,000 stream restoration projects carried out in the U.S.

b501b40fa388.title: Stream restoration
b501b40fa388.sentence: However, despite the large number of stream restoration projects carried out each year worldwide, the effectiveness of stream restoration projects remains poorly quantified.

3b43f605dc12.title: Stream restoration
3b43f605dc12.sentence: This situation appears to result from limited data on the restored streams' biophysical and geochemical contexts, to insufficient post-monitoring work and to the varying metrics used to evaluate project effectiveness.

4ba7855ce127.title: Stream restoration
4ba7855ce127.sentence: Stream restoration is gradually being introduced in the legislative framework of various states.

bb3b86f59b42.title: Stream restoration
bb3b86f59b42.sentence: Examples include the European water framework's commitment to restoring surface water bodies, the adoption of the concept of freedom space in the French legislation, the inclusion in the Swiss legislation of the notion of space reserved for watercourses and of the requirement to restore streams to a state close to their natural state, and the inclusion of river corridors in land use planning in the American states of Vermont and Washington.

c3aad6378b89.title: Dam removal
c3aad6378b89.sentence: Dam removal is the process of demolishing a dam, returning water flow to the river.

534d718c9c54.title: Dam removal
534d718c9c54.sentence: Arguments for dam removal consider whether their negative effects outweigh their benefits.

e5dfbbf92423.title: Dam removal
e5dfbbf92423.sentence: The benefits of dams include hydropower production, flood control, irrigation, and navigation.

e07ea24794fe.title: Dam removal
e07ea24794fe.sentence: Negative effects of dams include environmental degradation, such as reduced primary productivity, loss of biodiversity, and declines in native species; some negative effects worsen as dams age, like structural weakness, reduced safety, sediment accumulation, and high maintenance expense.

b1e3726af522.title: Dam removal
b1e3726af522.sentence: In the United States roughly 900 dams were removed between 1990 and 2015, and by 2015, the rate was 50 to 60 per year.

bda7ebf92d61.title: Dam removal
bda7ebf92d61.sentence: A number of major dam removal projects have been motivated by environmental goals, particularly restoration of river habitat, native fish, and unique geomorphological features.

91eabaa7adfa.title: Dam removal
91eabaa7adfa.sentence: For example, fish restoration motivated the Elwha Ecosystem Restoration and the dam removal on the river Allier, while recovery of both native fish and of travertine deposition motivated the restoration of Fossil Creek.

b226b0cbad4d.title: Dam removal
b226b0cbad4d.sentence: Oftentimes the sediment stored in a reservoir is good for the riparian corridor below the dam, can rebuild fish habitat, provide nutrients, and add onto a beach or estuary.

5a3582f27995.title: Dam removal
5a3582f27995.sentence: For example, when the Fort Edward Dam on the Hudson River was removed in the 1970s, PCBs in the sediment were released, affecting human and wildlife health downstream.

5970c2771b6b.title: Dam removal
5970c2771b6b.sentence: Removal is costly no matter what and expenses typically rise when greater weight is given to environmental concerns.

bceaa6fcceb1.title: Dam removal
bceaa6fcceb1.sentence: Fortunately, the cost of dam removal is usually shared by multiple stakeholders such as the dam owner and either the federal, state or local government.

7f32ccd32372.title: Dam removal
7f32ccd32372.sentence: According to the European Commission, at least 150 000 barriers in European rivers no longer serve their intended purpose or are no longer required.

98567ce364d6.title: Dam removal
98567ce364d6.sentence: To restore free-flow, the EU Biodiversity Strategy seeks to eliminate unnecessary dams and barriers across 25,000 kilometres (16,000 mi) of river by 2030.

534004688687.title: Urban flooding
534004688687.sentence: Urban flooding has significant economic implications.

8fa94005ef9d.title: Urban flooding
8fa94005ef9d.sentence: In the US, industry experts estimate that wet basements can lower property values by 10%-25% and are cited among the top reasons for not purchasing a home.

490ad3f828ce.title: Urban flooding
490ad3f828ce.sentence: According to the U.S Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), almost 40% of small businesses never reopen their doors following a flooding disaster.

b0658b712c0c.title: Urban flooding
b0658b712c0c.sentence: In the UK, urban flooding is estimated to cost £270 million a year in England and Wales; 80,000 homes are at risk.

e7d16da9565b.title: Urban flooding
e7d16da9565b.section: Modeling > Modeling of climate change impacts
e7d16da9565b.sentence: Scientists investigate climate change scenarios and their impacts on urban flooding and found that: "For example in the UK, expected annual damages from surface water may increase by £60–200 million for projected 2–4°C warming scenarios; enhanced adaptation actions could manage flooding up to a 2°C scenario but will be insufficient beyond that.

33a43c4f679b.title: Urban flooding
33a43c4f679b.section: Mitigation and management > Building gray infrastructure
33a43c4f679b.sentence: While gray infrastructure can be effective in preventing flooding-related damage and can be economically valuable, some models suggest that gray infrastructure may become less effective at preventing flood-related impacts in urban areas in the future as climate change causes flooding intensity and frequency to increase.

a4641ce07b98.title: Sponge city
a4641ce07b98.sentence: Excessive use and development of grey infrastructure can lead to water shortages, pollution, and overall degradation of water ecosystem services.

1f7ac4e39e4d.title: Urban flooding
1f7ac4e39e4d.section: Mitigation and management > Integrated urban water management
1f7ac4e39e4d.sentence: Integrated urban water management (IUWM) is the practice of managing freshwater, wastewater, and storm water as components of a basin-wide management plan.

47f971943deb.title: Urban flooding
47f971943deb.section: Mitigation and management > Integrated urban water management
47f971943deb.sentence: IUWM is commonly seen as a strategy for achieving the goals of Water Sensitive Urban Design.

115582a258b2.title: Urban flooding
115582a258b2.section: Mitigation and management > Integrated urban water management
115582a258b2.sentence: IUWM seeks to change the impact of urban development on the natural water cycle, based on the premise that by managing the urban water cycle as a whole; a more efficient use of resources can be achieved providing not only economic benefits but also improved social and environmental outcomes.

5de80c223e63.title: Stormwater
5de80c223e63.sentence: Also known as low impact development (LID) in the United States, or Water Sensitive Urban Design (WSUD) in Australia, IWM has the potential to improve runoff quality, reduce the risk and impact of flooding and deliver an additional water resource to augment potable supply.

593083ddbe48.title: Urban flooding
593083ddbe48.sentence: City planners distinguish pluvial flooding (flooding caused by heavy rain), fluvial flooding (caused by a nearby river overflowing its banks), or coastal flooding (often caused by storm surges).

dad24e55ce6e.title: Urban flooding
dad24e55ce6e.sentence: Different types of urban flooding create different impacts and require different mitigation strategies.

6eec8be9ce82.title: Urban flooding
6eec8be9ce82.sentence: In particular, erratic rainfall patterns are expected to increase the frequency and severity of both pluvial flooding (as excessive amounts of rainfall in urban areas and cannot be adequately absorbed by existing drainage systems and pervious areas) and fluvial flooding (as excessive rainfall over a river can cause flooding and overflow, either where it occurs or downstream along the path of the river).

5e1baae08787.title: Urban flooding
5e1baae08787.sentence: Coastal cities may be particularly affected by sea level rise and higher rainfall intensity.

a58bd0ca0ff2.title: Constructed wetland
a58bd0ca0ff2.section: Types and design considerations > Subsurface flow
a58bd0ca0ff2.sentence: In subsurface flow constructed wetlands the flow of wastewater occurs between the roots of the plants and there is no water surfacing (it is kept below gravel).

7682cae943c6.title: Constructed wetland
7682cae943c6.section: Types and design considerations > Subsurface flow
7682cae943c6.sentence: As a result, the system is more efficient, does not attract mosquitoes, is less odorous, and less sensitive to winter conditions.

ce4d05f1072f.title: Constructed wetland
ce4d05f1072f.section: Types and design considerations > Subsurface flow > Comparisons with other types
ce4d05f1072f.sentence: Subsurface flow systems have the advantage of requiring less land area for water treatment than surface flow.

02379046161a.title: Constructed wetland
02379046161a.section: Types and design considerations > Subsurface flow > Costs
02379046161a.sentence: The costs of subsurface flow constructed wetlands mainly depend on the costs of sand with which the bed has to be filled.

1b0caf85a3e2.title: Constructed wetland
1b0caf85a3e2.section: Types and design considerations > Subsurface flow > Design considerations
1b0caf85a3e2.sentence: Constructed subsurface flow wetlands are meant as secondary treatment systems, which means that the effluent needs to first pass a primary treatment which effectively removes solids.

786ab1979665.title: Constructed wetland
786ab1979665.section: Types and design considerations > Surface flow
786ab1979665.sentence: Surface flow wetlands, also known as free water surface constructed wetlands, can be used for tertiary treatment or polishing of effluent from wastewater treatment plants.

f4af2c2ad965.title: Constructed wetland
f4af2c2ad965.section: Types and design considerations > Surface flow
f4af2c2ad965.sentence: Surface flow constructed wetlands always have horizontal flow of wastewater across the roots of the plants, rather than vertical flow.

690418310a0a.title: Constructed wetland
690418310a0a.section: Types and design considerations > Surface flow
690418310a0a.sentence: They are also suitable to treat stormwater drainage.

2628a5abdcf5.title: Constructed wetland
2628a5abdcf5.section: Types and design considerations > Surface flow
2628a5abdcf5.sentence: Pathogens are destroyed by natural decay, predation from higher organisms, sedimentation and UV irradiation since the water is exposed to direct sunlight.

10a8544206df.title: Constructed wetland
10a8544206df.section: Types and design considerations > Surface flow
10a8544206df.sentence: They require a relatively large area to purify water compared to subsurface flow constructed wetlands and may have increased smell and lower performance in winter.

5644eef831c7.title: Constructed wetland
5644eef831c7.section: Types and design considerations > Surface flow
5644eef831c7.sentence: However, surface flow constructed wetlands may encourage mosquito breeding.

4823bfb693fc.title: Constructed wetland
4823bfb693fc.section: Types and design considerations > Surface flow
4823bfb693fc.sentence: They may also have high algae production that lowers the effluent quality and due to open water surface mosquitos and odours, it is more difficult to integrate them in an urban neighbourhood.

bfc1ddcb5f44.title: Water-sensitive urban design
bfc1ddcb5f44.section: Common WSUD practices > Road layout and streetscape > Infiltration trenches and systems
bfc1ddcb5f44.sentence: They are designed to hold stormwater runoff within a subsurface trench and gradually release it into the surrounding soil and groundwater systems.

8a7256e61222.title: Water-sensitive urban design
8a7256e61222.section: Common WSUD practices > Road layout and streetscape > Infiltration trenches and systems
8a7256e61222.sentence: Although they are generally not designed as a treatment measure but can provide some level of treatment by retaining pollutants and sediments.

aef515a27f9d.title: Water-sensitive urban design
aef515a27f9d.section: Common WSUD practices > Road layout and streetscape > Sand Filters
aef515a27f9d.sentence: Sand filters are a variation of the infiltration trench principle and operate in a way similar to bioretention systems.

3ea625950611.title: Water-sensitive urban design
3ea625950611.section: Common WSUD practices > Road layout and streetscape > Sand Filters
3ea625950611.sentence: Sand filters are very useful in treating runoff from confined hard surfaces such as car parks and from heavily urbanised and built-up areas.

3bbbba8f13a0.title: Water-sensitive urban design
3bbbba8f13a0.section: Common WSUD practices > Public open space > Sedimentation basins
3bbbba8f13a0.sentence: They operate through temporary stormwater retention and reduction of flow velocities to promote settling of sediments out of the water column.

4ac80a73febd.title: Water-sensitive urban design
4ac80a73febd.section: Common WSUD practices > Public open space > Sedimentation basins
4ac80a73febd.sentence: They are important as a pretreatment to ensure downstream elements are not overloaded or smothered with coarse sediments.

f4117eb10711.title: Water-sensitive urban design
f4117eb10711.section: Common WSUD practices > Public open space > Constructed wetlands
f4117eb10711.sentence: They usually comprise three zones: an inlet zone (sedimentation basin) to remove coarse sediments; a macrophyte zone, a heavily vegetated area to remove fine particulates and uptake of soluble pollutants; and a high flow bypass channel to protect the macrophyte zone.

d912e1b24f93.title: Sustainable drainage system
d912e1b24f93.sentence: It is used to manage stormwater runoff, for protection against flooding, for erosion control, and to serve as an artificial wetland and improve the water quality in adjacent bodies of water.

9ea849beda82.title: Sustainable drainage system
9ea849beda82.sentence: It is distinguished from a detention basin, sometimes called a "dry pond", which temporarily stores water after a storm, but eventually empties out at a controlled rate to a downstream water body.

194f23cd96dd.title: Sustainable drainage system
194f23cd96dd.sentence: It also differs from an infiltration basin which is designed to direct stormwater to groundwater through permeable soils.

a47ed1f85e7d.title: Permeable paving
a47ed1f85e7d.sentence: Nine different families of porous paving materials present distinctive advantages and disadvantages for specific applications.

7cdc0a1061ef.title: Permeable paving
7cdc0a1061ef.section: Types of permeable pavement > Pervious concrete
7cdc0a1061ef.sentence: Pervious concrete is widely available, can bear frequent traffic, and is universally accessible.

4ada17a3e167.title: Permeable paving
4ada17a3e167.section: Types of permeable pavement > Porous asphalt
4ada17a3e167.sentence: Porous asphalt is produced and placed using the same methods as conventional asphalt concrete; it differs in that fine (small) aggregates are omitted from the asphalt mixture.

8bc147b084da.title: Permeable paving
8bc147b084da.section: Types of permeable pavement > Porous asphalt
8bc147b084da.sentence: The remaining large, single-sized aggregate particles leave open voids that give the material its porosity and permeability.

61625ee02939.title: Permeable paving
61625ee02939.section: Types of permeable pavement > Plastic grids
61625ee02939.sentence: Plastic grids allow for a 100% porous system using structural grid systems for containing and stabilizing either gravel or turf.

a147125bd6f1.title: Permeable paving
a147125bd6f1.section: Types of permeable pavement > Plastic grids
a147125bd6f1.sentence: Plastic grid systems are also popular with homeowners due to their lower cost to install, ease of installation, and versatility.

3e25366acf0c.title: Permeable paving
3e25366acf0c.section: Types of permeable pavement > Permeable interlocking concrete pavements
3e25366acf0c.sentence: Permeable interlocking concrete pavements are concrete units with open, permeable spaces between the units.

4a972b2e8ccc.title: Permeable paving
4a972b2e8ccc.section: Types of permeable pavement > Permeable interlocking concrete pavements
4a972b2e8ccc.sentence: They give an architectural appearance, and can bear both light and heavy traffic, particularly interlocking concrete pavers, excepting high-volume or high-speed roads.

8e80b2771d74.title: Room for the River
8e80b2771d74.sentence: In the Netherlands, Room for the River (Dutch: Ruimte voor de Rivier) is a government design plan intended to address flood protection, master landscaping and the improvement of environmental conditions in the areas surrounding the Netherlands' rivers.

5a7a65f4a2b1.title: Room for the River
5a7a65f4a2b1.sentence: The project was active from 2006 to 2015.

d4cb959ed123.title: Room for the River
d4cb959ed123.sentence: In 1993 and 1995, floods threatened to devastate regions surrounding the delta.

a1ca952b9a90.title: Room for the River
a1ca952b9a90.sentence: In the neighbouring vicinity over 200,000 people were evacuated.

65e35acdc22e.title: Room for the River
65e35acdc22e.sentence: Measures in the plan include: placing and moving dykes, depoldering, creating and increasing the depth of flood channels, reducing the height of the groynes, removing obstacles, and the construction of a "Green River" which would serve as a flood bypass.

b5cc217a371f.title: Room for the River
b5cc217a371f.sentence: Completion of a basic package of forty projects is foreseen for 2015, with a budget of €2.2 billion.

5a237515a692.title: Floodplain restoration
5a237515a692.section: Examples of existing projects > Europe > Waal River Project (Netherlands)
5a237515a692.sentence: The Waal river project in Nijmegen is a flagship intervention within the Dutch Room for the River program, developed after the near-disaster floods of 1993 and 1995 revealed the limits of continually raising dikes.

9cae03a7ddeb.title: Floodplain restoration
9cae03a7ddeb.section: Examples of existing projects > Europe > Waal River Project (Netherlands)
9cae03a7ddeb.sentence: As part of the Room for the River project, the Waal project exemplifies a policy shift toward working with natural river dynamics.

59c601ea2546.title: Flood pulse concept
59c601ea2546.sentence: The flood pulse concept explains how the periodic inundation and drought (flood pulse) control the lateral exchange of water, nutrients and organisms between the main river channel (or lake) and the connected floodplain.

af54db74d7cb.title: Flood pulse concept
af54db74d7cb.sentence: The annual flood pulse is the most important aspect and the most biologically productive feature of a river's ecosystem. describing the movement, distribution and quality of water in river ecosystems and the dynamic interaction in the transition zone between water and land (aquatic/terrestrial transition zones - ATTZ).

d2df680f5e84.title: Flood pulse concept
d2df680f5e84.sentence: It contrasts with previous ecological theories which considered floods to be catastrophic events.

326944878f83.title: Flood pulse concept
326944878f83.sentence: The flood pulse helps maintain genetic and species diversity in the floodplain ecosystem, and it brings in oxygen to help fauna and decomposition.

bda93f3510c8.title: Flood pulse concept
bda93f3510c8.sentence: Through ecosystem alterations such as dams, debris removal, channelization, levees, navigation, irrigation, contamination, logging, fire suppression, species introduction, and agricultural runoff, humans have contributed to the destruction of wetlands and the extinction of species.

ebab5e313e0e.title: Flood pulse concept
ebab5e313e0e.sentence: This can have devastating effects on riparian ecosystems.

04d92005313c.title: River ecosystem
04d92005313c.section: Community patterns and diversity > River continuum concept
04d92005313c.sentence: The flood pulse concept, developed by W. J. Junk in 1989, further modified by P. B. Bayley in 1990 and K. Tockner in 2000, takes into account the large amount of nutrients and organic material that makes its way into a river from the sediment of surrounding flooded land.

b9f3c2916e0f.title: Flood pulse concept
b9f3c2916e0f.sentence: The flood pulse concept is one of three primary models describing large river ecosystems.

31ae95ffd8ec.title: Flood pulse concept
31ae95ffd8ec.sentence: The others include the river continuum concept (RCC) and the serial discontinuity concept.

fe166e7353d6.title: Beaver dam
fe166e7353d6.sentence: Humans sometimes build structures similar to beaver dams in streams, either to get the benefits of beaver dams in places without beavers, or to encourage beavers to settle in a particular area.

a1335d63c559.title: Beaver dam
a1335d63c559.sentence: These are often called "beaver dam analogs" (BDA) although other names are also used.

ffd8fa524ac1.title: Beaver dam
ffd8fa524ac1.sentence: BDA builders may use construction techniques beyond the beaver's capabilities, such as driving wooden posts into the stream bed to brace horizontal branches that would otherwise be washed away.

8fc054426abf.title: Beaver dam
8fc054426abf.sentence: Even if beavers do not take over the dam, BDAs provide many of the benefits of natural beaver dams.

4459cc7d55aa.title: Beaver dam
4459cc7d55aa.sentence: Inspired by the positive effects on the environment, humans build beaver dam analogues (BDAs), which can provide similar ecosystem services, deliberately deployed for water retention in the landscape and the construction of ponds as wetland and breeding ground for other species.

52615be85a93.title: Dam removal
52615be85a93.sentence: While fewer than 1% of United States dams are being considered for removal, there has been a push in recent years to address the deficiencies in existing dams without removing them.

d86a7de7b111.title: Dam removal
d86a7de7b111.sentence: Updating equipment and acknowledging that dams have a limited life span are two ways to achieve those goals.

5d9654bf108c.title: Dam removal
5d9654bf108c.sentence: Having variable amounts of water flow through the dam at different seasons mimics natural seasonal variations in water level from winter and spring storms.

e220b4a4bd91.title: Dam removal
e220b4a4bd91.sentence: There's debate about the effectiveness of fish ladders, but generally some fish will make it through as opposed to zero fish spawning in their traditional location.

8ff1c71899fd.title: Dam removal
8ff1c71899fd.sentence: As part of them, a plan for decommissioning the dam and restoring the river should be drawn up long before the dam exceeds its design life.

7f529ad4b2f9.title: Dam removal
7f529ad4b2f9.sentence: Four of the most common dam removal methods are described below.

4051270908ab.title: Dam removal
4051270908ab.sentence: Sediment management is a driving force in all of them.

a185dfba90be.title: Dam removal
a185dfba90be.section: Methods of removal > Notch and release approach
a185dfba90be.sentence: It is a slow method in which the reservoir is drained through notches cut into the dam.

c028660f52e7.title: Dam removal
c028660f52e7.section: Methods of removal > Notch and release approach
c028660f52e7.sentence: The sediment trapped behind the dam flows downstream in a fixed rate that allows the ecosystem to adjust to the changes.

e89a2094b163.title: Dam removal
e89a2094b163.section: Methods of removal > Notch and release approach
e89a2094b163.sentence: This method can take months or even over a year but has proven success with restoring fish species to rivers.

6854429a9f8a.title: Dam removal
6854429a9f8a.section: Methods of removal > Rapid release approach
6854429a9f8a.sentence: The rapid release approach is both the quickest and least expensive way to remove a dam, but comes with significant drawbacks.

a2c8cd96fe93.title: Dam removal
a2c8cd96fe93.section: Methods of removal > Rapid release approach
a2c8cd96fe93.sentence: The entire body of water will drain through this tunnel in a matter of minutes or hours and the massive release of water and sediment can cause severe flooding and erosion along the river downstream for miles.

054147cb97cc.title: Dam removal
054147cb97cc.section: Methods of removal > Dig and dewater approach
054147cb97cc.sentence: The dig and dewater approach is typically the most expensive dam removal method, but is necessary in some cases.

a82c8e3b93db.title: Dam removal
a82c8e3b93db.section: Methods of removal > Dig and dewater approach
a82c8e3b93db.sentence: It entails emptying the entire reservoir, allowing the sediment to dry, and then transporting it to a safe location for disposal.

53c0d9f5b2e9.title: Dam removal
53c0d9f5b2e9.section: Methods of removal > Dig and dewater approach
53c0d9f5b2e9.sentence: Another situation is if the sediments behind the dam contain toxins.

9da164c32b1b.title: Dam removal
9da164c32b1b.section: Methods of removal > Retained sediment approach
9da164c32b1b.sentence: The retained sediment approach is the final commonly used approach and involves leaving the sediment behind where it is.

93d2152dca6c.title: Dam removal
93d2152dca6c.section: Methods of removal > Retained sediment approach
93d2152dca6c.sentence: To do this, the river or creek must be rerouted around the damsite which can prove expensive and challenging.

c5fa7ac0da97.title: Riparian-zone restoration
c5fa7ac0da97.sentence: Revegetation can be accomplished through active or passive means, or a combination of the two.

b4635659568f.title: Riparian-zone restoration
b4635659568f.section: Methods > Restoration of riparian vegetation > Passive vegetation restoration
b4635659568f.sentence: Riparian vegetation may come back on its own if human-induced disturbances are stopped and/or hydrologic processes are restored.

74dc54014de8.title: Riparian-zone restoration
74dc54014de8.section: Methods > Restoration of riparian vegetation > Passive vegetation restoration
74dc54014de8.sentence: Active planting of riparian vegetation may be the fastest way to reestablish riparian ecosystems, but methods may be prohibitively resource-intensive.

cd506d2bb329.title: Riparian-zone restoration
cd506d2bb329.section: Methods > Restoration of riparian vegetation > Passive vegetation restoration
cd506d2bb329.sentence: For example, many studies show that preventing cattle grazing in riparian zones through exclusion fencing can allow riparian vegetation to rapidly increase in robustness and cover, and also shift to a more natural community composition.

ef4313adb0ec.title: Riparian-zone restoration
ef4313adb0ec.section: Methods > Restoration of riparian vegetation > Passive vegetation restoration
ef4313adb0ec.sentence: One potential hindrance to passive vegetation restoration is that exotic species may preferentially colonize the riparian zone.

7c06dbb4d694.title: Stream restoration
7c06dbb4d694.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Installation of in-stream structures > Engineered log jams
7c06dbb4d694.sentence: An emerging stream restoration technique is the installation of engineered log jams.

c16af6994b12.title: Stream restoration
c16af6994b12.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Installation of in-stream structures > Engineered log jams
c16af6994b12.sentence: Because of channelization and removal of beaver dams and woody debris, many streams lack the hydraulic complexity that is necessary to maintain bank stabilization and healthy aquatic habitats.

98a3273ff00e.title: Stream restoration
98a3273ff00e.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Installation of in-stream structures > Engineered log jams
98a3273ff00e.sentence: Log jams add diversity to the water flow by creating riffles, pools, and temperature variations.

09141f9f3ac5.title: Stream restoration
09141f9f3ac5.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration
09141f9f3ac5.sentence: Form-based stream restoration promotes the modification of a stream channel to improve stream conditions.

6a7c424e9f38.title: Stream restoration
6a7c424e9f38.sentence: Form-based restoration techniques include deflectors; cross-vanes; weirs, step-pools and other grade-control structures; engineered log jams; bank stabilization methods and other channel-reconfiguration efforts.

7a5ef74d3a54.title: Stream restoration
7a5ef74d3a54.sentence: These induce immediate change in a stream, but sometimes fail to achieve the desired effects if degradation originates at a wider scale.

28727ef630e3.title: Stream restoration
28727ef630e3.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Criticisms to form-based restoration
28727ef630e3.sentence: Despite its popularity, form-based restoration has been criticized by the scientific community.

4d6fb9f314e8.title: Stream restoration
4d6fb9f314e8.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Criticisms to form-based restoration
4d6fb9f314e8.sentence: Common criticisms are that the scale at which form-based restoration is often much smaller than the spatial and temporal scales of the processes that cause the observed problems and that the target state is frequently influenced by the social conception of what a stream should look like and does not necessarily take into account the stream's geomorphological context (e.g., meandering rivers tend to be viewed as more "natural" and more beautiful, whereas local conditions sometimes favour other patterns such as braided rivers).

a9d5fda118d8.title: Stream restoration
a9d5fda118d8.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Other channel-reconfiguration techniques
a9d5fda118d8.sentence: In the U.S., such work is frequently based on the Natural Channel Design (NCD), a method developed in the 1990s.

259f8dbeb738.title: Stream restoration
259f8dbeb738.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Other channel-reconfiguration techniques
259f8dbeb738.sentence: This method involves a classification of the stream to be restored based on parameters such as channel pattern and geometry, topography, slope, and bed material.

d7bfcc347cf3.title: Stream restoration
d7bfcc347cf3.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Other channel-reconfiguration techniques
d7bfcc347cf3.sentence: This classification is followed by a design phase based on the NCD method, which includes 8 phases and 40 steps.

0ca2280a7a52.title: Stream restoration
0ca2280a7a52.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Criticisms to form-based restoration
0ca2280a7a52.sentence: Numerous criticisms have also been directed at the NCD method by fluvial geomorphologists, who claim that the method is a "cookbook" approach sometimes used by practitioners that do not have sufficient knowledge of fluvial geomorphology, resulting in project failures.

beb727c776c0.title: Stream restoration
beb727c776c0.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Criticisms to form-based restoration
beb727c776c0.sentence: Another criticism is the importance given to channel stability in the NCD method (and with some other form-based restoration methods), which can limit the streams' alluvial dynamics and adaptability to evolving conditions.

51971173e75f.title: Stream restoration
51971173e75f.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Process-based restoration
51971173e75f.sentence: Contrary to form-based restoration, which consists of improving a stream's conditions by modifying its structure, process-based restoration focuses on restoring the hydrological and geomorphological processes (or functions) that contribute to the stream's alluvial and ecological dynamics.

000c23ba9444.title: Stream restoration
000c23ba9444.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Process-based restoration
000c23ba9444.sentence: This type of stream restoration has gained in popularity since the mid-1990s, as a more ecosystem-centered approach.

b013e3c2497e.title: Stream restoration
b013e3c2497e.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Process-based restoration
b013e3c2497e.sentence: Process-based restoration includes restoring lateral connectivity (between the stream and its floodplain), longitudinal connectivity (along the stream) and water and/or sediment fluxes, which might be impacted by hydro-power dams, grade control structures, erosion control structures and flood protection structures.

e8b7a6a9d6c1.title: Stream restoration
e8b7a6a9d6c1.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Process-based restoration > Improving connectivity
e8b7a6a9d6c1.sentence: Removal or modification of levees can allow a better connection between streams and their floodplain.

5e07a24206af.title: Stream restoration
5e07a24206af.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Process-based restoration > Improving connectivity
5e07a24206af.sentence: Similarly, removing dams and grade control structures can restore water and sediment fluxes and result in more diversified habitats, although impacts on fish communities can be difficult to assess.

a1ce25407e87.title: Stream restoration
a1ce25407e87.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Process-based restoration
a1ce25407e87.sentence: In general, process-based restoration aims to maximize the resilience of the system and minimize maintenance requirements.

3d6d2b820371.title: Stream restoration
3d6d2b820371.sentence: The beneficial effects of process-based restoration projects may sometimes take time to be felt since changes in the stream will occur at a pace that depends on the stream dynamics.

a75cda70cc46.title: Stream restoration
a75cda70cc46.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Process-based restoration > Implementing a minimum stream corridor width
a75cda70cc46.sentence: Another method of ensuring the ecological health of streams while limiting impacts on human infrastructures is to delineate a corridor within which the stream is expected to migrate over time.

d70804bfd065.title: Stream restoration
d70804bfd065.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Process-based restoration > Implementing a minimum stream corridor width
d70804bfd065.sentence: This method is based on the concept of minimum intervention within this corridor, whose limits should be determined based on the stream's hydrology and geomorphology.

8997f173c00f.title: Stream restoration
8997f173c00f.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Process-based restoration > Implementing a minimum stream corridor width
8997f173c00f.sentence: This concept has been developed and adapted in various countries around the world, resulting in the notion of "stream corridor" or "river corridor" in the U.S., "room for the river" in the Netherlands, "espace de liberté" ("freedom space") in France (where the concept of "erodible corridor" is also used) and Québec (Canada), "espace réservé aux eaux" ("space reserved for water(courses)") in Switzerland, "fascia di pertinenza fluviale" in Italy, "fluvial territory" in Spain and "making space for water" in the United Kingdom.

d2e032ff67eb.title: Stream restoration
d2e032ff67eb.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Process-based restoration > Implementing a minimum stream corridor width
d2e032ff67eb.sentence: A cost-benefit analysis has shown that this approach could be beneficial in the long term due to lower stream stabilization and maintenance costs, lower damages resulting from erosion and flooding, and ecological services rendered by the restored streams.

be1300fe019a.title: Stream restoration
be1300fe019a.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Bank stabilization
be1300fe019a.sentence: Bank stabilization is achieved through the installation of riprap, gabions or through the use of revegetation and/or bioengineering methods, which relies on the use of live plants to build bank stabilizing structures.

1fe766cdee98.title: Stream restoration
1fe766cdee98.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Bank stabilization
1fe766cdee98.sentence: As new plants sprout from the live branches, the roots anchor the soil and prevent erosion.

c38f9a46c71f.title: Stream restoration
c38f9a46c71f.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Bank stabilization
c38f9a46c71f.sentence: This makes bioengineering structures more natural and more adaptable to evolving conditions than "hard" engineering structures.

681e10c061dd.title: Stream restoration
681e10c061dd.section: Restoration approaches and techniques > Form-based restoration > Bank stabilization
681e10c061dd.sentence: Bank stabilization is a common objective for stream-restoration projects, although bank erosion is generally viewed as favorable for the sustainability and diversity of aquatic and riparian habitats.

b3783af67293.title: Stormwater
b3783af67293.sentence: A first flush is the initial runoff of a rainstorm.

4da3d076f298.title: Green infrastructure
4da3d076f298.section: Types of green infrastructure > Rain gardens
4da3d076f298.sentence: Ubiquitous lawn grass is not a solution for controlling runoff, so an alternative is required to reduce urban and suburban first flush (highly toxic) runoff and to slow the water down for infiltration.

32a58a482f74.title: Bioswale
32a58a482f74.sentence: Bioswales are created to handle the first flush of pollutants during the event of rain, therefore, locations that have high areas of impervious surface such as roads, parking lots, or rooftops can benefit from additions of bioswales.

db54b4c27152.title: Rainwater harvesting
db54b4c27152.sentence: Adding another supplement to the system such as a first flush diverter is also a common procedure to avoid contaminants of the water.

341cef0162ed.title: Water-sensitive urban design
341cef0162ed.section: Common WSUD practices > Water re-use > Rainwater tanks
341cef0162ed.sentence: An advised suitable configuration may include a water filter or first flush diversion, a mains water top-up supply (dual supply system), maintenance drain, a pump (pressure system), and an on-site retention provision.

a364dff1d537.title: Source water protection
a364dff1d537.sentence: Source water protection is a planning process conducted by local water utilities, as well as regional or national government agencies, to protect drinking water sources from overuse and contamination.

e256728cc6b4.title: Source water protection
e256728cc6b4.sentence: The process includes identification of water sources, assessment of known and potential threats of contamination, notification of the public, and steps to eliminate the contamination.

64be3df0c422.title: Source water protection
64be3df0c422.sentence: The process is applicable to lakes, rivers and groundwater (aquifers).

8148fc6aa0fb.title: Source water protection
8148fc6aa0fb.sentence: Source water protection is part of a multi-barrier approach to protecting municipal sources of drinking water that was recommended by the Canadian Justice Dennis O'Connor in his Walkerton reports.

97c3f692e55b.title: Source water protection
97c3f692e55b.sentence: This study was released in 2002 as a response to the Walkerton Tragedy, in which the town of Walkerton, Ontario's drinking water became contaminated with E. coli bacteria.

784407bffb46.title: Source water protection
784407bffb46.sentence: A recent study have also explored the integration of ecosystem service assessments into source water protection and drinking water risk management, extending the application of ecosystem service frameworks to drinking water resources.

98b931c5a8eb.title: Blue carbon
98b931c5a8eb.sentence: Blue carbon is a concept within climate change mitigation that refers to "biologically driven carbon fluxes and storage in marine systems that are amenable to management".

665b559d0800.title: Blue carbon
665b559d0800.sentence: Another definition states: "Blue carbon refers to organic carbon that is captured and stored by the oceans and coastal ecosystems, particularly by vegetated coastal ecosystems: seagrass meadows, tidal marshes, and mangrove forests."

b5fb262ef9eb.title: Blue carbon
b5fb262ef9eb.sentence: Most commonly, it refers to the role that tidal marshes, mangroves and seagrass meadows can play in carbon sequestration.

f859b00bf825.title: Blue carbon
f859b00bf825.sentence: The vegetated coastal ecosystems of tidal marshes, mangroves and seagrasses (which are grouped as "blue carbon") have high carbon burial rates.

0a9406893645.title: Blue carbon
0a9406893645.sentence: This is because they accumulate carbon in their soils and sediments.

d65da9fa2b01.title: Blue carbon
d65da9fa2b01.section: Carbon storage by type of biome > Seagrass meadows
d65da9fa2b01.sentence: Carbon primarily accumulates in marine sediments, which are anoxic and thus continually preserve organic carbon from decadal-millennial time scales.

d7298da1317f.title: Blue carbon
d7298da1317f.section: Carbon storage by type of biome > Seagrass meadows
d7298da1317f.sentence: Compared to terrestrial habitats that lose carbon stocks as CO2 during decomposition or by disturbances like fires or deforestation, marine carbon sinks can retain C for much longer time periods.

316020a9cda6.title: Blue carbon
316020a9cda6.sentence: However, when blue carbon ecosystems are degraded or lost, they release carbon back to the atmosphere, thereby adding to greenhouse gas emissions.

4a0142352245.title: Blue carbon
4a0142352245.sentence: The methods for blue carbon management fall into the category of "ocean-based biological carbon dioxide removal (CDR) methods".

e18912f7e347.title: Blue carbon
e18912f7e347.sentence: These ecosystems can play an important role for climate change mitigation and ecosystem-based adaptation.

383db5fbf4df.title: Blue carbon
383db5fbf4df.sentence: The term blue carbon was coined in 2009.

bc520810e964.title: Blue carbon
bc520810e964.sentence: At the time, the term was coined to highlight that coastal vegetated ecosystems have a disproportionately large contribution to global carbon sequestration.

37c633d12dad.title: Blue carbon
37c633d12dad.sentence: Seagrass, salt marshes and mangroves are sometimes referred to as "blue forests" in contrast to land-based "green forests".

d0b794d72bea.title: Coastal erosion
d0b794d72bea.sentence: Coastal erosion is the loss or displacement of land, or the long-term removal of sediment and rocks along the coastline due to the action of waves, currents, tides, wind-driven water, waterborne ice, or other impacts of storms.

23502cfa7ccc.title: Coastal erosion
23502cfa7ccc.sentence: Coastal erosion may be caused by hydraulic action, abrasion, impact and corrosion by wind and water, and other forces, natural or unnatural.

70a7d4fe1d84.title: Coastal erosion
70a7d4fe1d84.sentence: Hydraulic action occurs due to the physical weathering and mechanical response when waves strike a cliff face thus compressing air in cracks on the cliff face.

5ba48e76429e.title: Coastal erosion
5ba48e76429e.sentence: Attrition occurs when waves cause loose pieces of rock debris (scree) to collide with each other, grinding and chipping each other, progressively becoming smaller, smoother and rounder.

5aa42502be62.title: Coastal erosion
5aa42502be62.sentence: Solution is the process in which acids contained in sea water will dissolve some types of rock such as chalk or limestone.

57c16c8a7483.title: Coastal erosion
57c16c8a7483.sentence: Softer areas become eroded much faster than harder ones, which typically result in landforms such as tunnels, bridges, columns, and pillars.

44ac09dd7041.title: Coastal erosion
44ac09dd7041.sentence: Over time the coast generally evens out.

0a9629a2ce98.title: Coastal erosion
0a9629a2ce98.sentence: Storms can cause erosion hundreds of times faster than normal weather.

abc3a13f5de0.title: Coastal erosion
abc3a13f5de0.sentence: Climate change has contributed to coastal erosion in areas due to rising sea levels, increased storm frequency, and changes in wave patterns.

03b2b05002d1.title: Coastal erosion
03b2b05002d1.sentence: Sea-level rise allows waves to reach further inland, accelerating shoreline retreat and increasing the vulnerability of coastal infrastructure and ecosystems.

73e21440ab44.title: Coastal erosion
73e21440ab44.sentence: Coastal erosion can degrade and erode coastal landforms, such as dunes, wetlands, beaches, and barrier islands, which serve as natural protective buffers against storm surges and wave energy.

061f263a80f6.title: Coastal erosion
061f263a80f6.sentence: Habitat loss due to erosion reduces biodiversity and disrupts ecological processes along the coastline.

504903203a5f.title: Coastal erosion
504903203a5f.sentence: Coastline erosion can cause infrastructure damage, increased maintenance and protection costs, and loss of property and land.

cf740060314c.title: Coastal erosion
cf740060314c.sentence: Coastal erosion also affects economic activities along the coast, such as tourism and fisheries, by reducing the beach width and altering the coastal environment.

2506880a6b8d.title: Coastal erosion
2506880a6b8d.sentence: Human interference can also increase coastal erosion: Hallsands in Devon, England, was a coastal village washed away over the course of a year, 1917, directly due to earlier dredging of shingle in the bay in front of it.

431b7855c5a3.title: Coastal management
431b7855c5a3.sentence: Coastal management is defence against flooding and erosion, and techniques that stop erosion to claim lands.

066fbfee11ec.title: Coastal management
066fbfee11ec.sentence: Coastal zones occupy less than 15% of the Earth's land area, while they host more than 40% of the world population.

619b336d581a.title: Coastal management
619b336d581a.sentence: Nearly 1.2 billion people live within 100 kilometres (62 mi) of a coastline and 100 metres (328 ft) of sea level, with an average density three times higher than the global average for population.

b6a4f6ffba77.title: Coastal management
b6a4f6ffba77.sentence: Protection against rising sea levels in the 21st century is crucial, as sea level rise accelerates due to climate change.

983176638ddf.title: Coastal management
983176638ddf.sentence: Prior to the 1950s, the general practice was to use hard structures to protect against beach erosion or storm damages.

6f517c996f94.title: Coastal management
6f517c996f94.sentence: These structures included seawalls and revetments or sand-trapping structures such as groynes.

ed0668cbb622.title: Coastal management
ed0668cbb622.sentence: The obtrusiveness and cost of these structures led in the late 1940s and early 1950s, to a more dynamic approach.

9a274eb330fd.title: Coastal management
9a274eb330fd.sentence: Projects attempted to replicate the protective characteristics of natural beach and dune systems.

15fe1e3d5367.title: Coastal management
15fe1e3d5367.sentence: The resultant use of artificial beaches and stabilized dunes as an engineering approach was economically viable and more environmentally friendly.

73978d5c4b0c.title: Coastal management
73978d5c4b0c.sentence: In many cases, measures worked locally, but exacerbated problems at other locations -up to tens of kilometers away- or generated other environmental problems.

8357363e42d8.title: Managed retreat
8357363e42d8.sentence: Managed retreat involves the purposeful, coordinated movement of people and buildings away from risks.

ad3710dc4a29.title: Managed retreat
ad3710dc4a29.sentence: This may involve the movement of a person, infrastructure (e.g., building or road), or community.

86b54c254a98.title: Managed retreat
86b54c254a98.sentence: It can occur in response to a variety of hazards such as flood, wildfire, or drought.

2d736bfdeac2.title: Managed retreat
2d736bfdeac2.sentence: Politicians, insurers, and residents are increasingly paying attention to managed retreat from low-lying coastal areas because of the threat of sea level rise due to climate change.

17685c3db239.title: Managed retreat
17685c3db239.sentence: The type of managed retreat proposed depends on the location and type of natural hazard, and on local policies and practices for managed retreat.

5e47d87dfe22.title: Managed retreat
5e47d87dfe22.sentence: Some low-lying countries, facing inundation due to sea-level rise, are planning for the relocation of their populations, such as Kiribati planning for "Migration with Dignity".

44ffd8129512.title: Managed retreat
44ffd8129512.sentence: Managed retreat can be very controversial.

f72f702fbc1a.title: Managed retreat
f72f702fbc1a.sentence: Despite the controversy, as the costs of climate change adaptation increase, more communities are beginning to consider managed retreat.

203296b549a2.title: Managed retreat
203296b549a2.sentence: NIWA coastal hazards expert Rob Bell says the issue of retreat is primarily socio-political rather than technocratic.

7165e0bc8a99.title: Climate change adaptation
7165e0bc8a99.section: Aims > Reduce risk factors: vulnerability and exposure
7165e0bc8a99.sentence: It is possible to reduce exposure by retreating from areas with high climate risks, such as floodplains.

edb87d5c0d2f.title: Climate change adaptation
edb87d5c0d2f.section: Options by type of action > Behavioural and cultural options > Migration and managed retreat
edb87d5c0d2f.sentence: Migration counts as behavioural climate adaptation for some, although others refer to it as a climate response rather: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report states: "Some responses, such as migration, relocation and resettlement may or may not be considered to be adaptation".

e3cb113f2a2d.title: Seawall
e3cb113f2a2d.sentence: A seawall (or sea wall) is a form of coastal defense constructed where the sea, and associated coastal processes, impact directly upon the landforms of the coast.

d813daccccf6.title: Seawall
d813daccccf6.sentence: The purpose of a seawall is to protect areas of human habitation, conservation, and leisure activities from the action of tides, waves, or tsunamis.

19a65a4c92d9.title: Seawall
19a65a4c92d9.sentence: A seawall works by reflecting incident wave energy back into the sea, thus reducing the energy available to cause erosion.

d5067e7fe2f7.title: Seawall
d5067e7fe2f7.sentence: Wave reflection from the wall may result in hydrodynamic scour and subsequent lowering of the sand level of the fronting beach.

c851b3339b6d.title: Seawall
c851b3339b6d.sentence: Seawalls may also accelerate the erosion of adjacent, unprotected coastal areas by affecting the littoral drift process.

973de016e347.title: Seawall
973de016e347.sentence: As a seawall is a static feature, it will conflict with the dynamic nature of the coast and impede the exchange of sediment between land and sea.

d2b61a1e7fca.title: Seawall
d2b61a1e7fca.sentence: Various environmental issues may arise from the construction of a seawall, including the disruption of sediment movement and transport patterns.

a17c205682c9.title: Seawall
a17c205682c9.sentence: Combined with a high construction cost, this has led to increasing use of other soft engineering coastal management options such as beach replenishment.

1d3f6226e861.title: Seawall
1d3f6226e861.sentence: Sea level rise creates an issue for seawalls worldwide as it raises both the mean normal water level and the height of waves during extreme weather events, with which the current seawall heights may be unable to cope.

ba4122254e73.title: Seawall
ba4122254e73.sentence: At least 43 percent of Japan's 29,751 km (18,486 mi) coastline is lined with concrete seawalls or other structures designed to protect the country against high waves, typhoons, or even tsunamis.

c245c74b8552.title: Seawall
c245c74b8552.sentence: During the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami, the seawalls in most areas were overwhelmed.

50652ef27e8e.title: Seawall
50652ef27e8e.sentence: A cost-benefit approach is an effective way to determine whether a seawall is appropriate and whether the benefits are worth the expense.

3e090e161a25.title: Seawall
3e090e161a25.sentence: In the first century BCE, Romans built a seawall or breakwater at Caesarea Maritima creating an artificial harbor (Sebastos Harbor).

c790c459d6b2.title: Oyster reef
c790c459d6b2.sentence: An oyster reef is a dense aggregation of oysters forming a large colony.

142c3b9ccfe3.title: Oyster reef
142c3b9ccfe3.sentence: These dense aggregations of oysters are also called oyster reefs, oyster beds, oyster banks, oyster bottoms, or oyster bars, with no clear distinction and with regional variation.

89f7a7d56996.title: Oyster reef
89f7a7d56996.sentence: Because oyster larvae need to settle on hard substrates, new oyster reefs form on stone or hard marine debris.

da89a9ad7168.title: Oyster reef
da89a9ad7168.sentence: Later, the oyster reef will grow by spat settling on the shells of older or nonliving oysters.

dd42c3d28af8.title: Oyster reef
dd42c3d28af8.sentence: Over the last few centuries there have been significant declines in the extent and condition of oyster reefs globally, driven by overharvesting of oysters for food provision, lime production, and coastal degradation.

2aa26b2a45da.title: Climate change mitigation
2aa26b2a45da.section: Preserving and enhancing carbon sinks > Wetlands
2aa26b2a45da.sentence: Notably, 85% of oyster reefs globally have been removed in the last two centuries.

1800c6b4e587.title: Oyster reef
1800c6b4e587.sentence: The filter feeding behavior of oysters can buffer against environmental degradation caused by human-induced eutrophication of estuary systems.

52d28df72ac8.title: Oyster reef
52d28df72ac8.sentence: Oysters feed on suspended phytoplankton and other organic matter.

85839b516f4e.title: Oyster reef
85839b516f4e.sentence: Oyster reefs also stabilize shorelines by promoting sediment deposition and buffering wave energy, thereby allowing other habitats such as sea grass beds and marsh areas to form while simultaneously decreasing erosion of the shoreline.

8177e14a07fd.title: Oyster reef
8177e14a07fd.sentence: Oyster reef habitats have been recognized as green infrastructure for shoreline protection.

f4993c8c9b91.title: Oyster reef
f4993c8c9b91.sentence: For example, the complex three-dimensional interstitial spaces within oyster reefs provide refugia for prey or juvenile species, which increases prey biomass and thereby enhances trophic transfer.

64243e5c351d.title: Oyster reef
64243e5c351d.sentence: Restoration of intertidal eastern oyster reefs can match natural densities of oysters and mud crabs, and recover oyster stability in about 6 years.

5d474e1b3494.title: Beach nourishment
5d474e1b3494.sentence: Beach nourishment (also referred to as beach renourishment, beach replenishment, or sand replenishment) describes a process by which sediment, usually sand, lost through longshore drift or erosion is replaced from other sources.

e8d081968958.title: Beach nourishment
e8d081968958.sentence: A wider beach can reduce storm damage to coastal structures by dissipating energy across the surf zone, protecting upland structures and infrastructure from storm surges, tsunamis and unusually high tides.

0a3b6bcf658e.title: Beach nourishment
0a3b6bcf658e.sentence: A wide beach is a good energy absorber, which is significant in low-lying areas where severe storms can impact upland structures.

4986e6459d4f.title: Beach nourishment
4986e6459d4f.sentence: - Soft engineering: Beach nourishment is a type of soft approach which preserves beach resources and avoids the negative effects of hard structures.

e0950afac99b.title: Beach nourishment
e0950afac99b.sentence: Nourishment is typically a repetitive process because it does not remove the physical forces that cause erosion; it simply mitigates their effects.

5dc67b265eb5.title: Beach nourishment
5dc67b265eb5.sentence: The first nourishment project in the U.S. was constructed at Coney Island, New York in 1922–1923.

626e10a21fae.title: Beach nourishment
626e10a21fae.sentence: Since 1923, the U.S. has spent $9 billion to rebuild beaches.

a2c362b261d5.title: Beach nourishment
a2c362b261d5.sentence: The most important material characteristic is the sediment grain size, which must closely match the native material.

1ea2691922c6.title: Beach nourishment
1ea2691922c6.sentence: Nourishment may cause direct mortality to sessile organisms in the target area by burying them under the new sand.

bd7d81ead8d8.title: Beach nourishment
bd7d81ead8d8.sentence: The seafloor habitat in both source and target areas are disrupted, e.g. when sand is deposited on coral reefs or when deposited sand hardens.

a512340fdb42.title: Beach nourishment
a512340fdb42.sentence: Light availability may be reduced, affecting nearby reefs and submerged aquatic vegetation.

0ee6d2070aad.title: Beach nourishment
0ee6d2070aad.sentence: - Increases land value of nearby properties.

768f81da22c3.title: Beach nourishment
768f81da22c3.sentence: - Grows economy through tourism and recreation.

61d53b98505b.title: Beach nourishment
61d53b98505b.sentence: Conversely, high erosion rates may render nourishment financially impractical.

46502dd18dd1.title: Coastal management
46502dd18dd1.sentence: Five generic strategies are involved in coastal defense:

e5b480d04c08.title: Coastal management
e5b480d04c08.sentence: - Managed retreat or realignment, which plans for retreat and adopts engineering solutions that accommodate natural processes of adjustment

836696d40d5c.title: Coastal management
836696d40d5c.sentence: - Armoring by constructing seawalls and other hard structures

e38f7659d670.title: Coastal management
e38f7659d670.sentence: - Construct defenses seaward of the coast

bb445eb0d63b.title: Coastal management
bb445eb0d63b.sentence: - Adapting vertically by elevating land and buildings

5f89adec417d.title: Coastal management
5f89adec417d.sentence: The choice of strategy is site-specific, depending on pattern of sea-level change, geomorphological setting, sediment availability and erosion, as well as social, economic and political factors.

99a4c8081182.title: Coastal management
99a4c8081182.sentence: Alternatively, integrated coastal zone management approaches may be used to prevent development in erosion- or flood-prone areas, reducing the need to address the changes.

df448a3562f2.title: Coastal management
df448a3562f2.sentence: An upside to the strategy is that moving seaward (and upward) can create land of high value which can bring investment.

9463b05f0238.title: Coastal management
9463b05f0238.sentence: They will experience a so-called "coastal squeeze" whereby ecological or geomorphological zones that would normally retreat landwards encounter solid structures and can migrate no further.

d0ef10c45522.title: Coastal management
d0ef10c45522.sentence: Limited intervention is an action taken whereby the management only addresses the problem to a certain extent, usually in areas of low economic significance.

192c6933036a.title: Coastal management
192c6933036a.sentence: Limited intervention often includes the succession of haloseres, including salt marshes and sand dunes.

da5d99c08a93.title: Coastal management
da5d99c08a93.sentence: This normally results in protecting the land behind the halosere, as wave energy dissipates throughout the accumulated sediment and additional vegetation in the new habitat.

26d7dcd510c7.title: Soft engineering
26d7dcd510c7.sentence: Regarding the civil engineering of shorelines, soft engineering is a shoreline management practice that uses sustainable ecological principles to restore shoreline stabilization and protect riparian habitats.

68810e6ea41b.title: Soft engineering
68810e6ea41b.sentence: Soft Shoreline Engineering (SSE) uses the strategic placement of organic materials such as vegetation, stones, sand, debris, and other structural materials to reduce erosion, enhance shoreline aesthetic, soften the land-water interface, and lower costs of ecological restoration.

fee648e22ef0.title: Soft engineering
fee648e22ef0.sentence: - Imitate Nature - Imitating the characteristics of the natural environment is critical to the success of soft engineering efforts.

c26f2b8f756c.title: Soft engineering
c26f2b8f756c.sentence: Gradually inclined slopes along banks and shorelines allow for the dissipation of wave energy over a greater distance, reducing the force of erosion.

9ff3e33a4168.title: Soft engineering
9ff3e33a4168.sentence: - "Soft Armoring" - Soft armoring includes the use of materials such as live plants, shrubs, root wads, logs, vegetative mats, etc. These materials, which are alive, can adapt to changes in the environment and help maintain regular coastal processes by disrupting the natural shoreline in the least way possible.

928aaa6278ad.title: Soft engineering
928aaa6278ad.sentence: - Material Variety - A variety of textures and vegetation enhances aesthetic, diversifies the natural landscape, and maximizes biodiversity.

c430a9300e81.title: Soft engineering
c430a9300e81.sentence: The most basic and fundamental form of soft shoreline engineering is adding native vegetation to degraded or damaged shoreline areas to bolster the structural integrity of the soil.

c6c3ed77e79c.title: Soft engineering
c6c3ed77e79c.sentence: The deep roots of the vegetation bind the soil together, strengthening the structural integrity of the soil and preventing it from cracking apart and crumbling into the body of water.

a8369f349944.title: Soft engineering
a8369f349944.sentence: Erosion control coir logs are natural fiber products designed to stabilize soil by supporting erosion prone areas such as river banks, slopes, hills, and streams.

a633a12e9911.title: Soft engineering
a633a12e9911.sentence: Lives stakes and fascines are a specific tree or shrub species that thrive in moist soil conditions and can be strategically used to stabilize stream banks and shorelines.

e59fa8b2c576.title: Soft engineering
e59fa8b2c576.sentence: Brush mattresses, also known as live brush mats or brush matting, is a technique used to form immediate protective cover of a streambank.

af924b97c6e4.title: Soft engineering
af924b97c6e4.sentence: Live crib walls are structures that resemble that of a wooden log cabin built into a streambank and rilled with natural materials such as soil, dormant wood cuttings, and rock.

c7d2b4c8fd77.title: Soft engineering
c7d2b4c8fd77.sentence: Vegetated riprap is a soft shoreline engineering technique that is an alternative to conventional riprap for erosion protection.

2cc2afd2bc27.title: Soft engineering
2cc2afd2bc27.sentence: Towards the end of the 20th century, coastal engineering practices underwent a gradual transition towards incorporating the natural environment into planning considerations.

0a8530b8084b.title: Soft engineering
