670ef96665b6.title: Sand dune stabilization
670ef96665b6.sentence: Sand dune stabilization is a coastal management practice designed to prevent erosion of sand dunes.

69bc6132a6ec.title: Sand dune stabilization
69bc6132a6ec.sentence: Sand dunes serve an important purpose by protecting inland areas from coastal water intrusion.

3088acefe592.title: Sand dune stabilization
3088acefe592.sentence: They are able to absorb the impact and protect inland areas from high energy storms and act as a resilient barrier to the destructive forces of wind and waves.

7ee4bb5bca1b.title: Sand dune stabilization
7ee4bb5bca1b.sentence: They can protect beaches from erosion and recruit sand to eroded beaches.

23ddf82b75e4.title: Sand dune stabilization
23ddf82b75e4.sentence: Dunes provide habitat for highly specialized plants and animals, including rare and endangered species.

f397b82b506e.title: Sand dune stabilization
f397b82b506e.sentence: Planting vegetation reduces the impact of wind and water.

566919a3bcad.title: Sand dune stabilization
566919a3bcad.sentence: Wooden sand fences can help retain sand and other material needed for a healthy sand dune ecosystem.

d22404c6a32e.title: Sand dune stabilization
d22404c6a32e.sentence: Footpaths protect dunes from damage from foot traffic.

62e054dc23d0.title: Sand dune stabilization
62e054dc23d0.section: Coastal sand dune management > Human impacts
62e054dc23d0.sentence: Loss in vegetation cover exposes sand to the action of wind and leaves sand dunes vulnerable to increased erosion as it is vegetation that binds sand together.

d5b528c4cbde.title: Sand dune stabilization
d5b528c4cbde.section: Coastal sand dune management > Human impacts
d5b528c4cbde.sentence: The loss of vegetation causes sand to move inland which is a process known as sand encroachment, this process can having damaging effects on inland properties and leaves properties vulnerable to future coastal hazards for example storm surge.

ed82d9af34ba.title: Sand dune stabilization
ed82d9af34ba.section: Coastal sand dune management > Human impacts
ed82d9af34ba.sentence: For example, in the last 30 years, mainly because of tourism, nearly 75% of the Mediterranean's coastal dunes have been damaged or destroyed.

67f93954bae1.title: Sand dune stabilization
67f93954bae1.section: Coastal sand dune management > Integrated management
67f93954bae1.sentence: Sand dune management consists of restoring natural dune systems and processes with the implementation of “soft” technique which includes the cessation of any activity that adversely effects the sediment supply of the dunes, planting vegetation, fencing off sensitive areas, creating dune walkways, and providing information to the public regarding the importance of maintaining stable sand dunes.

96d42cfd4c4c.title: Sand dune stabilization
96d42cfd4c4c.section: Coastal sand dune management > Integrated management
96d42cfd4c4c.sentence: The problem with using these “hard” engineering methods is that they only provide temporary protection against ocean hazards and each "hard" method produces an “end effect” that causes erosion problems to adjacent coastal areas.

5eedc725d79a.title: Sand dune stabilization
5eedc725d79a.section: Coastal sand dune management > The public
5eedc725d79a.sentence: The public needs to be aware of the role that sand dunes play in coastal protection, because without public support, coastal sand dune management is virtually impossible.

2739d533cb87.title: Oyster reef restoration
2739d533cb87.sentence: Oyster reef restoration refers to the reparation and reconstruction of degraded oyster reefs.

4e0db61adfa9.title: Oyster reef restoration
4e0db61adfa9.sentence: By 2011, it was estimated that approximately 85% of global oyster reefs had been lost, highlighting the scale of this ecological crisis.

e4692e944e19.title: Oyster reef restoration
e4692e944e19.sentence: Centuries of unsustainable exploitation, including intense over-harvesting and destructive fishing practices, coupled with increasing pollution, and disease have severely degraded these habitats.

810687268abb.title: Oyster reef restoration
810687268abb.sentence: The typical desired outcomes of these restoration projects are the restoration of oyster reefs to produce a fully functioning, three-dimensional bed system that provides associated ecosystem services and biological functions, such as marine biodiversity, shoreline protection, sediment trapping, water quality improvement, and recreational fishing opportunities.

59eeaba6b98a.title: Oyster reef restoration
59eeaba6b98a.sentence: Determining the location for potential reefs is often done by comprehensive surveys that measure multiple variables.

97d3ed1f2651.title: Oyster reef restoration
97d3ed1f2651.sentence: The comprehensive survey consists of measuring salinity levels, water quality, previous existence of oyster reefs, substrate conditions, prevalence of diseases, tidal range, oxygen concentration, algae concentration, prevalence of predators, accessibility and security.

6084bd46b604.title: Oyster reef restoration
6084bd46b604.sentence: Oyster reef restoration can recover oyster densities to match those of healthy natural reefs.

de4ed554343a.title: Oyster reef restoration
de4ed554343a.sentence: Healthy oyster populations improve the quality of water, which in turn improves commercial and recreational fishing, recreational boating, and ecotourism.

18b9672cc363.title: Oyster reef restoration
18b9672cc363.sentence: Not only does oyster restoration create additional jobs through the duration of projects, but it also safeguards many other jobs ranging from marine construction to scientific research jobs.

333913579a48.title: Oyster reef restoration
333913579a48.sentence: Another issue of environmental harm is placing invasive or newly introduced oyster species in an unknown habitat that can cause more harm than good.

de455b351238.sentence: Mangroves make up only 0.7% of tropical forest area worldwide, yet studies calculate the effect of mangrove deforestation to contribute 10% of global CO2 emissions from deforestation.

c454c56f81d6.title: Mangrove restoration
c454c56f81d6.sentence: Depending on sediment accumulation, mangrove habitats will generally respond to sea level change in three different ways: (1) If the sediment in the mangrove forest rises faster than the sea level, plants from further inland may move into the area as the mangroves retreat; (2) if the rate of sediment accumulation is equal to the rate of sea level rise, the forest survives and is stable during this period and (3) if the rate of soil accumulation is slower than the rate of sea level rise, the mangrove forest will be submerged by the sea.

f75d5e6cfc78.title: Mangrove restoration
f75d5e6cfc78.sentence: Mangrove restoration is the rehabilitation of degraded, damaged, or destroyed mangrove forest ecosystems to return them to a state comparable to their pre-disturbed conditions.

39940aaa157f.title: Mangrove restoration
39940aaa157f.sentence: Located throughout coastal wetlands of tropical and subtropical environments, mangroves provide essential ecosystem services such as water filtration, aquatic nurseries, medicinal materials, food, and lumber.

409c07d10c52.title: Mangrove restoration
409c07d10c52.sentence: Additionally, mangroves contribute to climate change mitigation through carbon sequestration and protection from coastal erosion, sea level rise, and storm surges.

f03d9112e385.title: Mangrove restoration

f03d9112e385.sentence: Being the most carbon-rich tropical forest, mangroves are highly productive and are found to store three to four times more carbon than other tropical forests.

8bf9777f2c39.title: Mangrove restoration

e85e97c32b32.title: Mangrove restoration

0ff7cf57d4fb.title: Living shoreline

c05d391f22b5.title: Living shoreline
c05d391f22b5.sentence: Unlike traditional structures such as bulkheads or seawalls that worsen erosion, living shorelines incorporate as many natural elements as possible which create more effective buffers in absorbing wave energy and protecting against shoreline erosion.

e4ad1164421e.title: Living shoreline

090016cd1e52.title: Living shoreline
090016cd1e52.sentence: Structural and organic materials commonly used in the construction of living shorelines include sand, wetland plants, sand fill, oyster reefs, submerged aquatic vegetation, stones and coir fiber logs.

75ba6af63d08.title: Living shoreline

c32d0f847639.title: Living shoreline

d0b02f2114a9.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
d0b02f2114a9.sentence: Integrated mangrove-shrimp (IMS) aquaculture is a sustainable farming system used as one of the measures for mangrove rehabilitation and can be described as a method of organic aquaculture.

d5e063336632.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
d5e063336632.sentence: Silvoaquaculture or silvofisheries are also terms used to define this farming practice where mangrove trees are planted alongside shrimp ponds allowing for profitable net income from shrimp farming, as it replicates a more natural habitat.

04d5ca79616a.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
04d5ca79616a.sentence: One of the main causes of mangrove forest depletion is the expansion of shrimp aquaculture.

b01ae33f3080.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
b01ae33f3080.sentence: The performance and sustainability of shrimp ponds depend on the goods and services provided by mangrove ecosystems yet mangrove forests are being cleared to build these shrimp farms.

f81beebaba2d.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
f81beebaba2d.section: The integrated mangrove-shrimp system > The comparison with traditional farming practice
f81beebaba2d.sentence: IMS aquaculture is similar to extensive farming in that it doesn't depend on chemical inputs, formulated feed and shrimp larvae but instead relies on natural feed and natural shrimp recruitment from the exchange of tidal water.

5677e6164e53.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
5677e6164e53.section: The integrated mangrove-shrimp system > The comparison with traditional farming practice
5677e6164e53.sentence: Unlike intensive farming, where shrimp yield correlates with high investment, this sustainable practice has a low operational cost.

dde1ba51cb87.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
dde1ba51cb87.section: The integrated mangrove-shrimp system > Ideal conditions
dde1ba51cb87.sentence: Based on multiple studies on IMS cultivation in Vietnam, the optimal mangrove coverage to maximize net profit from shrimp production was found to be between 30%-50%.

24aaad0ed6d1.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
24aaad0ed6d1.section: The integrated mangrove-shrimp system > Ideal conditions
24aaad0ed6d1.sentence: The challenge in these cases are due to the regulations stipulating that mangrove coverage need to be above optimal percentages, between 60-80%, which has led to over logging and the reluctance to practice silvoaquaculture.

b381592a210b.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
b381592a210b.sentence: - Biodiversity of flora and fauna: the increase in mangrove area helps maintain biodiversity as mangroves provide nursing grounds for a number of aquatic species and are home to numerous animal species.

019a7735f627.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
019a7735f627.sentence: - Blue carbon sequestration: the restoration of mangrove forests by practicing IMS aquaculture can help reduce greenhouse gas emissions as these trees are highly efficient in capturing and storing carbon.

5e1cb0db6949.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
5e1cb0db6949.sentence: - Sustainable livelihood: IMS cultivation provides local communities with regular income from shrimp farming (continuous harvest) as well as from timber production and other fishery products, while rehabilitating mangrove forests.

004d5ee89ef9.title: Integrated mangrove-shrimp aquaculture
004d5ee89ef9.sentence: - Benefit sharing from timber production: farmers can be discouraged from shifting to IMS farming because the income from mangrove forest exploitation may not be as profitable for them due to unequal benefit sharing with forest companies or relevant stakeholders in the timber industry.

5cd610c6cb2f.title: Coral reef restoration
5cd610c6cb2f.sentence: The process of cultivating coral polyps is known as coral gardening.

d26b2a95963f.title: Coral reef restoration
d26b2a95963f.sentence: Growing small coral fragments through asexual reproduction until they are fully mature is the fundamental technique of coral gardening, with ocean-based or land-based nurseries being the two primary methods utilized.

0fe8734bad39.title: Coral reef restoration
0fe8734bad39.sentence: Fragmentation involves dividing a wild coral colony (an attached group of genetically identical group of polyps) into smaller pieces.

07467be3bc5b.title: Coral reef restoration
07467be3bc5b.sentence: These smaller pieces are grown asexually into additional colonies.

8badeb1f4d74.title: Coral reef restoration
8badeb1f4d74.sentence: These fragmented colonies are genetically identical to the host colony.

025f109f2dec.title: Coral reef restoration
025f109f2dec.sentence: Ocean-based nurseries involve growing coral fragments underwater, attaching them to structures and monitoring their growth until they reach maturity as new colonies.

8c689940e192.title: Coral reef restoration
8c689940e192.sentence: Land-based nurseries grow coral fragments in tanks on land, which allows micro fragmenting.

7348fda7598a.title: Coral reef restoration
7348fda7598a.sentence: Fragmentation allows for about an 8x increase in reproduction (colony growh) compared to that of the donor coral.

21c4b82d7ccf.title: Coral reef restoration
21c4b82d7ccf.sentence: Since most colonies grow only about one inch per year, faster-growing practices are help accelerate restoration.

efa2700aa85a.title: Coral reef restoration
efa2700aa85a.sentence: Additionally, growing colonies on land can protect them from temperature changes, storms, predators, disease, and other problems.

7af7df063638.title: Coral reef restoration
7af7df063638.sentence: Micro-fragmentation involves cutting small (>1 cm) pieces of live coral from a colony.

6ba5713efb74.title: Coral reef restoration
6ba5713efb74.sentence: These pieces are affixed to a ceramic or cement base called a plug and placed in tanks.

d02d96e2b56b.title: Coral reef restoration
d02d96e2b56b.sentence: Micro-fragmentation was developed by David Vaughan in 2006.

672298ab9c7d.title: Coral reef restoration
672298ab9c7d.sentence: It relies on coral's ability to clone itself.

c15713532a48.title: Coral reef restoration
c15713532a48.sentence: Reef-building corals are the prime species for this technique, because micro-fragmentation accelerates their growth from years often to months.

a4d8ecbaae7a.title: Community Based Mangrove Management
a4d8ecbaae7a.sentence: Community Based Mangrove Management (CBMM) is a sustainable approach for conserving the rapidly disappearing mangrove forests.

bef13e9910e9.title: Community Based Mangrove Management
bef13e9910e9.sentence: It can be defined as community driven management and rehabilitation of mangrove forests involving resource users in the management process directly.

9745e6ee7264.title: Community Based Mangrove Management
9745e6ee7264.sentence: CBMM decentralizes authority and power from government to local communities.

b2b76f2fa50e.title: Community Based Mangrove Management
b2b76f2fa50e.sentence: The dual aim of CBMM is the ongoing conservation of mangroves and generation of sustainable livelihood.

2fb719195a54.title: Community Based Mangrove Management
2fb719195a54.sentence: Traditionally local communities managed the mangroves but during the colonial and post-colonial periods these forests came under the control of state government which gave incentive to farming and other land use changes.

0cf92f34ab49.title: Community Based Mangrove Management
0cf92f34ab49.sentence: Due to complete control of government over these forests, local communities were alienated and started perceiving these forests as extra source of income.

256898f384f5.title: Community Based Mangrove Management
256898f384f5.sentence: Hence, indiscriminate farming and intense logging destroyed this valuable ecosystem.

d5c9bdb213c0.title: Community Based Mangrove Management
d5c9bdb213c0.sentence: Scientists observed that community managed mangroves have remarkable recovery potential and local people are effective stewards for management of these resources.

8cdb4f36c269.title: Community Based Mangrove Management
8cdb4f36c269.sentence: Any CBMM initiative depends upon the willingness to pay (WTP) of local communities.

ab69420539c3.title: Community Based Mangrove Management
ab69420539c3.sentence: Hence, ecological, economic and social sustainability need to be considered for the holistic success of CBMM programs.

44fc157324d5.title: Sea rewilding
44fc157324d5.sentence: Sea rewilding (also known as marine rewilding) is an environmental conservation process involving rewilding, restoring organisms and ecosystems to their natural states.

98ce1607415a.title: Sea rewilding
98ce1607415a.sentence: Sea rewilding aims to create conditions where a marine ecosystem is able to recover from prior damage and stressors so that it may thrive independently over time.

0c969ad20405.title: Sea rewilding
0c969ad20405.sentence: Activities to facilitate this process include species reintroduction and replenishing, i.e. of oysters, kelp, and seagrass beds.

e442d6e608ae.title: Sea rewilding
e442d6e608ae.sentence: Sea rewilding aids in combating the climate crisis by capturing carbon dioxide, supporting local economies with ecotourism, reversing biodiversity loss, and improving health and well being by providing restored natural landscapes, clean air, water, and healthy soil.

93d6f74f4f1d.title: Sea rewilding

8b9186a4aa98.title: Sea rewilding

30066955ff33.title: Urban heat island
30066955ff33.sentence: The urban heat island (UHI) effect is a meteorological and climatological phenomenon in which urban areas experience significantly warmer temperatures than surrounding rural areas.

37f1f4a788b8.title: Urban heat island
37f1f4a788b8.sentence: The main cause of the UHI effect is from the modification of land surfaces, while waste heat generated by energy usage is a secondary contributor.

4e448ce8f09b.title: Urban heat island
4e448ce8f09b.sentence: For example, dark surfaces absorb significantly more solar radiation, which causes urban concentrations of roads and buildings to heat more than suburban and rural areas during the day; materials commonly used in urban areas for pavement and roofs, such as concrete and asphalt, have significantly different thermal bulk properties (including heat capacity and thermal conductivity) and surface radiative properties (albedo and emissivity) than the surrounding rural areas.

bd189cd35c36.title: Urban heat island
bd189cd35c36.sentence: By virtue of their high heat capacities, urban surfaces act as a reservoir of heat energy.

60dfbb38b260.title: Urban heat island
60dfbb38b260.sentence: The temperature difference is usually larger at night than during the day, and is most apparent when winds are weak, under block conditions, noticeably during the summer and winter.

556228600d10.title: Urban heat island
556228600d10.sentence: Urban areas occupy about 0.5% of the Earth's land surface but host more than half of the world's population.

79aac3d33e69.title: Urban heat island
79aac3d33e69.sentence: As UHIs are characterized by increased temperature, they can potentially increase the magnitude and duration of heat waves within cities.

a8e9588f817c.title: Urban heat island
a8e9588f817c.section: Impacts > On energy usage for cooling
a8e9588f817c.sentence: Another consequence of urban heat islands is the increased energy required for air conditioning and refrigeration in cities that are in comparatively hot climates.

312220f70eb7.title: Urban heat island
312220f70eb7.section: Impacts > On water bodies and aquatic organisms
312220f70eb7.sentence: Hot pavement and rooftop surfaces transfer their excess heat to stormwater, which then drains into storm sewers and raises water temperatures as it is released into streams, rivers, ponds, and lakes.

854cd76822e6.title: Urban heat island
854cd76822e6.section: Causes > Climate change as an amplifier
854cd76822e6.sentence: Climate change is not a cause but an amplifier of the urban heat island effect.

5a39dbafb913.title: Urban heat island
5a39dbafb913.section: Options for reducing heat island effects
5a39dbafb913.sentence: Strategies to improve urban resilience by reducing excessive heat in cities include: Planting trees in cities, cool roofs (painted white or with reflective coating) and light-coloured concrete, green infrastructure (including green roofs), passive daytime radiative cooling.

68b8fa4a04a1.title: Urban heat island
68b8fa4a04a1.section: Society and culture > History of research
68b8fa4a04a1.sentence: The phenomenon was first investigated and described by Luke Howard in the 1810s, although he was not the one to name the phenomenon.

7263ae595bda.title: Urban heat island
7263ae595bda.section: Society and culture > History of research
7263ae595bda.sentence: A description of the very first report of the UHI by Luke Howard said that the urban center of London was warmer at night than the surrounding countryside by 2.1 °C (3.7 °F).

56282ba882c6.sentence: The World Health Organization (WHO) defined urban green spaces as "all urban land covered by vegetation of any kind".

6900be17ae08.title: Urban green space
6900be17ae08.sentence: These include plant life, water features – also known as blue spaces – and other kinds of natural environments.

0dfdd4956d51.title: Urban green space
0dfdd4956d51.sentence: The landscape of open spaces in urban areas can range from playing fields and other highly maintained environments to more natural landscapes that appear less managed.

4d928c39a9e2.title: Urban green space
4d928c39a9e2.sentence: The benefits that urban open spaces provide to citizens can be categorized into four basic forms: recreation, ecology, aesthetic value, and positive health impacts.

0ab162594432.title: Urban green space
0ab162594432.sentence: Green spaces may improve the air quality of urban areas and provide habitat for wildlife, improving the overall ecological health of urban environments.

3831198e9a40.title: Urban green space
3831198e9a40.sentence: They may also reduce the risk of flooding by providing rainwater drainage.

e005ffc4662f.title: Urban green space
e005ffc4662f.sentence: Properties near urban open spaces tend to have a higher value.

d78ce096b96a.title: Urban green space
d78ce096b96a.sentence: Psychological research shows that benefits to visitors of urban green spaces increased with their biodiversity, indicating that "green" alone is not sufficient: the quality and variety of the urban green space are important as well.

6c4982d44259.title: Urban green space
6c4982d44259.sentence: The term "rus in urbe" meaning "country in the city" was used in Rome around the first century C.E.

e62cc63c3094.title: Green roof
e62cc63c3094.sentence: A green roof or living roof is a roof of a building that is partially or completely covered with vegetation and a growing medium, planted over a waterproofing membrane.

463303a96dc6.title: Green roof
463303a96dc6.section: Environmental benefits > Thermal reduction and energy conservation
463303a96dc6.sentence: Green roofs improve and reduce energy consumption.

50c913ac7b98.title: Green roof
50c913ac7b98.section: Environmental benefits > Thermal reduction and energy conservation
50c913ac7b98.sentence: They can reduce heating by adding mass and thermal resistance value, and can reduce the heat island effect by increasing evapotranspiration.

89ccd4b31683.sentence: A study presented at the Green Roofs for Healthy Cities Conference in June 2004, cited by the EPA, found water runoff was reduced by over 75% during rainstorms.

4bba08767c70.title: Green roof
