b0cc13c7829b.sentence: Academic discussion of urban resilience has historically focused primarily on three threats: climate change, natural disasters, and terrorism.

1ca42404dc8f.title: Urban resilience
1ca42404dc8f.sentence: A recent study of 616 cities (home to 1.7 billion people, with a combined GDP of US$35 trillion, half of the world's total economic output), found that floods endanger more city residents than any other natural peril, followed by earthquakes and storms.

0ae5165d8235.title: Urban resilience
0ae5165d8235.section: Climate change > Adapting for heat and drought resilience > Greening, reflecting and whitening urban spaces
0ae5165d8235.sentence: Greening urban spaces is among the most frequently mentioned strategies to address heat effects.

afd619123933.title: Urban resilience
afd619123933.section: Climate change > Adapting for heat and drought resilience > Greening, reflecting and whitening urban spaces
afd619123933.sentence: Covering as much surface as possible with greenery will both reduce the total quantity of thermally absorbent artificial material, and by creating shade, will reduce the amount of light and heat that reaches the concrete and asphalt that cannot be replaced by greenery.

a6ae590e41c7.title: Urban resilience
a6ae590e41c7.section: Flooding > Adapting for flood resilience > Urban greening
a6ae590e41c7.sentence: Replacing as much non-porous surface as possible with greenery will allow the ground and plants to help absorb excess water.

03ecaf1bacfc.title: Urban resilience
03ecaf1bacfc.section: Flooding > Adapting for flood resilience > Urban greening
03ecaf1bacfc.sentence: The deeper the soil, the more rainwater it can absorb and therefore the more potential floodwater it can prevent from reaching the ground.

ac13c69eb5c6.title: Urban resilience
ac13c69eb5c6.section: Climate change > Social factors for heat vulnerability
ac13c69eb5c6.sentence: Statistically, senior citizens represent the majority of heat (and cold) related deaths within urban areas.

6111862251a2.title: Urban resilience
6111862251a2.section: Climate change > Social factors for heat vulnerability
6111862251a2.sentence: This increased heat-related mortality among the elderly population is associated with social isolation common in urban environments.

93b86606c932.title: Urban resilience
93b86606c932.sentence: Building resilience in cities relies on making investment decisions that prioritize funding activities that offer alternatives suitable for variable future conditions.

860655b1fb6d.title: Urban resilience
860655b1fb6d.sentence: Such decisions need to take into account future risks and uncertainties as risk can never be fully eliminated; emergency and disaster planning is crucial.

7530e7ae3c78.title: Blue roof
7530e7ae3c78.sentence: A blue roof is a roof of a building that is designed explicitly to provide initial temporary water storage and then gradual release of stored water, typically rainfall.

885342075842.title: Blue roof
885342075842.sentence: Blue roofs are constructed on flat or low sloped roofs in urban communities where flooding is a risk due to a lack of permeable surfaces for water to infiltrate, or seep back into the ground.

de3d2376b218.title: Blue roof
de3d2376b218.section: Stormwater management and other benefits > Flood mitigation
de3d2376b218.sentence: This lack of area for stormwater to infiltrate back into the ground leaves cities vulnerable to flooding.

13def8fe649a.title: Blue roof
13def8fe649a.section: Stormwater management and other benefits > Pollution reduction
13def8fe649a.sentence: While blue roofs do not remove pollutants from water by temporarily detaining it, they do reduce the load severe rain events place on storm sewers which stops emergency overflow from combined sewer systems from discharging untreated wastewater into rivers, streams, and coastal waters.

c2052c93e0a5.title: Blue roof
c2052c93e0a5.sentence: Active blue roof systems control the rate at which water drains from a rooftop through mechanical means.

b2318337477e.title: Blue roof
b2318337477e.sentence: Unlike active systems which inhibit water flow through drainage pipes, passive systems temporarily detain water on the surface of the roof by lengthening the path the water must take in order to reach outlet drains.

05f12040d7e2.title: Blue roof
05f12040d7e2.section: Stormwater management and other benefits > Water scarcity
05f12040d7e2.sentence: In drier climates, blue roofs act as a water conservation tool harvesting the water that falls on a roof's surface and collecting it at a controlled rate.

e2a3716b4745.title: Green roof
e2a3716b4745.sentence: A blue-green roof combines blue roof technology with that of a green roof to optimize the benefits of greening roof scapes, storing water beneath layers of substrate and vegetation.

85a6d3db05d6.title: Green roof
85a6d3db05d6.sentence: Benefits include mitigating stormwater runoff impacts, reusing stormwater for irrigation of the green roof, and cooling indoor temperatures of buildings.

6aac36fa1103.title: Urban agriculture
6aac36fa1103.sentence: Many communities make community gardening accessible to the public, providing space for citizens to cultivate plants for food, recreation and education.

f33fec1b68dc.title: Urban agriculture
f33fec1b68dc.sentence: In many cities, small plots of land and also rooftops are used for community members to garden.

118fb143c33f.title: Urban agriculture
118fb143c33f.sentence: Many gardens facilitate the improvement of social networks within the communities that they are located.

97c31eb25cf3.title: Urban agriculture
97c31eb25cf3.sentence: For many neighborhoods, gardens provide a "symbolic focus", which leads to increased neighborhood pride.

cd462ade26bc.title: Urban agriculture
cd462ade26bc.section: Impacts and solutions > Health inequalities and food justice
cd462ade26bc.sentence: A 2009 report by the USDA determined that "evidence is both abundant and robust enough for us to conclude that Americans living in low-income and minority areas tend to have poor access to healthy food", and that the "structural inequalities" in these neighborhoods "contribute to inequalities in diet and diet-related outcomes".

1e824bcbb447.title: Urban agriculture
1e824bcbb447.section: Impacts and solutions > Health inequalities and food justice
1e824bcbb447.sentence: Although the definition and methods for determining "food deserts" have varied, studies indicate that, at least in the United States, there are racial disparities in the food environment.

0628293813e6.title: Urban agriculture
0628293813e6.sentence: When urban agriculture leads to locally grown fresh produce sold at affordable prices in food deserts, access to healthy food is not just available for those who live in wealthy areas, thereby leading to greater equity in rich and poor neighborhoods.

f9359fabf730.title: Urban park
f9359fabf730.sentence: Parks can be divided into active and passive recreation areas.

ba3854267f0d.title: Urban park
ba3854267f0d.sentence: Active recreation is that which has an urban character and requires intensive development.

f439212761d3.title: Urban park
f439212761d3.sentence: Passive recreation, also called "low-intensity recreation" is that which emphasizes the open-space aspect of a park and allows for the preservation of natural habitat.

c7c4550b099d.title: Urban park
c7c4550b099d.sentence: Active recreation such as team sports, due to the need to provide substantial space to congregate, typically involves intensive management, maintenance, and high costs.

c7aa7716d5ff.title: Urban park
c7aa7716d5ff.sentence: It usually involves a low level of development, such as rustic picnic areas, benches, and walking trails.

4b26047a1bea.title: Urban park
4b26047a1bea.sentence: Passive recreation typically requires little management and can be provided at very low costs.

4a28d24cfba7.title: Urban park
4a28d24cfba7.sentence: A linear park is a park that has a much greater length than width.

1edd2edea90c.title: Urban park
1edd2edea90c.sentence: A typical example of a linear park is a section of a former railway that has been converted into a park called a rail trail or greenway (i.e. the tracks removed, vegetation allowed to grow back).

915c8c2c79b6.title: Urban park
915c8c2c79b6.sentence: Some examples of linear parks in North America include New York's High Line and the Village of Yorkville Park in Toronto, which won an award from the American Society of Landscape Architects.

7870d958d26c.title: Ecologically sustainable development
7870d958d26c.sentence: Specifically increasing the size of green areas and developing a network of green corridors is a successful way to maintain high levels of urban biodiversity.

665e8399fa94.title: Urban ecology
665e8399fa94.sentence: Research in countries of temperate areas indicates that, on a small scale, urbanization often increases the biodiversity of non-native species while reducing that of native species.

ca774d92a182.title: Urban ecology
ca774d92a182.sentence: This normally results in an overall reduction in species richness and increase in total biomass and species abundance.

3e4f19bc8e44.title: Urban ecology
3e4f19bc8e44.section: Biodiversity and urbanization > Cause of diversity change
3e4f19bc8e44.sentence: The urban environment can decrease diversity through habitat removal and species homogenization—the increasing similarity between two previously distinct biological communities.

8a2d9db47880.title: Urban ecology
8a2d9db47880.section: Biodiversity and urbanization > Cause of diversity change
8a2d9db47880.sentence: Habitat degradation and habitat fragmentation reduces the amount of suitable habitat by urban development and separates suitable patches by inhospitable terrain such as roads, neighborhoods, and open parks.

6e54274902d7.title: Ecologically sustainable development
6e54274902d7.sentence: The incorporation of a green roof on a sustainable development can facilitate urban biodiversity from different types of vegetation that can be installed on a green roof, thus increasing the overall biodiversity of an area.

b06d67a50104.title: Urban forestry
b06d67a50104.section: Wildlife habitat management > Biodiversity and threatened/endangered species
b06d67a50104.sentence: Urban Forestry Management Plans in conjunction with Wildlife Management Plans can support and improve urban biodiversity by including following attributes: routine tree inventories to identify a biodiversity baseline for goal setting, intentional tree planting of hardy species to promote biodiversity, and lastly to focus on the preservation and improvement of urban parks and woodlots as vital wooded and edge habitats.

03b128a5b36c.title: Urban wildlife
03b128a5b36c.sentence: Providing safe movement paths for wildlife, improving habitat quality, and limiting anthropogenic threats are important for sustaining urban biodiversity.

1865fa3e304b.title: Urban forestry
1865fa3e304b.sentence: A street tree is any tree that is growing in a city thoroughfare, whether between the sidewalk and the curb or in an unimproved right-of-way.

abd62cc95a6a.title: Urban forestry
abd62cc95a6a.sentence: Street trees provide valuable ecosystem services including stormwater mitigation, air pollutant removal, and shade to mitigate the urban heat island effect.

5d2272542951.title: Urban forestry
5d2272542951.sentence: Since street trees are often planted in areas with a high percentage of impervious surfaces, they are an important fraction of an area's overall urban tree cover.

a9dc98ae5b13.title: Urban rewilding
a9dc98ae5b13.sentence: Urban rewilding is a specific form of rewilding, a movement that gained prominence in the 1990s.

74dde2c77980.title: Urban rewilding
74dde2c77980.sentence: Urban rewilding aims to integrate ecosystems into cities, blending nature and urban settings.

d725ea5faf6b.title: Urban rewilding
d725ea5faf6b.sentence: This nature can be anything from vegetation to animals.

52de205ac081.title: Urban rewilding
52de205ac081.sentence: There are four types of urban rewilding: urban greening, corridors, small scale, and large scale.

abea0874232b.title: Urban rewilding
abea0874232b.section: Different types of urban rewilding > Small scale
abea0874232b.sentence: A small-scale urban rewilding project is under 50 hectares and involves restoring distinct urban landscape elements within an ecosystem.

e4432bf8b076.title: Urban rewilding
e4432bf8b076.section: Different types of urban rewilding > Large scale
e4432bf8b076.sentence: Urban rewilding projects are large scale when they are over 50 hectares and restore large areas to support healthy, self-sustaining habitats and wildlife.

7f484ab7b9e3.title: Urban rewilding
7f484ab7b9e3.section: Different types of urban rewilding > Corridors
7f484ab7b9e3.sentence: In the context of urban rewilding, corridors connect habitats so that animals in cities can freely move throughout the urban environment.

58e36682a47c.title: Urban rewilding
58e36682a47c.section: Different types of urban rewilding > Corridors
58e36682a47c.sentence: Restored bodies of water or green pathways are examples of corridors.

96afacbe6e96.title: Urban rewilding
96afacbe6e96.sentence: For example, greenery can help filter pollutants, creating cleaner air.

39464c552778.title: Urban rewilding
39464c552778.sentence: Furthermore, urban rewilding projects have been found to lower carbon amounts, helping to fight climate change.

b57d702f5014.title: Urban rewilding
b57d702f5014.sentence: Urban Rewilding leads to higher levels of pollination, soil fertility, and clean water.

f6c5e27b5f50.title: Urban rewilding
f6c5e27b5f50.sentence: Alongside the physical benefits of providing cleaner air, urban rewilding also leads to decreased stress and an overall boost to mental health.

65147a25913a.title: Urban rewilding
65147a25913a.sentence: The combination of initial investments and long-term funding required makes urban rewilding projects expensive.

3ef090b34815.title: Urban rewilding
3ef090b34815.sentence: Furthermore, using land for urban rewilding projects has an opportunity cost.

a645b6b9948a.title: Urban rewilding
a645b6b9948a.sentence: Property owners could utilize the land used in urban rewilding projects for a different purpose that is more economically beneficial.

67c90d86b0d9.title: Biophilic design
67c90d86b0d9.sentence: Timothy Beatley believes the key objective of biophilic cities is to create an environment where the residents want to actively participate in, preserve, and connect with the natural landscape that surrounds them.

00daebfb90ab.title: Biophilic design
00daebfb90ab.sentence: He established ways to achieve this through a framework of infrastructure, governance, knowledge, and behavior; these dimensions can also be indicators of existing biophilic attributes that already exist in current cities.

7ad2b02abc5c.title: Biophilic design
7ad2b02abc5c.sentence: - Biophilic Conditions and Infrastructure: The idea that a certain number of people at any given time should be near a green space or park.

f3b0edfe5308.title: Biophilic design
f3b0edfe5308.sentence: On the urban scale, Timothy Beatley believes that biophilic design will allow cities to better adapt to stresses that occur from changes in climate and thus, local environments.

5249fd766441.title: Biophilic design
5249fd766441.section: City-scale examples of application > Singapore, Singapore
5249fd766441.sentence: Nicknamed a "city in a garden", Singapore has dedicated many resources to make a system of nature preserves, parks and connectors (ex.

fb34977b76d6.title: Biophilic design
fb34977b76d6.section: City-scale examples of application > Singapore, Singapore
fb34977b76d6.sentence: Southern Ridges), and tree-lined streets that promote the return of wildlife and reduce the heat island effect that is often seen in dense city centers; local governments agree with Kellert and Beatley that daily doses of nature enhance the wellbeing of its citizens.

3f35783a52e5.title: Pocket forest
3f35783a52e5.sentence: A pocket forest is created by planting various native trees and shrubs in close proximity, generally as a means of rapidly restoring native plant species in damaged ecosystems.

0327a520b6c3.title: Pocket forest
0327a520b6c3.sentence: While forests naturally grow through a primary stage and then a secondary stage before reaching their climax stage, pocket forests are created by a dense planting of climax stage species which grow rapidly in competition for sunlight.

4e7f819ade1b.title: Pocket forest
4e7f819ade1b.sentence: The growing interest in pocket forests was inspired in large part by the work of Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki, whose "Miyawaki forests" have influenced the development of a variety of pocket forest methodologies adapted to different climates and spatial constraints.

de7c35ff63ed.title: Pocket forest
de7c35ff63ed.sentence: Forestry scholars have noted that in the 2020s unsubstantiated claims of Miyawaki forest growing ten times as fast as other reforestation techniques have become common in social media and websites.

bcbd15fc4888.title: Pocket forest
bcbd15fc4888.sentence: The Miyawaki forest method is regarded as high-cost being particularly cost-inefficient in Mediterranean climate areas where maintenance require expensive water resources and some plants may suffer from photoinhibition.

ec61a2eaa91e.title: Pocket forest
ec61a2eaa91e.sentence: The Miyawaki technique is regarded as unfeasible for large areas.

48f85b6551ca.title: Pocket forest
48f85b6551ca.sentence: The dense pocket forest forms a capture mechanism for wind-blown embers, dried ground litter is an ignition source, and the multi-layered pocket forest forms a fuel ladder with wildfire risks in urban areas.

e08b32881fbf.title: Green urbanism
e08b32881fbf.sentence: Green urbanism has been defined as the practice of creating communities beneficial to both humans and the environment.

dad9a1df37b7.title: Green urbanism
dad9a1df37b7.sentence: According to Timothy Beatley, it is an attempt to shape more sustainable places, communities and lifestyles, and consume less of the world's resources.

566482001765.title: Green urbanism
566482001765.sentence: All of these principles are based on the understanding that urbanization is a key driver of carbon emissions, resource depletion and environmental degradation.

4073d0821b2b.title: Green urbanism
4073d0821b2b.sentence: These are zero fossil-fuel energy use, zero waste and zero emissions especially aimed for low-to-no-carbon emissions.

53435b9947d6.title: Green urbanism
53435b9947d6.sentence: In 1989, American ecologist H.T. Odum called cities ‘parasites’ living off the resources of natural and domesticated environments; a city makes no food, cleans no air and cleans only a small amount of water for reuse it only consumes.

9acb848f55e5.title: Green urbanism
9acb848f55e5.sentence: Green urbanism is interdisciplinary, combining the collaboration of landscape architects, engineers, urban planners, ecologists, transport planners, physicists, psychologists, sociologists, economists and other specialists in addition to architects and urban designers.

799222d38d5e.title: Reforestation
799222d38d5e.sentence: Reforestation is the practice of restoring previously existing forests and woodlands that have been destroyed or damaged.

6c9e58791342.title: Reforestation
6c9e58791342.sentence: The prior forest destruction might have happened through deforestation, clearcutting or wildfires.

ff1b2e8bb8bb.title: Reforestation
ff1b2e8bb8bb.sentence: Three important purposes of reforestation programs are for harvesting of wood, for climate change mitigation, and for ecosystem and habitat restoration purposes.

064c66fddb26.title: Reforestation
064c66fddb26.sentence: Afforestation on the other hand means establishing new forest on lands that were not forest before (for example, abandoned agriculture).

9de4f6336c1b.title: Reforestation
9de4f6336c1b.sentence: First, by increasing the volume of existing forest.

8b2f307c2d53.title: Reforestation
8b2f307c2d53.sentence: Second, by increasing the carbon density of existing forests at a stand and landscape scale.

1dd35e664b55.title: Reforestation
1dd35e664b55.sentence: Third, by expanding the use of forest products that will sustainably replace fossil-fuel emissions.

947e7abfd61f.title: Reforestation
947e7abfd61f.sentence: Fourth, by reducing carbon emissions that are caused from deforestation and degradation.

c69b5bb1b5ad.title: Reforestation
c69b5bb1b5ad.sentence: It takes much longer − several decades − for the carbon sequestration benefits of reforestation to become similar to those from mature trees in tropical forests.

885e1440670f.title: Reforestation
885e1440670f.sentence: Therefore, reducing deforestation is usually more beneficial for climate change mitigation than is reforestation.

74928246f8a9.title: Reforestation
74928246f8a9.section: Methods > Forest plantations > Using existing trees and roots
74928246f8a9.sentence: Planting new trees often leads to up to 90% of seedlings failing.

d54e3ef7a5ff.title: Reforestation
d54e3ef7a5ff.sentence: Trees used in some reforesting efforts (for example, Eucalyptus globulus) tend to extract large amounts of moisture from the soil, preventing the growth of other plants.

8cd84b2dd1c0.title: Reforestation
8cd84b2dd1c0.sentence: For example, in China, the Three Northern Protected Forest Development Program – informally known as the "Great Green Wall" – was launched in 1978 and scheduled to last until 2050.

996cf2f681af.title: Reforestation
996cf2f681af.sentence: Such programs often blur the boundaries between reforestation and afforestation (the latter being the establishment of a forest in an area where there was no forest before).

63c5acf35f79.title: Afforestation
63c5acf35f79.sentence: Afforestation is the establishment of a forest or stand of trees in an area where there was no recent tree cover.

2ca6690a63cf.title: Afforestation
2ca6690a63cf.sentence: The same definition in other words states that afforestation is "conversion to forest of land that historically has not contained forests".

718756e5da09.title: Afforestation
718756e5da09.sentence: In comparison, reforestation means the "conversion to forest of land that has previously contained forests but that has been converted to some other use".

5b5a89ebf702.title: Afforestation
5b5a89ebf702.sentence: There are three types of afforestation: natural regeneration, agroforestry and tree plantations.

8929c403a3a5.title: Afforestation
8929c403a3a5.sentence: In the context of climate change, afforestation can be helpful for climate change mitigation through the route of carbon sequestration.

bf4cb3aa9876.title: Afforestation
bf4cb3aa9876.sentence: Afforestation can also improve the local climate through increased rainfall and by being a barrier against high winds.

00289ccb8355.title: Afforestation
00289ccb8355.sentence: The additional trees can also prevent or reduce topsoil erosion (from water and wind), floods and landslides.

375ba08ad67b.title: Afforestation
375ba08ad67b.sentence: Afforestation projects create employment opportunities, particularly in rural areas, thus promoting sustainable livelihoods.

d8c5eb9c4d2a.title: Afforestation
d8c5eb9c4d2a.sentence: Finally, additional trees can be a habitat for wildlife, and provide employment and wood products.

eb1617149cca.title: Afforestation
eb1617149cca.sentence: The process of afforestation begins with site selection.

2591d4e96ea7.title: Afforestation
2591d4e96ea7.sentence: Several environmental factors of the site must be analyzed, including climate, soil, vegetation, and human activity.

33b8bd552270.title: Afforestation
33b8bd552270.sentence: These factors will determine the quality of the site, what species of trees should be planted, and what planting method should be used.

42ea4ec518ff.title: Afforestation
42ea4ec518ff.sentence: However, there has been debate about whether afforestation is beneficial for the sustainable use of natural resources, with some researchers pointing out that tree planting is not the only way to enhance climate mitigation and CO2 capture.

4d563be3b65f.title: Afforestation
4d563be3b65f.sentence: Australia, Canada, China, India, Israel, United States and Europe have afforestation programs to increase carbon dioxide removal in forests and in some cases to reduce desertification.

1e1c9859ee62.title: Ecological restoration
1e1c9859ee62.sentence: Ecological restoration, or ecosystem restoration, is the process of assisting the recovery of an ecosystem that has been degraded, damaged, destroyed or transformed.

886498f8cdda.title: Ecological restoration
886498f8cdda.sentence: It is distinct from conservation in that it attempts to retroactively repair already damaged ecosystems rather than take preventative measures.

27f7ed324d2e.title: Ecological restoration
27f7ed324d2e.sentence: Ecological restoration can help to reverse biodiversity loss, combat climate change, support the provision of ecosystem services and support local economies.

e0601c1d6e13.title: Ecological restoration
e0601c1d6e13.sentence: Ecological restoration includes a wide diversity of methods including erosion control, reforestation, removal of non-native species and weeds, revegetation of disturbed areas, daylighting streams, the reintroduction of native species, habitat and range improvement for targeted species and establishing wildlife corridors.

4c95b488c36c.title: Ecological restoration
4c95b488c36c.sentence: The Society for Ecological Restoration defines restoration as "the process of assisting the recovery of an ecosystem that has been degraded, damaged, or destroyed." Restoration ecology is the academic study of the science of restoration, whereas ecological restoration is the implementation by practitioners.

4ae644d457b7.title: Ecological restoration
4ae644d457b7.sentence: The number and size of ecological restoration projects have increased exponentially in recent years, with hundreds of thousands of projects across the globe.

a59d7950741c.title: Ecological restoration
a59d7950741c.sentence: - Restoring natural capital such as drinkable water or wildlife populations

19bc0b9c108a.title: Ecological restoration
19bc0b9c108a.sentence: - Helping human communities and the ecosystems upon which they depend adapt to the impacts of climate change (through ecosystem-based adaptation)

1e74aa4b0c2f.title: Ecological restoration
1e74aa4b0c2f.sentence: - Mitigating climate change (e.g. through carbon sequestration)

6029ac0dcf20.title: Ecological restoration
6029ac0dcf20.sentence: Some view ecosystem restoration as impractical, partially because restorations often fall short of their goals.

851988685c91.title: Ecological restoration
851988685c91.sentence: High economic costs can also be perceived as a negative impact of the restoration process.

ccb263955393.title: Ecological restoration
ccb263955393.sentence: Public opinion is very important in the feasibility of a restoration; if the public believes that the costs of restoration outweigh the benefits they will not support it.

78139b7a4027.title: Ecological restoration
78139b7a4027.sentence: The United Nations has named 2021–2030 the Decade on Ecosystem Restoration.

34654364638a.title: Rewilding
34654364638a.sentence: Rewilding is a form of ecological restoration aimed at increasing biodiversity and restoring natural processes.

d0d614776569.title: Rewilding
d0d614776569.sentence: It differs from other forms of ecological restoration in that rewilding aspires to reduce human influence on ecosystems.

462fbff48faa.title: Rewilding
462fbff48faa.sentence: A key feature of rewilding is its focus on replacing human interventions with natural processes.

8d4e1e6f498e.title: Rewilding
8d4e1e6f498e.sentence: It is also distinct from other forms of restoration in that, while it places emphasis on recovering geographically specific sets of ecological interactions and functions that would have maintained ecosystems prior to human influence, rewilding is open to novel or emerging ecosystems which encompass new species and new interactions.

afe36f4c2a23.title: Rewilding
afe36f4c2a23.sentence: This mechanism of rewilding is a process of restoring natural processes by introducing or re-introducing large mammals to promote resilient, self-regulating, and self-sustaining ecosystems.

82ef03f17777.title: Rewilding
82ef03f17777.sentence: The term rewilding was coined by members of the grassroots network Earth First!, first appearing in print in 1990.

9cb74412e1b6.title: Rewilding
9cb74412e1b6.sentence: It was refined and grounded in a scientific context in a paper published in 1998 by conservation biologists Michael Soulé and Reed Noss.

30aa33d5eecf.title: Rewilding
30aa33d5eecf.sentence: Soulé and Noss envisaged rewilding as a conservation method based on the concept of 'cores, corridors, and carnivores'.

175010996b78.title: Rewilding
175010996b78.sentence: The key components of rewilding incorporate large core protected areas, keystone species, and ecological connectivity based on the theory that large predators play regulatory roles in ecosystems. '3Cs' rewilding therefore relied on protecting 'core' areas of wild land, linked together by 'corridors' allowing passage for 'carnivores' to move around the landscape and perform their functional role.

96c176265733.title: Rewilding
96c176265733.sentence: Rewilding can respond to both the causes and effects of climate change and has been posited as a 'natural climate solution'.

95a7c731242f.title: Rewilding
95a7c731242f.sentence: Rewilding's creation of new ecosystems and restoration of existing ones can contribute to climate change mitigation and adaptation through, inter alia, carbon capture and storage, altering the Earth's albedo, natural flood management, reduction of wildfire risk, new habitat creation, and enabling or facilitating the movement of species to new, climate safe habitats, thus protecting biodiversity and maintaining functioning, climate resilient ecosystems.

52eac1ffbdca.title: Rewilding
52eac1ffbdca.sentence: A study in a tropical forest in Guyana found that an increase in mammal species from 5 to 35 increased tree and soil carbon storage by four to five times, compared to an increase of 3.5 to four times with an increase of tree species from 10 to 70.

64fa40377334.title: Rewilding
64fa40377334.sentence: While rewilding initiatives can be controversial, the United Nations has listed rewilding as one of several methods needed to achieve massive scale restoration of natural ecosystems, which they say must be accomplished by 2030 as part of the 30x30 campaign.

6c20b4668d43.title: Reforestation
6c20b4668d43.sentence: Policies that promote reforestation for incentives in return have shown promising results of being an effective and motivative concept to re-plant globally on a mass scale.

dd0aededa69e.title: Reforestation
dd0aededa69e.sentence: Some incentives for reforestation can be as simple as a financial compensation.

99a66c919b95.title: Reforestation
99a66c919b95.sentence: A compensated reduction of deforestation approach has been proposed which would reward developing countries that disrupt any further act of deforestation: Countries that participate and take the option to reduce their emissions from deforestation during a committed period of time would receive financial compensation for the carbon dioxide emissions that they avoided.

3a8d57131968.title: Reforestation
3a8d57131968.sentence: This whole process of cutting emissions would be voluntary, but once the country has agreed to lower their emissions they would be obligated to reduce their emissions.

59787c766147.title: Reforestation
59787c766147.sentence: However, if a country was not able to meet their obligation, their target would get added to their next commitment period.

378e4e07c55b.title: Reforestation
378e4e07c55b.sentence: Another emerging revenue source to fund reforestation projects deals with the sale of carbon sequestration credits, which can be sold to companies and individuals looking to compensate their carbon footprint.

7293e54fdf1a.title: Reforestation
7293e54fdf1a.sentence: This approach allows for private landowners and farmers to gain a revenue from the reforestation of their lands, while simultaneously benefiting from improved soil health and increased productivity.

1964c43a1d76.title: Reforestation
1964c43a1d76.sentence: Alongside past financial incentive strategies, reforestation tax benefits have been another way the government has encouraged companies to promote reforestation tactics through the promises of a tax break.

7788caa70ef4.title: Reforestation
7788caa70ef4.sentence: Plantation forests are intensively managed, composed of one or two species, even-aged, planted with regular spacing, and established mainly for productive purposes.

de92b5e910a4.title: Reforestation
de92b5e910a4.sentence: Plantation forests cover about 131 million ha, which is 3 percent of the global forest area and 45 percent of the total area of planted forests.

0ef7c87074ae.title: Reforestation
0ef7c87074ae.sentence: Globally, planted forests increased from 4.1% to 7.0% of the total forest area between 1990 and 2015.

d123f37ff722.title: Reforestation
d123f37ff722.sentence: Other planted forests, which comprise 55 percent of all planted forests, are not intensively managed, and they may resemble natural forests at stand maturity.

e9eca5d98cf6.title: Reforestation
e9eca5d98cf6.sentence: The purposes of other planted forests may include ecosystem restoration and the protection of soil and water values.

3ccc24d5aa7a.title: Reforestation
3ccc24d5aa7a.sentence: Over 90% of the world's forests regenerate organically, and more than half are covered by forest management plans or equivalents.

8c54b7fc7d96.title: Reforestation
8c54b7fc7d96.sentence: Of the planted forests worldwide, 18% of that area consists of exotic or introduced species while the rest consist of species native to the country where they are planted.

276e7ecb5ae0.title: Reforestation
276e7ecb5ae0.sentence: Secondly, tree plantations are often monocultures which comes with a set of disadvantages, for example biodiversity loss.

3155435e6dca.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
3155435e6dca.sentence: The United Nations Decade on Ecosystem Restoration runs from 2021 to 2030.

af3312016f63.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
af3312016f63.sentence: It is intended to facilitate global cooperation for the restoration of degraded and destroyed ecosystems, and to foster efforts to combat climate change, safeguard biodiversity, promote food security, and secure water supply.

14d6925af9db.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
14d6925af9db.sentence: The United Nations Decade on Ecosystem Restoration began on World Environment Day, 5 June 2021.

d8f84b8c78e2.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
d8f84b8c78e2.sentence: On 1 March 2019, the UN General Assembly officially adopted the resolution declaring 2021–2030 the UN Decade of Ecosystem Restoration.

bc974de48812.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
bc974de48812.sentence: During the Bonn Challenge 3.0 high-level meeting in March 2018, El Salvador announced plans to propose a United Nations Decade on Ecosystem Restoration 2021–2030, aimed at boosting existing efforts to restore degraded ecosystems.

eed34390f491.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
eed34390f491.sentence: In a June 2021 report to help launch the decade, the UN called for nations to deliver on existing ecosystem restoration commitments, which in total add up to over 1 billion hectares, an area bigger than China.

ca490f2fd039.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
ca490f2fd039.sentence: About half the world's GDP is directly dependent on nature, yet mankind is depleting natural resources at about 1.6 times the rate at which nature can restore them.

f131ccb492e5.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
f131ccb492e5.sentence: The UN define ecosystem restoration as "the process of halting and reversing degradation, resulting in improved ecosystem services and recovered biodiversity".

4e79fbd35aa7.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
4e79fbd35aa7.sentence: The UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration is co-led by two UN agencies – the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).

96340cea5833.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
96340cea5833.sentence: Approaches they recommend include regenerative agriculture, ecological restoration and rewilding.

127774bf6ab4.title: Ecological restoration
127774bf6ab4.section: Challenges > Restoration as a substitute for steep emission reductions
127774bf6ab4.sentence: It risks "over-relying on land for mitigation at the expense of phasing out fossil fuels".

c5ee75aac8d1.title: Ecological restoration
c5ee75aac8d1.section: Challenges > Restoration as a substitute for steep emission reductions
c5ee75aac8d1.sentence: Climate benefits from nature restoration are "dwarfed by the scale of ongoing fossil fuel emissions".

6ca797b8bbf0.title: Ecological restoration
6ca797b8bbf0.section: Challenges > Restoration as a substitute for steep emission reductions
6ca797b8bbf0.sentence: Despite these issues, nature restoration is receiving increasing attention, with a study concluding that "Land restoration is an important option for tackling climate change but cannot compensate for delays in reducing fossil fuel emissions" as it is "unlikely to be done quickly enough to notably reduce the global peak temperatures expected in the next few decades".

f5bb93ad3e96.title: Ecological restoration
f5bb93ad3e96.section: Challenges > Restoration as a substitute for steep emission reductions
f5bb93ad3e96.sentence: Researchers have found that, in terms of environmental services, it is better to avoid deforestation than to allow for deforestation to subsequently reforest, as the former leads to irreversible effects in terms of biodiversity loss and soil degradation.

e2e9ba22cb2e.title: Ecological restoration
e2e9ba22cb2e.sentence: Forestry-based carbon offsetting is controversial and sometimes critiqued as carbon colonialism.

38924506b882.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
38924506b882.sentence: The Great Green Wall or Great Green Wall for the Sahara and the Sahel (French: Grande Muraille Verte pour le Sahara et le Sahel; Arabic: السور الأخضر العظيم, romanized: as-Sūr al-ʾAkhḍar al-ʿAẓīm) is a project adopted by the African Union in 2007, initially conceived as a way to combat desertification in the Sahel region and hold back expansion of the Sahara Desert, by planting a wall of trees stretching across the entire Sahel from Djibouti City, Djibouti, to Dakar, Senegal.

b84586aca331.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
b84586aca331.sentence: The original dimensions of the "wall" were to be 15 km (9 mi) wide and 7,775 km (4,831 mi) long, but the program expanded to encompass nations in both northern and western Africa.

6930cc371da9.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
6930cc371da9.sentence: The concept evolved into promoting water harvesting techniques, greenery protection and improving indigenous land use techniques, aimed at creating a mosaic of green and productive landscapes across North Africa.

ecc560074065.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
ecc560074065.sentence: Originally a tree planting initiative, the project evolved into a development programming tool.

4032cccb380e.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
4032cccb380e.sentence: The ongoing goal of the project is to restore 100 million hectares (250 million acres) of degraded land, capture 250 million tonnes of carbon dioxide, and create 10 million jobs in the process, all by 2030.

fbbac7a6d75b.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
fbbac7a6d75b.sentence: On the occasion of the fifteenth anniversary of the launch of the program, a report was commissioned by the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) and published on September 7, 2020.

d79dccd2bfb1.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
d79dccd2bfb1.sentence: It was reported that the Great Green Wall had only covered 4% of the planned area, with only 4 million hectares (9.8 million acres) planted.

7f7187ec3c0e.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
7f7187ec3c0e.sentence: In January 2021, the project received a boost at the One Planet Summit, where its partners pledged USD 14.3 billion to launch the Great Green Wall Accelerator, aimed at facilitating the collaboration and coordination among donors and involved stakeholders across 11 countries.

5429c5f8843e.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
5429c5f8843e.sentence: As of March 2023, $2.5 billion of that pledge had been disbursed.

027ae82e42f2.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
027ae82e42f2.sentence: As of 2024, about 30 million hectares had been restored, completing 30% of the target.

c0a75e23e00b.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
c0a75e23e00b.sentence: As of 2023, the Great Green Wall was reported as "facing the risk of collapse" due to terrorist threats, absence of political leadership, and insufficient funding.

826a56dbf67a.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
826a56dbf67a.sentence: The Great Green Wall program has received criticism for having colonial origins, specifically relating to the use of the term 'desertification', which stems from French colonial influence.

1ebcdcf9a5f0.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
1ebcdcf9a5f0.sentence: It has also been criticised for receiving predominantly European funding, which can be seen as a form of neocolonialism.

c08ed1b9f853.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
c08ed1b9f853.sentence: The African Union endorsed it in 2007 as the Great Green Wall for the Sahara and the Sahel Initiative (GGWSSI).

597e3beef8bf.title: Drylands
597e3beef8bf.section: Dryland restoration > Case Studies > The Great Green Wall
597e3beef8bf.sentence: As of 2022, over 56 000 ha of degraded lands have been restored with almost 90 000 people involved.

9db9e05fa02b.title: Species reintroduction
9db9e05fa02b.sentence: Species reintroduction is the deliberate release of a species into the wild, from captivity or other areas where the organism is capable of survival.

1e10149019f6.title: Species reintroduction
1e10149019f6.sentence: The goal of species reintroduction is to establish a healthy, genetically diverse, self-sustaining population to an area where it has been extirpated, or to augment an existing population.

2219e11273e6.title: Species reintroduction
2219e11273e6.sentence: Species that may be eligible for reintroduction are typically threatened or endangered in the wild.

cc0bdea226ca.title: Species reintroduction
cc0bdea226ca.sentence: However, reintroduction of a species can also be for pest control; for example, wolves being reintroduced to a wild area to curb an overpopulation of deer.

d313b6c2307b.title: Species reintroduction
d313b6c2307b.sentence: The first matter to address when beginning a species reintroduction is whether to source individuals in situ, from wild populations, or ex situ, from captivity in a zoo or botanic garden, for example.

998b3e9d6c52.title: Species reintroduction
998b3e9d6c52.section: Methods for sourcing individuals > In situ sourcing
998b3e9d6c52.sentence: Ideally, populations should be sourced in situ when possible due to the numerous risks associated with reintroducing organisms from captive populations to the wild.

840d22c97295.title: Species reintroduction
840d22c97295.section: Methods for sourcing individuals > In situ sourcing
840d22c97295.sentence: To ensure that reintroduced populations have the best chance of surviving and reproducing, individuals should be sourced from populations that genetically and ecologically resemble the recipient population.

94d71567023c.title: Species reintroduction
94d71567023c.section: Methods for sourcing individuals > In situ sourcing
94d71567023c.sentence: Generally, sourcing from populations with similar environmental conditions to the reintroduction site will maximize the chance that reintroduced individuals are well adapted to the habitat of the reintroduction site otherwise there are possibilities that they will not take to their environment..

84b30278cab1.title: Species reintroduction
84b30278cab1.sentence: Consequently, animals adapted to captivity show reduced stress tolerance, increased tameness, and loss of local adaptations.

80983de08a64.title: Species reintroduction
80983de08a64.sentence: If the species slated for reintroduction is rare in the wild, it is likely to have unusually low population numbers, and care should be taken to avoid inbreeding and inbreeding depression.

1ceff0d5f299.title: Species reintroduction
1ceff0d5f299.sentence: Inbreeding can change the frequency of allele distribution in a population, and potentially result in a change to crucial genetic diversity.

334062430a6a.title: Species reintroduction
334062430a6a.sentence: No strict and accepted definition of reintroduction success exists, but it has been proposed that the criteria widely used to assess the conservation status of endangered taxa, such as the IUCN Red List criteria, should be used to assess reintroduction success.

20291316d0cc.title: Species reintroduction
20291316d0cc.sentence: Successful reintroduction programs should yield viable and self-sustainable populations in the long-term.

4c3e8d0e04d0.title: Novel ecosystem
4c3e8d0e04d0.sentence: Novel or emergent ecosystems emerge when human activities, land use, and anthropogenic climate change push ecological assemblages to morph outside of historical configurations, creating systems with no precedent in the ecological record.

e825ff048177.title: Novel ecosystem
e825ff048177.sentence: Novel ecosystems exist in urban, suburban, rural, and even wilderness areas that have been altered in structure and function by human agency, but a self-sustaining ecosystem is allowed to establish itself in the absence of ongoing human management.

6cbffbeb13ec.title: Novel ecosystem
6cbffbeb13ec.section: Definition > Origin and development of the term
6cbffbeb13ec.sentence: The term "novel ecosystem" was first used in 2006 to describe 1.) recent or future anthropogenic changes characterized by new species combinations that have the potential to change ecosystem function and 2.) ecosystems resulting from either deliberate or inadvertent human actions that do not require maintenance to persist.

430f8c398ef8.title: Novel ecosystem
430f8c398ef8.section: Definition > Origin and development of the term
430f8c398ef8.sentence: - That the ecosystem components (abiotic, biotic, and social) have been altered beyond a certain threshold, which is subjectively defined by location, not broadly.

a9289dd58bb7.title: Novel ecosystem
a9289dd58bb7.section: Definition > Origin and development of the term
a9289dd58bb7.sentence: - The alteration was caused by human actions, whether direct or indirect.

732a939a92fb.title: Novel ecosystem
732a939a92fb.section: Definition > Origin and development of the term
732a939a92fb.sentence: - The ecosystem is self-sustaining or continues to develop novel properties after the anthropogenic disruption occurred.

80a747700209.title: Novel ecosystem
80a747700209.section: Definition > Origin and development of the term
80a747700209.sentence: One analysis of novel ecosystem spread indicated that, unless rapid climate change mitigation tactics were taken, the coverage of novel ecosystems could include more than 50% of Earth's land surface by the year 2100, and 80% by the year 2300.

a4ca0121899c.title: Novel ecosystem
a4ca0121899c.sentence: - A decommissioned quarry that has been colonized by ruderal species

74aeb20115d0.title: Novel ecosystem
74aeb20115d0.sentence: - Algal dominated coral reefs caused by pollution, ocean acidification, and climate warming

3ecb320495cc.title: Ecological restoration
3ecb320495cc.sentence: It can be difficult to set restoration goals because, as Anthony Bradshaw writes, "ecosystems are not static, but in a state of dynamic equilibrium." Some scientists argue that, though an ecosystem may not be returned to its original state, the functions of a "novel ecosystem" are still valuable.

ecd41dc2fba8.title: Land restoration
ecd41dc2fba8.sentence: Land restoration, which may include renaturalisation or rewilding, is the process of restoring land to a different or previous state with an intended purpose.

f8e29f79a74a.title: Land restoration
f8e29f79a74a.sentence: That purpose can be a variety of things such as what follows: being safe for humans, plants, and animals; stabilizing ecological communities; cleaning up pollution; creating novel ecosystems; or restoring the land to a historical condition, for example how indigenous people managed the land.

f0203c91459d.title: Land restoration
f0203c91459d.sentence: Ecological destruction or degradation, to which land restoration serves as an antidote, is usually the consequence of human influence's intended or unintended consequences.

069eaaac5fa0.title: Land restoration
069eaaac5fa0.sentence: This can include pollution, deforestation, salination, or species endangerment, among many more.

1379d5aff874.title: Land restoration
1379d5aff874.sentence: Land restoration is not the same as land reclamation, where existing ecosystems are altered or destroyed to give way for cultivation or construction.

1067c8322f4c.title: Land restoration
1067c8322f4c.sentence: Land restoration can enhance the supply of valuable ecosystem services that benefit people.

c20193be8aa9.title: Land restoration
c20193be8aa9.sentence: Additionally, in order to monitor the success of a restoration project, a reference model or reference ecosystem should be selected in order to make comparisons.

e17832f7467a.title: Land restoration
e17832f7467a.sentence: Along with this, proper surveys of existing conditions should take place.

d1f9e5b505db.title: Land restoration
d1f9e5b505db.sentence: Using traditional ecological knowledge alongside Western ecological knowledge is becoming the more mainstream approach to landscape restoration, as many landscapes have evolved alongside humans over thousands of years, and because often times the ideal landscape used as the reference ecosystem is the pre-colonial ecological landscape.

21b892eea099.title: Land rehabilitation
21b892eea099.sentence: Land rehabilitation as a part of environmental remediation is the process of returning the land in a given area to some degree of its former state, after some process (industry, natural disasters, etc.) has resulted in its damage.

236f803864fc.title: Land rehabilitation
236f803864fc.sentence: Many projects and developments will result in the land becoming degraded, for example mining, farming and forestry.

c8a1a5d0cec7.title: Land rehabilitation
c8a1a5d0cec7.sentence: In some jurisdictions, including parts of the United States, the term "reclamation" can refer to land rehabilitation, as in returning disturbed lands to an improved state, instead of the land fill of water bodies.

bb7bc0bef899.title: Land rehabilitation
bb7bc0bef899.sentence: - Waste dumps are contoured to flatten them out, to further stabilize them against erosion.

f8d2ee819a30.title: Land rehabilitation
f8d2ee819a30.sentence: - Landfills are covered with topsoil, and vegetation is planted to help consolidate the material.

8576072410ac.title: Land rehabilitation
8576072410ac.sentence: - If the ore contains sulfides it is usually covered with a layer of clay to prevent access of rain and oxygen from the air, which can oxidize the sulfides to produce sulfuric acid.

5a748884355b.title: Land rehabilitation
5a748884355b.sentence: Also possible is that the section of the mine that is below ground, is kept and used to provide heating, water and/or methane.

2d7a598f823d.title: Land rehabilitation
2d7a598f823d.sentence: An added advantage of recovering the methane finally is that the methane does not come into the atmosphere, and so does not contribute to global warming.

4d8642413f38.title: Reforestation
4d8642413f38.section: Challenges > Competition with other land uses and displacement risk
4d8642413f38.sentence: Reforestation can compete with other land uses, such as food production, livestock grazing, and living space, for further economic growth.

b9b03509caca.title: Reforestation
b9b03509caca.section: Challenges > Competition with other land uses and displacement risk
b9b03509caca.sentence: Reforestation can also divert large amounts of water from other activities.

3054f06ca4c6.title: Reforestation
3054f06ca4c6.section: Challenges > Competition with other land uses and displacement risk
3054f06ca4c6.sentence: An assessment of the pledges of governments for reforestation found that the sum of global pledges translates to a required land area of 1.2bn hectares, until 2060, which is equal to a tenth of the global land area und thus deemed unrealistic without a significant encroachment on non-forest areas.

7c45c8f3e1d1.title: Reforestation
7c45c8f3e1d1.section: Challenges > Competition with other land uses and displacement risk
7c45c8f3e1d1.sentence: A study found that almost 300 million people live on tropical forest restoration opportunity land in the Global South, constituting a large share of low-income countries' populations, and argues for prioritized inclusion of "local communities" in forest restoration projects.

3d1f7ffdd0d7.title: Reforestation
3d1f7ffdd0d7.section: Challenges > Competition with other land uses and displacement risk
3d1f7ffdd0d7.sentence: Possible solutions include the integration of other land uses into forests through agroforestry, such as growing coffee plants under trees, reducing the delineation between forests and other land uses.

cdb1120dbf49.title: Reforestation
cdb1120dbf49.sentence: Some reforestation programs have attempted the idea of focusing more on carbon storage rather than the needs of nearby communities, and have been criticized for this.

fd0ff02214eb.title: Reforestation
fd0ff02214eb.sentence: There is also the risk that, through a forest fire or insect outbreak, much of the stored carbon in a reforested area could make its way back to the atmosphere.

6022d07f0dc2.title: Reforestation
6022d07f0dc2.sentence: Also, the possible harvesting and utilization of wood from reforested areas, limits the permanence of carbon sequestered through reforestation.

5703d3f2a3cb.title: Reforestation
5703d3f2a3cb.sentence: For example, it was found that nearly half of the pledges under the Bonn Challenge were areas earmarked for commercial wood use.

c445d83bbe2a.title: Reforestation
c445d83bbe2a.sentence: The global greenhouse gas emissions caused by damage to tropical rainforests may be underestimated by a factor of six.

9130c6fea790.title: REDD+
9130c6fea790.section: Outcomes and effectiveness > Common limitations and uncertainties
9130c6fea790.sentence: - Non-permanence (reversals): forest carbon gains may be reversed by fire, illegal logging or later land-use change; the Cancun safeguards call for actions to address reversal risk, and many standards use buffers and monitoring to manage reversals.

ffe5ce97d80e.title: Afforestation
ffe5ce97d80e.sentence: The canopy cover of mature trees could make the surface albedo darker, which causes more heat to be absorbed, potentially raising the temperature of the planet.

d026867fc3b5.title: Afforestation
d026867fc3b5.sentence: This is particularly relevant in parts of the world with high levels of snow cover, due to the significant difference in albedo between highly reflective white snow and darker forest cover which absorbs more solar radiation.

9ba414422eb0.title: Albedo
9ba414422eb0.section: Examples of terrestrial albedo effects > Trees
9ba414422eb0.sentence: For this reason, the greater heat absorption by trees could offset some of the carbon benefits of afforestation (or offset the negative climate impacts of deforestation).

bd6b4b9c0448.title: Albedo
bd6b4b9c0448.section: Examples of terrestrial albedo effects > Trees
bd6b4b9c0448.sentence: Research in 2023, drawing from 176 flux stations globally, revealed a climate trade-off: increased carbon uptake from afforestation results in reduced albedo.

aae29db87f75.title: Afforestation
aae29db87f75.sentence: By contrast, tropical reforestation projects lead to a positive change such as the formation of clouds.

de708c0b1216.title: Afforestation
de708c0b1216.sentence: These clouds then reflect the sunlight, lowering temperatures.

c613c1562391.title: Afforestation
c613c1562391.section: Criticism > Afforestation in grasslands and savanna
c613c1562391.sentence: Tree-planting campaigns are criticised for sometimes targeting areas where forests would not naturally occur, such as grassland and savanna biomes.

a56452773c57.title: Afforestation
a56452773c57.sentence: Afforestation critics argue that ecosystems without trees are not necessarily degraded, and many of them can store carbon as they are; for example, savannas and tundra store carbon underground.

f02a5e1e56b4.title: Afforestation
f02a5e1e56b4.section: Criticism > Afforestation in grasslands and savanna
f02a5e1e56b4.sentence: Carbon sequestration forecasts of afforestation programmes often insufficiently consider possible carbon reductions in soils as well as slowing tree growth over time.

cce819ed55be.title: Afforestation
cce819ed55be.sentence: Monocultures, often planted for commercial purposes or ease of management, lack the biodiversity of natural forests.

056e395091bb.title: Afforestation
056e395091bb.sentence: These single-species forests provide limited food sources, shelter, and nesting sites for a wide range of wildlife, and in purely coniferous forests low levels of light may reach the forest floor reducing habitat and variety of plant life.

b3f922597638.title: Afforestation
b3f922597638.sentence: A meta-analysis found that mixed species plantations would increase carbon storage alongside other benefits of diversifying planted forests.

6847e92e415f.title: Ecological restoration
6847e92e415f.sentence: Ecological succession is the process by which a community changes over time, especially following a disturbance.

c00b23990913.title: Ecological restoration
c00b23990913.sentence: In many instances, an ecosystem will change from a simple level of organization with a few dominant pioneer species to an increasingly complex community with many interdependent species.

f9b1bcdd4d03.title: Ecological restoration
f9b1bcdd4d03.sentence: Restoration often consists of initiating, assisting, or accelerating ecological successional processes, depending on the severity of the disturbance.

6e55a4450842.title: Ecological restoration
6e55a4450842.sentence: However, in a system that has experienced a more severe disturbance (such as in urban ecosystems), restoration may require intensive efforts to recreate environmental conditions that favor natural successional processes.

dbf20a586f67.title: Secondary forest
dbf20a586f67.sentence: A secondary forest (or second-growth forest) is a forest or woodland area which has regenerated through largely natural processes after human-caused disturbances, such as timber harvest or agriculture clearing, or equivalently disruptive natural phenomena.

88348658405c.title: Secondary forest
88348658405c.sentence: It is distinguished from an old-growth forest (primary or primeval forest), which has not recently undergone such disruption, and complex early seral forest, as well as third-growth forests that result from harvest in second growth forests.

d39f30499131.title: Secondary forest
d39f30499131.sentence: An area that has been cleared will first be colonized by pioneer species, followed by shrubs and bushes.

4ff549b85825.title: Secondary forest
4ff549b85825.sentence: Over time, trees that were characteristic of the original forest begin to dominate the forest again.

74d31647c291.title: Secondary forest
74d31647c291.sentence: It typically takes a secondary forest 40 to 100 years to begin to resemble the original old-growth forest; however, in some cases a secondary forest will not succeed, due to erosion or soil nutrient loss in certain tropical forests.

9cf4c18e2694.title: Secondary forest
9cf4c18e2694.sentence: Today, most of the forests of the United States – especially those in the eastern part of the country – as well as forests of Europe consist of secondary forest.

c5d3fbdf9966.title: Secondary forest
c5d3fbdf9966.sentence: Patterns of regeneration in secondary forests show that species richness can quickly recover to pre-disturbance levels via secondary succession; however, relative abundances and identities of species can take much longer to recover.

0e926621b088.title: Secondary forest
0e926621b088.sentence: Though not as effective as primary forests, secondary forests store more soil carbon than other land-uses, such as tree plantations.

4753a9da4fde.title: Secondary forest
4753a9da4fde.sentence: They protect the watershed from further erosion and provide habitat; secondary forests may also buffer edge effects around mature forest fragments and increase connectivity between them.

f5c6f6d7ad92.title: Secondary forest
f5c6f6d7ad92.sentence: Secondary forests may also be a source of wood and other forest products for rural communities.

5cc8d4ca0b58.title: Climate change mitigation
5cc8d4ca0b58.section: Preserving and enhancing carbon sinks > Forests > Afforestation, reforestation and preventing desertification
5cc8d4ca0b58.sentence: By some estimates, for every acre of original old-growth forest cut down, more than 50 acres of new secondary forests are growing.

effd69b89b6f.title: Forest restoration
effd69b89b6f.sentence: Forest restoration is defined as "actions to re-instate ecological processes, which accelerate recovery of forest structure, ecological functioning and biodiversity levels towards those typical of climax forest", i.e. the end-stage of natural forest succession.

cc9cf6039ade.title: Forest restoration
cc9cf6039ade.sentence: Climax forests are relatively stable ecosystems that have developed the maximum biomass, structural complexity and species diversity that are possible within the limits imposed by climate and soil and without continued disturbance from humans (more explanation here).

d455f9a977bf.title: Forest restoration
d455f9a977bf.sentence: Forest restoration is a specialized form of reforestation, but it differs from conventional tree plantations in that its primary goals are biodiversity recovery and environmental protection.

1f56c3666584.title: Forest restoration
1f56c3666584.sentence: Forest restoration may include simply protecting remnant vegetation (fire prevention, cattle exclusion etc.) or more active interventions to accelerate natural regeneration, as well as tree planting and/or sowing seeds (direct seeding) of species characteristic of the target ecosystem.

c03d35fb0a42.title: Forest restoration
c03d35fb0a42.sentence: Its ecological success is measured in terms of increased biological diversity, biomass, primary productivity, soil organic matter and water-holding capacity, as well as the return of rare and keystone species, characteristic of the target ecosystem.

2107779259aa.title: Forest restoration
2107779259aa.sentence: Economic indices of success include the value of forest products and ecological services generated (e.g. watershed protection, carbon storage etc.), which ultimately contribute towards poverty reduction.

19d7fd397708.title: Forest restoration
19d7fd397708.sentence: Payments for such ecological services (PES) and forest products can provide strong incentives for local people to implement restoration projects.

8c488193c865.title: Forest restoration
8c488193c865.sentence: Active restoration has been shown to accelerate the carbon recovery of human-modified tropical forests by as much as 50%.

9abbd6c0927f.title: Forest restoration
9abbd6c0927f.sentence: Since climate is a major factor that determines climax forest composition, global climate change may result in changing restoration aims.

7e7a4a5be88e.title: Forest restoration
7e7a4a5be88e.sentence: Forest landscape restoration (FLR) is defined as "a planned process to regain ecological integrity and enhance human well-being in deforested or degraded landscapes." It comprises tools and procedures to integrate site-level forest restoration actions with desirable landscape-level objectives, which are decided upon via various participatory mechanisms among stakeholders.

62bd26546d0d.title: Forest restoration
62bd26546d0d.sentence: The concept has grown out of collaboration among some of the world's major international conservation organizations including the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), the World Resources Institute and the International Tropical Timber Organization (ITTO).

7faedb412d7f.title: Forest restoration
7faedb412d7f.sentence: The concept of FLR was conceived to bring about compromises between meeting the needs of both humans and wildlife, by restoring a range of forest functions at the landscape level.

b326e2c64a3b.title: Forest restoration
b326e2c64a3b.sentence: The participation of local communities is central to the concept, because they play a critical role in shaping the landscape and gain significant benefits from restored forest resources.

895d551fd794.title: Forest restoration
895d551fd794.sentence: - Identification of the root causes of forest degradation and prevention of further deforestation,

0864552ab10f.title: Forest restoration
0864552ab10f.sentence: - Positive engagement of people in the planning of forest restoration, resolution of land-use conflicts and agreement on benefit-sharing systems,

585b3feeb72d.title: Forest restoration
585b3feeb72d.sentence: These may include protection and management of secondary and degraded primary forests, standard forest restoration techniques such as "assisted" or "accelerated" natural regeneration (ANR) and the planting of framework tree species to restore degraded areas, as well as conventional tree plantations and agroforestry systems to meet more immediate monetary needs.

4130d9e7bc5a.title: Forest restoration
4130d9e7bc5a.sentence: In 2014, the Food and Agricultural Organization of the United Nations established the Forest and Landscape Restoration Mechanism.

c63fc3d50136.title: Forest restoration
c63fc3d50136.sentence: The Mechanism supports countries to implement FLR as a contribution to achieving the Bonn Challenge—the restoration of 150 million hectare of deforested and degraded lands by 2020—and the Convention on Biological Diversity Aichi Biodiversity Targets—related to ecosystem conservation and restoration.

c053010bda76.title: Bonn Challenge
c053010bda76.sentence: The Bonn Challenge is a global effort to restore 150 million hectares of the world's degraded and deforested lands by 2020 and 350 million hectares by 2030.

d56182417749.title: Bonn Challenge
d56182417749.sentence: It was hosted and launched by Germany and the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) in Bonn on 2 September 2011, in collaboration with the Global Partnership on Forest/Landscape Restoration and targets delivery on the Rio Conventions and other outcomes of the 1992 Earth Summit.

a546c6a7f252.title: Bonn Challenge
a546c6a7f252.sentence: The IUCN estimates that fulfilling the goals of the Bonn challenge would create approximately $84 billion per year in net benefits that could positively affect income opportunities for rural communities.

8456f083938a.title: Bonn Challenge
8456f083938a.sentence: It is also estimated that a reduction of the current carbon dioxide emissions gap by 11-17% will be achieved by meeting the challenge.

a6515a5b45ac.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
a6515a5b45ac.sentence: Achieving the Bonn Challenge objective of restoring at least 350 million hectares of degraded landscapes by 2030 could realize up to $9 trillion in net benefits, and alleviate poverty in many rural communities.

3689672404d7.title: Reforestation
3689672404d7.sentence: Pakistan's Billion Tree Tsunami restored 350,000 hectares of forests and degraded land to surpass its Bonn Challenge commitment.

03a761ae3bdb.title: Assisted natural regeneration
03a761ae3bdb.sentence: Assisted natural regeneration (ANR) (also termed managed regrowth) is the human protection and preservation of natural tree seedlings in forested areas.

17a4e8fada00.title: Assisted natural regeneration
17a4e8fada00.sentence: It typically involves the reduction or removal of barriers to natural regeneration such as soil degradation, competition with weeds, grasses or other vegetation, and protection against disturbances, which can all interfere with growth.

ac2f86f34184.title: Assisted natural regeneration
ac2f86f34184.sentence: Seedlings are, in particular, protected from undergrowth and extremely flammable plants such as Imperata grass.

61e041a38ac0.title: Assisted natural regeneration
61e041a38ac0.sentence: In addition to protection efforts, new trees are planted when needed or wanted (enrichment planting).

3ef1d25b52b9.title: Assisted natural regeneration
3ef1d25b52b9.sentence: It also serves as a cheaper alternative to reforestation due to decreased nursery needs.

0c8df6ad030f.title: Assisted natural regeneration
0c8df6ad030f.sentence: This allows for a low-cost method that removes the expenses associated with site preparation and planting/raising seedlings themselves, which can be appealing in large-scale restoration projects.

a6a8793253d2.title: Assisted natural regeneration
a6a8793253d2.sentence: With ANR, forests grow faster than they would naturally, resulting in a significant contribution to carbon sequestration efforts.

a1ae67333afb.title: Assisted natural regeneration
a1ae67333afb.sentence: One involves a sufficient density of naturally regenerated seedlings, though the specific density required is dependent on specific factors, such as, distribution, species composition, growth rates, soil fertility, etc. A density range of 200 to 800 seedlings per hectare has been suggested to ensure optimal regeneration.

dd3b7cd4b91e.title: Assisted natural regeneration
dd3b7cd4b91e.sentence: The availability of seed sources from nearby remnant forests is necessary to serve as seed inputs for colonization of vegetation.

ef665cad2a49.title: Assisted natural regeneration
ef665cad2a49.sentence: The control or removal of all disturbances (such as, grazing, fires, and logging) is also crucial.

8e815354085a.title: Assisted natural regeneration
8e815354085a.sentence: ANR requires high maintenance and can be labor-intensive, and involve methods of weeding, grass pressing, establishing and maintaining firebreaks, etc. This can ultimately help to create jobs and improve livelihoods in local and/or impoverished communities.

3f1ee39253e5.title: Reforestation

3f1ee39253e5.sentence: While this method has existed for centuries, it is now sometimes referred to as farmer-managed natural regeneration or assisted natural regeneration.

0dbad5a11757.title: Reforestation
0dbad5a11757.section: Methods > Forest plantations > Using existing trees and roots
0dbad5a11757.sentence: Additionally, they are much more likely to survive as their root systems already exist and can tap into groundwater during harsher seasons with no rain.

ba96797fc6a8.title: Tree planting
ba96797fc6a8.sentence: A practical solution is to plant tough, fast-growing native tree species which begin rebuilding the land.

bedf1fbbe0db.title: Passive rewilding
bedf1fbbe0db.sentence: Passive rewilding refers to actively unmanaged environments that are allowed to regain natural dominance, typically after their abandonment.

bb3652e635d9.title: Passive rewilding
bb3652e635d9.sentence: A type of rewilding, passive rewilding aims to restore natural ecosystem processes via minimal or the total withdrawal of direct human management of the landscape.

d8cd0e7686ac.title: Passive rewilding
d8cd0e7686ac.sentence: Sometimes referred to as natural regeneration, spontaneous regeneration, and, informally, as nature's reclamation, it differs from other forms of rewilding in that direct human management or intervention is absent, whereby the environment is subsequently overgrown and occupied by natural elements on its own.

b6e348ceef5f.title: Passive rewilding
b6e348ceef5f.sentence: There are three important factors to passive rewilding; Reviving trophic complexity, or biodiversity, by allowing wildlife to return (such as by limiting hunting), though in other cases it may involve resettlement.

0affdb29825f.title: Passive rewilding
0affdb29825f.sentence: The second factor is allowing landscapes to rejoin, so in a way that plants and animals can travel around.

d1aa33b90fb0.title: Passive rewilding
d1aa33b90fb0.sentence: The third component is permitting erratic disturbances such as fires, pests and floods.

d569f1706810.title: Passive rewilding
d569f1706810.sentence: Land is abandoned to passive rewilding either purposely, or due to socio-economic change.

fa82c7bdcb07.title: Passive rewilding
fa82c7bdcb07.sentence: Forest recovery has been occurring in abandoned pastures, scrubby bush and forest margins throughout Europe and North America, since nature abhors an ecological vacuum and therefore hastily fills it.

4f73b1d62ad1.title: Passive rewilding
4f73b1d62ad1.sentence: This spontaneous forest establishment has several consequences for society and nature, such as increase of fire risk and frequency and biodiversity loss.

b92dd9b088de.title: Passive rewilding
b92dd9b088de.sentence: Regarding biodiversity loss, research findings from the Mediterranean basin showed that this is very site-dependent.

3cc935f00d68.title: Passive rewilding
3cc935f00d68.section: Regional examples > Central and Eastern Europe
3cc935f00d68.sentence: The Chernobyl Exclusion Zone has seen the return of previously extirpated indigenous species such as boars, lynxes, wolves, brown bears, and 200+ species of bird, in addition to a thriving herd of re-introduced Przewalski's horses, with streets and buildings being surrounded by overgrowth of vegetation.

7f0395d00e16.title: Passive rewilding
7f0395d00e16.sentence: In 1998, science fiction author Bruce Sterling coined the term involuntary park to describe previously inhabited areas that for environmental, economic, or political reasons have lost their value for technological functionalism and been allowed to return to an overgrown, feral state.

fcf7b9ad8305.sentence: The publication provides updated and expanded guidance on the practice of ecological restoration, clarifies the breadth of ecological restoration and allied environmental repair activities, and includes ideas and input from a diverse international group of restoration scientists and practitioners.

c5d20d08f7bf.title: Ecological restoration
c5d20d08f7bf.section: International Principles & Standards for the Practice of Ecological Restoration
c5d20d08f7bf.sentence: - Present a robust framework to guide restoration projects toward achieving intended goals.

20ab4f6b224d.sentence: The second edition builds on the first edition of the Standards, which was released December 12, 2016, at the Convention on Biological Diversity's 13th Conference of the Parties in Cancun, Mexico.

57370ec5abd5.title: Ecological restoration

57370ec5abd5.sentence: The Society for Ecological Restoration (SER) released the second edition of the International Standards for the Practice of Ecological Restoration on September 27, 2019, in Cape Town, South Africa, at SER's 8th World Conference on Ecological Restoration.
