32b9feed0ee3.sentence: - Provide a technical appendix on sourcing of seeds and other propagules for restoration.

4b027555b3ab.title: Ecological restoration
4b027555b3ab.section: Contrasting restoration ecology and conservation biology
4b027555b3ab.sentence: Both restoration ecologists and conservation biologists agree that protecting and restoring habitat is important for protecting biodiversity.

6912ae9ae132.title: Ecological restoration
6912ae9ae132.section: Contrasting restoration ecology and conservation biology
6912ae9ae132.sentence: Because of that, it is generally organized at the population genetic level and assesses specific species populations (i.e. endangered species).

662f5abc1c15.title: Ecological restoration
662f5abc1c15.section: Contrasting restoration ecology and conservation biology
662f5abc1c15.sentence: Restoration ecology is organized at the community level, which focuses on broader groups within ecosystems.

462cd202d711.title: Ecological restoration
462cd202d711.section: Contrasting restoration ecology and conservation biology
462cd202d711.sentence: In addition, conservation biology often concentrates on vertebrate and invertebrate animals because of their salience and popularity, whereas restoration ecology concentrates on plants.

8de9b6b4ed81.title: Ecological restoration
8de9b6b4ed81.section: Contrasting restoration ecology and conservation biology
8de9b6b4ed81.sentence: Restoration ecology focuses on plants because restoration projects typically begin by establishing plant communities.

d95ea5bb920b.title: Ecological restoration
d95ea5bb920b.section: Contrasting restoration ecology and conservation biology
d95ea5bb920b.sentence: Finally, restoration ecology has a stronger focus on soils, soil structure, fungi, and microorganisms because soils provide the foundation of functional terrestrial ecosystems.

a81191241a14.title: Ecological restoration
a81191241a14.sentence: Restoration ecology emerged as a separate field in ecology in the late twentieth century.

264a08efda0d.title: Ecological restoration
264a08efda0d.sentence: One of the struggles for both fields is a divide between restoration ecology and ecological restoration in practice.

4a0cbb936cbd.title: Ecological restoration
4a0cbb936cbd.sentence: In a 2009 survey of practitioners and scientists, the "science-practice gap" was listed as the second most commonly cited reason limiting the growth of both science and practice of restoration.

012b92e669f2.title: Ecological restoration
012b92e669f2.sentence: However, it has been well established that one of the main issues is that the questions studied by restoration ecologists are frequently not found useful or easily applicable by land managers.

0a7eb56e6c4c.title: Ecological restoration
0a7eb56e6c4c.sentence: Additionally many restoration ecology studies are carried out under controlled conditions and frequently at scales much smaller than actual restorations.

426536b7cce9.title: Ecological restoration
426536b7cce9.sentence: Many restoration projects are limited by time and money, so data collection and record-keeping are not always feasible.

d0cfc55f9259.title: Ecological restoration
d0cfc55f9259.sentence: However, this limits the ability of scientists to analyze restoration projects and give recommendations based on empirical data.

99939ee2c9ff.title: Ecological restoration
99939ee2c9ff.sentence: Traditional ecological knowledge (TEK) from Indigenous Peoples demonstrates how restoration ecology is a historical field, lived out by humans for thousands of years.

5a920d897262.title: Ecological restoration
5a920d897262.sentence: Indigenous people have acquired ecological knowledge through observation, experience, and management of the natural resources and the environment around them.

7aee8264b1ac.title: Ecological restoration
7aee8264b1ac.sentence: In the past, they managed their environment and changed the structure of the vegetation to not only meet their basic needs (food, water, shelter, medicines) but also to improve desired characteristics and even increasing the populations and biodiversity.

6db1bf5f84d9.title: Ecological restoration
6db1bf5f84d9.sentence: Restoration ecologists must consider that TEK is place dependent due to intimate connection and thus when engaging Indigenous Peoples to include knowledge for restoration purposes, respect and care must be taken to avoid appropriation of the TEK.

76d91e7a7c5f.title: Ecological restoration
76d91e7a7c5f.sentence: Successful ecological restoration which includes Indigenous Peoples must be led by Indigenous Peoples to ensure non-indigenous people acknowledge the unequal relationship of power.

794e942ee0f8.title: Ecological restoration
794e942ee0f8.sentence: For example, the California Indians have a rigid and complex harvesting, management and production practice, largely typical horticultural techniques and concentrated forest burning.

fa50c1bc7e73.title: Mine reclamation
fa50c1bc7e73.sentence: Mine reclamation is the process of modifying land that has been mined to restore it to an ecologically functional or economically usable state.

bf71ce47c824.title: Mine reclamation
bf71ce47c824.sentence: Although the process of mine reclamation occurs once mining is complete, the planning of mine reclamation activities may occur prior to a mine being permitted or started.

15dd72f5b831.title: Mine reclamation
15dd72f5b831.sentence: As a practice, mine reclamation began at the start of the 20th century.

cf28f35347f8.title: Mine reclamation
cf28f35347f8.sentence: Many abandoned mine sites have no reclamation works undertaken.

47b560938c61.title: Mine reclamation
47b560938c61.sentence: Returning the landscape to its original state is not possible in all cases.

e6f97ecbffbf.title: Mine reclamation
e6f97ecbffbf.sentence: In most cases the physical and chemical stabilization of mine waste is the limit of mine remediation.

6ab6ae3d6570.title: Mine reclamation
6ab6ae3d6570.sentence: In open cut mines rocky material is used for backfilling the excavation.

cab0f711e044.title: Mine reclamation
cab0f711e044.sentence: A layer of soil that was stored in the premining is placed on top of the rocky material.

24add453bbeb.title: Mine reclamation
24add453bbeb.sentence: On top of this layer is placed a layer of topsoil.

add5d6205389.title: Mine reclamation
add5d6205389.sentence: The final step is the restoration of vegetation and long-term development of plant succession.

32e45c407354.title: Mine reclamation
32e45c407354.sentence: Reforestation is a dominant way of post mining sites restoration.

a685c6bd0afb.title: Mine reclamation
a685c6bd0afb.section: United States > Under the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977
a685c6bd0afb.sentence: In addition to providing the reclamation plan, operators must also post a performance bond to ensure that monies will be available to complete the reclamation if the operator goes out of business prior to finishing the reclamation or is otherwise unable to complete the reclamation.

fd5f5b191ec4.title: Mine reclamation
fd5f5b191ec4.section: United States > Under the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977
fd5f5b191ec4.sentence: The amount of the bond must equal the amount of the proposed reclamation plan.

b433ada8e129.title: Mine reclamation
b433ada8e129.section: United States > Under the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977
b433ada8e129.sentence: The bond is not released to the operator until after the state or federal regulatory office has concluded that the reclamation is successful, which could be over 10 years after the reclamation process has been completed.

d79764ba01bc.title: Mine reclamation
d79764ba01bc.section: United States > Abandoned Mine Lands Program
d79764ba01bc.sentence: Mine operators must pay a tax of $0.12 per ton for underground mined coal and $0.28 per ton for surfaced mined coal; the proceeds from this tax are put into the Abandoned Mine Reclamation Fund (created by SMCRA) to pay for the reclamation of abandoned mines.

2297e441d5cc.title: Mine reclamation
2297e441d5cc.section: United States > Under the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977
2297e441d5cc.sentence: The Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 (SMCRA) is the primary federal law that regulates the environmental effects of coal mining in the United States.

Referring to the span of project types they stated, 'Rewilding now incorporates a variety of concepts, including Pleistocene megafauna replacement, taxon replacement, species reintroductions, retrobreeding, release of captive-bred animals, land abandonment, and spontaneous rewilding.'

ad5efe153790.title: Rewilding

9ba1bd1fd4a9.sentence: Pleistocene rewilding is the (re)introduction of extant Pleistocene megafauna, or the close ecological equivalents of extinct megafauna, to restore ecosystem function.

8c0b12369f27.sentence: Advocates of the approach maintain that ecosystems where species evolved in response to Pleistocene megafauna now lack large mammals, and they may be in danger of collapse.

e00458053b2d.sentence: Meanwhile critics argue that it is unrealistic to assume that ecological communities today are functionally similar to their state 10,000 years ago.

8752f4d6d665.sentence: Trophic rewilding is an ecological restoration strategy focused on restoring trophic interactions and complexity (specifically top-down and associated trophic cascades where a top consumer/predator controls the primary consumer population) through species (re)introductions, in order to promote self-regulating, biodiverse ecosystems.

9079d720666f.title: Forest restoration
9079d720666f.sentence: Nevertheless, in some specific cases, wild fires do actually allow to increase the biodiversity index of the burnt area, in which case the Forest Restoration Strategies tend to look for a different land-use.

58dffed01f81.title: Forest restoration
58dffed01f81.section: Natural regeneration > Protecting regeneration areas from browsing animals
58dffed01f81.sentence: Forest in the process of restoration face many challenges, such as seed and nutrient availability, but are notable susceptible to browsing animals.

5a12fae7cfaa.title: Forest restoration
5a12fae7cfaa.section: Natural regeneration > Protecting regeneration areas from browsing animals
5a12fae7cfaa.sentence: Although browsing animals are necessary in maintaining the understory of forests, they can easily over-graze a freshly replanted swath of forest, where young samplings are easily accessible.

ac09adfa70c4.title: Forest restoration
ac09adfa70c4.section: Natural regeneration > Protecting regeneration areas from browsing animals
ac09adfa70c4.sentence: Over-grazing is particularly problematic in this case as the samplings and other young plants may be damaged beyond the point of recovery, resulting in a decrease in biodiversity.

8ca024476bcd.title: Forest restoration
8ca024476bcd.section: Natural regeneration > Protecting regeneration areas from browsing animals
8ca024476bcd.sentence: Care must be taken to use "deer fencing" to protect the regeneration area, or where not financially possible, to plant trees which prioritize structural growth and recovery.

036b26a8d84c.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
036b26a8d84c.sentence: The benefits obtained from ecosystem generation on average exceed the costs of the initial investment tenfold, whereas the cost of inaction is at least three times the cost of ecosystem restoration.

9eb23fb60426.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
9eb23fb60426.sentence: The restoration of 350 million hectares of degraded terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems by 2030 could generate US$9 trillion in ecosystem services and remove 13 to 26 gigatons of greenhouse gases from the atmosphere.

5b3af9da58f6.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
5b3af9da58f6.sentence: Degradation of land and marine ecosystems adds to the threat of mass species extinction, and has a negative impact on the well-being of some 3.2 billion people, costing around 10% of the annual global gross domestic product (c. $6.3 trillion) in loss of species and ecosystem services.

9a41244c5bc9.title: Peatland restoration
9a41244c5bc9.sentence: A subsequent study found that if peatland restoration took place by 2027, it would provide £191 million of economic benefits annually for the country, net of restoration costs.

c79979dc210f.title: Restoration economy
c79979dc210f.sentence: Per million invested, 15-24 jobs were created, and each invested dollar generated an additional 1.4 to 2.4 dollars in economic activity as it cycled through the economy, depending on the specific type of project.

14e5df0872a3.title: Restoration economy
14e5df0872a3.sentence: The restoration economy is the economic activity associated with regenerative land use, such as ecological restoration activities.

fc7b2be96a57.title: Restoration economy
fc7b2be96a57.sentence: It stands in contrast to economic activity premised on sprawl, or on the extraction or depletion of natural resources.

bea22645217f.title: Restoration economy
bea22645217f.sentence: The term is meant to convey that activities meant to repair past damage to natural and human communities are often economically beneficial at local, regional, and national scales.

942b8981fb72.title: Restoration economy
942b8981fb72.sentence: The phrase gained popularity with the publication in 2002 of The Restoration Economy by Storm Cunningham.

9aa30096d098.title: Restoration economy
9aa30096d098.sentence: That book created an eight-sector taxonomy for "restorative development", with a chapter on each.

403fafce65e1.title: Restoration economy
403fafce65e1.sentence: The other four sectors primarily focused on the natural environment: ecological restoration, watershed restoration, fishery restoration and regenerative agriculture.

19a24b3e494f.title: Restoration economy
19a24b3e494f.sentence: While investments in restoration benefit the environment, restoration projects also require workers, materials, and services to implement.

deeffc065c2b.title: Restoration economy
deeffc065c2b.sentence: The marketplace for these goods and services can create employment, spur business and workforce development, and increase activity in local economies.

c8e1e6eec022.title: Restoration economy
c8e1e6eec022.sentence: A study that looked at investments in restoration projects through both federal agencies and nongovernmental organizations across the state of Oregon found that restoration investments have similar economic and employment impacts as other public infrastructure projects such as road building.

1dde387a31ff.title: Restoration economy
1dde387a31ff.sentence: In addition, labor-intensive activities (e.g. planting trees, thinning) tend to pay less than traditional logging jobs, be less reliable, and be dominated by immigrant workers.

bae3119928ea.title: Novel ecosystem
bae3119928ea.section: Novel ecosystem research and management > Ecocentric approach to novel ecosystems
bae3119928ea.sentence: The anthroposphere is a term, first used in the 1940s, that refers to the part of the Earth system that is inhabited and influenced by humans; this led to the term anthrome emerging in the early 2000s, which describes the terrestrial biosphere in its modern, human-altered form.

2d7dfe92ba8f.title: Novel ecosystem
2d7dfe92ba8f.section: Novel ecosystem research and management > Ecocentric approach to novel ecosystems
2d7dfe92ba8f.sentence: Anthromes are delineated using the framework of biome definition to separate global patterns of sustained and direct human land use.

04ba069586a5.title: Novel ecosystem
04ba069586a5.section: Novel ecosystem research and management > Ecocentric approach to novel ecosystems
04ba069586a5.sentence: Each anthrome is composed of a heterogenous mosaic of land uses and land cover, usually including areas that are partially reclaimed by nature.

7f5fda196173.title: Novel ecosystem
7f5fda196173.section: Novel ecosystem research and management > Ecocentric approach to novel ecosystems
7f5fda196173.sentence: - Intensive land-use biome: 1.) annual croplands, 2.) sown livestock pastures, 3.) plantations, 4.) urban and industrial ecosystems (dense settlement areas), and 5.) derived semi-natural pastures and old fields.

e0b8e997536c.title: Novel ecosystem
e0b8e997536c.section: Novel ecosystem research and management > Ecocentric approach to novel ecosystems
e0b8e997536c.sentence: - Artificial wetlands biome: 1.) large reservoirs, 2.) constructed lacustrine wetlands, 3.) rice paddies, 4.) freshwater aquafarms, 5.) canals, ditches, and drains

6298d34268d4.title: Novel ecosystem
6298d34268d4.section: Novel ecosystem research and management > Management strategies
6298d34268d4.sentence: Management strategies characterized by action, rather than inaction, are divided into two approaches: managing against novel ecosystems, and managing for novel ecosystems.

8271e5fdc3f2.title: Novel ecosystem
8271e5fdc3f2.section: Novel ecosystem research and management > Management strategies
8271e5fdc3f2.sentence: This, along with inadequate funding, resources, information, has led to tolerance and inaction as the default approach to managing these complex environments.

360f4c2b54ec.title: Novel ecosystem
360f4c2b54ec.section: Novel ecosystem research and management > Management strategies
360f4c2b54ec.sentence: The managing against strategy contains traditional restoration ecology approaches, where efforts are focused on returning degraded habitats and biomes to historical reference benchmarks through eradication of non-native species and re-colonization of native species.

e33542d6e27d.title: Novel ecosystem
e33542d6e27d.section: Novel ecosystem research and management > Management strategies
e33542d6e27d.sentence: However, accelerating climate change often renders those baselines unattainable, and the novel ecosystems so thoroughly integrated that it leads to a state of practical unrestorability.

6b38660ad113.title: Novel ecosystem
6b38660ad113.section: Novel ecosystem research and management > Management strategies
6b38660ad113.sentence: Pristine restoration is often impossible, so ecosystem scientists have moved toward a goal of managing for and fostering resilient and adaptive ecosystems.

85d266c92dc2.title: Land restoration
85d266c92dc2.sentence: Stabilizing and fixating the soil is usually done in several phases.

61c30f66512e.title: Land restoration
61c30f66512e.sentence: The first phase is fixating the soil to such extent that dune movement is ceased.

6de0bc1c20dc.title: Land restoration
6de0bc1c20dc.sentence: This is done by grasses, and plants providing wind protection such as shelterbelts, windbreaks and woodlots.

c8b8461f400e.title: Land restoration
c8b8461f400e.sentence: Shelterbelts are wind protections composed of rows of trees, arranged perpendicular to the prevailing wind, while woodlots are more extensive areas of woodland.

3300d58217eb.title: Land restoration
3300d58217eb.sentence: The second phase involves improving/enriching the soil by planting nitrogen-fixating plants and using the soil immediately to grow crops.

7061269b9d8f.title: Land restoration
7061269b9d8f.sentence: In addition, each year the plots are used for another type of crop (known as crop rotation) to prevent depleting the soil on specific trace elements.

a36d614f48a2.title: Land rehabilitation
a36d614f48a2.sentence: Before mining activities begin, a rehabilitation security bond must be provided.

8e1ad6539198.title: Land rehabilitation
8e1ad6539198.sentence: Mine rehabilitation, a legal obligation for mining companies in Australia for which they are required to pay bonds, could be a source of considerable employment generation and economic investment in regional areas, if governments were willing to enforce the laws covering the process.

a602ca9edf02.title: Land rehabilitation
a602ca9edf02.sentence: The Australian mine rehabilitation bonds totals $9.49 billion, with the state of NSW bond totaling $2.68bn in 2019.

d4eea3aff700.title: Land rehabilitation
d4eea3aff700.sentence: The size of mining security bonds has been questioned by NSW's Auditor General as being insufficient to cover the complete costs associated with mine rehabilitation activities.

55651480d75c.title: Land rehabilitation
55651480d75c.sentence: The cost of reclaiming the abandoned mines in the US is estimated at $9.6bn.

f623c5058a3b.title: Land rehabilitation
f623c5058a3b.sentence: The financing for restoring abandoned mines is drawn from operating mines and public sources.

2a2252c7e61e.title: Exclosure
2a2252c7e61e.sentence: An exclosure, in an area being used extensively for grazing, is a limited area from which unwanted browsing animals, such as domestic cattle or wildlife such as deer, are excluded by fencing or other means.

cf9bae668252.title: Exclosure
cf9bae668252.sentence: Most commonly, exclosures are areas that are set aside for regreening.

bfac76c44c15.title: Exclosure
bfac76c44c15.sentence: Wood harvesting and livestock range are not allowed there.

d07663ed037c.title: Exclosure
d07663ed037c.sentence: In developing countries, people commonly have economic benefits from these exclosures through grass harvesting, beekeeping and other non-timber forest products.

ace1525d21f0.title: Exclosure
ace1525d21f0.sentence: Exclosures have as an additional benefit that the surrounding communities may receive carbon credits for the sequestered CO2, as part of a carbon offset programme.

7a510fed133d.title: Exclosure
7a510fed133d.sentence: The revenues are then reinvested in the villages, according to the priorities of the communities; it may be for an additional class in the village school, a water pond, conservation in the exclosures, or a store for incense.

92259aadc88c.title: Mine reclamation
92259aadc88c.sentence: Within the past decade, a new approach to reforestation—the Forestry Reclamation Approach, or FRA—has been promoted by state mining agencies and the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement (OSMRE) as an appropriate and desirable method for reclaiming coal-mined land to support forested land uses under SMCRA.

0efb00b0443c.title: Mine reclamation
0efb00b0443c.sentence: The FRA establishes guidelines for achieving successful reforestation on mined lands, and can be summarized in the following five steps:

8570e11f6768.title: Mine reclamation
8570e11f6768.sentence: - Create a suitable rooting medium for good tree growth that is no less than four feet deep and made of topsoil, weathered sandstone, and/or the best available material.

16e41ef7722c.title: Mine reclamation
16e41ef7722c.sentence: - Loosely grade the topsoil or topsoil substitute established in step one to create a non-compacted growth medium.

0a290b2a857a.title: Mine reclamation
0a290b2a857a.sentence: - Plant two types (or more) of trees: early successional species for wildlife and soil stability, then commercially valuable crop trees.

26fc7cb0f0ab.title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
26fc7cb0f0ab.sentence: The UN Decade builds on regional restoration efforts, such as Initiative 20x20 in Latin America, which aims to restore 20 million hectares of degraded land by 2030; and the AFR100 African Forest Landscape Restoration Initiative, that aims to bring 100 million hectares of degraded land under restoration by 2030.

07ae8c332805.title: Bonn Challenge
07ae8c332805.sentence: The African Forest Landscape Restoration Initiative fits within the Bonn Challenge and has a goal of having 100 million hectares in the process of restoring by 2030.

3b66db5b7460.title: Bonn Challenge
3b66db5b7460.sentence: 28 African countries have made a total commitment of 113 million hectares to the initiative.

fe22bae59558.title: Peatland restoration
fe22bae59558.section: Approaches to restoration > Methods and techniques > Rewetting
fe22bae59558.sentence: Rewetting involves returning a degraded peatland to its original waterlogged conditions, which are critical to restoring peat-forming vegetation and suppressing the risk of forest fire, aerobic microbial metabolism, and enzyme activity.

5fe089f35669.title: Peatland restoration
5fe089f35669.section: Approaches to restoration > Methods and techniques > Rewetting
5fe089f35669.sentence: The purpose of rewetting is to preserve soil moisture and decrease the rate of drainage, achieved by blocking and filling canals, and digging deep wells.

b4cdf1663166.title: Peatland restoration
b4cdf1663166.section: Approaches to restoration > Methods and techniques > Rewetting
b4cdf1663166.sentence: - Peat-dams are artificial barriers constructed from soil material, which are intended to block the flow of water in channels or gullies.

762d2d319290.title: Peatland restoration
762d2d319290.section: Approaches to restoration > Methods and techniques > Rewetting
762d2d319290.sentence: - Plastic dams are barriers made of interlocking sheets of impermeable plastic piling that are used to block gullies.

512f0e67bd3c.title: Peatland restoration
512f0e67bd3c.section: Targets of restoration > Climate change mitigation and adaptation
512f0e67bd3c.sentence: Rewetting and restoring peatlands can significantly reduce these emissions by raising water tables which slower down the plant decomposition.

83e2fc2d7a08.title: Peatland restoration
83e2fc2d7a08.section: Targets of restoration > Climate change mitigation and adaptation
83e2fc2d7a08.sentence: The resulting anaerobic decomposition produces the greenhouse gas methane, but since methane does not remain in the atmosphere as long as other GHGs, the net effect on the climate is likely cooling if a long time frame is considered (decades).

56313b4f8dde.title: Peatland restoration
56313b4f8dde.sentence: In the United Kingdom, research conducted to assess the value that society places on the benefits of peatland restoration found that restoring 20% of Scotland's peatland would result in economic benefits estimated at between £80 and £336 million per year.

69ca842ad066.title: Peatland restoration
69ca842ad066.sentence: Delaying peatland restoration until 2039–2050 would lead to a significant loss of economic benefits to society.

fb54a7d78263.title: Peatland restoration
fb54a7d78263.section: Approaches to restoration > Methods and techniques > Paludiculture
fb54a7d78263.sentence: Paludiculture is a form of rewetting drained peatlands while it is further used for agriculture.

788694fea8e1.title: Peatland restoration
788694fea8e1.section: Approaches to restoration > Methods and techniques > Paludiculture
788694fea8e1.sentence: The idea is to regenerate wet peatlands and increase the water table to get the peatland-ecosystem back to work, which stores high amounts of carbon.

8ec5ad21d5e2.title: Peatland restoration
8ec5ad21d5e2.section: Approaches to restoration > Methods and techniques > Paludiculture
8ec5ad21d5e2.sentence: A main benefit is, that the land is used in two ways, as carbon sinks (peat) and for agricultural purposes.

770fd9d56039.title: Peatland restoration
770fd9d56039.section: Approaches to restoration > Methods and techniques > Paludiculture
770fd9d56039.sentence: Among potential crops and usages are different kinds of berries, herbs, timber and biomass for biofuel.

009c75cf9754.title: Paludiculture
009c75cf9754.section: Characteristics > Impact of peatland drainage and rewetting
009c75cf9754.sentence: Covering only 3% of the Earth's land surface, they store more than 450 gigatonnes of carbon – more than stored by forests (which cover 30% of the land surface).

af8fe933d0a2.title: Sustainable agriculture
af8fe933d0a2.sentence: Sustainable agriculture is a form of farming that reduces environmental harm, aids and expands natural resources and ensures that non-renewable resources are harnessed for productive purposes.

0d956b43ec24.title: Sustainable agriculture
0d956b43ec24.sentence: Agriculture has an enormous environmental footprint, playing a significant role in causing climate change (food systems are responsible for one third of the anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions), water scarcity, water pollution, land degradation, deforestation and other processes; it is simultaneously causing environmental changes and being impacted by these changes.

331cef331156.title: Sustainable agriculture
331cef331156.sentence: Sustainable agriculture consists of environment friendly methods of farming that allow the production of crops or livestock without causing damage to human or natural systems.

59f79c0008d4.title: Sustainable agriculture
59f79c0008d4.sentence: It involves preventing adverse effects on soil, water, biodiversity, and surrounding or downstream resources, as well as to those working or living on the farm or in neighboring areas.

529ed178d812.title: Sustainable agriculture
529ed178d812.sentence: Elements of sustainable agriculture can include permaculture, agroforestry, mixed farming, multiple cropping, and crop rotation.

128c3ff7340b.title: Sustainable agriculture
128c3ff7340b.sentence: The term "sustainable agriculture" was defined in 1977 by the USDA as an integrated system of plant and animal production practices having a site-specific application that will, over the long term:

11b4319c49ee.title: Sustainable agriculture
11b4319c49ee.sentence: - satisfy human food and fiber needs

e34639828b51.title: Sustainable agriculture
e34639828b51.sentence: - enhance environmental quality and the natural resource base upon which the agriculture economy depends

8283bb4f1f84.title: Sustainable agriculture
8283bb4f1f84.sentence: - make the most efficient use of nonrenewable resources and on-farm resources and integrate, where appropriate, natural biological cycles and controls

d91010909305.title: Sustainable agriculture
d91010909305.sentence: - sustain the economic viability of farm operations

405707322eb9.title: Sustainable agriculture
405707322eb9.sentence: - enhance the quality of life for farmers and society as a whole.

d6667ee1b8bd.title: Sustainable agriculture
d6667ee1b8bd.sentence: Costs, such as environmental problems, not covered in traditional accounting systems (which take into account only the direct costs of production incurred by the farmer) are known as externalities.

ba1979f1214a.title: Sustainable agriculture
ba1979f1214a.sentence: As funding become scarce, a possible solution is "investment in sustainable agriculture, which is four times more cost-effective than direct food assistance but only accounts for three percent of humanitarian funds."

d971638571c0.title: Sustainable agriculture
d971638571c0.sentence: Numerous sustainability standards and certification systems exist, including organic certification, Rainforest Alliance, Fair Trade, UTZ Certified, GlobalGAP, Bird Friendly, and the Common Code for the Coffee Community (4C).

4e29f5baeeb4.title: Sustainable agriculture
4e29f5baeeb4.section: Challenges and debates > Different viewpoints about the definition
4e29f5baeeb4.sentence: There is a debate on the definition of sustainability regarding agriculture.

1659b3ba5de5.title: Sustainable agriculture
1659b3ba5de5.section: Challenges and debates > Different viewpoints about the definition
1659b3ba5de5.sentence: The definition could be characterized by two different approaches: an ecocentric approach and a technocentric approach.

1fa8fc2f7c09.title: Sustainable agriculture
1fa8fc2f7c09.section: Challenges and debates > Different viewpoints about the definition
1fa8fc2f7c09.sentence: The ecocentric approach emphasizes no- or low-growth levels of human development, and focuses on organic and biodynamic farming techniques with the goal of changing consumption patterns, and resource allocation and usage.

f3bc38b2cf88.title: Sustainable agriculture
f3bc38b2cf88.section: Challenges and debates > Different viewpoints about the definition
f3bc38b2cf88.sentence: The technocentric approach argues that sustainability can be attained through a variety of strategies, from the view that state-led modification of the industrial system like conservation-oriented farming systems should be implemented, to the argument that biotechnology is the best way to meet the increasing demand for food.

004cbb5aeafd.title: Sustainable agriculture
004cbb5aeafd.sentence: The term became popular in the late 1980s.

19fd2a90c24d.title: Soil health
19fd2a90c24d.sentence: Soil health is a state of a soil meeting its range of ecosystem functions as appropriate to its environment.

7adc1a933763.title: Soil health
7adc1a933763.sentence: In more colloquial terms, the health of soil arises from favorable interactions of all soil components (living and non-living) that belong together, as in microbiota, plants and animals.

abe28b96d007.title: Soil health
abe28b96d007.sentence: - Sustaining plant and animal productivity (agronomic focus);

8bc472d76b57.title: Soil health
8bc472d76b57.sentence: - Maintaining or enhancing water and air quality (environmental/climate focus);

c21efd99dc72.title: Soil health
c21efd99dc72.sentence: The phrase "soil health" has largely replaced the older "soil quality".

f13eed2ef2d1.title: Soil health
f13eed2ef2d1.sentence: The primary difference between the two expressions is that soil quality was focused on the ability of the soil serve a particular purpose, as in "quality of soil for maize production" or "quality of soil for roadbed preparation" and so on.

fb032c2f61c4.title: Soil health
fb032c2f61c4.sentence: Soil health depends on soil biodiversity (with a robust soil biota), and it can be improved via soil management, especially by care to keep protective living covers on the soil and by natural (carbon-containing) soil amendments.

992d93f3e520.title: Soil health
992d93f3e520.sentence: Some microbiologists now believe that 80% of soil nutrient functions are essentially controlled by microbes.

a777d941a825.title: Soil health
a777d941a825.sentence: However, in this same time USA soils have also lost up to 75% of their carbon (humus), causing biological fertility and ecosystem functioning to decline; how much is debatable.

aecf861ce005.title: Soil health
aecf861ce005.sentence: It is possible that a soil can be healthy in terms of ecosystem functioning but not necessarily serve crop production or human nutrition directly, hence the scientific debate on terms and measurements.

0d6b9e8f76f0.title: Carbon farming
0d6b9e8f76f0.sentence: Carbon farming is a set of agricultural methods that aim to store carbon in the soil and biomass.

d4a93f7f6cc6.title: Carbon farming
d4a93f7f6cc6.sentence: The overall aim of carbon farming is to store carbon in the soil, crop roots, wood and leaves.

c8246f864016.title: Carbon farming
c8246f864016.sentence: The overall goal of carbon farming is to create a net loss of carbon from the atmosphere.

cf0a985aebb3.title: Carbon farming
cf0a985aebb3.sentence: This is done by increasing the rate at which carbon is sequestered into soil and plant material.

918443de8f04.title: Carbon farming
918443de8f04.sentence: When a soil is converted from natural land or semi natural land, such as forests, woodlands, grasslands, steppes and savannas, the SOC content in the soil reduces by about 30–40%.

627baf7f74af.title: Carbon dioxide removal
627baf7f74af.sentence: Agricultural methods for carbon farming include adjusting how tillage and livestock grazing is done, using organic mulch or compost, working with biochar and terra preta, and changing crop types.

74a177b6ce00.title: Carbon farming
74a177b6ce00.section: Methods used in agriculture > Working with biochar and terra preta
74a177b6ce00.sentence: Mixing anaerobically burned biochar into soil sequesters approximately 50% of the carbon in the biomass.

52004b0b6c82.title: Carbon farming
52004b0b6c82.sentence: Carbon farming can offset as much as 20% of 2010 carbon dioxide emissions annually.

9a10c7c5cf1f.title: Carbon farming
9a10c7c5cf1f.sentence: As of 2016, variants of carbon farming reached hundreds of millions of hectares globally, of the nearly 5 billion hectares (1.2×10^10 acres) of world farmland.

61087c71cd75.title: Carbon farming
61087c71cd75.sentence: However, the effects of soil sequestration can be reversed.

a3595dd37d66.title: Carbon farming
a3595dd37d66.sentence: If the soil is disrupted or intensive tillage practices are used, the soil becomes a net source of greenhouse gases.

29bbab2edc73.title: Carbon farming
29bbab2edc73.sentence: One concern to note is that if policy and incentives are only aimed towards carbon sequestration, then carbon farming could actually be harmful to ecosystems.

19398fea2318.title: Carbon farming
19398fea2318.sentence: Carbon farming could inadvertently cause an increase of land clearing and monocultures when species diversity is not a goal of the landscapes project, so there should be attempts to balance the goals of carbon farming and biodiversity should be attempted.

47878d1dde71.title: Carbon farming
47878d1dde71.sentence: Farmers who sequester carbon can sell carbon credits to companies in need of carbon offsets.

0b6f1da5e9f3.title: Crop rotation
0b6f1da5e9f3.sentence: Crop rotation is the practice of growing a series of different types of crops in the same area across a sequence of growing seasons.

afdbf6c46da9.title: Crop rotation
afdbf6c46da9.sentence: This practice reduces the reliance of crops on one set of nutrients, pest and weed pressure, along with the probability of developing resistant pests and weeds.

5e9e87bb462d.title: Crop rotation
5e9e87bb462d.sentence: Growing the same crop in the same place for many years in a row, known as monocropping, gradually depletes the soil of certain nutrients and promotes the proliferation of specialized pest and weed populations adapted to that crop system.

805489f5a508.title: Crop rotation
805489f5a508.sentence: A great advantage of crop rotation comes from the interrelationship of nitrogen-fixing crops with nitrogen-demanding crops.

8091e307bbea.title: Crop rotation
8091e307bbea.sentence: Legumes, like alfalfa and clover, collect available nitrogen from the atmosphere and store it in nodules on their root structure.

b59a509563f6.title: Crop rotation
b59a509563f6.sentence: When the plant is harvested, the biomass of uncollected roots breaks down, making the stored nitrogen available to future crops.

7d34e0213647.title: Crop rotation
7d34e0213647.sentence: Crop rotations greatly increase soil organic carbon (SOC) content, the main constituent of soil organic matter.

3a19f9970823.title: Crop rotation
3a19f9970823.sentence: Highly diverse rotations spanning long periods of time have shown to be even more effective in increasing SOC, while soil disturbances (e.g. from tillage) are responsible for exponential decline in SOC levels.

db83069ff002.title: Crop rotation
db83069ff002.sentence: The changing of crops in a sequence decreases the population level of pests by (1) interrupting pest life cycles and (2) interrupting pest habitat.

e9dbc8839727.title: Crop rotation
e9dbc8839727.sentence: Different crops in the rotation can reduce the risks of adverse weather for the individual farmer.

ca19d014a095.title: Crop rotation
ca19d014a095.sentence: In the Green Revolution of the mid-20th century, crop rotation gave way in the developed world to the practice of supplementing the chemical inputs to the soil through topdressing with fertilizers, adding (for example) ammonium nitrate or urea and restoring soil pH with lime.

67249696ac42.title: Crop rotation
67249696ac42.sentence: Crop rotation is a required practice, in the United States, for farms seeking organic certification.

a455d5955157.title: Crop rotation
a455d5955157.sentence: Ancient Near Eastern farmers practiced crop rotation in 6000 BC, alternately planting legumes and cereals.

360cfcbd7349.title: Agricultural pollution
360cfcbd7349.sentence: Agricultural pollution problem refers to biotic and abiotic byproducts of farming practices that result in contamination or degradation of the environment and surrounding ecosystems, and/or cause injury to humans and their economic interests.

7642aea2e1ed.title: Agricultural pollution
7642aea2e1ed.sentence: The pollution may come from a variety of sources, ranging from point source water pollution (from a single discharge point) to more diffuse, landscape-level causes, also known as non-point source pollution and air pollution.

4b62db0b3980.title: Agricultural pollution
4b62db0b3980.sentence: Pollutants from farming include sediments, nutrients, pathogens, pesticides, metals, and salts.

2f6eee44ab9d.title: Agricultural pollution
2f6eee44ab9d.sentence: Pollutants from agriculture greatly affect water quality and can be found in lakes, rivers, wetlands, estuaries, and groundwater.

47fee9568e60.title: Agricultural pollution
47fee9568e60.sentence: Bad management practices include poorly managed animal feeding operations, overgrazing, plowing, fertilizer, and improper, excessive, or badly timed use of pesticides.

7fd14520a16c.title: Agricultural pollution
7fd14520a16c.sentence: Animal agriculture has an outsized impact on pollutants that enter the environment.

4f8501377090.title: Soil conservation
4f8501377090.sentence: Soil conservation is the prevention of loss of the topmost layer of the soil from erosion or prevention of reduced fertility caused by over usage, acidification, salinization or other chemical soil contamination.

6e49af8eba01.title: Soil conservation
6e49af8eba01.sentence: A consequence of deforestation is typically large-scale erosion, loss of soil nutrients and sometimes total desertification.

7fa0d484e094.title: Soil conservation
7fa0d484e094.sentence: Techniques for improved soil conservation include crop rotation, cover crops, conservation tillage and planted windbreaks, affect both erosion and fertility.

99453b649975.title: Soil conservation
99453b649975.sentence: Farmers have practiced soil conservation for millennia.

e5cdfbcdf577.title: Soil conservation
e5cdfbcdf577.sentence: In Europe, policies such as the Common Agricultural Policy are targeting the application of best management practices such as reduced tillage, winter cover crops, plant residues and grass margins in order to better address soil conservation.

142450a14a7d.title: Soil conservation
142450a14a7d.sentence: Political and economic action is further required to solve the erosion problem.

edef53e096a8.title: Soil conservation
edef53e096a8.sentence: A simple governance hurdle concerns how we value the land and this can be changed by cultural adaptation.

9acdaeccf9d8.title: Soil conservation
9acdaeccf9d8.sentence: Each one percent increase in soil organic matter helps soil hold 20,000 gallons more water per acre.

2a45185e697a.title: Soil conservation
2a45185e697a.section: Methods > Reducing the use of pesticides
2a45185e697a.sentence: Differentiated taxation schemes are among the options investigated in the academic literature to reducing their use.

d1fe590a719d.title: Regenerative agriculture
d1fe590a719d.sentence: Regenerative agriculture is a conservation and rehabilitation approach to food and farming systems.

da370f3f4bb7.title: Regenerative agriculture
da370f3f4bb7.sentence: It focuses on topsoil regeneration, increasing biodiversity, enhancing ecosystem services, supporting biosequestration, increasing resilience to climate change, and strengthening the health and vitality of farm soil.

5a53c7ef8553.title: Regenerative agriculture
5a53c7ef8553.sentence: Regenerative agriculture is not a specific practice.

d60727f5c37c.title: Regenerative agriculture
d60727f5c37c.sentence: It combines a variety of sustainable agriculture techniques.

b5e511a3c0f0.title: Regenerative agriculture
b5e511a3c0f0.sentence: Practices include maximal recycling of farm waste and adding composted material from non-farm sources.

ca0388f1f31f.title: Regenerative agriculture
ca0388f1f31f.sentence: In the early 1980s, the Rodale Institute began using the term 'regenerative agriculture'.

7b9e6c34ed40.title: Regenerative agriculture
7b9e6c34ed40.sentence: A 2020 review of 229 journal articles and 25 practitioner websites found that regenerative agriculture lacked both a legal or regulatory definition and a broadly accepted definition in common usage.

f1d9ed6f1f60.title: Regenerative agriculture
f1d9ed6f1f60.sentence: Definitions varied considerably: some focused on particular practices, such as cover cropping, livestock integration, and reduced tillage, while others emphasized outcomes such as improved soil health, carbon sequestration, and increased biodiversity.

cf8c7b99ffff.title: Regenerative agriculture
cf8c7b99ffff.sentence: The 4 most consistent principles were found to be, 1) enhancing and improving soil health, 2) optimization of resource management, 3) alleviation of climate change, and 4) improvement of water quality and availability.

203585334a42.title: Regenerative agriculture
203585334a42.sentence: It is estimated that 30–75% of global soil organic matter has been lost since the advent of tillage-based farming.

a22329c091d4.title: Regenerative agriculture
a22329c091d4.sentence: A 2023 literature review found that several practices commonly associated with regenerative agriculture (reduced tillage, crop-residue retention, cover cropping, crop–livestock integration, and agroforestry) can improve soil carbon, soil health, or crop yields under certain climatic and soil conditions.

74bf0676f612.title: Regenerative agriculture
74bf0676f612.sentence: However, the authors noted that many farmers remain reluctant to adopt regenerative practices because evidence for their claimed benefits and profitability is still limited.

33e68e15c0f4.title: Regenerative agriculture
33e68e15c0f4.sentence: Some members of the scientific community have criticized some of the claims made by proponents of regenerative agriculture as exaggerated and unsupported by evidence.

39b14fe6421f.title: No-till farming
39b14fe6421f.sentence: No-till farming (also known as zero tillage or direct drilling) is an agricultural technique for growing crops or pasture without disturbing the soil through tillage.

8825b24f5dd5.title: No-till farming
8825b24f5dd5.sentence: No-till farming decreases the amount of soil erosion tillage causes in certain soils, especially in sandy and dry soils on sloping terrain.

ee96fd8f0e9f.title: No-till farming
ee96fd8f0e9f.sentence: Other possible benefits include an increase in the amount of water that infiltrates the soil, soil retention of organic matter, and nutrient cycling.

23c4f681aa15.title: No-till farming
23c4f681aa15.sentence: In 1999, about 45 million ha (170,000 mi2) was under no-till farming worldwide, which increased to 72 million ha (280,000 mi2) in 2003 and to 111 million ha (430,000 mi2) in 2009.

3503d601d0a5.title: No-till farming
3503d601d0a5.section: Adoption across the world > South America
3503d601d0a5.sentence: In Argentina the usage of no-till resulted in reduction of soil erosion losses by 80%, cost reductions by more than 50% and increased farm incomes.

d9e3ab5b34c8.title: No-till farming
d9e3ab5b34c8.section: Adoption across the world > South America
d9e3ab5b34c8.sentence: In Paraguay, net farm incomes increased by 77% after adoption of no-till farming.

dd6a1d82ca01.title: No-till farming
dd6a1d82ca01.section: Adoption across the world > United States
dd6a1d82ca01.sentence: By minimizing soil disturbance, no-till farming reduces the number of passes required with machinery, leading to lower fuel and labor expenses.

4f0366b02dda.title: No-till farming
4f0366b02dda.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Increased herbicide use
4f0366b02dda.sentence: Herbicides such as glyphosate are commonly used in place of tillage for seedbed preparation, which leads to more herbicide use in comparison to conventional tillage.

bc17eb67410f.title: No-till farming
bc17eb67410f.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Fertilizer
bc17eb67410f.sentence: One of the most common yield reducers is nitrogen being immobilized in the crop residue, which can take a few months to several years to decompose, depending on the crop's C to N ratio and the local environment.

b091e564aa28.title: No-till farming
b091e564aa28.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Fertilizer
b091e564aa28.sentence: Fertilizer needs to be applied at a higher rate.

667150e7ebd8.title: No-till farming
667150e7ebd8.section: Benefits and issues > Profit, economics, yield
667150e7ebd8.sentence: A problem with no-till farming is that the soil warms and dries more slowly in spring, which may delay planting.

f0bd48405c51.title: No-till farming
f0bd48405c51.section: Benefits and issues > Environmental > Greenhouse gases
f0bd48405c51.sentence: There is debate over whether the increased sequestration sometimes detected is actually occurring or is due to flawed testing methods or other factors.

1cb20ef55ff7.title: No-till farming
1cb20ef55ff7.section: Benefits and issues > Environmental > Greenhouse gases
1cb20ef55ff7.sentence: A 2014 study claimed that certain no-till systems may sequester less carbon than conventional tillage systems, saying that the "no-till subsurface layer is often losing more soil organic carbon stock over time than is gained in the surface layer." The study also highlighted the need for a uniform definition of soil organic carbon sequestration among researchers.

66870321923e.title: No-till farming
66870321923e.sentence: The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) offers incentives to farmers to convert to no-till farming, such as a payment of £73 per hectare of land eligible for this scheme.

f447fb612900.title: No-till farming
f447fb612900.sentence: A formalized opposition to plowing started in the 1940s with Edward H. Faulkner, author of Plowman's Folly.

f00af570b014.title: Permaculture
f00af570b014.sentence: Permaculture is an approach to land management and settlement design that adopts arrangements observed in flourishing natural ecosystems.

571aec23cf51.title: Permaculture
571aec23cf51.sentence: It includes a set of design principles derived using whole-systems thinking.

d9ee7e0a28cb.title: Permaculture
d9ee7e0a28cb.sentence: It applies these principles in fields such as regenerative agriculture, town planning, rewilding, and community resilience.

e5aec8b0cebc.title: Permaculture
e5aec8b0cebc.sentence: The term was coined in 1978 by Bill Mollison and David Holmgren, who formulated the concept in opposition to modern industrialized methods, instead adopting a more traditional or "natural" approach to agriculture.

6a7f086ba93b.title: Permaculture
6a7f086ba93b.sentence: In 1911, Franklin Hiram King wrote Farmers of Forty Centuries: Or Permanent Agriculture in China, Korea and Japan, describing farming practices of East Asia designed for "permanent agriculture".

8ca61c64d944.title: Permaculture
8ca61c64d944.sentence: In 1929, Joseph Russell Smith appended King's term as the subtitle for Tree Crops: A Permanent Agriculture, which he wrote in response to widespread deforestation, plow agriculture, and erosion in the eastern mountains and hill regions of the United States.

63a565c0ba54.title: Permaculture
63a565c0ba54.sentence: Holmgren articulated twelve permaculture design principles in his Permaculture: Principles and Pathways Beyond Sustainability:

b22d35bcdbe8.title: Permaculture
b22d35bcdbe8.sentence: - Observe and interact: Take time to engage with nature to design solutions that suit a particular situation.

73e12d05ec67.title: Permaculture
73e12d05ec67.sentence: - Catch and store energy: Develop systems that collect resources at peak abundance for use in times of need.

ad891277e699.title: Permaculture
ad891277e699.sentence: - Obtain a yield: Emphasize projects that generate meaningful rewards.

676a899e111d.title: Permaculture
676a899e111d.sentence: Low-effort permaculture favours perennial crops which do not require tilling and planting every year.

45469983109b.title: Permaculture
45469983109b.sentence: The broad range of topics discussed in permaculture has led to criticism that permaculture is not clearly defined.

e2cf4fba6595.title: Permaculture
e2cf4fba6595.sentence: Permaculture as a popular movement has been largely isolated from scientific literature.

6fce27625fef.title: Cover crop
6fce27625fef.sentence: In agriculture, cover crops are plants that are planted to cover the soil rather than for the purpose of being harvested.

64c05236dec7.title: Cover crop
64c05236dec7.sentence: Cover crops manage soil erosion, soil fertility, soil quality, water, weeds, pests, diseases, biodiversity and wildlife in an agroecosystem—an ecological system managed and shaped by humans.

8c863ca0a75e.title: Cover crop
8c863ca0a75e.sentence: Although cover crops can perform multiple functions in an agroecosystem simultaneously, they are often grown for the sole purpose of preventing soil erosion.

968e3fb3d8f9.title: Cover crop
968e3fb3d8f9.sentence: Cover crops reduce soil loss by improving soil structure and increasing infiltration, protecting the soil surface, scattering raindrop energy, and reducing the velocity of the movement of water over the soil surface.

faa535013d4b.title: Cover crop
faa535013d4b.section: Soil quality management > Soil health and ecosystem services
faa535013d4b.sentence: A global meta-analysis of 102 field studies reported that cover crops increased saturated hydraulic conductivity by about 106%, and raised total organic carbon and total nitrogen in the topsoil by approximately 10% and 20%, respectively, relative to systems without cover crops.

098131c49ab0.title: Cover crop
098131c49ab0.sentence: Cover crops reduce water pollution risks and remove CO2 from the atmosphere.

334283d24b49.title: Cover crop
334283d24b49.sentence: Thick cover crop stands often compete well with weeds during the cover crop growth period, and can prevent most germinated weed seeds from completing their life cycle and reproducing.

79b799cd0e01.title: Cover crop
79b799cd0e01.sentence: This is often termed the cover crop smother effect.

62aded0d0cd6.title: Cover crop
62aded0d0cd6.sentence: In addition to competition-based or physical weed suppression, certain cover crops are known to suppress weeds through allelopathy.

b51cab5585b9.title: Cover crop
b51cab5585b9.sentence: During the migration and breeding season, they found that songbird densities were 7–20 times higher in the cotton fields with an integrated clover cover crop than in the conventional cotton fields.

598272381043.title: Cover crop
598272381043.section: Soil quality management > Soil health and ecosystem services
598272381043.sentence: At the same time, meta-analyses highlight important trade-offs and context dependence: in some environments, cover crops may reduce soil water availability to the following cash crop or have neutral or variable effects on yields, particularly in semi-arid regions or when termination is poorly timed, and long-term impacts on productivity and profitability are still uncertain in several climatic zones due to limited multi-decadal studies.

4a2b02adb1d8.title: Intercropping
4a2b02adb1d8.sentence: Intercropping is a multiple cropping practice that involves the cultivation of two or more crops simultaneously on the same field, a form of polyculture.

8ac6f466f083.title: Intercropping
8ac6f466f083.sentence: The most common goal of intercropping is to produce a greater yield on a given piece of land by making use of resources or ecological processes that would otherwise not be utilized by a single crop.

c9a101b4adcc.title: Intercropping
c9a101b4adcc.sentence: It is particularly important not to have crops competing with each other for physical space, nutrients, water, or sunlight.

209f7477f3b5.title: Intercropping
209f7477f3b5.sentence: Examples of intercropping strategies are planting a deep-rooted crop with a shallow-rooted crop, or planting a tall crop with a shorter crop that requires partial shade.

cec3e78e121a.title: Intercropping
cec3e78e121a.sentence: Intercropping systems can provide higher yields for the same input, or more stable yields with less input, in low-input or subsistence systems.

9b49eec1bfdb.title: Intercropping
9b49eec1bfdb.sentence: For example, plants that are prone to tip over in wind or heavy rain (lodging-prone plants), may be given structural support by their companion crop.

2eb9e9baf82d.title: Intercropping
2eb9e9baf82d.sentence: Some plants are used to suppress weeds or provide nutrients.

adc1180f5eaa.title: Intercropping
adc1180f5eaa.sentence: In a systematic review of the literature, in 2008, in the studies examined, predators of pests tended to increase under crop diversification strategies in only 53 percent of studies, and crop diversification only led to increased yield in only 32% of the studies.

c7100c4ea2b9.title: Intercropping
c7100c4ea2b9.sentence: Crop rotation is a related practice but is not a form of intercropping, as the different crops are grown in separate growing seasons rather than in a single season.

a43182816419.title: Agroecology
a43182816419.sentence: Agroecology is an academic discipline that studies ecological processes applied to agricultural production systems.

22e50c0f1db3.title: Agroecology
22e50c0f1db3.sentence: Dalgaard et al. refer to agroecology as the study of the interactions between plants, animals, humans and the environment within agricultural systems.

11ef5564b193.title: Agroecology
11ef5564b193.sentence: The term can refer to a science, a movement, or an agricultural practice.

f8ac307f37d6.title: Agroecology
f8ac307f37d6.sentence: - A scientific discipline, focused on ecological and agricultural processes that support sustainable food systems

2417b75465ac.title: Agroecology
2417b75465ac.sentence: - A set of agricultural practices that harness ecological processes, biodiversity, nutrient recycling, agroforestry, intercropping, composting, and other nature-based methods.

b40894ba5cd4.title: Agroecology
b40894ba5cd4.sentence: - A social and political movement aimed at transforming food systems by promoting food sovereignty, equity, environmental justice, and the recognition of Indigenous and farmer knowledge

6ae9d488b519.title: Agroecology
6ae9d488b519.sentence: Agroecology is inherently multidisciplinary, including sciences such as agronomy, ecology, environmental science, sociology, economics, history and others.

3d2954a6b4ff.title: Agroecology
3d2954a6b4ff.sentence: The system properties of agroecosystems studied may include: productivity, stability, sustainability and equitability.

229a2ff96d15.title: Agroecology
229a2ff96d15.sentence: Agroecology is not limited to any one scale; it can range from an individual gene to an entire population, or from a single field in a given farm to global systems.

96dbb1a50730.title: Agroecology
96dbb1a50730.sentence: Paul Wojtkowski differentiates the ecology of natural ecosystems from agroecology inasmuch as in natural ecosystems there is no role for economics, whereas in agroecology, focusing as it does on organisms within planned and managed environments, it is human activities, and hence economics, that are the primary governing forces that ultimately control the field.

47a5f8bdc6bd.title: Agroecology
47a5f8bdc6bd.sentence: These are firstly biodynamic farming, secondly organic agriculture, and thirdly Green Food (managed by China Green Food).

9493231d84c4.title: Agroecology
9493231d84c4.sentence: Biodynamics is the oldest of the certified agroecologies, Organics is the most widely practiced certified agroecology (in 188 countries), and Green Food is the newest certified agroecology and was developed in China.

7073f7042d2c.title: Agroecology
7073f7042d2c.sentence: Groups like La Via Campesina have used agroecology as a method for achieving food sovereignty.

b38ca6371406.title: Agroecology
b38ca6371406.sentence: Academic research areas that focus on topics related to agriculture or ecology, such as agronomy, veterinary science, environmental science, and others, are heatedly debating which model of agriculture or agroecology should be supported through policy.

1933d4cc5edc.title: Agroecology
1933d4cc5edc.sentence: Wezel et al. say the first mention of the term agroecology was in 1928, with the publication of the term by Basil Bensin.

9d474751ccfc.title: Agroecology
9d474751ccfc.sentence: Tischler's 1965 book Agrarökologie may be the first to be titled 'agroecology'.

fe010f940333.title: Agroforestry
fe010f940333.sentence: Agroforestry (also known as agro-sylviculture or forest farming) is a land use management system that integrates trees with crops or pasture.

bd9a1792b035.title: Agroforestry
bd9a1792b035.sentence: At its most basic, agroforestry is any of various polyculture systems that intentionally integrate trees with crops or pasture on the same land.

339965a2c046.title: Agroforestry
339965a2c046.sentence: As a polyculture system, an agroforestry system can produce timber and wood products, fruits, nuts, other edible plant products, edible mushrooms, medicinal plants, ornamental plants, animals and animal products, and other products from both domesticated and wild species.

9f45abba6531.title: Agroforestry
9f45abba6531.sentence: An agroforestry system is intensively managed to optimize helpful interactions between the plants and animals included, and "uses the forest as a model of practices".

061ad8f24b2b.title: Agroforestry
061ad8f24b2b.sentence: Benefits include increasing farm productivity and profitability, reduced soil erosion, creating wildlife habitat, managing animal waste, increased biodiversity, improved soil structure, and carbon sequestration.

bb9473c9cb24.title: Agroforestry
bb9473c9cb24.sentence: These benefits are conditional on good farm management.

2c4b7b13a332.title: Agroforestry
2c4b7b13a332.sentence: - Diversification of agricultural products, such as fuelwood, medicinal plants, and multiple crops, increases income security

17f5fc000e41.title: Agroforestry
17f5fc000e41.sentence: Agroforestry practices can increase carbon stocks in soil and woody biomass.

627b3338501d.title: Agroforestry
627b3338501d.sentence: Trees in agroforestry systems, like in new forests, can recapture some of the carbon that was lost by cutting existing forests.

d96b8ffd17ac.title: Agroforestry
d96b8ffd17ac.sentence: Agroforestry practices are especially prevalent in the tropics, especially in subsistence smallholdings areas, with particular importance in sub-Saharan Africa.

686b6b15ef90.title: Agroforestry
686b6b15ef90.sentence: Due to its multiple benefits, for instance in nutrient cycle benefits and potential for mitigating droughts, it has been adopted in the US and Europe.

36bf6bd45ad9.title: Agroforestry
36bf6bd45ad9.sentence: A study from the CGIAR research program on Climate Change, Agriculture and Food Security found from a survey of over 700 households in East Africa that at least 50% of those households had begun planting trees in a change from earlier practices.

ff8038a6160a.title: Agroforestry
ff8038a6160a.sentence: The term "agroforestry" was coined in 1973 by Canadian forester John Bene, but the concept includes agricultural practices that have existed for millennia.

38933f23fe66.title: Landscape-scale conservation
38933f23fe66.sentence: Landscape-scale conservation is a holistic approach to landscape management, aiming to reconcile the competing objectives of nature conservation and economic activities across a given landscape.

0b4878d5de68.title: Landscape-scale conservation
0b4878d5de68.sentence: It can be seen as an alternative to site based conservation.

3e5c36d7b77e.title: Landscape-scale conservation
3e5c36d7b77e.sentence: Many global problems such as poverty, food security, climate change, water scarcity, deforestation and biodiversity loss are connected.

3771ecf093f8.title: Landscape-scale conservation
3771ecf093f8.sentence: Proponents of landscape management argue that as these problems are interconnected, coordinated approaches are needed to address them, by focussing on how landscapes can generate multiple benefits.

7fedddf3725c.title: Landscape-scale conservation
7fedddf3725c.sentence: For example, a river basin can supply water for towns and agriculture, timber and food crops for people and industry, and habitat for biodiversity; and each one of these users can have impacts on the others.

a6a12127d769.title: Landscape-scale conservation
a6a12127d769.sentence: Instead of focussing on a single use of the land it aims to ensure that the interests of different stakeholders are met.

3d134d21c778.title: Landscape-scale conservation
3d134d21c778.sentence: During the Livelihoods and Landscapes Strategies programme the International Union for Conservation of Nature applied this approach to locations worldwide, in 27 landscapes in 23 different countries.

95ff2d9004d8.title: Landscape-scale conservation
95ff2d9004d8.sentence: The UN Environment Programme stated in 2015 that the landscape approach embodies ecosystem management.

eb22a560b275.title: Landscape-scale conservation
eb22a560b275.sentence: Landscape approaches intend to include different sectors, and thus achieve the multiple objectives of the Sustainable Development Goals – for example, working within catchment area of a river to enhance agricultural productivity, flood defence, biodiversity and carbon storage.

b60452d2943c.title: Landscape-scale conservation
b60452d2943c.sentence: Many of these goals have potential synergies or trade-offs: some therefore argue that addressing these goals individually may not be effective, and landscape approaches provide a potential framework to manage them.

5c52592aef82.title: Landscape-scale conservation
5c52592aef82.sentence: A literature review identified five main barriers, as follows:

3563c6b8423a.title: Landscape-scale conservation
3563c6b8423a.sentence: - Terminology confusion: the variety of definitions creates confusion and resistance to engage.

7f0b3ab3f808.title: Landscape-scale conservation
7f0b3ab3f808.sentence: - Time lags: substantial time and resources are invested in developing and planning, while resources are inadequate for implementation.

8ce77e561df3.title: Landscape-scale conservation
8ce77e561df3.sentence: - Operating silos: Each sector pursues its goals without giving consideration to the others.

65e7fb20916e.title: Riparian buffer
65e7fb20916e.sentence: A riparian buffer or stream buffer is a vegetated area (a "buffer strip") near a stream, usually forested, which helps shade and partially protect the stream from the impact of adjacent land uses.

8662408d808b.title: Riparian buffer
8662408d808b.sentence: Riparian buffers act to intercept sediment, nutrients, pesticides, and other materials in surface runoff and reduce nutrients and other pollutants in shallow subsurface water flow.

f6afad61ea12.title: Riparian buffer
f6afad61ea12.sentence: They counteract eutrophication in downstream lakes and ponds which can be detrimental to aquatic habitats because of large fish kills that occur upon large-scale eutrophication.

247e205a1e2e.title: Riparian buffer
247e205a1e2e.sentence: Riparian buffers also stabilise the bank surrounding the water body which is important since erosion can be a major problem in agricultural regions when cut (eroded) banks can take land out of production.

50147f13ee07.title: Riparian buffer
50147f13ee07.sentence: They also serve to provide habitat and wildlife corridors in primarily agricultural areas.

6b836a0c38e5.title: Riparian buffer
6b836a0c38e5.sentence: The habitat provided by the buffers also double as corridors for species that have had their habitat fragmented by various land uses.

00e04950e9c4.title: Riparian buffer
00e04950e9c4.sentence: It found that these buffers removed at least 60% of the nitrogen in the runoff, and at least 65% of the phosphorus from the fertilizer application.

fde9573ddc22.title: Riparian buffer
fde9573ddc22.sentence: Buffers increase land value and allow for the production of profitable alternative crops.

9e60f34678d0.title: Riparian buffer
9e60f34678d0.sentence: Vegetation such as black walnut and hazelnut, which can be profitably harvested, can be incorporated into the riparian buffer.

81b0940a773f.title: Riparian buffer
81b0940a773f.sentence: The Conservation Reserve Program (CRP), a farming assistance program in the United States, provides many incentives to landowners to encourage them to install riparian buffers around water systems that have a high chance of non-point water pollution and are highly erodible.

2e44dce5984a.title: Riparian buffer
2e44dce5984a.sentence: These incentives are offered to agriculturists to compensate them for their economic loss of taking this land out of production.

7cc1e8a56b77.title: Riparian buffer
7cc1e8a56b77.sentence: But another study in 2017 did not find efficiency (or a very limiting capacity) for reducing glyphosate and AMPA leaching to streams; spontaneous herbaceous vegetation RBS is as efficient as Salix plantations and measures of glyphosate in runoff after a year, suggest an unexpected persistence and even a capacity of RBS to potentially favor glyphosate infiltration up to 70 cm depth in the soil.

5229cea178f5.title: Sustainable agriculture
5229cea178f5.sentence: Land sharing, also known as "wildlife-friendly agriculture", involves integrating biodiversity into agricultural production areas.

c44035e67037.title: Sustainable agriculture
c44035e67037.sentence: This approach focuses on the combination of agriculture and biodiversity by reducing the intensification of farming practices.

ae4453899f0a.title: Sustainable agriculture
ae4453899f0a.sentence: This is illustrated notably by agroecological practices such as agroforestry and mixed crop-livestock systems.

04d76d87b41e.title: Sustainable agriculture
04d76d87b41e.sentence: A literature review of empirical studies indicates that land sparing is generally favored for conserving tropical forest biodiversity (67% of relevant studies), whereas land sharing (58% of studies) is more often considered more beneficial for the food security and livelihoods of farmers in developing countries.

b90b1e3b36fd.title: Sustainable agriculture
b90b1e3b36fd.sentence: Land sparing is a strategy that involves strictly separating land dedicated to agricultural production from land dedicated to conservation of natural habitats.

adeb3c332835.title: Sustainable agriculture
adeb3c332835.sentence: This strategy promotes increasing the yield of agricultural land, particularly through intensive farming.

76a67182b5c4.title: Sustainable agriculture
76a67182b5c4.sentence: This is done to preserve areas of major biodiversity interest from agricultural expansion.

5fcb3cf364dd.title: Sustainable agriculture
5fcb3cf364dd.sentence: This has been the dominant strategy in developed countries for over 150 years.

198fe20db919.title: Sustainable agriculture
198fe20db919.sentence: In this context, two landscape management strategies are traditionally opposed: land sparing and land sharing.

bd34b91d920b.title: Sustainable agriculture
bd34b91d920b.sentence: These two strategies have generated intense debate within the scientific community for over a decade, with no clear consensus emerging on their relative effectiveness in balancing biodiversity conservation with food production and rural livelihoods.

e0a0c9eb799a.title: Sustainable agriculture
e0a0c9eb799a.sentence: Recently, a third alternative has been introduced to the debate: the so-called land blending strategy, an intermediate approach between the two traditional ones, as the effectiveness of both strategies appears to vary depending on the landscape context.

2432c69b1a64.title: Sustainable agriculture
2432c69b1a64.sentence: Sustainable intensification encompasses specific agriculture methods that increase production and at the same time help improve environmental outcomes.

a411b65f90b0.title: Sustainable agriculture
a411b65f90b0.sentence: The desired outcomes of the farm are achieved without the need for more land cultivation or destruction of natural habitat; the system performance is upgraded with no net environmental cost.

93ed49249713.title: Sustainable agriculture
93ed49249713.sentence: Sustainable intensification differs from prior intensification methods by specifically placing importance on broader environmental outcomes.

03b32d477fe4.title: Sustainable agriculture
03b32d477fe4.sentence: By 2018; it was predicted in 100 nations a combined total of 163 million farms used sustainable intensification.

dc1c37ea7623.title: Sustainable agriculture
dc1c37ea7623.sentence: The amount of agricultural land covered by this is 453 million ha of land.

071357b099d2.title: Sustainable agriculture
071357b099d2.sentence: That amount of land is equal to 29% of farms worldwide.

0669f8c50035.title: Sustainable agriculture
0669f8c50035.sentence: The capacity for ecosystem services to be strong enough to allow a reduction in use of non-renewable inputs whilst maintaining or boosting yields has been the subject of much debate.

9e5130a68849.title: Sustainable agriculture
9e5130a68849.sentence: Recent work in irrigated rice production system of east Asia has suggested that – in relation to pest management at least – promoting the ecosystem service of biological control using nectar plants can reduce the need for insecticides by 70% whilst delivering a 5% yield advantage compared with standard practice.

e240d929f227.title: Hedge
e240d929f227.sentence: A hedge or hedgerow is a line of shrubs and sometimes trees, planted and trained to form a barrier or to mark the boundary of an area, such as between neighbouring properties.

bebf351715aa.title: Hedge
bebf351715aa.sentence: Hedges that are used to separate a road from adjoining fields or one field from another, and are of sufficient age to incorporate larger trees, are known as hedgerows.

16bbc6d5f22c.title: Hedge
16bbc6d5f22c.sentence: Often they serve as windbreaks to improve conditions for the adjacent crops, as in bocage country.

4895f898ce2d.title: Hedge
4895f898ce2d.sentence: The first hedges enclosed land for cereal crops during the Neolithic Age (4000–6000 years ago).

86ec44273a21.title: Hedge
86ec44273a21.sentence: Increasingly, they are valued too for the major role they have to play in preventing soil loss and reducing pollution, and for their potential to regulate water supply and to reduce flooding.

fd572b75ade2.title: Hedge
fd572b75ade2.sentence: Hedges' roots provide healthy moisture to deep soil; hedges also mitigate water runoff and flooding.

66b1cb73ffc4.title: Hedge
66b1cb73ffc4.sentence: Larkin et al. 2013 find 100% of northwest European farms have hedges, providing 43% of the wildlife habitat there.

30683c4304ce.title: Hedge
30683c4304ce.sentence: The removal of hedgerows gives larger fields making the sowing and harvesting of crops easier, faster and cheaper, and giving a larger area to grow the crops, increasing yield and profits.

efe4a651fbf3.title: Hedge
efe4a651fbf3.sentence: Removal thus weakens the soil and leads to erosion.

39d97bcf141d.title: Hedge
39d97bcf141d.sentence: Hedge removal was subsidised following World War II; in the following years, the amount of hedgerow in the UK greatly decreased.

d14ff2d6530a.title: Hedge
d14ff2d6530a.sentence: >... since the 1950s over half [of hedgerows] have vanished.

c2619a393eb1.title: Hedge
c2619a393eb1.sentence: Over time, the British government moved to protect hedgerows.

e92d5bcada71.title: Hedge
e92d5bcada71.sentence: According to The Economist, "Hedges—and their inhabitants—have been among the few winners of Brexit"; with independent farm policy, the government has increasingly compensated farmers for providing public goods such as maintaining hedges, with farmers being "paid £70m for tending to hedgerows in 2024, up from £26m the year before."

913d84cbd496.title: Rotational grazing
913d84cbd496.sentence: In agriculture, rotational grazing, as opposed to continuous grazing, describes many systems of pasturing, whereby livestock are moved to portions of the pasture, called paddocks, while the other portions rest.

66838fb94433.title: Rotational grazing
66838fb94433.sentence: The intent is to allow the pasture plants and soil time to recover.

34c90f382a4f.title: Rotational grazing
34c90f382a4f.sentence: The approach often produces lower outputs than more intensive animal farming operations, but requires lower inputs, and therefore sometimes produces higher net farm income per animal.

9f668e3bdbc3.title: Rotational grazing
9f668e3bdbc3.sentence: Although milk yields are often lower in rotational systems, net farm income per cow is often greater as compared to confinement operations.

760c415b6ef7.title: Rotational grazing
760c415b6ef7.sentence: Another consideration is that while production per cow is less, the number of cows per acre on the pasture can increase.

89a719669743.title: Rotational grazing
89a719669743.sentence: The net effect is more productivity per acre at less cost.

629039835c50.title: Rotational grazing
629039835c50.sentence: Many pastures undergoing certain types of rotational grazing are less susceptible to soil erosion.

936743eccc75.title: Rotational grazing
936743eccc75.sentence: Rotational grazing may reduce greenhouse gas emissions such as carbon dioxide, nitrous oxides, and methane.

22c958a39945.title: Rotational grazing
22c958a39945.sentence: Although grazers remove nutrient sources from the pasture system when they feed on forage sources, the majority of the nutrients consumed by the herd are returned to the pasture system through manure.

65ad70e6c7c1.title: Rotational grazing
65ad70e6c7c1.sentence: If pasture systems are seeded with more than 40% legumes, commercial nitrogen fertilization is unnecessary for adequate plant growth.

45062f39ebb9.title: Rotational grazing
45062f39ebb9.sentence: Ruminal tympany, also known as bloat, is a common serious problem when ruminants graze on fresh, young pasture, and if left untreated can be fatal.

4c03a763a41d.title: Rotational grazing
4c03a763a41d.sentence: Depending on the management model, plant production has been shown to be equal or greater in continuous compared to rotational grazing in 87% of the experiments.

828dcec227ef.title: Rotational grazing
828dcec227ef.sentence: - Virtual fencing is an emerging technology that uses GPS-enabled collars and auditory cues to influence and control livestock movement without the use of fencing.

6a55dd611ebe.title: Rotational grazing
6a55dd611ebe.sentence: These systems allow farmers/ranchers to automate rotations and reduce labor costs, however, they still remain at low adoption rates.

a2b871d9996b.title: Silvopasture
a2b871d9996b.sentence: Silvopasture (silva is forest in Latin) or wood pasture is the practice of integrating trees, forage, and the grazing of domesticated animals in a mutually beneficial way.

f2830ef1c2e7.title: Silvopasture
f2830ef1c2e7.sentence: It utilizes the principles of managed grazing, and it is one of several distinct forms of agroforestry.

fe75e079722b.title: Silvopasture
fe75e079722b.sentence: Properly managed silvopasture (grazed woodland) can increase overall productivity and long-term income due to the simultaneous production of tree crops, forage, and livestock.

ad52ad0c25fb.title: Silvopasture
ad52ad0c25fb.section: Benefits > Potential for climate change adaptation
ad52ad0c25fb.sentence: By retaining partial tree cover, silvopastures create a more moderated environment that helps mitigate temperature extremes and optimize soil conditions.

a9860d3e1219.title: Silvopasture
a9860d3e1219.section: Benefits > Potential for climate change adaptation
