a9860d3e1219.sentence: One study measured air temperatures near the soil surface (0.25 m) to be consistently cooler in silvopastures than in open pastures, with reductions of up to 7%, while soil temperatures at depths of 5–10 cm are also significantly lower in silvopastoral systems compared to open pastures.

fb9867f664d1.title: Silvopasture
fb9867f664d1.sentence: Studies show that carbon uptake (negative emissions) is lowest in open pastures, intermediate in silvopastures, and highest in reference forests.

d14c5fbc87e0.title: Silvopasture
d14c5fbc87e0.sentence: Establishing silvopastures requires substantial upfront investment in tree planting, fencing, and rotational grazing systems.

7d5dbdf47772.title: Silvopasture
7d5dbdf47772.sentence: Studies indicate that agroforestry systems, including silvopastures, typically take 3–6 years to generate returns, leading to a delayed return on investment (ROI).

79573120d287.title: Silvopasture
79573120d287.sentence: Some of the most common challenges and barriers to silvopasture adoption include policy and regulatory hurdles, land tenure, lack of knowledge and awareness, economic constraint and cultural change.

9f5016d6fc17.title: Silvopasture
9f5016d6fc17.sentence: If done correctly, silvopastures can count as nature-based solutions to climate change.

bb6de756ddc3.title: Conservation agriculture
bb6de756ddc3.sentence: Conservation agriculture (CA) can be defined by a statement given by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations as "Conservation Agriculture (CA) is a farming system that can prevent losses of arable land while regenerating degraded lands.

af5ff846d4d5.title: Conservation agriculture
af5ff846d4d5.sentence: It promotes minimum soil disturbance (i.e. no-till farming), maintenance of a permanent soil cover, and diversification of plant species.

c5a6dcaa1cc0.title: Conservation agriculture
c5a6dcaa1cc0.sentence: The first key principle in CA is practicing minimum soil disturbance which is essential to maintaining minerals within the soil, stopping erosion, and preventing water loss from occurring within the soil.

4baf280178ae.title: Conservation agriculture
4baf280178ae.sentence: The principle of managing the top soil to create a permanent organic soil cover can allow for growth of organisms within the soil structure.

8e6e8bbd7e15.title: Conservation agriculture
8e6e8bbd7e15.sentence: The presence of mulching also reduce the velocity of runoff and the impact of rain drops thus reducing soil erosion and runoff.

123b43674ce1.title: Conservation agriculture
123b43674ce1.sentence: The breaking down of this mulch will produce a high organic matter level which will act as a fertilizer for the soil surface.

3ad02a119b37.title: Conservation agriculture
3ad02a119b37.sentence: The third principle is the practicing diverse crop rotations or crop interactions.

1175bf867188.title: Conservation agriculture
1175bf867188.sentence: Not allowing insects or weeds to establish a pattern will help to eliminate problems with yield reduction and infestations within fields (FAO 2007).

fda7364dd2ef.title: Conservation agriculture
fda7364dd2ef.sentence: Establishing crops in a rotation allows for an extensive buildup of rooting zones which will allow for better water infiltration (Hobbs et al. 2007).

6f6e11e175db.title: Conservation agriculture
6f6e11e175db.sentence: Producers can save 30% to 40% of time and labor by practicing the no-till process.

80a9e21510d0.title: Conservation agriculture
80a9e21510d0.sentence: Since CA takes time to build up enough organic matter and have soils become their own fertilizer, the process does not start to work overnight.

3340be65906a.title: Conservation agriculture
3340be65906a.sentence: The process of CA takes time; when a producer first becomes a conservationist, the results can be a financial loss to them (in most cases, the investment and policy generally exist).

4678a982da17.title: Conservation agriculture
4678a982da17.sentence: It can be many years before a producer will start to see better yields than he/she has had previously.

993e22079c10.title: Conservation agriculture
993e22079c10.sentence: Examples of these disadvantages include high initial costs of specialized planting equipment, and a new dynamic farming system that requires new management skills and a learning process by the farmer.

9a9d5b9d9d6f.title: Conservation agriculture
9a9d5b9d9d6f.sentence: The application of CA requires a critical level of crop residues remaining on the surface, while traditionally most of these residues are used for feeding livestock.

99bd6d4b2fea.title: Climate-smart agriculture
99bd6d4b2fea.sentence: Direct GHG emissions include those from rice and livestock farming.

63dae5c01996.title: Climate-smart agriculture
63dae5c01996.sentence: Indirect emissions from the conversion of non-agricultural land such as forests into agricultural land are also important.

f5a9e3541fe3.title: Climate-smart agriculture
f5a9e3541fe3.sentence: Greenhouse gas emissions from the agriculture, forestry, and land use sectors contribute 13%–21% of global GHG emissions.

c831ceec7266.title: Climate-smart agriculture
c831ceec7266.sentence: With regard to direct emissions, nitrous oxide and methane makeup over half of total GHG emissions from agriculture.

045226612ef9.title: Climate-smart agriculture
045226612ef9.section: Major initiatives > Global Roadmap to 2050 for Food and Agriculture
045226612ef9.sentence: Livestock production (beef, pork, chicken, sheep, and milk) alone accounts for almost 60% of total global food system GHG emissions.

251b05cef82a.title: Carbon farming
251b05cef82a.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting livestock grazing
251b05cef82a.sentence: Ruminants like cows and sheep produce not only CO2, but also methane due to the microbes residing in their digestive system.

0ba3a06b7741.title: Climate-smart agriculture
0ba3a06b7741.sentence: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA), or climate resilient agriculture, is a set of farming methods that has three main objectives with regard to climate change.

d6170a9ab5b4.title: Climate-smart agriculture
d6170a9ab5b4.sentence: First, they use adaptation methods to respond to the effects of climate change on agriculture (this also builds resilience to climate change).

45f60410d867.title: Climate-smart agriculture
45f60410d867.sentence: Second, they aim to increase agricultural productivity and to ensure food security for a growing world population.

928b7704ed80.title: Climate-smart agriculture
928b7704ed80.sentence: Third, they try to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture as much as possible (e.g., by following carbon farming approaches).

993c25c9b843.title: Climate-smart agriculture
993c25c9b843.sentence: The World Bank Group described climate-smart agriculture (CSA) as follows: "CSA is a set of agricultural practices and technologies which simultaneously boost productivity, enhance resilience and reduce GHG emissions." Also, "CSA is an integrated approach to managing landscapes—cropland, livestock, forests and fisheries--that address the interlinked challenges of food security and climate change."

07b6696ee1f0.title: Climate-smart agriculture
07b6696ee1f0.sentence: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) says CSA "is not a new set of sustainability practices or production systems, but an approach that involves different elements embedded in local contexts.

481de771281a.title: Climate-smart agriculture
481de771281a.sentence: CSA can include the planting of heat tolerant crop varieties, mulching, boundary trees, and appropriate housing and spacing for cattle.

f457eabfd9e8.title: Climate-smart agriculture
f457eabfd9e8.sentence: Carbon farming is one of the components of CSA and aims at reducing or removing greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture.

fa3bb9342ce1.title: Climate-smart agriculture
fa3bb9342ce1.sentence: Rainfed agriculture accounts for 80% of global agriculture.

4ec8c405c6ee.title: Climate-smart agriculture
4ec8c405c6ee.sentence: Many of the 852 million poor people in the world live in parts of Asia and Africa that depend on rainfall to cultivate food crops.

81b6b7289358.title: Climate-smart agriculture
81b6b7289358.sentence: The greatest concern with CSA is that no universally accepted standard exists against which those who call themselves climate-smart are actually acting smart.

88dc81eca766.title: Climate-smart agriculture
88dc81eca766.sentence: Until those certifications are created and met, skeptics are concerned that big businesses will continue to use the name to greenwash their organizations—or provide a false sense of environmental stewardship.

0789f2c1cb93.title: Climate-smart agriculture
0789f2c1cb93.sentence: In 2014, The Guardian reported that climate-smart agriculture had been criticized as a form of greenwashing.

b5d5cac9b038.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
b5d5cac9b038.sentence: Biodiversity in agriculture is the measure of biodiversity found on agricultural land.

0752a7459c89.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
0752a7459c89.sentence: In agricultural areas, biodiversity decreases as varying landscapes are lost and native plants are replaced with cultivated crops.

ca22c9bac6f2.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
ca22c9bac6f2.sentence: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations estimates that more than 40% of Earth's land surface is currently used for agriculture.

f86dcc9839de.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
f86dcc9839de.sentence: Because so much land has been converted to agriculture, habitat loss is recognized as the driving force in biodiversity loss.

907767fbae66.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
907767fbae66.sentence: Land that is not cropped, such as fallow land, grass margins in the spaces between different fields, and strips of scrub along field boundaries increase heterogeneity and thus the biodiversity of a farm.

a3e72ec6a7eb.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
a3e72ec6a7eb.sentence: Of the features associated with species diversity is land size, where a study proved a relationship between smaller agricultural fields and increased species richness.

e567836a9266.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
e567836a9266.sentence: In Asian rice, one study showed crop diversification by growing flowering crops in strips beside rice fields could reduce pests so that insecticide spraying was reduced by 70%, yields increase by 5%, together resulting in an economic advantage of 7.5%.

6d4fb388d1d0.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
6d4fb388d1d0.sentence: For example, low crop diversity can increase pests and their resistance to pesticides, resulting in large ecological disturbances and economical losses.

8187b299ad03.title: Agricultural pollution
8187b299ad03.sentence: Not all nutrient applied through fertilizer are taken up by the crops, and the remainder accumulates in the soil or is lost as runoff.

907718f8b7ed.title: Agricultural pollution
907718f8b7ed.sentence: Although leading to increased crop yield, nitrogen fertilizers can also negatively affect groundwater and surface waters, pollute the atmosphere, and degrade soil health.

4e09295361a6.title: Agricultural pollution
4e09295361a6.sentence: > With average crop yields remaining at the 1900 level the crop harvest in the year 2000 would have required nearly four times more land and the cultivated area would have claimed nearly half of all ice-free continents, rather than under 15% of the total land area that is required today.

a4f6eb5ff3ca.title: Agricultural pollution
a4f6eb5ff3ca.sentence: High application rates of nitrogen-containing fertilizers combined with the high water-solubility of nitrate leads to increased runoff into surface water as well as leaching into groundwater, thereby causing groundwater pollution.

1dfe168cafb8.title: Agricultural pollution
1dfe168cafb8.sentence: Nitrate levels above 10 mg/L (10 ppm) in groundwater can cause "blue baby syndrome" (acquired methemoglobinemia) in infants and possibly thyroid disease and various types of cancer.

2acfca2a00d5.title: Agricultural pollution
2acfca2a00d5.sentence: Phosphorus is largest contributor to eutrophication, especially in freshwaters.

b7a95c8288b0.title: Agricultural pollution
b7a95c8288b0.sentence: Fertilization can also release N2O which is a greenhouse gas and can facilitate the destruction of ozone (O3) in the stratosphere.

24bd8f034d4f.title: Sustainable agriculture
24bd8f034d4f.sentence: Ecological farming is a concept that focused on the environmental aspects of sustainable agriculture.

043575751002.title: Sustainable agriculture
043575751002.sentence: Ecological farming includes all methods, including organic, which regenerate ecosystem services like: prevention of soil erosion, water infiltration and retention, carbon sequestration in the form of humus, and increased biodiversity.

990184af696c.title: Sustainable agriculture
990184af696c.sentence: Many techniques are used including no-till farming, multispecies cover crops, strip cropping, terrace cultivation, shelter belts, pasture cropping etc.

7e4c89b0b627.title: Sustainable agriculture
7e4c89b0b627.sentence: Crop genetic diversity is one method that is used to reduce the risks associated with monoculture crops, which can be susceptible to a changing climate.

24962ae32c54.title: Sustainable agriculture
24962ae32c54.sentence: Previously described as a "mixed strategy", a term considered too ambiguous in ecology, land blending is an intermediate approach between land sparing and land sharing.

28d13c6f4960.title: Sustainable agriculture
28d13c6f4960.sentence: Unlike these two traditionally opposed strategies, land blending offers a flexible combination of the two approaches, adapted to the specific landscape features.

0b14a5a877f9.title: Sustainable agriculture
0b14a5a877f9.sentence: This third strategy has only recently emerged as a credible and viable alternative to the traditional land sparing and land sharing.

d4009ada36d2.title: Sustainable agriculture
d4009ada36d2.sentence: Recent research has highlighted its potential for effectively reconciling biodiversity conservation and agricultural production, while enhancing resilience in the face of change and uncertainty.

6261b7dc59e8.title: Sustainable agriculture
6261b7dc59e8.section: Challenges and debates > Different viewpoints about the definition
6261b7dc59e8.sentence: The central argument of multifunctionality is that agriculture is a multifunctional enterprise with other functions aside from the production of food and fiber.

7269a536055a.title: Sustainable agriculture
7269a536055a.section: Challenges and debates > Different viewpoints about the definition
7269a536055a.sentence: These functions include renewable resource management, landscape conservation and biodiversity.

8268ad77dfa8.title: Sustainable agriculture
8268ad77dfa8.section: Challenges and debates > Different viewpoints about the definition
8268ad77dfa8.sentence: Those that employ the multifunctional agriculture philosophy focus on farm-centered approaches, and define function as being the outputs of agricultural activity.

8c1ad55a960a.title: Sustainable agriculture
8c1ad55a960a.section: Challenges and debates > Different viewpoints about the definition
8c1ad55a960a.sentence: The ecosystem service-centered approach posits that individuals and society as a whole receive benefits from ecosystems, which are called "ecosystem services".

d552d2db24b8.title: Sustainable agriculture
d552d2db24b8.section: Challenges and debates > Different viewpoints about the definition
d552d2db24b8.sentence: In sustainable agriculture, the services that ecosystems provide include pollination, soil formation, and nutrient cycling, all of which are necessary functions for the production of food.

e40001099660.title: Crop rotation
e40001099660.sentence: Agronomists describe the benefits to yield in rotated crops as "The Rotation Effect".

801f223ef887.title: Crop rotation
801f223ef887.sentence: The factors related to the increase are broadly due to alleviation of the negative factors of monoculture cropping systems.

eb064b63946a.title: Crop rotation
eb064b63946a.sentence: Specifically, improved nutrition; pest, pathogen, and weed stress reduction; and improved soil structure have been found in some cases to be correlated to beneficial rotation effects.

6f6510c10962.title: Crop rotation
6f6510c10962.sentence: Available land was divided into three sections.

c95545aad00d.title: Crop rotation
c95545aad00d.sentence: The first section grew autumn planted crops such as rye and wheat.

8bce74801fef.title: Crop rotation
8bce74801fef.sentence: The second section grew spring planted crops such as oats; barley; and legumes: peas, lentils, or beans.

9ba7debb85ff.title: Crop rotation
9ba7debb85ff.sentence: The third section was left fallow.

1d138b980dc3.title: Crop rotation
1d138b980dc3.sentence: From the 9th century to the 11th century, farmers in Europe transitioned from a two-field system to a three-field system.

784edc4edb90.title: Crop rotation
784edc4edb90.sentence: This system persisted until the 20th century.

5df292bf0bd9.title: Crop rotation
5df292bf0bd9.sentence: Under the new three-field rotation system, two thirds of the land was planted, potentially yielding a larger harvest.

ed9e769bb8b6.title: Crop rotation
ed9e769bb8b6.sentence: Since the spring crops were mostly legumes, which fix nitrogen needed for plants to make proteins, they increased the overall nutrition of the people of Europe.

9553ba9a6b56.title: Crop rotation
9553ba9a6b56.sentence: The British agriculturist Charles Townshend (1674–1738) popularised this system in the 18th century.

c25cda40c60c.title: Crop rotation
c25cda40c60c.sentence: The sequence of four crops (wheat, turnips, barley and clover), included a fodder crop and a grazing crop, allowing livestock to be bred year-round.

f95e1c518350.title: Crop rotation
f95e1c518350.sentence: The four-field crop rotation became a key development in the British Agricultural Revolution.

b06f0e78e3a1.title: Agroforestry
b06f0e78e3a1.sentence: With alley cropping, crop strips alternate with rows of closely spaced tree or hedge species.

caafce172399.title: Agroforestry
caafce172399.sentence: Normally, the trees are pruned before planting the crop.

9178ee7c665a.title: Agroforestry
9178ee7c665a.sentence: The cut leafy material - for example, from Alchornea cordifolia and Acioa barteri - is spread over the crop area to provide nutrients.

26039d7284a2.title: Agroforestry
26039d7284a2.sentence: The hedges serve as windbreaks and reduce erosion.

492a35048d0c.title: Agroforestry
492a35048d0c.sentence: Weed control is inherent to the practice, providing mulch and shade.

d16500231e15.title: Agroforestry
d16500231e15.sentence: Forest farming is the cultivation of high-value specialty crops under a forest canopy that is intentionally modified or maintained to provide shade levels and habitat that favor growth and enhance production levels.

454f87f13598.title: Agroforestry
454f87f13598.sentence: In forest farming, high-value crops are grown under a suitably-managed tree canopy.

7f3d59c374ce.title: Agroforestry
7f3d59c374ce.sentence: Forest farming encompasses a range of cultivated systems from introducing plants into the understory of a timber stand to modifying forest stands to enhance the marketability and sustainable production of existing plants.

bb4769fd6a35.title: Agroforestry
bb4769fd6a35.sentence: In 1929, J. Russell Smith, emeritus Professor of Economic Geography at Columbia University, published "Tree Crops – A Permanent Agriculture," which stated that crop-yielding trees could provide useful substitutes for cereals in animal feeding programs, as well as conserve environmental health.

9df5a3f33050.title: Agroforestry
9df5a3f33050.sentence: Forest gardening is a low-maintenance, sustainable, plant-based food production and agroforestry system based on woodland ecosystems, incorporating fruit and nut trees, shrubs, herbs, vines and perennial vegetables which have yields directly useful to humans.

c038c5451c4c.title: Agroforestry
c038c5451c4c.sentence: Making use of companion planting, these can be intermixed to grow in a succession of layers to build a woodland habitat.

64fa671af1db.title: Agroforestry
64fa671af1db.sentence: Forest gardens are probably the world's oldest form of land use and most resilient agroecosystem.

fa1372abec52.title: Agroforestry
fa1372abec52.sentence: Forest gardens, or home gardens, are common in the tropics, using intercropping to cultivate trees, crops, and livestock on the same land.

98e257ae7ce2.title: Agroforestry
98e257ae7ce2.sentence: They have been shown to be a significant source of income and food security for local populations.

fbc27ab77464.title: Agroforestry
fbc27ab77464.sentence: In the 1980s, Robert Hart coined the term "forest gardening" after adapting the principles and applying them to temperate climates.

97f2ca618df4.title: Agroforestry
97f2ca618df4.sentence: Robert Hart adapted forest gardening for the United Kingdom's temperate climate during the 1980s.

1c9e10a87636.title: Agroforestry

8e38909e4534.sentence: Anaerobic digestion is the biological treatment of liquid animal waste using bacteria in an area absent of air, which promotes the decomposition of organic solids.

a20604a24803.title: Agricultural pollution
a20604a24803.section: Biotic sources > Animal management > Manure treatment > Anaerobic digestion and lagoons
a20604a24803.sentence: The remaining liquid is nutrient rich and can be used on fields as a fertilizer and methane gas that can be burned directly on the biogas stove or in an engine generator to produce electricity and heat.

6dd6cba161b4.title: Agricultural pollution
6dd6cba161b4.sentence: Pesticide persistence is nonetheless a major issue.

77ac4f5afd56.title: Agricultural pollution
77ac4f5afd56.sentence: For example 2,4-D and atrazine have with lifetimes up to 20 years.

31183976809c.title: Agricultural pollution
31183976809c.sentence: It has been conceded that in the absence of pest control measures, crop losses before harvesting would typically amount to 40 percent.

fd8d1d144bcd.title: Agricultural pollution
fd8d1d144bcd.sentence: DDT, aldrin, dieldrin, endrin, heptachlor, and toxaphene are also long-lived.

35140d7ea4d7.title: Intercropping
35140d7ea4d7.sentence: Inga alley cropping offers an alternative to the ecologically destructive slash and burn cultivation.

193afe78dd29.title: Intercropping
193afe78dd29.sentence: They are leguminous, fixing nitrogen into a form usable by plants.

610540935088.title: Intercropping
610540935088.sentence: The leaves form a thick mulch that protects both soil and roots from sun and rain.

10961bfc71a8.title: Intercropping
10961bfc71a8.sentence: It increases yields and is more sustainable as it allows the land to be cultivated repeatedly, eliminating the need for slash and burn to get fertile plots.

20643be5581e.title: Intercropping
20643be5581e.sentence: The technique was developed and trialled by tropical ecologist Mike Hands in Costa Rica in the late 1980s and early '90s.

f327a7501869.title: Intercropping
f327a7501869.sentence: Further temporal separation is found in relay cropping, where the second crop is sown during the growth, often near the onset of reproductive development or fruiting, of the first crop, so that the first crop is harvested to make room for the full development of the second.

94b0455dc78b.title: Intercropping
94b0455dc78b.sentence: Temporal intercropping uses the practice of sowing a fast-growing crop with a slow-growing crop, so that the fast-growing crop is harvested before the slow-growing crop starts to mature.

c1e65239bc18.title: Intercropping
c1e65239bc18.sentence: This can provide greater yield than either crop alone.

3f3d9d3ccf23.title: Silvopasture
3f3d9d3ccf23.sentence: Wood pasture, one of the oldest land-use practices in human history, is a historical European land management system in which open woodland provided shelter and forage for grazing animals, particularly sheep and cattle, as well as woodland products such as timber for construction and fuel, coppiced stems for wattle and charcoal making and pollarded poles.

cb710e436d8e.title: Silvopasture
cb710e436d8e.sentence: Since Roman times, pigs have been released into beech and oak woodlands to feed on the acorn and beech mast, and into fruit orchards to eat fallen fruit.

64dd8483f3e4.title: Landscape-scale conservation
64dd8483f3e4.sentence: Integrated landscape management is a way of managing sustainable landscapes by bringing together multiple stakeholders with different land use objectives.

1d23339061ad.title: Landscape-scale conservation
1d23339061ad.sentence: In 2012 Scherr invented a new term, integrated landscape management(ILM), to describe her ideas for developing entire regions, not at just a farm or plot level.

99771229ab49.title: Landscape-scale conservation
99771229ab49.sentence: By 2016 it had five elements, namely:

e5ea489c6df6.title: Landscape-scale conservation
e5ea489c6df6.sentence: - stakeholders come together for cooperative dialogue and action;

eb11a6fd5958.title: Landscape-scale conservation
eb11a6fd5958.sentence: - they exchange information systematically and discuss perspectives to achieve a shared understanding of the landscape conditions, challenges and opportunities;

25c4fc588ebc.title: Landscape-scale conservation
25c4fc588ebc.sentence: - collaborative planning to develop an agreed action plan;

a8166876b683.title: Landscape-scale conservation
a8166876b683.sentence: - monitoring and dialogue to adapt management.

72bc3b7d1e5b.title: Landscape-scale conservation
72bc3b7d1e5b.sentence: - Emphasis on synergies: It tries to exploit "synergies" among conservation, agricultural production, and rural livelihoods.

ed086468aade.title: Riparian buffer
ed086468aade.sentence: An alternative to the fixed width design is to adapt the buffer width according to local hydrological conditions.

51f6081b56dc.title: Riparian buffer
51f6081b56dc.sentence: The amount of groundwater running into a stream is not always constant but can be concentrated in certain hotspots following topography.

4b3e68410ecc.title: Riparian buffer
4b3e68410ecc.sentence: These groundwater discharge hotspots are connected to many riparian buffer functions such as: controlling stream water temperature, soil pH and acidity of the stream water and nutrient cycling and retention in the riparian zone.

e47823c15aa1.title: Riparian buffer
e47823c15aa1.sentence: These discharge zones can extend further into the landscape than fixed riparian buffers widths but are disproportionately important to the buffer's functioning.

76992c4e58b8.title: Riparian buffer
76992c4e58b8.sentence: To create buffers that take hydrology and ground water levels into account, soil wetness maps can be created from digital elevation models.

d81216f02b6a.title: Riparian buffer
d81216f02b6a.sentence: These maps can identify areas where riparian buffers should be wider than a fixed-width buffer.

3c7dd0dc9195.title: Riparian buffer
3c7dd0dc9195.sentence: Designing buffer zones based on their hydrological function instead of a traditionally used fixed width method, can be economically beneficial in forestry practices.

9df9dd08c633.title: Riparian buffer
9df9dd08c633.sentence: A riparian buffer is usually split into three different zones, each having its own specific purpose for filtering runoff and interacting with the adjacent aquatic system.

a3fde53f0188.title: Riparian buffer
a3fde53f0188.sentence: This zone should function mainly to shade the water source and act as a bank stabilizer.

2f629335cad4.title: Riparian buffer
2f629335cad4.sentence: The zone should include large native tree species that grow fast and can quickly act to perform these tasks.

b6fc8a31646c.title: Riparian buffer
b6fc8a31646c.sentence: Usually made up of native shrubs, this zone provides a habitat for wildlife, including nesting areas for bird species.

c6a7e14cb29e.title: Riparian buffer
c6a7e14cb29e.sentence: This zone also acts to slow and absorb contaminants that Zone 3 has missed.

a0f838346beb.title: Riparian buffer
a0f838346beb.sentence: This zone is important as the first line of defense against contaminants.

343d036ebf6e.title: Riparian buffer
343d036ebf6e.sentence: It consists mostly of native grasses and serves primarily to slow water runoff and begin to absorb contaminants before they reach the other zones.

5d4851bc381e.title: Riparian buffer
5d4851bc381e.sentence: It is generally recommended that native species be chosen to plant in these three zones, with the general width of the buffer being 50 feet (15 m) on each side of the stream.

b7bc0cacc0b0.title: Conservation agriculture
b7bc0cacc0b0.sentence: In 1992, 'agri-environment schemes' became compulsory for all European Union Member States.

660433bce77b.title: Conservation agriculture
660433bce77b.sentence: As the changes in practices that ensure the protection of the environment are costly to farmers, the EU developed agri-environment schemes to financially compensate individual farmers for applying these changes and therefore increased the implementation of conservation agriculture.

022528b48a51.title: Conservation agriculture
022528b48a51.sentence: The schemes are voluntary for farmers.

f6d7e65e4735.title: Conservation agriculture
f6d7e65e4735.sentence: Once joined, they commit to a minimum of five years during which they have to adopt various sustainable farming techniques.

6844bea9ced0.title: Conservation agriculture
6844bea9ced0.sentence: According to the Euro-stat website, in 2009 the agricultural area enrolled in agri-environment schemes covered 38.5 million hectares (20.9% of agricultural land in the 27 member states of the EU at the time) (Agri-environmental indicator 2015).

0e6bf195742e.title: Conservation agriculture
0e6bf195742e.sentence: The European Commission spent a total of €3.23 billion on agri-environment schemes in 2012, significantly exceeding the cost of managing special sites of conservation (Natura 2000) that year, which came to a total of €39.6 million (Batáry et al. 2015).

ae9003237a96.title: Conservation agriculture
ae9003237a96.sentence: Initially, they sought to protect threatened habitats, but gradually shifted their focus to the prevention of the loss of wildlife from agricultural landscapes.

2f5423a7600a.title: Conservation agriculture
2f5423a7600a.sentence: Most recently, the schemes are placing more emphasis on improving the services that the land can provide to humans (e.g. pollination).

6a4896f78689.title: Conservation agriculture
6a4896f78689.sentence: In a 2015 review of studies examining the effects of the two schemes, it was found that out-of-production schemes had a higher success rate at enhancing the number of thriving species around the land.

ac86d2239946.title: Hedge
ac86d2239946.sentence: In essence, hedgelaying consists of cutting most of the way through the stem of each plant near the base, bending it over and interweaving or pleaching it between wooden stakes.

aefddf39f682.title: Hedge
aefddf39f682.sentence: This also encourages new growth from the base of each plant.

b2116f0f8339.title: Hedge
b2116f0f8339.sentence: Originally, the main purpose of hedgelaying was to ensure the hedge remained stock-proof.

f8fd2ea387a7.title: Hedge
f8fd2ea387a7.sentence: Hooper's rule (or Hooper's law, named after Dr. Max Hooper) is based on ecological data obtained from hedges of known age, and suggests that the age of a hedge can be roughly estimated by counting the number of woody species in a thirty-yard section and multiplying by 110 years.

63bd89a07a9c.title: Hedge
63bd89a07a9c.sentence: Max Hooper published his original formula in the book Hedges in 1974.

fe6425c8704b.title: Hedge
fe6425c8704b.sentence: This method is only a rule of thumb, and can be off by a couple of centuries; it should always be backed up by documentary evidence, if possible, and take into account other factors.

3aee7ecd2b14.title: Hedge
3aee7ecd2b14.sentence: The formula also does not work on hedges more than a thousand years old.

50913632b390.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
50913632b390.sentence: Heterogeneity, the diversity of the landscape, has been shown to be associated with species diversity.

d8a4d4c742f0.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
d8a4d4c742f0.sentence: Heterogeneity is essential in increasing species heterogeneity, which maintain stable ecological structures essential to providing ecosystem services.

9d98334a8a31.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
9d98334a8a31.sentence: For example, butterfly abundance has been found to increase with heterogeneity.

1de71ba4fe57.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
1de71ba4fe57.sentence: Since 1966, the Green Revolution enhanced agricultural productivity through technological, economic, and political advancements in an effort to increase food security globally.

c65e5ea102fe.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
c65e5ea102fe.sentence: These advancements also led to increased global geographical spread of 52 agricultural crops with cereals such as wheat, rice, and maize showing the greatest increase in the past 50 years.

e9026d060158.title: Biodiversity in agriculture
e9026d060158.sentence: The loss of agricultural heterogeneity decreases local food security due to a loss in crop diversity, despite its accommodation of global food demands.

ac690a4eb1aa.title: Regenerative economics
ac690a4eb1aa.sentence: Regenerative economics is an economic system that works to regenerate capital assets.

af041dd2973d.title: Regenerative economics
af041dd2973d.sentence: Regenerative economics is based on the notion of Earth as the original capital asset, and so places value on the environment.

d342148a93d7.title: Regenerative economics
d342148a93d7.sentence: In standard economic theory, one can either “regenerate” one's capital assets or consume them until the asset cannot produce a viable stream of goods and/or services.

fc96f3c0cbf8.title: Regenerative economics
fc96f3c0cbf8.sentence: Proponents of regenerative economics believe that disregarding this value has created the unsustainable economic condition referred to as uneconomic growth, a phrase coined by leading ecological economist and steady-state theorist Herman Daly.

6e45e07034c5.title: Regenerative economics
6e45e07034c5.sentence: The authors of the regenerative economic theory believe uneconomic growth is the opposite of regenerative economics.

d73c9754e737.title: Regenerative economics
d73c9754e737.sentence: There are four components of regenerative economics: circulation, organizational structure, relationships and values, and collective learning.

a7daf2c24baa.title: Regenerative economics
a7daf2c24baa.sentence: It focuses on setting systematic limits to the current economic system, unlike regenerative economics' focus on reproduction of life in nature.

9abadf83e7fe.title: Regenerative economics
9abadf83e7fe.sentence: Regenerative finance (ReFi) is an approach to investing that builds on sustainable finance to promote ecological health, social well-being, and economic resilience in accordance with principles of regenerative economics.

eca23ad2bfec.title: Regenerative economics
eca23ad2bfec.sentence: This approach often includes, but is not limited to, the use of decentralized finance.

0684c7827744.title: Integrated pest management
0684c7827744.sentence: Integrated pest management (IPM), also known as integrated pest control (IPC) combines both non-chemical and chemical practices for economic control of pests, reducing reliance on chemicals while improving productivity and health.

23e7565864be.title: Integrated pest management
23e7565864be.sentence: It combines biological, chemical, physical and crop specific (cultural) management strategies and practices to grow healthy crops and minimize the use of pesticides, reducing or minimizing risks posed by pesticides to human health and the environment for sustainable pest management."

0ec315e7c6c9.title: Integrated pest management
0ec315e7c6c9.sentence: Acceptable pest levels—IPM holds that wiping out an entire pest population is often impossible, and the attempt can be expensive and unsafe.

7ddb3fe77b66.title: Integrated pest management
7ddb3fe77b66.sentence: Emphasis is placed on control, not eradication.

d7769daa5a3c.title: Integrated pest management
d7769daa5a3c.sentence: Cultural practices—The first line of defense for a garden or farm is to select varieties suited to local growing conditions such as resistant varieties and maintain healthy crops.

70e369454c20.title: Integrated pest management
70e369454c20.sentence: Cultural practices may include techniques such as crop rotation and intercropping to promote healthy growing conditions.

0e9ef2f13184.title: Integrated pest management
0e9ef2f13184.sentence: IPM is a safer pest control framework than reliance on chemical pesticides, mitigating risks such as insecticide-induced resurgence, pesticide resistance and (especially food) crop residues.

b682b779ac74.title: Integrated pest management
b682b779ac74.sentence: Similarly, the repeated use of a single class of controls will create pest populations that are more resistant to that class, whereas alternating among classes helps prevent this.

b08763ac4847.title: Integrated pest management
b08763ac4847.sentence: Using these components, integrated pest management becomes an ongoing process that can be thought of in terms of six repeatable steps:

25181cefe364.title: Integrated pest management
25181cefe364.sentence: Step 1 | Sample for Pests (Inspect and Monitor) | Is there a real problem?

a81790c3cee5.title: Integrated pest management
a81790c3cee5.sentence: Step 2 | Proper Identification | Is it really the pest you think it is?

97d8ec882b14.title: Integrated pest management
97d8ec882b14.sentence: Step 3 | Learn the Pest Biology | Will it be a long-term problem or will it be gone next week?

38d4766eb279.title: Integrated pest management
38d4766eb279.sentence: Step 4 | Determine an Action Threshold | Do you need to act?

1e32c29cb8ad.title: Integrated pest management
1e32c29cb8ad.sentence: Step 5 | Choose Tactics | What's the best treatment?

aff24eb9d723.title: Integrated pest management
aff24eb9d723.sentence: Step 6 | Evaluate | How did it work?

8b3ab6789f48.title: Integrated pest management
8b3ab6789f48.sentence: In 1986, Indonesia banned 57 pesticides and completely stopped subsidizing their use.

5ad823eee8b5.title: Integrated pest management
5ad823eee8b5.sentence: In the United States, the idea that "biological and chemical control are considered as supplementary to one another" was stated as early as 1939, in an influential paper by California entomologists William Muriece Hoskins, Arthur D. Borden, and Abraham E. Michelbacher.

c87d479a608d.title: Integrated pest management
c87d479a608d.sentence: An economic injury level is the pest population level at which damage to a crop will be greater than the cost of treating the pest.

0c8a5dfe2cb5.title: Integrated pest management
0c8a5dfe2cb5.sentence: An economic threshold is the population size at which action must be taken to prevent the pest population from reaching the economic injury level.

2059d2bae1b7.title: Integrated pest management
2059d2bae1b7.sentence: IPM programs identify acceptable pest levels or action thresholds based on estimated economic injury, and apply controls if those thresholds are exceeded.

122f978b3ea4.title: Integrated pest management
122f978b3ea4.sentence: Thresholds are pest and site specific, meaning that it may be acceptable to have a weed such at one site, but not at another site.

6fe78061881c.title: Integrated pest management
6fe78061881c.sentence: Allowing a pest population to survive at a reasonable threshold reduces selection pressure.

045946706861.title: Intercropping
045946706861.sentence: - Push-pull cropping, this is a mixture of trap cropping and repellant intercropping.

85f5f942fd94.title: Intercropping
85f5f942fd94.sentence: An attractant crop attracts the pest and a repellant crop is also used to repel the pest away.

10cbcbd26d2f.title: Intercropping
10cbcbd26d2f.sentence: In a review of 100 trap cropping examples in 2006, only 10 trap crops were classified as successful at a commercial scale, and in all successful cases, trap cropping was supplemented with management practices that specifically limited insect dispersal from the trap crop back into the main crop.

78a16084ec2f.title: Greenwashing
78a16084ec2f.sentence: Greenwashing, or Green Sheen, is any advertisement or PR campaign designed to deceive the public into thinking an organization's products, goals, or policies are environmentally friendly.

4c2678e9b462.title: Greenwashing
4c2678e9b462.sentence: The term is a compound of 'Green' and 'Whitewashing'.

1231714278a0.title: Greenwashing
1231714278a0.sentence: Firms engage in greenwashing for three primary reasons: to gain legitimacy among people concerned for the environment, to project an image of environmental responsibility or broader sustainability to the wider public, and to distance themselves from their environmental lapses or those of their suppliers.

9f791aa3b4e2.title: Greenwashing
9f791aa3b4e2.sentence: A common rule of thumb for determining if an organization is greenwashing is whether an organization spends significantly more resources on advertising a 'green' image than actually doing environmentally sound practices.

daa1a8780463.title: Greenwashing
daa1a8780463.sentence: Since there is no universally agreed definition of greenwashing, determining whether a given instance is or isn't greenwashing can be challenging for consumers and regulatory bodies.

dbed880de328.title: Greenwashing
dbed880de328.sentence: The term is subjective, and depends on interpreting an action as genuine or purely concerned with boosting an organization's image.

18efea4f58ba.title: Greenwashing
18efea4f58ba.sentence: The term "greenwashing" was coined by New York environmentalist Jay Westerveld in a 1986 essay about the hotel industry's hypocritical practice of placing notices in bedrooms promoting the reuse of towels to "save the environment".

2d42c45ec498.title: Greenwashing
2d42c45ec498.sentence: He noted that these institutions often made little or no effort toward reducing energy waste, although towel reuse saved them laundry costs.

b35f2f8b5557.title: Greenwashing
b35f2f8b5557.sentence: A 2020 European Union study found that over 50% of examined environmental claims in the EU were vague, misleading, or unfounded, while 40% of them were unsubstantiated.

3df40717452d.title: Greenwashing
3df40717452d.sentence: Many companies have committed to reducing their greenhouse gas emissions to net zero after the Paris Agreement was signed in 2015.

2cc5130a7ab2.title: Greenwashing
2cc5130a7ab2.sentence: However, companies are not actually cutting emissions, but are creating unfeasible plans and attempting to improve other things rather than their emissions.

08dc9a7001fd.title: Greenwashing
08dc9a7001fd.sentence: Critics of the practice suggest that the rise of greenwashing, combined with ineffective regulation and lack of its actual enforcement, contributes to consumer skepticism of all green claims and diminishes the power of consumer choice to influence companies toward greener manufacturing processes and business operations.

08dbeb921902.title: Monoculture
08dbeb921902.sentence: In agriculture, monoculture is the practice of growing one crop species in a field at a time.

1f16702a3aeb.title: Monoculture
1f16702a3aeb.sentence: Monocultures increase ease and efficiency in planting, managing, and harvesting crops short-term, often with the help of machinery.

14f296825aa9.title: Monoculture
14f296825aa9.sentence: In crop monocultures, each plant in a field has the same standardized planting, maintenance, and harvesting requirements resulting in greater yields and lower costs.

06c67c610542.title: Monoculture
06c67c610542.sentence: However, monocultures are more susceptible to diseases or pest outbreaks long-term due to localized reductions in biodiversity and nutrient depletion.

ecc21360b580.title: Monoculture
ecc21360b580.sentence: Crop diversity can be added both in time, as with a crop rotation or sequence, or in space, with a polyculture or intercropping.

3ee05b95711a.title: Monoculture
3ee05b95711a.sentence: Modern practices such as monoculture planting and the use of synthesized fertilizers have reduced the amount of additional land needed to produce food, called land sparing.

17561bcf7610.title: Monoculture
17561bcf7610.sentence: Monocultures of perennials, such as African palm oil, sugarcane, tea and pines, can change soil chemistry leading to soil acidification, degradation, and soil-borne diseases, ultimately having a negative impact on agricultural productivity and sustainability.

34b5ac494d07.title: Monoculture
34b5ac494d07.sentence: As soil health declines, use of synthetic fertilizers on monocultural fields increases, often having negative implications on human health via chemical run-off.

c96066a0242c.title: Monoculture
c96066a0242c.sentence: For example, excess nitrogen from synthetic fertilizers can leach into ground and surface waters, leading to nitrate contamination of drinking water.

5c47b76ae334.title: Monoculture
5c47b76ae334.sentence: Agricultural runoff can also degrade aquatic ecosystems through nutrient loading, which subsequently leads to eutrophication harmful algal blooms (HABs).

6537abe0f261.title: Monoculture
6537abe0f261.sentence: Following pest outbreaks, over 600 million liters of pesticides are sprayed annually, contaminating nearby small-scale farming and causing communal health decline.

b1aa8329f4be.title: Monoculture
b1aa8329f4be.sentence: Agroecological practices, silvo-pastoral systems, and mixed-species plantations are common alternatives to monoculture that help preserve biodiversity while maintaining productivity.

ccba1695acaf.title: Albedo
ccba1695acaf.sentence: Albedo (/ælˈbiːdoʊ/ ⓘ al-BEE-doh; from Latin albedo 'whiteness') is the fraction of sunlight that is diffusely reflected by a body.

d7839142383e.title: Albedo
d7839142383e.sentence: It is measured on a scale from 0 (corresponding to a black body that absorbs all incident radiation) to 1 (corresponding to a body that reflects all incident radiation).

4a531410f332.title: Albedo
4a531410f332.sentence: The albedo in visible light ranges from about 0.9 to 0.95 for fresh snow to about 0.04 for charcoal, one of the darkest substances.

d55b751ef549.title: Albedo
d55b751ef549.sentence: When seen from a distance, the ocean surface has a low albedo, as do most forests, whereas desert areas have some of the highest albedos among landforms.

5345491ec2c4.title: Albedo
5345491ec2c4.section: Examples of terrestrial albedo effects > Climate and weather
5345491ec2c4.sentence: Albedo affects climate by determining how much radiation a planet absorbs.

1fd59205e3cb.title: Albedo
1fd59205e3cb.section: Examples of terrestrial albedo effects > Trees
1fd59205e3cb.sentence: Deciduous trees have an albedo value of about 0.15 to 0.18 whereas coniferous trees have a value of about 0.09 to 0.15.

c60c4bbe49df.title: Albedo
c60c4bbe49df.section: Terrestrial albedo > Changes to albedo due to human activities
c60c4bbe49df.sentence: Human activities (e.g., deforestation, farming, and urbanization) change the albedo of various areas around the globe.

0ff5f0acef48.title: Albedo
0ff5f0acef48.section: Terrestrial albedo > Changes to albedo due to human activities
0ff5f0acef48.sentence: Human impacts to "the physical properties of the land surface can perturb the climate by altering the Earth's radiative energy balance" even on a small scale or when undetected by satellites.

caaebb5154bf.title: Albedo
caaebb5154bf.sentence: The term albedo was introduced into optics by Johann Heinrich Lambert in his 1760 work Photometria.

321dff2dcdc1.title: Tree planting
321dff2dcdc1.sentence: Tree planting is the process of transplanting tree seedlings, generally for forestry, land reclamation, or landscaping purposes.

35f007ed1bdb.title: Tree planting
35f007ed1bdb.sentence: In silviculture, the activity is known as "reforestation", or "afforestation," depending on whether the area being planted has recently been forested or not.

581f9433b2a3.title: Tree planting
581f9433b2a3.sentence: Tree planting is grounded in forest science and, if performed properly, can result in the successful regeneration of a deforested area.

50facbd1a0f1.title: Tree planting
50facbd1a0f1.sentence: However a planted forest rarely replicates the biodiversity and complexity of a natural forest.

607d70d9bed4.title: Tree planting
607d70d9bed4.sentence: It is often much more profitable to outside interests to plant fast-growing species, such as eucalyptus, casuarina or pine (e.g., Pinus radiata or Pinus caribaea), even though the environmental and biodiversity benefits of such monoculture plantations are not comparable to native forest, and such offset projects are frequently objects of controversy.

8f9e6c9fd984.title: Tree planting
8f9e6c9fd984.sentence: To promote the growth of native ecosystems, many environmentalists advocate only indigenous trees be planted.

52948839241a.title: Tree planting
52948839241a.sentence: Planted forests account for 8% of the total forest area, covering an estimated 312 million ha in 2025.

ae821528daa0.title: Tree planting
ae821528daa0.sentence: The area of planted forests has increased in all regions (by a total of 120 million ha) since 1990, but, globally, the rate of increase slowed between 2015 - 2025.

ecd77a89b1f6.title: Tree planting
ecd77a89b1f6.sentence: Almost all plantation forests (95%) in South America are composed of introduced species.

618b9f615d63.title: Ecological restoration
618b9f615d63.sentence: However, afforestation can have negative impacts on biodiversity especially when considering tree-planting initiatives in tropical savannas.

770cbf0e8953.title: Tree plantation
770cbf0e8953.sentence: A tree plantation, forest plantation, plantation forest, timber plantation, or tree farm is a forest planted for high volume production of wood, usually by planting one type of tree as a monoculture forest.

dc00396b132f.title: Tree plantation
dc00396b132f.sentence: While forests managed for wood production commonly yield between 1 and 3 cubic meters per hectare per year, plantations of fast-growing species commonly yield between 20 and 30 cubic meters or more per hectare annually; a grand fir plantation in Scotland has a growth rate of 34 cubic meters per hectare per year, and Monterey pine plantations in southern Australia can yield up to 40 cubic meters per hectare per year.

0f0f96706e0f.title: Tree plantation
0f0f96706e0f.sentence: In 2000, while plantations accounted for 5% of global forest, it is estimated that they supplied about 35% of the world's roundwood.

905bada67ecd.title: Tree plantation
905bada67ecd.sentence: Individual blocks are usually even-aged and often consist of just one or two species.

7df68ef1ed6e.title: Tree plantation

2f2adbec2c8b.title: Greenwashing
2f2adbec2c8b.sentence: Greenscamming describes an organization or product taking on a name that falsely implies environmental friendliness.

8f60bf3d74ee.title: Greenwashing
8f60bf3d74ee.sentence: Greenscamming is used in particular by industrial companies and associations that deploy astroturfing organisations to try to dispute scientific findings that threaten their business model.

06289e33b94a.title: Greenwashing
06289e33b94a.sentence: One example is the denial of man-made global warming by companies in the fossil energy sector, also driven by specially-founded greenscamming organizations.

ead76f318c65.title: Greenwashing
ead76f318c65.sentence: One reason to establish greenscamming organizations is that openly communicating the benefits of activities that damage the environment is difficult.

621a23b9890e.title: Greenwashing
621a23b9890e.sentence: Anti-environment initiatives, therefore, must give their front organizations deliberately deceptive names if they want to be successful, as surveys show that environmental protection has a social consensus.

f3f74d7760b1.title: Greenwashing
f3f74d7760b1.sentence: An important financier of greenscamming organizations was the oil company ExxonMobil, which financially supported more than 100 climate denial organizations and spent about 20 million U.S. dollars on greenscamming groups.

56d2329fe0fc.title: Greenwashing
56d2329fe0fc.sentence: Additionally, TerraChoice, an environmental consulting division of UL, described the "seven sins of greenwashing" in 2007 to "help consumers identify products that made misleading environmental claims":

b21e9de025c8.title: Greenwashing
b21e9de025c8.sentence: - "Hidden Trade-off", which claims a product is "green" based on an unreasonably narrow set of attributes without attention to other critical environmental issues.

9c172d6dbf77.title: Greenwashing
9c172d6dbf77.sentence: - "No proof", a claim that cannot be substantiated by easily accessible information or a reliable third-party certification.

66753166171f.title: Greenwashing
66753166171f.sentence: - "Vagueness" is a poorly defined or broad claim that the consumer will likely misunderstand, such as 'all-natural.'

5c2bf2c734f9.title: Greenwashing
5c2bf2c734f9.sentence: - "Worshipping False Labels", which is a claim that, through words or images, gives the impression of a third-party endorsement where none exists.

24e6ec82ffc1.title: Greenwashing
24e6ec82ffc1.sentence: - "Irrelevance", which is a claim that may be truthful but unimportant or unhelpful to consumers seeking environmentally preferable products.

a9728eafd722.title: Greenwashing
a9728eafd722.sentence: - "Lesser of Two Evils", a claim that may be true within the product category, but risks distracting consumers from the more significant environmental impact of the category.

68743d4b1c24.title: Greenwashing
68743d4b1c24.sentence: - "Fibbing", which is a claim that is simply false.

fafb1fec47dd.title: Greenwashing
fafb1fec47dd.sentence: Considering these ways of identifying greenwashing, TerraChoice noted that by 2010, approximately 95% of consumer products in the U.S. claiming to be green were discovered to commit at least one of these sins.

28b34676368f.title: Greenwashing
28b34676368f.sentence: According to the United Nations, greenwashing can present itself in many ways, such as claiming that the company will achieve future environment milestones while not putting sufficient plans in place to do so, being intentionally vague about operations or using vague claims that cannot be specifically proven (like saying they are "environmentally friendly" or "green"), saying that a product does not contain harmful materials or use harmful practices that they would not use anyways, highlighting one thing the company does well regarding the environment while not doing anything else, and promoting products that meet regulatory minimums as if peer products do not.

e2aa46eecc34.title: Greenwashing
e2aa46eecc34.sentence: Greenwashing can take different forms, which change depending on where and how the environmental misconduct or environmental claim occurs within an organization or its supply chain.

a6f63c80d08b.title: Greenwashing
a6f63c80d08b.sentence: Greenwashing can also take different forms depending on whether it is on a firm-level or a product-level.

ec837f1e3ab4.title: Greenwashing
ec837f1e3ab4.sentence: The first type is direct greenwashing, which occurs when a firm's own processes are inconsistent with its environmental claims and lead to blaming the entire company and having low intention to invest.

1470373f3c6b.title: Greenwashing
1470373f3c6b.sentence: The second type is indirect greenwashing, which happens when a supplier makes false environmental claims, thus the company it supplies is also negatively impacted and is blamed even though the company itself did not commit any misconduct.

b9e2f0261d23.title: Greenwashing
b9e2f0261d23.sentence: The third type is vicarious greenwashing, which occurs when a "green" company partners with a non-environmentally friendly supplier.

5f518495ad8f.title: Greenwashing
5f518495ad8f.sentence: In this case the company is held liable for the supplier's misconduct because of its stated commitment to sustainability.

ce21a7a383c6.title: Greenwashing
ce21a7a383c6.sentence: "Product-level greenwashing" mainly focuses on the products or services provided by the company.

ea460e0afd45.title: Greenwashing
ea460e0afd45.sentence: On this level, "claim greenwashing" occurs when there is a use of misleading statements about the environmental benefits and vague, unverified, and false certifications such as "eco-friendly".

a215b4f8c3f4.title: Greenwashing
a215b4f8c3f4.sentence: Moreover, "executional greenwashing" happens when companies rely on visuals and symbols, such as green colors and nature imagery, that connect to sustainability and mislead consumers into believing that a product is more ecological than it is.

8bcee94022db.title: Greenwashing
8bcee94022db.sentence: On the other hand, "firm-level greenwashing" happens at the organizational level, for example when a firm uses advertising and campaigns to promote sustainability while still having operations that damage the environment.

ab6395fb78d4.title: Tree plantation
ab6395fb78d4.sentence: In principle this is true because due to the high productivity of plantations less land is needed.

5d026adef6c1.title: Tree plantation
5d026adef6c1.sentence: Many point to the example of New Zealand, where 19% of the forest area provides 99% of the supply of industrial round wood.

c5602dc1e466.title: Tree plantation
c5602dc1e466.sentence: According to the FAO, about 7% of the natural closed forest being lost in the tropics is land being converted to plantations.

14e52e7dc112.title: Tree plantation

71b3a6bf984d.title: Tree plantation
71b3a6bf984d.sentence: Worldwide, an estimated 15% of plantations in tropical countries are established on closed canopy natural forest.

517611bb72d5.title: Tree plantation
517611bb72d5.sentence: In the Kyoto Protocol, there are proposals encouraging the use of plantations to reduce carbon dioxide levels (though this idea is being challenged by some groups on the grounds that the sequestered CO2 is eventually released after harvest).

b0d70cd6be41.title: Blue economy
b0d70cd6be41.sentence: However, the term is generally used in the scope of international development when describing a sustainable development approach to coastal resources and ocean development.

677ba2ce1ab9.title: Economic analysis of climate change
677ba2ce1ab9.sentence: Economic analysis of climate change uses economic tools and models to calculate the scale and distribution of damages caused by climate change.

6d730b796424.title: Economic analysis of climate change
6d730b796424.sentence: Economic analysis of climate change investigates the economic impacts of the effects of climate change, the costs and benefits of preventing climate change, and the cost of adapting to a changing climate.

a943ae171ee9.title: Economic analysis of climate change
a943ae171ee9.sentence: It can also give guidance for the best policies for mitigation and adaptation to climate change from an economic perspective.

8d6e2b995d5e.title: Economic analysis of climate change
8d6e2b995d5e.section: Types of economic models > Process-based models
8d6e2b995d5e.sentence: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has relied on process-based integrated assessment models (PB-IAM) to quantify mitigation scenarios.

008f1ad183e6.title: Economic analysis of climate change
008f1ad183e6.section: Types of economic models > Structural models > Computable general equilibrium models
008f1ad183e6.sentence: Computable general equilibrium (CGE) models are a class of economic models that use actual economic data to estimate how an economy might react to changes in policy, technology or other external factors.

1fbd49d4a75e.title: Economic analysis of climate change
1fbd49d4a75e.section: Types of economic models > Structural models > Aggregate cost-benefit models
1fbd49d4a75e.sentence: Integrated assessment models (IAMs) are also used to make aggregate estimates of the costs of climate change.

31b5400bfd3a.title: Economic analysis of climate change
31b5400bfd3a.section: Types of economic models > Statistical (econometric) methods
31b5400bfd3a.sentence: A third modelling approach uses empirical, statistical methods to investigate how the economy is affected by weather variation.

eac46b115f42.title: Economic analysis of climate change
eac46b115f42.sentence: Econometric models (statistical models) are used to estimate the impacts of weather and climate on economic variables, either globally or for a specific sector.

bfeb1656a5f2.title: Economic analysis of climate change
bfeb1656a5f2.section: Types of economic models > Statistical (econometric) methods
bfeb1656a5f2.sentence: This approach can identify effects of temperature, rainfall, drought and storms on agriculture, energy demand, industry and other economic activity.

ce8fb7181533.title: Economic analysis of climate change
ce8fb7181533.sentence: The economics of climate change mitigation is a contentious part of climate change mitigation – action aimed to limit the dangerous socio-economic and environmental consequences of climate change.

ec558b661d07.title: Economic analysis of climate change
ec558b661d07.section: Economics of climate change mitigation > Economic barriers to addressing climate change mitigation
ec558b661d07.sentence: Economic components like the stock market underestimate or cannot value social benefits of climate change mitigation.

ca165005bddb.title: Climate risk
ca165005bddb.sentence: Climate risk is the potential for problems for societies or ecosystems from the impacts of climate change.

66c9ecb3b218.title: Climate risk
66c9ecb3b218.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report defines climate risk is the potential for negative consequences for society or ecosystems from the impacts of climate change.

136c4e0228e8.title: Climate risk
136c4e0228e8.sentence: This can refer to both physical risks, such as extreme weather, as well as any costs associated with transitioning to a lower carbon society, known as transition risks.

f86aa7fdf5b3.title: Climate risk
f86aa7fdf5b3.sentence: Risk is used mainly to talk about the potential effects of climate change, but it may also result from the measures that we take to respond to those changes.

312b4d1b33c1.title: Climate risk
312b4d1b33c1.sentence: This can also be applied to climate risk although there are distinct differences: The climate system is no longer staying within a stationary range of extremes.

92cf72f78524.title: Climate risk
92cf72f78524.sentence: Risk assessments are based on responses of a climate system that is no longer staying within a stationary range of extremes.

11baa64cc6e0.title: Climate risk
11baa64cc6e0.sentence: Scientists use various climate change scenarios when they carry out climate risk analysis.

f23ded7d1053.title: Climate risk
f23ded7d1053.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report considers risks within important sectors affected by climate change, like agriculture, water, cities, ecosystems, health and livelihoods.

82ca6d60ab72.title: Climate risk
82ca6d60ab72.sentence: In 2020 the World Economic Forum ranked climate change as the biggest risk to economy and society.

cc9bf6a711da.title: Climate risk
cc9bf6a711da.sentence: Climate change adaptation and climate change mitigation can reduce climate-related risks.

35c1dda264c5.title: Climate risk
35c1dda264c5.sentence: These two types of climate action can be complementary and can result in synergies, and thus more successful results.

5629aee0ac02.title: Social cost of carbon
5629aee0ac02.sentence: The social cost of carbon (SCC) is an estimate, typically expressed in dollars, of the economic damages associated with emitting one additional ton of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

00af3e571a13.title: Social cost of carbon
00af3e571a13.sentence: By translating the effects of climate change into monetary terms, the SCC provides policymakers with a tool to assess the potential impacts of actions that increase or reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

87fac7c34cc1.title: Social cost of carbon
87fac7c34cc1.sentence: The concept of pricing environmental externalities was first proposed by economist Arthur Pigou in 1912, who suggested taxing activities that generate negative externalities, such as pollution.

80bd486208fe.title: Social cost of carbon
80bd486208fe.sentence: Although Pigou's framework did not specifically address carbon dioxide emissions, it laid the intellectual foundation for the development of the Social Cost of Carbon.

38695cd5ee9d.title: Social cost of carbon
38695cd5ee9d.sentence: - Political manipulation and lack of transparency: the U.S. federal government under different administrations has produced wildly divergent SCC values, ranging from $6/ton under Trump (using a 7% discount rate) to over $51/ton under Biden (using a 3% discount rate).

95e2c430d66e.title: Social cost of carbon
95e2c430d66e.sentence: The SCC is distinct from carbon pricing tools such as taxes or cap-and-trade systems.

c534d6b2cc4c.title: Social cost of carbon
c534d6b2cc4c.sentence: - Marginal logic vs. Planetary boundaries: Some scholars argue that the marginal nature of the SCC is fundamentally mismatched to the climate crisis.

0b2562d50505.title: Social cost of carbon
0b2562d50505.sentence: In this view, carbon budgets or absolute emissions caps may be more appropriate than pricing frameworks based on marginal harm.

273e2f3ca32c.title: Social cost of carbon
273e2f3ca32c.sentence: The United States formalized the Social Cost of Carbon under President Barack Obama in 2010.

914fef5d669e.title: Carbon accounting
914fef5d669e.sentence: Carbon accounting, also called greenhouse gas accounting or GHG accounting, is a framework of methods to measure and track how much greenhouse gas (GHG) an organization emits.

7be3ddfb0964.title: Carbon accounting
7be3ddfb0964.sentence: Organizations will often set an emissions baseline, create targets for reducing emissions, and track progress towards them.

dd0bb58717be.title: Carbon accounting
dd0bb58717be.sentence: These techniques can be used at different scales, from those of companies and cities, to the greenhouse gas inventories of entire nations.

3adaa8454b7a.title: Carbon accounting
3adaa8454b7a.sentence: Markets for buying and selling carbon credits depend on accurate measurement of emissions and emission reductions.

f7be168ed930.title: Carbon accounting
f7be168ed930.sentence: A variety of standards and guidelines can apply, including the Greenhouse Gas Protocol and ISO 14064.

745c3dbb14b2.title: Carbon accounting
745c3dbb14b2.section: Frameworks and standards > Corporate/local government standards > Greenhouse Gas Protocol
745c3dbb14b2.sentence: Scope 1 covers all direct GHG emissions within a corporate boundary (owned or controlled by a company).

6dc9518504b1.title: Carbon accounting
6dc9518504b1.section: Frameworks and standards > Corporate/local government standards > Greenhouse Gas Protocol
6dc9518504b1.sentence: Scope 2 covers indirect GHG emissions from consumption of purchased electricity, heat, cooling or steam.

d145f4a7e943.title: Carbon accounting
d145f4a7e943.section: Frameworks and standards > Corporate/local government standards > Greenhouse Gas Protocol
d145f4a7e943.sentence: Scope 3 emission sources include emissions from suppliers and product users (also known as the "value chain").

67abbb7bd040.title: Carbon accounting
67abbb7bd040.section: Frameworks and standards > Corporate/local government standards > Greenhouse Gas Protocol
67abbb7bd040.sentence: Scope 3 emissions often represent the largest source of corporate greenhouse gas emissions, for example the use of oil sold by Aramco.

171ded0225f4.title: Carbon accounting
171ded0225f4.sentence: Accurate reporting of Scope 3 emissions is a particular challenge.

75a9ed5c596b.title: Carbon accounting
75a9ed5c596b.sentence: There is some evidence that programs that require GHG accounting help to lower emissions.

38915876a6d4.title: Carbon accounting
38915876a6d4.sentence: GHG accounting methods help investors better understand the climate risks of companies they invest in.

d0163c152aa6.title: Stern Review
d0163c152aa6.sentence: The Stern Review on the Economics of Climate Change is a 700-page independent review released for the Government of the United Kingdom on 30 October 2006 by economist Nicholas Stern, chair of the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment at the London School of Economics (LSE) and also chair of the Centre for Climate Change Economics and Policy (CCCEP) at Leeds University and LSE.

a35fa9ea6af3.title: Stern Review
a35fa9ea6af3.sentence: The Review states that climate change is the greatest and widest-ranging market failure ever seen, presenting a unique challenge for economics.

8abd1b28699a.title: Stern Review
8abd1b28699a.sentence: The Stern Review's main conclusion is that the benefits of strong, early action on climate change far outweigh the costs of not acting.

f068c5f95aad.title: Stern Review
f068c5f95aad.sentence: According to the Review, without action, the overall costs of climate change will be equivalent to losing at least 5% of global gross domestic product (GDP) each year, now and forever.

88d6eaa2b2de.title: Stern Review
88d6eaa2b2de.sentence: Including a wider range of risks and impacts could increase this to 20% of GDP or more, also indefinitely.

27e2dcd14a01.title: Stern Review
27e2dcd14a01.sentence: The Review proposes that one per cent of global GDP per annum is required to be invested to avoid the worst effects of climate change.

ff3fc224d869.title: Stern Review
ff3fc224d869.sentence: In June 2008, Stern increased the estimate for the annual cost of achieving stabilisation between 500 and 550 ppm CO2e to 2% of GDP to account for faster than expected climate change.

cae71979ef37.title: Stern Review
cae71979ef37.sentence: One of the issues debated among economists was the discount rate used in the Review.

c62248f6bf06.title: Stern Review
c62248f6bf06.section: Response of economists > Discounting > Inherent discounting
c62248f6bf06.sentence: Stern accepts the case for discounting, but argues that applying a PTP-rate of anything much more than zero to social policy choice is ethically inappropriate.

c46201609205.title: Stern Review
c46201609205.sentence: Several economists have been critical of the Review, for example, a paper by Byatt et al. (2006) describes the Review as "deeply flawed".

1ccade8f0e48.title: Stern Review
1ccade8f0e48.section: Response of economists > General comments > Comparison with climate damages
1ccade8f0e48.sentence: However, I believe that Stern's fundamental conclusion is justified: we are much better off reducing CO2 emissions substantially than risking the consequences of failing to act, even if, unlike Stern, one heavily discounts uncertainty and the future.

b8659018be07.title: Stern Review
b8659018be07.sentence: In April 2008 Stern said that the severity of his findings were vindicated by the 2007 IPCC report and admitted that in the Stern Review, "We underestimated the risks [...] we underestimated the damage associated with temperature increases [...] and we underestimated the probabilities of temperature increases".

5591f29c662d.title: Climate change scenario
5591f29c662d.sentence: A climate change scenario is a hypothetical future based on a "set of key driving forces" behind climate change.

d69de7061728.title: Climate change scenario
d69de7061728.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report defines scenario as follows: "A plausible description of how the future may develop based on a [...] set of assumptions about key driving forces and relationships." A set of scenarios shows a range of possible futures.

869855181d23.title: Climate change scenario
869855181d23.sentence: Scenarios explore the long-term effectiveness of climate change mitigation and adaptation.

75b69b5267a5.title: Climate change scenario
75b69b5267a5.sentence: In other words: pathways are a roadmap which list actions that need to be taken to make a scenario come true.

9f239679d327.title: Climate change scenario
9f239679d327.sentence: Pathways are more concrete and action-oriented compared to scenarios.

b5733f9a09b0.title: Climate change scenario
b5733f9a09b0.sentence: Three important parameters are the number of people (and population growth), their economic activity and new technologies.

4664b87837dc.title: Climate change scenario
4664b87837dc.sentence: A baseline scenario is used as a reference for comparison against an alternative scenario, e.g., a mitigation scenario.

89d987ec3891.title: Climate change scenario
89d987ec3891.sentence: Economic growth was found to be compatible with increasing or decreasing GHG emissions.

f52dd33a15d2.title: Climate change scenario

3bb4e4f7857c.title: Climate change scenario

5f280a7c5296.title: Climate change scenario

614296d2a4bf.title: Integrated assessment modelling
614296d2a4bf.sentence: Integrated assessment modelling (IAM) or integrated modelling (IM) is a type of scientific modelling that tries to link main features of society and economy with the biosphere and atmosphere into one modelling framework.

f51536779c69.title: Integrated assessment modelling
f51536779c69.sentence: The goal of integrated assessment modelling is to accommodate informed policy-making, usually in the context of climate change though also in other areas of human and social development.

9a561b6fd6c9.title: Integrated assessment modelling
9a561b6fd6c9.sentence: While the detail and extent of integrated disciplines varies strongly per model, all climatic integrated assessment modelling includes economic processes as well as processes producing greenhouse gases.

8367cc6a6552.title: Integrated assessment modelling
8367cc6a6552.sentence: Integrated assessment modelling does not provide predictions for the future but rather estimates what possible scenarios look like.

741a57b8a51e.title: Integrated assessment modelling
741a57b8a51e.sentence: One classification distinguishes between firstly models that quantify future developmental pathways or scenarios and provide detailed, sectoral information on the complex processes modelled.

7cc947ab31fb.title: Integrated assessment modelling
7cc947ab31fb.sentence: Here they are called process-based models.

9546d2c2de25.title: Integrated assessment modelling
9546d2c2de25.sentence: Secondly, there are models that aggregate the costs of climate change and climate change mitigation to find estimates of the total costs of climate change.

8baae87c5398.title: Integrated assessment modelling
8baae87c5398.sentence: Cost-benefit integrated assessment models are the main tools for calculating the social cost of carbon, or the marginal social cost of emitting one more tonne of carbon (as carbon dioxide) into the atmosphere at any point in time.

b87f8dc947b6.title: Integrated assessment modelling
b87f8dc947b6.sentence: For instance, the DICE, PAGE, and FUND models have been used by the US Interagency Working Group to calculate the social cost of carbon and its results have been used for regulatory impact analysis.

cae9d1650266.title: Integrated assessment modelling
cae9d1650266.sentence: It has been argued that "IAM-based analyses of climate policy create a perception of knowledge and precision that is illusory, and can fool policy-makers into thinking that the forecasts the models generate have some kind of scientific legitimacy".

84ce459a2b2f.title: Integrated assessment modelling
84ce459a2b2f.sentence: Furthermore, IAMs are criticized to insufficiently deal with issues of justice.

7d3200d810b8.title: Integrated assessment modelling
7d3200d810b8.sentence: IAMs have also been criticised for undervaluing or underestimating the role of primary renewable electricity, generated primarily through wind and solar power, and closely related integration concepts like sector coupling, electrification of end-use and power-to-X, while overvaluing the role of bioenergy and CCS.

b8decda478ec.title: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
b8decda478ec.sentence: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) are climate change scenarios of projected socioeconomic global changes up to 2100 as defined in the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report on climate change in 2021.

743c3c42bd29.title: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
743c3c42bd29.sentence: The SSPs provide narratives describing alternative socio-economic developments.

2a751b8307ff.title: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
2a751b8307ff.sentence: In terms of quantitative elements, they provide data accompanying the scenarios on national population, urbanization and GDP (per capita).

05157657b1bc.title: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
05157657b1bc.sentence: They are used to derive greenhouse gas emissions scenarios with different climate policies.

bcc8eca1498f.title: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
bcc8eca1498f.sentence: The SSPs can be quantified with various Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs) to explore possible future pathways both with regard to socioeconomic and climate pathways.

03af29dc67df.title: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways

03af29dc67df.sentence: "The world follows a path in which social, economic, and technological trends do not shift markedly from historical patterns.

7d943eb007bc.sentence: "Highly unequal investments in human capital, combined with increasing disparities in economic opportunity and political power, lead to increasing inequalities and stratification both across and within countries.
