f8fb8ed31eee.sentence: The marginal abatement cost, in general, measures the cost of reducing one more unit of pollution.

155b8465d8bf.title: Marginal abatement cost
155b8465d8bf.sentence: Abatement cost is the cost of reducing environmental negatives such as pollution.

40dbff4c301d.title: Marginal abatement cost
40dbff4c301d.sentence: Marginal cost is an economic concept that measures the cost of an additional unit.

54fb96403acf.title: Marginal abatement cost
54fb96403acf.sentence: Marginal abatement costs are also called the "marginal cost" of reducing such environmental negatives.

875e518ec0be.title: Marginal abatement cost
875e518ec0be.sentence: Although marginal abatement costs can be negative, such as when the low carbon option is cheaper than the business-as-usual option, marginal abatement costs often rise steeply as more pollution is reduced.

de9389bf4ecc.title: Marginal abatement cost
de9389bf4ecc.sentence: In other words, it becomes more expensive [technology or infrastructure changes] to reduce pollution past a certain point.

70b3cd216f76.title: Marginal abatement cost
70b3cd216f76.sentence: Marginal abatement costs are typically used on a marginal abatement cost curve, which shows the marginal cost of additional reductions in pollution.

44674708851e.title: Marginal abatement cost
44674708851e.sentence: Policy-makers use marginal abatement cost curves as merit order curves, to analyze how much abatement can be done in an economy at what cost, and where policy should be directed to achieve the emission reductions.

09caf9f7d310.title: Marginal abatement cost
09caf9f7d310.sentence: Carbon traders use marginal abatement cost curves to derive the supply function for modelling carbon price fundamentals.

6817760da4cd.title: Marginal abatement cost
6817760da4cd.section: Examples of existing marginal abatement cost curves
6817760da4cd.sentence: Worldwide, marginal abatement cost studies show that improving the energy efficiency of buildings and replacing fossil fuelled power plants with renewables are usually the most cost effective ways of reducing carbon emissions.

523ac43a095a.title: Marginal abatement cost
523ac43a095a.sentence: The way that marginal abatement cost curves are usually built has been criticized for lack of transparency and the poor treatment it makes of uncertainty, inter-temporal dynamics, interactions between sectors and ancillary benefits.

0806826fd9e8.title: DICE model
0806826fd9e8.sentence: The Dynamic Integrated Climate-Economy model, referred to as the DICE model or Dice model, is a neoclassical integrated assessment model developed by 2018 Nobel Laureate William Nordhaus that integrates in the neoclassical economics, carbon cycle, climate science, and estimated impacts allowing the weighing of subjectively guessed costs and subjectively guessed benefits of taking steps to slow climate change.

cbf185936ad1.title: DICE model
cbf185936ad1.sentence: The model appears to have first been proposed by economist William Nordhaus in a discussion paper for the Cowles Foundation in February 1992.

656877a65b58.title: DICE model

fbc017f14ad5.title: DICE model

f8003680d067.title: Kaya identity

fb86181d4385.title: Kaya identity

c575dfc9255e.title: Carbon lock-in

It has since gained popularity in climate change policy discussions, especially those focused on preventing the globalization of carbon lock-in to rapidly industrializing countries like China and India.

88d8100211c6.sentence: A fat-tailed distribution is a probability distribution that exhibits a large skewness or kurtosis, relative to that of either a normal distribution or an exponential distribution.

00a673b97195.title: Fat-tailed distribution
00a673b97195.section: Fat tails and risk estimate distortions
00a673b97195.sentence: Compared to fat-tailed distributions, in the normal distribution, events that deviate from the mean by five or more standard deviations ("5-sigma events") have lower probability, meaning that in the normal distribution extreme events are less likely than for fat-tailed distributions.

72753dc13ad0.title: Fat-tailed distribution

b5cac6f4e8ab.title: Climate sensitivity

5ce6f14c84ce.title: Climate sensitivity

c27fba7668fb.title: The Green Paradox
c27fba7668fb.sentence: The Green Paradox is a controversial book by German economist, Hans-Werner Sinn, describing the observation that an environmental policy that becomes greener with the passage of time acts like an announced expropriation for the owners of fossil fuel resources, inducing them to accelerate resource extraction and hence to accelerate global warming.

3b936b48180a.title: The Green Paradox
3b936b48180a.sentence: That is the green paradox: environmental policy slated to become greener over time acts as an announced expropriation that provokes owners to react by accelerating the rate of extraction of their fossil fuel stocks, thus accelerating climate change.

43d9e3241e0f.title: The Green Paradox
43d9e3241e0f.sentence: According to Sinn green policies, by heralding a gradual tightening of policy over the coming decades, exert a stronger downward pressure on future prices than on current ones, decreasing thus the rate of capital appreciation of the fossil fuel deposits.

19120552f492.title: The Green Paradox

f4fff98e3fca.title: The Green Paradox
f4fff98e3fca.sentence: They burn the carbon set free by the “green” countries (leakage effect) and they also burn the additional carbon extracted as a reaction to the announced and expected price cuts resulting from the gradual greening of environmental policies (green paradox).

905f9a91245e.title: The Green Paradox
905f9a91245e.sentence: An effective climate policy must perforce focus on the hitherto neglected supply side of the carbon market in addition to the demand side.

676f68d74914.title: The Green Paradox
676f68d74914.sentence: The ways proposed as practicable by Sinn include levying a withholding tax on the capital gains on the financial investments of fossil fuel resource owners, or the establishment of a seamless global emissions trading system that would effectively put a cap on worldwide fossil fuel consumption, thereby achieving the desired reduction in carbon extraction rates.

501f96733b24.title: Demand response
501f96733b24.sentence: Demand response is a change in the power consumption of an electric utility customer to better match the demand for power with the supply.

9af16e212b11.title: Demand response

78d67501eb5d.title: Demand response

40b51e727533.title: Demand response
40b51e727533.sentence: Utilities may signal demand requests to their customers in a variety of ways, including simple off-peak metering, in which power is cheaper at certain times of the day, and smart metering, in which explicit requests or changes in price can be communicated to customers.

efe511a26f42.title: Demand response

f6ccb6f4347f.title: Demand response

e9d2f567650f.title: Demand response

bf7259414664.sentence: Solar and wind electricity therefore substantially reduce the amount of highly priced peak electricity that transmission companies need to buy, during the times when solar/wind power is available, reducing the overall cost.

4da540efc701.title: Merit order
4da540efc701.section: The effect of renewable energy on merit order
4da540efc701.sentence: A study by the Fraunhofer Institute ISI found that this "merit order effect" had allowed solar power to reduce the price of electricity on the German energy exchange by 10% on average, and by as much as 40% in the early afternoon.

719d80375235.title: Merit order
719d80375235.section: The effect of renewable energy on merit order
719d80375235.sentence: For each additional GWh of renewables fed into the grid, the price of electricity in the day-ahead market was reduced by 0.11–0.13 ¢/kWh.

348f004d63b2.title: Merit order
348f004d63b2.section: The effect of renewable energy on merit order
348f004d63b2.sentence: On the other hand, solar energy tends to be most abundant at noon, whereas peak demand is late afternoon in warm climates, leading to the so-called duck curve.

0127bd450a66.title: Climate change mitigation
0127bd450a66.sentence: Climate change mitigation, also called decarbonisation, is an action to limit the greenhouse gases in the atmosphere that cause climate change.

3f212ef4130e.title: Climate change mitigation
3f212ef4130e.sentence: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) defines mitigation (of climate change) as "a human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance the sinks of greenhouse gases".

ebe3ec378c12.title: Climate change mitigation
ebe3ec378c12.sentence: Climate change mitigation actions include conserving energy and replacing fossil fuels with clean energy sources.

ecfee4b85d2c.title: Climate change mitigation
ecfee4b85d2c.sentence: Secondary mitigation strategies include changes to land use and removing carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere.

8efb0e85e3fb.title: Climate change mitigation
8efb0e85e3fb.sentence: There are four types of measures:

061ecac0bea4.title: Climate change mitigation
061ecac0bea4.sentence: - Energy conservation, including efficient energy use

7b67203c31d0.title: Climate change mitigation
7b67203c31d0.sentence: - Sustainable agriculture and green industrial policy

ce14be92b855.title: Climate change mitigation
ce14be92b855.sentence: - Enhancing carbon sinks and carbon dioxide removal (CDR), including carbon sequestration

38bed611c261.title: Climate change mitigation
38bed611c261.sentence: 2022 assessments emphasize that global greenhouse gas emissions must peak before 2025 and decline by about 43% by 2030 to limit warming to 1.5 °C, requiring rapid transitions in energy, transport, and land-use systems.

250ebb90f06b.title: Climate change mitigation
250ebb90f06b.sentence: The adopted climate change mitigation policies are insufficient, as they contribute to some changes but fail to accelerate transitions at the scale and speed required, and would still result in global warming of about 2.7 °C by 2100, significantly above the 2015 Paris Agreement's goal of limiting global warming to below 2 °C.

139a1503e327.title: Climate change mitigation
139a1503e327.sentence: Solar energy and wind power can replace fossil fuels at the lowest cost compared to other renewable energy options.

c0f0e09faba6.title: Climate change mitigation
c0f0e09faba6.sentence: Certain processes are more difficult to decarbonise, such as air travel and cement production.

c65542b90254.title: Climate change mitigation
c65542b90254.sentence: While climate mitigation is often cast as a burden to be distributed in some or other way, it can also be seen as an opportunity for industrial development, exports, and status seeking for countries.

bc4b440e8937.title: Carbon sequestration
bc4b440e8937.sentence: Carbon sequestration is a natural process of storing carbon in a carbon pool.

48f4121c994b.title: Carbon sequestration
48f4121c994b.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report defines carbon sequestration as "The process of storing carbon in a carbon pool".

30367e63d01b.title: Carbon sequestration
30367e63d01b.sentence: Subsequently, a pool is defined as "a reservoir in the Earth system where elements, such as carbon and nitrogen, reside in various chemical forms for a period of time".

80144ccfa1db.title: Carbon sequestration
80144ccfa1db.sentence: It plays a crucial role in effectively managing the global carbon cycle and limiting climate change by reducing the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

df1cbbdff5c8.title: Carbon sequestration
df1cbbdff5c8.sentence: There are two main types of carbon sequestration: biologic (also called biosequestration) and geologic.

1b292c82c11b.title: Carbon sequestration
1b292c82c11b.sentence: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air as they grow, and bind it into biomass.

84e053081fd9.title: Carbon sequestration
84e053081fd9.sentence: These processes can be accelerated for example through changes in land use and agricultural practices, called carbon farming.

dde7acb83718.title: Carbon sequestration
dde7acb83718.sentence: However, biological stores (such as forests and kelp beds) may be temporary carbon sinks, as long-term sequestration cannot be guaranteed.

e57e35e748c9.title: Carbon sequestration
e57e35e748c9.sentence: Wildfires, disease, economic pressures, and changing political priorities may release the sequestered carbon back into the atmosphere.

2a1dbca7698e.title: Carbon sequestration
2a1dbca7698e.sentence: Carbon dioxide that has been removed from the atmosphere can also be stored in the Earth's crust by injecting it underground, or in the form of insoluble carbonate salts.

5396ec325796.title: Carbon sequestration
5396ec325796.sentence: This means the carbon is "locked away" for thousands to millions of years.

a55577ef3552.title: Carbon sequestration
a55577ef3552.section: Roles > In climate change mitigation and policies
a55577ef3552.sentence: Within the carbon capture and storage approaches, carbon sequestration refers to the storage component.

2aef1cb764a7.title: Carbon sequestration
2aef1cb764a7.section: Roles > In climate change mitigation and policies
2aef1cb764a7.sentence: Noting that the planet's carbon sequestration capacity is not unlimited, a 2025 study concluded that fully using Earth's geologic storage capacity would help limit global warming by only 0.7 °C (1.3 °F).

029ea7435ae5.title: Carbon budget
029ea7435ae5.sentence: It examines the "maximum amount of cumulative net global anthropogenic carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions that would result in limiting global warming to a given level".

4e88cff70cb9.title: Carbon budget
4e88cff70cb9.sentence: Emissions budgets indicate a finite amount of carbon dioxide that can be emitted over time, before resulting in dangerous levels of global warming.

8f6dc0c6c178.title: Carbon budget
8f6dc0c6c178.sentence: It can be expressed relative to the pre-industrial period (the year 1750).

d40a7f7ad051.title: Carbon budget
d40a7f7ad051.sentence: In this case, it is the total carbon budget.

0644e182760e.title: Carbon budget
0644e182760e.sentence: Or it can be expressed from a recent specified date onwards.

b1f6871ed2d1.title: Carbon budget
b1f6871ed2d1.sentence: In that case it is the remaining carbon budget.

1ff5fb3a7ba3.title: Carbon budget
1ff5fb3a7ba3.sentence: A carbon budget that will keep global warming below a specified temperature limit is also called an emissions budget or quota, or allowable emissions.

ffbacafab732.title: Carbon budget
ffbacafab732.section: Estimations > Carbon budget in gigatonnes and factors
ffbacafab732.sentence: The finding of an almost linear relationship between global temperature rise and cumulative carbon dioxide emissions has encouraged the estimation of global emissions budgets in order to remain below dangerous levels of warming.

0aab08e601e5.title: Carbon budget
0aab08e601e5.sentence: The change in global temperature is independent of the source of these emissions, and is largely independent of the timing of these emissions.

95b82608bb48.title: Carbon budget
95b82608bb48.section: Estimations > Carbon budget in gigatonnes and factors
95b82608bb48.sentence: Since the pre-industrial period (year 1750) to 2019, approximately 2390 Gigatonnes of CO2 (Gt CO2) has already been emitted globally.

5049e84beaf1.title: Carbon budget
5049e84beaf1.section: Estimations > Carbon budget in gigatonnes and factors
5049e84beaf1.sentence: The estimates vary according to the global temperature target that is chosen, the probability of staying below that target, and the emission of other non-CO2 greenhouse gases (GHGs).

2a29ba4e04a0.title: Carbon budget
2a29ba4e04a0.section: Estimations > Carbon budget in gigatonnes and factors
2a29ba4e04a0.sentence: Carbon budget estimates thus depend on how successful society is in reducing non-CO2 emissions together with carbon dioxide emissions.

bc4f1988a82d.title: Carbon budget
bc4f1988a82d.section: Estimations > Recent and currently remaining carbon budget
bc4f1988a82d.sentence: They found we can emit 250 GtCO2 or 6 years of emissions at current level starting from January 2023, for having a 50% chance to stay below 1.5 degrees.

483ed0576a45.title: Carbon budget
483ed0576a45.section: Estimations > Recent and currently remaining carbon budget
483ed0576a45.sentence: To have a 50% chance of staying below 2 degrees humanity can emit 1220 GtCO2 or 30 years of emissions at current level.

574df3929534.title: Low-carbon economy
574df3929534.sentence: A low-carbon economy is an economy which absorbs as much greenhouse gas as it emits.

04713b6eb9f8.title: Low-carbon economy
04713b6eb9f8.sentence: The UK Office for National Statistics published the following definition in 2017: "The low carbon economy is defined as economic activities that deliver goods and services that generate significantly lower emissions of greenhouse gases; predominantly carbon dioxide."

da9680ee8b51.title: Low-carbon economy
da9680ee8b51.sentence: There are many synonyms or similar terms in use for low-carbon economy which stress different aspects of the concept, for example: green economy, sustainable economy, carbon-neutral economy, low-emissions economy, climate-friendly economy, decarbonised economy.

01b4f87389c2.title: Low-carbon economy
01b4f87389c2.sentence: The term carbon in low-carbon economy is short hand for all greenhouse gases.

8696b9742f7d.title: Low-carbon economy
8696b9742f7d.sentence: Achieving a low-carbon economy involves reducing greenhouse gas emissions in all sectors that produce greenhouse gases, for example energy, transportation, industry, and agriculture.

e5c36f1553d2.title: Low-carbon economy
e5c36f1553d2.sentence: There are many strategies and approaches for moving to a low-carbon economy, such as encouraging renewable energy transition, efficient energy use, energy conservation, electric vehicles, heat pumps, and climate-smart agriculture.

a93976c899da.title: Low-carbon economy
a93976c899da.sentence: This requires for example suitable energy policies, financial incentives (e.g. emissions trading, carbon tax), individual action on climate change, business action on climate change.

9b9ff8a67846.title: Low-carbon economy
9b9ff8a67846.sentence: The main benefit of a transition to low-carbon economies is that it would contribute towards climate change mitigation.

8532326ef44c.title: Low-carbon economy
8532326ef44c.sentence: Apart from that, other co-benefits can also be identified: Low-carbon economies present multiple benefits to ecosystem resilience, trade, employment, health, energy security, and industrial competitiveness.

e1bff3710c77.title: Low-carbon economy
e1bff3710c77.sentence: During the green transition, workers in carbon-intensive industries are more likely to lose their jobs.

a6b7b5858676.title: Low-carbon economy
a6b7b5858676.sentence: Employment opportunities by the green transition are associated with the use of renewable energy sources or building activity for infrastructure improvements and renovations.

53cebb535165.title: Low-carbon economy
53cebb535165.sentence: According to the Low Emission Development Strategies Global Partnership (LEDS GP), there is often a clear business case for switching to lower emission technologies, with payback periods ranging largely from 0.5–5 years, leveraging financial investment.

d2e0ef537b1c.title: Carbon capture and storage
d2e0ef537b1c.sentence: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) is a process by which carbon dioxide (CO2) from industrial installations or natural sources is separated before it is released into the atmosphere, then transported to a long-term storage location.

67adafcd5eb4.title: Carbon capture and storage
67adafcd5eb4.sentence: The CO2 is captured from a large point source, such as a natural gas processing plant and is typically stored in a deep geological formation.

cdbeefa27e24.title: Carbon capture and storage
cdbeefa27e24.sentence: Around 80% of the CO2 captured annually is used for enhanced oil recovery (EOR), a process by which CO2 is injected into partially depleted oil reservoirs in order to extract more oil and then is largely left underground.

34aa233e4d18.title: Carbon capture and storage
34aa233e4d18.sentence: Since EOR utilizes the CO2 in addition to storing it, CCS is also known as carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS).

221b0c49de08.title: Carbon capture and storage
221b0c49de08.sentence: Most commonly, the gas stream passes through an amine solvent, which binds to the CO2 molecule.

164654c227d2.title: Carbon capture and storage
164654c227d2.section: Role in climate change mitigation > Pace of implementation
164654c227d2.sentence: As of 2023 CCS captures around 0.1% of global emissions — around 45 million tonnes of CO2.

996dc2c3b47f.title: Carbon capture and storage
996dc2c3b47f.sentence: If the facility produces a gas mixture with a high concentration of CO2, as is the case for natural gas processing, it can be captured and compressed for US$15–25/tonne.

ac11430c5070.title: Carbon capture and storage
ac11430c5070.sentence: Power plants, cement plants, and iron and steel plants produce more dilute gas streams, for which the cost of capture and compression is US$40–120/tonne CO2.

0de7d7cf9a0f.title: Carbon capture and storage
0de7d7cf9a0f.section: Role in climate change mitigation > Comparison with other mitigation options
0de7d7cf9a0f.sentence: Compared to other options for reducing emissions, CCS is very expensive.

044ec6b19378.title: Carbon capture and storage
044ec6b19378.section: Role in climate change mitigation > Comparison with other mitigation options
044ec6b19378.sentence: There are many ways to reduce emissions that cost less than US$20 per tonne of avoided CO2 emissions.

89a6d10b776a.title: Carbon capture and storage
89a6d10b776a.sentence: CCS implementations involve multiple technologies that are highly customized to each site, which limits the industry's ability to reduce costs through learning-by-doing.

45602ecb143e.title: Carbon capture and storage
45602ecb143e.section: Role in climate change mitigation > Priority uses
45602ecb143e.sentence: In the literature on climate change mitigation, CCS is described as having a small but critical role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

9f18ffd02367.title: Carbon capture and storage
9f18ffd02367.sentence: Public statements from fossil fuel companies and fossil-based electric utilities ask for "recognition" that fossil fuel usage will increase in the future and suggest that CCS will allow the fossil fuel era to be extended.

dc262708ab46.title: Carbon capture and storage
dc262708ab46.sentence: CCS has been discussed by political actors at least since the start of the UNFCCC negotiations in the beginning of the 1990s, and remains a very divisive issue.

987545efe32d.title: Biochar
987545efe32d.sentence: Biochar is a form of charcoal, sometimes modified, that is intended for organic use, as in soil.

97567ca137f3.title: Biochar
97567ca137f3.sentence: Biochar is defined by the International Biochar Initiative as the "solid material obtained from the thermochemical conversion of biomass in an oxygen-limited environment".

5d839784e3be.title: Biochar
5d839784e3be.sentence: Biochar is a high-carbon, fine-grained residue that is produced via pyrolysis.

8eeb5bdd0cd4.title: Biochar
8eeb5bdd0cd4.sentence: It is the direct thermal decomposition of biomass in the absence of oxygen, which prevents combustion, and produces a mixture of solids (biochar), liquid (bio-oil), and gas (syngas) products.

eac815217a26.title: Biochar
eac815217a26.sentence: Biochar is mainly used in soils to increase soil aeration, reduce soil emissions of greenhouse gases, improve soil fertility, reduce nutrient leaching, reduce soil acidity, and potentially increase the water content of coarse soils.

9bae46d876bc.title: Biochar
9bae46d876bc.sentence: However, when applied excessively or made from feedstock unsuitable for the soil type, biochar soil amendments also have the potential for negative effects, including harming soil biota, reducing available water content, altering soil pH, and increasing salinity.

023beb4b30b8.title: Biochar
023beb4b30b8.sentence: Due to its refractory stability, biochar can stay in soils or other environments for thousands of years.

55a1e6db367f.title: Biochar
55a1e6db367f.sentence: This has given rise to the concept of biochar carbon removal, a process of carbon sequestration in the form of biochar.

3ac4fe3b56a0.title: Biochar
3ac4fe3b56a0.sentence: Pre-Columbian Amazonians produced biochar by smoldering agricultural waste (i.e., covering burning biomass with soil) in pits or trenches.

83be0d10e043.title: Biochar
83be0d10e043.sentence: European settlers called it terra preta de Indio.

cb78839eeb3c.title: Biochar
cb78839eeb3c.sentence: Biochar offers multiple soil health benefits in degraded tropical soils but is less beneficial in temperate regions.

5ac6af7daa9f.title: Biochar
5ac6af7daa9f.sentence: Studies have found that a 1–2% weight concentration of biochar is optimal for use in concrete mixes, from both a cost and strength standpoint.

e8304d9c886e.title: Biochar
e8304d9c886e.sentence: Biochar has been shown to be an effective SCM, reducing concrete production emissions while maintaining required strength and ductility properties.

fc256dd22037.title: Climate change mitigation
fc256dd22037.sentence: Co-benefits of climate change mitigation, also often referred to as ancillary benefits, were firstly dominated in the scientific literature by studies that describe how lower GHG emissions lead to better air quality and consequently impact human health positively.

dfaa28d8270f.title: Climate change mitigation
dfaa28d8270f.sentence: Co-benefits can positively impact employment, industrial development, states' energy independence and energy self-consumption.

43b8743c7dfd.title: Climate change mitigation
43b8743c7dfd.sentence: A 2023 study estimated that fossil fuels kill over 5 million people each year, as of 2019, by causing diseases such as heart attack, stroke and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

da08cc99f8a9.title: Climate change mitigation
da08cc99f8a9.sentence: Depending on the country and deployment scenario, replacing coal power plants with renewable energy can more than double the number of jobs per average MW capacity.

f1552a8567a3.title: Climate change mitigation
f1552a8567a3.sentence: Countries which rely on energy imports can enhance their energy independence and ensure supply security by deploying renewables.

3ed4c28e1bf5.title: Climate change mitigation
3ed4c28e1bf5.sentence: The IPCC pointed out in 2007: "Co-benefits of GHG mitigation can be an important decision criteria in analyses carried out by policy-makers, but they are often neglected" and added that the co-benefits are "not quantified, monetised or even identified by businesses and decision-makers".

1461fff5b503.title: Climate change mitigation
1461fff5b503.sentence: Appropriate consideration of co-benefits can greatly "influence policy decisions concerning the timing and level of mitigation action", and there can be "significant advantages to the national economy and technical innovation".

59f435b24816.title: Climate change mitigation
59f435b24816.sentence: Reducing demand for products and services that cause greenhouse gas emissions can help in mitigating climate change.

edc952fa9847.title: Climate change mitigation
edc952fa9847.sentence: One is to reduce demand by behavioural and cultural changes, for example by making changes in diet, especially the decision to reduce meat consumption, an effective action individuals take to fight climate change.

d1d58d5eafb5.title: Climate change mitigation
d1d58d5eafb5.sentence: Another is by reducing the demand by improving infrastructure, by building a good public transport network, for example.

edf0631a1a97.title: Climate change mitigation
edf0631a1a97.sentence: Lastly, changes in end-use technology can reduce energy demand.

881860909132.title: Climate change mitigation
881860909132.sentence: For instance a well-insulated house emits less than a poorly-insulated house.

9ea03ba73f14.title: Climate change mitigation
9ea03ba73f14.sentence: Recent research shows that demand-side climate solutions—such as shifts in transportation behavior, dietary change, improved building energy efficiency, and reduced material consumption—could reduce global greenhouse gas emissions by 40% to 70% by 2050 while improving human well-being.

971bdaad7983.title: Climate change mitigation
971bdaad7983.sentence: High-consumption lifestyles have a greater environmental impact, with the richest 10% of people emitting about half the total lifestyle emissions.

2a909b4c7084.title: Climate change mitigation
2a909b4c7084.sentence: People who wish to reduce their carbon footprint can take high-impact actions such as avoiding frequent flying and petrol-fuelled cars, eating mainly a plant-based diet, having fewer children, using clothes and electrical products for longer, and electrifying homes.

e0cbb347e5a2.title: Climate change mitigation
e0cbb347e5a2.sentence: The building sector accounts for 23% of global energy-related CO2 emissions.

58eaa9e80d98.title: Climate change mitigation
58eaa9e80d98.sentence: Transportation accounts for 15% of emissions worldwide.

197d3832291c.title: Climate change mitigation
197d3832291c.sentence: Industry is the largest emitter of greenhouse gases when direct and indirect emissions are included.

167ef80495b6.title: Climate change mitigation
167ef80495b6.section: Mitigation by sector > Agriculture, forestry and land use
167ef80495b6.sentence: Almost 20% of greenhouse gas emissions come from the agriculture and forestry sector.

7a4929be285c.title: Climate change mitigation
7a4929be285c.sentence: About half of the energy is used for space and water heating.

c434851496b3.title: Climate change mitigation
c434851496b3.sentence: Increasing the use of public transport, low-carbon freight transport and cycling are important components of transport decarbonisation.

d01a3f071954.title: Climate change mitigation
d01a3f071954.sentence: Electric vehicles and environmentally friendly rail help to reduce the consumption of fossil fuels.

e628a07b31a4.title: Climate change mitigation
e628a07b31a4.sentence: Electrification can reduce emissions from industry.

083878e04644.title: Climate change mitigation
083878e04644.sentence: Green hydrogen can play a major role in energy-intensive industries for which electricity is not an option.

3eaeb9335845.title: Climate change mitigation
3eaeb9335845.sentence: Finally, circular economy measures reduce the need for new materials.

2e2e3f281b66.title: Climate change mitigation
2e2e3f281b66.section: Mitigation by sector > Agriculture, forestry and land use
2e2e3f281b66.sentence: With 21% of global methane emissions, cattle are a major driver of global warming.

2e853fccdd0d.title: Climate change mitigation
2e853fccdd0d.sentence: A modern heat pump typically transports around three to five times more thermal energy than electrical energy consumed.

631893eb1940.title: Climate change mitigation
631893eb1940.sentence: This refers to the management of Earth's natural carbon sinks in a way that preserves or increases their capability to remove CO2 from the atmosphere and to store it durably.

58030635694d.title: Climate change mitigation
58030635694d.sentence: Globally, the two most important carbon sinks are vegetation and the ocean.

d23af4b3d985.title: Climate change mitigation
d23af4b3d985.sentence: Examples are preventing deforestation and restoring natural ecosystems by reforestation.

cbfd8568f7e1.title: Climate change mitigation
cbfd8568f7e1.sentence: But ecosystem restoration and reduced conversion are among the mitigation tools that can yield the most emissions reductions before 2030.

106a871b02fd.title: Climate change mitigation
106a871b02fd.sentence: The economic potential of these activities has been estimated to be 4.2 to 7.4 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (GtCO2 -eq) per year.

499446a11c8b.title: Climate change mitigation
499446a11c8b.section: Preserving and enhancing carbon sinks > Forests > Conservation
499446a11c8b.sentence: The Stern Review on the economics of climate change stated in 2007 that curbing deforestation was a highly cost-effective way of reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

e22f57257372.title: Carbon sequestration
e22f57257372.sentence: Biological carbon sequestration (also called biosequestration) is the capture and storage of the atmospheric greenhouse gas carbon dioxide by continual and enhanced biological processes.

c9fe99cfc335.title: Carbon sequestration
c9fe99cfc335.sentence: This form of carbon sequestration occurs through increased rates of photosynthesis via land-use practices such as reforestation and sustainable forest management.

7db1e583751d.title: Carbon sequestration
7db1e583751d.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Forestry
7db1e583751d.sentence: By removing the greenhouse gas CO2 from the air, forests function as terrestrial carbon sinks, meaning they store large amounts of carbon in the form of biomass, encompassing roots, stems, branches, and leaves.

e5bb2a31d763.title: Carbon sequestration
e5bb2a31d763.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Agriculture
e5bb2a31d763.sentence: When soil is converted from natural land or semi-natural land, such as forests, woodlands, grasslands, steppes, and savannas, the SOC content in the soil reduces by about 30–40%.

647216761dcb.title: Carbon sequestration
647216761dcb.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Wetlands
647216761dcb.sentence: Wetland soil, particularly in coastal wetlands such as mangroves, sea grasses, and salt marshes, is an important carbon reservoir; 20–30% of the world's soil carbon is found in wetlands, while only 5–8% of the world's land is composed of wetlands.

08b082ecd192.title: Carbon sequestration
08b082ecd192.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
08b082ecd192.sentence: Geological sequestration refers to the storage of CO2 underground in depleted oil and gas reservoirs, saline formations, or deep, coal beds unsuitable for mining.

d14107b1304e.title: Carbon sequestration
d14107b1304e.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
d14107b1304e.sentence: Once CO2 is captured from a point source, such as a cement factory, it can be compressed to ≈100 bar into a supercritical fluid.

796b63da3b51.title: Carbon sequestration
796b63da3b51.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
796b63da3b51.sentence: In this form, the CO2 could be transported via pipeline to the place of storage.

51143d6fea80.title: Carbon sequestration
51143d6fea80.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
51143d6fea80.sentence: The CO2 could then be injected deep underground, typically around 1 km (0.6 mi), where it would be stable for hundreds to millions of years.

d2af31adbd00.title: Carbon sequestration
d2af31adbd00.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
d2af31adbd00.sentence: The medium in which the CO2 is to be stored ideally has a high porosity and permeability, such as sandstone or limestone.

e3efa3395675.title: Carbon sequestration
e3efa3395675.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
e3efa3395675.sentence: The porous rock must be capped by a layer of low permeability, which function as a seal, or caprock, for the CO2.

371895804bb5.title: Carbon sequestration
371895804bb5.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
371895804bb5.sentence: Shale is an example of a very good caprock, with a permeability of 10^−5 to 10^−9 Darcy.

d8c4c00458ae.title: Carbon sequestration
d8c4c00458ae.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
d8c4c00458ae.sentence: If there are fault planes near the injection zone, there is a possibility the CO2 could migrate along the fault to the surface, leaking into the atmosphere, which would be potentially dangerous to life in the surrounding area.

8249a417c635.title: Carbon sequestration
8249a417c635.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
8249a417c635.sentence: Another risk related to carbon sequestration is induced seismicity.

961c99fc5c31.title: Carbon sequestration
961c99fc5c31.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
961c99fc5c31.sentence: If the injection of CO2 creates pressures underground that are too high, the formation will fracture, potentially causing an earthquake.

7f51b080f10b.title: Carbon sequestration
7f51b080f10b.section: Geological carbon sequestration > Underground storage in suitable geologic formations
7f51b080f10b.sentence: In 2025, research indicated that, of nearly 12,000 GtCO2 of theoretical carbon storage capacity, just 1,460 GtCO2 is risk-free, significantly less than most estimates suggested.

d00e47faf6cd.title: Carbon sequestration

183cf42a8cbe.sentence: Supply-side environmental policy refers to regulations that limit or discourage the extraction of natural resources.

ce4d89436d4b.title: Supply-side environmental policy

dd529bec9ab8.title: Supply-side environmental policy

0a7f3413e1fe.title: Supply-side environmental policy

80b42ac6e898.title: Supply-side environmental policy
80b42ac6e898.sentence: Hoel (1994) subsequently showed that an optimal climate policy for a country, or a coalition of countries, is generally a combination of two policy instruments: Demand-side policies and supply-side policies.

d4c52eb532ea.title: Supply-side environmental policy

dead68d8bbd4.title: Supply-side environmental policy

5cc6b9e1924a.title: Net-zero emissions
5cc6b9e1924a.sentence: Global net-zero emissions are reached when greenhouse gas emissions and removals due to human activities are in balance.

bf10840a317f.title: Net-zero emissions
bf10840a317f.sentence: Net-zero emissions is often shortened to net zero.

4fe931beed59.title: Net-zero emissions
4fe931beed59.sentence: Reaching net zero is necessary to slow global warming.

a2795031165d.sentence: Once global net zero is achieved, further global warming is expected to significantly slow down, but the effects of existing atmospheric greenhouse gases will still contribute to continued warming.

57f1ff56e297.title: Net-zero emissions

122bdd817f85.title: Net-zero emissions

2f2d991f7fce.title: Net-zero emissions

e4a482f1cbb7.title: Net-zero emissions

c123a7e6cebd.title: Net-zero emissions

4b618e01235f.title: Net-zero emissions

5294e5767cc2.title: Net-zero emissions

35b57e19a12c.title: Net-zero emissions

9f840570650e.title: Carbon dioxide removal
9f840570650e.sentence: Carbon dioxide removal (CDR) is a process in which carbon dioxide (CO2) is removed from Earth's atmosphere by deliberate human activities and durably stored in geological, terrestrial, or marine reservoirs, or in products.

250e98c81b72.title: Carbon dioxide removal
250e98c81b72.sentence: This process is also known as carbon removal, greenhouse gas removal or negative emissions.

24098a61ee22.title: Carbon dioxide removal
24098a61ee22.sentence: Synonyms for CDR include greenhouse gas removal (GGR), negative emissions technology, and carbon removal.

8edbf238daec.title: Carbon dioxide removal
8edbf238daec.sentence: Achieving net zero emissions will require first and foremost deep and sustained cuts in emissions, and then—in addition—the use of CDR ("CDR is what puts the net into net zero emissions" ).

d783b441b063.title: Carbon dioxide removal
d783b441b063.sentence: It is not feasible to bring net emissions to zero without CDR as certain types of emissions are technically difficult to eliminate.

1847defb12ed.title: Carbon dioxide removal
1847defb12ed.sentence: Emissions that are difficult to eliminate include nitrous oxide emissions from agriculture, aviation emissions, and some industrial emissions.

2539c7464968.title: Carbon dioxide removal

d8af150ebdd4.sentence: This is equivalent to 4% of the greenhouse gases emitted per year by human activities.

23e7e31edb92.title: Carbon dioxide removal
23e7e31edb92.sentence: When used to sequester the carbon from a fossil fuel-fired power plant, CCS reduces emissions from continued use of the point source, but does not reduce the amount of carbon dioxide already in the atmosphere.

d7430286b72b.title: Direct air capture
d7430286b72b.sentence: Direct air capture (DAC) is the use of chemical or physical processes to extract carbon dioxide (CO2) directly from the ambient air.

029fc6a3f915.title: Direct air capture
029fc6a3f915.sentence: If the extracted CO2 is then sequestered in safe long-term storage, the overall process is called direct air carbon capture and sequestration (DACCS), achieving carbon dioxide removal.

995d290d44b4.title: Direct air capture
995d290d44b4.sentence: In contrast to carbon capture and storage (CCS) which captures emissions from a large point source such as a factory, DAC reduces the carbon dioxide concentration in the atmosphere as a whole.

b0d76557fa5e.title: Direct air capture
b0d76557fa5e.sentence: In the contacting stage, the DAC system transports atmospheric air containing CO2 to the equipment using large-scale fans.

15ae61e5b83e.title: Direct air capture
15ae61e5b83e.sentence: Subsequently, in the CO2 capture stage, CO2 rapidly and effectively binds with liquid solvents in chemical reactors or solid sorbents in filters, which must possess binding energies equivalent to that of CO2.

c7201910e118.title: Direct air capture
c7201910e118.sentence: These chemical media are subsequently stripped of CO2 through the application of energy (namely heat), resulting in a CO2 stream that can undergo dehydration and compression, while simultaneously regenerating the chemical media for reuse.

42a0da45d1e1.title: Direct air capture

fb75552ca8ba.sentence: Bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS) is the process of extracting bioenergy from biomass and capturing and storing the carbon dioxide (CO2) that is produced.

0bf654b5ce00.title: Bioenergy with carbon capture and storage

6a0406499839.title: Bioenergy with carbon capture and storage

f2487e34502c.title: Bioenergy with carbon capture and storage

3807a30a87d5.title: Geoengineering
3807a30a87d5.sentence: Geoengineering (also known as climate engineering or climate intervention) is the deliberate large-scale interventions in the Earth’s climate system intended to counteract human-caused climate change.

4d31c28cb35d.title: Geoengineering
4d31c28cb35d.sentence: The term commonly encompasses two broad categories: large-scale carbon dioxide removal (CDR) and solar radiation modification (SRM).

fb5560c22bf6.title: Geoengineering
fb5560c22bf6.sentence: CDR involves techniques to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and is generally considered a form of climate change mitigation.

ef0df8eb3ca0.title: Geoengineering
ef0df8eb3ca0.sentence: SRM aims to reduce global warming by reflecting a small portion of sunlight (solar radiation) away from Earth and back into space.

77ce8ed4441b.title: Geoengineering
77ce8ed4441b.sentence: Although historically grouped together, these approaches differ substantially in mechanisms, timelines, and risk profiles, and are now typically discussed separately.

2b7f41f685eb.title: Geoengineering
2b7f41f685eb.sentence: One common objection is that focusing on these technologies could undermine efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

c772c2e4ce35.title: Geoengineering

20cbb919998b.title: Solar radiation modification
20cbb919998b.sentence: Solar radiation modification (SRM), also called solar geoengineering, is a group of large-scale approaches to reduce global warming by increasing the amount of sunlight that is reflected away from Earth and back to outer space.

08c068ed4a21.title: Solar radiation modification
08c068ed4a21.sentence: It is not intended to replace efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, but rather to complement them as a potential way to limit global warming.

1d6f4540eb78.title: Solar radiation modification

aecca308b088.title: Solar radiation modification
aecca308b088.sentence: However, its effects would vary by region and season, and the resulting climate would differ from one that had not experienced warming.

58885c90ea28.title: Solar radiation modification

f417aff3e457.title: Solar radiation modification

3000e0b3adab.title: Solar radiation modification

6757a3932270.sentence: One of the main reasons for the low credibility of many net zero claims is their heavy reliance on carbon credits.

16540678ceee.sentence: Enhanced weathering, also termed ocean alkalinity enhancement when proposed for carbon credit systems, is a process that aims to accelerate natural weathering by spreading finely ground silicate rock, such as basalt, onto surfaces, speeding up chemical reactions between rocks, water, and air.
