e715896c8de8.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
e715896c8de8.section: Membership and participation > Annex I countries
e715896c8de8.sentence: There are 43 Annex I Parties including the European Union.

68256f2e135b.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
68256f2e135b.section: Membership and participation > Annex I countries
68256f2e135b.sentence: Of these, 24 are also Annex II Parties, including the European Union, and 14 are Economies in Transition.

e1992fb99f2b.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
e1992fb99f2b.section: Membership and participation > Classification of Parties and their commitments
e1992fb99f2b.sentence: The 14 EITs are the former centrally-planned (Soviet) economies of Russia and Eastern Europe.

3bcc8670deba.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
3bcc8670deba.sentence: The developed countries are called Annex I countries, and should adopt national policies and take corresponding measures to limit their emissions of greenhouse gases.

770636ff740f.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
770636ff740f.sentence: They should report on steps for returning individually or jointly to their 1990 greenhouse gas emission levels.

b993dfc98399.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
b993dfc98399.section: Membership and participation > Classification of Parties and their commitments
b993dfc98399.sentence: - Annex II: Of the Parties listed in Annex I of the convention, 24 are also listed in Annex II of the convention, including the European Union.

4f6ca457d269.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
4f6ca457d269.section: Membership and participation > Classification of Parties and their commitments
4f6ca457d269.sentence: These Parties are made up of members of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD): these Parties consist of the members of the OECD in 1992, minus Turkey, plus the EU.

848d767567e9.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
848d767567e9.section: Membership and participation > Classification of Parties and their commitments
848d767567e9.sentence: Annex II Parties are required to provide financial and technical support to the EITs and developing countries to assist them in reducing their greenhouse gas emissions (climate change mitigation) and manage the impacts of climate change (climate change adaptation).

7be0f0207757.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
7be0f0207757.section: Membership and participation > Classification of Parties and their commitments
7be0f0207757.sentence: - Least-developed countries (LDCs): 49 Parties are LDCs, and are given special status under the treaty in view of their limited capacity to adapt to the effects of climate change.

eed22f3a407f.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
eed22f3a407f.section: Membership and participation > Classification of Parties and their commitments
eed22f3a407f.sentence: Developing countries may volunteer to become Annex I countries when they are sufficiently developed.

c811774427c1.title: Kyoto Protocol
c811774427c1.sentence: The Kyoto Protocol (Japanese: 京都議定書, Hepburn: Kyōto Giteisho) was an international treaty which extended the 1992 United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) that commits state parties to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, based on the scientific consensus that global warming is occurring and that human-made CO2 emissions are driving it.

44d19a57dbe4.title: Kyoto Protocol
44d19a57dbe4.sentence: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in Kyoto, Japan, on 11 December 1997 and entered into force on 16 February 2005.

0752933a5a3a.title: Kyoto Protocol
0752933a5a3a.sentence: The main feature of the Protocol is that it established legally binding commitments to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases for Annex I Parties.

c7e797be9417.title: Kyoto Protocol
c7e797be9417.sentence: The Protocol was based on the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities: it acknowledged that individual countries have different capabilities in combating climate change, owing to economic development, and therefore placed the obligation to reduce current emissions on developed countries on the basis that they are historically responsible for the current levels of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

cebd5d2b58e9.title: Kyoto Protocol
cebd5d2b58e9.sentence: The Kyoto Protocol applied to the seven greenhouse gases listed in Annex A: carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), perfluorocarbons (PFCs), sulfur hexafluoride (SF6), nitrogen trifluoride (NF3).

dbca3328b46f.title: Kyoto Protocol
dbca3328b46f.sentence: The Protocol's first commitment period started in 2008 and ended in 2012.

4b715c68d11a.title: Kyoto Protocol
4b715c68d11a.sentence: In total, the 36 countries that fully participated in the Protocol were committed to reducing their aggregate emissions by 4% from the 1990 base year.

106d22d6ee13.title: Kyoto Protocol
106d22d6ee13.sentence: Their average annual emissions in 2008–2012 were 24.2% below the 1990 level.

1c2804e8947a.title: Kyoto Protocol
1c2804e8947a.sentence: The large reductions were mainly thanks to the dissolution of the Soviet Union, which reduced the emissions of the Eastern Bloc by tens of percents in the early 1990s.

c650e1c27383.title: Kyoto Protocol
c650e1c27383.sentence: In addition, the 2008 financial crisis significantly reduced emissions during the first Kyoto commitment period.

e63089d445cb.title: Kyoto Protocol
e63089d445cb.sentence: Even though these countries significantly reduced their emissions during the Kyoto commitment period, other countries increased their emissions so much that the global emissions increased by 32% from 1990 to 2010.

116bc38133c3.title: Kyoto Protocol
116bc38133c3.sentence: The 36 countries that were committed to emission reductions only accounted for 24% of the global greenhouse gas emissions in 2010.

a6e7e4267468.title: Kyoto Protocol
a6e7e4267468.sentence: Because the United States did not ratify and Canada withdrew, the emission limits remained in force for 36 countries.

10508a83ab13.title: Kyoto Protocol
10508a83ab13.sentence: Other developed countries without second-round targets were Canada (which withdrew from the Kyoto Protocol in 2012) and the United States (which did not ratify).

f1cd781232fd.title: Kyoto Protocol
f1cd781232fd.sentence: This resulted in the 2015 adoption of the Paris Agreement, which is a separate instrument under the UNFCCC rather than an amendment of the Kyoto Protocol.

b895609e9ca0.title: Paris Agreement
b895609e9ca0.sentence: The Paris Agreement (also called the Paris Accords or Paris Climate Accords) is an international treaty on climate change that was signed in 2016.

46f274537710.title: Paris Agreement
46f274537710.sentence: The treaty covers climate change mitigation, adaptation, and finance.

f8edc8993ad3.title: Paris Agreement
f8edc8993ad3.sentence: The Paris Agreement has a long-term temperature goal which is to keep the rise in global surface temperature to well below 2 °C (3.6 °F) above pre-industrial levels.

da09ffd39659.title: Paris Agreement
da09ffd39659.sentence: The treaty also states that preferably the limit of the increase should only be 1.5 °C (2.7 °F).

1c49b62ee0ed.title: Paris Agreement
1c49b62ee0ed.sentence: They should even reach net zero by the middle of the 21st century.

73b62d261fa1.title: Paris Agreement
73b62d261fa1.sentence: The Paris Agreement was negotiated by 196 parties at the 2015 United Nations Climate Change Conference near Paris, France.

68e505796c6b.title: Paris Agreement
68e505796c6b.sentence: After the European Union ratified the agreement, sufficient countries had ratified the agreement responsible for enough of the world's greenhouse gases for the agreement to enter into force on 4 November 2016.

c24dd5d23de2.title: Paris Agreement
c24dd5d23de2.sentence: Under the agreement, each country must determine, plan, and regularly report on its contributions.

7800726a18bc.title: Paris Agreement
7800726a18bc.sentence: No mechanism forces a country to set specific emissions targets, but each target should go beyond previous targets.

9ebeeeebb973.title: Paris Agreement
9ebeeeebb973.sentence: In contrast to the 1997 Kyoto Protocol, the distinction between developed and developing countries is blurred, so that the latter also have to submit plans for emission reductions.

c34d5e5e9a00.title: Paris Agreement
c34d5e5e9a00.section: Parties > Countries that have ratified or acceded
c34d5e5e9a00.sentence: The EU and 194 states, totalling over 98% of greenhouse gas emissions, have ratified or acceded to the agreement.

2dcd2b342488.title: Paris Agreement
2dcd2b342488.sentence: The United States, the second largest emitter, withdrew from the agreement in 2020, rejoined in 2021, and withdrew again in 2026.

400a5470179c.title: Paris Agreement
400a5470179c.section: Specific topics of concern > Loss and damage
400a5470179c.sentence: It is recognized as a separate pillar of the Paris Agreement.

28eb6c7328cb.title: Paris Agreement
28eb6c7328cb.section: Specific topics of concern > Loss and damage
28eb6c7328cb.sentence: In the end, the agreement calls for "averting, minimizing, and addressing loss and damage" but specifies that it cannot be used as the basis for liability.

01d2eb8d7b94.title: Paris Agreement
01d2eb8d7b94.sentence: After the Paris Agreement was signed, global emissions continued to rise rather than fall.

53d6b3370f22.title: Paris Agreement
53d6b3370f22.sentence: The effectiveness of the Paris Agreement to reach its climate goals is under debate, with most experts saying it is insufficient for its more ambitious goal of keeping global temperature rise under 1.5 °C.

36a8c9647743.title: Paris Agreement
36a8c9647743.sentence: Drafted | 30 November – 12 December 2015 in Le Bourget, France

c05f9ff386dc.title: Paris Agreement
c05f9ff386dc.sentence: The Paris Agreement was opened for signature on 22 April 2016 (Earth Day) at a ceremony inside the UN headquarters in New York City.

3877ca6d519f.title: Nationally determined contribution
3877ca6d519f.sentence: The nationally determined contributions (NDCs) are commitments that countries make to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions as part of climate change mitigation.

88125f3ee1fb.title: Nationally determined contribution
88125f3ee1fb.sentence: NDCs embody efforts by each country to reduce national emissions and adapt to the impacts of climate change.

3b68c134b87a.title: Nationally determined contribution
3b68c134b87a.sentence: Nationally determined contributions (NDCs) are "at the heart of the Paris Agreement and the achievement of its long-term goals".

a32d0726302f.title: Nationally determined contribution
a32d0726302f.sentence: Countries determine themselves what contributions they should make to achieve the aims of the treaty.

12b5968e301d.title: Nationally determined contribution
12b5968e301d.sentence: The contributions should be set every five years and are to be registered by the UNFCCC Secretariat.

15b69e4fa8ff.title: Nationally determined contribution
15b69e4fa8ff.sentence: Each further ambition should be more ambitious than the previous one, known as the principle of progression.

7817df7e32b4.title: Nationally determined contribution
7817df7e32b4.sentence: While the NDCs themselves are not binding, the procedures surrounding them are.

b0eaad57894b.title: Nationally determined contribution
b0eaad57894b.sentence: These procedures include the obligation to prepare, communicate and maintain successive NDCs, set a new one every five years, and provide information about the implementation.

bf73fe3ab3c4.title: Nationally determined contribution
bf73fe3ab3c4.sentence: There is no mechanism to force a country to set a NDC target by a specific date, nor to meet their targets.

3c3269352cee.title: Nationally determined contribution
3c3269352cee.sentence: Some of the pledges in the NDCs are unconditional, but others are conditional on outside factors such as getting finance and technical support, the ambition from other parties or the details of rules of the Paris Agreement that are yet to be set.

95f2ab124e96.title: Nationally determined contribution
95f2ab124e96.sentence: NDCs are the first greenhouse gas targets under the UNFCCC that apply equally to both developed and developing countries.

c75c411a3e40.title: Nationally determined contribution
c75c411a3e40.sentence: The rates of emissions reductions need to increase by 80% beyond NDCs to likely meet the 2 °C upper target range of the Paris Agreement (data as of 2021).

44a67572e90e.title: Nationally determined contribution
44a67572e90e.sentence: Therefore, with current trends the probability of staying below 2 °C of warming is only 5% – and if NDCs were met and continued post-2030 by all signatory systems the probability would be 26%.

884876987da4.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
884876987da4.sentence: Article 6 of the 2015 Paris Agreement sets out how countries (“Parties”) may cooperate voluntarily to implement their nationally determined contributions (NDCs).

f0930dbc2a4c.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
f0930dbc2a4c.sentence: It is intended to allow higher ambition in mitigation and adaptation while promoting sustainable development, and it conditions cooperation on environmental integrity, transparency and robust accounting, especially to avoid double counting of the same mitigation outcome across countries’ NDCs.

e4ac457728b7.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
e4ac457728b7.sentence: The article establishes three cooperation pathways.

eedc0c0b0db3.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
eedc0c0b0db3.sentence: Under Article 6.2, Parties may use “cooperative approaches” to transfer and use internationally transferred mitigation outcomes (ITMOs) through bilateral or multilateral arrangements, subject to guidance adopted by the Conference of the Parties serving as the meeting of the Parties to the Paris Agreement (CMA).

8a375863ed8a.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
8a375863ed8a.sentence: Article 6.4 creates a UNFCCC-supervised crediting mechanism—referred to by the UNFCCC as the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM)—that registers mitigation activities and issues units (A6.4ERs), including provisions such as a share of proceeds for the Adaptation Fund and cancellation of a portion of units to deliver an overall mitigation in global emissions (OMGE).

c8b13c331ee4.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
c8b13c331ee4.sentence: Article 6.8 establishes a framework and work programme for “non-market approaches”, which support cooperation without international transfers of mitigation outcomes.

b3243cfbd84d.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
b3243cfbd84d.sentence: Parties adopted the core “Article 6 rulebook” at COP26, and later CMA decisions have continued to operationalize technical standards and reporting infrastructure.

ec7dba764220.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
ec7dba764220.sentence: Following the adoption of the “Article 6 rulebook” at the COP26 (CMA.3, Glasgow, 2021), negotiations under Article 6 have focused largely on implementation—i.e., how the agreed rules are applied in practice through reporting, centralized infrastructure and technical standards—rather than on whether cooperation mechanisms should exist.

6c21d00dae53.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
6c21d00dae53.sentence: Article 2 of the convention says this "should be achieved within a time-frame sufficient to allow ecosystems to adapt naturally to climate change, to ensure that food production is not threatened and to enable economic development to proceed in a sustainable manner".

1c8f82b8ee47.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
1c8f82b8ee47.section: Analysis > Interpreting ultimate objective in Article 2
1c8f82b8ee47.sentence: To stabilize atmospheric GHG concentrations, global anthropogenic GHG emissions would need to peak then decline (see climate change mitigation).

9957cc6e4608.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
9957cc6e4608.section: Analysis > Interpreting ultimate objective in Article 2
9957cc6e4608.sentence: Lower stabilization levels would require emissions to peak and decline earlier compared to higher stabilization levels.

7d22dbf98c85.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
7d22dbf98c85.section: Analysis > Interpreting ultimate objective in Article 2
7d22dbf98c85.sentence: There are a range of views over what level of climate change is dangerous.

fff951073fc0.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
fff951073fc0.section: Analysis > Interpreting ultimate objective in Article 2
fff951073fc0.sentence: Scientific analysis can provide information on the risks of climate change, but deciding which risks are dangerous requires value judgements.

8638c82ae688.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
8638c82ae688.section: Analysis > Interpreting ultimate objective in Article 2
8638c82ae688.sentence: Following the precautionary principle, uncertainty (about the exact effects of climate change) is not a reason for inaction, and this is acknowledged in Article 3.3 of the UNFCCC.

e681b07da2f8.title: Climate target
e681b07da2f8.sentence: A climate target, climate goal or climate pledge is a measurable long-term commitment for climate policy and energy policy with the aim of limiting the climate change.

cdec7f3293bc.title: Climate target
cdec7f3293bc.sentence: Researchers within, among others, the UN climate panel have identified probable consequences of global warming for people and nature at different levels of warming.

31420ab3dd6f.title: Climate target
31420ab3dd6f.sentence: Based on this, politicians in a large number of countries have agreed on temperature targets for warming, which is the basis for scientifically calculated carbon budgets and ways to achieve these targets.

4474a250282b.title: Climate target
4474a250282b.sentence: This in turn forms the basis for politically decided global and national emission targets for greenhouse gases, targets for fossil-free energy production and efficient energy use, and for the extent of planned measures for climate change mitigation and adaptation.

6fc9a0e8e10d.title: Climate target
6fc9a0e8e10d.sentence: At least 164 countries have implemented climate targets in their national climate legislation.

6da0a8eaca1c.title: Climate target
6da0a8eaca1c.sentence: - Targets for 2008 to 2012: In the Kyoto Protocol of 1997, 160 countries committed to reducing their greenhouse gas emissions by an average of 5.2 percent over the period 2008 to 2012 compared to 1990 levels.

31049b8e3dde.title: Climate target
31049b8e3dde.sentence: An "emissions target" may be distinguished from an emissions budget, as an emissions target may be internationally or nationally set in accordance with objectives other than a specific global temperature.

0c31f0b36564.title: Climate target
0c31f0b36564.sentence: This includes targets created for their political palatability, rather than budgets scientifically determined to meet a specific temperature target.

ada7ab3e4b22.title: Climate target
ada7ab3e4b22.sentence: Many countries' emissions targets are above the scientifically calculated allowable emissions to remain below a certain temperature threshold.

86c47ad7a5b1.title: Climate target
86c47ad7a5b1.sentence: Many emissions pathways, budgets and targets also rely on the implementation of negative emissions technology.

0f9540d3ebe6.title: Climate target
0f9540d3ebe6.sentence: These currently undeveloped technologies are predicted to pull net emissions down even as source emissions are not reduced.

231e83a58354.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
231e83a58354.sentence: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) is a principle that was formalized in the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) of Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro, 1992.

22ac53c8feb2.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
22ac53c8feb2.sentence: The CBDR principle acknowledges that all states have shared obligation to address environmental destruction but denies equal responsibility of all states with regard to environmental protection.

5d9d1cd9bbed.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
5d9d1cd9bbed.sentence: Industrialization proceeded in developed countries much earlier than it did in developing countries.

ae5f2e28207d.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
ae5f2e28207d.sentence: States came to an agreement that developed countries contributed more to environmental degradation and should have greater responsibility for climate change mitigation than developing countries should.

83ea28e6d2ac.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
83ea28e6d2ac.sentence: The CBDR principle could therefore be said to be based on the polluter-pays principle where historical contribution to climate change and respective ability to combat climate change become measures of responsibility for environmental protection.

0f9a5da96233.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
0f9a5da96233.sentence: UNFCCC 1992, Article 3 paragraph 1, "The Parties should protect the climate system for the benefit of present and future generations of humankind, on the basis of equity and in accordance with their common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities.

4094339c5d75.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
4094339c5d75.sentence: Accordingly, the developed country Parties should take the lead in combating climate change and the adverse effects thereof."

214faaa0dde2.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
214faaa0dde2.sentence: Under prior agreements, such as the Kyoto Protocol, there was a rigid distinction between Annex 1 and Annex 2 countries among the parties to the Kyoto Protocol, which determined the countries' responsibilities.

cab000e8428d.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
cab000e8428d.sentence: Industrialized (Annex 1) countries had to observe strict limits on emissions, while other countries did not.

57588fc007cc.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
57588fc007cc.sentence: Under the Paris Agreement, each country makes its own nationally determined contribution based on its own national circumstances, and as circumstances change, so do the responsibilities.

c1b50c0d06b3.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
c1b50c0d06b3.sentence: In 2002, Lavanya Rajamani argued that developing countries would have an unfair economic advantage because they would not face the same restrictions as developed counties would.

ffc6357ee1cf.title: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities
ffc6357ee1cf.sentence: Developing countries, however, argued that their carbon emissions are essential to their survival, while those of the developed countries are 'luxury emissions.'

9207f2a0e112.title: Climate finance
9207f2a0e112.sentence: Public finance is provided directly by governments or via intermediaries such as development finance institutions (e.g. MDBs or other development agencies).

cb83aa72a5dd.title: Climate finance
cb83aa72a5dd.sentence: It can also be channeled through multilateral climate funds.

2ca5e518e71a.title: Climate finance
2ca5e518e71a.sentence: Private finance can come from commercial banks, institutional investors, other private equity or other companies or from household or community funding.

0fdf0c7d9c4d.title: Climate finance
0fdf0c7d9c4d.sentence: The vast majority of tracked finance (around 98%) has originated from public sources.

6d4998c87e7c.title: Climate finance
6d4998c87e7c.sentence: This is partly because of the lack of a well-defined income stream or business case with an attractive return on investment on projects.

1310e67f6e81.title: Climate finance
1310e67f6e81.sentence: Only around 4-8% of total climate finance has been allocated to adaptation.

2594c23410fe.title: Climate finance
2594c23410fe.section: Subcategories > Finance for adaptation > Adaptation costs and adaptation financing needs
2594c23410fe.sentence: In economic terms, the cost to benefit ratio of adaptation shows that each dollar can deliver large benefits.

34bf4ffafc9b.title: Climate finance
34bf4ffafc9b.section: Subcategories > Finance for adaptation > Adaptation costs and adaptation financing needs
34bf4ffafc9b.sentence: For example, it is estimated that every US$1 billion invested in adaptation against coastal flooding leads to a US$14 billion reduction in economic damages.

5a5bcb6c644c.title: Climate finance
5a5bcb6c644c.section: Subcategories > Finance for adaptation > Adaptation costs and adaptation financing needs
5a5bcb6c644c.sentence: A 2023 study found the overall adaptation costs for all developing countries to be around US$215 billion per year for the period up to 2030.

9e4159ae3b9d.title: Climate finance
9e4159ae3b9d.section: Subcategories > Finance for adaptation > Current levels of financing and the finance gap
9e4159ae3b9d.sentence: 63% of the adaptation-specific funding was provided as loans, and 36% as grants.

ff36dbbea0aa.title: Climate finance
ff36dbbea0aa.section: Subcategories > Finance for adaptation > Current levels of financing and the finance gap
ff36dbbea0aa.sentence: Disbursement of funds for adaptation, at 66% of the amounts committed, is much lower than for mitigation.

1eb6e5f00f32.title: Climate finance
1eb6e5f00f32.sentence: On a worldwide scale, mitigation financing accounts for over 90% of investment in climate finance.

c7bf72ce4989.title: Climate finance
c7bf72ce4989.sentence: Around 70% of this mitigation money has gone towards renewable energy, however low-carbon mobility is a key development sector.

f437d97036d8.title: Climate finance
f437d97036d8.sentence: Key sectors for investment have been renewable energy, energy efficiency and transport.

c2540e8a2cd9.title: Climate finance
c2540e8a2cd9.sentence: Most of the estimated US$83.3 billion provided to developing countries in 2020, was targeted at mitigation (US$48.6 billion, or 58%).

7f682203afd0.title: Climate finance
7f682203afd0.section: Subcategories > Finance for mitigation > Mitigation costs and mitigation financing needs
7f682203afd0.sentence: The IEA estimates that limiting the rise in global temperature to below 2 Celsius by the end of the century will require an average of $3.5 trillion a year in energy sector investments until 2050.

0cfc5d85e6ca.title: Climate finance
0cfc5d85e6ca.sentence: The 2018 Biennial Assessment estimated financing needs for mitigation between 2020 and 2030 to be US$1.7-2.4 trillion per year.

c1c47e7f70ef.title: Global stocktake
c1c47e7f70ef.sentence: The Global Stocktake (GST) is a fundamental component of the Paris Agreement which is used to monitor its implementation and evaluate the collective progress made in achieving the agreed goals.

657bd7f0ffe9.title: Global stocktake
657bd7f0ffe9.section: Role as part of the Paris regime
657bd7f0ffe9.sentence: In addition, a Global Stocktake is carried out once every five years to assess the collective progress made towards achieving the long-term goals.

1499790750b5.title: Global stocktake
1499790750b5.sentence: The Global Stocktake thus links implementation of nationally determined contributions (NDCs) with the overarching goals of the Paris Agreement, and has the ultimate aim of raising climate ambition.

c5cc00c4c2ec.title: Global stocktake
c5cc00c4c2ec.section: Role as part of the Paris regime
c5cc00c4c2ec.sentence: The outcomes of the stocktake are to be taken into account when developing nationally determined contributions.

8a96cdbb5996.title: Global stocktake
8a96cdbb5996.sentence: However, the Global Stocktake takes a collective rather than an individual approach.

93516070963c.title: Global stocktake
93516070963c.sentence: This means that individual countries are not singled out and the outcomes of the stocktaking process should not allow conclusions to be drawn about the state of implementation in individual states.

580385abf289.title: Global stocktake
580385abf289.sentence: The question of whether the Global Stocktake should be limited to mitigation or should also include other aspects such as adaptation and the provision of climate finance has been the subject of controversial debate.

fc2ca1b6ee18.title: Global stocktake
fc2ca1b6ee18.sentence: In the run-up to the Climate Change Conference in Paris, however, the view prevailed that the Global Stocktake should take in all three.

bf5f397980c2.title: Global stocktake
bf5f397980c2.sentence: As part of the Global Stocktake, Article 14 of the Paris Agreement lists adaptation and the means of implementation and support.

9e7f50c25c74.title: Global stocktake
9e7f50c25c74.sentence: The modalities for implementation agreed at the Climate Change Conference in Katowice provide for three stocktake phases:

778ba1da3ed5.title: Global stocktake
778ba1da3ed5.section: Three-phase Global Stocktake > Phase 1: Information collection and preparation
778ba1da3ed5.sentence: Phase 1 involves collecting and preparing information needed to conduct the stocktake.

51ff9d118296.title: Global stocktake
51ff9d118296.section: Three-phase Global Stocktake > Phase 2: Technical assessment of information
51ff9d118296.sentence: In Phase 2, the information is assessed for collective progress in implementing the Paris Agreement and its long-term goals.

05cd607e2837.title: Global stocktake
05cd607e2837.section: Three-phase Global Stocktake > Phase 3: Political messages derived from the technical assessment
05cd607e2837.sentence: In Phase 3, the outcomes of the assessment flow into the policy process.

46dd1dd19b79.title: Global stocktake
46dd1dd19b79.sentence: The second Global Stocktake will begin in November 2026 at COP 31 in Antalya, Turkey, and will be concluded two years later at COP 33.

13de39446065.title: Paris Agreement
13de39446065.sentence: Article 13 of the Paris Agreement articulates an "enhanced transparency framework for action and support" that establishes harmonized monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) requirements.

60625cfb05fc.title: Paris Agreement
60625cfb05fc.sentence: The parties are legally bound to have their progress tracked by technical expert review to assess achievement toward the NDC and to determine ways to strengthen ambition.

630c511ed80a.title: Paris Agreement
630c511ed80a.sentence: Both developed and developing nations must report every two years on their mitigation efforts, and all parties will be subject to technical and peer review.

ee47230391b1.title: Paris Agreement
ee47230391b1.sentence: While the enhanced transparency framework is universal, the framework is meant to provide "built-in flexibility" to distinguish between developed and developing countries' capacities.

d40046bf61e0.title: Paris Agreement
d40046bf61e0.sentence: Flexibility can be incorporated into the enhanced transparency framework via the scope, level of detail, or frequency of reporting, tiered based on a country's capacity.

0626dcd47eff.title: Climate debt
0626dcd47eff.sentence: Climate debt is the debt said to be owed to developing countries by developed countries for the damage caused by their disproportionately large contributions to climate change.

075193df541b.title: Climate debt
075193df541b.sentence: The concept of climate debt is part of the broader concept of ecological debt.

99cac33560c8.title: Climate debt
99cac33560c8.sentence: The concept of climate debt was first introduced in the 1990s by non-governmental organizations.

50b477be7658.title: Climate debt
50b477be7658.sentence: The main components of climate debt are adaptation debt and emissions debt.

513d0858f9f9.title: Climate debt
513d0858f9f9.sentence: Adaptation debt is claimed to be owed by developed countries to developing countries to assist them in their adaptation to climate change.

1f54180f9c79.title: Climate debt
1f54180f9c79.sentence: Emissions debt is claimed to be owed by developed countries for their disproportionate amount of greenhouse gas emissions.

4ab44a68a463.title: Climate debt
4ab44a68a463.sentence: It has received increased attention since its submission to the 2009 United Nations Climate Change Conference, where developing countries, led by Bolivia, sought the repayment of climate debt.

00f3a64ac5c4.title: Climate debt
00f3a64ac5c4.sentence: Support for climate debt generally comes from developing countries and environmentalist NGOs, with criticisms of climate debt usually coming from developed nations.

5e2eeefff807.title: Climate debt
5e2eeefff807.sentence: Arguments used to support this claim include the following: although countries are responsible for the emissions they have made, they should not bear the guilt or owe debts; the negative effects of carbon emissions were not understood until recently, and therefore any emissions made before this understanding should not be a source of guilt; countries should not bear the guilt for the actions of their ancestors, over which the current generation had no control.

fdf53b1a28fe.title: Climate debt
fdf53b1a28fe.sentence: Many critics have claimed that, although the concept of climate debt may be ethically sound, it may actually undermine political negotiations regarding climate change due to its "adversarial" basis, and negotiations should instead use a different framework.

95bd52a4c621.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
95bd52a4c621.section: Development > Six priority areas (Action for Climate Empowerment)
95bd52a4c621.sentence: Action for Climate Empowerment (ACE) is a term adopted by the UNFCCC in 2015 to have a better name for this topic than "Article 6".

977c0a6c061e.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
977c0a6c061e.section: Development > Six priority areas (Action for Climate Empowerment)
977c0a6c061e.sentence: It refers to Article 6 of the convention's original text (1992), focusing on six priority areas: education, training, public awareness, public participation, public access to information, and international cooperation on these issues.

9895bb8cb855.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
9895bb8cb855.section: Development > Six priority areas (Action for Climate Empowerment)
9895bb8cb855.sentence: ACE calls on governments to develop and implement educational and public awareness programmes, train scientific, technical and managerial personnel, foster access to information, and promote public participation in addressing climate change and its effects.

3bb23f547353.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
3bb23f547353.sentence: The overall umbrella and processes of the UNFCCC and the adopted Kyoto Protocol have been criticized by some as not having achieved their stated goals of reducing the emission of greenhouse gases.

26d8459531a9.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
26d8459531a9.sentence: The UNFCCC is a multilateral body concerned with climate change and can be an inefficient system for enacting international policy: Because the framework system includes over 190 countries and because negotiations are governed by consensus, small groups of countries can often block progress.

eb736e9b704e.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
eb736e9b704e.sentence: In 2010, Japan stated that it will not sign up to a second Kyoto term, because it would impose restrictions on it not faced by its main economic competitors, China, India and Indonesia.

8021c30c2075.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
8021c30c2075.sentence: Further, the UNFCCC (mainly during the Kyoto protocol) failed to facilitate the transfer of environmentally sound technologies (SETs) which are mechanisms used to decrease the vulnerability of the human race against the unfavorable effects of climate change.

95b394c36bd2.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
95b394c36bd2.sentence: A "National Communication" is a type of report submitted by the countries that have ratified the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

7bbabd20baad.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
7bbabd20baad.sentence: National Communication reports are often several hundred pages long and cover a country's measures to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions as well as a description of its vulnerabilities and impacts from climate change.

761bcbccd46e.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
761bcbccd46e.sentence: Developed countries are required to submit National Communications every four years and developing countries should do so.

a36854c28e94.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
a36854c28e94.sentence: The (Intended) Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) that form the basis of the Paris Agreement are shorter and less detailed but also follow a standardized structure and are subject to technical review by experts.

d05fc275a29f.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
d05fc275a29f.sentence: Some Least Developed Countries have not submitted National Communications in the past 5–15 years, largely due to capacity constraints.

c75f9f1f30ed.title: Kyoto Protocol
c75f9f1f30ed.sentence: A second commitment period was agreed to in 2012 to extend the agreement to 2020, known as the Doha Amendment to the Kyoto Protocol, in which 37 countries had binding targets: Australia, the European Union (and its then 28 member states, now 27), Belarus, Iceland, Kazakhstan, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, and Ukraine.

07e48561a48a.title: Kyoto Protocol
07e48561a48a.sentence: On 8 December 2012, at the end of the 2012 United Nations Climate Change Conference, an agreement was reached to extend the Protocol to 2020 and to set a date of 2015 for the development of a successor document, to be implemented from 2020 (see lede for more information).

2d6d539423c8.title: Kyoto Protocol
2d6d539423c8.sentence: Japan, New Zealand, and Russia had participated in Kyoto's first-round but did not take on new targets in the second commitment period.

35cea26c78a9.title: Kyoto Protocol
35cea26c78a9.sentence: The Kyoto second commitment period applies to about 11% of annual global emissions of greenhouse gases.

b644125b6620.title: Kyoto Protocol
b644125b6620.sentence: It entered into force on 31 December 2020, following its acceptance by the mandated minimum of at least 144 states, although the second commitment period ended on the same day.

16daad36c021.title: Kyoto Protocol

16daad36c021.sentence: One of the environmental problems with IET is the large surplus of allowances that are available.

1ae528647eff.sentence: Unless other commitments were made to reduce the total surplus in allowances, such trade would not actually result in emissions being reduced (see also the section below on the Green Investment Scheme).

ca2e3457dd86.section: Principal concepts > Flexibility mechanisms > International emissions trading > Intergovernmental emissions trading
ca2e3457dd86.sentence: When the Kyoto treaty was negotiated, it was recognized that emissions targets for the EITs might lead to them having an excess number of allowances.

763b5a6cc3ed.sentence: This excess of allowances were viewed by the EITs as "headroom" to grow their economies.

f719b6ee5bff.section: Principal concepts > Flexibility mechanisms > International emissions trading > Intergovernmental emissions trading
f719b6ee5bff.sentence: OECD countries with a deficit could meet their Kyoto commitments by buying allowances from transition countries with a surplus.

3efeb2087d70.title: Kyoto Protocol
3efeb2087d70.section: Details of the agreement > Mechanism of compliance
3efeb2087d70.sentence: The protocol defines a mechanism of "compliance" as a "monitoring compliance with the commitments and penalties for non-compliance." According to Grubb (2003), the explicit consequences of non-compliance of the treaty are weak compared to domestic law.

f6d88498060c.section: Details of the agreement > Enforcing emission cuts
f6d88498060c.sentence: If the enforcement branch determines that an Annex I country is not in compliance with its emissions limitation, then that country is required to make up the difference during the second commitment period plus an additional 30%.

81c7b849f65a.section: Details of the agreement > Enforcing emission cuts
81c7b849f65a.sentence: In addition, that country will be suspended from making transfers under an emissions trading program.

0ee3014fed78.title: Kyoto Protocol
0ee3014fed78.section: Details of the agreement > Mechanism of compliance
0ee3014fed78.sentence: Yet, the compliance section of the treaty was highly contested in the Marrakesh Accords.

244baf600c82.title: 2 degree climate target
244baf600c82.sentence: The two degree target is the international climate policy goal of limiting global warming to less than two degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit) compared to pre-industrialization levels (1850–1900).

1e7f477379a9.title: 2 degree climate target
1e7f477379a9.sentence: This objective is a political determination based on scientific knowledge concerning the probable consequences of global warming, which dates from the Copenhagen Conference in 2009.

3bd346c0a25b.title: 2 degree climate target
3bd346c0a25b.sentence: It is an integral part of the Paris climate agreement.

a859d284ea0d.title: 2 degree climate target
a859d284ea0d.sentence: As a global target for limiting emissions, the 2 °C target has frequently been criticized for being higher than desirable, because two degrees of warming will have serious consequences for humans and the environment.

e179f9021bce.title: 2 degree climate target
e179f9021bce.sentence: The IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 °C (2018) included detailed analysis of the probable differences in impact of "limiting global warming to 1.5 °C compared with 2 °C", warning that a 2 °C temperature increase would worsen impacts that include extreme weather, Arctic sea ice decline, rising sea levels, coral bleaching, and ecosystem loss.

c301ec996e5d.title: 2 degree climate target
c301ec996e5d.sentence: As a result the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change predicts a likely increase between 2.1 and 2.9 °C in temperature by 2100, exceeding the 2 °C climate target.

00042f375e85.title: 2 degree climate target
00042f375e85.sentence: Even if temperatures increase above 2 °C, it may become possible to halt or reverse increases by late in the century and bring CO2 levels back to the levels identified by the Paris climate agreement.

a9870fa32360.title: 2 degree climate target
a9870fa32360.sentence: This type of scenario is referred to as an "overshoot pathway".

09bd0d4d42cb.title: 2 degree climate target
09bd0d4d42cb.sentence: Achieving such an outcome will require multigenerational management over many decades.

f148920ab096.title: Paris Agreement
f148920ab096.sentence: Many of the exact provisions of the Paris Agreement have yet to be straightened out, so that it may be too early to judge effectiveness.

200e3ce00d45.title: Paris Agreement
200e3ce00d45.sentence: According to the 2020 United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), with the current climate commitments of the Paris Agreement, global mean temperatures will likely rise by more than 3 °C by the end of the 21st century.

a1dea3162980.title: Paris Agreement
a1dea3162980.sentence: A pair of studies in Nature found that as of 2017 none of the major industrialized nations were implementing the policies they had pledged, and none met their pledged emission reduction targets, and even if they had, the sum of all member pledges (as of 2016) would not keep global temperature rise "well below 2°C".

95aeef89b445.title: Paris Agreement
95aeef89b445.sentence: According to the stocktake report, the agreement has a significant effect: while in 2010 the expected temperature rise by 2100 was 3.7–4.8 °C, at COP 27 it was 2.4–2.6 °C and if all countries will fulfill their long-term pledges even 1.7–2.1 °C. Despite it, the world is still very far from reaching the aim of the agreement: limiting temperature rise to 1.5 degrees.

14a32fa8b49f.title: Nationally determined contribution
14a32fa8b49f.sentence: Prior to the Paris Agreement in 2015, the NDCs were referred to as intended nationally determined contributions (INDCs) and were non-binding.

dacc8b82d092.title: Nationally determined contribution
dacc8b82d092.sentence: The INDCs were initial, voluntary pledges made by countries, whereas the NDCs are more committed but also not legally binding.

1a7299d0c0e3.title: Nationally determined contribution
1a7299d0c0e3.sentence: All countries that were parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) were asked to publish their intended nationally determined contributions (INDC) at the 2013 United Nations Climate Change Conference held in Warsaw, Poland, in November 2013.

be313a51f256.title: Nationally determined contribution
be313a51f256.sentence: The term was intended as a compromise between "quantified emissions limitation and reduction objective" (QELROs) and "Nationally Appropriate Mitigation Actions" (NAMAs) that the Kyoto Protocol used to describe the different legal obligations of developed and developing countries.

16149c092d0d.title: Nationally determined contribution

16149c092d0d.sentence: On 27 February 2015, Switzerland became the first nation to submit its INDC.

9c920cd1d0ec.title: Nationally determined contribution
9c920cd1d0ec.section: History > Intended nationally determined contributions (INDC) submissions
9c920cd1d0ec.sentence: Of surveyed countries, 85% reported that they were challenged by the short time frame available to develop INDCs.

34a74c9b292c.title: Nationally determined contribution
34a74c9b292c.sentence: However, they are set within a binding iterative "catalytic" framework designed to ratchet up climate action over time.

f83dcc1548a3.title: Nationally determined contribution
f83dcc1548a3.sentence: Once states have set their initial NDCs, these are expected to be updated on a 5-year cycle.

1bfeeafbcaea.title: Nationally determined contribution

7dc233e23043.title: Nationally determined contribution
7dc233e23043.sentence: These will be subjected to technical review, and will collectively feed into a global stocktaking exercise, itself operating on an offset 5-year cycle, where the overall sufficiency of NDCs collectively will be assessed.

a948d467351f.title: Nationally determined contribution
a948d467351f.sentence: The information gathered from parties' individual reports and reviews, along with the more comprehensive picture attained through the "global stocktake" will, in turn, feed back into and shape the formulation of states' subsequent pledges.

935a97e969e2.title: Pledge and review
935a97e969e2.sentence: Pledge and review is a method for facilitating international action against climate change.

034f2a56d52d.title: Pledge and review
034f2a56d52d.sentence: It involves nations each making a self-determined pledge relating to actions they expect to take in response to global warming, which they submit to the United Nations.

c2b969b677f7.title: Pledge and review
c2b969b677f7.sentence: Some time after the pledges have been submitted, there is a review process where nations assess each other's progress towards meeting the pledges.

807276f39071.title: Pledge and review
807276f39071.sentence: Then a further round of enhanced pledges can be made, and the process can further iterate.

189f21f186da.title: Pledge and review
189f21f186da.section: History > Relationship with other climate change mitigation methods
189f21f186da.sentence: The acceptance of legally binding emissions reductions targets imposed in a "top down" way by a central body such a United Nations agency.

c3798a6220dd.title: Pledge and review
c3798a6220dd.section: History > Relationship with other climate change mitigation methods
c3798a6220dd.sentence: And the "bottom up" pledge-and-review system where each party autonomously decides its own contribution.

460418e677ae.title: Pledge and review
460418e677ae.sentence: The pledge-and-review system was first proposed by Japan in 1991.

f4fe29771df4.title: Pledge and review
f4fe29771df4.sentence: The pledge-and-review system was formally rejected at the first Conference of the Parties (COP) which took place in Berlin, 1995.

7c2a972a9da8.title: Pledge and review
7c2a972a9da8.sentence: The focus switched to negotiations aimed at legally binding emission reduction targets, as embodied by the 1997 Kyoto Protocol.

321d8620c780.title: Pledge and review
321d8620c780.sentence: Due to challenges in securing international agreement to strengthen the only partially successful Kyoto Protocol, pledge-and-review was re-introduced as part of the 2009 Copenhagen Accord.

281555721603.title: Pledge and review
281555721603.sentence: The nations which had made a Copenhagen pledge were collectively responsible for about 80% of global GHG emissions, much more than the 25% covered by Kyoto targets in the first commitment period or the 15% covered by the commitment period later agreed at the 2012 Doha summit.

90f646ef114e.title: Pledge and review
90f646ef114e.sentence: Initially seen as an interim measure, by 2015 it had become the central approach of international efforts to encourage climate mitigation.

c721325d82f8.title: Pledge and review
c721325d82f8.sentence: Though in negotiations leading to the 2015 Paris Agreement, the name pledge-and-review was dropped; pledges are now formally called Nationally Determined Contributions.

ae331a135c3c.title: Pledge and review
ae331a135c3c.section: History > Relationship with other climate change mitigation methods
ae331a135c3c.sentence: In practice however, it has been much more challenging to get nations to agree to binding targets relating to GHG.

e9bed0017a88.title: Pledge and review
e9bed0017a88.section: History > Relationship with other climate change mitigation methods
e9bed0017a88.sentence: And even when they had signed up to a legally binding target, there is no reliable way to enforce such international law on a powerful nation.

d7bd03ff708d.title: Pledge and review
d7bd03ff708d.section: History > Relationship with other climate change mitigation methods
d7bd03ff708d.sentence: So after the relative failure of the Kyoto protocol and attempts to establish a more effective set of targets at Copenhagen, the pledge-and-review system became the dominant approach.

a91c5cf0ca79.title: Pledge and review
a91c5cf0ca79.sentence: In the early 1990s, the pledge-and-review system was heavily criticised by environmental groups; for example, Climate Action Network labelled it "hedge and retreat".

8d0331947f9f.title: Pledge and review
8d0331947f9f.sentence: It has also been criticised by academics, especially after the system was revived at Copenhagen with some calling it "scientifically inadequate" or "second best".

8c038f70110f.title: Pledge and review
8c038f70110f.sentence: However, other academics described pledge-and-review as an "essential pillar for climate change mitigation".

cbb9e4fcf6b6.title: Glasgow Climate Pact

7ba201a0a14d.title: Glasgow Climate Pact
7ba201a0a14d.sentence: The pact is the first climate agreement explicitly planning to reduce unabated coal usage.

403b1aa62b8b.title: Glasgow Climate Pact
403b1aa62b8b.sentence: A pledge to "phase out" coal was changed to "phase down" late in negotiation, for coal in India and coal in China and other coal reliant countries.

9ab9235edef0.title: Glasgow Climate Pact

b3dae82d045d.title: Glasgow Climate Pact

6f5b9bb9122c.title: Glasgow Climate Pact
6f5b9bb9122c.sentence: - A commitment to climate finance for developing countries.

4e70cac099b3.title: Glasgow Climate Pact
4e70cac099b3.sentence: The number of countries pledged to reach net-zero emissions passed 140.

cafe8ba89cba.title: Glasgow Climate Pact
cafe8ba89cba.sentence: More than 100 countries, including Brazil, pledged to reverse deforestation by 2030.

da1521538bdb.title: Montreal Protocol

e8b7af5ef5fd.title: Montreal Protocol

ad822283a781.title: Climate club
ad822283a781.sentence: A climate club is an international coalition of nations aimed a addressing global climate change mitigation.

6137a36d5c02.title: Climate club

c5931e02e29e.title: Climate reparations

c69037843fce.title: Climate reparations

81de8c217da4.title: Climate reparations

8f5ef14e5999.title: Climate reparations

febcbd87319c.title: Climate reparations

2c3d016a1679.title: Climate reparations

e6409bbc50be.title: Climate reparations

a19f89eebaa0.sentence: Green banks use public funds to leverage private investment in clean energy technologies that, despite their commercial viability, have struggled to establish a widespread presence in consumer markets.

67280dd6f91b.title: Green bank

67280dd6f91b.sentence: Green banks play a critical role in mitigating risks associated with low-carbon projects, rendering them more appealing to private investors.

6f53985fb03e.title: Green bank

6f53985fb03e.sentence: Different green banks employ various de-risking mechanisms, such as concessional finance or guarantees, to achieve this.

8a1186339bdb.title: Green bank

12b20b3e3f1c.sentence: - Internationally transferred mitigation outcomes (ITMOs): quantified mitigation outcomes (emission reductions or removals) transferred between Parties under Article 6.2 and used toward an NDC or another authorized international purpose, subject to agreed reporting and accounting rules intended to avoid double counting.

8de98e505636.sentence: In practice, ITMOs can represent quantified emission reductions or removals and may be expressed in greenhouse-gas metrics (such as tCO2e) or, where Parties determine, in other metrics.

7f68ebf09da0.sentence: Cooperative approaches can be implemented through a variety of bilateral or multilateral arrangements, including crediting-based transfers and policy-based cooperation such as linked emissions trading systems, provided Parties authorize the use of outcomes and apply the agreed accounting framework.

4baf21886bcf.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
4baf21886bcf.sentence: By 2024, over 80 bilateral cooperation agreements were reported as being in place, and early transactions included an ITMO trade between Thailand and Switzerland (reported as the first completed ITMO trade in January 2024), as well as a later transfer from Ghana to Switzerland in 2025 linked to an improved cookstove project.

df432e543dca.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
df432e543dca.sentence: - Double counting: umbrella term commonly used for different problems, including double issuance (more than one unit issued for the same outcome), double claiming (both Parties claim the same outcome toward their NDCs), and double use (the same unit is used more than once or for more than one claim).

ecfd0f0fab1e.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
ecfd0f0fab1e.sentence: Participating Parties are expected to report what they authorize, transfer, acquire, cancel or use, and how those actions are reflected in NDC accounting, including the corresponding adjustments used to avoid double claiming for authorized international uses.

146bccdf0386.title: Cooperative mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement

9e140bbb3ea9.sentence: Unlike cooperative approaches under Article 6.2 and the crediting mechanism under Article 6.4, NMAs do not involve the international transfer of mitigation outcomes between Parties.

7ffbda434477.sentence: UNFCCC guidance describes NMAs as cooperation that can integrate mitigation and adaptation and may also involve finance, technology transfer, and capacity building, while contributing to sustainable development and poverty eradication.

6ad7911f02bd.sentence: Under Article 6.4, Parties established a UNFCCC-supervised crediting mechanism—referred to by the UNFCCC as the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM)—to register mitigation activities and issue units for verified emission reductions or removals, while supporting sustainable development and delivering an overall mitigation in global emissions.

01f576f8665b.section: Approaches under Article 6 > Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (Article 6.4)
01f576f8665b.sentence: The PACM registers eligible mitigation activities and issues units known as Article 6.4 emission reductions (A6.4ERs), which are recorded in a mechanism registry with unique identifiers to enable tracking (e.g., issuance, transfer, cancellation, and use).

2fec840a3c07.sentence: COP26 decisions also included a share of proceeds for the Adaptation Fund and cancellation of a portion of issued units to deliver an overall mitigation in global emissions (OMGE).

6cd475110c70.sentence: In outline, an Article 6.4 activity is developed against approved requirements (including methodologies), validated and registered under the mechanism, monitored and independently verified for a crediting period, and then issued as A6.4ERs into the mechanism registry.

37cac931ac94.title: Global climate regime

f70de72f7446.title: Global climate regime

e599ef376fc6.title: Global climate regime
e599ef376fc6.sentence: Under the Paris climate regime, all countries have signed on to the goal of net balance between sources and sinks of greenhouse gases in the second half of the 21st century.

1d73e23d05d9.sentence: Contraction and Convergence (C&C) is a proposed global framework for reducing greenhouse gas emissions to combat climate change.

5932e7c750e4.title: Contraction and Convergence
5932e7c750e4.sentence: Conceived by the Global Commons Institute (GCI) in the early 1990s, the Contraction and Convergence strategy consists of reducing overall emissions of greenhouse gases to a safe level (contraction), resulting from every country bringing its emissions per capita to a level which is equal for all countries (convergence).

b841b243f2d4.title: Contraction and Convergence
b841b243f2d4.sentence: It is expressed as a simple mathematical formula.

e6519977135d.title: Contraction and Convergence
e6519977135d.sentence: Initially, these entitlements would be based on current emissions but would gradually converge towards equal per capita entitlements across the globe, depending on the negotiated "rate of convergence." The timing of convergence is crucial, as an earlier date would lead to an increase in entitlements for countries with lower per capita emissions (typically poorer countries), while a delayed convergence could hinder the development prospects of these nations.

d9b5646a5df8.title: Contraction and Convergence
d9b5646a5df8.sentence: As noted by Professor Ross Garnaut in his "Review" for the Australian Government, the rate of convergence serves as a crucial equity mechanism in the negotiations.

67c74cbce56d.title: Obligations of States in respect of climate change

14982ec4d602.title: Obligations of States in respect of climate change
14982ec4d602.sentence: These include adopting mitigation and adaptation measures, submitting nationally determined contributions (NDCs), acting in accordance with the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, and cooperating in good faith.

3ff158642830.title: Obligations of States in respect of climate change

a0f9a3fec4be.title: Obligations of States in respect of climate change

c07ecb2f4f31.title: Ecological economics
c07ecb2f4f31.sentence: Ecological economics, bioeconomics, ecolonomy, eco-economics, or ecol-econ is both a transdisciplinary and an interdisciplinary field of academic research addressing the interdependence and coevolution of human economies and natural ecosystems, both intertemporally and spatially.

7d97803430e4.title: Laws of thermodynamics

ba92683f2c1c.title: Laws of thermodynamics
ba92683f2c1c.sentence: By 1860, as formalized in the works of scientists such as Rudolf Clausius and William Thomson, what are now known as the first and second laws were established.

a787a5d5872e.title: Entropy
a787a5d5872e.section: Approaches to understanding entropy > Energy dispersal
a787a5d5872e.sentence: The concept of entropy can be described qualitatively as a measure of energy dispersal at a specific temperature.

3a8b0f481bde.title: Entropy
3a8b0f481bde.section: Approaches to understanding entropy > Order and disorder
3a8b0f481bde.sentence: Entropy is often loosely associated with the amount of order or disorder, or of chaos, in a thermodynamic system.

1a9468af51ad.title: Entropy
1a9468af51ad.sentence: Hence, in a system isolated from its environment, the entropy of that system tends not to decrease.

7cf083185890.title: Entropy
7cf083185890.section: Approaches to understanding entropy > Relating entropy to energy usefulness
7cf083185890.sentence: It is possible (in a thermal context) to regard lower entropy as a measure of the effectiveness or usefulness of a particular quantity of energy.

21350721b6bc.title: Entropy
21350721b6bc.section: Approaches to understanding entropy > Relating entropy to energy usefulness
21350721b6bc.sentence: Energy supplied at a higher temperature (i.e. with low entropy) tends to be more useful than the same amount of energy available at a lower temperature.

aa6c5a0dd54b.title: Entropy
aa6c5a0dd54b.sentence: In 1865, Clausius named the concept of "the differential of a quantity which depends on the configuration of the system" entropy (Entropie) after the Greek word for 'transformation'.

8540ede9e77a.title: Entropy

b18a2382297a.title: Entropy

b18a2382297a.sentence: Entropy is the only quantity in the physical sciences that seems to imply a particular direction of progress, sometimes called an arrow of time.

e79218b8eafd.title: Uneconomic growth
e79218b8eafd.sentence: Uneconomic growth is economic growth that reflects or creates a decline in the quality of life.

469cfdeec465.title: Uneconomic growth
469cfdeec465.sentence: It is usually attributed to ecological economist Herman Daly, though other theorists may also be credited for the incipient idea, According to Daly, "uneconomic growth occurs when increases in production come at an expense in resources and well-being that is worth more than the items made."

1447d2e5a88e.title: Uneconomic growth
1447d2e5a88e.sentence: The cost, or decline in well-being, associated with extended economic growth is argued to arise as a result of "the social and environmental sacrifices made necessary by that growing encroachment on the eco-system."

c3b475b662c2.title: Uneconomic growth
c3b475b662c2.sentence: Canadian scientist David Suzuki argued in the 1990s that ecologies can only sustain typically about 1.5–3% new growth per year, and thus any requirement for greater returns from agriculture or forestry will necessarily cannibalize the natural capital of soil or forest.

f8aec978f17f.title: Herman Daly
f8aec978f17f.sentence: He is widely credited with having originated the idea of uneconomic growth, though some credit this to Marilyn Waring who developed it more completely in her study of the UN System of National Accounts.

32e5dd151f73.title: Spaceship Earth
32e5dd151f73.sentence: Spaceship Earth (or Spacecraft Earth or Spaceship Planet Earth) is a worldview encouraging everyone on Earth to act as a harmonious crew working toward the greater good.

b2176dc2c737.title: Spaceship Earth
b2176dc2c737.sentence: The earliest known use of the term is a passage in Henry George's best known work, Progress and Poverty (1879).

dadde84d6f28.title: Spaceship Earth
dadde84d6f28.sentence: In 1966, Kenneth E. Boulding, who was influenced by reading Henry George's work, used the phrase in the title of his essay, The Economics of the Coming Spaceship Earth.

f97e88a3000d.title: Spaceship Earth
f97e88a3000d.sentence: Boulding described the past open economy of apparently illimitable resources, which he said he was tempted to call the "cowboy economy", and continued: "The closed economy of the future might similarly be called the 'spaceman' economy, in which the earth has become a single spaceship, without unlimited reservoirs of anything, either for extraction or for pollution, and in which, therefore, man must find his place in a cyclical ecological system".

08c70e0b9fcc.title: Kenneth E. Boulding
08c70e0b9fcc.section: Work > The Economics of the Coming Spaceship Earth, 1966
08c70e0b9fcc.sentence: Boulding in his influential 1966 essay "The Economics of the Coming Spaceship Earth" identified the need for the economic system to fit itself to the ecological system with its limited pools of resources.

08291e77bcbf.title: Spaceship Earth
08291e77bcbf.sentence: The phrase was also popularized by Buckminster Fuller in his Dymaxion philosophy, who authored the 1968 book Operating Manual for Spaceship Earth.

d71de9f5599a.title: Environmentalism

a62fe2f05664.title: Spaceship Earth
a62fe2f05664.sentence: Sociologist Steffen Roth has argued that, if realized, Spaceship Earth would epitomise the most total institution ever created in human history.

8e09909202b9.title: First law of thermodynamics
8e09909202b9.sentence: The first law of thermodynamics is a formulation of the law of conservation of energy in the context of thermodynamic processes.

df3b3639e487.title: First law of thermodynamics
df3b3639e487.sentence: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, but it can be transformed from one form to another.

ac3a3d4068d8.title: First law of thermodynamics
ac3a3d4068d8.sentence: In an externally isolated system, with internal changes, the sum of all forms of energy is constant.

b2d750d52242.title: First law of thermodynamics
b2d750d52242.sentence: For a thermodynamic process affecting a thermodynamic system without transfer of matter, the law distinguishes two principal forms of energy transfer, heat and thermodynamic work.

051bd199a7a0.title: First law of thermodynamics

11dd7e089784.title: Steady-state economy

11b5da517421.title: Embodied energy
11b5da517421.sentence: Embodied energy is the sum of all the energy required to produce any goods or services, considered as if that energy were incorporated or 'embodied' in the product itself.

4cc277f35014.title: Embodied energy
4cc277f35014.sentence: Embodied energy is an accounting method that aims to find the sum total of the energy necessary for an entire product lifecycle.

8d245ca7b077.title: Embodied energy
8d245ca7b077.sentence: Determining what constitutes this lifecycle includes assessing the relevance and extent of energy in raw material extraction, transport, manufacture, assembly, installation, disassembly, deconstruction and/or decomposition, as well as human and secondary resources.

1cc2e0e73f05.title: Embodied energy

e2e026e598ee.title: Embodied energy

4c48a7400340.sentence: In energy economics and ecological energetics, energy return on investment (EROI), also sometimes called energy returned on energy invested (ERoEI), is the ratio of the amount of usable energy (the exergy) delivered from a particular energy resource to the amount of exergy used to obtain that energy resource.

c7b7f11455bf.title: Buddhist economics

980c85ae6450.title: Buddhist economics
980c85ae6450.sentence: In Buddhist economics, there are three major functions to work, "to give man a chance to utilise and develop his faculties; to enable him to overcome his ego-centredness by joining with other people in a common task; and to bring forth the goods and services needed for a becoming existence." This shift in the way work is viewed, both by employers and employees, if applied to the western world, would be fundamentally altering to the incentives driving modern economies.

5a2949939dc5.title: Buddhist economics

361f45309db9.title: Thermoeconomics

6c886bc04a3a.title: Thermoeconomics
