5fcdcd4e28be.sentence: Value is not attributed to material accumulation, and it instead takes a more spiritual and communitarian approach to economic activity.

92d81c1b560d.title: Ecological economics
92d81c1b560d.section: History and development > Schools of thought > Non-traditional approaches to ecological economics
92d81c1b560d.sentence: Ecological Swaraj originated out of India, and is an evolving world view of human interactions within the ecosystem.

2ed3f9765275.title: Ecological economics
2ed3f9765275.section: History and development > Schools of thought > Non-traditional approaches to ecological economics
2ed3f9765275.sentence: This train of thought respects physical bio-limits and non-human species, pursuing equity and social justice through direct democracy and grassroots leadership.

5e99de3715da.title: Ecological economics
5e99de3715da.section: History and development > Schools of thought > Non-traditional approaches to ecological economics
5e99de3715da.sentence: E.F. Schumacher introduced examples of non-western economic ideas to mainstream thought in his book, Small is Beautiful, where he addresses neoliberal economics through the lens of natural harmony in Buddhist economics.

c225199a01c8.title: Ecological economics
c225199a01c8.section: History and development > Schools of thought
c225199a01c8.sentence: Various competing schools of thought exist in the field.

9e4af4b60c89.title: Ecological economics
9e4af4b60c89.section: History and development > Schools of thought
9e4af4b60c89.sentence: Some are close to resource and environmental economics while others are far more heterodox in outlook.

d2eda42c60f0.title: Ecological economics
d2eda42c60f0.section: History and development > Schools of thought
d2eda42c60f0.sentence: Clive Spash has argued for the classification of the ecological economics movement, and more generally work by different economic schools on the environment, into three main categories.

7be8b3b1ddb9.title: Ecological economics
7be8b3b1ddb9.section: History and development > Schools of thought
7be8b3b1ddb9.sentence: These are the mainstream new resource economists, the new environmental pragmatists, and the more radical social ecological economists.

5b43488ae136.title: Ecological economics
5b43488ae136.section: History and development > Schools of thought
5b43488ae136.sentence: A growing field of radical social-ecological theory is degrowth economics.

2f502b761596.title: Ecological economics
2f502b761596.section: History and development > Schools of thought
2f502b761596.sentence: Degrowth addresses both biophysical limits and global inequality while rejecting neoliberal economics.

1409270bfc8c.title: Ecological economics
1409270bfc8c.section: History and development > Schools of thought
1409270bfc8c.sentence: Critics of the degrowth movement include new resource economists, who point to the gaining momentum of sustainable development.

8df6c68e132a.title: Ecological economics
8df6c68e132a.section: History and development > Schools of thought
8df6c68e132a.sentence: These economists highlight the positive aspects of a green economy, which include equitable access to renewable energy and a commitment to eradicate global inequality through sustainable development (See Green Economics).

519d783eced9.title: Laws of thermodynamics
519d783eced9.sentence: The second law of thermodynamics indicates the irreversibility of natural processes, and in many cases, the tendency of natural processes to lead towards spatial homogeneity of matter and energy, especially of temperature.

aeb7fd59b1fd.title: Laws of thermodynamics
aeb7fd59b1fd.sentence: One of the simplest is the Clausius statement, that heat does not spontaneously pass from a colder to a hotter body.

2767eb59a43e.title: Laws of thermodynamics
2767eb59a43e.sentence: While reversible processes are a useful and convenient theoretical limiting case, all natural processes are irreversible.

15b8409e3af8.title: Laws of thermodynamics
15b8409e3af8.sentence: The first established thermodynamic principle, which eventually became the second law of thermodynamics, was formulated by Sadi Carnot in 1824 in his book Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire.

ed52f24aa92c.title: Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen
ed52f24aa92c.section: Work > Magnum opus on The Entropy Law and the Economic Process > The relevance of thermodynamics to economics
ed52f24aa92c.sentence: The second law of thermodynamics – also known as the entropy law – states that in an isolated system, entropy, a measure of the disorder in a system, normally cannot decrease.

d4a7ee9f478d.title: Conservation of mass
d4a7ee9f478d.sentence: In physics and chemistry, the law of conservation of mass or principle of mass conservation states that for any system which is closed to all incoming and outgoing transfers of matter, the mass of the system must remain constant over time.

0e872635b7f7.title: Conservation of mass
0e872635b7f7.sentence: The law implies that mass can neither be created nor destroyed, although it may be rearranged in space, or the entities associated with it may be changed in form.

596b6bb507ed.title: Conservation of mass
596b6bb507ed.sentence: For example, in chemical reactions, the mass of the chemical components before the reaction is equal to the mass of the components after the reaction.

e50bc96df397.title: Conservation of mass
e50bc96df397.sentence: Historically, mass conservation in chemical reactions was primarily demonstrated by Jean Rey (in 1630) and finally confirmed by Antoine Lavoisier in the late 18th century.

ed8011cfca5f.title: Conservation of mass
ed8011cfca5f.sentence: Many engineering problems are solved by following the mass distribution of a given system over time; this methodology is known as mass balance.

761e93f4218f.title: Conservation of mass
761e93f4218f.sentence: The conservation of mass is a law that holds only in the classical limit.

2479a8a7dd98.title: Conservation of mass
2479a8a7dd98.sentence: The law of conservation of mass and the analogous law of conservation of energy were finally generalized and unified into the principle of mass–energy equivalence, described by Albert Einstein's equation E=mc2.

8a199bf5018b.title: Water cycle
8a199bf5018b.sentence: The more common method relies on the principle of conservation of mass (water balance) and assumes the amount of water in a given reservoir is roughly constant.

979281647b88.title: Conservation of mass
979281647b88.sentence: A more refined series of experiments were later carried out by Antoine Lavoisier who expressed his conclusion in 1773 and popularized the principle of conservation of mass.

1de2a4e254b2.title: Metabolic rift
1de2a4e254b2.sentence: Metabolic rift is a theory of ecological crisis tendencies under the capitalist mode of production that sociologist John Bellamy Foster ascribes to Karl Marx.

ba05dd8d62a6.title: Metabolic rift
ba05dd8d62a6.sentence: Quoting Marx, Foster defines this as the "irreparable rift in the interdependent process of social metabolism".

e60c91858fc0.title: Metabolic rift
e60c91858fc0.sentence: Foster, rather than Marx, coined the term "metabolic rift".

513cffdf157b.title: Metabolic rift
513cffdf157b.sentence: Starting with his book Marx's Ecology: Materialism and Nature, Foster argues that Marx theorized a rupture in the metabolic interaction between humanity and the rest of nature emanating from capitalist agricultural production and the growing division between town and country.

4faf2f75add0.title: Metabolic rift
4faf2f75add0.section: Origins > Soil exhaustion and agricultural revolutions
4faf2f75add0.sentence: Marx's writings on metabolism were developed during England's "second" agricultural revolution (1815–1880), a period which was characterized by the development of soil chemistry and the growth of the use of chemical fertilizer.

811c7eb8f31b.title: Metabolic rift
811c7eb8f31b.section: Origins > Soil exhaustion and agricultural revolutions
811c7eb8f31b.sentence: The depletion of soil fertility, or "soil exhaustion", had become a key concern for capitalist society, and demand for fertilizer was such that Britain and other powers initiated explicit policies for the importation of bone and guano, including raiding of Napoleonic battlefields and catacombs, British monopolization of Peruvian guano supplies, and, in the United States, "the imperial annexation of any islands thought to be rich in [guano]" through the Guano Islands Act (1856).

14703461e19f.title: Metabolic rift
14703461e19f.sentence: German agricultural chemist Justus von Liebig, in his Organic Chemistry in Its Applications to Agriculture and Physiology (1840), presented the first convincing explanation of the role of soil nutrients in the growth of plants.

c8f2d59244ce.title: Metabolic rift
c8f2d59244ce.section: Environmental contradiction under capitalism > Town and country
c8f2d59244ce.sentence: The nutrients of the soil were sent to cities in the form of agricultural produce, but these same nutrients, in the form of human and animal waste, were not returned to the land.

15865b53186c.title: Metabolic rift
15865b53186c.section: Environmental contradiction under capitalism > Town and country
15865b53186c.sentence: Thus there was a one-way movement, a "robbing of the soil" in order to maintain the socio-economic reproduction of society.

41568f29910d.title: Metabolic rift
41568f29910d.section: Environmental contradiction under capitalism > Town and country
41568f29910d.sentence: Marx thus linked the crisis of pollution in cities with the crisis of soil depletion.

3cd0a34fd26c.title: Metabolic rift
3cd0a34fd26c.sentence: While originally limited to questions of soil fertility—essentially a critique of capitalist agriculture—the concept of metabolic rift has since been taken up in numerous fields and its scope expanded.

2a5ed2e81e91.title: Metabolic rift
2a5ed2e81e91.sentence: For example, Clausen and Clark have extended the use of metabolic rift to marine ecology, while Moore uses the concept to discuss the broader concerns of global environmental crises and the viability of capitalism itself.

b0fb24c32d64.title: Metabolic rift
b0fb24c32d64.sentence: With increasing amounts of carbon dioxide being released into the environment from capitalist production, the theory of a carbon rift has also emerged.

85464ef77ab0.title: Metabolic rift
85464ef77ab0.sentence: As opposed to those who have attributed to Marx a disregard for nature and responsibility for the environmental problems of the Soviet Union and other purportedly communist states, Foster sees in the theory of metabolic rift evidence of Marx's ecological perspective.

0aee3ab303f5.title: Steady-state economy
0aee3ab303f5.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Role of technology
0aee3ab303f5.sentence: This view of the role of technology in the economy has been termed 'entropy pessimism'.

988800d03446.title: Steady-state economy
988800d03446.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Role of technology
988800d03446.sentence: In physical terms, any technology — useful though it is — works largely as a medium for transforming valuable natural resources into material goods that eventually end up as valueless waste and pollution, thereby increasing the entropy — or disorder — of the world as a whole.

7faead9c4cbd.title: Steady-state economy
7faead9c4cbd.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Role of technology
7faead9c4cbd.sentence: - In neoclassical economics, on the one hand, the role of 'technology' is usually represented as yet another factor of production contributing to economic growth, like land, labour and capital contribute.

8714a08f4c56.title: Steady-state economy
8714a08f4c56.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Role of technology
8714a08f4c56.sentence: However, in neoclassical production functions, where the output of produced goods are related to the inputs provided by the factors of production, no mention is made of the contribution of natural resources to the production process.

ae7ccfbc7fa3.title: Steady-state economy
ae7ccfbc7fa3.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Role of technology
ae7ccfbc7fa3.sentence: - In ecological economics, on the other hand, 'technology' is represented as the way natural resources are transformed in the production process.

3c80579f17e9.title: Steady-state economy
3c80579f17e9.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Role of technology
3c80579f17e9.sentence: From the neoclassical point of view, leading growth theorist and Nobel Prize laureate Robert Solow has defended his much criticised position by replying in 1997 that 'elementary physics' has not by itself prevented growth in the industrialized countries so far.

5571dd2dc070.title: Steady-state economy
5571dd2dc070.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Resource decoupling and the rebound effect
5571dd2dc070.sentence: Resource decoupling occurs when economic activity becomes less intensive ecologically: A declining input of natural resources is needed to produce one unit of output on average, measured by the ratio of total natural resource consumption to gross domestic product (GDP).

cf9f13690e9e.title: Steady-state economy
cf9f13690e9e.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Resource decoupling and the rebound effect
cf9f13690e9e.sentence: Relative resource decoupling occurs when natural resource consumption declines on a ceteris paribus assumption — that is, all other things being equal.

0349b57a252b.title: Steady-state economy
0349b57a252b.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Resource decoupling and the rebound effect
0349b57a252b.sentence: Absolute resource decoupling occurs when natural resource consumption declines, even while GDP is growing.

9f734b0b6f2f.title: Steady-state economy
9f734b0b6f2f.sentence: In 2019 a research, presenting an overview of the attempts to achieve constant economic growth without environmental destruction and their results, was published.

6f7ebbe79cf3.title: Steady-state economy
6f7ebbe79cf3.sentence: It shows that by the year 2019 the attempts were not successful.

45f2c5c6c2ac.title: Steady-state economy
45f2c5c6c2ac.sentence: During the short period of time from 1966 to 1972, four works were published addressing the importance of natural resources and the environment to human society:

cf670f79ec6f.title: Steady-state economy
cf670f79ec6f.sentence: Taken together, these four works were seminal in bringing about the formation of ecological economics later on.

f0447872d7d2.title: Steady-state economy
f0447872d7d2.sentence: - In his 1966 philosophical-minded essay on The Economics of the Coming Spaceship Earth, economist and systems scientist Kenneth E. Boulding argued that mankind would soon have to adapt to economic principles much different than the past 'open earth' of illimitable plains and exploitative behaviour.

b4d4d6480b7a.title: Steady-state economy
b4d4d6480b7a.sentence: Therefore, mankind would have to find its place in a cyclical ecological system without unlimited reservoirs of anything, either for extraction or for pollution — like a spaceman on board a spaceship.

aee0bcedeca5.title: Steady-state economy
aee0bcedeca5.sentence: - In his 1971 magnum opus on The Entropy Law and the Economic Process, Romanian American economist Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen integrated the thermodynamic concept of entropy with economic analysis, and argued that all natural resources are irreversibly degraded when put to use in economic activity.

750b5e2b3ad4.title: Steady-state economy
750b5e2b3ad4.sentence: - Also in 1971, pioneering ecologist and general systems analyst Howard T. Odum published his book on Environment, Power and Society, where he described human society in terms of ecology.

286da48d2af7.title: Steady-state economy
286da48d2af7.sentence: He formulated the maximum power principle, according to which all organisms, ecosystems and human societies organise themselves in order to maximize their use of available energy for survival.

4df62d054a41.title: Steady-state economy
4df62d054a41.sentence: - In 1972, environmental scientist and systems analyst Donella Meadows and her team of researchers had their study on The Limits to Growth published by the Club of Rome.

551d90e6520e.title: Steady-state economy
551d90e6520e.sentence: The Meadows team modelled aggregate trends in the world economy and made the projection — not prediction — that by the mid to latter part of the 21st century, industrial production per capita, food supply per capita and world population would all reach a peak, and then rapidly decline in a vicious overshoot-and-collapse trajectory.

d874c2a5efde.title: Steady-state economy
d874c2a5efde.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Pushing some of the terrestrial limits into outer space
d874c2a5efde.sentence: Ever since the beginning of the modern Space Age in the 1950s, some space advocates have pushed for space habitation, frequently in the form of colonization, some arguing as a reason for alleviating human overpopulation, overconsumption and mitigate the human impact on the environment on Earth (if not for other reasons).

26f381bc768f.title: Steady-state economy
26f381bc768f.section: Conceptual and ideological disagreements > Pushing some of the terrestrial limits into outer space
26f381bc768f.sentence: In the 1970s, physicist and space activist Gerard K. O'Neill developed a large plan to build human settlements in outer space to solve the problems of overpopulation and limits to growth on earth without recourse to political repression.

2a35a5e6a7f1.title: Sustainability science
2a35a5e6a7f1.sentence: Sustainability science first emerged in the 1980s and has become a distinct academic discipline.

4f2e3f3f23ab.title: Sustainability science
4f2e3f3f23ab.sentence: Sustainability science focuses on issues relating to sustainability and sustainable development as core parts of its subject matter.

27e093ee5656.title: Sustainability science
27e093ee5656.sentence: Ecologist William C. Clark proposes that it can be usefully thought of as a field "defined by the problems it addresses rather than by the disciplines it employs", and that "serves the need for advancing both knowledge and action by creating a dynamic bridge between the two".

a441567a8be6.title: Sustainability science
a441567a8be6.sentence: Sustainability science began to develop in the 1980s in response to various foundational publications that articulated the need for knowledge in support of sustainable development, including the World Conservation Strategy (1980), the Brundtland Commission's report Our Common Future (1987), and the U.S. National Research Council’s Our Common Journey (1999).

8f3782fc199d.title: Sustainability science
8f3782fc199d.sentence: Sustainability science was officially introduced as a new international field of science at the World Congress Challenges of a Changing Earth 2001 in Amsterdam, organized by the International Council for Science (ICSU), the International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme (IGBP), the International Human Dimensions Programme on Global Environmental Change and the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP).

245b4a2340c7.title: Sustainability science
245b4a2340c7.sentence: The recognition of the epochal impacts of today's unsustainable systems – the so-called Anthropocene – is at the core of much sustainability science.

81cd66be664b.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
81cd66be664b.sentence: Ecologically or ecological unequal exchange is a concept from ecological economics that builds from the notion of unequal exchange.

2a6db9bd98ef.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
2a6db9bd98ef.sentence: It considers the inequities hidden in the monetary value of trade flows not only in terms of wages, and quantities of labor but also regarding materials, energy and environmental degradation.

9f0468153c88.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
9f0468153c88.sentence: Ecologically unequal exchange (EUE) refers to the environmental aspects of unequal exchange: it is an empirical evidence-based concept that refers to the effect of the structure of international trade under capitalism, in particular to the asymmetric flow of embodied materials and energy from peripheral countries - mainly located in the Global South - to the core developed world.

1b53fdd5c1c7.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
1b53fdd5c1c7.sentence: From this perspective, Global South countries tend to serve as a source of raw materials, sink for waste products and places to establish sacrifice zones, perpetuating global inequalities and uneven environmental impacts which disproportionately harm the people in developing countries but serve the productive capacity and the economy of the so-called developed.

c1fdf31704c9.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
c1fdf31704c9.sentence: The EUE theory is based on the world-systems perspective developed by Immanuel Wallerstein, Samir Amin, Giovanni Arrighi and Andre Gunder Frank.

1785b2ca9c3f.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
1785b2ca9c3f.sentence: The idea behind world-system theory is that the capitalist-world economy is economically and geographically divided into an affluent core and less developed periphery, and in which surplus value flows from the periphery to the core.

99276a078b4a.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
99276a078b4a.sentence: They depend in large part on extraction from the global south: half of the total materials consumed by high-income countries are extracted from poorer countries.

34b870d48b93.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
34b870d48b93.sentence: - High-income nations gain a monetary trade surplus via this resource appropriation.

4be97119dfdc.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
4be97119dfdc.sentence: They take into consideration the global distribution of ten selected environmental pressures and impacts, as well as value added induced by EU consumption from 1995 to 2019, and show how large parts of all such negative environmental impacts are outsourced to regions outside the EU, while more than 80% of the economic benefits stay within the member countries.

4535e99d3b05.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
4535e99d3b05.sentence: The logical result of EUE theory is that the Global North owes to the Global South an ecological debt.

2ad1a02af657.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
2ad1a02af657.sentence: EUE can be seen as the mechanism and ecological debt as the historical accumulation of debt by rich countries because of EUE.

7f2856a0cd08.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
7f2856a0cd08.sentence: Jason Hickel is one of the most popular scholars exploring degrowth in the global north as a solution to end relations of EUE.

2e71e225d21b.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
2e71e225d21b.sentence: Hickel suggests reducing consumption and production in the Global North to sustainable levels, which would alleviate the pressure on ecosystems and communities in the Global South.

296914fbaeea.title: Ecologically unequal exchange
296914fbaeea.sentence: Peter Somerville, writing for the journal Capitalism Nature Socialism, criticized ecological unequal exchange theory as "confused, internally inconsistent, and misrepresents the nature of global extractivism and labour exploitation."

932af28a9cce.title: Unequal exchange
932af28a9cce.sentence: Unequal exchange is used primarily in Marxist economics, but also in ecological economics (more specifically also as ecologically unequal exchange), to describe the systemic hidden transfer of labor and ecological value from poor countries in the imperial periphery (mainly in the Global South) to rich countries and monopolistic corporations in the imperial core (mainly in the Global North) due to structural inequalities in the global economy.

c5f4de17d7ac.title: Unequal exchange
c5f4de17d7ac.sentence: Due to biased terms of trade and the undervaluation of labor and goods from the global South compared to the North, poor countries are forced to export a much larger quantity of labor and resources than they import to maintain a monetary balance of trade.

ef9f1ec77a07.title: Unequal exchange
ef9f1ec77a07.sentence: The theory of unequal exchange is a rejection of the fundamental assumptions of Ricardian and neoclassical theories of comparative advantage, which claim that free trade based on comparative costs is beneficial to all parties and in turn represents the theoretical justification of neoliberal trade policies.

d19e6a3ca1b6.title: Unequal exchange
d19e6a3ca1b6.sentence: Amin and Emmanuel’s understanding of unequal exchange somewhat differs from the other thinkers, as they focus on the differences between national wages as a key factor producing the conditions for unequal exchange.

8c1f0a8eb826.title: Unequal exchange
8c1f0a8eb826.sentence: Amin underlined that unequal value transfers in global trade were not determined primarily by asymmetries in productivity, but by the profound wage differences between core and periphery.

fab43f633a59.title: Unequal exchange
fab43f633a59.sentence: Jason Hickel et al., using a similar method, calculated the amount that was drained from the Global South between the years 1990 to 2015 was equivalent to 242 trillion in 2010 US Dollars.

a0ec8e0b06f1.title: Unequal exchange
a0ec8e0b06f1.sentence: One central element to consider is that through patents, northern firms set prices artificially high.

77b55211bdab.title: Unequal exchange
77b55211bdab.sentence: As 97% of all patents are held by corporations in high-income countries, this skews the equilibrium disproportionally in favor of the latter.

e8df2f3cf286.title: Unequal exchange
e8df2f3cf286.sentence: A common critique is that wage inequalities between the South and the North can be explained by the higher productivity of northern workers in comparison to southern workers.

9fc6f1388ca5.title: Unequal exchange
9fc6f1388ca5.sentence: However, productivity in conventional economics is determined by prices, not by actual productivity.

1628e38a8390.title: Stock-flow consistent model
1628e38a8390.sentence: Stock-flow consistent models (SFC) are a family of non-equilibrium macroeconomic models based on a rigorous accounting framework, that seeks to guarantee a correct and comprehensive integration of all the flows and the stocks of an economy.

353d2df60ba5.title: Stock-flow consistent model
353d2df60ba5.sentence: These models were first developed in the mid-20th century but have recently become popular, particularly within the post-Keynesian school of thought.

31e01130dcf9.title: Stock-flow consistent model
31e01130dcf9.sentence: Stock-flow consistent models are in contrast to dynamic stochastic general equilibrium models, which are used in mainstream economics.

d13a7fba1602.title: Stock-flow consistent model
d13a7fba1602.sentence: Someone's asset is someone else's liability and someone's inflow is someone else's outflows.

0a94c6872376.title: Stock-flow consistent model
0a94c6872376.sentence: No fund can come from (or end up) nowhere.

2556ff3fa8d1.title: Stock-flow consistent model
2556ff3fa8d1.sentence: Wynne Godley, one of the pioneers of the SFC approach since the 1970s, had warned since 2000 in publications that the US housing market would weaken and cause a recession.

5cd16b30237e.title: Stock-flow consistent model
5cd16b30237e.sentence: While ecological aspects were not considered by post-Keynesian authors like Godley or Lavoie, SFC models are now widely used within Ecological Macroeconomics.

dbcd30fb4712.title: Stock-flow consistent model
dbcd30fb4712.sentence: In addition to cash flows, resource or energy flows and stocks or an ecosystem with renewable resources are modeled.

950f16aff8f2.title: Stock-flow consistent model
950f16aff8f2.sentence: References are made in particular to the flow-fund models of Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen.

e2621b037205.title: Heterodox economics
e2621b037205.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of individual behavior
e2621b037205.sentence: Many heterodox schools are critical of the homo economicus model of human behavior used in the standard neoclassical model.

a7164640660a.title: Heterodox economics
a7164640660a.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of individual behavior
a7164640660a.sentence: Neoclassical economics begins with the a priori assumptions that agents are rational and that they seek to maximize their individual utility (or profits) subject to environmental constraints.

b7df1520f654.title: Heterodox economics
b7df1520f654.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of individual behavior
b7df1520f654.sentence: These assumptions provide the backbone for rational choice theory.

a7acd88149b8.title: Heterodox economics
a7acd88149b8.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of individual behavior
a7acd88149b8.sentence: Indeed, for a number of economists, the notion of rational maximizing behavior is taken to be synonymous with economic behavior (Hirshleifer 1984).

ac95b3bc4823.title: Heterodox economics
ac95b3bc4823.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of individual behavior
ac95b3bc4823.sentence: Human beings may, for example, be unable to make choices consistent with pleasure maximization due to social constraints and/or coercion.

bb3beef41365.title: Heterodox economics
bb3beef41365.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of individual behavior
bb3beef41365.sentence: Humans may also be unable to correctly assess the choice points that are most likely to lead to maximum pleasure, even if they are unconstrained (except in budgetary terms) in making such choices.

0e2d47663dac.title: Heterodox economics
0e2d47663dac.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of individual behavior
0e2d47663dac.sentence: Shiozawa emphasizes that economic agents act in a complex world and it is therefore impossible for them to attain maximal utility point.

44a851cc1f27.title: Heterodox economics
44a851cc1f27.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of individual behavior
44a851cc1f27.sentence: They instead behave as if there are repertoires of many ready-made rules, one of which they choose according to the relevant situation.

72f8f4ba0efc.title: Heterodox economics
72f8f4ba0efc.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of market equilibrium
72f8f4ba0efc.sentence: However, the concept of market equilibrium has been criticized by Austrians, post-Keynesians and others, who object to applications of microeconomic theory to real-world markets, when such markets are not usefully approximated by microeconomic models.

6b5ba4d69ea4.title: Heterodox economics
6b5ba4d69ea4.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of market equilibrium
6b5ba4d69ea4.sentence: Heterodox economists assert that micro-economic models rarely capture reality.

a75186f5175d.title: Heterodox economics
a75186f5175d.section: Rejection of neoclassical economics > Criticism of the neoclassical model of market equilibrium
