51e6fb1b7599.sentence: Modern proponents of the concept have suggested that overpopulation, population growth and overconsumption are interdependent and collectively are the primary drivers of human-caused environmental problems such as climate change.

cfc69b72d2a3.title: Human overpopulation
cfc69b72d2a3.sentence: By the early 19th century, intellectuals such as Thomas Malthus predicted that humankind would outgrow its available resources because a finite amount of land would be incapable of supporting a population with limitless potential for increase.

aee85e1b4f6a.title: Human overpopulation
aee85e1b4f6a.section: Proposed impacts > Poverty and infant and child mortality
aee85e1b4f6a.sentence: Although proponents of human overpopulation have expressed concern that growing population will lead to an increase in global poverty and infant mortality, both indicators have declined over the last 200 years of population growth thanks to the agricultural and technological revolutions.

cf0322bebf52.title: Human overpopulation
cf0322bebf52.sentence: Predicted exponential population growth or any "population explosion" did not materialise; instead, population growth slowed.

74726cde04c1.title: Human overpopulation
74726cde04c1.sentence: The concept of human overpopulation has been criticized by some scholars and environmentalists as being racist and having roots in colonialism and white supremacy, since control and reduction of human population is often focused on the global south, instead of on overconsumption and the global north, where it occurs.

50266a49728b.title: The Limits to Growth
50266a49728b.sentence: The Limits to Growth (LTG) is a 1972 report that discussed the possibility of exponential economic and population growth with a finite supply of resources, studied by computer simulation.

95b48a927770.title: The Limits to Growth
95b48a927770.sentence: Commissioned by the Club of Rome, the study saw its findings first presented at international gatherings in Moscow and Rio de Janeiro in the summer of 1971.

ff47aeec34ef.title: The Limits to Growth
ff47aeec34ef.sentence: The report's authors are Donella H. Meadows, Dennis L. Meadows, Jørgen Randers, and William W. Behrens III, representing a team of 17 researchers.

c8f8e79f750c.title: The Limits to Growth
c8f8e79f750c.sentence: The study used the World3 computer model to simulate the consequence of interactions between the Earth and human systems.

df1eb8cb654c.title: The Limits to Growth
df1eb8cb654c.sentence: The model was based on the work of Jay Forrester of MIT, as described in his book World Dynamics.

17c7920a8a46.title: The Limits to Growth
17c7920a8a46.sentence: Two of the scenarios saw "overshoot and collapse" of the global system by the mid- to latter part of the 21st century, while a third scenario resulted in a "stabilized world."

db483a371227.title: The Limits to Growth
db483a371227.sentence: > If the present growth trends in world population, industrialization, pollution, food production, and resource depletion continue unchanged, the limits to growth on this planet will be reached sometime within the next one hundred years.

d7a7775aac9a.title: The Limits to Growth
d7a7775aac9a.sentence: The most probable result will be a rather sudden and uncontrollable decline in both population and industrial capacity.

130eae8a1d99.title: The Limits to Growth
130eae8a1d99.sentence: It is possible to alter these growth trends and to establish a condition of ecological and economic stability that is sustainable far into the future.

d9cf54065bc5.title: The Limits to Growth
d9cf54065bc5.sentence: Peter Passell and two co-authors published a 2 April 1972 article in the New York Times describing LTG as "an empty and misleading work... best summarized... as a rediscovery of the oldest maxim of computer science: Garbage In, Garbage Out." Passell considered the study's simulation simplistic and that it assigned little value to the role of technological progress in solving the problems of resource depletion, pollution, and food production.

5326589dc3bb.title: The Limits to Growth
5326589dc3bb.sentence: Yet price predictions based on resource scarcity failed to materialize in the years since publication.

824c59a83f3f.title: The Limits to Growth
824c59a83f3f.sentence: Since its publication, some 30 million copies of the book in 30 languages have been purchased.

e2fbe5b79bc8.title: The Limits to Growth
e2fbe5b79bc8.sentence: Although it faced severe criticism and scrutiny upon its release, the report influenced environmental reforms for decades.

2fa837510127.title: The Limits to Growth
2fa837510127.sentence: Beyond the Limits and The Limits to Growth: The 30-Year Update were published in 1992 and 2004 respectively; in 2012, a 40-year forecast from Jørgen Randers, one of the book's original authors, was published as 2052: A Global Forecast for the Next Forty Years; and in 2022, two of the original Limits to Growth authors, Dennis Meadows and Jørgen Randers, joined 19 other contributors to produce Limits and Beyond.

636ca6df0587.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
636ca6df0587.sentence: In energy conservation and energy economics, the rebound effect (or take-back effect) is the reduction in expected gains from new technologies that increase the efficiency of resource use, because of behavioral or other systemic responses.

bc338fe54874.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
bc338fe54874.sentence: These responses diminish the beneficial effects of the new technology or other measures taken.

f4be70d7d47d.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
f4be70d7d47d.sentence: The rebound effect is generally expressed as a ratio of the lost benefit compared to the expected environmental benefit when holding consumption constant.

e866bd2f7bec.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
e866bd2f7bec.sentence: For instance, if a 5% improvement in vehicle fuel efficiency results in only a 2% drop in fuel use, there is a 60% rebound effect (since (5-2)⁄5 = 60%).

0ae2f272cd02.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
0ae2f272cd02.sentence: The 'missing' 3% might have been consumed by driving faster or further than before.

cc4a43327ad4.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
cc4a43327ad4.sentence: Generally, economists and researchers seem to agree that there exists a rebound effect, but they disagree about its volume and importance.

6e6804e8a4ee.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
6e6804e8a4ee.sentence: The rebound effect was first described by William Stanley Jevons in his 1865 book The Coal Question, where he observed that the invention in Britain of a more efficient steam engine meant that the use of coal became economically viable for many new uses.

62b2964074fd.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
62b2964074fd.sentence: While the literature on the rebound effect generally focuses on the effect of technological improvements on energy consumption, the theory can also be applied to the use of any natural resource or other input, such as labor.

ee9d9c7a7ad0.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
ee9d9c7a7ad0.sentence: Work examining home heating, cooling, and personal transport often finds rebound levels in the range of 20–50%, meaning that a substantial portion of the energy savings predicted from efficiency improvements does not fully materialize.

2f16ef2e3e3a.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
2f16ef2e3e3a.section: Types of effects > Income level variation
2f16ef2e3e3a.sentence: Studies have also observed higher rebounds in low-income houses for improvements in heating technology.

efba788b4bfc.title: Rebound effect (conservation)
efba788b4bfc.section: Types of effects > Income level variation
efba788b4bfc.sentence: But low-income households are more price sensitive, and have made thermal sacrifices due to the cost of heating.

0803a452a6b2.title: I = PAT
0803a452a6b2.sentence: I = PAT is the mathematical notation of a formula put forward to describe the impact of human activity on the environment.

38b0a6559c21.title: I = PAT
38b0a6559c21.sentence: The expression equates human impact (I) on the environment to a function of three factors: population (P), affluence (A) and technology (T).

e0ccdc790e7b.title: I = PAT
e0ccdc790e7b.sentence: The equation was developed in 1970 during the course of a debate between Barry Commoner, Paul R. Ehrlich and John Holdren.

961e3d2aeb53.title: I = PAT
961e3d2aeb53.sentence: Commoner argued that environmental impacts in the United States were caused primarily by changes in its production technology following World War II and focused on present-day deteriorating environmental conditions in the United States.

25e0142769d8.title: I = PAT
25e0142769d8.sentence: Ehrlich and Holdren argued that all three factors were important but emphasized the role of human population growth, focusing on a broader scale, being less specific in space and time.

e9761dce707c.title: I = PAT
e9761dce707c.sentence: It represents the average consumption of each person in the population.

d93ff2f86ebe.title: I = PAT
d93ff2f86ebe.sentence: A common proxy for measuring consumption is through GDP per capita or GNI per capita.

6446861dbbd5.title: I = PAT
6446861dbbd5.sentence: The T variable in the I=PAT equation represents how resource intensive the production of affluence is; how much environmental impact is involved in creating, transporting and disposing of the goods, services and amenities used.

bcf8d680885d.title: I = PAT
bcf8d680885d.sentence: For example, for a situation where the human impact on climate change is being measured, an appropriate unit for T might be greenhouse gas emissions per unit of GDP.

7f4d4b3f0785.title: I = PAT
7f4d4b3f0785.sentence: Impact may be measured using ecological footprint analysis in units of global hectares (gha).

8212b53f0166.title: I = PAT
8212b53f0166.sentence: If "I" exceeds the carrying capacity, then the system is said to be in overshoot, which may only be a temporary state.

0f8c950ce6d5.title: I = PAT
0f8c950ce6d5.sentence: It is similar in form to the Kaya identity, which applies specifically to emissions of the greenhouse gas carbon dioxide.

f416afd95c30.title: I = PAT
f416afd95c30.sentence: The I=PAT equation has been criticized for being too simplistic by assuming that P, A, and T are independent of each other.

df6a8936595a.title: I = PAT
df6a8936595a.sentence: For example, a doubling of technological efficiency, or equivalently a reduction of the T-factor by 50%, does not necessarily reduce the environmental impact (I) by 50% if efficiency induced price reductions stimulate additional consumption of the resource that was supposed to be conserved, a phenomenon called the rebound effect or Jevons paradox.

704004c9108a.title: I = PAT
704004c9108a.section: Criticism > Neglect of political and social contexts
704004c9108a.sentence: Another major criticism of the I=PAT model is that it ignores the political context and decision-making structures of countries and groups.

f5b77881df1c.title: I = PAT
f5b77881df1c.section: Criticism > Neglect of political and social contexts
f5b77881df1c.sentence: Also, the P factor does not account for the complexity of social structures or behaviors, resulting in blame being placed on the global poor.

5c8efe52d1ff.title: I = PAT
5c8efe52d1ff.sentence: It underpins the entire World3 simulation model, which is the most influential sustainability model ever created, and is essentially an extended application of the IPAT equation.

fcc80dba9e47.title: Eco-economic decoupling
fcc80dba9e47.sentence: In economic and environmental fields, decoupling refers to an economy that would be able to grow without corresponding increases in environmental pressure.

63e21521a007.title: Eco-economic decoupling
63e21521a007.sentence: In many economies, increasing production (GDP) raises pressure on the environment.

74a886dd4ddf.title: Eco-economic decoupling
74a886dd4ddf.sentence: An economy that would be able to sustain economic growth while reducing the amount of resources such as water or fossil fuels used and delink environmental deterioration at the same time would be said to be decoupled.

0c5acdd346b9.title: Eco-economic decoupling
0c5acdd346b9.sentence: Environmental pressure is often measured using emissions of pollutants, and decoupling is often measured by the emission intensity of economic output.

1f84fbde4463.title: Eco-economic decoupling
1f84fbde4463.sentence: In 2002, the OECD defined the term as follows: "the term 'decoupling' refers to breaking the link between "environmental bads" and "economic goods." It explains this as having rates of increasing wealth greater than the rates of increasing impacts.

4a96fc15b62c.title: Eco-economic decoupling
4a96fc15b62c.sentence: In cases where evidence of decoupling exists, one proposed explanation is the transition to a service economy.

4d8c8d2efe2c.title: Eco-economic decoupling
4d8c8d2efe2c.sentence: The environmental Kuznets curve is a proposed model for eco-economic decoupling.

3d1de4a8d413.title: Eco-economic decoupling
3d1de4a8d413.sentence: In 2011 the International Resource Panel, hosted by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), warned that by 2050 the human race could be devouring 140 billion tons of minerals, ores, fossil fuels and biomass per year—three times its current rate of consumption—unless nations can make serious attempts at decoupling.

9a82377f4ca5.title: Eco-economic decoupling
9a82377f4ca5.sentence: In 2016, the International Resource Panel published a report indicating that "global material productivity has declined since about the year 2000 and the global economy now needs more materials per unit of GDP than it did at the turn of the century" as a result of shifts in production from high-income to middle-income countries.

aac395fc1f50.title: Eco-economic decoupling
aac395fc1f50.sentence: This is the opposite of decoupling, a situation that some people call overcoupling.

539719cf905b.title: Eco-economic decoupling
539719cf905b.sentence: Several technologies have been described in the Decoupling 2 report, including:

a44f01e07aa8.title: Eco-economic decoupling
a44f01e07aa8.sentence: - Technologies to save energy (technologies directly reducing fossil fuel consumption, saving electricity in industry, reducing fossil-fuel demand in transportation,...)

570e8028d376.title: Eco-economic decoupling
570e8028d376.sentence: - Technologies saving metals and minerals (technologies reducing metal use, saving materials from waste streams,...)

28383001a9a4.title: Eco-economic decoupling
28383001a9a4.sentence: - Technologies saving freshwater and biotic resources (technologies saving freshwater extraction, protecting soil fertility, saving biotic resources,...)

2cbdfe2d213b.title: Degrowth
2cbdfe2d213b.sentence: Degrowth is an academic and social movement, predominantly in Europe, aimed at the planned and democratic reduction of production and consumption as a solution to social-ecological crises.

43b2597520a4.title: Degrowth
43b2597520a4.sentence: Commonly cited policy goals of degrowth include reducing the environmental impact of human activities, redistributing income and wealth within and between countries, and encouraging a shift from materialistic values to a convivial and participatory society.

5391910cfe38.title: Degrowth
5391910cfe38.sentence: Degrowth is critical of the concept of growth in gross domestic product as a measure of human and economic development.

2ce7e9d0aa1c.title: Degrowth
2ce7e9d0aa1c.sentence: It argues that modern capitalism's unitary focus on growth causes widespread ecological damage and is unnecessary for the further increase of human living standards.

26628bfcf941.title: Degrowth
26628bfcf941.sentence: The degrowth movement heavily critiques this idea and argues that absolute decoupling is only possible for short periods, specific locations, or with small mitigation rates.

6f41158268d0.title: Degrowth
6f41158268d0.sentence: Degrowth literature, however, warns about these technological advances due to the "rebound effect", also known as Jevons paradox.

8cabcf9ec2b3.title: Degrowth
8cabcf9ec2b3.sentence: This concept is based on observations that when a less resource-exhaustive technology is introduced, behavior surrounding the use of that technology may change, and consumption of that technology could increase or even offset any potential resource savings.

cc80eef9cf7b.title: Degrowth
cc80eef9cf7b.section: Origins of the movement > Influence of Georgescu-Roegen
cc80eef9cf7b.sentence: The degrowth movement recognises Romanian American mathematician, statistician and economist Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen as the main intellectual figure inspiring the movement.

395e84757250.title: Degrowth
395e84757250.section: Origins of the movement > Influence of Georgescu-Roegen
395e84757250.sentence: As a result, in 1979, Grinevald published a French translation of a selection of Georgescu-Roegen's articles entitled Demain la décroissance: Entropie – Écologie – Économie ('Tomorrow, the Decline: Entropy – Ecology – Economy').

a0b1e189990a.title: Degrowth
a0b1e189990a.section: Origins of the movement > Influence of Georgescu-Roegen
a0b1e189990a.sentence: When the first international degrowth conference was held in Paris in 2008, the participants honoured Georgescu-Roegen and his work.

ce64080b5288.title: Degrowth
ce64080b5288.sentence: Critics also note that far-reaching degrowth scenarios are projected to increase extreme poverty, with no historical precedent of the poorest benefiting in a shrinking economy.

e1e1aec882aa.title: Green growth
e1e1aec882aa.sentence: Green growth is a concept in economic theory and policymaking used to describe paths of economic growth that are environmentally sustainable.

a5f2a21011ca.title: Green growth
a5f2a21011ca.sentence: The concept of green growth assumes that economic growth and development can continue while associated negative impacts on the environment, including climate change, are reduced (or while the natural environment continues to provide ecosystem services), meaning that a decoupling takes place.

6287358adad2.title: Green growth
6287358adad2.sentence: It is based on the understanding that as long as economic growth remains a predominant goal, a decoupling of economic growth from resource use and adverse environmental impacts is required.

83b35095c2c3.title: Green growth
83b35095c2c3.sentence: The term was coined in 2005 by the South Korean Rae Kwon Chung [de], a director at UNESCAP.

3cd3319af252.title: Green growth
3cd3319af252.sentence: The term "green growth" originates from the Asia Pacific Region and first emerged at the Fifth Ministerial Conference on Environment and Development (MCED) in Seoul, South Korea in 2005, where the Seoul Initiative Network on Green Growth was founded.

1085dda00547.title: Green growth
1085dda00547.sentence: Several international organisations had since turned their attention to green growth, in part to stimulate the economy during the 2008 financial crisis: At the request of countries, the OECD in 2011 published a Green Growth Strategy and in 2012, the World Bank, UNEP, OECD and GGGI launched the Green Growth Knowledge Platform (GGKP).

1a0e2c997d85.title: Green growth
1a0e2c997d85.sentence: According to the International Labour Organization, a shift to a greener economy could create 24 million new jobs globally by 2030, if environmental policies are put in place.

27f4be08d49e.title: Green growth
27f4be08d49e.sentence: The DMC, however, does not consider the shift of resource use which results from global supply chains, which is why another proposed metric is the material footprint (MF).

2112610267ed.title: Green growth
2112610267ed.sentence: Research based on the MF indicates that resource use might be growing similarly to GDP for a number of countries, as for example for the EU-27 or the member countries of the OECD.

397433e4c29d.title: Green growth
397433e4c29d.sentence: Recent analysis from the Energy & Climate Intelligence Unit found that 92% of global GDP and 89% of global emissions are in economies that have decoupled, either relatively or absolutely, up from 77% for both in the decade before the Paris Agreement (2006–2015).

1c68573e15f6.title: Green growth
1c68573e15f6.sentence: Between 2015 and 2023, countries representing more than 46% of global GDP achieved absolute decoupling, up from just over 38% in the pre-Paris period.

6212b248419e.title: Green growth
6212b248419e.sentence: A 2020 two-part systematic review published in Environmental Research Letters analyzed the full texts of 835 papers on the relationship between GDP, resource use (materials and energy) and greenhouse gas emissions.

f1cbedb94fb0.title: Green growth
f1cbedb94fb0.sentence: A potentially fundamental incompatibility between economic growth and systemic societal changes to address the climate crisis is rarely considered." The second part concluded "that large rapid absolute reductions of resource use and GHG emissions cannot be achieved through observed decoupling rates, hence decoupling needs to be complemented by sufficiency-oriented strategies and strict enforcement of absolute reduction targets."

3ca8f53f4a07.title: Resource efficiency
3ca8f53f4a07.sentence: It means using the Earth's limited resources in a sustainable manner while minimising environmental impact.

b437173c9905.title: Resource efficiency
b437173c9905.sentence: The UK Government has defined resource efficiency for research purposes as "the optimisation of resource use so that a given level of final consumption can be met with fewer resources".

a2085d5c145d.title: Resource efficiency
a2085d5c145d.sentence: It has been noted that improvements in resource efficiency can occur at production, consumption, and end of product life stages.

608548295baa.title: Resource efficiency
608548295baa.sentence: Resource efficiency measures, methods, and aims are quite similar to those of resource productivity/resource intensity and of the slightly more environmentally-inclined concept of ecological efficiency/eco-efficiency.

2607b10b8705.title: Resource efficiency
2607b10b8705.section: Resource use measurement and identification of hotspots
2607b10b8705.sentence: A key tool in resource efficiency is measuring different aspects of resource use (e.g. carbon footprint, water footprint, land footprint or material use), then identifying 'hot spots' where the most resources are used or where there are the best opportunities to reduce this resource use.

5c1ea829330e.title: Resource efficiency
5c1ea829330e.section: Examples of initiatives and programmes > Europe 2020
5c1ea829330e.sentence: The resource-efficient Europe "flagship initiative" was one of seven such initiatives set out in the Europe 2020 Strategy (2010-2020), the EU's growth strategy for a smart, inclusive and sustainable economy.

29a6f23ba2f7.title: Resource efficiency
29a6f23ba2f7.section: Examples of initiatives and programmes > Europe 2020
29a6f23ba2f7.sentence: The Commission stated that there were strong synergies between resource efficiency and other policy aims which could be beneficial, such as green growth industries providing secure employment, but a number of trade-offs needed to be managed, for example the promotion of green vehicle technologies supported the continued reduction in fossil fuel usage but also introduced new resource pressures such as electricity supply and sufficiency in the supply of rare-earth elements and lithium for vehicle batteries.

27add12a9273.title: Sustainable consumption
27add12a9273.sentence: Sustainable consumption (sometimes abbreviated to "SC") is the use of products and services in ways that minimizes impacts on the environment.

5938b997800b.title: Sustainable consumption
5938b997800b.sentence: Sustainable consumption refers to the deliberate process of making decisions throughout the consumption cycle—including choice, use, and disposal—so as to meet present needs while minimizing adverse impacts on the environment, economy, society, and culture.

63c3b275f215.title: Sustainable consumption
63c3b275f215.sentence: Sustainable consumption encompasses proactive behaviours such as purchasing sustainable products and services, avoidance behaviours including reducing consumption of unsustainable offerings, and practices that extend product lifecycles such as reuse and recycling.

40fc2d2ded96.title: Sustainable consumption
40fc2d2ded96.sentence: A global food emissions database shows that food systems are responsible for one third of the global anthropogenic GHG emissions.

b5156210417c.title: Sustainable consumption
b5156210417c.sentence: Therefore, sustainable consumption also includes food consumption – shifting to more sustainable diets.

58851a71b16c.title: Sustainable consumption
58851a71b16c.section: Consumption shifting > Fairness and income/spending freedoms
58851a71b16c.sentence: High-income individuals usually have higher energy footprints as they disproportionally use their larger financial resources – which they can usually spend freely in their entirety for any purpose as long as the end user purchase is legal – for energy-intensive goods.

17f07a5ef5c2.title: Sustainable consumption
17f07a5ef5c2.section: Consumption shifting > Fairness and income/spending freedoms
17f07a5ef5c2.sentence: In particular, the largest disproportionality was identified to be in the domain of transport, where e.g. the top 10% consume 56% of vehicle fuel and conduct 70% of vehicle purchases.

e70a9bdc4ed4.title: Sustainable consumption
e70a9bdc4ed4.section: Consumption shifting > Fairness and income/spending freedoms
e70a9bdc4ed4.sentence: The bottom half of the population is directly responsible for less than 20% of energy footprints and consume less than the top 5% in terms of trade-corrected energy.

f807e3289f70.title: Sustainable consumption
f807e3289f70.sentence: In 1992, the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), also referred to as the Earth Summit, recognized sustainable consumption as a concept.

b98e054e461c.title: Sustainable consumption
b98e054e461c.sentence: - 1992—At the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) the concept of sustainable consumption was established in chapter 4 of the Agenda 21.

d5b6a277cd9a.title: Sustainable consumption
d5b6a277cd9a.sentence: SDG 12 is meant to "ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns".

e22138a841e7.title: Sustainable consumption
e22138a841e7.sentence: Studies found that systemic change for "decarbonization" of humanity's economic structures or root-cause system changes above politics are required for a substantial impact on global warming.

4aaa6dcc287b.title: Sustainable consumption
4aaa6dcc287b.sentence: Nevertheless, ethical consumerism usually only refers to individual choices, and not the consumption behavior and/or import and consumption policies by the decision-making of nation-states.

fe96b12b2668.title: Kuznets curve
fe96b12b2668.sentence: In economics, the Kuznets curve (/ˈkʌznɛts/) is a hypothesized relationship between income and inequality proposed by economist Simon Kuznets in the 1950s and 1960s, who argued that as an economy develops, market forces first increase and then decrease economic inequality.

4b027845ea67.title: Kuznets curve
4b027845ea67.sentence: Kuznets believed that inequality would follow an inverted "U" shape as it rises and then falls again with the increase of income per-capita.

bd7ba3b09cbc.title: Kuznets curve
bd7ba3b09cbc.sentence: One explanation of such a progression suggests that early in development, investment opportunities for those who have money multiply, while an influx of cheap rural labor to the cities holds down wages.

11d38a064c6a.title: Kuznets curve
11d38a064c6a.sentence: Inequality is then expected to decrease when a certain level of average income is reached and the processes of industrialization – democratization and the rise of the welfare state – allow for the benefits from rapid growth, and increase the per-capita income.

c6c971bef776.title: Kuznets curve
c6c971bef776.sentence: The hypothesis remains highly contested among economists, with no consensus regarding its validity.

f48463c2a832.title: Kuznets curve
f48463c2a832.sentence: Inequality has risen in most developed countries since the 1960s, so graphs of inequality over time no longer display a Kuznets curve.

e0a1312290a6.title: Kuznets curve
e0a1312290a6.sentence: In a biography about Simon Kuznets's scientific methods, economist Robert Fogel noted Kuznets's own reservations about the "fragility of the data" which underpinned the hypothesis.

14656d749f48.title: Kuznets curve
14656d749f48.sentence: Fogel emphasized Kuznets's opinion that "even if the data turned out to be valid, they pertained to an extremely limited period of time and to exceptional historical experiences." Fogel noted that despite these "repeated warnings", Kuznets's caveats were overlooked, and the Kuznets curve was "raised to the level of law" by other economists.

7a4e666c38b2.title: Kuznets curve
7a4e666c38b2.section: Evidence > The Kuznets curve and development economics
7a4e666c38b2.sentence: The East Asian miracle (EAM) has been used to criticize the validity of the Kuznets curve theory.

d4e2dc106f9c.title: Kuznets curve
d4e2dc106f9c.section: Evidence > The Kuznets curve and development economics
d4e2dc106f9c.sentence: The rapid economic growth of eight East Asian countries—Japan; the Four Asian Tigers South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Hong Kong; Indonesia, Thailand, and Malaysia—between 1965 and 1990, was called the East Asian miracle.

c616db26c88b.title: Kuznets curve
c616db26c88b.section: Evidence > The Kuznets curve and development economics
c616db26c88b.sentence: Yet, contrary to Kuznets' historical examples, the EAM saw continual increases in life expectancy and decreasing rates of severe poverty.

cc87de581e90.title: Doughnut (economic model)
cc87de581e90.sentence: The Doughnut, or Doughnut economics, is a visual framework for sustainable development – shaped like a doughnut or lifebelt – combining the concept of planetary boundaries with the complementary concept of social boundaries.

84720792e972.title: Doughnut (economic model)
84720792e972.sentence: The centre hole of the model depicts the proportion of people that lack access to life's essentials (healthcare, education, equity and so on) while the crust represents the ecological ceilings (planetary boundaries) that life depends on and must not be overshot.

99d1ef6c10b7.title: Doughnut (economic model)
99d1ef6c10b7.sentence: The diagram was developed by University of Oxford economist Kate Raworth in her 2012 Oxfam paper A Safe and Just Space for Humanity and elaborated upon in her 2017 book Doughnut Economics: Seven Ways to Think Like a 21st-Century Economist and paper.

49a4a783bf7b.title: Doughnut (economic model)
49a4a783bf7b.sentence: In this model, an economy is considered prosperous when all twelve social foundations are met without overshooting any of the nine ecological ceilings.

1620568bad98.title: Doughnut (economic model)
1620568bad98.sentence: This situation is represented by the area between the two rings, considered by its creator as a safe and just space for humanity.

8ae91f885693.title: Doughnut (economic model)
8ae91f885693.sentence: The social foundations are inspired by the social aims of the Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations.

9fd3a856ae11.title: Doughnut (economic model)
9fd3a856ae11.sentence: The nine ecological ceilings are from the planetary boundaries put forward by a group of Earth-system scientists led by Johan Rockström and Will Steffen.

42156f3fb8d7.title: Doughnut (economic model)
42156f3fb8d7.section: Real-world economies in the Doughnut perspective
42156f3fb8d7.sentence: An empirical application of the doughnut model showed in 2018 that so far across 150 countries not a single country satisfies its citizens' basic needs while maintaining a globally sustainable level of resource use.

f91a4acc5db5.title: Doughnut (economic model)
f91a4acc5db5.section: Real-world economies in the Doughnut perspective
f91a4acc5db5.sentence: Raworth states that "significant GDP growth is very much needed" for low- and middle-income countries to be able to meet the goals of the social foundation for their citizens.

437a225dc4e5.title: Doughnut (economic model)
437a225dc4e5.sentence: The doughnut model has been criticized for lacking empirical support.

ca938fc781cf.title: Doughnut (economic model)
ca938fc781cf.sentence: On the contrary, the results often showed that higher levels of economic freedom were associated with less imbalance according to the measures derived from the model.

721bfb707ceb.title: Doughnut (economic model)
721bfb707ceb.sentence: Branko Milanović of CUNY’s Stone Center on Socio-Economic Inequality criticises the doughnut model for ignoring that if everyone were to reach the current median income of rich countries, world GDP would need to triple—an issue Raworth does not address.

71e009db99a7.title: Kuznets curve
71e009db99a7.sentence: The environmental Kuznets curve (EKC) is a hypothesized relationship between environmental quality and economic development: various indicators of environmental degradation tend to get worse as modern economic growth occurs until average income reaches a certain point over the course of development.

9889a7163795.title: Kuznets curve
9889a7163795.sentence: Although subject to continuing debate, there is considerable evidence to support the application of the environmental Kuznets curve for various environmental health indicators, such as water, air pollution and ecological footprint which show the inverted U-shaped curve as per capita income and/or GDP rise.

3045bfd9c2db.title: Kuznets curve
3045bfd9c2db.sentence: It has been argued that this trend occurs in the level of many of the environmental pollutants, such as sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxide, lead, DDT, chlorofluorocarbons, sewage, and other chemicals previously released directly into the air or water.

cb3a875d6b3e.title: Kuznets curve
cb3a875d6b3e.sentence: For example, between 1970 and 2006, the United States' inflation-adjusted GDP grew by 195%, the number of cars and trucks in the country more than doubled, and the total number of miles driven increased by 178%.

3da5dabe1941.title: Kuznets curve
3da5dabe1941.sentence: However, during that same period certain regulatory changes and technological innovations led to decreases in annual emissions of carbon monoxide from 197 million tons to 89 million, nitrogen oxides emissions from 27 million tons to 19 million, sulfur dioxide emissions from 31 million tons to 15 million, particulate emissions by 80%, and lead emissions by more than 98%.

0406da2e3c7a.title: Kuznets curve
0406da2e3c7a.sentence: Among countries with a per capita GDP of at least $4,600, net deforestation has ceased.

1986bb7451db.title: Kuznets curve
1986bb7451db.sentence: Yet it has been argued that wealthier countries are able to maintain forests along with high consumption by 'exporting' deforestation, leading to continuing deforestation on a worldwide scale.

859233514548.title: Kuznets curve
859233514548.sentence: For example, energy, land and resource use (sometimes called the "ecological footprint") may not fall with rising income.

98101c73ea5f.title: Kuznets curve
98101c73ea5f.sentence: While the ratio of energy per real GDP has fallen, total energy use is still rising in most developed countries as are total emission of many greenhouse gases.

56eee9064e24.title: Kuznets curve
56eee9064e24.sentence: Yandle et al. argue that the EKC has not been found to apply to carbon because most pollutants create localized problems like lead and sulfur, so there are a greater urgency and response to cleaning up such pollutants.

2231fe6ea83c.title: Kuznets curve
2231fe6ea83c.sentence: Conversely, reducing carbon dioxide emissions does not have a dramatic impact at a local level, so the impetus to clean them up is only for the altruistic reason of improving the global environment.

11a1e0304639.title: Kuznets curve
11a1e0304639.sentence: This becomes a tragedy of the commons where it is most efficient for everyone to pollute and for no one to clean up, and everyone is worse as a result (Hardin, 1968).

507af6ab4916.title: Kuznets curve
507af6ab4916.sentence: For example, Millimet and Stengos regard the traditional "inverse U" shape as actually being an "N" shape, indicating that pollution increases as a country develops, decreases once the threshold GDP is reached, and then begins increasing as national income continues to increase.

c6b21733c72c.title: Kuznets curve
c6b21733c72c.sentence: While such findings are still being debated, they could prove to be important because they pose the concerning question of whether pollution actually begins to decline for good when an economic threshold is reached or whether the decrease is only in local pollutants and pollution is simply exported to poorer developing countries.

9048704d4ee8.title: Resource intensity
9048704d4ee8.sentence: Resource intensity is a measure of the resources (e.g. water, energy, materials) needed for the production, processing and disposal of a unit of good or service, or for the completion of a process or activity; it is therefore a measure of the efficiency of resource use.

4f97364e7760.title: Resource intensity
4f97364e7760.sentence: In national economic and sustainability accounting it can be calculated as units of resource expended per unit of GDP.

d6b4b60b3a67.title: Resource intensity
d6b4b60b3a67.sentence: Relatively high resource intensities indicate a high price or environmental cost of converting resource into GDP; low resource intensity indicates a lower price or environmental cost of converting resource into GDP.

f7ec4065dbd0.title: Resource intensity
f7ec4065dbd0.sentence: Although these concepts are two sides of the same coin, in practice they involve very different approaches and can be viewed as reflecting, on the one hand, the efficiency of resource production as outcome per unit of resource use (resource productivity) and, on the other hand, the efficiency of resource consumption as resource use per unit outcome (resource intensity).

56d65dc87852.title: Resource intensity
56d65dc87852.sentence: The sustainability objective is to maximize resource productivity while minimizing resource intensity.

c3149360fc0c.title: Resource intensity
c3149360fc0c.section: Use in policy and sustainability measurement
c3149360fc0c.sentence: Organisations such as the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) use resource intensity indicators to assess progress toward decoupling economic growth from environmental degradation.

086a05928695.title: Planned obsolescence
086a05928695.sentence: In economics and industrial design, planned obsolescence (also called built-in obsolescence or premature obsolescence) is the concept of policies planning or designing a product with an artificially limited useful life or a purposely frail design, so that it becomes obsolete after a certain predetermined period of time upon which it decrementally functions or suddenly ceases to function, or might be perceived as unfashionable.

1431a121a9ad.title: Planned obsolescence
1431a121a9ad.sentence: Once regarded as a conspiracy theory, the rationale behind this strategy is to generate long-term sales volume by reducing the time between repeat purchases (referred to as "shortening the replacement cycle").

e3fd9b99a840.title: Planned obsolescence
e3fd9b99a840.sentence: Planned obsolescence tends to work best when a producer has at least an oligopoly.

5e1a0b7a299c.title: Planned obsolescence
5e1a0b7a299c.sentence: In these cases of planned obsolescence, there is an information asymmetry between the producer, who knows how long the product was designed to last, and the customer, who does not.

a4116546f058.title: Planned obsolescence
a4116546f058.sentence: When a market becomes more competitive, product lifespans tend to increase.

b2f445c024a0.title: Planned obsolescence
b2f445c024a0.sentence: For example, when Japanese vehicles with longer lifespans entered the American market in the 1960s and 1970s, American carmakers were forced to respond by building more durable products.

5604c7f0d5ca.title: Planned obsolescence
5604c7f0d5ca.sentence: In 1924, the American automobile market began reaching saturation point.

69e70e751629.title: Planned obsolescence
69e70e751629.sentence: To maintain unit sales, General Motors executive Alfred P. Sloan Jr. suggested annual model-year design changes to convince car owners to buy new replacements each year, with refreshed appearances headed by Harley Earl and the Art and Color Section.

ab8d074e92b4.title: Planned obsolescence
ab8d074e92b4.sentence: In 2015, the French National Assembly established a fine of up to €300,000 and jail terms of up to two years for manufacturers planning the failure of their products.

cdfd77f2de00.title: Planned obsolescence
cdfd77f2de00.sentence: The rule is relevant not only because of the sanctions that it establishes but also because it is the first time that a legislature recognized the existence of planned obsolescence.

397ef54d85ce.title: Planned obsolescence
397ef54d85ce.sentence: In the US, planned obsolescence is being tackled through right to repair laws which have been enacted by several states, including California, Minnesota, New York and Colorado.

9f8ca0a68871.title: Planned obsolescence
9f8ca0a68871.sentence: Philip Kotler argues that: "Much so-called planned obsolescence is the working of the competitive and technological forces in a free society - forces that lead to ever-improving goods and services."

25c129e128dd.title: Planned obsolescence
25c129e128dd.sentence: Critics such as Vance Packard argues the process is wasteful and exploits customers.

a6d8a282df6e.title: World3
a6d8a282df6e.sentence: The World3 model is a system dynamics model for computer simulation of interactions between population, industrial growth, food production and limits in the ecosystems of the earth.

eb7872f63d81.title: World3
eb7872f63d81.sentence: It was originally produced and used by a Club of Rome study that produced the model and the book The Limits to Growth (1972).

7bbf065313b6.title: World3
7bbf065313b6.sentence: The creators of the model were Dennis Meadows, project manager, and a team of 16 researchers.

e2eff864168f.title: World3
e2eff864168f.sentence: It added new features to Jay Wright Forrester's World2 model.

979519567e91.title: World3
979519567e91.sentence: The nonrenewable resource system starts with the assumption that the total amount of resources available is finite (about 110 times the consumption at 1990s rates for the World3/91 model).

c751f628e5db.title: World3
c751f628e5db.sentence: An important assumption that was made is that as the non-renewable resources are extracted, the remaining resources are increasingly difficult to extract, thus diverting more and more industrial output to resource extraction.

1cee84b1b02a.title: World3
1cee84b1b02a.sentence: The "reference run" is the one that "represent the most likely behavior mode of the system if the process of industrialization in the future proceeds in a way very similar to its progress in the past, and if technologies and value changes that have already been institutionalized continue to evolve." In this scenario, in 2000, the world population reaches six billion, and then goes on to peak at seven billion in 2030.

939814cff18a.title: World3
939814cff18a.sentence: Persistent pollution peaks in the year 2035 at 11 times 1970s levels.

a8dcc88a4290.title: World3
a8dcc88a4290.sentence: > We have great confidence in the basic qualitative assumptions and conclusions about the instability of the current global socioeconomic system and the general kinds of changes that will and will not lead to stability.

db64f4de0b4c.title: World3
db64f4de0b4c.sentence: We have a mixed degree of confidence in the numerical parameters of the model; some are well-known physical or biological constants that are unlikely to change, some are statistically derived social indices quite likely to change, and some are pure guesses that are perhaps only of the right order of magnitude.

71766b742acc.title: World3
71766b742acc.sentence: Czech-Canadian scientist and policy analyst Vaclav Smil disagreed with the combination of physically different processes into simplified equations:

50609287d1a7.title: World3
50609287d1a7.sentence: Lumping together (to cite just a few scores of possible examples) highly substitutable but relatively limited resources of liquid oil with unsubstitutable but immense deposits of sedimentary phosphate rocks, or short-lived atmospheric gases with long-lived radioactive wastes, struck me as extraordinarily meaningless.

abe08d0bcd32.title: World3
abe08d0bcd32.sentence: Recent results published in Yale's Journal of Industrial Ecology found that current empirical data is broadly consistent with the 1972 projections, and that if major changes to the consumption of resources are not undertaken, economic growth will peak and then rapidly decline by around 2040.

3326a2d9ece8.title: Ecological overshoot
3326a2d9ece8.sentence: Ecological overshoot is the phenomenon which occurs when the demands made on a natural ecosystem exceed its regenerative capacity.

fcc19f311d9b.title: Ecological overshoot
fcc19f311d9b.sentence: Global ecological overshoot occurs when the demands made by humanity exceed what the biosphere of Earth can provide through its capacity for renewal.

e1d24e3c353d.title: Ecological overshoot
e1d24e3c353d.sentence: Scientific use of the term in the context of the global ecological impact of humanity is attributed to a 1980 book by William R. Catton, Jr. titled Overshoot: The Ecological Basis of Revolutionary Change.

22589bb5be2d.title: Ecological overshoot
22589bb5be2d.sentence: These ecological resource accounts reveal that the global community has been exceeding the regenerative capacity of the Earth since 1970, which was the year when the consumption capacity of humanity first exceeded Earth's biocapacity.

e601a0926cb9.title: Ecological overshoot
e601a0926cb9.sentence: Each year since 1970 humanity has witnessed global ecological overshoot.

1b5186571526.title: Ecological overshoot
1b5186571526.sentence: A country has an ecological reserve if its Ecological footprint is smaller than its biocapacity; otherwise it is operating with an ecological overshoot.

9d4313b21315.title: Ecological overshoot
9d4313b21315.sentence: Over 85% of the world population lives in countries operating with an ecological overshoot.

814b38495be7.title: Ecological overshoot
814b38495be7.section: Measurement of ecological overshoot > Earth Overshoot Day
814b38495be7.sentence: This problem is highlighted each year on Earth Overshoot Day, an illustrative calendar date obtained through calculation, on which day humanity's resource consumption for the year is considered to have exceeded the Earth's capacity to regenerate those resources for that year.

f7525593a150.title: Ecological footprint
f7525593a150.sentence: Global Footprint Network estimates that, as of 2022, humanity has been using natural capital 71% faster than Earth can renew it, which they describe as meaning humanity's ecological footprint corresponds to 1.71 planet Earths.

924aff724b74.title: Ecological footprint
924aff724b74.sentence: If this rate of resource use is not reduced, persistent overshoot would suggest the occurrence of continued ecological deterioration and a potentially permanent decrease in Earth's human carrying capacity.

1b7dacecf5c6.title: Ecological footprint
1b7dacecf5c6.sentence: In its Living Planet Report 2022, the WWF documents a 69% decline in the world's vertebrate populations between 1970 and the present, and links this decline to humanity greatly exceeding global biocapacity.

f4a8a792640e.title: Agrowth
f4a8a792640e.sentence: Agrowth ("agnostic or atheistic about growth") is a concept in economic policy according to which it is preferable to be indifferent to the growth of gross domestic product (GDP growth) when devising policies to further economic and societal progress.

448eab19855c.title: Agrowth
448eab19855c.sentence: The reasoning behind agrowth is that GDP growth does not correlate closely with such progress.

01db02a5cd33.title: Agrowth
01db02a5cd33.sentence: The concept has been particularly discussed in the context of environmental policy, where it is opposed to both green growth and degrowth.

d2462cba34fb.title: Agrowth
d2462cba34fb.sentence: For example, environmental economist Jeroen C. J. M. van den Bergh argues for an agnostic attitude toward economic growth.

bbdecbdc62b4.title: Agrowth
bbdecbdc62b4.sentence: According to him, environmental policy should not be aimed at pursuing or avoiding growth in the hope of reducing environmental damage, but at direct deployment of effective instruments such as pricing externalities (for example, via environmental taxes or emission rights).

226e9504986f.title: Agrowth
226e9504986f.sentence: Whether the economy grows, stagnates or shrinks as a result is of secondary importance.

f7c13d1617d9.title: Ecomodernism
f7c13d1617d9.sentence: Ecomodernism is an environmental philosophy which argues that technological development can protect nature and improve human wellbeing through eco-economic decoupling, i.e., by separating economic growth from environmental impacts.

543b680c8f78.title: Ecomodernism
543b680c8f78.sentence: Ecomodernism embraces substituting natural ecological services with energy, technology, and synthetic solutions as long as they help reduce impact on environment.

927d72829531.title: Ecomodernism
927d72829531.sentence: Key among the goals of an ecomodern environmental ethic is the use of technology to intensify human activity and make more room for wild nature.

af631a2370da.title: Ecomodernism
af631a2370da.sentence: - Cities allow humans to live well while using less land.

ba10f0fed1a5.title: Ecomodernism
ba10f0fed1a5.sentence: - High-yield agriculture can spare forests and habitats.

fc252945dc97.title: Ecomodernism
fc252945dc97.sentence: In April 2015, a group of 18 self-described ecomodernists collectively published An Ecomodernist Manifesto.

ad3c1d3afcef.title: Ecomodernism
ad3c1d3afcef.sentence: In these debates, ecomodernism distinguishes itself from other schools of thought, including ecological economics, degrowth, population reduction, laissez-faire economics, the "soft energy" path, and central planning.

dd1f087adde1.title: Ecomodernism
dd1f087adde1.sentence: Eighteen ecological economists published a long rejoinder titled "A Degrowth Response to an Ecomodernist Manifesto", writing "the ecomodernists provide neither a very inspiring blueprint for future development strategies nor much in the way of solutions to our environmental and energy woes."

9c828796b2ce.title: Ecomodernism
9c828796b2ce.sentence: > the mass extinction of life forms that the human enterprise has set into motion receives no mention in the Manifesto.

21ca20237726.title: Ecomodernism
21ca20237726.sentence: Ecomodernism has been criticized for inadequately recognizing what Holly Jean Buck, Assistant Professor of Environment and Sustainability, says is the exploitative, violent and unequal dimensions of technological modernisation.

f6073b45d4ca.title: Green New Deal
f6073b45d4ca.sentence: The Green New Deal (GND) is a conceptual environmentalist movement that calls for public policy to address climate change, along with achieving other social aims like job creation, economic growth, and reducing economic inequality.

db1d83c0be08.title: Green New Deal
db1d83c0be08.sentence: The public contended that the US needed to address the climate crisis with a large-scale initiative, similar to the New Deal that was implemented under the Roosevelt administration.

53532b647718.title: Green New Deal
53532b647718.sentence: On October 22, 2008, UNEP's Executive Director Achim Steiner unveiled a Global Green New Deal initiative as a response to the Great Recession, aiming to create jobs in "green" industries, thus boosting the world economy and curbing climate change at the same time.

0cff58e955c6.title: Green New Deal
0cff58e955c6.sentence: In the UK, the Green New Deal Group and the New Economics Foundation produced the A Green New Deal report asking for a Green New Deal as a way out of the Great Recession, demanding a reform of the financial and tax sectors and a revolution of the energy sector in the country.

7d6ba9c594f1.title: Green New Deal
7d6ba9c594f1.section: United States > The Rep. Ocasio-Cortez and Sen. Markey Green New Deal > Green New Deal Resolution
7d6ba9c594f1.sentence: On February 7, 2019, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Senator Edward Markey released a fourteen-page resolution for their Green New Deal (House Resolution 109, closely related to S. Res.

1193c84c8db2.title: Green New Deal
1193c84c8db2.section: United States > The Rep. Ocasio-Cortez and Sen. Markey Green New Deal > Green New Deal Resolution
1193c84c8db2.sentence: Their proposal advocated transitioning the United States to 100% renewable, zero-emission energy sources, along with investment in electric cars and high-speed rail systems, and implementing the "social cost of carbon" that had been part of the Obama administration's plan for addressing climate change within 10 years.

eae4df412786.title: Green New Deal
eae4df412786.sentence: Environmental justice is explicitly referenced as a crucial component of the Green New Deal, integrating various principles into its framework.

1cacc8f23841.title: Green New Deal
1cacc8f23841.sentence: In the context of the Green New Deal, environmental justice refers to the promotion of policies that recognize historical and ongoing injustices perpetuated against vulnerable populations such as communities of color, Indigenous populations, and low-income communities.

02c36eb926b9.title: Green New Deal
02c36eb926b9.sentence: In December 2019, the newly elected European Commission under Von der Leyen presented a set of policy proposals under the name European Green Deal.

c052dc0503e9.title: Green New Deal
c052dc0503e9.sentence: Compared to the United States plan, it has a less ambitious decarbonisation timeline, with an aim of carbon neutrality in 2050.

20742fa67dae.title: Green New Deal
20742fa67dae.section: United States > The Rep. Ocasio-Cortez and Sen. Markey Green New Deal > Criticism
20742fa67dae.sentence: Many who support some goals of the Green New Deal express doubt about feasibility of one or more of its parts.

ac3ce2bbdc90.title: Green New Deal
ac3ce2bbdc90.section: United States > The Rep. Ocasio-Cortez and Sen. Markey Green New Deal > Criticism
ac3ce2bbdc90.sentence: John P. Holdren, former science advisor to Obama, thinks the 2030 goal is too optimistic, saying that 2045 or 2050 would be more realistic.

73b45d3b7ca1.title: Eco-sufficiency
73b45d3b7ca1.sentence: Ecological sufficiency, or simply sufficiency, refers to the concept or strategy to reduce the environmental footprint of societies through moderating the need for energy, carbon and material-based services and products.

02bab67e0b2c.title: Eco-sufficiency
02bab67e0b2c.sentence: As a goal, sufficiency is about ensuring that all humans can live a good life within planetary boundaries, meaning without overshooting the ecological limits of the Earth and thus limiting resource use and pollution.

39c7563775a4.title: Eco-sufficiency
39c7563775a4.sentence: As a sustainability strategy, sufficiency is mainly concerned with the limitation and reduction of consumption and production levels without threatening the fulfillment of fundamental human needs.

612b1b3b7d33.title: Eco-sufficiency
612b1b3b7d33.sentence: The IPCC defines sufficiency as "a set of policy measures and daily practices that avoid the demand for energy, materials, land, water, and other natural resources while providing wellbeing for all within the planetary boundaries".

2475d3483cd3.title: Eco-sufficiency
2475d3483cd3.sentence: The term was popularised by authors such as Thomas Princen, a professor at MIT, in his 2005 book The Logic of Sufficiency.

c5ea0556474c.title: Eco-sufficiency
c5ea0556474c.sentence: Drawing on the limits of technical efficiency and rebound effects, sufficiency proponents argue that energy demand and its associated emissions cannot be sufficiently reduced if the root causes of this demand are not addressed, that is the nature and level of the energy services our societies rely on.

9dc7d4e4ccba.title: Eco-efficiency
9dc7d4e4ccba.sentence: Together with consistency and eco-sufficiency, it is well-established in sustainability science as a fundamental sustainability strategy.

489be7dfdbcc.title: Eco-sufficiency
489be7dfdbcc.sentence: A German study found that sufficiency measures could lead to a theoretical reduction of 70% of energy consumption at the level of households.

d6facadfc17d.title: Eco-sufficiency
d6facadfc17d.sentence: The "Four D's" suggested by Wolfgang Sachs are one example:

b2f1c83f7c70.title: Eco-sufficiency
b2f1c83f7c70.sentence: - Decommercialization (leaving less room for the market).

328ebe8da8bb.title: Eco-sufficiency
328ebe8da8bb.sentence: A common criticism, shared with the degrowth concept, is that this would hurt economic growth, increase unemployment and lead to social problems.

fa1cc4e9f918.title: Eco-sufficiency
fa1cc4e9f918.sentence: A third objection to sufficiency is that, as for efficiency, the energy and material savings could lead to indirect rebound effects.

d118610b4c6a.title: Sustainability strategies
d118610b4c6a.sentence: Sustainability strategies are mechanisms that contribute to achieving sustainability and are well-established in the field of sustainability science.

ba0564316e77.title: Sustainability strategies
ba0564316e77.sentence: Originally, the term centered on a triad introduced by Joseph Huber, encompassing sufficiency, efficiency, and consistency.

e2650248f7c8.title: Sustainability strategies
e2650248f7c8.sentence: Sufficiency focuses on reducing consumption and production levels without threatening human needs.

d4ab025f7932.title: Sustainability strategies
d4ab025f7932.sentence: Sufficiency is often discussed in the context of the degrowth paradigm of sustainability.

1a1efd5ffcfa.title: Sustainability strategies
1a1efd5ffcfa.sentence: Efficiency aims to reduce resource use, energy consumption, or pollution per unit of consumption or production within existing production and consumption systems - such as improved fuel efficiency in cars or energy-saving appliances.

66429548e3e4.title: Sustainability strategies
66429548e3e4.sentence: It is often considered to share an elective affinity with the green growth paradigm.

700550c35455.title: Sustainability strategies
700550c35455.sentence: Consistency involves shifting to new industrial metabolisms that are more consistent with nature’s metabolism and hence cause less environmental damage (such as renewable energies and circular design).

5e5affc3fd7c.title: Sustainability strategies
5e5affc3fd7c.sentence: This strategy is implicitly advocated by the circular economy approach and rooted in industrial ecology.

1f75eaa7d1b8.title: Sustainability strategies
1f75eaa7d1b8.sentence: Following the typology by Maria Sandberg, four types of sufficiency can be distinguished, namely absolute reduction of consumption (e.g. less travels), modal shifts (e.g. switching from air travels to trains), sharing (e.g. carpooling) and increased longevity (e.g. repairing a bike instead of buying a new one).

ca8b7b0f487e.title: Post-growth
ca8b7b0f487e.sentence: Post-growth is an umbrella term that refers to a broad family of economic, ecological, and political perspectives responding to the limits-to-growth dilemma—the recognition that infinite economic growth is biophysically unsustainable on a finite planet.

1bcc9053a5e3.title: Post-growth
1bcc9053a5e3.sentence: Central to post-growth thinking is the shift of the focus out of GDP growth as the main goal of the economy.

3a80e7d73911.title: Post-growth
3a80e7d73911.sentence: Instead, well-being becomes the main objective.

3e00715f6a27.title: Post-growth
3e00715f6a27.sentence: Post-growth puts emphasis on decoupling societal well-being from economic growth, advocating for the possibility of prosperity beyond growth.

ae9a9d6e29d2.title: Post-growth
ae9a9d6e29d2.sentence: Some describe it as comprising two main categories: degrowth (a stance advocating for a deliberate and equitable reduction in material consumption and economic activity) and agrowth (an agnostic stance towards economic growth, holding that policymakers should remain neutral about GDP growth because it may have either positive or negative effects on environmental or social objectives).

574cd1d3ebae.title: Post-growth
574cd1d3ebae.sentence: Paradigmatic post-growth policies are working time reductions, universal basic income, wealth taxes, carbon taxes combined with strong wealth redistribution and universal basic services.

1eaf4d140419.title: Post-growth
1eaf4d140419.sentence: While post-growth generally refers to prioritising sustainability and social justice over economic growth, degrowth goes further by advocating a deliberate reduction in the scale of economic activity to achieve these aims.

b0a05daf0ca2.title: Post-growth
b0a05daf0ca2.sentence: A 2023 study of nearly 800 climate policy researchers around the world found that 73% support post-growth (45% agrowth and 28% degrowth).

cc19f77af473.title: Growth imperative
cc19f77af473.sentence: Growth imperative is a term in economic theory regarding a possible necessity of economic growth.

fb7fab73dcf3.title: Growth imperative
fb7fab73dcf3.sentence: These definitions can be summarized that a growth imperative exists if exterior conditions make it necessary for agents to increase their economic efforts as to avoid existential consequences.

9c543dd23363.title: Growth imperative
9c543dd23363.sentence: On the micro level, it describes mechanisms that force firms or consumers (households) to increase revenues or consumption to not endanger their income.

1e590c3cb0a0.title: Growth imperative
