bfa9c1331707.title: Kuznets curve
bfa9c1331707.section: Environmental Kuznets curve > Kuznets curves for steel and other metals
bfa9c1331707.sentence: This discovery, and the first usage of the term "Kuznets Curve for Steel" and "Metal intensity Kuznets Curve" were by Huw McKay in a 2008 working paper (McKay 2008).

2ec77906acfb.title: Conviviality
2ec77906acfb.sentence: Conviviality, or Convivialism, is the ability of individuals to interact creatively and autonomously with others and their environment to satisfy their own needs.

3c94c1c2ad87.title: Conviviality
3c94c1c2ad87.section: Conviviality in left-wing politics > Ivan Illich
3c94c1c2ad87.sentence: As described here, this new usage for the term conviviality was introduced by Ivan Illich in his 1973 book, Tools for Conviviality.

a003ef78461a.title: Conviviality
a003ef78461a.section: Conviviality in left-wing politics > Ivan Illich
a003ef78461a.sentence: He contrasted this with industrialised societies where individuals are reduced to "mere consumers", unable to choose what is produced or how things are made in a world governed by a "radical monopoly" that divided the population into experts that could use the tools and laypeople that could not.

f54eb85466b3.title: Conviviality
f54eb85466b3.section: Conviviality in left-wing politics > Ivan Illich
f54eb85466b3.sentence: By contrast, convivial tools were those that promoted and extended autonomy, including most hand tools, bicycles, and telephones.

cfcb1b281bcd.title: Conviviality
cfcb1b281bcd.section: Conviviality in left-wing politics > Ivan Illich
cfcb1b281bcd.sentence: Examples of non-convivial tools that Illich was railing against included open-pit mines, road networks and schools, this last example linking to his previous work critiquing mass education systems, Deschooling Society.

d1599128ccc9.title: Conviviality
d1599128ccc9.section: Conviviality in left-wing politics > Contemporary movements > Degrowth
d1599128ccc9.sentence: Conviviality is one of the core concepts of the Degrowth movement, appearing in representative texts such as Degrowth: A Vocabulary for a New Era.

605216d28e3c.title: Conviviality
605216d28e3c.section: Conviviality in left-wing politics > Contemporary movements > Degrowth
605216d28e3c.sentence: It is generally accepted within this literature that any technologies suitable for a degrowth society must be convivial.

d79faff05c12.title: Conviviality
d79faff05c12.section: Conviviality in left-wing politics > Ivan Illich
d79faff05c12.sentence: Convivial tools share many similarities with the intermediate technology or 'technology with a human face' described in Small is Beautiful by Illich's contemporary E. F. Schumacher.

f9a795e162a3.title: Bright green environmentalism
f9a795e162a3.sentence: Bright green environmentalism is an environmental philosophy and movement that emphasizes the use of advanced technology, social innovation, eco-innovation, and sustainable design to address environmental challenges.

44f042dc12e5.title: Bright green environmentalism
44f042dc12e5.sentence: This approach contrasts with more traditional forms of environmentalism that may advocate for reduced consumption or a return to simpler lifestyles.

8cfefac79bf0.title: Bright green environmentalism
8cfefac79bf0.section: Origin and evolution of bright green thinking
8cfefac79bf0.sentence: The term bright green, coined in 2003 by writer Alex Steffen, refers to the fast-growing new wing of environmentalism, distinct from traditional forms.

dbd945fb822f.title: Bright green environmentalism
dbd945fb822f.section: Origin and evolution of bright green thinking
dbd945fb822f.sentence: Their principal focus is on the idea that through a combination of well-built communities, new technologies and sustainable living practices, the quality of life can actually be improved even while ecological footprints shrink.

82abacc68536.title: Bright green environmentalism
82abacc68536.section: Dark greens, light greens and bright greens > Dark green
82abacc68536.sentence: Dark greens may point to effects like the Jevons paradox to argue limits to the benefits of technological approaches such as advocated by bright greens.

2fed12c40110.title: Eco-economic decoupling
2fed12c40110.section: Terminology > Five axes to assess decoupling
2fed12c40110.sentence: There are at least five axes to assess eco-economic decoupling:

00b0d5454db4.title: Eco-economic decoupling
00b0d5454db4.section: Terminology > Five axes to assess decoupling
00b0d5454db4.sentence: Overall decoupling refers to cases where decoupling occurs between GDP and all environmental indicators (e.g. water use, land use, greenhouse gas emissions, etc.), while partial for cases where it only concerns one or more environmental indicator, but not all of them.

58d73fc645fe.title: Eco-economic decoupling
58d73fc645fe.section: Terminology > Five axes to assess decoupling
58d73fc645fe.sentence: This axis is particularly important for cases where decoupling occurs on one environmental indicator, but at the expenses of another one (e.g. reducing greenhouse gas emissions, but increasing mining).

853757064200.title: Eco-economic decoupling
853757064200.section: Terminology > Five axes to assess decoupling
853757064200.sentence: Local decoupling refers to cases where decoupling is observed between variables relative to a restricted geographical perimeter (e.g. a country or a water basin), while global decoupling corresponds to decoupling between two variables at the planetary scale (e.g. world GDP and world greenhouse gas emissions).

fb703f74316c.title: Eco-economic decoupling
fb703f74316c.section: Terminology > Five axes to assess decoupling
fb703f74316c.sentence: This axis is particularly important for cases where decoupling occurs in some countries, but at the expense of increasing environmental stress in other countries (essentially, outsourcing production).

bb133a7abf04.title: Eco-economic decoupling
bb133a7abf04.section: Terminology > Five axes to assess decoupling
bb133a7abf04.sentence: Yet, economic growth and environmental pressures can re-couple later on, making the decoupling only temporary.

a21816e8c8f0.title: Eco-economic decoupling
a21816e8c8f0.section: Terminology > Five axes to assess decoupling
a21816e8c8f0.sentence: In order to be effective, decoupling should be large and fast enough to prevent environmental stress from reaching critical environmental tipping points (often described as planetary boundaries), which lead to de facto irreversible environmental effects.

563d3725b481.title: Eco-economic decoupling
563d3725b481.sentence: Resource decoupling refers to reducing the rate of resource use per unit of economic activity.

4784e7804a2f.title: Eco-economic decoupling
4784e7804a2f.sentence: Impact decoupling required increasing economic output while reducing negative environmental impacts.

4db4235bfdca.title: Eco-economic decoupling
4db4235bfdca.sentence: The "dematerialization" is based on using less material, energy, water and land resources for the same economic input.

1dc0b0d2c892.title: Eco-economic decoupling
1dc0b0d2c892.sentence: These impacts arise from the extraction of resources.

733d767fbeb6.title: Degrowth
733d767fbeb6.sentence: Less than 1% favoured pursuing economic growth regardless of its environmental impacts ("growth at all costs"), 42% supported the view that growth can be made compatible with environmental sustainability ("green growth"), 31% preferred to ignore economic growth as a policy objective ("agrowth"), and 17% favoured halting economic growth altogether ("degrowth").

fc22114a6e13.title: Degrowth
fc22114a6e13.sentence: Alternatives to degrowth include green growth (economic growth and sustainability are deemed compatible) and agrowth (agnostic on growth, focusing on reducing environmental harm through effective instruments, regardless of whether the economy is growing, stagnant, or contracting).

53b02d809fed.title: Degrowth
53b02d809fed.sentence: Drews and Van den Bergh surveyed scientists' views on economic growth versus the environment.

712e8db4e335.title: Degrowth
712e8db4e335.sentence: Another survey of nearly 800 climate policy researchers around the world found that 28% support degrowth.

14c352ba0b7c.title: Green economy
14c352ba0b7c.sentence: Critics point instead to alternative frameworks for economic change such as a circular economy, steady-state economy, degrowth, doughnut economics and others.

13070268db3b.title: Degrowth
13070268db3b.section: Origins of the movement > Recent developments
13070268db3b.sentence: In a June 2020 paper published in Nature Communications, the authors state that a change in economic paradigms is imperative to prevent environmental destruction, and suggest a range of ideas from the reformist (agrowth) to the radical (degrowth, eco-socialism and eco-anarchism).

edbbc6988154.title: Planned obsolescence
edbbc6988154.sentence: Obsolescence of desirability or stylistic obsolescence occurs when designers change the styling of products so trendsetting customers will purchase the latest styles.

60de2d020bcd.title: Planned obsolescence
60de2d020bcd.sentence: Although similar, it is a result of consumer perception rather than premeditated (planned) by the designer.

808e5e7341e5.title: Planned obsolescence
808e5e7341e5.sentence: An example of such a product is clothing.

328e0f9b1a08.title: Planned obsolescence
328e0f9b1a08.sentence: Such products experience a cycle of desirability referred to as a "fashion cycle".

0b093a0ae4c0.title: Planned obsolescence
0b093a0ae4c0.sentence: By continuously introducing new aesthetics, and retargeting or discontinuing older designs, a manufacturer can "ride the fashion cycle", allowing for constant sales despite the original products remaining fully functional.

ca2098498cc2.title: Planned obsolescence
ca2098498cc2.sentence: There are several variants of planned obsolescence.

a67f855ced84.title: Planned obsolescence
a67f855ced84.sentence: Contrived durability is a strategy of shortening the product lifetime before it is released onto the market, by designing it to deteriorate quickly.

9ed82c571e26.title: Planned obsolescence
9ed82c571e26.sentence: A possible method of limiting a product's durability is to use inferior materials in critical areas, or suboptimal component layouts which cause excessive wear.

e0de4616d2dc.title: Planned obsolescence
e0de4616d2dc.sentence: Such products are often designed to be difficult to service; for example, electronics may have internal components coated in glue.

192d3b9b19c3.title: Planned obsolescence
192d3b9b19c3.sentence: Manufacturers may make replacement parts either unavailable or so expensive that they make the product uneconomic to repair.

9c357f44c63d.title: Planned obsolescence
9c357f44c63d.sentence: In some cases, notification may be combined with deliberate artificial disabling of a functional product to prevent it from working, thus requiring the buyer to purchase a replacement.

32a01f57ac52.title: Planned obsolescence
32a01f57ac52.sentence: For example, inkjet printer manufacturers employ smart chips in their ink cartridges to prevent them from being used after a certain threshold (number of pages, time, etc.), even though the cartridge may still contain usable ink or could be refilled (with ink toners, up to 50 percent of the toner cartridge is often still full).

65634db80a27.title: Sustainability strategies
65634db80a27.sentence: The framework identifies a total of ten sustainability strategies, divided into five intergenerational and five intragenerational strategies.

e13c94cfc9f5.title: Sustainability strategies
e13c94cfc9f5.sentence: A comprehensive conceptual framework was introduced by Eric Hartmann, defining sustainability strategies as mechanisms that help guarantee central human capabilities or limit and reduce environmental impacts, thereby promoting both intergenerational and intragenerational justice.

d9e0afb9a1ab.title: Sustainability strategies
d9e0afb9a1ab.sentence: They are based on the established triad of sufficiency, efficiency increase and consistency increases.

35ab0663d04e.title: Sustainability strategies
35ab0663d04e.sentence: This triad is complemented by two additional strategies, namely population reduction and regeneration expansion.

eebce87593db.title: Sustainability strategies
eebce87593db.sentence: Regeneration expansion encompasses processes that reduce absolute environmental pressure and restore the environment—activities such as reforestation or carbon dioxide removal.

59b1bda79999.title: Sustainability strategies
59b1bda79999.sentence: A set of five intragenerational strategies can be utilized to ensure everyone's central capabilities and satisfy fundamental human needs, including capability empowerment, equalization, eco-efficiency increase, impact expansion and population reduction.

ebf28a504c09.title: Sustainability strategies
ebf28a504c09.sentence: Sustainability, in this view, is achieved when all individuals can satisfy fundamental human needs while environmental impacts remain within safe thresholds.

d2d495a9de7d.title: Growth imperative
d2d495a9de7d.section: Macroeconomic theories > Monetary system and the role of positive interest rates
d2d495a9de7d.sentence: For a long time, several authors especially from German-speaking countries have been locating a macroeconomic growth imperative in the monetary system, especially due to the combination of credit money and compound interest.

88857b4a0e98.title: Growth imperative
88857b4a0e98.section: Macroeconomic theories > Monetary system and the role of positive interest rates
88857b4a0e98.sentence: This is considered to lead inevitably and system-immanently to an exponential growth of debt and interest-bearing deposits.

e14a64ffeca6.title: Growth imperative
e14a64ffeca6.section: Macroeconomic theories > Monetary system and the role of positive interest rates
e14a64ffeca6.sentence: In his book The Growth Spiral (2013), Hans Christoph Binswanger estimated a necessary minimum growth rate to be 1.8 %, while Mathias Binswanger (2009) derived a minimum growth rate of 0.45 %, such that enterprises can still generate profits in the aggregate.

b99be4ea1f01.title: Growth imperative
b99be4ea1f01.section: Macroeconomic theories > Monetary system and the role of positive interest rates
b99be4ea1f01.sentence: Other authors criticise the results of Beltrani as well as H. C. and M. Binswanger on the basis that they are based on inconsistent economic models and therefore not valid (→ Stock-Flow consistent model).

aedf54f0818d.title: Growth imperative
aedf54f0818d.section: Macroeconomic theories > Monetary system and the role of positive interest rates
aedf54f0818d.sentence: Those models show how repaid interest is not simply 'removed' from circulation, but flows back into the economy where it can be earned and repeated used to service debts.

a01d4e37714c.title: Growth imperative
a01d4e37714c.section: Macroeconomic theories > Monetary system and the role of positive interest rates
a01d4e37714c.sentence: Models such as those created by Jackson & Victor show that, if no money is accumulated, then all debt can be serviced, and hence that no growth imperative arises from the creation of money as debt, 'per se'.

84be85b2fae8.title: Growth imperative
84be85b2fae8.section: Macroeconomic theories > Monetary system and the role of positive interest rates
84be85b2fae8.sentence: They argue that ultimately it is not the interest rate but the savings rate that is decisive for the stability of a stationary economy.

66b0dc970446.title: Environmental space
66b0dc970446.sentence: The concept of environmental space is the amount of any particular resource that can be consumed by a country without threatening the continued availability of that resource (sustainability), assuming that everyone in the world is entitled to an equal share.

f3abc2d06df0.title: Environmental space
f3abc2d06df0.sentence: The weakness of the concept is that it requires calculating the maximum sustainable consumption rate of each different resource globally.

6a4eb6795a5a.title: Environmental space
6a4eb6795a5a.sentence: This rate could be set by either the maximum sustainable yield (say for forests or fisheries) or the assimilative capacity of the environment (e.g. for CO2 or chlorine), but both quantities are very difficult to determine, so the 'environmental space' has rather large error limits and is therefore hard to defend in policy discussions.

5b365ad2d786.title: Environmental space
5b365ad2d786.sentence: A further difficulty is that there is a different 'environmental space' for each kind of resource, and as they each necessarily have different units of measure, they cannot be added to get an overall environmental space for all the resources consumed by a country.

1d2cb95d355f.title: Environmental space
1d2cb95d355f.sentence: The idea of environmental space was promoted quite strongly by Friends of the Earth Europe in the mid-1990s, but it is rarely used now, because of the aforementioned difficulties, and has essentially been superseded by 'ecological footprint'.

5dc4d76ff435.title: Environmental space
5dc4d76ff435.sentence: The advantage of the ecological footprint is that every kind of resource use is converted to a land area basis, so that they can be added to produce an overall figure for a country, allowing comparisons to be made.

ca1fba51c0f7.title: Khazzoom–Brookes postulate
ca1fba51c0f7.sentence: In the 1980s, the economists Daniel Khazzoom and Leonard Brookes independently put forward ideas about energy consumption and behavior that argue that increased energy efficiency paradoxically tends to lead to increased energy consumption.

798e0577dbcc.title: Khazzoom–Brookes postulate
798e0577dbcc.sentence: In short, the postulate states that "energy efficiency improvements that, on the broadest considerations, are economically justified at the microlevel, lead to higher levels of energy consumption at the macrolevel." This idea is a more modern analysis of a phenomenon known as the Jevons Paradox.

02288bff024b.title: Khazzoom–Brookes postulate
02288bff024b.sentence: In 1992, the US economist Harry Saunders dubbed this hypothesis the Khazzoom–Brookes postulate, and showed that it was true under neo-classical growth theory over a wide range of assumptions.

0a779f64dab8.title: Khazzoom–Brookes postulate
0a779f64dab8.sentence: Increased energy efficiency can increase energy consumption by three means.

0d4623999805.title: Khazzoom–Brookes postulate
0d4623999805.sentence: Firstly, increased energy efficiency makes the use of energy relatively cheaper, thus encouraging increased use.

79a01f92a587.title: Khazzoom–Brookes postulate
79a01f92a587.sentence: Secondly, increased energy efficiency leads to increased economic growth, which pulls up energy use in the whole economy.

f7a281674d0c.title: Khazzoom–Brookes postulate
f7a281674d0c.sentence: Thirdly, increased efficiency in any one bottleneck resource multiplies the use of all the companion technologies, products and services that were being restrained by it.

889e218e0267.title: Khazzoom–Brookes postulate
889e218e0267.sentence: The work done by Khazzoom and Brookes began after the OPEC oil crises of 1973 and 1979, when demand for more fuel-efficient automobiles began to rise.

b3fce69b9ce3.title: Khazzoom–Brookes postulate
b3fce69b9ce3.sentence: Although greater fuel efficiency was achieved for each automobile on average, overall consumption has continued to increase.

dee7dd590681.title: Khazzoom–Brookes postulate
dee7dd590681.sentence: This effect is comparable to the Jevons paradox.

c76a00573aaa.title: Factor 10
c76a00573aaa.sentence: The goal of Factor 10 is to assure that nations do not exceed the planet's carrying capacity but leave sufficient resources for future generations.

a56d7671e8a5.title: Factor 10
a56d7671e8a5.sentence: With the predicted rise in population and economic growth to maintain the level of pollution we have today, we need to be able to produce the same output for 10% of the impact.

054086881da0.title: Factor 10
054086881da0.sentence: Friedrich Schmidt-Bleek, from the Wuppertal Institute for Climate, Environment and Energy, first proposed the Factor 10 and dematerialization concepts in the early 1990s.

3885f2a6f67a.title: Factor 10
3885f2a6f67a.sentence: Factor 10 evolved from the less dramatic Factor 4 was originally proposed by L. Hunter Lovins and Amory Lovins of the Rocky Mountain Institute and Ernst von Weizsäcker, the founder of the Wuppertal Institute for Climate, Environment & Energy.

2889bb2847f7.title: Factor 10
2889bb2847f7.sentence: The concept attempts to reduce resource and energy use by 75% by doubling output and halving input of production.

da6fe745e22b.title: Factor 10
da6fe745e22b.sentence: Factor 10 goes farther as a response to the United Nations Environment Programme call for a tenfold reduction in resource consumption in industrialized countries as a necessary long-term target if adequate resources are to be released for the needs of the developing countries.

7371e7367f3d.title: Factor 10
7371e7367f3d.sentence: Eco-efficiency, environmental purchasing design for environment, policies and environmental taxes have already been used by business and governments implementing the Factor 10 theory.

edf8aa54e9d4.title: Bright green environmentalism
edf8aa54e9d4.section: Dark greens, light greens and bright greens
edf8aa54e9d4.sentence: Alex Steffen describes contemporary environmentalists as being split into three groups, dark, light, and bright greens.

e08a7646c418.title: Bright green environmentalism
e08a7646c418.section: Dark greens, light greens and bright greens > Light green
e08a7646c418.sentence: Light greens see protecting the environment first and foremost as a personal responsibility.

03c336d249f1.title: Bright green environmentalism
03c336d249f1.section: Dark greens, light greens and bright greens > Light green
03c336d249f1.sentence: Instead, they often focus on environmentalism as a lifestyle choice.

051c9101704b.title: Bright green environmentalism
051c9101704b.section: Dark greens, light greens and bright greens > Dark green
051c9101704b.sentence: In contrast, dark greens believe that environmental problems are an inherent part of industrialized, capitalist civilization, and seek radical political and social and cultural change.

7948cd23ae03.title: Bright green environmentalism
7948cd23ae03.section: Dark greens, light greens and bright greens > Dark green
7948cd23ae03.sentence: Dark greens claim this is caused by the emphasis on economic growth that exists within all existing ideologies, a tendency sometimes referred to as growth mania.

bd06771856a9.title: Bright green environmentalism
bd06771856a9.section: Dark greens, light greens and bright greens > Bright green
bd06771856a9.sentence: More recently, bright greens emerged as a group of environmentalists who believe that radical changes are needed in the economic and political operation of society in order to make it sustainable, but that better designs, new technologies and more widely distributed social innovations are the means to make those changes—and that society can neither stop nor protest its way to sustainability.

c9af6b649425.title: Degrowth in the Global South
c9af6b649425.sentence: Degrowth in the Global South examines the relevance, critiques, and adaptations of degrowth principles within countries typically classified as part of the Global South.

de84961334c6.title: Degrowth in the Global South
de84961334c6.sentence: However, applying degrowth to the Global South is debatable.

246f9f5ddc50.title: Degrowth in the Global South
246f9f5ddc50.sentence: Many countries in the South are still struggling with unmet basic needs, infrastructure deficits, and historical patterns of exploitation.

6cd3b500994a.title: Degrowth in the Global South
6cd3b500994a.sentence: Critics question whether degrowth is appropriate for regions that may still require some forms of material growth to ensure well-being.

2bcfaa87e80b.title: Degrowth in the Global South
2bcfaa87e80b.sentence: Although degrowth has been largely developed in the North, many of its philosophical roots lie in Southern traditions.

3ec2fa35b380.title: Degrowth in the Global South
3ec2fa35b380.sentence: Philosophies like Buen Vivir in the Andean region and Ubuntu in Southern Africa emphasize community, harmony with nature, and relational well-being, offering Southern alternatives to growth-centric models.

4133a9e40e67.title: Degrowth in the Global South
4133a9e40e67.sentence: Degrowth in the North is also framed by some as an act of decolonization, aiming to reduce the North's ecological footprint and create space for the South to pursue its own pathways.

bde63ed12748.title: Degrowth in the Global South
bde63ed12748.sentence: The concept of ecological debt—the idea that the North owes the South for centuries of environmental exploitation—figures prominently in this narrative.

e075fe11af57.title: Degrowth in the Global South
e075fe11af57.sentence: - Degrowth in the North could destabilize export-dependent economies in the South, particularly those reliant on commodity exports.

c1e57d849472.title: Recycling
c1e57d849472.sentence: Recycling is the process of converting waste materials into new materials and objects.

b2e6776f0727.title: Recycling
b2e6776f0727.sentence: Recycling is a key component of modern waste reduction and represents the third step in the "Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle" waste hierarchy, contributing to environmental sustainability and resource conservation.

e81e07b841b1.title: Recycling
e81e07b841b1.sentence: It is an alternative to "conventional" waste disposal that can save material and help lower greenhouse gas emissions.

fbf85f42a4a9.title: Recycling
fbf85f42a4a9.sentence: It can also prevent the waste of potentially useful materials and reduce the consumption of fresh raw materials, reducing energy use, air pollution (from incineration) and water pollution (from landfilling).

27ff411298ad.title: Recycling
27ff411298ad.sentence: In ideal implementations, recycling a material produces a fresh supply of the same material—for example, used office paper would be converted into new office paper, and used polystyrene foam into new polystyrene.

89024f6ed807.title: Recycling
89024f6ed807.sentence: Some types of materials, such as metal cans, can be remanufactured repeatedly without losing their purity.

2e8ee045a174.title: Recycling
2e8ee045a174.sentence: With other materials, this is often difficult or too expensive (compared with producing the same product from raw materials or other sources), so "recycling" of many products and materials involves their reuse in producing different materials (for example, paperboard).

df8474e09d4f.title: Recycling
df8474e09d4f.sentence: Recycling aluminium uses only 5% of the energy of virgin production.

d2e0ddff77d5.title: Recycling
d2e0ddff77d5.sentence: Steel and other metals have intrinsically higher recyclate quality; it is estimated that two-thirds of all new steel comes from recycled steel.

f3fb85326a2f.title: Recycling
f3fb85326a2f.sentence: Much of the difficulty inherent in recycling comes from the fact that most products are not designed with recycling in mind.

d0df09a77f9a.title: Recycling
d0df09a77f9a.sentence: In the USA around 6 to 7 percent of plastic is recycled.

ba0983a9e914.title: Recycling
ba0983a9e914.sentence: A considerable investment in recycling occurred in the 1970s due to rising energy costs.

e94651f4e0ff.title: Circular economy
e94651f4e0ff.sentence: Circular economy, also called circularity, is a economic system that aims to keep products, components, and materials in use at their highest value for as long as possible.

981ec3874275.title: Circular economy
981ec3874275.sentence: It is often contrasted with the linear economy, sometimes described as a “take-make-waste” model, in which resources are extracted, used, and discarded.The linear model puts great pressure on the environment through resource extraction, energy-intensive production, and large amounts of waste.

8adfcf91d439.title: Circular economy
8adfcf91d439.sentence: Extraction and processing of material resources accounts for over 55 percent of the global GHG-emissions.

c773ab912a85.title: Circular economy
c773ab912a85.sentence: In general terms, there are four ways to increase the circularity of our resource use:

17a5a85fa794.title: Circular economy
17a5a85fa794.sentence: - Narrowing the loop: using fewer resources per product or service, for example by avoiding unnecessary production or consumption (refuse) or by manufacturing more efficiently (reduce).

15e1c6de770e.title: Circular economy
15e1c6de770e.sentence: - Slowing the loop: extending the lifespan of products through reuse and repair.

98176ede878e.title: Circular economy
98176ede878e.sentence: - Closing the loop: recovering materials from waste through (preferably high-quality) recycling, so that they can be used again.

dc4c0f6beecd.title: Circular economy
dc4c0f6beecd.sentence: - Substituting inputs: replacing finite or polluting resources with renewable or less harmful materials.

c05712a9609e.title: Circular economy
c05712a9609e.sentence: In its core principle, the European Parliament defines the circular economy as "a model of production and consumption that involves sharing, leasing, reusing, repairing, refurbishing, and recycling existing materials and products as long as possible.

7ab6abe8158e.title: Circular economy
7ab6abe8158e.sentence: Global implementation of circular economy can reduce global emissions by 22.8 billion tons, equivalent to 39% of global emissions produced in 2019.

8d832988e9df.title: Circular economy
8d832988e9df.sentence: Economist Kenneth E. Boulding, in his 1966 paper "The Economics of the Coming Spaceship Earth", argued that a circular economic system is a prerequisite for the maintenance of the sustainability of human life on Earth.

53b5e5435e24.title: Circular economy
53b5e5435e24.sentence: Boulding describes the so-called "cowboy economy" as an open system in which the natural environment is typically perceived as limitless: no limit exists on the capacity of the outside to supply or receive energy and material flows.

9543f6bd31fe.title: Circular economy
9543f6bd31fe.sentence: Boulding's essay "The Economics of the Coming Spaceship Earth" is often cited as the first expression of the "circular economy", although Boulding does not use that phrase.

6e26bd19862b.title: Circular economy

a37eafac2514.sentence: The term itself is a play on the popular corporate phrase "cradle to grave", implying that the C2C model is sustainable and considerate of life and future generations—from the birth, or "cradle", of one generation to the next generation, versus from birth to death, or "grave", within the same generation.

9eb96ee7e5ab.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
9eb96ee7e5ab.sentence: It is a holistic, economic, industrial and social framework that seeks to create systems that are not only efficient but also essentially waste free.

d4f1c6bc35cf.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
d4f1c6bc35cf.sentence: Building off the whole systems approach of John T. Lyle's regenerative design, the model in its broadest sense is not limited to industrial design and manufacturing; it can be applied to many aspects of human civilization such as urban environments, buildings, economics and social systems.

81915ea5ea7d.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
81915ea5ea7d.sentence: The roof is part of an $18 million rainwater treatment system designed to clean 20 billion US gallons (76,000,000 m3) of rainwater annually.

c05a7e4e82f8.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
c05a7e4e82f8.sentence: This saved Ford $30 million that would otherwise have been spent on mechanical treatment facilities.

3621f3ac3e51.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
3621f3ac3e51.sentence: A major constraint in the optimal recycling of materials is that at civic amenity sites, products are not disassembled by hand and have each individual part sorted into a bin, but instead have the entire product sorted into a certain bin.

aedca2d5c47c.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
aedca2d5c47c.sentence: This makes the extraction of rare-earth elements and other materials uneconomical (at recycling sites, products typically get crushed after which the materials are extracted by means of magnets, chemicals, special sorting methods,...) and thus optimal recycling of, for example metals is impossible (an optimal recycling method for metals would require to sort all similar alloys together rather than mixing plain iron with alloys).

d9929764d2f3.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
d9929764d2f3.sentence: The term "Cradle to Cradle" is a registered trademark of McDonough Braungart Design Chemistry (MBDC) consultants.

f12082e0b7b8.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
f12082e0b7b8.sentence: The Cradle to Cradle Certified Products Program began as a proprietary system; however, in 2012 MBDC turned the certification over to an independent non-profit called the Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute.

8bf3f4b42c67.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
8bf3f4b42c67.sentence: McDonough and Braungart responded to this criticism by giving control of the certification protocol to a non-profit, independent Institute called the Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute.

576fcae5d1a3.title: Waste valorization
576fcae5d1a3.sentence: Waste valorization, beneficial reuse, value recovery or waste reclamation is the process of waste products or residues from an economic process being valorized (given economic value), by reuse or recycling in order to create economically useful materials.

b2476d9dedf3.title: Waste valorization
b2476d9dedf3.sentence: The term is usually applied in industrial processes where residue from creating or processing one good is used as a raw material or energy feedstock for another industrial process.

0e92791dfd3b.title: Waste valorization
0e92791dfd3b.sentence: Industrial wastes in particular are good candidates for valorization because they tend to be more consistent and predictable than other waste, such as household waste.

a299998a5b39.title: Waste valorization
a299998a5b39.sentence: Increased regulation of residual materials and socioeconomic changes, such as the introduction of ideas about sustainable development and circular economy in the 1990s and 2000s increased focus on industrial practices to recover resources as value add materials.

82f1d5771679.title: Waste valorization
82f1d5771679.sentence: Additionally, demand for the rare minerals found in tailings is increasing.

1eef944531c0.title: Waste valorization
1eef944531c0.sentence: Numerous uses of the highly alkaline substance have been proposed, among them mitigating acid mine drainage.

32c470450cc5.title: Waste valorization
32c470450cc5.sentence: There are active industrial scale applications of waste valorization using spent nuclear fuel - primarily nuclear reprocessing using the PUREX process which yields reactor grade plutonium for use in MOX-fuel as well as reprocessed uranium.

cf4a2f4a32e0.title: Remanufacturing
cf4a2f4a32e0.sentence: Remanufacturing is "the rebuilding of a product to specifications of the original manufactured product using a combination of reused, repaired and new parts".

8974f5613bc7.title: Remanufacturing
8974f5613bc7.sentence: Remanufacturing is a form of a product recovery process that differs from other recovery processes in its completeness: a remanufactured machine should match the same customer expectation as new machines.

2bfe362d6749.title: Remanufacturing
2bfe362d6749.sentence: Through a series of industrial processes in a factory environment, a discarded product is completely disassembled.

b88598ed6f2e.title: Remanufacturing
b88598ed6f2e.sentence: Useable parts are cleaned, refurbished, and put into inventory.

c3c380d0e413.title: Remanufacturing
c3c380d0e413.sentence: Then the product is reassembled from the old parts (and where necessary, new parts) to produce a unit fully equivalent and sometimes superior in performance and expected lifetime to the original new product".

82ce9af648d4.title: Remanufacturing
82ce9af648d4.sentence: The United States remanufacturing industry grew by 15% between 2009 and 2011, and in 2020 it accounted for 2% of all manufacturing in the US and 1.9% in the European Union.

59eee7fe1c9f.title: Remanufacturing
59eee7fe1c9f.sentence: There are three main types of remanufacturing activities, each with different operational challenges.

194f3cc7e2ba.title: Remanufacturing
194f3cc7e2ba.sentence: - Remanufacturing with loss of original product identity With this method, used goods are disassembled into pre-determined components and repaired to stock, ready to be reassembled into a remanufactured product.

e8a20a61b62b.title: Remanufacturing
e8a20a61b62b.sentence: This is the case when remanufacturing automobile components, photocopiers, toner and ink cartridges, furniture, ready-to-use cameras and personal computers.

6ee768caa4cc.title: Upcycling
6ee768caa4cc.sentence: Upcycling, also known as creative reuse, is the process of transforming by-products, waste materials, useless, or unwanted products into new materials or products perceived to be of greater quality, such as artistic value or environmental value.

510615c4f181.title: Upcycling
510615c4f181.sentence: Upcycling is a subset of the recycling process.

3163094bf1be.title: Upcycling
3163094bf1be.sentence: Upcycling is a process that instead adds value to a newly created product.

648d2b1c36d7.title: Upcycling
648d2b1c36d7.sentence: Downcycling, however, is an opposing recycling process that degrades waste materials into new products of lower quality.

143cb2c77a12.title: Upcycling
143cb2c77a12.sentence: Prior to the Industrial Revolution, upcycling was a common practice used to repair goods.

26c14c01ffd6.title: Upcycling
26c14c01ffd6.sentence: A linear economic model emerged that encouraged used products to be thrown away and replaced by newly produced ones.

8b94e1d5b59d.title: Upcycling
8b94e1d5b59d.sentence: This rise in consumerism resulted in a decrease of the pre-industrial upcycling practices.

1da5d49f4026.title: Upcycling
1da5d49f4026.sentence: The terms upcycling and downcycling were first used in print in an article in SalvoNEWS by Thornton Kay quoting Reiner Pilz and published in 1994.

fa7966b3826a.title: Upcycling
fa7966b3826a.sentence: Upcycling is a strategy used in the circular economy to reduce resource consumption by improving the value of products and closing material cycling through re-use.

b68735aa3f78.title: Upcycling
b68735aa3f78.sentence: The lifespan of products is extended through the repair and repurposing that upcycling drives.

5d56105c7e84.title: Upcycling
5d56105c7e84.sentence: While developing countries' practice of upcycling used goods reflects a lack of access to buy new goods, in developed countries it reflects a greater importance assigned to environmentally friendly practices.

f0c2579726d8.title: Material flow analysis
f0c2579726d8.sentence: Material flow analysis (MFA), also referred to as substance flow analysis (SFA), is an analytical method to quantify flows and stocks of materials or substances in a well-defined system.

dc13bf794230.title: Material flow analysis
dc13bf794230.sentence: It is considered a core method of industrial ecology or anthropogenic, urban, social and industrial metabolism.

7043f29f549b.title: Material flow analysis
7043f29f549b.sentence: An MFA system always consists of the system boundary, one or more processes, material flows between processes, and stocks of materials within processes.

056a65c7c9a2.title: Material flow analysis
056a65c7c9a2.sentence: Unlike economic accounting, MFA also covers non-economic waste flows, emissions to the environment, and non-market natural resources.

0edcce1625f1.title: Material flow analysis
0edcce1625f1.sentence: MFA can also be applied to a single industrial installation, for example, for tracking nutrient flows through a waste water treatment plant.

db1cca4fcc37.title: Material flow analysis
db1cca4fcc37.section: Examples of applications on different spatial and temporal scales
db1cca4fcc37.sentence: - Corporate material flow analysis, or MFA along an industrial supply chain involves a number of companies: The goal of material flow analysis within a company is to quantify and then optimize the production processes so that materials and energy are used more efficiently manner, e.g., by recycling and waste reduction.

aede4909583e.title: Material flow analysis
aede4909583e.section: Examples of applications on different spatial and temporal scales
aede4909583e.sentence: - In the life cycle of a product: The life cycle inventory, whose compilation is at the core of life cycle assessment, follows the MFA methodology as it is based on an explicit system definition and process balances.

e0f913b36d73.title: Material flow analysis
e0f913b36d73.section: Examples of applications on different spatial and temporal scales
e0f913b36d73.sentence: - MFA on a national or regional scale (also referred to as material flow accounting): In this type of study, the material exchanges between an economy and the natural environment are analyzed.

b1a711a6eab8.title: Material flow analysis
b1a711a6eab8.sentence: - The methodology of MFA was developed during the 1980s and 1990s.

7a527903bd96.title: Bioeconomy
7a527903bd96.sentence: Biobased economy, bioeconomy or biotechonomy is an economic activity involving the use of biotechnology and biomass in the production of goods, services, or energy.

7ceedf9b0803.title: Bioeconomy
7ceedf9b0803.sentence: The bioeconomy comprises those parts of the economy that use renewable biological resources from land and sea – such as crops, forests, fish, animals and micro-organisms – to produce food, health, materials, products, textiles and energy.

32185f3bc166.title: Bioeconomy
32185f3bc166.sentence: It aims to ensure food security and to promote more sustainable natural resource use as well as to reduce the dependence on non-renewable resources, e.g. fossil natural resources and minerals.

f4f9f6129dbf.title: Bioeconomy
f4f9f6129dbf.sentence: The term 'bioeconomy' became popular from the mid-2000s with its adoption by the European Union and Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development as a policy agenda and framework to promote the use of biotechnology to develop new products, markets, and uses of biomass.

7d9bc1c1ae74.title: Bioeconomy
7d9bc1c1ae74.sentence: Since then, both the EU (2012) and OECD (2006) have created dedicated bioeconomy strategies, as have an increasing number of countries around the world.

c83bf5facb5f.title: Bioeconomy
c83bf5facb5f.sentence: The product of bioeconomy are typically food, feed and other biobased products, bioenergy and services based on biological resources.

4bec2afc17ff.title: Bioeconomy
4bec2afc17ff.section: Issues > Degrowth, green growth and circular economy
4bec2afc17ff.sentence: The bioeconomy has largely been associated with visions of "green growth".

3340cf808525.title: Bioeconomy

3340cf808525.sentence: However, some are concerned that with a focus or reliance on technological progress a fundamentally unsustainable socioeconomic model might be maintained rather than be changed.

f503a8a6eab4.sentence: Some are concerned it that may not lead to an ecologization of the economy but to an economization of the biological, "the living" and caution that potentials of non-bio-based techniques to achieve greater sustainability need to be considered.

9cbb39ddbf52.sentence: The three main categories of collection are drop-off centers, buy-back centers and curbside collection.

56ce9609f78b.title: Recycling
56ce9609f78b.sentence: A number of systems have been implemented to collect recyclates from the general waste stream, occupying different places on the spectrum of trade-off between public convenience and government ease and expense.

b07f6aeba425.title: Recycling

b07f6aeba425.sentence: At buy-back centers, separated, cleaned recyclates are purchased, providing a clear incentive for use and creating a stable supply.

015ab57bd96c.title: Recycling

14a0d89bb92a.sentence: Source separation is the other extreme, where each material is cleaned and sorted prior to collection.

0e3f497f18bd.title: Recycling
0e3f497f18bd.section: Recycling consumer waste > Collection > Curbside collection > Source separation
0e3f497f18bd.sentence: It requires the least post-collection sorting and produces the purest recyclates.

f4722178bd16.title: Recycling
f4722178bd16.sentence: For a recycling program to work, a large, stable supply of recyclable material is crucial.

2659856abc31.title: Recycling
2659856abc31.sentence: Four forms of legislation have also been used to increase and maintain the demand for recycled materials: minimum recycled content mandates, utilization rates, procurement policies, and recycled product labeling.

1e4cb383c171.title: Recycling
1e4cb383c171.sentence: Three legislative options have been used to create such supplies: mandatory recycling collection, container deposit legislation, and refuse bans.

b20ef8662d4e.title: Recycling
b20ef8662d4e.sentence: Content mandates specify that a certain percentage of a new product must consist of recycled material.

4888d9c8dacc.title: Recycling
4888d9c8dacc.sentence: Recycling is commonly categorized into different types based on the process used and the final output:

4badc0b302b0.title: Recycling
4badc0b302b0.sentence: - Mechanical recycling: Physical processing of materials such as shredding, melting, and reforming (commonly used for plastics and metals).

fe3d0bf6d962.title: Recycling
fe3d0bf6d962.sentence: - Chemical recycling: Breaking down materials into their chemical components for reuse in manufacturing.

7c3f5b61c91e.title: Recycling
7c3f5b61c91e.sentence: - Closed-loop recycling: Materials are recycled into the same product without significant loss of quality.

4be48004a1da.title: Recycling
4be48004a1da.sentence: - Open-loop recycling: Materials are recycled into different products, often with reduced quality (also known as downcycling).

990bf6625600.title: Recycling
990bf6625600.sentence: Closed-loop recycling is generally regarded as more sustainable as it minimizes resource loss.

ada2d265c326.title: Circular economy
ada2d265c326.section: Circular developments around the world > Circular bio-economy
ada2d265c326.sentence: The bio-economy, especially the circular bio-economy, decreases dependency on natural resources by encouraging sustainable goods that generate food, materials, and energy using renewable biological resources (such as lupins).

8cea780ba033.title: Circular economy
8cea780ba033.section: Circular developments around the world > Circular bio-economy
8cea780ba033.sentence: According to the European Commission's EU Science Center, the circular bio-economy produces €1.5 trillion in value added, accounting for 11% of EU GDP.

6453153e0fcd.sentence: In 2024 and 2025, the committee published a series of four new ISO standards:

5f2247b18c2a.title: Pay as you throw
5f2247b18c2a.sentence: Pay as you throw (PAYT) (also called trash metering, unit pricing, variable rate pricing, or user-pay) is a usage-pricing model for disposing of municipal solid waste.

033781f2d615.title: Pay as you throw
033781f2d615.sentence: Users are charged a rate based on how much waste they present for collection to the municipality or local authority.

9891ed09ad81.title: Pay as you throw
9891ed09ad81.sentence: All users pay the same flat rate or tax regardless of how much waste they present for pickup.

f308ecd39c83.title: Pay as you throw
f308ecd39c83.sentence: Under the flat-rate system there is no incentive to reduce waste produced.

6a179cbcc7ca.title: Pay as you throw
6a179cbcc7ca.sentence: PAYT is based on two guiding principles of environmental policy: the polluter pays principle and the shared responsibility concept.

2df50f7b9db7.title: Pay as you throw
2df50f7b9db7.sentence: Waste can be measured by weight or size, or by unit counts, identified using different types of bags, tags, containers or even RFID.

5a759b8fd860.title: Pay as you throw
5a759b8fd860.sentence: Services for waste diversion, like recycling and composting, are often provided free of charge where pay-as-you-throw systems are implemented.

0c08e838224f.title: Pay as you throw
0c08e838224f.sentence: PAYT programs resulted in residential waste declining from 9 - 38% and increased recycling from 6 – 40%.

267633ad0b7d.title: Pay as you throw
267633ad0b7d.sentence: For example, a study conducted in Ferrara, Italy discovered that the implementation of the PAYT policy lead to a 30% overall reduction in waste production.

1620f901a40f.title: Pay as you throw
1620f901a40f.sentence: Furthermore accompanying this, it was discovered that there was also a 40% increase in recycling uptake.

f2b11c01bb68.title: Pay as you throw
f2b11c01bb68.sentence: Charging for waste often results in illegal dumping (also known as "fly-tipping") or the waste being passed to unlicensed or illegal disposal methods.

6c526b06bb59.title: Pay as you throw
6c526b06bb59.sentence: Studies have found that unit pricing, which involves charging a set price per bag of garbage thrown out, contribute to illegal dumping.

2f2842901645.title: Product-service system
2f2842901645.sentence: Product-service systems (PSS) are business models that provide for cohesive delivery of products and services.

7c0f5dbdf87d.title: Product-service system
7c0f5dbdf87d.sentence: As defined by van Halen, te Riele, Goedkoop "a marketable set of products and services capable of jointly fulfilling a user's needs", PSS can be realized by smart products.

f1a685beb0e1.title: Product-service system
f1a685beb0e1.sentence: The concept is based on the idea that what customers want from products is not necessarily ownership, but rather the function that the product provides or the service the product can deliver.

24020c905ad4.title: Product-service system
24020c905ad4.sentence: This means that the provider of "servicizing solutions" may get paid by the unit-of-service (or product function) delivered, as opposed to the (more traditional) unit-of-products sold.

1eaf4a4639dc.title: Product-service system
1eaf4a4639dc.sentence: This research has identified three classes of PSS:

a33d71bc8c10.title: Product-service system
a33d71bc8c10.sentence: - Product Oriented PSS: This is a PSS where ownership of the tangible product is transferred to the consumer, but additional services, such as maintenance contracts, are provided.

8aa64726ac9c.title: Product-service system
8aa64726ac9c.sentence: - Use Oriented PSS: This is a PSS where ownership of the tangible product is retained by the service provider, who sells the functions of the product, via modified distribution and payment systems, such as sharing, pooling, and leasing.

0ff30a206cd2.title: Product-service system
0ff30a206cd2.sentence: - Result Oriented PSS: This is a PSS where products are replaced by services, such as, for example, voicemail replacing answering machines.

8ccf5f616374.title: Product-service system
8ccf5f616374.sentence: - Xerox' pay-per-copy model for selling office equipment

c15e4fac4b4b.title: Product-service system
c15e4fac4b4b.sentence: - Philips' pay-per-lux model for selling lighting equipment, whereby customers pay for a promised level of illuminance in a building

b736ac4352e6.title: Product-service system
b736ac4352e6.sentence: While not all product service systems result in the reduction of material consumption, they are more widely being recognized as an important part of a firm's environmental strategy.

ae0f0481b3ab.title: Product-service system
ae0f0481b3ab.sentence: The Product-Service System (PSS) concept was first developed at the Politecnico di Milano between 1993 and 1996 by Francesco Mauri and Gianluca Brugnoli while they were studying how Design integrates with business strategy.

ae56116d1d0b.title: Product-service system
ae56116d1d0b.sentence: Several authors assert that product service systems will improve eco-efficiency by what is termed "factor 4", i.e. an improvement by a factor of 4 times or more, by enabling new and radical ways of transforming what they call the "product-service mix" that satisfy consumer demands while also improving the effects upon the environment.

19c9415114b6.title: Biorefinery

d4fa61b0e1fb.title: Biorefinery
d4fa61b0e1fb.sentence: As refineries, biorefineries can provide multiple chemicals by fractioning an initial raw material (biomass) into multiple intermediates (carbohydrates, proteins, triglycerides) that can be further converted into value-added products.

1b82d3492572.title: Biorefinery

c9efbff90995.title: Biorefinery

6a1f2f190b9f.sentence: Right to repair is a legal right for owners of devices and equipment to freely maintain, repair, or modify products such as automobiles, electronics, and farm equipment.

ba4abfb87912.title: Right to repair
ba4abfb87912.sentence: Common obstacles to repair include requirements to use only the manufacturer's maintenance services, restrictions on access to tools and components, and software barriers.

4a33b7f28197.title: Right to repair
4a33b7f28197.sentence: These obstacles represent a repair monopoly, an aftermarket monopoly where a company controls the market for repairing and maintaining their products, making it difficult or even impossible for anyone to fix them.

fd369c27e88d.title: Right to repair
fd369c27e88d.sentence: Repair monopolies have been found to lead to higher prices, increased delays, reduced serviceability, and less choice for consumers.

2dadaa4daffd.title: Right to repair
2dadaa4daffd.sentence: Some goals of the right to repair are to favor repair instead of replacement, and make such repairs more affordable leading to a more sustainable economy and reduction in electronic waste.

2d0f4219d563.title: Right to repair
2d0f4219d563.sentence: While initially driven mostly by automotive consumer protection agencies and the automotive after sales service industry, the discussion about establishing a right to repair, not only for vehicles but for any kind of electronic product, gained traction as consumer electronics such as smartphones and computers became universally available, causing broken and used electronics items to become the fastest growing waste stream.

8dbde04aad0f.title: Right to repair
8dbde04aad0f.sentence: Adopted on May 30, 2024, the European Union's Right to Repair Directive (R2RD) requires manufacturers to offer repair services that are both efficient and affordable, while also making sure consumers are aware of their repair rights.

78fb7296d01f.title: Right to repair
78fb7296d01f.sentence: On November 7, 2024, Bill C-244 received royal assent and became law, making Canada the first country to enact a national right-to-repair law.

858c8e22a8d0.title: Microplastics
858c8e22a8d0.sentence: Microplastics are "synthetic solid particulate matter or polymeric matrices, with regular or irregular shape and with size ranging from 1 μm to 5 mm, of either primary or secondary manufacturing origin, which are insoluble in water." Microplastics cause pollution by entering natural ecosystems from a variety of sources, including cosmetics, clothing, construction, renovation, food packaging, and industrial processes.

a98453674cf3.title: Microplastics
a98453674cf3.sentence: Primary microplastics include any plastic fragments or particles that are already 5 mm in size or less before entering the environment.

53242e305862.title: Microplastics
53242e305862.sentence: These include microfibers from clothing, microbeads, plastic glitter and plastic pellets (also known as nurdles).

402972b91cf9.title: Microplastics
402972b91cf9.sentence: Secondary microplastics arise from the degradation (breakdown) of larger plastic products through natural weathering processes after entering the environment.

77aacd5ec662.title: Microplastics
77aacd5ec662.sentence: It is estimated that by 2050, the weight of microplastics in the sea will exceed that of the fish.

9243e743cb33.title: Microplastics
9243e743cb33.sentence: Because some plastics degrade slowly (often over hundreds to thousands of years), microplastics have a high probability of ingestion, incorporation into, and accumulation in the bodies and tissues of many organisms.

dcd5a98e7619.title: Resource recovery
dcd5a98e7619.sentence: For example, organic materials can be treated by composting and anaerobic digestion and turned into energy, compost or fertilizer.

e4639d1e0f27.title: Resource recovery
e4639d1e0f27.sentence: Disposed materials that are organic in nature, such as plant material, food scraps, and paper products, can be recycled using biological composting and digestion processes to decompose the organic matter.

838f0cfdacac.title: Resource recovery
838f0cfdacac.sentence: In addition, waste gas from the process (such as methane) can be captured and used for generating electricity and heat (CHP/cogeneration) maximising efficiencies.

b7389732d744.title: Resource recovery
b7389732d744.sentence: Anaerobic digestion of the organic fraction of municipal solid waste (MSW) has been found to be more environmentally effective, than landfill, incineration or pyrolysis.

5a5eaa10d8f5.title: Resource recovery
5a5eaa10d8f5.section: Sources of recovery > Wastewater and excreta
5a5eaa10d8f5.sentence: Valuable resources can be recovered from wastewater, sewage sludge, fecal sludge and human excreta.

99aa9a630843.title: Resource recovery
99aa9a630843.section: Sources of recovery > Wastewater and excreta
99aa9a630843.sentence: These include water, energy, and fertilizing nutrients nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, as well as micro-nutrients such as sulphur and organic matter.

d73a5a250f8a.title: Resource recovery
d73a5a250f8a.section: Sources of recovery > Wastewater and excreta
d73a5a250f8a.sentence: Originally, wastewater systems were designed only to remove excreta and wastewater from urban areas.

423e241d9d2a.title: Resource recovery
423e241d9d2a.section: Sources of recovery > Wastewater and excreta
423e241d9d2a.sentence: Since the 1970s, there has been increasing interest in treating the wastewater to protect the environment, and efforts focused primarily on cleaning the water at the end of the pipe.

bd3a2b4ad1d0.title: Resource recovery
bd3a2b4ad1d0.section: Sources of recovery > Wastewater and excreta
bd3a2b4ad1d0.sentence: Since around the year 2003, the concepts of ecological sanitation and sustainable sanitation have emerged with the focus on recovering resources from wastewater.

40bbc5ad69d8.title: Reuse
40bbc5ad69d8.section: Business models providing opportunities > Reuse of waste water and excreta in agriculture
40bbc5ad69d8.sentence: The nutrients, i.e. nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and micronutrients, and organic matter contained in wastewater, excreta (urine and feces) and greywater have traditionally been reused in agriculture in many countries and are still being reused in agriculture to this day - unfortunately often in an unregulated and unsafe manner.

c2c3d1fd5457.title: Reuse
c2c3d1fd5457.section: Business models providing opportunities > Reuse of waste water and excreta in agriculture
c2c3d1fd5457.sentence: The WHO Guidelines from 2006 have set up a framework how this reuse can be done safely by following a multiple barrier approach.

f133c007b0cb.title: Zero waste
f133c007b0cb.section: How to achieve > Zero Waste Hierarchy
f133c007b0cb.sentence: The Zero Waste Hierarchy describes a progression of policies and strategies to support the zero-waste system, from highest and best to lowest use of materials.

edfbaf08b051.title: Zero waste
edfbaf08b051.section: How to achieve > Zero Waste Hierarchy
edfbaf08b051.sentence: It aims to provide more depth to the internationally recognized 3Rs (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle); to encourage policy, activity and investment at the top of the hierarchy; and to provide a guide for those who wish to develop systems or products that move us closer to zero waste.

833311956a81.title: Zero waste
833311956a81.section: How to achieve > Zero Waste Hierarchy
833311956a81.sentence: It is designed to be applicable to all audiences, from policymakers to industry and the individual.

aa09c6bdb09e.title: Zero waste
aa09c6bdb09e.section: How to achieve > Zero Waste Hierarchy
aa09c6bdb09e.sentence: It enhances the zero-waste definition by providing guidance for planning and a way to evaluate proposed solutions.

dd768761bcfb.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
dd768761bcfb.sentence: Initially defined by McDonough and Braungart, the Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute's five certification criteria are:

e9032604ac0f.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
e9032604ac0f.sentence: - Material health, which involves identifying the chemical composition of the materials that make up the product.

02c893d1ca60.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
02c893d1ca60.sentence: - Material reutilization, which is about recovery and recycling at the end of product life.

05bc3ac7b46a.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
05bc3ac7b46a.sentence: The risk for each material is assessed against criteria and eventually ranked on a scale with green being materials of low risk, yellow being those with moderate risk but are acceptable to continue to use, red for materials that have high risk and need to be phased out, and grey for materials with incomplete data.

89fa05d8cf79.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
89fa05d8cf79.sentence: - Downcycling is the reuse of materials into lesser products.

818a12b5ac5c.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
818a12b5ac5c.sentence: For example, a plastic computer case could be downcycled into a plastic cup, which then becomes a park bench, etc.; this eventually leads to plastic waste.

6c15828f23ea.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
6c15828f23ea.sentence: In this manner these materials can be used over and over again instead of being "downcycled" into lesser products, ultimately becoming waste.

291c534c254e.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
291c534c254e.sentence: In the cradle-to-cradle model, all materials used in industrial or commercial processes—such as metals, fibers, dyes—fall into one of two categories: "technical" or "biological" nutrients.

c9391caa8f0f.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
c9391caa8f0f.sentence: - Technical nutrients are strictly limited to non-toxic, non-harmful synthetic materials that have no negative effects on the natural environment; they can be used in continuous cycles as the same product without losing their integrity or quality.

cbb73c340e88.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
cbb73c340e88.sentence: - Technical nutrients are basically inorganic or synthetic materials manufactured by humans—such as plastics and metals—that can be used many times over without any loss in quality, staying in a continuous cycle.

b70ea42c0dd9.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
b70ea42c0dd9.sentence: - Biological nutrients are organic materials that, once used, can be disposed of in any natural environment and decompose into the soil, providing food for small life forms without affecting the natural environment.

27d79274a629.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
27d79274a629.sentence: The sole might be made of "biological nutrients" while the upper parts might be made of "technical nutrients".

94c3a490ddd0.title: Cradle-to-cradle design
94c3a490ddd0.sentence: When the manufacturer separates the sole from the upper parts (separating the technical and biological nutrients), the biological nutrients are returned to the natural environment while the technical nutrients can be used to create the sole of another shoe.

80e97c5d42e0.title: Life cycle thinking
80e97c5d42e0.sentence: Life cycle thinking is an approach that emphasizes the assessment and minimization of environmental impacts at all stages of a product's life.

4f5190bce3f1.title: Life cycle thinking
4f5190bce3f1.sentence: This concept seeks to avoid shifting environmental burdens from one stage of the product's life to another.

096fde02a5c4.title: Life cycle thinking
096fde02a5c4.sentence: An important component is the avoidance of burden shifting, which ensures that improvements in one stage are not achieved at the expense of another stage.

97d1b76add04.title: Life cycle thinking
97d1b76add04.sentence: Corporations utilize this approach in the creation of environmentally friendly products.

481cf4faa86c.title: Life cycle thinking
481cf4faa86c.sentence: Consumers apply it in their mindful choices of products, and governments incorporate it into regulatory frameworks aimed at lessening environmental impacts.

e0528ec57192.title: Life cycle thinking
e0528ec57192.sentence: Life-cycle assessment (LCA or life cycle analysis) is a technique used to assess potential environmental impacts of a product at different stages of its life.

c6bc139b8737.title: Life cycle thinking
c6bc139b8737.sentence: Life cycle management is a business approach to managing the total life cycle of products and services.

2d7f2b062831.title: Life cycle thinking
2d7f2b062831.sentence: Life cycle costing (or life cycle cost analysis) is the total cost analysis of a process or system.

d8d69868fd6f.title: Life cycle thinking
d8d69868fd6f.sentence: Design for the Environment Program (DfE) was created in 1992 by the United States Environmental Protection Agency and works to prevent pollution and reduce the risks pollution presents to humans and the environment.

d41577829063.title: Life cycle thinking
d41577829063.sentence: Product service systems (PSS) are sets of marketable products and services that work together to fulfill a user's needs.

12a5f267d76b.title: Life cycle thinking
12a5f267d76b.sentence: Integrated product policy works to minimize environmental degradation caused by products by looking at all phases of a product's life cycle to pinpoint where taking action is most effective.

1283f13e3aae.title: Life cycle thinking
1283f13e3aae.sentence: This technique takes a "cradle-to-grave" or a "cradle-to-cradle" approach and looks at environmental impacts that occur throughout the lifetime of a product from raw material extraction, manufacturing and processing, distribution, use, repair and maintenance, disposal, and recycling.

0c555ff250c7.title: Waste hierarchy
0c555ff250c7.sentence: The European Union Waste Framework Directive has introduced the concept of life-cycle thinking into waste policies.

8ba6b84d9140.title: Eco-efficiency
8ba6b84d9140.sentence: Eco-efficiency refers to the delivery of goods and services to meet human needs and improve quality of life while progressively reducing their environmental impacts of goods and resource intensity during their life-cycle.

3fb8b1bbbde8.title: Eco-efficiency
3fb8b1bbbde8.sentence: It is based on the concept of creating more goods and services while using fewer resources and creating less waste and pollution.

03b378a747a2.title: Eco-efficiency
03b378a747a2.sentence: "It is measured as the ratio between the (added) value of what has been produced (e.g. GDP) and the (added) environment impacts of the product or service (e.g. CO2 emissions)." The term was coined by the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD) in its 1992 publication "Changing Course".

3d5a4a67af6c.title: Eco-efficiency
3d5a4a67af6c.sentence: At the 1992 Earth Summit, eco-efficiency was endorsed as a new business concept and means for companies to implement Agenda 21 in the private sector.

837bc8cca0ad.title: Eco-efficiency
837bc8cca0ad.sentence: According to Boulanger, all versions of eco-efficiency share four key characteristics:

9ba45a4f14d2.title: Eco-efficiency
9ba45a4f14d2.sentence: - Confidence in technological innovation as the main solution to un-sustainability;

e1fa88dd56e2.title: Eco-efficiency
e1fa88dd56e2.sentence: - Reliance on business as the principal actor of transformation.

5a836eb99a8c.title: Eco-efficiency
5a836eb99a8c.sentence: - Trust in markets (if they are functioning well);

e4372b7315ae.title: Eco-efficiency
e4372b7315ae.sentence: - "Growthphilia": the idea that there is nothing wrong with growth as such.

48ecd7fc1a36.title: Eco-efficiency
48ecd7fc1a36.sentence: The view that improvements in eco-efficiency are sufficient for achieving sustainability has been challenged by Huesemann and Huesemann, who demonstrate using extensive historical evidence that increases in technological efficiency have not reduced overall resource use and pollution.

a8d3a1e5da62.title: Product stewardship
a8d3a1e5da62.sentence: Product stewardship is an approach to managing the environmental impacts of different products and materials and at different stages in their production, use and disposal.

ce6fa18ac28f.title: Product stewardship
ce6fa18ac28f.sentence: It acknowledges that those involved in producing, purchasing, selling, using and disposing of products have a shared responsibility to ensure that those products or materials are managed in a way that reduces their impact, throughout their lifecycle, on the environment and on human health and safety.

d4272a7cb627.title: Product stewardship
d4272a7cb627.sentence: For manufacturers, this responsibility includes planning for, and if necessary, paying for the recycling or disposal of the product at the end of its useful life.

7ccbc796b4a8.title: Product stewardship
7ccbc796b4a8.sentence: This may be achieved, in part, by redesigning products to use fewer harmful substances, to be more durable, reusable and recyclable, and by making products from recycled materials.

8a3e133dfc06.title: Product stewardship
8a3e133dfc06.sentence: While both concepts bring the onus of waste management for end-of-life products from the government to the manufacturers, Product stewardship further extends this responsibility to everyone involved in the life-cycle of the product: not only manufacturers, but also retailers, consumers and recyclers.

31604117851c.title: Product stewardship
31604117851c.sentence: Australia's Product Stewardship Act 2011 provides a framework for managing the environmental, health and safety impacts of products, and in particular those impacts associated with the disposal of products and their associated waste.

e79fc311c3cb.title: Product stewardship
e79fc311c3cb.sentence: The framework includes voluntary, co-regulatory and mandatory product stewardship.

8582b33ffe96.title: Product stewardship
8582b33ffe96.sentence: The scheme has recycled approximately 230,000 tonnes of electronic waste since its inception.

ff1628a44c8a.title: Product stewardship
ff1628a44c8a.sentence: One familiar example is the container-deposit legislation.

dcae4bef2f5a.title: Product stewardship
dcae4bef2f5a.sentence: A fee is paid to buy the bottle, separately from the fee to buy what it contains.

a1afe18b091e.title: Product stewardship
a1afe18b091e.sentence: If the bottle is returned, the fee is returned, and the supplier must return the bottle for re-use or recycling.

139f1bea6f33.title: Product stewardship
139f1bea6f33.sentence: If not, the collected fee can be used to pay for landfill or litter control measures.

1da2435222b0.title: Product stewardship
1da2435222b0.sentence: Also, since the same fee can be collected by anyone finding and returning the bottle, it is common for people to collect these and return them as a means of surviving: this is quite common, for instance, among homeless people in U.S. cities.

3f392a6d12e9.title: Product stewardship
3f392a6d12e9.sentence: However, the principle is applied very broadly beyond bottles to paint and automobile parts such as tires.

e6fba0064f9f.title: Product stewardship
e6fba0064f9f.sentence: When purchasing paint or tires in many places, one simultaneously pays for the disposal of the toxic waste they become.

200d4e95a667.title: Industrial symbiosis
200d4e95a667.sentence: Industrial symbiosis is a subset of industrial ecology, with a particular focus on material and energy exchange.

3a0f9bbe7b3a.title: Industrial symbiosis
3a0f9bbe7b3a.sentence: Industrial symbiosis engages traditionally separate industries in a collective approach to competitive advantage involving physical exchange of materials, energy, water, and/or by-products.

15fec4b3c8bd.title: Industrial symbiosis
15fec4b3c8bd.sentence: Industrial symbiosis systems collectively optimize material and energy use at efficiencies beyond those achievable by any individual process alone.

c4efe7153d4b.title: Industrial symbiosis
c4efe7153d4b.sentence: The keys to industrial symbiosis are collaboration and the synergistic possibilities offered by geographic proximity".

0bc458fb51c6.title: Industrial symbiosis
0bc458fb51c6.sentence: Although geographic proximity is often associated with industrial symbiosis, it is neither necessary nor sufficient—nor is a singular focus on physical resource exchange.

a7200a5d004b.title: Industrial ecology
a7200a5d004b.sentence: The Kalundborg industrial park is located in Denmark.

afcd59bc6024.title: Industrial ecology
afcd59bc6024.sentence: For example, the Energy E2 Asnæs Power Station produces gypsum as a by-product of electricity generation; this gypsum becomes a resource for BPB Gyproc A/S which produces plasterboards.

fb3d3ee3eb9b.title: Industrial symbiosis
fb3d3ee3eb9b.sentence: IS systems such as the web of materials and energy exchanges among companies in Kalundborg, Denmark have spontaneously evolved from a series of micro innovations over a long time scale; however, the engineered design and implementation of such systems from a macro planner's perspective, on a relatively short time scale, proves challenging.

9afd0c9a831d.title: Industrial symbiosis
9afd0c9a831d.sentence: Often, access to information on available by-products is difficult to obtain.

71fce73719c5.title: Industrial symbiosis
71fce73719c5.sentence: These by-products are considered waste and typically not traded or listed on any type of exchange.

9913284ff5b9.title: Industrial symbiosis
9913284ff5b9.sentence: In practice, using industrial symbiosis as an approach to commercial operations—using, recovering and redirecting resources for reuse—results in resources remaining in productive use in the economy for longer.

b614c231aa58.title: Industrial symbiosis
b614c231aa58.sentence: This in turn creates business opportunities, reduces demands on the earth's resources, and provides a stepping-stone towards creating a circular economy.

994bfce21a76.title: Sustainable city
994bfce21a76.sentence: The United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) defines eco-industrial park as a community of businesses located on a common property in which businesses seek to achieve enhanced environmental, economic, and social performance through collaboration in managing environmental and resource issues.

6c93d3f72906.title: Sustainable city
6c93d3f72906.sentence: This is an industrial symbiosis where companies gain an added benefit by physically exchanging materials, energy, water, and by-products, thus enabling sustainable development.

01b4a4535425.title: Eco-industrial development
01b4a4535425.sentence: Industrial Symbiosis often becomes manifest in Eco-industrial parks.

7cd35ce2ebc1.title: Sustainable city
7cd35ce2ebc1.sentence: In terms of material flows, the companies in an eco-industrial park may have common waste treatment facilities, a means for transporting by-products from one plant to another, or anchoring the park around resource recovery companies that are recruited to the location or started from scratch.

7858d641b9a0.title: Sustainable city
7858d641b9a0.sentence: To create more efficient water flows in industrial parks, the processed water from one plant can be reused by another plant and the park's infrastructure can include a way to collect and reuse stormwater runoff.

815d4fdfcd61.title: Waste valorization
815d4fdfcd61.sentence: Transforming food waste into either food products, feed products, or converting it to or extracting food or feed ingredients is termed food waste valorisation.

44a22920e78e.title: Waste valorization
44a22920e78e.sentence: One of the more fruitful fields of work is food waste—when deposited in landfills, food waste produces the greenhouse gas methane and other toxic compounds that can be dangerous to humans and local ecosystems.

5b23563a4f1a.title: Waste valorization
5b23563a4f1a.sentence: Food wastes have been demonstrated to be valuable bioresources that can be utilised to obtain a number of useful products, including biofertilizers, bioplastics, biofuels, chemicals, and nutraceuticals.

46efb8818830.title: Waste valorization
46efb8818830.sentence: There is much potential to recycle food wastes by conversion to insect protein.

b9507e11c2e5.title: Upcycling
b9507e11c2e5.sentence: Approximately 30% of the food livestock consumes, in total, comes from food waste in the supply chain, or crops that are grown and processed.

c446fece353c.sentence: They comprise a whole family of materials with different properties and applications.

462496866622.sentence: Some bioplastics (based on polyhydroxylbutyrate or polyhydroxylalkanoates) are produced from sugar using genetically modified microbes.

cb58212f7443.title: Industrial ecology
cb58212f7443.sentence: - Biodegradable plastic created from polymerized chicken feathers, which are 90% keratin and account for over 6 million tons of waste in the EU and US annually.

5f35a018a3f8.section: Fields > Energy > Getting the most out of the biomass

09a064af9d36.sentence: This pattern depends on the types of biomass used.
