ec64c4287774.sentence: The whole of finding the most suitable pattern is known as biorefining.

3a0b15e76ec8.title: Waste hierarchy
3a0b15e76ec8.sentence: Source reduction involves efforts to reduce hazardous waste and other materials by modifying industrial production.

21166aab0c77.title: Waste hierarchy
21166aab0c77.sentence: Source reduction methods involve changes in manufacturing technology, raw material inputs, and product formulation.

2242e10bdd8e.title: Waste hierarchy
2242e10bdd8e.sentence: At times, the term "pollution prevention" may refer to source reduction.

a0ecb16e02b3.title: Waste hierarchy
a0ecb16e02b3.sentence: Toxics use reduction is a more controversial approach to source reduction that targets and measures reductions in the upstream use of toxic materials.

39e707d1fcc9.title: Waste hierarchy
39e707d1fcc9.sentence: Toxic use reduction emphasizes the more preventive aspects of source reduction but, due to its emphasis on toxic chemical inputs, has been opposed more vigorously by chemical manufacturers.

3dceb0b8da6b.title: Product-service system
3dceb0b8da6b.sentence: "Product Servitization" is a transaction through which value is provided by a combination of products and services in which the satisfaction of customer needs is achieved either by selling the function of the product rather than the product itself, by increasing the service component of a product offer, or by selling the output generated by the product.

d4ed80c359da.title: Product-service system
d4ed80c359da.sentence: This servicized purchase extends the buying transaction from a one-time sale (product acquisition), to a long-term service relationship (such as in the case of a long-term maintenance-free service contract).

342cca1189e8.title: Product-service system
342cca1189e8.sentence: Another type of servicizing may be a strategy for providing access to services for people who cannot afford to buy products outright.

2d63b64797f8.title: Product-service system
2d63b64797f8.sentence: For example, in the case where auto ownership is economically unfeasible, creative servicizing offers at least three possible solutions: one in which transportation can be achieved simultaneously (as in car-pooling); one in which transportation can be achieved sequentially (as in car-sharing); and one in which transportation can be achieved eventually (rent-to-own).

30478f2a6bc9.title: Sustainable materials management
30478f2a6bc9.sentence: Sustainable Materials Management is a systemic approach to using and reusing materials more productively over their entire lifecycles.

9c4986980e97.title: Sustainable materials management
9c4986980e97.sentence: According to the Annex to the G7 Leaders’ June 8, 2015 Declaration, global raw material use rose during the 20th century at about twice the rate of population growth.

6a7c5f8e6646.title: Sustainable materials management
6a7c5f8e6646.sentence: For every 1 percent increase in gross domestic product, raw material use has risen by 0.4 percent.

398ffeb06448.title: Sustainable materials management
398ffeb06448.section: Introduction > Differences between Waste Management and SMM
398ffeb06448.sentence: - SMM focuses on the entire lifecycle of materials and products while waste management focuses on just the end-of life management of waste products

19b7fe3fb5a9.title: Sustainable materials management
19b7fe3fb5a9.section: Introduction > Differences between Waste Management and SMM
19b7fe3fb5a9.sentence: - SMM considers all industries and consumers associated with the lifecycle of a material and product as a responsible party where as waste management only considers the generators of the waste as the responsible party

4a8e59a9c33e.title: Sustainable materials management
4a8e59a9c33e.sentence: SMM has been adopted as a regulatory approach to manage materials by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and many other governments around the world.

79f626b7d557.title: Sustainable materials management
79f626b7d557.section: Implementing SMM Globally > The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD)
79f626b7d557.sentence: In 2012, the OECD put out a Green Growth Policy Brief on Sustainable Materials Management.

a4198da39843.title: Sustainable materials management
a4198da39843.sentence: Traditional patterns of material consumption in the United States follow a Cradle-to-Grave pattern of raw material extraction, product manufacturing, distribution to consumers, use by consumers, and disposal; coined by The Story of Stuff author Annie Leonard as the "take-make-waste" linear economy and commonly referred to as the throw-away society, these familiar waste management practices are being revised to bring about sustainable management of resources.

238e8574a45c.title: Circular economy
238e8574a45c.section: Sustainability > Moving away from the linear model
238e8574a45c.sentence: Linear "take, make, dispose" industrial processes, and the lifestyles dependent on them, use up finite reserves to create products with a finite lifespan, which end up in landfills or in incinerators.

9960fae20738.title: Circular fashion
9960fae20738.sentence: It involves moving away from the traditional linear model of take-make-use-and-dispose towards a circular model of reduce-reuse-recycle-and-regenerate.

50deb78a0f0c.title: Sustainable materials management
50deb78a0f0c.sentence: The U.Ks Waste and Resource Action Programme (WRAP) defines the Circular Economy as being an alternative to the traditional take, make, waste economy to one that keeps resources in use as long as possible, extracts the maximum value from the materials while they are in use, then recovers the materials to generate new products at the end of the service life.

1dfbf431cb79.title: Life cycle thinking
1dfbf431cb79.sentence: Integrated policy measures used to act upon recommendations include economic instruments, substance bans, voluntary agreements, environmental labeling, and product design guidelines; the use of a variety of tools, rather than a single policy measure, is a central feature of an integrated approach.

352ff290d976.title: Life cycle thinking
352ff290d976.sentence: The European Commission issued a green paper on IPP on 7 February 2001.

af7dce5ad523.title: Life cycle thinking
af7dce5ad523.sentence: This includes costs incurred over the life of the system and is frequently used to find the most cost-effective means for providing goods and services.

7b2e9aae2656.title: Life cycle thinking
7b2e9aae2656.sentence: This applies to life cycle thinking because it involves looking at the life-cycle cost of a product (i.e. maintenance and storage costs) for a consumer and reducing that cost by providing services with the purchased good.

50ba1c437734.title: Life cycle thinking
50ba1c437734.sentence: If more individuals practiced life cycle thinking when looking for new materials or methods, they would be more aware of how the environmental cost of ownership of products can be influenced by the running costs of energy and consumables.

6b0beb801e64.title: Circular fashion
6b0beb801e64.sentence: Circular fashion is an application of circular economy to the fashion industry, where the life cycles of fashion products are extended.

6147bb47c4c4.title: Circular fashion
6147bb47c4c4.sentence: The aim is to create a closed-loop system where clothing items are designed, produced, used, and then recycled or repurposed in a way that minimizes waste and reduces the environmental impact of the fashion industry.

dc2e232d62a9.title: Circular fashion
dc2e232d62a9.sentence: According to the definition of The European Parliament, this involves "sharing, leasing, reusing, repairing, refurbishing and recycling existing materials and products as long as possible." As suggested by The European Commission report, circular fashion encompasses a range of practices and strategies such as designing clothes for longevity, using sustainable materials, implementing recycling programs, and promoting secondhand markets.

84c347a887da.title: Circular fashion
84c347a887da.sentence: Pioneering work and terminology on circular fashion reached the mainstream through a 2017 report by the Ellen MacArthur Foundation titled "A New Textiles Economy: Redesigning Fashion's Future".

de8d7e4b1012.title: Circular procurement
de8d7e4b1012.sentence: Circular procurement is the procurement of products and services that follow circular economy principles, prioritizing reuse, durability, and recycling within supply chains to extend product life cycles and minimize waste.

3fe895664140.title: Circular procurement
3fe895664140.sentence: It may involve acquiring goods and services designed for longevity or reuse, incorporating shared-use models, refurbishing existing assets, and purchasing products containing recycled materials.

47cbabf2033e.title: Circular procurement
47cbabf2033e.sentence: Circular procurement is often regarded as an aspect of sustainable procurement and can be incorporated into supply chain management or public procurement frameworks.

aebd4d9cc370.title: Circular procurement
aebd4d9cc370.sentence: In particular SDG 12, Responsible Consumption and Production, includes a target to promote sustainable public procurement practices in line with national policies and priorities.

49238a7ab17b.title: Circular procurement
49238a7ab17b.sentence: Identified risks include vulnerability to greenwashing and insufficient assessment of environmental and social impacts.

12cffc3c1c4d.title: Circular procurement
12cffc3c1c4d.sentence: Practical barriers include high infrastructure costs, the absence of standardized definitions or enforcement mechanisms, and limited scalability beyond pilot projects.

8596729313f6.title: Urban mining
8596729313f6.sentence: An urban mine is the stockpile of rare metals in the discarded electronic waste of a society.

5671f4de183e.title: Urban mining
5671f4de183e.sentence: Urban mining is the process of recovering these rare metals through mechanical and chemical treatments.

96e78fcc2aba.title: Urban mining
96e78fcc2aba.sentence: Research published by the Japanese government's National Institute of Materials Science in 2010 estimated that there were 6,800 tonnes of gold recoverable from used electronic equipment in Japan.

5a509522494d.title: Urban mining
5a509522494d.sentence: In urban mining, the main motivation is recovery of materials while in "landfill mining" the goal is solving the problem at the disposal level.

aeabfb03098d.title: Urban mining
aeabfb03098d.sentence: In developing countries, people tend to recycle e-waste at informal sites, including inside homes, without the use of proper equipment and waste management techniques.

e355fabf0677.title: Material flow analysis
e355fabf0677.sentence: The gradual shift from primary material production to urban mining in developed countries requires a detailed assessment of in-use and obsolete stocks of materials within human society.

671e01da9a6d.title: Environmental resource management
671e01da9a6d.sentence: Environmental resource management or environmental management is the management of the interaction and impact of human societies on the environment.

569850c7c195.title: Environmental resource management
569850c7c195.sentence: It is not, as the phrase might suggest, the management of the environment itself.

ef0c83f04a1b.title: Environmental resource management
ef0c83f04a1b.sentence: Environmental resources management aims to ensure that ecosystem services are protected and maintained for future human generations, and also maintain ecosystem integrity through considering ethical, economic, and scientific (ecological) variables.

7233d2251e37.title: Environmental resource management
7233d2251e37.sentence: It is thus linked to environmental protection, resource management, sustainability, integrated landscape management, natural resource management, fisheries management, forest management, wildlife management, environmental management systems, and others.

768fea34e3f7.title: Environmental resource management
768fea34e3f7.sentence: The economy functions within and is dependent upon goods and services provided by natural ecosystems.

577f33836a8c.title: Environmental resource management
577f33836a8c.sentence: Environmental resource management strategies are intrinsically driven by conceptions of human-nature relationships.

7c03aaef499c.title: Environmental resource management
7c03aaef499c.sentence: Anthropocentrism looks at nature as existing solely for the benefit of humans, and as a commodity to use for the good of humanity and to improve human quality of life.

56ef08e90452.title: Environmental resource management
56ef08e90452.sentence: Ecocentrists believe in the intrinsic value of nature while maintaining that human beings must use and even exploit nature to survive and live.

057be16fd315.title: Environmental resource management
057be16fd315.sentence: The ISO 14001 standard is the most widely used standard for environmental risk management and is closely aligned to the European Eco-Management and Audit Scheme (EMAS).

47aff619d1e6.title: Adaptive management
47aff619d1e6.sentence: In this way, decision making simultaneously meets one or more resource management objectives and, either passively or actively, accrues information needed to improve future management.

5020ab8a0ad8.title: Adaptive management
5020ab8a0ad8.sentence: - Iterative decision-making (evaluating results and adjusting actions on the basis of what has been learned)

7c015a54f917.title: Adaptive management
7c015a54f917.sentence: - Embracing risk and uncertainty as a way of building understanding

83926fde21fc.title: Adaptive management
83926fde21fc.sentence: Passive adaptive management values learning only insofar as it improves decision outcomes (i.e. passively), as measured by the specified utility function.

2f18a9da00de.title: Adaptive management
2f18a9da00de.sentence: In contrast, active adaptive management explicitly incorporates learning as part of the objective function, and hence, decisions which improve learning are valued over those which do not.

65990ed0971e.title: Adaptive management
65990ed0971e.sentence: The challenge in using the adaptive management approach lies in finding the correct balance between gaining knowledge to improve management in the future and achieving the best short-term outcome based on current knowledge.

c44fc807ffa9.title: Adaptive management
c44fc807ffa9.sentence: Two ecologists at The University of British Columbia, C.S. Holling and C.J Walters further developed the adaptive management approach as they distinguished between passive and active adaptive management practice.

32edaab52493.title: Adaptive management
32edaab52493.sentence: The three components of adaptive management in environmental practice are:

eceba00a4ef9.title: Adaptive management
eceba00a4ef9.sentence: - Testing assumptions is about systematically trying different actions to achieve a desired outcome.

6d4517c9c952.title: Adaptive management
6d4517c9c952.sentence: - Adaptation involves changing assumptions and interventions to respond to new or different information obtained through monitoring and project experience.

6f128a43ec26.title: Adaptive management
6f128a43ec26.sentence: - Learning is about explicitly documenting a team's planning and implementation processes and its successes and failures for internal learning as well as learning across the conservation community.

6a71fc6a65e9.title: Adaptive management
6a71fc6a65e9.sentence: It is difficult to test the effectiveness of adaptive management in comparison to other management approaches.

3056e4c54bed.title: Adaptive management
3056e4c54bed.sentence: One challenge is that once a system is managed using one approach it is difficult to determine how another approach would have performed in exactly the same situation.

6ecc05df786f.title: Environmental governance
6ecc05df786f.sentence: Environmental governance are the processes of decision-making involved in the control and management of the environment and natural resources.

bde6aff51b2c.title: Environmental governance
bde6aff51b2c.sentence: These processes includes government, business and civil society.

8ad478a19215.title: Environmental governance
8ad478a19215.sentence: - Embedding the environment in all levels of decision-making and action

4959f5cb7ac5.title: Environmental governance
4959f5cb7ac5.sentence: - Conceptualizing cities and communities, economic and political life as a subset of the environment

ff25d0a58cdc.title: Environmental governance
ff25d0a58cdc.sentence: - Promoting the transition from open-loop/cradle-to-grave systems (like garbage disposal with no recycling) to closed-loop/cradle-to-cradle systems (like permaculture and zero waste strategies).

1c2caa1a33c5.title: Environmental governance
1c2caa1a33c5.sentence: - Lack of coordination within the UN, governments, the private sector and civil society

29940bc43f04.title: Environmental governance
29940bc43f04.sentence: - International imbalance between environmental governance and trade and finance programs, e.g., World Trade Organization (WTO).

84104e8885dc.title: Environmental governance
84104e8885dc.sentence: - Time lag between human action and environmental effect, sometimes as long as a generation

f0b87f7e5c00.title: Environmental governance
f0b87f7e5c00.sentence: Numerous new international institutions and actors have emerged in this field since the 1970s.

c193124a328d.title: Environmental governance
c193124a328d.sentence: This growth has resulted in overlapping institutional roles, contributing to both fragmentation and complexity.

ad9110286eb3.title: Environmental governance
ad9110286eb3.sentence: However, it also creates opportunities for cooperation and productive interactions between institutions, involving multiple actors and levels of governance.

fb935baf779c.title: Environmental governance
fb935baf779c.section: Example thematic issues at the local level > Biodiversity
fb935baf779c.sentence: A 2018 global study published in Nature analyzed population trends of 461 species of waterbirds across more than 25,000 sites and found that strong environmental governance was one of the most reliable predictors of conservation success.

7f04cb5d5293.title: Environmental governance
7f04cb5d5293.sentence: Community participation and partnership along with the decentralisation of government power to local communities are important aspects of environmental governance at the local level.

9b4e6ac07b56.title: Environmental governance
9b4e6ac07b56.sentence: Initiatives such as these are integral divergence from earlier environmental governance approaches which was "driven by state agendas and resource control" and followed a top-down or trickle down approach rather than the bottom up approach that local level governance encompasses.

1e9c661fb58a.title: International environmental agreement
1e9c661fb58a.sentence: An international environmental agreement or sometimes environmental protocol, is a type of treaty among countries seeking to reach an environmental goal.

753ce317f067.title: International environmental agreement
753ce317f067.sentence: In other words, it is "an intergovernmental document intended as legally binding with a primary stated purpose of preventing or managing human impacts on natural resources."

e4e82f7bd9ba.title: International environmental agreement
e4e82f7bd9ba.sentence: An agreement between two nations is known as a bilateral environmental agreement.

f12c99d43316.title: International environmental agreement
f12c99d43316.sentence: If the agreement is made among three or more nations, it is called a multilateral environmental agreement (MEA).

4d69584a03a2.title: International environmental agreement
4d69584a03a2.sentence: The use of multilateral environment agreements began in 1857, when a German agreement regulated the flow of water from Lake Constance to Austria and Switzerland.

0fd1500117e7.title: International environmental agreement
0fd1500117e7.sentence: Between 1857 and 2012, a total of 747 multilateral environmental agreements have been concluded.

6f1c2f53d403.title: International environmental agreement
6f1c2f53d403.sentence: Following the Stockholm Intergovernmental Conference in 1972, creation of international environmental agreements proliferated.

44a70cc1d2fc.title: International environmental agreement
44a70cc1d2fc.sentence: The Stockholm Declaration was adopted by all 113 countries in attendance at the conference, and was the first universal document of importance on an environmental issue.

8af60a0a6e09.title: International environmental agreement
8af60a0a6e09.sentence: One example is the use of sanctions: under the Montreal Protocol, signatories were forbidden to purchase chlorofluorocarbons from non-signatories, in order to prevent any windfall benefits.

52f6cec6a94f.title: International environmental agreement
52f6cec6a94f.sentence: Funding has also been used to overcome North-South conflict: members of the Montreal Protocol created a fund of $240 million to redistribute the costs of transition.

741f2bc90c31.title: International environmental agreement
741f2bc90c31.sentence: Differential obligations are also seen in the Kyoto Protocol and can encourage wider participation, where every country have very different targets mainly based on their development.

d8baeb44ef51.title: International environmental agreement
d8baeb44ef51.sentence: First, maintenance of sovereignty means that no country can be forced to participate, only urged to do so.

2aecf7541513.title: International environmental agreement
2aecf7541513.sentence: If environmental protocols will cause economic difficulties or harm to a country, it may shirk the protocols while other countries adhere to them, creating a classic free-rider problem.

35e08b59a426.title: National park
35e08b59a426.sentence: A national park is a nature park designated for conservation purposes because of unparalleled national natural, historic, or cultural significance.

7eda969b111e.title: National park
7eda969b111e.sentence: It is an area of natural, semi-natural, or developed land that is protected and owned by a government.

dca85e0c44f4.title: National park
dca85e0c44f4.sentence: The United States established Yellowstone National Park, the first "public park or pleasuring-ground for the benefit and enjoyment of the people", in 1872.

504263a40abd.title: National park
504263a40abd.sentence: Although Yellowstone was not officially termed a "national park" at the time, in practice it is widely held to be the first and oldest national park in the world.

e1a533f21931.title: National park
e1a533f21931.sentence: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and its World Commission on Protected Areas (WCPA) have defined "National Park" as its Category II type of protected areas.

6ce455d50d5a.title: National park
6ce455d50d5a.sentence: - Minimum size of 1,000 hectares within zones in which protection of nature takes precedence

fb00fbbd34f4.title: National park
fb00fbbd34f4.sentence: - Prohibition of exploitation of natural resources (including the development of dams) qualified by such activities as sport, hunting, fishing, the need for management, facilities, etc.

8f763065acbb.title: National park
8f763065acbb.sentence: As many countries do not adhere to the IUCN definition, the term "national park" may be used loosely.

0b39106d6eb2.title: National park
0b39106d6eb2.sentence: In the United Kingdom, and in some other countries such as Taiwan, a "national park" simply describes a general area that is relatively undeveloped, scenic, and attracts tourists, with some form of planning restrictions to ensure it maintains those characteristics.

b2b952bfdb7d.title: National park
b2b952bfdb7d.sentence: There may be substantial human settlements within the bounds of a national park.

1ffc1d5056aa.title: National park
1ffc1d5056aa.sentence: Parks Canada, established on May 19, 1911, is the world's oldest national park service.

36edce26ea52.title: National park
36edce26ea52.sentence: Canada now has the largest protected area in the world with 450,000 km2 of national park space.

27fb018440e1.title: National park
27fb018440e1.sentence: The term national park is perceived as a brand name that is associated with nature-based tourism and it symbolizes a "high quality natural environment with a well-designed tourist infrastructure".

b3e406cedf8a.title: National park
b3e406cedf8a.sentence: In Costa Rica for example, a megadiverse country, tourism to parks has increased by 400% from 1985 to 1999.

707ea3f7b6af.title: National park
707ea3f7b6af.sentence: National parks in former European colonies have come under criticism for allegedly perpetuating colonialism.

a0fb2e7ebd36.title: National park
a0fb2e7ebd36.sentence: Yet, in some instances, the lands that were to be set aside and protected in formerly colonized lands were already being inhabited by native communities, who were then removed off of these lands to create pristine sites for public consumption.

b57744679274.title: National park
b57744679274.sentence: Critics claim that the removal of people from national parks enhances the belief that nature can only be protected when humans do not exist within it, and that this leads to perpetuating the dichotomy between nature and humans (also known as the nature–culture divide).

97e4ac33847e.title: European Green Deal
97e4ac33847e.sentence: The European Green Deal, approved in 2020, is a set of policy initiatives by the European Commission with the overarching aim of making the European Union (EU) climate neutral in 2050.

6088695b3be4.title: European Green Deal
6088695b3be4.sentence: The plan is to review each existing law on its climate merits, and also introduce new legislation on the circular economy (CE), building renovation, biodiversity, farming and innovation.

5f1b89767efb.title: European Green Deal
5f1b89767efb.sentence: The plan includes potential carbon tariffs for countries that don't curtail their greenhouse gas pollution at the same rate.

6d6a5fe2c15b.title: European Green Deal
6d6a5fe2c15b.sentence: The mechanism to achieve this is called the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).

a8ba6eac3733.title: European Green Deal
a8ba6eac3733.sentence: The Farm to Fork (F2F) strategy pursues the issue of food system sustainability as well as the support allocated to the producers such as farmers and fishermen.

ebe9f13e8b7c.title: European Green Deal
ebe9f13e8b7c.sentence: The 'Zero Pollution Action Plan' that aims to be adopted by the commission in 2021 intends to achieve no pollution from "all sources", cleaning the air, water and soil by 2050.

9a0c7c9e04b5.title: European Green Deal
9a0c7c9e04b5.section: Policy areas > Biodiversity and ecosystem health
9a0c7c9e04b5.sentence: The EU Biodiversity Strategy was published in 2020 and adopted by the European Parliament on June 9, 2021.

f709929c0186.title: European Green Deal
f709929c0186.section: Policy areas > Biodiversity and ecosystem health > Nature Restoration Law
f709929c0186.sentence: The law is a core element of the European Green Deal and the EU Biodiversity Strategy and makes the targets set therein for the "restoration of nature" binding.

53a738e2d225.title: European Green Deal
53a738e2d225.sentence: The "Just Transition Mechanism", expects to distribute the burden of transitioning to a greener economy more fairly.

0036862a5643.title: European Green Deal
0036862a5643.sentence: This policy means that countries that have more workers in coal and oil shale sectors, as well as those with higher greenhouse emissions, will receive more financial aid.

363c2f6103e2.title: European Green Deal
363c2f6103e2.sentence: - In 2017, more than 75% of greenhouse gas emissions within the EU were related to the production and use of energy.

af16d224bb29.title: European Green Deal
af16d224bb29.sentence: The current proposals have been criticised for falling short of the goal of ending fossil fuels, or being sufficient for a green recovery after the COVID-19 pandemic.

b32c8b906e3d.title: European Green Deal
b32c8b906e3d.sentence: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán blamed a record-breaking surge in energy prices on the European Commission's Green Deal plans.

34a6d27c96a3.title: European Green Deal
34a6d27c96a3.sentence: EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism not adjusting exports could reduce the competitiveness of exporting industries and contributes to deindustrialization.

c7e3bb6e66b1.title: European Green Deal
c7e3bb6e66b1.sentence: European farmers have protested against proposed environmental regulations (such as a carbon tax, pesticide bans, nitrogen emissions curbs and restrictions on water and land usage), low food prices and trade in agricultural products with non-European Union member states, such as Ukraine and the Mercosur bloc of South America.

746415b6f7c6.title: European Green Deal
746415b6f7c6.sentence: - 11 December 2019: The European Green Deal was presented.

9f01eea9edc6.title: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
9f01eea9edc6.sentence: The Rio Declaration on Environment and Development, often shortened to Rio Declaration, was a short document produced at the 1992 United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), informally known as the Earth Summit.

75dd1ff7ae17.title: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
75dd1ff7ae17.sentence: The Rio Declaration consisted of 27 principles intended to guide countries in future sustainable development.

d2622ff3c005.title: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
d2622ff3c005.sentence: The first principle states that sustainable development primarily concerns human beings, who are entitled to live healthy and productive lives in harmony with nature.

37b35ed06db5.title: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
37b35ed06db5.sentence: Further articles include formulations of the precautionary principle, which should be "widely applied by states according to their capabilities" (principle 15), and of the polluter pays principle, which states are encouraged to adopt where it is in the public interest to do so and it will not distort international trade and investment (principle 16).

9267a94089bb.title: Aarhus Convention
9267a94089bb.sentence: It is by far the most impressive elaboration of principle 10 of the Rio Declaration, which stresses the need for citizens' participation in environmental issues and for access to information on the environment held by public authorities.

0dc9f6ede36b.title: Declaration of the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
0dc9f6ede36b.sentence: Given that the Stockholm Conference had previously set the standard for future international environmental conferences, the Rio Declaration adopted three of the documents drafted in the Stockholm Declaration.

988c736a4e25.title: Declaration of the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
988c736a4e25.sentence: The aim of the Rio Declaration, which was a step forward from the Stockholm Declaration, was to create, clarify, and rearticulate principles that states can incorporate into their domestic legislation.

292704568e76.title: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
292704568e76.sentence: While the document helped to raise environmental awareness, evidence from 2007 suggested that little of the document's environmental goals had at that time been achieved.

70dead9230f7.title: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
70dead9230f7.sentence: The Rio Conference, which adopted the Declaration, took place from 3 to 14 June 1992.

aa73694637c0.title: Agenda 21
aa73694637c0.sentence: Agenda 21 is a non-binding action plan of the United Nations with regard to sustainable development.

c02f48ff8188.title: Agenda 21
c02f48ff8188.sentence: It is a product of the Earth Summit (UN Conference on Environment and Development) held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in June 1992.

ebbe0ac5e9a3.title: Agenda 21
ebbe0ac5e9a3.sentence: The full text of Agenda 21 was made public at the UN Conference on Environment and Development (Earth Summit), held in Rio de Janeiro on 13 June 1992, where 178 governments voted to adopt the program.

a15e9ed39aa8.title: Agenda 21
a15e9ed39aa8.sentence: - Section I: Social and Economic Dimensions is directed toward combating poverty, especially in developing countries, changing consumption patterns, promoting health, achieving a more sustainable population, and sustainable settlement in decision making.

360ff8423a08.title: Agenda 21
360ff8423a08.sentence: - Section II: Conservation and Management of Resources for Development includes atmospheric protection, combating deforestation, protecting important environments, conservation of biological diversity (biodiversity), control of pollution and the management of biotechnology, and radioactive wastes.

40e367c7808d.title: Agenda 21
40e367c7808d.sentence: - Section III: Strengthening the Role of Major Groups includes the roles of children and youth, women, NGOs, local authorities, business and industry, and workers; and strengthening the role of indigenous peoples, their communities, and farmers.

3096dccc2961.title: Agenda 21
3096dccc2961.sentence: - Section IV: Means of Implementation includes science, technology transfer, education international institutions, and financial mechanisms.

c1773b6426b8.title: Agenda 21
c1773b6426b8.sentence: It is an action agenda for the UN, other multilateral organizations, and individual governments around the world that can be executed at local, national, and global levels.

1179002c77d6.title: Agenda 21
1179002c77d6.sentence: One major objective of the Agenda 21 initiative is that every local government should draw its own local Agenda 21.

856510273f59.title: Agenda 21
856510273f59.sentence: Implementation by member states remains voluntary, and its adoption has varied.

2d6953207032.title: Agenda 21
2d6953207032.section: Development and evolution > Sustainable Development Summit (2015)
2d6953207032.sentence: Agenda 2030, also known as the Sustainable Development Goals, was a set of goals decided upon at the UN Sustainable Development Summit in 2015.

e6bfccda7752.title: Agenda 21
e6bfccda7752.section: Development and evolution > Sustainable Development Summit (2015)
e6bfccda7752.sentence: It takes all of the goals set by Agenda 21 and re-asserts them as the basis for sustainable development, saying, "We reaffirm all the principles of the Rio Declaration on Environment and Development…" Adding onto those goals from the original Rio document, a total of 17 goals have been agreed on, revolving around the same concepts of Agenda 21; people, planet, prosperity, peace, and partnership.

0f4942f82620.title: Agenda 21
0f4942f82620.sentence: Anti-Agenda 21 theories have circulated in the U.S. Some Tea Party movement activists and others promoted the notion that Agenda 21 was part of a UN plot to deny property rights, undermine U.S. sovereignty, or force citizens to move to cities.

459089456066.title: Agenda 21
459089456066.sentence: In 1997, the UN General Assembly held a special session to appraise the status of Agenda 21 (Rio +5).

8fb3595f545c.title: Agenda 21
8fb3595f545c.sentence: In 2012, at the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development the attending members reaffirmed their commitment to Agenda 21 in their outcome document called "The Future We Want".

c37d8ecee2b7.title: Ecosystem management
c37d8ecee2b7.sentence: Ecosystem management is an approach to natural resource management that aims to ensure the long-term sustainability and persistence of an ecosystem's function and services while meeting socioeconomic, political, and cultural needs.

8673d4c9d361.title: Ecosystem management
8673d4c9d361.sentence: Although indigenous communities have employed sustainable ecosystem management approaches implicitly for millennia, ecosystem management emerged explicitly as a formal concept in the 1990s from a growing appreciation of the complexity of ecosystems and of humans' reliance and influence on natural systems (e.g., disturbance and ecological resilience).

e4f2700443bf.title: Ecosystem management
e4f2700443bf.sentence: The term “ecosystem management” was formalized in 1992 by F. Dale Robertson, former Chief of the U.S. Forest Service.

cda5087c2cbe.title: Ecosystem management
cda5087c2cbe.sentence: In contrast to command and control approaches to natural resource management, which often lead to declines in ecological resilience, ecosystem management is a holistic, adaptive method for evaluating and achieving resilience and sustainability.

bafda6ce1064.title: Ecosystem management
bafda6ce1064.sentence: In industrialized Western society, ecosystems have been managed primarily to maximize yields of a particular natural resource.

f7e7366b27e2.title: Ecosystem management
f7e7366b27e2.sentence: For example, this perspective informed the long-held belief in forest fire suppression in the United States, which drove a decline in populations of fire-tolerant species and a buildup of fuel, leading to higher intensity fires.

2c444e1770e7.title: Ecosystem management
2c444e1770e7.sentence: A fundamental concern of ecosystem management is the long-term sustainability of the production of goods and services by ecosystems, as "intergenerational sustainability [is] a precondition for management, not an afterthought." Ideally, there should be clear, publicly stated goals with respect to future trajectories and behaviors of the system being managed.

9a5a77376d73.title: Ecosystem management

188608a72641.sentence: Many of the countries that have not ratified the treaty, such as the U.S., nonetheless recognize its provisions as reflective of international customary law.

591adc551862.title: Law of the sea
591adc551862.section: Recognition and enforcement of law of the sea
591adc551862.sentence: A specialized agency of the United Nations, the International Maritime Organization, monitors and enforces certain provisions of the convention, along with the intergovernmental International Seabed Authority (ISA), which was established by the convention to organize, regulate and control all mineral-related activities in the international seabed area beyond territorial limits.

6931cca1d5e5.title: Law of the sea
6931cca1d5e5.section: Recognition and enforcement of law of the sea
6931cca1d5e5.sentence: UNCLOS established the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS), based in Hamburg, Germany, to adjudicate all disputes concerning the interpretation or application of the convention (subject to the provisions of Article 297 and to the declarations made in accordance with article 298 of the convention).

eb990b1afffe.title: Marine protected area
eb990b1afffe.sentence: Approximately 64% of the world's oceans are "international waters" and subject to regulations such as the Law of the Sea and the governance of UN bodies such as the International Seabed Authority.

f14531c9fc9f.title: Law of the sea
f14531c9fc9f.section: History > UN Convention of the Law of the Sea
f14531c9fc9f.sentence: With more than 160 nations participating, the conference lasted until 1982, resulting in the UN Convention of the Law of the Sea, also known as the Law of the Sea Treaty, which defines the rights and responsibilities of nations in their use of the world's oceans.

01cf28c3a8ed.title: Law of the sea
01cf28c3a8ed.section: History > UN Convention of the Law of the Sea
01cf28c3a8ed.sentence: The convention came into force on 16 November 1994, one year after it was ratified by the 60th state, Guyana; the four treaties concluded in the first UN Conference in 1956 were consequently superseded.

e7f2765c2991.title: Global governance
e7f2765c2991.sentence: The most pressing transboundary environmental challenges include climate change, biodiversity loss, and land degradation.

459c7ddfe0fd.title: Global governance
459c7ddfe0fd.sentence: A publication of 2020 described global environmental governance as "one of the institutionally most dynamic areas in world politics" in the last thirty years.

fd283367023a.title: Global governance
fd283367023a.section: Global environmental governance > International conventions and agreements
fd283367023a.sentence: The International Environmental Agreement Database Project currently (as of 2020) comprises almost 1300 multilateral agreements and over 2200 bilateral agreements (see also list of international environmental agreements).

423ac7b69071.title: Global governance
423ac7b69071.section: Global environmental governance > International conventions and agreements
423ac7b69071.sentence: Until now, the formulation of environmental policies at the international level has been divided by theme, sector or territory, resulting in treaties that overlap or clash.

11ac938bc58e.title: Global governance
11ac938bc58e.section: Global environmental governance > United Nations Environmental Programme (UNEP)
11ac938bc58e.sentence: The United Nations Environmental Programme (UNEP) is responsible for coordinating responses to environmental issues within the United Nations System.

bfb905cbd4ca.title: Global governance
bfb905cbd4ca.section: Global environmental governance > United Nations Environmental Programme (UNEP)
bfb905cbd4ca.sentence: However, UNEP has been widely considered as a weak international organization.

cd9fb9d7327c.title: Global governance
cd9fb9d7327c.section: Global environmental governance > Aspects of Global North and Global South
cd9fb9d7327c.sentence: Scholars have noted that unindustrialized countries in the Global South sometimes are disconnected from environmentalism and perceive environmental governance to be a "luxury" priority for the Global North.

f965c14bf4b4.title: Global governance
f965c14bf4b4.section: Global environmental governance > Aspects of Global North and Global South
f965c14bf4b4.sentence: Also, environmental governance priorities in the Global North have been at odds with the desire to focus on economic development in the Global South.

6613618965ea.title: Race to the bottom
6613618965ea.sentence: Race to the bottom is a socio-economic concept describing a scenario in which individuals, companies, or governments compete by incrementally lowering standards or regulations to reduce costs in order to attract economic activity.

91816a34f18f.title: Race to the bottom
91816a34f18f.sentence: This can include labor laws and enforcement, tax rates, and environmental regulations.

a610501f32b2.title: Race to the bottom
a610501f32b2.sentence: The race to the bottom phenomenon is in contrast with traditional competition, which tends to improve goods and services.

de500057ec17.title: Race to the bottom
de500057ec17.sentence: Countries/localities with higher labor, environmental standards, or taxes can lose business to countries/localities with less regulation, which in turn makes them want to lower regulations in order to keep firms' production in their jurisdiction, hence driving the race to the lowest regulatory standards.

393f178fca68.title: Race to the bottom
393f178fca68.sentence: The term "race to the bottom" can be traced back to the early 1900s, when United States Supreme Court Justice Louis Brandeis used the term in a court ruling.

0fe251e1aebe.title: Race to the bottom
0fe251e1aebe.sentence: The concept of a regulatory "race to the bottom" emerged in the United States during the late 1800s and early 1900s, when there was charter competition among states to attract corporations to base in their jurisdiction.

e285aa0a5af0.title: Race to the bottom
e285aa0a5af0.sentence: It is expensive to treat chemical waste, so corporations wanting to keep production costs low, may move to countries which do not require them to treat their waste before dumping it.

826cdbf16ff6.title: Environmental economics
826cdbf16ff6.sentence: Another context in which externalities apply is when globalization permits one player in a market who is unconcerned with biodiversity to undercut prices of another who is – creating a race to the bottom in regulations and conservation.

8dd7d3434cc5.title: Race to the bottom
8dd7d3434cc5.sentence: Whether the race to the bottom persists in global markets today is debated among academic circles, with empirical evidence supporting both sides.

4ebd018e121e.title: Race to the bottom
4ebd018e121e.sentence: International Political Economy scholar Daniel Drezner (of Tufts University) has described the "race to the bottom" as a myth.

eac2e507bdc8.title: Race to the bottom
eac2e507bdc8.sentence: A 2022 study found no evidence that global trade competition led to a race to the bottom in labor standards.

01e74cee07f7.title: Race to the bottom
01e74cee07f7.sentence: Nita Rudra has found evidence of a race-to-the-bottom in developing countries, but not in developed countries; she argued that this is due to the elevated bargaining power of labor in developed countries.

cf634d549fae.title: Race to the bottom
cf634d549fae.sentence: Conversely, some states have begun to pursue a race to the top strategy, which stresses innovative environmental policies at the state level, with the hopes that these policies will later be adopted by other states.

f9bcb4d59758.title: Stewardship
f9bcb4d59758.sentence: Stewardship is a practice committed to ethical value that embodies the responsible planning and management of resources.

51f3b186ebef.title: Stewardship
51f3b186ebef.sentence: The concept of stewardship can be applied to the environment and nature, economics, health, places, property, information, theology, and cultural resources.

1a5e734bb529.title: Stewardship
1a5e734bb529.sentence: Stewardship was originally made up of the tasks of a domestic steward, from stiġ (house, hall) and weard, (ward, guard, guardian, keeper).

1267b60236d0.title: Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
1267b60236d0.sentence: The Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer is a multilateral environmental agreement signed in 1985 that provided frameworks for international reductions in the production of chlorofluorocarbons due to their contribution to the destruction of the ozone layer, resulting in an increased threat of skin cancer.

814da9743c93.title: Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
814da9743c93.sentence: During the 1970s, research indicated that man-made chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) reduce and convert ozone molecules in the atmosphere.

1bc7f5113daa.title: Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
1bc7f5113daa.sentence: CFCs are stable molecules composed of carbon, fluorine, and chlorine that were used prominently in products such as refrigerators.

467d02cde076.title: Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
467d02cde076.sentence: The Vienna Convention was agreed upon at the Vienna Conference of 1985 and entered into force in 1988.

e12127c7f91f.title: Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
e12127c7f91f.sentence: The Vienna Convention provided the framework necessary to create regulatory measures in the form of the Montreal Protocol.

e2feba7633ba.title: Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
e2feba7633ba.sentence: While not a binding agreement, it acts as a framework for the international efforts to protect the ozone layer; however, it does not include legally binding reduction goals for the use of CFCs, the main chemical agents causing ozone depletion.

7235c2b16d9c.title: Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
7235c2b16d9c.sentence: In terms of universality, it is one of the most successful treaties of all time, having been ratified by 198 states (all United Nations members as well as the Holy See, the State of Palestine, Niue and the Cook Islands) as well as the European Union.

c050fd9dce95.title: Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
c050fd9dce95.sentence: The Multilateral Fund has aided thousands of projects in nearly 150 countries, preventing the usage of roughly 250,000 tons of ozone-depleting chemicals.

6901e0450fc2.title: Agenda 21
6901e0450fc2.sentence: Some national and state governments have legislated or advised that local authorities take steps to implement the plan locally, as recommended in Chapter 28 of the document.

135cd5ad4251.title: Agenda 21
135cd5ad4251.sentence: These programs are often known as "Local Agenda 21" or "LA21".

d94b3ff17d3e.title: Agenda 21
d94b3ff17d3e.sentence: The Rio+10 report identified over 6400 local governments in 113 countries worldwide that were engaged in Local Agenda 21 (LA21) activities, a more than three-fold increase over less than five years.

bbe1c68d0be9.title: Agenda 21
bbe1c68d0be9.sentence: 80% = 5120 of these local governments, were located in Europe.

fbbc3c9fb7bc.title: Agenda 21
fbbc3c9fb7bc.sentence: Sweden reported that 100% of the municipalities had adopted LA21 by 2002.

7b9b0d5ba272.title: Agenda 21
7b9b0d5ba272.sentence: The group, ICLEI-Local Governments for Sustainability, formed in 1990; today its members come from over 1,000 cities, towns, and counties in 88 countries and is widely regarded as a paragon of Agenda 21 implementation.

c91334c1368d.title: Bloomington school
c91334c1368d.sentence: The Bloomington school or Bloomington school of political economy is a new institutionalist research tradition in political science, economics, sociology, and public administration associated with the work of Elinor Ostrom and Vincent Ostrom at Indiana University Bloomington.

e3bd580a2e22.title: Bloomington school
e3bd580a2e22.sentence: The school focuses on governance, collective action, and institutional diversity, particularly in relation to common-pool resources (CPRs), decentralization, and self-governance.

c8177689de63.title: Bloomington school
c8177689de63.sentence: The Ostroms founded the Workshop in Political Theory and Policy Analysis in 1973, which became the institutional home for research on self-governance and institutional diversity.

6f0c355ed5e1.title: Bloomington school
6f0c355ed5e1.sentence: Her research identified "eight design principles" that contribute to the success of CPR governance, including clearly defined boundaries, collective decision-making, monitoring, graduated sanctions, and conflict-resolution mechanisms.

11962a498e6e.title: Bloomington school
11962a498e6e.sentence: Elinor Ostrom was awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 2009, becoming the first woman to receive the prize in this category.

4ca391db8aa5.title: Bloomington school
4ca391db8aa5.sentence: Some economists argue that Ostrom's findings on CPR management are difficult to scale up to national or global levels.

0bb509e5b814.title: Bloomington school
0bb509e5b814.sentence: Additionally, scholars from Marxist and critical political economy traditions have criticized the school for not sufficiently addressing power dynamics and inequalities in governance structures.

e24261e8793a.title: Fisheries co-management
e24261e8793a.sentence: Fisheries co-management is flexible and cooperative management of the aquatic resources by the user groups and the government.

6aa1b0533c8a.title: Fisheries co-management
6aa1b0533c8a.sentence: The responsibility of the resource is shared between the user groups and the government, both the community and the government are involved during the decision making, implementation and enforcement processes.

5ab0c7d7f861.title: Fisheries co-management
5ab0c7d7f861.sentence: Depending on the level of participation between the government and the community, five different types of co-management have been identified.

895fc33159a8.title: Fisheries co-management
895fc33159a8.sentence: Instructive management is top-down management from the government.

1a461eb74067.title: Fisheries co-management
1a461eb74067.sentence: In consultative management, the government consults with the community either through public hearings or advisory boards.

6edec395c4ab.title: Fisheries co-management
6edec395c4ab.sentence: In cooperative management, there is a degree of co-management of the resource by the government and the user group.

86673cc226bd.title: Fisheries co-management
86673cc226bd.sentence: In advisory management, users decide what decisions should be made and advise the government as such, the government than endorses the decision.

5acf58cfab3e.title: Fisheries co-management
5acf58cfab3e.sentence: In informative management, the user group makes all of the decisions, and informs the government once they have decided.

d69afe328a5d.title: Fisheries co-management
d69afe328a5d.sentence: Co-management developed due to an attempt to improve the success of fisheries management as many of the aquatic resources risked being or were already depleted.

9ea318cb0a47.title: Fisheries co-management
9ea318cb0a47.sentence: The top-down approach of fisheries management has frequently failed as it often goes against the community and their internal structure.

8e02d39588a2.title: Fisheries co-management
8e02d39588a2.sentence: Furthermore, the reason for the new governmental regulations and laws such as a decrease in total allowable catch (TAC) or catch per unit effort (CPUE) were often poorly understood by the community due to lack of education.

a401138654bd.title: Fisheries co-management
a401138654bd.sentence: Without proper enforcement or co-management the community would often disregard the law and continue as they previously were, often despite the detrimental impact this may have on the ocean.

de892d64158b.title: Fisheries co-management
de892d64158b.section: Difference between community management and co-management
de892d64158b.sentence: Co-management is different from community management as the government plays an important part in the decision making process.

8038d500d76b.title: Fisheries co-management
8038d500d76b.section: Difference between community management and co-management
8038d500d76b.sentence: In co-management the user group and the government develop laws and regulations together and works towards implementing them as a unit.

d15cdaa08734.title: Fisheries co-management
d15cdaa08734.sentence: The community, specifically the users of the resource often possess knowledge that can aid the government in the decision making process, therefore co-management is the combination of scientific and traditional knowledge, this process ensures the best possible outcome.

187c83cec202.title: Fisheries co-management
187c83cec202.sentence: If the community is involved with and agrees on the new laws and decisions they are more likely to comply and may even aid in ensuring the new laws are enforced and maintained.

913203fe9273.title: Fisheries co-management
913203fe9273.sentence: Co-management is known to be time consuming, as one must spend time collecting surveys and gaining trust within the community.

e73a5d5c338c.title: Fisheries management
e73a5d5c338c.section: Issues in fishery management > Business training barriers
e73a5d5c338c.sentence: Additionally, others have argued that co-management only empowers the wealthy and powerful which in turn solidifies and validates the already existing inequalities of fisheries management.

265398487a56.title: Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution
265398487a56.sentence: The Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution, often abbreviated as Air Convention or CLRTAP, is intended to protect the human environment against air pollution and to gradually reduce and prevent air pollution, including long-range transboundary air pollution.

8de42642e2a7.title: Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution
8de42642e2a7.sentence: The aim of the Convention is that Parties shall endeavour to limit and, as far as possible, gradually reduce and prevent air pollution including long-range transboundary air pollution.

93e6cfc043be.title: Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution
93e6cfc043be.sentence: The convention opened for signature on November 13, 1979, and entered into force on March 16, 1983.

d45562439f18.title: Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution
d45562439f18.sentence: The Convention, which now has 51 Parties, identifies the Executive Secretary of the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) as its secretariat.

77cd714185b8.title: Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution
77cd714185b8.sentence: The Convention has been extended by eight protocols that identify specific measures to be taken by Parties to cut their emissions of air pollutants:

30fc483f9dc1.title: Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution
30fc483f9dc1.sentence: - 1985 Helsinki Protocol on the Reduction of Sulphur Emissions

ef2a1f6f4c0f.title: Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution
ef2a1f6f4c0f.sentence: - 1999 Gothenburg Protocol to Abate Acidification, Eutrophication and Ground-level Ozone (1999)

5e842870c950.title: Global commons
5e842870c950.sentence: The 1979 Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution, or CLRTAP, is an early international effort to protect and gradually reduce and prevent air pollution.

83d9d94beca9.title: London Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter
83d9d94beca9.sentence: The Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter 1972, commonly called the "London Convention" or "LC '72" and also abbreviated as Marine Dumping, is an agreement to control pollution of the sea by dumping and to encourage regional agreements supplementary to the convention.

a40c43401b37.title: London Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter
a40c43401b37.sentence: It covers the deliberate disposal at sea of wastes or other matter from vessels, aircraft, and platforms.

8ba16ac8c7f7.title: London Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter
8ba16ac8c7f7.sentence: It entered into force on 30 August 1975 when 15 nations ratified.

ad0a68145719.title: London Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter
ad0a68145719.sentence: It follows a "black list/grey list" approach to regulating ocean dumping; Annex I materials (black list) generally may not be ocean dumped (though for certain Annex I materials dumping may be permissible if present only as "trace contaminants" or "rapidly rendered harmless" and Annex II materials (grey list) require "special care".

1d9d4a00927b.title: London Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter
1d9d4a00927b.sentence: Among the most important innovations brought by the 1996 protocol is the codification of the "precautionary approach" and the "polluter pays principle." Reflecting these principles, the protocol embodies a major structural revision of the convention the so-called "reverse list" approach.

05fbe13dcb30.title: London Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter
05fbe13dcb30.sentence: Now, instead of prohibiting the dumping of certain (listed) hazardous materials, the parties are obligated to prohibit the dumping of any waste or other matter that is not listed in Annex 1 ("the reverse list") of the 1996 protocol.

2ba6454781b9.title: London Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter
2ba6454781b9.sentence: It does not cover discharges from land-based sources such as pipes and outfalls, wastes generated incidental to normal operation of vessels, or placement of materials for purposes other than mere disposal, providing such disposal is not contrary to aims of the convention.

8b7baeda927d.title: London Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter
8b7baeda927d.sentence: The convention was called for by the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment (June 1972, Stockholm), the treaty was drafted at the Intergovernmental Conference on the Convention on the Dumping of Wastes at Sea (13 November 1972, London) and it was opened for signature on 29 December 1972.

80bac89e9633.title: London Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter
80bac89e9633.sentence: On 17 November 1996, a special meeting of the Contracting Parties adopted the "1996 Protocol to the Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter, 1972" which is to replace the 1972 Convention, subject to ratification.

da99f3da4813.title: Forest Principles
da99f3da4813.sentence: The Forest Principles (also Rio Forest Principles, formally the Non-Legally Binding Authoritative Statement of Principles for a Global Consensus on the Management, Conservation and Sustainable Development of All Types of Forests) is a 1992 document produced at the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (the "Earth Summit").

97e8b18f420b.title: Forest Principles
97e8b18f420b.sentence: It is a non-legally binding document that makes several recommendations for conservation and sustainable development forestry.

b98613d5d3fb.title: Forest Principles
b98613d5d3fb.sentence: At the Earth Summit, the negotiation of the document was complicated by demands by developing nations in the Group of 77 for increased foreign aid in order to pay for the setting aside of forest reserves.

4843dc16137c.title: Forest Principles
4843dc16137c.sentence: Developed nations resisted those demands, and the final document was a compromise.

8016d80ae8a3.title: Forest Principles
8016d80ae8a3.sentence: These linked the problem of deforestation to third world debt and inadequate technology transfer and stated that the "agreed full incremental cost of achieving benefits associated with forest conservation...should be equitably shared by the international community" (para1(b)).

16f099d8dbea.title: Forest Principles
16f099d8dbea.sentence: The Montréal Process, also known as the Working Group on Criteria and Indicators for the Conservation and Sustainable Management of Temperate and Boreal Forests, was started in 1994 as a result of the Forest Principles.

c7e2fb3cb2e3.title: Earth system governance
c7e2fb3cb2e3.sentence: Earth system governance (or earth systems governance) is a broad area of scholarly inquiry that builds on earlier notions of environmental policy and nature conservation, but puts these into the broader context of human-induced transformations of the entire earth system.

f727df7b057b.title: Earth system governance
f727df7b057b.sentence: A simpler version of the same definition is: Earth system governance is the combination of various rules and efforts from actors at all levels of society, from local to global, aimed at guiding actions to prevent, reduce, and adapt to environmental changes.

8cc392fd868f.title: Earth system governance
8cc392fd868f.sentence: The integrative paradigm of earth system governance (ESG) has evolved into an active research area that brings together a variety of disciplines including political science, sociology, economics, ecology, policy studies, geography, sustainability science, and law.

1e6347d76a82.title: Earth system governance
1e6347d76a82.sentence: ESG research can be carried out under a conceptual framework of five analytical problems which are all highly interlinked.

f850044b48a6.title: Earth system governance
f850044b48a6.sentence: These analytical problems are "problems of the overall architecture of ESG, of agency beyond the state and of the state, of the adaptiveness of governance mechanisms and processes, of their accountability and legitimacy and of modes of allocation and access in ESG".

d626dbd47052.title: Earth system governance
d626dbd47052.sentence: They share at least four cross-cutting themes which are "power, knowledge, norms and scale".

b5f6394f0d5b.title: Earth system governance
b5f6394f0d5b.sentence: ESG is not simply about the global level but all levels are relevant.

32f8e2bfa088.title: Earth system governance
32f8e2bfa088.sentence: The new paradigm of earth system governance was originally developed in the Netherlands by Professor Frank Biermann in his inaugural lecture at the VU University Amsterdam, which was published later in 2007.

33b3e4ab0dee.title: Earth system governance
33b3e4ab0dee.sentence: Based on this pioneering contribution, Biermann was invited by the International Human Dimensions Programme on Global Environmental Change to develop a long-term comprehensive international program in this field, which became in 2009 the global Earth System Governance Project (ESG Project).

7a0e14049845.title: Earth system governance
7a0e14049845.sentence: The idea of earth system governance (ESG) has been criticized for being too top-down, for placing too much emphasis on global governance structures.

0c152744e392.title: Earth system governance
0c152744e392.sentence: According to Mike Hulme, ESG represents an attempt to "geopolitically engineer" our way out of the climate crisis.

c9f9a6e17362.title: Earth system governance
c9f9a6e17362.sentence: He questions whether the climate is governable and argues that it is way too optimistic and even hubristic to attempt to control the global climate by universal governance regimes.

79ae3f70dede.title: Integrated coastal zone management
79ae3f70dede.sentence: Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM), also known as Integrated Coastal Management (ICM) or Integrated Coastal Planning, is a coastal management process that considers geographical and political boundaries and focuses on sustainability.

0fc66d6b4cd2.title: Integrated coastal zone management
0fc66d6b4cd2.sentence: Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) is a decision-making framework developed to address region-specific environmental implications for coastal zones by considering interactions between natural, social, and economic systems in coastal areas.

4234e943b6c4.title: Integrated coastal zone management
4234e943b6c4.sentence: The concept was developed in 1992 during the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro and outlined in the proceedings of Agenda 21, Chapter 17.

206111b00864.title: Integrated coastal zone management
206111b00864.section: Overview > Context > Management of coastal zones
206111b00864.sentence: Coastal margins represent 8% of the world's surface area while providing 25% of global resources.

e965273a1bb7.title: Integrated coastal zone management
e965273a1bb7.section: Overview > Context > Management of coastal zones
e965273a1bb7.sentence: Approximately 70% of the world's population lives within a day's walk of the coast, and two-thirds of the world's cities are coastal.

9e66ad721753.title: Integrated coastal zone management
9e66ad721753.sentence: - Situation assessment: Issues are identified and prioritized with input from government, local and regional non-governmental entities, and local residents

1c464281204e.title: Integrated coastal zone management
1c464281204e.sentence: - Plan: A plan specific to the area is developed to address identified issues

8d82ade7dbbc.title: Integrated coastal zone management
8d82ade7dbbc.sentence: - Institutionalization of plan: Plan is accepted by involved agencies either in the form of legally binding measures or as non-statutory guidance or policy.

ac0a8598c498.title: Integrated coastal zone management
ac0a8598c498.sentence: - Implementation: The plan is implemented through law enforcement, education, development, or other mechanisms

57484c7ca38d.title: Integrated coastal zone management
57484c7ca38d.sentence: - Evaluation: ICZM is an ongoing process targeted to improving sustainability and as such has no ‘end state'.

3685eaf146a9.title: Integrated coastal zone management
3685eaf146a9.section: Overview > Constraints > Top-down and bottom-up approach
3685eaf146a9.sentence: Major constraints of ICZM are institutional, rather than technological.

553bc2874829.title: Integrated coastal zone management
553bc2874829.sentence: The idea of the coast being common property fouls ‘top-down ’ approaches.

c528d1e65db6.title: Rio Convention
c528d1e65db6.sentence: Rio Convention relates to the following three conventions, which were agreed at the Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro in June 1992.

2920ac61cec8.title: Rio Convention
2920ac61cec8.sentence: - UNFCCC, the abbreviation of United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change

b11285eee223.title: Rio Convention
b11285eee223.sentence: - CBD, the abbreviation of Convention on Biological Diversity

dd328b9cde9d.title: Rio Convention
dd328b9cde9d.sentence: - UNCCD, the abbreviation of United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification

a3f0362a4b49.title: Rio Convention
a3f0362a4b49.sentence: The resulting documentation from the two-week deliberations and meetings included the following: Agenda 21 (a non-binding action plan of the United Nations promoting sustainable development), the Statement of Forest Principles, the Rio Declaration on Environment and Development, and the following Conventions were formed: the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), and the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).

4c9ff55dea2d.title: Rio Convention
4c9ff55dea2d.section: Goals of the Three Rio Conventions > The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)
4c9ff55dea2d.sentence: Established on December 29th, 1993, the Convention on Biological Diversity works to maintain the following three objectives:

b956e8299c0d.title: Rio Convention
b956e8299c0d.section: Goals of the Three Rio Conventions > The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)
