8c1b74ebb01f.sentence: It has two supplementary agreements, the Cartagena Protocol and Nagoya Protocol.

cb42f253b0fb.title: Convention on Biological Diversity
cb42f253b0fb.sentence: - Regulated access to genetic resources and traditional knowledge, including Prior Informed Consent of the party providing resources.

c5fd028bad9a.title: Convention on Biological Diversity
c5fd028bad9a.sentence: The notion of an international convention on biodiversity was conceived at a United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) Ad Hoc Working Group of Experts on Biological Diversity in November 1988.

e95a72aafd8b.title: Convention on Biological Diversity
e95a72aafd8b.sentence: The CBD Secretariat, based in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, operates under UNEP, the United Nations Environment Programme.

4ba44bbc668e.title: Convention on Biological Diversity
4ba44bbc668e.sentence: The Convention's Strategic Plan for Biodiversity 2011–2020, created in 2010, include the Aichi Biodiversity Targets.

434b69227d3e.title: Convention on Biological Diversity
434b69227d3e.section: Protocols and plans developed by CBD > Post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework
434b69227d3e.sentence: A new plan, known as the post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) was developed to guide action through 2030.

cb460daeb009.title: Protected area
cb460daeb009.sentence: Protected areas or conservation areas are locations that receive protection because of their recognized natural or cultural values.

c8b2c20aab40.title: Protected area
c8b2c20aab40.sentence: Protected areas are those areas in which human presence or the exploitation of natural resources (e.g. firewood, non-timber forest products, water,...) is limited.

8d065070c698.title: Protected area
8d065070c698.sentence: > A clearly defined geographical space, recognized, dedicated and managed, through legal or other effective means, to achieve the long-term conservation of nature with associated ecosystem services and cultural values.

8d3c18d1263a.title: Protected area
8d3c18d1263a.sentence: As of 2016, there are over 161,000 protected areas representing about 17 percent of the world's land surface area (excluding Antarctica).

995213ad4b82.title: Protected area
995213ad4b82.sentence: For waters under national jurisdiction beyond inland waters, there are 14,688 Marine Protected Areas (MPAs), covering approximately 10.2% of coastal and marine areas and 4.12% of global ocean areas.

5bdbc215075d.title: Protected area
5bdbc215075d.sentence: Although biodiversity is usually the main reason for constructing protected areas, the protection of biodiversity also protects the ecosystem services society enjoys.

4723df327c11.title: Protected area
4723df327c11.sentence: Under Article 8 of the CBD, parties who entered the treaty agreed to, among other things, "establish a system of protected areas".

04b2ed836365.title: Protected area
04b2ed836365.sentence: Protecting places and natural resources is by no means a modern concept, whether it be indigenous communities guarding sacred sites or the convention of European hunting reserves.

944b75c456c4.title: Protected area
944b75c456c4.sentence: Over 2000 years ago, royal decrees in India protected certain areas.

3aabdb7ebbaf.title: Protected area
3aabdb7ebbaf.sentence: Enforcing protected area boundaries is a costly and labour-heavy endeavour, particularly if the allocation of a new protected region places new restrictions on the use of resources by the native people which may lead to their subsequent displacement.

5c476d4d78f8.title: Protected area
5c476d4d78f8.sentence: This has troubled relationships between conservationists and rural communities in many protected regions and is often why many Wildlife Reserves and National Parks face the human threat of poaching for the illegal bushmeat or trophy trades, which are resorted to as an alternative form of substinence.

8b810e7ecc51.title: Genetic resources
8b810e7ecc51.sentence: Genetic resources are genetic material of actual or potential value, where genetic material means any material of plant, animal, microbial or other origin containing functional units of heredity.

0d211a4808e5.title: Genetic resources
0d211a4808e5.sentence: Genetic resources is one of the three levels of biodiversity defined by the Convention on Biological Diversity in Rio, 1992.

50c1328241ac.title: Genetic resources
50c1328241ac.sentence: - Germplasm, genetic resources that are preserved for various purposes such as breeding, preservation, and research

758e07ed3a8c.title: Access and Benefit Sharing Agreement
758e07ed3a8c.sentence: The CBD, which came into effect in 1992, acknowledged that each state had sovereign rights over the genetic resources found in its territory and gave the state government power to make decisions about access to these resources, unlike earlier agreements that regarded genetic resources as common heritage.

ce770fd39562.title: Access and Benefit Sharing Agreement
ce770fd39562.sentence: The common heritage approach has been criticized, particularly those from developing countries, because such a perception meant that their biological resources would be considered free to exploit without compensation, and the exploitation of their genetic resources would then lead to the commercialization of these products in industrialized nations.

44915179b341.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
44915179b341.sentence: The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), also called the Law of the Sea Convention or the Law of the Sea Treaty, is an international treaty that establishes a legal framework for all marine and maritime activities.

350e5b84502e.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
350e5b84502e.sentence: The convention resulted from the third United Nations Conference on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS III), which took place between 1973 and 1982.

dde49c6e10c3.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
dde49c6e10c3.sentence: The resulting convention came into force on 16 November 1994, one year after the 60th state, Guyana, ratified the treaty.

4525f826893d.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
4525f826893d.sentence: All waters beyond national boundaries were considered international waters: free to all nations, but belonging to none of them (the mare liberum principle propounded by Hugo Grotius).

7bdcda6c8d4d.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
7bdcda6c8d4d.sentence: The convention set the limit of various areas, measured from a carefully defined baseline.

4bf599a83a3e.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
4bf599a83a3e.sentence: - Exclusive economic zones: These extend 200 nmi (370 km; 230 mi) from the baseline.

c252a957e2f1.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
c252a957e2f1.sentence: It establishes an International Seabed Authority (ISA) to authorize seabed exploration and mining and collect and distribute the seabed mining royalty.

e129ed730656.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
e129ed730656.section: Part XII – Protecting the marine environment
e129ed730656.sentence: Part XII of UNCLOS contains special provisions for the protection of the marine environment, obligating all states to collaborate in this matter, as well as placing special obligations on flag states to ensure that ships under their flags adhere to international environmental regulations, often adopted by the IMO.

65c9693e53d2.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
65c9693e53d2.sentence: The convention has been ratified by 172 parties, which includes 168 UN member states, one UN Observer state (Palestine), two non-member states (the Cook Islands and Niue) and the European Union.

41710bac7815.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
41710bac7815.sentence: - United States (see United States and the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea)

496494427f9b.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
496494427f9b.sentence: In 2023, agreement was reached on a High Seas Treaty to be added as an instrument of the convention, to protect ocean life in international waters.

b8119dd6df87.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
b8119dd6df87.sentence: This was considered necessary because UNCLOS did not provide a framework for areas beyond national jurisdiction.

4678265df77c.title: Sustainable Development Goal 14
4678265df77c.sentence: Sustainable Development Goal 14 (Goal 14 or SDG 14) is about "Life below water" and is one of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals established by the United Nations in 2015.

2c124b437499.title: Sustainable Development Goal 14
2c124b437499.sentence: The official wording is to "Conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources for sustainable development".

1482b7f7547e.title: Sustainable Development Goal 14
1482b7f7547e.sentence: The Goal has ten targets to be achieved by 2030.

5cc2dba76889.title: Sustainable Development Goal 14
5cc2dba76889.sentence: The UN has defined 10 targets and 10 indicators for SDG 14 that include preventing and reducing marine pollution and ocean acidification, protecting marine and coastal ecosystems, and regulating fishing.

3672e7d4f2c5.title: Sustainable Development Goal 14
3672e7d4f2c5.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 14.5: Conserve coastal and marine areas
3672e7d4f2c5.sentence: The full title of Target 14.5 is: "By 2020, conserve at least 10 per cent of coastal and marine areas, consistent with national and international law and based on the best available scientific information".

e4bef2af713c.title: Sustainable Development Goal 14
e4bef2af713c.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 14.5: Conserve coastal and marine areas
e4bef2af713c.sentence: This target has one indicator: Indicator 14.5.1 is the "coverage of protected areas in relation to marine areas".

9f7a2adf8a25.title: Sustainable Development Goal 14
9f7a2adf8a25.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 14.4: Sustainable fishing
9f7a2adf8a25.sentence: This target has one indicator: Indicator 14.4.1 is "the proportion of fish stocks within biologically sustainable levels".

0dcb4f2ebcb9.title: Sustainable Development Goal 14
0dcb4f2ebcb9.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 14.3: Reduce ocean acidification
0dcb4f2ebcb9.sentence: The pH of the ocean now averages at 8.1, therefore the acidity of the ocean is around 30% more acidic than in pre-industrial times.

6d24fb34afc9.title: Sustainable Development Goal 14
6d24fb34afc9.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 14.4: Sustainable fishing
6d24fb34afc9.sentence: A report at the High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development in 2021 stated that: "Sustainable fisheries accounted for approximately 0.1 per cent of global GDP in 2017".

14453c3cf86e.title: Sustainable Development Goal 14
14453c3cf86e.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 14.a: Increase scientific knowledge, research and technology for ocean health
14453c3cf86e.sentence: Oceans cover over 70% of the Earths surface, yet from 2013 to 2021, only 1.1% of national research budgets were allocated for ocean science.

cba1b4425c28.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13
cba1b4425c28.sentence: Sustainable Development Goal 13 (SDG 13 or Global Goal 13) is the United Nations Global Goal to limit and adapt to climate change.

1aaee45ff9c9.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13
1aaee45ff9c9.sentence: The official mission statement of this goal is to "Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts".

cdc474323d56.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13
cdc474323d56.sentence: SDG 13 has five targets which are to be achieved by 2030.

39bd6dbc26df.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13
39bd6dbc26df.sentence: The targets include to strengthening resilience and adaptive capacity to climate-related disasters (Target 13.1), integrate climate change measures into policies and planning (Target 13.2), build knowledge and capacity to meet climate change (Target 13.3), implement the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (Target 13.a), and promote mechanisms to raise capacity for planning and management (Target 13.b).

d876acf1a979.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13
d876acf1a979.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 13.a: Implement the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
d876acf1a979.sentence: The full text of Target 13.a is: "Implement the commitment undertaken by developed-country parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change to a goal of mobilizing jointly $100 billion annually by 2020 from all sources to address the needs of developing countries in the context of meaningful mitigation actions and transparency on implementation and fully operationalize the Green Climate Fund through its capitalization as soon as possible."

2764327ae74f.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13
2764327ae74f.sentence: Under the 2015 Paris Agreement, nations collectively agreed to keep warming "well under 2 °C".

10d3b6e6faae.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13
10d3b6e6faae.sentence: However, with pledges made under the Agreement, global warming would still reach about 2.7 °C (4.9 °F) by the end of the century.

ad9d0342700f.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13
ad9d0342700f.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 13.2: Integrate climate change measures into policy and planning
ad9d0342700f.sentence: - Indicator 13.2.1: "Number of countries with nationally determined contributions, long-term strategies, national adaptation plans, strategies as reported in adaptation communications and national communications".

373c05ef7416.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13

373c05ef7416.sentence: This resulted in a 6% drop in greenhouse gas emissions from what was initially projected for 2020, however these improvements were only temporary.

1f7ef5041e2a.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13
1f7ef5041e2a.sentence: SDG 13 does not directly address the link between nations most vulnerable to climate change and increased migration flows (climate migration).

6309d15e33a1.title: Sustainable Development Goal 13
6309d15e33a1.sentence: It therefore misses the chance to recognize migration as an adaptive response of mobile populations.

a3fe528e7d19.title: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
a3fe528e7d19.sentence: It serves a similar role to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), though in addition to undertaking scientific assessments, IPBES also supports efforts to generate new knowledge, build capacity and promote the development and use of policy support tools.

511ce2b07928.title: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
511ce2b07928.sentence: In 2010 a resolution by the 65th session of the United Nations General Assembly urged the United Nations Environment Programme to convene a plenary meeting to establish IPBES.

294115ebc953.title: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
294115ebc953.sentence: IPBES parties meet every one to two years in sessions designated as Plenaries.

6516a2eb5854.title: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
6516a2eb5854.sentence: From 29 April to 4 May 2019, representatives of the 132 IPBES members met in Paris, France, to discuss the Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services and to adopt its summary for policymakers (SPM).

446e50b9acbc.title: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
446e50b9acbc.sentence: The report also emphasized that preventing pandemics through biodiversity conservation and reduced environmental degradation is more cost-effective than responding after outbreaks occur.

6732820545c1.title: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
6732820545c1.sentence: In October 2022, the IPBES and the IPCC shared the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity, because the two intergovernmental organisations "produce scientific knowledge, alert society, and inform decision-makers to make better choices for combatting climate change and the loss of biodiversity".

b176cf6060e2.title: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
b176cf6060e2.sentence: In January 2026, the United States announced its withdrawal from the organization.

d34b3272253c.title: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
d34b3272253c.sentence: On 6 May 2019, the 40-page document was released, aiming to empower policymakers with the knowledge and evidence to make better decisions when developing policies and taking actions for the benefit of humans and nature.

e61aa85aaa11.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
e61aa85aaa11.sentence: The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in Those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, Particularly in Africa (UNCCD) is a Convention to combat desertification and mitigate the effects of drought through national action programs that incorporate long-term strategies supported by international cooperation and partnership arrangements.

859b0116a0fd.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
859b0116a0fd.sentence: The Convention, the only convention stemming from a direct recommendation of the Rio Conference's Agenda 21, was adopted in Paris, France, on 17 June 1994 and entered into force in December 1996.

dde6478395dd.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
dde6478395dd.sentence: It is the only internationally legally binding framework set up to address the problem of desertification.

145f8d18fa49.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
145f8d18fa49.sentence: It has 197 parties, making it near universal in reach.

9f79625d064d.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
9f79625d064d.sentence: National Action Programmes (NAP) are one of the key instruments in the implementation of the Convention.

eeaca8d31436.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
eeaca8d31436.sentence: National Action Programmes are developed in the framework of a participative approach involving the local communities and they spell out the practical steps and measures to be taken to combat desertification in specific ecosystems.

d7f8e97a62fa.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
d7f8e97a62fa.sentence: At its thirteenth session in 2017, the Conference of the Parties adopted the UNCCD 2018–2030 Strategic Framework and encouraged parties to apply it in national policies, programmes, plans and processes related to desertification, land degradation and drought.

981979277c69.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
981979277c69.sentence: According to the UNCCD, parties at COP16 focused on land restoration, drought resilience and international cooperation, while more than US$12 billion was pledged to address desertification, land degradation and drought, especially in vulnerable countries.

0737378b637c.title: Biodiversity action plan
0737378b637c.sentence: A biodiversity action plan (BAP) is an internationally recognized program aimed at protecting and restoring threatened species and habitats, and at strengthening the resilience of biological systems.

d16c927f7596.title: Biodiversity action plan
d16c927f7596.sentence: The concept emerged from the 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), which called on participating nations to develop strategies for conserving biodiversity.

f2ec82833cfc.title: Biodiversity action plan
f2ec82833cfc.sentence: The core components of a typical BAP include: (a) compiling inventories of biological data for selected species or habitats; (b) assessing the conservation status of species within defined ecosystems; (c) setting clear targets for conservation and restoration; and (d) developing budgets, timelines, and institutional partnerships for implementation.

20a922f178fc.title: Biodiversity action plan
20a922f178fc.sentence: Once a determination has been made of conservation status (e.g. rare, endangered, threatened, vulnerable), a plan can then be created to conserve and restore the species population to target levels.

1a0f222401ee.title: Biodiversity action plan
1a0f222401ee.sentence: Where a number of threatened species depend upon a specific habitat, it may be appropriate to prepare a habitat protection element of the Biodiversity Action Plan.

5d4edceae519.title: Biodiversity action plan
5d4edceae519.sentence: Biodiversity Action Plans for agricultural production are necessary to ensure biodiversity friendly production.

592a7b3f740b.title: Biodiversity action plan
592a7b3f740b.sentence: As of 2009, 191 countries had ratified the CBD, although only a portion of them had produced comprehensive BAP documents.

6aa9c8364e6a.title: Biodiversity action plan
6aa9c8364e6a.sentence: Preparation of a country BAP may cost up to 100 million pounds sterling, with annual maintenance costs roughly ten percent of the initial cost.

9cbb7a0321c3.title: Biodiversity action plan
9cbb7a0321c3.sentence: The plans are costly to produce, a fact which makes it difficult for many smaller countries and poorer countries to comply.

99a30758b598.title: Biodiversity action plan
99a30758b598.sentence: In terms of the plans themselves, many countries have adopted pro-forma plans including little research and even less in the way of natural resource management.

1194d04c70f1.title: Biodiversity action plan
1194d04c70f1.sentence: Almost universally, this has resulted in plans which emphasize plants and vertebrate animals, and which overlook fungi, invertebrate animals and micro-organisms.

8d6714109349.title: Biodiversity action plan
8d6714109349.sentence: Some developing countries criticize the emphasis of BAPs, because these plans inherently favour consideration of wildlife protection above food and industrial production, and in some cases may represent an obstacle to population growth.

d8e283e13eea.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
d8e283e13eea.sentence: Sustainable Development Goal 15 (SDG 15 or Global Goal 15) is about "Life on land".

a5604b16bfac.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
a5604b16bfac.sentence: One of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals established by the United Nations in 2015, the official wording is: "Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss".

b1206ad32eaf.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
b1206ad32eaf.sentence: The Goal has 12 targets to be achieved by 2030.

f6a013d7da3a.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
f6a013d7da3a.sentence: Progress towards targets will be measured by 14 indicators.

3b211642c1da.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
3b211642c1da.sentence: The nine outcome targets include: Conserve and restore terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems; end deforestation and restore degraded forests; end desertification and restore degraded land; ensure conservation of mountain ecosystems, protect biodiversity and natural habitats; protect access to genetic resources and fair sharing of the benefits; eliminate poaching and trafficking of protected species; prevent invasive alien species on land and in water ecosystems; and integrate ecosystem and biodiversity in governmental planning.

4c75758a38b7.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
4c75758a38b7.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 15.1: Conserve and restore terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems
4c75758a38b7.sentence: Forests cover roughly 4 billion hectares or 30.7 per cent of the world's land area.

94d259196d35.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
94d259196d35.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 15.1: Conserve and restore terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems
94d259196d35.sentence: 93 percent are natural forests and 7 percent are planted.

b1e14d79d7c7.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
b1e14d79d7c7.section: Targets, indicators and progress > Target 15.9: Integrate ecosystem and biodiversity in governmental planning
b1e14d79d7c7.sentence: The full title of Target 15.9 is: "By 2020, integrate ecosystem and biodiversity values into national and local planning, development processes, poverty reduction strategies and accounts."

a7473590ab91.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
a7473590ab91.sentence: As of 2023, there is approximately a $700 billion gap in financial support to help low-income countries protect biodiversity.

82eee4aa92b3.title: Sustainable Development Goal 15
82eee4aa92b3.sentence: It is estimated that deforestation increased by 12% from 2019 to 2020, and plastic consumption and waste may also increase during pandemic.

1710b5096e81.title: World Heritage Site
1710b5096e81.sentence: World Heritage Sites are landmarks and areas with legal protection under an international treaty administered by UNESCO for having cultural, historical, or scientific significance.

9b21fe67e7a0.title: World Heritage Site
9b21fe67e7a0.sentence: The sites are judged to contain "cultural and natural heritage around the world considered to be of outstanding value to humanity".

137e2208a4e0.title: World Heritage Site
137e2208a4e0.sentence: Based on the draft convention that UNESCO had initiated, a single text was eventually agreed upon by all parties, and the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage was adopted by the General Conference of UNESCO on 16 November 1972.

dd6c5b667100.title: World Heritage Site
dd6c5b667100.sentence: The convention came into force on 17 December 1975.

35ad9aca0793.title: World Heritage Site
35ad9aca0793.sentence: As of November 2024, it has been ratified by 196 states: 192 UN member states, two UN observer states (the Holy See and the State of Palestine), and two states in free association with New Zealand (the Cook Islands and Niue).

41d03e6c48f2.title: World Heritage Site
41d03e6c48f2.sentence: Nominated sites must be of "outstanding universal value" and must meet at least one of the ten criteria.

7a7534e6745f.title: World Heritage Site
7a7534e6745f.sentence: - "To contain the most important and significant natural habitats for in-situ conservation of biological diversity, including those containing threatened species of outstanding universal value from the point of view of science or conservation"

dd1d4de3cc3c.title: World Heritage Site
dd1d4de3cc3c.sentence: A listed site gains international recognition and legal protection, and can obtain funds from, among others, the World Heritage Fund to facilitate its conservation under certain conditions.

85981ebd50b7.title: World Heritage Site
85981ebd50b7.sentence: Additionally, the local population around a site may benefit from significantly increased tourism revenue.

17048aef90ba.title: Biodiversity loss
17048aef90ba.section: Proposed solutions > Other international and national action
17048aef90ba.sentence: Nearly three-quarters of bird species, two thirds of mammals and more than half of hard corals have been recorded at World Heritage Sites, even though they cover less than 1% of the planet.

17560f54b849.title: World Heritage Site
17560f54b849.sentence: A site may be added to the List of World Heritage in Danger if conditions threaten the characteristics for which the landmark or area was inscribed on the World Heritage List.

d50a3118ca5d.title: World Heritage Site
d50a3118ca5d.sentence: Only three sites have ever been delisted: the Arabian Oryx Sanctuary in Oman, the Dresden Elbe Valley in Germany, and the Liverpool Maritime Mercantile City in the United Kingdom.

2c00eca1b9c3.title: World Heritage Site
2c00eca1b9c3.sentence: Site listing bids are often lengthy and costly, putting poorer countries at a disadvantage.

7f360ec75d77.section: List of wetlands of international importance
7f360ec75d77.sentence: The list of wetlands of international importance included 2,531 Ramsar sites in February 2025 covering over 2.6 million square kilometres (1,000,000 sq mi).

bef96cc84055.title: Ecological values of mangroves
bef96cc84055.sentence: To become a signatory to the Ramsar Convention, a country had to designate at least one such site and guarantee its protection.

531168717ca0.title: Ramsar Convention
531168717ca0.sentence: February 2 is World Wetlands Day, marking the convention's adoption on 2 February 1971.

11942775f678.title: Ramsar Convention
11942775f678.section: Deficiencies in the treaty and its implementation
11942775f678.sentence: Despite its quasi-universal application, the domestic response to this treaty is often half-hearted and inadequate.

54da37880df5.title: Ramsar Convention
54da37880df5.sentence: The conference, which adopted the terms of the agreement, was held in the Iranian Caspian Sea resort of Ramsar on 2 February 1971.

e0315fc9172b.title: Convention on Biological Diversity
e0315fc9172b.sentence: The Aichi Biodiversity Targets were 20 international goals set under the Convention to protect biodiversity, sustainable use of natural resources, and to protect species.

5b0119285011.sentence: The Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and the Fair and Equitable Sharing of Benefits Arising from their Utilization to the Convention on Biological Diversity, also known as the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS), is a 2010 supplementary agreement to the 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).

9e62b3f7f475.title: Access and Benefit Sharing Agreement

5f729ed34b40.title: Nagoya Protocol

839168f58289.title: Access and Benefit Sharing Agreement

342e92c20826.sentence: The term differs from indigenous land rights, Aboriginal title or Native Title by directly indicating relationship to land based on ancestry, while domain indicates relationships beyond material lands and territories, including spiritual and cultural aspects that may not be acknowledged in land titles and legal doctrine about trading ownership.

83f18d1a1123.title: Ancestral domain

9066ec247e6c.title: Ancestral domain

0970e17daff5.title: Ancestral domain

f26a7da5b862.title: Ancestral domain

3117733abe13.title: Ancestral domain

7adea19244d9.title: Ancestral domain

f8e9dabbcd9f.title: Feminist political ecology
f8e9dabbcd9f.sentence: Feminist political ecology is a feminist approach within political ecology that draws on various theoretical traditions, including Marxism, post-structuralism, feminist geography, ecofeminism, and cultural ecology.

98ed943c59d7.title: Feminist political ecology
98ed943c59d7.sentence: Scholars in this field argue that gender is an important factor in shaping access to, control over, and knowledge of natural resources, and that mainstream environmental policies often rely on gender-neutral assumptions that can overlook women's knowledge of resource management.

08c181d9fa8a.title: Feminist political ecology
08c181d9fa8a.sentence: Feminist political ecology thus combines three areas it considers to be gendered: knowledge, environmental rights, and grassroots activism.

cd572b637035.title: Feminist political ecology
cd572b637035.sentence: Feminist political ecology argues that differences in environmental experience should not be explained as biological, but as shaped by social constructs of gender that vary by culture, class, race, location, and historical period.

e41de3b7d705.title: Feminist political ecology
e41de3b7d705.sentence: A commonly cited publication in the development of this field is the 1996 book Feminist Political Ecology by Dianne Rocheleau et al which shows how gender shapes environment and labor patterns, and how environmental problems affect women in specific ways.

9bea621ba012.title: Rights of nature law

42ae8f60e2f1.title: Rights of nature law

5c2c0d347747.title: Rights of nature law

The Article adds enforcement language as well, stating that "Any person... may demand the observance of the rights of the natural environment before public bodies", and echoing Christopher Stone, Article 72 adds that “Nature has the right to be completely restored... independent of the obligation... to compensate people”.

1289e8650068.title: Poverty
1289e8650068.sentence: Poverty is a state or condition in which an individual lacks the financial resources and essentials for a basic standard of living.

cbe1d6d69361.title: Poverty
cbe1d6d69361.sentence: When evaluating poverty in statistics or economics there are two main measures: absolute poverty which compares income against the amount needed to meet basic personal needs, such as food, clothing, and shelter; secondly, relative poverty measures when a person cannot meet a minimum level of living standards, compared to others in the same time and place.

4962a526ce92.title: Poverty
4962a526ce92.sentence: The "dollar a day" poverty line was first introduced in 1990 as a measure to meet such standards of living.

a6e8bceb9569.title: Poverty
a6e8bceb9569.sentence: From 1993 through 2005, the World Bank defined absolute poverty as $1.08 a day on such a purchasing power parity basis, after adjusting for inflation to the 1993 US dollar In 2009, it was updated as $1.25 a day (equivalent to $1.00 a day in 1996 US prices) and in 2015, it was updated as living on less than US$1.90 per day, and moderate poverty as less than $2 or $5 a day.

64ad2ae21a17.title: Poverty
64ad2ae21a17.sentence: Rather, it is determined by the purchasing power parity rate, which would look at how much local currency is needed to buy the same things that a dollar could buy in the United States.

feb1f4aa4c14.title: Poverty
feb1f4aa4c14.sentence: Statistically, as of 2019, most of the world's population live in poverty: in PPP dollars, 85% of people live on less than $30 per day, two-thirds live on less than $10 per day, and 10% live on less than $1.90 per day.

b2f71950edd5.title: Poverty

0ad8cb616b4d.title: Poverty

6d9b49f2429b.title: Poverty

065aabc61ea4.title: Sustainable livelihood

52de714b6b3d.title: Sustainable livelihood
52de714b6b3d.sentence: The term reflects a concern with extending the focus of poverty studies beyond the physical manifestations of poverty to include also vulnerability and social exclusion.

2167d0dec2fa.title: Sustainable livelihood
2167d0dec2fa.sentence: The sustainable livelihoods idea was first introduced by the Brundtland Commission on Environment and Development, and the 1992 United Nations' Conference on Environment and Development expanded the concept, advocating for the achievement of sustainable livelihoods as a broad goal for poverty eradication.

985f83d7535b.title: Sustainable livelihood
985f83d7535b.sentence: The sustainable livelihood approach focuses on finding resolutions to the problems of vulnerable communities by creating human-centered, participatory, and dynamic development opportunities.

9f6799729871.title: Sustainable livelihood
9f6799729871.sentence: Stemming from theory regarding sustainable development, a sustainable livelihood approach incorporates the collective concerns for environmental and economic resources and individual focus.

d6a74003b75c.title: Sustainable business
d6a74003b75c.sentence: Sustainable business refers to business practices that aim to engage in business activities while minimizing negative impacts on the global or local environment, community, and society.

232b2f264585.title: Sustainable business
232b2f264585.sentence: Businesses that undertake these practices aim to achieve the triple bottom line: profit, people, and the planet, by integrating environmental, economic, and social considerations when making business decisions.

50cd8e10a0ed.title: Sustainable business

cf29504c8fc5.title: Sustainable business

68c9ff68dc16.title: Sustainable business

f8ccdf0e25d4.title: Sustainable business

d2195c8eaa1d.sentence: If an organization’s current business model is inherently unsustainable, becoming truly sustainable requires a complete makeover of the business model (e.g. from selling cars to offering car sharing and other mobility services).

ef1779d5bb5d.title: Sustainable business
ef1779d5bb5d.sentence: Companies often comply with the lowest economic, social and environmental sustainability standards, when in fact the true sustainability can be achieved when the business is focused beyond compliance with integrated strategy and purpose.

531285fcc183.title: Nature-positive
531285fcc183.sentence: Nature-positive is a concept and goal to halt and reverse nature loss by 2030, and to achieve full nature recovery by 2050.

9bb8e7bc145b.title: Nature-positive
9bb8e7bc145b.sentence: Nature positive was defined by the Nature Positive Initiative as a global societal goal to "halt and reverse nature loss by 2030 on a 2020 baseline, and achieve full recovery by 2050." This means that progress towards stopping the loss of nature would be measured relative to levels of biodiversity in 2020.

d280f529fa99.title: Nature-positive
d280f529fa99.sentence: The nature-positive goal aligns with the 2030 mission and 2050 vision of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF).

a1fad38f25fb.title: Nature-positive
a1fad38f25fb.sentence: However, the GBF does not explicitly mention nature positive.

e03072c4b15d.title: Nature-positive
e03072c4b15d.sentence: By 2020, proponents of nature positive argued that there was no concise headline goal to address biodiversity loss – while the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development proposes equitable human development, the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change puts forward a carbon-neutral goal of net zero emissions for 2050, and the Paris Climate Change Agreement aims to limit global warming to 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels, there was no equivalent for biodiversity loss.

463d4500c374.title: Nature-positive
463d4500c374.sentence: Nature positive was therefore proposed as a "global goal for nature" to integrate with climate and development goals and direct future global agreements to an "Equitable, Nature-Positive, Carbon Neutral world."

5e4404bfcd9b.title: Nature-positive
5e4404bfcd9b.section: Definition > Distinction from existing policy approaches
5e4404bfcd9b.sentence: The scope of nature positive extends beyond direct impacts, to the whole value chain of a company (all activities needed to deliver goods or services to customers) of a company and to sector-wide for transformative improvements in sustainability practices.

536b87eaf193.title: Nature-positive
536b87eaf193.section: Definition > Distinction from existing policy approaches
536b87eaf193.sentence: It also aims to scale against global or regional societal goals to achieve absolute gains for biodiversity, instead of relative gains.

8675f0bf207d.title: Nature-positive
8675f0bf207d.sentence: Over 90 world leaders have signed the Leaders' Pledge for Nature, which calls for a nature-positive future by 2030.

0c9e6be164bc.title: Nature-positive
0c9e6be164bc.sentence: A commitment to nature positive was also signed by the members of the G7 at the 47th summit in 2021 and a G7 Alliance on Nature Positive Economies has since been launched.

93cab7e03f2d.title: Nature-positive
93cab7e03f2d.sentence: Nature-positive has been criticised as vague and vulnerable to greenwashing.

34a2f224a01f.title: Nature-positive
34a2f224a01f.sentence: Concerns have also been raised over the vulnerability of nature positive to greenwashing, the "net" approach to biodiversity, and over the "financialization of nature".

78f99e22cd79.title: Nature-positive
78f99e22cd79.sentence: In a 2022 paper, E.J. Milner-Gulland proposed that, to avoid greenwashing, the nature-positive goal requires a measured biodiversity baseline, a timeframe, a target, a clear set of actions, an analysis of how these actions will add up to reach net gain, regular monitoring, and disclosure of progress.

452a7b58cdbc.title: Nature-positive
452a7b58cdbc.sentence: This implies that loss and degradation of biodiversity will continue.

ab125cdeb1da.title: Environmental management system
ab125cdeb1da.sentence: An environmental management system (EMS) is "a system which integrates policy, procedures and processes for training of personnel, monitoring, summarizing, and reporting of specialized environmental performance information to internal and external stakeholders of a firm".

488bba605c29.title: Environmental management system
488bba605c29.sentence: The most widely used standard on which an EMS is based is International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 14001.

2f601b59c198.title: Environmental management system
2f601b59c198.sentence: The goals of EMS are to increase compliance and reduce waste:

f6265961a761.title: Environmental management system
f6265961a761.sentence: - Compliance is the act of reaching and maintaining minimal legal standards.

f5156440f9a6.title: Environmental management system
f5156440f9a6.sentence: - Waste reduction goes beyond compliance to reduce environmental impact.

1e76f3fdfad0.title: Environmental audit
1e76f3fdfad0.sentence: An EMS meeting the requirements of ISO 14001 is a management tool enabling an organization of any size or type to:

f0dff0737002.title: Environmental audit
f0dff0737002.sentence: - Identify and control the environmental impact of its activities, products or services;

5d9342fe9030.title: Environmental audit
5d9342fe9030.sentence: - Improve its environmental performance continually, and

8878cb50a764.title: Environmental audit
8878cb50a764.sentence: - Implement a systematic approach to setting environmental objectives and targets, to achieving these and to demonstrating that they have been achieved.

bfc8a641bcb4.title: Environmental management system
bfc8a641bcb4.sentence: An EMS follows a Plan-Do-Check-Act, or PDCA, Cycle.

845b4b98e52d.title: Environmental management system
845b4b98e52d.sentence: The model is continuous because an EMS is a process of continual improvement in which an organization is constantly reviewing and revising the system.

d9a74dc2d1f2.title: Environmental management system
d9a74dc2d1f2.sentence: This is a model that can be used by a wide range of organizations – from manufacturing facilities to service industries to government agencies.

85d7942aeaa3.title: Environmental audit
85d7942aeaa3.sentence: Organizations implementing ISO 14001 usually seek to obtain certification by independent Certification Bodies.

1dbb7ab40c17.title: Environmental audit
1dbb7ab40c17.sentence: Certification indicates that the documentation, implementation and effectiveness of the EMS conform to the specific requirements of ISO 14001.

98aedf190d87.title: Environmental management system
98aedf190d87.sentence: - Encourages contractors and suppliers to establish their own EMS.

d3e1d3dbd9dc.title: Environmental audit
d3e1d3dbd9dc.sentence: An environmental audit is a type of evaluation intended to identify environmental compliance and management system implementation gaps, along with related corrective actions.

08c068d9bf28.title: Environmental audit
08c068d9bf28.sentence: In this way they perform an analogous (similar) function to financial audits.

70922a42e96d.title: Environmental audit
70922a42e96d.sentence: There are generally two different types of environmental audits: compliance audits and management systems audits.

f50b3f41e6e4.title: Environmental audit
f50b3f41e6e4.sentence: Environmental compliance audits are intended to review the site's/company's legal compliance status in an operational context.

4faefab413b2.title: Environmental audit
4faefab413b2.sentence: Compliance audits generally begin with determining the applicable legal compliance requirements against which the operations will be assessed.

5f56feceb453.title: Environmental audit
5f56feceb453.sentence: This tends to include federal regulations, state regulations, permits and local ordinances/codes.

6a37750406ee.title: Environmental audit
6a37750406ee.sentence: Compliance audits may be multimedia or programmatic.

52830ed8b90c.title: Environmental audit
52830ed8b90c.sentence: Multimedia audits involve identifying and auditing all environmental media (air, water, waste, etc.) that apply to the operation/company.

05593333feab.title: Environmental audit
05593333feab.sentence: Programmatic audits (which may also be called thematic or media-specific) are limited in scope to pre-identified regulatory areas, such as air.

88f528e12566.title: Environmental audit
88f528e12566.sentence: A common misconception is that ISO 14001 certification automatically implies legal compliance.

f95d94a8f6c4.title: Environmental audit
f95d94a8f6c4.sentence: Certification under ISO 14001 does not directly reflect compliance with any legal requirements or regulations, although ISO 14001 demands the organization to evaluate its compliance with legal requirements.

b061b03e623b.title: Environmental audit
b061b03e623b.sentence: The term "protocol" means the checklist used by environmental auditors as the guide for conducting the audit activities.

9c71c91ed73f.title: Environmental audit
9c71c91ed73f.sentence: There is no standard protocol, either in form or content.

414978d679ee.title: Environmental audit
414978d679ee.sentence: There is a long-standing debate among environmental audit professionals on the value of large, highly detailed and prescriptive protocols (i.e., that can, in theory, be completed by an auditor with little or no technical experience) versus more flexible protocols that rely on the expertise and knowledge of experienced auditors and source documents (regulations, permits, etc.) directly.

8707c9f2a78c.title: Environmental audit
8707c9f2a78c.sentence: An emerging technology in environmental auditing is the use of Satellite imagery and Geographic Information Systems.

b440990030dd.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
b440990030dd.sentence: The EU taxonomy for sustainable activities (a green taxonomy) is a classification system established to clarify which economic activities are environmentally sustainable, in the context of the European Green Deal.

2a4a4253c63d.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
2a4a4253c63d.sentence: The aim of the taxonomy is to prevent greenwashing and to help investors make informed sustainable investment decisions.

ed1d656939a8.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
ed1d656939a8.sentence: The Taxonomy covers activities contributing to six environmental objectives: climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation, the transition to a circular economy, pollution prevention and control, sustainable use and protection of water and marine resources, and protection and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems.

117c81df97a8.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
117c81df97a8.sentence: The Taxonomy came into force in July 2020.

c00a9e724369.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
c00a9e724369.sentence: The European Union (EU) Taxonomy was implemented as part of the European Green Deal initiatives.

33f216de66c3.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
33f216de66c3.sentence: The EU launched the European Green Deal in line with the Paris Agreement goals, setting out the objectives to achieve a carbon neutral economy by 2050.

4b0a2d72c308.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
4b0a2d72c308.sentence: The preparatory work started in 2018, when the Commission set up a Technical Expert Group on Sustainable Finance, to assist in developing the EU Taxonomy, with the OECD as an observer.

d0bf09aa72f4.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
d0bf09aa72f4.sentence: In the case of Taxonomy, the main task of the TEG was to develop technical screening criteria that would be used to determine whether an activity is environmentally sustainable.

c68743062871.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
c68743062871.sentence: The Environmental Delegated Act covering the 4 remaining environmental objectives in the EU Taxonomy was formally published in the Official Journal of the European Union on 21 November 2023.

f3751eaf96a5.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
f3751eaf96a5.sentence: Essentially, it outlines Technical Screening Criteria for selected economic activities under the following objectives: I) Sustainable use and protection of water and marine resources; II) Transition to a circular economy; III) Pollution prevention and control; and IV) Protection and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems.

53978aa1a938.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
53978aa1a938.sentence: In March 2021, the EBA proposed to oblige banks to disclose a "green asset ratio" and other KPIs, effective as of 2024.

a7dcf1c49ce7.title: EU taxonomy for sustainable activities
a7dcf1c49ce7.sentence: According to early estimates, EU banks had an average green asset ratio of 2.23%.

90e75520ef60.title: Sustainable finance
90e75520ef60.sentence: To date, there are no regulations requiring the borrower to specify its "green" intentions in writing, however, the EU is currently developing a green bond standard which will force issuers to fund activities aligned with the EU taxonomy for sustainable activities.

6f7d933b43d5.title: Design for the environment
6f7d933b43d5.sentence: Design for the environment (DfE) is a design approach to reduce the overall human health and environmental impact of a product, process or service, where impacts are considered across its life cycle.

fc9fbdb70e1c.title: Design for the environment
fc9fbdb70e1c.sentence: Four main concepts that fall under the DfE umbrella.

04cd98f5dd7f.title: Design for the environment
04cd98f5dd7f.sentence: - Design for environmental processing and manufacturing: Raw material extraction (mining, drilling, etc.), processing (processing reusable materials, metal melting, etc.) and manufacturing are done using materials and processes which are not dangerous to the environment or the employees working on said processes.

fbdac058e948.title: Design for the environment
fbdac058e948.sentence: - Design for environmental packaging: Materials used in packaging are environmentally responsible, which can be achieved through the reuse of shipping products, elimination of unnecessary paper and packaging products, efficient use of materials and space, use of recycled and/or recyclable materials.

24071474a94f.title: Design for the environment
24071474a94f.sentence: - Design for disposal or reuse: The end-of-life of a product is very important, because some products emit dangerous chemicals into the air, ground and water after they are disposed of in a landfill.

e31f5ead3eba.title: Design for the environment
e31f5ead3eba.sentence: - Design for energy efficiency: The design of products to reduce overall energy consumption throughout the product's life.

763cd273b3d9.title: Design for the environment
763cd273b3d9.sentence: Life-cycle assessment (LCA) is employed to forecast the impacts of different (production) alternatives of the product in question, thus being able to choose the most environmentally friendly.

c1e8914303f8.title: Design for the environment
c1e8914303f8.sentence: The benefits of incorporating DfE include: cost savings, reduced business and environmental risks, expanded business and market opportunities, and to meet environmental regulations.

470ac01516be.title: Sustainable business
470ac01516be.sentence: Designing for the environment (DFE) is also an element of sustainable business.

711a91889c40.title: Sustainable business
711a91889c40.sentence: Sustainable business leaders also take into account the life cycle costs for the items they produce.

d9e27060b8de.title: Sustainable business
d9e27060b8de.sentence: Corporate sustainability strategies can aim to take advantage of sustainable revenue opportunities, while protecting the value of business against increasing energy costs, the costs of meeting regulatory requirements, changes in the way customers perceive brands and products, the volatile price of resources.

f03910dfe4f5.title: Sustainable business
f03910dfe4f5.sentence: The widely practiced strategies include Innovation, Collaboration, Process Improvement and Sustainability reporting.

7e44aa5e243a.title: Sustainable business
7e44aa5e243a.sentence: - Greening the Supply Chain: Sustainable procurement is important for any sustainability strategy as a company's impact on the environment is much bigger than the products that they consume.

8a156d97f4a7.title: Sustainable business
8a156d97f4a7.sentence: The Sustainability Balanced Scorecard is a performance measurement and management system aiming at balancing financial and non-financial as well as short and long-term measures.

f5998d0b154e.title: Sustainable business

ea581f4ed42d.sentence: A 2023 Swiss survey of 514 SMEs reported that 89% had never produced a sustainability report, citing limited internal resources and unfamiliarity with international standards as main barriers.

5c22cf74d10c.title: World Resources Institute
5c22cf74d10c.sentence: WRI worked with companies to develop a common standard, the Greenhouse Gas Protocol for quantifying and managing GHG emissions.

d857cd9bb6fe.title: Carbon accounting

7525f89e53e2.sentence: The Greenhouse Gas Protocol (for carbon accounting of organizations) calls these Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions.

463b52d2b9aa.title: Carbon footprint

15473bfe72cd.title: Corporate social responsibility
15473bfe72cd.sentence: One motivation for corporations to adopt CSR is to satisfy stakeholders beyond those of a corporation's shareholders.

baad9646cdef.title: Corporate social responsibility
baad9646cdef.sentence: The term stakeholder was coined in English by Eric Rhenman, a Swedish management scholar, in his 1968 book named Industrial Democracy and Industrial Management..

ba00f85c58e8.title: Corporate social responsibility
ba00f85c58e8.sentence: Robert Edward Freeman elaborated on Rhenman's initial conceptualization of stakeholder theory in his landmark book Strategic Management: A Stakeholder Approach.

0e5a91aadd8b.title: Corporate social responsibility

4284e354853f.title: Corporate environmental responsibility

7e8213a7e6da.title: Corporate social responsibility
7e8213a7e6da.sentence: The stakeholder perspective fails to acknowledge the complexity of network interactions in cross-sector partnerships.

a129bda27870.title: Corporate social responsibility
a129bda27870.sentence: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) refers to companies conducting their core operations in a responsible and sustainable way to create a positive corporate social impact.

e0f2a469fc61.title: Corporate social responsibility
e0f2a469fc61.sentence: It is a form of international private business self-regulation, which aims to contribute to societal and environmental goals by reducing harm.

e4c73b2f7caa.title: Corporate social responsibility
e4c73b2f7caa.sentence: For instance, by reducing a company's carbon footprint or increasing positive outcomes for all stakeholders.

edf792f22d73.title: Corporate social responsibility
edf792f22d73.sentence: Since the 1960s, corporate social responsibility has attracted attention from a range of businesses, academics and stakeholders and been referred to by a number of other terms, including "corporate sustainability", "sustainable business", "corporate conscience", "corporate citizenship", "purpose", "social impact", "conscious capitalism", and "responsible business".

0f532a766b18.title: Corporate social responsibility
0f532a766b18.sentence: A wide variety of definitions have been developed, but with little consensus.

e2ec89b99dcf.title: Corporate social responsibility
e2ec89b99dcf.sentence: A business person may define CSR as a business strategy, an NGO activist may see it as 'greenwash' while a government official may see it as voluntary regulation.

b19212cb3064.title: Corporate social responsibility
b19212cb3064.sentence: Howard R. Bowen's 1953 book, Social Responsibilities of the Businessman, is widely regarded as the foundational work in modern CSR and "regarded as a classic in the fields of business ethics and management".

5c8306826b0e.title: Corporate social responsibility
5c8306826b0e.sentence: Bowen was among the first to theorize that, because businesses have significant influence over society, business leaders have responsibilities that go beyond generating profit and should consider the wider social consequences of their decisions.

7570fc27e0fc.title: Corporate social responsibility
7570fc27e0fc.sentence: Businesses engage in CSR for strategic, ethical, or instrumental reasons.

df0caf03aea9.title: Corporate social responsibility
df0caf03aea9.sentence: For publicly listed companies, CSR often takes the form of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices and reports, but many companies have pledged to go beyond that.

994ee496c3ce.title: Corporate social responsibility
994ee496c3ce.sentence: Further, CSR has been considered a form of corporate self-regulation, shifting from voluntary decisions at the level of individual organizations to mandatory schemes at regional, national, and international levels.

39845149aefc.title: Corporate social responsibility
39845149aefc.sentence: Initially, CSR emphasized the official behaviour of individual firms.

f7b5b952f38e.title: Corporate social responsibility
f7b5b952f38e.sentence: Later, it expanded to include supplier behaviour, the uses to which products were put, and how articles were disposed of after they lost value.

38b77b9bdc38.title: Corporate social responsibility
38b77b9bdc38.sentence: Proponents argue that corporations increase long-term profits by operating with a CSR perspective, while critics argue that CSR distracts from businesses' economic role.

3bd6dfa4820e.title: Corporate social responsibility
3bd6dfa4820e.sentence: Critics have questioned the "lofty" and sometimes "unrealistic expectations" of CSR, or observed that CSR is merely window-dressing, or an attempt to pre-empt the role of governments as a watchdog over powerful multinational corporations.

239df262abe2.title: Sustainability reporting
239df262abe2.sentence: Sustainability reporting refers to the disclosure, whether voluntary, solicited, or required, of non-financial performance information to outsiders of the organization.

07f21a31337e.title: Sustainability reporting
07f21a31337e.sentence: Sustainability reporting deals with qualitative and quantitative information concerning environmental, social, economic, and governance issues.

c9ea2488b242.title: Sustainability reporting
c9ea2488b242.sentence: These are the criteria often gathered under the acronym ESG (environmental, social and corporate governance).

2b9b24a8ec4e.title: Sustainability reporting
2b9b24a8ec4e.sentence: There is a wide range of terminology used to qualify this same concept of sustainability reporting: ESG reporting, non-financial reporting, extra-financial reporting, social reporting, CSR reporting, and socio-economic and socio-environmental reporting.

2f9e2a632747.title: Sustainability reporting
2f9e2a632747.sentence: Corporate sustainability reporting has a history linked to environmental reporting.

4daeeb93b545.title: Sustainability reporting
4daeeb93b545.sentence: Early examples have been traced to the seventeenth and late nineteenth centuries and environmental reporting became popular in the 1970s.

0f499680df72.title: Sustainability reporting
0f499680df72.sentence: The practice of sustainability reporting has existed in a scattered way since the 1980s but has really expanded over the last twenty years.

1e7aa9d20c68.title: Sustainability reporting
1e7aa9d20c68.sentence: Corporate sustainability reporting practice is rooted in the multidimensional concept of CSR and in the stakeholders model of corporate governance in Europe, which places emphasis on the importance of understanding the company as an entity with relationships with its stakeholders and the environment.

af05d82329cf.title: Sustainability reporting

395b533075b0.title: Sustainability reporting
395b533075b0.sentence: This is notably due to the global awareness of the ecological crisis and the common interest in sustainable development, but also to the numerous corporate governance scandals of large companies (Enron scandal, Parmalat Financial Fraud...) over the last two decades or the 2008 financial crisis.

04b7bf2e9e85.title: Sustainability reporting

8bb36d507ff7.title: Sustainability reporting
8bb36d507ff7.sentence: Such behaviour can be associated with the practice known as greenwashing.

01efda5bef79.sentence: Today, Bloomberg and Reuters provide "environmental, social, and governance" ratings directly to the financial data screens of hundreds of thousands of stock market traders.

56f26cb6a3b8.sentence: Friedman argued each person should be free to spend their own money on social causes if they wished, but that business owners should avoid putting a "tax" on consumers as "unwitting puppets" of socialism by raising prices to support business practices with social goals unrelated to profit.

7591f8e631a3.sentence: In the 1930s, two law professors, A. A. c27f9395b1eb.title: Sustainability reporting
c27f9395b1eb.sentence: The directive provides a uniform regulatory framework for non-financial information for EU Member States.

2d4491a38d90.title: Sustainability reporting

2d4491a38d90.sentence: The CSRD was adopted in December 2022 and came into force on January 5, 2023.

581ee74cc5a2.title: Sustainability reporting

581ee74cc5a2.sentence: Its provisions apply progressively from January 1, 2024, depending on company size and type.

9bf9b01e7d42.title: Sustainability reporting

9bf9b01e7d42.sentence: The CSRD initially increased the scope of reporting entities to about 50.000 organizations in Europe.

7539c27a83ff.sentence: All companies exceeding two of the following three thresholds are required to publish a sustainability report: i) 250 employees; ii) Balance sheet of €25 million; and iii) Net turnover of €50 million.

989638edc06d.title: Sustainability reporting

989638edc06d.sentence: However, on 26 February 2025 the European Commission proposed a legislative package to simplify EU rules and boost competitiveness (known as Omnibus package).

903c46f8fe41.title: Nature-positive

903c46f8fe41.sentence: This involves embedding nature in decision-making, governance, strategy, and management of risks – a process described as mainstreaming.

aa7484491b66.title: Nature-positive

aa7484491b66.sentence: Mainstreaming distinguishes nature positive from NNL and NPI approaches, where biodiversity considerations are generally dealt with by ecological managers at project sites.

84bb4a0ba790.title: Economic analysis of climate change
84bb4a0ba790.sentence: Policymakers and investors are beginning to recognize the implications of climate change for the financial sector, from both physical risks (damage to property, infrastructure, and land) and transition risk due to changes in policy, technology, and consumer and market behavior.

f16dc2057be1.title: Sustainable finance
f16dc2057be1.sentence: - Climate finance and transition risk – the financial implications of climate change, including carbon pricing, stranded assets, and the role of instruments such as green bonds.

b75d6a512ad5.title: Carbon bubble
b75d6a512ad5.sentence: In 2015, Mark Carney, the Governor of the Bank of England, in his lecture to Lloyd's of London, warned that limiting global warming to 2 °C appears to require that the "vast majority" of fossil fuel reserves be "stranded assets", or "literally unburnable without expensive carbon-capture technology", resulting in "potentially huge" exposure to investors in that sector.

0d56b100f9ad.title: Supply chain sustainability
0d56b100f9ad.sentence: Consumers increasingly demand transparency and traceability in supply chains, especially where disturbing social breakdowns occur, such as with forced labour and child labour for globally traded goods.

b8daaacf9f7c.title: Supply chain sustainability
b8daaacf9f7c.sentence: Forced labor, understood as work that is performed involuntarily or under coercion, occurs in different industries, often upstream in the supply chain with limited visibility to buyers, customers, and end-users.

fbabe92ef558.title: Sustainable consumption

fbabe92ef558.sentence: Transparency of supply chains is important for global goals such as ending net-deforestation.
