8d93ed92c09f.sentence: Transparency in the supply chain influences how consumers view and support companies, so improving data driven sustainability efforts can positively affect supply chain business.

c01a5e5acef6.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
c01a5e5acef6.sentence: The United Nations Conference on the Human Environment was held in Stockholm, Sweden, during June 5–16, 1972.

727ad5c21e0b.title: Earth Summit
727ad5c21e0b.sentence: The 1972 United Nations Conference on the Human Environment (UNCHE) or the Stockholm Conference, was the first global conference to address environmental issues.

fa8506846b24.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
fa8506846b24.sentence: Sweden first suggested to the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) in 1968 the idea of having a UN conference to focus on human interactions with the environment.

39c50edcb568.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
39c50edcb568.sentence: Preparations for the conference were extensive, lasting four years, including 114 governments, and costing over $30,000,000.

d5a6f0fdd9cd.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
d5a6f0fdd9cd.sentence: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) was created as a result of this conference.

f603d6bc9cf0.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
f603d6bc9cf0.sentence: Developing nations supported the creation of the UNEP, not because they supported environmental governance, but because of its headquarters' location in Nairobi, Kenya, as the UNEP would be the first UN agency to be based in a developing country.

0421372518e2.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
0421372518e2.sentence: The meeting agreed upon a Declaration containing 26 principles concerning the environment and development, an Action Plan with 109 recommendations, and a Resolution.

27ae895e1550.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
27ae895e1550.sentence: At the conference itself, divisions between developed and developing countries began to emerge.

59d6b6dcbd2d.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
59d6b6dcbd2d.sentence: This stance emboldened other developing countries, which made up 70 of the 122 countries attending.

75bf4b514819.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
75bf4b514819.sentence: The Soviet Union and other Warsaw Pact nations boycotted the conference due to the lack of inclusion of East Germany, which was not allowed to participate.

f92b93fb9050.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
f92b93fb9050.sentence: One of the seminal issues that emerged from the conference is the recognition for poverty alleviation for protecting the environment.

08ad9a114b60.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
08ad9a114b60.sentence: The Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in her seminal speech in the conference brought forward the connection between ecological management and poverty alleviation.

dddc9dd188ef.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
dddc9dd188ef.sentence: The Stockholm Conference motivated countries around the world to monitor environmental conditions as well as to create environmental ministries and agencies.

d7ca3dc45129.title: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
d7ca3dc45129.sentence: The succeeding United Nations Conference on Environment and Development convened in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 (the Rio Earth Summit), the 2002 World Summit on Sustainable Development in Johannesburg and the 2012 United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development (Rio+20) all take their starting point in the declaration of the Stockholm Conference.

d2eecd3ac704.title: Earth Summit
d2eecd3ac704.sentence: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), also known as the Rio de Janeiro Conference or the Earth Summit (Portuguese: ECO92, Cúpula da Terra), was a major United Nations conference held in Rio de Janeiro from 3 to 14 June 1992.

dfdc1de948bb.title: Earth Summit
dfdc1de948bb.sentence: The Rio conference was attended by 108 heads of state and government, and helped establish and disseminate the concept of sustainable development.

a23681b1bf84.title: Earth Summit
a23681b1bf84.sentence: A key achievement of the 1992 conference was the establishment of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) established in part as an international environmental treaty to combat "dangerous human interference with the climate system" and to stabilize greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere.

06ab87f312f2.title: Earth Summit
06ab87f312f2.sentence: It was signed by 154 states at the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED).

f80a741c0dab.title: Earth Summit
f80a741c0dab.sentence: An important achievement of the summit was an agreement on the Climate Change Convention, which in turn led to the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement.

43022d6bc824.title: Earth Summit
43022d6bc824.sentence: The Convention on Biological Diversity was opened for signature at the Earth Summit and made a start towards a redefinition of measures that did not inherently encourage the destruction of natural ecoregions and so-called uneconomic growth.

8e3bec2eabe7.title: Earth Summit
8e3bec2eabe7.sentence: - Rio Declaration on Environment and Development

30ec956f6f79.title: Earth Summit
30ec956f6f79.sentence: In order to ensure compliance to the agreements at Rio (particularly the Rio Declaration on Environment and Development and Agenda 21), delegates to the Earth Summit established the Commission on Sustainable Development (CSD).

d77070aa3345.title: Earth Summit
d77070aa3345.sentence: The Earth Summit played an influential role in diffusing several key principles of environmental treaties, such as the precautionary principle, common but differentiated responsibilities, and the polluter pays principle.

c06f5e94c8f0.title: Earth Summit
c06f5e94c8f0.sentence: Critics point out that many of the agreements made in Rio have not been realized regarding such fundamental issues as fighting poverty and cleaning up the environment.

be2039d78a63.title: Earth Summit
be2039d78a63.sentence: Malaysia was successful at blocking the US-proposed convention on forests and its prime-minister Mahathir Mohamad accused later the global North of exercising eco-imperialism at this summit.

4c27e763dbc8.title: Classical economics
4c27e763dbc8.sentence: Classical economics, also known as the classical school of economics or classical political economy, is a school of thought in political economy that flourished primarily in Britain in the late 18th and early-to-mid 19th century.

340fb0daf3ad.title: Classical economics
340fb0daf3ad.sentence: Its main thinkers are held to be Adam Smith, Jean-Baptiste Say, David Ricardo, Thomas Robert Malthus, and John Stuart Mill.

c5a4fbc05269.title: Classical economics
c5a4fbc05269.sentence: Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations in 1776 is usually considered to mark the beginning of classical economics.

5aafbc4e52d5.title: Classical economics
5aafbc4e52d5.sentence: These economists produced a theory of market economies as largely self-regulating systems, governed by natural laws of production and exchange (famously captured by Adam Smith's metaphor of the invisible hand).

c3b26b4bb22c.title: Classical economics
c3b26b4bb22c.sentence: Adam Smith, following the physiocrat François Quesnay, identified the wealth of a nation with the yearly national income, instead of the king's treasury.

5eb8b6525cd2.title: Classical economics
5eb8b6525cd2.sentence: Smith saw this income as produced by labour, land, and capital.

06da3fc84e28.title: Classical economics
06da3fc84e28.sentence: With property rights to land and capital held by individuals, the national income is divided up between labourers, landlords, and capitalists in the form of wages, rent, and interest or profits.

e722fe57f29a.title: Classical economics
e722fe57f29a.sentence: In terms of international trade, the classical economists were advocates of free trade, which distinguishes them from their mercantilist predecessors, who advocated protectionism.

f80db0bd7162.title: Classical economics
f80db0bd7162.sentence: Ricardo’s most famous economic theory was the theory of comparative advantage as the foundation of the international division of labor.

a41cac87b081.title: Classical economics
a41cac87b081.section: Classical theories of growth and development
a41cac87b081.sentence: However, John Stuart Mill believed that a future stationary state of a constant population size and a constant stock of capital was both inevitable, necessary and desirable for mankind to achieve.

2e3202a7769c.title: Classical economics
2e3202a7769c.section: Classical theories of growth and development
2e3202a7769c.sentence: This is now known as a steady-state economy.

49adaa98cb2c.title: Classical economics
49adaa98cb2c.sentence: Classical economics and many of its ideas remain fundamental in economics, though the theory itself has yielded, since the 1870s, to neoclassical economics.

ec09cf494963.title: Definitions of economics
ec09cf494963.section: Definitions > Say, Carlyle, Mill, and Menger
ec09cf494963.sentence: On the satirical side, Thomas Carlyle (1849) coined 'the dismal science' as an epithet for classical economics, a term often linked to the pessimistic analysis of Malthus (1798).

9e9ceaeb5723.title: Our Common Future
9e9ceaeb5723.sentence: Our Common Future, also known as the Brundtland Report, was published in October 1987 by the United Nations through the Oxford University Press.

b1f04bf832d2.title: Our Common Future
b1f04bf832d2.sentence: Author | World Commission on Environment and Development

03a71f711cf1.title: Our Common Future
03a71f711cf1.sentence: The report's definition of "sustainable development" is possibly the best-known definition of this concept:

eb1809246e61.title: Our Common Future
eb1809246e61.sentence: The report defines sustainable development as "development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs."

af01641f64b2.title: Our Common Future
af01641f64b2.sentence: Our Common Future placed environmental issues firmly on the political agenda: it aimed to discuss the environment and development as one single issue.

04ddc75b9ddd.title: Our Common Future
04ddc75b9ddd.sentence: The report emphasized the interlocking relationship between economic, environmental, and social factors in human development.

7d0d58b77fac.title: Our Common Future
7d0d58b77fac.sentence: The Brundtland Report asserts that poverty reduces sustainability and accelerates environmental pressures – creating a need for the balancing between economy and ecology.

410db7010244.title: Our Common Future
410db7010244.sentence: The report recognized that human resource development in the form of poverty reduction, gender equity, and wealth redistribution was crucial to formulating strategies for environmental conservation, and it also recognized that environmental-limits to economic growth in industrialized and industrializing societies existed.

2c24b7dabaea.title: Our Common Future
2c24b7dabaea.sentence: The document was the culmination of a "900-day" international exercise which catalogued, analysed, and synthesised written submissions and expert testimony from "senior government representatives, scientists and experts, research institutes, industrialists, representatives of non-governmental organizations, and the general public" held at public hearings throughout the world.

693dba860dcd.title: Our Common Future
693dba860dcd.sentence: This publication was in recognition of Gro Harlem Brundtland, former Norwegian Prime Minister and Chair of the World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED).

73f3d89e610d.title: Our Common Future
73f3d89e610d.sentence: The publication of Our Common Future and the work of the World Commission on Environment and Development laid the groundwork for the convening of the 1992 Earth Summit and the adoption of Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration, and led to the establishment of the Commission on Sustainable Development.

8d73835feaa1.title: Our Common Future
8d73835feaa1.sentence: However, in 1988, the Norwegian politician Helge Ole Bergesen wrote that this report is perceived by the Third World elites as green imperialism.

ed21708db4ef.title: Conservation movement
ed21708db4ef.sentence: The conservation movement, also known as nature conservation, is an environmental, social, and political movement, that seeks to manage and protect natural resources, including animal, plant, and other living species as well as their habitat for the future.

8640aa59f71b.title: Conservation movement
8640aa59f71b.sentence: The early conservation movement evolved out of necessity to maintain natural resources such as fisheries, wildlife management, water, soil, as well as conservation and sustainable forestry.

b2811bbefc22.title: Conservation movement
b2811bbefc22.sentence: The conservation movement can be traced back to John Evelyn's work Sylva, which was presented as a paper to the Royal Society in 1662.

048e86df9543.title: Conservation movement
048e86df9543.sentence: Timber resources in England were becoming dangerously depleted at the time, and Evelyn advocated the importance of conserving the forests by managing the rate of depletion and ensuring that the cut down trees get replenished.

969616056105.title: Conservation movement
969616056105.section: History > Origins of the modern conservation movement
969616056105.sentence: The conservation ethic that began to evolve included three core principles: that human activity damaged the environment, that there was a civic duty to maintain the environment for future generations, and that scientific, empirically based methods should be applied to ensure this duty was carried out.

f51b8cbed8df.title: Conservation movement
f51b8cbed8df.section: History > Origins of the modern conservation movement
f51b8cbed8df.sentence: Conservation was revived in the mid-19th century, with the first practical application of scientific conservation principles to the forests of India.

2b35ab2a19c3.title: Conservation movement
2b35ab2a19c3.sentence: The contemporary conservation movement has broadened from the early movement's emphasis on use of sustainable yield of natural resources and preservation of wilderness areas to include preservation of biodiversity.

a7792bfec2fd.title: Conservation movement
a7792bfec2fd.section: History > Racism and the conservation movement
a7792bfec2fd.sentence: The early years of the environmental and conservation movements were rooted in the safeguarding of game to support the recreation activities of elite white men, such as sport hunting.

7cee1bb0343d.title: Conservation movement
7cee1bb0343d.section: History > Racism and the conservation movement
7cee1bb0343d.sentence: Game parks in England and the United States allowed wealthy hunters and fishermen to deplete wildlife, while hunting by Indigenous groups, laborers and the working class, and poor citizens - especially for the express use of sustenance - was vigorously monitored.

ff89746362f1.title: Silent Spring
ff89746362f1.sentence: Silent Spring is an environmental science book by Rachel Carson.

0f0b47e2e329.title: Silent Spring
0f0b47e2e329.sentence: Published on September 27, 1962, the book documented the environmental harm caused by the indiscriminate use of DDT, a pesticide used by soldiers during World War II.

c9317fbcdbf9.title: Silent Spring
c9317fbcdbf9.sentence: Her main argument is that pesticides have detrimental effects on the environment.

8ec68a2b1560.title: Silent Spring
8ec68a2b1560.sentence: She argues these are more properly termed "biocides" because their effects are rarely limited to solely targeting pests.

591b1b11b2e6.title: Silent Spring
591b1b11b2e6.sentence: Carson accuses the chemical industry of intentionally spreading disinformation and public officials of accepting industry claims uncritically.

6217c27828ed.title: Silent Spring
6217c27828ed.sentence: The book was met with fierce opposition by chemical companies, but it swayed public opinion and led to a reversal in US pesticide policy, a nationwide ban on DDT for agricultural uses, and an environmental movement that led to the creation of the US Environmental Protection Agency.

242bc599225b.title: Silent Spring
242bc599225b.section: Impact > Grassroots environmentalism and the EPA
242bc599225b.sentence: Silent Spring became a rallying point for the new social movement in the 1960s.

04f227dd3a11.title: Silent Spring
04f227dd3a11.section: Impact > Grassroots environmentalism and the EPA
04f227dd3a11.sentence: According to environmental engineer and Carson scholar H. Patricia Hynes, "Silent Spring altered the balance of power in the world.

8191db11f97a.title: Silent Spring
8191db11f97a.section: Impact > Grassroots environmentalism and the EPA
8191db11f97a.sentence: No one since would be able to sell pollution as the necessary underside of progress so easily or uncritically." Carson's work and the activism it inspired are partly responsible for the deep ecology movement and the strength of the grassroots environmental movement since the 1960s.

987a19a60d1f.title: Silent Spring
987a19a60d1f.section: Impact > Debate over environmentalism and DDT restrictions
987a19a60d1f.sentence: Carson has been targeted by some organizations opposed to the environmental movement, including Roger Bate of the pro-DDT advocacy group Africa Fighting Malaria and the libertarian think tank Competitive Enterprise Institute (CEI); these sources oppose restrictions on DDT, attribute large numbers of deaths to such restrictions, and argue that Carson was responsible for them.

5a9b3e81b684.title: Silent Spring
5a9b3e81b684.section: Impact > Debate over environmentalism and DDT restrictions
5a9b3e81b684.sentence: These arguments have been dismissed as "outrageous" by former World Health Organization scientist Socrates Litsios.

f17d32080c88.title: Silent Spring
f17d32080c88.section: Impact > Debate over environmentalism and DDT restrictions
f17d32080c88.sentence: Investigative journalist Adam Sarvana and others characterize this notion as a "myth" promoted principally by Bate.

31b06893535c.title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
31b06893535c.sentence: The United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development (UNCSD), also known as Rio 2012, Rio+20 (Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈʁi.u ˈmajʒ ˈvĩtʃi]), or Earth Summit 2012 was the third international conference on sustainable development aimed at reconciling the economic and environmental goals of the global community.

226367dd91bb.title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
226367dd91bb.sentence: Hosted by Brazil in Rio de Janeiro from 13 to 22 June 2012, Rio+20 was a 20-year follow-up to the 1992 United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) held in the same city, and the 10th anniversary of the 2002 World Summit on Sustainable Development (WSSD) in Johannesburg.

e4874f9e29d8.title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
e4874f9e29d8.sentence: The official discussions had two main themes, how to build a green economy to achieve sustainable development and lift people out of poverty, including support for developing countries that will allow them to find a green path for development; and how to improve international coordination for sustainable development by building an institutional framework.

2cbbdf390f0c.title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
2cbbdf390f0c.section: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development > The future we want
2cbbdf390f0c.sentence: At the Rio+20 Conference in June 2012, the heads of state of the 192 governments in attendance, renewed their political commitment to sustainable development and declared their commitment to the promotion of a sustainable future through the 49-page nonbinding document, "The Future We Want: Outcome document of the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, 20–22 June 2012." The dates 20 to 22 June reflect the three-day meeting of world leaders, the culmination of Rio+20.

0fc627071e40.title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
0fc627071e40.section: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development > The future we want
0fc627071e40.sentence: The document, "The Future We Want," called for the development of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a set of measurable targets aimed at promoting sustainable development globally.

ef78f72cd247.title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
ef78f72cd247.section: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development > The future we want
ef78f72cd247.sentence: According to a 23 June 2012 The Guardian article, nations agreed to explore alternatives to GDP as a measure of wealth that take environmental and social factors into account in an effort to assess and pay for 'environmental services' provided by nature, such as carbon sequestration and habitat protection.

2fc2535811a5.title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
2fc2535811a5.section: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development > The future we want
2fc2535811a5.sentence: All nations reaffirmed commitments to phase out fossil fuel subsidies.

f29c49e95ab8.title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
f29c49e95ab8.sentence: The conference also popularised the term blue economy.

7ff6f23cb127.title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
7ff6f23cb127.sentence: A few key global leaders – mostly G20 leaders and namely United States President Barack Obama, German Chancellor Angela Merkel, and UK Prime Minister David Cameron – did not attend the conference and blamed their absence on the ongoing European sovereign-debt crisis.

0b4e8a922d68.title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
0b4e8a922d68.sentence: Their collective absence was seen as a reflection of their administrations' failure to prioritize sustainability issues.

b24fa34f2286.title: Club of Rome
b24fa34f2286.sentence: The Club of Rome is a nonprofit, informal organization of intellectuals and business leaders whose goal is a critical discussion of pressing global issues.

84e619bbbdb6.title: Club of Rome
84e619bbbdb6.sentence: The Club of Rome was founded in 1968 at Accademia dei Lincei in Rome, Italy.

c9ce69805e65.title: Club of Rome
c9ce69805e65.sentence: In 1965, the Italian industrialist Aurelio Peccei gave a speech about the dramatic scientific and technological changes happening in the world.

ead06f45fdb4.title: Club of Rome
ead06f45fdb4.sentence: The speech was noticed by Alexander King, a British scientist who had advised the British government, and who was currently serving as Director-General for Scientific Affairs at the OECD.

cc6e17de5b24.title: Club of Rome
cc6e17de5b24.sentence: The pair shared a lack of confidence that the problems faced by the world could be solved by development and technological progress.

ce38f6839fac.title: Club of Rome
ce38f6839fac.sentence: After the meeting, Peccei, King, Jantsch, and Hugo Thiemann decided to form the Club of Rome, named for the city of their meeting.

b171d192c8f8.title: Club of Rome
b171d192c8f8.sentence: Published in 1972, its computer simulations suggested that growth of production and consumption could not continue indefinitely because of either resource depletion or unmanageable levels of pollution.

da49e24186f9.title: Club of Rome
da49e24186f9.sentence: The report went on to sell 30 million copies in more than 30 languages, making it the best-selling environmental book in history.

981c8a786559.title: Club of Rome
981c8a786559.sentence: Although the Club of Rome had enjoyed some influence at the OECD, their questioning of the value of growth "deepened the internal fractures within the OECD and provoked hostile reactions, leading to a revitalization of the strong pro-growth position." A 1973 booklet on the OECD's approach to environmental issues stated that the role of governments in "an acceptable human environment must now be developed in the framework of policies for economic growth".

25cc87293056.title: Club of Rome
25cc87293056.sentence: The OECD had given up on the Club of Rome, and set its course on a trajectory of unfettered growth.

f598552463cb.title: Club of Rome
f598552463cb.sentence: Economist Robert Solow, recipient of a Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, criticized The Limits to Growth (LTG) as having "simplistic" scenarios.

0cba3df55ec6.title: Club of Rome
0cba3df55ec6.sentence: In 1973, an interdisciplinary team at Sussex University's Science Policy Research Unit reviewed the structure and assumptions of the models used and published their analysis in Models of Doom, finding that the forecasts of the world's future are very sensitive to a few unduly pessimistic key assumptions.

42697694e725.title: Club of Rome
42697694e725.sentence: [But] Thirty years later, the situation may have changed.

d016c996aa24.title: Club of Rome
d016c996aa24.sentence: It is possible that real demands on natural resources, and therefore on the natural environment, will be dramatically different in a world in which India and China, and other countries, too, grow at 8 or 10 percent a year, and need to pass through the material-goods-intensive phase of growth before they arrive at the service economy... it will probably be more important in the future to deal intellectually, quantitatively, as well as practically, with the mutual interdependence of economic growth, natural resource availability, and environmental constraints."

72eb224f3624.title: Club of Rome
72eb224f3624.sentence: As of 2025, there have been 55 reports to the club.

859952fed6a2.title: Club of Rome
859952fed6a2.sentence: Led by the Club of Rome, the BI Norwegian Business School and the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, a group of researchers and policymakers assessed global risks and identified five pathways to catalyze transformation and systemic change towards sustainability: energy, food, poverty, inequality and population (including health and education).

040c37be1d59.title: Club of Rome
040c37be1d59.sentence: The results are published in the book "Earth for All" in 2022 alongside the 50th anniversary of the first Earth Summit in Stockholm and the initial publication of the Limits to Growth in 1972.

14e7b36289bb.title: Earth Day
14e7b36289bb.sentence: Earth Day is an annual event on April 22 to demonstrate support for environmental protection.

9c0a92415d32.title: Earth Day

166d7a802c85.title: International Union for Conservation of Nature
166d7a802c85.sentence: IUCN is considered one of the most influential conservation organizations and, together with World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) and the World Resources Institute (WRI), is seen as a driving force behind the rise of the influence of environmental organizations at the UN and around the world.

17cf45f123e9.title: World Resources Institute
17cf45f123e9.sentence: WRI partnered with Google Earth Engine to develop Global Forest Watch (GFW), an open-source web application that uses Landsat satellite imagery to map forest changes.

b0933aeae3aa.title: World Resources Institute
b0933aeae3aa.sentence: In 1997 and 2000, WRI published the first comparative study of material flow accounting (MFA), using time series data to comprehensively assess all material inputs and outputs (excluding water) used by industrial economies.

ff4afe301a25.title: World Resources Institute

9fa368374dda.title: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
9fa368374dda.sentence: The Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market (ICVCM) is an independent governance body that publishes the Core Carbon Principles (CCPs) and related guidance intended to define high-level integrity criteria for carbon credits used in the voluntary carbon market.

7d32df06919d.title: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
7d32df06919d.sentence: ICVCM was established in 2021 following recommendations of the Taskforce on Scaling Voluntary Carbon Markets (TSVCM).

85317835a236.title: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
85317835a236.sentence: In January 2021, the Taskforce on Scaling Voluntary Carbon Markets (TSVCM), a private-sector initiative, published a blueprint for scaling voluntary carbon markets and said it planned to launch a governance body intended to set "core carbon standards".

2c2a3071bbc5.title: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
2c2a3071bbc5.sentence: ICVCM publishes an assessment framework, definitions, and an assessment procedure, and it assesses carbon crediting programs against those requirements to determine whether a program is "CCP-Eligible".

7b0784a8c3a8.title: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
7b0784a8c3a8.sentence: Carbon crediting programs may be assessed as CCP-Eligible, and CCP-Eligible programs may apply a registry-based "CCP-Approved" label to credits from approved categories, using ICVCM implementation guidance for tagging and labelling.

25f435b39b22.title: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
25f435b39b22.sentence: In 2024, ICVCM said that several renewable energy crediting methodologies would not be eligible for the CCP label, citing additionality concerns.

b4fa84cd372d.title: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
b4fa84cd372d.sentence: Reuters has also covered ICVCM benchmark tests and later decisions on approval of specific credit types under the CCP framework, including an August 2024 test in which around a third of credits did not meet the benchmark threshold, and later approvals of certain deforestation and clean cookstove credit types under the benchmark.

21f3b4c70043.title: Psychological impact of climate change
21f3b4c70043.sentence: The psychological impacts of climate change concerns effects that climate change can have on individuals' mental and emotional well-being.

c6e85aa40882.title: Psychological impact of climate change
c6e85aa40882.sentence: Three causal pathways by which climate change causes psychological effects have been suggested: direct, indirect, or via psychosocial awareness.

3730f080dc36.title: Psychological impact of climate change
3730f080dc36.sentence: The direct channel includes stress-related conditions being caused by exposure to extreme weather events, such as cyclones and wildfires, causing conditions such as PTS and anxiety disorder.

97ba3cd63dce.title: Psychological impact of climate change
97ba3cd63dce.sentence: Climate change reduces agricultural output and makes an area unattractive for tourism.

3c7f53c20b85.title: Psychological impact of climate change
3c7f53c20b85.sentence: This can cause significant stress, which in turn can lead to depression and other adverse psychological conditions.

f171521a273b.title: Psychological impact of climate change
f171521a273b.section: Pathways > Direct impact > Increased temperatures and heatwaves > Suicide rates
f171521a273b.sentence: Using data from the US and Mexico, suicide rates were found to increase by 0.7% and 3.1%, respectively, for a 1 °C increase in monthly average temperature.

ee6fb6e903b7.title: Psychological impact of climate change
ee6fb6e903b7.sentence: Conditions such as eco-anxiety are very rarely severe enough to require clinical treatment.

2c2d4075f5ec.title: National Adaptation Programme of Action
2c2d4075f5ec.sentence: A National Adaptation Programme of Action (NAPA) is a type of plan submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) by least developed countries, to describe the country's perception of its most "urgent and immediate needs to adapt to climate change".

df60190b5faf.title: National Adaptation Programme of Action
df60190b5faf.sentence: As part of the NAPA process, LDC government ministries, typically assisted by development agencies, assess their countries' vulnerability to climate change and extreme weather events.

f3abe59e533c.title: National Adaptation Programme of Action
f3abe59e533c.sentence: LDCs then develop a prioritized list of adaptation projects that will help the country cope with the adverse effects of climate change.

074e6e910019.title: National Adaptation Programme of Action
074e6e910019.sentence: NAPAs are not supposed to include original research, but use existing information and include profiles of priority projects that are intended to address those needs that have been identified.

3812136ca042.title: National Adaptation Programme of Action
3812136ca042.sentence: The Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF) was established to finance the preparation of NAPAs and to implement the projects that they propose.

1494aad5211e.title: National Adaptation Programme of Action
1494aad5211e.sentence: LDCs who submit NAPAs to the UNFCCC then become eligible for funding through the LDCF for NAPA projects.

d6000d05cc7d.title: National Adaptation Programme of Action
d6000d05cc7d.sentence: The LDCF currently has resources of at least US$415 million, of which US$177 million has been approved for 47 projects, attracting more than US$550 million in co-financing in the process.
